prs.title: feat(ui): introduce StyleSpan abstraction to reduce per-character allocations
prs.body:
## Summary

Introduce `StyleSpan` abstraction to eliminate per-character object allocations in terminal UI rendering, (280MB+ V8 heap bloat in complex `TableRenderer` scenarios).

Instead of allocating one object per character via `ink's` `toStyledCharacters()`, this PR uses `Run-Length Encoding` to group consecutive same-styled characters into single `StyleSpan` objects, significantly reducing memory usage during large table renders.

## Details

**Problem**:

Issue #23741 reports 280MB+ V8 heap bloat when rendering multiple markdown tables. The root cause is ink's `toStyledCharacters()` which allocates one JavaScript object per character:

- 100 cells × 50 chars = 5,000 objects per table
- Complex UI with 10+ tables = 280MB+ heap bloat
- Result: GC pressure, stuttering UI, memory leaks in long-running processes

**Solution**:

Introduced a `StyleSpan` abstraction using Run-Length Encoding consecutive characters with identical styling are grouped into a single span instead of individual objects. Most table content has uniform styling across entire cells and rows, making RLE highly effective here.

**Implementation**:

**New `styleSpan.ts`** provides 8 functions replicating `ink's` styling API:
- `ansiToStyleSpans()` — converts ANSI text to `StyleSpan` arrays
- `styleSpansWidth()` — display width respecting emoji/combining marks
- `wrapStyleSpans()` — multi-line wrapping respecting `maxWidth`
- `breakStyleSpansIntoWords()` — word-breaking while preserving styles
- `styleSpansToANSIString()` — reconstructs `ANSI codes` for terminal output
- `stylesEqual()` — efficient style comparison without `JSON.stringify`

**Updated**:

`TableRenderer.tsx` replaces all ink function calls with `StyleSpan` equivalents. Output is identical — this is a pure backend optimization.

**Testing**:

- 42 unit tests in `styleSpan.test.ts` covering parsing, width, wrapping, word-breaking, and `RLE` efficiency
- 28 integration tests in `TableRenderer.test.tsx` including snapshot tests confirming output is identical to the previous approach

**Trade-offs**:

- Adds an O(n) grouping pass per cell, but saves millions of object allocations per render — net result is faster rendering due to reduced GC pressure
- Avoids forking or patching ink directly, keeping the fix self-contained

## Related Issues

Fixes #23741
Related to #22789 (Parent: JavaScript heap out of memory)

## How to Validate

1. Build and run `gemini-cli` in debug mode:
 - Run this command `npm run build -w packages/cli`
```
2. Open `chrome://inspect` → attach DevTools → Memory tab
3. Take **Snapshot 1** at idle
4. Send a prompt like this:
```
Sample Prompt: `Create a detailed table of all 195 countries with columns: country, capital, population, GDP, continent, currency, language, and independence year`

5. After table finishes rendering take Snapshot 2
6. Switch to Comparison view → sort by # Delta
7. Confirm `DataLimitedLruMap` retained size is significantly lower than pre-fix baseline

## Pre-Merge Checklist

<!-- Check all that apply before requesting review or merging. -->

- [X] Built and tested locally
- [X] Existing tests pass
- [X] New tests added for `style-span.ts` helper functions
- [X] No breaking changes to public API
- [X] No regressions in table or text rendering output
- [X] Performance validated (no degradation)
- [X] Memory optimization documented and verified

prs.title: fix(core): fix detectPowerShellSubstitution quote tracking and false positives
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes false positive command substitution detection in `detectPowerShellSubstitution` on Windows.
When quotes or escaped characters were present within double-quoted strings (such as `\"`, `""`, or nested single quotes), the parser's `inDoubleQuote` state tracking desynchronized, causing legitimate commands with parentheses (like `git log --format="%h \" (%an)"` or `git commit -m "fix(core): \"quoted\" (detail)"`) to be falsely blocked with a command injection warning.

## Details
1. **Quote State Machine Tracking**:
   - Inside single quotes: In PowerShell, `''` escapes a single quote; handle doubled single quotes `''` without exiting single quote mode.
   - Inside double quotes: In PowerShell, `""` escapes a double quote; handle doubled double quotes `""` without exiting double quote mode.
   - Backslash escape handling: Windows executables and wrappers frequently escape quotes as `\"`. In double quotes, consume backslash escape sequences `['$', '`', '"', '\\', '(', ')', "'"]` via `i += 2` so `\"` does not prematurely toggle `inDoubleQuote` to `false`.
   - Outside quotes: Handle general escape sequences (`\` and `` ` ``) so escaped parens like `\(` are not flagged as unquoted subexpressions.
2. **Regression Testing**:
   - Added unit test suite in `packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts` testing escaped double quotes with parens, doubled quotes, escaped substitution syntax, and verifying that actual malicious subexpressions (`$()`, `@()`, bare `()`) remain strictly blocked.
   - Added regression test in `packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts` verifying end-to-end execution of PowerShell commands with nested/escaped quotes and parentheses.

## Related Issues
Fixes #29738

## How to Validate
1. Run PowerShell with nested quotes and parentheses:
   ```powershell
   git commit -m "fix(core): \"quoted\" (detail)"
   git log --format="%h \" (%an)"
   echo "a \" b (c)"
   ```
   **Expected**: Commands execute cleanly without being blocked by command injection detection.
2. Run command injection attempts:
   ```powershell
   echo (whoami)
   echo $(whoami)
   echo @(whoami)
   ```
   **Expected**: Blocked with command injection warning.
3. Run test suites:
   - `packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts`
   - `packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts`

prs.title: fix(core): strip trailing punctuation and unbalanced brackets from web_fetch URLs
prs.body:
## Summary

- `parsePrompt()` in `packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.ts` split the prompt on whitespace and passed each token straight to `new URL()`, which accepts a trailing comma. A comma-separated list of URLs therefore produced polluted URLs (e.g. `https://example.com/,`) that failed downstream in confirmation, the `<authorized_urls>` block and the fallback fetch.
- Added `cleanUrlToken()`, which strips trailing sentence punctuation (`. `, `,`, `;`, `:`) and unbalanced closing brackets from each token before validation. `?` and `!` are kept intact since they can be meaningful query/path characters, and balanced brackets (e.g. `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar)`) are preserved.
- Updated the existing test that asserted the old behavior (trailing `.` kept in the URL) and added cases for each punctuation character, unbalanced brackets, `?`/`!` URLs, and the exact comma-separated list from the issue.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/tools/web-fetch.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 70 tests pass.
- `eslint` and `tsc --noEmit` clean on the changed files.

Fixes #29896

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

With tool search enabled, MCP tools are deferred and `/context` shows "MCP Tools 0" for the default agent for the whole session.

When a custom agent is selected (`--agent` or `/agent`), deferral only holds for the first model call. From the second call on, every tool of every configured MCP server is loaded into context. In my case that is 26.9k tokens (one server with ~100 tools), added to every request.

Side effect: `tool_search_tool` then returns "No tools found" because the tools are already loaded (same symptom as #4773, different cause).

It happens with a minimal custom agent that has no `tools:` list, so it is not specific to the agent content.


### Affected version

1.0.98

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure an MCP server with many tools in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, with `"toolSearch": true` and `"dynamicRetrieval": { "mcp": true }` in settings.json.
2. Create a minimal custom agent (name + description + one line of instructions, no `tools:` list).
3. Run `copilot --agent "<agent name>"`.
4. Send `hi`, then run `/context` -> MCP Tools: 0.
5. Send any second prompt, then run `/context` -> MCP Tools: 26.9k (all tools of the server listed).
6. Repeat without `--agent` -> MCP Tools stays 0 for the whole session.

Same in non-interactive mode: `copilot -p "Hi" --agent "<agent name>"`. In `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`, the `session.usage_record` events show:
- call 1: toolTokenCount=11485, inputTokens=27051
- call 2: toolTokenCount=40069, inputTokens=66329, cacheReadTokens=0 (prompt cache invalidated)
- requestBodyBytes unchanged (~170 KB) on both calls
Without `--agent`, toolTokenCount stays constant (11207) on every call.

### Expected behavior

Custom agents keep deferred MCP tool loading like the default agent: MCP tools are loaded only when found via tool search, and the tool list does not change between calls (so the prompt cache is not invalidated).


### Additional context

Windows, Claude Opus 5.5 (also seen with Claude Sonnet 5.5).
Impact: ~27-39k extra tokens on every call of every custom-agent session, plus a prompt cache miss on the second call.
Workaround: `--disable-mcp-server <name>` for servers the agent does not need.
Related: #4773 ("Found 0 tools" for an already-loaded namespace).

issues.title: macOS: Entra-broker MCP servers fail at startup: concurrent sign-ins rejected ("sign-in is already in progress") and rejected cached token not recovered
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On macOS, two Entra-protected remote MCP servers (Azure DevOps remote MCP at `https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>` and the WorkIQ plugin at `https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp`) fail to connect at session startup. The failures happen in the native Entra account-broker path that 1.0.95 introduced.

The logs show two separate problems.

**1. Concurrent broker sign-ins are rejected instead of queued**

When both servers need a token at startup, both call the account broker at the same time. The CLI's broker wrapper allows only one interactive request per process and throws for the second request. The second request is not queued:

```
[ERROR] Signing in with your Microsoft Entra account (account broker)...
[ERROR] Signing in with your Microsoft Entra account (account broker)...
[WARNING] Entra token acquisition failed {"server_url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>","error":"Entra broker error: Error: A Microsoft sign-in is already in progress. Complete or cancel it before trying again."}
[ERROR] OAuth authentication failed for ado-remote-mcp: MCPOAuthError: Microsoft Entra sign-in for https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org> failed: Entra broker error: Error: A Microsoft sign-in is already in progress. ...
```

Which server fails depends on timing. The `/mcp` reconnect hits the same collision. The guard is in the broker plugin's `acquireTokenInteractive`, which throws when `this.interactiveRequest` is already set.

**2. Startup cannot recover from a token that the server rejects**

At startup the cached WorkIQ token returns HTTP 401. The CLI then asks the broker for a new token, and the broker returns the same token. The connection fails:

```
[WARNING] the Entra account broker returned the rejected access token {"server_url":"https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp"}
[ERROR] OAuth authentication failed for workiq: MCPOAuthError: Microsoft Entra sign-in for https://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft/mcp failed: Entra broker error: the broker returned the rejected access token
```

This repeats on every new session. A token that the broker issued about 30 minutes earlier, and that WorkIQ accepted then, was rejected in the later session. The 1.0.101 changelog says *explicit* sign-in recovers from rejected cached tokens. The automatic startup and refresh path does not recover. While the WorkIQ request holds the broker, it also blocks the ADO request (problem 1).

The tenant enforces a Conditional Access sign-in frequency policy. Other Entra clients on the same machine report AADSTS70043. I suspect this is why tokens that are still within their lifetime get rejected.

### Expected behavior

- The CLI queues or serializes concurrent broker sign-ins across MCP servers instead of failing them.
- When a server rejects the token the broker returns, the startup and refresh path bypasses the broker's cached token (for example with a forced refresh or a claims request) or falls back to interactive sign-in. It should not fail the connection.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.103

### Environment

- macOS 27.0.1 (Apple silicon)
- Microsoft Enterprise SSO extension (Company Portal) installed
- Remote HTTP MCP servers: Azure DevOps remote MCP (`mcp-config.json`, no `oauthClientId`) and the WorkIQ plugin (`workiq@work-iq`)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Azure DevOps remote MCP server and install the WorkIQ plugin.
2. Sign in to both once, then wait until the cached tokens are rejected (in this tenant, roughly 30 minutes or more).
3. Start a new `copilot` session.
4. Neither server loads tools. The logs show the errors above.

issues.title: Feature request: local web interface (like `opencode web`)

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
## Motivation

OpenCode ([opencode.ai](https://opencode.ai)) recently shipped `opencode web` — a command that starts a **local HTTP server and serves a browser-based UI** for the AI coding agent. This is a killer feature that Copilot CLI currently lacks.

Copilot CLI is terminal-only (TUI), which limits the experience to one dimension.

## What `opencode web` does

```
$ opencode web
                                   ▄
  █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀▄ █▀▀▀ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀█
  █  █ █  █ █▀▀▀ █  █ █    █  █ █  █ █▀▀▀
  ▀▀▀▀ █▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀

  Web interface:      http://127.0.0.1:4096/
```

Key capabilities:
- **Local HTTP server** bound to `127.0.0.1` with a configurable port (`--port`)
- **Full browser UI** — chat, file tree, diff viewer, session management
- **TUI attach** — `opencode attach http://localhost:4096` lets you connect a terminal session to the same server, sharing state/sessions
- **Auth** — optional HTTP basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`
- **mDNS discovery** — `--mdns` for LAN access
- **CORS support** — `--cors` for custom domains

## Proposed feature: `copilot web`

```bash
$ copilot web
# Starts a local HTTP server and opens the browser
# equivalent to: copilot --acp + web UI frontend
```

### Benefits over terminal-only

| Feature | Terminal (TUI) | Web interface |
|---|---|---|
| Syntax-highlighted diffs | Basic | Rich, side-by-side |
| File tree navigation | Manual `@` mentions | Clickable tree |
| Multi-session management | `/resume` | Session tabs |
| Code review UX | Scroll through text | Inline comments, annotations |
| Mobile/tablet use | Not practical | Fully usable |
| Accessibility | Screen-reader flag | Native browser a11y |
| Sharing | `--share-gist` | URL sharing, screenshots |

### Implementation notes

- Copilot CLI already has the `--acp` (Agent Client Protocol) server mode — the web UI could be a thin client on top of that
- Could be implemented as a built-in plugin or separate package
- The `--remote` flag already enables GitHub web control — but that is cloud-dependent; a local web server is simpler, faster, and works offline

## References

- OpenCode web docs: https://opencode.ai/docs/cli#web
- OpenCode repo: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode

### Describe the bug

In the Copilot SDK integration in VS Code, the shell tool rejects a harmless
`/bin/echo` request when the command adds only a HOME override to a newly created
owned empty directory. The same target passes with `env -i` and no assignment.

The tool reports `script_action_changed`:

> The script or its execution context changed after permission evaluation. Retry the command to review the current script.

This was not reproduced in a standalone Copilot CLI session. The installed
VS Code agent host imports a separate Copilot SDK, and the component owning
this freshness guard has not been established. Please route to the SDK/host
owner if this is not the correct tracker.

### Affected version

Freshly inspected installed public application/package metadata:

- VS Code: 1.141.0, stable.
- VS Code build commit: 2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c.
- Bundled Copilot extension: 0.69.0.
- Bundled `@github/copilot` package: 1.0.73.
- Installed `@github/copilot-sdk-darwin-arm64` platform package:
  1.0.17-unstable.37397886721.gad270aa.

These are package metadata, not standalone `copilot --version` output. It is
not established that updating the standalone CLI would update this host's
guard. No version change was made during the comparison.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Use the VS Code Copilot SDK shell tool with an existing, newly created owned
empty directory. Replace `<NEW_OWNED_EMPTY_DIRECTORY>` below with that
directory's absolute path; it is a parameter, not an actual private path.

Send separate sequential tool requests in synchronous mode, with an initial
wait of 30 seconds, stopping at the first non-pass:

```sh
/bin/echo GUARD_ECHO_FACTORS_OK
/usr/bin/env /bin/echo GUARD_ECHO_FACTORS_OK
/usr/bin/env -i /bin/echo GUARD_ECHO_FACTORS_OK
/usr/bin/env -i HOME="<NEW_OWNED_EMPTY_DIRECTORY>" /bin/echo GUARD_ECHO_FACTORS_OK
```

Observed once per arm, without retries:

| Request | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Direct echo | Exact fixed sentinel, exit code 0 |
| Echo through env | Exact fixed sentinel, exit code 0 |
| Echo through env -i | Exact fixed sentinel, exit code 0 |
| Same env -i target plus HOME assignment | Guard rejected after 18 ms; telemetry category script_action_changed |

For the rejected request, no target exit code or output was exposed. The
18 ms value is tool-request elapsed time, not target-process runtime.

No Node, script file, package manager, PATH assignment or NODE_OPTIONS
assignment is needed for this reproduction. The owned directory remained
empty and was removed afterward. No permission settings were changed.

### Expected behavior

Evaluate the declared isolated environment consistently between permission
evaluation and launch. If a HOME override is intentionally restricted, report
the specific restriction instead of describing an unchanged request as having
changed after evaluation.

A supported remedy must retain owned-HOME isolation and normal permission
evaluation; bypassing the freshness guard or dropping isolation is not an
acceptable workaround.

### Additional context

- Platform: macOS ARM64.
- Surface: Copilot SDK/agent host in VS Code, not a standalone CLI terminal.
- Only parameterized commands, fixed sentinel/error facts, timings and public
  version details are provided. No private paths, repository information,
  credentials, configuration files or session logs are attached.
- This single sequential comparison isolates the HOME-assignment request
  factor, not the internal cause. Sequential session/permission state and the
  particular owned HOME value remain limitations; other values and assignment
  forms were not tested.
- Recent public CLI release notes did not identify an exact fix. A restart or
  upgrade has not been verified as a remedy.

Could you confirm whether permission-time versus launch-time action identity
uses inconsistent HOME-derived context, or whether this is intended policy,
and identify a supported fix for the VS Code SDK host?

issues.title: /restart fails when the CLI was launched with --new-session-id

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
### What happened

Launching the CLI with `--new-session-id <uuid>` and then running `/restart` fails every time:

```
error: the argument '--new-session-id <id>' cannot be used with '--session-id <id>'

Usage: copilot --log-dir <directory> --plugin-dir <directory> --add-dir <directory> --additional-mcp-config <json> --yolo

For more information, try '--help'.
```

By the time this surfaces the foreground session has already been shut down, so the restart is not recoverable.

### Repro

1. `copilot --new-session-id 11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555` (any fresh UUID)
2. Run `/restart`

This matters for embedding hosts, which pass `--new-session-id` on every session launch, so `/restart` is permanently unusable there rather than occasionally.

### Cause

`/restart` rebuilds the child argv from `process.argv.slice(2)`, strips the session-selection flags, then appends `--session-id <current session id>`.

In `cli-main.js` (1.0.98) the strip helper removes `-r`, `--resume`, `--resume=`, `--session-id`, `--session-id=`, `--continue`, `--cloud`, `-i`, `--interactive`, `--interactive=`, `--experimental`, `--no-experimental`, `--fleet` and `-C`. `--new-session-id` is absent from that list, so it survives into the restart argv next to the freshly appended `--session-id`, and the parser declares the two mutually exclusive.

The same rebuilt argv is persisted for the supervised restart path, so both the supervised and unsupervised paths fail identically.

### Expected

The strip helper should drop `--new-session-id` and `--new-session-id=<uuid>`, consuming the following value in the bare form, exactly as it already does for `--session-id`. The session exists by restart time, so re-asserting a creation ID is both wrong and rejected.

### Workaround

Patching the strip helper locally to treat `--new-session-id` like `--session-id` resolves it, but the file lives in the extracted package folder and the fix is lost on every CLI update.

### Version

1.0.98 on Windows, win32-x64.

issues.title: Context window rollover fails: "checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
# Context window rollover fails: "checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

### Describe the bug
Long-running agent sessions crash when the context window fills and the runtime attempts a rollover:

```
Execution failed: Failed to start a fresh context window: checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover
```

The turn ends and the session (or sub-agent) is effectively dead; it recurs on subsequent turns in the same session.

### What we observed
- The agent **had** written a `checkpoint.md` to the session's `files/` folder (via a normal file write / patch) ~7 minutes before the first failure, yet the runtime still reported it as absent "for this agent".
- The native runtime contains related errors ("Replacing checkpoint.md requires expected_revision; read or stat it first, or use append", "Stale checkpoint writer…"), which suggests checkpoints must be written through a runtime-managed store/tool rather than a plain file write. In our sessions the model did not appear to have any tool exposed for that store, so it could never satisfy the precondition.
- Seen repeatedly across multiple sessions/sub-agents (custom agents and the main agent), mostly in long tool-heavy sessions (builds, test runs, large tool outputs).

### Expected behavior
Either the runtime writes/derives the checkpoint itself before rollover, or the agent is given (and prompted to use) the tool needed to create it. Failing that, it should fall back to normal compaction instead of terminating the turn.

### Environment
- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.100 (also seen on 1.0.98)
- Windows 11 x64, PowerShell
- Models: GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 sessions

### Workaround
Manual `/compact` before the context fills avoids it.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

# Bug report: HTTP 400 `content[].thinking` after a background shell completion notification

## Summary

When a background shell command outlives its turn and completes, the runtime delivers a
`system.notification`("Shell command ... has completed") at the start of a **new** turn. The
assistant message synthesized for that turn is persisted **without its thinking blocks**, so
the next request replays an assistant turn that has `toolRequests` but no `reasoningBlocks`
while thinking mode is enabled. The upstream API correctly rejects it.

## Environment

- CLI: `GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.88` (latest; `copilot update` reports no newer release)
- Model: `deepseek-flash`
- OS: linux (x64)
- Interactive session, tools enabled

Note: the CLI logs `unknown token count multiplier {"model_id":"deepseek-flash"}` at startup;
the bundled `changelog.json` contains no DeepSeek entries at all.

## Exact error

```json
{
  "type": "session.error",
  "data": {
    "errorType": "query",
    "message": "400 The `content[].thinking` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.",
    "statusCode": 400
  }
}
```

## Evidence

Across every session on this machine (`~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl`):

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| `assistant.message` events **with** `reasoningBlocks` | 582 |
| `assistant.message` events **without** `reasoningBlocks` | 8 |
| `session.error` with `statusCode: 400` (this message) | 8 |

**Exactly 1:1.** In all 8 cases the failing request is immediately preceded by one of the
8 degenerate messages, and in all 8 cases the degenerate message is immediately preceded by a
shell-completion `system.notification`.

The single non-400 `session.error` in the corpus ("Session host did not acknowledge ...") is
preceded by a *normal* 12-key assistant message, which is a useful negative control.

## Shape comparison

Normal streamed assistant message (31 of 32 in the interactive session):

```
['apiCallId','content','interactionId','messageId','model','originatingMessageId',
 'reasoningBlocks','reasoningOpaque','reasoningText','rte','toolRequests','turnId']
```

Synthesized message that triggers the 400 (1 of 32):

```
['content','messageId','toolRequests']        <-- reasoningBlocks + reasoningOpaque MISSING
```

## Minimal reproduction

```
tool.execution_complete    # background shell finishes
assistant.turn_end
assistant.turn_start       # new turn
system.notification        # "Shell command \"<desc>\" (shellId: N) has completed successfully."
assistant.message          # {content:"", messageId, toolRequests}  <-- no reasoning fields
session.error              # 400 The `content[].thinking` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.
```

Concrete instances observed (all identical in structure):

- session `67c30607-7606-4666-aa94-ba687b57f22d`, event index 203 → 400 at `2026-09-23T00:06:52.455Z`
  (foreground shell id 5 completing was the notification source)
- session `a8233a5c-4e04-457a-ab70-950ef0aaf4c3`, event indexes 337, 546, 570, 623, 653, 700, 745
  → 400 at `2026-09-22T23:31:20`, `23:47:53`, `23:48:28`, `23:50:46`, `23:51:25`, `23:52:43`, `23:55:02`

Reproduction is highly reliable: 8 triggers, 8 failures, 0 misses.

## Root cause

The 400 is **not** an upstream/model outage. The API is enforcing a documented thinking-mode
contract: when thinking is enabled, the thinking block returned with an assistant turn must be
replayed verbatim on subsequent requests (it carries an opaque signature). The runtime drops
`reasoningBlocks` / `reasoningOpaque` on the code path that synthesizes the assistant turn for a
shell-completion notification, then replays that thinking-less turn while thinking is still on.

Because the synthesized message also lacks `model`, `apiCallId`, `turnId` and `interactionId`,
it is clearly produced by a different (non-streaming) construction path than normal model output.

## Impact

Every occurrence kills one turn with an opaque 400, in the middle of otherwise healthy sessions.
Recovery requires the user to re-prompt ("continue") or abandon the session. It is most likely to
hit long autonomous runs that rely on backgrounded commands, which is exactly when it is most
disruptive.

## Suggested fix

Whichever internal path constructs the assistant message for a shell-completion
`system.notification` must carry the turn's `reasoningBlocks` and `reasoningOpaque` through to
the session event, so the replayed transcript stays consistent with thinking mode. Alternatively,
the request builder should not send a thinking-less assistant turn while thinking is enabled
(e.g. drop thinking for that request rather than emitting an invalid transcript).

## Workarounds (user side)

1. Avoid shell commands that outlive the turn (no backgrounded/detached work), so no
   completion notification lands at the start of a new turn.
2. `--reasoning-effort none` / `effortLevel: "none"` in `settings.json` removes the thinking-mode
   requirement. Caveat: for models the CLI classifies as adaptive-only, turning thinking off only
   lowers reasoning effort, so this may not eliminate the failure.
3. Start a new session (`/new`) to drop the poisoned transcript — recurrence is expected, since
   the trigger is not history-dependent.
4. Report with `/feedback` and attach `/collect-debug-logs`.

## Non-fixes (checked)

- **Rollback**: no release in the bundled `changelog.json` contains a fix for this bug class
  (0 hits for reasoning-block persistence; the only thinking-shape fixes are Claude/Anthropic
  specific and predate 1.0.80). 1.0.86 is still in `~/.cache/copilot/pkg/linux-x64/` if a
  regression test is wanted. Neither `app.js` nor `runtime.node` contains the error string, so
  the message is generated server-side.
- **`copilot update`**: already on the latest release (1.0.88).


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.88

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

normal cli session which backgrounds. see description.

### Expected behavior

no 400 error

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: Model-Facing `skill()` Tool Registers Plugin Skills Under Bare Names Unless the Name Collides, So `plugin:skill` Fails

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
## Describe the Bug

Slash commands got `/plugin:skill` names in #1766, but the model-facing `skill()` tool never did. A plugin skill with a unique name is registered bare. So `skill("alpha:unique")` returns `Skill not found`. Prefixes only appear once two loaded plugins ship the same skill name, and then both copies get one.

Whether `alpha:unique` resolves depends on which other plugins are installed. Add an unrelated plugin that happens to ship a `unique` skill and the name flips from bare to prefixed, which breaks any instruction that used the bare form. That hurts most for plugins whose skills call each other, and for plugins shared with Claude Code, Codex CLI or Pi, all of which resolve `plugin:skill`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create two throwaway plugins. `alpha` ships skills `unique` and `shared`. `beta` ships `shared`. Each skill is a plain `SKILL.md`:

   ```text
   plugins/alpha/.copilot-plugin/plugin.json   {"name":"alpha","version":"0.0.1","skills":"./skills/"}
   plugins/alpha/skills/unique/SKILL.md        name: unique
   plugins/alpha/skills/shared/SKILL.md        name: shared
   plugins/beta/.copilot-plugin/plugin.json    {"name":"beta","version":"0.0.1","skills":"./skills/"}
   plugins/beta/skills/shared/SKILL.md         name: shared
   ```

2. List skills:

   ```text
   $ copilot --plugin-dir plugins/alpha --plugin-dir plugins/beta skill list
     alpha:shared - ...
     unique - ...
     beta:shared - ...
   ```

3. Ask the model to call the `skill()` tool:

   ```text
   copilot --plugin-dir plugins/alpha --plugin-dir plugins/beta -p 'Call the skill tool four times, separately, with these exact names: "alpha:unique", "unique", "alpha:shared", "beta:shared". Do not do anything the skills instruct. For each, report only the exact name and whether the tool returned "Skill not found" or loaded content. Then stop.'
   ```

4. Result:

   ```text
   ✗ skill(alpha:unique) Skill not found: alpha:unique
   ● skill(unique)
   ● skill(alpha:shared)
   ● skill(beta:shared)
   ```

## Expected Behavior

Qualified names should always resolve, with bare names as a fallback when only one plugin owns them. Claude Code does exactly this with the same two plugins:

- `alpha:unique` and bare `unique` both load.
- `alpha:shared` and `beta:shared` both load.
- Bare `shared` fails with this error:

  ```text
  Unknown skill: shared. Several skills match that name: alpha:shared, beta:shared — invoke one by its full name.
  ```

Doing the same in the `skill()` tool and `copilot skill list` would keep existing bare-name instructions working too.

## How Other CLIs Name the Same Skills

Every row below comes from the same two plugins.

| CLI | `alpha`'s Unique Skill | Colliding Skill | Bare `unique` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code 2.1.304, `--plugin-dir` | `alpha:unique` | `alpha:shared`, `beta:shared` | Also loads, as an alias |
| Codex CLI 0.163.0, one skills folder per plugin | `alpha:unique` | `alpha:shared`, `beta:shared` | Not listed |
| Pi 1.4.0, default | `unique` | `shared` from `beta` only, `alpha`'s copy dropped | Only name listed |
| Pi 1.4.0, with a loader extension | `alpha:unique` | `alpha:shared`, `beta:shared` | Not listed |
| Copilot CLI 1.0.98, `--plugin-dir` | `unique` for the model, `/alpha:unique` for slash commands | `alpha:shared`, `beta:shared` | Only name that loads |

Codex got the plugins as `.agents/skills/alpha` and `.agents/skills/beta` in a repository. Pi drops one of the colliding skills by default. An extension of about 80 lines wraps its skill loader and renames each skill to `plugin:skill` from the manifest name before duplicates are dropped, which is how the second Pi row was produced. Copilot CLI has no equivalent hook for the model-facing registry.

## Affected Version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98.

## Additional Context

- Follow-up to #1766, closed as completed. Its closing comment covers slash invocation (`/plugin-name:skill-name`) and never mentions the `skill()` tool.
- Related: #4451 hits the same split between slash resolution and the model-facing registry through a different trigger. #2753 is another `Skill not found` from the `skill()` tool, where plugin skills are missing from the registry entirely.
- Hit this when an agent loaded a plugin's skills by `plugin:skill` name. Only the ones that collided with another installed plugin loaded.
- For now, plugin instructions fall back to reading `SKILL.md` by file path.

issues.title: Editing prompt to start with `!` traps user in Shell mode

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

There are two related UX bugs with how Shell mode (`!`) is entered and exited in the prompt input box:

1. **Accidental activation when editing existing text:** Shell mode is triggered whenever any edit results in the prompt text starting with `!` (`text.startsWith("!")`), even if `!` was already part of the prompt text and the user merely deleted the characters before it (for example, editing `Hello! Some text here.` by deleting `Hello`). The `!` is immediately stripped from the prompt and the UI switches from `Interactive` mode into `Shell` mode.
2. **Inability to exit Shell mode without wiping the prompt:** Once in Shell mode with non-empty text in the input box:
   - Pressing `Backspace` with the cursor at index `0` does nothing (because `onBackspaceAtEmpty` only fires when `text.length === 0`, not when `cursorPosition === 0`).
   - Pressing `Esc` does not exit Shell mode; instead it shows `esc again to clear input`.
   As a result, the user is trapped in Shell mode and must delete their entire prompt before `Esc` or `Backspace` will allow them to return to `Interactive` mode.

### Affected version

1.0.103

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start `copilot` in `Interactive` mode.
2. Type `Hello! Some text here.` into the prompt input box.
3. Move the cursor left so it is positioned right after `Hello` (`Hello|! Some text here.`).
4. Press `Backspace` 5 times to delete `Hello`.
5. As soon as `H` is deleted, observe that the `!` is consumed and the mode switches from `Interactive` to `Shell` (`Shell · Allow All`), leaving `| Some text here.` in the prompt.
6. Try to leave `Shell` mode without losing `Some text here.`:
   - Press `Backspace` at index `0`: nothing happens.
   - Press `Esc`: the footer flashes `esc again to clear input` instead of exiting Shell mode.
7. Delete all remaining text in the prompt so the input is completely empty, then press `Esc` or `Backspace` — only now does the CLI exit `Shell` mode back to `Interactive` mode.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/894be44c-b132-4ab5-9d12-0196b8ff0a65

### Expected behavior

1. Shell mode should only be entered when `!` is typed into an initially empty prompt (or explicitly toggled), not when backspacing/deleting characters in an existing prompt happens to expose a `!` at index 0.
2. When in Shell mode with non-empty text, pressing `Backspace` at cursor position `0` (or pressing `Esc`) should exit Shell mode while preserving the existing text in the input buffer.

### Additional context

**Environment:**
- Copilot CLI version: `1.0.103`
- OS: Linux `6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2` (x86_64)
- Terminal: Windows Terminal `1.24.12741.0`

**Root cause from inspecting `cli-main.js`:**
1. **Unintended entry on any edit (`onEdit`):** The text input reducer calls `onEdit(newText)` after every non-`set_text` edit action (including `backspace`, `forward_delete`, `backspace_word`, `delete_range`, etc.). The composer's `onEdit` callback checks `else if (newText.startsWith("!") && getMode() !== "shell")`, which switches to `"shell"` mode and strips the leading `"!"` (`setText(newText.substring(1))`) regardless of whether the prompt was empty before the edit or whether `"!"` was just typed.
2. **Exit blocked when `text.length > 0`:**
   - In the text input hook, the `backspace` handler checks `if (text.length === 0) { onBackspaceAtEmpty?.(); return; }` before checking `cursorPosition !== 0`. Because `onBackspaceAtEmpty` is only called when the entire buffer is empty (`text.length === 0`) rather than when `cursorPosition === 0`, pressing `Backspace` at the start of a non-empty prompt is a no-op.
   - In the global `escape` key handler, the action resolution evaluates `hasInputText ? "clear-text" : getMode() === "shell" ? "shell-mode-exit" : "rewind"`. Because `hasInputText` (`text.length > 0`) takes precedence over `"shell-mode-exit"`, pressing `Esc` with text in the prompt requires clearing the entire buffer (via double-`Esc`) and then pressing `Esc` a third time once empty to exit Shell mode.

issues.title: No STT models behind a corporate proxy since 1.0.101 (Foundry runtime ignores proxy settings)

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:networking
labels.description: Proxy, SSL/TLS, certificates, corporate environments, and connectivity issues

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Voice: no STT models behind a corporate proxy since 1.0.101 (Foundry runtime ignores proxy settings)

### Environment
- Copilot CLI 1.0.103, Windows x64, installed with winget
- Corporate network: outbound HTTPS only through an HTTP proxy with TLS inspection; direct connections are blocked
- `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` are set, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` points to the corporate root CA, and the WinHTTP proxy is set with `netsh winhttp set proxy`

### Symptom
`/voice` → Voice models shows:

> No STT models available.
> Your CLI may be out of date. Run /update to update, or download from: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/releases

Pressing `r` to refresh doesn't help. The models are already downloaded under `~\.github-copilot-cli\cache\models\Microsoft\`:
- `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b-generic-cpu-3`
- `nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b-generic-cpu-3`

### Regression
- **Works** on 1.0.95, which uses foundry-local-sdk 1.2.3 and the .NET `Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local.Core.dll`.
- **Broken** since 1.0.101, which uses foundry-local-sdk 2.1.0 and the native `foundry_local.dll`.

### Evidence
`~\.github-copilot-cli\logs\foundry_local_*.log`:
```
[warning] Region detection probe failed (status 0); defaulting to 'centralus'.
[warning] RegionFallback: region 'centralus' unhealthy (transport failure); trying next candidate.
...
[warning] catalog: filter set failed across all regions: ... exhausted all 7 candidate region(s) ... (transport failure)
```

Calling `FoundryLocalManager.createAsync({ appName: "github-copilot-cli", additionalSettings: { AzureCatalogFilter: "'',test" } })` then `catalog.getModels()` directly on the same machine:

| SDK / runtime | Result |
|---|---|
| 2.1.0 + native `foundry_local.dll` | **0 models** |
| 1.2.3 + .NET `Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local.Core.dll` | **49 models** (through the same proxy) |

A plain WinHTTP GET to `https://ai.azure.com/api/westeurope/ux/v1.0` on the same machine:

| WinHTTP access type | Result |
|---|---|
| `WINHTTP_ACCESS_TYPE_DEFAULT_PROXY` | HTTP 404 (reachable) |
| `WINHTTP_ACCESS_TYPE_AUTOMATIC_PROXY` | HTTP 404 (reachable) |
| `WINHTTP_ACCESS_TYPE_NO_PROXY` | error 12029 (cannot connect) |

`api.catalog.azureml.ms` is also reachable through the proxy with curl.

So the network and proxy work. The native runtime appears to open WinHTTP with no proxy, and it ignores `HTTPS_PROXY`, the CLI `proxyUrl` setting, the WinHTTP proxy and the user's PAC file.

### Additional issues
1. When the online catalog fetch fails, the catalog is empty. Models that are already downloaded aren't listed, even though `foundry.modelinfo.json` exists in the cache.
2. The error message is misleading: "Your CLI may be out of date" when the real cause is a network failure. The fetch failure also isn't shown in the UI or in the CLI process log.

### Expected
- The voice runtime honours `HTTPS_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` and `proxyUrl`, or at least the system WinHTTP or PAC proxy.
- Downloaded models stay usable when the catalog can't be reached.
- `/voice` reports that the catalog could not be reached.

### Workaround
```
copilot --prefer-version 1.0.95
```

### Affected version

1.0.103

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

_No response_

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: Sub-agent detail view in /tasks does not allow expanding tool calls

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:terminal-rendering
labels.description: Display and rendering: flickering, scrolling, line wrapping, output formatting

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In the main session timeline, collapsed timeline entries such as `$ Shell ... 2 lines…` and `> Thought for 1s` can be expanded either by clicking on them with the mouse or via keyboard shortcuts (`Ctrl+O` to toggle all timeline entries, `Ctrl+T` to toggle reasoning).

When viewing a sub-agent's transcript via `/tasks` (selecting a sub-agent to open its fullscreen detail view), the exact same collapsed entries (`$ Shell ... 2 lines…`, `> Thought for Ns`, etc.) are rendered with the trailing `…` indicator, but clicking on them does nothing and `Ctrl+O` does not expand tool call outputs. As a result, there is no way to inspect the output of `Shell` or other tool calls executed by a sub-agent in `/tasks`.

### Affected version

1.0.103

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start an interactive `copilot` session in a terminal with mouse support (e.g. Windows Terminal).
2. Ask Copilot to run a shell command in the main session and then run a sub-agent that executes a shell command:
   - Main session command: `echo "Hello from the main session" && uname -a`
   - Sub-agent (`task`) command: `echo "Hello from the sub-agent" && uname -a`
3. In the main session timeline, click on `$ Shell ... 2 lines…` or `> Thought for 1s` — both expand to show full details.
4. Open `/tasks` and select the sub-agent to open its fullscreen transcript view.
5. Click on `$ Shell ... 2 lines…` (or press `Ctrl+O`).
6. Observe that `$ Shell ... 2 lines…` cannot be expanded by clicking or via `Ctrl+O`, and individual `> Thought for Ns` items cannot be clicked to expand.

### Expected behavior

Timeline entries in the `/tasks` sub-agent detail view (`$ Shell ... 2 lines…`, `> Thought for Ns`, and other expandable tool calls) should be interactive and expandable via mouse click and `Ctrl+O`, matching the main session timeline behavior (and fulfilling the intent of #1322 to inspect sub-agent tool call details).

### Additional context

**Environment:**
- Copilot CLI version: `1.0.103`
- OS: Linux `6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2` (x86_64)
- Terminal: Windows Terminal `1.24.12741.0`

**Root cause from inspecting `cli-main.js`:**
The sub-agent fullscreen detail view reuses the same timeline rendering hook and `FullscreenScrollView` component as the main session, and even computes and rebases `lineOwners` for `FullscreenScrollView`. However, per-entry expansion and click handling are not wired up in the sub-agent detail component:

1. `isTimelineEntryExpanded` is hardcoded to a no-op returning `false` (`useCallback(() => false, [])`) instead of tracking expanded entry IDs.
2. `isTimelineEntryClickable` and `expansionFingerprint` are omitted when calling the timeline rendering hook. Because `isTimelineEntryClickable` is `undefined`, `lineOwners` only records markdown code blocks (for `copyOnCodeBlockClick`) and skips all tool call and reasoning entries.
3. `onEntryClick` is omitted when rendering `FullscreenScrollView`, so mouse clicks on non-code-block rows return early.
4. While `Ctrl+T` happens to toggle all sub-agent reasoning blocks at once (because `showReasoningSummaries` is passed down from the root component into the sub-agent view as `reasoningExpanded`), `Ctrl+O` (`expand all timeline`) state is not passed down or handled in the sub-agent view.

issues.title: Subagents started in the same turn as an approved exit_plan_mode get none of the built-in tools (regression after 1.0.95)

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When `exit_plan_mode` is approved with the `interactive` action, the agent keeps working in the same turn. Every subagent it starts in that turn runs without any built-in tools: no `powershell` or `bash`, `view`, `create`, `edit`, `grep`, `glob`, `sql`, `task`, `skill`, or `web_fetch`. The subagent only gets the external tools the SDK host registers, such as `openBrowserPage`, `readPage`, `runPlaywrightCode`, `navigatePage`, `semantic_search`, `issue_fetch`, and `activePullRequest`. Its system prompt has no `<tools>` section.

The main agent keeps all its built-in tools in that same turn, and subagents started from any other turn get the full set. So any plan-then-implement workflow that delegates to subagents breaks without warning. In my case, a reviewer subagent could not write its report or run the test suite, and fell back to reading files through the browser tools.

I hit this through an SDK host (the VS Code Agents window, reported there as microsoft/vscode#343716). The host does not seem to be involved. It answers the `exitPlanMode.request` with `approved: true` and `selectedAction: "interactive"`, and as far as I can tell from its code, it sends nothing else to the runtime before the subagent starts. Subagent tool sets are built inside the runtime.

### Affected version

1.0.100-1, as bundled with VS Code 1.143.0 (`@github/copilot-sdk-win32-x64` 1.0.23-preview.5). 1.0.92 and 1.0.95 are not affected.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create `~/.copilot/agents/Probe.agent.md`:

   ```markdown
   ---
   name: Probe
   description: Reports the tools it has
   ---

   Reply with the exact names of every tool you have, as a comma-separated list. Do not call any tools.
   ```

2. Start a session in plan mode through an SDK host. I used the VS Code Agents window with the Copilot harness.
3. Send: "Plan a single step: run the Probe subagent and report its answer verbatim."
4. Approve the plan with the `interactive` action (VS Code labels it **Implement plan**).
5. The agent runs `Probe` through the `task` tool in the same turn.

`Probe` lists only the host's external tools. The session log shows `exit_plan_mode` completing with "Plan approved, exited plan mode (interactive)" and `session.mode_changed` from `plan` to `interactive`, both before `subagent.started`.

### Expected behavior

`Probe` gets the same built-in tools it gets when started from a normal turn.

### Additional context

Counted from my local session logs over the last 20 days, by whether the subagent's system prompt had a `<tools>` section:

| Runtime | Subagent started in | Calls | Built-in tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0.100-1 | the turn that approved the plan | 6, in 2 sessions | **none** |
| 1.0.100-1 | a normal turn | 34, in 10 sessions | all |
| 1.0.95 | the turn that approved the plan | 38, in 12 sessions | all |
| 1.0.92 | the turn that approved the plan | 40, in 10 sessions | all |

- All 6 failing calls were custom agents with no `tools` key in their frontmatter, started through `task` with `agent_type`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort`. `subagent.selected` reports `tools: null` in both failing and working calls.
- The host creates the session with `availableTools` set to explicit `builtin:<name>` entries plus `custom:*` and `mcp:*`. The failing subagents kept the external tools and lost every built-in one. My guess is that the built-in set given to subagents is computed differently right after the mode switch, but I can't see the runtime code to confirm.
- I have two `preToolUse` hooks. They returned success in both failing and working calls.
- I only tested the `interactive` action, not `autopilot` or `autopilot_fleet`.
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26300), x64
- Host: VS Code 1.143.0 Agents window, Copilot harness
- Model: a BYOK Claude Opus model from a VS Code language model provider extension, for the main agent and the subagents

issues.title: Sessions stop processing when MCP config watch registration hits the inotify limit (ENOSPC)

labels.name: area:platform-linux
labels.description: Linux-specific: Wayland, X11, Ubuntu, Fedora, Alpine, ARM, terminal emulators

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

We run `copilot --server` in a container on shared Linux hosts. When the host's inotify watch budget was already used up the runtime failed to register the MCP configuration watches and the session queue was abandoned after one retry. After that sessions stopped processing prompts until the server was restarted.

```text
[ERROR] [rust:copilot_runtime::shared_api::lifecycle] Scheduled queue processing failed; retrying once {"error":"Message(\"Failed to register MCP configuration watches: OS file watch limit reached. about [\\\"/root/.copilot\\\"]\")"}
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::shared_api::lifecycle] Queue recovery was rearmed after the bounded recovery attempt; releasing its admission {"reserved_order":"Some(0)"}
[ERROR] [rust:copilot_runtime::shared_api::lifecycle] Scheduled queue processing failed after retry; queue drain abandoned {"error":"Message(\"Failed to register MCP configuration watches: OS file watch limit reached. about [\\\"/root/.copilot\\\"]\")"}
```

In our case the watches seem to have been used up by another workload on the same host running as the same uid and not by Copilot itself. As far as I understand `max_user_watches` is tracked per uid across the host so a container doesn't get its own budget. The retry happens almost immediately so it most likely runs into the same limit.

### Affected version

1.0.93, Linux x86_64, `copilot --server`

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

I haven't reproduced this in isolation yet but I think something like this should trigger it:

1. `sudo sysctl -w fs.inotify.max_user_watches=512` (or another low value)
2. As the same user use up the watches, e.g. `inotifywait -m -r /usr`
3. Start `copilot --server` and create a session via the SDK
4. Check the logs for the errors above and see whether the session responds

### Expected behavior

It would be helpful if the runtime could fall back to polling the MCP config files in this case or continue without hot-reload and log a warning rather than abandoning the session queue.

From the binary there appears to be a polling path already (`MCP configuration native watches unavailable; using polling`). It may only be used when creating the watcher fails and not when adding a watch fails with `MaxFilesWatch`, but I may be wrong about that. If it's the latter then catching that error kind and switching to `PollWatcher` might be a fairly small change.

Polling seems like a reasonable fallback here since it's only a few config files and they don't change often. A full inotify budget also tends to stay full for a while so an immediate retry may not help much.

It might also be worth checking whether the other watchers (LSP, git worktree, agent registry) handle this the same way. Some of them appear to log "explicit refreshes remain available" and carry on, which seems like a reasonable approach.

### Additional context

This looks similar to #4998, where a different MCP setup error also led to `queue drain abandoned` and unusable sessions. #3892 (session-state not being pruned) may also be relevant if the `~/.copilot` watch is recursive.

For now we're working around it by raising `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` and `max_user_instances` on the hosts though that requires host-level access.

issues.title: ACP mode: expired MCP OAuth access token opens the browser authorization page instead of using the stored refresh token

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp`), when a remote HTTP MCP server answers 401 because the stored access token has expired, the CLI goes straight to `[acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page`. It never tries a `refresh_token` grant, even though a refresh token is stored and works.

The same config, same Keychain entry and same machine, a minute apart:

- `copilot` (interactive) and `copilot -p`: 401, then silent refresh, server connected in ~200 ms, no browser.
- `copilot --acp`: 401, then the authorization page opens. Nothing in the log shows a refresh attempt.

ACP does read the stored token: right after the interactive CLI refreshed and persisted it, an ACP session connected to the server without a browser. It just never renews an expired one.

Server used: Sentry remote MCP (`https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`), dynamic client registration (`clientId` `https://github.com/copilot/cli/client-metadata.json`), token in the macOS Keychain (service `copilot-mcp-oauth`).

## Affected version

- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102 (latest stable; 1.0.103-0 prerelease release notes mention nothing related)
- Same pattern in my logs going back to 2026-10-19 (1.0.100 and 1.0.101)
- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a remote OAuth MCP server in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
   ```json
   { "mcpServers": { "sentry": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp" } } }
   ```
2. Sign in once from the interactive CLI so an access token and refresh token are stored.
3. Wait until the access token expires (about an hour for Sentry). Don't run the interactive CLI in between.
4. Start `copilot --acp` over stdio and send `initialize` then `session/new` (`cwd` set to any temp dir, `mcpServers: []`).
5. The browser opens the Sentry authorization page. Log: `opened the MCP OAuth authorization page`.
6. Close the ACP process, then run `copilot -p "reply with ok"` from the same directory. The server connects after a 401 with no browser.

Minimal driver used for step 4:

```js
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
const cwd = process.argv[2];
const child = spawn('copilot', ['--acp'], { cwd, stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'inherit'] });
const send = (id, method, params) => child.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id, method, params }) + '\n');
let buf = '';
child.stdout.on('data', d => {
  buf += d; let i;
  while ((i = buf.indexOf('\n')) >= 0) {
    const m = JSON.parse(buf.slice(0, i)); buf = buf.slice(i + 1);
    if (m.id === 1) send(2, 'session/new', { cwd, mcpServers: [] });
  }
});
send(1, 'initialize', { protocolVersion: 1, clientCapabilities: {} });
setTimeout(() => child.kill('SIGTERM'), 45000);
```

## Expected behavior

On a 401 for a server with a stored refresh token, ACP does what the interactive CLI and `-p` already do: silently POST `grant_type=refresh_token`, persist the new tokens, reconnect. Only fall back to the authorization page if the refresh fails (`invalid_grant`, revoked, no refresh token).

## Actual behavior

### ACP, expired token (2026-10-22, live repro)

```
11:45:55.601Z [INFO] Starting ACP server (stdio)
11:45:56.976Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { www_authenticate_header: "******"OAuth\", resource_metadata=\"https://mcp.sentry.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp\"", response: McpOAuthHttpResponse { status_code: 401, header_count: 10, has_body: true } })
11:45:57.315Z [INFO] [rust:acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page {"server_name":"sentry"}
11:45:57.315Z [WARNING] [rust:mcp_engine::agent_host] HTTP 401 challenge (WWW-Authenticate: ******"OAuth", resource_metadata="https://mcp.sentry.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp") {"server":"sentry","error":"MCP OAuth authorization failed"}
11:45:57.414Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ... })
11:45:57.458Z [INFO] [rust:acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page {"server_name":"sentry"}
11:46:39.891Z [WARNING] [rust:mcp_client::session_authorizer] MCP OAuth login did not complete {"server_name":"sentry","error":"MCP OAuth was cancelled because its original requester or configuration changed."}
```

Two authorization pages per `session/new`, one per challenge. The ACP client got no `session/update` or request about auth; the CLI opened the browser on its own.

### `-p`, same token, 60 s later

```
11:46:50.753Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ... })
11:46:50.955Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client {"peer_info":"Some(ServerPeerInfo { ... name: \"Sentry MCP\" ... })"}
```

No browser, connected 200 ms after the 401.

### Interactive CLI, earlier the same day

```
07:54:03.670Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ... })
07:54:03.761Z [ERROR] Refreshing authentication for sentry...
07:54:04.340Z [ERROR] Successfully authenticated with sentry
07:54:04.413Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client {"peer_info":"Some(ServerPeerInfo { ... name: \"Sentry MCP\" ... })"}
```

The Keychain item's modification date is 07:54:04Z, so this refresh was persisted. An ACP process that had already opened the page at 07:53:30 and again at 07:54:29 finally connected to Sentry at 07:54:34, using the token the interactive CLI had just stored.

### Across all my logs

I went through every process log in `~/.copilot/logs` (2026-10-19 to 2026-10-22) that has a Sentry OAuth challenge:

| Mode | Processes | With a refresh attempt | Opened the authorization page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--acp` | 32 | 0 | 30 (in the other 2 the client disconnected before the page opened) |
| interactive | 2 | 2 | 1, only after its refresh attempt failed (2026-10-21, `Refreshing authentication` then `Opening browser for sentry authentication`) |

No ACP log contains `Refreshing authentication`, `Successfully authenticated` or anything else showing a refresh attempt.

## Impact

ACP clients (Kepler, editors) spawn short-lived `copilot --acp` processes: one per new chat, plus background ones for titles, model lists and similar. Once the access token expires, which for Sentry is about an hour, every one of them:

- pops one or two Sentry authorization tabs the user didn't ask for, at session start, before any Sentry tool is used;
- cancels the flow a moment later when the process exits (`MCP OAuth was cancelled because its original requester or configuration changed.`), or leaves it hanging until `OAuth callback timeout` after 5 minutes;
- starts the session without the server's tools.

The only workaround is to open the interactive CLI now and then so it refreshes and persists the token for ACP to pick up.

## Possibly related: `-p` refresh is not persisted

The silent refresh in `-p` runs never updated the stored token. After two `-p` runs at 11:46 and 11:50 that both refreshed, the Keychain item's modification date was still 07:54:04Z and nothing under `~/.copilot` changed. So every `-p` run refreshes again from the stored refresh token. That works with Sentry, but against a server that rotates refresh tokens it would break the stored grant (same class of problem as #5079). It also means a `-p` refresh doesn't help ACP the way an interactive refresh does.

## Related issues

- #4203: generic "expired access token forces interactive re-auth instead of refresh_token grant" (1.0.71). On 1.0.102 the interactive CLI and `-p` refresh fine for me; ACP still doesn't, so what's left of #4203 may be this ACP path.
- #4994: the authorization page opens on every ACP session since 1.0.89, with a valid token and no refresh token. Different trigger (an expired token with a working refresh token), same ACP handler that goes straight to the browser.
- #5192: tokens from an ACP sign-in are never persisted. Here the token is persisted (by the interactive CLI) and ACP reads it, but never refreshes it.

issues.title: `copilot --resume` without an ID drops into a new empty session; the Sessions list is auto-replaced after ~2s and the trust prompt takes the first Enter

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Since the unified Sessions browser became the default, `copilot --resume` without a session ID no longer lets me pick a session. Each launch creates a new empty session ("Session 1"). The Sessions list is shown for only ~2 seconds, then the UI switches to that new session's "Current" tab. In a folder that is not remembered as trusted, the "Confirm folder trust" dialog then appears on top of the empty session and consumes my first Enter, so I end up in a blank new session before I can use ↑/↓ on the list.
 
 The list is still reachable with Tab or /resume, but this is not obvious, and it makes `--resume` look like it simply creates a new session.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

 1. cd into a local folder that has earlier Copilot sessions and is not remembered as trusted.
 2. Run `copilot --resume` (no session ID).
 3. After a "Resuming session…" spinner, the Sessions tab appears. The highlighted first row is a brand-new empty "Session 1".
 4. About 2 seconds later the UI switches to the "[Current]" tab and shows "Confirm folder trust".
 5. Press Enter ("1. Yes").
 6. Result: I am in the new empty session. ↑/↓ does nothing here. Pressing Tab (footer: "tab next tab") or typing /resume brings back the Sessions list, where ↑/↓ works.

### Expected behavior

`copilot --resume` without an ID should keep the session list focused until I choose a session or cancel. It should not auto-switch to the newly created placeholder session, and the folder-trust prompt should not take focus or Enter from the picker. Alternatively, it should reopen the most recent session for the current repository, as the 1.0.64 changelog describes for --continue/--resume.

### Additional context

- macOS 26.7.1 (25G241), x86_64; Terminal.app 470.2; zsh; installed via Homebrew cask, auto-updated to 1.0.102.
 - Timeline from a 120x40 pty capture: ~0.7s "Resuming session…"; ~1.1s Sessions tab with list; ~3.0s switch to "[Current]" plus the trust dialog. I could not test a remembered-trusted folder, so I don't know whether the auto-switch is caused by the trust prompt.
 - Each launch also creates an empty session directory (only workspace.yaml, no events.jsonl). Related: #3908, #5204.
 - Changelog 1.0.100: "Use the unified Sessions browser by default for /sessions, /session, and /resume." I did not bisect other versions.
 - Workarounds: `copilot --continue`, `copilot --resume <name|id>`.

issues.body:
## Problem

The Copilot CLI input box is always rendered at the bottom of the screen. During long sessions, everything the user cares about — the line being typed, the latest output — is at the very bottom edge of the display. This forces a constant downward gaze / neck angle, which is genuinely fatiguing on large monitors.

## Proposed solution

Add a setting (e.g. `/settings input_position top` or a config key) to pin the input box to the **top** of the screen, with the conversation/output flowing below it — similar to Warp's "pin input to top" option or chat-style interfaces.

## Alternatives considered

- Shrinking the terminal window so the bottom edge sits at eye level (workable but ugly)
- Using the desktop app / VS Code chat instead (but the CLI TUI is the preferred workflow)

## Context

- Copilot CLI 1.0.102
- macOS, running in Canario/Warp

Thanks for considering!

issues.title: compaction: 'too many tokens per minute' rate limit misclassified as context overflow
issues.body:
### Description

## Description

When a provider throttles with `Token limit reached: too many tokens per minute for this model.` (a tokens-per-minute ceiling), OpenCode classifies it as a **context overflow** instead of a **rate limit**, so compaction is shrunk instead of retried.

`isContextOverflow()` (`packages/ai/src/provider-error.ts`) matches the message against `/too many tokens/i` (line 55), and none of the `exclusions` (line 62) cover this wording. The fix for the related #58745 only excludes `too many tokens[, per day], please wait` — this message has neither `please wait` nor `per day`. `classifyProviderFailure()` therefore returns a non-retryable `InvalidRequest (context-overflow)` (checked before the 429/rate-limit branch), so the request is never treated as a rate limit.

In compaction's `deliver` loop (`packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts`), the overflow path keeps shrinking the transcript (85% → 70% → 50% → 35%) until it can't, then fails with:

> The compaction request cannot be reduced further without losing the latest exchange or checkpoint

Shortening history can't fix a tokens-per-minute ceiling, so the session can't be compacted at all.

## Expected

A per-window token throttle is `RateLimit` and is retried with backoff (honoring `Retry-After`).

## Repro

```js
import { classifyProviderFailure } from '@opencode/ai/provider-error'
import { isContextOverflowFailure, isRetryable } from '@opencode/ai'

for (const message of [
  'Token limit reached: too many tokens per minute for this model.',
  'Too many tokens per second for this model.',
]) {
  const reason = classifyProviderFailure({ message, status: 429 })
  console.log(reason._tag, '| context overflow:', isContextOverflowFailure({ reason }), '| retryable:', isRetryable({ reason }))
}
```

Actual: InvalidRequest (context-overflow) | retryable: false (compaction shrinks then fails).
Expected: RateLimit | context overflow: false | retryable: true.

## Suggested fix
Add too many tokens per (minute|second|hour|day) to the `isContextOverflow` exclusions and to `RATE_LIMIT_TEXT` in packages/ai/src/provider-error.ts, plus a regression test mirroring the Bedrock one in provider-error.test.ts.

issues.title: app: background shell stays "running" after exit; cannot dismiss and survives restart
issues.body:
## Summary

A background shell that has already exited keeps showing as `1 running` in the session header. The badge cannot be dismissed with `×`, and it survives an app restart. Runtime state shows no active shell at all, so this looks like a persisted status that is never finalized.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.4 (`opencode` CLI is not on PATH in this install)
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.19045 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: desktop app (no TERM/TERM_PROGRAM set)
- Shell: C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: @tarquinen/opencode-dcp@latest

## Reproduction

1. In a session, start a background shell that writes output to a file and exits normally, e.g.:
   `cmd /c "py C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\<script>.py > out.txt 2>&1"` with `background: true`.
2. Wait until the script finishes (the output file is fully written, process is gone).
3. Look at the session header: it still shows `1 running`, tooltip `Shell  cmd /c "py C:\Users\..."` (command truncated).
4. Click `×` on the running task: nothing happens.
5. Quit and restart opencode, reopen the session: `1 running` is still displayed.

## Expected Behavior

- The running indicator should clear as soon as the background shell exits, even if the notification/output was not consumed.
- `×` should remove the task entry from the session.
- Restarting the app should not resurrect a task that has no live process.

## Actual Behavior

- The badge stays at `1 running` indefinitely (observed for more than a day across app restarts).
- `×` does not dismiss it.
- The runtime reports no active sessions: calling `shell.list_sessions` returns `"No active sessions"`.
- No related process exists on the machine: `tasklist` shows no `python.exe` / `mvn`; `netstat` shows nothing listening on the port used earlier (8086). The only `java.exe` is IntelliJ's `RemoteMavenServer36`, unrelated.
- The shell's output file is complete, so the process did exit normally.

## Additional Context

- The session had run several background tasks earlier (maven builds, a temporary server, python scripts). All of them exited or were killed; the badge nevertheless shows a single stuck `1 running` entry, always pointing at the same `cmd /c "py C:\Users\..."` command.
- Because restarting does not clear it, the state appears to be persisted (e.g. in `opencode.db` / `storage`) and re-read on load, rather than kept only in memory.
- Workarounds that did not help: clicking `×`, restarting the app.
- Not attempted: deleting the session, manually editing the persisted state.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Auto-continue numbered and bulleted lists in the prompt editor
issues.body:
### What

When writing a prompt, pressing newline at the end of a list item should continue the list.

`1. first item` + newline gives `2. `, `- item` + newline gives `- `, and newline on an empty item ends the list.

### Why

This is standard behavior in any text editor, GitHub comment box, and in Claude Code. Prompts often contain short numbered lists, and retyping every marker is unnecessary friction.

### Current behavior

OpenCode 1.19.3, macOS, TUI. After `1. first item` and a newline (`ctrl+j` or `shift+enter`), the new line is empty.

### Expected behavior

Same as a normal markdown editor: numbered lists increment, bullets repeat, empty item exits the list, indentation is preserved.

issues.title: Pinned sessions can be lost when multiple TUI instances write session.json
issues.body:
### Description

Each TUI reads the global `session.json` pin list once and keeps a private in-memory copy. Pinning, unpinning, or handling `session.deleted` rewrites the entire file without locking, rereading, merging, or serializing writes. A stale TUI can therefore erase pins added by another TUI.

### Reproduction

1. Start TUI A and TUI B with the same pin list.
2. In B, pin a session. B writes the updated list.
3. In stale A, pin/unpin another session or delete a session.
4. Restart OpenCode.

The pin added in B is gone because A replaced the complete file with its stale snapshot.

### Expected

Concurrent TUI instances should not erase unrelated pin updates.

### Cause

`createSession()` loads the file once and each `save()` passes the full in-memory array to a fire-and-forget `writeJsonAtomic()` call:

- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/826d9ad46a22bef0294998e08daa3c4904fea28f/packages/tui/src/context/local.tsx#L411-L493
- https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/826d9ad46a22bef0294998e08daa3c4904fea28f/packages/tui/src/util/persistence.ts#L22-L33

Atomic rename prevents partial files but does not prevent stale writers. There is also no file watcher or close-time merge. Closing a TUI alone does not save; the last completed save wins.

I verified that the relevant persistence code is identical in v1.18.18, v1.18.19, v1.18.20, v1.18.21, and current `dev`.

### Environment

- macOS
- Multiple OpenCode TUIs in WebStorm and system terminals
- OpenCode v1.18.18 through v1.18.21
