issues.title: `openapi.json` no longer documents SSE payloads (`V2Event` / `SessionLogItem`) after the effect beta.107 regen
issues.body:
## Summary

I ran into this while refreshing the pinned `openapi.json` for a .NET SDK I'm building for opencode.

Since the effect `4.0.0-beta.101 → beta.107` bump, the generated `packages/protocol/openapi.json` no longer contains the actual payload schemas for the two SSE endpoints (`v2.event.subscribe`, `v2.session.log`).

Before the bump, the stream `data` field was represented as a JSON string with a `contentSchema` pointing back to the full payload union. After the first regen under beta.107, that became an opaque string and the whole event schema tree disappeared with it, 74 component schemas in that single regen.

The wire protocol itself hasn't changed, so nothing is broken at runtime. But anything consuming the OpenAPI document now loses the entire typed event surface.

I dug into the regression, traced it back to the effect upgrade, and verified that the current effect version can still generate everything needed to restore it. I also have a working restore patch and would be happy to send a PR.

## Before / after

The break is pretty clean and sits between two adjacent commits.

At [`d9b81d2233`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/d9b81d2233a5c70f52ae1fbcd4cccef2ea57c7b1) (2026-08-17, the effect bump itself, the document still carries the previous regen), the stream payload was still fully documented:

```jsonc
// components.schemas
"V2EventJsonString": {
  "type": "string",
  "contentSchema": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/V2Event" },
  "contentMediaType": "application/json"
},
"V2Event": { "anyOf": [ /* 84 event variants */ ] },
"V2Event.server.connected": { /* ... */ }
// ... full event model tree
```

Then one commit later, at [`aca42423d3`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/aca42423d3dd9f6d1c7d531e4525a42a5776316a) (`chore: generate`, the first regen under beta.107), the same part became:

```jsonc
"V2EventEncoded": {
  "type": "string",
  "contentMediaType": "application/json"
}

// V2Event, SessionLogItem and every event leaf schema: gone
```

`components.schemas` went from 314 to 240 entries in that one regen, and nothing in the document mentions `server.connected`, or any other event type anymore.

The same thing happened to `SessionLogItemJsonString` → `SessionLogItemEncoded`.

## What changed

`script/generate-openapi.ts` itself didn't change between those commits, so I followed the behavior change into effect.

As far as I can tell, there are two changes interacting here:

- **beta.102, [Effect-TS/effect#6424](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/6424)** — the SchemaRepresentation overhaul. OpenAPI/JSON Schema generation now projects the *encoded* side of a schema, and `contentSchema` moved from a structural field to an ordinary annotation (`Annotations.Augment.contentSchema`). `HttpApiSchema.StreamSse`'s event schema encodes `data` as a plain string, but nothing re-attaches the payload schema as that annotation, so the link disappears.

- **beta.103, [Effect-TS/effect#6781](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/6781)** — the OpenAPI generator stopped emitting component schemas that aren't reachable from a generated root. Once the `contentSchema` link is gone, the event union is no longer reachable from the OpenAPI root and the whole tree gets pruned.

- Also in beta.103, [Effect-TS/effect#6782](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/6782) renamed the fallback definitions from `*JsonString` to `*Encoded`. That part looks cosmetic, but it happened in the same window.

opencode's own TypeScript clients generate directly from the effect schemas, so this doesn't break anything in-repo. The OpenAPI document is basically the only surface that regressed.

## Impact

For anything generating a client from `openapi.json`, the two streams are now effectively documented as `string`.

That means the regular OpenAPI surface no longer describes any of the actual event payloads.

The same document is also copied to `packages/www/openapi.json`, so the public version has the same gap.

## I verified the schemas are still recoverable

I also wanted to make sure this wasn't simply a dead end caused by the newer effect representation.

I reproduced generation at the current v2 tip ([`8c126e98da`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/8c126e98dad9165a0cf64440a0879eadc2973edb), effect `4.0.0-rc.111`), and all the information is still there:

- `Schema.toJsonSchemaDocument(OpenCodeEvent)` still compiles the complete union, 138 definitions, root `$ref: V2Event`.

- The JSON Schema emitter still understands `contentSchema`; it's still a first-class annotation key and gets emitted when present.

- If I merge those compiled definitions back into `components.schemas` and re-attach `contentSchema: { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/V2Event" }` on `V2EventEncoded`, the previous OpenAPI shape comes back.

I also compared the two generation paths. Of the 46 compiled schemas that already exist in the document, 45 are byte-identical, so the two pipelines still agree almost completely.

And importantly, this isn't restoring an old snapshot: the resulting union contains the current 85 event variants, including types added after the regression window such as `session.viewed` and `worktree.*`.

So the live protocol can still be fully documented with the current effect version.

## Possible fix

The restore is fairly small: roughly a ~30-line post-processing step in `script/generate-openapi.ts` / `openapi-stabilize.ts`:

1. compile the two stream payload schemas,
2. merge their definitions into `components.schemas`,
3. set `contentSchema` on the two `*Encoded` envelopes.

I already have this working locally and I'm happy to open the PR.

<summary>The core of the restore step (from my local experiment, slightly simplified)</summary>

```ts
import { Schema } from "effect"
import { OpenCodeEvent } from "../src/groups/event.js"

// after: const doc: any = stabilizeOpenApi(OpenApi.fromApi(ClientApi))
const compiled = Schema.toJsonSchemaDocument(OpenCodeEvent)

// draft-2020-12 refs -> OpenAPI component refs
const { schema, definitions } = JSON.parse(
  JSON.stringify({ schema: compiled.schema, definitions: compiled.definitions })
    .replaceAll("#/$defs/", "#/components/schemas/"),
)

const components = doc.components.schemas
for (const [name, s] of Object.entries(definitions)) {
  components[name] ??= s // 45 of the 46 overlaps are byte-identical already
}
components["V2EventEncoded"] = { ...components["V2EventEncoded"], contentSchema: schema }

// same step for the session.log payload union -> "SessionLogItemEncoded"
```

## Context

For context, I'm building [Blind-Striker/opencode-sdk-dotnet](https://github.com/Blind-Striker/opencode-sdk-dotnet), a typed .NET SDK for opencode.

It uses a fail-closed custom generator over opencode's OpenAPI dialect, tagged unions, `x-effect-stream` SSE framing metadata, cursor pagination, etc., and generates a fully typed client.

The OpenAPI document is intentionally the SDK's sole protocol input.

I had it pinned to [`a6a712a3`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/a6a712a3ac72248c9b2f2f883e752e6e18ef8c40) (2026-08-13), and when I tried to refresh that pin to the current v2 tip, the generator refused to ingest the new document because schemas it had previously used to type the streams (`EventLogSynced`, `SessionCreated`, …) were simply gone.

That's what led me down this rabbit hole.

External SDKs consuming `openapi.json` depend on it being a complete description of the protocol, so I figured this was worth reporting.

Happy to send the restore PR.

issues.title: server: V1 sessions created after migration.v1-v2 completes are never imported
issues.body:
### Description

OpenCode 2 performs a one-time V1 to V2 session import whose state lives in `kv['migration.v1-v2']`. Once that key is `{"phase":"completed"}`, any V1 session that appears in the same database afterwards is never imported: it stays in the legacy `session` / `message` / `part` tables, is absent from `session_v2`, `GET /api/session/{id}` returns 404, and desktop tabs that reference it show "the session this tab points to no longer exists on this server".

I hit this because I kept using a V1 client (1.18.31) alongside the V2 desktop app. The migration completed on 2026-09-17 (first V2 startup, 2.0.3); 11 sessions created with V1 after that were invisible in V2. The same first run also skipped 29 V1 sessions that already existed in the database. The data was never lost, but nothing surfaced the problem.

### Plugins

oh-my-openagent@latest

### OpenCode version

2.0.10 (desktop bundled CLI; `migration.v1-v2` state was created by 2.0.3, 2.0.5 and 2.0.8 were also installed in between)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create sessions with a V1 client (1.18.x) in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`.
2. Let a V2 build finish a startup so `kv['migration.v1-v2']` becomes `{"phase":"completed"}` (here: 2.0.3, even though 29 V1 sessions were already present).
3. Create new sessions with the V1 client against the same database.
4. Open the V2 desktop app: the new sessions are missing. `opencode api get /api/session/<id>` returns 404, `opencode api get /api/experimental/migration/v1` keeps returning `{"status":"completed"}`.

### Expected behavior

The one-time import should only be marked completed after it has actually drained existing V1 history, or it should notice new V1 rows and run/resume instead of reporting `completed` forever. At minimum, unimported V1 sessions should be surfaced instead of making session tabs 404.

### Actual behavior

- `kv` row `migration.v1-v2 = {"phase":"completed"}`, created 2026-09-17 10:19:31.
- 40 V1 sessions existed in `session` (versions 1.18.31 x11, 1.4.7 x20, 1.2.24 x9), 0 of them were copied to `session_v2`.
- All 19901 rows in the `event` table still carry the default `created = 0`, suggesting the `phase === undefined` branch (clear events) did not do what it looks like it should on this V1 database.
- Log: the client kept polling `GET /api/session/ses_...` and got 404 while the row existed in `session`.

### Additional context

Recovery/workaround that brought everything back without data loss:

1. Back up `opencode.db`.
2. `UPDATE kv SET value='{"phase":"sessions"}' WHERE key='migration.v1-v2';`
3. Boot any V2 server (e.g. `opencode api --standalone get /api/experimental/migration/v1`) so the importer resumes.
4. It copied all 40 sessions and converted 2211 V1 messages into `session_message` correctly, then wrote `{"phase":"completed"}` again.

So the import/conversion logic itself works; the completion/"already completed" gate is the problem. In the shipped binary the state is read with an early `if (state.phase === "completed") return`, and `loose_psylocke` already knows how to detect V1-only history (`Previous V2 database contains V1-only session history`), but there is no equivalent check or re-arm for V1 sessions newer than the last completed import.

### OS

Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.6-arch2-1 (x86_64)

### Terminal

OpenCode desktop app 2.0.10 (Electron); same behavior visible from the CLI (`opencode api`).

issues.title: session: migrated session missing messages written after V1→V2 migration; export truncated
issues.body:
### Description

## Summary

After upgrading from OpenCode 1.19.0 → 2.0.29 → 2.0.32, a migrated long-running session shows only part of its history in the TUI. About 812 messages written between the V2 migration and the exit of the pre-upgrade client process exist in the legacy `message`/`part` tables (and in the `event` log) but were never projected into `session_message`. `opencode session export` is truncated for the same reason, so the missing history cannot be exported.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.32 (session created on 1.19.0; upgraded to 2.0.29, then 2.0.32)
- OS: Linux 5.15.0-52-generic #58~20.04.1-Ubuntu SMP x86_64
- Terminal: TERM_PROGRAM=vscode, TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /bin/sh
- Install/channel: latest (curl installer, `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`)
- Active plugins: none found (global config has no plugin entries)

## Reproduction

1. On OpenCode 1.19.0, start a long-running session and keep its client/server process open.
2. Upgrade to 2.0.29 without stopping that process; keep appending messages through the old process for several days.
3. Upgrade to 2.0.32 and open the same session in V2.
4. The TUI shows history only up to the migration snapshot; messages written between the snapshot and the old process exit are absent.
5. Verify with SQLite (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`):
   - `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM message WHERE session_id=?` → 1973
   - `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session_message WHERE session_id=?` → 1185
   - Missing range (3 days, 662 assistant + 150 user messages).
6. The event-sourced log still contains the missing events:
   - `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event WHERE aggregate_id=? AND seq BETWEEN 1162 AND 12163` → 10999 (`message.updated`, `message.part.updated`, `session.updated`).
   - However `event_sequence.seq` for the session is 12344, so V2 treats them as already processed and never projects them.
7. `opencode session export "<session-id>"` returns 1184 messages (export reads `session_message`), so the missing history is truncated there too.

## Expected Behavior

Migrated sessions should include all messages present in the legacy `message`/`part` tables, including those appended after the initial migration (e.g., by re-projecting late legacy messages at startup or when the session is opened). At minimum, `session export` should not silently omit them.

## Actual Behavior

- The TUI and `session export` omit roughly 812 messages written by the pre-upgrade process after migration.
- Manually reconstructing `session_message` rows from the retained `event` log causes `failed to decode session message` (HTTP 500 from `/api/experimental/session/<session-id>/export`) for some reconstructed rows, so the projection schema contains constraints that are not publicly documented.

## Additional Context

- DB: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`.
- Version timeline from logs: 1.19.0 until 10-15 21:45 (local); 2.0.29 from 10-15 21:45; 2.0.32 from 10-19 14:43.
- The pre-upgrade process kept running with a deleted binary (`/proc/<pid>/exe -> ~/.opencode/bin/opencode (deleted)`) and wrote only the legacy tables until it exited on 10-19.
- Workarounds tried:
  - `opencode session export` + `session import`: import refuses with "Session already exists"; export is truncated anyway.
  - Rewinding `event_sequence.seq`: **do not do this** — it is the event append cursor, not a projection cursor. It causes new events to reuse sequence numbers and overwrite the log (observed on a DB copy).
  - Manual projection from `event` into `session_message`: partial success, but the decoder rejects some reconstructed rows (tool `state.content`, error-state shape, etc.), so it is not safe as an end-user workaround.
- Suggestion: provide a repair/re-projection command (or automatically project late legacy messages) and let `session export` fall back to legacy tables.
- Data safety: raw `message`/`part`/`event` rows are intact; only the `session_message` projection is missing.

issues.title: [BUG]: bun run generate fails on dev - httpapi-codegen reports Referenced Promise types are not implemented
issues.body:
## Summary

`bun run generate` in `packages/client` fails on a clean `dev` checkout. The codegen throws before writing anything, so the generated client cannot be regenerated at all.

## Environment

- `dev` at `f0200df8e6` (reproduced on a clean tree, no local changes)
- `bun 1.4.2` (Windows x64)

## Reproduction

```
cd packages/client
bun run generate
```

```
1122 | function structuralType(schema: Schema.Top) {
1123 |   const document = SchemaRepresentation.toCodeDocument(SchemaRepresentation.toRepresentations([promiseTypeAst(schema)]))
1124 |   if (document.artifacts.length > 0 || Object.keys(document.references.recursives).length > 0) {
1125 |     throw new GenerationError({ reason: "Referenced Promise types are not implemented" })
             ^
error: Referenced Promise types are not implemented
    at structuralType (packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts:1125:11)
    at typeOf (packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts:809:18)
    at renderPromiseTypes (packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts:834:50)
    at emitPromise (packages/httpapi-codegen/src/index.ts:352:36)
    at packages/client/script/build.ts:97:9
```

Exit code 1; no files are written.

## Expected

The generated client is regenerated, or the tool names the schema that produced the reference so it can be fixed.

## Notes

Found while adding a field to `Session.Info`. Hand-patching `packages/client/src/promise/generated/types.ts` was the only way to keep that change moving, which is exactly the situation the generator exists to avoid.

The error names no schema, so the failing type has to be bisected out of the protocol surface.

issues.title: migration: one-time V1-to-V2 session import misses sessions and messages created by V1 afterwards
issues.body:
## Summary

The V1→V2 session migration is a one-time import: after it completes, any sessions **and messages** created by a still-installed V1 app (e.g. the V1 desktop app) are never imported, so they are invisible to V2. This makes restored desktop tabs point at sessions the V2 server cannot find ("This session cannot be found / this tab points to a session that no longer exists on this server"), and it silently truncates the transcripts of sessions that were migrated before being continued in V1.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.1.4 (V2 server/desktop; bundled CLI 2.1.4). Previously V1 desktop app running server v1.19.4.
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: N/A — OpenCode desktop app
- Shell: cmd.exe
- Install/channel: desktop app, `latest` channel
- Active plugins: none found in config

## Reproduction

1. Have the V1 desktop app installed (its server writes the legacy `session`, `message`, `part` tables in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`). Also start a V2 binary (CLI 2.1.4) once — the one-time migration runs and marks itself completed (`kv` key `migration.v1-v2` = `{"phase":"completed"}`).
2. Keep using the V1 desktop app for a while: create new sessions and continue old ones. These writes go to the legacy tables only.
3. Uninstall the V1 desktop and install the V2 desktop (2.1.4). The V2 server serves sessions only from the new `session_v2` / `session_message` tables.
4. On first launch the desktop restores its previous tab layout (kept in `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop`, which the uninstaller does not remove). Tabs pointing at V1-created sessions fail with "This session cannot be found — this tab points to a session that no longer exists on this server".

## Expected Behavior

V2 should surface sessions/messages written by V1 after the one-time import — e.g. re-run the legacy import incrementally at server start (import legacy rows missing from `session_v2`/`session_message`), or merge both tables when serving. The V1→V2 migration guide states non-API V1 behavior is intended to remain compatible; sessions created right before upgrading are effectively lost from the UI otherwise.

## Actual Behavior

Observed on this machine (data was recovered manually; nothing was actually deleted):

- 5 sessions created by the V1 app after the import had completed were present in the legacy `session` table (with all messages in `message`/`part`) but absent from `session_v2`, so `GET /api/session` did not list them and `GET /api/session/{id}` 404'd. Sizes: 712, 104, 80, 18 and 2 messages respectively (916 total).
- 1 already-migrated session continued in V1 lost visibility of ~380 messages appended after the import: the API served only its first 30 messages even though the legacy tables held ~410.
- The kv table contains `migration.v1-v2` = `{"phase":"completed"}` with a timestamp between the two batches, which is why the later batch was never imported.

Workaround used (documenting for others hitting this): copy the legacy `session` rows into `session_v2` (NULL for v2-only columns, `resume_attempts=0`), and transform `message`+`part` rows into `session_message` (role → `type`, legacy order → `seq`, `state.output` → `state.content[0].text`, `state.error` string → `state.error = {type: "tool.execution", message}`, `callID`→`id`, `tool`→`name`, part-level `metadata`→`providerState`, drop `step-start`/`step-finish`/`patch` parts but keep `snapshot.start`/`snapshot.end`/`snapshot.files`, drop `title`/`time` from state, `meta.variant` → `model.variant` defaulting to `default`). This reproduces what the one-time importer produces (verified byte-identical against all 650 messages it had already imported on this machine).

## Additional Context

- The V1 desktop and V2 desktop share the same data directory (`~/.local/share/opencode/`), including `opencode.log`, so the two server versions log side by side; V1 runs logged `version=1.19.4` on session creation while V2 sessions log `version=2.1.4`.
- Uninstalling the V1 desktop does **not** clear `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop` (tab/window state), which is why stale tabs referencing now-invisible sessions surface immediately after upgrading.
- Recovery was verified end-to-end via the V2 API (all 916 messages served and rendered correctly, including tool parts, reasoning, snapshots, tokens, errored and aborted tools).
- Frequency: deterministic for any V1 session/message created after the one-time import has run.

issues.title: Custom providers cannot request tool approval: provider-emitted tool-approval-request is never answered
issues.body:
A custom LanguageModelV3 provider emitting tool-approval-request (alone, or paired with a provider-executed tool-call) gets no permission prompt in the TUI or in headless run, and no tool-approval-response is ever sent back, with or without --auto.

Observed on opencode v2.1.4 (Linux), standalone server and normal TUI:
- A bare tool-approval-request is silently ignored; the turn completes normally.
- Paired with a tool-call, the run fails only on the missing provider tool result (unknown tool name) or waits for it, but no verdict ever arrives for the approval.
- When the provider stream stays open awaiting the verdict, the headless server connection dies (Transport ECONNRESET); the TUI hangs indefinitely with no prompt.

Expected: core surfaces the approval (permission prompt / auto policy) and routes the verdict back as tool-approval-response so the provider can continue.

Repro: any custom provider emitting the chunk. Our instance is opencode-muse (a Muse MSP bridge): a gated tool action parks the turn server-side, the bridge emits tool-call + tool-approval-request, and nothing comes back. Related bridge-side tracking: pgquiles/opencode-muse#22.

prs.title: fix(ai): send OpenAI Chat options that were silently dropped
prs.body:
## Problem

Chat Completions models take the same `providerOptions` type as Responses, so `serviceTier`, `textVerbosity`, `parallelToolCalls`, `metadata` and `safetyIdentifier` type-check, but the Chat request builder only sent `store`, `prompt_cache_key` and `reasoning_effort`. The rest were silently dropped. `toolChoice.disableParallelToolUse` was ignored too, even though Responses and Anthropic honor it.

This hit `openai.chat` and every provider built on the Chat protocol (azure, deepseek, fireworks, togetherai, deepinfra, cerebras, baseten, digitalocean, bedrock mantle, cloudflare, openai-compatible, ...).

## Change

The Chat builder now sends these, using Chat's own wire names from the Chat Completions API reference. Nothing is sent when the option is unset.

| option | Responses sends | Chat now sends |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `serviceTier` | `service_tier` | `service_tier` |
| `textVerbosity` | `text.verbosity` | `verbosity` (top level) |
| `parallelToolCalls`, or `disableParallelToolUse` | `parallel_tool_calls` | `parallel_tool_calls`, only when tools are present |
| `metadata` | `metadata` | `metadata` |
| `safetyIdentifier` | `safety_identifier` | `safety_identifier` |

The parallel tool calls value reuses the same resolver as Responses (explicit option wins, else `!disableParallelToolUse`). OpenAI returns a 400 for `parallel_tool_calls` without tools, so it's only sent when tools are present.

Note: OpenAI Chat rejects `metadata` unless `store: true` ("The 'metadata' parameter is only allowed when 'store' is enabled."). OpenAI chat models default to `store: false`, so callers who set `metadata` also need `store: true`. I left that as a loud API error instead of dropping `metadata` again.

## Out of scope

- Groq has its own wrapper that already sets `parallel_tool_calls` and `service_tier` from its own options, and it overwrites the base values, so Groq behaves as before.
- The Chat stream parser doesn't surface the response's `service_tier` in provider metadata yet.

prs.title: fix(tui): use php_only grammar for PHP syntax highlighting
prs.body:
## Problem

PHP code blocks without a `<?php` opening tag are not syntax highlighted in the TUI. This was [reproduced in #58664](https://github.com/sst/opencode/issues/58664).

The root cause is that `tree-sitter-php.wasm` is the **HTML-embedded** PHP grammar: it expects a `<?php` tag to switch from HTML into PHP mode. When a code block contains bare PHP (no `<?php`), the parser never enters PHP mode and produces no highlight tokens.

## Fix

Switch to `tree-sitter-php_only.wasm`, the **bare PHP** grammar published alongside `tree-sitter-php.wasm` in the same release. This grammar parses PHP directly without requiring an HTML embedding context.

The matching highlight query is available from nvim-treesitter at `queries/php_only/highlights.scm` (HTTP 200 confirmed).

```diff
- wasm: ".../tree-sitter-php.wasm",
+ wasm: ".../tree-sitter-php_only.wasm",
  queries: {
    highlights: [
-     ".../tree-sitter-php/raw/refs/heads/master/queries/highlights.scm",
+     ".../nvim-treesitter/.../queries/php_only/highlights.scm",
    ],
  },
```

No other files changed.

prs.title: fix(ai): preserve reasoning after the finish reason
prs.body:
## Problem

Some Chat-compatible hosts send reasoning after `finish_reason`. This currently fails an otherwise complete step and prevents native reasoning metadata from being reused in the next request.

## Change

I keep the first finish reason and continue accumulating supported reasoning and usage until the stream ends.

```text
finish_reason  -> remember the outcome
late reasoning -> retain text and replay metadata
stream end     -> close reasoning, publish tool calls, finish
```

Late answer text, refusals, and tool-call changes still fail. Explicit provider errors and missing required finish reasons are still checked.

## Out of scope

No Core, schema, retry-policy, or public API changes. Core already stores the final reasoning text and native metadata, then replays them for the same model.

prs.title: refactor(core): convert tool schemas once at registration
prs.body:
## Problem

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58798 cached converted tool schemas in two module-level WeakMaps, so every step and session shares the same schema objects. Session hooks (`context`, `compaction`, `generate`) only get a shallow copy, so a hook that edits a nested field changes the shared schema for good:

```text
hook: input.required.push("extra")

         before    after
step 1   ["a","extra"]    ["a","extra"]
step 2   ["a","extra"]    ["a","extra","extra"]
step 3   ["a","extra"]    ["a","extra","extra","extra"]
```

The edits also leak across sessions and agents.

Fixing that with another cache at the hook boundary would mean three caches for one value. The registry already converts every schema at registration to validate it, then throws the result away.

## Change

The registry keeps that result, so nothing needs a cache:

```diff
 registry add/update:
-    convert to validate, discard
+    convert once, store with the tool

 each step:
-    definition(tool)           (served from the runtime.ts WeakMaps)
+    stored definition
-    definition(codeModeTool)   (served from the runtime.ts WeakMaps)
+    converted once per registry revision, kept with the CodeMode catalog cache

 session hooks:
-    { ...inputSchema }         (shallow, nested edits leak)
+    JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(inputSchema))
```

- `runtime.ts` goes back to a plain `definition()` with no WeakMaps.
- The hook copy is about 55 µs per step for 30 tools on a synthetic benchmark, vs about 830 µs for converting every schema each step.
- Serialized definitions are unchanged, so prompt caches aren't affected.

Tests: a registry test that two snapshots return the same stored definitions with no extra conversions, and a hook test that edits a nested schema field across two requests. The old "reuses converted schemas" test is removed along with the caches it covered.

## Out of scope

- The tool input repair plugin still calls `definition()` per tool call, as it did before the caches in that PR. It reads tools through the public plugin API, which doesn't expose the stored definition.
- The CodeMode runtime still converts its tools once per inventory. Reading the stored definitions would mean changing the inventory type.

prs.title: fix(core): repair V1 global sessions left by completed imports
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #49827 for people who already upgraded.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

#56322 attributes V1 global sessions to their folder's project during the import, but only for imports that hadn't finished. Anyone who already upgraded still has those sessions under `global`, where the per-folder session lists can't find them.

This adds a one-time repair that runs in the background on server start, after the import:

```text
if the import is completed and the repair hasn't run:
    for each folder of V2 sessions still under global that came from V1:
        look up the folder's V2 project (same lookup as the import: 5s limit, stop after a timeout)
        nothing found, or it's global again -> skip
        one transaction:
            insert the project row if missing (never replace)
            set project_id + path, only where the session is still global; time_updated is kept
    mark the repair done
```

- Only touches `session_v2` rows that are still `global`, have no workspace, and also exist in the V1 `session` table. Sessions created in V2 are left alone.
- Lookups run outside transactions, and each folder is its own short transaction. If it stops partway, finished folders stay fixed and the next start does the rest.
- If the repair hits a database error it logs a warning, leaves the migration status alone, and retries next start.
- Fresh imports mark the repair done in their completion transaction, since they already attribute sessions.
- Undoable: the V1 `session` table still has the original `global` project ids.

Also points the orphan-session test at a missing folder inside its own temp dir instead of `/tmp/orphan`, which could exist on a machine.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test: a completed import with V1 global sessions in a plain folder, a git repo subfolder, a missing folder, plus a V2-native global session. Only the first two move, time_updated is kept, and the repair is marked done. Fails without the change.
- Ran the repair on a copy of a real already-migrated database (kv, project, session, session_v2 only): 346 sessions moved in about 100ms, 9 new projects, no other session column changed, no non-global session changed, 138 stayed global because their folders are gone.
- `bun run check` passes; `v1-migration` and `project` tests pass with `--rerun-each 3`.

prs.title: fix(core): keep a spawn failure from failing the whole step in Snapshot.capture
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #58685

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`Snapshot.capture` is best-effort by contract: log a warning, return `undefined`, let the step continue. Its handler uses `Effect.catch`, which in Effect v4 recovers **typed failures** only. A `child_process` spawn failure (`EPERM: uv_spawn git.EXE` on Windows) arrives as a **defect** — the stack in the issue starts at `spawn (node:child_process)` as a plain `Error`, not an `AppProcess.AppProcessError` — so it sailed past the handler into `SessionRunner.runStep`: the step died, the session recorded a bare `idle` message, and the user saw no error.

The fix adds `Effect.catchDefect` with the same warning-and-`undefined` recovery next to the existing `Effect.catch` (5 lines). I understand why it works: `catch` and `catchDefect` cover the failure and die channels of the Effect respectively, and interruption is a third channel that still propagates — so only the spawn-defect case changes behavior.

### How did you verify your code works?

Defect-injection repro of the exact handler shape, before vs after:

| | typed failure (control, e.g. Git exit) | spawn defect (the reported case) |
|---|---|---|
| before | recovered → `undefined` | **escalated — step dies** |
| after | recovered → `undefined` | recovered → `undefined` |

prs.title: fix(core): give session hooks their own copy of tool schemas
prs.body:
## Problem

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58798 caches each tool's converted JSON schema, so every step and every session now gets the same schema object. Session hooks (`context`, `compaction`, `generate`) only got a shallow copy, so a hook that edits anything nested changes the cached schema for good:

```text
hook: input.required.push("extra")

         before that PR   after that PR
step 1   ["a","extra"]    ["a","extra"]
step 2   ["a","extra"]    ["a","extra","extra"]
step 3   ["a","extra"]    ["a","extra","extra","extra"]
```

Edits also leak across sessions and agents. MCP tools already had this problem before it, since their raw JSON schema was always passed through as-is.

## Change

Hooks now get a deep copy of each input schema. The JSON text is cached per schema, so each step only pays for a `JSON.parse`:

```text
first time:  json = JSON.stringify(schema), cache it
each step:   hook input = JSON.parse(json)
```

On a made-up set of 30 tools this is about 46 µs per step, vs about 330 µs for `structuredClone` and about 830 µs for converting every schema again. Key order is preserved, so the bytes sent to the provider stay the same.

Added a test in `session-model-request-hooks.test.ts` where a hook edits a nested schema field across two requests.

## Out of scope

Output schemas aren't exposed to hooks, so they're left alone.

prs.title: fix(ai): absorb post-finish deltas in OpenAI Chat streams
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #56455

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`step()` failed every delta — content, refusal, reasoning, tool calls — that arrived after the chunk carrying `finish_reason`, with `OpenAI Chat received content after the finish reason`, discarding the whole step. Two wire shapes hit this in practice:

1. A reasoning-only trailing chunk (DeepInfra/StreamLake via OpenRouter, ~0.1–0.2% of requests — #56455).
2. A gateway that emits the `finish_reason` chunk *before* the model output (radoxai.com). There every request fails and the settled step is an empty assistant message; the strict check throws away the entire reply and its token usage.

The intent of the strict check (introduced in #40798) is to reject genuine protocol corruption. But the finish event and usage are only published once, when the stream ends (`finishEvents`), not when a `finish_reason` chunk is observed — so tolerating post-finish deltas keeps event ordering legal: absorbed deltas join the same open text / refusal / reasoning channels, and the real output plus its usage survive. The AI SDK, LiteLLM, and the official SDKs all pass these chunks through; this makes OpenCode absorb them the same way while keeping the settlement path intact.

Concretely:

- `step()` — the error path is gone; post-finish deltas are processed by the existing pipeline.
- The first terminal chunk wins: a `finish_reason` seen on a later chunk does not rewrite the already-recorded reason.
- `finishEvents` — tool calls that opened after the finish are finalized by the terminal's tool-call close, so a `"stop"` finish upgrades to `"tool-calls"` when late calls streamed in (seen on vLLM backends — reported in the linked thread). The `length` / `content-filter` truncation rule is unchanged: late calls under those finishes stay unconfirmed, as with any finish that truncates on purpose.

`mistral-chat.ts` keeps its own strict check; I left it alone deliberately — this change covers the OpenAI Chat protocol family and should be justified separately there if wanted.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `packages/ai/test/provider/openai-chat.test.ts` (native route) and `packages/ai/test/provider/openai-compatible-chat.test.ts`: text streaming after the finish chunk; reasoning-only trailing chunk; a tool call that opens after `"stop"` (reason upgrades to `"tool-calls"`, call parsed with complete input); the first finish reason kept when trailing chunks repeat one; usage merged from a trailing usage chunk after late deltas. The old `"rejects content after a terminal chunk"` assertion on the throw was reworked into the absorbed-tool-call case.
- Focused: `openai-chat` 82/82, `openai-compatible-chat` 28/28, `openrouter` 23/23, `mistral-chat` 19/19.
- Full `packages/ai` suite: 1884 pass, 0 fail, 28 skip (recorded cassettes unchanged).
- `bun run typecheck` in `packages/ai`: both passes clean (`check --no-script` and the types config).
- `bunx oxlint` on the three changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Prettier clean.
- The gateway shape I described (finish first, content after, usage trailing) comes from a live deployment where every request failed on v2.1.4; with a local stream-ordering middleware implementing exactly these semantics, all four models stream text and complete tool-call turns.

### Screenshots / recordings

n/a — parser behavior, no UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

## Problem

Video inputs used file encoding by default, and tool-returned video needed provider-specific placement.

## Change

I made the shared Responses encoder use standard video blocks. Exceptions stay private in the existing provider adapters.

| --- | --- |

Audio support and provider capability detection.

prs.title: feat(core): accept a pasted redirect URL for MCP OAuth
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/54495
Addresses https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/33966

### Problem

MCP sign-in only finishes when the browser reaches the callback server on `127.0.0.1`. Over SSH, in a container, or with the TUI attached to a remote server, the browser is on another machine, so it lands on a page that doesn't load and the login never completes.

### Change

The login still waits for the browser, and now also accepts the URL the browser was redirected to, pasted from the address bar. Whichever arrives first finishes the login. No flag, no mode to pick up front.

```text
show the sign-in link
wait for either:
    browser reaches the callback server  → finish login (unchanged)
    user pastes the redirect URL         → same state/code/error checks, finish login
wrong paste (other sign-in, not a URL, no code) → error, keep waiting
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Client as TUI / CLI
    participant Server
    participant Login as MCP login
    Client->>Server: connect oauth
    Server-->>Client: attempt { mode: "auto", paste: true }
    User->>Client: paste redirect URL
    Client->>Server: complete { code: <redirect URL> }
    Server->>Login: submit(url)
    Login-->>Server: rejected (stays pending) or handed to the token exchange
    Client->>Server: poll status (unchanged)
    Server-->>Client: complete / failed
```

- **Core**: the MCP login gets a `submit` hook that feeds a pasted URL into the same place the callback server feeds the browser redirect. `oauth.complete` forwards a `code` to it for `auto` attempts, where it used to die.
- **Schema**: `Integration.Attempt` gets an optional `paste: true` so clients know to show the box. Old clients ignore it and keep waiting for the browser.
- **Server**: `oauth.complete` now returns the real failure message instead of always "Authentication failed", so a wrong paste says why.
- **TUI**: the waiting dialog becomes a prompt when `paste` is set. Enter on an empty prompt opens the link, `tab` copies it (new `dialog.integration.copy` keybind).
- **CLI**: `opencode mcp auth` shows a paste prompt alongside the wait. A rejected paste asks again.
- Docs for the new MCP section and keybind, regenerated client and OpenAPI.

Nothing breaks: the field is optional, and the `complete` request already took an optional `code`.

### Out of scope

- A configurable callback listen address (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/33966). The paste covers the same setups without opening a port.
- Bare authorization codes. Only the full URL is accepted, so the paste is always checked against this login's `state`.
- Other `auto` logins (provider plugins). The hook is generic, but only MCP uses it here.


---
<!-- opencode-github-bot:pr-section -->
_Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._

Related: #33966, #57130, #58095

Public API: adds optional `paste` to Integration.Attempt and lets oauth.complete take a pasted redirect URL for auto attempts; new `dialog.integration.copy` keybind (backwards compatible)
<!-- /opencode-github-bot:pr-section -->

prs.title: feat(core): add GitHub Copilot auto model
prs.body:
Fixes #34644

Copilot Student and Free plans now only allow auto model selection, so every model from Copilot's `/models` has `model_picker_enabled: false` and Copilot showed up with no models. This adds `github-copilot/auto`, matching how VS Code handles Auto.

## How it works

- **Catalog:** when `/models` advertises auto candidates (`billing.auto_discount`), the Copilot sync adds an `Auto` model. Its limits are the smallest across candidates.
- **Routing:** a new `model.resolve` session hook lets a plugin swap the selected model for another model in the same provider's catalog, including hidden ones. The Copilot plugin uses it to call `POST /auto` with the latest user prompt and swap `auto` for the chosen model.
- **Requests:** everything after resolution is the chosen model's normal route (native Anthropic for Claude, Responses or chat for the rest) with its own limits and reasoning. History records the real model. The `Copilot-Session-Token` from `/auto` is added in the existing `model.request` hook.
- **Caching:** routes are cached per session until 5 minutes before the 24h token expires. If routing fails, it falls back to the `is_chat_fallback` model and retries after 5 minutes.

## Verification

- Live against Copilot: `opencode run -m github-copilot/auto` resolved to `gpt-6-luna` and streamed, including a multi-step tool call.
- Tests cover the auto catalog entry, core retargeting to a hidden model, and plugin routing, caching, session token header and fallback.
- Not yet verified on a real Student account.

prs.title: fix(core): revalidate the models.dev catalog with its ETag
prs.body:
### Problem

The models.dev refresh runs every 5 minutes. Each tick reads and parses the ~6 MB cached catalog from KV just to check its age, then downloads the whole catalog (about 6 MB raw, ~413 KB brotli) and hashes it, even though models.opencode.ai serves an ETag and answers revalidation with an empty `304`. When the body matched the cache it returned early without recording the check, so the next process or tick never saw it as fresh.

### Change

I moved the freshness info (`updatedAt`, `digest`, `etag`) into its own small KV key next to the catalog, and the refresh tick only reads that key.

```diff
 refresh()
-  read + parse 6 MB catalog entry   (age + digest)
-  GET api.json                      -> 200, full body
-  same digest?  return              (check not recorded)
+  read ~150 B meta entry            (age + digest + etag)
+  GET api.json  If-None-Match: <etag>
+  304 or same digest?  write meta only, publish nothing
   otherwise     decode, write catalog + meta, invalidate, publish Refreshed
```

- The catalog entry keeps its current shape, so `get()` and older builds read it as before. It's only written when the catalog actually changes.
- The meta key is written after the catalog write succeeds, so a backend that rejects the big value (Durable Objects) never ends up with an ETag pointing at a catalog it doesn't have.
- If there's no meta key yet (entries from older builds), it falls back to `updatedAt`/`digest` from the catalog entry once.
- Removing a corrupt catalog entry also removes its meta key.
- Forced refreshes skip `If-None-Match`, and responses without an ETag behave like before.

No migration and no public schema change.

### Out of scope

Durable Object deployments still can't cache the catalog at all (it's over their 2 MB value limit), so they keep fetching the full body.

prs.title: feat(ai): replace experimental evaluation with Decision
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Follow-up to https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58382, https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58381 and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58379.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Decision models (TypeSafe Jev, OpenAI GPT-6 Luna, Cloudflare Clef and others) lived under `@opencode/ai/experimental` as `Evaluation`, with a System One shaped request: map-keyed questions, `boolean`, string state, no media. This replaces it with a first-class `Decision` API that uses OpenAI's Decisions vocabulary and takes media. Hard rename, no aliases.

```ts
const response = yield* Decision.generate({
  model: OpenAI.decision("gpt-6-luna"),          // was provider.experimental.evaluation(id)
  input: [                                       // JSON object, or ordered text / json / media parts
    { type: "text", text: "Receipt:" },
    { type: "media", media: receipt },
  ],
  questions: [                                   // list with required names
    { name: "refund", type: "predicate", instructions: "Refund request?" },
    { name: "team", type: "choice", instructions: "Which team?", choices: [{ value: "billing" }, { value: "tech" }] },
    { name: "urgency", type: "score", instructions: "How urgent?", levels: [{ label: "Later" }, { label: "Now" }] },
  ],
  providerOptions: { promptCacheKey: "support-v1" }, // typed by the selected model
})

response.answers // in question order:
// { name: "refund", type: "predicate", probability }
// { name: "team", type: "choice", choice, probabilities: [{ value, probability }], confidence }
// { name: "urgency", type: "score", score, probabilities: [{ value, label, probability }], confidence }
// { name, type: "error", reason: "refusal" }   per-question refusal, the rest still come back
```

- Answers that don't match the questions (missing, an option that wasn't offered, a score off the scale) fail the whole call.
- No `rounding` field and no System One `legend` (labels are on the score probabilities).

Each protocol puts media where its host reads it, and fails the call when the host has no place for that kind:

| Protocol | Hosts | Media |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI Decisions | OpenAI, Vercel (now `/v1/decisions` instead of the custom `/v1/evaluate` code) | `input_image` parts; audio and video fail |
| System One, `assets` (default) | TypeSafe, OpenCode, DigitalOcean (Jev) | TypeSafe `assets` map with references in the state, plus `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true` |
| System One with Baseten's placement (its provider fixes it; not a models.dev value) | Baseten | `image_url` parts in a user message inside `state.messages`; text and JSON parts become text parts |
| System One, `state` | OpenRouter | `image_url` / `input_audio` / `video_url` items inside the state list |
| Cloudflare Run (System One body) | Workers AI Clef, AI Gateway Jev | top-level `images` / `audio` / `videos` lists |

URL media is downloaded first for System One and Cloudflare, which only take inline data (the protocol declares `inlineMedia`). The TypeSafe image header is always sent by the TypeSafe, OpenCode and DigitalOcean providers: TypeSafe rejects images without it, and text-only requests are unchanged with it (same answers and token count, checked live).

```diff
 src/
+├── decision.ts                         # types, Decision.request / generate
+├── decision-client.ts                  # runs the route, checks answers
+├── route/decision.ts                   # DecisionRoute.make(...).with(...).model(...), like Route for language models
 ├── protocols/
+│   ├── openai-decisions.ts
+│   ├── system-one.ts
+│   └── cloudflare-run-decisions.ts
 ├── experimental/
-│   ├── evaluation.ts
-│   ├── evaluation-client.ts
-│   ├── system-one.ts
-│   ├── openai-decisions.ts
-│   └── cloudflare-run-evaluation.ts
 └── providers/*.ts                      # experimental.evaluation(id) -> decision(id)
```

Models are built the same way as language models:

```ts
// protocols/system-one.ts
export const route = DecisionRoute.make({ id: "system-one", provider: "typesafe-ai", protocol, endpoint: Endpoint.path("/systemone", { baseURL }) })

// providers/openrouter.ts
SystemOne.route
  .with({ provider: id, providerMetadataKey: "openrouter", endpoint: { baseURL }, auth })
  .model<OpenRouterDecisionOptions>({ id, compatibility: { imageInput: "state" } })
```

Host quirks go in `DecisionModelCompatibility` (`imageInput`, from models.dev's `compatibility.image_input`), like `LanguageModelCompatibility`. OpenAI Decisions reads its options through a schema (`promptCacheKey`, `promptCacheOptions`, `safetyIdentifier`) and passes anything else through.

`DecisionClient` is part of `AIClient.layer` and the promise API.

Not in this PR: each protocol's own call for things outside the common API (System One `box` questions, OpenAI conversation input), reading models.dev's per-model `image_input` (each provider uses one default for now), Ollama's raw-base64 `images`, and llama.cpp.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/ai`; `bun run test` there: 1874 pass, 0 fail.
- The 8 existing recorded decision cassettes replay unchanged against the new request shape (renamed to `*-decision`).
- Live with a red and a blue image through the package: TypeSafe (`assets`), OpenRouter Clef Flash (`state`), OpenAI, and Vercel with both GPT-6 Luna and Jev all answered correctly. Not live: OpenCode Zen (my key gets "Model access is disabled") and Cloudflare Clef with images (my token lacks Workers AI access).

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR


---

Public API: replaces experimental Evaluation with Decision / DecisionClient / DecisionRoute and provider.decision(id) (breaking for @opencode/ai/experimental callers)

prs.title: fix(tui): retry prompts after workspace catalogs load
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related to #52171, specifically the [v2.1.4 silent-submit reproduction](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/52171#issuecomment-6372395616). The older report's newline-insertion symptom is not reproduced, so this deliberately does not auto-close that issue.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Keep an Enter submission pending while the selected worktree's agents, models, or config are loading, then submit once using the destination's settings. Previously the missing agent caused an immediate, silent return; missing config could also select the wrong default model.

Show the normal prompt spinner with `Loading workspace…` while a submission waits for those catalogs. Respect disabled animations, reserve space for the loader on narrow terminals, and clear it when the submission proceeds, is cancelled, or fails. The draft remains editable; the interrupt hint still appears only for an actually running session.

Cancel pending input when its draft, mode, session, or location changes, a dialog opens, or the external editor starts. Ownership changes also invalidate queued native Enter callbacks, and submissions remain blocked throughout the editor handoff. This prevents stale sends even if the editor returns before Enter's IME timers fire. The draft stays intact for a fresh Enter.

Keep the waiting send active through temporary catalog failures, joining the location provider's background loads and matching its bounded retry policy (three attempts, 500 ms then 1 s backoff). A typed `LocationNotFoundError` fails immediately; exhausted retries clear the spinner and show an error without losing the draft. Cancelling the send also prevents subsequent retries from submitting or displaying stale errors.

Slash input also waits for the destination command catalog, so commands cannot become ordinary prompts because of response ordering. Ordinary prompts do not wait for commands.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Real TUI tests drive `Ctrl+P` → Manage workspaces → another worktree → Enter, with destination responses gated independently.
- Regression cases cover catalog loading, duplicate Enter, editing, navigation/modal cancellation, queued native callbacks, slow/fast external-editor handoff, slash-command ordering, ordinary/unknown-slash text, and failure/retry. Loader coverage includes animated/static modes at 44 and 100 columns and cleanup on editing, navigation, editor handoff, and terminal failure. Retry cases cover automatic agent/command recovery, editing during retry, exhaustion with manual resubmission, and immediate missing-location failure.
- Twenty-eight focused tests passed across ten runs: **280 pass, 0 fail**. The cancellation, command-readiness, loader, and transient-recovery regressions failed before their fixes. The five retry scenarios also passed with randomized order.
- **51 related tests** also passed.
- TUI `bun typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full TUI suite after the follow-ups: **1,574 pass, 2 skip, 1 fail**. The sole failure is the unchanged `test/component/go-upsell-art.test.tsx` logo expectation; it also fails in isolation, without importing the prompt component.
- Repository-wide `bun run check` passed lint, reported the existing Vite plugin type mismatches in the Console/Stats packages under the local hoisted install, and then its Bun/Turbo runner crashed (SIGSEGV). TUI package checks passed separately.

### Screenshots / recordings

Captured from the production TUI renderer with gated fixture responses at 100 × 30. These are fixture captures, not a live-service recording or a visual mock-up. Tests also cover 44-column terminals.

**Animations enabled — one captured spinner frame:**

![Production TUI showing the normal spinner and Loading workspace while the draft remains visible](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/pedro757/a2b86ebc2df9c0036b5cf1cdbd47caa5/raw/5e5723bb3566e5dcec24d24ab59be38ec9785ff8/workspace-loading-animated.svg)

### Issue for this PR

Closes #58648

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

When the effective tool set for a request is empty but the conversation history contains tool calls/results, the chat protocol sends an explicit `"tools": []` (added for Anthropic-via-LiteLLM and Bedrock, which require the field to be present). Strict OpenAI-compatible upstreams reject that with 400 "`tools` must not be an empty array", and there was no way to opt out — so e.g. every compaction request from a session whose tools were cleared by a plugin failed against those upstreams.

This adds an `omitEmptyTools` boolean to the model compatibility flags. The flag goes through the existing provider/model compatibility merge, so it is configurable per provider/model (`providers.<id>.compatibility`), and since `openai-compatible-chat` reuses `OpenAIChat.protocol` end-to-end it applies there as well. This follows the same compatibility-flag shape proposed in the issue discussion (`compatibility: { "omitEmptyTools": true }`).

prs.title: fix(core): preserve file mode when patch move emulates rename
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #58651

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A patch `Update File ... Move to ...` is applied as "write destination, then remove source" rather than a rename, so the destination is a freshly created file that inherits the process umask. A `0755` script moved through a patch became `0644`/`0664` depending on the machine and could no longer be executed (exit 126).

The fix adds a `copyMode` operation to the `Files` contract — it copies the source file's permission bits onto an existing destination — and the patch move branch runs it between the write and the remove, so the bits are carried over before the source disappears. It follows the source's final symlink, because a link entry carries no mode worth copying and its target's bits are the ones a copy-then-delete move must preserve.

Implemented for all three environment backends: local (`fs.stat` + `fs.chmod`), GNU exec (`chmod --reference` with a `stat -L` precheck so a missing or dangling source still classifies as `NotFound`), and memory (file nodes now store a `mode`). The workspace proxy forwards the call.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Reproduced the bug on a real Linux box first: a `0755` script moved via the patch flow came out `0664` (host umask `0002`), non-executable.
- Verified the `copyMode` shell semantics on Linux across a matrix: file→file copies 755; symlink→file follows the link and copies 755; dangling symlink / missing source / missing destination all fail with `NotFound`.
- Added a regression test in `tool-patch.test.ts` ("preserves the executable bit when moving a file") and a conformance check for `copyMode` exercised by both the local and GNU exec harnesses; both self-skip on Windows, where there is no exec bit.

prs.title: fix(core): report a background subagent's later turns to its parent
prs.body:
## What it does

When a background subagent keeps working after it first reports, its parent now gets the real result. Before this, if a child ended a step with an empty response and went idle, the parent got "Subagent completed without a text response." If a plugin or a synthetic message then woke the child, it carried on working, but its result never reached the parent.

## How it works

`SubagentJob` remembers each child it puts in the background, along with the idle marker of the last busy period the parent heard about. When one of those children succeeds or fails outside a subagent job, it reads that busy period, from its idle marker back to the previous one. It reports the busy period to the parent in the usual `<subagent …>` message only when it carries news:

- Text results and failures are reported.
- Empty successes are not, so a plugin retrying empty steps, or a compact, move or revert wake, doesn't wake the parent each time.
- Interruptions are not. Job cancellation already reports those, and this avoids waking a parent that is being deleted.
- A busy period that contains a user prompt is skipped. That's someone talking to the child directly.

The job's own result is still delivered by the existing job path. Until that delivery finishes, follow-ups wait; then the newest busy period is checked once, so nothing is lost or reported out of order. Foreground children aren't tracked. Tracking is cleared when the child or its parent is deleted.

## Risk

- A parent can now get more than one message from the same background child. Each one is a real result it was missing. Children that finish in one busy period behave exactly as before.
- Tracking is in memory. If the server restarts during a continuation, that continuation isn't reported. Restart recovery for the original job is unchanged.

## Proof

New tests in `tool-subagent.test.ts`. The last three fail against the first version of this PR:

- A child whose first step is empty, then is woken: the parent gets the real text after the first notice.
- Prompting a child directly doesn't notify the parent.
- Two empty continuations in a row don't notify the parent; the next one with text does.
- Interrupting a continuation doesn't notify the parent.
- Deleting the parent while its child is continuing sends nothing.

Targeted runs: `tool-subagent`, `subagent-lifetime`, `command-subagent`, `session-execution`, `job` and `location-layer` give 94 pass. `tool-subagent` passed 5 runs in a row. Typecheck is clean.

prs.title: fix(ai): classify failed Google Interactions by reported errors
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No linked issue.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem.** When a Google Interactions stream ends with `interaction.completed` and `status: "failed"` (or `"cancelled"`), the parser reported only `Google Interactions failed`. The official Interaction resource carries the reason in `errors: [{ code, message }]`, but the classifier never looked inside that list. So `permission_denied` and `insufficient_quota` came out as a retryable `UnknownProvider` error with no useful message. This affects both Google and Google Vertex, since they share the protocol.

**Change.** The protocol now decodes `errors` on the terminal interaction and gives the existing classifier the provider's own details:

```diff
 interaction.completed (failed | cancelled)
   classifyProviderFailure
-    message: "Google Interactions failed"
-    data:    interaction
+    message: every non-empty errors[].message, joined by newlines
+             (falls back to "Google Interactions <status>" when there are none)
+    data:    first errors[] entry with a code (falls back to interaction)
     rawBody: the full original event (unchanged)
```

| Terminal `errors` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[{ code: "permission_denied", message: "Access denied" }]` | UnknownProvider, "Google Interactions failed" | Authentication, "Access denied" |
| `[{ message: "Out of credits" }, { code: "insufficient_quota", message: "Add billing" }]` | UnknownProvider | QuotaExceeded, both messages |
| `[]` or absent | UnknownProvider, "Google Interactions failed" | unchanged |

When there are several errors, the first one with a code decides the classification. That matches how the shared message decoder already reads `errors[0]`. All messages stay visible, and the raw body and HTTP details are kept as before.

**Out of scope:** mapping generic codes such as `not_found` on `error` events, HTTP 200 JSON bodies sent to SSE routes, retry policy, and status/overflow precedence.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added one table-driven test in `packages/ai/test/provider/google-vertex-interactions.test.ts`. It runs the real stream parser with SSE fixtures and checks the error tag, message and raw body. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `bun run test` in `packages/ai`: 1873 pass, 28 skip, 0 fail.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/ai`: passes.

prs.title: fix(ai): classify AWS modeled errors from every restJson1 identity location
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No tracked issue. The problem is described below.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

**Problem.** AWS restJson1 services name the modeled error in one of three places: the `X-Amzn-Errortype` header, a `__type` body field, or a `code` body field. The value can be namespaced (`ns#Name`) or carry a suffix (`Name:uri`), and the [Smithy spec](https://smithy.io/2.0/aws/protocols/aws-restjson1-protocol.html#operation-error-serialization) asks clients to accept all three locations and to strip both decorations. `providerCodes` only read a bare `code`. The header was kept only as a diagnostic header, and `__type` was never read. So the same AWS error was classified differently depending on where it appeared:

| HTTP 400, `"message":"Slow down"`, error identity in | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| body `code: ThrottlingException` | RateLimit | RateLimit |
| body `__type: ThrottlingException` | InvalidRequest | RateLimit |
| body `code: com.amazonaws.bedrock#ThrottlingException:http://internal.amazon.com/coral/` | InvalidRequest | RateLimit |
| header `X-Amzn-Errortype: ThrottlingException:http://…` only | InvalidRequest | RateLimit |

These are synthetic inputs that test the protocol shape. They don't claim that Bedrock sends throttles as HTTP 400. The Bedrock HTTP 429 "Too many tokens" case was fixed separately in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58759.

**Change.** The fix adds the cleaned AWS identity to the existing list of codes. Raw codes stay in the list unchanged, so the existing typed reasons (`RateLimit`, `ValidationException` → `InvalidRequest`, and so on) classify it.

```diff
 classifyProviderFailure
   codes = [
     ...providerCodes(data | body | message)
+        decoded.__type → awsErrorType
+        decoded.code   → awsErrorType   (added next to the raw code)
     ...gateway [code] label
+    ...awsErrorType(http.headers["x-amzn-errortype"])
   ]
```

```text
awsErrorType(value)
  drop everything from the first ":"
  drop everything up to and including the first "#"
```

The cleaned value is only added, never substituted. Non-AWS codes still match exactly as they did before. Only the top-level `code` and the AWS-specific `__type` field and header get cleaned. The raw body, headers and cause on the error stay the same.

**Out of scope.** Classification precedence is unchanged: the overflow regexes, status and text ordering, and the retry policy. Google Interactions error details are also unchanged.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added one table-driven case to `packages/ai/test/executor.test.ts` that goes through the real `RequestExecutor.httpFailure` path for all four identity locations. It fails without the source change (`Expected: "RateLimit"`, `Received: "InvalidRequest"`) and passes with it.

prs.title: fix(schema): validate base64 attachments in linear time
prs.body:
## Problem

`Prompt.Base64` validated with `/^(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{4})*(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{2}==|[A-Za-z0-9+/]{3}=)?$/u`. That check doesn't only run on input. It runs every time we decode a stored user message or inbox row, so every step's history reload, the inbox (twice), the projector and GET messages.

The repeated 4-char group is slow on big strings: about 50 ms per 6.7 MB of base64 on Bun 1.4.4. In an image attachment benchmark it was 69% of server CPU, with event loop stalls up to 2.2 s.

## Change

The runtime check is now "only base64 chars followed by 0-2 `=`, and length divisible by 4", which accepts exactly the same strings and takes about 2 ms for the same 6.7 MB.

```diff
 Prompt.Base64
-  run: /^(?:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{4})*(?:..==|...=)?$/
+  run: length % 4 === 0 && /^[A-Za-z0-9+/]*={0,2}$/
   metadata: original pattern (OpenAPI, error message, codegen)
```

I kept the original pattern's annotations on the filter, so the OpenAPI `pattern`, the error message and the generated client stay byte for byte the same. I checked the two against each other on random strings and real base64 with zero mismatches.

prs.title: perf(core): resize images in a worker and release photon memory when idle
prs.body:
**What it does**

Resizing a large image used to freeze the server for 420–460 ms per image, because photon (WASM) ran on the main thread. It also kept about 250 MB of WASM memory for the life of the process. Resizes now run in a worker thread, and that worker shuts down after 10 seconds idle so its memory goes back to the OS. The output bytes are the same as before.

This is #4 from Aiden's server perf findings. cc @rekram1-node

**How it works**

1. The resize code moves unchanged into `image/photon-normalize.ts` and returns plain data, so it can run in either place.
2. `image/photon-worker.ts` loads photon and resizes on request. `Image.Photon` starts it on first use and keeps it in an `RcRef` with a 10 s idle time-to-live. When it's released, the worker is terminated.
3. If the worker can't start (no `worker_threads`, a bundle without the worker file, or photon failing to load inside it), we log a warning once and resize on the main thread exactly as before.
4. A WASM panic or an unreadable message kills the worker. Every call in flight fails the way an in-process photon throw does today, and the next call gets a fresh worker. That way no queued job runs on a broken WASM heap.
5. Images that already fit get an `Unchanged` reply, so the base64 isn't copied back from the worker.
6. The compiled CLI build adds the worker as a second entrypoint (`cli/src/photon-worker.ts`), so it sits next to the chunks that load it.

**Risk**

- Server-only. The call site API and its errors are unchanged.
- workerd: unchanged. It still fails with `ResizerUnavailableError` before touching any worker code. The workerd bundle probe passes; `node:worker_threads` shows up only as a lazy import there and never runs.
- Node single-file build (`opencode2-node`): this build doesn't include the worker yet, so it keeps resizing on the main thread, with a one-time warning. Shipping the worker there needs its own Vite build and an asset in the build's asset hash. Left for a follow-up.
- The first image after an idle period pays about 50 ms to start the worker.
- If a worker dies mid-resize, those calls fail instead of the server crashing.

**Proof**

Measured on a Mac with a 4032×3024 PNG (31 MB) and three resizes, using an event-loop lag probe and RSS after GC:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Longest main-thread stall per resize | 420–460 ms | 5–9 ms |
| RSS after resizing | 418 MB | 624 MB (worker alive) |
| RSS after 15 s idle | 416 MB | 132 MB |
| Output | — | byte-identical |

A compiled Bun binary built with the same entrypoints gave the same numbers (5–9 ms; RSS back to 54 MB after idle). A bundle built without the worker entry fell back to the main thread and produced the same bytes. A Node build of the worker stalled the main thread for at most 3 ms.

Tests and checks:
- `bun run test test/image-photon.test.ts test/tool-read.test.ts test/config/image.test.ts`: 35 pass. The new tests cover: same bytes as the old resizer (fixed SHA-256), concurrent calls sharing one worker with correct outputs, a crash mid-resize failing every in-flight call and the next call getting a fresh worker, termination after idle, and fallback with one warning when the worker can't start.
- `bun run typecheck` (core, cli): clean
- `oxlint` and `ast-grep` Effect patterns on the changed files: clean
- `bun run script/workerd-probe.ts`: OK

Checked by an independent cross-model review before pushing; its findings are fixed in the second commit.

prs.title: fix(cli): bound server shutdown with a 10 s deadline
prs.body:
Fixes #58816

**What it does**

After SIGTERM or SIGINT, the server could hang in teardown forever, and the logs never named the step it was stuck on. Teardown now has a 10 s deadline. When the deadline passes, the process logs what is still pending and exits 1. A second signal during teardown does the same immediately.

**How it works**

1. `ShutdownDeadline.install()` in the CLI entry starts a timer on the first SIGTERM or SIGINT. `runMain` still interrupts the main fiber as before. Startup order and listener shutdown are unchanged.
2. When the timer fires, the process prints the pending work to stderr, logs `shutdown deadline exceeded`, waits 1.5 s so the file logger can flush, then exits 1. A second signal prints the same report and exits at once.
3. Pending work is recorded in a small registry, `Teardown.track` / `pending` in `@opencode/util/teardown`:
   - `LayerNode.compile` brackets each node's release, so a stuck layer shows up as `layer <name> releasing`.
   - The cross-spawn spawner tracks each child from spawn until close or scope release, as `child <pid> running: <command>`.
4. Closing a child's scope now escalates to SIGKILL after 3 s (`RELEASE_FORCE_KILL_AFTER`) unless the command sets its own `forceKillAfter`. Before, release sent SIGTERM and waited forever.

Example report:

```
shutdown did not finish within 10s; exiting. Still pending:
  10.0s  child 73484 running: bun -e setInterval(() => {}, 1000)
  10.0s  layer test/Hung releasing
```

**Risk**

- Server and CLI shutdown, plus child process release everywhere the cross-spawn spawner is used.
- The 3 s default force-kill also applies when a scope closes mid-session (tool cancellation). That's safe: shell, MCP, standalone and ssh children already set 2–3 s, and before this change a child that ignored SIGTERM hung tool cancellation too.
- A teardown that legitimately needs more than 10 s would now be cut off. Nothing in the tree is expected to need that long.
- Not verified against a real hung production server. The tests use a fixture with a deliberately stuck finalizer and a real child process.

**Proof**

Reviewed by Argon before push (verdict: ship). Its two follow-ups are in the second commit: settle released children, and handle a second signal.

- `bun test --timeout 30000 test/shutdown-deadline.test.ts test/service-lifecycle.test.ts test/standalone.test.ts` (packages/cli): pass. The new tests spawn a real server-shaped process with a hung layer and a child, then check the report, exit code 1, and that a second signal exits without waiting for the deadline.
- `bun run script/test.ts test/effect/cross-spawn-spawner.test.ts test/effect/layer-node test/process/process.test.ts test/mcp.test.ts` (packages/core): pass. The new spawner test checks that a released child whose grandchild holds its pipes is no longer listed as pending. It fails without the fix.
- `bun typecheck` in util, cli and core: pass.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep the service's XDG_STATE_HOME out of tool shells and name the port owner
prs.body:
**What it does**

If the service's saved env sets `XDG_STATE_HOME` (`opencode service set env XDG_STATE_HOME …`), every tool shell the service starts inherited it. Anything started from that shell then looked for the service registration in the wrong place. That includes a nested `opencode` and the desktop app relaunched by an agent. They reported the service "missing" and started a second server, which failed after 15 s with "port … already in use". Retrying failed the same way.

This PR stops the saved env from moving the registration. The port-in-use error now also names the process holding the port.

**How it works**

1. `ServiceConfig.processEnv` drops `XDG_STATE_HOME` from the saved env. The server uses it when it copies the saved env into `process.env`, which tool shells, PTYs, MCP servers and LSPs inherit. The CLI uses it when it spawns the service with that env.
2. The service registers under the state directory it was launched with, so its children now see that same directory.
3. On a bind conflict, `PortOwner.describe` runs `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN -t` and `ps -o command= -p <pid>` (1 s timeout each, whitespace collapsed, capped at 200 chars). The error then reads `already in use by PID 123 (…)`. If the lookup fails, and on Windows, it keeps "another process".

Why fix it in the server rather than in Desktop (for example, Desktop ignoring an inherited `XDG_STATE_HOME`):
- `XDG_STATE_HOME` is how every client finds the service: Desktop's `service-probe` fallback, the CLI's `Global.state` and the SSH bootstrap. A value only the service's children see can only split them from it.
- Desktop test roots and isolated mode set `XDG_STATE_HOME` on purpose, so ignoring it there would break them.
- A nested CLI in a tool shell would still have the same problem.

`XDG_DATA/CONFIG/CACHE_HOME` and `OPENCODE_DB` still pass through. They don't affect discovery, and a nested CLI keeps finding the same database and config.

**Risk**

- CLI only (server process and `opencode service` spawn). A saved `XDG_STATE_HOME` is now ignored. Before this, it only worked when the CLI spawned the service, and even then clients couldn't find the registration.
- When Desktop spawns the service directly, `global-roots.ts` reads `XDG_DATA/CONFIG/CACHE_HOME` at import time, before `config.env` is applied. So only `OPENCODE_*` vars reliably relocate server paths. A possible follow-up is to strip all four or document it.
- The port-owner lookup runs only on the failure path, after the 15 s retry window, and is bounded at about 2 s.

**Proof**

Reviewed by Argon before push; verdict ship, with one nit applied (collapse whitespace in the `ps` output).

I ran the tests with any inherited `OPENCODE_*`/`XDG_*` vars unset:
- `bun test test/service.test.ts -t "saved service environment|port owner|unresponsive managed port|service config manages environment"`: 5 pass. The new tests cover env filtering, `options()` env and file, and the port owner for a listening and a free port. The existing conflict test now expects `PID <pid> (`.
- `bun test test/service-lifecycle.test.ts -t "unrelated process on the port"`: 1 pass.
- `bun run typecheck` (cli): clean.
- `oxlint` on the changed files: clean.
