prs.title: perf(core): skip integration list rebuilds when nothing changed
prs.body:
## What it does

Every session step rebuilt the full integration list several times: `Provider.snapshot` called `Integration.list()` before checking its cache, and `Model.snapshot` reads the provider snapshot on every read. Each rebuild loaded and decoded every stored credential and projected and sorted every integration. A CPU profile of a 300-step replay saw about 8 rebuilds per step, roughly 4% of server CPU. This PR skips those rebuilds while nothing they depend on has changed.

## How it works

1. `Credential` gets a synchronous `revision()` counter, bumped right after each write (`create`, `activate`, `update`, `remove`) and before the event is published. Bumping at the write site rather than on the bus means the very next read sees the change; bus delivery is async.
2. `Integration.list` keeps its last result, keyed on the integration state, the credential revision, a new connection-status counter (bumped in `connection.status`) and which of the integrations' declared env variables are currently set. The declared env names are collected once per integration state, so the env part costs one `process.env` read per declared name. It returns that same frozen array while the key is unchanged. `Interface["list"]` now returns `readonly Info[]` because plugins get the shared array through `PluginHost`; nothing else needed changing.
3. `Provider.snapshot` returns `cached.value` early when both `records` and the list array are unchanged, and stores `connections` on its cache entry.

`Model.snapshot` needs no change: its provider reads now hit the cache.

## Risk

Server only. Every in-process credential write goes through `Credential.Service`, and each write path bumps the revision. An env variable that appears or disappears at runtime changes the key too.

The one remaining gap: **credentials written by another OpenCode process sharing the database stay cached** until an in-process credential write or a restart. Dev re-read SQLite on every call. Bus events and provider plugins are already per-process, so such a write wasn't announced before either.

### Overlap

#56994 (base `beta`) and #57315 (base `dev`) also edit `Provider.snapshot` (`provider.ts` ~447–485) to skip publishing catalog events when a rebuild changes nothing. They conflict with this PR line by line but don't clash in behavior. When merging with either one, keep the early `cached.records === records && cached.connections === connections` return and store `connections` on `cached` in both return paths.

## Proof

A temporary bench (deleted before commit) used 234 integrations and providers, 4 credentials and 4 model reads per step, about what the profile shows:

| | list rebuilds per step | time per step |
|---|---|---|
| before | 4 | ~0.8 ms |
| after | 0 | ~0.06 ms |

The "after" row includes the env check, with 2 declared env names per integration (468 names, about 1,900 `process.env` reads per step). The profile saw about 8 rebuilds per step, so the real saving should be larger than this bench shows.

A new `catalog.test.ts` case checks that repeat list and snapshot reads return the same objects, and that a credential create, rename, activate and remove, plus a connection status change, each show up on the very next read. It fails on dev, and it fails again if the `activate` revision bump is removed.

- `bun test test/catalog.test.ts test/integration.test.ts test/credential.test.ts test/mcp-oauth.test.ts test/config/config.test.ts test/mcp.test.ts test/mcp-attach.test.ts test/provider.test.ts test/model.test.ts test/model-plugins.test.ts test/usage-limits.test.ts` (packages/core): all pass
- `bun test test/plugin/provider-snowflake-cortex.test.ts` (packages/core): passes. Its "environment PATs" case caught the env gap in the first version of this PR. The rest of `test/plugin/` passes too, except 6 `DigitalOceanPlugin` OAuth cases, which fail the same way locally on dev.
- `bun test test/provider.test.ts` (packages/server): passes
- `bun run typecheck` in core and server: clean. The pre-push hook's full `turbo typecheck` also passed.
- `oxlint` on the changed files: clean

prs.title: fix(core): skip execution claims held by another live process during restart recovery
prs.body: ### Issue for this PR Closes #51213 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? Startup recovery treats every execution claim as orphaned. That holds for a successor managed server, but not when an unregistered `opencode serve` (for example, one bundled by a desktop client) shares the database. The service then resumes that server's live sessions, and both servers run the same session. This PR records the owning process on claims (a new nullable `session_v2.claim_pid` column) and on recoverable background job records (an optional `pid` in the KV payload). The sweep skips claims and jobs whose process is still alive and isn't the current one. Claims with no pid, a dead pid, or this process's pid behave as before, so crash and restart recovery don't change. Re-claiming keeps the original claim time but moves the pid to the resuming process, so a later sweep won't treat a resumed session as orphaned. The liveness check is `process.kill(pid, 0)`. If that API isn't available, the claim is treated as dead, which is today's behavior. Subagent recovery is skipped when either the parent or the child is held by a live process, since that owner delivers the result. Claim owners are read again right before the final resume loop, so a session claimed while jobs recover isn't taken over. Known limits: the liveness check only sees processes on the same host, so servers in separate containers or hosts sharing one database aren't protected (and two containers where both servers are PID 1 look like the same owner). Pids ≤ 1 are treated as unknown and resumed as before. A reused PID can make a dead owner look alive, which leaves the session suspended until a later boot rather than taking it over. Background shells in an idle session aren't claim-backed, so they're covered only through their job record. ### How did you verify your code works? - 11 new tests in `packages/core/test/session-execution.test.ts`, covering claim stamping, live owner skipped, dead owner resumed, re-stamp on resume, job pid persisted, live-owner job left pending, a live-owned child claim kept, pid 1 treated as unknown, a mixed local/foreign sweep, and subagent jobs skipped when the child or parent is live-owned. They spawn real live and exited processes via `process.execPath`, not mocks. All 46 tests in that file pass. Deleting each guard (child-claim retention, the subagent skip, the pid validation) fails its test. - `bun typecheck` in `packages/core` and `packages/server`, `bun run migration --check`, and oxlint and prettier on the changed files. - Ran 14 related core test files against both this branch and `origin/v2`, one file at a time. Results match everywhere; two tests fail identically on both (`mcp` "exposes every connection operation", one in `session-checkpoint-transport`). - End-to-end with isolated XDG dirs: server A running two subagents, then server B started with `--service`. Before this change, A's next step failed with `Anthropic Messages system updates cannot split a local tool call from its tool result`. With it, B leaves the session alone and A finishes normally. As a control, killing A with `-9` and restarting B still resumes the session. ### Screenshots / recordings Not a UI change. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(tui): add paged transcript output experiment
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #51203 

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When I use AI tools, whether it's opencode or other, I get dizzy from trying to read the output. I'm reading one line, and as new text is being generated, the line I'm reading jolts up and gives me a small vertigo sensation. Throughout the workday, I get hundreds of these sensations, and I leave my computer feeling like I just ended a VR session, nauseous and exhausted.

The goal of this PR was to try a different flow inspired by e-readers. The idea is the page generates once initially, and then page-up and page-down flips back and forth pages rather than scrolling up a number of lines. When you skim something interesting, and you want to read it more in detail, you can use page-up to find the page, and all the text is in the same location as when the page was generated the first time. There is no jolt of text infinitely scrolling upwards, so hopefully no dizziness.

--
AI description:

This adds an experiment, `experimental.paged_output`, that pins the transcript to page boundaries instead: text fills the current page without moving, then the view advances one page when the page is full. Each page repeats a few lines from the previous page so you don't lose your place, and page up/down snap to the same boundaries the page was generated on, so revisiting a page looks the way it did while streaming. Scrolling away pauses follow and returning to the page bottom resumes it; the transcript and history are untouched.

Native sticky-follow can't do this by itself. It reacts to the content height on the frame it grows, before the bottom padding that creates the flip room is applied, so it moves one line and bounces back on every streamed line. The paging controller therefore owns the viewport from the frame loop against a dynamic bottom pad, and native sticky is disabled while paging.

Opt in with `{ "experimental": { "paged_output": true } }` or the Experiments dialog (Ctrl+P).

### How did you verify your code works?

I tested with `bun run dev` locally, and there is an included test file.

`packages/tui/test/component/paged-scroll.test.tsx` drives the real OpenTUI renderer and checks that per-frame scroll movement is only ever a full page step (the bounce above), that follow pauses on scroll-up and resumes at the page bottom, that enabling it mid-session does not yank a scrolled-away reader down, and that page navigation lands back on the exact generated page tops.

Ran `bun run lint`, `bun typecheck`, and `bun test` in `packages/tui`. There is also a storybook fixture (`OPENCODE_STORY=paged-output`) that streams output and shows live movement/jitter counters, overlap cycling, and page navigation.

prs.title: feat(core): remind a switched model which editing tools it lacks
prs.body:
## Summary

GPT models edit through `patch`; every other model gets `edit` and `write` instead. When a user switches models mid-session, the new model inherits a history full of calls to a tool it does not have and tends to call it anyway, wasting a step on `No tool named "patch" is currently available`.

This adds an internal plugin on the `session.context` hook. On each primary request it compares the tool calls in the outgoing history with the tools the request actually offers. When calls made by a *different* model name tools this request does not offer, it inserts one reminder before the user's prompt and persists it as a synthetic message:

> \<system-reminder\>
> You are continuing a conversation started by a different model. Some tools it used are not available to you. `patch` is no longer available and must not be called; use `edit` and `write` instead.
> \</system-reminder\>

Going the other way it reads "`edit` and `write` are no longer available and must not be called; use `patch` instead."

## How it decides

Everything comes from the request and the durable history; no separate switch event, no model-family rules.

- **Missing tools**: tool calls in the history whose names are not in `event.tools` for this request. Runs after the patch plugin so it sees the editing tools left for this model.
- **Different model**: only calls made by assistant turns whose `model` differs from the request's model count. A tool the *same* model used and then lost (config change) is not a model switch and gets nothing.
- **Once**: the persisted reminder records which tools it named in its metadata. If the most recent reminder already covers every missing tool, nothing is added. So GPT → MiniMax → DeepSeek produces one reminder about `patch`, not two; switching back to GPT afterwards produces one about `edit`/`write`.
- **Replacements**: the only fixed knowledge is that `patch` and `edit`/`write` stand in for each other. The "use … instead" clause names only replacements the request actually offers, and is omitted otherwise.

Nothing is said when the history never used a tool this request lacks, when only the variant changed, or when two models share the same tools.

## Benchmark

Seven small models (`glm-5.3-flash`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `space-bunny-free`, `gpt-5-nano`, `gpt-6-luna`) each took over a 22-turn history recorded by a model on the other side of the `patch`/`edit` split and were asked for one more small edit. 42 trials per arm.

| | Without this change | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| Stayed inside its tool set | 62% | 100% |
| Calls to a tool it did not have | 16 | 0 |
| Completed the edit | 98% | 95% |

Without the reminder, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` called `patch` in every trial and `glm-5.3-flash` in five of six. With it, no model called a missing tool. Session exports confirm the reminder is persisted once per session and not repeated on later steps.

## Testing

- `packages/core/test/plugin/model-switch.test.ts`: both directions, singular and plural phrasing, replacement clause omitted when not offered, the silent cases (same tools, read-only history, same model), and the no-repeat rule including the switch-back case.
- `bun test test/plugin/model-switch.test.ts test/plugin/plan.test.ts test/tool-patch.test.ts test/plugin/module.test.ts` in `packages/core`: all pass.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`: clean for the changed files.

Requested by: @rekram1-node (Aiden via Slack)

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #50604

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Completes slash commands anywhere in the prompt, the way `@` mentions already do, and fixes the submission bug that behaviour exposed.

The trigger already found a `/` token mid-prompt, but the command list was gated on `store.index === 0` and `insertSlash` cleared everything before the cursor. Mid-prompt the popup was therefore empty ("No matching commands") and its `Enter` binding swallowed submission (#50604).

Changes in `packages/tui`:

- `autocomplete.tsx`
  - Commands are listed mid-prompt. Action commands (no `arguments`) stay prompt-initial only, so a completion can never run a command from mid-sentence; text-expanding commands (custom/server commands, `/cd`, `/rename`, …) complete anywhere.
  - `insertSlash` splices the command at `store.index` instead of deleting from offset 0, preserving the text before the cursor.
  - Mid-prompt matching is a prefix on the command name/alias. Fuzzy matching would let arbitrary text match a command *description* (e.g. `'` matches the apostrophe in "session's") and reopen the popup over a normal sentence.
  - A mid-prompt command token that matches nothing closes the popup, so `Enter` submits instead of being swallowed.
- `display.ts`
  - A bare `/` mid-prompt no longer triggers: it is indistinguishable from a path separator (`find /`). The list still opens at the prompt start.

This mirrors the behaviour proposed for the v1 line in #47450; this PR targets `v2`.

- "This device" and the full link list (loopback included) are unchanged.

The JSON payload is denser and grows with each address. A QR row that wraps is unscannable, so the dialog now measures the rendered width:

- Wide layout (width >= 96): the code stays beside the links when it fits the space there (53 columns). Otherwise it moves below them.
- Narrow layout: when the code is wider than the dialog body, the dialog shows "Widen the terminal to show the QR code." in its place. Before, the rows wrapped into an unscannable block.

issues.title: httpIdleTimeoutMs is enforced as a total request deadline, not an idle timeout

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
# `httpIdleTimeoutMs` is enforced as a total request deadline, not an idle timeout

## Summary

The setting is documented as an HTTP **idle** timeout:

> `httpIdleTimeoutMs` — HTTP header and body idle timeout in milliseconds. Set to `0` to disable. Default `300000`.
> — `docs/settings.md`

But in the request path it is passed to `AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)`, which is a **total deadline measured from request start**, not an inactivity timeout. A request that keeps streaming tokens normally for more than 5 minutes is still aborted.

This makes pi hard to use with slow inference, especially:

- locally hosted models (llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio) on consumer hardware,
- very large contexts where prefill alone can take minutes,
- high thinking levels, where a single turn can legitimately run longer than 5 minutes.

## Environment

- pi: 1.4.0 (npm `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`)
- OS: Windows 10 x64 (Git Bash)
- Provider: OpenAI-compatible gateway
- Model: `deepseek-v4.1-flash`
- Thinking level: `max` (also observed with `high`)
- `httpIdleTimeoutMs`: not set (default `300000`)
- `retry.provider.timeoutMs`: not set (defaults to `httpIdleTimeoutMs`)
- `retry.maxRetries`: not set (default `3`)

## What happens

A long agent run aborts mid-task. The session records assistant messages with `stopReason: "error"` and an empty content array:

```
Request timed out.
Connection error.
terminated
500 Unknown Error
```

Across 17 session files, 34 assistant turns ended this way. All of them are transport-level failures; none were tool errors or logic errors. Retry attempts are visible and spaced by exponential backoff (roughly 10s, 13s, 15s, 19s), after which the run gives up.

The turns that survive are exactly the ones that finish inside the deadline. Turns that involve a long reasoning phase or a slow stream do not.

## Evidence

**1. The setting is documented as idle, not total**

`docs/settings.md`:

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `httpIdleTimeoutMs` | `300000` | HTTP header and body **idle** timeout in milliseconds. Set to `0` to disable. |
| `retry.provider.timeoutMs` | `httpIdleTimeoutMs` | Provider **request** timeout in milliseconds. |

**2. It is used as a total deadline**

`dist/core/sdk.js`:

```js
const buildRequestOptions = (options = {}) => {
    const providerRetrySettings = settingsManager.getProviderRetrySettings();
    const httpIdleTimeoutMs = settingsManager.getHttpIdleTimeoutMs();
    const effectiveTimeoutMs = httpIdleTimeoutMs === 0 ? 2147483647 : httpIdleTimeoutMs;
    return {
        ...options,
        timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs ?? providerRetrySettings.timeoutMs ?? effectiveTimeoutMs,
        ...
    };
};
```

The bundled provider request path then consumes it as a single absolute timer:

```js
let timeoutSignal = options?.timeoutMs !== undefined
    ? AbortSignal.timeout(options.timeoutMs)
    : undefined,
    signal = options?.signal && timeoutSignal
        ? AbortSignal.any([options.signal, timeoutSignal])
        : options?.signal ?? timeoutSignal;
```

`AbortSignal.timeout()` fires once after N ms regardless of how much data has arrived in the meantime. So this is a wall-clock cap on the whole request, not an inactivity detector.

**3. Related fixes in the changelog confirm the failure mode is real**

From `CHANGELOG.md`:

> Fixed Mistral streams being aborted mid-generation (e.g. during long thinking) after the request timeout; the timeout now applies only to waiting for response headers

> compaction and branch summaries use the model's output limit, so long reasoning no longer makes them fail

The Mistral fix addresses the same class of problem for one provider by narrowing the timer to headers only. The generic OpenAI-compatible path still uses a whole-request deadline.

## Reproduction

1. Use an OpenAI-compatible provider that streams slowly, or a local server on modest hardware.
2. Send a request whose full response takes longer than 5 minutes even though chunks keep arriving (e.g. a large-context task, or a reasoning model that streams `reasoning` deltas slowly).
3. The request is aborted at ~5 minutes with `Request timed out.`, despite a healthy stream.

A deterministic version: point pi at a mock OpenAI-compatible endpoint that streams one token every 5 seconds for 10 minutes. The stream is healthy, but pi aborts at 300s.

## Workaround

```json
{
  "httpIdleTimeoutMs": 0
}
```

`0` maps to `2147483647`, effectively disabling the deadline. A large finite value (e.g. `1800000`) also works, but then a genuinely stuck connection is not detected either.

## Suggested fix

1. **Make the timer match the name.** Reset it on every received chunk (true idle timeout). A stuck connection is then detected in 5 minutes, while a slow-but-healthy stream is allowed to finish.
2. **Or split the two concepts explicitly**, e.g. `httpIdleTimeoutMs` (between chunks) and `requestDeadlineMs` (absolute cap, default `0`/unset).
3. **Fix the docs regardless of which option is chosen.** Today the table says "idle" while the code enforces "total", which sends users debugging the wrong layer.
4. Optionally, relax the default for `llama.cpp` / local providers, where multi-minute turns are normal rather than exceptional.

## Why this matters beyond one setup

Local inference is a first-class use case for pi (`docs/llama-cpp.md`, the `/llama` router, and `docs/models.md` document local endpoints). On consumer GPUs, a long-context prefill plus generation can easily exceed 5 minutes while making steady progress. With the current implementation, the faster the machine, the more likely a long task succeeds — which is the opposite of what a deadline should do.

issues.title: Declared contextWindow above the served limit re-overflows after every recovery compaction

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Custom OpenAI-compatible provider (local vLLM) whose declared `contextWindow` is larger than the served limit. The model (gpt-oss-20b, served as `code-large`) is declared in models.json with `contextWindow: 1000000`; the engine runs with `--max-model-len 57344`.

Long sessions hit a hard server 400 at 57344 tokens:

```
400: {"message":"Input length (60061) exceeds model's maximum context length (57344).","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}
```

Overflow recovery does fire: pi compacts and the retry succeeds. But every later threshold check and the context-usage display keep trusting the declared 1000000, so nothing ever compacts proactively. The session grows back to the real limit and hits the same 400 again, roughly every 15 minutes of work. Server capture log from a real session: prompt tokens climb 51227, 53847, 55176, 56780 (all 200), next request 400.

Correcting the declaration to 57344 fixes the session (same workload then compacts at the threshold, zero errors), but the declaration is never validated anywhere, and for a remote/self-hosted server the real limit is only knowable from the server itself.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Serve a model with vLLM at a reduced `--max-model-len` (e.g. 57344 for gpt-oss-20b, whose native window is 131072).
2. Declare it as a custom provider in models.json with a larger `contextWindow` (e.g. 1000000) and no `maxTokens`.
3. Run a tool-heavy pi session past 57344 context tokens.
4. Observe the 400 above, one emergency overflow compaction, then the same 400 again after the context regrows past 57344.

### Expected behavior

Once a provider reports its limit in an overflow error, the session uses the smaller reported limit for threshold compaction and context usage until the model changes, instead of trusting the declaration again.

I have a fix with regression tests and would like to submit it: https://github.com/chris-heney/pi/tree/fix/learn-reported-context-window

- `packages/ai`: `getReportedContextWindow()` extracts the limit from known overflow formats (vLLM, LiteLLM, OpenRouter, xAI, Together, Google, Mistral, DS4, Anthropic). It captures the limit, never the requested length, which comes first in several formats.
- `packages/coding-agent`: `AgentSession` learns the reported limit on an overflow error and applies `min(declared, reported)` in `_checkCompaction`, `_exceedsCompactionThreshold`, and `getContextUsage()`; the learned value resets on model change.
- Tests: 15 new cases in `packages/ai/test/overflow.test.ts`, one regression test in `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/agent-session-compaction.test.ts`. `npm run check` passes; both test files pass. Happy to wait for approval per CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a PR.

### Version

1.4.0 (also present in current main)

AI-generated with human direction and review.

issues.title: Configurable MCP output limit (maxOutputBytes)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Make the fixed 20 KB (20 * 1024 bytes) limit on MCP result text sent to the model configurable,
in bytes. Because mcp.json sets server and global defaults rather than per-tool limits, the most
specific value set wins:
1. _meta["pi/maxOutputBytes"] on the tool in tools/list (set by the server)
2. maxOutputBytes on the server entry in mcp.json (also pi.registerMcpServer)
3. top-level maxOutputBytes in mcp.json (project overrides global)
4. 20 KB default
read_mcp_resource and resource listings for one server use 2-4; across all servers they use 3-4.

### Why?

Some tools return schemas, file trees, or search results over 20 KB. pi keeps the start and end,
saves the full text to a temp file, and the model spends extra reads to get the middle back.
There is no way to raise or lower the limit. Codex sets it per tool in config
(output_token_limit) and Claude Code lets servers declare it per tool
(_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]).

An extension's tool_result hook is a poor fit: ToolInfo does not expose a tool's tools/list
_meta, and rebuilding the text from structuredContent means duplicating pi's unexported MCP
content conversion (resource links, embedded resources, binary temp files) after pi has already
cut the text and written a temp file. Per-tool values in _meta and per-server values in mcp.json
(next to timeout) also avoid relying on one global limit.

### How? (optional)

Everything stays in extensions/mcp/ except adding maxOutputBytes to the shared server config
type and validator in core/mcp-servers.ts. The MCP extension resolves the limit and passes it to
limitMcpContent. Values must be positive integers: invalid mcp.json values are reported as
config errors, invalid _meta values are ignored. Codemode scripts still get the full result.

I'd like to implement this. Branch with docs and tests:
https://github.com/buYoung/pi/tree/feat/mcp-max-output-bytes

issues.title: Pasted ANSI leaves escape-sequence corpses in the prompt, and an unterminated bracketed paste wedges the editor (Ctrl+C dead)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## What

Pasting terminal output that contains ANSI escapes puts the escape bodies into the prompt as literal text, and an unterminated bracketed paste leaves the editor unable to accept any input — Ctrl+C included.

## Why

`pi-tui` 1.4.0, `components/editor.ts`:

`handlePaste()` filters pasted text per character:

```ts
let filteredText = cleanText
  .split("")
  .filter((char) => char === "\n" || char.charCodeAt(0) >= 32)
  .join("");
```

ESC (0x1b) is dropped and the rest of the sequence is kept, so `\x1b[38;2;111;63;32m` is inserted as the visible text `[38;2;111;63;32m`, and `\x1b[<35;153;17M` as `[<35;153;17M`. A pasted screenful of coloured/mouse-reporting output turns into thousands of characters of that. The comment a few lines above already documents this same class of leak for tmux csi-u re-encoding.

`handleInput()` then handles `isInPaste` before every keybinding and returns:

```ts
if (this.isInPaste) {
    this.pasteBuffer += data;
    const endIndex = this.pasteBuffer.indexOf("\x1b[201~");
    if (endIndex !== -1) { ... }
    return;
}
...
if (kb.matches(data, "tui.input.copy")) {   // Ctrl+C, unreachable while isInPaste
    return;
}
```

If `\x1b[201~` never arrives — another process on the same tty reads it first, the paste is cut short, or a split read loses it — every later keystroke, Ctrl+C included, is appended to `pasteBuffer` and dropped. The session cannot be typed into again; only a new paste (its own terminator closes the stale one) or killing the process recovers.

## Repro

1. Start `pi` in a pane whose tty is shared with another process that can read stdin — e.g. a `sudo`/`SUDO_ASKPASS` fallback doing `read -rs … < /dev/tty`, or a tool that hands the terminal to a child.
2. Paste terminal output containing ANSI (truecolor SGR, SGR mouse reports).
3. The escape bodies appear as literal text in the prompt. If the paste terminator was consumed by the other reader, the editor stops accepting input permanently and Ctrl+C does nothing.

Observed on macOS in a multiplexer pane (pi 1.4.0), where a password prompt owned the tty while the paste was in flight.

## Suggested fix

- Strip whole escape sequences (there is already a `stripTerminalSequences` helper) before the per-character filter, so a pasted ANSI stream degrades to plain text instead of escape corpses.
- Bound `isInPaste`: clear it on an idle timeout or on a lone ESC, so one missing terminator cannot wedge the editor.

issues.title: Extension-registered providers: fresh sessions intermittently ignore defaultProvider/defaultModel and start on another provider's default

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

A fresh pi session intermittently does **not** start with the configured
`defaultProvider`/`defaultModel` from settings.json when that provider is
registered by an extension via `pi.registerProvider(name, config)`. Instead, pi
silently falls back to another provider's default model
(`defaultModelPerProvider`) — in our case `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`,
which our Google credential (free tier, quota `limit: 0`) cannot serve, so the
first request fails with a 429.

Measured over repeated fresh launches: ~4 of 10 sessions start on the wrong
model; the rest start correctly on the configured default. Instrumenting
`findInitialModel` (step 3) shows the outcome correlates 1:1 with the
availability snapshot state at resolution time:

```text
step3 <default-provider>/<default-model> -> HIT auth=false  → session starts on the fallback
step3 <default-provider>/<default-model> -> HIT auth=true   → session starts on the configured default
```

Root cause: `createAgentSession` resolves the initial model
(`restoreModelFromSession` / `findInitialModel`) before name+config provider
registrations from extensions are applied to the model registry.

- `pi.registerProvider(name, config)` queues into
  `runtime.pendingProviderRegistrations` while extensions are loading
  (loader.js, "Pre-bind: queue registrations…"); the queue is flushed in
  `bindCore`, which runs when the `AgentSession` is constructed — after
  initial model resolution.
- `findInitialModel` step 3 (model-resolver.js) requires
  `getModel(provider, id)` **and** `hasConfiguredAuth(provider)`; the latter
  reads `snapshot.configuredProviders`, which is rebuilt asynchronously by
  `runAvailabilityRefresh` and can lag the registration.
- When step 3 misses, step 4 returns the first `defaultModelPerProvider`
  match from the available snapshot — silently, with no warning.

Note that `pi.registerNativeProvider(provider)` (object form) is flushed in
`createAgentSessionServices` _with_ an awaited
`modelRuntime.refresh({ allowNetwork: false })` before model resolution — the
name+config form has no equivalent before `findInitialModel`.

Possibly a residual of #6948 / #6922 (async provider model refresh vs startup
resolution, addressed for the built-in llama.cpp provider): model lists now
hydrate from the store at startup, but the configured/auth snapshot can still
lag, and the fallback is silent instead of an error. #2291 is an earlier
instance of the same ordering problem from a `session_start` hook.

Suggested direction: after extension loading completes, flush both pending
registration queues (`name+config` and native) and await
`modelRuntime.refresh({ allowNetwork: false })` before initial-model
resolution — mirroring what `createAgentSessionServices` already does after
extension load. Happy to send a PR if the direction looks right.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register a provider from an extension using the name+config form:

```ts
export default function (pi) {
  pi.registerProvider("acme", {
    name: "acme",
    baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1", // never called in this repro
    api: "openai-completions",
    models: [
      {
        id: "acme-model",
        name: "Acme Model",
        contextWindow: 128000,
        maxTokens: 8192,
      },
    ],
    auth: {
      apiKey: {
        name: "acme",
        check: async () => ({ type: "api_key" }),
        resolve: async () => ({ auth: { apiKey: "demo" }, source: "acme" }),
      },
    },
    fetchModels: async () => [],
  });
}
```

2. Add a stored credential for it in auth.json:

```json
"acme": { "type": "api_key", "key": "demo" }
```

3. settings.json:

```json
{ "defaultProvider": "acme", "defaultModel": "acme-model" }
```

4. Launch several fresh sessions back-to-back and inspect each session
   journal's first `model_change` entry:

```bash
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  d=/tmp/repro-$i; mkdir -p "$d"; (cd "$d" && pi -p "hi" >/dev/null 2>&1)
done
# first model_change per journal: acme-model @ acme on good launches,
# gemini-3.1-pro-preview @ google on fallback launches
```

Measured: 4 of 10 fresh sessions started on the fallback provider; 10 of 10
with the refresh applied before resolution started on the configured default.

### Expected behavior

Every fresh session starts with `defaultProvider`/`defaultModel` from
settings.json — regardless of how long extension loading takes. If the
configured provider cannot be resolved yet, pi should say so explicitly
instead of silently starting on an unrelated provider's default model.

### Version

0.84.4

issues.title: pi --list-models ignores enabledModels / --models scope

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

`pi --list-models` dumps the **entire** available catalogue (`modelRuntime.getAvailable()`), then optionally fuzzy-filters by a search string. It does **not** apply the same scope used everywhere else:

- `settings.enabledModels` (saved via `/scoped-models` / Ctrl+S scope)
- CLI `--models <patterns>`

So a machine with a tight `enabledModels` list (e.g. a handful of `opencode-go/*` + Anthropic models) still prints hundreds of OpenRouter/HuggingFace rows. That makes `--list-models` slow and noisy, and it breaks integrators that treat the command as “models the user can actually pick” (e.g. Poracode’s Pi capabilities probe runs `pi --list-models` with a ~15s timeout and often gets an incomplete or empty set).

Measured locally (Pi 1.4.0): full `--list-models` ≈ 650 lines / ~1 minute; scoped defaults are ~30 `enabledModels` entries with `defaultProvider: opencode-go`, `defaultModel: deepseek-v4.1-flash`.

## Expected

`--list-models` should list the **scoped** set when a scope exists:

1. `--models` patterns if passed on the CLI
2. else `settings.enabledModels` if non-empty
3. else the full available catalogue (today’s behaviour)

Optional search pattern should filter **within** that set.

## Suggested fix

Reuse the same resolution path `main.ts` already uses for sessions:

```ts
const modelPatterns = parsed.models ?? settingsManager.getEnabledModels();
const scopedModels =
  modelPatterns && modelPatterns.length > 0
    ? await resolveModelScope(modelPatterns, modelRuntime, { signal })
    : [];
```

Then in the `--list-models` branch, either:

**A (preferred).** Pass the scoped models into `listModels` when non-empty; fall back to `getAvailable()` when there is no scope:

```ts
// packages/coding-agent/src/cli/list-models.ts
export async function listModels(
  modelRuntime: ModelRuntime,
  searchPattern?: string,
  signal?: AbortSignal,
  scopedModels?: Model<Api>[],
): Promise<void> {
  const models = scopedModels?.length
    ? [...scopedModels]
    : [...(await modelRuntime.getAvailable(undefined, { signal }))];
  // existing fuzzy filter + table print
}
```

```ts
// packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts — listModels branch
const modelPatterns = parsed.models ?? settingsManager.getEnabledModels();
const scoped =
  modelPatterns?.length
    ? (await resolveModelScope(modelPatterns, modelRuntime, {
        signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15_000),
      })).models // or whatever resolveModelScope returns
    : undefined;
await listModels(modelRuntime, searchPattern, AbortSignal.timeout(15_000), scoped);
```

**B.** Add an explicit escape hatch for the full dump, e.g. `--list-models --all` / `--list-all-models`, so packaging/debug still works.

Also update `packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md` so `--list-models` documents that it respects `--models` / `enabledModels`.

## Tests

- `enabledModels: [opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash]` → `--list-models` prints only that row (plus header)
- `--models anthropic/* --list-models` scopes without reading settings
- no `enabledModels` and no `--models` → full catalogue (compat)
- search pattern still filters inside the scoped set
- empty scope match → clear message (not silent full dump)

## Refs

- `packages/coding-agent/src/cli/list-models.ts` — currently only `getAvailable()` + fuzzy search
- `packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts` — session path already does `parsed.models ?? settingsManager.getEnabledModels()` + `resolveModelScope`; list-models branch skips it
- Settings: `enabledModels` is documented as patterns for startup selection and cycling (same format as `--models`)

issues.title: stripAnsi leaves private-parameter CSI payloads in tool output (ESC[<...M mouse reports, ESC[>...c replies)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

`stripAnsi` in `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/ansi.ts` treats `<`, `=` and `>` as a valid CSI final byte, so for these sequences it strips only the first three bytes and leaves the parameters as text:

| input | returns |
| --- | --- |
| `ESC [ < 35 ; 59 ; 1 M` (SGR mouse report) | `35;59;1M` |
| `ESC [ > 0 ; 276 ; 0 c` (device attributes reply) | `0;276;0c` |
| `ESC [ 3 8 ; 5 ; 1 9 6 m` (control) | `` |

A private parameter byte should only belong to the sequence when digits or `;`/`:` follow it.

### Why?

The transcript renders tool output through `getTextOutput()`, which is `sanitizeBinaryOutput(stripAnsi(text))` (`src/core/tools/render-utils.ts:67`). `sanitizeBinaryOutput` then drops the leftover ESC, because `0x1B` is inside `[\x0E-\x1F]`, so the parameters get drawn as ordinary characters. On 1.4.0, `node -e "process.stdout.write('\u001b[<35;59;1Mstep 1\n')"` through the bash tool shows `35;59;1Mstep 1`.

The sanitizer also contradicts the input side of this repo: `packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts:113` already parses this shape as one sequence (`/^<\d+;\d+;\d+[Mm]$/`). 8bf2bfab aligned `stripAnsi` with chalk `strip-ansi`, so the current behavior is deliberate. I think correctness wins for this one shape, since the two halves of pi disagree about it.

### How?

Insert `"[<=>]?(?:\\d{1,4}(?:[;:]\\d{0,4})*)?"` before the final byte, leave `CSI_FINAL` alone. Patch and two regression tests are ready: 0 of 237 existing cases change, and in a 720-case sweep only the 432 private-parameter shapes change. I can send a PR after `lgtm`.

issues.title: Extensions that `sendMessage` at `session_start` turn every session into a legacy transcript

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
## Problem
`getInitialSystemMessage` reads `messages[0]`. Extensions that `sendMessage` during `session_start` (pi-memory, pi-session-search) put a custom/user message ahead of pi's system message, so every session is treated as a "legacy" transcript:

- Anthropic requests lose the `system` field and native inline tool changes (`tool_addition`), so loading a deferred tool via `tool_search` changes the tools block and rewrites the whole prompt cache (e.g. cacheRead 0 / cacheWrite 18,589 on the first call after a load, vs. cacheRead 18,330 / cacheWrite 246 once fixed).
- Codex runs under "You are a helpful assistant." instead of pi's prompt.

Also: a `before_agent_start` handler returning `systemPrompt` collapses all system messages into one head and disables native tool changes (tools grow in place, no `tool_addition`).

## Repro
`pi -p` with pi-session-search (or pi-memory) installed and any `deferred` tool; ask the agent to `tool_search` for it and call it. Compare usage on the turn after the load with and without the extension.

## Suggested fix
Persist the initial system message before dispatching `session_start`, or let providers find the first system message past leading custom/user messages.

## Workaround
We hoist the system message to the head from a `context_with_system` hook (QuinRiva/loom#412).

issues.title: TUI pins a full core while streaming: uncached Intl.Segmenter + per-chunk Markdown rebuild

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
## What happened?

Long sessions: the TUI uses ~100% of one core while the model streams. Reproduces with `pi -ne`, so it's core, not an extension.

spindump hot path: render timer → `Markdown.render` → wrap → `Intl.Segmenter` (ICU BreakIterator). Two causes:

1. Grapheme segmentation is uncached in the wrap/truncate path — non-ASCII lines (RU/emoji/box-drawing) re-segment every frame.
2. `AssistantMessageComponent.updateContent()` does `clear()` + `new Markdown(...)` on every `message_update`, so pi-tui's own `cachedLines` never hits while streaming. The whole message-so-far is re-lexed/wrapped/segmented up to 60fps; cost grows with answer length.

Measured (M3, Node 22.23, pi 0.80.7): **~105% of a core per streaming session.**

Related (auto-closed, still present): #4721 (segmenter), #3758 (streaming rebuild).

I made a plugin `pi-render-cache` that caches both → ~105% → ~10–16%, byte-identical (64 tests + fuzz). Happy to help with a core fix.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Stream a long markdown answer with non-ASCII (RU/emoji), or resume a large session.
2. Run with `pi -ne` to rule out extensions.
3. Watch CPU during the stream — one core pinned, scales with answer length.

## Expected behavior

Streaming re-render is O(new tail), not O(whole message); segmentation cached.

## Version

0.80.7

issues.title: Compaction composability: model-callable compact with span args, summary-model override, entry refs, model-facing unfold

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Context

We run multi-day pi sessions (infra ops, 100k+ token contexts) with an extension that implements **block-level folding** on top of the compaction seams (cancel auto-compaction, propose extension-provided entries). It works, but compaction is currently *take-over-only*: an extension can cancel it and rebuild everything itself, but cannot compose with it. The result is ~10k lines of re-implemented machinery (span extraction, summary generation, refs, restore, search) that would mostly disappear if compaction exposed a few composable primitives.

Concrete evidence from one long session: context reduced 6.3M → 40K tokens across 40 independent blocks, every block recoverable on demand. Whole-session span replacement cannot express this without either folding live context or losing recovery.

## Gaps

1. **No model-callable compact entry point.** `/compact` is user-only; auto-compaction picks the span mechanically (keepRecent boundary). The model — which knows which context is dead vs load-bearing — cannot express "fold this span, keep that part active". Proposal: `CompactOptions` gains an optional span/entry-range, and/or a built-in tool wrapping `ctx.compact()` so models can fold precisely around live work.

2. **Summary model is not configurable.** `settings.compaction.*` exposes token knobs only; the summarization request always uses the session model. (#7553 tracks model/thinking configurability; #9773 notes compaction requests also bypass `before_provider_request`.) Proposal: `compaction.model: provider/id` config, or a hook that lets an extension supply the summary text.

3. **Entries carry no stable message refs.** A `CompactionEntry` is an opaque span. Without refs the model cannot (a) request folding of a specific range, (b) refer to already-folded content, or (c) ask for a restore. Proposal: stable per-entry (or per-message) refs surfaced in the model-facing projection.

4. **No model-facing unfold.** Raw entries remain stored (good), but the model has no way to request omitted content back into context. One-way compaction makes models conservative about folding anything that might matter later. Proposal: a native, model-callable unfold (scoped or full) that restores omitted entries.

5. **No summary-quality seam.** There is no extension hook between "summary text generated" and "entry committed" for validation (structure/leak checks). (#9647 asks for lifecycle events; a validation hook is the same seam taken one step further.)

## Non-goals / compatibility

- All opt-in; default auto-compaction behavior unchanged.
- Entries remain plain persisted data; refs are additive metadata.

Happy to contribute PRs for 1 and 2 — both look small (`CompactOptions.span` + a config read in the summarization call).

issues.title: openai-codex Connection Reliability Issues

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
## Summary

`openai-codex` / `gpt-5.5` sometimes leaves the interactive TUI stuck on `Working...` with no streamed text, no tool call, and no visible error. The only way to recover is pressing Escape, which records an aborted assistant turn.

This has happened repeatedly over the last couple of days in normal interactive use.

## Environment

- pi: `0.75.5`
- Node: `v22.22.1`
- Provider/model: `openai-codex` / `gpt-5.5`
- Thinking level: `xhigh`
- No explicit `transport` setting in user settings
- Default tools/extensions enabled

## Observed behavior

When the issue occurs:

- TUI keeps showing `Working...` for minutes.
- No assistant text is streamed.
- No tool call is emitted.
- Pressing Escape aborts the turn.
- The saved session entry for that assistant turn has:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "stopReason": "aborted",
  "content": [],
  "usage": {
    "input": 0,
    "output": 0,
    "cacheRead": 0,
    "cacheWrite": 0,
    "totalTokens": 0
  }
}
```

I saw this pattern multiple times, including cases where the previous turn had completed normally and the next user message then hung before any provider usage was recorded.

This looks different from a long reasoning turn: there is no usage, no partial reasoning/text, and no tool call.

## Expected behavior

If the provider/transport stalls before the first event, pi should eventually surface a timeout/transport error or retry in a bounded way, instead of keeping the TUI in `Working...` indefinitely until the user manually aborts.

## Suspected area

From the installed `0.75.5` package:

- `SettingsManager.getTransport()` returns `"auto"` when no setting is present.
- The docs/settings table says the default is `"sse"`, so there may also be a docs/runtime default mismatch.
- For `openai-codex-responses`, `transport=auto` attempts WebSocket first.
- `retry.provider.timeoutMs` appears to be passed into `streamSimple()`, but the `openai-codex-responses` implementation does not seem to apply it to the Codex fetch/WebSocket wait path in the same way as SDK-based providers.
- The WebSocket event loop can wait for the first message/completion without an obvious idle timer.

So the likely failure mode is: Codex WebSocket/transport waits before the first event; no assistant event is produced; interactive UI keeps showing `Working...`; Escape finally records an aborted zero-usage turn.

## Suggested fix / mitigation

Possible fixes:

1. Add a hard idle timeout for `openai-codex-responses` WebSocket and SSE stream waits, especially before the first event.
2. Ensure `retry.provider.timeoutMs` or `httpIdleTimeoutMs` applies consistently to this provider path.
3. If `auto` is intended as the runtime default, update docs; if `sse` is intended, adjust `SettingsManager.getTransport()`.
4. Optionally show a clearer status/error when a provider turn has produced zero events for a long time.

Local workaround I am considering, but have not applied yet:

```json
{
  "transport": "sse",
  "httpIdleTimeoutMs": 120000
}
```

I can provide more sanitized session metadata if helpful, but I avoided attaching raw session logs because they contain private conversation/tool context.

issues.title: kimi-coding (api.kimi.com/coding) misdetected: developer role sent to Anthropic-compatible endpoint that rejects it

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Symptom

Model calls against `kimi-coding` provider (`https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/messages`, anthropic-messages API) fail with:

```
400: {"message":"role 'developer' is not allowed","type":"invalid_request_error"}
```

## Root cause

In `openai-completions` chunk, `isMoonshot` detection only matches `provider === "moonshotai"` / `"moonshotai-cn"` / `baseUrl.includes("api.moonshot")`. The Kimi Coding platform domain is **`api.kimi.com/coding`** — it is not matched, so `supportsDeveloperRole` evaluates to `true` (since not isNonStandard) and Pi sends the system prompt as a `developer` message, which this endpoint rejects.

Manual probe confirms the endpoint behavior:
- `{"role":"system","content":...}` → 200 OK
- `{"role":"developer","content":...}` → 400 `role 'developer' is not allowed`

## Fix suggestion

Add `baseUrl.includes("api.kimi.com")` (or provider === "kimi-coding") to the moonshot/kimi detection branch so `supportsDeveloperRole` defaults to false for these endpoints.

## Workaround

Setting `compat.supportsDeveloperRole: false` in `models.json` for the model/provider fixes it.

Reproduced on pi-coding-agent 1.4.0.

issues.title: find returns no results for path patterns like src/**/*.ts on Windows

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

On Windows the find tool answers "No files found matching pattern" for any
pattern that contains a path separator, like `src/**/*.spec.ts`. Plain
filename patterns like `*.spec.ts` work fine.

The cause is in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/find.ts`. When the
pattern has a slash, find runs fd with `--full-path`. fd builds the glob with
forward slashes but matches it against the native absolute path, which uses
backslashes on Windows, so nothing ever matches. Known fd problem:
sharkdp/fd#1227. Running the bundled fd by hand shows it:

    fd --glob --hidden --no-require-git --full-path -- "**/src/**/*.spec.ts" C:\some\fixture

No output, exit 0. The same layout matches fine on Linux.

Because of this the regression test for #3302
(`test/suite/regressions/3302-find-path-glob.test.ts`) fails on a Windows
checkout, 3 of its 4 tests. CI only runs on Linux so it never shows up there.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows checkout, `npm install --ignore-scripts`, `npm run build`
2. `cd packages/coding-agent`
3. `node node_modules/.bin/vitest --run test/suite/regressions/3302-find-path-glob.test.ts`
4. 3 of 4 tests fail with `expected [] to deeply equal [...]`

Or in `pi -ne`: any find call with a `/` in the pattern comes back empty.

### Expected behavior

Path patterns match the same files as on Linux and macOS.

I want to fix this myself. Idea: keep fd for listing files so the gitignore
behavior from #5960 stays as is, and on win32 match path patterns in pi with
minimatch (already a dependency) against posix style paths. fd still
pre-filters on the last pattern segment so it stays fast. Patterns written
with backslashes work too. Fix plus regression tests:
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/compare/main...Hotragn:pi:fix/find-windows-path-globs
The #3302 test goes green on Windows, no change on other platforms,
`npm run check` passes.

### Version

0.80.10 (main, 3da591ab), fd 10.4.2, Node 24.14.0, Windows 11

### What do you want to change?

Keep the caller's `context.messages` array isolated in `agentLoopContinue` / `runAgentLoopContinue`, matching `agentLoop` / `runAgentLoop`. If mutation is intentional, clarify this difference in the low-level API documentation instead.

issues.title: pi.exec() crashes the whole process with RangeError: Invalid string length when a child's output exceeds the V8 string limit

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### Summary

`pi.exec()` (the execution helper behind extension `pi.exec`) accumulates a child's stdout/stderr into unbounded strings. A subprocess that emits more output than V8's maximum string length (~536M chars) makes the string concatenation throw `RangeError: Invalid string length` **inside the `Socket` `data` callback**, which escapes as `uncaughtException` and kills the whole Pi process — every session in it, not just the tool call.

We hit this in real usage on Pi 1.4.0 (the process exited with):

```
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
RangeError: Invalid string length
    at Socket.<anonymous> (.../dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-KHTE6L5W.js:706:2453)
    at Socket.emit (node:events:531:35)
    at addChunk (node:internal/streams/readable:561:12)
    at readableAddChunkPushByteMode (node:internal/streams/readable:512:3)
    at Readable.push (node:internal/streams/readable:392:5)
    at Pipe.onStreamRead (node:internal/stream_base_commons:189:23)
```

`chunk-KHTE6L5W.js:706:2453` maps to the stdout data handler in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/exec.ts`.

### Root cause

`execCommand()` has no output bound; it keeps concatenating whatever the child emits:

https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/1e42501bb8043cd0dd533f57af0d1ec4e05ba2ac/packages/coding-agent/src/core/exec.ts

```ts
stdout += stdoutDecoder.write(data);   // no cap on the accumulated string
...
stderr += stderrDecoder.write(data);
```

Present since the unified-extensions exec helper was introduced; identical in v1.3.0 and v1.4.0. #11326 fixed the *decoding* of each chunk (multi-byte characters split across pipe chunks) but not the *accumulation* — the decoded string still grows without bound, so the crash above is still reachable on current `main` (`1e42501bb`).

### Repro

Any extension calling:

```ts
await pi.exec(process.execPath, ["-e", 'process.stdout.write("a".repeat(600 * 1024 * 1024))'], cwd);
```

The child only wrote ~600 MB — well within any reasonable tool-run — but the host process dies with `RangeError: Invalid string length` instead of the tool call failing. Because the throw happens inside a stream callback, it is not catchable by the caller; the extension cannot handle it, and anything else running in the same process goes down with it. The offending child is left running.

### Suggested semantics

A tool execution helper should fail like a tool call, not take the host down:

- bound the **combined** stdout+stderr bytes (we use 16 MiB downstream);
- once the cap is hit: stop draining the streams, terminate the child (SIGTERM, then escalate based on actual child exit), and return a normal result — nonzero exit with an explicit `output exceeded ... bytes; output is incomplete` indication — never a silent truncation that reads as success;
- (optionally, opt-in) record metadata-only diagnostics — counts and termination state, never output or arguments — so the original producer of oversized output can be identified after the fact.

This is the same crash class as #8028 (TUI `fullRender` clamped for the same reason), just on the exec path. We have been running the bound described above downstream since 2026-10-24 (with regression tests for: 17 MiB producer → capped 16 MiB + nonzero + explicit marker + following command still works; normal-sized output unaffected). Happy to send a PR if the approach sounds right.

issues.title: Allow `watchEvents` in pi-durable resume from the last seen entry
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Provide the ability for `watchEvents` to resume from a previously seen point by passing an entry id as a "last seen" argument .

When provided the returned `snapshot.entries` holds only the active entries with a higher ID, and includes `snapshot.after` to confirm this is a resumed stream. The rest of the snapshot (including partial message, tools, inbox, agent, usage) are still sent in full.

The client drops its entries before the marker's `head`. If the "last seen" is an unknown value the snapshot is returned in full without the `after` key.

### Why?

If a client disconnects or goes offline, on reconnection it would be ideal to only have to stream the events that happened since the reconnection rather than retransmitting the full stream.

This can be implemented in user land by discarding the earlier events but ideally it'd be built in.

### How? (optional)

Something like:

```ts
const stream = await watchEvents(harness, id, context, { after: lastSeenId });
```

Entries are already stored with increasing IDs. So ideally we'd check the `after` value then filter `snapshotOf(view).entries`.

An example of an expected stream including compaction.

 Fresh stream `watchEvents(harness, id, ctx)`

 ```jsonc
   {
     "type": "snapshot",
     "entries": [
       { "id": 214, "kind": "pi.compaction", "head": 180, "data": { "summary": "…" } },
       { "id": 180, "kind": "pi.user", "model": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Fix the flaky login test" }] },
       { "id": 181, "kind": "pi.assistant", "model": [{ "role": "assistant", "content": [ … ] }] },
       // … 30 more entries, 182–211 …
       { "id": 212, "kind": "pi.assistant", "model": [{ "role": "assistant", "content": [{ "type": "toolCall", "name": "bash", … }] }] },
       { "id": 213, "kind": "pi.tool-result", "model": [{ "role": "toolResult", "toolCallId": "call_9", … }] }
     ],
     "run": { "inputs": [41] },
     "generation": { "attempt": 1, "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "The test fails because" }] } },
     "tools": [], "nestedTools": [], "compactions": [], "inbox": [],
     "agent": { … }, "usage": { … }
   }
 ```

Resumed stream `watchEvents(harness, id, ctx, { after: 212 })`

 ```jsonc
   {
     "type": "snapshot",
     "after": 212,
     "entries": [
       { "id": 214, "kind": "pi.compaction", "head": 180, "data": { "summary": "…" } },
       { "id": 213, "kind": "pi.tool-result", "model": [{ "role": "toolResult", "toolCallId": "call_9", … }] }
     ],
     "run": { "inputs": [41] },
     "generation": { "attempt": 1, "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "The test fails because" }] } },
     "tools": [], "nestedTools": [], "compactions": [], "inbox": [],
     "agent": { … }, "usage": { … }
   }
 ```

 After the snapshot, both streams are the same:

 ```jsonc
   [{ "type": "message_update", "usage": { … }, "changes": [{ "type": "text_delta", "contentIndex": 0, "delta": " the session cookie" }] }]
   [{ "type": "message_update", "usage": { … }, "changes": [{ "type": "text_delta", "contentIndex": 0, "delta": " expires mid-test." }] }]
   [{ "type": "message_end", "entry": { "id": 215, "kind": "pi.assistant", … } },
    { "type": "turn_end" }, { "type": "run_end", "inputs": [41] }, …]
 ```

issues.title: pi-durable: infinite loop when generation response errors

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
### What happened?

If the host restarts while a response is still streaming, the reopened `pi.generation` task runs `request` again. `convertPartial` saves the partial as an `aborted` entry and sends the same request again. If the generation is flawed (in my case a DurableObject OOM), then this repeats indefinitely.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use Node SQLite storage and a provider that streams slowly.
2. Kill the process each time a partial has been committed, then reopen and call `resume()`.
3. Each reopen adds an `aborted` entry and re-sends the request. Nothing stops it or reports it.

### Expected behavior

Ideally there would be a configurable limit to repeated failures to avoid runaway crash-loops.

### Version

@earendil-works/pi-durable 1.0.3 (same behavior in 1.3.0)

issues.title: Credential-shaped strings are stored verbatim in the session file

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

A stock way to keep credential-shaped strings out of the session file, either:

1. a `redactSecrets` setting in the session options, on the same shape as the Beacon runtime's `redact_secrets: true`, that rewrites a credential-shaped string to a marker carrying the shape id before the message is appended, or
2. a documented, supported way to do it from an extension.

### Why?

The session file is the durable store for everything a tool printed. A tool result that echoes a credential-shaped string is written verbatim, and the file lives under the user's home, is copied into backups, and is searched by other tools. Redaction has to happen before the append, because a row already in the store stays there.

### What already works, measured

An extension on the stock extension point already does this. It registers two handlers, `tool_result` and `message_end`, and rewrites token-shaped strings out of both before returning. A live canary on 2026-10-23 put one fake string per shape through a tool result and scanned the resulting session file: 0 shapes stored, 6 `[REDACTED:<shape-id>]` markers instead. The same run with the extension off, as the negative control, stored all 6 shapes. 42 tests cover it.

That works, so this is a request for the same behaviour in core, or for the extension hook to be named as the supported path in the docs, so a reader does not have to find out that `message_end` fires before `appendMessage` by reading the source.

### What an extension cannot do

- It cannot cover the built-in tools it does not wrap. Only `tool_result` and `message_end` are visible, so a string that reaches the file by another route is not redacted.
- It cannot redact a session file that already exists.
- It runs only when the user loads it, so it is off by default for everyone who has not installed it.

### Environment

Pi 1.4.0, Linux, `--print` with `--session-dir` and `-e`.

prs.title: fix(ai): route Bedrock models Converse does not serve through Bedrock Mantle
prs.body:
Stacked on #11371. Addresses #5363 for Bedrock API keys.

pi lists 16 Bedrock models that Bedrock only serves on Mantle, its OpenAI-compatible endpoint: OpenAI GPT-5.4 through GPT-6.1, gpt-oss, Grok 4.3/4.6, and Gemma 4. pi sends them to Converse, which rejects them as invalid model identifiers. models.dev v2 lists each model's APIs, so the catalog now maps models without a Converse API to the Responses API at the Mantle URL models.dev gives, with `{region}` filled in per request.

`src/api/bedrock-mantle.ts` wraps the OpenAI Responses implementation:
- **Region**: `AWS_REGION`, then `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, then `us-east-1`, as for Converse.
- **Auth**: a Bedrock API key, from a stored bearer token or `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`.

## Not supported yet: IAM and profile credentials

Mantle requests are not signed with SigV4, and no short-term bearer token is minted from the credential chain. Profile or IAM users get a clear error for these models instead of Converse's invalid-model error. #8572 explores SigV4 with additional dependencies; that could follow separately.

## Catalog compatibility

Released 1.4.0 clients only implement Converse for `amazon-bedrock`. The 1.4.1 `MINIMUM_PI_VERSION` bump from the Vertex PR covers this; its comment now lists both reasons.

## Testing

- Catalog routing for the 16 Mantle-only models.
- A request through the real OpenAI SDK, asserting the regional Mantle URL and bearer header.
- The error when no key is set.
- Existing Bedrock tests still pass.

Not verified against a live Mantle endpoint.

No changelog entry because this PR targets a branch other than `main`.

prs.title: feat(ai): serve Claude models on Google Vertex AI
prs.body:
Stacked on #11370. `google-vertex` now lists the 13 non-deprecated Claude models that models.dev catalogs on Vertex's Anthropic Messages API (for example `claude-opus-4-8@default`).

## How it works

`src/api/google-vertex-anthropic.ts` reuses the Anthropic Messages implementation with a `fetch` wrapper:
- `/v1/messages` becomes `…/publishers/anthropic/models/{model}:streamRawPredict` (or `rawPredict`); token counting becomes `count-tokens:rawPredict`.
- The model moves from the body into the URL, and the body gets `anthropic_version: "vertex-2023-10-16"`.
- Authentication uses an Application Default Credentials or service-account access token instead of an Anthropic key.

The provider dispatches `anthropic-messages` models to this wrapper and Gemini to the existing Vertex API. Claude family rules (adaptive thinking, effort levels, temperature) apply as on other hosts.

## Dependencies

`google-auth-library@10.6.2` becomes a direct dependency. It is already in the tree through `@google/genai`, so the lockfile and install lock each gain one line. A `browser` field maps it to an empty module so browser bundles still build. Claude on Vertex needs ADC, which a browser can't provide anyway.

## Catalog compatibility

Released 1.4.0 clients only implement Google's Vertex API for `google-vertex`. This PR bumps `MINIMUM_PI_VERSION` to 1.4.1, so they keep the last compatible catalog.

## Testing

- **Unit tests**: cover the URL, body and header rewrite. One test drives the real Anthropic SDK through the wrapper and asserts the request it sends.
- **E2E**: a block gated on `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`.

Not verified against a live Vertex project. The `@default` model ids are models.dev's; opencode uses the same ids through the AI SDK.

No changelog entry because this PR targets a branch other than `main`.

- **Separate key variables**: the pay-as-you-go providers bill the account balance. They read their own variables, so a key set for `zai` or a Token Plan never makes metered models selectable.

## Naming decisions

The provider ids and variable names are mine:
- `zai` is already the Coding Plan, so the pay-as-you-go APIs became `zai-api` and `zai-api-cn`.
- `ZAI_PAYG_*` avoids reusing `ZAI_API_KEY`.

## Testing

- Catalog tests for endpoints, compat, effort gating, and own-price handling.
- Default-model checks.
- E2E blocks in the usual matrix, skipped without keys.

Not verified against the live APIs: no keys were available.

No changelog entry because this PR targets a branch other than `main`; add one when retargeting.

prs.body:
fix(coding-agent): normalise compaction usage to prevent footer crash on resume

AI-assisted content (per CONTRIBUTING.md): drafted by my local agent, reviewed and posted by me.

The compaction writer persisted `summaryUsage` straight from the provider
response on both passthrough branches (compaction.ts:1055/:1075) without
normalising — a provider that doesn't report cost (Ollama 0.34.0, local
OpenAI-compatible endpoints) produced a `{input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}`
entry with no `totalTokens` and no `cost` object. `addUsageToTotals` then read
`usage.cost.total` unguarded (usage-totals.ts:27) and the footer's
`FooterComponent.render` crashed with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of
undefined (reading 'total')` on every resume of the affected session (repro in
the issue).

Two layers:
1. Both passthrough branches now route through a `toCanonicalUsage` helper that
   fills in `totalTokens` (component sum) and the `cost` object (zeros) when the
   provider omits them, so newly persisted entries are always canonical.
2. `addUsageToTotals` tolerates a missing `cost` (`usage.cost?.total ?? 0`) as a
   belt-and-braces guard for malformed historical entries.

Tests: packages/coding-agent test/usage-totals.test.ts — new cases feed the
issue's raw provider shape through both layers and assert `totalTokens` and
`cost` are filled (fails with a TypeError before this change); related suite
55/55 green.

Closes #10092

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): exit with a clear error for unusable proxy URLs
prs.body:
## Summary

- An `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` value that undici cannot use, such as `socks5h://...`, a URL without a scheme, or a URL with a path, crashed startup with undici's `Invalid URL protocol` error and a Node stack. The same happened for the `httpProxy` setting.
- `configureHttpDispatcher()` now catches the error from `EnvHttpProxyAgent` and throws `Invalid proxy URL in HTTPS_PROXY. Use an http://, https://, or socks5:// URL without a path.` The CLI and RPC entry points, plus the startup path that applies the `httpProxy` setting, print it as one `Error:` line and exit 1.
- The message names the variable undici reads (a defined lowercase variable wins), or `the httpProxy setting` when that setting supplied the value. It omits the URL and undici's message. The original error can carry the URL with credentials, because `ERR_INVALID_URL` keeps it in `input`.
- undici still decides which URLs it accepts; pi does not validate proxy URLs itself, so anything undici accepts keeps working. `socks5://` already works through undici 8.10 and sends hostnames to the proxy, which covers what `socks5h://` is used for. I did not map `socks5h` to `socks5` or fall back to a direct connection, because either would silently change what the user configured.

Fixes #11195

## Validation

Before, on main:

```
$ HTTPS_PROXY=socks5h://127.0.0.1:8081 pi --version
node_modules/undici/lib/core/util.js:229
    throw new InvalidArgumentError('Invalid URL protocol: the URL must start with `http:` or `https:`.')
          ^

InvalidArgumentError: Invalid URL protocol: the URL must start with `http:` or `https:`.
    at parseURL (node_modules/undici/lib/core/util.js:229:11)
    ...
    at new EnvHttpProxyAgent (node_modules/undici/lib/dispatcher/env-http-proxy-agent.js:35:32)
    at configureHttpDispatcher (packages/coding-agent/src/core/http-dispatcher.ts:87:3)
    ...
  code: 'UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG'
```

After:

```
$ HTTPS_PROXY=socks5h://127.0.0.1:8081 pi --version
Error: Invalid proxy URL in HTTPS_PROXY. Use an http://, https://, or socks5:// URL without a path.

$ HTTPS_PROXY=socks5://127.0.0.1:8081 pi --version
1.4.0
```

issues.title: perf(memory): auto-memory extractor re-sends its context uncached on every run (40-entry sliding tail + own system prompt)

issues.body:
## Summary

The managed auto-memory extraction agent re-sends its whole context as uncached input on every run. In one month of a long-lived deployment this cost 56.1M cold input tokens at run starts (the extractor contributed 72.2M uncached tokens in total, 57.1% of all uncached model input), and its cache-hit rate has an architectural ceiling of ~65.8% because of how its request prefix is built.

## Method

qwen-code 0.25.1 (a51d56c708), OpenAI-compatible provider with implicit prefix caching, legacy recall mode (`enableStructuredMemoryRecall` off). Per-request `input` / `cached` token counts from the usage log, extraction runs correlated with transcript telemetry (`qwen-code.api_response`), one deployment, one month. No request-body capture: the first request of a run is the first request after an extraction run starts, and its `cached` count is the provider's own report.

## Findings

- 1,096 extraction runs, 3.04 requests/run, ~190K input/run.
- First request of a run: median input **64,318**, median cached **6,272** → median hit **10.0%**. 710/1,096 runs had cached in 5K–9K tokens, i.e. exactly the extractor's own system prompt — the history behind it never cached.
- 1,061 adjacent run pairs, median gap **1.4 min**, median cached/theoretical **10.2%**: runs one minute apart do not reuse each other's prefix.
- Hit rate collapses as context grows:

  | first-request input | hit rate |
  | --- | ---: |
  | < 20K | 65.0% |
  | 20–40K | 26.8% |
  | 40–60K | 16.6% |
  | 60–80K | 7.7% |
  | ≥ 80K | 9.5% |

- Month totals: extractor input 207,976,203, cached 135,806,464 (65.3%). Run starts: 64.7M input, 8.7M cached → **56.1M cold input**. 32.9% of runs write nothing.
- Control, same deployment: main sessions reach 95.2% cached/theoretical on same-session turn starts ≤ 10 min and 94.0% on tool-loop continuations. The provider and the measurement are not the limiting factor; the extractor's request prefix is.

## Root cause

The extractor does not share the parent session's cacheable prefix:

1. `captureCacheSafeParams()` captures only `getHistoryTailShallow(40, true)` (`packages/core/src/core/client.ts:1474`), so the history handed to the extractor is a **sliding tail of the last 40 entries**. Every new turn shifts the window, so the bytes right after the first message change on every run.
2. `runAutoMemoryExtractionByAgent` then rewrites that history (`buildAgentHistory`, `packages/core/src/memory/extractionAgentPlanner.ts:91-128`: strips `<system-reminder>` blocks, drops messages, appends synthetic `Acknowledged.` turns) and runs it under a dedicated system prompt (`EXTRACTION_AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `packages/core/src/memory/extractionAgentPlanner.ts:338`) through the AgentHeadless path, which does not set `renderedSystemPrompt`.
3. The prefix-sharing mechanism that already exists for forks (`promptConfig.renderedSystemPrompt`, `packages/core/src/agents/runtime/agent-core.ts:596-604`, used by the Agent-tool fork at `packages/core/src/tools/agent/agent.ts:2124`) is not used here.

The only stable bytes in the extractor request are its constant system prompt; the history behind it is re-derived and re-sanitized every run, so the provider caches the first few thousand tokens and little else.

## Why this matters

Memory maintenance is not free: in this deployment the memory subsystem (extractor + dream + user-dream + catalog) was ~293M input tokens, 47% of all model input, and the extractor alone was 33.6% of all input. Fixing the prefix is the difference between paying for the whole history on every run and paying for the new turn only.

## Proposed fixes

1. Give the extractor the parent's exact prefix: set `renderedSystemPrompt` to the parent's rendered system instruction and pass the parent history verbatim (full history, not a 40-entry tail) as `initialMessages`, with the extraction task prompt appended as the final user message. The task prompt is short and at the tail, so it does not disturb the prefix.
2. Stop re-deriving the tail. If a cap is needed for cost, use a stable anchor + append-only scheme, not a sliding window: a window whose first bytes move cannot be cached. Prefer no cap and rely on the parent cache, since the main session has already cached that history.
3. Skip no-op runs before issuing a request: 32.9% of runs write nothing. A cheap precheck (or the opt-in `QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_EXTRACT_NOOP_SKIP_TURNS` from #13571, currently default off) avoids the whole request for those runs.

## Expected effect

With the parent prefix shared, extractor `cached/input` should approach the main-session control (~94%), and cold input drops from ~56M/month to roughly the size of the extraction task prompts. The hit-rate collapse by context size should disappear.

## Related

- #15027 (catalog / prefix design tracker)
- #13612 (known 40-entry tail limitation)
- #13571 (opt-in no-op skip)

issues.body:
## Summary

Long sessions that read images (screenshots, image files) have their inline image payloads silently rewritten out of the chat history once the inline count reaches a threshold. The threshold defaults to 20, accepts only integers >= 1 (no off value), is not declared in the settings schema, and the rewrite mutates the history in place — on providers with implicit prefix caching this forces a cache rebuild from the rewrite point. There is no supported way to keep image payloads in history.

## Current behavior

- `resolveCompactionTuning` (`packages/core/src/services/compactionInputSlimming.ts:176`) resolves `imagePayloadThreshold` from `QWEN_IMAGE_PAYLOAD_THRESHOLD` / settings / `DEFAULT_IMAGE_PAYLOAD_THRESHOLD = 20`, with `{ integer: true, minInclusive: 1 }`. There is no `0` / `-1` / `Infinity` off value.
- When the inline image count in the request history reaches the threshold, `getRequestHistory` (`packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts:2658`) calls `replaceImagePayloadsInPlace`, which **mutates the history**: deletes `inlineData`, stores the payload in an in-memory store, and replaces the part text with a reference (`packages/core/src/services/image-payload-references.ts:72`). The most recent `maxRecentImages` (default 3) are reattached to the current turn.
- `model.chatCompression` is declared in the settings schema as a bare object (`packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts:1883`) with no `properties`, so `imagePayloadThreshold` / `maxRecentImagesToRetain` / `enableScreenshotTrigger` are not discoverable through settings help, validation, or the settings dialog.

## Why it matters

1. No opt-out: a user who wants image payloads preserved (e.g. a vision workflow that needs every frame in history) cannot disable this. Setting a huge number is the only workaround and it is not documented.
2. Cache cost: the rewrite changes the request bytes in the middle of the history. With implicit prefix caching, every eviction invalidates the cached prefix from the first rewritten part onward and re-sends the remainder uncached. In a long image-heavy session this can dominate input cost.
3. Silent data change: the history the model sees on later turns is not the history the transcript shows — image parts become text references.

## Proposed fix

- Accept an off value (e.g. `0` or `-1`) for `imagePayloadThreshold`, or add an explicit boolean `imagePayloadEviction: false`, and document it.
- Declare `chatCompression`'s fields in the settings schema (type, default, min) so the knobs are discoverable and validated.
- Consider not mutating the stored history for a request-only transformation: keep the original parts and rewrite only the outgoing copy, with an explicit restore (the `maxRecentImages` reattach logic already assumes the store holds the originals), or document that eviction is permanent.

## Related

- #15027 (prefix/cache design tracker)
