prs.title: feat(core,cli): add toolParametersMandatory opt-in for strict OpenAI-compatible servers
prs.body: ## What this PR does Adds `model.generationConfig.toolParametersMandatory`, default `false`. When it is set on a route, a tool that takes no arguments is sent with `"parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": {} }` instead of the field being omitted. The repair applies on whichever provider serves that route, including one selected because the model id looks like a vendor model (`deepseek`, `glm-`, `mimo-`, `mistral`), so it works on a self-hosted gateway that serves those ids at a loopback address. It is scoped to the route it is set on: a side model — a subagent, a fork, or a `baseLlmClient` target — pointed at its own baseUrl does not inherit the parent's value, and its own entry can override it, including with `false`. ## Why it's needed **Update: TabbyAPI no longer requires `tools[].function.parameters` since [this commit](https://github.com/theroyallab/tabbyAPI/commit/fb80a9372859acd9173f2ff9912fb28793d58c1e).** A server that types `tools[].function.parameters` as a required field rejects the whole request when a parameterless tool omits it, and the request dies before the model sees any tool, so no tool call can be made at all. The rejection text names the server more reliably than its vendor does: serde-based Rust servers and litellm routers report `missing field parameters`, while Pydantic-based servers reported `Field required`. The omission is deliberate rather than an oversight: the relaxation that strips an empty `properties` exists for older llama.cpp grammars (#10080), and the shape it strips has only ever been measured on the three llama.cpp builds that relaxation was verified on, so the two classes of server are treated as wanting opposite things and the shared conversion step cannot be made to serve both. The choice therefore has to be per route and opt-in. ## Reviewer Test Plan ### How to verify **Update: TabbyAPI no longer requires `tools[].function.parameters` since [this commit](https://github.com/theroyallab/tabbyAPI/commit/fb80a9372859acd9173f2ff9912fb28793d58c1e).** - Works on 0.23.1 - Broken on ≥ 0.23.2 against TabbyAPI (TabbyAPI logs following warning "chat/completions: client disconnected, generation cancelled") - Manually re-adding the field makes the request succeed ### Exact error from TabbyAPI ```json { "detail": [ { "type": "missing", "loc": ["body", "tools", 6, "function", "parameters"], "msg": "Field required", "input": { "name": "cron_list", "description": "..." } }, { "type": "missing", "loc": ["body", "tools", 15, "function", "parameters"], "msg": "Field required", "input": { "name": "list_agents", "description": "..." } } ] } ``` ### Evidence (Before & After) Live A/B against the TabbyAPI route recorded 2026-09-19, three payloads differing only in that field: ```text ARM omitted http=422 body={"detail":[{"type":"missing","loc":["body","tools",0,"function","parameters"],"msg":"Field required","input":{"name":"cron_list","description":"List all cron jobs"}}]} ARM bare http=200 body={"id":"cmpl-8eecd4409cb14547a15986b347013eb9","choices":[{"index":0,"finish_reason":"length",... ARM emptyObject http=200 body={"id":"cmpl-e77b9dab7ec94d3eb01d5951c9e744de","choices":[{"index":0,"finish_reason":"length",... ``` Setting `model.generationConfig.toolParametersMandatory` to `true` in settings.json makes the request succeed Unit coverage: 26 cases pin the wire per route — the four model-name routes, each asserting its vendor provider stays selected, the plain route in both states plus a tool that declares no schema at all, a list whose parameterless tools sit at several positions with a declared schema left intact, DashScope in both states, MiniMax with the setting unset, opted in, and explicitly set to `false` — that last one being the only thing asserting the published promise that the injection cannot be turned off on the MiniMax route — a declared schema passed through unchanged, and a request without tools — with the flag as the discriminator rather than a provider class: neutralising the opt-in reddens eleven of them while the MiniMax, omission and passthrough cases stay green. Seven of the 26 cover entries the repair must not rewrite: a custom or grammar tool handed back by identity, a non-function entry that still carries a `function` object — the only input that separates the helper's type check from the null check behind it, since removing the former alone leaves every other case green — and an entry reached through `extra_body` that claims `type: 'function'` while carrying no `function` object — the flat shape `extra_body` accepts — measured both through the helper and through an opted-in route's merged `extra_body`, through the route that injects whatever the setting says with the setting off, and beside a nullish member and a `function` that is present but null when the helper is called directly, which is where those two shapes are pinned without a request behind them. ### Tested on | OS | Status | | :--------: | :----: | | 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ | | 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ | | 🐧 Linux | ✅ | ## Risk & Scope - Main risk or tradeoff: the empty-object schema is the shape #10080's grammar relaxation strips away for older llama.cpp builds, and nothing beyond the three builds that relaxation was verified on has been measured, so the key must be set only on a route whose server requires the field, and it stays off by default. A server that rejects an empty `properties` object must not opt in. The 400 in #11410 is not a report of that: it rejected the bare shape for lacking `properties`, and no issue in this lineage mentions vLLM at all. - Scope of the default: on a route that does not opt in, the repair never runs, so the request that route builds is the same one it built before. One difference is not the flag's to control. MiniMax requires the field and has always injected it unconditionally, and that injection now shares one implementation with the opt-in repair — guards included. So there, a `tools` entry that `extra_body` admits in one of four malformed shapes — a nullish member, an entry that claims type: "function" while carrying no function object, which is the flat shape extra_body accepts, one whose function is present but null, or an entry whose type is not function that nonetheless carries a function object — passes through exactly as written instead of aborting request building with a `TypeError` that names no tool: the repair rewrites tool schemas, it does not vet a user's own list. That is strictly less crashy than the unguarded injection it replaced, it is pinned by cases that run with the setting off, and it is the whole of the off-state difference: every other route is gated on the flag. The same guards run wherever the flag does gate, and a malformed entry is pinned to survive there too. - Not validated / out of scope: a live re-run against the `deepseek-v4.1-flash` gateway reported in #11956 — that route is pinned by a unit case only. The Responses wire, the Anthropic and Gemini generators, and detecting any self-hosted server from its URL are unchanged. Reports that this shape was accepted as a local patch on two other strict gateways (`api-inference.modelscope.cn`, `apihub.agnes-ai.com`) are third-party reports that predate this change, so they corroborate the choice rather than verify it. - Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The setting key is new and unreleased, as is the dedicated provider this PR first added — that class is gone, and the behaviour now sits on the shared request path plus one call on the route that builds its request independently. ## Design notes - [English](https://github.com/kaylster/qwen-code/blob/fix/11956-always-emit-parameterless-tool-parameters/docs/design/2026-09-17-parameterless-tool-parameters.md) - [中文](https://github.com/kaylster/qwen-code/blob/fix/11956-always-emit-parameterless-tool-parameters/docs/design/2026-09-17-parameterless-tool-parameters.zh-CN.md) ## Linked Issues Fixes #11956

prs.title: fix(ci): scope the sdk-java test lock to the cache write-back
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR moves the self-hosted SDK Java test lane's per-host lock off its Maven suites and onto the shared Maven cache write-back. The lane now seeds a job-local Maven repository from the host cache, runs the SDK and Managed Agent suites against that copy without the lock, and acquires the ticketed host lock only to publish the new artifacts back to the host cache. The write-back's children close the inherited lock descriptor, so a cancelled job's survivor cannot keep holding the lock.

## Why it's needed

The Managed Agent fast tier can fail before reporting a single test result when it waits out its 90-minute host-lock budget behind a long suite hold. The MariaDB integration lane already scoped its lock to the write-back, but the test lane still held the same lock across both of its Maven suites, so a roughly 90-minute full-tier Java 21 leg on the same host could starve the fast tier — the failure shape reported in #15262. With the suite unlocked, a hold measures the bounded cache copy instead of the suite, and the fast tier's wait budget is again far above one hold.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

On a self-hosted pool runner (or by reading the rendered job log), confirm the order inside the self-hosted SDK Java test step: the job-local repository is seeded, both Maven suites run, and only then does the lane acquire the host lock for the cache write-back. During the suite there must be no "Waiting for the sdk-java host lock" line. A second fast-tier job on the same host should start Maven without waiting for the first job's suite to finish; it may wait only for the short write-back.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI-internal change, no user-visible surface. Before: the test lane acquired the host lock before Maven and held it across both suites. After: Maven runs unlocked from a job-local repository; the lock is taken only for the bounded write-back.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Workflow guard tests under Node 22 on Linux; no self-hosted pool was available locally.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the lane now resolves from a job-local repository seeded from the host cache, so a first run on a cold host downloads more than before. The seed and the write-back are best-effort and cannot redden the lane.
- Not validated / out of scope: the real self-hosted pool run is left to CI after merge; this PR changes no test selection or suite contents.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; the reusable workflow's external contract is unchanged.
- Overlap: an open autofix PR for sibling issue #15242 proposes the same test-lane lock scope. Maintainers should land one and close the other.

Design docs: [English](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.md) · [中文](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15262

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

本 PR 把自托管 SDK Java 测试通道的每宿主机锁从 Maven 套件上移走，只包住共享 Maven 缓存的写回。该通道现在先从宿主机缓存播种一个 job 本地 Maven 仓库，在不持锁的情况下用该副本运行 SDK 和 Managed Agent 两套 Maven 套件，最后只为把新产物写回宿主机缓存而获取排队锁。写回的子进程会关闭继承来的锁描述符，因此被取消 job 的幸存进程无法继续持锁。

## 为什么需要

当 Managed Agent fast 档排在长时间套件持锁之后、等满 90 分钟宿主机锁预算时，它会在报告任何测试结果之前失败。MariaDB 集成通道已经把锁收窄到写回，但测试通道仍把同一把锁持在两套 Maven 套件之上，因此同一宿主机上一条约 90 分钟的 full 档 Java 21 leg 可能饿死 fast 档——这正是 #15262 报告的失败形态。套件移出锁后，一次持锁只量有界缓存复制，而不再量整套测试，fast 档的等待预算又远大于一次持锁时长。

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

在自托管 pool runner 上（或阅读渲染后的 job 日志），确认自托管 SDK Java 测试步骤内的顺序：先播种 job 本地仓库，再运行两套 Maven 套件，最后才为缓存写回获取宿主机锁。套件运行期间不应出现 "Waiting for the sdk-java host lock" 日志行。同一宿主机上的第二个 fast 档 job 应当无需等待第一个 job 的套件结束就开始 Maven；它最多只等待短暂的写回。

### 证据（修改前 / 修改后）

N/A——CI 内部改动，没有用户可见界面。修改前：测试通道在 Maven 之前取锁，并在两套套件期间一直持锁。修改后：Maven 从 job 本地仓库不持锁运行；只有有界写回才取锁。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

Linux 上 Node 22 的 workflow guard 测试；本地没有可用的自托管 pool。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：该通道现在从基于宿主机缓存播种的 job 本地仓库解析，冷宿主机上的首次运行会比以前多下载一些。播种和写回都是尽力而为，不会让通道变红。
- 未验证 / 范围外：真实自托管 pool 运行留给合并后的 CI；本 PR 不改变测试选择或套件内容。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无；可复用 workflow 的外部契约不变。

prs.title: fix(core): respect read-only files and hard links in atomic writes
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Writes that replace an existing file now check that the destination is writable before committing, and keep hard links together when they do. An atomic replace commits by renaming a temporary file over the destination; the destination's own permissions were never consulted, and the rename gave the written name a new inode, so other hard links kept the previous content.

## Why it's needed

Marking a file read-only is how users and tools signal "do not modify this", but a replace-by-rename ignored that signal even though a plain write would fail with a permission error. The same rename also split hard-linked names: editing one name silently left every other name on the old content. Both behaviors are surprising for a file-writing tool, and the sandboxed write path already behaves correctly, so the two paths disagreed.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Create a file, make it read-only, and write to it. The write should fail with a permission error, the content should be unchanged, and no temporary file should be left behind. Then create a file, hard-link it to a second name, and write through the first name. Both names should show the new content, the link count should stay at two, and the inode should be unchanged.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the four new regression tests fail (asynchronous and synchronous writers, read-only and hard-link cases). After: the atomic write suite passes in full (87 tests), the changed files pass ESLint and Prettier, and the repository typecheck passes.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 24.22.1, pnpm 11.24.0, unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a hard-linked destination is written in place, so a crash during that write can leave a partial file. Single-link files keep the atomic rename path.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows and Linux were not exercised locally. The read-only cases skip where permission bits are not enforced (Windows, root). Concurrent readers can still observe an in-place write.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: replacing a read-only file now fails with a permission error instead of succeeding, matching what a plain write does.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15454

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

覆盖已有文件的写入现在会在提交前检查目标是否可写，并在目标存在硬链接时把链接保持在一起。原子替换的提交方式是把临时文件 rename 到目标上；目标自身的权限从未被检查，而 rename 又给写入的那个名字换了新 inode，导致其它硬链接仍停留在旧内容上。

## 为什么需要

把文件标记为只读，是用户和工具表达"不要修改"的方式，但 replace-by-rename 忽略了这个信号，而普通写入本会因权限失败。同一个 rename 还会拆散硬链接：编辑其中一个名字，其它名字会静默保留旧内容。对一个写文件的工具来说，这两种行为都很意外；而且沙箱写入路径本来就是正确行为，两条路径并不一致。

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

创建一个文件、设为只读，然后向它写入。写入应以权限错误失败，内容保持不变，且不残留临时文件。再创建一个文件并硬链接到第二个名字，通过第一个名字写入；两个名字都应显示新内容，链接数保持为 2，inode 不变。

### 证据（修改前后）

修改前：新增的四条回归测试失败（异步/同步写入器 × 只读/硬链接）。修改后：原子写入测试套件全部通过（87 条），改动文件通过 ESLint 与 Prettier，仓库 typecheck 通过。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

Node.js 24.22.1、pnpm 11.24.0，仅单元测试。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：硬链接目标改为原地写入，写入过程中崩溃可能留下不完整的文件；普通单链接文件仍走原子 rename。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：本地未覆盖 Windows 与 Linux；只读用例在权限位不生效的环境（Windows、root）会跳过。并发读者仍可能观察到原地写入的中间状态。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：覆盖只读文件现在会以权限错误失败，而不是成功，这与普通写入的行为一致。

## 关联 Issue

对应 issue #15454。

</details>

- Adds a CI guard ensuring every runnable integration test is selected by the no-AK gate or explicitly exempted, preventing accidental omissions. ([#14989](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14989)) by @zonemeen
- Improves internal CLI test reliability by resolving temporary Git fixture paths under symlinked directories. ([#15133](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15133)) by @wenshao
- test(managed-agent): refuse a second fire while the turn runs (FG11d) ([#14998](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14998)) by @wenshao

- Makes Hosted MCP fault test fixtures claim close operations atomically, preventing race conditions from interfering with intended fault scenarios. ([#15158](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15158)) by @yiliang114
- Adds a test ensuring the branch picker shows the Sets upstream on push hint when a branch has no upstream configured. ([#15073](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15073)) by @yiliang114
- Corrects the daemon E2E install warning and adds safeguards that keep Build, Bundle, and Java daemon E2E steps in the expected order. ([#14884](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14884)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Adds a regression test ensuring the VS Code webview language attribute is HTML-escaped correctly. ([#10492](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/10492)) by @CanReader
- Stabilizes the SDK Java idle-watchdog timing test without changing runtime watchdog behavior. ([#15103](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15103)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot

issues.title: skills: the ambient index caps descriptions at 400 chars with no config knob and no signal in the prompt or to the model

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed issues for "skill description", "skills index", "skill catalogue", "truncat", "MAX_SKILL_DESCRIPTION_CHARS", "skills budget", "prompt budget". Related but distinct: #7066 (bundled install / per-skill disable / explicit-only policy), #6526 (same failure class on standing instructions: hard-coded ceilings, no knobs, invisible trim), #4698 (routing metadata for the bundled pack, closed). This issue is about the ambient skills index: what the model is allowed to see, and what nobody is told when text is cut.

## What problem does this solve?

Codewhale puts a bounded index of skills into every system prompt. Each row is a name, a slice of the skill's `description`, and the `SKILL.md` path. The slice is capped by a compile-time constant; the block is capped by a share of the route window. When either limit bites, the model gets a shortened description — and the only disclosure anywhere is a per-skill note behind `/skills inspect`, a diagnostic subcommand.

**The mechanics, verified at `f19aa7772` (0.10.2):**

- Per-row cap: `MAX_SKILL_DESCRIPTION_CHARS = 400` — `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:52`.
- Block budget: `window_tokens × 4 chars × 5%`, floor 2 400, ceiling 40 000 chars — `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:56-68`, `:84-97`. Neither value is configurable.
- Three tiers — `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:1948-1954`:
  1. full rows, each capped at 400;
  2. proportional shortening when the total does not fit, with a 40-char floor (`:71`);
  3. names only, plus an omission line (`:2167`).
- A row is split into summary + trigger at an English marker, and the trigger is promised at least half the cap when both exist (`:1903-1946`). Only four markers are recognized: `use when:`, `use when `, `use this when `, `use this skill when `.
- Cut text ends in `…`, added by `truncate_for_prompt` (`:2177-2188`).

**What is surfaced today — and credit where it is due.** `/skills inspect` prints a per-skill note when a description exceeds the cap, added in `ba386a0cf` (2026-09-02):

```
note: description is N chars; the model index shows at most 400 — trim it,
or end it with `Use when: <trigger>` so the trigger survives shortening
```

`crates/tui/src/commands/groups/skills/skills.rs:486-501`, inside `inspect_skills` (`:445`). Reachability matters: bare `/skills` opens the Extensions UI (`:313-315`), and `/skills <prefix>` prints descriptions without this note (`:376-441`). The comment above the note states the intent exactly: "say so here instead of cutting an imported skill mid-sentence with nobody told."

That note is useful, and the authoring advice in it is correct. It is also the whole of the disclosure:

- **It is user-facing only, and behind a diagnostic subcommand.** Bare `/skills` opens Extensions; the note is in `/skills inspect`. The model's prompt does not carry the count, a footer, or a marker beyond `…`; the Usage paragraph tells the model to use `load_skill` "if the index was truncated" (`mod.rs:1971-1976`), a condition the model cannot reliably detect.
- **It fires only for the tier-1 cap** (`description > 400`). When the pack overflows the block budget, tier 2 shortens descriptions proportionally — including descriptions well under 400 — with no note anywhere, and tier 3 drops names with an in-prompt omission line only.
- **It is not a startup or discovery signal.** Nothing is written to the log, and `/context` reports the rendered block with no note that rows were shortened (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:595-622`). A user who never runs `/skills inspect` never sees it; a session that loads a new pack never sees it.
- **It is not a count.** With 50+ skills the note appears in a long list, per skill, with no aggregate ("23 of 47 descriptions shortened").

**Measured on a real 52-skill pack under `~/.agents/skills` (identifiers redacted):**

- 32 099 chars of `description` in total; 20 091 (~63%) can reach the model.
- 47 of the 52 carry a "Not for" clause; in 23 of them the clause is absent from the rendered row. Checked by re-implementing `split_trigger` + `description_split` from the code and comparing the rendered string, not by raw offsets.
- 18 of the 52 have no recognized trigger marker, so their row is cut mid-sentence before the triggers.
- Fixed scaffolding (names + paths) is ~3 300 chars. At a 400 cap this pack renders ~23.8k chars.

The budget is not the binding constraint on large routes; the constant is. On a 1M-token route the index budget is ~36 000 chars after the fixed header/usage cost and the warning reservation; the pack's untruncated rows would need ~35.8k (the four bundled skills add ~0.75k), so the budget would force only a small trim — yet the 400 cap removes ~12.0k chars. The warning reservation is easy to miss: when discovery produced any warning, the renderer withholds up to 20% of the block budget for warnings, capped at 3 232 chars (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:2026-2032`). On a 150k route the index then gets ~26 000 chars, and the cap could rise to ~450 before tier 2 begins; on 128k the index gets ~21 600, which this pack at 400 already exceeds, so it is already in tier 2 with no note anywhere.

**Why this matters beyond one pack.** Most users install published skills rather than writing them. Sampled `description` lengths in `anthropics/skills` are 204, 277, 319, 437, 837 and 952 chars, while the Agent Skills spec allows 1024. A large share of published skills therefore arrives truncated, and the authoring fix ("keep it short, end with `Use when:`") is advice the author only meets if they happen to run `/skills inspect` on the machine where the skill is installed.

**The recovery path exists but is unbudgeted.** `load_skill name="list"` returns full descriptions (`crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:140-146`) — ~32k chars for this pack, i.e. a large unbudgeted read the model has no reliable reason to take.

**Prior art inside the repo.** `/skills inspect` already names the cap; #6526 proposes the same pattern for standing instructions — config-optional ceilings plus a bounded first-turn notice when content is trimmed. The skills index has the ceiling and the human note, but not the config, the aggregate, the log line, or the first-turn notice.

## What should Codewhale do?

Four separable pieces, smallest first.

**1. Extend the existing notice beyond `/skills inspect`.**

- Add one aggregate line to the block when any row is shortened at any tier: `- ... descriptions shortened for N of M skills; load_skill name="list" returns full text.` Cost ~90 chars.
- Emit a discovery-time warning when `description` exceeds the cap and no `when_to_use` is present, through the channel that already exists: the `### Skill load warnings` section (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:1976`, `:2153-2165`) and `logging::warn` — the same path that already reports shadowed skills and unknown frontmatter keys. The `/skills inspect` note and this warning should come from one computation, not two.
- Record the same fact in the context report entry for `SourceKind::SkillsBlock` (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:613-622`), so `/context` shows a degradation, not only a size.

**2. Tell the model that something was lost — open question below.**

A footer is the cheapest honest signal. A per-row marker costs chars on every row, and `…` is ambiguous because authors use it. Keep `…` as the visual cue; make the count explicit once per block.

**3. Make the limits configurable, mirroring the ecosystem.**

- `[skills] listing_max_description_chars` — per-entry cap. Default today is 400; the spec allows 1024, Claude Code defaults to 1 536 for `description + when_to_use`.
- `[skills] listing_budget_fraction` — share of the route window. Default 0.05 today; Claude Code uses 0.01.
- Precedence: explicit config > window-derived default, resolved in one place and used by both prompt build (`crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:1367`) and `/context` (`crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:595`).

**4. Add a per-skill "name-only" state.**

Today the only per-skill lever is `disable-model-invocation: true`, which removes the skill from the model catalogue entirely (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:866-877`, `docs/SKILLS.md:151-153`). A middle state would keep the name in the index and spend zero description budget — the same idea as Claude Code's `skillOverrides: "name-only"`. It is also a better fallback than the current 40-char floor: a 40-char fragment costs almost as much as a name and routes worse than no description at all. This overlaps with #7066's proposed `explicit_only` list; the two could share one policy surface.

**Sequencing options** (maintainers decide; effort/risk are estimates):

- **Option A — report only.** Footer + discovery warning + context-report note, sharing one computation with the existing `/skills inspect` note. Small diff, no config, no behaviour change. Risk: ~90 chars per request.
- **Option B — A + two config keys.** Adds docs and, if the flag is user-visible, a `docs/features.toml` row (`AGENTS.md:114-116`). Medium diff. Risk: two knobs that interact with the window-derived default; needs one resolver.
- **Option C — B + name-only state.** Larger; touches prompt rendering and the skills manager; coordinate with #7066. Risk: policy surface grows; must stay distinct from `explicit-only` (which hides the skill from the catalogue entirely).
- **Option D — raise the default cap to 1024 without knobs.** Small diff, large prompt-cost change on small windows: at a 128k window the index budget is ~21.6k after the warning reservation and this pack already exceeds it, so a higher cap deepens tier 2 instead of revealing more text.

Recommendation: A first, then B; C with #7066. Do not raise the default before the total budget is configurable.

## Where?

- TUI (terminal interface)
- Docs

## Workarounds or other tools (optional)

Today: keep `description` short by hand and end it with `Use when: …` (the advice `/skills inspect` already prints); set `disable-model-invocation: true` per skill; restrict discovery with `[skills] scan_codewhale_only = true` (`docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2582`); move skill directories out of the scanned roots. None of these makes a shortened row visible to the model or at startup, and none covers tier 2.

Claude Code, for comparison:

- Listing budget is 1% of the context window by default (`skillListingBudgetFraction`), or a fixed character count via `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET`. Ours is 5% of the window — more generous in total, not configurable.
- Per-entry text (`description` + `when_to_use`) is capped at 1 536 chars by default (`skillListingMaxDescChars`), configurable. Ours is 400, below the spec's 1024.
- On overflow Claude Code keeps every skill name and drops descriptions starting with the least-used skills. Codewhale shortens every row proportionally to a 40-char floor, so every skill degrades a little instead of a few degrading to a name.
- It warns in the debug log, reports the applied listing size in `/context`, and estimates cost per skill in `/doctor`. Codewhale reports the block size, and only a per-skill note in `/skills inspect` for the 400 cap.
- `skillOverrides` has four per-skill states written from the `/skills` menu: `on`, `name-only`, `user-invocable-only`, `off`. Codewhale has on / fully off.
- `when_to_use` is a first-class Claude Code field appended to the description and counted toward the same cap; Codewhale implements the same field (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:855`) — good — but spec-only distribution paths reject it, so it is not a portable substitute for a well-formed description.

The Agent Skills specification: `description` is required, 1–1024 characters, and must say both what the skill does and when to use it; `name` is ≤64 chars; `compatibility` ≤500; progressive disclosure is metadata (name + description) always, body on activation, `scripts/`/`references/`/`assets/` on demand.

## Open questions

1. **Should the model be told that rows were shortened?** Arguments for: the model is the only consumer of the routing surface, and today it can only suspect a cut from `…`; a footer lets it decide to call `load_skill name="list"`. Arguments against: ~90 chars on every request, and the model rarely needs the full text; a per-row marker is noisier still. Precedent: #6526 proposes a bounded first-turn notice for trimmed instructions, and `AGENTS.md` says "Model-visible means logged".
2. Should truncation be a session event? The rendered prompt is logged, but the decision to shorten is not.
3. Usage-based dropping vs proportional shortening: Claude Code drops descriptions of the least-used skills first. Does Codewhale have or want usage data? Is a uniform 40-char fragment the right fallback?
4. Default cap: 400 (today), 1024 (spec), or 1 536 combined (Claude Code)? What happens to prompt-cache stability when the cap depends on the route window?
5. `when_to_use` is appended unconditionally (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:855`). When the description already contains `Use when:`, this produces a second marker; `split_trigger` resolves by marker priority and then first occurrence, so the appended sentence ends up in the trigger tail and can be cut when the combined text exceeds the cap. Should the append be skipped when a marker is already present?
6. Companion files: `collect_companion_files` lists only files directly beside `SKILL.md` (`crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:321-346`); `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/` are never enumerated, so the spec's resource layer is invisible unless the body names the files. Intended (body must reference them) or a gap?

## References

- Agent Skills specification — https://agentskills.io/specification
- Optimizing skill descriptions — https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/optimizing-descriptions ("the description carries the entire burden of triggering")
- Claude Code skills documentation (frontmatter reference; "Skill descriptions are cut short"; `skillOverrides`) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
- Claude Code settings reference (`skillListingBudgetFraction`, `skillListingMaxDescChars`) — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference
- Public skill samples — https://github.com/anthropics/skills
- Related issues: #7066 (bundled install / per-skill disable / explicit-only), #6526 (config knobs + visible notice for trimmed standing instructions), #4698 (routing metadata for the bundled pack, closed)
- Code at `f19aa7772`: `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:52`, `:56-71`, `:84-97`, `:855`, `:866-877`, `:1903-1946`, `:1948-1954`, `:1971-1978`, `:2153-2170`, `:2177`; `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/skills/skills.rs:313-315`, `:376-441`, `:445`, `:486-501`; `crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:140-146`, `:273`, `:321-346`; `crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:1367`; `crates/tui/src/context_report.rs:595-622`; `docs/SKILLS.md:151-153`, `:264-265`; `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2582`

## Reproduction

1. Put ~50 skills with 600–1000-char descriptions under `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, or install a published pack.
2. Start a session with `CODEWHALE_DUMP_SYSTEM_PROMPT=1` (`crates/tui/src/client/chat.rs:1949`) and read the `## Skills` block from the dump.
3. Rows end in `…`. The block carries no count; `/context` reports only the block size; the log has no line. `/skills inspect` prints a per-skill note, but only for descriptions over 400 chars and only when the user runs that subcommand.
4. Force the block over budget (e.g. a small route window) to see tier 2 shorten descriptions below 400 with no note anywhere.
5. `load_skill name="list"` returns the full descriptions, i.e. the text exists and was silently cut from the routing surface.

Environment: codewhale 0.10.2 (dev), commit `f19aa7772`, Linux; reproduced on a 1M-token route and a 150k-token route.

## Contributing

- [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this.

issues.title: codewhale review accepts DeepSeek's leaked DSML tool-call markup as the review and exits 0 with no tally

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
**Version:** 0.10.2 (`ff466b2ed0bf`, npm build), Linux. Provider `deepseek`, model `deepseek-flash`, `reasoning_effort = "high"`, UI locale zh-Hans.
**Target:** 0.10.3 · Related: #7067

## Repro
Same setup as #7067: a one-file +10/−1 working-tree diff with no sensitive paths, so triage classes it as Low risk, which offers **0 tools**. Run `codewhale review`. In 1 of 4 runs it printed this as the entire review and exited normally:

```
<｜｜DSML｜｜ calls>
<｜｜DSML｜｜ invoke name="read_file">
<｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter name="path" string="true">tides.py</｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter>
</｜｜DSML｜｜ invoke>
<｜｜DSML｜｜ invoke name="search_repository">
<｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter name="query" string="true">parse_reading\|high_tides\|low_tides\|tides</｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter>
</｜｜DSML｜｜ invoke>
</｜｜DSML｜｜ calls>
```

There were no findings, no "Checked, nothing wrong" section and no `<!-- codewhale-review: … -->` tally. The other three runs hit the #7067 output cap.

## Cause
- The engine already knows this shape. `crates/tui/src/core/engine/streaming.rs:~586` says: "DeepSeek also emits a doubled-delimiter form (`<｜｜DSML｜｜ calls>`) when a request offers no tools; one-shot `codewhale exec` printed it verbatim as the answer." It's handled there through `TOOL_CALL_MARKER_PAIRS` and `contains_fake_tool_wrapper` (`streaming.rs:717`).
- The review path builds its own requests in `crates/tui/src/tools/review_core.rs` and never applies that check. Neither `review_core.rs`, `review.rs` nor the CLI path in `lib.rs` references `contains_fake_tool_wrapper` or the marker tables. So non-empty text is accepted as a completed review.
- The Low tier's zero-tool budget is what invites the model to fake tool calls in the first place (#7067).

## Expected
A response that is, or contains, fake tool-call markup is never published or printed as a review. Either treat it as a failed or incomplete pass with a clear message (and no tally, so CI gating sees "no verdict"), or, once review offers read-only tools at every risk level (#7067), parse it as a request for the tools that were offered.

## Fix direction
Reuse `contains_fake_tool_wrapper`. Don't add a second detector. Run it on each pass's visible text in `review_core`, and route a hit to the same incomplete outcome the exhausted-allowance path uses. The GitHub Action's `--post` path must not publish such a body. Its outcome should be `incomplete`, not `reviewed_clean`.

Found while recording a Chinese-language 0.10.2 demo. I have the raw TUI recording of the leaking run if needed.

issues.title: zh-Hans (and every non-English locale): common TUI strings are hardcoded English — /undo note, /diff title, approval and plan-handoff chrome, /color note

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: localization
labels.description: Localization, i18n, and non-English language support

issues.body:
**Version:** 0.10.2 (`ff466b2ed0bf`, npm build), Linux, `locale = "zh-Hans"` in `settings.toml`.
**Target:** 0.10.3

With the UI in Simplified Chinese, the main flow is translated: the composer placeholder 输入消息…, approval options 仅允许本次 / 不允许, the pet status 思考 / 回复 / 完成, the plan-handoff question 你想如何继续？, and the footer. But several messages you see in an ordinary session stay in English. None of these strings are in `crates/localization/locales/*.json`; they're hardcoded at the call site:

| What you see | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `/undo` note: `Undid your request "…". 1 file is back as it was before it: … The request and its reply were removed from the conversation.` | `crates/commands/src/debug/undo.rs:323` (`format!("Undid {request}. {count} before it:…")`) |
| `/diff` pager title `Changes since session start` | `crates/commands/src/debug/undo.rs:174` |
| `/color` note `Composer color for this chat: red` / `…reset to the theme default` | `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/session/color.rs:73-74` |
| Tool card status `… · waiting for approval` | `crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1411` |
| Plan handoff / question chrome: `Action required`, `Question 1 of 1`, `Other`, `Type a custom response`, `1-4 quick pick ↑/↓ move Enter confirm ←/h back Esc cancel` | `crates/tui/src/tui/user_input.rs` (e.g. `:459`) |
| Approval card `Save:   always ask first` | `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/approval/ask_rules.rs` |
| Grouped activity `Explored 3 files: explore +3 ›`, `patch done · Updated tides.py · +1 -1` | `crates/tui/src/tui/history/tool_run.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs` |

## Repro
1. Put `locale = "zh-Hans"` in `$CODEWHALE_HOME/settings.toml`, or choose 简体中文 in `/settings`.
2. In a Git repo, ask for a fix that runs a shell command and edits a file, approve the card, then run `/diff`, `/undo` and `/color`.

## Expected
These go through `tr(locale, MessageId::…)` like their neighbours, and appear in `en.json` and every locale pack. `scripts/check-tui-locale-parity.py` only checks keys that exist, so it can't catch strings that never became keys.

## Notes
- The CHANGELOG for 0.10.2 also says the pet's activity words and the update note follow the UI language, and both do. These strings are the visible gap next to them.
- Fix direction: move each string to a `MessageId`, add the en/zh-Hans/zh-Hant/ja values (the other locales can fall back), and consider a small lint that flags new user-facing `format!`/string literals in `crates/tui/src/tui/` and `crates/commands/src/` outside the localization crate.

issues.title: write silently restores CRLF despite an explicit request to save with LF

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

Leave these confirmations unchecked until you have personally verified them before submission. This draft does not claim a fresh duplicate search or reproduction on the latest release.


### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Codewhale's write tool converts CR-free content to CRLF when the overwritten file used CRLF (first newline decides) and reports plain success, so a user's explicit request to save with LF endings is silently not honored and the agent tells the user the file is LF.

Observed behavior:
write with LF-only content -> 'Successfully wrote 215 bytes'; the file on disk keeps CRLF on every line (next read and final workspace file); the agent claimed LF endings in 9/10 runs (grep_files for \r returned 0 matches).

write 'Creates the file if it does not exist, overwrites it if it does' with the given content; the user explicitly required LF line endings only. Caveat: CRLF preservation is an intentional upstream fix (#5909/#5911) for unintended conversions.

## Steps to reproduce 

1. Use the tested revision and reproduction environment below.
2. Prepare the fixture described here:

Prepare notes.txt with CRLF endings and the words verison, shure, and Anounce. The recorded fixture had seven CRLF lines. Inspect the raw bytes after write; a rendered text preview alone cannot establish LF conversion.

3. Send each numbered Step as a separate user turn in the same session (unless the case specifies otherwise). Preserve the supplied text:

issues.title: Composer history ignores CODEWHALE_HOME: typed prompts go to $HOME/.codewhale and are shared across isolated homes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
**Version:** 0.10.2 (`ff466b2ed0bf`, npm build), Linux.
**Target:** 0.10.3

## Repro
```sh
export CODEWHALE_HOME=/tmp/cw-isolated   # an explicit, isolated home
codewhale                                # type and send any prompt, then quit
ls ~/.codewhale/composer_history.jsonl   # exists, and holds the prompt
ls /tmp/cw-isolated/composer_history.jsonl  # absent
```
I saw this across several sessions, each with its own `CODEWHALE_HOME`. All their prompts went to one `$HOME/.codewhale/composer_history.jsonl`, so Up-arrow history in each "isolated" home shows the others' prompts.

## Cause
`composer_history::default_history_path()` builds the path from `effective_home_dir()` (the user's `$HOME`) plus `.codewhale` (`crates/tui/src/composer_history.rs:43-72`). It never consults `CODEWHALE_HOME`. It can also fall back to `~/.deepseek/composer_history.jsonl` when that file exists.

## Why it matters
- `docs/REBRAND.md` says: "An explicit `CODEWHALE_HOME` intentionally isolates that home and disables the ambient `~/.deepseek` fallback." Composer history breaks both halves of that.
- History holds everything the user typed, which can include pasted secrets. People use a separate home for CI, demos, classrooms or per-client separation, and they don't expect prompts to land in, or be read back from, the shared ambient home.

## Expected
When `CODEWHALE_HOME` is set, read and write `$CODEWHALE_HOME/composer_history.jsonl`, with no `~/.deepseek` fallback. Keep today's resolution only when `CODEWHALE_HOME` is unset.

## Not this issue
`~/.codewhale/pet-shared` is also written under `$HOME`. That looks deliberate, since it has its own `CODEWHALE_PET_HOME` override and the pet is shared across terminals.

issues.title: Plan→Work handoff seeds a To-do titled with the raw plan markdown (lines run together) that is never completed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
**Version:** 0.10.2 (`ff466b2ed0bf`, npm build), Linux, provider DeepSeek.
**Target:** 0.10.3

## Repro
1. `/mode plan`, then ask for a short plan, e.g. "Plan adding a low_tides() function next to high_tides, with a test."
2. At **How do you want to continue?**, pick **Work (Ask)** or **Work (Auto-Review)**.
3. Look at the Tasks tab in the work bar.

## Observed
The seeded To-do row is the plan's raw markdown with newlines dropped, so the lines run together:

```
1 · ○ ## GoalAdd `low_tides(lines)` to `tides.py` beside `high_tides`, with one matching test in `test_t...   pending
1 · ○ Read `tides.py` and the existing test. Plan:**1. `tides.py` — add below `high_tides`**```python...    pending
```

In the Work (Ask) run the model finished ("Done — 3 passed") without writing its own checklist. The panel still showed **To-do · 0/1 · pending** afterwards.

## Cause (read-only trace)
- `plan_handoff_seed_title` (`crates/tui/src/tui/ui/handlers.rs:1548-1557`) is `plan.text.trim()` cut to 1024 characters. Markdown and newlines are kept. `seed_plan_handoff_todos` (`:1561-1603`) pushes it as a Pending item.
- The row renderer uses `node.title.clone()` (`work_surface/model.rs:~2739`) and only truncates by width. Ratatui drops the `\n`, which is why "## Goal" + "Add" becomes "## GoalAdd". A newline-collapsing helper already exists (`sanitize_summary_title`, `model.rs:~1554`) but this path doesn't use it.
- Nothing completes or clears the seed after a Work choice. `seeded_todo_id` is only used for rollback (Keep planning, Revise, or a failed checkpoint). The proceed message (`"Go ahead with the plan.\n\n{plan}"`) never tells the model a To-do or its id exists.

## Expected
A short plain-text title, such as the first meaningful line with markdown markers stripped. The item should then be completed or cancelled when the Work turn ends, or the model should be told its id so it can update it.

## Fix direction
- Derive the title from the first non-heading, non-fence line: strip `#`, `*` and backticks, and collapse whitespace. Also collapse newlines in the row renderer as a backstop.
- Name the seeded To-do id in the proceed message, or complete or cancel the seed when the Work turn ends with no checklist update.

issues.title: codewhale review: Low-risk 4000-token output cap starves reasoning models, and the error reports 65536 / 16384 instead

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
**Version:** 0.10.2 (`ff466b2ed0bf`, npm build), Linux. Provider `deepseek`, model `deepseek-flash`, config `reasoning_effort = "max"`.
**Target:** 0.10.3

## Repro
1. In a Git repository, make a small working-tree change. I used one Python file, +10/−1, with no sensitive paths, so triage classes it as Low risk.
2. Run `codewhale review`.

In 3 of 4 runs it failed with:

```
error: Review pass 1/1 exhausted its output allowance and produced no review text. This is an infrastructure/budget outcome, not a review result: the provider stopped with reason `max_output_tokens` after reporting 2943 of 65536 requested output tokens as reasoning; this model's review reserve is 16384 tokens (25% of the allowance) and the pass's reasoning level was capped to fit that reserve. ... accumulated usage: {"input_tokens":2005,"output_tokens":4000,...,"reasoning_tokens":2943,"request_usages":[{"input_tokens":2005,"output_tokens":4000,...}]}
```

The one successful run was a normal review: Merge risk High, one traced `[BLOCKER]`, and the `<!-- codewhale-review: ... -->` tally.

## What happens
- **The request is capped at 4000.** The Low tier gets `max_output_tokens = 4_000` (`crates/tui/src/tools/review_triage.rs:188-192`). The request then sends `effective_max_output_tokens(..).min(review_budget.max_output_tokens)`, which is min(65536, 4000) = **4000** (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs:10521-10525`, sent as `max_tokens` via `review_core.rs`). DeepSeek stopped at exactly that cap.
- **The error message reports numbers that were never sent.** `review_allowance` (65536) and `review_reserve_tokens` (16384) are computed from the route ceiling *before* the triage `min` (`lib.rs:~10479-10485`). The message at `lib.rs:10586` prints them, so "65536 requested" and "16384 reserve" are both wrong for this request.
- **"Produced no review text" is not accurate.** About 1,057 visible tokens came back (4000 − 2943). Any incomplete stop reason discards them.
- **The effort cap has no effect here.** `review.rs:76-89` caps effort to Medium against the 65536-based reserve. DeepSeek then rounds `medium` up to `high` (`reasoning_preference.rs:278-284`), which is the default tier. So nothing actually leaves room inside the 4000 cap, and a single reasoning pass of about 3k tokens fails or passes by chance.

## Expected
A Low-risk review on a reasoning model either completes, or fails with an accurate message.

## Fix direction
- Compute the reported allowance and reserve, and size the effort cap, from the `min`'d value that is actually sent. On DeepSeek with a cap of 8k or less, that means `low`.
- And/or raise the Low-tier output floor for reasoning models, e.g. to max(4000, reasoning headroom).
- Say "truncated" rather than "no review text" when visible tokens came back.

issues.title: skills: first-class control over bundled install, per-skill disable, and explicit-only

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

_Searched open and closed issues for "bundled skills", "skills_dir", "system skills", "disable bundled", "per-skill", and "explicit-only"; related work is listed under References. I did not find a per-skill install/disable policy._

## What problem does this solve?

Codewhale ships a starter pack of bundled skills and installs it into `~/.codewhale/skills` on first launch and on generation upgrades. The pack is effectively all-or-nothing, and the only supported-looking way to stop installation is an undocumented side effect of `skills_dir`:

1. **Install is coupled to discovery.** `Config::bundled_skills_install_dir()` returns `None` whenever top-level `skills_dir` is set (`crates/tui/src/config.rs:7155-7158`). The installer is then never called (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs:13656`, `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:1735`). Setting `skills_dir` to the default path works as an off switch, but that is not documented; setting it to another path also changes discovery precedence.
2. **There is no per-skill control.** `SkillsConfig` has only `registry_url`, `max_install_size_bytes`, `scan_codewhale_only`, and `flat_workspace_root` (`crates/tui/src/config.rs:2993-3011`). To stop one bundled skill, a user must delete or move its directory. That is not discoverable, and the generation marker makes the result fragile: a missing `.system-installed-version` treats a missing directory as a fresh install (`crates/tui/src/skills/system.rs:581-591`). Deleting the marker while `skills_dir` is set changes nothing, because the installer never runs — a surprising interaction I hit while testing.
3. **A bundled name shadows a user's own skill.** The owned global root is discovered before `~/.agents/skills` (`crates/tui/src/skills/roots.rs:133-235`), so a bundled `debug` or `security-review` wins over a same-named skill in `~/.agents/skills`. Today the workarounds are to delete or move the bundled directory, create a project-level copy, or point `skills_dir` at a higher-precedence copy. None of these is a declarative per-name policy.
4. **Prompt visibility is per-file, not configurable.** The system prompt carries a bounded index of model-invocable skills (`crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:1968-1975`, budget at `:53-89`); bodies load only through `load_skill` (`crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:120`, `:193-197`). `explicit-only` skills cost zero prompt space, but a user cannot mark a bundled skill explicit-only in place without editing its `SKILL.md`; the edited body is then treated as user-owned and stops updating. On 0.10.2-dev, 43 model-invocable bundled skills in the current 47-skill pack contribute ~9.4k characters / ~2.4k tokens of index at full descriptions, while `batch`, `dependency-update`, `help`, and `release` are explicit-only and cost zero. That is small compared with a large `.agents` pack, but it is exactly the kind of cost a user should be able to trim declaratively.

## What should Codewhale do?

Add a declarative policy for bundled skills, separate from discovery:

```toml
[skills.bundled]
# auto (default): current behavior — install/update existing copies when
#                  skills_dir is unset; a missing directory stays gone
# all: config-authoritative — install/update every enabled name, including
#      missing ones, into the owned global root
# none: never copy or update bundled skills
install = "auto"          # "auto" | "all" | "none"

# Empty = all bundled names. Non-empty = allowlist for install and discovery.
selected = []

# Never install or discover these bundled names. Wins over `selected`.
disabled = []

# Keep these bundled names loadable through `/skill <name>`, but omit them
# from the ambient prompt index.
explicit_only = []
```

Semantics:

- `install` controls writes only; it never deletes existing files.
- `selected` (when non-empty) limits bundled names for both install and discovery.
- `disabled` wins over `selected` and `explicit_only`; the bundled copy is ignored, so a lower-precedence root such as `~/.agents/skills` can supply the same name.
- `explicit_only` applies to enabled bundled names. The skill stays available through `/skill <name>`; `load_skill` already refuses explicit-only skills for model invocation (`crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:193-197`).
- Aliases follow their canonical skill: disabling `docx` also disables `documents`, and selecting `docx` keeps `documents` available. List canonical names in the config; alias names are accepted and mapped to the canonical skill.
- Names in all three lists are validated against `BUNDLED_SKILLS`; unknown names must produce a `doctor` warning, not silently do nothing. Entries in `explicit_only` that are not enabled by `selected`/`disabled` are reported as ignored.
- Defaults preserve current behavior. `skills_dir` remains a discovery override; in `auto` mode it keeps its current implicit install-off behavior, and `install = "all"` is the explicit override. With `install = "none"` (or `auto` plus `skills_dir`), the generation marker is irrelevant because the installer never runs.
- Config never deletes files. A disabled bundled skill remains on disk until the user removes it.
- Disabled names are reported as disabled, not as unrecognized or missing.
- The existing user-edited-body guard remains: `all` does not overwrite a modified `SKILL.md`.
- The policy applies to the bundled copy only; manually installed skills and compatible-root copies with the same name are not disabled implicitly.

### Installation and re-enabling

- `auto` (default): install/update existing copies; an enabled name whose directory is missing stays gone. This preserves today's deletion-as-opt-out heuristic.
- `all`: config is authoritative; install/update every enabled name, including missing ones, even if `.system-installed-version` is current. To keep a skill gone, list it in `disabled`; deleting its directory is not an opt-out in this mode.
- `none`: no files are written; `selected`/`disabled` only filter discovery.
- `selected`/`disabled` always filter which bundled names participate. In `auto`, they do not force a missing name back; in `all`, an enabled missing name is installed.
- `install = "none"` leaves the marker untouched; switching back to `auto` resumes the marker heuristic, while `all` forces enabled names.

Diagnostics:

- `codewhale doctor` should print a bundled-skills line: install mode, marker generation, installed count, selected-but-not-installed names, disabled count, explicit-only count, shadowed names, and unknown/ignored names from the lists.
- `/skills` or `/skills inspect` should show the same status with paths and a reason per skill (`installed`, `disabled by config`, `explicit-only by config`, `shadowed by <path>`).
- `codewhale skills bundled status` is optional; config is the source of truth.

Implementation sketch:

- Add a `bundled` sub-struct to `SkillsConfig`.
- Gate `bundled_skills_install_dir()` and `install_one()` on `install`, `selected`, and `disabled`.
- During discovery, filter bundled names through `disabled`/`selected` before the first-wins merge; apply `explicit_only` to the bundled copy only, before prompt rendering.
- Reuse `SkillInvocation::ExplicitOnly` for presentation.
- Tests: `install_none_writes_nothing`, `install_none_leaves_marker_and_files_untouched`, `selected_installs_only_selected`, `disabled_bundled_copy_reveals_agents_copy`, `install_all_reinstalls_enabled_missing_skill`, `auto_keeps_deleted_bundled_skill_gone`, `disabled_bundled_skill_is_not_reinstalled`, `explicit_only_bundled_skill_is_not_in_index_but_user_invocable`, `disabling_a_canonical_alias_hides_both`, `unknown_bundled_names_are_reported_not_silent`, `doctor_reports_bundled_policy`, `defaults_preserve_current_behavior`.

### Options considered

**A. Minimal install-only switch.** Add `[skills] install_bundled = false` and `bundled_exclude = [...]`. Low effort; solves copy/update but not shadowing or prompt visibility for existing files.

**B. Separate install, discovery, and presentation (preferred).** The `[skills.bundled]` table above. Medium effort; one coherent policy, no file deletion, covers all three problems.

**C. B plus CLI/UI management.** Add `codewhale skills bundled disable/enable/status` and `/skills` toggles backed by config. Higher effort; useful for discoverability, but B is enough for a first slice.

### Use cases

- "Only `fleet-manager`, `github`, `goals`, `pdf`; do not install the rest." → `selected = [...]`, `install = "none"` or `"all"`.
- "Use my `~/.agents/skills/debug`, keep the bundled copy on disk." → `disabled = ["debug"]`.
- "Keep `handoff` installed but out of the ambient prompt." → `explicit_only = ["handoff"]`.
- "Stop all bundled installs, keep discovering what I already have." → `install = "none"`.
- "Fresh start without changing discovery of my own skills." → `install = "none"` plus `disabled = [...]` for existing bundled names.

### Impact

- No behavior change with defaults.
- Users can stop installation without a fake `skills_dir`.
- Users can choose their own version of a skill without deleting bundled files.
- Prompt budget can be trimmed without editing files.
- `doctor` and `/skills` become truthful about what is installed, disabled, shadowed, and visible.

### Open questions

- Should `disabled` reveal the next root with the same name, or hide the name entirely? Proposal: reveal the next root (the common "use my `.agents` version" case).
- Should `selected` filter discovery as well as install, or install only? Proposal: both, with `disabled` winning.
- Should `skills_dir` keep its implicit install-off behavior, or should `install` be the only switch? Proposal: keep it in `auto` mode for compatibility; `install = "all"` overrides.
- Should `explicit_only` apply to user copies too, or only bundled copies? Proposal: bundled only for the first slice; a general per-name presentation override can follow.
- Should `auto` reinstall an enabled-but-missing skill, or keep deletion-as-opt-out? Proposal: keep deletion-as-opt-out in `auto`; `all` is the explicit force-install mode.
- Should the hidden-from-index state remain `explicit-only` (user invocation only), or should there be a separate `ambient = false` state that keeps model `load_skill` available? Proposal: reuse `explicit-only` for the first slice; a separate state is a follow-up.
- Nested `[skills.bundled]` vs flat `[skills]` keys? Nested reads better; flat is easier to parse.

## Where?

TUI (terminal interface), CLI (`codewhale doctor`, proposed `codewhale skills bundled`), Docs.

## Workarounds or other tools (optional)

Today: set top-level `skills_dir` to the default path (disables the installer by side effect), delete or move individual directories, or edit a bundled `SKILL.md` to `explicit-only` (which stops updates). These work but conflate discovery and installation, are invisible to `doctor`, and are easy to undo by accident.

## Contributing

- [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this.

## References

- `crates/tui/src/config.rs:7155-7158` — `bundled_skills_install_dir()` returns `None` when `skills_dir` is set.
- `crates/tui/src/skills/system.rs:627` — `install_system_skills()`; `:581-591` — per-skill install decision.
- `crates/tui/src/lib.rs:13656`; `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:1735` — installer call sites.
- `crates/tui/src/skills/roots.rs:133-235` — global owned root before global `.agents`.
- `crates/tui/src/skills/mod.rs:53-89` — prompt budget; `:1274-1283` — configured `skills_dir` union; `:1968-1975` — index header; `:2037-2050` — full-description tier.
- `crates/tui/src/tools/skill.rs:120` — `name="list"` filters model-invocable; `:193-197` — explicit-only refusal.
- `docs/CONFIGURATION.md:2566-2581`; `docs/SKILLS.md:363-376` — current docs.
- `2c550fa8c` — commit that introduced the `skills_dir` install gate.
- #4691 — original default skill-pack design; #4698 — routing metadata and explicit-only follow-up; #4876/#4891 — marker repair; #4879 — explicit invocation and alias routing; #6779 — configured skills dirs and workspace trust.

issues.title: Engine: commit execution checkpoints atomically with transcript and results

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: reliability
labels.description: Reliability, flaky behavior, retries, fallbacks, and robustness

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against 0.10.1 development (integration commit 3a788990d0, 2026-10-04; ancestor of v0.10.1).
>
> **What remains**
> - Add one awaited commit boundary in the session owner covering step identity, phase cursor, transcript entry, tool intent/result, usage settlement and the Runtime projection; start from turn admission at crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:14653
> - Land or fold in the #6555 fsync/rename repairs first so the boundary does not duplicate them
> - Add process-kill regressions around each boundary and make restart recovery (runtime_threads.rs:18600-18670) read the committed prefix instead of terminalizing
> - Document process-crash versus power-loss guarantees and legacy-record migration
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - The cited gap is unchanged at v0.10.1: crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:14653-14663 persists save_turn_operation_binding, save_item, save_turn and save_thread one after another inside a closure, with cleanup on error but no single commit boundary
> - Store writes remain per-record: save_thread, save_turn and save_item are separate methods at crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:3019, :3031 and :3049
> - Restart recovery contains repair code for partial commits ('repair stores written by older builds that committed the interrupted parent first and crashed before its items', runtime_threads.rs:18623-18627), which confirms record sets can be partially visible
> - No commit reachable from v0.10.1 references #6837 (git log v0.10.1 --grep '#6837' is empty)
> - Prerequisite #6555 (crash-atomic write defects this issue says to reuse) is still OPEN in milestone v0.10.2

---

Source audit: public integration commit 3a788990d03a5f8b844ddbcecb9a797d6670f386, 2026-10-04. These are source-observed gaps; no process-crash reproduction or recovery test was run for this intake. Refresh consumers before implementing.

[Turn admission](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/blob/3a788990d03a5f8b844ddbcecb9a797d6670f386/crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs#L14427>) persists binding, item, turn and thread sequentially. Tool/model phase recovery needs a committed state boundary that cannot advertise partial settlement.

## Implementation and acceptance

* Introduce an awaited commit boundary in the existing session owner for step identity/version, phase cursor, exact model-visible input/history identity, transcript entry or reference, tool intent/result, usage/goal settlement and corresponding Runtime projection/event.
* A record set is visible together or rejected/recovered together. Failed commits do not dispatch handlers or publish authoritative completion. Preview deltas, if retained, are explicitly nonterminal and cannot authorize effects.
* Preserve operation-key dedup, owner-generation fencing and integrity validation. Different intent under an existing identity fails closed.
* Keep one canonical append/transcript path; migrate every touched consumer and read legacy records without losing history. No added independent session database.
* After implementation, kill a real process around each boundary and interrupt writes. Verify committed prefixes, no orphan runnable step, no falsely completed projection, duplicate admission prevention, cancellation and explicit unsupported/newer-schema handling.
* Document the actual process-crash versus power/host-loss guarantees and migration/rollback limitations.

This extends beyond #6555's enumerated repairs; reuse those fixes rather than duplicate them.

Reuse Engine::run_turn and the canonical session/transcript owner. Runtime records remain projections/indexes rather than a second transcript authority. Choose transaction mechanics in the owning implementation; this ticket does not mandate a new database or parallel writer. milestone.title: v1.0
milestone.description: Everything after 0.9.14 that belongs to the 1.0 product, undated: Responses/dialect architecture (#5092, #5093), the docs localization epic (#5482), semantic code search (#4066, #5830), CJK input (#2323), session recovery and steering designs, parked migrations (Keychain worker path #5718, account link #6028, provider wire #5851), subscription login and voice input (#5845, #5846), the desktop app (#4986), Model Lab (#1977) and cloud computers (#5836, #5837, Studio IDE #5838).

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against 0.10.1 development (integration commit 3a788990d0, 2026-10-04; that commit is an ancestor of v0.10.1 with 198 commits after it).
>
> **What remains**
> - Whole epic is open; keep this as the tracking issue and do the packets in order: #6837 (atomic checkpoint commit) first, then #6838, then #6839 and #6840
> - #6841 (Code Mode child catalogs and docs) can proceed independently
> - Acceptance journey (forced termination at admission, model/tool boundaries, nested calls, human wait, child completion) has not been built; restart path to replace is crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:18600-18670
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Restart still terminalizes work instead of recovering it at v0.10.1: crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:18616-18645 marks Queued/InProgress turns and their items Interrupted with RUNTIME_RESTART_REASON ('Interrupted by process restart', :638)
> - Engine event delivery is still an in-memory queue: crates/tui/src/core/engine/streaming.rs:31-32 reserve_event_capacity over tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender<Event>
> - Turn admission still writes binding, item, turn and thread as separate sequential saves: crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:14653-14663
> - No commit reachable from v0.10.1 references #6836, #6837, #6838, #6839, #6840 or #6841 (git log --grep, each empty)
> - All five execution packets are still OPEN on GitHub: #6837, #6838, #6839, #6840 (milestone v0.11) and #6841 (v0.10.2); reuse issues #6555, #6556, #6472, #6492, #6160, #6139 are also OPEN

---

An accepted Codewhale turn should recover its committed execution state after process restart, reuse completed work, and present an actionable unknown outcome when an external effect cannot be reconciled.

Source audit: public integration commit 3a788990d03a5f8b844ddbcecb9a797d6670f386, 2026-10-04. These are source-observed gaps; no process-crash reproduction or recovery test was run for this intake. Refresh consumers before implementing.

Current building blocks include durable admission identities, owner locks, session history, queued work and persist-before-broadcast Runtime events. However, [Runtime restart recovery](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/blob/3a788990d03a5f8b844ddbcecb9a797d6670f386/crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs#L18365>) terminalizes queued/running turns instead of recovering an execution checkpoint. [Engine event delivery](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/blob/3a788990d03a5f8b844ddbcecb9a797d6670f386/crates/tui/src/core/engine/streaming.rs#L163>) acknowledges an in-memory queue rather than a durable execution commit. Code Mode also keeps nested effect receipts in memory until its outer result.

## Work to complete

* Atomic execution checkpoint/transcript/result commit through the current authority.
* Durable model/tool intents, results and recovery policy, including every nested Code Mode call and extension core/call.
* Recoverable human waits/deadlines with explicit restart semantics.
* Durable child completion delivery and owner acknowledgment.
* Permitted Code Mode composition in canonical child catalogs, plus accurate documentation.
* Reuse existing PTY/job and client qualification issues rather than creating duplicate managers.

## Existing work to reuse

* [#6555](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/6555>): enumerated crash-atomic write defects.
* [#6556](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/6556>): retry/idempotency defects.
* [#6472](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/6472>): approval grants and pending-ask stop-on-restart policy.
* [#6492](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/6492>): machine-built child result content.
* [#6160](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/6160>): PTY byte/reconnect contract.
* [#6139](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/6139>): shared Runtime client acceptance.
* Closed [#6509](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/6509>) and [#6562](<https://github.com/Hmbown/Codewhale/issues/6562>) remain implementation context, not proof of crash durability.

## Acceptance

One provider-free, real-Engine journey is forcibly terminated at admission, model/tool boundaries, between nested calls, during a human wait, and around child completion. Restart reconstructs authorized work, never reruns a committed effect, preserves canceled/expired/denied state, deduplicates client retry and completion delivery, and shows unknown effects honestly. Reconnect is consistent across clients. PTYs attach to the same owned process or report verified loss; never silently create a replacement shell. Record exact commits, actual counts and unsupported boundaries.

An interrupted provider request may incur another charge unless the provider supports request reconciliation; ordinary shell/MCP effects cannot be promised universally exactly-once. Process-crash and power/host-loss guarantees must be stated separately.

Reuse Engine::run_turn and the canonical session/transcript owner. Runtime records remain projections/indexes rather than a second transcript authority. Choose transaction mechanics in the owning implementation; this ticket does not mandate a new database or parallel writer. Preserve migration/data-loss handling, permissions, account/workspace isolation, cancellation, route identity and budget accounting. Claim exact paths in the existing Core execution plan before product edits. Implement first, then add meaningful crash regressions; local proof, hosted CI, packaged clients and live-provider proof remain separate.

References: [Pi Durable](<https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/tree/200387122ca450d6387f033949423114a270b96c/packages/durable>), [Core execution plan](<https://linear.app/shannon-labs/document/codewhale-core-execution-plan-a11e2e1c601d>). This intake tracks implementation; it neither declares the work complete nor changes the current release cut.

## Execution packets — 2026-10-04

* Hmbown/Codewhale#6837 — Engine: commit execution checkpoints atomically with transcript and results; available to claim.
* Hmbown/Codewhale#6838 — Engine: recover model and tool steps from durable intents and results; blocked by Hmbown/Codewhale#6837.
* Hmbown/Codewhale#6839 — Engine: persist human waits and continuation deadlines with explicit restart policy; blocked by Hmbown/Codewhale#6837, Hmbown/Codewhale#6838.
* Hmbown/Codewhale#6840 — Engine: persist child completion delivery and owner acknowledgment; blocked by Hmbown/Codewhale#6837, Hmbown/Codewhale#6838.
* Hmbown/Codewhale#6841 — Code Mode: retain permitted composition in child catalogs and reconcile documentation; available to claim.

Implement checkpoint commits first, then durable effect/phase recovery, then human waits and child delivery. Code Mode child/documentation parity can proceed independently; its durability claims depend on Hmbown/Codewhale#6838. Reuse #6160 for PTY/jobs and #6139 for shared Runtime client acceptance. Client packaging/native qualification stays with existing client owners. No new source writer has been appointed by this intake.

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against 0.9.12 (source-verified at 89621d5a5 on 2026-09-11).
>
> **What remains**
> - Write the short design the issue asks for: one id scheme for workshop outputs, scratchpad files and Agent Mail under the session directory, with the session-specific path appended as history and not spliced into the frozen prompt prefix
> - Smallest useful slice: one tool to send Agent Mail to a thread/task id and one to read the caller's inbox, on top of crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs (list_agent_mail_for_thread) and crates/protocol/src/agent_mail.rs
> - Decide cross-scope reads of art_<id> handles inside one session tree (crates/tui/src/tools/tool_result_retrieval.rs:485): resolve with owner disclosure or mint scope-naming handles
> - Create the session scratch directory and name its shape in the base prompt
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - No session scratchpad exists: 'scratchpad' appears only in unrelated files (crates/tui/src/tui/setup/model_draft.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/setup/fleet_draft.rs, crates/tui/src/tui/underwater.rs, docs/design/WORKFLOWS_GOAL_PARITY.md) and the only prompt hit is a test helper comment at crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:3652
> - Agent Mail protocol and routes exist - crates/protocol/src/agent_mail.rs; crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs:2484-2492 (POST /v1/agent-mail, GET /v1/threads/{id}/agent-mail, deliver, read); crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:9128 (list_agent_mail_for_thread)
> - Agent Mail still has no agent-facing surface: git grep for agent_mail/agent-mail in crates/tui/src/tools, crates/tui/src/commands and crates/tui/src/prompts at v0.10.1 returns nothing; crates/tui/src/tools/ has no mail tool file
> - Cross-scope artifact handles still fail with the same message quoted in the 2026-09-15 comment - crates/tui/src/tools/tool_result_retrieval.rs:485 ('was not found for the active session')
> - No commit in v0.10.0..v0.10.1 references #6086; no scratchpad or Agent Mail entry in CHANGELOG.md:10-1306

---

Founder direction (carried since the 2026-09-11 handoff): scratchpad, Agent Mail and workshop should work together.

## Current state (source-verified 2026-09-11 at 89621d5a5)

- **Scratchpad: does not exist.** The sole base prompt (`crates/tui/src/prompts/text.rs`, `BASE_PROMPT`) never mentions a scratch directory, so the model writes into the user's repo or `/tmp`. Repo-wide, "scratchpad" appears only in unrelated strings.
- **Agent Mail: real.** `RuntimeThreadManager::list_agent_mail_for_thread` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:5970`) — addressable per thread, durable envelopes, read-marking, and an explicit trust framing ("non-authoritative and cannot grant permission") that must be kept. Consumed at `runtime_api.rs:4762`. Parent/child messaging is a separate channel (`tools/subagent/mod.rs`, `queue_parent_message`).
- **Workshop: bounds outputs.** `[workshop] read_result_max_bytes` (`config.rs:3202`, `tools/file.rs:519-528`, `tools/large_output_router.rs`) — an output-size bound, not an agent working store.

## Proposed shape (to be settled by design)

Three stores, one addressing scheme, session-scoped under `~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>/` where the approval log already lives:

- workshop bounds *outputs*,
- scratchpad bounds *working files*,
- Agent Mail bounds *messages*.

## Hard constraint

The base prompt is a session-pinned KV-cache prefix (`docs/CACHE.md`). The *shape* of the path may go in the frozen prefix; the session-specific value must be appended as history, never spliced into the prefix.

## Notes

Unfiled until now; no implementation exists. This needs a short design pass before a slice.
