issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against v0.10.0 (filed 2026-09-25; cites commit 5cf9db3 on the 0.10.1 development line).
>
> **What remains**
> - Add author (owner or agent session) and date fields to memory entries in crates/memory/src/model.rs and to instruction layers loaded by crates/tui/src/project_context, taking repo-file authorship from git
> - Render agent-authored memory and instruction text as notes rather than rules during prompt assembly in crates/tui/src/prompts.rs, with a test
> - Add a non-overridable honesty statement to BASE_PROMPT in crates/tui/src/prompts/text.rs and a regression test beside only_the_constitution_states_precedence
> - Add the 'file says X, you said Y; update it?' offer when a live request contradicts an instruction file
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - The ranking exists and puts the user's turn above the constitution: '### Whose word wins' lists '1. The user's request, this turn. 2. This constitution.' (crates/tui/src/prompts/text.rs:96-109)
> - Only facts are protected: 'the user may override a fact, but no one may invent one' (crates/tui/src/prompts/text.rs:107-109; repeated in AUTHORITY_RECAP at crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:1019-1023); no clause makes honesty non-overridable (git grep for honesty/cannot remove/always agree in crates/tui/src/prompts finds only text.rs:55)
> - The test the issue wants a neighbour for exists and has no honesty counterpart: only_the_constitution_states_precedence (crates/tui/src/prompts.rs:2831)
> - Memory entries carry no author field: struct Memory has id, revision, status, draft, created_at, updated_at, content_hash (crates/memory/src/model.rs:188-196); git grep for author/proposed_by/approved_by in crates/memory/src/store.rs and lib.rs finds nothing
> - crates/tui/src/native_memory.rs has no author or claim marking (git grep for author/agent_authored/claim returns nothing)
> - Prompt-segment provenance exists only for the preview of where prompt bytes came from, not for who wrote instructions (SegmentProvenance, crates/tui/src/prompts/base_preview.rs:72)

---

The instruction ranking already exists in `crates/tui/src/prompts/text.rs` ("Whose word wins", 5cf9db3). This issue adds the three pieces the prompt text can't enforce by itself. Founder-approved direction, 2026-09-25 (from codewhale-app #90).

## Why

Instruction files and memory are snapshots of someone's past intent. Often a past agent session wrote them, not the owner, and people change. Today agent-written text ranks the same as owner-written text, and nothing in code keeps a live request from switching off the agent's honesty.

## Scope

1. **Provenance as data.** Every instruction layer and memory entry the Engine loads carries its author (owner, or agent session) and a date, as real fields rather than prose. Repo files get this from git; Engine memory needs it natively. A deletion leaves a trace.
2. **Agent-written text is a claim, not a rule.** Prompt assembly marks agent-authored instruction or memory content as notes. It needs owner confirmation before it acts as a rule. Anything the owner wrote or approved outranks it.
3. **Name conflicts, don't resolve them silently.** When the live request contradicts a file, follow the request, then offer to update the file ("AGENTS.md says X, you said Y; update it?").
4. **Honesty can't be overridden.** A live request ("always agree with me") cannot remove honesty or the agent's values. Today the user's turn ranks above the constitution, and only facts are explicitly protected ("no one may invent one"). Add a regression test next to `only_the_constitution_states_precedence`.

## Acceptance

* Provenance fields are served for instruction layers and memory entries, and are visible in the prompt projection.
* A test shows agent-authored memory is rendered as a claim, not a rule.
* A test shows a user turn cannot drop the honesty clause from the assembled prompt.
* The precedence statement still lives only in `BASE_PROMPT`.

## Not in scope

* UI. The desktop app will show provenance once the Engine serves it.
* Any second prompt authority, and any TypeScript or Effect port. Rust types and tests carry the enforcement.

issues.title: Model Lab: turn local session traces into datasets, evals and fine-tuning jobs

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: providers
labels.description: Model providers, routing, auth, catalogs and pricing

milestone.title: Backlog
milestone.description: Kept ideas without a release commitment: platform requests, integrations and speculative features. Say why when you pick one up or close it; nothing here blocks a release.

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against 0.8.42 (filed 2026-05-24; body sequences work from v0.8.43 onward and targets v0.10.0).
>
> **What remains**
> - Pick one first slice and file it separately: a local, explicit redacted-trace JSONL export built on the existing /export handler in crates/tui/src/commands/groups/session/export.rs
> - Rewrite the issue body: its dependency and sequencing sections cite v0.8.43-v0.10.0 milestones that have all shipped without this work
> - Keep docs/MODEL_LAB.md as the single design source and reduce this issue to a tracking epic that links to it
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - No /model-lab command, workset installer or ModelLab type exists: git grep -i 'model[-_ ]lab|workset|ModelLab' v0.10.1 -- crates returns no code matches (only unrelated model_label strings)
> - docs/MODEL_LAB.md:1-10 at v0.10.1 describes Model Lab as roadmap language only
> - docs/MODEL_LAB.md:33-43 lists native HF Hub workflows, Unsloth/NeMo/Arcee integrations, a Model Lab UI and eval/training orchestration as 'Still Planned'
> - The only shipped dependency is the Hugging Face inference provider: crates/config/src/lib.rs:359 (huggingface provider config) and docs/MODEL_LAB.md:20-23
> - CHANGELOG.md:9201-9204 records that eval/export surfaces, model passports and Hub workflows were explicitly deferred from v0.9 (#2705, #2680, #2727)
> - Session export today is transcript-to-clipboard/file only, with no redacted dataset or trace JSONL: crates/tui/src/commands/groups/session/export.rs:37

---

## Goal

Let users turn their own CodeWhale coding sessions into curated datasets, eval suites, and optional fine-tuning jobs for open-weight models. CodeWhale becomes the harness where people can improve open models, not just consume them.

## Where this fits in the stack

- **CodeWhale** is the workbench — runs the agent, owns the traces, owns the consent surface.
- **Providers** are where models run (DeepSeek, Hugging Face Inference Providers, OpenRouter, Novita, Fireworks, Together, Hyperbolic, SiliconFlow, NVIDIA NIM, plus local: vLLM, SGLang, Ollama, llama.cpp, TGI).
- **Worksets** are curated optional capability packs — they extend the lab without bloating core.
- **Fin** is the cheap evaluator / router / verifier seam (Goal mode in v0.8.43, generalized verifier preview in v0.8.46, eval pipeline in v0.9.0).
- **Goal mode** (v0.8.43, #1976) is the long-running loop that turns model changes into measured improvements.

Model Lab is the user-facing surface that sits on top of all of that. It turns the workbench's accumulated traces into datasets, runs eval replays, hands curated data to a fine-tuning backend, and integrates open-source worksets without vendoring them into core.

## Non-goals

- **No automatic upload.** Nothing leaves the user's machine unless they explicitly ran an export command.
- **No hidden telemetry.** Each workset declares its telemetry posture; off by default.
- **No silent hosted routing.** Provider / backend selection is always explicit.
- **No "download random model and trust it."** Every model installed to the lab goes through an explicit install with license + provenance shown.
- **No proprietary-model-first workflow.** Open-weight models are the first-class target.
- **No provider lock-in.** Hosted backends are pluggable; the export format is provider-neutral.
- **No vendoring of heavy GPU / Python / NVIDIA dependencies into CodeWhale core.** Worksets install on-demand.

## Provider vs Workset — the architectural split

- **Providers** live in CodeWhale's provider abstraction (v0.8.47 work). They are where models run. They are not optional; they are how the agent talks to a model. Each one has a config block, an auth path, and parity coverage in v0.8.45.
- **Worksets** live in Model Lab. They are optional capability packs that bring open-source ML tooling into the lab loop. Each one installs on-demand and declares license, telemetry posture, network egress, GPU / Python deps, and what data leaves the machine if any.

**Hugging Face is BOTH** — it is a first-class provider (Inference Providers / Router) AND the open-model registry workset (Hub API, model cards, datasets, adapters, Safetensors, Jobs). The two roles ship through different surfaces; they share auth (`HF_TOKEN` / `HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY` alias).

## Architecture: Worksets as the integration shape

CodeWhale core stays lean. Worksets are curated optional packs.

```
/model-lab worksets list                # show installed + available
/model-lab worksets install hf
/model-lab worksets install unsloth
/model-lab worksets install nemo
/model-lab worksets install arcee
/model-lab worksets install serving
/model-lab worksets install eval
/model-lab worksets install observability
/model-lab worksets install training-infra
/model-lab worksets remove <pack>
/model-lab worksets info <pack>         # license, telemetry, network, deps
```

## Initial worksets

### Hugging Face Workset

The open-model operating system. Even though HF is also a first-class **provider** for inference (lands in v0.8.47), the **workset** is the registry / dataset / adapter / model-card layer.

- **Model discovery**: search open-weight coding models, filter by license, base model, quantization, tool/reasoning support.
- **Model passport**: show license, base model, context length, chat template, tool-call support, reasoning support, eval results, gated / private status. Pulls from HF Hub API + model cards.
- **Hub integration**: private / public model repos, adapter upload, dataset upload, model-card generation.
- **Dataset path**: export CodeWhale transcripts → redact → dataset → train / eval.
- **Runtime bridges**: Transformers, PEFT, TRL, Accelerate, Safetensors, Inference Providers, LightEval.
- **HF Jobs** (later): compute workflows for training/eval runs initiated from the lab.

Auth: `HF_TOKEN` (canonical) or `HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY` (alias). No upload without an explicit command. Boundary: gated models require explicit consent flow before any pull.

Docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers · https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/main/api · https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/model-cards · https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/jobs

### Unsloth Workset

Local fine-tuning, oriented around the "make Brother Whale better at my workflow" path.

- SFT / LoRA / QLoRA as the first simple path.
- Later: DPO / GRPO-style preference-based improvement loops.
- Fin as preflight: checks dataset shape, license / provenance, VRAM estimate, model compatibility, and whether the result is actually deployable.
- Output adapters can be pushed to the user's HF repo via the HF Workset.

Docs: https://unsloth.ai/docs

### NeMo Workset (NVIDIA NeMo, Apache-2.0)

- **Data Designer** — synthetic dataset generation from seed traces (https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/DataDesigner). Telemetry opt-in per their README.
- **Curator** — PII / secret redaction (`PiiModifier` over email, person, phone, URL, location). Useful before any trace export leaves the machine.
- **Evaluator** — reproducible model evaluation; OpenAI-compatible API; coding benchmarks; function-calling; long-context; agentic suites (https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Evaluator).
- **Guardrails** — optional policy rails on prompt injection, tool-use boundaries, data export (https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails).
- **Aligner** — later-stage post-training path (https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo-Aligner). Not a first-run default.

Boundary: no traces sent to NVIDIA Build or any hosted endpoint by default.

### Arcee Workset (Arcee open-source catalog)

The "make your own model" path — merge, distill, evaluate, serve open-weight checkpoints.

- **Trinity model family** — open-weight multi-turn / tool-use / structured-output (`arcee-ai/Trinity-Large-Thinking`, `Trinity-Large-Preview`, `Trinity-Mini`, `Trinity-Nano-Preview`).
- **MergeKit** (https://github.com/arcee-ai/mergekit) — model-merging library. Build "my coding agent blend" from open checkpoints, run through CodeWhale evals.
- **DistillKit** (https://github.com/arcee-ai/DistillKit) — distillation toolkit.
- **Spectrum + Arcee Fusion** — advanced merge methods as recipes.
- **Coder / Caller / Maestro / Blitz lines** — verify license + availability before first-class.

```
/model-lab arcee merge <recipe>
/model-lab arcee distill <recipe>
/model-lab arcee eval <model>
/model-lab arcee compare <model-a> <model-b>
```

### Serving Workset

Local runtime recipes for self-hosted serving.

- **vLLM** — high-throughput batched serving.
- **SGLang** — structured generation, good for tool-use workloads.
- **TGI** (Text Generation Inference) — HuggingFace's serving stack.
- **llama.cpp / Ollama** — CPU / consumer-GPU path.

Each gets a recipe: install + config + smoke test + which CodeWhale provider config to use to talk to it.

### Eval Workset

Reproducible eval harnesses and CodeWhale-specific replay evals.

- **SWE-bench** — software-engineering benchmark.
- **Terminal-Bench** — terminal-agent benchmark.
- **BFCL** — Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard.
- **LiveCodeBench** — live coding benchmark.
- **CodeWhale replay evals** — exported traces become eval suites; baseline-vs-finetune comparisons.

### Observability Workset

Trace export and analysis sinks (all opt-in).

- Per-turn cost / latency / reasoning-token / tool-call / failure stats.
- Phoenix-style local trace UI.
- Opik / Langfuse-style export adapters (later).
- Boundary: opt-in per sink, redaction review mandatory before any external sink.

### Training Infra Workset

Hosted execution adapters for fine-tuning / eval runs.

- **Prime Intellect** — distributed fine-tuning.
- **Tinker** — managed fine-tuning service.
- **HF Jobs** — compute workflows on the HF Hub.
- **RunPod / Lambda-style** — on-demand GPU rental (later).

```
/model-lab finetune --provider prime-intellect
/model-lab finetune --provider tinker
/model-lab finetune --provider hf-jobs
```

## Core surface (CodeWhale-native, no workset required)

```
/model-lab capture                      # mark current session as a candidate trace
/model-lab export                       # selected sessions → redacted JSONL on disk
/model-lab redact                       # local redaction review before any upload
/model-lab dataset --from successful-turns
/model-lab eval --against current
/model-lab promote --if-better          # only swap default model if eval clears bar
```

Each session export includes prompts, tool calls, diffs, test results, approvals, failures, and final outcome labels — enough to reconstruct the task and grade it. Format is provider-neutral.

## Strong-shape future flow

```
/model-lab capture
/model-lab redact
/model-lab dataset --from successful-turns
/model-lab finetune --workset unsloth --base qwen-or-deepseek-or-glm
/model-lab eval --against current
/model-lab promote --if-better
```

## Dependencies (what unblocks this work)

- **Goal mode + Fin wakeup** (v0.8.43, #1976) — the loop that produces measurable outcomes.
- **HF as first-class provider** (v0.8.47) — the provider abstraction that makes HF Inference Providers / Router a real config block.
- **Verifier preview** (v0.8.46) — generalizes Fin to all claim-of-done events.
- **Eval pipeline** (v0.9.0 sub-project B) — the measurement substrate that grades outcomes.

Until those land, Model Lab is design-only. After they land, the export → redact → eval → finetune surface (plus worksets) becomes implementable.

## Sequencing

- **v0.8.43 → v0.9.0**: stabilize the substrate. No Model Lab implementation yet; this issue stays as living design.
- **Post-v0.9.0 (target v0.10.0)**: scope a dedicated Model Lab release. First wave: HF + Unsloth + NeMo + Arcee + Serving + Eval. Hosted backends: Prime Intellect + Tinker + HF Jobs.
- **v0.10.x**: Observability + Training Infra worksets + community-contributed adapters.

## Safety boundary recap

- Exports require an explicit command — no background telemetry, no session shipping, no auto-fine-tune.
- Redaction review is mandatory before any upload.
- Provider adapters and worksets are opt-in per backend / per pack.
- Each workset declares license, telemetry, network egress, and dependency footprint at install time.
- Gated HF models require explicit consent before any pull.

## Related

- #1976 (v0.8.43) Goal mode — the loop this depends on.
- v0.8.46 verifier preview — the generalized Fin path.
- v0.8.47 milestone — HF as first-class provider lands here.
- v0.9.0 milestone — the eval pipeline that grades the outcomes.

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against v0.10.0 (filed 2026-09-24; feature proposal, not version-specific).
>
> **What remains**
> - Founder decisions D1-D8 are still pending; nothing can be built until they are recorded in the issue
> - Add a class (ordinary / elevating / secret / handoff) to SettingDef in crates/config/src/settings_schema.rs
> - Add crates/tui/src/tools/settings.rs with search/read/propose, the proposal event and approval card, applying through set_config_value
> - Extend settings_command in crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/config.rs to start a model turn for free text and to support /settings undo
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - No settings tool exists: git ls-tree v0.10.1 crates/tui/src/tools/ has no settings*.rs file
> - /settings still rejects free text: settings_command returns 'Usage: /settings [text]' for any argument other than text/show/diagnostic(s) (crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/config.rs:547-553; usage string at crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/mod.rs:83)
> - No change classification in the schema: git grep for elevating/SettingClass/ChangeClass in crates/tui/src finds only unrelated sandbox elevation (crates/tui/src/tui/approval/elevation.rs:19)
> - Building blocks the design relies on are present: SETTINGS_SCHEMA (crates/config/src/settings_schema.rs:503), set_config_value (crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/config.rs:1954) and nearest-key lookup (config.rs:536)
> - No commit in v0.10.0..v0.10.1 and no CHANGELOG line cites #6564 (git log --grep '#6564' is empty)

---

Founder ask: tell Codewhale what you want the settings to be, it proposes concrete changes, you approve or reject each.

## Design
- A new `settings` tool with actions `search`, `read` and `propose`. It never writes. The catalog stays out of the static prompt.
- `propose` blocks on the same wait as `request_user_input`. The card shows one row per change: current → new value, file/scope, takes effect now / next session / restart, and a "what this does" line from the schema. The model's reason is shown separately as untrusted text.
- Each accepted row applies through `commands::set_config_value` (the same path as `/config`, `/set`, presets and the settings editor), using the existing lossless writers.
- `/settings <what you want>` starts a model turn. `/settings undo` restores the values saved before the last apply.

## Guardrails
- Each change has a class: ordinary / elevating / secret / handoff. Loosening posture or sandbox, shell, allow rules, telemetry, notes_path and exec-policy off are elevating. Each elevating row needs its own confirmation and is never part of "Apply all".
- Secrets are never proposable.
- base_url, MCP servers, hooks, trust paths and the router are handoff rows: they show a ready-to-run command and don't write.
- Only an interactive parent session with a person present may `propose`. Sub-agents, automations and headless runs get search/read only, and this is not inherited by children.
- v1 writes user scope only.
- Keys must exist in `SETTINGS_SCHEMA`; unknown keys get the nearest valid key. Values are dry-run through the real parser.

## Slice 1
Schema classification, the sub-agent model keys, nearest-key lookup, `tools/settings.rs`, the proposal event and card, `/settings` entry and undo, docs and tests: nothing written on propose; "Apply all" excludes elevating rows; children can't propose; secrets are refused.

Decisions pending: D1–D8 (founder).

<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): partly done. Filed against 0.10.0-dev (main, 2026-09-24).
>
> **What remains**
> - Declare every config.toml key in one table (extend SETTINGS_SCHEMA in crates/config/src/settings_schema.rs or a sibling), replacing OTHER_READER_ROOT_KEYS in crates/tui/src/config_keys.rs, with a CI test that each key has a non-test reader
> - Generate the docs/CONFIGURATION.md key table and the config doctor unknown-key warnings from that table
> - Write config_version and run a one-time lossless migration that also moves ~/.deepseek state to ~/.codewhale and root model to [providers.<active>]
> - After the migration window, delete the .deepseek path and DEEPSEEK_* legacy readers
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - Legacy root base_url/api_key migration shipped: crates/config/src/legacy_root.rs:1-28 canonicalizes them into [providers.<name>] on every parse and write, with 'codewhale config migrate --prefer' (crates/cli/src/lib.rs:5390); CHANGELOG.md:618 (#6394)
> - Unknown/unread config.toml keys are now detected from the reader structs for 'config set' and 'config doctor' (crates/tui/src/config_keys.rs:1-10, #6563; ConfigCommand::Doctor at crates/cli/src/lib.rs:5365), and dead keys were removed in 6d526eabfb (#6516)
> - NOT done: SETTINGS_SCHEMA still declares only settings (crates/config/src/settings_schema.rs:503); config.toml roots are covered by a hand-kept OTHER_READER_ROOT_KEYS list plus struct reflection (crates/tui/src/config_keys.rs:21-40), not one declaration table
> - NOT done: no config_version key anywhere (git grep 'config_version|CONFIG_VERSION' in crates is empty); only route_preferences_version exists (config_keys.rs:39)
> - NOT done: legacy readers remain - 971 lines mention '.deepseek' and 1,388 lines mention DEEPSEEK_* in crates/**/*.rs at v0.10.1 (git grep -c)

---

Follow-up to #6516 (dead keys) and #6394 (legacy root base_url).

1. **Declared keys.** Extend the `SETTINGS_SCHEMA` rule, which today covers only `settings.toml`, to every `config.toml` key. Add a CI test that every active key has a non-test reader. Generate the CONFIGURATION.md key table and the `config check` unknown/dead-key warnings from that table, so docs and code cannot drift.
2. **Versioned migration.** Write `config_version` into config. Migrate once, losslessly (the writer already keeps unknown keys): root `base_url`/`api_key`/`model` move to `[providers.<active>]` with an explicit `provider =`, and `~/.deepseek` paths move to `~/.codewhale`. After the migration window, delete the legacy readers (~271 `.deepseek` path references, ~400 `DEEPSEEK_*` literals, including the dead env twins in #6516).
- A migration never resurrects removed credentials, and never silently resets a config that fails to parse (both are Cline failure modes to avoid).

releases.name: Codewhale v0.10.2
releases.body:
## What's in v0.10.2


Codewhale v0.10.2 adds an animated pet view (`/pet on`), a live Terminal work
dock, per-chat composer colors (`/color`) and a one-time note on the first
start after an update that says what changed. It closes three session
data-loss paths and a `codewhale web` session leak; adds the default Runtime
daemon socket locations to the sandbox deny-list; holds a `curl` or `wget` that uploads a
credential; refuses shell commands containing invisible Unicode; keeps the
Linux sandbox working when a hidden credential directory is a symlink; and
reduces idle TUI redraw work. `/undo` takes back a whole
request, including long and multiline prompts. `exec --auto` explains its
Full Access default, honors an explicitly stricter sandbox, and saves
tool-enabled runs and their failure receipts. Local runtimes appear during
onboarding, `/diff` works outside a Git repository, DeepSeek's Responses route
no longer rejects replayed tool history, and contributor fixes improve token
accounting, relay model lists, localized replies and Windows launcher
guidance. Delegated work continues without model-invented turn or time caps,
and independent workflow steps can continue after another child fails.

## Install

### Recommended — official GitHub release

New macOS/Linux install (checksummed binaries from this release):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | CODEWHALE_VERSION="v0.10.2" sh
"$HOME/.local/bin/codewhale" --version
```

For Windows, use the matching installer or archive below. For an existing
direct install, run `codewhale update`; it prints the executable path and
keeps newer builds. If the install directory is occupied by a different build,
use the fresh-directory migration in [the installation guide](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md).

### Secondary packaging — npm and Cargo

```bash
npm install -g codewhale
# or build from source
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The wrapper downloads the matched `codewhale` and `codew` command assets
from this Release. Both contain the same compiled runtime.

### Docker / GHCR

```bash
docker run --rm -it \
  -e DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" \
  -v codewhale-home:/home/codewhale/.codewhale \
  ghcr.io/codewhale-hq/codewhale:v0.10.2
```

The image exposes the same runtime as both `codewhale` and `codew`. The
`latest` tag is also updated on release.

### Cargo (Linux / macOS)

```bash
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The Cargo package installs `codewhale`. Cargo cannot create a second command
alias from one binary target; users who want the shorter spelling can add a
`codew` symlink to that installed executable. The npm, Homebrew, archive,
shell-installer, and container channels install both command names directly.

### Manual download — platform archives (recommended)

Each archive below contains the same runtime under the `codewhale` and
`codew` command names, plus an install script:

| Platform | Archive | Install script |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x64 | `codewhale-linux-x64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Linux ARM64 | `codewhale-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Android ARM64 (Termux) | `codewhale-android-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| macOS x64 | `codewhale-macos-x64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| macOS ARM | `codewhale-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Windows x64 (installer) | `CodeWhaleSetup.exe` | NSIS setup |
| Windows x64 | `codewhale-windows-x64.zip` | `install.bat` |
| Windows x64 (portable) | `codewhale-windows-x64-portable.zip` | — |
| Windows ARM64 | `codewhale-windows-arm64.zip` | `install.bat` |
| Windows ARM64 (portable) | `codewhale-windows-arm64-portable.zip` | — |

**Unix (Linux / macOS):**
```bash
tar xzf codewhale-<platform>.tar.gz
cd codewhale-<platform>
./install.sh
```

**Windows:**
- For the installer path, run `CodeWhaleSetup.exe`; it installs
  `codewhale.exe`, `codew.exe`, and `codewhale.bat` under
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CodeWhale\bin`, adds that directory to the
  current-user PATH, and creates a Start Menu shortcut that prefers
  Windows Terminal (`wt.exe`) when it is installed.
- Extract the archive for your machine: `codewhale-windows-x64.zip` or
  `codewhale-windows-arm64.zip`
- Double-click `codewhale.bat` (not the raw `.exe`) to launch
- Run `install.bat` to copy the binaries and launcher to `%USERPROFILE%\bin`
- Add `%USERPROFILE%\bin` to your PATH

The **portable** Windows archive skips the install script — extract and run `codewhale.bat` from any directory. The NSIS installer is currently unsigned and may trigger Windows SmartScreen until a signing certificate is wired into the release pipeline.

Each platform also has **bare, unarchived** `codewhale-<platform>` and
`codew-<platform>` assets. The seven `codewhale-tui-<platform>` filenames
attached to v0.9.5 are byte-identical compatibility copies used only to let
already-installed v0.9.4 clients discover and cross this single-binary
transition; current installers do not expose a third runtime. The legacy npm
package `deepseek-tui` is deprecated and is not republished. For migration
from v0.8.x legacy binary names, see `docs/REBRAND.md`.

### Verify (recommended)

Download the checksum manifests from this Release and verify:

```bash
# Linux — archive bundles
sha256sum -c codewhale-bundles-sha256.txt --ignore-missing

# Linux — individual binaries
sha256sum -c codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt --ignore-missing

# macOS
shasum -a 256 -c codewhale-bundles-sha256.txt --ignore-missing
shasum -a 256 -c codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt --ignore-missing
```

<details>

<summary>Full release notes</summary>

The full notes exceed GitHub's release-description limit. Read the [complete changelog for v0.10.2](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/blob/v0.10.2/CHANGELOG.md).

</details>

issues.body:
## Summary

Map user message edits in MS Teams into the same routed system events the Slack channel already emits, so the agent learns when a user changes their message after sending it. Teams delivers these edits to the bot as a standard `messageUpdate` activity — Microsoft documents that "When you edit a message, the agent gets a notification of the edit message activity" — but the OpenClaw MS Teams extension currently drops that activity at its ingress admission gate. Slack, Telegram, Signal, and Matrix already surface user edits to the agent; MS Teams is the only major channel where the platform hands the event to the bot and the extension discards it.

## Problem to solve

On every major bundled channel except MS Teams, a user's message edit reaches the agent through a routed system event — `docs/channels/slack/events.md` states the contract: "Message edits/deletes are mapped into system events," and Telegram/Signal/Matrix implement it in code. MS Teams is the outlier in the opposite direction: the platform half goes further than any sibling — the edit activity is delivered straight to the bot — and the extension discards it. The user's correction produces no re-processing, no follow-up correction, no system event: a documented contract unfulfilled on the one channel whose platform already delivers the raw material.

Three layers of evidence:

1. **The platform delivers edits to the bot.** From the official Microsoft Teams agent documentation ("Conversations with an agent", section *Receive edit message activity*, scope listed as **All**):
   - "When you edit a message, the agent gets a notification of the edit message activity."
   - The handler example reads the new text directly: `app.on('messageEdit', async ({ activity, send }) => { const editedMessage = activity.text; ... })`.
   - The documented payload is a standard activity: `"type":"messageUpdate"` with `"channelData":{"eventType":"editMessage"}` — i.e. the edit carries the full new text and is distinguishable from undelete/soft-delete events.

2. **The extension discards it.** In `extensions/msteams/src/msteams-ingress.ts`, the admission gate only lets two activity types through:

   ```ts
   function isDispatchableActivity(activity: MSTeamsIngressActivity): boolean {
     return (
       activity.type === "message" ||
       (activity.type === "invoke" && activity.name === "adaptiveCard/action")
     );
   }
   ```

   A repo-wide search for `messageUpdate` finds no non-test handling anywhere — the only MS Teams hit is the ingress test, which journals the drop: `await ingress.accept(activity({ id: "edit", type: "messageUpdate" }));` followed by `expect(...).toEqual(["adaptive", "message"])` ("journals only message turns and adaptive-card agent turns"). There is no `messageUpdate` branch, no `OnMessageEdit`-equivalent hook on the extension's `MSTeamsActivityHandler`, and no routed system event.

3. **The rest of the family already does this.**
   - Telegram registers edits straight into the inbound pipeline: `bot.on("edited_message", pipeline.handle); bot.on("edited_channel_post", pipeline.handle);` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-pipeline.ts`).
   - Signal folds the edit envelope into the normal data message: `const dataMessage = envelope.dataMessage ?? envelope.editMessage?.dataMessage;` (`extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts`).
   - Matrix consumes `m.replace` relations (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/media-text.ts`) and documents it in `SPEC-SUPPORT.md` ("| Edits | `m.replace` | in/out/tools |").
   - Slack routes them as system events via `enqueueRoutedSystemEvent` (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/messages.ts`).
   - The outbound side is already merged: PR #49925 ("msteams: add message edit and delete support") brought the agent's own `editMessageMSTeams`/`deleteMessageMSTeams` proactive actions "bringing feature parity with Slack, Discord, and Telegram for Tier 1 messaging operations". The inbound half of that parity — reacting to what *users* edit — is what's missing.

## Proposed solution

Keep the existing system-event contract and wire edits in at the ingress, mirroring the Slack `message_changed` shape:

1. **Admission**: extend `isDispatchableActivity` in `extensions/msteams/src/msteams-ingress.ts` to also accept `activity.type === "messageUpdate"`.
2. **Identity/dedupe**: the ingress currently uses the raw activity id as the stable redelivery key (per its own comment: "@microsoft/teams.api's Activity contract defines id as unique on the channel... the raw activity id is the stable redelivery key"). Teams edit activities reuse the original message's activity id, so a bare id would make every edit look like a redelivery of the original message. Compose the event id with the update semantics, e.g. `${activity.id}:messageUpdate`, and coordinate with the durable-ingress dedupe work tracking in #130038 (which already documents id-aliasing surprises) so the two fixes agree on one dedupe key design.
3. **Event mapping**: in the monitor/turn handling, map a `messageUpdate` whose `channelData.eventType === "editMessage"` to a routed system event like Slack's: `eventKind`/describe/contextKey triple, e.g. describe `` `MSTeams message edited in ${channelLabel}.` `` with a contextKey of `msteams:message:edited:${conversationId}:${activityId}` and the new text attached, so reply-chain/session context resolves the same way as a fresh message.
4. **Scope — edits only**: handle `eventType === "editMessage"`. `softDeleteMessage`/`undeleteMessage` events share the `messageUpdate`/`messageDelete` types but are a separate behavioral surface; leave them out of this change and their `messageDelete` counterpart can be a follow-up, matching how the Telegram/Signal/Matrix precedents cover the edit face.
5. **Tests**: extend `msteams-ingress.test.ts` — a `messageUpdate` activity with `channelData.eventType = "editMessage"` must be journaled and dispatched; one with a different eventType must still be dropped; a repeated edit (same id) must not be treated as a redelivery of the original message.

## Alternatives considered

- **Drop the admission gate and filter later in the monitor**: keeps `isDispatchableActivity` untouched but floods the journal queue with reaction/typing/invoke noise the gate exists to exclude, and turns the `unsupported-activity` error reason into dead code. The gate is the right place for the type decision.
- **Silently rewrite the stored message history instead of emitting a system event**: the agent would see new text only if it re-read history; nothing tells a running session that a correction arrived. The Slack contract ("mapped into system events") exists precisely so a live session can react; history rewrite alone doesn't trigger anything.
- **Wait for #130038's dedupe fix to land first**: the two changes touch the same key semantics, but #130038 is about route-distinct activities sharing an id; this proposal needs the update face of the same design. Doing them together is the cheapest way to one coherent dedupe key, not a reason to sequence them.
- **Bundle deletes/undeletes with edits**: Telegram, Signal, and Matrix precedents cover the edit face; the delete face adjoins the outbound delete family and deserves its own issue with its own evidence.

## Impact

- MS Teams users get an agent that notices corrections: "actually, use X instead" on an already-answered message re-enters the session instead of being silently ignored.
- MS Teams is a major, bundled channel, and the edit notification is delivered for **All** scopes (personal, group, channel) per Microsoft's activity table — so this closes the gap everywhere the bot is installed.
- No new permissions, API surface, or schema: the activity already arrives at the bot's messaging endpoint; this only routes what arrives today into the existing routed-system-event pipeline, matching the other four channels.

## Evidence / examples

- Microsoft Teams agent docs, *Receive edit message activity* (scope: All): "When you edit a message, the agent gets a notification of the edit message activity." Handler: `app.on('messageEdit', ...)`; payload: `"type":"messageUpdate"`, `"channelData":{"eventType":"editMessage"}`. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/bots/build-conversational-capability
- Gate: `extensions/msteams/src/msteams-ingress.ts` `isDispatchableActivity` accepts only `message` and `invoke`+`adaptiveCard/action`; `extensions/msteams/src/msteams-ingress.test.ts` ("journals only message turns and adaptive-card agent turns") journals the drop of a `messageUpdate` activity.
- Family contract: `docs/channels/slack/events.md` — "Message edits/deletes are mapped into system events."; implementation `extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/message-subtype-handlers.ts` (`eventKind: "message_changed"`) + `extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/messages.ts` (`enqueueRoutedSystemEvent`).
- Precedents: `extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-pipeline.ts` (`bot.on("edited_message", ...)`), `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts` (`envelope.editMessage?.dataMessage`), `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/media-text.ts` + `SPEC-SUPPORT.md` (`m.replace`, in/out/tools).
- Outbound parity already merged: PR #49925 — "Adds message edit/update and delete support for the MS Teams extension, bringing feature parity with Slack, Discord, and Telegram for Tier 1 messaging operations" (proactive `updateActivity`/`deleteActivity`). This issue is the inbound complement.
- Related: #130038 (ingress dedupe aliases route-distinct activities sharing an id) — same dedupe key semantics; this proposal's composed event id should be designed together with that fix.
- Honest limitation: we could not find any existing user report about Teams edits specifically — the evidence above is the platform contract plus four in-repo channel implementations.

## Do you plan to open a PR?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional info

- Sibling channels for reference: Slack (`message_changed`), Telegram (`edited_message`/`edited_channel_post`), Signal (`editMessage` envelope), Matrix (`m.replace`).
- Discord (#53654, #20173) and Mattermost (#71930) have open issues for the same family on their own channels; MS Teams had none — its gap is different in kind because the platform event already reaches the bot.
- The outbound edit/delete actions this channel already has (merged PR #49925) are a different surface: those let the agent edit *its own* messages; this issue is about reacting to *user* edits.
- Related work (boundary disclosure):
  - #55691 ("Support message recall/edit events to cancel running tasks", closed by the staleness bot for inactivity on 2026-09-20, labeled 🌊 off-meta tidepool) is a cross-channel request on a different axis: recall → cancel running tasks, which its own review calls "a new lifecycle capability rather than a bounded regression repair" and "new behavior rather than reporting violation of an established contract" (comment 4336340852). This issue is not that: it reports a platform-delivered activity (`messageUpdate`) that the extension already receives and drops, wired into the documented edit→system-event contract Slack documents and Telegram/Signal/Matrix implement — no cancellation semantics, no lifecycle seam. #55691's optional "Message edit → update context" stretch goal is met on those three channels today; this issue extends the same contract to MS Teams.
  - #62307, a community WhatsApp edit PR closed as "duplicate or superseded" with an invitation to file "a fresh current-main PR" (clawsweeper[bot], comment 4357803735), is family prior art on the WhatsApp face only; it never covered MS Teams, and this issue is verified against current main, where `messageUpdate` remains unhandled. That closure's canonical pointer (#55691) is delineated above.

issues.body:
`agents.entries.<id>.tts` lets every agent have its own voice for TTS replies, but Talk ignores it: `talk.speak` resolves its provider from the global `talk.provider` / `talk.providers` only, and `talk.realtime` is likewise global. When Talk targets a non-default agent, it speaks in the default agent's voice.

In a multi-agent setup each agent is a distinct persona (we use a different local Kokoro voice per agent via `tts-local-cli`). Switching voice by surface — one voice in voice notes, another in Talk — breaks that.

**Proposal:** allow `agents.entries.<id>.talk` (provider, providers, speechLocale, realtime.speakerVoice, …) overriding the global `talk` block, resolved from the agent the Talk session targets.

**Minimal version:** when `agents.entries.<id>.tts.provider` is set and no agent-level talk override exists, use it for `talk.speak` in that agent's Talk sessions.

**Related, not the same:** #130054 (voice-call realtime is one global setting), #139277 (Android Talk agent selection reverting — shows Talk already targets different agents), #113321 (iOS native Talk ignores configured provider).

**Environment:** OpenClaw 2026.9.7, iOS Talk (native speech loop), `talk.provider: tts-local-cli`, five agents each with their own `agents.entries.<id>.tts`.

issues.body:
## Summary

The official `@openclaw/typesafe` decision provider remains unavailable on OpenClaw 2026.9.8 even though the plugin is enabled, loaded, correctly declares its capability-owned `apiKey` secret input, and valid SecretRefs have been tested through both the shared store and environment sources.

The runtime consistently reports:

```json
{
  "providerId": "typesafe",
  "pluginId": "typesafe",
  "configured": true,
  "credentialReady": false,
  "callable": false,
  "reasons": {}
}
```

Hosted Jev therefore appears unavailable in the Decision Model UI.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.8
- @openclaw/typesafe: 2026.9.8
- Node.js: 24.19.0
- OS: Linux
- Architecture: aarch64
- Gateway: systemd --user
- TypeSafe plugin: trusted official install

## Plugin runtime

The TypeSafe plugin reports:

- enabled: true
- explicitlyEnabled: true
- activated: true
- status: loaded
- service: `decisions:typesafe`
- configured: true
- credentialReady: false
- callable: false

A full Gateway restart produces a new `runtimeGeneration`, but readiness remains false.

Example after restart:

```text
configured=true
credentialReady=false
callable=false
runtimeGeneration=6646fdef-763a-456a-b587-0884267e8e80
```

## Installed plugin manifest

The installed `openclaw.plugin.json` contains:

```json
{
  "secretInputs": {
    "bundledDefaultEnabled": false,
    "paths": [
      {
        "path": "apiKey",
        "expected": "string",
        "ownerKind": "capability"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

So the plugin appears to correctly declare `apiKey` as a capability-owned secret input.

## Store SecretRef reproduction

A protected TypeSafe secret exists in the shared OpenClaw secret store.

`openclaw secrets audit --check` reports:

```text
plaintext=5
unresolved=0
shadowed=0
storeResidue=0
legacy=0
```

The TypeSafe credential was configured using:

```json
{
  "source": "store",
  "provider": "default",
  "id": "TYPESAFE_API_KEY"
}
```

The following were tested:

1. Existing `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` shared-store secret.
2. A newly-created second shared-store secret with the same TypeSafe credential.
3. `openclaw secrets reload --json` (returned `ok: true`, `warningCount: 0`).
4. Full Gateway restart after rebinding the SecretRef.

All cases still reported:

```text
credentialReady=false
callable=false
```

## Env SecretRef A/B

To rule out a shared-store-specific issue, the same credential was also tested through an env SecretRef:

```json
{
  "source": "env",
  "provider": "default",
  "id": "TYPESAFE_API_KEY"
}
```

After a full Gateway restart, `runtimeGeneration` changed again, confirming a new runtime, but the result was still:

```text
configured=true
credentialReady=false
callable=false
```

This suggests the failure is not specific to the shared secret store.

## Secrets provider configuration

These paths are unset and therefore use runtime defaults:

```text
secrets.defaults.store
secrets.providers
```

## Relevant earlier log

During an earlier `secrets reload` on OpenClaw 2026.9.6:

```text
Plugin typesafe forced retirement after 5000ms:
1 still-running call(s), 0 retained consumer(s);
resource cleanup remains pending.
```

The installation was later upgraded to 2026.9.8. During that upgrade, TypeSafe initially logged a deferred state migration warning, followed by:

```text
Deferred state migration completed for plugin "typesafe".
```

The Gateway was then fully restarted.

## Expected behavior

A valid prepared SecretRef for the TypeSafe capability should result in:

```text
credentialReady=true
callable=true
```

or, if preparation fails, the runtime should expose a diagnostic reason explaining why.

## Actual behavior

```text
configured=true
credentialReady=false
callable=false
reasons={}
```

The empty `reasons` object makes the failure difficult to diagnose.

## Notes

- The TypeSafe API key itself is not included here.
- Two independent shared-store secret entries were tested.
- An env SecretRef was also tested.
- Full Gateway restarts were used to avoid hot-reload ambiguity.
- Each restart produced a new `runtimeGeneration`.
- The issue reproduces after upgrading both OpenClaw and `@openclaw/typesafe` to 2026.9.8.

This looks like either a prepared capability-secret activation issue for the TypeSafe decision provider, or a missing diagnostic path when credential preparation fails.

issues.body:
### Summary

An opt-in setting for realtime outbound calls that waits for the callee's first words before speaking the opening line, with a configurable fallback when the callee stays silent.

### Problem to solve

On a realtime outbound call, the opening line is triggered as soon as the model session is ready, whether or not the callee has the phone to their ear or has said anything. People expect a caller to wait for their "hello"; an assistant that starts talking over the pickup sounds like a robocall, and the first words are often lost.

### Proposed solution

An outbound option, for example `outbound.openingTrigger: "ready" | "callee-speech"` (default `"ready"`, today's behavior). With `"callee-speech"`:
- the opening line is part of the session instructions from the start (so the model knows what to say whatever arrives first);
- the plugin does not trigger the greeting on ready; the model answers the callee's first words with the opening line;
- if the callee stays silent for N seconds (for example 5, configurable), the greeting is triggered anyway, so silent pickups still work.

Inbound calls keep their greeting on ready.

### Alternatives considered

Asking for "wait for the callee" in the realtime instructions does not work reliably: without the opening line in the session, the model either speaks first or answers the callee without knowing its mission.

### Impact

Affected: `voice-call` realtime outbound calls that use an opening line (for example calls to businesses).
Severity: the call still works, but the first seconds decide whether the callee keeps listening; talking over the pickup makes it sound like a robocall.
Frequency: every such outbound call.
Consequence: lost opening words and callees hanging up or treating the call as spam.

### Evidence/examples

I run this as a local patch on 2026.9.6 with GPT-Live (`gpt-live-1-codex`) over Telnyx: the assistant waited for "Hello, salon X" and then spoke the opening line once. The silent-pickup fallback is implemented but not yet exercised on a live call. It relies on the local speech detector already used for barge-in.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

Related: #164979 (doubled/invented greetings on GPT-Live outbound calls), #85846.

issues.body:
## Summary

Please make **bundled stock skills** and **default/stock plugins** **opt-in** (or installable profiles), instead of shipping and auto-discovering them as part of the default OpenClaw package/runtime.

Today, a fresh `npm install -g openclaw` / upgrade ships a large set of built-in skills under the package `skills/` tree and many stock plugins under `dist/extensions/`. Operators who only need a small Gateway + a few channels end up repeatedly pruning directories and fighting `doctor --fix` / upgrades that restore noise.

This aligns with the existing product posture reflected by label **`r: skill`** (“skills should be published on ClawHub, not added to core”).

## Problem

1. **Install / upgrade rehydration**
   - Upgrades re-materialize bundled skill directories.
   - `openclaw doctor --fix` can write `skills.entries.<name>.enabled=false` for skills that are present but missing bins/env, which re-bloats `openclaw.json`.
   - Physical deletion works operationally, but it is a local workaround, not a supported product path.

2. **Operator intent is inverted**
   - Unused skills/plugins are “on by discovery” unless explicitly disabled or deleted.
   - Minimal/self-hosted setups want the opposite: **core gateway only**, then opt into skills/plugins from ClawHub / npm.

3. **Noise and maintenance cost**
   - Doctor warnings about unavailable bundled skills.
   - Larger install surface and more config drift after every upgrade.
   - Duplicated capability surfaces (e.g. web search via plugin vs other providers) that users must manually disable.

## Proposal

Introduce an explicit **slim/core** packaging and load policy:

### A. Install profiles (preferred)

- `openclaw` **core** package: Gateway/CLI + essential channel/runtime primitives only.
- Optional skill packs / plugin packs:
  - ClawHub skill packs
  - Official plugin packages (already partially true for some providers)
- Or an installer flag / config:
  - `openclaw install --profile core|default|full`
  - `openclaw.json` → `skills.bundled: "none" | "minimal" | "all"`
  - `plugins.bundled: "none" | "minimal" | "all"`

### B. Runtime policy if keeping files in the tarball

Even if files remain in the package for convenience:

1. Do **not** auto-load bundled skills unless opted in.
2. Do **not** enable stock plugins unless opted in (except a documented minimal set such as the active channel(s)).
3. `doctor --fix` should **not** invent large `skills.entries.*.enabled=false` maps for unused bundled skills when the operator chose `bundled: none` / slim profile.
4. Document a supported “minimal operator” path that survives upgrades without custom shell hooks that `rm -rf` skill dirs.

### C. Catalog-first distribution

- Default discovery should prefer **ClawHub / plugin registry** install flows over “everything is already in core”.
- Related direction already discussed in catalog/UI work (e.g. Gateway ClawHub catalog parity).

## Suggested minimal set (for discussion)

Keep in core only what is required to boot and operate a Gateway:

- CLI + Gateway runtime
- Config/doctor primitives
- Channel plugins the user explicitly enables
- Model/provider plugins the user explicitly enables

Move to optional packs / ClawHub:

- Convenience skills (`spotify-player`, `1password`, `notion`, `tmux`, …)
- Non-essential stock plugins users did not select during onboarding

## Alternatives considered

1. **Local prune scripts after every update/doctor** (current workaround) — fragile, undocumented, breaks on path changes.
2. **Mass `enabled: false` entries in config** — works briefly, then doctor/upgrades reintroduce drift and config bloat.
3. **Fork / custom builds** — high cost; should not be required for a minimal deployment.

## Benefits

- Smaller default attack/maintenance surface
- Cleaner upgrades for self-hosted operators
- Matches ClawHub-first skill distribution
- Better onboarding: install only what you need

## Environment (repro context)

- OpenClaw `2026.9.8` (npm global install)
- macOS, Gateway via LaunchAgent
- Operator goal: Telegram + Tavily (+ a few local extensions); no interest in most bundled skills/stock plugins

Happy to refine the profile matrix (`core` / `default` / `full`) with maintainers if useful.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a call-language setting to voice-call so classic (non-realtime) calls can understand and speak languages other than English.

### Problem to solve

The classic call flow always uses English speech recognition and English `<Say>` output.

- Twilio: `<Gather input="speech" … language="${input.language || "en-US"}">` and `<Say voice="${pollyVoice}" language="${input.locale || "en-US"}">` (`extensions/voice-call/src/providers/twilio.ts`).
- Telnyx: `language: input.locale || "en-US"` for speak and `input.language || "en"` for gather (`providers/telnyx.ts`).
- Plivo: `<GetInput … language="…">` and `<Speak language="…">` default to `en-US` (`providers/plivo.ts`).

Nothing ever sets `language` or `locale`. In `manager/outbound.ts`, `playTts` passes `{callId, providerCallId, text, voice}` and `startListening` passes `{callId, providerCallId[, turnToken]}`. The voice-call config schema has no language or locale field.

A German or Spanish caller on a classic call therefore goes through English speech recognition, so the transcript the agent receives is wrong. Realtime calls don't have this problem, but realtime isn't available on every carrier (Plivo is classic-only) or every model setup.

### Proposed solution

- Add a `language` (BCP-47) setting at the voice-call level, overridable per `numbers.<E.164>` route.
- Pass it as `startListening({ language })` and `playTts({ locale })`. The three providers already accept these fields; nothing populates them today.
- Optionally let a call override it (for example on `initiate_call`), for outbound calls in a different language.

### Alternatives considered

- **Realtime voice:** multilingual, but needs a realtime-capable provider and carrier (not Plivo), and changes the whole call mode.
- **Twilio media `streaming` with a multilingual transcription provider:** Twilio-only, and only covers recognition.
- **Choosing a non-English Polly voice through `tts`/voice mapping:** the `<Gather>`/`<Say>` `language` attribute stays `en-US`.

### Impact

- **Affected:** any non-English deployment on classic voice calls (Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo).
- **Severity:** blocks classic calls for non-English callers.
- **Frequency:** every classic call.
- **Consequence:** wrong transcripts, so wrong answers, for every non-English caller.

### Evidence/examples

Read at v2026.9.8 and main `f4870f5`:

- `providers/twilio.ts`: the `<Gather>` and `<Say>` `language` attributes.
- `providers/telnyx.ts`: the speak and gather `language` fields.
- `providers/plivo.ts`: `xmlSpeak` and `xmlGetInputSpeech` default to `en-US`.
- `types.ts`: the optional `locale`/`language` on the play and listen inputs.
- `manager/outbound.ts`: the `playTts`/`startListening` call sites, which pass no language.
- `config.ts`: no language field.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.body:
## Summary
Add an enforceable foreground-by-default policy for interactive user requests. A task should not be intentionally detached or yield to background continuation unless the user explicitly requests asynchronous work. Preserve progress streaming for the active turn.

## Problem
A Telegram user can receive the generic “I’m continuing this work and will send the result when it is ready.” while the task moves to a pending continuation. Even with Telegram progress streaming and toolProgress enabled, the channel may have no meaningful post-yield activity. Workspace instructions to avoid background work are behavioral guidance, not an enforced runtime control. No confirmed global foreground-only switch was found in the current configuration.

## Requested behavior
- Provide a supported per-agent or global execution policy: foreground by default, with explicit user opt-in for asynchronous tasks.
- When enabled, reject discretionary sessions_yield, detached/background execution, and equivalent automatic continuation paths for ordinary interactive requests without user opt-in. Distinguish necessary tool/runtime suspension from intentional background delegation.
- Keep foreground tool progress visible; if suspension is unavoidable, show the pending operation and a reliable completion/resumption path rather than only a generic acknowledgment.
- Preserve async/yield workflows for explicitly authorized work, scheduled jobs, and noninteractive operations. Specify how timeouts are handled without indefinitely blocking a conversation.

## Why existing features are insufficient
Telegram streaming.progress.toolProgress shows events while the turn produces them; it does not enforce foreground execution. A USER.md preference can guide the model but cannot enforce the boundary. #150696 addresses visibility of Codex-native children after yield; #161732 asks for read-only status in Discord. Neither provides opt-in for background execution.

## Acceptance criteria
With the policy enabled, an ordinary interactive Telegram request remains foreground through execution and verification or stops with a concrete blocker. A discretionary background/yield attempt without user opt-in is not admitted. A request explicitly asking for async work retains existing behavior. Progress remains visible in both modes.

Observed on OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (Linux, Telegram). This is a feature request, not a claim that every generic continuation notice has the same trigger.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an explicit **Current installed instructions → Proposed instructions** diff to pending update suggestions in Skill Workshop, before Apply.

## Problem to solve

Observed in Control UI on OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8): the Suggestions reader renders the complete proposed skill as Markdown, with Evaluate, Apply, Revise, and Reject actions, but does not show which instructions differ from the installed skill.

For a small change in a long skill, reviewers must switch between Skills and Suggestions and manually compare the entire text, or ask their agent to compute the difference. A reviewer cannot quickly answer “What exactly will Apply change?”

The installed Skills view's saved-version comparisons are a different comparison: saved instructions versus the currently installed skill. They do not answer current-installed versus pending-proposal changes.

## Proposed solution

In the pending update suggestion reader, provide:

1. A **Changes** view alongside the existing **Proposed instructions** view, comparing the current installed target with the exact selected proposal revision.
2. Clearly labeled baselines: **Current installed** and **Proposed vN**, not merely “old” and “new.”
3. Added/removed line highlighting, line numbers, change counts, and collapsible unchanged context. Unified diff is sufficient; optional side-by-side mode would be helpful.
4. A read-only **Current instructions** view so both complete bodies remain directly readable.
5. Exclude proposal lifecycle metadata (status, draft date/version) from the instruction diff. Show meaningful skill metadata changes, such as name/description, separately rather than hiding them.
6. Include changed supporting files when present, or explicitly state that the comparison is SKILL.md-only.
7. Refresh the comparison after Revise. If the live target changes while a proposal is pending, identify the baseline change and avoid presenting a stale comparison as current.

No Apply, evaluation, or revision should be necessary merely to inspect changes. Existing lifecycle authorization should remain unchanged.

## Alternatives considered

- Switch between Skills and Suggestions and compare manually: cumbersome and easy to miss deletions in long documents.
- Ask an agent or use external diff tools: accurate, but makes basic proposal review depend on another interface.
- Use installed-skill saved-version history: useful for past changes, but has different baseline semantics and cannot replace a pending-proposal diff.
- Show only an AI-generated change summary: useful as an optional supplement, but not a substitute for the actual diff.

## Impact

- Affected: operators reviewing pending Workshop skill updates in Control UI.
- Severity: moderate review/UX friction; no state corruption or Apply failure is alleged.
- Frequency: whenever a pending update changes only a small portion of a larger skill.
- Consequence: extra manual comparison work and reduced confidence about what approving an update will change.

## Evidence/examples

An observed pending update to an argument-analysis skill added exactly one source-retrieval instruction under Workflow step 1 and removed no existing instructions. The Suggestions reader displayed the entire draft, making that small addition indistinguishable without comparing it with the installed body. The installed body and pending proposal were read independently to verify the difference.

Inspection of the locally shipped 2026.9.8 UI bundle confirms that the suggestion detail renders the proposal body as Markdown. The saved-version diff reader belongs to the installed Skills view, not the pending suggestion reader. This is evidence from the installed release, not a claim about current upstream main.

Related but distinct:

- #161775 concerns a clean current-instructions view and clearer saved-version/date labels for installed skills. This request concerns **pre-Apply review of pending proposals**.
- #151530 concerns consolidation of existing diff presentation. A pending-proposal diff could reuse that shared presentation while preserving its own explicit baseline semantics.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only.

## Additional information

Suggested acceptance checks: a one-line addition is immediately visible; a deletion is visible; unchanged bodies report no instruction changes; revising the proposal refreshes the diff; a changed live baseline is clearly identified; simply opening the comparison never activates or modifies the skill.

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw doctor --fix` (v2026.9.8) **self-deadlocks** on `state/openclaw.sqlite`: the doctor's own read connection blocks the exclusive maintenance lease it subsequently tries to acquire, and `busyTimeoutMs=0` makes SQLite fail instantly with `SQLITE_BUSY`. As a result the migration chain aborts and no repairs run. This reproduces 3/3 times, regardless of how the gateway is stopped.

## Environment

- *** 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)
- Linux (WSL2), gateway as `systemd --user` service on `127.0.0.1:18789`
- Databases: `state/openclaw.sqlite` (~58MB), `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` (~665MB)
- Both databases pass `PRAGMA integrity_check` (74 tables, healthy) — **no corruption involved**

## Steps to reproduce

1. With the gateway running, stop it — any of these three variants:
   - `openclaw gateway stop`
   - `openclaw gateway stop` + `pkill -f 'openclaw.*worker.js'`
   - `systemctl --user stop openclaw-gateway` + `sleep 5` + verify with `pgrep -af 'openclaw|dist/index.js'` (empty)
2. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`
3. Doctor runs migrations and fails at the same point every time.

## Actual behavior

```
[sqlite/transaction] SQLite transaction lock wait failed async=false busyTimeoutMs=0
  database=/home/mpque/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite
  operation=agent.database.maintenance.lease
  code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR failureKind=lock-contention
  sqliteErrcode=5 sqlitePrimaryCode=5 step=begin

***StateLeaseError: agent database maintenance lease core:agent-database-maintenance/global was lost
Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue.
Failing check media-persistence (step-refused)
Failing check transcript-directives (blocked-by-prior-refusal)
Failing check profile-workspace (blocked-by-prior-refusal)
Failing check plugin-migration-preparation (blocked-by-prior-refusal)
Failing check orphan-session-keys (blocked-by-prior-refusal)
```

The `readerDiagnostics` of the blocked connection is the smoking gun:

| Field | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ownerKind` | `main` | the doctor process itself owns the blocking connection |
| `threadId` | `0` | doctor main thread |
| `transactionOpen` | `false` | idle read connection, not an active lease |
| `ageMs` | ≈ 32 min | **resets each attempt**, matching the start of that doctor run |
| `connectionId` | 246 → 476 → 478 | **new connection each attempt** |
| `busyTimeoutMs` | `0` | no wait → immediate `SQLITE_BUSY` |

## Expected behavior

Migrations apply; the command completes.

## Root-cause analysis

The doctor:
1. Opens a **read** connection on `state/openclaw.sqlite` (integrity_check / schema read)
2. The pool keeps that connection **alive** (`ownerKind: main`, `transactionOpen: false`)
3. The doctor then tries `BEGIN` on the **exclusive maintenance lease** (`agent.database.maintenance.lease`)
4. The lease needs a write lock; the doctor's own read connection holds a read lock
5. With `busyTimeoutMs=0`, SQLite returns `SQLITE_BUSY` (errcode 5) **immediately**, with no retry
6. `StateLeaseError` → `media-persistence` refuses → the 4 downstream migrations are blocked by reflex
7. The doctor aborts **before touching the schema** (state stays consistent)

**Why it is not residual processes:** if an orphan worker held the lock, `ownerKind` would be `gateway`/`worker` (never `main`), `transactionOpen` would be `true` (a lease is an open long transaction), and `ageMs` would be monotonic and independent of the doctor's start — instead it resets each attempt. Three different shutdown methods changed nothing.

## Suggested fix

1. Close/release read connections on the target database before `BEGIN` on the lease, or
2. Acquire the lease on a **dedicated connection** separate from the read pool, or
3. Set a reasonable `busy_timeout` (5–30s) on the connection that acquires the lease

## Impact

- Databases remain intact; no corruption.
- Gateway starts normally after each failure (`healthz`/`readyz` HTTP 200 in ms).
- 5 features stay unmigrated: `media-persistence`, `transcript-directives`, `profile-workspace`, `plugin-migration-preparation`, `orphan-session-keys`.
- No operational urgency, but `doctor --fix` is effectively unusable.

## Additional notes

Diagnosis independently confirmed by two models (`deepseek-v4-pro` and `minimax-m3`), both converging on the self-deadlock (ordering bug) conclusion. Full logs available on request (`log-console.txt`, `log-console-2.txt`, `log-console-3.txt`).

issues.body:
### Problem statement

The Control UI (2026.9.x) has no way to cancel an in-flight automation run without pausing/disabling the job. Pausing changes enabled state and requires re-enabling afterwards; it also cancels via a different code path (`"Cron job disabled by operator."`).

Reported originally as #164882, where triage noted that *"a separate cancel-only action that preserves scheduling would be a distinct feature request."* This is that request.

### Proposed solution

A **"Cancel current run"** action on the Automations job detail view (or job row menu), enabled while run history shows a status of `running`. It should call the existing gateway cancellation path (`requestActiveCronJobCancellation`, reachable via `cron.stop`) with a reason like `"Cancelled by operator"`, leaving `enabled`, schedule, and failure counters untouched. Run history should record the run as cancelled/interrupted with the operator reason.

### Alternatives considered

- **Pause → wait → re-enable:** changes job state, risks forgetting to re-enable, and cancels with the wrong reason string.
- **Chat composer Stop / `/stop` on the run's session:** doesn't surface for isolated cron runs, which don't appear in the session list until finished; the Automations run viewer only lists completed runs.
- **CLI:** no `openclaw cron cancel` subcommand exists (subcommands are add/enable/disable/edit/run/runs/rm/show/status/scratch).

### Scope/changes

UI action + confirmation only; the backend cancellation primitive already exists and is used by the disable and agent-removal paths (`jobs-mutation-persistence.ts`, `active-jobs.ts`). Blast radius should be small.

### Context

Prior triage thread: #164882 (closed as "cannot reproduce" because the requested capability was assessed as intentional removal — but the same review conceded this feature-request shape).

issues.title: [Bug]: Progress indicator collapses assistant responses on v2026.10.7
issues.body:
## Problem

Assistant responses are being collapsed under a "Worked for Xs" progress indicator on OpenClaw v2026.10.7. The full response is hidden inside the collapsed section and requires manual expansion to read.

## Environment

- **Gateway:** OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (157d8c2)
- **Surfaces affected:** Android app (Pixel 10a, app 2026.10.50), web Control UI, desktop app — all three reproduce
- **Frequency:** Nearly every response that takes >1s to generate, regardless of length or presence of tool calls

## Example

User asked "What can you do?" at 23:00 EDT. The response appeared collapsed under "Worked for 2s" on all three clients. Expanding the progress indicator reveals the full assistant response inside.

## Screenshots
![Screenshot_20261024-233921.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfc19d77-be23-438f-99f7-a4eca48a4f31)
![Screenshot_20261024-233912.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed1c8032-d896-4174-81d6-cf761efac68c)


## Relationship to #165892 and PR #167054

This appears to be a **different path** from the paragraph-break collapse fixed in PR #167054 (merged in v2026.10.5). That fix addressed tool-call-adjacent text losing  separators.

This issue is about the **progress indicator itself** becoming a persistent collapsed container in the final rendered message, rather than disappearing aft after the response completes.

## Expected behavior

The "Worked for Xs" progress indicator should only show during generation and disappear once the response is complete, leaving the assistant's message fully visible without requiring expansion.

## Observed behavior

The progress indicator persists as a collapsible section in the final delivered message, with the assistant's response hidden inside it by default.
