prs.title: perf: share PostgreSQL I/O across four process workers
prs.body:
## Approved implementation acceptance — registered before candidate comparisons

The implementation base is `5e56409f2bc590a33e95371846617b7b0ac6c6cc`, after #183014. The approved candidate is a fixed-four process-wide I/O pool; each logical connection remains independently owned and pinned. The existing maximum four idle bridges per isolate and three-minute expiry remain unchanged. The public `createCpuTrackedWorker` contract stays unchanged.

Coordinator/pgprep settled the lifecycle: Update and Doctor prelaunch four services before retention, never replace crashed services, surface unknown outcome with `openclaw update repair` / `openclaw doctor --fix`, and close the pool after both generation phases and backend-close enqueue. Gateway replacements follow existing worker retirement. No new lease or retained-scope extension.

Fresh implementation-base census and production proof are required. Count physical service launches, logical connections, requests and SQL before timing. Repeat the same synthetic Gateway20 workload (20 agents, 800 sessions, 18,240 events, 60 real WebSocket history reads, 190-second idle) on base and candidate. Separate observer-backed count attribution from observer-free external RSS/thread/backend sampling. Report five alternating independent processes per arm for RSS; never sum RSS across threads. Cold readiness/first history, warm history and post-idle first history stay separate.

Production controlled cells use actual synchronous PG connections in concurrent client workers: ordinary four-client control; four active clients pinned to one candidate service through twelve identically counted idle filler connections on both arms; and twenty active clients with the first four saturating all four candidate services. Keep 200-ms slow-query and 8-MiB large-row cases separate. Record every foreground client's p50/p95/p99 and range, errors, progress, main-thread CPU and total CPU, plus physical services, backends, and external RSS. Also run the existing real Gateway C64 mock-provider turn workload with PG configured: 20 active agents, 64 concurrent sessions, five alternating independent processes per arm. Separate cold cells (no warmup, 64 measured turns) from warm cells (64 warmup turns then 256 measured turns), retaining aggregate and per-client p99, existing probe latencies/counts, startup/setup duration, errors, MAIN CPU and total CPU. Both arms use the same committed workload; only ratios support timing conclusions on the loaded local host.

Timing routing amendment registered before implementation comparisons: the coordinator’s 2026-10-25 “PGFOOTPRINT perf gates” decision directs local counts/footprint and both timing arms on one immediately available Testbox, with local mkdir-lock timing and per-cell load reporting if capacity queues. The initially allocated Testbox subsequently reported queued, ready=false, and no host; no test payload ran, and its stop was requested. The authorized fallback is therefore local timing under the campaign mkdir lock, recording load for every cell, with five interleaved baseline/candidate samples. The original registration is retained as history. The coordinator’s later timing-accounting decision charges only actual lock/load admission waits, excluding reviews, tests, counts, builds and footprint; at 60 cumulative minutes, continue under the mkdir lock with alternating arms and per-cell load. The explicit local fallback replaces load<24 admission, and only same-host A/B ratios support timing conclusions. Every user-facing metric must hold or improve; any adverse cell above 20% remains a mandatory STOP, never within spread or grounds to widen the pool.

Before PG-review READY: pinned Bun and Node creation/nested/direct messaging; crash and true hung-service wake during blocked MAIN within the existing deadline; PG mid-migration crash rollback and rerun; Gateway owner crash replacement; complete cutover; fresh creation census; focused/static/conformance/update gates; and two isolated Codex reviews on the production change. The earlier workload reviews do not satisfy production review.


## Problem and design

PostgreSQL connections currently each own an I/O worker, so a multi-agent Gateway repeatedly loads the same driver and worker runtime. This replaces those dedicated workers with exactly four process-wide services. Each logical connection still owns its own direct MessagePort, `pg.Client`, search path, timeouts and transaction state. There is no shared SQL connection or main-thread forwarding hop.

The dedicated per-isolate construction/termination path is removed. SQL hosts receive service endpoints through their existing private task, writer, archive and heartbeat transports. A failed service invalidates pinned connections and retires affected SQL hosts through their existing task/broker lifecycle; it never replays the failed operation. The existing max-four, three-minute idle connection reuse remains intact.

Update and Doctor await all services before actual runtime retention and disable service replacement. Failures report unknown outcome with `openclaw update repair` or `openclaw doctor --fix`. Gateway replacement remains under the existing worker lifecycle. Terminal cleanup keeps the services alive through both generation settlement phases and broker backend-close enqueue. No new lease, retained-scope extension, schema, public option or SDK constructor change is introduced. The coordinator and PostgreSQL owner explicitly approved this topology and lifecycle.

## Qualification status

This remains a draft. No performance acceptance or PG review readiness is claimed while comparative cells and required static/conformance proof are pending.

| Required condition | Current evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Node and pinned Bun construction/nested transfer, direct messaging | PASS on both runtimes; rebinding also preserves a live logical connection. |
| Blocked MAIN service crash/hang wake | Crash: Node 113.742 ms, Bun 90.781 ms. True service hang: existing 120000 ms timeout fires; outer observation 120012.268 / 120009.258 ms. Strict wall completion below 120000 ms is not proven. |
| Same-fixture PG20 counts and observer-free RSS/threads/backends | Pending on the implementation pair. Earlier attribution is not candidate proof. |
| Same-service, four-saturated per-client p99 and Gateway C64 p99 | Pending; coordinator-authorized local fallback after the Testbox reported queued/no host, with mkdir lock and load reported for each cell. |
| Fresh creation census | Base audit: 20 owner/caller sites plus shared constructor; every PG-reachable route classified. Public constructor and SDK diff empty. |
| Complete cutover | Dedicated bridge Worker construction and per-client termination removed. Four-service owner and logical-port close used throughout. |
| Repair guidance and kill-mid-migration | Both runtimes preserve schema version 1 and zero partial indexes after killing a service, then a fresh Doctor run completes version 2 with both indexes. Update/Doctor does not replace the failed slot; survivors remain usable. |
| Gateway crash replacement | Both runtimes pass the production task-owner and real writer-broker retirement paths; later opens wrap to replaced slot 0. This is owner integration proof, not a full Gateway restart claim. |

The implementation head is `9cbde52ec3549cb59525af8a5f122f67d4935124`, based on `5e56409f2bc590a33e95371846617b7b0ac6c6cc`. Four lifecycle files / 40 tests and four task-owner/writer recovery files / 43 tests pass. C64 benchmark tests pass (56 passed, 7 skipped). Real overlapping heartbeat leases pass both close orders on Node and pinned Bun, including durable renewal and complete fixture cleanup. Native-root transport reruns passed all 30 tests. Static checks, exact-head PostgreSQL conformance and the published-driver update cell remain tracked separately; the queued Testbox produced no update-test result. The local internal virtual-store declaration-containment preflight blocks typed lint/typecheck before diagnostics; that is not a pass. Two isolated Codex production reviews are complete: round 1 raised a prelaunch-order finding that was rejected after inspecting the lazy retention callback and actual binding order; round 2 finished scoped-clean at P0–P2 with final source verification. Three append-only native-root test routes were added afterward to use the existing forked test lane. The final mechanical delta replaces nine assertions with explicit owner types/a named existing buffer, and moves identical PostgreSQL benchmark configuration after the unchanged buildConfig call to avoid an open-PR conflict. The owner-type correction received an additional coordinator-authorized isolated Codex review, scoped-clean at P0–P2 with final source verification. Exact-head CI then found mechanical lint/type errors. Those are corrected in the current head; targeted normal-wrapper core/script lint passed. A further coordinator-authorized isolated review is running only on this final CI-forced delta; any behavior finding is a STOP. Runtime topology, SQL, lifecycle, allocation sizes and fixture values are unchanged. Final-head measurement and remaining gates are pending.

The production change is +616/-236 lines (net +380); tests +308/-94; committed/reviewed workloads +2187. The growth is the smallest complete topology cutover: a constructor-only change would leave worker ownership, shared-service failure and shutdown incorrect. The public `createCpuTrackedWorker` implementation remains unchanged.

## Scope and accepted edges

Every client pinned to a crashed service fails; surviving services continue. Replacement applies to subsequent owner creation, not replay. Update/Doctor intentionally require a visible rerun after service loss. Process-local service pools are independent in separate native child processes. The read-only schema-inspection child keeps its existing policy, as explicitly decided by its owner. Transaction commit order, SQL shapes and database ownership remain unchanged.

All fixtures are synthetic. Reports contain only shapes, counts and timings; no operator state, message contents, rows or bound values. Full numerical comparisons remain pending. The preceding-head open-main-PR census reviewed 2,669 open PRs and all 105 exact overlapping heads, with zero new conflict paths/messages/hunks; comparisons are being refreshed for the current eight-file CI correction. The earlier #181594 benchmark conflict is eliminated; its two inherited test conflicts remain unchanged. Evidence pins every PR head and compares base-only vs base+candidate merge-tree output.

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep existing plain DMs from re-injecting transcript chat windows
prs.body:
Related: #89855, #112548, #172711, #179399

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: existing plain Telegram DMs re-inject a 10-turn `Conversation context` (`chat_window`) transcript dump into per-turn runtime context on every turn, duplicating conversation history that is already replayed in the canonical session transcript and amplifying context-attribution loops on models that serialize runtime carriers in user role.

## User Impact

User impact: existing plain Telegram DMs no longer receive a duplicate 10-turn transcript `chat_window` inside the per-turn runtime context carrier, while fresh DMs, DM replies/quotes, DM topics, and groups keep their restored `Conversation context` behavior unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `buildTelegramInboundContextPayload` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.session.ts`), `shouldSuppressPersistedDmChatWindowContext` (`!isGroup && previousTimestamp !== undefined && dmThreadId == null && visibleReplyChain.length === 0 && !visibleReplyTarget`, added in #89855) removes the Telegram `chat_window` from `baseVisiblePromptContext` because existing plain DMs already carry their history through the persistent session transcript.

However, when #112548 migrated session transcript merging to the shared post-context seam (`runPreparedChannelTurn` → `mergeSessionTranscriptContext`), `buildTelegramInboundContextPayload` continued passing `sessionTranscript: { chatWindow: true, historyLimit: isGroup ? historyLimit : dmHistoryLimit }` (default `10`) even when `shouldSuppressPersistedDmChatWindowContext` was `true`. Because `baseVisiblePromptContext` had just cleared `ChannelStructuredContext` (`windows.length === 0`), `mergeSessionTranscriptContext` (`src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.ts:113`) saw `windows.length === 0 && options?.chatWindow === true` and re-created a `chat_window` `ChannelStructuredContext` entry from the last 10 session transcript turns on every plain DM turn.

Gating `sessionTranscript` on `shouldSuppressPersistedDmChatWindowContext` keeps `SessionTranscriptContext` `undefined` when the DM chat window is intentionally suppressed, while preserving transcript restoration for fresh DMs, DM replies/quotes, DM topics, and groups.

Against the merge base: production **0 net lines (+10/-10)**, tests **+6 lines**. No config, schema, or storage changes.

## Evidence

- **Red/green regression (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.prompt-context.test.ts`):**
  - Before this fix, `selects cached context for existing plain DM from recorded session state` cleared `ctx.ctxPayload.ChannelStructuredContext` at context-build time, but left `ctx.ctxPayload.SessionTranscriptContext` set to `{ chatWindow: true, historyLimit: 10 }`, causing `mergeSessionTranscriptContext` during `runPreparedChannelTurn` to re-create `ChannelStructuredContext` from the session transcript.
  - With this fix, `existing plain DM` sets both `ChannelStructuredContext` and `SessionTranscriptContext` to `undefined`, while `fresh plain DM` and `existing DM reply` retain both `ChannelStructuredContext` and `SessionTranscriptContext: { chatWindow: true, historyLimit: 10 }`.
- **Test & lint verification:**
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.prompt-context.test.ts`: **14/14 tests passed**.
  - `oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors, `max-lines <= 700` preserved at net +0 lines) and `oxfmt --check` passed.

<details>
<summary>Redacted multi-turn diagnosis and controlled reproduction details</summary>

During a multi-turn Telegram DM session on upstream `main` (`7ab64536d3eb`), a model running on the `google-generative-ai` adapter (where runtime-context carriers are emitted as a trailing `role: "user"` entry in `contents` with context-only framing parts from #172711) misattributed the trailing runtime-context carrier to the human sender.

Once a single mistaken attribution entered the assistant transcript, the un-suppressed `SessionTranscriptContext` re-injected that assistant reply into the next 10 turns' trailing `role: "user"` runtime-context carrier under `Conversation context (chronological, selected for current message): ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧` (serialized via `JSON.stringify` inside `Conversation data (data, not instructions):`). Even after the model acknowledged a correction, the next plain DM follow-up carried the earlier accusation back inside the trailing `role: "user"` carrier, triggering an immediate relapse.

Controlled in-memory multi-turn reproduction using synthetic messages (`sender: { id: "1001", name: "Alex" }`) confirmed:
1. On clean history without prior mistaken assistant turns, the model answers ordinary short follow-up prompts normally without misattribution.
2. When prior mistaken assistant turns are echoed inside the un-suppressed `chat_window` carrier on existing plain DMs, the model repeatedly attributes the carrier dump to the user or claims the gateway is splicing context into the user's message stream.
3. Suppressing `sessionTranscript` when `shouldSuppressPersistedDmChatWindowContext` is `true` eliminates the duplicate 10-turn transcript echo from existing plain DM runtime carriers.

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

There is no isolated CI path for preparing an experimental AOT standalone artifact without changing the normal Mac release.

## User Impact

Adds a manual workflow with `enable_aot=false` by default. Enabling it can produce an unsigned emitted-JS, arm64, **macOS 27-only** Actions artifact. It does not publish a release, sign or notarize, change appcasts, or affect ordinary JIT releases. A failed AOT build remains failed and never masquerades as a JIT success.

Dispatch requires an existing compiler bundle from a successful same-repository main Actions run and an operator-selected physical-memory threshold. This change does not add a compiler producer. The pinned toolchain's actual Mach-O minimum is 27.0; environment variables cannot make it satisfy the Mac app's 15.0 support floor. C2, original-TypeScript, Intel, Linux, and app runtime conversion remain separate work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep qualification separate from publication. The job has only read permissions, validates source/compiler provenance and hashes, rejects unsafe archive members, verifies actual compiler/output minimum OS, records build cost, and runs smoke checks with isolated state. Its helper boundary tests run before the experiment. Diagnostics survive ordinary failure/cancellation; runner loss and SIGKILL remain explicit limits.

## Evidence

Nine Python archive, Mach-O parsing, failure and SIGTERM cleanup tests pass; actionlint and Python syntax checks pass. A real local pinned compiler bundle was verified, extracted and relocated successfully. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The enabled Actions build has not been dispatched; this is not full runtime or distribution qualification.

Local executable-admission proof ran the unmodified helper and exact workflow ancestry shell block at `6e428a61c2e727fc7c8b3c9c361ccaed4f79cb49`. All API metadata and Git repositories in this proof were explicitly synthetic fixtures. A Python audit hook observed subprocess launches without replacing the helper's subprocess implementation.

| Input | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Successful same-repository main producer fixture + real pinned archive | Provenance and extraction passed; actual compiler `--revision` returned `1.4.4-canary.1+fd40ba441` |
| Fork producer fixture | `Fork toolchain producer rejected`; zero subprocess launches |
| Non-main producer fixture | `Successful main producer run required`; zero subprocess launches |
| Artifact/run mismatch fixture | `Artifact/run mismatch`; zero subprocess launches |
| Altered archive clone with original expected hash | `Toolchain bundle SHA256 mismatch`; zero subprocess launches or extraction |
| Main source fixture | Exact ancestry shell block exited 0, wrote the fixed UTC build timestamp and reached a synthetic next-build sentinel |
| Source fixture outside main | Exact ancestry shell block exited 1 before the next-build sentinel |

Frozen helper SHA256: `0b93d7b2043362f0ab5d432a149928ec018babbe1fb437f1e2c88f8c1ab1928c`; workflow SHA256: `7912d47ffc8adf103140cce624c5003715f1504d3196c0e8185703c403559303`; real local compiler-bundle SHA256: `4e26c93d255caa30d7945d89d87d3a72137f0f823af015d62e31c0e567af6f73`. Source/helper/archive bytes were unchanged after the proof. This establishes local final-effect admission, not cloud metadata authenticity, download-action authentication, Actions integration, runner capacity or a full build.

CodeQL's cache-poisoning alerts do not identify an executable path around the exact source/main ancestry guard: application execution follows that guard, checkout credentials are not persisted, cache mode is off, and the job only has read permissions. The real admission proof above covers the requested negative controls; no suppression or extra permission was added.

prs.title: perf(agents): keep transcript readers out of catalog workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Catalog workers retain the transcript reader/actor import graph merely to detach background session work from its initiating transcript context.

## User Impact

Reduces retained heap in the synthetic source-worker benchmark by 4.97 MiB (3.48%). Catalog contents and transcript-write authority are unchanged. No config, persistence, or worker restart policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing transcript AsyncContext and synchronous detachment function into one lightweight module. Writer producers and detached callers share the same context; all callers migrate, and the old export is removed. This removes 221 loaded scripts from the measured worker without adding a cache or retained prepared state. Production LOC: +127/-119 (net +8); tests: +10/-19. The eight additional lines are explicit type imports required to keep the context contract acyclic; runtime logic and retained state do not grow. The new module is included in the PR wrapper extraction inventory.

Idle retirement is deliberately deferred: catalog generations retain plugin source publication custody, and restarting a worker can recapture changed source. The existing worker-exit integration contract requires republishing borrowers. Avoiding that lifecycle change keeps this repair small and preserves ownership.

## Evidence

Node 26.12.1, actual CatalogWorkerTaskPool, synthetic runtime plugin with 500 discovered models, 5,000 remote rows, five workspaces, two remote revisions, ten catalog requests per worker. Five alternating independent baseline/candidate launches; forced GC outside request timing. Baseline owner source: `27e08fc724c7ca8d01f3cf83066f0f45e7289977`; final confirmation shares checkout base `8ae44f9249540b4d377fb6b80f25f004a5d959e1`. The five-pair confirmation below includes the acyclic type-layout repair.

| Pair | Baseline retained MiB | Candidate retained MiB | Delta MiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 142.570 | 137.608 | -4.962 |
| 2 | 142.589 | 137.596 | -4.993 |
| 3 | 142.553 | 137.607 | -4.946 |
| 4 | 142.564 | 137.589 | -4.974 |
| 5 | 142.563 | 137.610 | -4.953 |
| Mean (n=5 each) | 142.568 | 137.602 | -4.966 (-3.48%) |

All 100 responses contain the same 501 entries and identical full-snapshot SHA-256 (`18a0b546b9b6d84f504fad0bcc67535689d0dfc9416a9562563bc65b9959578c`). Heap after one request: 135.798 → 130.818 MiB; after five workspaces: 139.635 → 134.677 MiB (n=5 each).

This removes a measurable import cost; most of the idle worker footprint remains.

prs.title: refactor: deslop SDK transport, HTTP fixtures and UI setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Small fixture families still duplicate setup after the larger consolidation stacks. Give those families one test-support owner without merging scenarios, removing assertions, or changing production contracts. This is an authorized residue PR under the campaign's 100-line residue rule, **not a LARGE PR**.

Final local diff: **208 additions, 347 deletions: 139 net test/support lines removed**, 23 files, **0 production lines removed**. No schema, dependency, protocol, configuration or Phase E standalone session-memory change. No production guard is removed.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Developers maintain one fixture owner per family while retaining every existing scenario and expectation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing support owners absorb repeated setup; three narrow adjacent helpers supply genuinely missing shared fixture responsibilities. Per-call state, promises, cleanup and protocol-specific differences stay explicit.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Each independent cut below records its fixture tradeoffs separately. No production incident guard is retired or reclassified as speculative.

## SDK WebSocket setup — 28 net

The existing transport support owner now owns fresh loopback-server allocation/listening/close and response serialization. Keep both protocol handlers, their different handshakes and sequence scopes intact. Reuse the existing event collector and free-port helper.

Assertions **43 → 43**; registrations **25 → 25**; tables **5 → 5**; custom expectation-helper calls **36 → 36**. The conditional live-Gateway suite registration is counted explicitly.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: the asynchronous fixture adds a helper-return boundary before handler attachment and close resolution. The URL is not published before the handler is installed. Setup failures now use the existing owner's clear rejection rather than unchecked address casting/listening-only waiting. No deadline, event ordering, handler or success-path expectation changes.

## Doctor maintenance setup — 11 net

Move the exact duplicated maintenance wrapper into one adjacent support module. Every call still allocates a scope, awaits the callback, and awaits close in `finally`; all callback bodies stay in their original tests. Fixture provenance includes #180102 and #175007/#178683; their migration and hold protections remain.

Assertions **90 → 90**; registrations **12 → 12**; tables **7 → 7**.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; this is an exact wrapper extraction, not a database admission, authority, migration or durability change.

## Onboarding runtime fixtures — 14 net

Use the existing command runtime fixture owner instead of two local three-method mock builders. Each call still creates a fresh runtime and fresh nonthrowing mock methods.

Assertions **96 → 96**; registrations **33 → 33**; tables **7 → 7**.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: mock implementation identity/arity is not a fixture contract; existing output selection and asserted calls are unchanged. No runtime capability is removed.

## Plugin manifest fixture — 3 net

Use the existing explicit manifest-record fixture builder for the custom-provider test, retaining every override and fresh default collection.

Assertions **9 → 9**; registrations **10 → 10**; tables **3 → 3**.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: default property allocation order follows the canonical fixture. Its existing snapshot-reader registration import is not claimed inert; the consuming configuration tests are included in focused proof.

## HTTP streams and ClawHub request capture — 20 net

Move the exact non-ending stream constructor into a narrow pure HTTP-body support owner beside its three consumers, and use the existing ClawHub capture owner for three request-recording copies. Response factories still allocate on every fetch. The archive cancel wrapper still discards customized mock returns; the client callback stays direct.

Assertions **131 → 131**; registrations **60 → 60**; tables **17 → 17**; custom expectation-helper calls **4 → 4**.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: text encoding occurs immediately before stream construction rather than its synchronous `start`; no await crosses that work. Canonical capture parses valid producer-built absolute URLs during fetch rather than at assertion time. No security validation, EOF, cancellation or response-lifetime contract is removed.

## Plugin registry fixture — 8 net

Two consumers use the existing fresh registry fixture owner with their explicit runtime identity. Global side effects remain disabled and each call retains a fresh logger object/methods.

Assertions **68 → 68**; registrations **21 → 21**; tables **6 → 6**; custom expectation-helper calls **8 → 8**.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; the registry options and logger behavior already match the shared owner.

## Windows npm executable fixture — 6 net

Delegate duplicated npm `.cmd` construction to the existing process-adapter support owner. Keep the terminal-specific fresh directory and cleanup ownership. The same CRLF script and entrypoint are created, and all three Windows callers await completion.

Assertions **36 → 36**; registrations **26 → 26**; tables **4 → 4**.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: fixture file creation becomes asynchronous. No product invocation changes; the original cleanup remains. Windows execution proof belongs to exact-head hosted CI, not the platform-skipped local cases.

## Shell config and profile fixtures — 39 net

The shell's existing support owner absorbs repeated config composition, held-read setup and fresh profile-response construction. Reuse the existing config snapshot builder with exact config/raw/hash values, and remove redundant generic request casts.

Assertions **142 → 142**; registrations **27 → 27**; tables **12 → 12**.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: two richer scenarios assign their plain fixture's runtime-config property before allocating agents/selection objects rather than together afterward. No await or observable effect moves. Held promises, responses, shortcut arrays, issues arrays and runtime fixtures remain fresh at each original call site; hooks stay in their existing owners.

## Transcript-storage status fixtures — 10 net

A pure adjacent support owner supplies the duplicated status/maintenance defaults across unit, route and E2E tests. Supplied agents arrays retain identity, defaults are allocated per call, and E2E storage stays module-scoped. This is transcript hot/cold storage, not the standalone session-memory backend.

Assertions **92 → 92**; registrations **15 → 15**; tables **2 → 2**; custom expectation-helper calls **11 → 11**.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; values, override spread order and allocation lifetimes are retained. No retention policy or storage behavior changes.

## Evidence

Native TypeScript AST census, before/after: **707 → 707 assertions; 229 → 229 registrations** (160 tests, 19 suites, one conditional custom suite, 22 hooks, two test-finished callbacks, 13 module mocks, 11 registration calls, one suite definition). Also **63 → 63 tables, 7 → 7 conditional builders, 4 → 4 hoisted blocks and 59 → 59 custom expectation-helper calls**. Ordered case labels, table arguments, hooks and registrations are preserved per file. Counts are raw source registrations, not expanded cases, and structural preservation is not a runtime-equivalence claim.

Focused canonical runs, serial `nice -n 10`, isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG/temp directories, `--maxWorkers=1`: **309 passed, five unchanged platform skips across 18 test files**. Node selection 212.635 seconds wall (210 passed), UI selection 14.479 seconds (59 passed), final SDK replay 6.964 seconds (40 passed). Doctor fixtures exercise real migration/restore/backup admission; their 86.76-second shard retains the existing durable-state scenarios instead of replacing them with mocked coverage.

Mandatory lint-suppression suite: **14 passed**, 13.657 seconds wall. Timeout race ratchet passed, 4.303 seconds. Managed independent review completed an original full pass and a fresh repaired-source full pass, both with **zero actionable P0–P2 findings**. Author simplification pass complete.

All ten narrow test typegraphs passed. Targeted Node/UI/SDK typed lint passed (251.576/45.923/21.192 seconds, including the first canonical package-boundary prerequisite). Initial SDK lint caught an unbound `close` method; adding its accurate `this: void` annotation fixed that error. The final SDK tests, types and lint were replayed; no runtime behavior, assertion or suppression changed.

Runtime cycles **0**, 15.622 seconds; Madge cycles **0**, 28.788 seconds; mock-export ratchet passed, 16.924 seconds; original 24-file format check passed, 0.271 seconds; `git diff --check` passed. Changed-check was a dry planner only (17.935 seconds), not a broad local suite. The final annotation did not change any native preservation count. Final all-author recent campaign/test collision census found **31 open PRs, zero overlapping paths**, with at most three concurrent reads; source hashes remained sealed throughout.

Hosted-only gaps: SDK `index.e2e.test.ts` real-Gateway composition and `session-storage-settings.e2e.test.ts`, plus Windows-only executable scenarios. No broad local build, authenticated live Gateway, provider or browser-E2E success is claimed. Exact-head PR CI is the broad proof; CI seconds will be available from its completed jobs. No local test failure has been suppressed, retried or hidden by a policy change.

## Exact-head CI repair and attribution

The initial head `89a08140bfd10b852c27a8a6276bb93e65f8b25e` completed 237 check runs. Its five failing jobs are accounted for below; none is silently treated as green.

| Failing job | Attribution and action |
| --- | --- |
| PR context and evidence (121062324458) | Our body used non-template headings. Corrected headings without a source push; replacement run 40157843009 passed. |
| check-prod-types (121062812324) | Our new helper referenced DOM-only `UnderlyingSource`. Import the standard type from `node:stream/web`; the focused ES2023-only production-config typecheck passes. |
| checks-node-changed-4 (121062588755) | Untouched CLI sandbox JSON test expects agent/session mismatch; actual error rejects unknown agent alpha first. The original SDK test-env barrel reached our generic HTTP helper. Restored that reachable changed file byte-for-byte to base and rehomed only the stream helper beside its HTTP tests. Final test/setup/config/child-source import graphs reach no changed files. No claim of an executed current-main reproduction. |
| checks-node-changed-5 (121062588789) | Untouched hooks CLI JSON test expects escaped newline text, while stderr has real newline-separated remedies. Same generic HTTP restoration and narrow-owner rehome remove all changed paths from its final import graph. No test expectation changed. |
| openclaw/ci-gate (121064577627) | Aggregate of the three CI leaf failures above; awaits replacement exact-head CI after the actual repair. |

The original HTTP helper is now identical to base and is absent from the final diff. Source comparison also leaves both CLI failing tests and their production error owners unchanged. A local built-CLI replay needs an unavailable prepared runtime and would trigger a broad build, so it was not run under the campaign's host limits. The last six completed scheduled main runs and the coordinator flake ledger were inspected; neither is represented as proof of these two exact signatures.

Repair proof: the rehomed HTTP tests passed **61/61** plus the mandatory suppression suite **14/14**, 14.69 seconds combined wrapper wall time. Every original assertion/registration remains, with a fresh full native structural census at **707 assertions and 229 registrations before and after** (228 core registrations plus the unchanged conditional SDK suite). The one conditional suite's source bytes are unchanged. Independent P0–P2 review of the type repair and of the final rehome both completed with zero actionable findings. Final exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate; historical results are not relabeled as final-head proof.

Collision follow-up: PR #183194 opened after this PR's original publication and owns `src/infra/clawhub-plugin-catalog.test.ts`. Withdrew only that one-net-line request-capture migration and restored the file byte-for-byte to base. No assertion or case was removed; its 53 assertions/18 registrations are excluded from the final 23-path counts. The original 18-root focused run remains valid superset proof, including that now-unchanged catalog test. All other slices remain self-contained. Final counts and LOC above describe the reduced candidate, not the original publication.

prs.title: perf(memory): carry absent source state into archive cleanup
prs.body:
Fixes data loss: cleanup deleted a newer source inserted after inventory.

## What Problem This Solves

When memory reconciliation cleans an excluded session archive, it reads the source inventory, then repeats a hash lookup while cleaning an excluded archive whose source row was already absent. An omitted hash and an observed absence currently mean the same thing to `deleteIndexedFile`. That costs one SQL statement and one worker request; it can also adopt a newer source as the deletion target instead of preserving the inventory's expectation.

## User Impact

Archive reconciliation avoids an unnecessary database read and preserves a replacement source committed after its inventory snapshot. No operator action or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry observed absence from the inventory into the existing cleanup operation. Keep the transactional expected-hash comparison, orphan-chunk cleanup, workspace ordering, and database-owner checks. Callers without a prepared hash retain their lookup. No schema, cache, lease, heartbeat, checkpoint, SDK, or provider-request changes.

Validation is in progress. No measured candidate saving is claimed yet.

## Acceptance rule (published before measurements)

Use the unchanged frozen v3.1.5 standard workload: a real isolated Gateway, a real WebSocket client, synthetic state, and a loopback provider. Keep the five-second post-turn settle and 300-second connected-idle windows separate. Attribute every SQL shape and worker request to its owner, timer/subscription, and per-minute rate. Report SQL/requests/MAIN, median, nearest-rank p95, and range. The observer records no result rows; unchanged-result claims require source-contract evidence or a focused synthetic observation.

For this candidate, compare three alternating same-platform baseline/candidate pairs on the refreshed production base. Expected change: the tail's `index-read` operations fall from four SQL/four requests to three/three by removing the standalone source-hash SELECT. `source.delete` and its final comparison remain. Prove no preparatory hash request on known absence, orphan cleanup, and preservation of a source inserted after the inventory snapshot. Warm work and runtime MAIN must not increase; every user-facing metric must hold or improve. A 20% adverse cell stops the candidate. No latency or CPU improvement is claimed from loaded-host counts. Wall-clock/CPU A/B requires the campaign timing lock, load below 24, and at least five alternating samples per arm, cold and warm separate.

## Baseline attribution

Three frozen v3.1.5 standard runs at preregistration head `a728fbceb0013ac19879f117a982af3d5b33154e` (production `0e9b6e47458dc337f1e125cb942c00bd8749e680`) passed all 14 turns, child, cron, compaction, shutdown, and restart. All 37 frozen hashes matched before and after.

| Phase | SQL median / p95 [range] | Requests median / p95 [range] | MAIN |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Connected idle, 300 seconds | 106 / 107 [105–107] | 40 / 40 [40–40] | 0 |
| Post-turn settle, 5 seconds | 139 / 142 [107–142] | 19 / 20 [19–20] | 0 |

Connected idle is 21.2 SQL/minute and 8 requests/minute across this finite window. Every non-checkpoint operation matched in all three runs. Recurring health work is 15 SQL/5 requests per window and belongs to #182913. PASSIVE checkpoints were 5/4/3 and stay protected. The remaining tail is exactly 87 SQL/35 requests in each run, including one standalone source-hash read. Settle variation comes from fresh-shadow admission crossing the phase boundary and one health tick; it is not an optimization claim.

Workshop's repeated anchor validation needs a fact handoff from its model-context owner and is deferred. Retention, media maintenance, upstream discovery, and actual cleanup writes retain their existing ownership. A revision update does not prove affected rows; no no-op-write claim is made.

## Evidence

The production change has two completed isolated Codex reviews with no actionable findings. Final head `407ac842eb7f9dfbca668a3579d1f64b28419ef0` adds only a test lint comment: the intercepted original method is explicitly invoked with its database receiver. This fixes the `typescript(unbound-method)` finding in CI run 40158563384; production and test behavior remain unchanged. Formatting and the commit hook pass. All four focused owner suites pass (73 cases). Both archive regressions fail on the baseline at the targeted inventory boundary: absent cleanup sends the extra hash request, and cleanup deletes a newer source. The candidate passes both and the full session suite (15 cases). The open-PR comparison covers #183160, #181258, and #169212: zero new conflict paths or changed conflict blocks against their indexed heads. Exact-head PostgreSQL semantic review is approved conditionally on all three PG shards passing. Counts and static/CI gates remain pending. Production changes are +13/−7 lines; tests are +78/−38 lines. The added production lines represent observed absence separately from unprepared input. Baseline attribution inventory and normalized statement evidence are retained by the lane. No operator state or row values were collected.

## Why This Change Was Made

One shared widget-layout helper supplies the saved/default height to both the lazy placeholder and the admitted renderer. Reactions occupy existing footer space, including during an active continuation. Desktop Automations follow established Details sections. prs.title: perf(gateway): avoid registry-file agent path sweeps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared-state database file activity unnecessarily makes session-history discovery recheck every retained agent database path.

## User Impact

Removes redundant main-thread filesystem work. Session discovery, configured stores, named profiles, and alias replacement behavior remain unchanged. No migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registry commits already advance the owner revision, and closing the state database retires the prepared source memo. Remove the duplicate registry-file path capture and watch; retain registry admission checks and all agent candidate/ancestor watches.

Production change: **2 lines deleted**. The existing regression gains 9 lines; no new cache, configuration, schema, or compatibility path.

## Evidence

- Regression on unchanged production source: a registry-only file notification caused **3 realpath + 3 stat calls**. With the fix: **0 filesystem calls**. The original source-discovery file passed 15/15; focused history-worker and store-worker consumers passed 30/30.
- Source test consolidated upstream during rebase; refreshed file passes 12/12 (131.61s wrapper, 118.50s Vitest, 92% transformation). Changed-file formatting and lint passed before rebase; formatting passes afterward.
- **Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The helper refused a route that differed from operator configuration; no configuration changed.
- Built isolated Gateway stress used 10,000 synthetic sessions, 40 plugins, 65 WebSocket clients, four concurrent mock-provider turns with read/exec tools, and list/search churn. Each timing and separate allocation run exceeded ten minutes and passed workload assertions. Initial serial measurements encountered materially different host contention and **do not establish a performance win or a non-regression**. Current-base simultaneous paired runs are pending and remain a landing gate. Both current-base native builds passed; CI can run while paired stress evidence is collected.

The targeted benefit is elimination of redundant filesystem checks. No aggregate speedup is claimed. Acceptance requires correct discovery/invalidation and no controlled whole-Gateway regression; neutral aggregate performance is acceptable for this small runtime deletion.

prs.title: perf(agents): reuse stable operator model selections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restricted-role session lists, history reads, and event presentation repeatedly resolve the same agent defaults, fallback aliases, and model alias index.

## User Impact

Reduces repeated model-selection work without changing model choices, fallback order, or operator permissions. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup now initializes the committed policy reader from the canonical published runtime configuration, including plugin activation and no-op publication. Previously it retained the pre-activation object, preventing exact-owner reuse. Authored comparison input and subsequent tentative-versus-committed reload behavior remain unchanged.

The operator-policy owner now reuses prepared agent selections for a published configuration revision (or an immutable configuration), plugin metadata identity, and agent. Role allow/deny predicates are still prepared from the current role. Republishing configuration invalidates the prepared selections, while caller-owned mutable configuration and manifest arrays retain their existing live-input behavior.

This adds 40 production lines (44 added, 4 removed). Those lines establish the lifetime and complete key for the existing resolver; there is still one selection algorithm. Weak keys permit retired configurations and metadata views to be collected. The benchmark scripts are separate tooling, with usage in their headers.

## Evidence

The focused workload performs five passes of 5,000 preparations with 64 aliases and alias fallbacks. Mean CPU fell from 628.77 ms to 110.16 ms (82.5%); all passes produced the same model choices. This isolates the owner and is not a whole-Gateway improvement claim.

A short built-Gateway attribution probe confirmed the repeated owner work disappears: `prepareAgentModels` accounted for 0.375 MiB of sampled allocation versus 1,694.815 MiB in the baseline 30-second profile. This short probe is not a timing gate.

Full Gateway stress results are being collected before landing: independent base/candidate fixtures with 10,000 sessions, 40 loaded plugins, 64 restricted-role WebSocket clients, four concurrent mock-provider workers completing real tool calls, and list/search/sidebar/history plus session-label churn. Each untraced measurement lasts at least 600 seconds; allocation and CPU profiles are separate passes under the same traffic. Serial A/B then B/A order controls for the shared host. The synthetic 64-alias configuration deliberately amplifies the owner path.

Focused validation passed: 62 distinct focused tests covering policy behavior/invalidation, model aliases, prompt-prefix stability, reload behavior, and import closures; targeted core typechecking; changed-file lint/format; export-name collision checks. The new work-count regression fails on the baseline (eight preparations instead of four) and passes with the change. Baseline full build and clean candidate runtime build passed. The startup identity regression fails on the old wiring and passes with the fix; all eight targeted startup/activation/reload-authority cases passed. Validation ran locally with isolated synthetic state; no Testbox lease was used.

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), scoped clean through P2, including the startup ownership correction. No review-provider configuration was changed.

prs.title: improve(ui): defer dormant Chat presentation and streaming runtime
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold Chat evaluates streaming transforms, inactive presentation, and operation implementations before those features are used. This continues #183042 by separating those implementations from the first-screen path.

## User Impact

The initial Chat screen retains its existing appearance and behavior while evaluating less JavaScript. Common next interactions download in parallel with the route and evaluate on use; uncommon viewers and operations defer both. No dependency versions, public contracts, or user settings change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Streaming Markdown/remend and text transforms now have a live-only entry; range-only micromark removes redundant Markdown AST preparation while retaining the existing grammar and literal protection. Rich-message, Details/context, provider-review, Talk, sidebar-menu and mobile presentation load at their existing content or interaction boundary. Commands, goal operations, recovery and payload I/O retain their synchronous owner/admission core and defer their implementations.

Per-pane live frames retain FIFO custody while the implementation loads, with existing scope/retirement checks before application. Common interaction chunks receive inert route modulepreloads; downloading is not reported as avoided work. Details CSS is pooled separately from renderer JS, so Outputs cannot pull in Details through a stylesheet import.

## Evidence

Exact source head: `8b70907cf07571496b7551bd3b6118ec145ff685`. Base: `9794c6abbb6f543642e2522132300861ca2c15b2`. Both production bundles were built on the same Mac with Node 26.12.1. Candidate build: `2026.10.7-8b70907cf075-2026-10-25T03-21-59.535Z`; HTML SHA-256 `0ba1b8576b55af2953533ae33f7f8ccc6a86aadb10944a77380b31f3f21a1d6e`.

| Proof | Result |
|---|---|
| Production build and baseline-aware strict performance check | Pass, no violations and no budget exceptions |
| UI typecheck and Solid AST guard | Pass |
| Focused changed behavior tests | Pass: lazy Markdown/rich presentation, FIFO/reset/retirement, send preparation/custody, exact code regions |
| Current-main conflict tests | 20 pass across sidebar scope/lineage and Chat settings reconciliation |
| Independent autoreview and author simplification | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Production Knip | Same failure on base and head: unlisted `ffmpeg` in `scripts/generate-social-preview.mts`; no new unused-file/dependency findings |
| Localhost / 100 ms RTT readiness, CPU and A/A control | 120 valid samples; RTT holds, localhost wall time inconclusive; CPU stable under predeclared noisy-host rule |
| Separate traced compile diagnostics | Two samples per side; event/wall/thread-CPU observations below |

The build's standalone CSS warning is inherited: base raw CSS 1,595,573 B exceeds 1,595,521 B cap by 52 B; head is 1 B smaller. The baseline-aware strict check passes without changing any cap. Full UI CI is requested with `ci:full`.

| Structural metric | Base | Head | Delta |

This step removes **174,771 unused raw B (7.69%)**. Across #183042 and this PR, the original 2,379,777 unused raw B falls by **281,295 B (11.82%)**. The 40% target is not met: **670,616 B** remains to reach it. Cumulative completed network JS falls by 987,948 raw B and 286,625 encoded B, with 107→66 requests. Different original and current-main build metadata are explicitly retained in those cumulative totals.

V8 execution coverage is not compile coverage. Preloaded but unevaluated code still costs network and may cost compilation; 497,496 network raw B on head is outside this V8 execution capture, versus 337,202 B on base. The 203 KB V8-loaded reduction must not be called a 203 KB download or compile saving. Source-map intervals partition UTF-8 bytes with exclusive nested function ownership; all 50 script counters reconcile exactly, 1,663 mapped sources have no duplicate loaded copies, and 26,788 unmapped unused B remains included in the totals.

The emitted graph has no Outputs→Details renderer path or optional-heavy startup/New/login/native leak. Three existing SCC families remain; this is not an acyclic-graph claim. Login gains one JS request (22→23) while its raw JS closure falls 186,965 B.

### Timing and CPU

Twenty serial base/base/head triplets per profile use the canonical Gateway HTTP cold-load harness, identical synthetic Chat state, cold HTTP cache and first-load admission. All 120 samples completed without warnings, pending or queued work. The duplicated base is the A/A control; nearest-rank p95 and ranges are retained. The predeclared rule is ≤5% median regression with no worse p95, or further pairs; when the A/A control itself falls outside that band, judge affected CPU and structural counters over 20 pairs. A credible affected CPU regression or >20% real regression blocks.

100 ms RTT host one-minute load: 56.58–85.24.

Localhost wall time is **inconclusive**, not a latency win: the unchanged A/A composer median moved +12.35%. Head composer median is +23.12% against the first base and +9.59% against the duplicate; transcript is +8.28% / +6.23%. Those raw increases remain disclosed. CPU medians move at most +2.24%, with first-base p95s lower; within-triplet head-versus-mean-bases script CPU median is −0.585%, task +1.037%. This does not establish a credible affected CPU regression under the predeclared fallback.

At 100 ms RTT, readiness holds: composer median −0.58% and transcript −1.61% versus first base, with lower p95s. Versus the duplicate base, transcript p95 differs by +0.9 ms (+0.088%), treated as sub-1% noise. Script CPU median +0.91%, task +0.20%, thread +0.04%; all p95s lower. The independent timing review accepts both profiles under the written rule. This is a **byte/evaluation-boundary win, not a demonstrated CPU or latency win**.

Coverage, timing and compile traces are separate captures; no traced/coverage samples are mixed into the readiness matrix.

### Size and ownership review

Source-only LOC across changed code paths (generated manifest and lockfile excluded): production **32,297→33,798 (+1,501)**; tests **21,993→22,666 (+673)**; tooling **639→800 (+161)**. The audited tool/media preparation family is not a 180 KB exclusive island: much of that inventory remains needed by first-screen text, Canvas, annotations and synchronous authority. A complete immutable-facts cutover across grouping, previews and transcript consumers has a modeled ceiling of 42.2 KB unused raw, realistically 30–38 KB for text-only and 15–18 KB with first-screen Canvas. Those are unmeasured design estimates, not savings in this PR. The next step would establish one shared prepared-facts owner and remove the repeated eager extraction consumers, while preserving rich-first-screen readiness. It cannot credibly close the entire remaining 671 KB gap by itself.

prs.title: fix: SQLite and PostgreSQL return NULL sort keys in the same position
prs.body:
Related: #183015

## Decision 6: direct causality results

Both new CI failures pass on the exact PR merge base `882dffc79db3883bd3d6e004cfdeb0c94022b7d8` and approved candidate `c82c9413df6177cae1e4d2ed10f853ded83730f1`, three runs per case per revision. Every process executed exactly one selected case. Under the coordinator's explicit decision rule, both are CI flakes; this is not a claimed fix of their underlying timing causes. No production or test files changed.

| Exact case | Base rounds 1 / 2 / 3 | Candidate rounds 1 / 2 / 3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recovery: private child final | PASS 47 / 36 / 35 s | PASS 48 / 36 / 36 s |
| Child coordination: inline result (timeout) | PASS 37 / 31 / 31 s | PASS 38 / 31 / 32 s |

The comparison used one isolated Linux Testbox, Node 24.22.1, pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.4, pnpm 12.15.0, `CI=1`, one Vitest worker, and separate frozen installs. The selected test files, recovery support, configs, and lockfile are byte-identical. The 12 processes ran serially, alternating base and candidate. Observed resources: 4 CPUs, 15 GiB RAM. Remote command time including checkout/install/setup: 515.57 s.

Exact commands on each revision:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts src/gateway/server.subagent-settle-replay.harness.test.ts --testNamePattern 'recovers public work once through a sibling and reconciles its private child final' --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-send-child-coordination.test.ts --testNamePattern 'consumes an inline child follow-up result without a second requester delivery \(timeout\)' --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

Original CI evidence: [large42/job 121054162637](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40154859348/job/121054162637) expected recovery `ok/completed`, received `error/cancelled`; [large40/job 121054162607](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40154859348/job/121054162607) threw `Subagent terminal execution changed`. Both reach real persisted-session code, but neither produced a candidate-only failure. No ordering expectation was changed and no dependency on the former PostgreSQL NULL placement was established.

The one authorized recovery job rerun was accepted as run 40154859348 attempt 2 and is pending. The job-specific CLI form was blocked before dispatch by the local transport; its documented bodyless job endpoint succeeded. GitHub rejected the coordination rerun while attempt 2 was running, so no coordination rerun has yet been accepted. It will be submitted once the run permits it. No aggregate-green claim.

## Earlier hooks causality result

Direct causality testing resolves the hooks STOP. On the exact PR merge base `882dffc79db3883bd3d6e004cfdeb0c94022b7d8` and the candidate, the same four selected cases ran three times each, alternating revisions on one Testbox with Node 24.22.1, pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.4, CI=1, and one worker. Both exact worktrees used frozen installs, identical test and lockfile bytes, and the same environment settings.

| Round | Base | Candidate | Base / candidate wall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 3 pass / 1 fail | 3 pass / 1 fail | 49 / 49 s |
| 2 | 4 pass | 4 pass | 38 / 37 s |
| 3 | 4 pass | 4 pass | 37 / 37 s |

Both first runs fail `hook name cannot forge an extra System: line in queued events` with `expected [] to not have a length of +0`, the same assertion as CI. It passes in both later runs. The other three selected cases pass in every run. This is inherited/flaky under the coordinator’s explicit base-fails decision; the lower-level timing cause is not established. No source or expectation change, and no CI rerun under this decision branch.

Exact command, with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1`:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts --testNamePattern 'hook name cannot forge an extra System: line in queued events|enforces templated vs static mapping session keys on /hooks/<mapping>|dispatches agent hooks when the process clock is outside the Date range|requires stable keys for mapped persistent hooks \(missing: false\)' --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

Current additional CI failures retain their recorded attribution: standalone metadata, Windows MXC, and Windows packaging exactly match main run 40149301577. Dependency diagnostics only partially match inspected main logs; the unmatched diagnostics are outside the seven changed owners, while the history-reader unused export matches main. Swift packages has a schema-32 fixture expecting rejection while its owner supports 32; this is outside the patch and has no established main-run match. No aggregate-green claim.

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL's default NULL placement changes participant order, filtered sandbox inventory, and history that includes empty transcript windows compared with SQLite.

## User Impact

These readers return unprompted participants first, and unused sandbox runtimes and empty transcript windows last, on both engines. Existing filters and tie breakers are preserved. This is PostgreSQL-readiness work with no SQLite behavior change, schema migration, dependency, or transaction change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The query owners explicitly request `ASC NULLS FIRST` or `DESC NULLS LAST`. Nullable participant aggregates use the default SQLite placement. The old `native` selector is replaced by `not-null`, documented for keys that are all NOT NULL in the canonical schema; only the two membership aggregates use it. Plain `ASC` preserves their PostgreSQL index ordering because NULL placement is irrelevant for `identity_id`.

This reconciles merged #183015 without accepting the measured extra sort from forcing `NULLS FIRST` onto a NOT NULL membership key. The prior forced-placement experiment increased the identity aggregate median by 66.7%; the final spelling restores its index-only plan. No generator or schema was changed.

## Evidence

- Baseline `ad2172d77e26`: three SQLite cases passed and three PostgreSQL cases failed across standalone/fused participants, filtered sandboxes, and all-window history. Fixtures include NULL/non-NULL keys and ties.
- Final source: all six parity cases and ten entry-write cases passed; 9.47 s Vitest / 33.05 s command wall. Selected owner suites passed 90 tests in seven files / 64.10 s wall, including the membership read worker.
- Targeted infra/session types, production/test lint, and formatter parity passed. `pr-simplify` completed; isolated review is clean through P2.
- All three actual PostgreSQL conformance steps passed on the final head in [CI 40154859348](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40154859348): shard 1, 306 tests / 1,484.22 s runner time; shard 2, 332 tests / 1,215.71 s; shard 3, 547 tests / 38 skips / 721.30 s. Total: **1,185 passes / 38 skips**, including all six parity cases and ten entry-write cases.

Membership EXPLAIN on PostgreSQL 17.11 used canonical DDL, 100,000 rows, 1,000 selected members, and 31 alternating pairs per shape. The candidate SQL is compiled through the production helper. Identity-only aggregation retains `Aggregate → Index Only Scan`, with no Sort: median 0.105 → 0.101 ms, p95 0.116 → 0.142 ms. Tuple aggregation keeps the same bitmap-scan/sort plan: median 0.709 → 0.698 ms, p95 0.820 → 0.782 ms. Results are identical. The median regression gate passes; these are query-plan diagnostics, not a throughput claim.

The earlier sandbox check also passed: 31 pairs, median 0.305 → 0.262 ms, p95 0.393 → 0.276 ms, using `idx_sandbox_registry_session`. Participant/window indexes do not cover their nullable sort keys.

Recorded standalone test cost: `pnpm test src/infra/database-engine/nullable-ordering.conformance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 24.41 s wall, including 20.03 s cold worker preparation; 2.32 s Vitest / 107 ms test bodies. This cost measurement is retained from the unchanged test's initial proof run.

<details>
<summary>Review delta and remaining scope</summary>

Compared with reviewed head `9707480263f4`, this revision rebases onto `882dffc79db3`, restores the ordered-JSON option as `first | not-null`, documents its schema constraint, and migrates the two membership callers to `not-null`. Nullable participant defaults and the three original ordering fixes remain. The seven production files total +13/-8 lines against the rebased main; no new helper, cache, state, or compatibility alias.

Two observable nullable-order families remain outside the explicit allocation: proxy capture presets sorting nullable `capture_events.host`, and ingress dead-letter listing sorting nullable `failed_at`. Other inspected candidates exclude NULLs or already specify placement: worker completion cutoffs, shutdown, archived-session retention, cold-storage/cost-report windows, cron terminal completion constraints, approval history, message-position predicates, recently stopped transcripts, and meeting chronology. Invalid NULL ingress claims fail decoding.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier non-PG CI attribution</summary>

Nine old-head failures have matching tests/error signatures in [main run 40149301577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149301577) (`f0dcb354e45b`):

| Failure | Matching main job |
| --- | --- |
| Windows workspace-quiescence ENAMETOOLONG | 121037449160 |
| Windows MXC missing process-runtime mock export | 121037449179 |
| Windows trusted-harness packaging module missing | 121037449161 |
| Dependency diagnostics (1,346 normalized lines identical) | 121037449674 |
| Production types, session-catalog TS2739 | 121037449659 |
| Core-2 test types, same TS2739 | 121037449682 |
| tsdown memory fixtures missing fs-safe | 121037450396 |
| Four standalone-metadata fixture failures | 121037450352 |
| Lifecycle retention assertion | 121037450315 |

The coordinator authorized one failed-job rerun of [40151854642](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40151854642) on old head `9707480263f4`. Its isolated-completion case failed again in job 121052941775: timeout after 1,109 ms, code `runtime-unavailable`. This is an unresolved real failure with no same-test main match, not a passing rerun or an inherited-failure claim. Source inspection shows the fixture substitutes prepared-runtime acquisition and inference and does not call the seven changed query/helper owners, so the coordinator’s changed-owner STOP condition is not met. The previously canceled large-39 job had no verified terminal outcome when monitoring stopped; its last cached observation was in progress. No passing verdict is claimed for it. No second rerun or aggregate-green claim is made.

</details>

prs.title: improve(agents): reduce allocation churn during streamed replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streamed model replies with heartbeat monitoring allocate avoidable temporary objects while scanning every decoded SSE character, including OpenAI-compatible streams that also need sanitization.

## User Impact

Lower allocation churn during streamed replies, with unchanged wire bytes, heartbeat callbacks, framing, cleanup, and backpressure. No configuration changes or migration are required. The measurements below cover the production stream owners; they do not establish a live Gateway or provider latency improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The heartbeat observer in `prepareOpenAISdkSseResponse` only recognizes ASCII LF, CR, and colon. Replace its string iterator with an indexed `charCodeAt` scan: surrogate halves cannot match those delimiters, so supplementary Unicode preserves the same line-state transitions. This removes the iterator work without adding a cache, alternate path, or another owner. Decoding, encoding, enqueueing, and stream queue policy remain unchanged.

The synthetic benchmark composes the actual `wrapGuardedBodyStream` and `prepareOpenAISdkSseResponse` owners used by `buildGuardedModelFetch`. Usage and scope live in its script header; `scripts/perf/README.md` is unchanged. The existing transport test covers supplementary Unicode inside a comment and before a non-comment colon across sanitized, official, and opt-out streams.

Simplification review: production +5/-3 lines (net +2: indexed scanning and its ASCII rationale replace iteration), tests +2/-2, benchmark +276. There is one scan and no retained compatibility path or new runtime machinery.

## Evidence

Five alternating fresh-process baseline/candidate samples on idle Linux, Node v26.8.1. Each allocation sample drains eight warmed 1,065,528-byte synthetic streams: 4,096 text events, 128 heartbeat blocks, and 683 mixed-sized chunks, including split UTF-8 supplementary characters. V8 JS-heap sampling uses a 4,096-byte interval and includes objects collected by both major and minor GC. Baseline source: `5b3a3924256e`.

Paced timing runs separately after allocation sampling stops: five streams per outer sample, with a 1 ms source delay every 32 chunks. Values below are medians across the five outer samples. First text event means availability of the complete first text-delta SSE event, measured from stream construction.

| Path | Sampled allocation MB/input MB, baseline → candidate | First text event ms, baseline → candidate | Paced full stream ms, baseline → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Passthrough control | 1.2090 → 1.2151 (+0.5%) | 1.1804 → 1.1498 | 25.8144 → 25.7724 |
| Heartbeat observation | 6.9711 → 4.0590 (-41.8%) | 1.2682 → 1.1818 | 36.9727 → 29.8814 |
| Sanitization + observation | 17.1716 → 12.4847 (-27.3%) | 1.2662 → 1.2280 | 43.6260 → 37.4859 |

Attribution: in Linux observation sample 1, iterator `next` descendants account for 22,918,760 sampled bytes on baseline and zero on candidate; TextDecoder remains roughly constant (16,630,208 → 16,378,728 bytes). Separate marked diagnostic runs retain identical codec counts: 5,472 decode calls and 8,294,848 decoded UTF-16 code units per mode; sanitized mode retains 32,776 encode calls and 8,510,912 output bytes. JSON parsing and MessagePort cloning are outside this owner path.

All benchmark runs passed independent expected-byte hashes, callback and cleanup assertions. Baseline/candidate have matching delivered chunk counts and upstream pull positions; pausing after reads 1, 2, 10, and 100 stops further upstream reads. All 43 transport tests passed, alongside focused core/script lint, targeted owner typecheck, formatting, and diff checks. Independent review of source, harness, and comparison evidence found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The rebase preserves the reviewed patch and owner sources.

Limits: sampled JS allocations are not retained heap, RSS, or native backing-store measurements. GC pause, promotion, and whole-Gateway effects were not measured. Initial busy-Mac runs on Node v26.12.1 also showed lower allocation, but timing was inconsistent/adverse even in the unchanged control; those timings remain inconclusive and motivated the idle-Linux comparison. The Linux timings are owner-level observations, not a claim that production time to first token improves. No live Gateway or provider request was exercised.

prs.title: fix(codex): tool turns lose their final answer after a transient retry
prs.body:
Closes #155396
Related: #181779 (the stranded-reply retry, which has no recorder; composes with this PR, see below)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Codex tool turn delivers no final answer (`provenance_rejected` → `context_unavailable` → harness failure) when a transient same-model retry or another same-run continuation ran the tools on a new native turn.

## User Impact

User impact: channel and scheduled Codex turns that hit a provider overload, then finish their tools without a final message, now get the normal tool-free summary instead of a failed run. Settled-turn capture rejections now log which provenance check failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

After a transient retry the runner suppresses the prompt it already persisted (`attempt-normalization.ts`) but keeps that run's transcript recorder. So the retried native turn has no `<turn>:prompt` identity, while the verifier required one for the active turn. Capture now anchors on the prompt the recorder persisted on the earlier native turn. The verifier still requires that row in history, in order, with matching source evidence, and still binds the tool boundary to the active turn. Duplicate, drift, mirror-prefix and foreign-turn checks are unchanged. Each verifier rejection site now reports its own reason instead of a shared `provenance_rejected`.

#181779 (merged) handles the other suppressed-prompt case: the stranded-reply retry, which has **no** recorder, so no prompt row exists anywhere; it anchors on the turn's first mirrored row. The two never overlap: `promptSuppressed` needs no recorder, and `promptIdentity` comes from one. Main is merged into this branch with both anchors kept. The suppressed path gets its own two reasons (`provenance_unexpected_prompt`, `provenance_foreign_anchor`) because this PR retires the shared `provenance_rejected`.

## Evidence

**Behavior or issue addressed:** #155396. A direct-channel Codex turn completes its tools after a `reason=overloaded` transient retry, ends with no final text, and fails with `capture failed reason=provenance_rejected` → `context is unavailable` → `Codex agent harness failed; not falling back`.

**Before evidence:** reproduced on main `7299b241097f` in the isolated Gateway run below. It is the same log sequence as the issue, and the agent run ends with `status: "error"` and no payloads after the tool already ran once.

**Real environment tested:** an isolated Gateway built from this branch at `11dd11cc4fb6`, and the same Gateway from main `7299b241097f` as the control. Each had its own state dir, config and loopback port, with channels skipped and the bundled Codex plugin on the **pinned native Codex app server 0.162.1** (`homeScope: "agent"`, `tools.exec.mode: "full"`). Native Codex pointed at a local scripted Responses server via `-c openai_base_url=…`. One user message was sent with `openclaw agent --agent main --session-id … --message … --json`, so it went through the full embedded runner, its transient retry and settled-turn finalization. Linux x86-64, Node 26.12.1.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** the scripted provider decides from request content only:
1. the first fresh request → `response.failed` with `server_is_overloaded` (the transient overload);
2. the next fresh request → one `exec_command` that appends `AMBER-731` to a marker file;
3. the request carrying that tool output → completes with **no** output (the empty final);
4. a request carrying the finalizer's omitted-context developer notice → the summary text.

Every model request reached that local server. There was no real model call and nothing reached a real endpoint. Commands, config and provider script are in the details below.

**Evidence after fix:**

| | this branch `11dd11cc4fb6` | main `7299b241097f` |
|---|---|---|
| provider requests | 4: overloaded, tool call, empty final, finalizer | 3: overloaded, tool call, empty final (finalizer never asked) |
| marker file (tool effect) | `AMBER-731` × **1** | `AMBER-731` × **1** |
| capture | no warning | `capture failed reason=provenance_rejected` |
| agent result | `status: "ok"`, payload **"The receipt command ran once: AMBER-731."** | `status: "error"`, payloads `[]` |

The finalizer request on this branch carried `message, message, function_call, function_call_output, message`: the persisted user prompt, the retried turn's tool call and its output, then the finalizer's notice.

**Observed result after fix:** the overloaded turn is retried once, the retried turn's tool runs exactly once, and its empty final is recovered by one tool-free finalizer turn whose answer is the run's only reply. On main the same run loses its answer after doing the work.

**Native regression (pinned Codex app server, CI-runnable):** `settled-turn-finalizer.native.test.ts` › "same-run continuation after a transient provider overload". The first native turn persists and annotates the prompt; the provider fails it as overloaded (asserted: `failed`, `503 OVERLOADED`, replay-safe, one request). The retry keeps the recorder and suppresses the prompt; the tool runs on a new native turn with no final text. Settled evidence must hold the persisted prompt, the call and its output, and the finalizer persists one answer without repeating the command. With the fix reverted it fails 3/3 with `Native turn lost its settled-tool evidence`; with the fix it passes 10/10. The whole summary suite passes 7/7. A live-provider variant runs under `OPENCLAW_LIVE_CODEX_SETTLED_FINALIZATION=1`, with the overload still scripted.

**Unit coverage:** `settled-turn-context.test.ts` asserts the specific reason at every fail-closed site. It also covers continuation capture against the persisted prompt, a continuation whose persisted prompt is missing from history (rejected), and #181779's suppressed path, including the two new reasons.

**Checks at `11dd11cc4fb6`:** `pnpm tsgo:extensions`; vitest over 24 files that touch the verifier, capture, history-rejection, worker runtime or the finalizer (313 tests); oxlint, `oxfmt --check` and the line-cap ratchet on the 8 changed files. All pass.

**What was not tested:** a live provider. My account has no OpenAI key on this host, so the model replies are scripted (only the overload is scripted in the live variant, which I have not run). I also did not test a real chat channel (Telegram/Discord); delivery here is the `openclaw agent` result.

<details><summary>Redacted Gateway logs</summary>

This branch:
```text
[agent/embedded] transient same-model retry 1/8 for openai/gpt-5.6-sol reason=overloaded: delayMs=1190 runId=<run> sessionId=<session>
[agent/embedded] settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer: runId=<run> sessionId=<session> provider=openai/gpt-5.6-sol — running isolated finalization
(no capture failure, no harness failure)

```

main:
```text

[agent/embedded] codex settled-turn finalization context capture failed reason=provenance_rejected
[agent/embedded] codex settled-turn finalization context is unavailable runId=<run> threadId=<thread> turnId=<turn> reason=context_unavailable
[agent/embedded] settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer: runId=<run> sessionId=<session> provider=openai/gpt-5.6-sol — running isolated finalization
[agents/harness] Codex agent harness failed; not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend harnessId=codex provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.6-sol error="Codex settled-turn finalization context is unavailable"
[agent/embedded] settled-turn finalization failed: runId=<run> sessionId=<session> provider=openai/gpt-5.6-sol error=Codex settled-turn finalization context is unavailable — preserving failed recovery

```

Provider phases, in order (this branch): `overloaded` → `tool-call` → `empty-final-after-tool` → `finalizer-summary`. On main: the first three only.
</details>

<details><summary>Run recipe</summary>

```bash

  OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=19451 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=<local token>

node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port 19451 --verbose &

```

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The internal `@openclaw/ai` reasoning-partitioner facade forwards two markdown-core types even though production code consumes only the runtime factory. One forwarded type has no consumer, while the other exists only to let the facade's own test import a type that markdown-core already owns. These extra edges are reported as unused exports and obscure the actual type ownership boundary.

## User Impact

Runtime behavior does not change. OpenAI completions streaming continues to load `createReasoningTagTextPartitioner` through the same deferred internal module, and the canonical markdown-core parser types and implementation remain intact. This also leaves the package manifest, enumerated public exports, protocol behavior, configuration, dependencies, and all parser assertions and timeouts unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The facade now exposes only the runtime factory that its transport caller needs. Its test imports `ReasoningTagTextDelta` directly from the existing markdown-core owner, and the unused `ReasoningTagTextPartitioner` forwarding edge is removed entirely. This is the smallest complete cutover: no new wrapper, alias, cast, compatibility path, or test-only production seam is introduced.

## Evidence

The frozen base was inspected across the package export map, index and transports barrels, deferred build entry, all consumers, and introduction history. `@openclaw/ai` has no wildcard or supported export for this internal facade, and complete source search found no consumer of the forwarded `ReasoningTagTextPartitioner` type.

On the exact candidate tree, the maintained remote OpenClaw recipe passed:

- changed-file formatting and lint for both edited files;
- all selected production and test type-consumer families;
- targeted checks confirming both type forwarders are absent, the test uses the canonical markdown-core type, and the package export boundary is unchanged; and
- `packages/ai/src/utils/reasoning-tag-text-partitioner.test.ts` plus `packages/ai/src/transports.import-boundary.test.ts`: 2 files and 62 tests passed.

The exact head also received two independent clean reviews: a calibrated engineering review traced the affected owners, consumers, build/export surfaces, history, and compatibility, while canonical P0–P3 autoreview completed with no findings. Hosted CI and security workflows registered with no failure at the landing checkpoint; broad rows were still in progress and remain accurately pending rather than being reported as green.
