prs.title: fix(plugins): keep plugin service stop budgets on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin reload and one-shot diagnostic shutdown reporting timeouts too early or waiting beyond their budget when the system clock changes.

## User Impact

Service startup and cleanup observations retain their configured elapsed-time budgets across clock corrections. Outstanding cleanup remains owned until it physically settles.

## Why This Change Was Made

All deadline seeds and comparisons in the existing service lifecycle use `performance.now()`. The public `stop({ deadlineAtMs })` contract remains an epoch deadline: the service owner converts it once before the asynchronous stop chain. Startup, reload, drain, and stop durations and cleanup ownership remain unchanged.

The regression uses the existing service-handle suite. It replaces the contributor's Promise-race observation with direct checks immediately before and at the deadline and explicitly advances the monotonic clock alongside timers.

## Evidence

- Both new cases fail on the main baseline: a backward wall-clock step extends a caller deadline, while a forward step ends a one-shot stop budget early. The expected boundary is pending at 4,999 ms and timed out at 5,000 ms.
- The initial integrated candidate passed 51 focused service, reload, and scheduler-context tests. After the CI repair, the suppression-policy test and three affected service trace/deadline tests pass again on the final integrated head. Independent Codex reviews found no actionable P0–P2 issues; the full lifecycle owner and final repair were reviewed. Targeted Oxlint/Oxfmt pass. The first CI run caught a new suppression-policy violation in an optional allocation cleanup; that cleanup was removed. Final-head CI run [40148710589](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40148710589) passed; the repository watcher reports green after excluding superseded results.
- Prepared head: `743f9236fe347d4d6f47ac7186d002e179c2117e`, incorporating current main `bf7cce6522263`. Production LOC delta: 0. Nearby cleanup removes empty optional trace-object branches. The existing deferred rejection path preserves arbitrary thrown values without a new lint suppression. Tests: +54; documentation: +2. No new configuration or state format.
- Live limitation: the contributor's isolated Gateway and one-shot CLI clock-injection harness was unavailable, so those experiments were not independently repeated. The regression exercises the actual service lifecycle owner.

Contributor-provided shipped-entry evidence: before the fix, a Gateway reload with a one-hour backward clock step remained pending beyond 45 seconds. With the fix, the five-second service observation reported a timeout at about 4.86 seconds after the hook began. A separate one-shot agent run returned its expected response and reported its ten-second diagnostics timeout at about 10 seconds. These are contributor results; they establish observation timing, not cancellation of the retained cleanup.

Thanks @SunnyShu0925 for the fix and original Gateway/CLI proof.

prs.title: perf(sessions): skip empty prepared maintenance transactions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold first turns and explicit cron turns issue a prepared session-maintenance metadata request even when planning found no rows to change. The writer currently opens and commits an empty SQL transaction for that request. Three frozen v3.1.5 synthetic Gateway runs traced exactly one such pass in first-turn and restart-first-turn, and two in cron.

Carry the planner’s explicit `requiresWrite` fact to the existing metadata owner. A prepared empty plan still runs in that owner’s FIFO, applies its in-memory age fact, adopts the result, acknowledges captured changes, and releases its retained preparation; it returns the existing `not-committed` outcome without transaction admission or publication. Plans with selected victims, unprepared/native calls, age commands, and planner statistics retain their transactions and checks.

No schema, cache, generation, retention-policy, transcript-identity, or cross-store transaction change. Empty plans already accepted writes arriving after preparation: subsequent receipts preserve the next maintenance pass. Nonempty plans still compare current candidates and live protection before removal, then retain commit admission and publication. Cron claim/recovery receipts are unchanged.

## Evidence

Acceptance was published before measurement in the original draft and `scripts/perf/cold-turn-attribution.md`: frozen real-WebSocket synthetic Gateway workload, cold and warm separated, three alternating same-platform pairs, counts per phase/operation, zero runtime MAIN increase, and no unaccepted 20% metric regression. Profiles/counts establish no latency speedup. Wall-clock timing is not claimed.

Baseline attribution (v3.1.5, three complete runs; SQL / requests medians): first turn 216 / 67, restart first turn 160 / 54, cron 236 / 63; 30 warm turns 51 / 12. Every target/warm phase has MAIN 0. Source-attributed empty metadata envelope: first 2 SQL, restart 2 SQL, cron 4 SQL; no warm occurrence. Other dominant cold owners are required or assigned to separate lanes.

Two isolated Codex reviews of the production change were scoped-clean through P2. CI run 40157890856 found two old worker tests injecting only after the now-removed empty commit; test-only commit `20e9beb88ce1f32b248f3e4f52fd53913dd4b08b` moves those injections to the no-write result before host age-fact adoption and removes obsolete commit assertions. Both corrected cases pass, and the permitted CI-forced delta review is scoped-clean. Production blobs are unchanged. Final paired counts, static gates, exact-head CI, PostgreSQL approval, and open-PR comparison remain pending; this is not campaign READY.

## Scope and review

Three production files carry one prepared boolean and select the no-write branch; two existing test files are updated. The real-worker regression covers empty, foreground-write, and removal cases. Necessary production growth carries the prepared fact without a cache or another owner; the superseded callable-only return shape is removed from all callers. This SQL lane is not a defensive-site sweep.

Release-note context: avoid empty database transactions during cold session maintenance while retaining removal safety and cron recovery.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several extension tests still reconstruct fixtures that already have an owner: process results, loopback listeners, held operations, Teams references, JSON responses and QuickJS compiled modules. This finishes a small, independently reviewable fixture tail without changing production behavior or removing test coverage.

This is the coordinator-authorized **100+ line residue exception**, not a LARGE campaign PR: **94 additions, 197 deletions, 103 net lines removed across 23 files; production delta 0**. No config, schema, protocol, dependency, public SDK or feature changes. The standalone session-memory backend and its tests are untouched.

### Process-result fixtures — 46 net

Ten consumers reuse the existing pure `extensions/test-support/command-result.test-support.ts`: Linux Node, AutoReview, QA agent processes, Foundry CLI, local CLI TTS, AppleFM, Deepgram Flux, two Codex probes and Crabbox worker commands. Optional-field absence, explicit timeout/cleanup fields and final overrides stay intact. Buffered adapters keep both Buffer allocations local; AppleFM and Deepgram retain the narrow `exit` discriminant. Module constants still allocate once.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: local TTS result key insertion order changes, but values, own-key set, stdout identity, fresh stderr and every observer remain unchanged. No production guard is removed.

### Browser CDP loopback fixture — 5 net

Use the existing loopback bind owner. The real server, socket tracking, credential-header expectations, streaming response and cleanup callback remain.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: fixture bind diagnostics and error-listener cleanup use the existing owner's behavior instead of a local message.

### Copilot discovery response — 3 net

Reuse the same file's discovery-response helper for the tracked failing response. The original try/catch, error identity, text-read control and assertions remain.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; this removes an identical constructor.

### Teams conversation references — 8 net

Five copies use a constructor on the existing messenger test-helper owner. Default user, agent and conversation objects are fresh per call; supplied overrides preserve their identities. The raw legacy bot-only control stays unchanged.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: non-observed outer-key order in the tenant fixture changes. Production constructs the outbound reference explicitly; tenant/AAD forwarding and all assertions remain independent.

### Teams Graph response routing — 8 net

Reuse the existing same-file response router for five routes. Keep the original outer fetch mock and header recorder, so the redirect test still observes the actual Authorization header before routing through the real guarded download path.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: one internal mock and an async delegation hop replace the copied router. Status, headers, body, request order and the security oracle are preserved.

### Workboard card and identity gate — 7 net

Reuse the existing card factory with explicit identity/title/position and conditional metadata (4 net), and the already-imported deferred constructor for the held identity lookup (3 net). No renderer or UI behavior changes.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: ordinary card-input key order changes; nested freshness is retained. The deferred adds an unused reject member; resolve and wait behavior remain unchanged.

### Ordinary memory held operations — 7 net

Three entry/release fixtures reuse the existing `holdMemoryTestOperation` owner from #179767. Entry-before-wait ordering, fresh errors after release and every finally drain remain. This is ordinary MemoryIndexManager test setup, not the protected standalone session-memory backend.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: release wraps the same per-call native resolver; resolver function identity is not observed.

### QuickJS compiled fixture modules — 6 net

Expose the existing eager test-support promise and remove a second read/compile of the same two WASM files in its consumer. The dependency explicitly supports sharing compiled modules and instantiates a new VM and linear memory for every create/restore operation.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: compiled Module and extension-descriptor identities are shared between these test paths. VM instances, heaps, bridge state, snapshots and continuations remain independent; no production cache is changed.

### Calendar and Azure JSON responses — 13 net

Use native `Response.json` for defined authored object/array payloads in Calendar and Azure provider tests (8 net). Azure's generic unknown voice-catalog input uses the existing SDK `jsonResponse` through an already-present import (5 net), preserving JSON.stringify semantics including undefined. Response construction stays at the original per-call/callback boundary.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none for these inputs; bytes, status, statusText, headers, body consumption state and freshness were compared.

## Evidence

Preservation against base `eafdca06fb5779d31030852b7a007ede1d3fd2c3`: **609 assertions → 609; 196 terminal test declarations → 196; 24 suites → 24; 45 parameter tables → 45; 31 hook registrations → 31; 43 mock/hoist registrations → 43.** No case, assertion, table row, hook, mock registration, timeout, retry, skip or suppression was removed or weakened. Exact assertion inputs, registration inputs and tables match; complete-module/constructor expansion checks cover the fixture changes and nested freshness.

prs.title: fix: restore activity recaps with mixed provider catalogs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Activity recaps incorrectly reporting `recap unavailable: no Gateway model credential` when an available utility model shares a catalog with other providers' transports. A real foreground model/tool call can succeed while the recap preflight rejects the same model.

## User Impact

Activity recaps can use the configured utility model in mixed-provider catalogs. Existing runtime support, credential selection, fallback, cooldown, and authority checks remain in effect. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Utility preflight supplied the entire catalog's physical route variants to a decision for one selected model. The provider policy interpreted unrelated transports as alternatives for that model. Both utility runtime checks now use the existing catalog view's per-model identity grouping, matching the model catalog and isolated-completion owners.

This was found during PostgreSQL-readiness validation and reproduces with SQLite. It changes no database runtime behavior, schema, dependency, protocol, or configuration surface. The production change reuses an existing owner; the regression adds no production seam.

## Evidence

- RED on the main baseline (`95869afe436`): 18 existing tests pass; the new mixed-provider regression fails. With only the selected model present, the setup control stays available.
- GREEN: all 19 utility-runtime tests pass. Test cost: `pnpm test src/agents/utility-completion.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 28.33s in the test runner (26.60s Vitest; 46.28s including remote environment setup).
- Affected consumer suites: 83 tests pass across eight files, covering recap freshness/retry, utility fallback and harness selection, model choices, and isolated completion routing.
- Real Gateway with a fresh valid SQLite config and `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` for both foreground and utility: foreground `session_status` succeeds; automatic recap is nonempty and `current` through `sessions.list`; zero credential warnings; graceful exit 0. prs.title: fix(talk): honor chat model and runtime selection in browser calls
prs.body:
Closes #164730

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Browser Talk consultations using the agent's default model and runtime even when the current chat has a different session-only selection.

## User Impact

Browser Talk's backend agent follows the current chat's model/runtime selection, including changes made between voice turns. Explicit model pins retain their no-silent-fallback behavior. This does not change the realtime speech model, global defaults, or phone/meeting callers' explicit routes; no migration or new configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser caller now opts into session selection after the shared consultation path reads and updates its session entry. Selection reuses the existing stored-model, runtime-compatibility and fallback-policy owners, preserving resolved-route provenance, child-session fallback policy, and ignoring historical execution metadata. Existing locked-session and lifecycle checks remain in place.

Related: #164229 addresses CLI execution routing and #164417 addresses fallback dispatch. This change is scoped to the stored session selection missing at the consultation boundary, rather than duplicating those dispatch changes.

## Evidence

- Composition regressions extend the existing storage suite and exercise the real Browser Talk runner, shared consultation, admission and isolated session storage, mocking only model execution. On unchanged base `69a512d2526039663a19147533ea8fb0f2e28b3e`, the original four cases failed at dispatch: provider/model were undefined and the runtime/fallback selection was absent. An added visible-child case separately reproduced the wrong fallback ladder before child lineage was forwarded. All five selection cases now pass.
- **66 tests across five focused Talk files passed in 35.69 seconds**, covering changed pins, explicit/default/automatic selection, visible-child fallback policy, existing caller routes, cancellation, locked sessions, transcript identity and parent lineage. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.agent-consult.test.ts src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.agent-consult.retry-context.test.ts src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.storage.test.ts src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.lineage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Independent AutoReview (P0–P2): scoped-clean; no actionable findings. Its assessment was source-based; test execution was performed separately.
- Core production types and all 27 core-test type groups passed. After lint-only fixture-helper renames, the affected type group, focused tests and changed-file lint passed again. The remaining planned changed-scope guards passed, including schema, legacy-store, sidecar, import-cycle, webhook and pairing checks.
- `pnpm build` passed on final commit `4a1839274b63e299c1153c992df5eb047bdede96` in 7m 11.7s, including declaration generation, Plugin SDK checks, runtime packaging and Control UI build. Build and package-manager checks were run serially for the final proof.

### Authenticated backend proof — October 4, 2026

Executed the **actual `createTalkClientAgentConsultRunner(...).runArgs(...)` Browser Talk backend boundary** on head `4a1839274b63e299c1153c992df5eb047bdede96`, without mocking the runner, session store, admission, model selection, embedded execution, provider transport, or model responses. This is a terminal-driven live backend integration test, **not a browser microphone/WebRTC/speech-playback test**.

The task-owned process used an isolated state database and synthetic workspace, the existing OpenAI subscription via an expiring environment-backed token reference, no refresh-token copy, and a restrictive tool policy. Neither turn made tool calls. Production Gateway, configuration and auth files were not modified. Node 26.7.0 launched the source harness with the repository's `scripts/tsx.mjs` preload. The harness initialized the normal plugin registry, secrets snapshot, scheduler, real client voice-session record and consultation runner.

Configured default: `openai/gpt-6-luna`, runtime `codex`, no fallback models. In the same stored session and open voice-session record:

1. Persisted the explicit user selection `openai/gpt-6-sol` / `openclaw`; called the real runner and awaited the provider response.
2. Updated that session's selection to `openai/gpt-6-astra` / `openclaw`; reused the same runner and awaited the second provider response.
3. Independently reopened the isolated SQLite transcript read-only and verified both persisted assistant messages against the live lifecycle events and returned text.

Sanitized observed output (run identifiers and local paths omitted):

```text
HEAD 4a1839274b63e299c1153c992df5eb047bdede96
DEFAULT model=openai/gpt-6-luna runtime=codex fallbacks=[]
TURN 1 stored-selection=openai/gpt-6-sol runtime=openclaw
  actual embedded-run model=gpt-6-sol provider=openai api=openai-chatgpt-responses
  lifecycle=end stopReason=stop executionSettled=true replayInvalid=false
  returned=TALK_PROOF_1_OK elapsedMs=19836
  persisted assistant model=gpt-6-sol api=openai-chatgpt-responses
  persisted text=TALK_PROOF_1_OK usage.input=5381 usage.output=11 stopReason=stop
TURN 2 stored-selection=openai/gpt-6-astra runtime=openclaw
  actual embedded-run model=gpt-6-astra provider=openai api=openai-chatgpt-responses
  lifecycle=end stopReason=stop executionSettled=true replayInvalid=false
  returned=TALK_PROOF_2_OK elapsedMs=4440
  persisted assistant model=gpt-6-astra api=openai-chatgpt-responses
  persisted text=TALK_PROOF_2_OK usage.input=5396 usage.output=11 stopReason=stop
LIVE_CONSULT_RUNNER_PROOF_COMPLETE
process exit=0
```

Both turns used the OpenClaw embedded execution path instead of the configured Codex harness. The recorded provider responses and persisted assistant metadata establish execution beyond the previously mocked dispatch assertions. The second turn proves the runner rereads the stored selection rather than retaining the first turn's model. The runtime override remained `openclaw` on both turns; this is not a claim of switching from one runtime to another mid-call.

The successful run followed fixture-startup corrections (supported Node version, canonical secrets/scheduler initialization, tool policy, and the repository's ESM-only TypeScript preload). Earlier attempts ended in local setup/loader errors and are not counted as successful provider proof. No PR source or dependency changes were made for this evidence.

### Hosted CI failure attribution

The [failed `check-test-types-core-2` job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37178397572/job/111366096026) checks merge `07a019e17d69f525dc49dfccf30dd7086fc9c9d5` (base `9a18261098162c6de13566e9107ef699e82eb151` plus this PR head). It reports TS2559 at `ui/src/components/mcp-app-bridge.cursor.test.ts:13:57`.

Upstream [refactor 73149b26822ada60cdba47a3546704bdec94f2a9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/73149b26822ada60cdba47a3546704bdec94f2a9) removed the fourth boolean `supportsServerResources` parameter from `buildMcpAppHostCapabilities`; the untouched cursor fixture still supplies `true` in that now-object position. Both caller and callee blobs are identical between the tested upstream base and test-merge commit. Neither is changed by this Talk PR. The older local base retains the boolean parameter, explaining the passing local type checks. The CI failure is inherited; no rerun, unrelated UI patch, or merge exception is claimed.

Remaining validation limits: no browser microphone/WebRTC/speech-playback call, no live Codex-harness turn or runtime-to-runtime switch, and no entire-repository test run. The running installation was not patched. Review acceptance of this backend proof remains pending.

Implemented with AI assistance and independently reviewed.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): load remote transcripts during authentication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm remote chat reloads waited for `hello-ok` before requesting the selected transcript, adding a serial network round trip after connect. This follows the combined subscription/history change in #182846.

## User Impact

The selected transcript subscription and initial history now travel immediately behind connect. Sending and subscription publication still require accepted hello. Cached rows ready during connect preparation are adopted immediately after dispatch, before capturing their history cursor; slow storage never holds up the request. Cached transcript/title hydration can wait through a stalled connection until the existing opening/handshake timeout (normally 30 seconds); storage completing after an attempt retires can wait on the current retry receipt. This keeps rendering out of connect preparation without adding another timeout or retry owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already queues at most 15 following frames (64 KiB each), then dispatches them in order after hello delivery with the existing authorization checks. This uses protocol v4's existing behavior: no wire fields, server queue, or version bump. The protocol note records the additive-first version rule and connection retirement requirement. Old clients may keep waiting for hello.

The subscription coordinator remains the sole subscription owner. The initial read omits approval replay; after accepted hello, an approval-capable client obtains the stronger subscription in the background. This adds one subscription RPC on that connection without putting approval replay on the awaited transcript path.

Authenticated HTML stays network-first. It carries viewer-specific bootstrap/preferences and scope-filtered config (`control-ui-index.ts`), the same URL chooses public versus authenticated session entry (`control-ui-session-entry.ts`), and CSP reflects current terminal/ingress policy. Stale-while-revalidate would replay those online access/config decisions. The service worker's generic outage shell and build-mismatch fresh-document recovery retain their existing contracts. A cacheable online shell would first need to separate those per-request facts.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before[Before: four serial round trips to transcript]
    A[HTML] --> B[WS upgrade + challenge] --> C[connect / hello-ok] --> D[subscribe + history]
  end
  subgraph After[After: three serial round trips to transcript]
    E[HTML] --> F[WS upgrade + challenge] --> G[connect then queued subscribe + history]
    G --> H[hello-ok and history responses]
  end
```

Composer already has a three-round-trip path; it does not wait on history. Session switching remains one combined subscription/history request.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule recorded before timing: committed real-Gateway benchmark, two synthetic 120-message conversations, token authentication, cold load, asset-cached warm reload, and session switch. Localhost and 100 ms RTT / 10 Mbps; 20 serial interleaved A/B pairs and 10 A/A pairs per profile. The shared host is noisy, so also compare renderer thread CPU, Gateway CPU and request counts. Goal: another 20% reduction in warm remote transcript/composer medians; no attributable local regression. Timing band: median <=5% regression with p95 no worse, or the additional pairs/CPU control rule. A smaller clean win may land with the target gap stated.

Fresh remote/local A/A and 20-pair A/B cohorts are running for the final candidate. The earlier composer-regressing candidate was rejected; this PR will not be submitted for merge until the final measurements are recorded.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck | Pass |
| Pane lifecycle + cache hydration | 33 passed; final current-receipt hydration + warm reload check: 11 passed |
| Session subscription owner | 12 passed |
| Real-WebSocket hello order/auth failure | 7 passed |
| Canvas widget fixture | 2 passed |
| Regression on base | Both pre-hello pipeline cases fail waiting for the absent request |
| Focused lint/format | Pass |
| Production Knip | Same `scripts/generate-social-preview.mts: ffmpeg` unlisted-binary diagnostic on base and head; no new ignores |
| Build + strict size check | Pass; zero violations |
| Startup gzip | 281,893 -> 281,793 B (-100 B); 7 JS / 1 CSS requests unchanged |
| Startup CSS | 40,097 B gzip unchanged |

Independent P0-P2 review is complete. The board-restoration finding was checked against the full owner: restoration rereads the merged cache and honors explicit removal, so its proposed regression does not occur. One unnecessary test type argument was removed. An earlier candidate's composer regression was rejected; the final candidate defers cached transcript rendering until connect dispatch and is measured separately.

Solid refactor census in touched production files: render controllers, effects, render effects, `untrack`, DOM queries, `flush`, owner APIs, and `onCleanup` all 0 -> 0; plain-owner event listeners 2 -> 2.

LOC across touched files: production UI 3,387 -> 3,505 (+118), tests/helpers 1,649 -> 2,075 (+426), benchmark 1,335 -> 1,591 (+256), docs 541 -> 576 (+35). Production growth carries the per-connection dispatch receipt and pending subscription lifecycle. Benchmark growth keeps one isolated Gateway per source and serializes acknowledged browser samples, so A/A and A/B share the same worker lifecycle.

Final synthetic before/after screenshots will be embedded with the completed benchmark evidence before merge.

prs.body:
## Round 3 predeclared qualification

The lead accepts a Details-only PR with the closed dashboard as a non-regression control. The chat primary is zero warm Details skeleton flashes in 11/11 reloads. The prior candidate's chat CLS rise is rejected, despite overlapping IQRs. This remains a measurement draft until the geometry defect is attributed and repaired.

Before changing the Details owner, collect buffered layout-shift entries with structural node paths and previous/current rectangles on baseline and the rejected candidate. Then compare baseline and the repaired candidate in at least 11 unprofiled interleaved pairs on one quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, using the same Team-scale unchanged warm chat fixture, repository Chromium and live-fast latency. Chat CLS paired median must be at most +0.005, and candidate CLS must be no worse in at least 7/11 pairs. Hello-handled, FCP, first/final painted rows, LoAF and dashboard secondaries must not regress under the campaign's paired/IQR rule. Existing boot budgets remain unchanged; product runtime growth at most 30 lines. Avatar loading and nested-content experiments remain out of scope.

On a pass: focused unit and chat/Details browser tests, changed checks classified against main, independent review through P2, full UI e2e and exact-head CI, then a ready PR and stop before merge. The measurements and stop report below belong to round 2 and do not qualify this round.

---

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of an unchanged chat conversation briefly replaces a Details skeleton with real sections. Matching session-descriptor hydration can then replace the restored Details subtree again. The campaign evidence recorded fourteen loading states; the later structural probe isolated an approximately 40 ms Details skeleton flash after transcript content.

## Why This Change Was Made

Details already reserves its final desktop width and holds its lazy composition until the transcript mount. This candidate preserves both. Once the transcript owner has restored the session incarnation, the column remains blank while the composition loads. A genuinely cold panel retains its skeleton. Details presentation follows the accepted transcript incarnation; action guards still validate both transcript and live-descriptor identity.

The rejected eager imports and preload are removed. The nested FrameBody experiment is also removed: it supplied no additional median visible-wave reduction over Details alone. Avatar loading is unchanged and remains a visible wave owned by the separate avatar lane.

The desktop browser fixture now uses a browser-side import expression, avoiding Vitest's server import rewrite, and supplies actual Environment facts before saving its warm snapshot. Benchmark setup no longer waits for an open Details panel in the closed dashboard layout. The synthetic fixture includes tool reviews, a run failure, Details facts and assistant images, with unchanged cursor-delta replies.

## User Impact

**Stopped experiment; do not merge.** Details meets the chat-route gate, but the closed dashboard median stays at four visible waves. Under the stated requirement that both route medians fall, this does not qualify for a ready PR. No schema, configuration, protocol, persistence or budget changes.

## Evidence

Measured head: `a15c944ad03e91b3e33decf75ac73956dbc9bbd6`; pinned base: `9733a02026996c8d70ae7b74b8a06c15bd10f760`. The retained Details variant was built independently from the combined candidate. Eleven interleaved baseline / Details / Details+nested triplets ran on one quiet AWS **c7a.4xlarge** (16 vCPUs, 32 GiB), with repository Chromium, Team-scale full-UUID off-roster routes, warm unchanged snapshots and live-fast latency. Lease `cbx_7bdade23e0dd` is released. [Measurement run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3b7034e836573aa02b4931b3931ab33a).

Timing runs were unprofiled. Separate compositor screenshot captures validate visible changes; their timings are diagnostic only. Pixel comparisons crop the pane, require a channel change of at least 32 in at least 0.4% of pixels, and group changes within 100 ms. Structural mutations that do not paint are reported separately.

|---|---|---|
| Post-content visible waves, median [Q1, Q3] | 5 [4, 5] → 4 [4, 4] | 4 [3.5, 4] → 4 [3.5, 4] |
| Paired counts fewer or equal | 10/11 | 9/11 |
| Warm Details skeleton after content | 11/11 → 0/11 | 0/11 → 0/11 (closed) |
| Lazy-view skeleton after content | 0/11 → 0/11 | 0/11 → 0/11 |

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Assistant messages built by two shared test helpers reused one zero-usage object. Transcript normalization freezes nested message data for storage, so normalizing one fixture could leave a later independently constructed message with frozen usage and make transport error accounting throw instead of recording terminal availability.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. Default assistant test messages now own fresh usage and nested cost state, matching the independent lifetime that production transport outputs already use. Explicit caller-supplied usage still keeps its original identity, and production transport mutation, transcript normalization, configuration, and persistence behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both builders now call the existing `createZeroUsageFixture` factory rather than publishing the module-level shared object as their default. The shared constant remains available to tests that explicitly choose read-only aliasing.

The regression extends the existing transport-stream test owner. For each builder it normalizes one message through the real transcript path, constructs another message, verifies separate usage and nested cost ownership, and then exercises the real transport error assignment. It also verifies that an explicit usage override is still returned unchanged.

## Evidence

The deterministic base scenario reproduced the failure for both builders: after normalizing the first message, the second reused non-extensible usage and `assignTransportErrorDetails` threw `Cannot add property usageReport, object is not extensible`.

On the corrected candidate:

- changed-file formatting and lint passed with no warnings or errors;
- all affected type graphs selected by the repository's iteration helper passed; and
- the changed transport test and the existing transcript-normalizer caller test passed: 2 files, 16 tests.

Hosted CI, independent review, and automated exact-head review remain pending on this initial non-draft PR.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two cron integration cases intermittently exhaust deadlines while doing fixture setup on unchanged main. Failure-alert persistence assertions pass, then two fallback session events are still active at the final root-zero assertion. The first manual-run RPC can also spend its one-second deadline starting cron recovery, which the minimal Gateway fixture deliberately skipped.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. This repairs fixture readiness in cron integration tests while preserving production lifecycle behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare the existing main-session destination and reply runtime before failure alerts, and start the empty disabled cron owner before adding the busy job. Both fallback events still traverse real target preparation, dispatch, and settlement. Both manual requests still use the real WebSocket RPC and their original one-second deadlines. Every assertion, polling deadline, cleanup path and test remains unchanged.

The existing response-row assertion helper moves unchanged to the sibling assertion-support module so the integration file stays within its existing line cap. The committed repeat runner uses fresh processes and records every full-file outcome and host load. Its executable root is registered with Knip.

No production code, SQL, schema, cache, generation, admission or settlement ordering changes. The investigation found correctly retained active work during cold preparation, not a missing stop/drain. Tests for cold session creation, cancellation and recovery-before-admission remain at their owners.

## Acceptance rule (preregistered)

Run the committed `scripts/perf/repeat-cron-test.mjs` workload through the campaign proof semaphore on the same macOS host, using fresh per-process Gateway/test state and the pinned default Bun test runtime. Record host load and every outcome. Run at least 20 unchanged-main full-file samples and at least 20 candidate samples under comparable load. Keep cold process startup separate from any warm observations. The metric is target failure count per full-file run and active root work at the existing assertion; no elapsed-time or CPU-speed claim is made on this loaded host. A win requires reproducing the target failure on the base and zero target failures in all candidate samples, plus a focused regression red on the base. Any candidate target failure is a stop. Keep every existing assertion and deadline; no sleeps, retries, timeout increases, or skips.

## Evidence

Repeated comparison pending.

Candidate head: `2185ff94eb81bb9f83cec98242b967a7403e00fd`. Merge hold: the full-file comparison is running.

- Unchanged-base full file: first 5/5 passes, 75/75 tests. Starting one-minute loads: 74.83, 56.12, 55.51, 58.00, 69.08.
- Focused unchanged base: failure-alert root-zero assertion reproduced twice with actual 2. A two-case baseline diagnostic passed the busy-job case and reproduced the root failure.
- Corrected focused fixture: 2/2 passes. Both fallback events reached dispatch and completed settlement before the unchanged final assertion. The first fixture pilot failed in setup because it lacked an explicit session-store path; it is excluded from behavioral proof.
- Temporary stage tracing was removed exactly before publication. It is absent from this PR.
- Two isolated Codex fixture reviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings, including the final assertion-helper extraction. The workload runner had an earlier independent clean review. Formatting, JavaScript syntax and the unchanged line-cap ratchet pass. Type-aware local lint refuses the campaign external dependency store with “Declaration input escapes checkout”; its guard is preserved, and CI must supply the static result.
- At least 20 baseline and 20 candidate full-file samples, final overlap audit, and exact-head CI remain pending. This PR is not approved to land until those gates are recorded here.

## Workload

`node scripts/perf/repeat-cron-test.mjs <existing-output-directory> 20`

Each sample invokes the repository Vitest wrapper for `src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, saves its complete local log, and records exit status and host load. Synthetic fixtures only. prs.title: perf: stop polling while session projections reconcile
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session history readers repeatedly ask the worker whether their projection is ready while the reconcile owner is already doing that work.

## User Impact

Readers wait for their own session to become ready, including when unrelated sessions are still reconciling. Cancellation, the existing bounded rebuilding response, and logged background-failure behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing reconcile owner now holds per-session completion promises and publishes readiness after its finalize or a committed transcript writer's final ready receipt. Readers register before their single initial status read, then await that publication instead of sleeping and polling. Synchronous rewrite, replacement, JSON update, append, and manual compaction producers carry their established readiness through the existing publication owner. Manual compaction performs its existing rebuild inside the replacement operation before the final receipt.

No schema, SQL shape, cross-store commit ordering, cache, generation, or fencing change. This is based on #183034 and preserves its mutation options, logical accounting, and folded publication. Production delta: +121/-57, net +64 lines; the per-session completion map and producer facts replace polling and the later manual-compaction rebuild. Tests: +285/-21. Documentation/workload: +83/-9.

## Evidence

The committed `scripts/bench-session-projection-ready.mts` workload made a real WebSocket `chat.history` request against an isolated Gateway with six synthetic 100-message sessions. Production baseline `4ce728b934a` and candidate `6ae58e0339c9` both returned the correct session/latest message while five unrelated projections remained dirty; all five warm reads succeeded.

| Count | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold projection-status worker requests | 75 | 1 |
| SQL from those status requests | 225 | 3 |
| Cold total SQL / requests / MAIN | 554 / 105 / 0 | 332 / 29 / 0 |
| Warm SQL median / p95 / range | 6 / 7 / 6–7 | 6 / 6 / 6–6 |
| Warm requests median / p95 / range | 2 / 2 / 2–2 | 2 / 2 / 2–2 |
| Warm MAIN, every sample | 0 | 0 |
| Full run SQL / requests / MAIN | 1,611 / 291 / 59 | 1,380 / 213 / 59 |

The causal saving is 74 worker status requests and 222 statements per observed cold waiter. Full-run totals include boot, drain, all warm reads, and shutdown. Drain changes from 569 SQL / 42 requests to 571 / 44 as two generic execute requests move from cold to drain; the last reconciliation statement also moves from the first warm read into drain. The warm history and pending-input reads have identical SQL shapes/counts; the baseline's one extra warm statement is the reconcile worker's final WAL checkpoint. No warm owner gains work. Twelve helper-process boot statements are included in each total. This is one complete matched pair plus five dependent warm reads, not five independent cold samples.

Both runs verified all 36 frozen observer files, recorded 26 CPU profiles covering all 24 SQL-observed Gateway threads, and had no SQL prepare/execution or analyzer errors. Helper processes are counted separately and are not claimed as profiled. The calm-host wait exceeded one hour (runtime load 73.37 baseline, 58.27 candidate); these are operation-count/profile results, with no latency or CPU-speed claim.

All 178 focused tests across 16 owner/consumer suites passed, including 11 prompt-prefix tests. Regression proof is red on original behavior: held unrelated reconciliation produces four status reads rather than one after synchronous rewrite/replacement, and a >4,100-row manual compaction reaches the exact missing-ready-receipt assertion after trimming to three rows. Tests also cover synchronous JSON update, final ready/dirty/rollback receipts, cancellation, and the existing logged-failure settlement. Neither cited red is a setup or timeout failure.

The first Codex review was incomplete; the completed second review found an omitted synchronous JSON-update producer. That producer is fixed and covered by the held-reconcile regression. An additional authorized delta-only review is scoped-clean. The proposed listener-failure handshake was rejected because synchronous installation/invalidation finishes before waiter continuations, and callers retry their owning read; no stale-data harm was demonstrated.

Final Knip comparison, the type-only lint repair, exact-head CI, and PostgreSQL approval are pending. Local typed lint refused the required external dependency placement before analysis; no containment bypass or relocation was used.

## Overlaps

The complete shared open-PR index found 23 other main-target PRs touching these files. Base-only versus candidate merge-tree comparisons preserve existing conflict paths and marker counts for 21. Two overlaps were explicitly accepted:

- #177242 moves the test's `readVersion` import to a split read owner; this PR adds a mutation helper to the same import. Whoever rebases second should combine those imports.
- #164843 extracts `waitForPreparedSessionTranscriptProjection` from the wait body replaced here. Its prepared `sessionId` and options can remain at that helper boundary; the helper should register with the reconcile owner's per-session completion, perform the one initial status read, and await the owner signal instead of retaining the polling loop.

No speculative wrapper or unmerged API was added merely to hide those overlaps. The refreshed #183171 head also adds no conflicts. Other compared PRs: #183139, #182286, #170176, #169241, #163964, #162160, #162144, #162132, #162126, #161396, #161344, #161315, #152205, #151441, #150616, #150246, #148581, #146407, #142236, and #139998.

## Preregistered projection acceptance

The flow is a real WebSocket `chat.history` request to an isolated Gateway while six synthetic session projections reconcile. Both heads use the same repaired committed workload: six sessions, 100 messages each, 256-byte payload, target index zero, and five warm reads. The production three-second readiness deadline, 30-second client timeout, 120-second drain limit, and existing 100-ms external drain snapshots stay unchanged. No live state or logs are used.

Count before timing: record projection-status requests per cold waiter, all worker requests, SQL statements on main and workers, and normalized per-operation attribution for cold, drain, every warm read, boot, and shutdown. The baseline must reproduce more than one cold projection-status request; the candidate must use at most one. Record the cold result separately. Only the exact retryable `UNAVAILABLE`/`chat.history` rebuilding response with the existing message and 250-ms retry hint is accepted as a bounded cold non-success. Baseline cold success becoming candidate rebuilding is a regression. A cold rebuilding response never proves early readiness.

Both runs must finish with `complete=true`, exactly five successful warm reads, and validated requested-session/latest-message results. Warm operation counts must hold or improve. Compare matching phases; the earlier incomplete 107-projection-request/119-total-request/367-SQL baseline establishes attribution only and cannot supply warm or whole-run comparisons. Early readiness and background-failure behavior also require owner tests: a target completes while an unrelated reconcile remains blocked, and the existing logged background-failure fallback is preserved.

Capture the frozen v3.1.4 observer plus per-process/thread CPU profiles on each head and account for total work as well as main-thread work. Record host admission load and internal free space for each arm. Use three alternating baseline/candidate pairs when the one-minute load is below 64 and internal free space is at least 12 GiB; otherwise use one complete pair with source attribution. This lane has already exceeded its 60-minute calm-host wait, so these runs are counts/profile evidence only and make no wall-clock or latency improvement claim.

If qualified timing becomes available, take the campaign timing lock, require one-minute load below 24, and collect at least five interleaved samples per head (ABAB), keeping cold and warm separate. Report median, p95, and range. Every user-facing timing metric must hold or improve; any 20% regression stops the change. Five warm reads inside one Gateway are not five independent cold samples.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot configure cron and hook concurrency through a supported setting.

## User Impact

`cron.maxConcurrentRuns` accepts a positive integer and defaults to **8**. It controls the cron-service execution cap and shared cron-agent/hook lane budget. Command/script jobs use the service cap without consuming the agent/hook budget. Existing scheduling boundaries remain intact; capacity one retains forward progress.

This restores a deliberately retired control: retained config values become effective and Doctor preserves them. Higher limits increase resource and provider demand. The bounded-stop setting has moved to #165180; this draft now contains only concurrency behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing resolver supplies the configured value to service admission, Gateway lane budgets, and slot acquisition. The existing hook reservation remains bounded by available capacity. There is no new shared scheduler, environment variable, database format, or lease policy.

## Evidence

Standalone head: `2e17633288ee324f944a8322e4b57f54958f6c36`.

Both real foreground Gateway scenarios verified mixed hook/cron-agent traffic, overflow HTTP 503 without model I/O, and completion after release. The combined opt-in harness remains available at commit `55215079819821a750a6a7967823558bb5a3b836`; it is excluded from both split diffs because it requires both settings.

**Still draft:** maintainer acceptance of this restored public control remains outstanding. CI excludes drafts, so required exact-head CI is not claimed green. Full aggregate `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` remain incomplete. Prior package results do not replace standalone-head CI or package validation.

<details>

The original head merged upstream `e9edda34` normally; this split adds a follow-up commit without rewriting shared history. Repeated hydration of a retained exact transcript context recursively copies nested message payloads that the replica can own once.

## User Impact

Reduce repeated history-copy allocation without changing stored transcript bytes. Message/event envelopes and navigation containers remain independently writable for CLI and SDK consumers; initial model-context projection keeps writable nested data.

## Why This Change Was Made

After detaching the canonical worker snapshot, the existing replica seals its exact-context message descendants. The existing transcript copier then shares those immutable payloads on later reads while still detaching mutable envelopes and maps. Complete/window paths retain their current behavior. No cache, schema or configuration is added. Production code grows by 11 lines to establish the missing ownership fact.

Whole-message freezing was rejected during source audit: CLI reseeding assigns message timestamps, and SessionManager exposes writable envelopes. Prompt-cache consumer changes are outside this producer PR and are held identical between measurement arms.

Related: #182253, #182893.

## Evidence

The existing exact-context isolation regression fails on the base and passes with the fix. All 18 replica tests and 31 model-context snapshot tests pass, including nested initial-context mutation and durable/SDK isolation. Changed-file formatting and lint pass, including both measurement drivers. The targeted core typecheck passes. Independent production, regression, documentation, and benchmark review is clean: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable).

### Retained exact-context result

Two fresh, CPU-swapped baseline/candidate process pairs agree on a small container-retention saving. Each process used five within-process samples, 20 independent contexts per cohort, and 0/1/4 held rereads of a 64-message × 16 KiB synthetic transcript with a real compaction boundary.

| Held read views | Baseline MiB/context | Candidate MiB/context | Signed delta MiB | Paired relative delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 1.028266 | 1.028442 | +0.000176 | +0.0171% |
| 1 | 1.049453 | 1.042617 | -0.006836 | -0.6514% |
| 4 | 1.112219 | 1.084855 | -0.027365 | -2.4604% |

The first-read increment falls from 22,215.28 to 14,862.92 bytes (−7,352.36 bytes, −33.096%); additional reads fall from 21,938.59 to 14,763.27 bytes each (−7,175.32 bytes, −32.706%). Strings were already shared, so this does not save another full payload-sized string graph. Seed-only retention is effectively unchanged.

All four processes match the output golden and exact owner hashes. All 60 cohorts report zero released replica/view weak-reference survivors. Independent audit verified all 44 raw artifacts, CPU swaps, source/update pins, completion receipts and clean guard logs. Eight yielded forced collections bracket each heap reading. These are forced-GC owner-retention results; five samples within a process are not five independent pairs, and this does not qualify natural GC, latency, promotion or fingerprint retention.

### Measurement rule declared before capture

Measure two fresh, counterbalanced baseline/candidate process pairs, each with five within-process owner-retention samples of 20 independent exact contexts and 0/1/4 retained rereads. Report absolute MiB/context, incremental bytes/read, released weak references and full input/output equality. A real compaction boundary must select the exact path.

Coverage clarification, declared before any Gateway cost capture: the warmup diagnostic observed exact-context seeding in all four sessions but no retained exact rereads. Normal turn appends invalidate that snapshot; ordinary history polling and initial model-context reads use other owners. The unchanged Gateway turn mix therefore measures the added seeding cost and protects against turn/GC regressions. The direct owner rig supplies reread-retention proof. No Gateway reread or fingerprint benefit is assumed, and no artificial recovery flow is added to force cache hits. The original zero-hit diagnostic is retained as evidence.

Run at least two concurrent, CPU-swapped baseline/candidate pairs of the same Team-shaped isolated Gateway turn mix, each with a fixed 2,000 foreground turns and at least ten minutes of capture. Keep maintenance enabled. Gate untraced GC/work, event-loop and foreground latency under v5–v5.4: mean adverse >=20%, or >=10% in both pairs; p99 needs >=1,000 samples/side, p95 >=200; major tails are context below50 collections/side. Submillisecond mean pause-percentile changes are context. Preserve per-kind GC, absolute/relative deltas, both maximum pauses, and the max(50ms,2×baseline maximum) safeguard.

Before rejecting on GC/work, promotion or max pause, collect at least four matched identical-source A/A pairs in the same workload and mode. If controls trip a gate, classify the protocol inconclusive and lengthen fixed work with fresh controls. Any eligible mixed-sign or >5× baseline metric gets exactly one predeclared extra pair, adjudicated on signed absolute three-pair mean versus20% mean baseline. Never trim pauses, exclude maintenance after the fact, or normalize by major-cycle count. Guard-interrupted pairs are discarded and replaced with the same protocol, retaining their numbers.

Measure promotion in a separate traced pass with its own baseline; traced timing is context. Measure fingerprint-family surviving allocation separately over a separate 610-second Gateway turn mix with collected-object sampling disabled, requiring the profiler diagnostics sidecar to prove at least 600 seconds of sampling. Divide disjoint verified owner-frame samples by recorded completed-round model requests; continuous idle gaps remain sampled, so this is not an exact all-window per-request cost. Preserve the raw profile and frame coverage. This is sampled surviving allocation, not an exact WeakMap dominator total. Production deployment is not part of this PR.

The first CI run found an implicit array element type in the new retention rig (TS7034/TS7005). An explicit numeric result shape fixes it; a typecheck narrowed to that script passes. The correction is type-only and independently reviewed.

Measurements are pending; do not land before their results are recorded. The production patch rebased unchanged onto c800ae545e06dedfd4f65f1eac69a4a6a4d6809a; owner, hydration, snapshot, SessionManager and prompt-cache inputs are unchanged from the focused test proof. Both measurement arms will use this updated common source. PR CI validates the rebased head.

prs.title: perf(sessions): narrow transcript presentation imports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prewarmed transcript readers load process-tool output schemas and streaming tool-repair modules that history presentation does not use.

## User Impact

A small reduction in retained worker code and heap, with unchanged transcript output. This is a bounded simplification; it does not remove the larger database, Typebox, or Kysely graphs. No configuration, storage format, authority, or worker-pool changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing process-poll predicate, unchanged, into its sole activity-presentation consumer. Import the existing text-repair functions from their defining payload module instead of the streaming/promotion barrel. Eight source modules disappear from the foreground history worker's loaded graph, with no new cache or deferred handler.

Runtime production LOC: **−2**; benchmark/tooling **+182**; tests **+2** (whole diff **+182**). The benchmark growth supplies the requested reproducible worker/code measurement; it does not load in production. The existing import-boundary regression now guards these two paths.

## Evidence

Node 26.12.1, synthetic worker through the real worker-task transport, source-loader mode, five fresh isolates per side in alternating AB/BA order. The first task is a successful missing-database `prewarm`; forced GC follows task completion. Both sides resolve the same checkout, replacing only the three changed source files for baseline. Results below are arithmetic means on exact PR head `4e15960944715fa37f5e8e0e82e4dae75f4e709a`; all five observations are retained.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Delta | Samples/side |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Loaded file-backed scripts | 2,623 | 2,615 | −8 | 5 |
| Retained heap, bytes | 70,593,250 | 70,098,080 | −495,170 (−0.70%) | 5 |
| V8 code + bytecode metadata, bytes | 3,993,955 | 3,964,970 | −28,986 (−0.73%) | 5 |
| Cold ready, ms | 8,615.14 | 8,709.24 | +94.10 (+1.09%) | 5 |
| First prewarm round trip, ms | 22.06 | 46.76 | +24.69 (+111.91%) | 5 |

Heap ranges: baseline 70,572,104–70,620,888 bytes; candidate 70,088,448–70,104,720. Cold-ready ranges: 7,689.83–9,372.32 ms vs 6,835.04–10,722.36 ms. First-task ranges: 3.07–45.37 ms vs 19.23–129.89 ms. There are too few samples for p95/p99 gates.

Separate worker snapshots analyzed with `heap-snapshot-diff.mjs --code-by-script` and reviewed filesystem script identifiers show code/source retained bytes **31,795,632 → 31,594,608 (−201,024; −0.63%)**, n=1 per side. Shallow code bytes: 12,244,488 → 12,201,576. This development-loader evidence is not an estimate of the packaged Gateway's entire heap.

Latency is **inconclusive**, not a claimed improvement. An initial five-pair run on the loaded host measured first-task means 8.14 → 44.97 ms (ranges 3.36–18.49 vs 8.23–104.77), with cold-ready means 18,634.09 → 17,651.78 ms and heap means 70,590,888 → 69,931,483 bytes. Four identical-source A/A controls then measured 4.38 → 11.76 ms first-task means (+7.39 ms, +169%; ranges 2.87–8.77 vs 2.91–35.03), despite identical source and script counts. A subsequent five-pair run measured heap 70,585,482 → 70,097,013 bytes, cold ready 8,286.72 → 8,780.59 ms, and first task 9.23 → 10.32 ms. The exact-head repeat in the table followed a clean rebase with surrounding reader changes. Both later runs isolate HOME/state/TMPDIR and record code counters immediately after forced GC, before debugger/snapshot work. All runs and the adverse observations are reported; no pauses or samples were trimmed. Parent wall-clock timings include dispatch and rescheduling on this shared development host.

This is a small verified memory reduction without a new cache or additional production machinery. The lead must weigh the bounded simplification against the unresolved latency evidence; these local controls do not establish absence of a latency regression. It does **not** establish populated-history latency, every task kind's first-use behavior, natural GC/work, promotion, a packaged-build memory reduction, or a production-scale memory saving. Broad build/startup validation belongs to PR CI. After deployment, look for the eight removed presentation-only modules and a modest worker-heap reduction at matched activity; worker count and transcript caches should not change.

Reproduce from the baseline source at `5b3a3924256efaecaae16f6baea661121c4837e6` (materialize the three paths listed in the script under an owned baseline directory):

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-transcript-code-measure.mjs \
  --output <owned-output> --baseline-dir <baseline-source> --samples 5
# Same-source controls:
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-transcript-code-measure.mjs \
  --output <owned-control-output> --baseline-dir <baseline-source> --samples 4 --control
# Separate snapshot pass: add --snapshots; use the emitted *-scripts.txt allowlists.
```

Focused validation:

- `session-history-read.imports.test.ts -t 'keeps lazy readers independent of unrelated runtime barrels'`: fails on baseline with exactly the process-schema and streaming-repair backedges; passes on candidate.
- `agent-activity-events.test.ts`: 25 passed.
- `plain-tool-call-text.test.ts`: 44 passed.
- `eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts`: 22 passed.
- Export-name collision guard passed; changed-file formatting and lint checked.
- The full startup-import test file's static checks passed, but its dynamic worker startup triggered a large artifact build and timed out locally. That process was stopped under the local compute limit; runtime startup cases remain CI proof, not a claimed local pass.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Autoreview refused before inference because its selected provider did not match operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

prs.title: fix: exec lifecycle fixture recognizes anchored children
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the exec lifecycle test failing with “missing spawned child” on Linux, which blocked unrelated pull requests.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change. The test checks the command identity and cancellation lifecycle in both plain and memory-bounded exec configurations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Linux host exec supplies a memory budget, selecting a process-group anchor that launches the command in another process. The returned command PID is correct, but a spy on the test process's `ChildProcess.prototype.emit` cannot observe that child. macOS normally selects the plain path and masked this assumption.

The fixture now compares the returned PID with the synthetic command's own PID output (PowerShell emits its PID on Windows; POSIX exec replaces the shell), then checks cancellation, the terminal reason, physical exit, and empty process registries. Repeated nonterminal kill-error handling remains covered in the existing child-adapter owner regression, which now also checks error delivery and listener disposal. No production hooks, retries, platform skips, or weaker terminal assertions are added.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, recorded before testing: both configurations pass on Linux and macOS; returned PID equals child-produced PID; cancellation reports `manual-cancel`, the process exits, and registry counts return to zero. Repeated operational errors remain nonterminal and disposal releases listeners. This test-only repair changes zero production statements or worker requests; no performance claim or timing experiment.

- Red baseline: [Linux CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40152050530/job/121045724407), failed at the prototype-spy lookup. The complete exec/anchor path is unchanged on main.
- macOS, default pinned Bun: both plain and memory-bounded lifecycle cases pass; existing child-adapter suite passes (24 tests). Basic oxlint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Final-head Linux CI at `e8b323dd2e27`: both lifecycle cases and all 24 adapter tests pass ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40158258769/job/121064448198)); all [final-head CI tests and static gates pass](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40158258769), including test types, lint, source contracts, and baseline ratchets. The optional Testbox entered a queue and was stopped; no Testbox result is claimed.
- Two isolated Codex review rounds completed before the final fixture-only follow-ups. The reported `test.for` mismatch was corrected. CI then caught the unsupported numeric timeout overload, fixed with the typed options argument. The GitHub review identified the Windows shell/child identity distinction, now fixed by printing PowerShell's own PID. These follow-ups leave production code unchanged; Windows runtime proof is not claimed.
- Open-PR overlap index: no open main-targeting PR touches either changed file (complete shared index); no new merge conflicts.
- Local default build/typed lint stopped before test execution because the external-to-checkout dependency store is refused by declaration containment. The supported source-only replay passed; normal-install CI covers the required build and typed checks; no containment override.

Change size: zero production LOC; 29 net test lines removed. No SQL, schema, migration, SDK, or update path changes.

prs.title: fix(talk): show a Working badge while the agent works during a voice call
prs.body:
Closes #164472

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: during a Talk voice call there is no visible sign that the agent is still working, so long tool runs look like the call has stalled.

## User Impact

User impact: a persistent "Working..." badge sits beside the live microphone while the agent works on the current voice turn, and clears by itself when the work finishes, fails or is cancelled. Listening state stays visible alongside it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The badge shows while either of these is active:

- a delegated agent consult (`openclaw_agent_consult`), tracked from the existing Talk `tool.call` / `tool.result` / `tool.error` events. The gateway-relay transport now emits these lifecycle events for native consults, correlated by one call id, and stops emitting once the relay session has closed.
- a normal chat run started by a spoken turn. In the macOS app, spoken turns arrive as chat messages and the agent works in the main run rather than through a consult, so the badge also follows the composer's existing "run is abortable" state while voice is active.

## Evidence

Screenshots:

- Control UI browser E2E (`ui/src/e2e/browser-talk-working-status.e2e.test.ts`), mock gateway, delegated consult in flight:

  ![Control UI Talk working badge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scarabone/openclaw/pr-assets/talk-working-badge/pr-assets/voice-working-status.png)

- Live, macOS app on a 2026.9.7 gateway with this change applied, during a spoken turn while the agent was working (badge cleared on its own when the reply finished):

  ![macOS app Talk working badge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scarabone/openclaw/pr-assets/talk-working-badge/pr-assets/macos-live-working.png)

prs.title: perf(diagnostics): reduce stall recorder sampling overhead
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The always-on main-thread stall recorder collects more samples than needed to identify substantial stalls, adding background profiler and serialization work even when nobody requests a diagnostic profile.

## User Impact

Reduce background sampling work while retaining retrospective stall attribution. The tradeoff is roughly ten samples for a 250 ms stall instead of twenty-five. Exported event-loop metrics, stall thresholds, retention, and on-demand profile settings are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Change the recorder's existing sampling interval from 10 ms to 25 ms. Continuous recording and overlapping five-second windows remain: stopping the last profile discards the native code map, and restarting incurs a heap scan. Arming after detecting lag would miss the beginning of a synchronous stall.

Production LOC delta is zero: one existing constant changes, with no new production machinery. Benchmark-only instrumentation records native profile starts/stops, serialized bytes, main-thread CPU, and V8 cumulative allocation without starting another sampling profiler. The existing stress harness gains persistent per-viewer filter churn and a recorded preload identity.

## Evidence

Built isolated Gateway proof at 25 ms produced stall attribution for injected 323 ms and 1,001 ms pauses, including `pbkdf2Sync` in the inclusive frames (11 and 35 samples). Eight short rounds also exercised all sidebar filter shapes across round boundaries. Separate checks confirm the cost observer rejects overlapping benchmark CPU and heap captures.

Two matched, counterbalanced load pairs use 10,000 synthetic sessions, 6,000 settled runs, 40 synthetic plugins, 64 WebSocket clients, mock-provider tool turns, subagent activity, and sidebar/list/search/dashboard churn. Each side completed 512 foreground turns with 512 tool calls and matching results; pair 1 lasted 666.1/656.0 seconds and pair 2 lasted 1,040.8/1,041.0 seconds. Both arms use the same built Gateway with frozen owner artifacts differing by exactly the sampling constant, identical instrumentation, natural GC, and no CPU/heap sampling capture or GC tracing. The baseline is `a3f44fb8a9f6e78bf0baa5fd946e4e440ff4c81b`; the shared Mac has no CPU affinity, so whole-workload differences are noisy.

| Metric | Pair 1: 10 ms | Pair 1: 25 ms | Pair 2: 10 ms | Pair 2: 25 ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU | 51.51% | 51.44% | 38.11% | 38.24% |
| Main CPU per foreground turn | 670.19 ms | 659.06 ms | 774.79 ms | 777.53 ms |
| Main-isolate allocation | 174.67 MiB/s | 173.73 MiB/s | 125.73 MiB/s | 126.77 MiB/s |
| Allocation per foreground turn | 227.25 MiB | 222.60 MiB | 255.59 MiB | 257.76 MiB |
| Natural GC | 2.789 s/min | 2.766 s/min | 3.938 s/min | 4.068 s/min |
| Maximum GC pause | 314.58 ms | 262.11 ms | 252.74 ms | 263.46 ms |
| Event-loop p99 | 128.45 ms (n=21,944) | 118.23 ms (n=21,904) | 164.36 ms (n=27,492) | 166.46 ms (n=27,148) |
| sessions.list p99 | 601.27 ms (n=1,466) | 478.25 ms (n=1,427) | 684.43 ms (n=2,307) | 690.24 ms (n=2,308) |
| sessions.list p95 | 262.34 ms (same n) | 270.36 ms (same n) | 338.93 ms (same n) | 364.41 ms (same n) |
| Median RSS | 4716.0 MiB | 4616.9 MiB | 4395.9 MiB | 4213.5 MiB |
| Median main heap | 846.7 MiB | 916.4 MiB | 854.6 MiB | 823.3 MiB |
| Recorder rotations | 133 | 130 | 205 | 204 |
| Serialized profile bytes / rotation | 689,464 | 346,351 | 608,545 | 327,104 |
| Profile stop wall time / rotation | 3.979 ms | 1.753 ms | 2.307 ms | 2.173 ms |

The direct recorder work reduction is consistent: serialized bytes per rotation fell **49.77% and 46.25%** (paired mean −48.01%, −312,277 bytes/rotation). Native stop wall time fell 55.95% and 5.80%; it includes scheduler preemption, so it is not a CPU estimate. The production diff is deliberately small.

Whole-Gateway CPU and allocation are effectively neutral and mixed-sign: CPU rate changed −0.074/+0.127 percentage points (mean +0.027), allocation rate −0.938/+1.041 MiB/s (mean +0.051). Per foreground turn, signed paired means were −4.20 ms CPU (−0.65%) and −1.245 MiB allocation (−0.60%); these noisy totals are not claimed as a demonstrated speedup. Median RSS fell in both pairs (mean −140.7 MiB, −3.12%), but natural heap/worker lifecycle differences prevent attributing that to native metadata.

The predeclared rejection thresholds were not reached. Total GC changed −23.0/+129.7 ms/min (signed mean +53.3 ms/min, +1.23%), well below the relative adverse threshold; neither maximum GC pause exceeded twice its baseline. List p95 increased +8.03/+25.48 ms (mean +16.76 ms, +5.29%). Loop p99 changed −10.22/+2.10 ms and list p99 −123.02/+5.81 ms; these mixed-sign tails are inconclusive improvements, not a latency benefit. No GC/promotion/max-pause rejection was made, so no A/A rejection controls were needed. Promotion was not measured; no traced run was mixed into acceptance.

<details>
<summary>Natural GC detail and sample counts</summary>

All observations are included. Each cell is collection count / total seconds / p95 ms / p99 ms / maximum ms. The small major and incremental collection counts make their pause tails descriptive, not gating p95/p99 estimates.

| Kind | Pair 1: 10 ms | Pair 1: 25 ms | Pair 2: 10 ms | Pair 2: 25 ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Minor | 4264 / 27.220 / 21.502 / 49.150 / 314.579 | 4168 / 25.987 / 20.606 / 51.198 / 131.378 | 4770 / 61.242 / 50.686 / 92.158 / 252.744 | 4808 / 60.964 / 51.454 / 92.670 / 230.489 |
| Incremental | 52 / 0.162 / 4.350 / 25.470 / 34.596 | 46 / 0.111 / 5.598 / 15.230 / 15.170 | 67 / 0.247 / 20.734 / 27.006 / 39.534 | 91 / 0.304 / 4.638 / 52.990 / 60.473 |
| Major | 52 / 3.579 / 135.166 / 164.862 / 186.382 | 46 / 4.141 / 201.726 / 262.142 / 262.106 | 67 / 6.822 / 185.342 / 198.654 / 240.599 | 91 / 9.306 / 194.558 / 241.662 / 263.460 |

Event-loop maxima were 653.26/667.42 ms in pair 1 and 611.84/757.60 ms in pair 2. Natural GC and maintenance were not trimmed or excluded. The second pair ran under heavier host load (around 84), so only within-pair differences are compared.

</details>

The first attempt at pair 2 stopped when the baseline GitHub-options RPC timed out before completing a measured round; the unmatched candidate was stopped. A replacement failed before ready because rebased plugin source expected an export absent from the frozen package build. Neither attempt yielded an accepted measurement. Both sides were then regenerated and run from the original reviewed commit, preserving the exact source/build pairing used for pair 1. The published PR is rebased on newer main; the owner and harness had no intervening changes, but the performance results are pinned-baseline evidence rather than a rebuilt measurement of that rebased head.

A separate 10-minute recorder-on/off diagnostic measured main CPU 52.66%/52.49%, allocation 173.46/172.96 MiB/s, GC 3.063/3.069 s/min, event-loop p99 116.72/116.39 ms (20,080/20,003 samples), and sessions.list p99 386.40/405.23 ms (1,397/1,402 samples). This is diagnostic context, not the candidate acceptance comparison.

Native allocator lifecycle measurements reproduced substantial retained profiler metadata. At 25 ms, disposing the final profile immediately released 17.185 MiB. Cross-startup native totals are confounded by a temporary extra worker; **no native-memory saving is claimed**. Overlapping rotations reuse the code map; short runs showed no accumulating map-sized restart leak, but do not establish lifetime leak freedom.

Validation: baseline full build and candidate runtime build passed; recorder/shared-profile tests 48/48, event-loop health tests 20/20, closure guards 22/22, export-name collision guard, and changed-file formatting/lint passed. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) identified two benchmark issues; both were corrected and the correction review was clean. Broad validation passed on head `5d4d54280491dbcfeb985217e1eeb39dad89e455`: [required CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40157216789/job/121062504098). Hosted code review also completed with no findings. No Testbox lease or production Gateway load was used.

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164516

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes approved plugin tools refusing execution when runtime preparation captures a separate environment object.

## User Impact

Allow-once approval and tool execution retain the same plugin registration. Registration-local consent stays private and single-use; denied calls remain rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prepared runtime owns its captured environment and plugin generation. Defaulting tool resolution to `process.env` discarded that generation through an identity mismatch. Resolve an omitted environment from the prepared load context first. Explicit caller overrides still take precedence.

No Agent System changes, shared consent store, or approval bypass. No live deployment yet.

## Evidence

Local validation below ran on `v2026.9.7` plus the fix. The branch was then aligned to `main` (`28a6f71449a`) with a history-preserving merge; its net diff is exactly the two reviewed files. Post-merge checks have not been rerun.

- Reproduced on `v2026.9.7`: the new approval-ownership regression fails with `Approval missing from this registration`; the same regression passes with the fix.
- Five focused resolver/hook/inspection suites: **162 tests passed**. Coverage includes allow-once consumption, denied calls, and explicit environment overrides.
- Single-worker regression cost: **3 cases passed in 12.30 s wall** using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/tools.prepared.test.ts --reporter=dot --maxWorkers=1`; most time was compiler/harness preparation. CI timing is not yet available.
- Full `pnpm build`, focused lint, core type-check, and plugin-platform test type-check passed.
- `git diff --check` and formatting passed.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Validation limits: the complete `check:changed` gate did not pass. The bound Git launcher truncates the repository-wide file inventory, so the max-lines gate reports false stale-baseline entries. The autoreview helper could not resolve the managed checkout; independent source review was performed, but this is not its validated `scoped-clean` result. The live chat approval flow has not been rerun with the fix.
