prs.title: perf(acp): carry byte totals through replay eviction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ACP replay byte-budget eviction rereads the oldest session and total retained bytes after each 64-event deletion. The existing serialized retention transaction already owns the ordered sessions and the deleted-byte facts. Carry those facts through that transaction, preserving partial-session trimming, deterministic timestamp/session-ID order, incomplete histories, the delayed empty-session deletion, and the zero clamp for older understated accounting. No cache, schema, authority, worker request, or cross-store commit change.

The PostgreSQL portability prerequisite landed separately in #183044. This PR starts from main f64a730df184f9f7e96435e290de7a36c553c3d5. The candidate is `6c25da0976f7837a82288be3d2aed74c7be81af8`; the synthetic reproduction and production optimization are now committed.

## Acceptance rule (published before new measurements)

Flow: real ACP stdio client through an isolated token-authenticated loopback Gateway; three synthetic tied-age sessions with 130 events each and 64 KiB text. Cold newSession forces whole-session and partial-session byte eviction; the next newSession is the separate warm under-budget control. Workload: `scripts/perf/acp-ledger-eviction-measure.ts`, frozen SQL observer v3.1.4. Synthetic state and per-thread CPU profiles only.

Counts first: the deterministic retention request must fall from 11 budget reads to 2, and the attributed cold ledger flow from 43 statements to 34, with 3 requests and 0 MAIN statements unchanged. Warm ledger SQL/requests/MAIN must remain 23/3/0. Preserve retained rows, sequence gaps and clamped accounting on SQLite and real PostgreSQL. Any increase attributable to this owner stops the change; no user-facing metric may regress. No latency or CPU-saving claim: profile samples establish attribution only; elapsed fields are diagnostic, excluded from performance comparisons.

Rebuild both runtimes on this PR's base and candidate. Alternate M,C,M,C,M,C if admission load <64 and internal free space >=12 GiB; otherwise use one pair under the campaign loaded-host rule. Report count median and p95 with min–max; keep cold and warm separate. Wall-clock/CPU A/B would require the timing lock, load <24 and at least five samples per arm, and is outside the present counts-only claim.

Historical reproduction on main 3270e695 already established accurate and understated accounting both fail only the 11->2 count assertion, plus the real transport cold 43/3/0 and warm 23/3/0. Fresh-base proof will replace those transport numbers for this PR.

## Evidence

On the fresh base, both accurate and historically understated-accounting cases passed their retained-history and UTF-8 assertions, then failed only the expected 11-versus-2 budget-read assertion. On the candidate, all 15 focused ACP tests passed, including those two regressions, failed-insert rollback, shared handles, gapped sequences, Unicode accounting and replay bindings. All six ACP conformance cases passed across SQLite and real PostgreSQL 17, including partial eviction, clamped accounting and tied session-cap order.

The committed real ACP stdio/Gateway workload passed three interleaved baseline/candidate pairs with frozen observer v3.1.4. Baseline `f64a730df18`, candidate `6c25da0976f`; both built runtimes were verified against their worker source. Values below are median / p95 [min–max], with three samples per arm.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold retention request: budget reads | 11 / 11 [11–11] | 2 / 2 [2–2] |
| Cold ledger owner: SQL | 43 / 43 [43–43] | 34 / 34 [34–34] |
| Cold ledger owner: worker requests / MAIN SQL | 3 / 0, constant | 3 / 0, constant |
| Warm ledger owner: SQL | 23 / 23 [23–23] | 23 / 23 [23–23] |
| Warm ledger owner: worker requests / MAIN SQL | 3 / 0, constant | 3 / 0, constant |
| Whole cold phase: SQL | 81 / 81 [80–81] | 72 / 73 [72–73] |
| Whole warm phase: SQL | 64 / 65 [62–65] | 62 / 62 [61–62] |

Whole-phase requests stayed at cold 16 and warm 13; MAIN stayed zero. The cold owner saving is nine statements (20.9%), with no worker move or request deferral. All three samples preserved the expected retained history. Whole-phase variation outside the owner is reported without claiming additional savings.

Admission load was 61.59 with 32.48 GiB free, selecting the preregistered three-pair rule. Per-thread profiles (29 baseline, 33 candidate) contain the retention path; their sparse inclusive samples are attribution only. No latency, CPU-time or memory improvement is claimed. The first baseline setup attempt omitted a required root launcher module; copying the same pinned source's root launcher closure fixed setup, and the successful run reused the verified build.

Basic oxlint, formatting and diff checks passed. Two scoped-clean Codex reviews cover the byte-identical worker and proof changes; the transaction-local simplification pass found no further change. Production delta is +35/-15 (+20) lines, justified by explicit session/batch traversal and the stored clamp. The removed one-row query has no remaining caller. PostgreSQL review approved this exact head conditional on all three CI shards passing. Exact-head CI, final static comparison and open-PR conflict audit remain pending.

## Gates

Pending final static/export comparison, open-PR merge-tree comparison, and exact-head CI including all three PostgreSQL shards. Exact-head PostgreSQL semantic review is approved. No landing before those gates settle. Release-note context: ACP replay eviction avoids repeated ledger scans without changing retained history.

prs.title: perf(runtime): reuse optional module loads after first use
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated MCP requests/connections, invalid-config diagnostics, public-session reads and completion streams kept issuing dynamic imports after their implementation modules had loaded. Follow-up to #183017.

## User Impact

A small reduction in repeated loader work. Optional features remain lazy, and request behavior is unchanged. This does not change the shell parser or its WASM heap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain fixed module promises at the existing process-lifetime owners. A small sibling module owns the MCP import group reused by catalog loading, cleanup and error handling; this keeps the existing large runtime below its line-growth ratchet. Request state, credentials, authority decisions, config results and parser instances keep their existing lifetimes.

Production delta: +52 net lines (90 added, 38 removed). The added state holds module promises; it removes repeat loading work without adding a second behavior path. The diagnostic scripts extend the existing heap-rig workflow and provide reproducible feature-level count guards.

## Evidence

Synchronized source MCP proof: four A/A controls and five A/B pairs, 200 warm samples per family per side. Mean paired medians: calls 2.433→2.303 ms (−0.130 ms); fresh-session lifecycles 9.207→8.782 ms (−0.424 ms). Mean operation latency: 3.478→3.284 ms and 13.466→12.901 ms respectively. No steady regression observed. A/A median shifts were −5.18% for calls and +2.85% for fresh sessions, so these figures do not establish a precise speedup. The traced validation separately verified warm baseline call/fresh-session imports 2/22 versus candidate 0/0, with no reevaluations.

**The full Gateway paired check is pending. CI/review can run now; do not merge until its verdict is recorded.**

- Initial seven-file proof passed 129 tests. After extracting the MCP loader, 64/65 cases passed; one concurrent stdio-catalog fixture settled at 2085 ms before its tools/list receipt, with a 2000 ms connection deadline. The same-order serial replay passed all 65 cases. The original failure is retained; no timeout/assertion changes. Its underlying timing cause is unproven. The module group was already warm, and the connection deadline begins after the import await.
- Changed-file format and lint passed. Both eager-import/PR-wrapper closure files passed all 22 tests; export-name collision guard passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): all eight production owners and diagnostic tooling reviewed clean. The final formatted production diff matches the reviewed patches semantically.
- The committed feature probe verifies 20 operations per primary path. Final count guards pass for MCP (60 operations including fresh-session disposal), config, public HTTP (20 GETs plus conditional GET), and completion parsing. Warm imports/evaluations are zero. The six-cache intermediate version failed at the second fresh MCP session with 11 imports; the complete owner cutover passes.

The original mixed Responses/CodeMode workload did not invoke any of these four lazy features: source, completed module census and a separate traced Gateway run agree. Its pooled +38/+56 ms median shifts therefore cannot be described as first-use loading overhead. First-turn/steady-turn paired measurements are being rerun against the immediate pre-PR parent with the same extended rig, fixed artifacts, isolated synthetic states, Node 26.12.1 and untraced timings. Two A/A controls precede five A/B pairs. No build or test work runs during timed windows.

A separate built-Gateway shell mix completed ten verified turns, including two actual shell commands. The first shell command's control-command guard initialized web-tree-sitter's 33,554,432-byte heap on main thread 0; the second command reused it. Six parse calls and one initialization were observed. The original CodeMode arithmetic mix never invoked the shell tool. The `.javascript` heap-retainer key is Node's default ESM cache type, not a JavaScript grammar. This identifies a normal feature trigger, not the exact historical command that initialized a production snapshot.

Feature source-probe latency samples are contextual (source loading, small sample counts, busy host); complete Gateway turn comparisons decide the steady-turn verdict. No GC, promotion or tail-latency improvement is claimed.

prs.title: fix(logging): Google OAuth client secrets appear unmasked in log output
prs.body:
Closes #181502

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Google OAuth client secret (`GOCSPX-` followed by 28 URL-safe characters) shows up in clear text in console logs, `logs.tail` output and diagnostic exports when it appears as a bare value in a log line.

## User Impact

User impact: log readers and shared diagnostics now show `GOCSPX…xxxx` for these secrets, the same way they already show Google API keys (`AIza…`), access tokens (`ya29.…`) and refresh tokens (`1//0…`).

Model-visible tool output is unchanged. #169063 made it keep original text on purpose, and this PR stays inside the logging and diagnostic boundary that #169063 left masked.

## Why This Change Was Made

The default vendor token table had rules for every other Google credential shape and none for the OAuth client secret. A `client_secret` JSON field was already masked by the field-key rule, so the gap only showed for the bare value, for example `gcloud` or setup output that prints the secret on its own.

The change adds one entry next to the existing Google rules in `src/logging/redact-patterns.ts` and the matching `GOCSPX-` trigger in `src/logging/redact-prefilter.ts`. The prefilter comment requires every default pattern to stay reachable from the fast path, so the trigger is part of the fix. `{20,}` follows the tolerance the neighbouring Google rules use.

## Evidence

**Regression test.** `src/logging/redact.test.ts` adds a 28-character synthetic secret to "masks representative vendor token grammars through the default fast path", which checks each token in isolation through the default prefilter. `GOCSPX-docs` joins the existing short-documentation negatives.

- With the source change reverted and the test kept: `1 failed | 49 passed`, failing on the new `GOCSPX-…` case.
- With the change: `50 passed`.
- `pnpm test src/logging/redact.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 66.9 s wall on this host for the whole file. The added cases are two string fixtures inside existing tests, so the added cost is negligible.
- `pnpm test src/logging`: 64 files, 738 tests passed.

**Real logger and log reader.** A synthetic secret written through `createSubsystemLogger(...).warn(...)` into a configured file log, then read back with `readConfiguredLogTail`, the reader behind `logs.tail`:

```
main   console : google oauth setup returned 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 for the installed app
main   logs.tail: ... 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 ...                                     LEAK
branch console : google oauth setup returned GOCSPX…Fy1J for the installed app
branch logs.tail: ... GOCSPX…Fy1J ...                                                                MASKED
```

The raw file keeps the original value on both heads, as #170023 intends (file logs are masked at egress).

**How the gap was found.** A differential run fed bare credentials generated from the gitleaks rule set (160 rules with usable samples) through `redactSensitiveText`. This PR covers the Google client secret named in #181502. The run also reported other fixed-prefix formats that pass through unmasked (Shopify `shpat_`, HashiCorp Vault `hvs.`, RubyGems `rubygems_`, `AGE-SECRET-KEY-1`, New Relic `NRAK-`, Stripe `rk_test_`). Those are a separate scope decision, so they are left out of this PR and can follow as their own change if maintainers want them.

Environment: Node 24.22.1, head `fed1c12d0d4` plus this commit, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME`, synthetic secrets only.

prs.title: perf(ui): avoid repeated work while streaming replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streaming replies repeatedly redo Markdown and transcript work for text-only deltas, wasting browser CPU and leaving newly started paragraphs below the viewport for a frame.

## User Impact

New text remains visible on the next frame while safe Markdown formatting catches up within a fixed 50 ms window. Reader scroll-up, syntax, media, replacement, and final rendering retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A narrow live-text source keeps text-only deltas out of structural transcript and position projections. Literal text appends through the existing Markdown island; syntax, block boundaries, and completion remain canonical. The old live overlay/index replacement machinery is removed. Measured row growth reconciles through the existing end-anchor owner before paint, retaining reader authority and cancellation checks.

This head incorporates current main's prepared-DOM renderer and lazy transcript rows. The two optimizations share one renderer. Whole changed-file LOC is production 8,953 → 9,191 (+238), tests/support 5,973 → 6,399 (+426), docs 470 → 474 (+4), config 5 → 5. Effects/listeners/queries/flush/owner API counts are unchanged.

The coordinator explicitly approved the CPU/bytes tradeoff under the newer allowance for a clean ≥5% CPU win and up to approximately 2 KB gzip growth. After main’s dormant-chat deferral landed, the only merge conflict was the startup baseline. Fresh same-host builds preserve that reduction: startup 272,577 → 272,544 B (−33 B), Chat 1,247,947 → 1,248,649 B (+702 B), New Session 761,622 → 761,641 B (+19 B). Chat is 54 B above the previously approved +648 B, within the 64 B build-variance allowance. Requests and CSS are unchanged. The official checker ratchets startup to the measured 272,544 B.

## Evidence

Current head: `f6d1985f71a`; current bundle base: `9794c6abbb6`. CPU and visual proof used production `3f327131d31` against `8e7fedf560c`. Eighteen of nineteen lane production UI files remain byte-identical; the remaining change is main’s annotation-editor lazy load in `chat-view-frame.ts`, outside the streaming path. The later test assertions, Talk fixture repair, and baseline updates do not change runtime behavior.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Markdown lifecycle/highlighting | 18 passed |
| Streaming lifecycle and formatting deadline | 43 Chromium tests pass after replacing obsolete DOMParser-call counts with visible autolink deadline assertions |
| Live-DOM security corpus | 71 passed; safe intermediate DOM and final one-shot content equality, excluding renderer comments |
| First-paint follow regression | Red at 88 px before repair; 48 follow/geometry/anchor cases passed at `1b1fb96d018`; integrated production visibility probes below cover the final repair |
| Production next-frame visibility | 136/136 sampled text updates visible on integrated head; all four previously late paragraph starts pass on frame one |
| Burst latest-in-frame visibility | 27/27 on integrated head, versus 4/27 on base; superseded same-frame deltas are not treated as the current visible state |
| Talk handshake regression | Prior CI40156938097 failed one reduced-motion Talk test. The test could acknowledge the mock latest socket before the provider existed; CI remained in connecting. It now holds provider creation through the connecting assertions, waits for the actual provider setup frame, and acknowledges that socket; all10 targeted E2E tests, format and lint pass. |
| Types, changed-file lint, independent review | UI types/lint pass; no actionable P0–P2 findings |
| Production Knip | Fails identically on current head and exact base `9794c6abbb6`: one unlisted binary, `scripts/generate-social-preview.mts: ffmpeg`. No UI orphan is reported; the prior measured head passed. |
| Canonical production builds and strict size comparison | Fresh base/head builds pass on current main; baseline set by official checker; prior measured production source-map provenance retained |
| Full CI | [40154269167](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40154269167) passed on `07d03772e928`, before the config-only approved baseline update, including every `ci:full` UI unit, E2E, browser-extension, and real-Gateway shard |

The two Gateway type jobs in the prior [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40150325444) have the same sole diagnostic on the clean merge base: `src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog.test-helpers.ts(122,5)` TS2739 (`{}` lacks `minProtocol`, `maxProtocol`, and `client`). Both `pnpm tsgo:core` and the Gateway-methods test typecheck reproduce it at `8e7fedf560c`. UI, extension, and UI test type leaves passed. That prior run also identified two cadence assertions counting DOMParser calls, obsolete after main’s prepared-DOM renderer; these now assert the visible autolink deadline, and all 43 streaming browser tests pass locally. Earlier real scroll/Markdown regressions were repaired; they are not classified as inherited.

### Performance acceptance

Each workload runs 20 serial interleaved base/A-A/head triplets on this Mac, using production bundles, 400 history messages, 645 deterministic deltas, and native typing. Standard: 30 deltas/s; burst: 150/s in groups of five. Renderer thread CPU, input latency, frame gaps, dropped-frame estimates, structural counters, final output, and host load are retained. The A/A candidate is an identical base bundle.

Burst measurement is complete. Across 20 base/A-A/head sets, renderer-thread script CPU median is 636.6 → 531.8 ms (−16.5%; paired median −17.9%), and its p95 is 1,057.1 → 946.9 ms. Median per-run p95 input latency is 19.54 → 18.05 ms; p95 frame gap stays 33.4 ms. Dropped-frame median is 53.5 → 55.5, with p95 76.75 → 76.1; the A/A median is 61.5, showing shared-host frame-count noise. Position-rail observations fall 207.5 → 145 per stream; pane renders stay at one on the head. Every run ends at bottom gap 0 with the same comment-normalized final HTML hash.

Standard streaming is also complete: renderer-thread script CPU median is 1,736.95 → 1,375.20 ms (−20.8%; paired median −20.45%), with p95 1,891.60 → 1,401.00 ms. Renderer task CPU falls 4,652.78 → 4,297.64 ms. Median per-run p95 typing latency is 20.91 → 20.14 ms, and p95 frame gap remains 33.4 ms. Dropped-frame median is 247.5 → 255 (A/A 259), with p95 319.05 → 315.6. Rail observations fall 535.5 → 317 (−40.8%). All runs again have bottom gap 0 and identical comment-normalized final HTML.

The head improves script CPU in 20/20 standard pairs and 18/20 burst pairs. Burst run 30 remains an outlier at 1,828 ms script CPU, 1,529 HTML parses, and 3.37M parsed characters; it represents extra browser work, not just scheduling delay. A/A has parser/CPU outliers too. Publications and row resize deliveries remain roughly unchanged; the reliable structural reduction is position-rail work.

Neither the ≤1.0 s standard target nor the 50% burst CPU target is reached. These remain goals, not landing gates. The A/A dropped-frame and latency spreads exceed the timing band on this shared host (load roughly 50–90), so wall/frame outliers are treated as noise; twenty interleaved renderer-thread CPU pairs show the gain, and structural rail work falls in both workloads. Acceptance uses the campaign's ≤5% median/p95 band and noisy-host A/A rule. Earlier timing results are superseded because merging main changed the Markdown renderer itself.

### Bundle comparison

| Gzip surface | Base | Head | Requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS | 272,577 B | 272,544 B | 7 unchanged |
| Chat JS | 1,247,947 B | 1,248,649 B | 26 unchanged |
| New Session JS | 761,622 B | 761,641 B | 20 unchanged |

CSS bytes and requests are unchanged, including one startup CSS request. No new dependency or eager import was added by this lane.

### Visual proof

Inspected synthetic fixtures only. The failed-check labels are fixture content. The before/after completion captures retain code highlighting and tables. The contact sheet shows base above head, at delta 162, delta 323, and completion. Full burst captures contain 335/214 frames; the standard filmstrip reaches Chromium's 450-frame capture limit, while the independent visibility probe covers the entire stream.


![Before: completed streaming reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01239bef-196e-4f72-bc47-4099e8ba1c61)

![After: completed streaming reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f6d5111-3e2b-42ec-8323-568b08266574)

![Burst filmstrip: base above head](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/938c0856-eb21-4cfd-9275-f04f42ef8454)

The first landing attempt stopped before dispatch because main’s lower startup baseline conflicted. No request or intent was retained. Main was merged; the lower baseline was preserved and measured afresh. Independent review of the merged candidate is clean through P2. UI typecheck and the fresh strict size check pass. Native review/preparation is refreshing for the test-only Talk handshake repair at `f6d1985f71a`. CI40156938097 completed with that single E2E failure; it is repaired rather than classified as inherited, because the latest scheduled main shard passed.

prs.title: perf(gateway): skip unchanged session row materialization work
prs.body:
Related: #182754

## What Problem This Solves

Session-row reads construct and deeply compare an unchanged replacement graph before retaining the previous materialization. The measured timestamp-churn baseline reused 202 graphs only after constructing them, rebuilt 63, and skipped none. This follow-up skips that construction when the prepared inputs and their owner revisions are unchanged.

## User Impact

Unchanged session rows can retain their materialized graph without rebuilding it. Real changes still flow through materialization and publication. Paired performance acceptance is pending; no timing improvement is claimed yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

Credit to the cold-load session's source review of #182754 for the input-identity investigation and proposed early gate. The profile identity map, identity projection functions, and subagent inputs already retain references; the gate also checks their captured owner revisions. The existing preparation context now retains configured-agent membership, and equal compact child links reuse the previous projection. No second input graph or new cache is retained.

The single materialization owner compares prepared inputs against the existing graph, using identity first and field equality when necessary. It falls back to the existing construction/full-graph comparison. Native runtime ownership and automation are included: the dev diagnostic demonstrated that cron membership can change the visible row while its source is equal. Input preparation and live presentation still run.

Board changes invalidate sharing and publish selection; membership changes retire sharing; materialized/facts identity changes publish facts. Placement, permission and activity remain lazily read at presentation time. Existing regression coverage exercises real label, model, visibility and status changes. Freeze sites and immutable-snapshot semantics owned by #182210 are unchanged.

Production delta: +186 lines; tests: +22 lines. Growth implements the requested explicit input gate and bounded diagnostic counters. It removes per-slice configured-agent Set construction and redundant argument plumbing, and moves the existing fallback into one decision owner. The separate dev Gateway driver is benchmark tooling, not production code.

## Evidence

Measurement preceded optimization. A compiled Gateway diagnostic used 65 clients, 200 committed timestamp writes and 195 searches, with zero RPC failures. It recorded 399 first constructions, 202 rebuilt-then-reused graphs, 63 replacements, zero skips, and 202 full-graph comparisons: 76.23% effective repeated reuse. Repeated search-field rebuilds were zero. Main-thread CPU was 4,288.219 ms, or 16.493 ms per 260 measured completed sessions.list calls. This is mixed-workload Gateway CPU divided by list count, not exclusive RPC CPU. A single diagnostic is opportunity evidence, not paired timing acceptance.

A separate isolated dev Gateway completed 600 lists over six ordinary RPC phases: unchanged lists, cron rename, cron enable, cron disable, label change, and repeated label save. The first two phases made no materialization attempts (reuse rate N/A); each remaining phase rebuilt one row. All row, label and automation assertions passed. One earlier attempt failed readiness before fixture setup; it is preserved as invalid setup evidence. The driver now waits on the existing readiness probe.

The skipped-materialization regression failed on the observational baseline (0 versus expected 1), then passed with the fix. Thirty focused projection, native-ownership, retention and context tests passed; the final revision-getter change passed all 23 projection/context tests again. Both required closure files passed (22 tests), export-collision checks passed, and changed-file formatting/lint passed. One permitted local core typecheck found an optional-child-links type error; it was fixed and independently reviewed. PR CI will confirm typechecking on the final head. No broad local suite was run. The two focused extension tests and their lint command prepared the SDK artifacts they require; Gateway benchmark builds run on Team.

CI on the first candidate exposed missing materialization fields in two existing diagnostic test fixtures, an optional IPC-disconnect call in the dev driver, and missing invariant comments on new key casts. These were fixed in one reviewed batch: 12 tests in the two affected extension files passed, changed-file lint passed, and the ratchet parser reports zero unexplained assertions in the three affected production files. No CI rerun was requested. The required rebase incorporates current main’s session-read/schema changes, so the paired builds are regenerated from the new common parent; the earlier builds produced no acceptance samples.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) found no actionable findings in the final production change or dev driver. The summary review also passed after correcting mixed old/new artifact aggregation; a reproduction verifies both artifact orders.

Acceptance was predeclared before results: 15 concurrent baseline/candidate pairs from the same main parent, identical fresh synthetic fixtures and instrumentation, synchronized warm starts, counterbalanced launch order, and swapped interleaved 16-CPU placements under one shared quiet slot and the production guard. Invalid pairs are preserved and replaced. Apply v5.6 absolute GC materiality, v5.5 tail rules, sample counts and maximum-pause safeguards, and matched A/A controls before interpreting adverse GC/promotion/max-pause results. Exactly one extra pair is permitted only for mixed-sign or unstable-baseline metrics; no repeated sampling to chase a result.

Final results will report CPU/list, CPU/wave, skipped materializations, reuse rate, search/roster latency, consume time and GC with counts/maxima. First constructions stay separate from repeated reuse. A zero-opportunity phase remains a result; no synthetic invalidation manufactures hits. Explicitly requested changes may land with neutral timing only when correctness holds and there is no regression beyond noise.

prs.title: fix(discord): false "couldn't finish" notice when a queued message is answered in its thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord shows "⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this request" after the agent answered a message in a thread it created from that message, when the message arrived while the session was still busy with an earlier turn.

## User Impact

User impact: in Discord channels, a message that waits in the queue behind a running turn can be answered in its own thread (thread-create from the message, then thread-reply, ending with `NO_REPLY`) without a false failure notice in the channel. Messages handled right away were already fine.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord registers an active thread route for each inbound message so that a thread created from that message counts as replying to it (thread replies are tagged `sourceReplyRoute: "current-source"`). The route was released when the message's dispatch returned. A message queued behind an active turn returns from dispatch right after it is enqueued, so its queued run started later with no route. Its thread was never adopted, the thread replies did not count as the source reply, and the required-reply check reported an empty response.

The queued run now holds the same route from `onQueuedFollowupAdmitted` until `onQueuedFollowupSettled`. Route registration counts its holders, so a queued run admitted before its dispatch returns keeps the route after the dispatch releases its own hold. Those two hooks are now always set on Discord dispatches (before this change they were set only when a draft stream existed); the draft handling inside them is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live observation on a 2026.10.7 Gateway (Discord guild channel, `claude-cli` backend, automatic visible replies). Two turns in the same session did the same thing: thread-create from the source message, several thread-replies, then `NO_REPLY`. The turn that started right away completed silently. The next message had arrived during that turn (`injection_unavailable`, `disposition: followup-policy`) and ran about 2.5 minutes later as a queued follow-up. It logged `cli empty response diagnostics: backend=claude-cli reason=exit exitCode=0 … useResume=true` and posted the failure notice. The route lifecycle in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts` is the same on `main`.
- New regression tests in `message-handler.process.draft-final.test.ts`:
  - `keeps the source-message thread route for a queued turn until it settles`: the queued run is admitted after its dispatch returned.
  - `keeps the route for a queued turn admitted before its dispatch returns`: covers the holder count.
  - Both fail on `main` (`expected false to be true` when the thread reply is checked) and pass with this change.
- `pnpm test:extension discord`: 259 files, 2,637 tests passed. Focused `pnpm test` on the touched process and action tests: 91 passed.
- `pnpm format:check` and type-aware oxlint on the changed files are clean. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass.
- Gap: I did not run the Discord e2e skill against an isolated Gateway because I don't have Discord test bot credentials. The live evidence above is from the reporting Gateway before the fix.

prs.title: fix(ui): announce Web Push errors to assistive technology
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the Control UI **Settings → Notifications** section, the Web Push error rows render their message without `role="alert"`. The text reaches the page, but assistive technology is never told an error appeared, so a screen reader user gets no announcement when a subscription fails or a test notification is rejected.

Every other config form in the Control UI marks `.cfg-field__error` with `role="alert"`. These two render sites were the only exceptions in the tree.

Closes #183207.

## Evidence

### The accessibility tree, before and after

Playwright's ARIA snapshot of the same error text shows the semantic change directly:

| Phase | Accessibility tree |
|---|---|
| Before | `- text: This browser push subscription belongs to another Gateway.` |
| After | `- alert: This browser push subscription belongs to another Gateway.` |

Measured counts from the same probe:

```
before: alert-role-present=false  alertNodes=0  liveNodes=0
after:  alert-role-present=true   alertNodes=1  liveNodes=0
```

![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pick-cat/openclaw/proof/181242/.github/pr-assets/webpush-alert/ax-before.png)
![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pick-cat/openclaw/proof/181242/.github/pr-assets/webpush-alert/ax-after.png)

The pixels are identical in both phases, which is the point: this defect is invisible on screen and only shows up in the accessibility tree.

### Runtime measurement on the real component

Mounting the production `NotificationsSection` in jsdom with `webPush.error` set:

```
push.error span role=null alertNodes=0 liveNodes=0
```

The component contains no `[role="alert"]` and no `[aria-live]` element at all.

### Regression, red on the base and green with the fix

Reverting only `notifications-section.tsx` while keeping the new assertions:

```
× keeps settings available after an admitted command rejects
× announces a Web Push subscription error to assistive technology
Tests  2 failed | 10 passed (12)
```

With the fix applied:

```
Tests  12 passed (12)
```

## The fix

Two attribute additions in `ui/src/pages/config/notifications-section.tsx`:

| Site | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `renderWebPushError` | Shared fallback for **three** call sites: the command rejection, the read failure, and the function itself |
| `<Show when={props.push.error}>` | The subscription error, for example the VAPID mismatch case |

No CSS, i18n, type, or node-structure changes. Because only an attribute is added, the existing `.cfg-field__error` `toHaveLength(1)` assertions are unaffected.

## Scope

This PR announces the errors that already existed. It does not change what errors are produced or how they read.

## Checklist

- [x] The failing behavior is reproduced and the fix regresses it
- [x] Regression test fails on the base and passes with the fix
- [x] Change is limited to the two render sites and one test file

prs.title: improve: avoid repeated routing reads for warm transcript turns
prs.body:
Closes #182810. Follow-up to #183034; thanks @etzelm for identifying the repeated turn-commit work.

## What Problem This Solves

Warm fixed-message transcript turns still made a separate worker request to reread the window key, session node/snapshots, and participants before the writer read the same facts again.

## User Impact

Postgres-readiness preparation with no user-visible runtime behavior change. Eligible warm turns use one fewer worker request and three fewer SQL statements on both engines, including three fewer PostgreSQL trips. Schemas, configuration, dependencies, transcript bytes, and transaction boundaries stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing token-validated resident entry proves that the turn can enter the persisted writer. Inside the existing eagerly locked transaction, the writer reuses its full row/window facts to select the physical target and publishes its committed postimage through the existing owner. A resident entry never proves window ownership: cron base/run keys sharing a session ID still follow the locked window owner. Missing/stale facts, callbacks, and native compatibility retain their existing discovery paths.

No new cache, epoch, freshness probe, transcript identity fold, or state/agent transaction fusion. `pr-simplify` retained only target handoff/publication, the shared-ID regression, and the count observer/budget. Non-mechanical production delta: +182/-41; proof delta: +98/-12. The added handoff preserves the existing physical-target and scoped-publication contracts.

## Evidence

Pinned baseline: `090e6213e25e6b09f03590a41da2fddeaf9f611e`, after #183034. `pnpm bench:transcript-turn --check-budget` is RED on that baseline and GREEN with this change on both engines. Full fixture: 2,000 sessions, 5,000 history turns, five warmups and ten measured samples per shape/engine/arm; all 120 measured samples are exact.

R = completed worker requests, T = PostgreSQL query trips, S = SQL statements. Counts are per generic fixed-message warm transcript turn.

| Engine | Messages | Before R/T/S | After R/T/S |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL | 1 | 2 / 15 / 16 | 1 / 12 / 13 |
| PostgreSQL | 2 | 2 / 14 / 15 | 1 / 11 / 12 |
| PostgreSQL | 4 | 2 / 14 / 15 | 1 / 11 / 12 |
| SQLite | 1 | 2 / — / 17 | 1 / — / 14 |
| SQLite | 2 | 2 / — / 17 | 1 / — / 14 |
| SQLite | 4 | 2 / — / 17 | 1 / — / 14 |

SQLite's statement channel did not observe raw read-only routing handles. The benchmark now counts native SQLite executions and excludes duplicate SQLite channel events. Both arms use that same observer; the earlier channel-only SQLite writer count of 14 is not a whole-path baseline. PostgreSQL still uses `openclaw.database.statement`.

Behavior/static proof: 143 tests across 13 focused transcript/prefix files passed (146.84 s), including all 11 prompt-prefix stability cases. Targeted lint and core/scripts typechecks passed. The final observer replay and its targeted lint check also pass; the integrated isolated Codex autoreview is clean at P0–P2 with no material context gap. Both qaRuntime builds pass (baseline 53.9 s, candidate 48.7 s).

New test cost: `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-accessor.transcript-identity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 33.24 s wall time; 19 cases passed.

Fresh-config real Gateway proof: PASS on Homebrew PostgreSQL 17.11 and SQLite, using Node 24.22.1 and the real `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` model. Three turns per engine/arm (12 total) completed with identical six-message role/text readback in all four runs. Raw schema and CLI config validation passed; every Gateway exited cleanly.

Observed live SQL by turn: SQLite `[197, 55, 52] → [191, 55, 54]`; PostgreSQL `[201, 52, 50] → [201, 51, 50]`, with PG trips `[182, 43, 41] → [182, 42, 41]`. The SQLite warm +2 is an unchanged plugin-state list read occurring twice; the PG warm −1 is an unchanged upstream-watch read. These are whole-interval observations. Ordinary embedded model output uses the SessionManager writer, so this live proof establishes compatibility and history integrity; the table above is the targeted generic-writer saving. No ordinary-chat SQL, latency, or throughput improvement is claimed.

Required final-head PostgreSQL conformance shards 1/3, 2/3, 3/3: pending in [exact-head CI run 40158619601](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40158619601). Normal PR CI skips drafts; `scripts/pr ci-dispatch 183204` started this supported exact-head run while preserving draft status. This PR remains draft for the coordinator's PostgreSQL review gate.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): lean sidebar reload presentation [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a chat or dashboard deep link retains sidebar rows but fills unread marks, state glyphs, pull-request badges, avatars, and the Inbox count in later visual steps. The campaign's structural evidence found a cached paint followed by avatar fill, header/PR badges, and additional glyphs and avatars at the live handoff.

**Experiment only; do not merge.** Round 1 (#183009, closed unmerged) reduced median waves from 39 to 5 on chat and 52 to 6 on dashboard, with zero handoff pop-ins, but regressed chat transcript paint by 64 ms and hello by 34.4 ms. Its snapshot grew from 193,552 to 477,842 bytes and its UI runtime grew by 510 lines. Those results rejected that candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

This revision stores sparse visible facts once per row and references stable headers from the existing boot roster. It removes persisted attention/run domain objects and the full per-row presentation object. Avatar images use bounded native Blobs in the existing disposable IndexedDB snapshot; projection version 3 resets older snapshots, and the size budget includes the real Blob bytes.

The credential owner proves continuity from the same gateway credential scope, recovery scope, and profile before retaining loaded image/blob URLs. Pending requests still abort. Profile/account/gateway/credential-subject changes, logout, rejected admission, and policy revocation retire images. Established access revocation can arrive as a bare WebSocket 4001 close; that boundary now retires the admitted scope immediately. No Gateway schema, stored server record, configuration option, or public protocol change.

The existing sidebar handoff and foreground/hello scheduling remain in place. Cached expansion retains its last-visit slot summary until the live handoff. Cached facts never authorize actions, and incognito presentation remains excluded.

## User Impact

No rollout is proposed until the declared gates pass. The intended result is a sidebar whose first cached paint already contains the same visible facts as its live presentation, without delaying hello or transcript paint.

The current source audit remains materially above the requested +250 runtime-line target. This cost is recorded explicitly and is not a passing budget claim. If it remains above the target at measurement head, the experiment stops after the comparison and does not proceed to full-suite/ready qualification, even if its timing and visual gates pass.

## Evidence

Predeclared before the comparison: one quiet AWS **c7a.4xlarge** lease for the entire baseline/candidate comparison, repository Playwright Chromium, the Team-scale fixture, 11 alternating interleaved pairs on **each** chat and dashboard route. The committed `live-fast` latency profile schedules the challenge no earlier than 439 ms and applies a 41 ms connect reply floor; sidebar query floors are ownerFirst 400 ms, involvingMe 500 ms, ownerCounts 425 ms, and children 700 ms. Untraced timing and structural runs are separate. Filmstrips contain only synthetic data. No private captures are uploaded.

| Gate | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Visible sidebar waves after first paint | Candidate median <=2; improvement with non-overlapping IQR or >=9/11 better pairs and negative median paired delta |
| Handoff | Zero glyph/avatar pop-ins in every candidate reload |
| L178 lifecycle | One cached/live transition, no blank or shrink-grow, initial visible rows and mounted nodes retained |
| FCP | Median paired delta <=+15 ms |
| Hello handled, first transcript paint/rows, LoAF | No regression on both routes under the campaign's IQR/paired evidence rule |
| Final transcript | Ready, unchanged final row count |
| Snapshot | Report UTF-8 metadata plus Blob bytes; target <=250,000 bytes |
| Decode | Report actual-source schema decode and image-decode cost separately from navigation timings |
| Runtime LOC | Report whole-change delta versus main; target <=+250 |

Secondary regression means worse with non-overlapping IQR, or worse in >=9/11 pairs with median paired rise >max(10 ms, 3% of baseline median). Mixed signs inside overlapping IQRs are noise. Every metric includes median/IQR and per-pair deltas.

Performance results, sanitized before/after filmstrips, remote lease IDs, full UI e2e, changed-file classification versus main, and exact-head CI remain pending. This draft must be closed if qualification fails; it will not be merged by this lane.

Measurement head: `abefd9c6d1c40b02fbecb055212b812cf3879dac`; pinned main baseline: `8ae44f9249540b4d377fb6b80f25f004a5d959e1`.

Pre-comparison proof: 202 focused tests across 11 files passed serially on the Mac; the integrated row-render file passed 19/19 after rebasing (22.47 s for `pnpm test ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-row-render.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1`). The new Gateway avatar boundary file passed 9/9 (7.64 s); its bare-4001 revocation case failed before the fix. The strengthened archived-header case also failed before its fix. The decoder smoke completed both native-Blob and older data-URL paths. These are smoke/test wall times, not performance comparisons. Full integrated independent review is clean through P2.

Current UI runtime: **949 added / 322 deleted, net +627 LOC**. The requested literal diff-stat filters report 39 files, 1,358 insertions / 359 deletions (net +999), including benchmark/proof code and `.test.tsx` files. These are whole-change deltas against the pinned main, not reductions against round 1. Remaining growth is in the bounded image capture/restore lifecycle, explicit display-fact schema/capture, and sparse-row reconstruction/render consumption. The runtime target is not met.

prs.title: chore: reduce duplicate OAuth and MCP deadline test cost
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native MCP boundary suite waits for the full 60-second production request deadline in a synthetic child-process fixture. The OAuth boundary suite repeats provider failure parsing across both callers even though both use the same provider adapters.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. CI does less repeated test work when these owners are selected; no new suite, shard, or runner is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing MCP request-timeout setting to give just the deadline fixture a five-second deadline; retain its real stdio peer, real timer, callback cancellation, zero-lease assertion, reacquisition, human-input hold, and uncertain cleanup checks. Reduce 24 OAuth failure cases: SDK AuthStorage still exercises every provider and every failure mode, and the model manager retains builtin, facade, and direct-plugin failure paths. Both callers retain every success, omitted-refresh, and identity-verification-failure case. No production behavior, security check, SQL, schema, or CI capacity changes.

## Evidence

### Acceptance rule (recorded before local execution)

- Workload: the existing committed test entry point, `pnpm test src/agents/native-mcp-runtime.test.ts src/agents/sessions/auth-storage-oauth-boundary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`.
- Baseline: `c668bc0565187494726a7d065841ff7c551357f5`; candidate: this PR. Same host and runtime, serial alternating baseline/candidate samples, five per revision after unmeasured cache priming. New process per invocation; warm compiler cache is separate from any cold setup evidence.
- Measure test cases/fixture work first, then whole-command wall time, per-file test time, CPU, and peak RSS. Report median, p95, and range. Win: all retained contracts pass, OAuth cases 139 → 115, and combined wall median falls at least 15%. No measured user-facing metric may regress; a 20% adverse cell stops acceptance and requires investigation.
- Timing is admitted only under the campaign's shared timing lock and calm-host limit. If no eligible window appears after 60 minutes, publish count/profile evidence and explicitly leave wall-time improvement unclaimed.

## Contract coverage

All distinct provider serialization/parsing failures remain covered through SDK AuthStorage. The native builtin, facade, and plugin routes still assert thrown refresh failure, durable fence, no token replay, and one consumed grant. Identity failures and third-party compatibility paths remain unchanged. MCP still proves the real owner's deadline and child retirement, rather than substituting a mocked transport or advancing its cleanup clock.

## Cost inventory

Audited 40 high-cost files by single-job printed case duration, plus 13 files with unambiguous singleton Vitest wall summaries. The logs do not support inventing wall durations for the other 27. Three recent successful narrow PR runs (40157655365, 40157611888, 40157502914) selected 54, 33, and 13 reported changed-Node files; none of the ranked files was selected. This scope-biased sample does not estimate repository-wide frequency or justify a universal per-PR saving. The selected owners remain worthwhile targets when their scope is exercised.

## Initial attribution

Recent main CI runs 40151593226 and 40149301577 attribute 23.170s and 23.784s of printed case time to the 24 duplicate OAuth cases (not whole-file wall time). Native MCP's deadline case printed 66.484s in run 40151593226. The third inspected main run, 40155317862, had an incomplete log download and is not included in those timing figures.

Initial simplification pass: 24 duplicate executions and 24 fresh plugin-load/state lifecycles removed. Production LOC delta 0; test/helper delta +10 lines (18 added, 8 removed) to select retained routes and thread the existing timeout setting. No new tests or production testing seams. Two isolated Codex reviews are scoped-clean at P0–P2 against the diff and supplied owner context. Final validation and measurements are pending. Test-only change; no PostgreSQL or SDK API surface changes. Open-PR overlap index returned no overlapping PRs before editing.

prs.title: fix(memory): bound cache growth during full rebuilds
prs.body:
Closes #182886

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded embedding-cache growth during full memory rebuilds while preserving cached vectors that later rebuild batches still need.

This is a bounded-growth follow-up to #182968, which landed the provider-reuse fix while this investigation was in progress. The original cache-eviction cascade was reported by @etzelm.

## User Impact

Full rebuilds, including `memory index --force` and the rebuild after an agent database port, reuse cached embeddings within a bounded temporary cache budget. Successful publication restores the configured cap. Abort cleanup prunes only when that rebuild attempted a cache upsert, avoiding a publication-backend open when provider preparation fails before any cache write.

Accepted edge: **during a full rebuild the embedding cache may temporarily hold up to 2× maxEntries rows; it is pruned to the cap after publication or abort.** Suspended background rebuilds retain that budget. A process crash can leave temporary excess until the next normal cache write restores the cap. When a rebuild fills the temporary budget, the existing eviction policy applies.

No configuration, schema, dependency, port-format, or rebuild-scheduling changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing reservation operation enforces twice the normal capacity during full rebuilds and the normal capacity during incremental writes. The rebuild owner prunes against the completed published index and records an exact retained count after the final prune. Abort cleanup uses the same operation only after an accepted cache upsert was attempted. The write-triggered flag preserves the early-failure lifecycle: no cache writes means no extra publication open or close.

This preserves the existing eviction preference, pre-insertion reservation algorithm, incremental SQL/count behavior, and PostgreSQL write-lock/token handling. It avoids retaining vectors in an additional in-memory map.

## Evidence

Real CLI comparison, rerun on final head `00389f86f492`, with a loopback embedding server and Homebrew PostgreSQL 17.11: 960 generated chunks, 680 needed cache hits, 280 true misses, and a full 50,000-row cache containing newer superseded entries.

| Flow | Original starting main inputs | Final candidate inputs |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| SQLite `memory index --force` | 750 | 280 |
| SQLite → PostgreSQL port/rebuild | 735 | 280 |
| PostgreSQL → SQLite reverse port | not measured | 0 |

The historical column is main `23b07a8ce50a`, before #182968; current main already contains that PR's provider-reuse fix. These reductions demonstrate the complete repaired behavior, not an additional reduction attributable solely to this follow-up. Both final engines have exactly 50,000 cache rows and all 960 required vectors; PostgreSQL chunk hashes match the baseline. Final command wall times: force 300.515 s (including a 271.2 s source build), forward port 64.794 s, reverse port 49.115 s.

- The capacity regression is RED on base `79fc84c2f334`: five cache rows exceed the permitted four at cap two. It is GREEN here.
- The PostgreSQL provider-count regression is RED with the historical owner sources (three inputs instead of one), and GREEN here (one true miss; zero inputs on the next force rebuild).
- The original 61 focused tests passed. On this final head, the unchanged startup-close suite passed all 6 tests (35.505 s), and the capacity, abort/recovery, and resume suites passed all 41 tests (96.105 s). Existing incremental PostgreSQL count and multi-writer assertions also passed unchanged in CI.
- Final-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40152984019) passed all three PostgreSQL shards: 292 / 343 / 545 tests (1,180 total, 38 existing skips). The new provider-count regression actually ran in shard 1; retained-size/multi-writer and exact-count assertions ran in shard 3. All current-head checks completed without failures.
- Targeted production/test types, lint, format, line-cap, and `git diff --check` passed. `pr-simplify` and isolated Codex autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Test cost: `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-cache-rebuild.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — five tests passed, 33.745 s wall time on Blacksmith Testbox.

Proof is a scaled synthetic corpus at the real cache cap; no latency or throughput improvement is claimed. Original main also emitted `CLI cleanup timed out: plugin-registration-resources after 5000ms`; the final candidate did not reproduce it, and plugin cleanup is outside this change.

The previous PR run had inherited TS2739 errors in `src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog.test-helpers.ts:122`; identical failures appear in [main run 40149301577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149301577), jobs 121037449659 and 121037449682. Its separate startup-close failure was reproduced and fixed at the cache/rebuild owners; the original test passed unchanged on this head. Current-head type checks passed.

Two setup problems were diagnosed before the final port proof: the fresh throwaway database lacked the installed server's `vector` extension, and a retry prefix exceeded the existing 27-character configuration limit. The first port attempt failed after 210 inputs; the direct diagnostic exposed the missing extension; the invalid-prefix attempt stopped at preflight with zero inputs. After qualifying the fixture, the final count used a fresh baseline copy and a distinct valid schema, with the stub tracked for the full run. No production change or relaxed assertion was used to obtain the passing result.

## Re-verdict under v5.4 — land under the scoped LANDING GATE; GC direction inconclusive

**Final decision: land under the maintainer’s explicit LANDING GATE after the single lengthened protocol.** Four short untraced A/A controls exposed a max-pause rejection on identical source; the frozen workload was lengthened once from 20 to 60 turns. All four longer untraced controls and both candidate pairs completed, followed by separately traced matching promotion controls and candidates. The longer controls have no rejection-threshold crossings. No eligible candidate metric crosses an adverse gate, and promotion passes. GC/work remains **INCONCLUSIVE** because its two untraced deltas have opposite signs; its negative mean is not a proven GC improvement. No third pair is prescribed because those deltas would not otherwise gate. This is the requested, correctness-tested removal of repeated checks, with revocation preserved; the explicit landing instruction covers the remaining GC uncertainty. No sampled-allocation improvement is claimed.

Reopened at the maintainer’s instruction. The earlier single traced pair is **inconclusive**, not a rejection: #181973 separates untraced cost gates from traced promotion, and the A/A audit showed short-window gates could trip on identical source. Historical numbers below remain disclosed but do not supply the new verdict.

Frozen measurement candidate: `1a176abb77e7` on main `3bcc91708d8e`. During the measurement queue, main advanced and the PR developed benchmark conflicts. The landing candidate is now `74b79f0c43a5` on main `9733a0202699`. Three conflict repairs preserve upstream benchmark and test changes: independent option contracts remain intact, and cron counters now extend main’s shared authority-count observer instead of restoring its removed inline copy. The observer’s no-caller-stacks mode is preserved, and the controller regression cases use main’s consolidated test fixtures without restoring deleted duplicate coverage. Independent reviews found no actionable findings; the six runtime-owner files are byte-identical across the later rebases, and the optimization semantics remain unchanged across all three. Main’s native-execution plumbing is retained. All numbers below remain explicitly prior-head evidence from the frozen protocol; its source was not changed mid-experiment. Fresh affected host-capability proof passed (50 tests), followed by the shared benchmark helper’s focused file (9 tests) after the observer move and the controller file (31 tests) after test-fixture integration; changed-file lint and formatting passed. The frozen head previously passed 94 focused tests and CI (79 successful checks, 56 skips, one neutral). The prior landing head completed CI with 83 successful checks, 58 skips and one neutral result; no failures or pending checks. The superseded PR-context/evidence job was cancelled after a body update; required aggregate and security gates passed. Exact-head CI on `74b79f0c43a5` completed with 79 successful checks, 52 skips and one neutral result, with no failures or pending checks; required aggregate and security gates passed. GitHub reports the head mergeable.

### Longer untraced A/A controls: no rejection-calibration crossing

All four fresh controls completed **60 turns per side**, with identical baseline source, three tools, five message appends and one recovered source per turn. No source/runtime/affinity mismatch, diagnostic loss or guard interruption occurred. Starts differed by 0.70–5.36 ms; process ages were approximately 98.5–99.9 seconds. Each side covered 28–32 natural major collections, without forced capture collections or trimming.

Evaluate AA1–2 and AA3–4 separately: neither window crosses a v5 rejection threshold or the max-pause safeguard. GC paired means are **+0.790 ms/turn (+1.622%)** and **+0.248 ms/turn (+0.277%)**. Those sign reversals alone do not establish phase sensitivity. No third control pair is prescribed; any candidate metric that would gate with unstable/mixed evidence still requires the fixed third candidate pair.

The report generator originally labeled every mixed-sign control metric as whole-protocol phase sensitivity. ### Short untraced A/A controls: INCONCLUSIVE

All four controls completed 20 cron turns per side, with three tools, five message appends and one recovered source per turn. Both sides loaded the same baseline with matching source/runtime/affinity attestations. No guard interruption or diagnostic loss occurred. All results are retained.

| Control | GC ms/turn, left → right | Absolute / relative Δ | Max GC pause ms (observed GC events) | Loop p99 ms (samples), left → right | Major collections, left / right |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| AA1 | 50.80 → 54.10 | +3.30 / +6.49% | 64.66 (n=307) → 77.65 (n=305) | 41.320 (n=4305) → 42.336 (n=4313) | 9 / 9 |
| AA2 | 57.91 → 60.74 | +2.83 / +4.88% | 69.97 (n=333) → 147.77 (n=276) | 44.663 (n=4361) → 45.777 (n=4357) | 10 / 9 |
| AA3 | 51.68 → 53.69 | +2.02 / +3.90% | 76.92 (n=308) → 71.04 (n=302) | 41.517 (n=4174) → 41.583 (n=4171) | 8 / 8 |
| AA4 | 47.80 → 52.24 | +4.43 / +9.27% | 48.97 (n=309) → 72.80 (n=323) | 39.420 (n=4217) → 39.748 (n=4208) | 9 / 10 |

Evaluate windows 1–2 and 3–4 separately. Window 1–2 crosses the max-pause safeguard in AA2: 147.77 ms exceeds max(50 ms, 2×69.97 ms) = 139.93 ms on identical source. Window 3–4 has no rejection threshold crossing. Neither window crosses the v5 mean/both-pair gates for total GC, CPU, loop or latency; minor pause-percentile changes are context under the sample/absolute-delta rules, and major tails have fewer than 50 collections per side. Mixed signs in small CPU/latency deltas remain disclosed in the full analysis.

This is an observed calibration failure, not a candidate rejection or an estimated false-positive rate. The predeclared single lengthening is complete for controls: **60 turns per side, four fresh untraced controls**, reported above; the completed untraced candidate comparison follows it. No short candidate timings are used to bypass the failed controls. The separate traced promotion pass follows cost comparisons.

### Setup repair before valid controls

The first identical-source attempt failed during warmup on both sides, before measured work: the shell tool reported `service child cleanup identity lost: native owner closed without kernel descendant extinction`. Current main makes memory-bounded exec use Linux process-tree ownership; that owner explicitly requires built JavaScript, without a TypeScript loader. The source-loaded fixture had not registered a built owner.

Following the existing `scripts/android-release-e2e.ts` fixture pattern, compile only the canonical `serviceChildGroupAnchor` standalone entry with tsdown outside capture, then register it through `registerSealedRuntimeProcessEntrypoint` in the identical baseline/candidate preload. The built owner is hash-attested alongside the protocol. Keep the 16 GiB limits, real shell-tool workload, and all cleanup/authority checks. The failed attempt and original protocol are retained as invalid setup evidence; fresh fixtures and processes restart the control sequence. No production code was changed for this repair.

The next fresh A/A attempt was aborted by the unchanged shared guard during warmup after three consecutive failing minutes (load 95.75, 155.80, then 125.90; the last also had Dirty >2 GiB). It produced no measured pair, both owned scopes were verified inactive, and its fresh-fixture retry waited on slot A. Neither failed attempt counts toward the four A/A controls. One side completed warmup through the built native owner before the guard abort.

### Scheduling revision before any valid result

The fresh retry remained queued while other lanes held phase-wide batch locks. It was canceled before either Gateway launched; its manifest and the original protocol are retained as an unmeasured orchestration attempt. A separate immutable batch-runner/protocol tree now prepares all selected fixtures sequentially before acquiring slot A once for a phase of at most four pairs. Every pair still uses fresh processes, swapped interleaved CPUs, counterbalanced launch order, the common post-warm barrier, and its own unchanged guard wait/watch. Work count, runtime, loader topology, diagnostics and source snapshots are unchanged. This changes only between-pair lock scheduling, before the first valid control; it avoids rejoining the shared queue after every pair. Collect all four fresh A/A controls under this revision.

### Frozen revised protocol

Use the #181973 harness plus this PR’s authenticated cron-turn workload: fresh synthetic four-session fixtures, one active same-conversation scheduled turn, three real tools, five message appends, five streamed chunks, no session resets. Both sides use one source installation and six immutable, hash-attested owner overlays. A/A loads baseline on both sides. Keep maintenance enabled. Use fresh processes, equal warmup work, counterbalanced launch order, a common start five seconds after both sides report warm, and record actual starts/process ages and heap states.

Slot A only (`.quiet.lock`), alternating even CPUs 96–126 versus odd CPUs 97–127. Every scope has MemoryMax <=24G; preparation uses CPUs 0–63 and low CPU/IO weights. The shared production guard runs before and throughout each pair. A guard interruption or failed setup invalidates the whole pair and requires fresh fixtures; adverse outcomes never justify exclusion.

Initial fixed work: **20 cron turns per side**. Collect >=4 untraced A/A pairs, then two swapped untraced candidate pairs. Cost capture uses `--diagnostics` without trace or allocation sampling. Apply v5–v5.3 to predeclared control windows 1–2 and 3–4. If controls trip or leave phase sensitivity unresolved, use exactly one disclosed longer protocol: **60 turns per side**, with four fresh controls and new candidate comparisons. The prior 20-turn pilot observed 8–9 natural major collections per side; 60 turns targets broader natural-cycle coverage without stopping by observed GC count.

GC/work, loop, latency and maxima are gated only on untraced runs. GC and promotion cost/work use the whole measured chat window divided by validated completed turns, retaining between-round bookkeeping and maintenance; per-round values remain context. Promotion is a separate traced pass with matching instrumentation-mode baselines/controls; its timing is attribution only. Preserve all valid work, pauses, maintenance and per-kind GC. Report absolute and relative deltas, sample counts, both maxima and pooled cost/work. Mixed-sign/unstable gating results get one predeclared third candidate pair; decide on signed absolute mean versus 20% of mean baseline cost. No ratio-selected favorable verdict, trimming, forced collection during capture, or normalization by major-cycle count.

If accepted, land. If still inconclusive after that one lengthened protocol, the maintainer explicitly instructs landing under the scoped LANDING GATE: fewer checks, preserved revocation, tested correctness. Any inconclusive GC and uncovered proof remain explicit in the final body. This authorization does not turn inconclusive measurements into a performance claim.

## What Problem This Solves

Authenticated cron turns repeatedly traverse recovered operator authority during transcript target checks, bookkeeping, and synchronous tool registration. Prior diagnostic evidence in #182002 observed about 38,550 availability checks per turn.

## User Impact

Completed-output accounting and trajectory recording retain their exact run lifetime without repeating operator policy validation. Tool execution, approvals, credentials, and delivery retain full live-source validation, including synchronous policy-callback revocation.

## Why This Change Was Made

A prepared transcript target repeated a full source traversal already performed by its attempt controller. Use the controller’s source check, then verify the captured run binding. Recheck exact attempt ownership after source callbacks, since a synchronous callback can close or replace an attempt without closing its admitted run. Keep the final transcript commit assertion.

Receipt composition dropped its inputs' existing lifetime-only assertions, forcing bookkeeping back through full authority checks. Preserve that contract at the receipt owner, use it for bookkeeping/prepared data, and run one composed check during tool registration. No cache, new configuration, or state migration. Production delta: +31/-26 (net +5). The existing lifetime-only contract must survive receipt composition, and the attempt owner needs an explicit post-callback ownership check; those correctness requirements account for the small net growth.

The existing Gateway benchmark now creates an authenticated same-conversation scheduled job through the real automations tool, executes its tools, verifies its receipt, and attributes assertion calls by stack. The cron workload is adapted from #182002. The runtime-only delta above excludes this proof harness: the benchmark driver and shared observer together add 193/remove 9 lines (net +184), and its guide adds 38. The requested non-test filter therefore reports +262/−35 (net +227), because it includes benchmark support and that guide; the six runtime owners remain +31/−26 (net +5). The benchmark growth provides the repeatable authenticated cron/tool/delivery workload required for this investigation.

## Evidence

- 38 existing recovered-operator tests passed, including synchronous policy-callback revocation (62.10 seconds including compilation).
- The new bookkeeping/revocation test failed on the original policy check and passes with the change. It exercises the real admitted caller and host, records completed output after policy revocation, and verifies the next bound tool does not execute.
- Focused host lifetime/environment, tool authority, host capability, and Gateway caller tests pass. Final follow-up: 111 tests, 40.97 seconds including compilation. Earlier focused pass proved the 10 source-lifetime and 2 environment tests; three registration error-order failures were fixed and the affected file rerun.
- Both new synchronous callback regressions (close attempt / replace attempt) fail on the original attempt owner and pass with the fix. Dispatch-owner and lane-controller tests: 58 passed in 43.44 seconds. Transcript lifecycle and original controller coverage: 76 passed before the final ownership fix.
- Changed-file lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. No operator configuration changes. Hosted Codex review also completed on `d30a3133c2c856e1587840287827f81e49fb521c` without findings.
- Exact-head PR CI on `d30a3133c2c856e1587840287827f81e49fb521c`: 81 successful checks, no failures; CI gate and security-sensitive review passed.
- Count-only diagnostic on the revised transcript path: 38,807 → 29,170 availability checks, 13,565 → 10,213 recovery assertions, and 23,821 → 17,957 source assertions per turn (three tool completions, five message appends). All six candidate owner snapshots were attested as loaded. The earlier traced timing result is inconclusive under v5.4; revised untraced controls/comparisons and the separate promotion result are reported above. No Testbox lease used; broad validation belongs to PR CI.

### Historical protocol (superseded by v5.4 above)

Use an isolated Gateway and synthetic loopback model: four fixture sessions, one active cron turn, five stream chunks, real tool callbacks, successful same-conversation receipt, no session reset. Counts use a separate instrumented pass and never supply timing evidence. Compare at least five turns per side in each of two concurrent, exclusively locked pairs, swapping interleaved CPU placement. One source installation, separate state/ports, and attested baseline/candidate owner overlays.

Report assertions, allocation, CPU, and latency per turn; GC total/promotion per work unit; maxima and tail sample counts. Apply v5.3: reject ≥20% adverse paired mean or ≥10% in both pairs. Opposite signs or >5× baseline spread are inconclusive, require absolute deltas and a third gating pair. p99 requires 1,000 samples, p95 200, major-GC tails 50 collections. Sub-1 ms paired pause-percentile shifts are context. Fewer collections ≥20% with nonincreasing total GC makes pause percentiles context. Candidate max pause >max(50 ms, 2× baseline max) retains its gate. Discard guard-interrupted pairs.


### Caller classification

One baseline diagnostic turn: 38,853 availability checks, partitioned by first meaningful caller (179 distinct locations; no overlapping stack-substring counts). The final same-base count comparison above uses a later diagnostic turn, so incidental scheduling counts differ slightly. The workload performs three real tool completions, commits five message appends, and delivers its scheduled result.

| Caller group | Availability checks | Classification and action |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Session target settings validation | 9,978 | Current policy/target validation nested in authority; retain peer-adjacent owner. |
| Attempt controller `isCurrent` | 7,021 | Retain full validation as the prepared target’s single source check; recheck exact ownership after callbacks. |
| Prepared target’s explicit active assertion | 6,970 | Repeated synchronous validation; replace with final exact scope check. |
| Transcript lifecycle commit | 6,919 | State mutation boundary; retain prepared source validation. |
| Plugin construction/caller guards | 1,224 | Source/caller admission; retain. |
| Other target capture/admission | 1,009 | Original caller/source capture; retain. |
| Watchdog validity/attachment | 918 | Lifecycle bookkeeping (901) and attachment admission (17); unchanged, scope-only follow-up possible. |
| Tool construction preparation | 527 | Source-bound caller preparation; retain. |
| Exec/process/client-tool dispatch | 705 | Privileged effects; retain. |
| Session-tool operator authority | 114 | Privileged session-tool authority; retain. |
| Session state readers/writers | 313 | Storage/source boundaries; retain. |
| Native registration | 155 | Retain ownership; deduplicate synchronous active traversals in registration callback. |
| Audit owner binding | 102 | Owner bookkeeping across asynchronous binding; retain exact owner capture. |
| Runtime/model/workspace preparation | 1,717 | Mixed admission, credential/model policy and bookkeeping; unchanged. |
| Reply orchestration/policy/delivery | 883 | Mixed admission, delivery and terminal bookkeeping; unchanged. |
| Session admission/mailbox/tool snapshot | 129 | Source admission/ownership; retain. |
| Cron capture/settlement/heartbeat | 135 | Mixed occurrence admission, settlement and bookkeeping; unchanged. |
| Provider rate-limit stream | 34 | Request/authentication after awaited rate limit; retain. |
| **Total** | **38,853** | |

The built-in workload does not directly call host output-token/trajectory bookkeeping. Those scope-only changes are proven by the focused admitted-host revocation test; the count reduction principally demonstrates transcript-target and registration changes. The mixed residual buckets are not a claim that every remaining assertion is necessary. No global authority memoization or fail-open fallback is introduced.


### Historical traced measurement and limits

One valid concurrent pair, 20 completed cron turns per side, interleaved slot-B CPUs (baseline even 64–94; candidate odd 65–95), separate synthetic state and loopback ports. Both sides loaded all six attested owner files and every turn completed three tools, five message appends, and one recovered operator source. Common source installation pinned to `237fdc662d90`; candidate owner bytes match the reviewed PR head. Source-loader runtime, synthetic loopback model, five streamed chunks. These are **single-pair observations**, not swapped-pair conclusions.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Absolute / relative delta |

| Availability checks per turn (separate count pass) | 38,807 | 29,170 | −9,637 / −24.8% |
| Recovery assertions per turn | 13,565 | 10,213 | −3,352 / −24.7% |
| Source assertions per turn | 23,821 | 17,957 | −5,864 / −24.6% |
| Main-thread CPU / turn | 768.9 ms | 717.7 ms | −51.1 ms / −6.65% |
| Process CPU / turn | 5,827.9 ms | 5,739.2 ms | −88.8 ms / −1.52% |
| Mean cron completion latency | 5,873.8 ms | 6,033.4 ms | +159.6 ms / +2.72% |
| Total observed GC / turn | 79.65 ms | 135.40 ms | +55.75 ms / +69.98% |
| Main-isolate promotion / turn | 27.70 MB | 30.00 MB | +2.30 MB / +8.30% |
| Event-loop p99 | 48.33 ms (n=5,560) | 54.69 ms (n=5,518) | +6.36 ms / +13.15% |

Observer collection counts including incremental events: 298 → 229. Event-loop p99 covers the whole measured workload including between-round bookkeeping.

The long candidate collection occurred in turn 13. V8 attributed about 996 ms to the clearing phase, including weak-handle clearing and waiting for a GC job.
