prs.title: fix(state): explain lease ownership loss
prs.body:
Closes #183154. Related to #182476.

## What Problem This Solves

Native state-lease renewal and ownership verification collapse three persisted loss states into the same `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST` message: expired lease, replacement owner, and missing row. A failed update/repair can therefore retain a correct refusal but not the evidence needed to diagnose why it happened.

## User Impact

Lease-loss receipts now include a safe reason when the database supports one:

```text
state lease synthetic/diagnostics was lost (lease expired 1000 ms ago; last heartbeat 2000 ms ago)
state lease synthetic/diagnostics was lost (lease owner was replaced)
state lease synthetic/diagnostics was lost (lease record is missing)
```

The replacement owner token is never included. Error codes, lease duration, renewal cadence, acquisition, ownership, fencing, cleanup, and recovery behavior are unchanged. Existing callers that only match the established message prefix retain it.

## Why This Change Was Made

An observed Windows `2026.10.7` update repair spent 1,427,442 ms in final Doctor and 637,736 ms in plugin finalization, then retained only `plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global was lost`. That receipt could not distinguish event-loop starvation from a competing owner or missing state.

After a failed renewal, this change reads the row inside the same write transaction. Ownership verification uses the same database read boundary. A small structured reason is passed to the existing error owner, which formats only elapsed timing or a redacted state classification. If timestamps are incomplete or the row cannot support a safe conclusion, the existing generic message remains.

This follows the diagnostic-only approach used by #170835 and #154878: it makes the next incident actionable without claiming to fix the long-running work that caused the lease loss.

## Evidence

- Before production changes, the new renewal cases all failed with the same mismatch: expected an expired/replaced/missing reason, received `state lease synthetic/diagnostics was lost`.
- After the patch on current main `696f70f31`, the focused state-lease diagnostics file passed: **1 file / 14 tests**, including renewal and verification for all three loss states. The related worker regression set also passed with the repository unit config: **3 files / 23 tests**.
- Type-aware lint and TypeScript diagnostics passed for all seven changed files.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Production delta: +64/-5 lines. Test delta: +109/-8 lines. No schema, config, protocol, or dependency changes.
- Manual diff review covered transaction boundaries, replacement-owner redaction, compatibility, and focused test coverage; no actionable finding remained.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** persisted state-lease loss reasons were discarded from `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST`, including the receipt retained by update repair.
- **Real environment tested:** the original symptom was observed on Windows 11 `10.0.26200.x`, OpenClaw `2026.10.7`, Node.js `26.12.1`. The after-fix source proof ran on macOS against current main plus this patch with Node.js `24.22.1` and a real temporary OpenClaw SQLite state database.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** acquired a real native lease, mutated the persisted row to expired/replaced/missing, then invoked both `renewOpenClawStateLease()` and `verifyOpenClawStateLeaseOwnership()` through `src/state/openclaw-state-lease-diagnostics.test.ts`. Regression command: `/tmp/openclaw-node-runtime/bin/node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-diagnostics.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-worker.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-worker.transaction-group.test.ts`.
- **Evidence after fix:** `Test Files 3 passed (3)`; `Tests 23 passed (23)`; completed in 16.34 s. Type proof: `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --type-aware --type-check --deny-warnings <seven changed files>` exited 0.
- **Observed result after fix:** all six new production-storage cases emit the expected redacted reason while the existing diagnostics and worker ownership tests remain green.
- **What was not tested:** this branch was not deployed to the Windows host, a full Windows update was not rerun, and the complete repository test suite was not run locally. PR CI provides the broad repository lanes. This PR does not fix or benchmark the long-running Doctor/plugin work itself.

prs.title: fix: retain local helper programs in standalone builds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes local helper programs and runtime probes that depend on inline JavaScript or loose application files when OpenClaw is packaged. A bundled SQLite bootstrap could also look for its worker under a dist chunk and reject a supported runtime.

## User Impact

Repository publication and restoration, workspace manifests and Git history, shell environment capture, and runtime discovery use declared programs in ordinary Node/Bun installations and standalone builds. Sealed package recovery keeps working after the original package and neighboring worker assets are removed. No new configuration or dependencies are required.

Arbitrary external disk JavaScript remains outside the experimental AOT artifact's qualified behavior; external probes still use the exact selected runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process manifest owns local entrypoints and built script assets. Generation replaces runtime function compilation and inline local child programs while retaining remote command contracts. The shared SQLite capability owner supports an explicit in-process probe for sealed recovery; ordinary startup uses its declared worker. Bootstrap resolution preserves the manifest's source and built paths, and npm/npx selection preserves the selected installation's topology. Package, Docker, and isolated tooling inputs include the complete asset closure.

This is a focused runtime stage following #182405 and #182982. Complete build-time dynamic-target validation is a separate follow-up; no incomplete validator is enabled here.

## Evidence

- Focused repair replay: 160 selected cases passed with `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`; failed CI cases were selected by their owning contract. Wall times below include cold compiler/worker preparation.
- Targeted production, script, and test types; type-aware lint; format; generator freshness; environment-budget and duplicate-coverage checks passed. Workflow validation passed using the installed Python 3.12. The initial broad lint route timed out during unrelated SDK declaration preparation; dedicated source-backed lint configs passed without changing timeouts or skipping checks.
- The full candidate against current main passed independent Codex review through P2. The conflict integration passed all 38 quiescence/lifecycle/negotiation, build-graph and freshness cases in 340.76s wall. Bundled bootstrap controls reproduce the missing SQLite worker on the old code under both Node and Bun, then pass with the fix in both bundled and root layouts.
- Small extracted probes compiled with the experimental Bun AOT toolchain: undeclared Doctor/discovery/backup entries fail; declared entries pass all seven operations, including with sources hidden, with matching loose Node/Bun results. Eval hashing fails before the cutover and the static worker returns the same hash afterward. Additional AOT controls pass repository restore, shell capture, and manifest-dispatched inventory. No full OpenClaw AOT build or interpreter-tripwire claim.
- Prior unchanged-input package/launcher and import-closure proof passed 31 cases in 548.58s; runtime-stage generator/build-graph/Docker proof passed 19 cases in 191.85s. Overlapping groups are not additive coverage. Exact-head PR CI supplies broad proof.

<details>
<summary>Focused repair replay wall times</summary>

prs.title: fix: Stop omits native descendant requester lifecycle
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: stopping an exact Gateway run can stop its parent but leave native descendants running with a requester-generation error.

## User Impact

User impact: exact Stop cancels the selected request's native descendants while preserving other requests, replacement sessions, and already accepted cancellation outcomes. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reserved and indexed request paths omitted the selected physical session's lifecycle revision. Both now supply that revision only when the session ID matches, and retain the captured source identity across asynchronous metadata preparation. Native generation, custody, and live requester checks remain with their existing owners. Main's committed-cancellation callback is preserved.

Related: #181475 fixes retained-parent selection inside Codex; this fixes the earlier Gateway request producer. #174900 covers separate catalog and completion continuity.

## Evidence

- On unchanged main production, seven regressions fail: five exact-Stop routes omit the lifecycle revision and two metadata-preparation cases accept retargeted sources. The other 17 cases pass.
- After integration: 67 Gateway tests passed in 308.98s and 12 native cancellation tests passed in 121.13s. These suites exercise real request/cancellation ownership with fixed external transport fixtures; their imports dominate wall time.
- Added negative cases exercise foreign and revoked requesters through both reserved and indexed Gateway routes. The reserved route retains the parent cancellation accepted before revocation; native cancellation remains unconsumed. The native-owner regression explicitly checks zero `turn/interrupt` requests after revocation. Existing native tests cover authorized interruption/settlement and foreign custody.
- Targeted core/extension oxlint, formatting of all four changed files, and diff whitespace checks pass. Two independent P0–P2 reviews found no actionable issues; the second includes the corrected accepted-parent assertion. Local native typecheck could not use the nested checkout’s shared compiler layout; exact-head PR CI supplies broad type proof.
- CI found a test-only generic callback typing error: the observer mock erased the cancellation callback's return type. The observer is now separate from the real callback; behavior and authority checks are unchanged. Both affected reserved/indexed regressions passed again (540.19s total; 491.83s in the suite, dominated by cold compilation), and a fresh P0–P2 review of this correction found no actionable issue.
- Final-head [CI run 40157376307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40157376307) is green, including all six test-type jobs; prior superseded checks do not apply to this head.
- Production +57/-35 (net +22); tests +238/-34 (net +204). The production increase supplies the missing lifecycle on two distinct paths and shares the captured-identity assertion; further consolidation would mix different parent-settlement contracts.

A fresh Gateway-to-native live run was not performed: the existing tests do not expose that composition, and adding a new cross-boundary harness exceeds this bounded proof pass. The native tests exercise the real cancellation owner with a mocked app-server transport; they are not live-model evidence.

Original fix by @enki; contributor commits and authorship preserved.

prs.title: feat(doctor): report automations that will lose access or pause
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled jobs linked to the conversation that created them now run with that conversation's authority and pause when it is gone, but nothing tells an operator which of their existing automations will lose access, pause, or stay unbound before it happens.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor` (with or without `--fix`) now prints a read-only "Scheduled-run access review" under Cron. It lists:

- automations that will **lose access**, with the lost fields (owner-only tools when the creator is no longer an owner; unsandboxed execution when the creating conversation requires a sandbox);
- automations that will **pause** at the next run, with the conversation and the cause (removed, archived, or a missing worktree path);
- automations that are **unbound**: linked by conversation key only, or to a conversation that was reset after the job was created;
- automations on a **CLI backend** whose owner-only tools differ from embedded runs today and will match them once both runtimes read the scheduled-run authority;
- linked automations whose creating conversation has **no stored chat type** (conversations created by 2026.10.6 or earlier), so their runs get no conversation memory.

The review writes nothing and sends nothing. It does not repair anything; the chat-type backfill is separate follow-up work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The review reuses the same pieces occurrence admission uses: `scheduledParentLinkOf`, `parentRowFactsFromEntry`, `assembleScheduledAdmissionFacts`, the pure `buildScheduledExecutionContext`, and `compareScheduledDecisions` from the legacy projection. Doctor reads stored jobs with the existing read-only inventory (`inspectCronJobsForDoctor`), decodes them with the runtime row codec, and reads each named parent with `readSessionEntryReadOnlyInWorker`.

Owner checks that admission does through Gateway-resident state are done read-only here:
- profile requesters and the creator-role sandbox read the stored profile row (role and GitHub login) through the existing state-read worker instead of the resident profile catalog, which Doctor does not load;
- channel requesters use `isConfiguredCommandOwner`; a linked channel operator or an operator-source snapshot needs the running Gateway, so the review marks those losses "could not verify" rather than calling `prepareCommandOwnerAuthority`, which can write an authorization reference.

Shared-file change: `assembleScheduledAdmissionFacts` takes an optional `creatorRoleSandbox` that the caller already evaluated. Admission does not pass it and keeps its current behavior.

Accepted limits: the CLI backend is resolved from config (payload model or agent default, then `resolveCliRuntimeExecutionProvider`), not from a per-run session override. The chat-type check looks only at the parent row itself; a parent that is a spawned child is skipped because memory lineage resolves its root elsewhere. There is no `openclaw automations bind` command yet, so unbound jobs are told to recreate the automation from its conversation.

## Evidence

**Current-head unit tests** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor/cron/execution-context-report.test.ts src/commands/doctor/cron/execution-context-check.test.ts`): 20 passed (including linked main-target pause and command-payload exemption regressions). One or more cases per category: loss with lost fields, unverified loss, sandbox loss, no-loss owner; pause for removed, archived, missing worktree with path; unbound key-only and reset; runtime owner (only owner contexts on a CLI backend); missing chat type (root vs typed vs spawned parent); undecodable stored authority; collector profile and role rules, role sandbox, configured channel owner, archived parent read with `readConsistency: "latest"`, malformed rows skipped; linked main-target pauses included, a failing parent read listed without aborting the review.

`pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files: clean.

**Upgrade proof from v2026.10.6 (Crabbox, AWS)**

- Command: `CRABBOX_AWS_REGION=us-east-1 CRABBOX_CAPACITY_REGIONS=us-east-1,us-east-2,us-west-2 crabbox run --provider aws --timing-json --ttl 90m --idle-timeout 45m --label 0d5.15-doctor-proof-2 --download /tmp/0d5.15-out.tgz=... --shell -- "bash proof-0d5.15/remote.sh"` (local-only proof scripts, not committed)
- Tested source: `60b92158a97e4b5ffc1291cfe1cef2695d1e813a` working tree synced to the lease; remote `sha256sum` of the four changed source files matches the local head; the remote build rebuilt `dist` from that source (`dist is stale: missing_build_stamp`).
- Provider `aws`, lease `cbx_30739e0cce29` (c7a.8xlarge, us-east-1), run `run_b62ef4d054fde236e5d6640230543ace`: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_b62ef4d054fde236e5d6640230543ace. Exit 0. Lease released (`CRABBOX_AWS_REGION=us-east-1 crabbox stop --provider aws --id cbx_30739e0cce29` → `released lease=cbx_30739e0cce29`).

Steps on the lease:
1. `npm install openclaw@2026.10.6`; its Gateway, on a fresh isolated state dir, creates five conversations (live, archived, removed, reset, managed worktree) and eight automations: six linked by `sessionKey` (two to the live parent, one with a `claude-cli/...` model), and two unlinked (one with a `claude-cli/...` model). It then archives, deletes and resets the matching parents, and the worktree directory is removed after the Gateway stops.
2. The PR build runs `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes` (the normal upgrade step), then plain `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` twice. Per-table content hashes of the state and agent databases are taken around each plain run.

Observed review (identical in all three runs):

```text
Scheduled-run access review (read-only; nothing was changed).
2 automations will lose access because runs use the authority of the conversation and person that created them:
- linked-live (...): owner-only tools such as sessions, portal, nodes, gateway and plugins (the creator is not currently an owner)
- linked-cli (...): owner-only tools such as sessions, portal, nodes, gateway and plugins (the creator is not currently an owner)
3 automations will pause at the next run because the conversation that created them is unavailable:
- linked-archived (...): `<creating-conversation>` is archived
- linked-removed (...): `<creating-conversation>` was removed
- linked-worktree (...): `<creating-conversation>` has a missing worktree (`/tmp/0d5.15-up/state/worktrees/.../worktree-parent`)
1 automation is not bound to the conversation that created it:
- linked-reset (...): `<creating-conversation>` was reset after the automation was created
1 automation runs on a CLI backend, where scheduled runs get no owner-only tools today while embedded runs do:
- unlinked-cli (...): claude-cli
2 automations have a creating conversation with no stored chat type, so their runs get no conversation memory:
- linked-live (...), linked-cli (...): `<creating-conversation>`
```

Allowed vs refused cases: `unlinked` (no parent, embedded) produces no finding, while `unlinked-cli` (no parent, CLI backend, owner context) is listed as a runtime difference. `linked-cli` is a loss but not a runtime difference, because its context owner is false, which already matches today's CLI runs. The live-parent jobs were created over the Gateway token, so they record no creator profile; under the design's rule an unknown requester is not an owner, which is why both show the owner-only loss.

Read-only: in both plain runs no cron, session or profile table changed. On the first plain run after `--fix`, one agent-database `schema_meta` row was added (in the local reproduction its key is `historical-transcript-directives-v1`), which Doctor's transcript migration owns and completes on its first run after an upgrade (unrelated to this check). The second run changed no table at all. The same results reproduced in a local run of the same script.



## Current-head readiness

ClawSweeper reviewed `60b92158a97e4b5ffc1291cfe1cef2695d1e813a`: Ready for maintainer review, no actionable findings. The main-target exclusion is removed: main-target jobs report unavailable-parent pauses but not detached-context access changes. Command payloads honor the scheduler's no-pause exemption. Profile reads use the existing state-read worker; the mock-exports and database-worker ratchets pass. The new AWS proof above retested the final production source; remote hashes match all four changed production files. Current checks: 80 successful, 83 skipped, 1 neutral; none failing or pending. No production source changed after that proof. Lease inspection now reports `state: released`, `cleanupStatus: complete`, and `provisioningResourceMayExist: false`.

Static replay over the operator's stored state (online backups, no writes to live data): 105 jobs, no `gain-unexpected`. Labels (jobs can have multiple): 101 equal, 11 gain-intended, 3 retarget, 7 ownerEmbedded losses, 4 pauses. All four pauses name archived parents. All seven ownerEmbedded losses are marked owner-check unverified by the offline replay: their linked requester needs live Gateway authority, so these are conservative predictions rather than proof that the creator is not an owner. Private job names and conversation identifiers are retained only in local evidence, not published here. This is the replay script's scope (it excludes main-target jobs); new main-target behavior is covered by the focused regression.

prs.title: fix: reduce standalone worker memory and startup cost
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Standalone Gateways pay unnecessary startup CPU and memory for large embedded routing maps in every worker.

## User Impact

Workers allocate only the routing and metadata rows they use. Module aliases, direct embedded destinations, native dependency resolution, and file metadata retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Store sorted JSON-encoded rows as immutable embedded text, binary-search requested keys, and cache decoded values within each VM. This also removes the eager destination Set and the second eagerly materialized embedded-path dictionary.

## Evidence

The same large routing map reproduced the penalty when compiled as JavaScript; 10,000 unused TypeScript interfaces did not. With a fixed compiler, the controlled memory slope fell from 104.66 to 9.11 MiB per worker. The full original-source desktop image retained all 145,971 aliases; its same-entry worker heap fell from 28.58 to 5.16 MiB (emitted-JS control: 4.96 MiB).

Eight interleaved samples per image on a loaded Mac, using the same frozen compiler:

| Median | Original TS | Fixed TS | Emitted JS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Gateway ready CPU | 4.43 s | 2.59 s | 2.43 s |
| Gateway ready wall | 7.08 s | 6.18 s | 5.32 s |
| First turn wall | 1.93 s | 1.35 s | 1.08 s |
| Settled process-tree RSS | 3,304 MiB | 1,218 MiB | 1,111 MiB |

The full-image comparison uses the original-source integration build; this PR ports the identical lookup implementation to current main's standalone owners. The rebased six-file patch is byte-identical to the independently reviewed patch. Focused validation: 69 tests pass; four existing metadata-fixture failures reproduce on unchanged main with identical signatures. Targeted lint, script/tooling typechecks, formatting, and diff checks pass.

The fixed TS image and matched emitted-JS baseline passed the frozen core campaign (fresh/reused config, Doctor contributions, Gateway/agent behavior, clean shutdown, and crash audit). One real Codex turn reused the existing login and completed its native hook plus exact-file proof. No engine changes or cross-VM mutable sharing are involved.

The only failed CI test job is [checks-node-compact-small-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40153621051/job/121050493205): the two secret-resolver fixture cases read missing `params.args`, and the MXC/ACPX fixture cases lack the `resolvePluginRuntimeProcessAssetUrl` / `resolvePackageRuntimeProcessEntrypointUrl` bindings. These same four errors reproduce with unchanged main owners; the fixture and extracted owner inputs are unchanged by this PR. They remain failed and are being handled under the native inherited-failure landing policy. `security-fast` passed independently.

prs.title: perf(agents): avoid merged config work for GitHub identity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

GitHub identity checks construct a complete merged agent configuration just to read its unchanged `tools.github` entry, and publication options resolve the same selection twice.

## User Impact

This is a small internal allocation/CPU reduction. Identity selection, credential rotation, issuer binding, authority checks, and redaction retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the authored entry through the existing roster owner, whose index already follows config publication/immutable snapshots. Reuse the selection already made in the synchronous options preparation. This removes work without introducing another cache or caching credential validity. Production delta: **+3/−3 lines (net zero)**.

The repeatable owner benchmark uses 40 frozen agent entries split between system inheritance and agent overrides. The existing Gateway soak now supports its existing seven list/search filter shapes during mixed RPC traffic; benchmark usage is in script headers.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule declared before candidate measurements: preserve identity/credential behavior, reduce selection CPU/allocation, and check for material adverse effects in a matched synthetic Gateway soak. Timing/GC gates use untraced runs; allocation profiling is separate. Sub-millisecond tails and sparse major-GC percentiles are context; noisy adverse GC requires matched controls.

Two owner pairs, each side five warm samples of 20,000 selections; the second pair reverses source order:

| Pair | CPU µs/check, base → candidate | Sampled bytes/check, base → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.322 → 3.453 | 5,258 → 4,706 |
| 2 | 4.928 → 3.548 | 5,269 → 4,725 |

Mean paired changes: about **−24% CPU in the sampling-enabled owner pass**, **−10.4% sampled allocation**. Owner CPU includes allocation-profiler overhead; the untraced Gateway CPU is reported separately. These percentages do not describe the whole Gateway. Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/github-tool-selection-measure.ts 20000` with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.

- Focused identity/read/App tests: 58 passed across three files (146.14 s including first-use compilation; test execution was approximately 1% of that duration).
- Export-name collision guard and both eager-import/PR-wrapper closure files: passed (22 tests).
- Changed-file formatting and narrow core/script type-aware lint: passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. The helper refused the requested provider/config mismatch; no operator configuration was changed.

### Local dist Gateway load

Synthetic fixture: 10,000 sessions (including 2,000 archived), 8,000 settled runs, 40 synthetic plugins, 64 resident WebSocket clients, 16 concurrent mock-provider turns with tool calls, and sidebar/list/search/dashboard churn. Separate matching state directories, seed 1717, 60 s warmup, then at least 600 s measured. No production Gateway traffic. Base runtime: `a6c17d7a3cac77f7e6210fd19a8aa6829a6d445d`; measured candidate: `c9c4065fd325711c9e30eb24867b535b6b124f2e`. The branch was subsequently rebased to `2a82eb7795d8027885f39f6a663845a46b5a7f37`; the changed files and selection resolver are byte-identical after rebase. Full-Gateway figures remain evidence for the explicitly named measured revisions; current-head CI is separate.

Untraced windows were 609.82 → 609.74 s, with 416 → 544 completed turns and matching tool results. GitHub options calls were 1,371 → 1,350; previews 1,358 → 1,323; pull-request subscriptions 1,297 → 1,311. Both runs recorded zero diagnostic collection errors and zero dropped diagnostic events.

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Absolute change | Relative change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU, % | 47.42 | 53.72 | +6.30 | +13.3% |
| Main-thread CPU, ms/turn | 695.13 | 602.08 | -93.04 | -13.4% |
| GC, s/min | 3.19 | 2.95 | -0.24 | -7.6% |
| GC, ms/turn | 77.98 | 55.09 | -22.89 | -29.4% |
| Loop p99, ms | 149.03 | 95.09 | -53.94 | -36.2% |
| List p95, ms | 260.88 | 128.76 | -132.12 | -50.6% |
| List p99, ms | 668.22 | 276.11 | -392.11 | -58.7% |
| RSS peak, MiB | 4897.20 | 4807.60 | -89.60 | -1.8% |
| RSS end, MiB | 3985.62 | 4540.74 | +555.13 | +13.9% |
| Heap peak, MiB | 1238.22 | 1632.93 | +394.71 | +31.9% |
| Heap end, MiB | 796.54 | 765.17 | -31.38 | -3.9% |

Loop p99 sample counts: 18,037 → 21,890 (20 ms resolution); the existing diagnostics do not retain loop p95. List p95/p99 sample counts: 1,315 → 1,343. Maximum loop delay: 750.78 → 455.34 ms; maximum list latency: 1,686.62 → 611.31 ms.

GC counts: minor 3,500 → 4,327; major 63 → 78; incremental 63 → 78. Total time by kind: minor 27.503 → 25.452 s; major 4.816 → 4.353 s; incremental 0.121 → 0.165 s. Maximum pause across all kinds: 314.45 → 138.76 ms; minor maxima 183.79 → 138.76 ms; major maxima 314.45 → 135.54 ms. Minor p95/p99: 29.05/62.21 → 19.45/46.33 ms. Major p95/p99: 159.74/171.01 → 112.13/132.09 ms, context only because collection counts are below percentile sample thresholds.

This is one sequential full-Gateway pair on a shared Mac, not a controlled attribution of the large latency/throughput differences to three production lines. CPU/turn, GC, and latency improved in this pair; memory was mixed (higher peak heap and ending RSS, slightly lower peak RSS and ending heap). There is no claim of a whole-Gateway percentage improvement or retained-memory reduction. The repeatable selection allocation reduction is the demonstrated small win.

Separate sampling/traced windows: **621.55 → 641.30 s**, **496 → 288 turns**, **18,711 → 18,741 RPCs**, including **1,379 → 1,422 GitHub options calls**. Sampled allocation: **157.79 → 103.51 MiB/s** (−54.28 MiB/s, −34.4%), **197.73 → 230.49 MiB/turn** (+32.76 MiB/turn, +16.6%). Promotion: **18.54 → 20.96 MiB/turn** (+2.42 MiB/turn, +13.1%). The shared host became substantially more contended during the candidate pass; fixed-duration background RPC volume stayed nearly constant while turn throughput fell. This changed the work mix, so the whole-Gateway allocation/promotion comparison is **inconclusive for causal attribution**, not evidence of a global percentage improvement or a controlled adverse result. Traced timing/GC figures are not used as gates.

Sampled cumulative selection subtrees in the actual Gateway profile fell **4.67 → 1.22 MiB**; all identity subtrees were **73.74 → 71.63 MiB**. Those sparse module samples corroborate direction, not a precise percentage claim. The repeated isolated owner benchmark supplies the stable ~10.4% allocation result. This is a small residual optimization with net-zero production LOC, no additional cache, and unchanged live credential checks.

The first candidate profiling attempt ended after six rounds when `sessions.github.options` exceeded its 5 s deadline; concurrent unrelated `board.get` calls took 4–5 s, and cleanup also timed out. That incomplete run is excluded and its fixture retired. The full replacement above completed on fresh synthetic state with unchanged settings and deadlines, with zero diagnostic collection errors/dropped diagnostic events; post-measurement cron cleanup again timed out, so that fixture is also retired. These observed failures remain reported; a successful replacement does not establish their cause or claim to fix them.

Median sampled RSS/heap provide additional context, without replacing extrema: RSS 4,240.66 → 4,316.52 MiB; heap 821.33 → 782.25 MiB (28 → 36 non-forced-GC memory samples).

<details>
<summary>Gateway reproduction commands</summary>

Build the selected revision (`pnpm build` for the initial dist build; `pnpm build:runtime` for the candidate runtime), then use independent state directories and loopback ports for each side:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/team-shape-fixture.ts \
  --state-dir "$STATE" --sessions 10000 --runs 8000 --settled-runs \
  --transcript-mib 64 --projects 2 --cron 100 --approvals 200 \
  --seed 1717 --now 1792800000000 --port "$PORT" --github-options-connected
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts \
  --state-dir "$STATE" --entry dist/entry.js --scenario memory-soak \
  --clients 32 --exact-clients 8 --runs 16 --plugins 40 \
  --chunks 100 --chunk-interval-ms 10 --warmup-ms 60000 --duration-ms 600000 \
  --round-interval-ms 15000 --memory-interval-ms 15000 --retained-profile-ms 0 \
  --stress-tools --mixed-rpc --dashboard-rpc --github-options-connected \
  --list-filter-churn --list-interval-ms 1000 --poll-seed lane1717 \
  --row-mode sidebar --diagnostics --port "$PORT" --mock-port "$MOCK_PORT" \
  --revision "$REVISION"
```

For the separate allocation/promotion pass add `--allocations --heap-sampling-interval 32768`. It enables GC tracing; its latency and GC timings are not used as the untraced gate. All paths, credentials, provider responses, repository metadata, and identities are synthetic. No Testbox or remote load was used.

</details>

prs.title: refactor: simplify Feishu runtime logging and tool registration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu repeatedly probes for logger methods that its runtime contract requires. Call those methods directly at 21 sites while retaining optional runtime objects. Remove the unreachable missing-config branch from tool registration: the factory selection ends in the host’s required `api.config`.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The enabled-account/tool-family predicate, account and credential selection, external-response validation, and execution authority checks remain in place. Bundled plugins ship with the current host; this removes no supported older-host capability fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

22 redundant conditions across nine Feishu files; production diff is 21 additions / 22 deletions (net -1 line). prs.title: fix(macos): stop trusting the stale /etc/ssl/cert.pem bundle in services
prs.body:
## Summary

macOS gateway and node services defaulted `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`. Apple no longer updates that bundle, and Node treats the extra file as additive trust, so the default added roots that the macOS trust store distrusts. This PR removes that additional trust source (the existing `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` darwin default stays), treats the exact legacy value as unset when service environments are built, and makes `openclaw gateway install` refresh a service that still stores it. It complements the already-merged compromised-chain fixes in the Rust TLS build (#179246) and the secret egress proxy (#179249) by closing the Node service-environment path they do not touch.

## What Problem This Solves

**What this Problem Solves** — Fixes: macOS gateway and node services trust the stale `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` bundle on top of the macOS trust store, so a certificate chain the system distrusts is accepted for the service's own HTTPS traffic (model providers, channels, plugin downloads, `web_fetch`).

1. `src/bootstrap/node-startup-env.ts`: the darwin branch of `resolveNodeStartupTlsEnvironment` defaulted `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.
2. `src/daemon/service-env.ts`: `buildCommonServiceEnvironment` copied that value into the generated gateway and node service environments, so it was frozen into launchd definitions.
3. `src/cli/daemon-cli/install.ts`: reinstall preserved the stored value and the drift check had no leg for it, so an existing install was never refreshed.

Net effect: OpenClaw's own default added a stale trust source on top of the service's other roots.

## User Impact

Operators of macOS services no longer get the stale bundle added to their service's trust. Node's own bundled roots and the system store remain in effect as before, so this removes one additional trust source and does not make the service trust identical to the macOS trust store: a root that macOS distrusts but Node still bundles can stay trusted until the Node runtime itself is updated. After `openclaw gateway install` (or the automatic refresh on update) and a service restart, the stale bundle is gone from the service definition.

Compatibility: an operator whose HTTPS relies on a root present only in the stale bundle will see certificate errors after the refresh. Migration: configure an explicitly maintained CA bundle at a non-legacy path with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`; every non-legacy path is preserved byte for byte. Do not retain a compromised root merely to restore connectivity. An operator who deliberately set the exact string `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` cannot be told apart from the value OpenClaw wrote, so that setting is treated as unset.

Scope of the repair: it applies to service definitions OpenClaw generates and refreshes. A CLI respawn (`src/entry.respawn.ts`) or node-worker snapshot (`src/node-host/node-worker-environment.ts`) that inherits an environment already carrying the legacy value keeps it until its source service definition is rebuilt. This PR does not rewrite those inherited maps.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` as the darwin default: it reads the macOS trust store, so the launchd TLS behavior that motivated the original default still works without the stale bundle.
- Strip only the exact legacy value, in the resolver that owns the default, so service builders and the drift check agree on one rule. No new configuration surface and no exported symbols.
- The drift check asks the same resolver whether a stored value resolves to nothing; only the exact legacy darwin value can, so operator-chosen paths are never flagged.

## Evidence

| Path | Mode | Before (base `14530ae62b5`) | After (this branch) | How verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Generated darwin service env, gateway and node | no inherited value | `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`, `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` | `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` unset, `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` | real `buildServiceEnvironment` / `buildNodeServiceEnvironment`, `platform: "darwin"`, output below; `service-env.test.ts` |
| Generated darwin service env | inherited legacy `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` | value kept | unset, `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` | same run; `service-env.test.ts` |
| Generated darwin service env | inherited `/opt/corporate-ca.pem` | kept | kept | same run |
| Gateway install drift check | stored legacy value | no refresh | refresh warning, reinstall | `install.test.ts` with the real resolver forced to `darwin` |
| Gateway install drift check | stored `/opt/corporate-ca.pem` | n/a | not flagged | `install.test.ts` |
| Node TLS under each env (stand-in root, Linux host) | peer cert signed by a root only present in the extra bundle | trusted, 1 HTTP request reached the server | `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE`, 0 HTTP requests reached the server | trace below |

Generated service environments (real functions, `scripts/tsx`):

```
BEFORE (base)                                          AFTER (branch)
inherited=(unset)         gateway: EXTRA=/etc/ssl/cert.pem SYSTEM_CA=1     EXTRA=(unset)            SYSTEM_CA=1
inherited=(unset)         node:    EXTRA=/etc/ssl/cert.pem SYSTEM_CA=1     EXTRA=(unset)            SYSTEM_CA=1
inherited=/etc/ssl/cert.pem gateway: EXTRA=/etc/ssl/cert.pem SYSTEM_CA=1   EXTRA=(unset)            SYSTEM_CA=1
inherited=/etc/ssl/cert.pem node:    EXTRA=/etc/ssl/cert.pem SYSTEM_CA=1   EXTRA=(unset)            SYSTEM_CA=1
inherited=/opt/corporate-ca.pem gateway: EXTRA=/opt/corporate-ca.pem       EXTRA=/opt/corporate-ca.pem
inherited=/opt/corporate-ca.pem node:    EXTRA=/opt/corporate-ca.pem       EXTRA=/opt/corporate-ca.pem
```

Handshake trace. A local HTTPS server presents a leaf signed by a throwaway root that stands in for a distrusted root. A child Node runs under each env; the server counts requests that reach its handler:

```
BEFORE env (base): NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=<stale bundle>
    client: TRUSTED status 200
    HTTP requests that reached the application: 1
AFTER env (branch): NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS unset
    client: rejected UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE
    server saw TLS handshake failure: ECONNRESET
    HTTP requests that reached the application: 0
```

The original trace is Linux source-level evidence with a synthetic root. It does not establish macOS launchd behavior or rejection of the incident chains. The native qualification described below is required to close the launchd/install/upgrade gap; results will be recorded against the actual tested head.

## Boundary decisions requested

No additional product decision is requested. The exact legacy-path compatibility change is described under User Impact. Current CODEOWNERS patterns do not match these source/proof paths; this material security repair is proceeding under verified active organization-admin direction. Enforced GitHub reviews and gates remain required.

## Testing

- New and changed: `node-startup-env.test.ts` (legacy value dropped under both `includeDarwinDefaults` modes), `service-env.test.ts` (gateway and node service env, fresh and legacy-inherited), `install.test.ts` (legacy value triggers refresh and an operator-chosen path does not, both through the real resolver forced to `darwin`).
- Red on base: the new and changed expectations fail on the unpatched code; green on this branch (32/32 in `install.test.ts`).
- Existing `entry.respawn.test.ts` (2 cases) and `daemon-install-helpers.test.ts` (1 case) fail on this Linux host identically with and without this branch, and are unrelated to the diff.
- `scripts/check-changed.mjs`: typecheck core and core tests, format, changed-file lint and import cycles pass. The max-lines suppression ratchet, tsgo graph boundary, and dead export scan fail on files this diff does not touch.


## Native service qualification

The PR includes a secretless ephemeral `xcode-27` hosted lane for this PR only. It builds the exact source package, verifies the released `2026.10.7` predecessor archive, and exercises three flows through real generated launchd services: fresh default installation, upgrade of a legacy-default service, and upgrade retaining an explicit custom CA. Each flow exercises actual Gateway provider HTTPS, an OS-trusted positive control, and rejection of a synthetic legacy-bundle-only peer before any parsed HTTP request. Upgrade checks also require retained settings, workspace data, and usable predecessor conversation content after update/restart. The selected listening process, runtime binary hash, and all installed distribution files/root launchers are identified against the built candidate. This is a synthetic trust-source proof, not deployed-fleet or incident-chain qualification.

Local preparation on isolated Linux arm64: frozen install and `pnpm check:workflows` passed; nine required workflow guard files / 1,012 tests passed in two shards. Native execution and final-head CI are pending; no native passing claim is made by preparation. Independent reviews cover the full change and the subsequent installed-distribution identity repair with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

prs.title: fix(ui): let expired OAuth profiles reconnect
prs.body:
Closes #148323.

Supersedes #148325. **Still Draft:** conflict repair, public-code review and synthetic browser validation are complete; real expired-xAI authorization and credential persistence have not been exercised.

## What Problem This Solves

An expired OpenClaw-managed OAuth account in Models has no profile-level action to restart its provider's advertised authorization flow.

## User Impact

Reconnect opens the existing Gateway-owned OAuth/device-code wizard for an eligible expired account, then refreshes its status after completion. It does not change the active model. The recorded test demonstrates that UI path with fictional data, not compatibility with the real xAI service.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing login runner already owns authorization, mutation admission, cancellation and stale-result handling. This change reuses that owner instead of adding a credential store or authentication RPC.

Reconnect requires an expired OAuth profile, a positive Gateway `reconnectSupported` ownership capability, exactly one advertised OAuth/device-code route, and existing write/busy admission. Config display provenance and logout eligibility are not ownership authority. External or inherited profiles, missing local-ownership metadata and ambiguous routes fail closed; the Gateway excludes external IDs even if they overlap the local set. Existing logout behavior is unchanged.

### Conflict repair — 2026-10-25

Conflict-repair head: `ac5c975754f91d342e1cbe6de6557954c49f01c6`.
Merged actual upstream main `9629838ec1aab5d0917828453335473bfa385847` into prior published head `a6519de67ed551eec6b3c16553f9d55043dd805a`, preserving both parents and the original PR.

Resolved the two conflicts in the login controller and its browser suite. Reconnect now lives in current main's inline `providerActions` getter; removed single-use helper wrappers were not restored. The current model-access scenarios and their exact request/no-activation assertions are retained. The contribution remains 11 files (+518/-44) against that main commit; this is not a new feature expansion.

## Evidence

### Latest review follow-up — 2026-10-25

Current PR head: `1630a2cd749e6bf826b69f530d82956f03348dc0`.

Addressed the latest [ClawSweeper test-value feedback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150688#issuecomment-5710314969) with a test-only change (+2/-15, one file): remove seven duplicate missing-ownership variants from the component-level fixture loop. The registered-page tests still cover missing capability for external/config/inherited/saved profiles and the inherited/removable overlap. The retained non-expired and non-OAuth controls now have `reconnectSupported: true`, so each exercises its intended status/type guard rather than passing because ownership is absent. Write-permission, busy-state, credential-owner routing and unavailable/ambiguous-route checks are retained.

- **27/27 focused UI tests pass** across the changed component test and registered-page reconnect suite (Vitest 4.66s; wrapper wall time 8.08s). No hosted CI time is claimed for this new head.
- Targeted UI/E2E typecheck, typed lint of the changed test, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Fresh isolated independent **P0–P2 review of this test-only delta is scoped-clean**, with complete usage reporting. It assessed the full public component and overlapping page tests; it did not execute project code.
- No production code, Gateway behavior, auth flow or browser scenario changed. The 9/9 browser captures and prior production-contract evidence below are reused unchanged-input evidence from `ac5c975754`, not newly executed end-to-end tests on this test-only head.

The latest hosted ClawSweeper review of `ac5c975754` found no actionable correctness defects, but still requires **maintainer product acceptance** of the added account-row action and **authorized real-Gateway expired-xAI recovery through persistence/readback**. Those requirements are not claimed resolved. Hosted Codex's separate attempt failed with an unknown service error, not a code verdict; the independent local workflow review above is a separate result. Keep Draft and maintainer edits disabled; no real account authorization is performed.

### Retained conflict-repair validation

The following conflict-repair results were recorded at `ac5c975754f91d342e1cbe6de6557954c49f01c6`, using merged candidate tree `c3e55272164f394fd183f75aa5bc2b2ade713867` on task-only Node 24.22.1 with current main's frozen dependency lock, including Solid rc.18. The frozen-lock install passed; no dependency or lockfile change was authored.

- The existing Gateway auth-status/ordering/logout test file and **55 tests across five relevant UI files passed** in two Vitest shards (57.89s). They cover positive local/config-local ownership and fail-closed external, inherited, overlapping and missing-metadata cases, alongside existing login, completion and refresh behavior.
- **Recorded production-UI Chromium E2E: 9/9 passed** (Vitest 240.45s; test file 136.196s; production UI build 91s). This includes Expired → Reconnect → fictional device-code wizard → completion → Close → expand → restored-account readback, plus browser-callback and all three existing model-access/default-preservation cases. Auth routing is exact; no model activation or config patch is introduced.
- The first recorded attempt was **6 passed / 3 failed**, not hidden or counted as a passing run. All three failures were screenshot-surface checks against the non-rendering `openclaw-modal-dialog` host, not failed authorization/default assertions. The captures now target its visible inner `dialog`; all original behavior assertions remain. The complete 9-case suite then passed.
- Targeted Gateway/UI/E2E types, typed lint of all 11 contribution files, formatting, diff checks, English i18n verification and the max-lines/environment-count ratchet pass. One extra typecheck attempt encountered an active dist-artifact lock from the concurrent lint owner; it was rerun successfully after that owner finished, without deleting the lock or bypassing ownership.
- Fresh isolated Codex **P0–P2 independent review: scoped-clean**, two completed passes with complete usage reporting. It received the public candidate plus full public Gateway facts/config/runtime-ownership and login-wizard contracts. This static review did not execute the tests or validate real-provider credential replacement.
- Contribution diff SHA-256 against the merged main: `4716593e1944c7783bddcfcad1d88c4329405dcaf4651babc072aab0859b95a4`.
- GitHub confirmed conflict-repair head `ac5c975754` is mergeable. Current-head hosted CI/review results are separate; Draft-skipped tests are not passing CI proof.

### Conflict-repair browser captures — production unchanged

Real Chromium captures from the production UI. Emails, profiles, URLs and the displayed XAI-TEST code are fictional. These demonstrate the UI flow, not a real provider login.

**Expired account offers Reconnect:**

![Merged candidate: expired fictional xAI account with Reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/217ab66a-8292-4b7f-8d9d-48d2097ff50e)

**Existing wizard receives the advertised device-code route:**

![Merged candidate: fictional XAI-TEST device-code wizard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d524ca2b-686d-4394-bc64-22b7db38cd10)

**Completion, Close, expand and status readback:**

![Merged candidate: restored fictional xAI account](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7ee4ffa-7196-42f3-beaa-8f2ab6029bba)

### Retained earlier baseline and feedback context

The genuine **before** image below is from unmodified main `e39c150d7b9054a19d57f0d7b0613a4493978ceb` on 2026-10-23, not the newly merged 9629838ec1 baseline and not DOM editing. It shows the same fictional expired-account scenario without Reconnect. The earlier baseline 1/1 test, 117 focused tests and earlier 9/9 browser run belong to the Oct23 candidate, not additional unique tests for today's head.

![Historical before: unmodified Oct23 main without Reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9ae0231-7a21-4077-973a-0e0d7bff79ff)

The Oct23 ClawSweeper review had no actionable code findings, but explicitly required real-Gateway/expired-xAI recovery, persistence and readback proof. That gap remains. Its old `auto-response` failure was a Barnacle label-sync GET returning GitHub HTTP502 ([old job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39923930164/job/120315587025)); that is historical evidence, not a classification of any new-head failure.

## Safety Boundary and Remaining Proof

No real account authorization, paid model calls, personal notes, private Orca source, personal configuration, genuine logs, tokens or secrets were used or sent for review. Public GitHub noreply attribution is retained; maintainer edits remain disabled. No workflow permissions or secrets access were expanded.

**Still unverified:** completion against the real xAI service using an actually expired credential, credential persistence and real-provider status readback. That live operation has not been authorized. Keep this PR Draft; do not treat synthetic screenshots, local tests or static review as that missing proof.

prs.title: fix(agents): finish turns after tool-result recovery
prs.body:
Related: #130930, #169583

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes turn finalization losing the recovered turn after tool-result truncation while the transcript projection is rebuilding.

## User Impact

Recovered conversations retain the context engine's completed turn. Cancelling the run still stops finalization. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery can remove the manager's append receipt before its replacement projection is ready. The finalizer now joins the existing projection owner only when it must reconstruct the terminal anchor. It passes the actual run's abort signal through the wait and read, and checks cancellation before recording completion. The committed-anchor fast path and its existing ownership check are preserved.

Thanks to @MSNexploder for the fix and recovery/cancellation proof. Production is +14/-1 (net +13), tests +196. The added production lines carry cancellation and join the existing owner; no new state, reader policy, or abstraction is introduced. The regression uses the real worker because a mocked anchor would miss the failure.

## Evidence

- Local base `a31e54a90d6a5`: both recovery regression cases fail with expected `waiting`, received `finished`; finalization returns without a candidate. Duration 255.36 s, dominated by cold worker compilation and transforms.
- Candidate regression and affected lifecycle/cursor tests: 27 passed across three files (23 attempt-lifecycle cases and four projection/cursor cases), repeated successfully after merging main `6c33f5ff5ee0` into head `dc5b28f7791e`. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/harness/context-engine-recovery.projection.test.ts src/agents/harness/context-engine-transcript-cursor.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-phase-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Local tests used the four merged candidate files copied verbatim into the refreshed lane-owned installation. Other source differences from the merge base were unrelated test cleanup; exact-head PR CI covers the full integrated checkout.
- Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt and diff check passed. Isolated Codex autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean, with no actionable findings.
- Contributor built exact parent `b92e5655b908` and original head `a88842586500` and drove synthetic sessions through a local Gateway using `chat.send` and `chat.abort`: base records zero recovery candidates; head records one candidate and one final reply; cancellation records no candidate or late reply. Follow-up messages work and the synthetic precheck error is removed. This is retained contributor evidence, not a new local live run.
- No external model/channel round trip was repeated locally; the real-worker regression and retained deterministic Gateway comparison exercise this recovery boundary without credentials or a new harness.

prs.title: fix: keep resumed CLI sessions aware of conversation updates
prs.body:
Fixes #182649
Fixes #182711

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the next typed CLI-backed turn misses scheduled results and Talk corrections already visible in the same conversation, so it can act on stale context, including the wrong email draft reported in #182711.

## User Impact

Claude CLI and Gemini CLI receive newly committed conversation updates when the same native session resumes. The handoff is bounded to the newest eight user/assistant records, with each string capped at 2,000 characters. Stored transcript content and the stable system prompt stay unchanged. Hidden consult instructions, delivery bookkeeping, and already accepted steering are excluded.

Fresh-session seeding and older-history recovery retain their account-boundary rules. There is no new configuration or SQLite schema migration. Failed or interrupted turns and failed binding settlement may repeat quoted updates on retry; successful settlement consumes the handoff. Existing bindings without an input checkpoint use their last ordinary backend reply until a checkpoint is recorded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing CLI history owner now shares its bounded completion renderer across backends. A checkpoint on the native binding records the input snapshot and the turn's own transcript identities, so results arriving during a CLI turn remain available afterward. Execution attaches the handoff only to the actual matching resume; fresh recovery retries and forks do not inherit it. The existing Talk ancestry repair from #178259 is already present and its owner regressions pass, so this PR does not duplicate that producer fix.

**Maintainer decision:** authorize a narrow same-conversation handoff only for resumed native CLI sessions, including opaque native logins. The history boundary prevents saved history from seeding a session that may belong to another account; a resumed native session already holds this conversation, so handing it the conversation's own newly committed rows crosses no account boundary the resume itself does not. The concrete harm is the stale-draft email action in #182711. Fresh-session and older-history recovery keep the contiguous, account-owned, fail-closed rules from #140294 and #164796.

## Evidence

- Exact-head [CI run 40150649504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40150649504) completed on `98bb02122034fe78079a54682a84ded76c229613`: **all test jobs passed**, including all PostgreSQL conformance shards. The run and `openclaw/ci-gate` are **failed solely by the two inherited typecheck failures below** (46 successful jobs, 25 skipped, two failed checks plus their aggregate gate). No PR-caused failure, retry, or timeout exception was used. Prior head `ffeb644bfe07205be7e96e390b9f4e79f3bdf6f8` passed [CI run 40147422706](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40147422706); that remains prior-head evidence only.

- CI has two verified **inherited typecheck failures**: [check-prod-types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40150649504/job/121041831640) and [check-test-types-core-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40150649504/job/121041831623). Both emit the identical TS2739 at `src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog.test-helpers.ts:122` (`{}` lacks `minProtocol`, `maxProtocol`, and `client`) as latest scheduled [main run 40149301577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149301577) at `f0dcb354e45b06d60df466de136f85cd1b7b148e`: [main production job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149301577/job/121037449659), [main test-types job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149301577/job/121037449682). The failing source blob is unchanged from that main. The automatic classifier compared against an older completed passing main run; direct comparison against the latest scheduled run establishes the matching failure. No broad local reruns or CI retries were used.

- Source rechecked on fresh main `e2f634809c8ff06dfd8e9e6c0461d551cfd9196f`: the same omission remains. Original red-on-main reproduction at `f310725180103600d849d6ce94ff0bba7fc40da5`: [`session-history.ts:495`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f310725180103600d849d6ce94ff0bba7fc40da5/src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.ts#L495) classified only Claude CLI replies, omitting automation and embedded Talk results, and detached appends left account-owned recovery coverage behind. The final regressions fail on main for both backends because actual CLI input contains only the typed request. The actual-dispatch controls also fail on main for missing the same-session handoff.
- The five final regressions failed on main: cron/Talk handoff and dispatch controls for both backends, plus preserved-binding cursor settlement before the next queued command. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-runner/history-boundary.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.native-history-owner.test.ts src/agents/command/attempt-execution.cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'hands cron|catch-up out|preserved-same-native'` (exit 1, intended assertions).
- After integrating #172916, all **319 tests across 12 files passed locally**: `execute.native-history-owner`, all four `session-history*` files, `prompt-context`, `cli-run-settlement`, `history-boundary`, `cli-session`, `cli-session-store`, `attempt-execution.cli`, and `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <explicit files> --maxWorkers=1`. Runner group durations: 61.75s, 340.56s, 62.25s, and 372.82s on the cold local checkout. No failed tests or retries.
- [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183059#issuecomment-6391664916) completed on exact head `98bb02122034fe78079a54682a84ded76c229613`: **Findings: None**, **Before merge: None**. The conflict-repair request is resolved. [Re-review workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/40151196589). The existing [maintainer proof scope](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183059#issuecomment-6391692509) remains recorded.
- Isolated branch-mode Codex autoreview through P2: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings on the merged candidate. Fresh main `e2f634809c8ff06dfd8e9e6c0461d551cfd9196f` was merged before normal push, with no rebase or force-push; the resulting PR diff is byte-for-byte identical to the reviewed patch.
- Integration semantic checks: auth-profile/auth-epoch reseeds explicitly withhold catch-up and raw history; fresh, foreign, and forked attempts receive no same-session catch-up. The existing real-transcript cron/Talk regression now runs in native-only mode for both backends and proves concurrent results survive the input cursor and are consumed once. The merge needed no additional production change; integration-only test delta is +15/−5.
- Changed-file core oxlint and oxfmt passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Targeted test-project typechecks passed with `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p <project> --incremental` for `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands.json`.
- Proof uses real transcript commits, history-boundary planning, binding persistence, and CLI execution with synthetic subprocess I/O. Live Gateway/channel/provider e2e was skipped per maintainer policy; PR CI is the broad gate.

The simplification pass removed the Claude-only completion composition and retained one shared renderer. The line-cap guard required moving existing cache-boundary composition and settlement fixtures to their existing sibling owners; its final check passed. Delta against main: production +232/−93 (net +139), tests +392/−54, docs +26/−20. The positive production delta records the pre-turn input boundary, retains concurrent appends, and acknowledges successful preserved turns under the existing binding owner; no separate queue or state store was added.

prs.title: fix(models): escape terminal controls in auth profile listings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes auth-profile listings that emit terminal controls embedded in profile labels, model names, provider metadata, or the displayed auth-store path.

## User Impact

Human-readable listings preserve printable Unicode and visibly escape line breaks and tabs. Stored profile identities and `--json` field values remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single command-local output function applies the existing canonical `sanitizeTerminalText` after the JSON branch returns. This keeps the display policy in one place and removes repeated per-field sanitization from the submitted patch.

Thanks @Alix-007 for the fix, regression, and original real-CLI proof.

## Evidence

- The new command-level regression fails on unchanged main code: raw ANSI/newline in the auth-store path (1 failed, 17 skipped; 246.67s wall time).
- With the fix, all 18 tests in `src/commands/models/auth-list.test.ts` pass, including after integrating current main (185.46s command wall time on the integrated head; 325.28s initial run, mostly compiled fixture preparation). The regression also checks profile/model escaping, Unicode, raw JSON, and unchanged stored identity.
- Targeted typed oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.
- Against main: production +8/−6 (net +2), tests +20/−0, docs +2/−0. The remaining production growth is one canonical import and one output-boundary function.
- A fresh standalone CLI live replay was not repeated on this source-only, heavily loaded Mac. Inspected prior contributor proof used the built Linux CLI to save a synthetic local profile and run `models auth list`/`--json`: controls changed from 1 to 0; canonical profile readback and configuration bytes stayed unchanged. No provider calls were made. That evidence predates the current integration; it is not an exact-head live claim.

prs.title: fix: make Daybreak independent of retiring model aliases
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Daybreak workflows rely on Blue/Red aliases retiring October 28, 2026, and must retain automatic recovery through authorized Access configuration without changing the selected model or processing speed.

## User Impact

The chat menu uses segmented Access choices matching Speed and shows **Access above Effort above Speed**, but only when the active account/model/runtime explicitly advertises a Daybreak program. Unavailable options are absent; unknown or empty capabilities hide Access entirely. There are no requested/reported status or explanatory paragraphs below Access. **Use model default** clears the session override; Standard is an explicit selection. If account capabilities no longer expose Access, **Clear saved Access** remains available in the model menu. Clearing is explicit; unavailable program choices and explanatory Access paragraphs remain absent.

The advisory Doctor check reports configured retiring aliases without rewriting models or account pins. **Automatic cyber recovery retries the same model once with authorized Blue Access**, without changing the saved session selection. Exact model pins and an empty model-fallback list do not disable this configuration retry. Ordinary configured cross-model fallbacks remain separate. Review saved session overrides and scheduled jobs separately before retirement.

## Root Cause

Only the aliases retire. A replay-safe, structured cyber refusal in Standard/default mode can retry the same provider/model/runtime/account with Blue Access. Existing Blue/Red requests are not retried or downgraded, and `cyberFailover.mode=off` remains authoritative. Current account/credential/route grants are required before submission; there is no entitlement inferred from a model name, auth type, or another account. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to remove retired `cyberFailover.model` fields through the existing core/plugin migration owners; explicit mode/cooloff settings and ordinary primary/fallback model configuration are preserved. Program selection (`standard`, `daybreak_blue`, `daybreak_red`) remains independent of Fast/Ultrafast. Empty model configuration (`accessPrograms: {}`) leaves selection unspecified; null is invalid.

Authenticated ChatGPT model discovery supplies caller-specific program metadata. The Gateway projects it as optional `availableAccessPrograms.cyber` on each account/model/runtime choice, preserving unknown versus explicitly empty results. The existing account/catalog lifecycle owns invalidation; no new cache or state store is introduced. Saved session overrides are checked again at execution, and native Codex verifies the same client/account model catalog before its turn starts.

This OpenClaw integration supports the native Codex turn-scoped parameter with ChatGPT authentication and rejects explicit programs with native API-key authentication before submission. This is the integration’s current scope, not an upstream limitation: pinned Codex 0.162.1 rejects API-key programs when its separate feature is disabled and forwards them when enabled. **Platform API-key discovery now reads explicit caller-specific program metadata from the official Codex models endpoint, using the same selected key.** Public `/v1/models` remains the model-inventory authority; metadata cannot add an unlisted model. No model-name, plan, or approval-label inference and no billable Responses probe is used. Custom routes and header overrides cannot inherit official grants. The existing selected-account refresh now reaches the HTTP cache and publishes changed outcomes to open UI consumers. Native Codex API-key execution remains unsupported by this integration; official Platform and ChatGPT Responses endpoints remain separate. The 60-second HTTP-cache lifetime is not a polling timer or instantaneous revocation guarantee. Selected profile/key and route isolate observations; project/organization request-header overrides are ineligible for default-route grants. Missing, empty or failed metadata hides Access while ordinary inventory remains usable.

References: [Daybreak](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/daybreak), [Fast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode), [Ultrafast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode).

## Verification

### Current candidate and CI repair

Candidate **a38aceb6bd4046e3d772f8210c2a91042df959e0** retains published ancestry and integrates main **8f807addc796520a08729ea309d9dacf77a08430** to resolve a confirmed GitHub merge conflict. The sole manual conflict resolution unions the type/settings imports in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-session.ts`, preserving both explicit Access selection and upstream model-switch confirmation.

- **Current conflict-resolution proof:** chat-model-runtime, chat-send-settings, chat-settings-reconciliation, and new-session/model-control: **4 files, 47 tests passed**. The resolved file passes formatting; the complete staged diff passed `git diff --check`.
- **Stale Access is not bad authentication:** retained `reason: "format"` classification prevents shared credential-health writes and profile advancement. Real guard-to-prompt-failure regression failed before repair and passed **28/28** afterward.
- **UI readiness:** retained actual lazy-slider readiness wait. A delayed import reproduced the old failure; prior candidate UI suite passed **30/30**.
- **Foreign SQLite writer:** retained bounded **5,000 ms** timeout on the foreign test connection. The controlled lock-holder reproduced the old failure; prior candidate worker-profile suite passed **17/17**.
- **Frozen prior head 496303a:** Codex **15/15** and catalog **15/15** passed. An earlier combined run was invalidated by a concurrent local merge exposing temporary conflict markers; it is not product-failure evidence. The final frozen rerun cleared that uncertainty.
- Prior same-base interactive setup passed **8/8** across SQLite and PostgreSQL. No inherited-failure waiver is being used.
- Independent implementation repair review completed all six chunks. Its sole finding cited stale INDEX bytes; the accepted working-tree fix was subsequently committed. No clean-verdict claim or verdict-shopping rerun.
- **Exact-head core replays:** `a38aceb6bd4046e3d772f8210c2a91042df959e0`, tree `70c17803fb9966f902071b8402c5aac5c5db2c45`: Gateway catalog/worker-profile **32/32**, Access prompt-failure **28/28**, and Codex media understanding **15/15** passed. The isolated checkout was clean before the run and HEAD was unchanged afterward; overall exit 0. Exact-head installed-package upgrade proof passed as detailed below; hosted CI and current-head ClawSweeper acceptance remain pending. Prior-head receipts are historical supporting evidence, not final-head acceptance.

### Real behavior proof

The credential-health regression exercises the real Access guard through prompt-failure handling and checks that no shared profile-health write or profile advancement occurs. UI and SQLite fixes retain the original assertions; they wait for actual readiness or a bounded transient lock rather than weakening expectations. Existing screenshots and live UI proof below retain their captured SHA.

### What was not tested

No real cyber refusal or nonempty cooldown-store migration has been exercised by the installed-package harness. Synthetic package/state checks do not prove provider entitlement or billable model inference. Final package proof passed; no green-CI or satisfied-review claim is made yet.

### Upgrade proof: stable 2026.10.7 to exact candidate a38aceb

A real npm install of stable `OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (157d8c2)` was upgraded to a package built from **a38aceb6bd4046e3d772f8210c2a91042df959e0**, using isolated synthetic state, an empty environment and a loopback Gateway. The repeatable harness uses `$ART` for the throwaway directory.

1. Install stable core and `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.7`. Using the stable Gateway, create two sessions with two history messages each; one has an explicit account pin, high thinking and Fast enabled. Snapshot configuration, credentials, session rows and transcript hashes.
2. Build the clean candidate, run `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --skip-build --allow-unreleased-changelog`, and pack the candidate Codex plugin. Core tarball integrity passed. Core SHA-256: `2f2e6ca522fc116d4a226fd6303eac36af1664b6dc0b718b7b1254e1a097de1f`. Codex SHA-256: `dc026a91e09fb8352f79976c017ad834f68aa9b0edbafa3a6f4ba3209a5ae4dd`. Packaged `build-info.json` identifies the exact candidate commit.
3. Run the installed updater: `openclaw update --tag file:$ART/pack/openclaw-2026.10.7.tgz --no-restart --yes`. **Exit 0**; candidate snapshot, Doctor, config, plugins, recovery and Gateway-startup checks passed. Doctor lint emitted advisory warnings. Installed CLI reports **OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (a38aceb)**.
4. Install the packaged Codex plugin with `--force --accept-capabilities`, then run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`. **Both exit 0**.
5. Start the installed candidate Gateway on the upgraded state, not the source checkout. It loaded 15 plugins including Codex. Query `sessions.list` and `chat.history`, then shut down cleanly. **Gateway exit 0**, port freed.

prs.title: perf(gateway): avoid cloning WebSocket metric histograms
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Loaded Gateways allocate tens of kilobytes to copy each nine-field WebSocket diagnostic histogram. The numeric bucket keys cause V8's structured clone to expand sparse element storage, even though the data is already owned by the recorder.

## User Impact

Reduces diagnostic allocation and CPU under WebSocket traffic. Frame counts, raw and wire byte totals, cumulative buckets, attribution, consumer gating, and flush timing remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Freeze the completed histogram and retain an owned, frozen attribution snapshot in each existing counter. The diagnostic dispatcher can then reuse immutable nested data instead of cloning it. This removes two per-flush attribution assignments and adds six net production lines; the growth supplies the queued-snapshot immutability contract. No new cache, batching owner, or broadcast path is introduced.

The earlier flush optimization in #181323 is already an ancestor of the profiled build. This measures and removes its residual cost after #182677 rather than claiming it was already fixed.

## Evidence

Acceptance was declared before candidate runs: preserve exact exported metric values, demonstrate an allocation or CPU reduction, and check non-adverse GC/latency/memory using sample-count and absolute-delta rules. Allocation sampling is separate from untraced GC/latency measurement.

Five alternating owner pairs, 2,000 batches × 64 frames per side:

| Metric | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Mean paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sampled owner allocation, including collected objects | 543.47 MB | 72.77 MB | -86.61% |
| CPU | 448.91 ms | 287.46 ms | -35.35% |
| Total GC | 8.65 ms | 2.13 ms | -73.03% |

Every run retained exact frame, raw-byte, wire-byte and cumulative-histogram totals. These owner measurements are not a substitute for the built-Gateway stress proof below.

Built-Gateway comparison: baseline `f947c5ea66c4f19a20e18320e95fa56499e2a09b` versus that same source with this production patch. The patch-identical publication rebase is covered by PR CI. These are serial runs on a shared 32-core macOS host; whole-Gateway differences are workload context, not an isolated causal speedup claim. The committed `ws-counter-stress.ts` header documents fixture and run commands. Each side uses independently seeded 10,000-session state, 6,000 settled runs, 32 synthetic git worktrees, 40 plugin fixtures, 64 WebSocket clients, 32 concurrent mock-provider sessions performing file reads and grep, and sidebar/list/search churn. Each untraced window is at least 600 seconds, followed by a separate 60-second allocation window.

| Built-Gateway metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Untraced duration | 615.51 s | 613.70 s |
| Verified tool turns | 878 | 1,084 |
| Event frames | 823,448 | 1,009,392 |
| Main-thread CPU | 59.81% | 65.63% |
| Main-thread CPU / completed turn | 419.30 ms | 371.58 ms |
| GC | 1.930 s/min | 2.245 s/min |
| GC / completed turn | 22.55 ms | 21.19 ms |
| Event-loop p95 / p99 | 41.09 / 128.65 ms (30,382 samples) | 34.28 / 93.45 ms (34,044 samples) |
| sessions.list p95 / p99 | 1,761.95 / 2,676.75 ms (7,684 calls) | 1,313.40 / 1,995.62 ms (7,681 calls) |
| GC collections / total / max | 3,496 / 19.799 s / 349.61 ms | 4,129 / 22.966 s / 958.27 ms |
| Minor GC collections / total / max | 3,474 / 17.793 s / 178.09 ms | 4,107 / 19.792 s / 143.56 ms |
| Major GC collections / total / max | 11 / 1.969 s / 349.61 ms | 11 / 3.138 s / 958.27 ms |
| Incremental GC collections / total / max | 11 / 0.0377 s / 5.07 ms | 11 / 0.0362 s / 4.89 ms |
| End RSS / used heap / heap capacity | 4.754 / 1.086 / 2.170 GB | 4.548 / 1.475 / 1.737 GB |
| Separate sampled-allocation duration / turns | 76.32 s / 82 | 74.75 s / 106 |
| Total sampled allocation | 124.42 MB/s | 159.58 MB/s |
| Recorder-owned sampled allocation | 2.328 MB/s | 0.373 MB/s |
| Recorder-owned allocation / event frame | 2,279.48 B | 280.59 B |

The recorder's allocation falls 84.0% per second and 87.7% per frame in the real Gateway. Whole-process rates reflect 23.5% more completed turns; the CPU and GC costs per turn decrease. The allocation window likewise completes more turns, so its raw total allocation rate is higher. Memory snapshots are natural-GC endpoints, not retained-heap measurements. Major-pause percentiles have only 11 samples per side and are context only.

**Pending performance safeguard:** candidate maximum GC pause is above twice the baseline maximum. Four identical-code workload controls are being collected before deciding whether this is a real regression or shared-host variance. Do not merge until this is resolved.

Focused tests: 42 passed across `ws-connection.test.ts`, `ws-connection.serialized-json.test.ts`, `server-broadcast.metrics.test.ts`, and `service.gateway-ws.test.ts`. File-scoped formatting and lint, `pnpm tsgo:core`, export-collision checks, and 22 eager-import/PR-wrapper closure tests passed. Baseline used `pnpm build`; candidate used `pnpm build:runtime`. No Testbox lease was used; broad validation is delegated to PR CI.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean, no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings. The configured autoreview route refused provider mismatch; no operator configuration was changed.
