prs.title: fix(agents): keep agent.run drain deadline monotonic across clock skew
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: waiting for descendant agent runs can exceed or cut short its drain budget when the host wall clock changes during the wait.

## User Impact

The shared drain owner consumes its configured wait budget using elapsed time, while caller-supplied deadlines retain their epoch meaning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Convert the normalized epoch deadline once at entry, then use `performance.now()` throughout the drain loop. Existing invalid/overflow deadline normalization and run-owned execution budgets remain intact. The caller's separate outer follow-up loop is outside this fix (related work: #182144).

Thanks to @SunnyShu0925 for the fix and regression.

## Evidence


- Main `a2fbd0305d8893642f9f8feeef77cb4f94215341`: the regression failed with a 95,000 ms request after a 90-second rewind against a 5,000 ms limit. Fixed: 70/70 tests passed across the owner, async-observation, and both cron follow-up files.
- Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-ct-monoA pnpm test src/agents/run-wait.test.ts src/agents/run-wait.async-observation.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Red selected the owner file with `-t 'wall clock rewinds'`. The green cron shard took 185.59 seconds including worker preparation; agents took 30.29 seconds. The new regression uses fake time.
- Independent diff review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. The simplification pass retained the one necessary epoch conversion: production +5/-4 (net +1), tests +29. No shared generic monotonic-deadline helper exists, so this uses the same `performance.now()` primitive as the other timeout repairs.
- No new real-Gateway run was independently live-tested here; reproducing the contributor's standalone Gateway harness would exceed this revision's best-effort proof scope. Its original real-transport comparison is preserved below.

### Contributor-supplied Gateway comparison

The original contributor supplied the following real-Gateway comparison at `239b0157bd6cf7398bbefdd2d52fcce6554bcc60`. These traces were inspected, not independently rerun during this revision. They exercise the shared drain owner through its default Gateway client and real WebSocket `agent.wait` responses, using synthetic pending descendants and controlled clock rewinds.

**Raw terminal output (verbatim, head `239b0157bd6c`)**:

```console
$ real-gateway-elapsed-proof.mts postfix   # this PR
3000/-60000: agent.wait [2999] status=timeout | real wall elapsed 3069ms
5000/-90000: agent.wait [4999] status=timeout | real wall elapsed 5034ms
8000/-120000: agent.wait [7999] status=timeout | real wall elapsed 8032ms
PASS: drain deadline expired at the budget across all matrix inputs

$ real-gateway-elapsed-proof.mts prefix    # origin/main
3000/-60000: agent.wait [63000] status=timeout | real wall elapsed 63061ms
5000/-90000: agent.wait [95000] status=timeout | real wall elapsed 95057ms
8000/-120000: agent.wait [128000] status=timeout | real wall elapsed 128049ms
BUG REPRODUCED: drain deadline inflated by each rollback
```

**Before/after matrix — real elapsed time until the drain deadline expires** (genuinely-pending run, real WS `agent.wait` round-trip returning `status=timeout`):

| budget / rewind | origin/main (`Date.now()`) | this PR (`performance.now()`) |
|---|---|---|
| 3,000ms / −60s | **63,061 ms** (inflated ~63s) | **3,069 ms** (bounded) |
| 5,000ms / −90s | **95,057 ms** (inflated ~95s) | **5,034 ms** (bounded) |
| 8,000ms / −120s | **128,049 ms** (inflated ~128s) | **8,032 ms** (bounded) |

In every matrix cell the unpatched drain **stays blocked for budget+rewind seconds of real time** after a wall-clock rollback, while the patched drain **expires at the budget**. This is the shipped-Gateway elapsed-time path with real request/response round-trips (the previous transport-stub evidence exercised neither).

Closes #183096

## What Problem This Solves

The PostgreSQL arm of `scripts/bench-memory-search.mjs` omits `postgresVectorSearchVersion: 2`, so the documented production benchmark measures the legacy exact vector path instead of the binary-sketch prefilter enabled by current production agent stores.

## User Impact

The PostgreSQL benchmark now exercises the same versioned vector-search path as production, so reported latency reflects the current implementation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The engine only admits the binary candidate prefilter for schema version 2. The benchmark schema now declares that version, matching `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-engine.ts` and the capability gate in `src/infra/database-engine/postgres-vector.ts`.

## Evidence

- `node --check scripts/bench-memory-search.mjs` passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- The change is limited to the PostgreSQL benchmark schema; SQLite behavior and fixture data are unchanged.
- The issue's paired PostgreSQL runs measured 159.9–182.4 ms p50 on the shipped exact path versus 9.7–19.4 ms with this schema capability enabled.
- Full benchmark execution requires a disposable PostgreSQL/pgvector database (`PGMEMSEARCH_CONNECTION`), which is not configured in this checkout.

prs.title: refactor: remove redundant pairing and plugin serialization
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pairing and plugin persistence wrap already serialized owner operations in additional queues. Remove eight redundant serialization sites while preserving the existing owners and FIFO boundaries. This is a small final audit batch: the remaining surveyed queues protect multi-step mutation, publication, external effects, or a different key and stay in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

| Removed outer site | Surviving owner and ordering |
| --- | --- |
| Pairing rotate/revoke token; remove device; prune superseded silent devices; remove node role (5) | `executeDevicePairingMutation` synchronously reserves the same global reentrant pairing lock before its first await, then holds it through admission, commit, cleanup, and publication. Facades do no intervening async work. |
| Teams SSO save/remove (2) | Plugin-state `prepareCommandOrder` / `beginPluginStateMutation` synchronously reserve the physical database + plugin + account namespace order before awaiting earlier work. Both forward one mutation and have no post-commit effects. |
| Nostr cursor write-tail chain (1) | `activeFlush` owns one sequential loop. Preserve initial cursor capture, deferred writer invocation, the idle microtask checkpoint, retry/recovery, and rewind coalescing. |

## User Impact

No user-facing behavior change is intended. Pairing command/timestamp capture happens at submission, consistent with the existing unwrapped facades. The broker still checks current authority at admission/commit. Pruning still refuses connected candidates immediately before commit. Teams runtime active/current checks and token-use policy are unchanged. No SQL, schema, identity, SDK surface, cache, retention, or cross-store transaction changes.

Production reduction: **24 net lines** (tests add 65 net lines). Preservation tests cover pairing rotation/revocation FIFO and committed denial, interleaved Teams save/delete/save across account namespaces, and Nostr pending/in-flight rewinds plus persistence during an idle flush. No read or write is removed; no new production seam or test file.

## Acceptance rule (written before measurement)

This cleanup claims less serialization machinery, not fewer SQL statements. Five pairing actions drop a second call into the same reentrant lock wrapper; two Teams mutations drop their outer keyed queue; Nostr drops the stored promise tail and rejection-handled tail updates.

Run frozen SQL harness v3.1.4 once on baseline `e2f634809c8` and once on this candidate, on the same platform. Each invocation uses an isolated synthetic Gateway over WebSocket, ten warmed turns, and the existing full 14-turn/restart workload. Report warm per-turn SQL statements, worker requests and runtime MAIN: median, min/max and p95. Keep cold phases separate. Runtime MAIN must stay zero; no changed owner may issue more SQL or requests. Attribute any shared-family increase; a 20% increase in any cell stops acceptance. Counts only; no latency or CPU improvement claim from a loaded machine. The 36 frozen harness hashes are verified.

## Evidence

Focused owner tests pass on the pinned Bun runtime: pairing 17/17, Teams SSO 5/5, and Nostr cursor 6/6. Two isolated Codex reviews completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Initial CI caught a missing required `scopes` argument in the new pairing test; the follow-up supplies `scopes: []`, and pairing 17/17 passes again. Production is unchanged from both reviews.

Final-head CI [40152617324](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40152617324) and downstream [40153079524](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40153079524) are green. Types, type-aware lint, changed tests, source contracts, security checks, and Madge/import cycles pass. T1 is 170 -> 170, compatibility calls 15 -> 15, and changed-file dialect groups 0 -> 0. The local type-aware wrapper stopped before analysis because its declaration builder rejects the required external virtual-store path; no gate was bypassed. CI did not select Knip, correcting the earlier coverage expectation. Canonical `pnpm deadcode:exports` completed on both exact heads: 75 production, 98 full-tree, and 1,136 script findings on each. Exact finding sets are identical, with zero added or removed and no resolution errors or timeouts. Both exit 1 because of those inherited findings.

Open-PR overlap: #167137 has the same existing conflict in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/validator-registry.ts` on base and candidate (identical content after normalizing the branch label); #183075 at `53da38ad0e42693ffe84bafd4f1239eec71ea794` merges cleanly on both. No added conflict paths or hunks.

### Synthetic warm counts

Frozen harness v3.1.4; all 36 hashes verified. Baseline `e2f634809c8ff06dfd8e9e6c0461d551cfd9196f` and candidate `5da9761604fcfee833b00ea906dc272db8dddfb2` ran on the same Mac with Node 26.12.1. Both full workloads passed: isolated synthetic Gateway over WebSocket, 14 turns including ten warm turns, five-minute connected idle, shutdown and restart. One baseline/candidate pair for this defensive-pattern audit. Counts only; pre-run one-minute loads were 56.12 and 62.87.

| Raw warm-window metric | Baseline median [min–max]; p95 | Candidate median [min–max]; p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SQL statements | 50 [50–76]; 76 | 50.5 [50–75]; 75 |
| Worker requests | 12 [12–19]; 19 | 12 [12–19]; 19 |
| Runtime MAIN | 0 [0–0]; 0 | 0 [0–0]; 0 |

Warm totals: **533 SQL / 130 requests / 0 MAIN -> 535 / 130 / 0**. Whole-workload totals, including cold start and lifecycle: **3021 / 799 / 96 -> 3009 / 795 / 95**. Causal coverage is unavailable in both arms, so these are raw phase-window counts, not causal turn rates or live per-minute rates. No SQL, latency, or CPU gain is claimed.

The 20% stop was honored: restart-connect requests increased 12 -> 15 (+25%). Two sandbox reads moved from restart-first-turn, with equal whole-run counts (two requests each); a proactive-job tick moved into reconnect while whole-run proactive requests fell 13 -> 12. Passive checkpoint placement and a three-statement session patch moving from first-turn into warm turn 1 explain the warm SQL shift. Other operation increases were two memory-source reads during idle-settle and one zero-SQL skill scan at boot. The six affected owner files are byte-identical across heads, and none of the five changed pairing operations appears in either request ledger. The campaign coordinator explicitly accepted these background/phase-placement differences and released the count hold. Lower whole-run totals are not presented as a performance win.

prs.title: perf(node-host): return settled turn from journal owner
prs.body:
The node turn reader currently settles a turn whose physical owner was ended by a predecessor, then rereads that same turn. The proposed change returns the settlement owner’s native postimage, preserving external-writer observations and terminal receipt behavior. The existing unique partial index allows at most one running turn per owner.

This draft preregisters the synthetic workload and regression before the first run. Production code is unchanged until baseline reproduction and design approval.

Acceptance: twenty synthetic physical launches with running turns, ended offline by a predecessor (five each completed, failed, interrupted, cancelled), followed by an isolated Gateway and the real journal worker message transport. Read twenty recovered receipts, then twenty unchanged warm receipts. Target: exactly one fewer turn SELECT per recovery; no increased warm SQL, worker requests, or MAIN SQL. Preserve terminal state/error/result fields, monotonic timestamps, historical completed turns, and durable replay. This is a worker transport flow under real Gateway ownership, not a remote node WebSocket or model-latency claim.

Frozen sqlharness v3.1.4 records native executions and requests; startup, recovery, warm, and shutdown stay separate. Use three alternating pairs when host load <64 and internal free >=12GiB, otherwise one pair with attribution. Counts report median [min–max] and per-operation changes. Timing additionally requires the campaign lock, load <24, >=5 samples per arm, separate cold/warm median/p95/spread, and no >=20% adverse cell; otherwise make no latency/CPU-time claim. Per-thread CPU profiles provide attribution only.

Workload: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/node-worker-journal-measure.ts --root <owned-synthetic-root> --prepare`, then without `--prepare`, with the frozen observer and fresh internal output/phase. Acceptance and rerun instructions: `scripts/perf/node-worker-journal-measure.md`.

prs.title: refactor: deslop terminal, browser and command fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated test setup across terminal/browser UI, command/CLI, plugin and package tests has multiple fixture owners, alongside two small unused production surfaces.

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible feature, CLI/config/protocol or persisted-data change is intended. Test cases and assertions remain; the private image-error field removal has the explicitly accepted inspection tradeoff described below. No action is required from users.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consolidate each family under an existing test-support owner, or a narrow sibling when no suitable owner exists, and remove superseded copies. This stacks 34 independently attributable cuts across 71 paths. Existing authority, security, write settlement and ordinary durability behavior remain. The standalone session-memory backend (Phase E) and its machinery/tests are untouched; this PR is not a whole-lane exhaustion claim.

Local formatted diff against `fed1c12d0d4eeaec93bbd78a54e6926f4be76889`: **796 additions, 1,396 deletions, 600 net lines removed**, including **25 net production lines**. This is local Git sizing, not an observed GitHub PR size. Earlier 666 total/16 production figures were nominal source-packet estimates. Do not add family file-set counts or nominal nets: independent cuts share several files, especially terminal/browser and new-session transition.

Counts below come from the actual native census of the final formatted candidate, not older source estimates. Each line is **before = after**. A = assertion sites; R = registrations; T/S/CS/H/F/M/C/G/D = test declarations/suites/custom suites/hooks/test-finished callbacks/module mocks/conditional registration builders/register-prefixed calls/suite.define. R sums those nine categories. Table builders, hoisted initializers and custom assertion calls are separate; expect.assert guards are zero throughout. Parameter rows are not expanded. Family scopes overlap and are **not additive**; files below are the exact native family scope, including support owners where changed. For production-only cuts, zero sites in the changed module does not mean zero unchanged behavioral tests.

Provenance notes identify retained source/fixture history, not independently verified human-incident reports. Where no introducing PR was recorded, that gap is explicit. No production race/guard is deleted by declaring its origin speculative.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

prs.title: perf(ui): share row observers and avatar subscriptions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large session lists and transcripts allocate native observers and subscribe to the same owners once per rendered row, even when those rows share the same observation policy.

## User Impact

Session lists, avatars, overflow labels, and attachment visibility keep the same behavior with fewer native resources and source subscriptions. Hidden labels cancel pending measurement and marquee work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resize and intersection observation now share one native observer per document and complete option set, while each caller retains its own targets, callback batches, and teardown. Marquee labels share their motion/visibility/content observation and watch only registered label subtrees and host attributes. Agent chips share upstream subscriptions per application; avatar context and branding use their existing lazy projection owner.

The mutation observer does not watch unrelated document content: a clock update in a sibling row does not schedule label geometry. Removed targets are retired in one microtask because native MutationObserver has no unobserve operation; queued records for retained labels are delivered before rebuilding its targets.

## Evidence

Acceptance: preserve mounted row identity and visibility/cleanup contracts; reduce native resource counts; run 20 serial interleaved pairs for affected desktop/mobile flows and inspect script/task CPU median, p95, and range. On the loaded host, an identical-build A/A control determines whether wall/frame timing is usable. Instrumented count runs are separate from CPU comparisons. Fixtures use 1,000 sessions, 400-message transcripts, 1,000 models, and 500 cron jobs through the production renderer and synthetic Gateway; this is renderer proof, not live-Gateway proof.

| Proof | Base → head / result |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop 1,000-session roster: resize allocations | 1,365 → 15 |
| Desktop roster: active resize / intersection / mutation observers | 44 / 6 / 130 → 12 / 2 / 100 |
| Desktop roster: media-query listeners | 45 → 15 |
| Desktop roster: window / document listeners | 82 / 63 → 82 / 64 |
| Desktop 200-running-session clock fixture: active resize / intersection observers | 36 / 175 → 5 / 2 |
| Desktop clock fixture: intersection targets | 375 → 375 |

| Large-fixture assertions | All 10 desktop/mobile scenarios passed |
| Native hidden-tab idle, 3 seconds | Zero observer callbacks on either build; corrected warm CPU observation pending |

Idle observations are descriptive single instrumented samples, not statistical speedup claims. Earlier idle CPU numbers are superseded because deferred setup could overlap them. Hidden-state proof uses an owned Chromium process with native visibility (Playwright focus emulation disabled). All resize/intersection targets are retained. One shared document visibility listener is added so labels cancel pending work while hidden; the other listener and observer reductions outweigh that fixed cost. Roster scrolling creates 171 virtual rows and preserves the selected row; the base allocates 166 additional resize observers during scrolling and the head allocates none.

The corrected warm roster comparison completed: 20 interleaved pairs on desktop and 30 on mobile, including one additional 10-pair confirmation. All assertions passed. This is a structural resource win, not a claim of faster roster CPU. The corrected clock comparison completed 80/80 samples: 20 interleaved pairs per viewport, all assertions passed. The legacy dashboard chat-type migration is currently guarded by tests that import its private predicate directly. That test-only import forces the predicate to remain exported and proves the decision in isolation instead of proving how the Doctor repair scans and rewrites persisted session rows.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): align MCP discovery with session agent
prs.body:
Fixes #182555

## What Problem This Solves

During a session switch, Control UI could send `mcp.app.discover` with the new `sessionKey` but the independently updated agent selection. The Gateway correctly rejected that mixed pair with `FORBIDDEN`, leaving an access-error line in the log before the next discovery succeeded.

## User Impact

The Apps catalog and session surfaces now scope discovery to the agent named by the session key, so switching sessions no longer produces the avoidable `FORBIDDEN` / `SESSION_ACCESS_CHANGED` log entry. Gateway authorization is unchanged, and selection-only changes without a qualified session key still target the selected agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

A qualified session key already owns its agent. The new shared target constructor derives `agentId` from that key whenever `sessionKey` is present, rather than combining it with the separately updated selection. This applies to both the mounted catalog and the Apps page. The helper omits `agentId` if a non-empty key cannot be parsed instead of inventing a mismatched pair.

## Evidence

Two cross-agent regressions covered the mounted catalog and the Apps page. Both started with `sessionKey: agent:main:main` and selected agent `claude`. Before the change, both requested:

```text
mcp.app.discover { sessionKey: "agent:main:main", agentId: "claude" }
```

After the change, both request `agentId: "main"`, matching the session key. Existing target-race coverage was updated to reflect that a session-qualified target intentionally ignores an independent `agentId` prop change.

The complete adjacent suites pass:

```text
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       37 passed (37)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass. `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this host because the bundled `tsrs` binary requires GLIBC 2.34 while the host has an older libc; CI remains the type-check authority.

## AI Assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance under contributor direction and review.

prs.title: fix(agents): rescue plain-text calls to deferred tools instead of leaking raw tool_call XML
prs.body:
Related: #183085

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with Tool Search in its default `tools` mode, when the model calls a deferred tool (e.g. `skills_read`) by name and the provider returns that call as plain text inside a Qwen-style `<tool_call>` envelope, OpenClaw neither runs nor reroutes it — the raw `<tool_call>` block becomes the whole reply (`stopReason: "stop"`), the skill never loads, and the user has to step in. The reporter hit this 6 of 6 replies across three fresh sessions on 2026-10-24.

## User Impact

User impact: a plain-text call naming a deferred tool is now promoted and routed through normal execution — it runs, or fails with a tool error the model can recover from in the same turn — instead of ending the turn on raw XML. This restores the behavior the report describes from 2026.10.5, where the same bare-name call arrived structured, failed with `Tool skills_read not found`, and the model recovered immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The report's source analysis identified three gaps; this change closes all three at their owners:

1. **Envelope not scanned**: `scanXmlishToolCall` (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/grammar.ts`) only accepted text starting with `<function=`, so a `<tool_call>`-wrapped block (which the reporter verified parses once the first and last lines are removed) returned `invalid`. The scan now consumes the `<tool_call>` opener, requires the inner `<function=` form, and extends a complete result through the matching `</tool_call>`.
2. **Deferred names outside the rescue allowlist**: in `tools` mode the plain-text promotion allowlist was `liveAllowedToolNames` (the visible set only; `directory` mode used the whole catalog), so a rescued call naming a deferred tool was rejected anyway. Promotion now accepts the union of live and capability (deferred catalog) names (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream.ts`). A promoted deferred call routes through normal execution — or a recoverable tool error — exactly like the structured bare-name call did.
3. **Strip husk**: because the scanner now owns the full envelope, the strip path removes the entire block instead of leaving a `<tool_call>\n</tool_call>` husk behind.

Streaming semantics are preserved deliberately: a missing or partial `</tool_call>` close, or a partial opener (`<tool_`, ...), keeps the scan in `prefix` so stream buffering and stripping never act on a half-consumed envelope.

## Evidence

- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/grammar.test.ts`: enveloped scan cases — complete parse consuming the envelope (name, payload, `end` at the closing marker), missing/partial close stays `prefix`, partial opener (`<tool_`, `<tool_call>`, `<tool_call>\n`) stays `prefix`, envelope wrapping non-call text is `invalid`, and the bare function form still parses.
- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts`: end-to-end `parseStandalonePlainTextToolCallBlocks` on the exact report fixture (enveloped `skills_read` call with a deferred allowlist) yields the promoted block with parsed arguments.
- `packages/tool-call-repair` suite: 7 files / 188 tests green on head `366ce4aeaf6`; `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-tool-call-*.test.ts` (promotion, replay-sanitization, stream-normalization): 7 files / 42 tests green; `oxlint` on touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

## Risk and Compatibility

- `scanXmlishToolCall` is shared by parsing, stripping, and stream buffering; the envelope branch is strictly additive (text starting with `<function=` behaves identically) and the prefix rules for partial envelopes prevent premature execution or stripping during streaming.
- The promotion allowlist grows from visible-only to live ∪ capability in `tools` mode. A promoted deferred call that cannot execute still produces a normal tool error the model sees, matching pre-regression behavior; it cannot grant execution authority beyond the existing tool catalog policy.

## LOC

production +58 / −2 across 2 files; tests +89 in 2 files. No docs or generated code.

## Not Tested

- No live Strata/Qwen end-to-end run; the repaired scan is covered directly at the grammar boundary with the report's exact fixture shape, and the promotion allowlist change is covered by the existing promotion suites staying green.

prs.title: perf: remove redundant filesystem precondition probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resource loading and local file operations repeat filesystem probes whose answers the next operation already supplies.

## User Impact

Fewer filesystem calls in local resource and read-tool flows, preserving missing-file behavior, permissions, containment and executable attestation. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove filesystem probes whose following operation already owns the result: prompt and skill discovery, source metadata, local reads, tool installation, Gmail project discovery, Memory Wiki initialization, iMessage executable attestation, and QA asset versioning.

Twelve probe sites disappear, with no new cache or state owner. Missing optional inputs still follow the existing catch path; loaded resource metadata uses the known file parent; recursive mkdir supplies the directory-created fact. The prompt loader also no longer stages a second result array merely to preserve its loaded prefix on a metadata-stat failure.

Retained boundaries: local reads still reject directories/nonregular files and use fs-safe identity/open checks; iMessage still rejects remote hosts and requires positive Mach-O attestation (including the exact local wrapper contract); prompt/skill containment, tool-install lock/archive checks, Memory Wiki exclusive scaffold creation and cache invalidation, and QA URL containment remain. Concurrent external replacement is handled by the actual operation; no preflight observation is treated as authoritative. Probes that select a different diagnostic/fallback, cache absence, avoid failed spawns, or enforce watcher/security contracts remain.

Acceptance rule (registered before measurement): use synthetic fixtures only. Count filesystem operations through the production owners, with cold setup separate from repeated operations; expect one fewer readability access per successful local read, one fewer existence probe plus one metadata stat per explicit temporary prompt file, nine fewer existence stats per warm Memory Wiki initialization, and no added filesystem operation in those owner flows. Run one baseline/candidate warm pair on the same macOS host with the frozen SQL harness v3.1.4 (10 warm turns per fixture): report statements/worker requests/MAIN as median [min–max], plus operation attribution. The patch must add no owner-attributable SQL/request or runtime MAIN work. This is a work-count claim; no latency improvement is claimed on the shared loaded host. Any timing claim would require the campaign timing lock, quiet-host admission and interleaved five-sample proof.

## Evidence

The committed `scripts/bench-filesystem-preconditions.mts` exercises ten synthetic prompt loads and ten local read-tool calls. Five alternating baseline/candidate samples on the same macOS host, using an external owner-attributed filesystem counter:

| Count per prompt-load/read pair | Baseline median / p95 [min–max] | Candidate median / p95 [min–max] |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Counted filesystem calls | 7 / 7 [7–7] | 4 / 4 [4–4] |
| Existence probe | 1 / 1 [1–1] | 0 / 0 [0–0] |
| Prompt and metadata stats | 2 / 2 [2–2] | 1 / 1 [1–1] |
| Readability access | 1 / 1 [1–1] | 0 / 0 [0–0] |

The actual read, regular-file stat and fs-safe realpath remain. This is three removed probes per exercised action pair, not a universal per-Gateway-turn rate. Memory Wiki's nine removed existence stats are source-attributed; this workload does not exercise Wiki initialization.

One complete same-platform baseline/candidate pair with frozen SQL harness v3.1.4, fresh runtime builds, synthetic state, real Gateway transport and main/worker CPU profiles:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warm-window SQL median / p95 [min–max], 10 windows | 50 / 61 [50–61] | 50 / 75 [50–75] |
| Warm-window requests median / p95 [min–max] | 12 / 16 [12–16] | 12 / 18 [12–18] |
| Warm-window MAIN median / p95 [min–max] | 0 / 0 [0–0] | 0 / 0 [0–0] |
| Whole-workload statements / requests / MAIN | 2988 / 799 / 96 | 2986 / 797 / 94 |

**The 23% raw SQL p95 increase was reviewed and accepted as phase placement.** Its entire +14 statements/+2 requests in warm window 1 is the same plugin metadata refresh (9 SQL) and state-lease lookup/release (5 SQL/2 requests) occurring in the baseline's first-turn window. Their whole-workload counts are identical: metadata refresh 9 SQL/1 request and the lease family 9 SQL/6 requests in each arm. No touched filesystem owner appears in those SQL/request stacks. Both complete workloads pass, including restart and child cleanup. The raw increase is disclosed, not called “within spread.”

The frozen v3.1.4 causal hook labels all events background on this source revision, so these are execution-window/operation counts, not causal turn totals. Loaded-host profiles confirm main/worker capture but do not establish a CPU or latency improvement; none is claimed.

All 136 focused tests passed across 11 files in seven Vitest projects, including prompt-prefix stability, local reads, resource discovery, tool staging, Gmail discovery, Wiki initialization, symlinked iMessage attestation and QA assets. Ten additional plugin Doctor declaration/closure tests passed. Two isolated Codex P0–P2 reviews are scoped-clean. [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40152157049): 57 successful jobs, 25 skipped.

Local Madge reports zero cycles; worker ratchet T1 170→170 and compatibility 15→15, dialect ratchet, source contracts, core/script lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Local `check:changed` is **not** an overall pass: its type/declaration-dependent extension lint checks reject the required external dependency store, reproduced on baseline. CI types and lint pass. Canonical Knip findings are identical baseline/candidate: 75 production, 98 full-tree, 1,136 script entries; zero new findings. No guard or baseline was weakened.

Production delta: **−23 lines across nine files**, removing twelve probe sites. Test additions cover prompt omission/parent metadata, symlinked binary/wrapper attestation with remote rejection, and QA missing/directory/content version behavior. This is the smaller final batch after inventory retained the remaining candidates for real behavior, security or ownership contracts.

Open-PR overlap was refreshed through the shared index: #148724 (`e90c26213288`), #145732 (`975b4d932874`) and #135290 (`96deb4ca35f2`). Baseline→candidate merge-tree conflict regions are 0→0, 28→28 and 30→30; no new paths or regions. The latter two PRs already conflict on the baseline. No SQL, schema, public SDK, update/Doctor/migration/service-lifecycle or plugin-loader changes.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reduce database reads during session creation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Creating a second session and its native child repeats a full creation read immediately after target discovery. The row-metadata reader also fetches participants separately despite already having an aggregate-capable entry query. The standard synthetic workload attributes six statements and one worker request per spawn to those two classes.

## User Impact

Session creation and initial transcript reads perform less database work with the same stored result, permissions, and restart behavior. No user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing owner-published full entry facts for eligible unlabeled canonical creation, including known absence. Preserve separate existing/target entries, opaque alias resolution, labeled/cold fallback, physical source custody, replacement CAS, and final authority. Include participants in the existing aggregate when reading row transcript metadata. The `jsonOrderedArray` call and ordering are unchanged. No schema, new cache, generation, or cross-store transaction changes.

## Acceptance rule (registered before candidate A/B)

Flow: real isolated Gateway, loopback transport and mock provider, frozen v3.1.5 standard synthetic workload including native child, compaction, shutdown and restart. All data is synthetic.

Three alternating same-platform baseline/candidate pairs on base `b406c2b9c1aa310f933c66c3ff0867750af80c54` and this head. Count statements, worker requests and MAIN operations; report phase 04.second-session per-owner and execution/causal medians [min–max], plus cold and warm phases separately. Removed owner classes must strictly decrease; other touched-owner work must hold or improve. Runtime MAIN must not increase. Any adverse metric move of 20% stops for attribution. Profile all Gateway threads. No local latency claim on a loaded host; timing comparisons require the campaign timing lock, load <24, and at least five samples per arm with median/p95/spread.

Expected owner reduction, not yet an A/B result: creation −3 SQL/−1 request; row-facts −3 SQL/0 requests; total −6 SQL/−1 request/0 MAIN per phase04.

## Evidence

- All four regression cases fail on unchanged base for the intended extra reads and pass with the change. Full touched suites: 36/36 pass. Covers absent/resident creation facts and post-write visibility; participant snapshot consistency and post-commit visibility with and without reader continuation.
- Full two-file invocation: 119.51 seconds, mostly compiler work (81% transform); test execution 15%. No new test file, export, or test-only production seam.
- Basic changed-file oxlint and formatting pass; `git diff --check` passes.
- Local type-aware lint cannot pass declaration-custody preflight with the external virtual store. The exact-head CI run supplies the passing types and lint evidence; no local type-aware pass is claimed.
- Both isolated code reviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings. [Exact-head CI run 40154739914](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40154739914) passed, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, types, lint, source contracts, Madge and database ratchets. PostgreSQL semantic review is complete.
- Canonical Knip export scans have identical baseline/candidate findings: production 42/42, full-tree 57/57, scripts 14/14; zero new findings or resolution errors.
- The three alternating frozen A/B pairs and all-thread profiles remain queued behind local static/recovery checks. They will be posted when complete. The four base-red regressions establish the two removed read classes; no whole-flow measured saving or timing improvement is claimed yet.

The production diff adds 26 net lines to consume existing facts while keeping the required cold/labeled path. Tests add 76 net lines for the two distinct removed read classes. This is a SQL/request reduction, not a net-negative-code claim. Registry recovery, Team leases and spawn admission are unchanged. Historical `subagents.runs` JSON scans did not reproduce in three attribution runs and are excluded; pending-input and payload-owner work belong to separate lanes.

Shared open-PR index overlap check: #183114 at `c82c9413df6177cae1e4d2ed10f853ded83730f1` is clean against both base and candidate; #177242 retains the same 17 inherited conflict messages and unchanged conflict hunks; #146847 retains the same 25 inherited conflict messages and unchanged conflict hunks. prs.title: fix(control-ui): serve data avatars on session URLs
prs.body:
Fixes #182688

## What Problem This Solves

Agent avatars configured as supported `data:image/...` URLs were blank in session owner and participant surfaces because their bare `/avatar/<id>` URL returned `404`; the same avatar worked through the revisioned URL used elsewhere.

## User Impact

Data-URL agent avatars now load in session lists, stacked participant avatars, and owner menus without requiring a workspace-file workaround. Authentication, base-path handling, local-file delivery, local-file caching, and unsupported-source behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session identity projection emits a bare avatar URL, while the HTTP handler previously served prepared image data only when a `v` query parameter was present. The handler now serves an already prepared data image on the existing bare route when the resolved source is a data URL. It does not rewrite the projection or add image preparation to that synchronous path. Unsupported data sources still fall through to the existing `404` response.

## Evidence

The regression obtains the bare URL produced by `projectSessionParticipant()` for a data-URL agent avatar and requests it through the authenticated Control UI avatar handler. Before the production change, both methods failed as expected:

```text
serves a data URL avatar at its projected bare GET URL  -> expected 404 to be 200
serves a data URL avatar at its projected bare HEAD URL -> expected 404 to be 200
Tests 2 failed | 31 passed
```

After the change, GET and HEAD return `200`, an unauthenticated request returns `401`, and an unsupported data source remains `404`.

The complete adjacent suites pass:

```text

Tests       165 passed (165)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass. `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this host because the bundled `tsrs` binary requires GLIBC 2.34 while the host has an older libc; CI remains the type-check authority.

This change was developed with AI assistance under contributor direction and review.

prs.title: perf: reduce database work before dispatching new messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every newly submitted message performs a five-statement durable duplicate-input lookup before dispatch, even when its idempotency key is new.

## User Impact

Submitted messages retain the same durable reconnect, restart, and attachment protections while their source lookup uses one SQL statement. No configuration or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current-session join, pending input, and committed transcript all belong to the same agent database. A single Kysely SELECT can read them in one statement snapshot on SQLite and PostgreSQL without an explicit read transaction. A positive metadata lookup falls through to the existing bounded-payload and projection-status transaction unchanged; the maintainer-approved tradeoff is one extra statement on this rare recovery path (pending 5→6; committed 8→9). The worker request and all current-session/custody checks remain.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, registered before the first run: for a current session with a new idempotency key, reduce source lookup from five SQL statements to exactly one autocommit SELECT; retain one worker request and zero runtime main-thread SQL. Pending and committed source results, oversized-input rejection, stale-projection refusal, session replacement, restart/expired-memory/attachment duplicate-dispatch handling, and prompt-prefix stability must hold. Both engines require deterministic count proof, and the final head requires all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and engine-owner review.

Synthetic live workload: frozen SQL harness v3.1.4, first turn, ten warm turns, restart turn, and warm non-regression. Baseline/candidate alternate; three pairs when load is below 64 and internal free space is at least 12 GiB, otherwise one pair. Report statement/request/main-thread medians and ranges, separating cold and warm and attributing the changed operation. The observer's causal-attribution limitations will be disclosed. CPU profiles cover the real Gateway and worker threads. Any timing comparison requires the campaign timing lock, load below 24, five alternating samples per arm, and median/p95/spread; no latency claim otherwise. A 20% worsening in a measured timing cell stops the change.

Validation on `ef6c367f320`: 56 focused tests passed (39 Gateway admission/recovery, six source payload/projection, 11 prompt-prefix). Native count conformance passed all six SQLite/PostgreSQL cases: new input 1 SQL, pending recovery 6, committed recovery 9; session replacement and committed-source exclusion with `pendingOnly` also pass. The same tests fail on exact baseline `4c3bf18daa6` on both engines: new input is 5 statements, pending recovery 5, and committed recovery 8. Final PostgreSQL owner review approves this exact head. The completed real-Gateway measurements are below. The initial local PostgreSQL fixture omitted `unaccent`; after provisioning the standard extensions, the focused suite passed without a product change.

Two independent Codex review rounds completed, and a coordinator-authorized review limited to the later CI repair is scoped-clean. Initial CI exposed an unsupported SQLite boolean bind in the new query; the repaired query selects a NULL committed-source expression for `pendingOnly`, with an explicit regression assertion.

Exact-head [CI run 40139087907](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139087907) completed with 39 successful jobs, 26 skipped, and two inherited failures. [PostgreSQL shard 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139087907/job/121007278254) fails only seven `interactive-setup.integration.test.ts` fixture cases missing `runtime/standalone-runtime-profile.mjs`, introduced by #182856, reproduced on main `0f6631638b2e`, and fixed independently by #182990; the aggregate gate consequently fails. PostgreSQL shards 1 and 3 pass. Types, lint, source contracts, Madge/Kysely guards, and baseline/worker/dialect ratchets pass. No all-green CI claim. Canonical Knip baseline/candidate sets are identical: 1,136 script, 69 production, and 81 full-tree findings; zero new or removed findings and no resolution errors.

The original recovery transaction stays unchanged, including payload-size bounds, optional pending-table handling, and projection checks. A pending input accepted after the fast lookup belongs to the next submit/recovery lookup, matching the existing snapshot behavior. No schema, cache, generation, or worker request is added. Production growth is 47 lines because preserving the bounded recovery path requires a separate small metadata query; deleting that path would weaken duplicate-dispatch and payload safeguards.

prs.title: perf(sessions): avoid transaction envelopes for prepared run adoption
prs.body:
## Problem and design

A resident `session.actor.adoptRun` without a turn currently spends three SQLite statements on a single node update: BEGIN IMMEDIATE, the session_nodes UPSERT, and COMMIT. This change lets the existing entry writer certify an unchanged entry, one prepared node effect, or a transaction-required update. The actor does not maintain its own eligibility field list.

For an eligible SQLite write, the native begin hook records the actual pending scopes and revision. A protected, single-use preparation callback finishes the entry publication, exact receipt, reply serialization, and final admission before the native statement. Success installs staged facts through the existing postcommit owner. Cold, PostgreSQL, nested, cleanup, compound, and oversized-reply cases retain transactions. A fallback persists the already-reduced entry; reducers execute once.

Rejected preparation and definite BUSY/LOCKED/ABORT outcomes preserve prior resident facts and committed tokens. Indeterminate failures invalidate staged facts and use existing unknown-outcome recovery. Writer custody and `withSessionActorTransactionState` remain intact. The terminal query uses the same compiled UPSERT and existing statement lease; its release joins existing settlement. No schema, retention, identity-folding, cache, or epoch change.

## Acceptance rule — registered before measurement

Flow: synthetic real Gateway run adoption over the real transport on macOS/arm64, frozen SQL harness v3.1.5, pinned exact baseline and candidate heads. Run three alternating same-platform pairs (M,C,M,C,M,C), one fresh fixture per arm, default workload turns/restart/cron/compaction/child checks, with idle/settle waits disabled consistently. Keep boot, first-turn, warm turns, and restart separate. Baseline is fdad53b1bc1d66d98a11da12fb633a75f8285ecb.

Primary win: warm eligible adoptRun changes from 3 SQL / 1 request to 1 SQL / 1 request, with runtime MAIN remaining zero. Report per-operation counts and warm/affected-phase SQL, request, and MAIN medians [min–max], plus per-thread native CPU profiles. Attribute unrelated background count variation explicitly; no increase attributable to the changed operations is acceptable.

Wall-clock/CPU-speed comparisons require the campaign timing lock and one-minute load below 24, with at least five interleaved samples per head and cold/warm kept apart. Report median, p95, and spread only for qualified timing samples. Any user-facing regression stops acceptance; a 20% cell movement is a stop. If qualification is unavailable for 60 minutes, report counts and CPU profile attribution without a latency or CPU-speed claim.

Reproduction command: frozen `measure.py --repo <checkout> --out <fresh-output> --sha <exact-head> --repetitions 1 --idle-seconds 0 --settle-seconds 0`, alternating baseline and candidate; observer, causality, and workload remain frozen. Node 26.12.1, compile cache disabled, internal Bun/Vitest temporary caches. Native `--cpu-prof` propagates to Gateway workers through the existing benchmark preload.

## Validation and limits

Two isolated Codex reviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings. CI then found that the actor’s connection type did not preserve the query owner’s native-only certificate, plus two missing lifecycle test inputs. The correction carries the already-narrowed native connection through the entry certificate, supplies the empty lifecycle inputs, and removes a forwarding export in favor of direct imports. One authorized delta-only Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings in this correction. The final type-only simplification infers the certificate union from literal tags instead of duplicating its shape; it passes the normal line-cap hook and type-aware lint. PostgreSQL and SQLite carry-forward reviews approved corrected head 0594cde8d01d31c6589991a232b53d2b652b0b77. The final focused run passed 69 tests across the existing actor, receipt, and admission suites. The correction also passes the normal formatting and line-cap hooks. Native receipt and actor assertions verify SQLite's change count and retained native/resident facts, rather than treating a recorded method attempt as a committed effect. Both PostgreSQL and SQLite review carry forward to the corrected head. Exact-head [CI run 40154327446](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40154327446) passed, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the normal-install type/lint gates. The local check:changed run cannot execute typed lint/types because the campaign-required external dependency store is rejected by the declaration-containment guard; no guard was bypassed. Remaining local static checks and frozen Gateway pairs are running. No measurement result is claimed yet.

Regression coverage includes rejected preparation, definite ABORT, uncertain native failure, exact pending/committed receipts, changed-window fallback, oversized adoption, and single application of a non-idempotent reducer. Existing crash/restart recovery remains the slow path. PostgreSQL keeps BEGIN/advisory writer custody/UPSERT/COMMIT unchanged.

This is an approved owner redesign: it removes two recurring SQL control statements, not a net-negative source cleanup. Necessary growth is the entry-owned effect certificate and preparation inside the existing native receipt/settlement owners. Splitting those would leave an incomplete receipt cutover. Production delta against the merge base is +623/−134 (net +489); the growth implements the entry certificate and native preparation/settlement rather than a second publication system. Full normalized diff3 merge-tree comparisons against 19 overlapping open PRs add no conflicts except the accepted import-only conflict described below. No release changelog edit is included; this body records release-note context.

Open-PR overlap: one import-only conflict with #181057; bodies merge cleanly. Moving the import is undone by the repository formatter. The coordinator explicitly accepted this adjacent-insertion conflict and requested no production restructuring. The schema-facts forwarding export was removed to avoid enlarging the inherited #157427 conflict. The current shared PR index was refreshed after the final-head comparisons; unchanged peer/head comparisons were reused, and no other added conflict remains.

prs.title: fix(slack): wait for acknowledged interactions before Gateway suspension
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack could acknowledge a button or message shortcut while Gateway suspension reported ready and the listener had not yet handed off the interaction.

## User Impact

Planned suspension and account stop now wait for accepted listeners. New direct deliveries receive no success acknowledgement during drain or after account stop. Forced process loss can still lose an interaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before Bolt can acknowledge a direct delivery, the receiver acquires independent Gateway work through its existing account ingress monitor. The monitor reports activity before invoking the listener and releases the work when dispatch finishes, including on error. Ordinary Events API callbacks still acknowledge after a durable append. Direct interaction payloads are not stored.

## Evidence

Three Socket Mode receiver regressions failed on the unpatched base and passed on this candidate (219 ms combined test time; 41.92 s command wall with one worker). The monitor suite passed 35/35 (23.35 s command wall, one worker). Its new 9 ms test caught a previous candidate reporting idle during the synchronous part of direct dispatch. That previous candidate already released the root on a synchronous throw and joined stop initiated from inside dispatch. CI seconds are unavailable.

An independent run on the final candidate passed all three registered receiver cases plus the signed HTTP, loopback WebSocket, two-account and SQLite recovery checks. Its combined run was 44/45: an unchanged retention test hit its five-second timeout on both this candidate (5.008 s) and the clean base (5.013 s). Its timing cause is unresolved. The separate short-timeout append-before-dispatch control timed out on its tested base and earlier candidate; its failed-append/no-acknowledgement sibling passed. No live Slack or installed Gateway restart was exercised. Handoff here means session-event enqueue, not a delivered reply.

The public SDK counts match the base: 160 entrypoints, 3,823 exports and 2,216 callable exports. The checker still fails the three inherited limits. Focused runs used the locked Slack protocol libraries with a mixed development toolchain. Full type, lint and build checks on the frozen dependency graph remain unverified because package policy denied two locked dependencies.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting the Gateway with an older PostgreSQL agent schema reports an “identity migration” even when the pending change only rebuilds indexes. The PostgreSQL guide also omits how these upgrades run.

## User Impact

Operators get an accurate “Agent database migration” diagnostic with the same instruction to stop active agents and run `openclaw doctor --fix`. The guide explains the stopped-writer Doctor/update path and the state 32 / agent 34 index-ordering upgrade from #183015.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing maintenance-authority owner serves all agent database migrations and has no schema-version parameters, so this changes only its label. Gate conditions, error classes, exit codes, schema versions, queries, and migration behavior are unchanged. This is PostgreSQL readiness documentation and message polish, with no database runtime behavior change or new dependencies. No changelog edit.

The source-linked note scopes the earlier benchmark precisely: the three affected indexes on 500,000 rows rebuilt in 1.109 seconds. That is existing #183015 evidence, not a new benchmark or whole-install upgrade estimate. SQL/request/bridge-trip counts are unchanged by this patch; no latency improvement is claimed.

## Evidence

- The three existing maintenance-scope cases fail on the base specifically for the old diagnostic, before any database open; no new test case or setup was added.
- `pr-simplify`: one string replacement, one stronger existing assertion, and the concise documentation note. Production and test changes are each +1/-1; documentation is +12 lines.

- The above docs/test/lint/types ran serially on one task-owned Blacksmith Testbox. Exact-head [CI run 40154686821](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40154686821) passed, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards (15m16s / 20m23s / 20m26s job wall time). No CI rerun, admin exception, or PostgreSQL behavior-review gate was needed.

Related: #183015.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The broad-roster message-body opt-out already landed in #176457. A remaining path sends persisted `session.message` bodies to web sidebar clients solely because they hold `mode: "narration"` exact subscriptions. The narration owner consumes bounded narration, observer and tool events and ignores persisted message events.

## User Impact

The candidate reduces unused sidebar message traffic while keeping transcript, notification, attention, and older-client behavior. Performance acceptance remains pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

This experiment adds the `narration-message-bodies-optional` capability. Clients without it keep their exact-subscription contract. Full and provisional transcript observers, independently identified subscriptions, and explicit plugin body interest retain complete messages. All row envelopes, ordering, authorization and delivery baselines remain unchanged. No protocol version, configuration, or durable state change.

## Evidence

The supplied synthetic 66-client/three-audience consumer capture recorded 31,306 session deliveries, including 2,592 unused bodies (6,122,898 message-value bytes) on capable sidebar/narration clients. Another 3,996 bodies belong to legacy clients and must remain. A frame without a synchronous visible effect is not proven removable; this experiment does not suppress row events or merge distinct delivered histories.

Acceptance declared before new measurements: one quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge lease, at least 11 interleaved baseline/candidate pairs. Gateway CPU per wave and event-loop p99 must improve; sessions.list p50/p90/p95, chat.startup, open-transcript latency and browser onmessage must not regress under the campaign paired/IQR rules. Report per-pair deltas and wire counts. Correctness includes sidebar attention/unread/preview, plugin and full transcript interest, reconnect and baseline behavior.

Current proof: independent review clean through P2. AWS c7a.4xlarge lease `cbx_491666ca1959` passed 68 Gateway tests across four files and 21 UI tests across three files (85.56 seconds for both shards). The omission regression fails with the previous server policy; the actual WebSocket row-delta integration passes with narration omission and reconnect baseline reconstruction. Changed-file checks are running; full UI e2e and the quiet-host performance comparison remain pending. The local Gateway integration attempt was stopped after exceeding the one-minute local allowance without a verdict.

Draft exists for remote-clone validation only. Do not merge. No performance improvement claimed yet; this becomes ready only if the declared gates pass.

Production LOC delta against main: **+12** (17 added, 5 deleted) across the capability registry, existing delivery predicate, and web handshake. The separate capability is necessary to preserve the older public capability’s full-exact-body contract. Existing subscription aggregation and omission machinery remain the single owners.

prs.title: perf(ui): defer dormant chat work during cold boot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold Chat evaluates optional operation bodies and inactive renderers before they are used, and warms unrelated routes in the background. Keep admission, state, browser gestures, and event authority synchronous; defer operation implementations and absent renderers. Common interactions receive parallel modulepreloads without eager evaluation. Rare editor, creator, MCP catalog and annotation paths defer both. New Session retains its own idle warming.

The queue split retains synchronous FIFO admission and visible-history ownership before awaiting transport. Discarding the first early draft after changing panes still lets the admitted lane deliver the second draft; a single early interrupt still waits for explicit resume. The original regression tests are unchanged. Config-editor activation, schema receipts, event subscriptions, outbox custody and lazy-view focus retain their existing owners.

## Evidence

Final source head: `6ab0e0b2d30`. The last commit changes only the two CI readiness tests; runtime bytes are identical to `650f11a6913`. Production build metadata names parent `1acfef4c653`; the final changes are the measured startup ratchet, generated manifest/grouping and parameter rename present in that build. prs.title: fix(web-fetch): words from neighboring blocks run together in fetched pages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #176244

Fixes neighboring HTML blocks merging words in `web_fetch`, such as `Stay hungryThen he left.` or `Price10 EUR`.

## User Impact

Basic HTML extraction and the shared Readability Markdown renderer retain boundaries around quotes, captions, navigation, sidebars, and collapsible sections. A block following inline text starts a new line. Adjacent paragraphs and inline text keep their existing output. Readability text mode has a separate implementation and is outside this repair; #178569 tracks that path. Definition lists remain in #180557.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing block-tag set and insert a missing opening boundary at the shared renderer. Keep anchor-closing behavior and the existing preformatted-code owner. Thanks @L4XB for the fix and regressions.

The backward check is limited to 64 characters. Beyond a long whitespace tail it may retain a space rather than insert a newline; the words remain separated. This accepted formatting edge avoids repeated scans over unbounded whitespace.

## Evidence

- Six block-boundary cases fail on current main; the adjacent-paragraph control passes. The repair passes all 52 extraction, 23 normalizer, and 7 Readability tests. Final integrated Vitest durations: 1.89s, 3.85s, and 3.24s; combined wrapper wall time: 16.89s.
- Actual HTTP through `createWebFetchTool().execute`, with isolated state and plugins disabled, reproduces joined quote and price text on base in both text and Markdown modes. All six head fixtures pass (HTTP 200, `raw-html`), including unchanged adjacent-paragraph and inline-text controls. The server was stopped and temporary state removed. A full Gateway/model session was not run; the HTTP invocation exercises the changed fallback owner.
- Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Exact-head PR CI provides broad proof.
- Simplification keeps one renderer and one boundary helper. Production delta: +42 lines; tests: +18. Most growth enumerates missing HTML block tags and preserves existing paragraph/link behavior; no dependency or parallel renderer was added.
- Independent P0–P2 review with the complete renderer found no actionable findings.

Exact-head CI [40142104405](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142104405) passed on `7e627e9f661f85f7e18c4f4bb50ee377ad20f06f`.

prs.title: fix(android): preserve canonical thinking levels and honor write-authorized effort controls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android disables Thinking and Fast Mode for write-authorized connections even though the Gateway permits those session changes with `operator.write`.

## User Impact

Write-authorized users can adjust effort without administrator access. Read-only connections remain excluded, and connection, session ownership, pending changes, and active-run checks remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing write-scope predicate for both effort controls and their callbacks, matching `sessions.patch`. Current main already preserves the Gateway’s canonical thinking level, so this revision removes the separate clamp/rank table and send/reconnect normalization proposed earlier. Gateway metadata remains the single owner of effective thinking levels.

Original contribution by @dankarization (Daniil Karpenko). Contributor commits are retained.

## Evidence

- Existing composer interaction tests now run with read/write scopes and no administrator scope. The saved-callback regression also removes write access before invoking Thinking and Fast, while retaining the active-run check.
- Local Gradle execution stopped before tests: this Mac has no Java runtime or Android SDK. A local red/green run and a fresh Android device run could not be performed; exact-head CI supplies native test and Kotlin lint coverage.

prs.title: perf(transcripts): return summary presence with session list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw transcripts list` reads every session, then separately reads every summary identity and builds a JavaScript Set to compute `hasSummary`. Those two queries also require an explicit read transaction.

## User Impact

Transcript listing preserves the same sessions, ordering and summary availability while doing less database work. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return summary presence from the session query with a left join on the existing `(session_id, session_started_at)` primary key. Remove the obsolete summary-key query/export and the now-unneeded single-statement snapshot wrapper. The ordering, complete session identity, summary visibility after writes, and worker ownership stay the same. No schema, cache, authorization, retention, or write-order changes.

This is the final small batch from a result-reprocessing inventory: three removed sites, with the other examined candidates retained because they handle differing SQL/JavaScript ordering, Unicode identity, merged sources, pagination sentinels, or real predicates. In particular, actor-hydration re-sorts remain necessary because SQLite preserves inner descending order while the PostgreSQL aggregate orders ascending.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, recorded before performance runs: use the committed synthetic CLI workload with 64 sessions, repeated raw IDs and summaries for half of the complete identities. Use one baseline/candidate pair under the defensive-lane proof rule, on the same macOS platform, with the first read separate from five warm list operations per arm. A win is 2 SELECT + BEGIN/COMMIT becoming 1 SELECT per warm list, unchanged one worker request, unchanged output and zero added MAIN SQL. No count cell may regress; any 20% adverse movement stops the claim. Native CPU profiles are attribution evidence only. No wall-clock or CPU speedup is claimed on the loaded host. The comparative CLI pair was subsequently waived in favor of the native base-red regression and source attribution. The completed baseline recorded 4 SQL statements / 1 worker request / 0 MAIN per warm list, identically across five reads; cold open plus first list recorded 13 / 2 / 0. The candidate arm was not run. These are baseline counts, not comparative performance measurements. No Gateway steady-traffic saving is claimed: this reader's production entry point is the transcript CLI.

Validation: the native regression fails on base d3ae5134e20 with exactly two statements instead of one; identity, ordering, and post-write summary visibility assertions pass. Two isolated Codex reviews completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Formatting, basic lint, and diff checks pass. All 33 focused store cases passed; all selected static checks and all three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed on final head ae8041b186e in [CI run 40153343466](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40153343466). Local type-aware lint stopped before analysis because the campaign-required external dependency store violates the wrapper’s declaration-path check. Production delta: 13 added / 19 removed (net −6 lines), plus the synthetic workload and behavior coverage.

PostgreSQL checklist: (1) read-only single statement; no write envelope, CTE, string batch, or ON CONFLICT changes. (2) Same session rows and one boolean, no larger payload or iterator introduced; the independent full summary-key result disappears. (3) No revision/cache/invalidation change. (4) No PRAGMA or schema-admission change. (5) Same existing read worker, no MAIN move. (6) Existing meeting chronology PG fixture now checks exact summary identity; all three final-head conformance shards passed in CI run 40153343466.

Open-PR index: no other open main-targeting PR overlaps the seven changed files. PostgreSQL semantics review approved the full-key join and single-statement snapshot on the final production bytes; final-head conformance and selected CI static checks passed; the canonical Knip comparison also completed with identical finding sets: 53 production, 76 full-tree, and 1,136 scripts; zero new or resolved findings, with no timeout or module-resolution errors. The existing findings are inherited on the exact base, so both wrapper exits were 1.

The first optional CLI attempt stopped during fixture setup: repeated IDs shared a calendar date, which the public admission API correctly rejects. The workload now uses distinct dates. No measurements are claimed from that failed setup. This is a benchmark-only correction; production and behavior-test bytes remain unchanged.

Final gates: 42 jobs passed and 27 were skipped in exact-head CI; all three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed. Required dependency/security statuses and the corrected PR-context check passed. Two isolated Codex rounds cover the unchanged production bytes. The refreshed open-PR index contains only this PR for all seven files, so there are no other overlap heads to compare and no new merge conflicts. SDK/update validation is not applicable to this read-only transcript CLI change.

prs.title: perf(agents): remove retained trajectory projection branding
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Trajectory preparation leaves avoidable diagnostic-branding storage in the process after its event payloads have been flushed. Temporary bounded objects are collectible, but a global WeakSet used to mark them retains backing storage.

## User Impact

Lower retained memory and allocation during trajectory preparation, with identical event output, capture limits, credential/media redaction, and turn-end batching. No configuration, schema, durability, or public API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The limiter already creates the entire projected graph. Pass that producer-owned fact into the recursive projector instead of registering every object globally. Delete both internal factory helpers and the WeakSet, preserving ordinary-prototype/key-limit checks and the public descriptor-snapshot path. The internal export has no external-use or semver guarantee (`packages/ai/README.md`). Production delta: **29 added / 31 removed = −2 LOC**. No new cache or fenced-owner changes.

The original preparation payload is not a demonstrated leak. The SQLite sink holds serialized lines until logical-turn completion, then releases the committed batch. Original fixture objects collect while recorder handles remain live. A separate synthetic post-flush heap snapshot contained zero serialized trajectory event strings; the residual stack instead included 131,112 bytes at `createDiagnosticRecord > WeakSet.add`. Earlier flushing would undo #174619's one-append-per-normal-turn behavior and is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Reviewed/pushed head: `60e5a304bcaf18849861f15cf4a4a52609972990`. Lead owns merge; this lane does not merge.**

Node 26.12.1, real recorder and SQLite sink, synthetic preparation-shaped metadata. Five alternating baseline/candidate processes per mode; each keeps 64 recorder handles alive, records 128 measured events, and performs three forced collections after flush. Survivor and collected-object allocation sampling use a 1 KiB interval. Untraced timing and traced lifecycle promotion are separate passes. All 40 samples persisted 129 events including warmup, matched the same payload hash, collected all 2,816 original fixture objects, and observed an empty post-flush queue.

Source baseline: `ad2172d77e260e3039febbc4f531bd476245f912`; baseline/candidate overlays replace only the three changed production modules. Both use the same preload and dependencies. Those owners and the residual-measurement owners were unchanged by the subsequent required main rebase. Runs used the shared exclusive sandbox lock, interleaved slot CPU set, resource limits, and shared production guard. No guard interruption, excluded measurement window, or pause trimming.

### Five-sample means

Each row is per 64-recorder workload, not per Gateway turn. Timing includes fixture/hash/WeakRef bookkeeping and notification drain. CPU is process-wide; wall time is the capture window.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Absolute delta | Relative delta | Samples per side |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Post-flush sampled owner bytes | 141,812.8 | 11,507.2 | -130,305.6 | -91.89% | 5 / 5 |
| Legacy branding survivor bytes | 131,323.2 | 0.0 | -131,323.2 | -100.00% | 5 / 5 |
| Post-flush whole-heap delta bytes | 455,169.6 | 322,139.2 | -133,030.4 | -29.23% | 5 / 5 |
| Collected-object owner allocation bytes | 8,253,120.0 | 7,906,492.8 | -346,627.2 | -4.20% | 5 / 5 |
| Untraced process CPU ms | 29.2180 | 29.6602 | +0.4422 | +1.51% | 5 / 5 |
| Untraced wall ms | 9.4549 | 9.1941 | -0.2608 | -2.76% | 5 / 5 |
| Traced lifecycle main-isolate promoted bytes | 2,272,486.4 | 2,140,792.0 | -131,694.4 | -5.80% | 5 / 5 |
| Traced lifecycle all-thread promoted bytes | 11,673,027.2 | 12,102,032.0 | +429,004.8 | +3.68% | 5 / 5 |

Owner allocation improved in all five pairs; retained owner bytes fell 91.9%. Untraced process CPU was effectively neutral (+0.4422 ms/workload, +0.00691 ms/recorder). The separate forced-collection lifecycle pass showed main-isolate promotion −5.8%, but all-thread promotion +3.7%; both are reported, without claiming a whole-Gateway promotion improvement. This is a net-deletion retention improvement, not a throughput or latency claim.

<details><summary>Individual samples and GC counts/maxima</summary>

| Pair | Owner survivor bytes B → C | Owner allocated bytes B → C | Untraced CPU ms B → C | Untraced wall ms B → C | Main promoted bytes B → C | All-thread promoted bytes B → C |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 136,792 → 15,216 | 8,154,416 → 8,009,184 | 27.061 → 28.790 | 9.358 → 9.231 | 2,273,560 → 2,145,616 | 11,372,488 → 12,945,536 |
| 2 | 151,104 → 12,976 | 8,364,488 → 8,034,824 | 30.253 → 29.786 | 9.562 → 9.151 | 2,273,008 → 2,143,400 | 12,729,624 → 12,151,848 |
| 3 | 144,736 → 7,456 | 8,207,896 → 7,824,152 | 28.697 → 30.693 | 9.499 → 9.237 | 2,271,192 → 2,123,696 | 11,685,520 → 13,086,040 |
| 4 | 139,600 → 8,696 | 8,137,920 → 7,807,792 | 32.038 → 28.036 | 9.512 → 9.185 | 2,271,104 → 2,145,712 | 11,220,512 → 11,098,840 |
| 5 | 136,832 → 13,192 | 8,400,880 → 7,856,512 | 28.041 → 30.996 | 9.343 → 9.167 | 2,273,568 → 2,145,536 | 11,356,992 → 11,227,896 |

Untraced main-isolate natural GC: **zero observed collections, 0 ms total, no observed maximum** in every sample on both sides. These short owner windows cannot establish natural GC tail behavior; no p95/p99 or event-loop claim is made. `process.cpuUsage()` includes workers; the GC observer is main-isolate-only.

The following is **traced capture-through-flush/forced-GC context**, including every worker collection between the markers. It is not used as an untraced timing gate. Each process includes exactly three forced main-isolate major collections.

| Pair | All-thread collections B → C | Maximum single pause ms B → C |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 18 → 20 | 25.833 → 31.019 |
| 2 | 20 → 19 | 29.176 → 30.388 |
| 3 | 18 → 20 | 29.996 → 31.206 |
| 4 | 18 → 18 | 28.890 → 27.693 |
| 5 | 18 → 18 | 28.108 → 30.016 |

| Traced GC kind, all five processes | Collections B → C | Total ms B → C | Maximum ms B → C |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Minor | 76 → 77 | 45.394 → 56.838 | 1.720 → 8.013 |
| Major (includes forced) | 16 → 18 | 419.555 → 444.193 | 29.996 → 31.206 |

Survivor sampling produced 218–242 profile samples/process on baseline and 200–258 on candidate; allocation sampling produced 17,129–17,402 and 16,984–17,168 respectively. These are profile-wide sample counts, not GC counts. Candidate serialization-stack survivors were 0–2,112 bytes (mean 844.8), versus zero in these baseline samples; stack attribution includes helper allocations and is not proof of live event strings. The separate baseline heap snapshot found no event JSON strings. Initial harness setup failures (a module-frame-retained final fixture and an anonymous TSX stack-name mismatch) were repaired before valid comparisons. A queued earlier comparison was canceled before producing any samples to align timing with GC-notification drain.

</details>

### Requested residual checks on already-fixed owners

One current-source process per existing script/stage; no changes to those owners and no new before/after claim:

| Owner | Work count | Current residual |
|---|---|---|
| System-prompt report (#183010) | 200 retained reports × 80 skills | 3,099,496 retained bytes (15,497/report); 35,336 bytes after releasing reports; detached-catalog assertion passed |
| Replay normalization (#183011) | 200 attempts × 1,001 presented messages | 15,068,336 harness-sampled allocation bytes; 503,864 final heap bytes above warm; 199,000 reused prior-output messages/content arrays; 10,000 transformed references relative to input |
| Image sanitation (#183011) | 200 attempts × 1,001 presented messages | 26,850,456 harness-sampled allocation bytes; 1,059,016 final heap bytes above warm; 199,000 reused prior-output messages/content arrays; zero copied messages/content arrays |

Residual allocation profiles had 6,743 (normalization) and 17,925 (images) samples. These scripts include their own input-array/verification work, so their allocation totals are context, not attribution solely to the named function. No natural main-isolate GC occurred in either measured residual loop. No tail comparison is inferred from these single runs.

### Checks and review

151 focused tests passed: credential redaction plus runtime/tool-definition tests (37), runtime store writer (15), deferred lifecycle owner (17), provider-error public consumer (43), transport consumer (17), and eager-import/PR-wrapper closure (22). Changed-file formatting/lint, targeted `tsgo:scripts`, export-name collision guard, and `git diff --check` passed. PR CI's exact-head aggregate, dependency review, and security-sensitive review are green. An initial PR-body Evidence-heading failure passed after correcting the body; no CI rerun was requested. No Testbox lease was used.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): production and benchmark each received clean fresh reviews after addressing fixture lifetime, scope, and timing-window findings. The configured autoreview route refused to start; no configuration was changed. The GitHub fixture-lifetime finding is fixed by `recordPreparations()` returning before collection.

After deployment, the lead should look for disappearance of `createDiagnosticRecord`/`WeakSet.add` projection allocations and reduced post-flush trajectory-owner retention. Pending event lines should still exist until turn completion. No live production profile or whole-Gateway speed/GC result is claimed; production workload impact remains to be confirmed by the lead's matched-phase profile.
