prs.title: feat(memory): read sections by heading
prs.body:
Related: #173706

## What Problem This Solves

Agents that know a Markdown memory section by name currently need to discover its source line range before reading it, which can leave nearby conditions or exceptions out of a bounded excerpt.

## User Impact

Users can ask for a named section such as "Refunds" and receive its child "Exceptions" section too, within existing excerpt budgets and with accurate source line numbers. No configuration or migration is required, and reads without `heading` are unchanged.

First version: unique, exact ATX heading text (`#` through `######`); memory corpus only. Missing/duplicate headings fail explicitly instead of guessing. Other heading styles and wiki/all reads remain available through the existing line-based interface.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds optional `heading` to the existing memory-core tool and selects the section in the existing authorized memory reader. Child sections are preserved; headings inside fenced examples, HTML literal blocks, list/quote containers, and complete leading frontmatter are ignored, and the next same-or-higher-level heading ends the section. Keep `heading` with an absolute `from: nextFrom` for bounded continuation; offsets outside the section are rejected.

No new tool, index, database schema, permission, dependency, or configuration switch. The heading-aware retrieval idea is adapted from Orca, not a transfer of its application data or runtime.

### October 18 review repairs

- Container-prefixed fences now retain list indentation and quote prefixes through their closing fence or enclosing-container boundary. Coverage includes bullet/numbered lists, quotes, nested list/quote fences, and container exits.
- A first-line BOM is ignored only during heading recognition; original excerpt bytes and source line numbers remain intact.
- A leading `---` is excluded as frontmatter only when a closing delimiter exists. A horizontal rule without a close no longer hides the rest of the file.

## Evidence

### Follow-up review verification (2026-10-25)

Rechecked review comments `4357906127` (compact `># Quoted`) and `4357906142` (ordered delimiter `10.` → `2)`) on unchanged head `3455b524afb7a454d3796000efd5e77f03dca671`. Neither reported failure reproduced. Independent CommonMark parsing agrees with the production selector: the contained headings are excluded, and appending a real top-level `## Refunds` selects only `from:5, lines:2, text:"## Refunds\nReal policy"`, without ambiguity.

Fresh **shipped Gateway `POST /tools/invoke` proof: 15/15 scenarios passed in 6.358s** (the previous 10 scenarios plus five focused review controls). The original compact example also correctly excludes `Quoted`. All authenticated requests returned HTTP 200; unauthenticated access returned 401. Captured results include actual synthetic text and source ranges. Source/fixture hashes remained unchanged; the isolated Gateway and listener stopped, and temporary synthetic state was removed. Fresh task-only authentication only: no credential inheritance, private data, real account authorization, or model inference requests.

These are evidence-backed responses to the two comments, not additional production changes. Existing CodeQL annotation still requires maintainer triage; this run does not resolve or dismiss it.

Captured current-head review controls:

```json
{"fixture":"compact.md","heading":"Refunds","httpStatus":200,"status":"error","code":"MEMORY_HEADING_NOT_FOUND","text":""}
{"fixture":"compact.md","heading":"Quoted","httpStatus":200,"status":"error","code":"MEMORY_HEADING_NOT_FOUND","text":""}
{"fixture":"compact-real.md","heading":"Refunds","httpStatus":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\nReal policy","path":"memory/compact-real.md","from":5,"lines":2}
{"fixture":"changed.md","heading":"Refunds","httpStatus":200,"status":"error","code":"MEMORY_HEADING_NOT_FOUND","text":""}
{"fixture":"changed-real.md","heading":"Refunds","httpStatus":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\nReal policy","path":"memory/changed-real.md","from":5,"lines":2}
```


### Current review repair (3455b524afb7a454d3796000efd5e77f03dca671)

Addresses both new hosted P2 findings on `ed9f7df682`:

- Ordered-list siblings with non-1 markers rebuild their own container indentation before lazy-paragraph handling. Narrower/wider markers and both `.` / `)` delimiters are covered; nested heading-shaped text cannot create ambiguity or terminate the selected top-level section.
- Frontmatter follows the repository canonical delimiter contract: an optional opening BOM, column-zero `---` delimiters and trailing whitespace. Indented thematic breaks are ordinary Markdown, and `...` is not a canonical close. Source bytes, CRLF, line numbers and bounded continuation remain unchanged.

Current frozen-candidate execution uses task-only official Node 24.22.1:

- **157/157 focused tests across four files** (94 shaping, 32 authorized-reader/compatibility, 31 tool-contract; three shards, 65.81s). The original seven new boundary cases were red before repair. The additional canonical-closing regression was independently red (1 failed /93 passed) before its repair and now passes with all 94 shaping cases.
- Strict targeted types, typed lint, explicit formatting and diff checks pass.
- **8/8 current production tool-composition assertions pass** on isolated fictional files through the actual authorized reader. This is not a Gateway/model E2E or real-account test.
- Fresh independent P0-P2 review of the exact fully staged public candidate and canonical reader/frontmatter context is complete and scoped-clean. The reviewer did not execute tests; execution evidence is separate above.

### Current-head shipped Gateway proof (same `3455b524af`)

The standard complete `pnpm build` passed on Node24.22.1 in170.6s, without skipping build guards. The first sandboxed attempt failed on public npm DNS resolution; the same normal build succeeded with network access, not with relaxed checks.

Started the freshly built official `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --bind loopback --port <task-only-port>` in a fresh isolated home/config/state/workspace. Only Memory Core and `memory_get` were enabled for these calls; no provider credentials were inherited, no model request or real-account authorization was made. The real Gateway readiness check succeeded. A freshly generated task-only bearer was required: an unauthenticated tool call returned401. The token value, addresses, ports, raw logs and machine paths are not published.

**10/10 actual HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` scenarios passed in6.125s**, covering changing ordered-list sibling widths, indented thematic breaks, BOM/CRLF and the canonical frontmatter close, HTML-comment boundaries including `--!>`, continuation-line fence exits, bounded paging/continuation and non-memory path refusal. These are captured actual `result.details` values after exact assertions, not reconstructed expected output:

```json
{"fixture":"ordered.md","heading":"Refunds","httpStatus":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\n10. item\n2. note\n   ## Shipping\n   Example only\n","path":"memory/ordered.md","from":1,"lines":6}
{"fixture":"ordered.md","heading":"Shipping","httpStatus":200,"status":"error","code":"MEMORY_HEADING_NOT_FOUND","text":""}
{"fixture":"indented.md","heading":"Refunds","httpStatus":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\n30 days\n---","path":"memory/indented.md","from":2,"lines":3}
{"fixture":"frontmatter.md","heading":"Refunds","httpStatus":200,"status":"ok","text":"# Refunds\r\nBody\r","path":"memory/frontmatter.md","from":6,"lines":2}
{"fixture":"comment.md","heading":"Refunds","httpStatus":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\n30 days\n<!--\n--!>\n## Shipping\n-->\nMore refund details","path":"memory/comment.md","from":1,"lines":7}
{"fixture":"comment.md","heading":"Shipping","httpStatus":200,"status":"error","code":"MEMORY_HEADING_NOT_FOUND","text":""}
{"fixture":"fence.md","heading":"Refunds","httpStatus":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\n30 days\nCustom excluded","path":"memory/fence.md","from":6,"lines":3}
{"fixture":"fence.md","httpStatus":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\n30 days\n\n[More content available. Use from=8 to continue.]","path":"memory/fence.md","from":6,"lines":2,"truncated":true,"nextFrom":8}
{"fixture":"fence.md","heading":"Refunds","httpStatus":200,"status":"ok","text":"Custom excluded","path":"memory/fence.md","from":8,"lines":1}
{"fixture":"non-memory path","httpStatus":200,"status":"error","code":"MEMORY_PATH_NOT_ALLOWED","text":""}
```

All five fictional memory files and all eight contribution source files retained identical SHA-256 values after the run. The task-owned Gateway was stopped and its listener verified closed; temporary fictional configuration/state/data was removed. This is the real built Gateway tool boundary, not an installed release, mock Gateway or model-generated response.

Binding hashes: reader source `65a788de7d05b4624113423587efe3c2b1414e771f86390db50ff8a1f7a6073a`; official launcher `17aef9acdbe968fc07fa80685319c6fe974e019a89e0d657042b10129bc7ea51`; built entry `38c6371db5a2cdf22f6c315f7722fe9decd3dc6e7697546c875b7918b093a8cd`.

CodeQL's `js/bad-tag-filter` finding was investigated, not suppressed or dismissed. This routine selects raw Markdown source and is not an HTML filter/sanitizer. [CommonMark 0.31.2 type-2 HTML blocks](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#html-blocks) end at literal `-->`; the browser-only `--!>` behavior discussed in [the CodeQL sanitizer query](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/javascript/js-bad-tag-filter/) must not change Markdown section boundaries. Two negative fixtures and an already-installed CommonMark oracle confirm the distinction. An explanatory contract comment was added; maintainer triage of the alert remains necessary if it is a merge gate. No security check or CI gate was disabled.

Only the two existing parser-owner files changed in this repair. No private data, real credentials, new dependency or real-account authorization was used. GitHub CI and hosted review must assess this new head separately.

### Previous October 23 current-main repair (ed9f7df6826325e55ca70039db70900831bb6517)

Integrated fixed main `e39c150d7b9054a19d57f0d7b0613a4493978ceb` and repaired both current hosted P2 findings: list-continuation headings are not selectable and cannot terminate a section; fences opened on list-continuation lines inherit their container and stop at its actual boundary. Additional independently reproduced regressions cover lazy paragraph continuation, thematic breaks versus list markers, empty items, non-1 ordered text in paragraphs, tab/indent padding, and literal HTML blocks containing heading-shaped text.

Fences and HTML now share one private literal-block state in the existing reader; original source bytes, line numbers, authorization and excerpt/continuation budgets are retained. No new dependency, renderer policy, parallel parser service or configuration was introduced. This is bounded ATX-section selection, not a claim to implement every Markdown extension.

Current frozen candidate evidence:

- **145 focused tests passed across 4 files** in one frozen-byte run (82 shaping, 32 authorized-reader/compatibility, 31 tool-contract cases; 3 Vitest shards, 34.24s). The 16 added HTML cases failed against the preceding parser before this repair and now pass.
- Strict targeted types, typed lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Small dev-only comparisons against the already-installed CommonMark oracle found 0 mismatches in 2,160 synthetic HTML heading/range checks; the oracle is not a new production dependency or a full-spec certification.
- **8/8 production tool-composition assertions pass** through `createMemoryGetTool -> readAgentMemoryFile -> readMemoryFile` using isolated fictional files, including a commented fake Shipping heading, precise source ranges, bounded continuation and denied non-memory paths. This is not a new Gateway E2E or model-generated response.
- Fresh independent P0-P2 review of the exact public candidate and complete reader context: **scoped-clean**, complete assessment, no actionable findings. The reviewer did not execute the test suite; execution evidence above is separate.
- The existing real-manager fixture fails in `beforeAll` on an offline sqlite-maintenance lease in this local environment. A separate clean checkout of the same fixed main reproduces the same signature before exercising the feature. No database ownership guard was bypassed; those skipped tests are not counted as passing. This does not assert upstream GitHub CI is failing.

Only the public contribution and fictional tests are included. No private Orca material, existing user configuration, real logs, credentials or real-account authorization was used. Maintainer edits remain disabled. Feature acceptance remains a human maintainer decision.

### Earlier October 18 evidence (not a fresh current-head run)

### Regression, checks, and independent review

- On the original `5daa50b` implementation, the three reported examples each failed with `MEMORY_HEADING_NOT_FOUND` (3 failed / 22 passed in the initial augmented result-shaping suite).
- After repair: **59 focused tests passed across 3 files**: result shaping, authorized file reader, and real `memory_get`/manager integration. Wrapper wall time 93.04s, including fresh worker compilation; the existing manager suite took 79.65s (new heading feature case 41ms). Prior-head evidence also includes 28 passing tool-contract tests; those are not counted as fresh repair-head runs.
- Targeted lint, formatting, core production typecheck, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets passed. The official source CLI completed its runtime build successfully before the live Gateway check below. Broad suites and full test-typecheck matrices remain PR CI's responsibility.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of this repair: **scoped-clean at P0-P2**, with the complete result-shaping source supplied as context. No accepted/actionable findings. The review itself did not execute project code; the test and Gateway evidence are separate.
- Simplification: retain the existing reader, authorization, and truncation owners. This repair changes two existing files: production +37/-19, tests +45/-0. No new state or exports.

### Earlier built Gateway evidence (prior repair head, not rerun for October 23)

Launched the official `pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --auth none --port <claimed-test-port>` with a fresh task-only state directory, configuration, workspace, and a credential-free environment. Only `memory-core` was enabled and only `memory_get` was allowlisted. No existing Gateway was changed or restarted. The task-owned Gateway was stopped and its port claim released afterward.

The built Gateway's actual `POST /tools/invoke` endpoint received:

```json
{"tool":"memory_get","agentId":"main","args":{"path":"memory/store-policy.md","heading":"Refunds"}}
```

The synthetic source includes a list-prefixed fenced example before Refunds, an Exceptions child, and a following Shipping section. Selected terminal output (JSON-escaped):

```json
{"case":"section-and-child","http":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\nRefunds are available within 30 days.\n### Exceptions\nCustom items are excluded.","path":"memory/store-policy.md","from":6,"lines":4}
{"case":"bounded-first-page","http":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\nRefunds are available within 30 days.\n\n[More content available. Use from=8 to continue.]","path":"memory/store-policy.md","from":6,"lines":2,"truncated":true,"nextFrom":8}
{"case":"bounded-continuation","http":200,"status":"ok","text":"### Exceptions\nCustom items are excluded.","path":"memory/store-policy.md","from":8,"lines":2}
{"case":"leading-BOM-preserved","http":200,"status":"ok","text":"\uFEFF## Refunds\n30 days","path":"memory/bom.md","from":1,"lines":2}
{"case":"horizontal-rule-not-frontmatter","http":200,"status":"ok","text":"## Refunds\n30 days","path":"memory/rule.md","from":3,"lines":2}
{"case":"authorization-unchanged","http":200,"path":"private.md","text":"","status":"error","code":"MEMORY_PATH_NOT_ALLOWED","error":"path is not an allowed Markdown memory file"}
```

All six calls passed independent assertions. Shipping never appeared in the selected section or its continuation. The denied `private.md` file is also a synthetic fixture inside the temporary workspace, not a personal file.

Runtime reader SHA-256: `02e270cc0efa2545ae083e02063cf10154d7f85016265d2dc8159eea94fc7553`. This binds the compiled working-tree proof to the source bytes committed in this repair. The capture does not claim a released version or an authenticated model-generated agent response: it proves the real public Gateway tool-invocation boundary without tool/provider mocks or external model calls.

### Privacy and remaining decision

All documents and state used above are synthetic. No personal notes, existing configuration, OAuth profiles, credentials, IP addresses, non-public endpoints, or raw operator logs are included in this PR or proof. Maintainer edits remain disabled because workflow/secrets access on the fork has not been authorized.

This remains a new optional capability. Maintainer product acceptance is still required; the repair and runtime proof do not substitute for that decision. The previous CI pass belongs to `5daa50b`; the new repair head requires its own CI and hosted re-review.

prs.title: refactor(agents): use one MCP refresh deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MCP token refresh starts a 30-second exchange deadline before dispatch, passes its signal into both fetch and the response reader, then gives that reader another 30-second timeout. The second timer cannot extend the earlier deadline.

## User Impact

Keep the existing request deadline and timeout recovery behavior while removing one redundant timer per token refresh. Ordinary chat turns without a token refresh remove zero timers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let the existing exchange deadline own cancellation. The response reader still races the supplied signal, cancels pending stream reads and releases its reader. Credential lease checks, current-authority checks, response size limits, durable refresh claims and uncertain-outcome fencing are unchanged. No SQL statements, transaction shapes, schema, identity mapping or SDK exports change.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, registered before measurement: exercise a synthetic MCP refresh through the real SDK and credential owner, including a body that never completes. Cancellation must settle the read, cancel the stream and retain the uncertain-refresh fence without replaying the token grant. Timer count by source attribution falls from two to one per refresh. Run one frozen v3.1.4 baseline/candidate Gateway workload pair on the same platform, ten warm turns per revision and cold/restart separate, using `--repetitions 1 --idle-seconds 0 --settle-seconds 0`. Any attributed SQL or request increase, or any warm MAIN increase, stops the change. No latency/CPU-speed claim; any 20% raw movement requires attribution and disposition.

prs.title: fix(backup): older archives with hardlinks cannot be verified or restored
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw backup verify` and `backup restore` reject valid older backup archives whose hardlink targets are stored relative to the archived source directory instead of the archive root.

## User Impact

Older backups with legacy hardlinks verify and restore again; restored files keep their shared inode. Archives where the legacy target is missing or ambiguous still fail with a clear error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The verifier only recognized fully qualified or archive-root-prefixed hardlink targets. It now keeps that lookup precedence, then resolves an unqualified legacy target against the hardlink entry's ancestors inside the archive, accepting exactly one matching regular file and rejecting missing or ambiguous candidates. Restore keeps consuming the verifier's target map, so there is still a single resolver. The backup CLI docs describe the recovery behavior.

This finishes @zhangguiping-xydt's contributor fix (original commit preserved); the maintainer follow-up is documentation only. Production LOC +27/-5; tests +131/-0; docs +4/-0. No schema, dependency, SDK, or config change.

## Evidence

- Red on the contributor's parent: `src/commands/backup-legacy-hardlinks.test.ts` failed 2 of 6 (valid legacy targets rejected; ambiguity not classified).
- Green: `backup-legacy-hardlinks`, `backup-verify` and `backup-restore` suites passed 57 tests (1 skipped), using real compressed tar fixtures for legacy resolution, precedence, restore bytes and shared inode, missing, ambiguous, and non-file targets.
- Built CLI at the pushed head, isolated synthetic state: legacy `backup verify` and `backup restore` exited 0 with matching bytes and inode; ambiguous and missing-target archives exited 1.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, format, `git diff --check`, and an independent review passed with no actionable findings.
- Gap: this does not claim to fix the separately reported Linux `backup create --verify` exit 13 / truncated temporary archive. A 2 GiB `backup create --verify` on macOS passed (exit 0, `verified: true`) but Linux wasn't reproduced, so the issue stays open for that part.

Related: #89257

The SDK continues to reject malformed tool, resource and prompt entries before the collector receives a page.

prs.title: perf(workboard): fuse conditional card-write admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Accepted conditional Workboard card writes read the card predicate and board kind separately before updating the parent and twelve child collections. Every successful create or revision-checked update pays for an unnecessary SQL statement.

The persistence owner now combines those reads into one dialect-neutral admission query inside the existing write transaction. A rejected predicate returns before any parent or child write, and still precedes the Sessions-board error. Successful admission keeps the existing parent upsert, child replacements, rollback, and PostgreSQL advisory-lock custody. Supplied-key semantics, absent boards, and deferred payload binding are preserved. There is no new cache, schema, worker request, or main-thread database work.

Production is +7 lines overall: the two caller-side admission paths disappear, while the existing writer gains the conditional query and result. The separate revision predicate remains for conditional deletion. The added regression checks full child postimages, not only return values.

## Evidence

The acceptance rule was committed and published before the first measurement: remove one statement per accepted conditional write; reject without child writes; preserve contents, error order, rollback, worker requests, and MAIN counts. The real flow is one synthetic board, twenty cards, one WebSocket client, twenty warm-read waves and twenty accepted update/readback waves, at a 250 ms interval. Baseline production: `6113057491a29b36239ae8f9400617fb1e47729a`.

The committed workload is `scripts/perf/workboard-read-measure.ts` at `4a90e314b7cbaa0fd23e96da1e7574e249ba5e4a`, with `--boards 1 --cards 20 --clients 1 --waves 20 --interval-ms 250`, separate `--prepare`, and fresh synthetic state. prs.title: perf(gateway): reuse cron-owned heartbeat summaries in health
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Subscribed Gateway health refreshes reread cron's proactive receipts and selected jobs even when the live cron owner has not changed.

## User Impact

Health keeps the same heartbeat summaries while avoiding repeated database work between cron writes. Initial, changed-config, and invalidated reads retain the durable reader and its errors.

The matched full-cron comparison is complete. This draft remains blocked on attribution of the targeted cold MAIN increase and final repaired-head static checks. Contributor PR #89526 closed unmerged, so its former conflict hold no longer applies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron owner retains one successful heartbeat summary keyed by config object identity and the existing committed store revision. Health obtains the currently published owner. Before lazy loading, it uses the unchanged durable reader. Stop clears the result; failed and write-overtaken reads are not retained. The legacy monitor shares the same reader without exposing its Map or introducing a readiness state machine.

SDK writes already publish the store revision without emitting cron events, so event-only invalidation would miss them. The one producer repair publishes the existing revision when provisioning's worker reply is lost after a possible commit. No SQL text, schema, transaction ordering, or public API changes.

The memo is process-local. Offline/Doctor writers need exclusive custody and their changes are adopted on restart. A diagnostic response already in flight may finish across a config transition; the next refresh uses the current owner. Production changes are +33 net lines; the existing state types move to the contract module with all consumers migrated and the old exports removed.

## Evidence

### Acceptance rule (registered before first run)

Flow: one signed, subscribed WebSocket client on an isolated Gateway, with three synthetic agents/sessions, primary and converted proactive jobs, an absent receipt target, and an ordinary job. Workload: committed `scripts/perf/health-cron-fixture.ts` plus existing `scripts/perf/idle-gateway-measure.ts --subscribe --minutes 2 --settle-seconds 10`, frozen SQL observer and per-thread CPU profiles.

Count all-thread SQL statements, worker requests, and MAIN per steady minute; keep cold boot separate. Baseline must reproduce the receipt/job reader. Candidate must remove that reader from unchanged steady health refreshes while retaining initial/invalidation reads and primary-job precedence. Expected saving per refresh: one worker request, three receipt SELECTs, one selected-jobs SELECT, and the read transaction envelope. Actual observed counts decide. No warm statement/request/MAIN regression is accepted.

Use alternating baseline/candidate runs: three pairs when load <64 and internal free >=12 GiB; otherwise one pair with source-attributed limits. General frozen workload checks warm-turn non-regression. Timing claims require the campaign timing lock, load <24, at least five interleaved samples per side, and median/p95/range. Loaded-host counts/profiles are not latency evidence. Any 20% user-facing regression stops the change.

### Current validation

Baseline reproduced the target in both steady minutes: three receipt SELECTs, one selected-jobs SELECT, BEGIN/COMMIT, and one worker request per refresh. Those six statements and that request are absent from both candidate steady minutes. Total minute counts were 8/2/0 and 14/5/0 → 1/1/0 and 7/4/0 (SQL/requests/MAIN), including unrelated maintenance. The seventh raw statement reduction per minute is unrelated maintenance and is not claimed as this change's saving.

This is one loaded-host baseline/candidate pair with two one-minute windows per side. Steady medians [min–max] are SQL 11 [8–14] → 4 [1–7], requests 3.5 [2–5] → 2.5 [1–4], and MAIN 0 → 0. With two windows, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum and does not establish a tail-latency result. Each side has 24 thread profiles; profiles and counts establish no latency improvement. The candidate boot/settle windows show extra lease/diagnostic work (MAIN 92+8 → 93+16); that adverse cold result is retained, not described as a startup improvement. The completed general frozen pair and its adverse cells are reported below.

The frozen v3.1.4 general synthetic workload completed successfully on both heads, including cron execution, compaction, and restart. Whole-workload SQL/requests/MAIN were **3037/803/95 → 2972/795/95**. Across ten warm windows, SQL median/p95/range were **51/70/[50–70] → 50/74/[50–74]**; requests were **12/18/[12–18] → 12/20/[12–20]**; MAIN remained zero. This is one loaded-host pair, not qualified latency evidence or unconditional non-regression.

| Raw phase (SQL/requests/MAIN) | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First warm turn | 61/16/0 | 74/20/0 |
| Compaction | 103/20/0 | 134/21/0 |
| Initial boot | 310/101/48 | 547/133/49 |
| Restart connect | 20/9/0 | 29/15/0 |
| Connected idle | 87/30/0 | 92/35/0 |

The performance coordinator accepted these adverse phase cells as placement effects after reviewing the lower whole-run totals and the operation attribution below. The small actual whole-workload increases remain disclosed; the separate targeted cold MAIN comparison is still pending. Captured operation stacks attribute first-warm-turn growth to background work with identical whole-run counts: unknown mapped requests (+11 SQL/+5 requests in the window), plugin metadata refresh (+9/+1), and upstream-watch read (+1/+1). Compaction moves schema admission (45→69 SQL in-window), memory WAL setup (0→6), and projection (0→3), each with unchanged whole-run counts. Boot moves 181 agent-worker-opening statements into that phase; whole-run opening stays 181 SQL/two requests. Restart-connect changes likewise preserve whole-run counts for its changed operations.

There are also small actual whole-workload increases, not just phase relocation: memory-source inspection **2/2→4/4**, plugin model catalog **4/4→5/5**, session entry list **26/9→29/12**, target inventory **2/8→0/9**, and usage cost **19/5→21/5** (SQL/requests). Their captured stacks point to unchanged background owners; this does not by itself prove a cause or waive them. Shared exact-entry, actor-hydration, row-fact, model-context, and projection-snapshot families retain whole-run counts. The target heartbeat operation falls **39/13→18/6**, including **15/5→0/0** during five-minute idle. This accepted count disposition does not waive the targeted cold MAIN hold or establish a timing/tail improvement. If a production correction is needed, one new general pair is required on that corrected head.

Two regressions failed on the base for the expected reasons: repeated real-kernel health reads and a committed provisioning write with a lost worker reply. Candidate coverage includes successful/empty reuse, SDK invalidation, config/partition changes, write-overtaken reads, failures, stop/restart, and lazy fallback.

The full original cron file was run ten times in alternating baseline/candidate order, with unchanged assertions and deadlines and the same real-prewarm fixture on both arms. Each side completed five runs: baseline **73 passed / 2 failed**, candidate **74 passed / 1 failed**; both had four completely clean runs. The shared failure was the failure-alert case's final active-root count (expected zero, observed two). Baseline failure-only diagnostics identified `session:event (2)`; delivery and persistence assertions had already passed. The already-running `cron.run` RPC timeout occurred once on baseline and never on candidate. The coordinator accepted these results and assigned the inherited root/timeout flake to the separate CRONFLAKE lane (#183131); it is not changed here. An identical temporary failure-only diagnostic on both arms was never committed. One baseline result was recovered from its original complete test JSON plus the wrapper's success output; its exact final host-load sample was unavailable. All case outcomes are retained, and no completed arm was replayed.

Earlier candidate runs had finished-event/RPC timeouts. A deterministic owner diagnostic held revision publication after a terminal database commit: the candidate deliberately served its prior summary, baseline served the committed status, and both emitted the finished broadcast. Thus the proposed stale-summary suppression did not reproduce. The final 5+5 comparison above supersedes the earlier unmatched runs. Three test-fixture lines invoke the existing real reply-runtime prewarm that production already performs; no assertion, wait, deadline, or production delivery behavior changed.

Two independent Codex reviews completed without actionable findings, followed by clean reviews of the prewarm fixture and CI-forced repair delta. The latter moves the identical `DeferredHookWake` type into a leaf contract with all eight consumers migrated, registers the standalone workload with Knip, and corrects the selected-store regression to use machine state. The reviewer lacked unchanged consumer context; a repository-wide reference search confirmed the complete cutover. Runtime expressions and SQL remain unchanged by these repairs. PostgreSQL source review was carried forward to `ba43501d30f8`; Final head `67e963fe00ed` contains those repairs; exact-head static CI [40155165800](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40155165800) and PostgreSQL carry-forward remain pending. Published-driver update run [40152567800](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40152567800) passed, including package integrity, npm install acceptance, and the targeted Docker update lane.

The prior 18-PR overlap audit found no added conflicts. The CI-forced type move and Knip entry expand the touched-file set; the refreshed full overlap comparison is pending on final head `67e963fe00ed`. Contributor #89526 is closed unmerged.

### Matched cold comparison

Integrated main: `5281dc3a72b1`. Baseline `21f87046274f` includes that source, the committed synthetic workload, and the same real-prewarm fixture as candidate `ba43501d30f8`, with the health-summary production change absent. The full-cron A/B results above use these heads.

The earlier targeted fixture cold MAIN increase remains **unaccepted and blocking**: whole 105→114, including settle 8→16 and boot 92→93. A serialized comparison on these matched heads is queued to retain normalized SQL call stacks for every MAIN statement. It will distinguish existing lease checks from a new owner-load effect. Prior phase-placement acceptance covered the general workload only. The new injection and lazy getter are passive by source inspection; that alone does not waive the runtime hold.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three owners asked the database for a fact their next write already reports. Pairing redemption now consumes and returns the join-code row in one dialect-generated DELETE RETURNING. Selected capture deletion reports the two DELETE changes counts inside the existing transaction. Progress overflow pruning embeds the ordered cutoff query in the DELETE.

All pairing authority and validation checks remain: success, missing and expired response bytes, rate-limit error precedence, expired/malformed code consumption, and concurrent single use. Capture still deletes event metadata before session metadata, preserves shared blobs, and removes legacy files only after commit. Progress keeps its 200,000-row cap, 1,024-row prune batch, sequence ordering and affected-row cache update. No schema, public API, cache, worker-routing or cross-store commit change.

## Preregistered acceptance (before first run)

Base: 285029f87941081e3c46f78b8bc77c29f59d587f. Committed rule: scripts/perf/sql-probe.md.

Synthetic initialized-owner counts must change: join-code consume 3→2 table statements for present/missing/expired outcomes; selected capture deletion removes exactly two COUNTs per nonempty ID request; overflow progress append 5→4 table statements. Worker requests and main-thread work must not increase. Deterministic count regressions must fail on base, pass on candidate; outcome tests pass on both. Keep rollback, single-use, malformed row and exact HTTP response/error precedence tests.

Use isolated Gateway with real transport, frozen observer and three alternating baseline/candidate warm control pairs when admission load is below 64 (otherwise one pair under the loaded-host rule), with five warm target actions per arm; separate cold/warm. Report median/p95/range for repeated actions, statement/request/MAIN totals and operation attribution. Profile per thread with Node. No elapsed-time claim unless timing lock/load<24 and ≥5 interleaved samples per arm. Investigate each ≥20% increase; no 'within spread' exception. PostgreSQL conformance and exact-head review are required before landing.

## Evidence

The deterministic regressions failed on unchanged production only on the intended counts; the outcome and retained-state assertions passed. Candidate native capture, progress, real HTTP pairing, worker and async-consumer tests pass (53 tests; one PostgreSQL-only case skipped). SQLite and PostgreSQL join outcomes, PostgreSQL shared-blob deletion and progress retention pass (10 passed, the PostgreSQL-only capture case skipped for the SQLite half). Both independent Codex reviews found no actionable P0–P2 defects; the second covered the complete production patch.

## What Problem This Solves

Archived-result reads pulled the agent database writer dependency graph into the archive worker. Only the separate transcript worker's archive-presence check needs that retained lifecycle. The final/page readers already open and close their own fresh read-only handles.

## User Impact

Five paired runs reduce forced-GC retained archive-worker heap by **15.8 MiB (26.1%) after final-result reads**, and **5.3 MiB (8.1%) after paging**. Warm request latency and CPU are essentially unchanged. Archive contents, selection, identity validation, and cleanup retain their existing contracts; no configuration or storage migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Load the presence helper's database dependency when that helper is called, await its sole caller, and import the transcript decoder from its read-only owner. Identity validation still happens after the await and before the read. No cache, duplicate implementation, or new lifecycle owner. Production LOC: **+2 net**; the async import and ownership comment avoid a new module or cache.

## Evidence

The committed benchmark exercises the real archive worker and its database-admission exchange on Node 26.12.1 with 64 prepared archives × 100 synthetic messages. Five concurrent pairs use counterbalanced launch order, swapped interleaved CPUs, synchronized warm starts, and identical prepared fixtures. Each side runs 1,000 final-result reads and 1,000 page reads per pair; every reply is checked. Forced collections stay outside timed windows. Snapshot exploration is separate from timing. All five untraced and five traced pairs completed without a guard interruption.

Measurement base: `5281dc3a72b1016ee33b0c0d76c89cc7835acd33`. Both sides use identical source-substitution/probe hooks. The production patch rebases cleanly onto current main. These are source-runtime owner measurements, not a bundled production-Gateway memory guarantee.

Cold-import tradeoff: the first final-result read improves from **1,021.7 to 313.9 ms**. The first page read *after* that final read rises from **351.7 to 715.2 ms** because it now loads imports that the final read avoided. Combined initialization improves from **1,373.4 to 1,029.1 ms**. Cold paging is faster overall, while paging after a prior final-result read still pays the deferred import cost described above.

The short final-read loop p99 is unqualified: every candidate pair has fewer than 1,000 loop samples. Its mean rises 15.62→25.51 ms and is retained below rather than omitted. prs.title: refactor: test agent guards through runtime boundaries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two agent guard tests reached private implementation declarations directly: the browser loopback suite constructed its current-authority assertion by hand, and the CLI history suite imported a private error class only for an `instanceof` check. Those imports kept internal declarations exported and allowed the browser tests to bypass the async preparation path that production actually uses.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. Browser loopback previews still require current unrestricted execution authority, abort with their admitted turn, and retire after runtime configuration changes. CLI history ownership loss still stops model fallback after one provider attempt, leaves the session entry unchanged, and reports the same error name and message.

The change affects no public API, package export, configuration, schema, persisted data, dependency, permission, or migration contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser authority cases now assemble an admitted async tool surface and obtain the loopback guard from the prepared browser context. This exercises the real live approval reader and the same preparation lifecycle used by production, while retaining the existing assembled Browser availability matrix.

The two production declarations are now private without changing their bodies or callers. The CLI test asserts the error name consumed by fallback classification instead of its private class identity, while keeping the stronger behavioral controls around message, attempt count, state preservation, and replay suppression.

## Evidence

The exact candidate tree passed remote focused proof:

- changed-file format and lint, with zero warnings or errors;
- all selected production and test type graphs;
- `src/agents/agent-tools.browser-loopback-current.e2e.test.ts`: 4/4, covering approval revocation, turn abort, runtime-config publication, and assembled Browser availability;
- `src/agents/cli-runner/history-boundary.test.ts`: 27/27, including stable error classification, one provider attempt, unchanged entry, and no fallback replay.

The production and full-tree dead-code scans no longer report either declaration. Their aggregate commands still report existing unrelated entries elsewhere in the tree; this PR does not claim those broader inventories are clean.

On exact head `a613356cce96`, the required CI gate and every selected CI, CodeQL, security, lint, type, Node, UI E2E, guard, and source-contract row passed. A fresh calibrated review concluded clean after receiving the exact remote test output; canonical autoreview and ClawSweeper also reported no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(gateway): accept short-session navigation hints
prs.body:
Fixes #183056

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI writes `__openclawSessionKey` to short session URLs while the route resolves. Reopening such a URL through the canonical public-chat or protected session-entry path rejected the whole request as an unknown query key, producing a bare `404 Not found` instead of the app shell or login handoff.

## User Impact

Reloading, restoring, or following a short Control UI session URL now keeps the existing pathname-based authentication and target instead of stranding the user on a dead-end 404. Duplicate or blank navigation hints are still rejected, and the query value is not used for authentication or session lookup.

## Why This Change Was Made

`parseControlUiSessionReturnPath()` already preserves the equivalent `__openclawSessionFacePreference` hint for the same reload window, but omitted the session-key hint emitted by `sessionNavigationTarget()`. This adds the key to the allowlist and accepts at most one nonblank value. The authenticated target remains derived from the pathname.

## Evidence

The HTTP regression now uses a real short-session UUID and asserts that the generated URL contains `__openclawSessionKey`. On the unchanged implementation it fails with `404` where `200` is expected; the protected entry test likewise never reaches `serveApp`.

After the fix, both cases pass and the complete affected gateway suites pass:

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       40 passed (40)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass. `pnpm tsgo:core` could not run on this host because the bundled `tsrs` binary requires GLIBC 2.34 while the host has an older libc; CI remains the type-check authority.

## AI Assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance under contributor direction and review.

prs.title: fix(ui): reloading a session address with the navigation hint returns 404
prs.body:
Related: #183056

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: reloading a Control UI session address returns a bare `404 Not found` when the address still carries the sidebar's `__openclawSessionKey` navigation hint.

## User Impact

User impact: a reload, tab restore, proxy re-auth redirect, or gateway restart on a session page now shows the conversation instead of a blank "Not found" page. The session itself was never lost — only the address the app had just produced for it became unloadable.

## Why This Change Was Made

In-app sidebar navigation pins the already-resolved session key on a short session route so the chat loader does not have to rediscover it from `sessions.list`. That hint goes into the in-app location only; the shareable `href` stays clean on purpose.

The gateway accepts a fixed allow-list of query parameters on a return path, so any address still carrying the hint fell through to `end(404, "Not found")` — a 9-byte body with no link, no button, and no login affordance. The clean `href` hid this until a real full page load happened.

The fix accepts the parameter, rejects duplicates, and requires the hint to describe the pathname it accompanies: same agent, and for literal routes the exact session key, for short routes a trailing session id that still carries the short ref prefix. Short refs compare through `SESSION_UUID_SUFFIX_RE`, the same suffix contract `buildControlUiSessionPath` uses, so prefixed keys like `tui-<uuid>` match the route the builder emits for them. A hint can never select or authorize a session — the pathname stays authoritative and a mismatched hint is rejected outright.

The hint is also dropped before the reader's entry URL is built, so the anonymous representation and its cache identity stay keyed on the canonical path. A private session remains indistinguishable from the canonical route for an anonymous reader.

## Evidence

`pnpm test src/gateway/control-ui-session-entry.test.ts src/gateway/control-ui-public-chat.http.test.ts` — 45 passing. New cases: a matching hint keeps the authenticated target byte-identical to the canonical path; mismatched agent, mismatched id, malformed, over-long, and duplicated hints are all rejected without reaching `authenticate`; an ordinary generated short-session address carrying the hint serves the app to an authorized client and returns the same 404 handoff document as the canonical route to an anonymous one.

`pnpm --dir ui test src/lib/sessions/route-navigation.test.ts` — 5 passing.

`pnpm run check:changed` — clean (lint 0 warnings / 0 errors, all typecheck shards passing).

Direct checks against the parser:

| Return path | Result |
| --- | --- |
| short route + matching hint (`tui-<uuid>`, `session-<uuid>`, `dashboard:<uuid>`, bare `<uuid>` keys) | accepted, `kind: "short"` |
| short route, no hint | accepted (unchanged) |
| short route + hint naming a different id | rejected |
| short route + hint naming a different agent | rejected |
| duplicated hint | rejected |
| unknown query parameter | rejected (unchanged) |
| literal route + exactly matching hint | accepted |
| literal route + hint whose id drifted | rejected |

Gap: I did not add a browser-level screenshot, since the failure and the fix are both plain document responses and the HTTP tests assert the served body directly.

prs.title: perf(gateway): park unavailable orphan workspace lookups until owner changes
prs.body:
Orphan-result recovery currently retries unavailable session/worktree lookups every minute even when only an owner publication can make them usable. This change retains typed session-entry/local managed-worktree absence in the existing startup inventory, wakes it through existing owner publications, and retries on the existing bounded minute sweep. Generic, repository and device failures retain round-robin retry.

The committed owner implementation follows the baseline reproduction; the complete five-pair proof is in progress. No schema change, durable flag, TTL, freshness probe, new timer, or per-publication database request is added. The accepted restoration delay is the next eligible minute sweep, including its existing eight-attempt budget and foreground deferral. Destructive cleanup admission and retained-ref checks stay in place.

## Acceptance registered before first run

- Flow: real isolated token-auth Gateway, bundled iMessage synthetic bridge, 2,600 indexed session slots (2,599 stored entries), 177 retained placements, 46 missing local managed worktrees, 130 entries without workspace binding, one missing session entry. Synthetic state only.
- Baseline: fresh main b688518a2f9a38afa850d6394df7722fa2d84d23 plus identical workload. Candidate: that base plus approved owner change, at most +150 net production LOC.
- Frozen observer v3.1.5, hashes verified before/after; all-thread SQL statements, worker requests and MAIN statements, per-operation shapes and orphan-resolution attempts. `node --cpu-prof` per thread. No timing or CPU improvement claim unless timing lock and load <24 qualify both arms.
- Five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs (B,C repeated five times), each fresh fixture. Keep cold boot/initial discovery, post-discovery settlement, full 180-second warm idle, restoration and shutdown separate; report median, p95 and min/max. Initial discovery is observed at the unchanged cleanup-loop boundary before warm measurement starts.
- Separate transient-control workload: one retained placement bound to an unavailable repository; five serial alternating pairs, with the same cold/180-second warm separation. Resolution attempts must continue on the existing minute sweep in both arms; no parking by error text.
- Win: classified parked warm exact-session/registry reads and resolution attempts reach zero per minute in every candidate sample. Baseline must reproduce nonzero redundant attempts/reads or this item stops. Matching session/worktree publication permits the next eligible sweep to remove a real synthetic Git cleanup ref while preserving placement identity. Initial discovery and unrelated work must remain equivalent; no new SQL shapes or MAIN work.
- Nonregression: report all SQL/requests/MAIN for every phase and whole run, restoration work included so deferral cannot masquerade as deletion. Any >=20% adverse cell stops for attribution and explicit disposition; do not label it spread. Existing scheduler wakeups remain unchanged. Cold and warm never pooled.
- Behavior proof: base-red/candidate-green parked work-count regression; matching and unrelated session/worktree events, uncertain registry outcome, publication during awaited resolution, generic retry fairness, retained refs and actual Git cleanup, subscription disposal. Focused owners/consumers, changed-file type-aware checks, Madge, Knip against base, T1/dialect ratchets and applicable PG proof before landing.

Workload command (replace output and mode per arm):

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-ingress-polling.mts \
  --orphan-recovery --idle-seconds 180 --sparse-events 0 --cpu-profile \
  --observer /path/to/frozen-v3.1.5/observer.cjs --out /path/to/isolated-output
```

Use `--orphan-transient-control` instead of `--orphan-recovery` for the independent transient control. The observation-only loader records completed cleanup-loop attempts and discovery; it does not change decisions. Expected historical 58/41/0 to 30/13/0 per 180 seconds is conditional context, not a promised or measured result for this head.

## Review gates

Exact-head PG review is required for the indirect session/registry read and identity classification change. Before/after SQL shapes and checklist answers will be posted after proof. Open-PR overlap/conflict comparisons use the shared prindex before readiness. Item 24 is explicitly excluded.

## Fixture correction registered before the replacement run

The first baseline reproduced the 180-second warm waste (58 SQL, 41 requests, zero Gateway MAIN; 24 exact-session reads and four worktree-owner reads), but its restoration target was incorrectly chosen by numeric fixture index. The owner retries placements in lexical session-ID order: polling-46 is position 118, outside the unchanged eight-minute restoration deadline after three warm sweeps. This is a fixture failure, not a complete baseline sample or a product regression.

The replacement fixture selects polling-120 (lexical position 25), an existing no-binding placement, for restoration through the same public sessions.create request. Keep the 177/46 inventory, 180-second warm interval, eight-attempt minute budget, eight-minute restoration deadline, production baseline, observer and all acceptance rules unchanged. Restart the five alternating full baseline/candidate pairs with fresh output directories; retain the first warm window only as reproduction evidence. No product retry or deadline is widened.

## Candidate validation in progress

Current head e7cbfb8f88edc5f7daebe9a003b72fa9a7228077 parks only typed unavailable cases. A dirty marker preserves publications arriving during resolution. Generic failures retain the existing bounded retry. Net production change: 150 additions / 9 deletions, +141 lines.

The original parked work-count regression is red on the production base (resolver called twice instead of once). Earlier focused owners: 81 passed, with one fixture-only assertion corrected because post-commit observer errors become unknown publications rather than escaping; all three corrected cases pass and remove the real Git cleanup ref. Additional consumers: 74 passed. The final full owner suite is queued.

Two isolated Codex review rounds completed; the implementation review found a stale INDEX fixture selection, corrected in the committed fixture. Later automated review found a real shared-store wake mismatch: parked targets carry a physical store owner, while entry-patch publications may carry the logical session agent. The new regression fails on the previous head (expected a second resolution after restoration, observed only one). The correction matches keyed publications by canonical session key and physical store, preserving broad agent-scoped filtering. An explicitly authorized delta-only Codex review and final-head proof are pending.

Local T1/dialect, line-cap, mock, formatting and other completed ratchets pass. Local type checks hit the campaign-required internal virtual store outside the checkout, which the declaration-containment guard rejects; no guard was bypassed. Prior-head CI passed, including all three PostgreSQL shards, but final-head CI, Knip comparison and update proof are pending. No readiness claim is made.

## Final series registered before resumed runs

The completed r2 baseline B1 remains valid on baseline b688518a2f9a38afa850d6394df7722fa2d84d23 with the corrected fixture and unchanged frozen observer. Reuse that baseline as r3 B1; exclude the pre-correction r2 candidate C1 from final-head acceptance. Run corrected-head C1, then B2,C2 through B5,C5, followed by all five separate transient-control pairs. Preserve all original thresholds, deadlines, phases and sample counts. The build and candidate capsule are refreshed before C1. Reports identify the reused baseline explicitly.

The first pair's literal shape check stopped on varying numeric PRAGMA busy_timeout values (4881/4989/4996). Source attribution identifies the unchanged connection-local remaining admission timeout in src/infra/sqlite-busy-timeout.ts. The external comparator now canonicalizes only that integer RHS to a placeholder; all statements remain counted, original literal differences remain recorded, and the frozen observer is unchanged. No query-family or SQL-count difference is suppressed.

prs.title: fix(agents): background exec completion is announced again after process log already showed the result
prs.body:
Closes #183112

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where channel users would get a stray, out-of-context "command finished" message when the agent had backgrounded a command and then read its finished result with `process` `log` during the same turn. The completion stayed queued, and the next exec-event heartbeat relayed it to the user minutes later.

## Why This Change Was Made

On a process that has ended, `log` now does what a terminal `poll` already does. It ends with the same terminal line (`finishedSessionText`, e.g. `Process exited with code 0.`), and once the result is delivered it acknowledges the notify-on-exit completion (`acknowledgeNotifyOnExit`). The existing stale-wake check in `heartbeat-runner-prompt.ts` then drops the queued wake. The `/bash` chat command already acknowledges the same way after showing a finished session's output and exit label. `log` on a running process, and its paging, do not change.

## User Impact

An agent can read a finished background command with either `poll` or `log`, and the user is not sent the completion a second time. `log` on a finished process now also tells the model how it ended, which the tool description (`poll/log: status, output, ... completion`) already promised.

## Evidence

- New regression test `consumes a finished completion that the model reads with process log` in `src/agents/bash-tools.notify-on-exit-ack.test.ts`. It fails on `main` (the completion is still queued after the acknowledged `log` result: `expected [ { …(5) } ] to deeply equal []`) and passes with the fix.
- Updated the assertions that pinned finished-process `log` output to end at the last output line, keeping their paging, retention, and ordering checks: `bash-tools.test.ts`, `bash-tools.process.finished-retention.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` (whose `log` call is named `collect`), `bash-tools.process.delivery.test.ts` (Code Mode `details.output`, default tail and a one-line page), and `bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts`. The last two were flagged by the first CI run and pass locally after the update (35/35).
- Focused runs pass: `pnpm test src/agents/bash-tools.notify-on-exit-ack.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process.finished-retention.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process.delivery.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts` and the other process/exec tool suites (`bash-tools.process.*`, `bash-process-registry`, `bash-tools.exec-request-stop`, `bash-tools.exec.egress-lifecycle`, `tool-mutation`, `tool-loop-detection`, `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools`, `agent-tools-agent-config.exec`), and `bash-tools.process.e2e.test.ts` (8/8). oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files.
- Observed live on 2026.9.2, Codex app-server runtime on Telegram. A backgrounded command finished mid-turn, its exec-event wake was skipped (`requests-in-flight`) until the turn ended, the turn read the result with `gateway_process` `log`, and then a heartbeat sent the completion to the user as a new message. The same change on a 2026.9.34-based build passes an equivalent test against a real child process: a real notify-on-exit background exec, read with `log`, then acknowledged, leaves no completion queued.
- Production LOC: +5/-4 in `bash-tools.process.ts`. The gain is the acknowledgement on the `log` path. The terminal line reuses `finishedSessionText` in place of the old stopped-by-request-only branch.

prs.title: fix(database): make unbounded retention portable to PostgreSQL
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL rejects three retention queries with SQLSTATE `2201W` (`LIMIT must not be negative`). ACP replay session retention, channel-ingress capacity retention, and resolved session-suggestion pruning all used SQLite's `LIMIT -1` spelling. ACP byte trimming also used SQLite's scalar `max` form.

## What Changed

One database-engine helper supplies the unbounded limit expression: `-1` on SQLite and `ALL` on PostgreSQL. The three owners keep their existing OFFSET, ordering, predicates, and batching. ACP uses a Kysely CASE expression for the same zero-clamped subtraction.

No schema, retention policy, transaction, cache, identity, or worker-request change. ACP byte-budget optimization is deliberately separate and will follow in another PR.

## Evidence

The synthetic real-owner tests pass **7/7 on SQLite and fail 7/7 on PostgreSQL before the fix**, all with SQLSTATE `2201W`. With this repair, **14/14 pass on SQLite and real PostgreSQL 17**. They exercise:

- ACP partial-session trimming with accurate and understated byte totals, plus the exact 200-session cap under tied timestamps.
- Pending, completed, and failed ingress rows, including protected rows retaining their original capacity slots, 500-row batches, repeat pruning, and zero-cap tails.
- Resolved-suggestion tied ordering while retaining pending suggestions and another session's rows.

Changed-file type-aware lint and `git diff --check` pass. The independent Codex P0–P2 review is scoped-clean, and the committed tree matches the reviewed tree. PostgreSQL maintainer review is approved for this exact head. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40152322920) passed, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts, and baseline ratchets.

The local T1 and dialect ratchets, format, mock exports, and other completed contract checks passed. Local typecheck setup rejected the campaign-required external dependency store; CI supplies the passing typecheck and lint evidence. The duplicate local full-core lint was stopped after CI passed. All three local Knip comparisons exactly match the original base: production 72/72, full-tree 86/86, scripts 1,136/1,136, with zero added or removed findings.

## Class Audit

The shared helper repairs all three unguarded negative-LIMIT sites: `src/acp/event-ledger.worker.ts`, `src/channels/message/ingress-queue.kernel.ts`, and `src/config/sessions/session-suggestion-store.kernel.ts` (the latter used `eb.lit(-1)`). The remaining negative sentinel in `session-accessor.transcript-range.worker.ts` is explicitly inside the SQLite-only `!postgres` recursive branch; PostgreSQL has its own outer limit. All 13 other OFFSET chains use nonnegative limits.

## Open-PR Compatibility

prs.title: fix(agents): keep active code-mode run expiry on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes parked Code Mode work expiring early or lingering past its lifetime when the system clock changes.

## User Impact

Suspended runs retain their configured elapsed lifetime across forward and backward clock corrections, including pending agent-wait retention and settlement renewal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing lifecycle owner now creates, renews, compares, and schedules its in-process deadlines with `performance.now()`. Integer seeds preserve the shared duration normalizer's contract. These deadlines are transient, so no persisted state or configuration changes.

The regression parks through the real exec path, steps the wall clock, and parks another run to rearm the shared timer. It checks the configured TTL independently of the implementation's deadline value. The former Date-range overflow scenario no longer applies to process-relative deadlines.

## Evidence

- Both ±60-second regressions fail on the main baseline: a forward step aborts early, while a backward step leaves the run parked too long. On the fix, the run survives through 59,999 ms and expires at 60,000 ms.
- Prepared head: `f9adbe8a2d2b3d9696b13514b595c21db1a7b764`, incorporating main `3ec819f8c11c`. After integration, all five focused suites pass: 84 tests across wait, state, worker lifecycle, bridge lifecycle, and swarm retention. Exact-head CI run [40145919197](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40145919197) passed; the repository watcher reports green after excluding superseded checks.
- Production LOC delta: 0; tests: -7; documentation: +1. Targeted Oxlint and Oxfmt pass. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Live limitation: the contributor's Gateway clock-injection harness is unavailable, so the live-model exec/wait/swarm experiment was not independently repeated. The focused tests exercise the real exec/park lifecycle.

Contributor-provided isolated Gateway evidence used a local Responses fixture over real SSE transport: runs with a 15-second TTL disposed at about 14.95 seconds after parking under both ±120-second wall steps. A separate spawned-child trace observed `agentWait` settlement renewal with about 14.97 seconds remaining, then retained the run through a +120-second wall step. These are attributed contributor results, not a new live run.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.
