prs.title: perf(codex): share resident catalog preview strings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The resident Codex catalog retains separate detached copies of identical previews in different rows. Preview detachment is necessary to avoid pinning large native or JSON source strings, but equal retained text can share one detached value.

## User Impact

No catalog content or ordering changes. Native admission, persisted restoration, revisions, eviction, and shutdown use the same resident preview lifetime. There are no configuration or storage-format changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each catalog index now keeps a reference-counted table of its resident preview values and reuses those strings for matching fallback names. Replacement and eviction release references; close clears the table. Detachment remains at the existing decoding/projection boundaries. This reduces retained copies; transient producer copies are still made before admission.

Production delta: **+46 lines**. The growth enforces exact resident lifetime and preserves substring detachment; it introduces no global cache or retention beyond resident rows. The observer-ID audit found its normal producers already carry the original strings and #182998 already covers decoded digest IDs, so that path is unchanged.

## Evidence

Owner-level measurements on Node 26.12.1 used 6,200 rows, 64 distinct 500-code-unit Unicode previews, and three changing revisions. Each mode has **five alternating fresh-process samples per side, 18,600 operations/sample (93,000 operations/side)**. Runs held the shared quiet-slot lock, swapped interleaved CPU assignments, and used the shared production guard. Values below are means; differences are candidate minus baseline.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Native resident preview/fallback string nodes | 6,200 | 64 | −98.97% |
| Native resident preview/fallback string bytes | 6,299,200 | 65,024 | −6,234,176 (−98.97%) |
| Native owner retained heap, bytes | 19,984,342 | 13,778,782 | −6,205,560 (−31.05%) |
| Restore resident preview/fallback string nodes | 12,400 | 64 | −99.48% |
| Restore resident preview/fallback string bytes | 12,598,400 | 65,024 | −12,533,376 (−99.48%) |
| Restore owner retained heap, bytes | 26,303,368 | 13,783,616 | −12,519,752 (−47.60%) |
| Native CPU, ms/18,600 operations | 306.005 | 310.216 | +4.211 (+1.38%) |
| Restore CPU, ms/18,600 operations | 158.977 | 159.417 | +0.440 (+0.28%) |
| Native natural GC, ms/18,600 operations | 13.442 | 11.976 | −1.466 (−10.91%) |
| Restore natural GC, ms/18,600 operations | 8.683 | 8.586 | −0.098 (−1.12%) |
| Separately sampled allocation, bytes/operation | 11,943.39 | 12,059.83 | +116.44 (+0.97%) |

Owner heap is the forced-GC live heap minus the same process's forced-GC heap after index close. The merged heap analyzer's `--summary` duplicate-string potential savings fell from 12,832,475 to 6,598,366 bytes for native admission and from 19,379,779 to 6,846,475 bytes for restore. Those aggregate counts also contain independent search-index text; the resident-property counts above isolate this change.

**Unique-preview control (also five samples/side):** with 6,200 distinct previews, physical preview bytes stay at 6,299,200. Owner heap rises from 19,973,440 to 20,691,896 bytes: **+718,456 bytes (+3.60%, 0.69 MiB)**. CPU rises from 306.326 to 330.341 ms/18,600 operations: **+24.014 ms (+7.84%)**; elapsed time rises 9.84%. This is a consistent table-management cost, not a claimed improvement or dismissed as noise. The measured repeated-preview case trades this overhead for 6.2–12.5 MB less retained heap. Transient allocation is not reduced because producers still detach before admission.

The baseline fails `--verify-shared` (6,200 physical values instead of 64); all candidate samples pass. All 50 measurement samples preserve public preview values and contain zero old-revision preview strings, zero retained source backing strings, and zero sliced preview targets. A preliminary harness check found a sanitizer input retained by V8's RegExp last-match state; a successful empty match now clears that unrelated root before every snapshot on both sides. Pilot runs are not decision samples.

Natural-GC runs were untraced; sampled allocation was separate and included collected objects. Every observed natural collection was minor. There were 7 collections/sample/side for native and unique, and 5 baseline versus 6 candidate collections/sample for restore; no natural major collections. These counts cannot support p95/p99 or major-GC claims. Total GC decreased in each mode on average; no GC rejection or A/A rejection-control procedure was invoked. Forced-GC retention is not production GC throughput evidence.

<details>
<summary>Untraced GC totals and both maximum pauses, by pair (milliseconds)</summary>

| Mode / pair | Collections base → candidate | Total base → candidate | Max base → candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| native / 1 | 7 → 7 | 13.947 → 12.123 | 3.082 → 2.371 |
| native / 2 | 7 → 7 | 12.760 → 11.752 | 2.788 → 2.293 |
| native / 3 | 7 → 7 | 14.619 → 11.562 | 2.915 → 2.438 |
| native / 4 | 7 → 7 | 12.153 → 13.339 | 3.383 → 2.744 |
| native / 5 | 7 → 7 | 13.730 → 11.103 | 2.813 → 2.325 |
| restore / 1 | 5 → 6 | 7.910 → 8.056 | 2.165 → 2.043 |
| restore / 2 | 5 → 6 | 8.766 → 8.973 | 2.592 → 1.850 |
| restore / 3 | 5 → 6 | 9.074 → 9.097 | 2.350 → 2.246 |
| restore / 4 | 5 → 6 | 8.392 → 8.508 | 2.290 → 2.101 |
| restore / 5 | 5 → 6 | 9.275 → 8.295 | 2.609 → 1.874 |
| unique / 1 | 7 → 7 | 12.927 → 11.756 | 2.748 → 2.575 |
| unique / 2 | 7 → 7 | 13.965 → 13.943 | 2.939 → 2.961 |
| unique / 3 | 7 → 7 | 13.107 → 12.362 | 2.735 → 2.715 |
| unique / 4 | 7 → 7 | 13.533 → 15.086 | 2.901 → 3.315 |
| unique / 5 | 7 → 7 | 13.660 → 12.910 | 3.076 → 2.523 |

</details>

The separate native promotion pass also used **five alternating samples/side, 18,600 operations/sample**. Promotion observed inside the marked owner-work interval fell from **33,518,286 to 19,995,045 bytes/run: −13,523,242 bytes (−40.35%)**, or 1,802.06 → 1,075.00 bytes/operation. Each sample contained seven minor collections (35/side total), no major collections, and no other-isolate collections inside the interval. Fixture setup, forced GC, snapshotting, and cleanup were outside the markers. Traced timing is not used as a latency or GC-time gate.

| Promotion pair | Baseline bytes | Candidate bytes |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 33,513,416 | 19,989,008 |
| 2 | 33,524,328 | 19,995,784 |
| 3 | 33,508,472 | 20,004,736 |
| 4 | 33,522,608 | 19,997,760 |
| 5 | 33,522,608 | 19,987,936 |

All measurements are complete. The lead owns merging; this lane intentionally leaves the PR open.

Passed locally (single worker):

- `session-catalog-index.test.ts`, `session-catalog-index-events.test.ts`, `session-catalog-index-recovery.test.ts`, `session-catalog-index-capacity.test.ts`: **53 tests**; final catalog shard 41.83 seconds including transform/import, about two seconds of test execution.
- `eager-import-closure.test.ts`, `pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts`: **22 tests**; complete focused command 82.63 seconds including both shards.
- Export-name collision guard, changed-file oxfmt and oxlint, `git diff --check`, and targeted `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.scripts.json`.

prs.body:
Related: #164796

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes saved-history attribution to the native Claude login when administrator-managed settings make Claude authenticate through an API key, token, cloud provider, or API-key helper instead.

## User Impact

With native-login history attestation enabled, file-based managed authentication now prevents automatic saved-history replay under the wrong account. Managed settings without authentication overrides retain normal recovery. The existing spawn, prompt, private-hook, and transcript-coverage checks also observe managed authentication added during a turn.

MDM and server-managed policy remain outside this file-based check. Checking each managed file independently can conservatively refuse recovery when later settings override an earlier authentication key.

## Why This Change Was Made

The follow-up requested in #164796 belongs in the existing credential owner. It now checks the platform's managed-settings file and non-hidden JSON drop-ins alongside user settings and the child environment. Unreadable files are contained locally. There is no new configuration, SDK option, state, or migration.

The owner and its native-history consumers now share an isolated filesystem fixture, so a developer machine's managed policy cannot change their synthetic-account results. Original implementation and investigation by @etzelm.

## Evidence

- Regression on the unmodified production owner: 1 failed / 29 passed, returning the native account where the managed-auth case requires no owner (15.70 seconds wall time).
- Updated owner and five consumer suites: all passed through the repository runner with one worker. The cold run took 497.86 seconds including a 136.54-second worker build; individual integration cases remain unchanged.
- Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and whitespace checks passed before integration, on the identical edited files. Independent Codex review through P2: no actionable findings. Integrated local reruns initially lacked nested workspace dependency links; the repository helper restored links to matching installed dependencies without changing package files. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40153279011) is green, including the security-sensitive gate. [Fresh ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178929#issuecomment-6306198739) of `0d79dd4afdb30a0d610874f724ff21e268a2aa98` found no actionable defect and accepted the linked CLI evidence.

Production code is unchanged from that reviewed implementation.
- Not freshly live-tested against authenticated Claude: doing so would require another synthetic transport/profile harness or account credentials; current proof uses the real credential/history owners with isolated filesystem and provider-I/O fixtures.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reduce transcript turn database round trips
prs.body:
Refs #182810 — reported by @etzelm.

## What Problem This Solves

Persisting a user/assistant turn repeats transcript reads and per-message writes, including 24 synchronous PostgreSQL bridge trips for two messages.

## User Impact

This PostgreSQL-readiness optimization reduces database statements and bridge trips while preserving stored formats, message order, idempotency and cold restoration. No latency improvement is claimed from the loaded local host.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing transcript writer carries append state and final metadata through a fresh linear turn, batches bounded payload/identity and index writes, and updates the window once while preserving each message's timestamp advance. Warm turns defer cold restoration until locked admission requires it. Replay, explicit-parent, callback, custody and actor paths retain their existing contracts.

Identity storage stays separate. PostgreSQL retains its eager advisory lock before authoritative reads, BEGIN and COMMIT. State and agent database transactions never fuse. There is no schema, dependency, configuration or transcript-event contract change. Warm-turn handoff fusion follows the approved timing/visibility decision.

Three pre-transaction routing reads remain as follow-ups: session-window key lookup, session-node/snapshot lookup and participant lookup. They select guarded persistence versus the existing transcript-only/no-entry route (#119221); this PR does not refactor that routing owner.

## Evidence

Five warmups plus ten measured commits per shape; 2,000 synthetic sessions and one 5,000-turn history, using the gateway engine installation path and statement diagnostics in every worker. All 60 final samples match exactly.

| Messages | PG bridge trips, before → after | PG SQL, before → after | SQLite SQL, before → after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 17 → 15 | 18 → 16 | 15 → 14 |
| 2 | 24 → 14 | 25 → 15 | 28 → 14 |
| 4 | 38 → 14 | 39 → 15 | 50 → 14 |

- Count regression RED on main and GREEN on the candidate for 1/2/3/4/513 messages. Row, parent, identity, timestamp and publication assertions pass on both. Candidate CI count cases pass under Node and Bun.
- Native Homebrew PG17 proof passes: exact 513-message payload/parent readback, unchanged replay, conflicting replay rejected without mutation, contiguous concurrent writers and clean close.
- Fresh valid-config Gateways on Homebrew PG17 (state and agent families, own schema prefix) and SQLite each completed three real model turns through chat.send, agent.wait and chat.history. All six messages and order matched across engines; replay retained the run identity and byte-identical per-engine history; zero chat errors. Owned processes stopped cleanly. No live per-turn SQL counts are claimed.
- Core types and 193 tests in 20 focused files passed on the implementation. Subsequent source-preserving checks cover all 11 prompt-prefix cases and the wrapper extraction tests. Typed lint, formatting and line-cap checks pass. pr-simplify and independent Codex reviews are clean through P2.
- New test cost: pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-turn-count.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 (prepared node scripts/run-vitest.mjs entry point): five passing cases, 188.35 s Vitest / 230.66 s full wrapper, 0.997 s test bodies, including 118.304 s cold worker preparation on this loaded Mac.

The frozen census and C=64 are excluded because the fixture contains the heartbeat setting retired by #179387. Deterministic counts and valid-config real Gateway proof replace that route. The benchmark is available through pnpm bench:transcript-turn with OPENCLAW_TURN_TRACE and engine/root arguments.

## Rebased-head verification

Head: 4bad85065edbd686d949b66d9185b532ed3c8b7a, rebased onto 734822d0d863a0f1411ea6eb3fa2134feac9c511, including #182990. All 12 production files are byte-identical to the reviewed 746d0314807daccbdc58075dfc4c29724ae19993.

All five CI-omitted suites pass on this head: session-accessor.sqlite-append-participants (1), session-accessor.sqlite-branches (12), session-accessor.sqlite-import (12), session-accessor.transcript-turn-initialization (9), and transcript-append-redact (4). Exact command:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-append-participants.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-branches.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-import.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.transcript-turn-initialization.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript-append-redact.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

38 cases pass (exit 0). Test-group times: 234.13 s and 188.05 s; full wrapper: 705.14 s.

[Exact-head CI 40150140516](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40150140516) completed: all three PostgreSQL conformance shards pass (1/3: 25m17s; 2/3: 16m54s; 3/3: 16m52s). There are 155 successful jobs, 23 intentional skips, six inherited failures and the aggregate gate failure. CI is not reported as green.

Both type-check failures are the same session-catalog.test-helpers.ts:122 TS2739 error observed in [scheduled main 40149301577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149301577). This PR does not change that helper.

prs.title: fix(installer): piped PowerShell install fails NodeVersion validation before startup
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes** — This PR was created with the assistance of AI tools. Human author is responsible for the content.

Closes #183088

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users running the documented Windows install command (`iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex`) would see the installer abort before anything runs, with `Invoke-Expression: The attribute cannot be added because variable NodeVersion with value  would no longer be valid.`
- **Related:** #183088; clawsweeper review advised "a narrow parameter-validation correction is appropriate: accept the omitted value while preserving nonempty version validation, strict option binding, and runtime compatibility checks."

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** the optional `-NodeVersion` parameter accepts an omitted (empty) value when the script is evaluated through `Invoke-Expression`, while a supplied nonempty version must still match `x.y.z`. The documented piped install command starts the installer and reaches dry-run output.
- **Out of scope:** Node runtime compatibility checks, strict option binding, and `-NodeOnly`/`-NodePrefix` guards are unchanged; an omitted version still means "latest Node 26 release" downstream (existing behavior).
- **Highest-risk area:** parameter validation of `scripts/install.ps1`.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The pattern change is a single character-class (`(?:…)?`) that only widens the accepted set by the empty string; new regression tests pin omitted/valid/malformed behavior and the full piped entrypoint.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** `Get-Content -Raw scripts/install.ps1 | Invoke-Expression` with `OPENCLAW_DRY_RUN=1`, `OPENCLAW_NO_ONBOARD=1`, `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_METHOD=npm` prints the installer banner, `[OK] Windows detected`, `[OK] Dry run`, `[OK] Install method: npm`, `[OK] Onboard: skipped` and exits 0; `-NodeVersion 26.x` is still rejected with a pattern validation error (exit 1); `-File` dry-run behavior is unchanged.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `scripts/install.ps1` (param block, one line) and the two new cases in `test/scripts/install-ps1.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** full unmodified `scripts/install.ps1` evaluated through `Invoke-Expression` in PowerShell 7.6.8 (`pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive`), same engine family as the reporter's PowerShell 7.6.8, with `OPENCLAW_DRY_RUN=1`, `OPENCLAW_NO_ONBOARD=1`, `OPENCLAW_INSTALL_METHOD=npm`.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # regression tests (pwsh on PATH; runs both new cases)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/install-ps1.test.ts test/scripts/install-ps1.release.test.ts
  # targeted test-file type shard
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json --builders 1
  # reporter's full-script repro (after fix)
  pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command '$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"; $env:OPENCLAW_DRY_RUN = "1"; $env:OPENCLAW_NO_ONBOARD = "1"; $env:OPENCLAW_INSTALL_METHOD = "npm"; Get-Content -LiteralPath ./scripts/install.ps1 -Raw | Invoke-Expression'
  # malformed value still rejected / valid exact version / -File dry-run unchanged
  pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command '.\scripts\install.ps1 -NodeVersion 26.x -DryRun'
  pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command '.\scripts\install.ps1 -NodeOnly -NodePrefix /tmp/nv-183088 -NodeVersion 26.12.1 -DryRun'
  pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command '.\scripts\install.ps1 -DryRun -NoOnboard -InstallMethod npm'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  === A) reporter exact full-script repro (after fix) ===
    OpenClaw Installer
  [OK] Windows detected
  [OK] Dry run
  [OK] Install method: npm
  [OK] Onboard: skipped
  EXIT=0
  === B2) malformed NodeVersion exit code (no pipe) ===
  install.ps1: Cannot validate argument on parameter 'NodeVersion'. The argument "26.x" does not match the "^(?:\d+\.\d+\.\d+)?$" pattern. Supply an argument that matches "^(?:\d+\.\d+\.\d+)?$" and try the command again.
  EXIT=1
  === C) valid exact NodeVersion with -NodeOnly dry-run ===
  [OK] Windows detected
  [OK] Would install private Node.js to /tmp/nv-183088 (PATH unchanged).
  EXIT=0
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** the piped `Invoke-Expression` entrypoint starts the installer and completes the dry run with exit 0 (previously it aborted with the `ValidationMetadataException` before `[OK] Windows detected`); malformed nonempty versions are still rejected (exit 1); the valid exact version path and the `-File` dry-run path behave exactly as before. Both new regression tests fail on the base commit (RED: `expected 1 to be +0` with the identical attribute error) and pass after the patch; the full `test/scripts/install-ps1.test.ts` (13 tests) and `test/scripts/install-ps1.release.test.ts` (41 passed, 3 skipped) suites pass.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** on base `e2f634809c8` the same repro exits before any installer output: `Invoke-Expression: The attribute cannot be added because variable NodeVersion with value  would no longer be valid.`
- **What was not tested:** Windows PowerShell 5.1 on a real Windows host was not available locally; the engine-level behavior is covered by the new `runWithPowerShell` test which runs on Windows CI runners for both engines via the website-installer-sync probes. `pnpm tsgo:core` currently fails on pristine `origin/main` itself (`src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog.test-helpers.ts` TS2739, reproduced in a clean origin/main worktree) — pre-existing and unrelated to this diff. CI lanes pending.
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review

prs.title: perf(gateway): release decoded workspace tree inputs before worker settlement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace tree-input adapters keep decoded manifest inputs reachable until the worker finishes, even after encoding and transferring the worker request. Large queued operations unnecessarily extend the lifetime of those objects.

## User Impact

Pending tree-input preparation can release entries once the caller no longer needs them. Reconciliation bytes, recovery journals, cancellation, and errors remain unchanged. Recovery callers still retain entries that their journals need; this is not a claim that all pending recovery memory disappears.

## Why This Change Was Made

Return the existing promise from two async adapters instead of suspending their frames with `return await`. Keeping the functions async preserves rejected-promise behavior for encoding errors. Current main already transfers encoded payloads at admission and dispatch, so this adds no transfer path, cache, coalescing, or transport policy.

Gateway runtime LOC delta: **0** (two `await` removals); the required reproducible benchmark adds 261 tooling lines, and the regression adds 64 net test lines. The regression checks collection of the original objects during a deterministically held worker operation and unchanged rejection propagation. The standalone benchmark exercises 80,000 synthetic files through both `createWorkspacePatch → prepareWorkspaceTreeInput` and the direct tree-input owner.

## Evidence

- Retention regression: red on base (both original input and entries retained), green with the fix (both collected). Candidate regression: 487 ms.
- Node focused tests: **67 passed** across `workspace-manifest-worker.test.ts`, `workspace-manifest.test.ts`, `workspace-reconcile.test.ts`, and `workspace-reconcile-recovery.test.ts`. First three worker/reconcile files took 97.45 s including a cold runtime artifact build; manifest schema file took 0.96 s.
- Changed-file oxfmt, changed-file oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. The configured autoreview provider selector did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed.
- The retention regression also passes under the default Bun test runtime (255 ms).
- Broad proof: PR CI.

### Completed memory measurements

Node 26.12.1, 80,000 synthetic empty files with distinct manifest paths/digests, four occupied workspace worker slots, fixed 16-CPU affinity and 8 GiB memory limit. **Five serial alternating baseline/candidate samples per mode (20 total)**. Setup and guarded waits are excluded. Base source: `c28e83983a1f`; rebasing did not change the measured manifest/recovery/broker owners. No production data was used. These are owner-level retention runs, not whole-Gateway latency or GC-throughput gates.

Values below are means; retained memory is the forced-GC delta above the warmed process before input construction. RSS includes all worker isolates.

| Mode / metric (n=5 per side) | Baseline | Candidate | Mean paired delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Direct owner, queued retained heap | 22.100 MiB | 0.126 MiB | −21.974 MiB (−99.43%) |
| Direct owner, active retained heap | 22.072 MiB | 0.098 MiB | −21.974 MiB (−99.56%) |
| Recovery, queued retained heap | 48.803 MiB | 48.802 MiB | −0.001 MiB (neutral) |
| Recovery, active retained heap | 48.771 MiB | 48.770 MiB | −0.001 MiB (neutral) |
| Direct owner, queued / active ArrayBuffer counter | 15.946 / 15.946 MiB | 15.946 / 15.946 MiB | unchanged |
| Recovery, queued / active ArrayBuffer counter | 16.008 / 16.008 MiB | 16.008 / 16.008 MiB | unchanged |
| Both modes, queued / active external-byte delta | 15.946 / <0.001 MiB | 15.946 / <0.001 MiB | unchanged |
| Direct owner, process peak RSS | 942.177 MiB | 937.270 MiB | −4.907 MiB (−0.52%; context) |
| Recovery, process peak RSS | 990.054 MiB | 969.284 MiB | −20.770 MiB (−2.10%; context) |

Direct-owner queued retained-heap ranges: baseline 22.094–22.102 MiB, candidate 0.120–0.128 MiB. Recovery queued ranges: baseline 48.803–48.803 MiB, candidate 48.802–48.804 MiB. Peak-RSS ranges: owner 936.543–947.688 → 926.469–945.223 MiB; recovery 983.352–996.824 → 930.777–994.113 MiB.

Every queued sample had four active blocker tasks plus one queued manifest; every active sample had one manifest task. Base/applied recovery tree preparation stayed sequential. This does not establish duplicate identical production requests, and unique destination paths/refs must not be coalesced by workspace alone. The existing broker retains a queued payload and transfers it at dispatch; raw `arrayBuffers` can still count transferred backing stores, while external bytes drop back to baseline. No native-buffer reduction is claimed.

All ten direct-owner outputs had SHA-256 `c4276dcfb84b72beb58f4bf799bf555389b4958960b6da5c9b468c350ced84d2`. All ten recovery outputs had tree `aa7dfcc8ac322b96845b31ab170434bf61843f78`, empty patch, and identical pack SHA-256 `92a15b9ae6bab4611abe1c36766899c89b44f3d835f5feac74c632361ed433aa`. A final smoke of the lint-clean instrumentation reproduced the owner result and same output hash.

### Timing context and limits

Instrumented pre-release duration (includes entry construction and forced GC): owner 165.52 → 143.70 ms; recovery 291.25 → 303.92 ms. Instrumented total pending duration: owner 5.367 → 5.960 s (+11.05%, ranges 3.626–6.310 → 4.168–7.468 s); recovery 11.421 → 15.960 s (+39.75%, ranges 10.099–13.058 → 11.772–21.713 s). These serial runs include forced GC, deliberate blocking, and changing shared-host I/O contention. They are not matched untraced latency proof; the adverse timings are reported, not discarded, and no latency improvement is claimed. The completed untraced follow-up below covers this gap; the instrumented durations remain historical context.

This is a zero-runtime-LOC simplification with a proven owner-retention improvement and neutral rollback-patch-construction retained memory. It does **not** establish removal of a large production recovery holder: the caller legitimately retains entries for the journal. After deployment, look for decoded inputs no longer retained solely by these adapter frames; expect journal-owned arrays and transferred-buffer accounting to remain. No timeout, queue policy, schema, or transport internals changed.

### Untraced recovery latency follow-up

Acceptance rule was recorded before running: five serial alternating baseline/candidate fresh-process pairs of the same 80,000-file workload, identical outputs, and no reproducible latency regression (20% worsening is a stop). Node 26.12.1 on Linux, exclusive quiet-slot lock and existing production-load guard, 16 interleaved CPUs, 8 GiB limit, identical placement within each pair and alternate placement across pairs. Worker startup is warmed/excluded; input construction and the complete `createWorkspacePatch` call are timed. No forced GC, tracing, allocation sampling, or intentional blockers; `NODE_OPTIONS` and `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` are unset. An exploratory local series was stopped and excluded after recovering the original Linux-host requirement.

Reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/workspace-manifest-retention.ts <scratch> prepare 80000`, then mode `latency 80000` on each side. Usage is documented in the script header; the perf README is unchanged. Baseline is `7bddc5d70497`; candidate runtime differs only by the two await removals.

| Recovery wall time, n=5 per side | Baseline | Candidate | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| p50 | 12.085732 s | 11.690160 s | −3.27% |
| Mean | 12.111790 s | 11.906550 s | −1.69% |
| Range | 10.944128–13.255648 s | 11.197301–12.819195 s | context |

| Pair | Baseline (s) | Candidate (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 12.804312 | 12.819195 |
| 2 | 13.255648 | 11.414018 |
| 3 | 12.085732 | 12.412075 |
| 4 | 11.469130 | 11.690160 |
| 5 | 10.944128 | 11.197301 |

All ten outputs match the earlier tree, empty-patch, and pack hashes. The prior 11.421 → 15.960 s (+39.75%) rise is **not reproduced**. This is no speedup claim: paired differences are mixed and the mean change is only −0.205 s. The earlier durations included forced GC and deliberate blocking, and did not reserve an exclusive measurement slot; changing shared-host I/O/CPU contention was confounded with the edit. The new comparison removes deliberate instrumentation/blocking and reserves a benchmark slot, but cannot separately attribute the old rise to GC instrumentation versus contention. No comparable latency regression appears in the untraced workload.

### Holder ownership, overlap, and liveness

**Tree-input overlap:** `writeRawWorkspaceTree` is the only production caller of `prepareWorkspaceTreeInput`; each invocation has a random ref and private output repository/path, and base/applied preparations are sequential. Recovery entry owners serialize per environment. Same workspace alone is not equivalent work: source root/tree, destination path, ref, and entries all matter. See [tree preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf04d0e774d4237a238fb20b73920204452209ee/src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-reconcile-recovery.ts#L77) and [recovery serialization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf04d0e774d4237a238fb20b73920204452209ee/src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch-pending-results.ts#L494).

**Other manifest overlap:** independent forks of one source checkpoint can overlap identical staged-manifest reads. Separate PR #183128 joins only those pending reads, keyed by all request inputs, cwd, environment digest, and signal identity, with invalidation at the existing ref writer. Its interleaved work-count regression reduces ten physical reads to six for ten callers with six identities. It does not change this PR or claim to remove the tree-input holder.

**Queue/hang bound:** [Git worker admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf04d0e774d4237a238fb20b73920204452209ee/src/infra/git-worker.ts#L441) supplies a 30-minute deadline. The [pool arms it before enqueue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf04d0e774d4237a238fb20b73920204452209ee/packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-pool-core.ts#L254), and [host exchanges retain the original deadline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf04d0e774d4237a238fb20b73920204452209ee/packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-pool-owned.ts#L298). Queued expiry removes/rejects the task; worker exit also rejects. Timeout is a typed visible error, with a warning for a stalled host callback. Six existing owner tests passed for queued expiry, four host-wait deadline variants, and worker exit/OOM. Standard Git subprocesses use abort signals and deadlines (workspace commands: 10 minutes). The outer owner deliberately joins host callbacks and cleanup, so 30 minutes is not an unconditional wall-clock guarantee for arbitrary abort-ignoring callbacks or a stuck OS filesystem. No concrete standard-path indefinite wait was found; no speculative timeout was added.

**48.8 MiB journal retention:** the benchmark's recovery mode measures rollback-patch construction. The real apply caller needs both arrays *after* `createWorkspacePatch` to [write the journal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf04d0e774d4237a238fb20b73920204452209ee/src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-reconcile-apply.ts#L221), prepare targets, and recover if apply fails. Recovery replay also needs both sides for later conflict/final-state checks. Clearing caller-owned arrays at encoding would break recovery; streaming worker input alone would not release these journal owners. A different journal representation/lifecycle would be separate work. The measured rollback-patch-construction retained heap remains neutral.

Full apply also retains the base/current manifests, reconciliation maps, and preflight facts across patch construction for later revalidation and directory application ([apply owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf04d0e774d4237a238fb20b73920204452209ee/src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-reconcile-apply.ts#L63)). Those owners are outside the snapshot-construction benchmark; their contribution to the production total has not been quantified. The aggregate tree-input dominator does not identify request tuples or age, so it cannot establish duplicate equivalent work or a hang. Its retained size is not a measurement of memory this edit reclaims. After deployment, the expected signal is loss of retention solely through the two adapter frames; journal-owned arrays remain until their owner settles. The full large production holder is not claimed fixed.

### Final validation and CI

The original two commits were rebased patch-identically onto main `7bddc5d70497` and pushed with force-with-lease (`git range-diff` marks both unchanged). Follow-up head **`bf04d0e774d4237a238fb20b73920204452209ee`** adds only the timing mode. Changed-file lint/format, script typecheck, diff check, and fresh independent review passed. Existing retention/reconcile proof above remains applicable; the six deadline/exit tests also pass.

The earlier introduced lint-suppression issue was repaired by removing the suppression. Earlier inherited type errors are resolved by the rebase. Final-head CI is fully green: **69 passing, 56 skipped, no pending or failed checks**, including [the aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40151551937/job/121045533232). No merge was attempted; the lead owns landing.

prs.title: refactor: privatize fixture consumer contracts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Several internal fixture helpers were exported only so tests could name private implementation details. Those export edges made internal declarations look reusable even though production already exposed stronger owner-level contracts for the same behavior.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. Runtime APIs, package and Plugin SDK surfaces, configuration, stored data, and cleanup/message/channel behavior remain unchanged; the affected tests continue to cover the same cases, assertions, lifetimes, and timeouts through production owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes six declarations private and redirects their consumers to existing contracts:

- Abliteration live fixtures resolve the default through the production model ref and catalog.
- Feishu content cases run through the exported message-event parser.
- Zalouser lifecycle fixtures infer their type from the ingress monitor dispatch contract.
- Session cleanup fixtures infer summary types from `runSessionsCleanup` while the canonical result type remains unchanged.
- Message-hook fixtures use the generic hook-runner result contract.
- Tool metadata collision cases exercise `createPluginToolMetadataLookup` beside its owner instead of comparing the private serialized key.

No production function body changed. The metadata proof moved into a focused sibling file so the existing oversized optional-tools suite shrinks rather than growing.

## Evidence

- Verified all six unwanted export edges existed on the pinned base and have no production consumer or promoted package/SDK surface.
- Passed changed-file formatting with Bun/oxfmt parity, core and extension lint, and the selected production/test type graphs on the final candidate.
- Passed 21 changed and direct-importer test files across the owning Abliteration, Feishu, Zalouser, session-cleanup, message-hook, and plugin-metadata paths. After the owner-test extraction, the focused metadata rows and all 75 remaining optional-tools tests also passed.
- Passed the line-cap ratchet and exact static checks confirming all six export edges are absent.
- Ran all three maintained deadcode analyses: none reports the six removed edges. The commands remain nonzero on pre-existing, separately owned campaign rows; this PR does not relabel that backlog as green.
- The Abliteration live suite remains honestly gated: both model cases and their 120-second bounds are preserved, but no live provider call was made.

The independent full engineering review found no issues, and canonical autoreview was clean at its configured priority. Exact-head CodeQL, Critical Quality, Workflow Sanity, OpenGrep, Periphery, Security Review, and the selected CI lanes passed; the remaining broad gate and ClawSweeper verdict are still pending under the campaign's explicit focused-proof landing policy, with no failure or finding hidden.

prs.title: perf(gateway): share pending staged workspace manifest reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent readers of the same staged workspace result each submit a complete manifest load. Forking one source workspace into distinct sessions is one path that permits this overlap: the target sessions have independent owners, while both read the same source checkpoint.

## Change

Join matching pending staged-manifest reads at the existing result-ref owner. Identity includes the complete root/ref/build-cache input, current directory, a digest of the complete captured environment, and the exact cancellation signal. Different requests remain independent. Worker-context calls continue through their existing host-exchange owner.

The ref owner invalidates the pending lookup before and after its writes, including failed writes. Already admitted readers retain their outcome; later readers cannot join a pre-mutation result, and old settlement cannot evict a newer operation. Success and failure both remove entries. There is no completed-result cache or extra Git lookup.

This is separate from #183087 and does not change its two-await tree-input fix. It addresses staged-result read overlap; no reduction of recovery journal memory or of the previously observed 215 MiB tree-input holder is claimed.

## Evidence

The regression holds the real worker at Git I/O while interleaving ten staged reads. Six distinct identities cover differing root, ref, build-cache inputs, environment, and signal; repeated identical calls arrive between them.

| Work count | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Physical `cat-file commit` reads for ten overlapping callers | 10 | 6 |
| Extra read after the previous calls settle | 1 | 1 |

The first assertion fails on the base with `expected 10 to be 6` and passes with the fix. Additional regressions prove deletion during a held read, conditional cleanup after old settlement, cancellation isolation, and retry after failure. Independent validation of staged output, byte authentication, linked-worktree ref ordering, and Git history remains covered by the existing tests.

Validation: the initial 26-test run passed across `workspace-result-staging.reads.test.ts`, `workspace-result-staging.concurrent.test.ts`, `workspace-result-ref-mutation.test.ts`, and `workspace-result-history.test.ts` (77.78 seconds Vitest; 97.99 seconds including wrapper and cold artifact preparation). The test-only follow-up at `5dd6eb3d68de` releases the old read before waiting for the next worker, avoiding a single-worker test deadlock. All 16 tests in the changed reads file passed again in 50.83 seconds, including the mutation regression with both one and three compute workers (561 and 598 ms). Together with the unchanged 11 sibling tests from the earlier run, this covers 27 distinct tests. Scoped core oxlint (`--tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`), gateway-other test typecheck (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-other.json`), changed-file oxfmt, export-name collision guard, and `git diff --check` passed; affected gates were rerun for the follow-up. Fresh independent autoreviews of the production change and test follow-up found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Final head `5dd6eb3d68de72641506b2bc2fdf2357c785dbcf` is fully green: 66 passing checks, 56 skipped, no pending or failed checks. Both the [CI aggregate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40153145809/job/121050297828) and [maintainer aggregate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40153679293) passed. The completed exact-head review reports no findings. No merge was performed; the lead owns landing.

Production delta: +57 lines. The added owner state is needed to eliminate duplicate work while preserving cancellation domains and mutable-ref invalidation; it retains only unfinished promises and releases each on settlement. Test delta: +166 lines. No schema, public configuration, dependency, or timeout policy changes.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse resident strings in initial model context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a retained session and loading its initial model context retains a second copy of the same transcript strings. A synthetic persisted-session reproduction adds 2.00 MiB per run beyond the SessionManager itself.

Related: #182253.

## User Impact

Initial model history can reuse equal transcript strings already retained by the session. Model-context containers remain independently writable, including nested tool arguments and metadata. No configuration, schema, or provider-request changes are intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

Persisted initial-context payloads are mutable, so sharing entire payload objects would violate existing SDK isolation. The codec now reuses equal resident strings inside the context reader's already private message containers, then builds initial history. This preserves authoritative fields and property order without an extra container copy. Resident SDK edits, getters and proxies cannot replace selected context values. The admitted cohort still makes one mutable container copy while preserving primitive strings, and stops copying a header it immediately discarded.

Production code grows by 34 lines to preserve the existing mutable-container contract. This adds no retained cache, owner, or invalidation policy. The shared copier's existing immutable-payload default remains unchanged.

## Evidence

**The final revision qualifies on retention, untraced costs, and separately calibrated traced promotion.** Five fresh counterbalanced retained-heap comparisons reduced initial-context overhead from **2.008599 MiB/run to 0.195055 MiB/run**, saving **1.813545 MiB/run** (90.290% mean paired reduction). Total manager-plus-context retention fell from **5.977062 to 4.162101 MiB/run** (−30.365%); manager-only retention was effectively unchanged (3.968463 → 3.967046 MiB). Baseline source: `4b5aba362cafeb4c0f1b01a570633731fb2f0a76`; candidate production bytes match the revised PR head.

| Pair | Baseline added bytes/run | Candidate added bytes/run | Signed delta | Relative delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 2,097,933.2 | 198,895.6 | -1,899,037.6 | -90.519% |
| 2 | 2,110,492.0 | 223,185.2 | -1,887,306.8 | -89.425% |
| 3 | 2,100,897.6 | 191,232.4 | -1,909,665.2 | -90.898% |
| 4 | 2,120,749.6 | 212,571.6 | -1,908,178.0 | -89.977% |
| 5 | 2,100,772.8 | 196,764.0 | -1,904,008.8 | -90.634% |

Each cohort retained 20 managers; eight yielded forced collections bracketed each heap reading. All 400 released manager and 200 context weak references reported zero survivors. All ten output hashes, source/load receipts, mutation checks and mutable-container isolation checks matched. Independent and root audits verified all 114 artifacts. There were no guard warnings. Post-release heap drift of 18,640–471,632 bytes is preserved; zero root survivors does not imply that the entire heap returned exactly to baseline. These are forced-GC main-heap retention results, not natural-GC, allocation-churn, or live-service measurements.

The first implementation saved 1.818 MiB/run but was rejected by calibrated latency gates: initial-context means rose 22.893% and 28.747% (+2.940 ms paired mean, +25.820%); p95 rose 18.134%/23.028%, and p99 rose 20.908%/18.991% (2,000 samples per side). Its 12.977% GC/work improvement did not offset those gates. The controller stopped before promotion; no favorable extra was run. The revised implementation removes that additional ordinary-path container copy. Qualified baseline controls are reused only because baseline source, runtime, harness, workload and instrumentation are unchanged; all revised candidate observations are fresh.

The original owner reproduction independently found approximately 2.00 MiB/run of added context and no completed-run registry survivors. The public fixture helper reproduced the canonical synthetic fixture byte-for-byte. An earlier setup failure caused by a disappearing shared dependency was preserved and replaced before samples; subsequent captures use pinned lane-owned copies of the same dependency bytes.

The revised actor seed/read smoke passed exact/window/complete output equality and mutation isolation. Sampled bytes/read were 180,973.712 → 179,356.768 (−0.893%), 1,205,486.160 → 1,223,096.200 (+1.461%), and 1,197,393.504 → 1,199,830.592 (+0.204%), respectively. Each side used 1,000 calls, 32 warmups, and 32,768-byte sampling including collected objects. These are allocation-attribution observations only; the raw profile tree was not persisted. A Dirty admission warning of 2,759,960 kB was retained, followed by a passing guard; no capture was interrupted.

Two fresh CPU-swapped untraced pairs passed ordinary cost thresholds and maximum-pause safeguards. The table reports means of the two baseline/candidate observations; percentages are means of paired relative changes. All latency tails have 2,000 samples per side per pair. Loop tail counts were 3,051/3,092 and 3,034/3,103 (baseline/candidate).

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Signed mean delta | Mean paired delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GC ms/operation | 1.784572 | 1.547319 | -0.237253 | -13.289% |
| Whole-cycle mean ms | 29.902031 | 30.514828 | +0.612797 | +2.053% |
| Whole-cycle p95 ms (n=2,000/side) | 33.319672 | 34.123715 | +0.804043 | +2.414% |
| Whole-cycle p99 ms (n=2,000/side; adjudicated below) | 37.530267 | 36.819880 | -0.710387 | -1.855% |
| Initial-context mean ms | 11.621078 | 12.033793 | +0.412715 | +3.569% |
| Initial-context p95 ms (n=2,000/side; adjudicated below) | 14.466722 | 14.569597 | +0.102875 | +0.744% |
| Initial-context p99 ms (n=2,000/side) | 16.254006 | 16.617718 | +0.363712 | +2.270% |
| Loop p99 ms (counts above) | 24.035327 | 24.354815 | +0.319488 | +1.347% |
| Process CPU ms/operation (context) | 58.014128 | 60.273924 | +2.259796 | +3.898% |

Whole-cycle p99 and initial-context p95 had mixed pair signs, so one predeclared swap-0 extra adjudicated exactly those metrics. Their signed three-pair means were −0.561199 ms versus an adverse threshold of +8.277491 ms, and +0.357861 ms versus +2.995505 ms, respectively. Both qualify. The extra's higher absolute whole-cycle p99 (49.102 → 48.839 ms, n=2,000/side) is retained, not trimmed. Original pairs remain the primary window; the extra is not a new independent window. No admission/watch warnings or diagnostic loss/errors occurred in the revised timing comparisons.

| GC kind | Collection counts, pairs 1 / 2 (baseline → candidate) | Mean total ms per 2,000 operations | Signed delta | Mean paired delta |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Minor | 1,320 → 1,324 / 1,319 → 1,325 | 3406.739 → 2965.410 | -441.330 ms | -12.949% |
| Major | 16 → 13 / 16 → 13 | 146.591 → 116.423 | -30.169 ms | -20.577% |
| Incremental | 16 → 13 / 16 → 13 | 15.813 → 12.805 | -3.007 ms | -19.136% |

Weak-callback and unknown GC counts were zero. Minor p95 changed −0.544 ms (−11.031%) and p99 −0.832 ms (−14.457%), with the per-side counts above: submillisecond context under v5.3. Major p95 changed −0.352 ms (−3.143%) and p99 +0.192 ms (+1.761%); counts 16 → 13 per pair make both context-only. No normalization by major-cycle count.

| Pair | Baseline maximum GC ms | Candidate maximum GC ms | Signed delta | Safeguard threshold ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 12.017 | 15.347 | +3.330 | 50.000 |
| 2 | 11.315 | 11.940 | +0.625 | 50.000 |
| Declared extra | 40.959 | 15.071 | −25.888 | 81.918 |

Initial-read maxima were 18.760 → 27.029 ms and 20.294 → 21.519 ms (n=2,000/side); loop maxima were 31.556 → 34.701 ms and 34.472 → 32.227 ms (counts above). These are preserved context.

Separately traced promotion qualified after four fresh matched A/A pairs. The first control window had tiny mixed signs (−0.061468%, +0.081976%), so its one declared extra was included: the signed three-pair mean was +1,358.928 B/operation versus the +1,253,127.501 B/operation threshold. The other control window was +0.031861% mean and required no extra. No control triggered an adverse promotion gate.

| Traced pair | Baseline promoted B/operation | Candidate promoted B/operation | Signed delta | Relative delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6,262,333.920 | 4,373,235.972 | −1,889,097.948 | −30.166037% |
| 2 | 6,266,801.960 | 4,375,458.144 | −1,891,343.816 | −30.180367% |
| Mean | 6,264,567.940 | 4,374,347.058 | −1,890,220.882 | −30.173202% |

All four candidate raw trace totals independently match the reported main-isolate promotion. Each side captured 2,000 complete operations; minor counts were 1,317 → 1,324 and 1,318 → 1,324, major counts 16 → 14 in both pairs. Promotion by kind was 12,273,495,792 → 8,588,664,136 minor / 251,172,048 → 157,807,808 major bytes in pair 1, and 12,275,891,544 → 8,584,503,352 minor / 257,712,376 → 166,412,936 major bytes in pair 2. No GC-cycle normalization, capture trimming, forced main-isolate GC, guard warning, or interruption occurred. Maximum traced GC pauses were 21.465 → 18.995 ms and 15.312 → 26.638 ms; these are context only. Larger traced-control maxima, including 90.600 ms, remain in the evidence and are not untraced timing gates. All four sides retain the known post-capture 1+1 survivor diagnostic. Raw worker-isolate events are counted separately; this is not a worker-promotion or live-service claim.

The committed owner benchmark uses the real bounded open and initial-context read. Before candidate cost interpretation, four fresh matched A/A controls precede two CPU-swapped A/B pairs, separately for untraced costs and traced promotion. Each side performs 2,000 complete cycles after synchronized warmup, retains a rotating ring of 20 roots, and uses prepared synthetic state. Forced-GC retention is measured separately in five counterbalanced baseline/candidate samples. All comparisons retain guard outcomes, absolute and relative deltas, tail sample counts, GC kinds, and both maximum pauses. No deployed or whole-Gateway improvement claim.

Focused validation for the revision: 24 codec, 31 model-context snapshot, and 11 prompt-prefix tests passed. The snapshot tests cover writable nested values, frozen resident payloads, changed SDK values and property order, throwing accessors, proxies, and resident cycles. The final ownership-only adjustment moves context construction into the codec operation; all 31 snapshot tests passed again afterward. Changed-file lint has only the existing SessionManager size limit (baseline 706 counted lines, revised candidate 705, limit 700); an intermediate 710-line revision was rejected by the commit ratchet and corrected before commit. Formatting and the export-name collision guard passed. Prior `pnpm tsgo:core` and actor tests passed on the first candidate; the revised head relies on PR CI for broad proof. Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), clean after the ownership adjustment. The rebased revision preserves all reviewed production/test/doc bytes. All declared performance stages are complete.

The requested import-closure checks ran again on the revision: 19 passed and three wrapper bootstrap cases failed because this local install has `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.26.11 while the unchanged trust anchor requires 0.26.13. Both actual import-inventory checks and `pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts` passed. This is a local dependency setup gap; the test and wrapper source are unchanged by this PR. Exact-head PR CI completed using its lockfile installation; the local bootstrap gap remains recorded.

The final head `ddbd18a15b7f8c5f379ca6d45a03440a91892c15` completed [CI run 40149748949](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149748949). Its inherited failures and relevant sibling proof are detailed below. An earlier CI attempt caught two benchmark type declarations; both were repaired and the script typecheck passed, with production bytes unchanged.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve owner threads after subagent completions
prs.body:
Closes #181580
Related: #143386

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a restricted subagent completion replaces its owner's native Codex thread, and preserving that thread alone loses the completion's result on the next owner turn.

## User Impact

User impact: the owner resumes its original native thread with the unseen completion input and answer as quoted context. Completion restrictions and the child's persistent restrictions remain enforced. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify verified inherited completion restrictions as turn-scoped at the existing policy owner. The existing temporary-thread lifecycle then preserves the durable owner binding. On resume, exclude only mirrors from that owner's own thread; reuse the existing history cutoff and context renderer to supply the completion delta once.

Fresh host-admitted rows do not always identify a native thread. Keeping them can repeat quoted context after an accepted but failed turn; that recoverable duplication is preferable to silently losing a completion result. No new state or lifecycle owner is introduced.

## Evidence

- Red on unchanged main production: the policy regression expected `turn` but received `conversation` (29 other cases passed). Both native-mirror and host-admitted continuity regressions omitted the unique child result (the two existing durable-context cases passed).
- With the fix, 70 focused tests passed: requester policy and prompt-prefix stability (41), plus durable completion context, bounded continuity, and restricted-thread continuation (29). The four-attempt regressions exercise production attempt lifecycle and real SQLite transcripts with a mocked app-server transport, including original-thread reuse, result recall, retained restrictions, and no later replay.
- After merging main `478ab60992ab`, all four new policy/continuity regression cases passed again; the integrated replay took 168.52s.
- Measured cold baseline wall time was 179.97s for requester policy and 226.90s for durable context; the 70-test candidate run took 683.57s including compilation and cleanup. The native regression uses SQLite and the complete attempt lifecycle because a history-filter unit test would miss the thread-binding defect.
- Targeted core and extension oxlint, oxfmt on all changed files, the edited page's MDX validation, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The native PR worktree typecheck refused the intentionally shared compiler install (declaration input escapes checkout). The standalone package config also proved unsuitable for source-tree typechecking; exact-head PR CI supplies the full typecheck.
- Production: +8/−4 lines; tests: +167/−2; docs: +6/−1. The four-line net production increase adds the required policy classification and thread-specific exclusion without introducing another owner. The separate transcript-writer cases protect distinct admission paths.
- @Marvinthebored supplied the [pinned authenticated Gateway/Codex A/B replay](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6f89f479d5f678071271efe393ec2bf220448c9f/PROOF.md). Its two runs per revision record owner sequences `A,A,B,A,A` with this patch versus `A,A,B,C,C` on base, retained restrictions, correct result recall, and no fifth-turn replay. The report was inspected in this pass; it remains contributor-run live evidence.

Fresh authenticated native replay was not repeated: the existing pinned A/B replay covers this same production change; the fresh local proof uses a mocked app-server transport. Unrestricted catalog rotation remains separate under #167277.

Reported and reproduced by @Marvinthebored.

prs.title: test: use maintained transcript storage boundaries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Transcript storage tests currently reach through two production-internal seams. Archive tests decode bytes through the same helper that owns the decoding, so the round trip cannot independently detect an incompatible archive encoding. A canonical-replacement test calls the database kernel directly instead of the maintained transcript-instance reader. Those test-only edges also keep otherwise private implementation exported from production modules.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime, storage, schema, configuration, migration, or compatibility change. Archive bytes, digests, canonical events, bounded migration behavior, alias provenance, restored source metadata, and replacement behavior remain covered. The production surface becomes smaller: the unreachable archive decoder is removed, and the transcript database kernel is private to its maintained reader.

## Why This Change Was Made

Archive assertions now decode zstd bytes with Node's independent primitive, while file-backed cases continue through the real archive reader. This preserves the existing storage contract without making production expose a decoder only for tests. The alias-publication test now calls `listSessionTranscriptInstances` with the same main-agent database path and exact session options, so it proves provenance through the boundary used by runtime consumers. The implementation-only migration spy is removed while its observable unchanged-byte and migration-decision assertions remain.

## Evidence

The exact committed tree passed remote Oxfmt/Bun parity, focused oxlint, all selected production and test type graphs, and 35 related test files with 428 passing tests across the native Gateway, infra, runtime-config, Plugin SDK, command, and extension-database-worker owners.

The production, full-tree, and script dead-code scans also ran on this tree. Their pre-existing residual inventory remains outside this contribution, while neither `decodeSessionArchiveBytes` nor `listTranscriptInstancesFromDatabase` appears in any result. Hosted CI, exact-head independent review, and the required exact-head automated review remain pending after this early non-draft publication.

prs.body:
Related: #179369

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Mattermost default account losing its SecretRef-backed bot token after a named account with its own token is added.

## User Impact

The default bot can keep running alongside named bots without changing the existing configuration. Explicit default overrides and configurations without a root base URL continue to leave unused root credentials inactive.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mattermost account discovery already retains an implicit default when a root base URL and configured token exist. Secret collection now supplies the same readiness rule to the shared `createChannelSecretContract` hook, so that default owns its root credential. The shared collector still owns assignment, disabled-account behavior, and overrides.

Thanks to @wangmiao0668000666 for the fix, regression, and Gateway/upgrade evidence. Production delta is +24/-6 (net +18); tests are +44. The small production increase replaces the simple-contract shorthand with the existing explicit hook, without adding another collector or expanding the SDK.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on current-main source `a31e54a90d6a5` with the contributor regression: 1 intended failure / 16 passes. The Mattermost root token remained a SecretRef.
- Candidate files: 19 tests pass, including the implicit default, explicit default override, and missing root URL cases. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/secrets/runtime-channel-inactive-variants.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Local proof used the lane's owned installation with the three changed files copied verbatim. The integrated checkout's linked-install run stopped before tests because newer main needs UI dependencies absent from that installation. Exact-head PR CI provides broad validation of the integrated tree.
- Test cost on the loaded host: red run 422.45 s wall including cold worker compilation; green run 172.94 s wall (140.54 s Vitest duration). This extends the existing suite rather than adding a separate Gateway fixture.
- Targeted type-aware oxlint passed for the Mattermost contract and core test files; oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed. Isolated Codex autoreview through P2 reported no actionable findings.
- Contributor live evidence on the unchanged production fix: [isolated Gateway comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182706#issuecomment-6388550157) shows the base losing default and the fixed head starting both accounts; [published-stable upgrade comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182706#issuecomment-6388888485) preserves config and starts both accounts after migration.
- No authenticated Mattermost messaging was live-tested locally: this offline credential-collection fix is covered without an external workspace, and the linked Gateway evidence uses synthetic loopback endpoints.

prs.title: refactor: keep Gateway fixtures on production owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway integration fixtures were importing two inner declarations that production does not expose or consume: a duplicate worker-admission request schema and the inner cron agent runner. Those test-only import edges made the declarations appear necessary even though production already owns both behaviors at higher boundaries.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. Worker admission, scheduled commands, plugin loading, persisted jobs, restart behavior, requester authority, and fallback handling keep their existing behavior and coverage.

The maintenance benefit is that the fixtures now exercise the same owners as production, so unused-export analysis can remove the unsupported inner surfaces without weakening tests or adding an exception.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fake worker Gateway now validates the generic request envelope, matches the exact worker-admission method, and calls the production params validator before replying. This deletes the otherwise unconsumed request-frame schema while retaining the complete admission result and lifecycle assertions.

The scheduled-command fixture now constructs its cron dependencies through `createGatewayCronAgentDeps`. It consumes both the isolated agent runner and the loaded plugin schedule-host resolver returned by that owner. The runner implementation remains unchanged and becomes private.

This is a four-file cutover with no new abstraction, test seam, compatibility path, configuration, dependency, schema, or persisted state.

## Evidence

- Changed-file formatting and Oxlint passed with zero warnings or errors.
- `pnpm protocol:check`, `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, and `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` passed. Generated Gateway validators were unchanged, and the oversized worker runtime test has no line growth.
- All 38 selected production/test type graphs passed.
- Ten directly related worker, Gateway, and scheduled-command test files passed: 254 tests, zero failures or skips. The changed worker runtime file passed 69 tests in 56.24 seconds.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` no longer reports either removed inner declaration. The command remains nonzero for the existing unrelated export inventory; those findings were retained rather than suppressed or described as green.
- The committed tree is byte-identical to the remotely tested candidate.
- A fresh full calibrated review and the separate canonical P0-P2 autoreview both completed clean with no findings.

Broad hosted CI remains in progress on the published head with no observed failure at final qualification.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local lint still selects oxlint even though the pinned S3 Bun fork includes the native lint command.

## User Impact

Local `pnpm lint` and shared lint callers use the checksum-verified pinned Bun fork through `bun lint --no-script`. `OPENCLAW_LINT_TOOL=oxlint` remains available, and an unavailable implicit Bun selection emits the existing fallback notice. CI continues to require oxlint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selector now has one local default for format and lint, removing the retired lint qualification switch and lifecycle-environment workaround. CI compares Bun and oxlint on identical prepared configurations and targets without another job; full diagnostic multisets and exit status must match.

Synthetic lint fixtures deliberately test oxlint configuration, status, artifact ownership, and bounded diagnostic capture, so they explicitly select oxlint instead of accidentally depending on the developer default (bucket 2). The lint-status fixture also declares its runtime dependencies so the generated relocatable wrapper leaves JSON5 external; the original fixture failed all 17 cases on both runtimes after dependency refresh (bucket 2).

## Evidence

Pinned S3 `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de` was verified with `--revision`. On an M3 Ultra Mac (32 logical cores, 512 GiB RAM), one whole-repo `pnpm lint --format=json` run per tool under the shared build lock produced identical 243 diagnostics: zero missing/extra file/line/rule findings, and equal complete diagnostic payloads after rule-name/URL normalization. Both exited 1 on the same untouched baseline findings.

| Measurement | oxlint 1.88.0 | S3 Bun |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Whole command | 912.721 s | 635.015 s |
| Native scripts | 83.902 s | 89.350 s |
| Native extensions | 259.223 s | 450.885 s |
| Native core/UI/packages | 476.482 s | 497.600 s |
| Native sum | 819.608 s | 1,037.835 s |

The first run generated SDK declarations that the second reused; background load reached 86. The faster Bun whole-command time therefore does **not** establish a Mac speed gain, and native timings were slower. The docs retain the oxlint override and report this limitation alongside the earlier AWS 6.15× result. CI parity reuses existing preparation and jobs; the earlier AWS native total adds 23.3 s rather than a new runner. The CI checkout log confirms S3 was staged. Main subsequently advanced the shared pin for the independent TLS SNI fix in #183084; these measurements qualify S3 and make no speed claim for that later revision.

All six touched test files pass individually on Node and pinned S3 Bun (103 tests per runtime):


prs.title: feat(prometheus): expose provider usage windows
prs.body:
Closes #139188

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can monitor OpenClaw request and tool behavior through the authenticated Prometheus exporter, but cannot monitor provider subscription allowance windows or refresh health without maintaining a separate Gateway RPC collector.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing provider-usage cache with a sanitized, selection-bound metrics snapshot and gives only the official Prometheus exporter a lifecycle-scoped observer capability. The cache owns periodic refreshes and last-good retention; Prometheus scrapes remain synchronous, render-only, and network-free.

Credential-backed provider polling is explicit opt-in through `providerUsage.enabled`, which defaults to `false`. The selection contract follows the same default/legacy-agent credential selection as unscoped `usage.status`. Selection changes withdraw prior allowance series until the new selection produces an observation. Exported labels are bounded to provider, window, and refresh outcome; account emails, profile IDs, credential fingerprints, prompts, responses, and other identifiers are excluded.

## User Impact

When operators explicitly enable provider-usage polling, they can graph and alert on:

- provider allowance used ratios;
- allowance-window reset timestamps;
- last refresh attempt and success timestamps;
- refresh success and bounded failure outcomes.

Upgrades and fresh installs do not begin credential-backed provider polling unless `providerUsage.enabled` is explicitly set to `true`. No provider API call is triggered by a Prometheus scrape.

## Review Fixes

- Makes provider-usage polling explicit opt-in and default-off for upgrades and fresh installations.
- Supports lifecycle-safe hot enable/disable without changing ordinary diagnostics or Prometheus metrics.
- Releases the observer and withdraws provider metrics when diagnostics are disabled, and reacquires exactly once when re-enabled.
- Rejects callbacks from retired exporter generations and revoked service leases.
- Cancels future provider refresh scheduling after observer release.
- Reads lifecycle-managed runtime configuration instead of ambient configuration.
- Preserves bounded Z.AI window identities so allowance and reset series cannot overwrite one another.
- Integrates the restricted observer with current plugin-service ownership, reload, rollback, cleanup, retirement, pending-owner, and current-claim lifecycle fencing.
- Preserves explicit runtime-config overrides in capable-client cache tests after the latest upstream rebase.
- Updates the generated plugin config baseline for the intentional two-entry surface increase (`4623` to `4625`).

## Evidence

The exact published head `5bcdf1a3d62bf82e2badcef3919a07eab3628295` passed both the isolated Portainer candidate validator and the published-release upgrade proof before the PR branch was updated.

### Candidate validation

- Validation ref: `validate/pr-141276-5bcdf1a3d6`
- Verified target: `5bcdf1a3d62bf82e2badcef3919a07eab3628295`
- Validation base: `3150853d9dee8ad161011682c130ea5731faa365`
- Merge base: `2f228582f354803021c3d217d3a2fd79b54b0305`
- Candidate runtime handoff SHA-256: `924213e6e6d7dae92d5f038666360275f31423173fa3e87363b0a11db1235dee`
- Runtime build cache: rebuilt

Passed gates: locked dependency installation; changed-file diff hygiene, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and type-aware lint; core, extension, owning test-graph, and extension-test types; plugin contracts; focused provider-usage tests; exact-SHA runtime build; isolated managed-install lifecycle proof including auth-suspended revocation; and the final temporary-ref identity fence.

Managed-install evidence recorded an authenticated scrape, one initial provider request after explicit enablement, provider metrics observed, and zero requests caused by scraping, disabled startup, hot-disable release, plugin revocation, or authority revocation during authentication. The restricted observer capability remained unavailable to a non-official plugin.

### Published-release upgrade compatibility

- Integrity-pinned baseline: `openclaw@2026.9.4` and `@openclaw/diagnostics-prometheus@2026.9.4`
- Baseline/default-off provider requests: `0` / `0` over 65-second observations
- Database schema migration: `19` to `27`
- Operator intent and runtime invariants preserved: `true`
- Diagnostics, provider-plugin, Gateway configuration, and managed exporter installation preserved: `true`
- Initial/scheduled requests after explicit opt-in: `1` / `1`
- Observed cadence: `59852 ms`
- Scrape-triggered requests: `0`
- Requests after exporter disable: `0`
- Candidate exporter tarball SHA-256: `7fcd9712b575c84b346b6a50834f31a4f7e77a91948ec524d847b87bfbe58587`
- Final temporary-ref identity fence: passed

### Current upstream conflict check

Canonical `main` was refreshed to `2f2c09d1c12d93408692e950a82d01fd04fa5af1` after validation. An isolated real merge completed with zero conflicts.
## Maintainer Gate Still Required

The compatibility concern is addressed by making credential-backed polling explicit opt-in. The security-sensitive capability boundary still requires authorized maintainer review and approval for the exact published head.
