prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: fix(opencode-session-catalog): drive the pagination deadline from a monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: multi-page OpenCode session browsing can hang beyond its 30-second scan budget or time out early when the system wall clock changes between pages.

## User Impact

Catalog scans consume one elapsed-time budget across all pages, so system clock corrections do not extend or shorten browsing timeouts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pagination owner now creates and consumes its deadline with `performance.now()`. This preserves the existing shared scan budget and downstream CLI timeout behavior. The regression uses the existing subprocess fixture, verifies the returned live session, and restores its mocks even on failure. A redundant type assertion was removed.

Production: +2/-2, net 0. Tests: +32/-3, net +29. Thanks to @SunnyShu0925 for the fix and regression.

## Evidence

- Current-main base `d2d935290de62bf379e6bb30cce061b7cb8aac72`, regression only: a 60-second wall-clock rewind produced per-page budgets `[30000, 90000]`; the test failed on the inflated second budget.
- Fixed candidate: the full catalog file passed 21/21. Under the same rewind, budgets decreased from approximately 30,000 ms to 29,821 ms, and the live fixture session was returned.
- Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-ct-monoA pnpm test extensions/opencode/session-catalog.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The red run additionally selected `-t 'bounds per-page'`. The temporary budget measurement log was removed afterward.
- Targeted syntax-only oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent diff review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Local type-aware extension checks depend on SDK declaration preparation, which reached its 300-second timeout earlier in this lane; exact-head PR CI supplies broad validation.
- The regression exercises real child processes through the production process runner. A real OpenCode binary/Gateway round-trip was not independently live-tested; this comparison uses the existing synthetic CLI fixture.

### Contributor-supplied Gateway proof

The original contributor supplied the following comparison at head `f6821d5f52ae13fd61dae0be2a52974df9ade064`, inspected and preserved below. The comparison was **independently rerun against the current head `1709033e492ebc575073697ce7ee50202e4012db` on 2026-10-25** with identical results (see re-run logs at the end of this section). The production repair is unchanged.

Real behavior proof through a **running Gateway** (shipped `startGatewayServer` dispatcher + real authenticated `connectGatewayClient` handshake) driving the **real OpenCode v2.0.16 CLI** (`@opencode/cli`), with **archived-first pagination** and a **controlled +60s forward wall-clock step injected on the page-2 budget read** (`Date.now` intercepted only on the `queryOpenCodeSessions` stack). The catalog db holds 100 archived + 1 live session, so page 1 returns 100 archived (skipped, cursor advances) and page 2 returns the live one.

| | before (pre-fix, `Date.now()`) | after (post-fix, `performance.now()`) |
|---|---|---|
| `Date.now` reads on budget path | 3 (`skewCount=3`) | 0 (`skewCount=0`) |
| page-2 budget under +60s forward step | `deadline - Date.now()` collapses negative | `deadline - performance.now()` stays bounded |
| Gateway `sessions.catalog.list` res | `error: { code:"catalog_error", message:"OpenCode session scan exceeded the time limit" }`, hosts empty | `pending:true`, then streams the live session |
| incremental `sessions.catalog.host` event | none | `{hostId:"gateway:local", liveSessions:1, ids:["ses_live_1"]}` |
| bounded browsing outcome | ✗ scan killed, no live session | ✓ live session `ses_live_1` returned |

Before (source reverted to `Date.now()`):

```console
$ node proof-182295-running-gateway.mts prefix
[skew] stepped Date.now +60000ms at queryOpenCodeSessions 3rd read (page-2 budget)
[opencode/session-catalog] OpenCode catalog CLI failed: Error: OpenCode session scan exceeded the time limit
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ sessions.catalog.list … {catalogs:[{id:"opencode",hosts:[],error:{code:"catalog_error",message:"OpenCode session scan exceeded the time limit"}}]}
VERDICT: resElapsed=1715ms skewCount=3
         live session(s) streamed through running Gateway = []
```

After (current head):

```console
$ node proof-182295-running-gateway.mts postfix
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ sessions.catalog.list 1630ms … {catalogs:[{id:"opencode",hosts:[],pending:true}]}
[list] listLocalOpenCodeSessionPage -> 1 live session(s): threadId=ses_live_1 name="Live Session"
[ws] event sessions.catalog.host progressId=oc-proof-progress hosts=[{hostId:"gateway:local",liveSessions:1,ids:["ses_live_1"]}]
VERDICT: resElapsed=1640ms skewCount=0
         bounded browsing streamed 1 live session(s) through the running Gateway
```

### Current-head re-run (2026-10-25, exact head `1709033e492e`)

Same running Gateway (`startGatewayServer` + real authenticated `connectGatewayClient`) against the real OpenCode v2.0.16 CLI, same archived-first seed db (100 archived + 1 live) and same +60 s forward `Date.now` step on the page-2 budget read.

**Post-fix (current head, `performance.now`):**

```
[list] listLocalOpenCodeSessionPage -> 1 live session(s): threadId=ses_live_1 name="Live Session"
[ws] event sessions.catalog.host progressId=oc-proof-progress hosts=[{hostId:"gateway:local",liveSessions:1,ids:["ses_live_1"]}]
VERDICT: resElapsed=2246ms skewCount=0
         live session(s) streamed through running Gateway = [{"threadId":"ses_live_1","name":"Live Session"}]
VERDICT: PASS — post-fix path never read Date.now (performance.now bounded)
```

**Pre-fix (source reverted to `Date.now()`):**

```
[skew] stepped Date.now +60000ms at queryOpenCodeSessions 3rd read (page-2 budget)
[opencode/session-catalog] OpenCode catalog CLI failed: Error: OpenCode session scan exceeded the time limit
VERDICT: resElapsed=1700ms skewCount=3
         live session(s) streamed through running Gateway = []
```

prs.title: fix(ui): recover when restricted members cannot open Home
prs.body:
Related: #157182
Related: #183018

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: restricted members open an inaccessible agent Home, see only Retry, and keep making requests for a conversation they cannot use.

## User Impact

An unavailable Home offers **New conversation** for an allowed agent instead of a disabled composer and recurring Home reads. Accessible Home sessions still open normally. Session visibility, role scopes, configuration, and stored data are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ask the Gateway to resolve Home before mounting its route or dock consumers for `sessions.others: "none"`. The same non-enumerating recovery view serves both surfaces. The shell and sidebar now preserve an explicitly empty route selection instead of falling back to the Gateway’s ambient main session.

This PR addresses Home routing, the Home dock, and denied-read recovery only. The remaining role-ceiling/admin-upgrade guidance from the same issue is being addressed separately in [open companion PR #183018](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183018). This PR does not claim to resolve that separate slice or close the broader report.

This is UI recovery, not a new permission policy or a replacement for invited-guest welcome. It adds no denial cache, timer, session creation, or Gateway authorization change.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with a real isolated Gateway, trusted-proxy synthetic member, one allowed agent, foreign ambient Home sessions, and the production Control UI. Baseline recorded five denied descriptor reads for the selected Home; final candidate recorded none for that Home and no descriptor growth during the settled 12-second observation window. Initial default-main bootstrap probes remain bounded and are not claimed to be eliminated.
- Final session-only member flow reaches `/new?agent=team` through the visible recovery button and renders the new-session composer. A separate general-read/write member flow also opens Home in its dock and reaches the same recovery view without additional descriptor reads. The session-only role’s disabled Home-dock control remains unchanged.
- Route, dock, explicit-empty sidebar selection, and shell regressions fail against their original base implementations and pass with the fix. Focused routing, shell, sidebar lineage/projection, and focus-navigation consumers pass.
- Changed-test commands `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: Home dock 1.81 s; route resolution 1.59 s; shell view 3.48 s; sidebar personal-agent scope 2.87 s. Per-file CI timing has not been extracted; the exact-head CI run is linked below.
- Targeted UI typecheck, changed-file lint/format, UI i18n baseline/verification, Control UI controller guard, whitespace check, and line-cap/assertion-safety ratchets pass against prepared base `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2`.
- Initial CI found a missing required `scope` field in the new Home-dock test roster. The fixture now explicitly uses `per-sender`; the exact failing UI-components test typecheck, three dock tests, targeted lint, and formatting pass. This correction changes no production code. [Corrected-head CI run 40136865728](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136865728), attempt 1, passed for `a4c26c0635a382379fe55089c32bb7286b74bc2b`; the previously failing `check-test-types-core-2` job passes.
- Author simplification removed the ambient sidebar fallback; one Gateway-resolution helper and one recovery view serve both Home surfaces. Fresh independent AutoReview using `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` returned **scoped-clean at P0**. The [exact-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182941#issuecomment-6390249508) reports no findings and **Ready for maintainer review**, while retaining this PR’s explicitly partial scope. Exact-head CI, dependency review, security-sensitive review, and `openclaw/ci-gate` are successful.

No model inference or live deployment was performed. The isolated fixture has no model runtime; model-provider behavior is outside this change. The baseline standalone UI performance check already exceeded its absolute CSS budgets (296.5 versus 296.3 KiB gzip; 1558.7 versus 1558.1 KiB raw); no budget or baseline was changed. Production E2E bundle builds passed. The [exact-head hosted performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136865728/job/121000497401) also passed without changing a budget or baseline.

### Before and after

Production Control UI, real disposable Gateway, synthetic content; inspected and sanitized.

Before

![Before: inaccessible member Home shows only Retry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77a6d608-20e5-4dcd-9e85-5f174c590d3e)

After

![After: member Home offers an accessible new-conversation path](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fb24a17-3899-4b3b-bc5a-bea10dee91cd)

Contributor credit: requested by Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0429cac8-b8e2-4aab-b58d-a22f806e73ef)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/31a9b42d-320e-4b8c-a0b1-335855f95f42)

## Worked on by

- @etzelm

prs.title: fix(postgres): avoid full-table sorts for limited ordered reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PostgreSQL ordered scans that sort whole tables before applying a small limit because generated non-null indexes use the opposite null placement from PostgreSQL's default `ORDER BY`.

Follows #182821 (thanks @etzelm): with nullability-aware index ordering, NOT NULL index keys use PG-native order, so the explicit NULLS FIRST is dropped and the eviction keeps its index; every default ORDER BY on a NOT NULL explicitly indexed column gains index ordering.

Refs #182808

## User Impact

PostgreSQL: cache eviction, session recency, window lookup, and active-event lookup can stop after a bounded index scan. SQLite schema definitions and query results remain unchanged. Existing PostgreSQL stores upgrade through the normal backed-up schema admission path; nullable sort semantics stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generator now emits plain `ASC`/`DESC` for direct columns that the canonical schema declares NOT NULL (including primary-key columns). Nullable columns and expressions retain `ASC NULLS FIRST`/`DESC NULLS LAST`. This matches PostgreSQL's default ordering where null placement cannot affect results, while preserving indexed nullable meeting chronology and existing primary-key history scans.

Versioned migrations rebuild only changed, present indexes under the existing schema admission lock: state 32, agent 34, Workboard 4, Logbook 2, and Team Reports 2. Historical admission and recovery descriptors retain their original definitions; uninstalled optional fragments remain absent. A lazy fragment created on a pre-v32 state store keeps its historical index ordering until the versioned migration runs; this preserves public update capture and rollback admission. Redundant explicit null clauses are removed only from non-null ordered keys. The existing scratch-catalog comparison also needs to preserve PostgreSQL identifier quoting for the Team Reports namespace; stored schema seals keep their existing format.

The rule changes 190 explicit indexes: state 93 eager + 31 optional-fragment indexes, agent 48, Workboard 10, Logbook 7, Team Reports 1. No primary key or UNIQUE constraint is rebuilt. Nullable cross-engine ordering differences remain a separate follow-up.

## Evidence

Acceptance: compare old canonical DDL with freshly generated DDL on populated PostgreSQL 17. Require eviction to use its timestamp index with bounded rows, preserve PK-backed history and nullable chronology plans, and reject a hot-plan regression over 20%. The controlled run uses 31 balanced A/B pairs after warmup, 50,000 rows per populated table, unchanged query compilation, and only the redundant non-null chronology clauses removed. Both fixtures receive VACUUM (ANALYZE) before measurement.

| Statement | Base median ms | Candidate median ms | Plan result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Embedding-cache eviction | 11.267 | 0.097 | Timestamp index, 11 rows for LIMIT 10 |
| Transcript suffix | 0.030 | 0.028 | Same PK scan |
| History tail | 0.025 | 0.027 | Same PK scan |
| Joined history range | 0.125 | 0.132 | Same indexes, rows, and loops |
| Session recency | 9.146 | 0.022 | Bounded ordered index scan |
| Latest window | 8.491 | 0.017 | Bounded ordered index scan |
| Active-event sequence | 5.977 | 0.029 | Bounded ordered index scan |
| Archived sessions | 1.511 | 1.547 | No regression |
| Meeting chronology | 0.020 | 0.018 | Original ordered index-only scan, 51 rows |

An initial combined-head comparison regressed archived listing 1.528→4.909ms because base had been autovacuumed (633/633 all-visible pages) and candidate had not (0/633). Equalizing both fixtures with VACUUM (ANALYZE) restored identical index-only plans, zero heap fetches, and 1.511→1.547ms medians. Normal autovacuum applies after real upgrades; the migration owner has no post-migration ANALYZE hook, and this change adds no new machinery.

The host was heavily loaded; these are component diagnostics, not end-to-end latency or throughput claims. An earlier seven-pair sample overlapped schema-generation tests and had noisy microsecond-scale increases despite identical plans; the raw results were retained before the controlled repeat. All SELECT outputs matched.

<details>
<summary>Timing spread and migration cost</summary>

| Statement | Base p95 ms | Candidate p95 ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Eviction | 47.829 | 0.219 |
| Transcript suffix | 0.060 | 0.052 |
| History tail | 0.047 | 0.046 |
| Joined history | 0.300 | 1.951 |
| Session recency | 16.241 | 0.053 |
| Latest window | 57.729 | 0.024 |
| Active-event sequence | 17.145 | 0.072 |
| Archived sessions | 2.526 | 4.652 |
| Meeting chronology | 0.041 | 0.090 |

The populated agent/meeting fixture rebuilt 54 changed indexes in 3.819 seconds initially and 3.232 seconds on repeat (8.171 seconds in the later loaded-host run). With 500,000 transcript and active-event rows, the three changed active-event indexes rebuilt in 1.109 seconds total (593 ms, 477 ms, 31 ms). `transcript_events` has no explicit secondary index to migrate; its unchanged primary key took 0.684 seconds to REINDEX as a separate calibration. A linear extrapolation of that three-index rebuild to 5 million rows is about 11.09 seconds; it is not a full-install upgrade estimate. Existing Update/Doctor migration, backup, progress, and rollback ownership is retained.

</details>

The actual eviction regression passed on the combined candidate (156 ms test body) and failed at the missing timestamp-index assertion with the exact original-main cache owner and canonical DDL. All five upgrade/idempotence families and meeting chronology passed on the reviewed tree: 29 tests / six files in 45.84 seconds through the PostgreSQL conformance runner. Generated schemas verify up to date. Earlier Doctor backup/upgrade/rollback coverage passed all 17 tests in 148.72 seconds; the affected SQLite suites passed 89 tests in 49.77 seconds, and the additional Team Reports SQLite suite passed 15 tests in 27.07 seconds on the final tree. Both final targeted lint checks passed with zero warnings/errors. Follow-up CI repair proof passed 106 focused tests (two existing runtime-specific skips) in 277.94 seconds, and 57 PostgreSQL public update/rollback, port, vector-migration, and diagnostic tests in 237.14 seconds. The public v25 PostgreSQL capture/rollback regression that failed on the first PR head now passes (11.174 seconds). The final historical-state/refusal/diagnostics run passed 19 PostgreSQL tests in 78.72 seconds, plus four SQLite diagnostics tests in 50.15 seconds; regenerated snapshots change only the expected schema version fields/text. Final targeted typecheck and type-aware lint passed.

Simplification retained one generator policy and shared historical-restore handling across plugins, and replaced the duplicate upstream eviction test with one canonical-DDL regression. Necessary growth registers and restores all five versioned families. Whole change: 1,157 added / 446 deleted lines across 86 files, including generated artifacts.

Independent Codex review completed both original partitions and the final repair delta cleanly with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The conflict-free rebase leaves both commits patch-identical; PostgreSQL review approval carries to `7a0434fbac6f1b695bc3e6d1fd1b6c34afc0d5ab`. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards actually executed and passed on that head in [CI run 40149169028](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149169028): 1,179 tests passed, with 38 existing skips. The canonical-DDL eviction regression passed in 581 ms; the selective state/agent upgrade tests passed in 1,339/774 ms.

Test cost: the six-file focused PostgreSQL command takes 45.84 seconds, including cold compilation. The new state/agent upgrade file takes 22.99 seconds total with 794 ms in its two test bodies; the rest is cold compilation. The cache regression body takes 156 ms. The separate Doctor suite is deliberately slower because it verifies real backup, restore, rollback, and foreign-write refusal.

Post-land proof on merged `fdad53b1bc1d66d98a11da12fb633a75f8285ecb`: the actual merge-base owners (`dcb918e167a9`) created state 31 / agent 33 on disposable Homebrew PostgreSQL 17. The first Gateway start correctly refused the agent rebuild without stopped-writer maintenance (the existing guard's message calls it an identity migration). With the Gateway stopped, `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` saved PostgreSQL migration backups and advanced both physical and application metadata to state 32 / agent 34. The subsequent real Gateway reached `/readyz` with `ready=true` in 27.65 seconds, `gateway health --json` returned `ok=true`, and SIGTERM exited 0. Catalog comparison found 148 rebuilt present indexes, with all 144 pre-existing primary-key indexes unchanged. The eviction index changed from `updated_at NULLS FIRST` to native `updated_at`; nullable chronology retains `started_at_ms DESC NULLS LAST` with native non-null tie-breakers.

This proves the normal stopped-writer Doctor → Gateway upgrade path; direct Gateway startup did not bypass maintenance. Doctor also warned that the shared-volume permissions prevented a separate general pre-repair copy and that the synthetic fixture had no model context; the versioned PostgreSQL migration backups were saved. The loaded host reported CPU degradation while still reporting ready; startup time is a correctness observation, not a performance claim. Frozen Gateway throughput proof is outside this PR's required scope.

Final CI status on the rebased head: all three PostgreSQL shards are green; seven non-PG jobs are red. No CI reruns, longer timeouts, or weaker assertions were applied. Baseline attribution is recorded by exact test/error, rather than matching shard names:

| PR failure | Matching main execution | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Production types and core test types: `session-catalog.test-helpers.ts:122`, TS2739, missing `minProtocol`, `maxProtocol`, `client` | [Scheduled main 40149301577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149301577), jobs 121037449659 / 121037449682 | Same error |
| `package-openclaw-for-docker.e2e.test.ts`: trusted harness checkout without installed dependencies, missing `runtime-process-dependency-url.ts` | [Scheduled main 40149301577](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149301577), Windows job 121037449161 | Same test and missing dependency; PR reports it on Linux |
| `session-catalog.test.ts`: keeps a delayed source off the catalog RPC path | [Scheduled main 40142877272](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142877272), job 121018202179 | Same test failure |
| `cli-json-stdout.hooks.e2e.test.ts`: remote Gateway missing its URL | [Main qualification 40134503356](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40134503356), job 120994763231 | Same newline/Error-prefix mismatch |
| `cli-json-stdout.e2e.test.ts`: sandbox explain validation failures | [Main qualification 40134503356](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40134503356), job 120994763739 | Same unknown-agent versus mismatch message |
| `agent-terminal-delivery.e2e.test.ts`: strict NO_REPLY prefixes | [Main qualification 40149400985](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149400985), job 121039356537 | Same no-answer fallback versus output-token-limit warning |

The failing source paths are unchanged by this PR. Main qualification run 40134503356 tests main commit `dc3a0a6a3d7a2759c24d0ed41ac8761585b5745f`; run 40149400985 tests main commit `f29cd04d022e91958d54d1762b6582d4065bbd5d`. All seven red jobs are attributed to matching main failures. The former frozen-install overlap timeout cleared after the rebase.

Follow-up: partial-index predicates such as `archived_at IS NOT NULL` could establish non-nullability for ordering and remove the archived-listing sort; this change intentionally uses declared column/primary-key nullability only.

prs.title: fix(cli): escape terminal controls in DNS setup previews
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes DNS setup previews that emit terminal controls from a state-directory name, allowing a zone path to change styling or appear as extra report rows.

## User Impact

The preview displays control-bearing paths safely while preserving printable Unicode, the actual zone path, recommended JSON configuration, and setup behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `renderTerminalSafeTable`, which delegates to the canonical `sanitizeTerminalText`, at the table owner. The integration preserves the recent fix that awaits zone publication before restarting CoreDNS.

Thanks @Alix-007 for the fix and original real-CLI proof.

## Evidence

- Registered Commander regression: red on unchanged production code (1 failed), then green with the fix. All 7 DNS tests pass again after integrating current main, including the asynchronous zone-publication regression.
- The regression checks escaped controls, preserved Unicode and JSON guidance, and no dry-run filesystem writes or subprocess calls. Original focused run: 24.54s wall time, under 1s test time.
- Targeted typed oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. The final diff matches the reviewed candidate.
- Production +5/−2 (net +3), tests +21/−0, docs +2/−0. The small production increase is the existing safe-renderer import formatting; no new helper or policy.
- Optional broader `check-changed`: all checks except the dead-export scan passed, including core/test typechecks, lint, formatting, and boundaries. The export scan reports unrelated unchanged files; none of the DNS files appears in its findings.
- A fresh standalone CLI live replay was not repeated on this source-only, heavily loaded Mac. The contributor's earlier built Linux CLI dry run reported embedded controls changing from 4 to 0 while preserving Unicode, with no zone/config writes, installation, or service restart. That is prior contributor evidence, not exact-head live proof.

<details>
<summary>Prior contributor CLI traces (original base and contributor head)</summary>

Temporary fixture roots are replaced with `$FIXTURE`; host IPs and incidental toolchain paths are redacted. JSON escaping makes terminal-control bytes inspectable without executing them.

```json
{
  "phase": "red",
```

prs.title: fix: Windows workspace sync fails before lease acquisition
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Windows shared-host workspace synchronization failing before lease acquisition when a node uses the legacy fallback. That fallback passed the complete cross-platform quiescence program through `node -e`; the emitted command exceeded the Windows process argument limit before the program could select its small SQLite-backed Windows branch.

## User Impact

Windows nodes without the negotiated native quiescence capability can now acquire the existing shared-host workspace lease without hitting `ENAMETOOLONG`. There is no configuration, schema, protocol, dependency, permission, or migration change.

The current lease behavior is preserved: acquisition still uses the same SQLite transaction and JSON record, and renewal, release, expiry pruning, nonce validation, overlap exclusion, and interrupted-transaction rollback remain owned by the existing implementation. Native-capability dispatch and POSIX or dedicated-host behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The caller already distinguishes Windows-only absolute paths, shared-host mode, and negotiated native custody before dispatching a command. This change uses those existing facts to select a bounded legacy acquire program only for that Windows case.

The bounded and full programs compose the same extracted Windows acquire operation, so they cannot drift into competing lease algorithms. The full cross-platform program remains the owner for POSIX acquisition and for the generated native entrypoint; legacy renew and release retain their existing programs. The existing Windows real-spawn fixture now executes the bounded acquire program while keeping all of its current lifecycle and SQLite assertions.

The bounded composer also retains the existing mode validation. Production reaches it only for Windows shared-host acquisition, while the fixture can still prove the established Windows dedicated-mode rejection without first exceeding the process argument limit.

## Evidence

On the pinned base, the legacy acquire command measured 33,741 characters and included both the Windows lease implementation and the unused POSIX process probe. On this head, the bounded shared-host command measures 5,455 characters, contains the existing Windows lease implementation, and excludes the POSIX probe. The full program still contains the POSIX path and measures 33,826 characters.

An initial hosted Windows run confirmed the bounded shared-host lease lifecycle but found that the preserved dedicated-mode rejection control still used the full program and failed at launch. The correction carries that existing mode through the bounded composer and preserves its established `workspace quiescence requires POSIX` result; remote pre-push measurement shows the dedicated control at 5,453 characters. Exact-head Windows confirmation of both scenarios remains pending after this update.

Remote pre-publication validation passed on the exact committed tree:

- changed-file formatting and lint;
- generated runtime-script parity;
- the affected test-type graph and all remaining production/test type graphs;
- all seven test files that directly import the changed owners, including the existing caller, lifecycle, native-host, synchronization, and QA runtime suites: 53 tests passed;
- the Windows file loaded but its two platform-only real-spawn cases were skipped on Linux, as expected.

The required exact-head `checks-windows` job remains pending after publication. It must run `workspace-quiescence.windows.test.ts` on Windows and pass the existing real process-spawn, SQLite lease, concurrency, expiry, renewal, release, dedicated-mode rejection, and transaction-interruption scenarios before this PR is ready to land.

prs.title: fix(text): settle ownership after completed paragraphs
prs.body:
Supersedes #181708. Rebased onto current `main` after #181511 changed the checkpoint refresh path; all four changed files replayed cleanly and the list-after-code-block regression tests pass. The original branch cannot be force-pushed under the contribution workflow.

Fixes #181696

## What Problem This Solves

A streamed reply that began with a completed leaked plain-text tool call and then a paragraph re-projected the entire retained reply on every later delta. Visible output remained correct, but a 32 KB reply blocked the Gateway thread for roughly 12 seconds locally.

## User Impact

Completed tool calls now settle at the blank-line boundary, so ordinary prose after them streams with bounded work. The 32 KB repro drops from 12.3 s to 0.38 s and output remains identical to the canonical sanitizer. Nonblank LF and CRLF continuations retain the ownership cache instead of reintroducing repeated parsing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checkpoint ownership cache reused parsed ownership across a newly created blank line. The cached `retainStart` still pointed at the completed tool call, so `findTextCheckpoint()` kept returning the opening line and `projectPlainTextToolCallBlocks()` rescanned the whole reply for every delta.

The checkpoint now refreshes ownership on a genuine blank-line completion, treating a CRLF split across chunks as one line ending and ignoring ordinary nonblank lines. The shared reuse predicate remains stable, so settled XML output does not rescan the cumulative reply after each paragraph.

## Evidence

### Shipped Gateway proof

A temporary E2E harness exercised the real Gateway `agent` / `agent.wait` path and reconstructed the `chat` subscriber stream. It used a mock OpenAI-compatible provider that emitted 4-character deltas. The completed-tool-call case sent `[tool:read] {}\n\n` followed by 29,717 characters of ordinary prose; the Gateway subscriber received the exact 29,701-character visible reply in 4,445 ms, with `containsToolCall: false` and the expected trailing `Done.`.

```text
GATEWAY_STREAM_PROOF {"label":"tool-call-prose","elapsedMs":4445,"deltaEvents":45,"inputCharacters":29717,"outputCharacters":29701,"outputSha256":"68486157a2e817c71dff9748a3ceeb7c417bb995bbefef4eddf08f52eacc719b","outputPrefix":"Answer paragraph with ordinary prose and no tool markers. Answer paragraph with ","outputSuffix":"no tool markers. Answer paragraph with ordinary prose and no tool markers. Done.","containsRuntimeMarker":false,"containsToolCall":false}
```

The same run also streamed 262,144 ordinary characters with exact output and exercised a split runtime marker; the marker was stripped. The temporary proof harness was removed after capture.

### Regression and work bounds

The original P2 finding is fixed at `14e30dd4`. A follow-up P2 showed that putting the blank-line invalidation in the shared predicate also disabled settled XML reuse; that is fixed at `8804f3ee` by refreshing only the checkpoint ownership cache. Production-projector assertions cover nonblank multiline tool-call continuations for both LF and CRLF.

```text
Base 9fae: LF 18671 ms -> expected 2 to be >= 512
Base 9fae: CRLF 16661 ms -> expected 2 to be >= 512
Base 9fae: reusable LF 7303 ms -> expected 512 to be +0
Base 9fae: reusable CRLF 7006 ms -> expected 512 to be +0
Base 9fae: split CRLF -> expected false to be true
Head 14e30dd4: 5 passed, 25 skipped
Head: LF 196 ms, CRLF 159 ms, reusable LF 21 ms, reusable CRLF 17 ms, split CRLF 2 ms
```

XML work bound, `<tool_call>{}</tool_call>\n\n` followed by 512 blank-line-separated paragraphs in 4-character deltas:

```text
pre-fix 14e30dd4: 512 rejected ownership-reuse checks
fixed 8804f3ee: <16 rejected ownership-reuse checks
```

Deterministic work bound through `createAssistantVisibleStreamText("final_answer")`, 4-character deltas:

```text
base: 114,261,817 projected characters (budget 120,916)
head: 257,000 projected characters
```

Same-host shipping-path timings (Node 24.22.1, fresh process per data point):

| Payload | Base `e65af3ab` | This head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 16 KB `[tool:read] {}` | 3,088 ms | 198 ms |
| 32 KB `[tool:read] {}` | 12,258 ms | 382 ms |
| 16 KB `[tool:read]` + JSON | 3,181 ms | 194 ms |
| 32 KB `[tool:read]` + JSON | 12,319 ms | 309 ms |

Validation: 297 tests pass across `src/shared/text` and `packages/tool-call-repair`, including the new XML blank-line regression and the existing plain-tool-call bound; `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` pass.

## AI Assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance under contributor direction and review.

prs.title: refactor(team-reports): use one API request deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Team Reports arms a caller AbortController watchdog for 30 seconds and also asks the guarded transport for the same 30-second deadline. The native transport migration removed the alternate fetch path, so the guarded transport can now own that deadline alone.

## User Impact

No user-visible change: retain the same 30-second budget and timeout warning while removing one redundant timer per API request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the caller watchdog, controller and cleanup. Preserve the guarded transport timeout through response-body consumption, HTTPS/SSRF checks, final-effect authority and response release. Normalize its pre-header TimeoutError and native post-header AbortError to the existing timeout warning. There is no caller cancellation input on this function. No SQL, schema, SDK or PostgreSQL identity behavior changes.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule (registered before measurement): flow is a synthetic Team Reports GitHub roster request, including stalls before headers and during body consumption. Successful response data, timeout warning and released resources must hold; active caller/guard deadline timers must fall from two to one per API request. Ordinary chat turns remove zero timers. Timer savings are source-attributed operation counts, not a timing benchmark. Run one frozen v3.1.4 baseline/candidate Gateway workload pair on the same platform for warm SQL/request/MAIN non-regression (ten warm turns per revision, cold/restart phases separate), with attribution for any phase movement. Use `measure.py --repetitions 1 --idle-seconds 0 --settle-seconds 0`: all ten warm turns plus restart retained, idle-only sampling omitted because no idle owner changes. Any attributed SQL/request increase or any warm MAIN increase is a stop. No 20% regression will be called noise without evidence and disposition. Host contention makes latency unmeasured.

The full deadline inventory contains 122 grouped chains: 2 REMOVE, 111 KEEP and 9 OWNER-REDESIGN. This PR handles the Team Reports site; the independent MCP body-reader site is a separate follow-up. Retained deadlines cover credential discovery, cold capture setup, startup, queueing, pagination or cleanup beyond the transport request.

Validation: 38/38 tests pass in the pinned Bun GitHub, Discord and transport owner suites, including parameterized header/body timeout warnings and timer cleanup. Formatting and direct type-aware oxlint pass. Both isolated Codex reviews are clean. Exact-head CI [40150927347](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40150927347) passes, including types, lint, source/architecture checks and the final CI gate. The local repository lint wrapper rejected the prescribed external virtual-store path; no guard was changed, and CI supplied the complete static checks.

Frozen v3.1.4 baseline/candidate arms both pass all synthetic Gateway phases and child cleanup on the same macOS host. Counts below are ten warm windows per arm, median [min–max], with nearest-rank p95. The host was loaded; no latency/CPU-speed claim is made.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm SQL | 50.5 [50–64], p95 64 | 50 [50–70], p95 70 |
| Warm worker requests | 12 [12–17], p95 17 | 12 [12–16], p95 16 |
| Warm MAIN SQL | 0 [0–0] | 0 [0–0] |
| Whole-workload SQL / requests / MAIN | 2,897 / 758 / 95 | 2,876 / 754 / 96 |

Attribution and disposition: the +1 whole-workload MAIN statement is a cold-boot `PRAGMA busy_timeout` adjustment; all runtime MAIN remains zero. Compaction moves 108→146 SQL and 19→26 requests; the added window work is memory shadow/schema admission and source inventory, whose whole-workload operation counts are unchanged. Restart-connect moves 19→27 SQL and 6→14 requests as cron/background maintenance lands in a different window. These >20% cells are recorded explicitly, not accepted as a Team Reports regression: the touched HTTP owner performs no SQL or worker requests, and its operations add zero. Warm SQL p95 increases by six statements from unrelated work sharing the windows. Whole-workload operation differences are limited to background/session/device maintenance. The measured gain is one fewer deadline timer per Team Reports API request, not SQL savings.

Open-PR overlap: #145765 at `4054a59df7ea4b82f437bcab51655d3f28e6646a`; base-only versus base+candidate merge-tree has the same three pre-existing conflict files and same three content regions, zero new conflicts.

Production: 4 lines added / 5 removed (net -1), one timer site removed. Tests: 38 lines added in the existing owner suite. No schema, transaction, identity mapping, SDK surface or PostgreSQL-reachable SQL change.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): remove a transcript readiness round trip
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Remote chat reloads and session switches waited for a message-subscription acknowledgment before issuing the initial transcript request, adding a full network round trip.

## User Impact

The initial transcript arrives with the subscription acknowledgment. Live events remain covered by the admitted observer, and history failures retain the subscription and use the existing retry path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway accepts an optional `initialHistory` request on `sessions.messages.subscribe`, registers the observer first, and invokes the canonical `chat.startup` reader. The UI consumes that one-shot result through its existing history owner, including the exact cached cursor/state revisions and stale-result checks. Existing clients omit the new field and retain their response shape; the wire protocol remains v4. The UI and Gateway ship together.

Approval-enabled subscriptions keep their scoped read, replay, and session-access authority through history preparation and recheck immediately before committing the observer and publishing. The provisional observer already delivers events, so revocation can roll it back without leaving an unowned subscription. History read failure alone still returns a retryable history receipt with the authorized observer.

Snapshot restoration stays independent of subscription setup, which never waits for IndexedDB. The optional speculative validator prefetch was removed to retain the existing loader ownership and import budget. A full page requested before storage settles already covers a subsequently restored cache: the history owner consumes it under the original exact request parameters. Delta requests still discard mismatched cursor/state receipts and issue a current history read. A late stored snapshot cannot replace live history. Automatic reaction baseline reads wait for transcript readiness, using the existing hydration callback; live reaction events and writes remain immediate. HTML retains its existing `private, no-store` bootstrap contract. The transport requires `connect` as the first frame and admission before ordinary requests, so pre-connect pipelining cannot remove that exchange. HTML contains the current authority-scoped bootstrap preferences and plugin grants, so this change retains its existing cache contract rather than splitting them into another fetch.

```text
Warm reload, before (5 serial exchanges):
HTML → WebSocket upgrade + challenge → connect/hello → subscribe → chat.startup → transcript
Warm reload, after (4 serial exchanges):
HTML → WebSocket upgrade + challenge → connect/hello → subscribe + initialHistory → transcript

Session switch: subscribe → chat.startup → transcript  ⇒  subscribe + initialHistory → transcript
Composer on warm reload: HTML → upgrade/challenge → connect/hello → models.snapshot push → ready
```

Config reads, snapshot validation, and session resolution overlap this authenticated warm path. Composer readiness retains three client-initiated exchanges plus a server push; combining history does not remove a composer dependency.

The first cold read exposed a separate pool issue: the existing prewarm task prepared only whichever history worker accepted it. A later request could select the other foreground worker and spend over a second loading presentation modules. Each existing foreground worker now prepares that same module group at startup, including replacement workers. Database admission stays in its existing prewarm owner; search, projection, and maintenance workers retain their lazy graphs. The existing two-worker foreground pool and its capacity are unchanged; preparation now follows each worker's lifetime.

## Evidence

Rerunnable workload (both source checkouts detached, with their built bundles; output outside either repository):

```sh
  --bundle-dir dist/control-ui --compare-source-dir ../base \
  --compare-bundle-dir ../base/dist/control-ui --profile remote \
  --auth token --pairs 20 --output /absolute/proof/remote
```

Target: 30% lower remote warm transcript/composer medians. Local median regression must stay within 5% with no worse p95. When the A/A control falls outside the timing band, judge twenty paired samples with renderer thread CPU and structural counts; also report Gateway-process CPU and readiness RSS with their A/A variability. The final workload uses synthetic token authentication on both sides and waits, outside timed intervals, for the real app-written boot record and persisted transcript cursor. Earlier auth:none diagnostics are excluded from the final cohort; this is not a direct timing comparison with #182752.

The final five-pair A/A control and 20 interleaved base/head pairs per profile are complete. The A/A timing control missed the band, so CPU and structural counters are reported alongside all timings. No worker starts inside the window. Head’s two eager-prewarm workers already existed about 33 seconds before New Session. Continuous process CPU falls **1,336 → 1,137 ms**, main-thread CPU **373 → 338 ms**, and switch-window process CPU **442 → 314 ms**. The worker observed serving the RPC history task uses **54 → 8 ms** sampled switch CPU (it also serves reactions, pending inputs, and progress; this is not exclusive RPC CPU).

The task trace independently identifies a non-history `session-exact-entries` read overlapping switch readiness and continuing into the tail. Its worker’s sampled continuous CPU increases 246 → 298 ms while history-serving worker work falls. Native/nested/untracked CPU remains separate. These captures establish equal task counts, lower repeated history-serving work, and substantial background overlap; they cannot retroactively identify the exact cause of the original 193% process-window increase. No profiler is activated by these counter/task captures; product-owned automatic stall profiling may run independently. The instrumented all-isolate profiles were used only for exploration because their overhead changes scheduling.


The remote-link simulator was corrected before the accepted cohort: it now bounds each shared-bandwidth direction, rotates active flows in 16 KiB turns, overlaps propagation, honors backpressure, and drops cancelled flow reservations. The previous unbounded future reservations could make a cancelled speculative preload delay the next navigation. A real TCP half-close test and four shaping/cancellation tests pass; all accepted base/head measurements use the same corrected instrument.

Final matched builds at `1cb20e1b5258d68b7009c8fa1550feb8fc405f57` against base `db9330ab86addb6d08d0b0679f9b05b0122ad2bd` use one Node 26.12.1 / Vite 8.3.4 / Pako 3.0.2 toolchain and fixed build identity. Chat boot is **1,270,847 → 1,271,383 B (+536 B)** with 19 JS / 3 CSS requests; New Session is **766,679 → 766,731 B (+52 B)** with 16 JS / 3 CSS requests. All CSS is byte-identical; the absolute-only total-CSS ceiling remains exceeded on both sides (303,561 B versus 303,372 B), with zero growth and no allowance change.

The reaction owner suite passes 13 tests and post-transcript hydration passes seven on the integrated source. The actual-request reaction regression is red on the base and green with the guard. UI and core typechecks passed at `1cb20e1`; the latest merged-head core type exception is recorded below. The later CI repair also passes focused lint, the assertion-safety and manual-import ratchets, the mock-export guard, the line-cap ratchet (38 changed source files), and the zero-cycle import check. Four real-Gateway observers now recognize bundled history while retaining transcript, cursor, recovery, and readiness assertions; the selected-agent fixture uses the real session capability. After integrating main’s nonblocking cache restoration and owned-buffer serialization, the 27-test warm-startup file, five history-issuance tests, and 15 serialization/transport tests pass. The first added lazy-import assertion raced module loading; it now waits for the observable request while storage stays unresolved.

Focused proof: UI history issuance regression fails on the base and passes with the change; SDK one-shot ownership tests, protocol schema rejection, observer-before-history/failure tests, raw nested-array serialization, UI typecheck, scoped lint, and native protocol determinism pass. Production Knip was run on the integrated head and exact base `db9330ab86addb6d08d0b0679f9b05b0122ad2bd`: both fail with the same four unused files: `protocol-validator-schemas.ts`, `mcp-app-standalone-host.ts`, `repository-node-requirement.ts`, and `src/sessions/runtime-context.ts`. No ignore or allowance was added.

Independent Codex review: the full change, reaction scheduling fix, worker initialization, and measurement additions have no actionable P0–P2 findings; fresh full candidate review against integrated main completed in two isolated passes with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Review caught an event-triggered baseline read bypass in the first scheduling fix; the central owner now gates it. A subsequent hosted P1 found premature approval-authority release before initial history; the repair retains and rechecks that authority through publication. Its focused regression reaches the real history reader and is red on the previous handler. `pr-simplify`: the existing history owner still owns retries and publication; the subscription coordinator retains only the observer, not a reusable history snapshot.

LOC before/after across final changed files against the integrated base: production 7,923 → 8,151; tests 6,081 → 6,849; benchmark 1,196 → 1,522; protocol docs plus benchmark guide 1,002 → 1,050. The startup baseline remains unchanged from main. Generated validator output 23,052 → 23,071 lines; generated identifier renumbering accounts for the larger diff. Across the eight touched UI production files, the refactor census is 0 → 0 for rendering controllers, effects, render effects, untrack, DOM listeners/queries, flush, and owner APIs. No view owner is added.

Final functional smoke uses clean committed head `1cb20e1b5258d68b7009c8fa1550feb8fc405f57`, one run per profile. These runs verify readiness and wire counts; they are not a new timing cohort. The local trace before the final repair made one subscription plus one redundant startup request on warm reload; the final local and remote traces make one subscription and no standalone history request.

## What Problem This Solves

Session owner and participant avatars return 404 when an agent identity uses a data URL avatar.

Fixes #182688

## Why This Change Was Made

The avatar handler now serves prepared data URL thumbnails for unversioned session avatar requests and returns them with private, no-cache headers.

## User Impact

Session rows can display agent avatars configured with data URLs.

## Evidence

- Focused regression at the pinned base: failed as expected with `expected 200, received 404`.
- Focused regression at the rebased head: passed (1 test file, 32 tests; 35.32 s total).

prs.title: perf(diagnostics): add native allocation attribution probe
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adds a reproducible Linux probe to distinguish live native allocations from the residual obtained by subtracting V8 heap/external counters from Gateway RSS. The residual alone cannot identify an allocation owner.

## User Impact

There is no production behavior or configuration change and no deployment memory reduction claimed. Maintainers can profile an isolated synthetic Gateway with jemalloc, collect forced-GC observations from its isolates, and inspect allocator counters alongside mappings. The probe refuses missing replies or a changing worker census.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two fresh built Gateways on a 5,000-session / 6,000-settled-run fixture produced stable residual windows near 198 MiB. The leading sampled families were Node module/package loading (44.7–48.9 MiB), other V8 allocations (24.1–26.0 MiB), CPU-profiler metadata (18.9–19.5 MiB), SQLite (18.1–20.2 MiB), and V8 heap-page metadata (16.6–18.1 MiB). Compression contexts were not a large sampled owner.

The workload does not reproduce larger production worker/traffic/plugin mixes, so these results do not justify extrapolating a complete production attribution or changing worker lifetimes. Stopping the continuous stall recorder would remove useful behavior and reintroduce native code enumeration. No behavior-preserving optimization candidate was established.

The per-script guide contains the full measurement table, allocation-site interpretation, reproduction commands, and limitations. Runtime production LOC delta is zero; added benchmark-only code provides the missing native allocation boundary. No dependency, schema, runtime flag, or service configuration changes.

## Evidence

- Measured application source: `5281dc3a72b1016ee33b0c0d76c89cc7835acd33`; Node 26.12.1, V8 14.6.202.34-node.40, jemalloc 5.3.0-4. Linux rig, synthetic state, loopback, 12 GiB scope, low scheduling priority. No Testbox/Crabbox leases.
- Full runtime build on the rig passed (6m 48.6s); no local runtime build or test suite.
- First Gateway: six snapshots, 16/16/17/16/16/16 isolates; final three met the predeclared stable-census and allocation-spread rule. Second Gateway: four stable 16-isolate observations, then five idle transcript workers retired; both the immediate and settled retirement observations are reported. These are time points, not independent A/B pairs or a performance-candidate gate.
- Native profiles: 290 and 293 sampled live allocations; 145.2 and 146.4 MiB estimated live bytes. `external` overlaps these figures and is not added to them.
- Calibration: a known retained 64 MiB Buffer appeared as 64.5 MiB in jeprof; allocator/external increases and release after forced GC passed. Terminated-worker census cleanup passed. The final procfs mapping capture produced nonempty files.
- C addon compiled with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` against matching Node headers.
- Focused formatting, lint, syntax, `git diff --check`, and export-name collision guard passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 2 files / 22 tests passed.

Early source-mode probes included extra TypeScript worker isolates and are exploratory only. A worker exit correctly invalidated one collection. A procfs copy issue was fixed before the final mapping capture. Profiled/forced-GC runs do not establish CPU, latency, promotion, or natural-GC improvements. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) is scoped-clean through P2 after fixing dump-label collisions and shared-log draining. The collision rejection was exercised through the CLI before any command was sent. PR CI supplies the broad checks.
