prs.title: experiment(control-ui): cached chat pane content [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A warm reload can assemble a chat pane over several visible steps even when the conversation has not changed. Earlier evidence recorded 14 visual states for a signed-in dashboard deep link. This experiment targets late content inside the chat pane.

**Rejected experiment — do not merge.** The chat primary gate fails, Details still flashes a skeleton, and first painted rows regress. The draft will be closed; no release or deployment is requested.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cached messages already contain activity, tool review outcomes, and run-failure details. The candidate replaces nested lazy imports for activity and notice/divider renderers with ordinary imports, retaining error isolation. It preloads the existing docked Details composition during the transcript mount hold. Connection scheduling, cached anchors, server state, and resource admission stay with their existing owners. The route already has an early import and route module preloads; this experiment adds no competing route preloader or cache.

## User Impact

This candidate is insufficient for a one-step reload. Cached review and failure content joins the first row commit, but activity bodies, Details sections, avatar images, and row geometry still change later. Moving this work earlier also delays the first painted rows. No version, configuration, protocol, or server stored-shape changes.

The remaining work is at the presentation boundary: preparing nested run-frame content before the first reveal, deciding how cached Details facts can avoid its asynchronous first mount, and coordinating cached avatar admission with the shared loader work. The avatar's `mediaReadAllowed` boundary still delays creating the real avatar view; HTTP cache residency alone does not remove that phase. No second avatar loader was introduced here.

## Evidence

Pinned base: `7bddc5d70497c54c9a09574b9c124a6c11a93885`. Candidate: `30928f5566e04607d45ebd8cbc22008b89c2ce6d`.

AWS Crabbox lease `cbx_14a5d64d0532`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge`, Node 26.12.1, repository Playwright Chromium, Team-scale synthetic workload, live-fast latency, 11 alternating baseline/candidate chat pairs, unprofiled. The dedicated 16-vCPU machine had about 2.0–2.3 load during the measured runs. Every measured reload received `kind: delta` with zero messages; all 22 cached anchors retained zero offset shift. Structural measurements exclude hidden/clipped rows. Diagnostic filmstrips are separate from timing runs.

The primary requires at most two post-content visible waves on every unchanged reload and zero late lazy-view/Details skeletons. Baseline wave counts were `5,4,6,5,4,6,5,5,5,5,4`; candidate counts were `4,5,4,6,4,4,5,5,4,4,5`. Every candidate exceeds the structural proxy threshold; this alone does not prove the number of compositor-visible waves in all 11 pairs. Details skeletons appear after content in all 11 candidates. No lazy-view skeleton appears after content in either variant; a pre-content lazy-view phase remains.

First painted rows regress with non-overlapping IQRs and 10/11 pairs worse; median paired delta is +32 ms. Other measured secondary metrics do not regress under the campaign rule. A small FCP rise has overlapping IQRs and mixed pair signs.

**Dashboard gap:** its initial fixture setup timed out waiting for a visible Details section, before any measured run. The fixture starts on the dashboard face and waits before switching to the intended chat dashboard layout; a closed Details panel does not satisfy that wait. This is a harness gap, not a dashboard product result. There are no dashboard timing claims. The decisive chat failure ends qualification; no full UI suite, changed-file gate, or ready-PR CI was pursued.

prs.title: fix: stop dead-code checks flagging maintained inputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the repository's dead-code checks flag maintained path-invoked commands, dynamically loaded proof fixtures, generated protocol declaration companions, and two direct semantic-owner test seams as if they had no owner.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. Maintainers get more accurate unused-file and script-export results while unrelated orphan files and authored export findings remain detectable. Commands, benchmarks, generators, generated JavaScript, dependencies, schemas, configuration semantics, and product behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The affected files cross boundaries that static imports do not describe: maintainers invoke some commands by path, proof and test owners spawn or preload fixtures through computed paths, and bundled plugins select fixtures by basename or module specifier. This change registers those exact files through the existing literal entry arrays instead of adding a wildcard or ignore. Five test-only dynamic fixtures live only in the full-tree test-aware workspaces, so their imports cannot count as production consumers.

The script-only export pass also pulled 25 generated Gateway protocol declaration companions into its script graph even though the application scans own their same-basename runtime validators. The existing generated-declaration convention now covers that exact directory. Ordinary static imports are deliberately left out so Knip still follows the real graph, and the generated JavaScript remains analyzed.

Two internal decision owners are intentionally exercised directly by focused Doctor migration and worker exec-approval tests. Exact-file production-only `exports` entries preserve those semantic boundaries without exempting their types or any sibling declarations; the full-tree test-aware pass still audits both consumers.

## Evidence

- Remote changed-file formatting passed with oxfmt/Bun parity for both config files.
- All selector-required core test, core, UI, extension, extension-test, scripts, and root-test type graphs passed.
- `test/scripts/check-deadcode-exports.test.ts` and `test/scripts/check-deadcode-unused-files.test.ts`: 24 tests passed for the root-entry candidate; the affected export-owner suite then passed 15 tests after the declaration-only addition.
- The complete production/full-tree unused-file scan confirmed all 82 selected live inputs and both ordinary static imports were no longer residuals. Its post-scan verifier then rejected an outdated expectation that the Codex validator schema remain residual; the newly rooted validator benchmark statically imports that schema, so this is expected reachability rather than suppression.
- A focused `knip@6.40.0` script-export scan confirmed all 1,112 findings from the 25 generated declaration companions were removed while authored controls remained reported.
- Focused production and full-tree export scans confirmed exactly the two retained semantic-owner exports are omitted only from the production findings while their direct config/security consumers remain recognized by the full-tree graph.
- Effective-config inspection and a focused full-tree unused-file scan confirmed all five dynamic test fixtures are full-tree-only roots, resolve successfully, and leave unrelated residual controls reported.

Hosted CI and independent exact-head review continue after publication. No benchmark or generator command was executed.

prs.title: fix(plugins): stop executing escape sequences embedded in plugin manifest metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw plugins uninstall --dry-run` prints a plugin's manifest-derived display metadata before removing anything, so an installed plugin whose manifest carries ESC/BEL sequences repaints the operator's terminal at the exact moment they are inspecting what will be removed.

## Scope

This PR hardens only the uninstall preview — the surface the maintainer-assigned parallel repair in #172873 does **not** cover. An earlier revision of this branch also touched `plugins list` and `plugins inspect`; those files are dropped here so the two changes are not competing repairs (see the scope comment).

- `src/cli/plugins-uninstall-command.ts`: pass manifest-derived `name`, `pluginId` (both preview occurrences), and each package-entry id in `pluginIds` through the existing `sanitizeTerminalText` helper before styling. No new helper, option, output shape, colour, or `--json` changes; core-generated action labels (`Will remove: …`) are untouched.
- `src/cli/plugins-cli.uninstall.test.ts`: one regression that dry-runs the preview with ESC/BEL bytes in a package owner, child ids, and display name, asserting no control bytes remain while the printable text is preserved.

Not included (owned by #172873 / generated): `plugins-list-command.ts`, `plugins-list-format.ts`, `plugins-inspect-command.ts`, `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`.

## Evidence: shipped-CLI reproduction and proof

Proof host, Node `v24.22.1`, built `dist/entry.js`, isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, loopback-only, no registry access. Fixture: a local plugin directory (`openclaw.extensions` in `package.json`, `index.js`) whose `openclaw.plugin.json` declares `"name": "Second\u001b[1m plugin\u0007"`; installed through the shipped CLI with `plugins install -l` (local link), then previewed with `plugins uninstall --dry-run` (read-only; the dry run mutates nothing).

The changed production file is byte-identical to the PR base `e9a3cc9a2df` on the tree used for both runs (`plugins-uninstall-command.ts` md5 `2daf1faceb426628bdad6c07dbd088c2`); the only build-to-build difference is this PR's patch.

**Before** (tree with the base file, rebuilt `dist`):

```
$ openclaw plugins install -l /ws/OpenClaw/hbplug/evil-pack --force
Linked plugin path: /ws/OpenClaw/hbplug/evil-pack
Saved for the next Gateway start.

$ openclaw plugins uninstall evil-pack --dry-run
Plugin: Second<ESC>[1m plugin<BEL> (evil-pack)
Will remove: plugin settings, install record, load path
Dry run, no changes made.

control-byte scan: {"bytes":121,"esc":1,"bel":1}
```

**After** (same tree, this PR's production change applied, rebuilt `dist`):

```
$ openclaw plugins install -l /ws/OpenClaw/hbplug/evil-pack --force
Linked plugin path: /ws/OpenClaw/hbplug/evil-pack
Saved for the next Gateway start.

$ openclaw plugins uninstall evil-pack --dry-run
Plugin: Second plugin (evil-pack)
Will remove: plugin settings, install record, load path
Dry run, no changes made.

control-byte scan: {"bytes":116,"esc":0,"bel":0}
```

The printable text (`Second plugin (evil-pack)`) is preserved; only the ESC/BEL bytes disappear, and the action labels are unchanged.

## Owning-boundary tests

Remote runner, Node 24.22.1, isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; the changed files are identical on the PR base and current `main`, so the diff is the only variable.

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.uninstall.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
head:  Tests 16 passed (16)
base (production file reverted only):
       Tests 1 failed | 15 passed (16)
  ✗ strips terminal control sequences from plugin metadata in the uninstall preview
    expected 'Plugin: Second\^[[1m plugin (evil…' not to contain '\^['
```

Suite wall time on that runner: ~2 min. `git diff --check`, `oxfmt --check`, and `oxlint` (258 rules) are clean on both files.

## Not covered

The post-uninstall completion line (`Uninstalled … Removed …`) still renders plugin ids; it is out of scope here and left for a follow-up. The `plugins list` / `plugins inspect` surfaces are owned by #172873.

Exact head: `06ea4d039cb18e5c080a8ebfdd9e071fd9ccc4d8`.

prs.title: fix(memory-core): refuse to rewrite DREAMS.md containing invalid UTF-8
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes dream diary updates silently replacing malformed UTF-8 bytes in `DREAMS.md` and destroying the original content.

## User Impact

Diary writes refuse malformed text and preserve the original bytes. Optional diary history is omitted so other dreaming work can continue. Preserve the original and convert a copy to UTF-8 before retrying.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical diary reader uses the shared strict UTF-8 decoder. Its existing error type now carries a code that survives the remote memory worker's JSON error envelope; the optional-context boundary recognizes that code while required updates still fail. This removes the duplicate validator/error constructor from the original contribution by @SunnyShu0925 and preserves the existing read/write ownership.

## Evidence

- All four boundary checks failed on unchanged main: the update rewrote malformed input, optional history returned the marked entry, a generic coded error escaped optional handling, and the real remote worker returned replacement-decoded content (57.53 s Vitest). All 35 dreaming/remote-worker tests passed on the fix (179.31 s Vitest, 237.49 s wrapper, dominated by compilation). The four regressions passed again after current-main integration (130.52 s Vitest); the five-file patch stayed byte-identical.
- Typed extension/core oxlint and formatting passed. Independent P0–P2 autoreview was scoped-clean.
- The optional-context fixture contains a real marked diary entry, so the baseline cannot pass merely because there was no parseable history. Separate worker-envelope coverage verifies that malformed input remains distinguishable after remote error serialization.
- A fresh compiled CLI/Gateway was not run: a separate runtime build exceeds the bounded live-proof budget. The contributor's `openclaw memory rem-backfill --rollback` proof at prior head `3f94146ce3fad37328d6d1356d2bb9799a59759c` reported refusal with the original `0xff` byte preserved, while a valid diary control removed only the backfill entry. This is prior-head evidence, not a current-head live claim.

- Whole-PR delta: production +14/-3 (net +11), tests +59/-8 (net +51), docs +4. The production growth preserves actionable recovery text and gives the existing canonical error a transportable code; no new reader, validator, or protocol adapter is introduced.

CI follow-up: run 40150314078 on the earlier head failed production and Gateway test types with TS2739 at the untouched session-catalog test helper. Main commit 465fd7af01b62 had already removed the obsolete `{}` connect fallback. Integrated that landed repair normally; the five-file PR patch remains byte-identical. Both failed scopes now pass locally via `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json`.

Final-head CI run 40151055922 passed all 64 jobs, including both repaired typecheck scopes. Independent review and final-head ClawSweeper found no actionable code defects; the current compiled-CLI proof gap remains documented above.

prs.title: refactor: remove unreachable cooperative sort path
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The shared sort helper exposed a cooperative generator and maintained a run-merging branch that no production caller could reach. Tests called that generator directly, so the test-only path looked like supported runtime behavior even though every real caller used the synchronous `sortAndLimitBy` entry point.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. Existing callers keep the same stable ordering, tie handling, input immutability, bounded top-N selection for limits up to 200, and native full-sort behavior for wider or unlimited results.

The change removes an internal export and unreachable implementation path; it does not change configuration, data, schemas, dependencies, package exports, or public APIs.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sortAndLimitBy` previously delegated to `sortAndLimitByWork` without a yield callback. Under that production call shape, the cooperative run/merge branch was impossible to enter: small result windows used the existing top-N algorithm, while wider windows immediately used the native stable sort.

This change makes the production entry point own those two real paths directly. The owner test now checks stable ordering, immutability, and deterministic comparison-work bounds through `sortAndLimitBy`, while the cooperative-only assertion and its test-only export are removed.

The generic synchronous-work helper was introduced with this generator and had no other consumer, so it is removed with the seam instead of leaving an orphaned production file.

## Evidence

The exact committed tree passed the remote pre-commit gate on a retained Linux Testbox:

- changed-file formatting and core lint, with zero warnings or errors;
- all production and test type graphs selected for the changed shared module;
- `src/shared/sort-and-limit.test.ts`: 1 file passed, 9 tests passed.

The maintained dead-code scans confirm that `sortAndLimitByWork` and its synchronous-work helper no longer appear in the unused-file/export inventories. Those scans remain nonzero on unrelated baseline inventory already owned separately; no new row is introduced by this change.

The focused suite exercises limits on both sides of the top-N boundary, stable ties, reversed and already-sorted inputs, empty input, input immutability, ascending and descending first-page work bounds, and the 200-row comparison bound. Full hosted CI, dead-code closure checks, independent review, and automated review are pending on this published head.

## What Problem This Solves

The PostgreSQL operator guide and linked references lag behind shipped connection reuse, startup recovery, memory ranking, and backup behavior.

## User Impact

Operators can see the idle-connection bounds, timeout precedence, pgvector minimum version, startup failure/retry behavior, and the consequences of repairing missing local client credentials. Linked backup instructions now cover all declared PostgreSQL stores and archive restoration.

This is documentation only: no runtime, schema, configuration, or dependency change. PostgreSQL remains a supported alternative to SQLite. Existing port/cache guidance stays neutral about cache-cap behavior, and the pending index-ordering migration is not documented as shipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guide now follows the current owners for connection lifetime, admission, Doctor recovery, search, and backups. Separate PostgreSQL databases remain recommended; independent installations with distinct store namespaces in one database remain supported. One Gateway owns each store.

prs.title: fix(codex): context refresh blocks replies on managed inference routes
prs.body:
Related: #177716, #179099, #180204

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Codex follow-up fails after context projection refresh while a preview remains alive on an owned inference route.

## User Impact

Conversations can continue through a context-only refresh without stopping the preview when immutable policy and physical ownership still match. Existing foreground-work, same-client, configuration, authentication, permission, cancellation, and binding safeguards remain enforced. No migration or new configuration option is introduced. **Remaining validation: the fixed alpha runtime and public Discord transport have not been retested. These proof gaps remain visible for review.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Creation, resume, and warm reuse normalize private inference relay addresses to the owned route's stable logical identity. Projection retention omitted the inference argument and compared a physical `config.openai_base_url` against the logical creation fingerprint—even on the same client with unchanged upstream policy.

Pass `params` as the fifth argument to the existing complete fingerprint helper. Normalization applies only to a URL belonging to the current route; genuine upstream/auth/policy changes remain significant. No field is removed from identity and no ownership guard is weakened. Preserve the first-reason and physical-owner diagnostics from the initial draft.

## Evidence

- **Owning-boundary red/green:** the new lifecycle regression, using a real owned private inference route and synthetic native transport, failed before the one-line fix with the protected-thread refusal. With the fix it commits the successor, preserves the predecessor's cleanup custody and assignments, and releases cleanup after protection ends. This is not merely a hash-helper test.
- **84 selected tests passed** across five suites: assignment/diagnostics (21), native warm cleanup (4), warm cleanup (3), thread fingerprints and inference routing (56 combined). New lifecycle negative controls retain refusal and original binding/custody for upstream, valid auth-profile, persistent-instruction, permission-config, other immutable-config changes, and active foreground work.
- The existing native scenarios pass with pinned Codex **0.162.1**, isolated state, a scripted loopback provider, real background commands, and no operator credentials. They independently protect actual native cleanup/continuation behavior; the new owned-route regression uses synthetic native transport.
- **Qualified production package-entry typecheck passed here**, after building normalization-core, preparing SDK boundary declarations, and generating the canonical 18-entry-root Codex project. Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace passed. No suppression, weakened compiler config, dependency change, or review waiver.
- **Fresh independent Auto Review: scoped-clean at its configured P0-only threshold**, with unchanged owning-source context supplied. It did not rerun tests and is not a P0–P2 review. An earlier attempt failed during host cleanup; a same-route retry completed on unchanged sources. No host-infrastructure repair is claimed.

**Requester-supplied live evidence:** a controlled reproduction on Codex 0.163.0-alpha.11.2 reported `changedClient:false`, `claimed:false`, `protected:true`, and `backgroundOnly:true`. Normalizing only `config.openai_base_url` made the entire immutable fingerprint match, while the original comparison still authoritatively refused retention. That observed the defect/counterfactual, not a deployed product fix. The probes used authenticated local Gateway injection with Discord routing metadata and `deliver:false`; they do not prove a newly transmitted Discord message. Earlier uninstrumented incidents still lack exact failed-predicate evidence.

<details>
<summary>Commands, scope, timing, and prior evidence</summary>

```sh
node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.assignment-rotation.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.warm-cleanup.native.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.warm-cleanup.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-fingerprints.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-routing.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

# After canonical workspace-package / SDK preparation and project generation:
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .artifacts/extension-package-boundary/compile/codex.tsconfig.json --noEmit
```

The package-entry typecheck preserves SDK declaration aliases and the package root boundary. It does not claim the raw package tsconfig or full repository test-typecheck lane passed. Hosted exact-head CI and fixed live alpha/Discord proof remain pending.

The initial regression failed in 5.818 seconds test time (104.44 seconds cold wrapper). The corrected isolated case passed in 1.840 seconds test time (29.53 seconds wrapper). The final five-suite run completed in approximately 95.9 seconds wall time; its two Vitest shards reported 43.67 and 39.08 seconds including import/transform overhead. Hosted CI seconds are unavailable.

The previous [requester validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182755#issuecomment-6387856041) and P0–P2 local review applied to diagnostic head `40caaa2ef0e88d33bee4f6c353a6967966587606`, not this follow-up fix.

Relative to that diagnostic head: production +1/−0, tests +110/−3, docs +3/−1. Against the original base: production +87/−42, tests +227/−10, docs +18/−1. The product repair reuses the existing normalization owner; added test setup supplies actual route ownership without a new production seam, state owner, or policy exception.

</details>

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

## What Problem This Solves

Preserves the configured TLS server name when it is set before a socket connects.

## User Impact

Updates the shared Bun fork from `ef37c31de3` to `807211511f`, retaining WebKit `a2976f02e6`. A name supplied through `tlsSocket.setServername()` before connecting is sent as SNI, including with `autoSelectFamily`. The existing unconditional hook payload scan remains unchanged; this pin does not add Error.cause support.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fork comparison contains only [the TLS pre-connect servername fix](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/pull/197) as a production change. The Buffer copy reduction was withdrawn pending a container-neutral design. Serializer source is identical to the existing pin. The six-platform pin JSON is copied byte-for-byte from the verified release conversion.

## Evidence

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Wire identity | 288/288 identical outputs; 250,571,967 serialized bytes per runtime; local round trips and cross-deserialization passed |

prs.title: refactor: deslop session, gateway and handoff fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tests repeated transcript envelopes, Gateway subscription state, HTTP request-body readers, model literals and readonly handoff snapshots, creating extra setup owners without protecting different behavior.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. This fixture-only cleanup removes 212 net lines across 64 files (415 additions, 627 deletions), with 0 production lines removed. This uses the campaign's 100+ residue waiver; it is not a LARGE PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing fixture owners absorb the repeated setup while preserving per-call freshness and every assertion, scenario and registration. The independent cuts and their accepted tradeoffs are detailed below.

## Transcript event fixtures

Move 34 consumer files onto the existing messageEvent/timedMessageEvent test-support owner. Each call still creates a fresh outer event, retains the supplied message reference and preserves field ordering, parent/timestamp types and all scenario-specific payloads. The existing transcript contract accepts unknown events; this does not change production parsing or persisted shapes. The conformance file owned by another open test campaign is deliberately unchanged.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: tests now share the existing event-envelope constructor. No product guard, assertion, scenario, registration or durability mechanism is removed. Dedicated standalone-memory backend/factory/registry/expiry/federation owners remain untouched. Net 141 lines removed.

## Gateway setup fixtures

Give the identical subscription-parameter state one narrow support owner, retaining fresh schedulers/controllers/maps/mocks on every call and the tool-recipient alias to that call's chat state. Reuse existing deferred and model-definition fixture owners instead of copying their defaults.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: consumers share these test defaults; scenario-specific overrides remain local. No shared mutable fixture singleton or runtime seam is introduced. Net 28 lines removed.

## HTTP readers and Stop fixture

Delete readProviderBody and migrate all 21 affected files to the existing byte-identical readRequestText helper. Buffer chunks still allocate per request and retain UTF-8 decoding. One Stop fixture also stops rewriting a live kill owner's provisional row: it waits for published termination/removal and drives the existing clock-based reconciliation sweep, restoring Date.now in finally. This repairs the observed provisional-field race without changing production settlement or weakening cleanup expectations. The full 11-case Stop suite passed.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: the shared reader retains the same intentionally unbounded synthetic-request behavior. No product input bound or transport contract changes. The Stop clock affects only the same awaited fixture sweep and is always restored. Net 35 lines removed, including the 6-line Stop simplification against the conflict-repaired base.

## Readonly handoff snapshots

Move the identical ordered SELECT/JSON snapshot into the existing retained-custody support owner. Each call opens its own readonly database and closes it in finally, preserving fresh physical reads and ordered byte comparisons.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: the two test callers share the exact existing snapshot operation. No schema, transaction, permission, retention, recovery or production ownership change. Net 8 lines removed.

## Conflict-only base refresh

GitHub reported CONFLICTING, so the branch was rebased onto 0928840637da480b784a8c2c5e90669d1b0c493d. Main's #183054 guarded the same Stop fixture mutation; this branch instead removes that mutation and waits for terminal publication before driving the existing sweep. All 65 source files at rebased head 8113bc345b1f63bb41b6fd254d1b04967bf13bc8 were byte-identical to the independently reviewed original candidate. The three extra base guard lines explained the change from 219 to 222 net deletions.

CI run 40148493993 then found a PR-caused mock-exports ratchet failure: the optional health-snapshot extraction changed a grandfathered closed-mock fingerprint. That extraction was withdrawn, returning the entire build-admission test byte-for-byte to the base rather than expanding a baseline or adding a suppression. The failed static check now passes (7043 grandfathered factories). The retained 64 files are unchanged from the reviewed candidate; the final diff is 212 net. Independent source-bound comparison reconfirmed every retained assertion byte and complete registration signature below. Prior-head CI is not reported as green.

Fresh affected-graph proof on rebased head 8113bc345b1f63bb41b6fd254d1b04967bf13bc8 passed: frozen install 17.725s; full Stop suite 11/11, 223.31s Vitest / 239.78s canonical runner / 240.699s command wall time; Gateway-server test types 8.418s; scoped lint 36.540s and format 0.318s; runtime cycles 0 in 28.288s and Madge cycles 0 in 51.072s; lint-suppressions 14/14 in 10.484s; diff-check 0.342s. The original 68-command proof below remains prior-candidate evidence, not a claim that the complete runtime graph is unchanged. Exact-head hosted CI is still the broad gate.

## Assertion and registration preservation

Static AST comparison before/after formatting preserved every bound assertion-call byte and suite/test/hook/mock/registration signature. A separate complete registration check also includes wrapper-produced callbacks, not only inline callback expressions. Counts below are source sites, not expanded table rows or execution counts.

|Cut|Assertion entries before→after|Scenario registrations before→after|Suites before→after|Hooks before→after|Mock/hoist before→after|Register-helper calls before→after|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Transcript fixtures|1729→1729|281→281|10→10|29→29|16→16|1→1|
|Gateway setup|475→475|204→204|43+1live→43+1live|13→13|15→15|2→2|

|Total|2706→2706|530→530|56+1live→56+1live|56→56|45→45|3→3|

Assertion entries comprise 2660 expect, 32 Node assert and 14 Vitest assert. Scenario registrations comprise 528 native it/test and 2 platform-conditioned Unix aliases; these include nine existing wrapper-produced callbacks in the transcript-reports suite and two tagged-template it.each registrations. All cases, table rows, cleanup predicates and existing registrations remain; no skip, retry, timeout increase, baseline relaxation or lint suppression was added. The withdrawn file remains unchanged on main and its nine assertions/one scenario are excluded from this final-diff table. A final counting audit corrected scanner omissions: the earlier 65-file total missed the two tagged-template registrations; a subsequent recount missed the two Unix aliases. Neither omission was a source change. The table now includes both forms explicitly.

The withdrawal repair at 4151cb2e2658fb4100bc954ad1cb7b92fe65c8b7 has an independent P2-clean review with no findings. Fresh lint-suppressions passed 14/14 (15.12s canonical runner), and diff-check passed. Retained source bytes and their completed focused proof are reused; the new exact-head CI is the broad gate.

## Evidence

Exact-head run [40149612653](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40149612653), attempt 1, is complete: 75 terminal jobs, no pending or cancelled CI jobs. All three PostgreSQL shards, the repaired baseline ratchet and security-fast pass. Workflow elapsed time is 1648 seconds; summed job time is 9938 seconds.

The only failed leaves are inherited type failures: `check-prod-types` (job 121038915048) and `check-test-types-core-2` (job 121038915059), both `session-catalog.test-helpers.ts(122,5) TS2739` (`{}` lacks `minProtocol`, `maxProtocol`, `client`). The narrow Gateway-methods test typecheck reproduces the identical diagnostic on the actual CI main parent `ad2172d77e260e3039febbc4f531bd476245f912`. The failing helper and five determining type/schema owners are byte-identical there and in the tested merge `1e753e387497b112effc2d19cd8e629aa14ca2bf`; this PR changes none of them. Ordered parents and reconstructed merge tree match. Main subsequently repaired that exact fallback in [465fd7af01b6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/465fd7af01b62f893935031758ab85699bd866e9). This is scoped baseline attribution, not full import-graph or Linux-environment equivalence. The aggregate CI gate (job 121043554259) reflects those two failures; no failed CI is labeled green. Required review/security remain enforced. The body-template check has a successful same-head replacement after correcting its headings; those historical failures are not classified as inherited.

Before the conflict-only rebase, all 68 focused canonical-runner commands passed on the original candidate: 994 passed cases and 2 pre-existing live skips, 4496.536 seconds combined command wall time. The first profiles command selected no tests under the default config; the corrected explicit live-config route passed 169 synthetic cases with the same two existing live skips and both live-enable flags disabled. No completed passing command was rerun during that stage. Per-file wall times are below.

On that candidate, all nine targeted test typechecks, scoped lint and formatting passed. Independent review is clean at P2. Runtime cycles 0 (29.391s), Madge cycles 0 (46.289s), lint-suppressions 14/14 (30.958s), changed-file dry-run classification (1.978s) and diff-check (0.370s) passed. No local broad build, whole-graph typecheck or E2E suite was run.

Full Stop suite 11/11 PASS: 369.94s Vitest, 392.88s canonical runner. That local run preceded the fast-forward to f3107251 and is reused on identical test-source bytes with the named determining owners checked; it is not a new-head whole-graph claim. It is intentionally a real in-process Gateway/model lifecycle proof; the cheaper fixture counts cannot prove termination/settlement behavior. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad gate.

Eight built-runtime/E2E operands were deferred locally under the campaign's no-local-build/E2E budget; hosted selected-lane evidence supplies the broad gate, not an independent claim for each deferred operand. No external-provider/channel/device claim is made. All local runtime proof uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG paths, nice 10 and one worker; no real operator state is used.

<details>
<summary>Original focused canonical-runner command wall times before the conflict-only rebase (seconds)</summary>

All commands used nice 10, one worker and isolated state. These wall times include compilation/import/setup, not just test bodies. prs.title: fix(tts): backport Microsoft speech synthesis fix to 2026.9.33
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the 2026.9 maintenance line, Microsoft Edge text-to-speech fails with `Unexpected server response: 403`. The bundled `node-edge-tts@1.2.10` still opens the retired Bing synthesis endpoint, so every spoken reply and `/tts audio` request fails.

Upstream fixed this in #172381 by moving to `node-edge-tts@1.2.11`, which targets `api.msedgeservices.com`. This PR carries that same fix onto `extended-stable/2026.9.33`, because the 2026.9 line is the current extended-stable (LTS-equivalent) line and the regression is user-facing.

## What This Change Does

- bumps `node-edge-tts` from 1.2.10 to 1.2.11 in `package.json` and `extensions/microsoft/package.json`
- regenerates `pnpm-lock.yaml` and adds the reviewed exact-version exemption in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
- adds an offline regression asserting the `api.msedgeservices.com` synthesis host and path
- documents the outbound allowlist (`api.msedgeservices.com` for synthesis, `speech.platform.bing.com` for voice discovery)

No configuration keys, plugin SDK surface, migrations or runtime requirements are added.

## Evidence

Environment: OpenCode container, branch `backport/2026.9.33-edge-tts-172381` at `670157f00d0065ed79010acf06bc10e444f3f0c8`, base `extended-stable/2026.9.33` (`5873f8174e`). The live test used an empty isolated `HOME`, so it did not read personal configuration, credentials, or a newer OpenClaw state database.

### Real Microsoft behavior proof on the September candidate

Command:

```console
HOME=/workspace/openclaw/.live-home-proof node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-live.mts --no-quiet -- extensions/microsoft/microsoft.live.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

Redacted output (public format identifiers only; no IPs, keys, phone numbers, or private endpoints):

```text
RUN  v5.0.1 /workspace/openclaw

Microsoft synthesis: {
  bytes: 24336,
  format: 'audio-24khz-48kbitrate-mono-mp3',
  extension: '.mp3'
}
✓ microsoft plugin live > synthesizes nonempty MP3 audio 1099ms
✓ microsoft plugin live > lists Edge speech voices 1472ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       2 passed (2)
Duration    56.04s
```

This exercises the production provider path through `buildMicrosoftSpeechProvider().synthesize()` and confirms that the September candidate returns nonempty MP3 audio from the real Microsoft transport.

### Additional validation

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: passed; `node-edge-tts` 1.2.11 installed
- `extensions/microsoft/tts.test.ts`: 6/6 passed, including the new endpoint guard
- `extensions/microsoft/speech-provider.optional-capture.test.ts`: 3/3 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` (extension production typecheck): passed, exit 0
- CI rerun `39029180596`: extension test types, production types, lint, dependency checks, docs, package boundary, and relevant Node shards passed at the time this evidence was added

The broad local extension wrapper could not verify managed-process cleanup in this container before starting Vitest. The focused live runner above completed successfully and produced the requested real behavior proof.

No push to upstream and no merge were performed.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.

prs.title: feat(inworld): realtime voice provider for Talk and Voice Call
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators who chose an Inworld voice for Talk, voice notes or telephony TTS cannot use that voice in realtime (full-duplex) mode: OpenClaw's realtime voice registry only offers OpenAI and Google, each with vendor voices. Inworld's Realtime API runs STT, an LLM/router and TTS-2 on one WebSocket using the OpenAI Realtime protocol, so an Inworld realtime provider closes that gap with the same host contract (consult and end-call tools, barge-in, telephony audio) and no change for existing TTS users. Tracking issue: #168030.

## Summary

Adds a realtime voice provider to the official `inworld` plugin so Talk (`talk.realtime.provider: "inworld"`) and Voice Call (`realtime.provider: "inworld"`) can run full-duplex speech-to-speech on Inworld's Realtime API with Inworld TTS-2 voices, while the OpenClaw agent stays the brain through the shared `openclaw_agent_consult` / `openclaw_end_call` tools.

Closes #168030. Builds on #167951 for the `speakingRate` / `deliveryMode` naming.

## What changes

- `extensions/inworld/realtime-voice-*.ts`: WebSocket bridge modeled on the bundled xAI realtime provider (Inworld follows the OpenAI Realtime event protocol): `Authorization: Basic <apiKey>` with the dashboard credential, session URL `wss://api.inworld.ai/api/v1/realtime/session?key=…&protocol=realtime`, `session.update` carrying model, instructions, `audio.input/output.format`, STT model, `semantic_vad` (eagerness) or `server_vad`, `audio.output.{voice,model,speed}`, and `providerData` (`auto_tool_response: false`, TTS delivery/steering/segmenter, responsiveness; back-channel is rejected until the host has an out-of-band playback path). Tool calls are emitted at `response.done`; results go back as `function_call_output` followed by a host-owned `response.create`. Barge-in cancels and truncates playback. Inworld has no session resumption, so an unexpected close is terminal rather than retried.
- Lazy catalog descriptor keeps `ws` off the startup path; manifest declares the `realtimeVoiceProviders` contract and the `ws` dependency; `index.ts` registers the provider next to the existing speech provider.
- Audio: PCM16 24 kHz and G.711 µ-law 8 kHz, both passed through without host transcoding.
- Docs: `docs/providers/inworld.md` (new "Realtime voice" accordion), `docs/tools/media-overview.md`, generated plugin inventory. Config-doc baseline hash regenerated; counts unchanged (no new `configSchema` entries: realtime config lives under `talk.realtime.providers.inworld` / the voice-call realtime provider map like the other providers).

- `providerData`: a bounded passthrough for the documented Inworld extension sections only (`stt`, `tts`, `memory`, `responsiveness`; unknown sections rejected, 8 KiB cap). Typed settings win over it, and `auto_tool_response: false` is pinned after the merge so no passthrough can hand `response.create` back to the server.

Defaults preserved: nothing changes for existing Inworld TTS users; the realtime provider only activates when selected.

## Config example

```json5
{
  talk: {
    realtime: {
      provider: "inworld",
      mode: "realtime",
      transport: "gateway-relay",
      brain: "agent-consult",
      providers: {
        inworld: {
          apiKey: { source: "env", provider: "default", id: "INWORLD_API_KEY" },
          model: "openai/gpt-4.1-mini",
          voiceId: "Sarah",
          ttsModel: "inworld-tts-2",
          speakingRate: 1.0,
          deliveryMode: "BALANCED",
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Evidence

### Tests and gates

- `extensions/inworld`: 53/53 tests (20 new provider cases: metadata/capabilities, config normalization, session policy for both VAD modes and both audio formats, credential/startup failures, audio + playback marks + transcripts, tool call → result → `response.create`, suppressed results, server-VAD and host barge-in, terminal close, bounded `providerData` normalization, and the exact emitted `session.update` payload with the passthrough merged under typed keys and `auto_tool_response` pinned, back-channel config rejected and back-channel events tolerated without audio, marks or truncation), 2 lazy-descriptor cases.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint, oxfmt, `pnpm plugins:inventory:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check` all clean.
- Plugin contract suite: 1079/1079 on the rebased branch (capability-catalog, registry, extension-runtime-dependencies and runtime-api guardrails).

### Real behavior proof (authenticated, redacted live logs)

Run on 2026-10-09 against this branch at its base commit (dc46466756e, before the `providerData` passthrough commit, which only adds the bounded merge covered by the emitted-payload test) through the provider's own `createBridge` with a real Inworld key (header redacted), then through a second isolated Gateway (`--profile`, own port) built from this branch where `talk.catalog` reported the provider configured and ready and `talk.session.create` returned `provider: "inworld"` at PCM16 24 kHz.

```

2026-10-09T23:34:29.958Z [A-pcm16-luna] READY (session.updated received)
```

Case A is a Talk-style PCM16 session on `inworld-tts-2` with `speakingRate: 1.3` and `deliveryMode: CREATIVE`; Case B is the telephony µ-law path with the host-shaped `openclaw_agent_consult` tool registered, called by the model, answered, and the follow-up spoken.

### Spoken input, interruption and providerData at 183f08f6889 (historical run, authenticated, redacted)

Second live run, recorded at the earlier head 183f08f6889 (its `backchannel` settings are rejected by the current head's config normalizer; everything else in the run is unchanged code), through the provider's `createBridge` with PCM16 24 kHz. The two "user" utterances were synthesized with the plugin's own Inworld TTS and streamed as 20 ms frames like a microphone; `providerData` was set (`tts.segmenter_strategy: "sentence"`, `memory: { enabled: true, turn_interval: 2 }`, and at that time `backchannel: { require_pause: false }`) with `deliveryMode: CREATIVE` (`backchannel` had been set on this run; it is withdrawn in the head commit, see below), and the session was accepted (`session.updated`). The server detected speech, transcribed it, answered with audio, was interrupted by a second spoken utterance mid-answer (barge-in cleared playback, the response ended `cancelled` with `turn_detected`), transcribed the interruption, called `openclaw_agent_consult`, and the response carrying that tool call completed. Bounds: this is the provider's bridge driven directly, not a Gateway Talk or Voice Call session; the run ended at that tool-call terminal, before the tool-result continuation and the final spoken answer were awaited; no back-channel interjection fired.

```

```

Also addressed from review: back-channel is withdrawn rather than half-supported. Inworld delivers interjections out of band (`response.backchannel.audio.delta`, while the user is still speaking), and the host playback contract has no out-of-band channel today (the Talk relay sink requires a live response owner; Voice Call truncates every snapshot item on `speech_started`), so the adapter no longer accepts `backchannel` in config or `providerData`, never enables it, and tolerates stray `response.backchannel.*` events as diagnostics without delivering audio. The low-value lazy metadata test was removed; the branch is rebased on current main.

### Host-routed Voice Call at fe4765c713e (authenticated, redacted)

Outbound telephony call placed by the Voice Call plugin on a gateway built from this head (`openclaw voicecall call --mode conversation`, `realtime.provider: "inworld"`, Twilio), answered by a human and driven entirely through the shipped host path. Gateway journal, identifiers and numbers removed; counts are line counts from the plugin's own log lines.

```
20:02:11 [voice-call] Outbound call initiated mode=conversation
20:02:31 [voice-call] Serving realtime TwiML for Twilio call (direction=outbound-api)
20:02:31 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting (initialGreeting=queued)
20:02:32 .. 20:05:20  realtime local speech detected: 42 events
20:02:34 .. 20:05:20  realtime input transcript final=true: 13 user turns (104 partials)
2x        [voice-call] realtime outbound audio cleared by provider barge-in (caller interrupted mid-sentence; queuedBytes>0)
20:05:22 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized endReason=completed  (2 min 51 s)
```

What this does and does not show: the host-routed bridge ran a full spoken conversation over mu-law telephony with the caller interrupting twice and the provider clearing queued audio both times, and the call ended normally. The caller did not ask anything that triggered `openclaw_agent_consult` during this call (the test agent behind the bridge had no identity to consult), so tool-result continuation on the host path is covered only by the direct-createBridge runs above. The browser Talk button on that gateway's Control UI requested the client-owned session mode (`talk.client.create`) and was refused with INVALID_REQUEST (`use talk.session.create for gateway-relay`), so no browser realtime session was exercised; that path is not claimed here.

### Host consultation to spoken answer at fe4765c713e (authenticated, redacted)

Inbound Twilio call to a production gateway running this head with `voice-call.realtime.provider: "inworld"` (talker model on Inworld's router, voice Luna, `openclaw_agent_consult` wired to a real OpenClaw agent on its main session). The caller asked a question only the agent could answer. Gateway journal, identifiers and numbers removed.

```
21:29:52 [voice-call] Serving realtime TwiML for Twilio call (direction=inbound)
21:29:53 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting (initialGreeting=queued)
21:30:02 .. 21:30:51  5 final caller turns transcribed; 1 provider barge-in clearing 6,897 queued bytes (caller interrupted)
21:30:51 [voice-call] realtime tool call received tool=openclaw_agent_consult
21:30:51 [voice-call] realtime tool call executing tool=openclaw_agent_consult hasHandler=true
21:31:20 .. 21:31:31  two unrelated runs on the agent's main session finish (consult queued behind them: lane wait 40,003 ms)
21:31:46 [voice-call] realtime tool call received tool=openclaw_agent_consult   (model asked again while waiting)
21:31:46 [voice-call] realtime tool call sharing in-flight agent consult ageMs=54870
21:31:49 [voice-call] realtime tool call completed tool=openclaw_agent_consult status=ok elapsedMs=57939
21:32:07 .. 21:34:48  conversation continues: 15 further final caller turns
21:34:53 [voice-call] Max duration reached (300s), ending call   → Call finalized endReason=timeout
```

The operator on the call reported watching the consult arrive in the agent's chat, the agent compose its answer, and the realtime voice speak that answer immediately after; the voice-call host does not log output audio events, so the spoken continuation is evidenced by the completed consult followed by three more minutes of two-way turns. The 58 s consult round trip was dominated by a 40 s queue behind other turns on the same agent session, not by the provider; a dedicated consult agent avoids that. The call ended at the host's configured 300 s maximum, not on error.

### Live PSTN call on c15240b (2026-10-10, authenticated, redacted)
A real inbound Twilio call through the Voice Call plugin with the Inworld realtime provider, `audio/pcmu` negotiated, driven by a human caller: four caller barge-ins, all `conversation.item.truncate` events accepted with no `realtime voice error`, three `openclaw_agent_consult` host consultations (7.9 s, 26.7 s, 29.9 s) whose results were spoken back, normal hang-up. The earlier live interruption test had exposed that Inworld times G.711 μ-law items as bytes/24 ms rather than real time, so truncates on that format were rejected (`audio_end_ms N exceeds actual audio duration M ms`); the fix converts 8 kHz G.711 truncates into Inworld's timebase after the byte clamp, PCM16 keeps ordinary units, and the live (bytes, ms) pairs are regression fixtures on both playback paths. Journal excerpt and tables: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168036#issuecomment-6101451830

### Required maintainer actions
- This PR carries the `dependencies-changed` label: per CONTRIBUTING, an outside author needs a maintainer to post `/allow-dependencies-change` on the current head before that guard can pass.
- Feature scope decision (realtime provider in the bundled Inworld extension vs. third-party plugin); we will follow whichever the maintainers prefer.

## Out of scope

WebRTC / client-owned browser sessions and Inworld session tokens; Inworld's hosted memory as a replacement for OpenClaw memory (passthrough only, off by default).

prs.title: fix(infra): keep astral automation summaries whole at the heartbeat preview cap
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`emitLegacyHeartbeatCronOutcome` projects the last automation run's completion summary into the `preview` field of the heartbeat diagnostic event with a plain UTF-16 code-unit cut:

```ts
preview: evt.summary?.slice(0, 2000),
```

When the summary is longer than 2000 code units and code unit 1999 is the high half of a surrogate pair, the emitted `preview` ends in a lone surrogate. Every downstream consumer of the `last-heartbeat` event then receives malformed UTF-16, which renders as U+FFFD (mojibake).

## User Impact

Automation summaries routinely carry astral characters (emoji status lines, CJK extension B glyphs). A summary whose boundary straddles one of those characters is corrupted at the 2000-code-unit display cap, and the corruption is silent: there is no truncation marker, so it reads as data damage rather than a display bound. The broken value is surfaced through:

- the Gateway `last-heartbeat` RPC (`src/gateway/server-methods/system.ts:210`);
- the Control UI Debug page "Last heartbeat" block (`ui/src/pages/debug/debug-page.tsx:160`, rendered at `:363`);
- `openclaw system heartbeat last` (`src/cli/system-cli.ts:103`);
- `openclaw status --json` (`src/commands/status-runtime-shared.ts:144`, projected at `src/commands/status-json-command.ts:150`);
- Gateway event subscribers, which broadcast the payload (`src/gateway/server-runtime-subscriptions.ts:582`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the helper the repository already owns instead of a raw code-unit slice: `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. The change is a drop-in at the cut point with no other behavior change: same 2000-unit cap, same `undefined` passthrough, but a surrogate pair that straddles the cap is dropped whole instead of being split in half. This follows the two merged fixes for the same class this week, #181742 and #181741.

## Which completions reach the cut

The projection is fed only by receipt-owned converted/default automations: `refreshLegacyMonitorProjection()` seeds its map from `readHeartbeatSummarySnapshot()` → `readDefaultProactiveJobsAsync` (`src/infra/heartbeat-summary-snapshot.ts:36`, `src/gateway/server-cron.ts:350-370`), and `emitLegacyHeartbeatCronOutcome` is called only for those jobs on `action === "finished"` (`src/gateway/server-cron.ts:601-610`). A plain user-created cron job never enters that path.

Two producers can hand it a `summary`:

- Agent-turn completions: `pickSummaryFromOutput` already caps the text at 2,000 units **with `truncateUtf16Safe`** (`src/cron/isolated-agent/helpers.ts:67-74`), so an agent summary can never straddle the boundary. (My first attempt at an end-to-end run used the migrated agent-turn automation and produced a well-formed 1,999-unit preview on both base and head — a real control, but not a reproducer.)
- Command completions: the same converted automation can be pointed at a command payload through the shipped CLI (`openclaw automations edit <id> --command …`; command payloads are legal on the migrated `session:` target per `src/cron/service/jobs-validation.ts:113`). `runCronCommandJob` returns the command output as the run `summary` (`src/gateway/server-cron.ts:443-464`, `src/cron/command-output-summary.ts`), which is **not** pre-capped at 2,000. That summary is the input that reaches the cut.

## Evidence: shipped run against the same tree, one variable

Proof host, Node `v24.22.1`, built `dist/entry.js`, isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, loopback Gateway on `127.0.0.1:18961`, no network, no model credentials, no installs.

Setup, all through the shipped CLI: a config carrying legacy `agents.defaults.heartbeat` is migrated by `openclaw doctor --fix` into the receipt-owned automation (`automation-default:/tmp/hbstate/cron/jobs.json:main` → `{"phase":"complete","heartbeatEnabled":true}`), the same automation is pointed at a command payload whose output is `"s" * 1999 + U+1F600 + "tail"` (2,005 UTF-16 units), the run is triggered with `openclaw automations run <id>`, and the result is read back with `openclaw system heartbeat last --json`.

The changed production file is byte-identical to the PR base `b2754d0da28` on the tree used for both builds (`src/infra/heartbeat-events.ts` md5 `98268327e415dec50be48e24a810db27`), so the only difference on this projection's code path is this PR's patch. (The post-change build also carries an unrelated `plugins uninstall` preview patch from a separate worktree; it does not touch `last-heartbeat`.)

**Before** (`dist` built from that tree, i.e. the base content of the changed file):

```
$ openclaw system heartbeat last --json
{"status":"ok-empty","units":2000,"loneSurrogates":1,"wellFormed":false,
 "tail":["U+73","U+73","U+73","U+73","U+73","U+73","U+73","U+D83D"]}
```

**After** (same tree, this PR's production change applied, rebuilt `dist`):

```
$ openclaw system heartbeat last --json
{"status":"ok-empty","units":1999,"loneSurrogates":0,"wellFormed":true,
 "tail":["U+73","U+73","U+73","U+73","U+73","U+73","U+73","U+73"]}
```

The boundary-crossing emoji is dropped whole rather than half-written; the receipt row for that run shows `payload_kind: "command"` for the same `jobId` the receipt names.

Legal control (fixed build, same projection): a command output of `"s" * 1999 + "tail"` (2,003 units, no astral character) still yields `units: 2000`, `loneSurrogates: 0`, `wellFormed: true`, ending `… s, t`. The 2,000-unit cap itself is unchanged; only the pair boundary moves.

Owning-boundary vitest against upstream main `b2754d0da28`:

- Base tree (upstream + this PR's test only): `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `Tests 1 failed | 10 passed (11)`; the only failure is `keeps an astral automation summary whole at the preview cap`, and the reporter shows the received value ending in U+FFFD.
- Head tree (same tree + this fix): `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 11 passed (11)`.
- Second new test (control): a summary that fits the cap with the astral character fully inside it (`"s" * 1998 + U+1F600`) is unchanged on base and head.

Formatting: `node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/infra/heartbeat-events.ts src/infra/heartbeat-events.test.ts` → `All matched files use the correct format.`

Exact head SHA: `a015d7f89645fd66158711318982628097953295`

## Not tested

The Control UI Debug page and `status --json` were not separately exercised; they consume the same `last-heartbeat` RPC field that the shipped run above read. No other producer of this projection was found: agent-turn summaries are pre-capped safely, and the skip/defer summaries are short static strings.

## Precedent

Same shape as merged #181742 (`src/gateway/server-methods/plugins.ts`: plugin `runtime.error` 2000) and #181741 (`src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-events.ts`: MCP Events catalog `description` 4096). This is the sibling diagnostics projection: the same truncate-at-a-report-cap defect, reached from automation completion (`CronEvent.summary`) instead of a plugin catalog, and emitted through the `last-heartbeat` RPC.

prs.title: fix(web-push): agent-finished pushes were indistinguishable across sessions
prs.body:
Closes #143946

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agent-finished Web Push notifications are indistinguishable when more than one session runs under the same agent — every notification renders the generic "An agent completed its response."

## User Impact

User impact: agent-finished pushes now identify themselves with the conversation's actual reply (e.g. "Deploy finished, tests green."), prefixed with the agent name when the payload identifies it. Users who prefer not to see content keep the generic body — the existing detail-level and per-category notification preferences govern this unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#143946 noted `agent-finished` is the only remaining event-push category without a producer-owned label. This follows the same `identifiedBody` pattern `scheduled-task-failed` and `human-mentioned` already use: the first readable text of the final assistant message, whitespace-normalized, capped at 140 chars with an ellipsis, falling back to the generic body when the message carries nothing readable. Privacy posture is unchanged — `identifiedBody` is consumed only for non-private detail levels by the existing delivery gate, so `private` recipients keep the generic body and no icon.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/event-web-push.test.ts`: 43/43 passing (39 pre-existing + 4 new):
  - final assistant text lands as the identified body
  - agent label prefix when the payload identifies the agent
  - long replies truncate to ≤140 chars with an ellipsis
  - whitespace-only text keeps the generic body
- Targeted run: `vitest run src/gateway/event-web-push.test.ts` → 43 passed.
- `pnpm check` on this branch: all sub-checks pass except the pre-existing `max-lines suppression ratchet` failure, which reproduces identically on pristine `main` (three `ui/src/pages/**` files, untouched by this PR).

prs.title: refactor: privatize standalone runtime profile resolver
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The standalone runtime-profile resolver is exported only so a direct unit test can classify build metadata. Production code uses the public `getRuntimeExecutionProfile()` boundary, and the extra resolver export is consequently reported as unused by the production export scan.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. Standalone images still classify missing, JIT, and bytecode build facts as dynamic execution and AOT build facts as embedded AOT, and the selected profile still remains stable for the process after later global metadata changes.

The packaged root module, its `RuntimeExecutionProfile` type, and the documented `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-profile` and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` getter surfaces remain unchanged. This requires no configuration, migration, dependency, or caller action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root standalone module already owns both classification and process caching. This change keeps the resolver private to that owner, removes its matching declaration and redundant `src/infra` forwarding edge, and moves the existing four-row classification table to fresh imports of the public getter.

That makes the tests follow the same boundary as production without adding a test hook or duplicating classification logic. Module and global cleanup remains explicit between table rows, and the separate process-stability assertion remains intact.

## Evidence

The exact committed tree passed the maintained remote OpenClaw recipe on a Blacksmith Testbox:

- Changed-file formatting and lint passed.
- Selected type checks passed for core production and test graphs, UI, extensions and extension tests, scripts, and test-root consumers.
- Eight affected test files passed across six Vitest shards: 104 tests, including all four standalone mode rows, the process-stability case, the infra owner suite, and affected getter consumers.
- The repository dependency, unused-file, and export scans ran on the candidate. They still report the pre-existing unrelated cleanup inventory, but `resolveRuntimeExecutionProfile` and its forwarding edge are absent from both production and full-tree export results, and no changed file became unused.

Hosted CI, automated review, and the independent source reviews are pending on the published head.

prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

## Evidence

Current author head: `02db206611aaf040ab37ea819889b8264483914b`. It normally merges CI-green head `1c771bb8` with official main `0372963434f6a0b79394dbe330abde2ae34f2a89` to resolve one new generated Discord-delta conflict that arose while the prior CI was running.

- The canonical generator resolved the actual conflicts, without hand-editing any fixture. First integration `556aa634` merged repaired head `ce374565` with main `4c35e950` and resolved two fixtures; it passed **34 focused tests / 3 files** and the six-artifact check. The current merge resolves only the later Discord delta, passes **13 snapshot-owner tests** and the canonical **six-artifact check**, and has an independent generated-resolution review plus zero-finding secret gate.
- Product discovery, discovery assertions, shared tool-description source and public Gateway E2E remain byte-identical to `ce374565`, including removal of the retired heartbeat setting. The two corrected subagent fixture files are byte-identical to CI-green `1c771bb8`. No production behavior, authorization, assertion, timeout or CI routing was changed by these integrations.
- [CI on `556aa634`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39905954094) exposed the existing subagent progress fixture: it expected optional external silence from a public completion cohort. The exact same-order Bun file replay reproduced **1 failed / 25 passed**; it was not dismissed as a flake. The correction binds the current requester incarnation as native spawn does and chooses private/parent completion for that optional-silence case. Production public/internal visible-reply requirements and every retire-count assertion are preserved.
- Corrected fixture proof at `1c771bb8`: **26 / 26 same-order Bun tests passed**, plus the exact case passed separately. Type-aware lint, format, diff check, independent parent review, fresh scoped Codex review and zero-finding secret gate passed. The private review snapshot is not a public ancestor.
- [CI on `1c771bb8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39908612884) completed **SUCCESS: 83 jobs, 56 successful / 27 skipped / zero failed**, including the real Gateway E2E and previously failing fixture lane. All current checks and both ci-gate contexts were terminal success/skip/neutral. That success is attributed to its own head; later main introduced the new generated conflict now resolved above.
- [Current-head CI `39910370654`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39910370654) completed **SUCCESS on `02db2066`: 81 jobs, 54 successful / 27 skipped / zero failed**. Gateway E2E, the corrected fixture lane, UI, types, lint and both ci-gate contexts passed. Latest-check readback: **75 success / 52 skipped / 1 neutral, zero failure or pending**. An older PR-context attempt was cancelled and superseded by its successful current attempt; it is not a product CI failure. Prior local Gateway proof at `ce374565` and earlier failed/cancelled/successful heads remain historical evidence.
- Final GitHub mergeability returned UNKNOWN. A read-only merge-tree against actual main `d3359fe448d37a56e4f9e38451832e6088f4842e` at 2026-10-23 06:26:52 UTC returned **exit0 / zero conflicts**. No freshness-only merge was made. No new post-push review request or non-author comment was present at final review readback.
- This work performs no employee/runtime update, private Core distribution, permission workaround or freshness-only merge. Only actual conflicts blocking this PR's validation are integrated. The maintainer disclosure/implementation-owner decision below is unchanged.

### Prior validation (historical)

Current author head: `bb51672d391105ad3b06ae1336ce1c1d1f5ee97e`. Integrated official main `79262d0571694dbf083b7d1bf5a206cc8fb93936` with an ordinary merge to resolve the named cached-title CI failure. It contains the adopted repairs #178510 and #178474. The existing feature patch is preserved; earlier validation below is attributed to prior head `f729bed82a2cbe2419ecfe49d0d913fd11caac58`.

- Focused current discovery tests: **2 files / 14 tests passed**.
- Core and extension typechecks, touched-source/proof type-aware lint, format, official prompt-snapshot check, and candidate diff check passed. The initial proof lint required only braces around two `for...of` assertions; no assertion changed.
- Fresh independent review of the full proposal found no P0-P2 defect. A separate fresh review of the final proof found no P0-P2 defect.
- Compiled real Gateway, public authenticated **POST /tools/invoke**: **PASS**, using synthetic configuration and standard QA child lifecycle. The committed opt-in case is `extensions/qa-lab/src/agents-list-descriptions.e2e.test.ts`.
- Public-entry proof: all **10 authorized rows** retained in order; the restricted requester sees exactly its **2 allowed rows**; the split-surrogate boundary returns **512 valid UTF-16 units**; CJK descriptions consume exactly **4096 weighted units**; late and blank descriptions are omitted without losing agent rows; configured model and current `auto`/`implicit` discovery metadata remain intact.
- The proof performs no inference or external delivery because discovery is a read-only Gateway-owned tool. It does not claim a live Slack/provider test or a package upgrade. Standard cleanup stopped owned Gateway PID 51147; process liveness readback confirmed it stopped.
- Opt-in E2E: 1 test passed, 53.50 seconds command wall time / 50.01 seconds Vitest duration (about 19 seconds test body, including Gateway startup and cleanup). Unit tests keep the cheaper budget cases.
- The first hosted run caught an unsupported, unused `label` cleanup option in the new proof (TS2353). It is removed; the canonical `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` now passes. This does not change runtime cleanup or assertions. [Prior-head CI 39421952171](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39421952171) completed. Canonical `check-test-types`, all five core-test type shards and the other product/static/test leaves succeeded. The only failed leaf is [UI cold-load case 118626035515](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39421952171/job/118626035515), plus its dependent aggregate. It is the same intermittent failure recorded on official main `6a2e9a1f9ea002b14e2847e8ca89e2b90c37f59d`, [main job 118557975798](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39401671859/job/118557975798): `expected 'New session' to be 'Synthetic cold-load conversation'`. No new or unclassified failed leaf remains.
- The integrated-base green CI [39417964143](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39417964143) skipped UI E2E; a later full main run [39415536071](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39415536071) passed the mocked UI shards. These are kept distinct from a green control for this case. Under CONTRIBUTING's known-main-failure policy, this PR adds no unrelated CI-only repair, weakening, rerun or budget change. Maintainers retain inherited-failure acceptance; this is **not** an all-green-CI claim.

### Captured public Gateway proof output

The following is the captured stdout from the existing successful Gateway run, copied with ANSI escapes and duplicate reporter lines removed. It is not a newly generated result summary. Only fixed proof fields and the test result are retained; no credential, endpoint, IP address, configuration dump, or conversation text is included. The HTTP response bodies were not separately saved. The committed scenario's assertions check the exact full/restricted agent IDs, bounded description strings, omitted fields and metadata before emitting `AGENTS_DESCRIPTION_PROOF`.

```text
AGENTS_DESCRIPTION_OWNER {"pid":51147}
AGENTS_DESCRIPTION_PROOF {"gatewayHttp":true,"rosterCount":10,"restrictedCount":2,"unicodeUnits":512,"aggregateWeightedUnits":4096,"modelMetadataRetained":true,"noInferenceOrExternalDelivery":true}
✓ extensions/qa-lab/src/agents-list-descriptions.e2e.test.ts > bounds configured descriptions without changing the authorized Gateway roster 19298ms
✓ bounds configured descriptions without changing the authorized Gateway roster 19298ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed (1)
Duration  50.01s (transform 52%, tests 39%, import 8%, worker 1%)
```

The capture precedes the final removal of an unused unsupported cleanup label option. That one-line type fix leaves production code, response assertions and runtime cleanup unchanged; the current-head canonical test-type gates pass. This capture claims the compiled candidate tree's public Gateway behavior, not an employee runtime or official package upgrade.

Reproduce the public entry proof after installing dependencies:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
```
