prs.title: feature(channels): add channels start|stop|reconnect for existing Gateway RPCs
prs.body:
Implements #183098

## What Problem This Solves

Docs already prescribe `channels.stop` / `channels.start` for non-destructive per-account recovery (keep pairing/credentials; crash-loop safe-mode manual override), but operators must hand-craft `openclaw gateway call` JSON. The channels CLI has list/status/login/logout/dead-letters but no first-class start/stop.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw channels stop|start|reconnect --channel <id> [--account <id>] --json` wraps the existing Gateway RPCs. Blank `--account` fails closed. Unknown channel fails closed. Prefer these over `gateway call`. Distinct from `channels logout` (clears credentials) and `gateway restart` (whole process).

## Why This Change Was Made

Thin Alix-style CLI adapters under the **existing** `channels` tree only: forward validated params (including Gateway `--port`/`--url`) to `channels.start` / `channels.stop`, update recovery docs and the crash-loop manual-start hint, and keep Gateway semantics unchanged. No new Gateway methods, schema, or permissions.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/channels/start-stop.ts`, `src/cli/channels-cli.ts`, `src/infra/gateway-boot-lifecycle.ts` (+ tests), `docs/cli/channels.md`, `docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md`, `docs/channels/troubleshooting.md`
- Unit: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/channels/start-stop.test.ts` — **6 passed**; `src/infra/gateway-boot-lifecycle.test.ts` hint cases — **19 passed**
- Packaged CLI e2e below on local Gateway with Telegram accounts

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Operators need native `openclaw channels start|stop|reconnect` that call existing `channels.start` / `channels.stop`; stop/start must return Gateway `stopped` / `started`+`outcome`; blank `--account` and unknown channel must fail closed; status probe remains available after recovery.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw channels stop|start|reconnect` → `channelsStopCommand` / `channelsStartCommand` / `channelsReconnectCommand` → `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport("channels.stop"|"channels.start", …)` → `src/gateway/server-methods/channels.ts`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses `addGatewayClientOptions`, `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport`, and `parseAccountSelector`. Does not own channel lifecycle; reuses existing Gateway account start/stop owners (same path login already uses for `channels.start`).

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI after `qaRuntime` build on Node 24.22.1; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`; local `openclaw gateway run --port 18821` with token auth; Telegram channel enabled with fake BotFather tokens (accounts `default` + `proof`).

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node openclaw.mjs channels stop --channel telegram --account proof --url ws://127.0.0.1:18821 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs channels start --channel telegram --account proof --url ws://127.0.0.1:18821 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs channels start --channel telegram --account proof --port 18821 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs channels reconnect --channel telegram --account proof --url ws://127.0.0.1:18821 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs channels status --channel telegram --probe --json
node openclaw.mjs channels start --channel telegram --account "" --json   # blank reject
node openclaw.mjs channels start --channel definitely-not-a-channel --url … --json
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
# channels --help lists start / stop / reconnect
  start         Start one channel account runtime without re-authenticating (channels.start)
  stop          Stop one channel account runtime without clearing credentials (channels.stop)
  reconnect     Stop then start one channel account (non-destructive reconnect)

# stop (exit 0)
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "accountId": "proof",
  "stopped": true
}

# start --url … (exit 0)
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "accountId": "proof",
  "started": true,
  "outcome": { "status": "handed-off" }
}

# start --port 18821 … (exit 0) — same started/outcome shape
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "accountId": "proof",
  "started": true,
  "outcome": { "status": "handed-off" }
}

# reconnect (exit 0)
{
  "stop": { "channel": "telegram", "accountId": "proof", "stopped": true },
  "start": {
    "channel": "telegram",
    "accountId": "proof",
    "started": true,
    "outcome": { "status": "handed-off" }
  }
}

# status --probe after recovery (exit 0) — probe present; running reflects lifecycle
# (fake token → probe 401 Unauthorized; recovery path exercised)

# blank --account (exit 1)
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "--account must not be blank" } }

# unknown channel (exit 1)
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "invalid channels.start channel" } }

# unconfigured account (Gateway semantics: exit 0, started:false skipped/unconfigured)
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "accountId": "definitely-missing-acct",
  "started": false,
  "outcome": { "status": "skipped", "reason": "unconfigured" }
}
```

## Notes for reviewers

- Extends existing `channels` CLI tree (not a new top-level namespace).
- Crash-loop recovery hint now points at `openclaw channels start --channel …` instead of `gateway call`.
- AI-assisted. Maintainers can edit.

prs.body:
# refactor: deslop settings, plugin and model test fixtures

The initial hosted run had an unresolved search-visibility failure. The shared-owner changes reachable from that test have now been withdrawn to baseline, with the canned fixtures placed in narrow adjacent owners instead. The repaired exact head passed all selected UI suites; this is not a claimed product-race fix. Two independently matched inherited Gateway type errors remain red, with their downstream aggregate, and use the authorized native exception below.

## What Problem This Solves

Settings, plugin and model tests repeat browser-context options, synthetic config/protocol responses, rosters, actors, capability records and schema fixtures. Copies obscure their actual allocation/lifecycle contract and make fixture changes drift between scenarios. Consolidate these 18 independent cuts onto their existing test-support owners, adding narrow constructors only where needed. No production implementation, user feature, public contract or persisted schema changes.

GitHub reports **1,288 additions / 1,691 deletions =403 net lines removed across 78 paths; production net0**. Local Git against base 103129e1ae6e6b4796f22ae0f2b8054f5c3827cc reports 1,296 additions / 1,699 deletions, with the same403net reduction. This is an explicitly authorized 100+ residue/split PR, **not a LARGE 500-line campaign claim**. Canonical import/reflow changes contribute to Git's net; no performance win or purely structural 403-line estimate is claimed.

Whole-file changes to ui/src/pages/plugins/plugins-page.test.ts and ui/src/lib/channels/index.test.ts were withdrawn after prior collision receipts identified open test-LOC work in #182922 and #182960. Both remain unchanged at the selected base; no cases or assertions were deleted. A new publication collision was then confirmed OPEN at #182992, head5a2c8a3158564a274f7a62efed5adbabb0e385b4, on ui/src/components/mcp-servers-card.test.ts. Its whole6net change was also withdrawn, restoring that file to exact selected-base bytes while preserving all other78 candidate hashes. Its101 assertions/21 registrations/7 table builders are outside this changed-file census, not deleted from the repository. Final fresh78path collision clearance passed as recorded below. The plugins-page baseline remains selected as an affected-owner sibling; channels/index is a baseline guard, not a changed-file census input.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. This removes duplicated test setup while retaining every scenario and expectation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each fixture family now has one test-support owner; distinct response shapes, allocation lifetimes and lifecycle hooks stay explicit at their original call sites.

## Preservation and count definition

Actual native census over all 78 BEFORE/CANDIDATE modules passes per-file raw call counts, registration labels/table arguments/hooks/order, and structural awaited-callee AST/order. **Assertions 2,310 → 2,310; registrations 383 → 383**. The one expect.assert guard is already included in assertions; custom expect calls 240 → 240 are separate. Tests 286 → 286; suites 16 → 16; custom suites 1 → 1; hooks 27 → 27; onTestFinished 3 → 3; mocks 2 → 2; suite.define 48 → 48. The 73 → 73 table builders are separate from the 383 registrations; counts are raw source calls, not expanded table rows or executed-test totals. No hook-relocation exception. Conditional builders and direct register* calls are 0 → 0.

Each cut below lists its exact native-receipt file set and BEFORE/AFTER tuple in this order: **[assertions, custom expect calls, tests, suites, custom suites, hooks, onTestFinished, mocks, suite.define, table builders]**. Registration totals sum tests/suites/custom suites/hooks/onTestFinished/mocks/suite.define/direct register calls/conditional builders, excluding tables. Some files have more than one independent cut: **per-cut counts overlap and must not be summed**. The unique 78-file totals above are authoritative. Historical 78-path Babel totals are superseded here, not inflated or presented as current results. Fixture freshness and intentionally shared/module-snapshot identities remain required; no test case, assertion, registration, skip/retry/timeout or expectation was weakened.

## Cuts and Best-effort tradeoffs accepted


The changed-file census excludes the two general helpers restored byte-for-byte to the selected baseline. The 80-file preservation union, including those unchanged helpers, still has 2,312 assertions and 389 registrations before and after; no coverage was deleted.

### 1. Fresh settings browser-context options

Eight invocation sites must retain separate outer objects and viewports, independent of that existing shared snapshot. The qualified 70-line net includes 37 lines of canonical indentation/wrapping beyond the 33-line structural estimate.

### 2. Default dark browser-context copies

prs.title: fix: selected Docker plugins resolve shared dependencies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes source-built Docker distributions where a plugin selected through `OPENCLAW_EXTENSIONS` can fail at runtime when the unified build places plugin-owned code in a shared root chunk. The frozen install already contains the selected plugin's exact production packages, but those packages were linked only beneath the packaged plugin root; native Node resolution from a root chunk could not reach them. For `memory-lancedb`, the complete selected graph placed LanceDB's Apache Arrow load in root chunks even though Arrow remained available only from the plugin root.

## User Impact

Selected Docker plugins can now use their already-installed runtime packages from both plugin-local chunks and shared root chunks. The final distribution preserves the same package versions, optional platform packages, plugin-local identities, unified build, and selection behavior. This does not add dependencies, change source manifests or the lockfile, run another install, or affect ordinary images without selected external plugins. An incompatible existing root binding fails closed instead of being replaced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The post-install prune step already owns the final selected-plugin dependency layout. It now reuses the existing package-composition contract to add selected plugins' exact production and optional pins to the distribution manifest, then links only package identities already present in the frozen selected-plugin install into the root resolution scope. The existing plugin-root links remain in place for plugin-local imports, while the shared link primitive keeps POSIX-relative and Windows-junction behavior consistent.

The test fixture now models that real root-plus-plugin layout and invokes the same materialization owner before exercising the packaged memory store. Packaging-owner coverage also proves compatible composition, optional-package handling, conflict refusal without clobbering an existing root package, and unchanged unselected pruning.

## Evidence

- Before the correction, the exact full memory-selected unified graph contained 1,244 entries and emitted LanceDB/Arrow into root chunks owned by `memory-lancedb`. The root `createRequire(import.meta.url)` search path excluded the plugin's packaged `node_modules`; root declared no Arrow, the plugin declared `apache-arrow@21.2.0`, and resolution failed.
- On the exact candidate tree, changed-file formatting/lint and all ten selected type graphs passed remotely.
- Six focused owner/control files passed 95 tests. Both quiet and verbose memory artifact modes stored, recalled, reopened, directly read LanceDB, and observed a declared native binding with the original assertions and timeouts.
- The full `tsdown-config` owner group completed 68 tests in 51.07 seconds; all focused test groups completed in 60.54 seconds.
- The exact native CLI entrypoint was also exercised against an isolated post-install distribution: the same installed package resolved from root and plugin scopes, an unavailable optional remained declared without a fabricated link, and an omitted plugin was pruned.
- Independent calibrated and canonical reviews found no actionable defect in the exact patch.

Hosted CI passed every branch-relevant packaging, build-artifact, docs, lint, test, security, and type row. Its only failures are the same TS2739 in the unchanged catalog test helper, plus the aggregate gate; that shared synthetic-client fixture is independently owned by #183071.

prs.body:
## Problem and impact

Single-consumer internal modules, forwarding callbacks and handwritten result packets add surface without an independent owner. This stack moves implementations to their existing consumers and derives private results from their producers. No intended user-visible change, new option, SDK/protocol/config/data-shape change, or lazy-import cutover.

The independent cuts below can be withdrawn separately for CI attribution. Public-entry assertions stay; removed tests targeted retired private seams. Phase E standalone session memory and its factory, registry, expiry, federation and tests are untouched.

## Plugin directory and action owners

Fold Buzz directory and LINE binding donors into their actual plugin slots. Localize Zalo actions/routes and ClickClack target forwarding, retaining their public-entry assertions. Remove the private IRC group-result mirror.

### Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. Directory authentication, timeout, snapshot fallback, relay cleanup, binding normalization and matching, target isolation and action behavior remain. Main's independently landed Zalo classifier/status changes are preserved, not credited here.

## QA report and preflight frames

Put the sole-consumer runtime report contract with its producer, derive its private result, and localize the parity preflight at the admitted CLI branch. Remove private candidate-option and timing envelopes.

### Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

The private preflight wrapper's extra completion microtask disappears. The preflight still runs first, requires executed coverage when failures are allowed, reports the same artifact paths, and rejects the same blocking scenarios otherwise. Runtime report fields, coverage checks, cache diagnostics and CLI contracts remain.

## Matrix, Feishu, OMLX, Tencent and Teams frames

Move Matrix config-string resolution into its existing field loop and infer its private profile result. Put Feishu history filtering at its concrete caller and document-upload envelopes in the existing switch; localize its comment queue key. Fold OMLX's explicit-auth predicate, Tencent's effort signature and Teams' standard-channel finder into their only owners.

### Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. Matrix SecretRef/env policy and suppression remain. Feishu sender/history policy, per-message parallel checks, input-resolution-before-image-block ordering and upload/patch order remain. OMLX explicit bearer/custom-header auth still replaces stale Authorization with the same blank/null policy. Teams keeps token resolution before missing-team rejection, standard-channel restriction, the 100-page bound, outsider denial, requester fast path and current read-authority/release behavior.

## UI private preparation frames

Localize Channels mutation presentation, Chat/Question preparation, attachment, CI-details, picker, favicon, creation-composer and session-page frames in their sole owners. Remove the remaining erased translation alias. Fold omitted-media normalization into its existing content loop, derive diagnostics from its producer, display device rotation outcomes at their caller and construct model-default patches at the admitted mutation.

### Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. Rendering, text, styles, Solid primitives and lazy boundaries are unchanged. Separate epoch/presentation memos, optimistic lifetime, retirement and settlement stay. Omitted-media keeps all four input checks and URL/artifact precedence. Diagnostics retain request/signal/agent behavior. Returned rotation secrets remain visible after connection reset. Defaults retain omitted fields, null resets, fallback copies, replacePaths and config authority. The proposed login fold was withdrawn because it lost native narrowing; the core-load fold was withdrawn because formatting erased its savings.

## Native result types and public test entry points

Infer the native stop-timeout and branch-landing results without changing their implementations. Retain image-preparation and safe-timeout regression assertions through their real package entry points. Delete orphaned private-seam tests and exactly two obsolete mock-export baseline rows plus one obsolete native-Bun qualification entry.

### Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

None. Shutdown cancellation/durable settlement, Git-ref landing facts, image MIME/bounds/errors, auth timeout overflow/floor behavior and public exports remain. No active baseline allowance is widened; no assertion, timeout, retry or skip is relaxed.

## Size and local proof

Against base `906369321f0bea19387d29ffa332c3ab53e1bb16`: **941 additions / 1,442 deletions = 501 net removed across 59 paths**, including tests and shrink-only inventories; production scope is **436 net removed**. This replaces the original 651-net published stack after the targeted CI withdrawal below; these are whole-PR figures, not incremental savings.

Each retained slice has scoped source inspection, author simplification and independent review through P2. Focused public-entry tests, targeted native types, typed lint and formatting were run per slice; unchanged-input proof is reused. The replacement extension cuts pass **112 cases across three files**, Teams **55 across three files**, and the four replacement UI cuts **135 across 11 files**. No test source changed in these replacements. Initial UI narrowing errors led to withdrawing the login cut, not casts or suppressions.

Local execution uses isolated HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state, nice 10, serial commands and one Vitest worker. No broad local suite, whole-graph typecheck, build, live channel/device proof or operator-state access is claimed. Exact repaired-head hosted CI is the broad gate. Prior-head CI is not relabeled green.

Current repaired-source structural gates pass: assertion-safety and mock-export ratchets, line caps across 47 changed source files, zero runtime value cycles, zero static cycles, all 14 lint-suppression cases, all 11 stable-tool-prefix cases and all three wrapper inventory/import-closure cases. After interruption, completed ratchet results were retained and only the remaining checks resumed. Fresh independent review of the final four UI paths is scoped-clean through P2.

## CI repair and withdrawal

Published head `356ddc642e475eb0346854fc5048e964470670e7`, CI run `40145683238`:

| Job | Attribution | Resolution / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-20-2` / `121026686367` | Chat-startup replay inconclusive | `server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts:1953` failed before reasoning projection with session-access facts unavailable. This proves neither inheritance nor a fix. Under campaign rule 8, restore all 44 changed production paths reachable in the conservative union graph, plus their two assertion and twelve wrapper-inventory rows, exactly to PR base. All 46 restored blobs were verified byte-for-byte. |
| `checks-node-changed-compact-large-30-1` / `121026686458` | Proven inherited stale lifecycle expectation | `server-plugins.lifecycle.test.ts:459` expects `restartRequired: false`; base-ancestor #182403 (`ae81c0703e7ca223cb671612e74834e414670a0c`) deliberately requires true for loaded bundled instances. All 137 exact-head check runs were enumerated. prs.title: perf(gateway): reuse audience field indexes in session broadcasts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session-event projections repeat row-field enumeration and allocate key/value pairs that are immediately discarded when clients have different delivered-row histories. A real Gateway workload with 66 connections and three operator audiences produced 47.5 delivery plans per message publication and 45.3 per roster publication, despite sharing the authorized row itself.

## User Impact

**Decision: do not merge; measurement says skip.** The candidate reduces projection allocation, but fails the predeclared list-latency gate. This PR is closed without a production change. The source cause of the latency stalls is not established; the acceptance result is sufficient to reject this candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare the immutable row's ordered field index once in its existing audience record. Build wire-copy entries only for fields that survive filtering. The per-recipient authority checks, history plans, equality checks, publisher snapshot timing, and serialization identities remain intact. The synchronous wire-copy callback reads through the existing variant-local payload, avoiding a lexical capture of the longer-lived delivery binding; the proposed retention mechanism remains unproven. The final candidate was measured against the same baseline, rather than claiming that this one-word change independently caused the observed differences. Production code grows by one line for the audience-owned field index; its lifetime and invalidation are exactly those of the existing audience cache.

The benchmark additions reproduce three operator roles, staggered joins, 10,000 synthetic sessions, 40 synthetic startup plugins, mixed legacy/delta capabilities, narration and chat subscriptions, and concurrent mock-provider tool/subagent turns. They also count delivery-plan misses, attribute bundled projection allocations, and feed real Control UI session consumers. Consumer results explicitly distinguish unused message bodies from whole-event effects; absence of an observed synchronous effect is not treated as proof that a frame can be dropped.

## Evidence

Matched owner comparison: common runtime and baseline owner from `7221ce54924ac848aa14ac75c5a74b269102d280` (main at investigation start, including #182362), with only the candidate projector replaced by the reviewed source on `759ef86832989f8cabbfd07066e35655aef308f4`. Shared benchmark instrumentation and Linux native-owner setup are identical on both arms.

Acceptance declared before paired runs: the primary metric is allocation attributed to session-event projection per delivered session event; whole-Gateway CPU, allocation, GC, loop delay, and pauses are reported alongside it. Use concurrent baseline/candidate Gateways, identical prepared fixtures, swapped interleaved CPU placement, synchronized warm start, maintenance enabled, and the shared production guard unchanged. Untraced CPU/GC/loop measurements and sampled allocation/promotion captures are separate. Apply the campaign's sample minimums, absolute GC/tail materiality, and matched A/A controls before rejecting on noisy GC/promotion/max-pause signals.

Diagnostic baseline (normal count pass, four rounds): 34,342 delivered session events, zero missing row baselines, zero failed consumer refreshes. Three authorized audiences still produced 47.5 delivery plans per message publication and 45.3 per roster publication because capability and delivered-history facts differ. Subscription filtering already runs before projection.

The local no-inline allocation capture attributes 463.5 MB to envelope construction, 230.4 MB to field indexing, and 303.1 MB to wire-field copying. Native entry arrays, sorting, and object construction account for the reported native frames; UTF-8 encoding is a separate allocation site. Candidate attribution shows 36.4 MB for field indexing and 254.8 MB for wire copying: reductions of 84.2% and 15.7% per delivered event. This is diagnostic attribution, not acceptance timing: the candidate local build includes newer unrelated main changes, and the profiler disables inlining. Matched Team pairs use the same baseline plus this patch.

The real session consumer probe found 6,993 unused sidebar message bodies (14.4 MB), about 56.6 bodies/second. It also recorded 9,650 deliveries without an observed synchronous consumer effect, but asynchronous refresh and baseline maintenance mean these are not proven removable frames. Narration subscriptions explicitly retain full bodies; this patch preserves that contract.

Final acceptance used two swapped untraced pairs, two separate sampled-allocation pairs, and the one extra untraced pair required by the predeclared instability rule. Every valid arm completed 16 primary turns with zero diagnostic errors or dropped samples. The final candidate reduced projection bytes per delivered event by **15.132% and 13.429%** (paired mean **14.281%**); broadcast allocation per delivered event fell **7.52%**. Whole-Gateway allocation per turn changed **+2.303% and -1.431%** (mean **+0.436%**). Traced promotion changed **+27.709% and +0.207%** (mean **+13.958%**), which does not meet the mean-or-both-pairs gate. Timing from these traced passes is diagnostic only.

The two primary untraced pairs averaged **-1.64% main-thread CPU/turn** and **-6.05% GC/min**. List p95 was unstable: **48.851→738.991 ms** and **3003.335→2976.290 ms**, with **366/335** and **325/336** samples. Baselines differed 61.48× and the paired signs opposed, so one extra pair was declared before running it. That pair measured **104.418→647.618 ms**, with **350/321** samples. Across all three, the signed absolute mean increase is **402.098 ms**, against a mean baseline of **1052.201 ms**: **+38.215%**, exceeding the 20% threshold (**210.440 ms**). The misleading mean relative percentage is not used. All three untraced pairs averaged main CPU -4.02%, GC/min -11.15%, and loop p99 +0.568 ms; these improvements do not offset the latency rejection. All per-kind GC counts, tails, and both maxima are retained below.

In-window diagnostics show long asynchronous list yield/read waiting, but do not prove the source cause. Later archive-materialization log messages do not align with the first bad round and also occur on baseline, so they are not used as causal evidence. No valid sample, maintenance window, or adverse pair was trimmed or discarded.

The initial variant was also rejected: projection allocation fell 18.78%/19.94%, but list p95 rose 11.39/19.85 ms and GC rose 177.80/234.48 ms/min. Its four predeclared untraced A/A controls averaged CPU +0.27%, GC +6.06 ms/min (+0.81%), and list p95 -2.89 ms (-4.14%). Per-kind GC tails did not gate. Aggregate GC p95 across all four controls was +0.296 ms (+6.88%), while grouping controls 3/4 alone gives +1.008 ms (+20.21%). Neither that partition nor a mixed-kind percentile gate was explicit; this ambiguity is retained rather than describing the controls as uniformly clean. Initial-variant rejection is independently supported by list latency.

Setup failures are preserved separately and excluded from paired acceptance. The first source-entry attempt failed before warmup because Linux native child ownership rejects source-loader hooks; the benchmark now binds the compiled native owner through the canonical sealed-entry API, matching the existing matrix harness. A direct child execution and both cleanup joins passed. Later attempts missed the start barrier, and one was interrupted by the unchanged shared guard. The private runner was corrected to stop if either arm failed, check the guard after warmup, and use a symmetric 15-second lead. A concrete publication race was then found: shell redirection exposed an empty start file, which the reader parsed as fallback epoch 1. The timestamp is now written to a temporary file and atomically renamed. This mechanism is reproduced, but the generic error does not prove it caused every earlier failure. Successful pairs demonstrably read complete equal timestamps and released within 0–7 ms; their results remain counted. Both fixtures were regenerated after asymmetric failed attempts. The failed allocation pair was replaced with the same swapped protocol, followed by the already-declared third untraced pair.


Validation:

- New work-count assertion fails on baseline: four full-row enumerations versus a bound of two, with interleaved authorities, capabilities, and delivered baselines.
- Candidate real-Gateway consumer probe: 31,306 session-event deliveries across 66 clients and three roles, zero missing baselines, zero failed refreshes, all consumers ready.
- Focused Gateway tests: 6 passed across session-row-delta-audiences, session-row-event-parity, and session-row-publication-authority. Diagnostics collector: 4 passed.
- Targeted core typecheck and changed-file format/lint passed.
- Export collision guard passed; runtime-import/PR-wrapper closure guards: 22 tests passed.
- Prior-head PR CI run 40136487491 passed on b314c79a6a8fd61dc7b1d2b083a9418a57425ce3. The benchmark setup follow-up passed 14 focused profiler tests and changed-file format/lint. CI run 40141155643 passed on prior head 75c2ce12312feaa3d325ea067b0471babdce1da6. The capture refinement passed all six focused Gateway tests and changed-file format/lint; current-head CI run 40144464703 and follow-up security/dependency review 40144942347 passed on 759ef86832989f8cabbfd07066e35655aef308f4. No Testbox lease used.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean through P2 after fixing narration subscription classification in benchmark byte attribution. Separate independent reviews of the Linux benchmark setup follow-up and the capture refinement are also clean through P2; the setup review caught and resolved file-URL eval-fixture handling.


<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

The committed driver is `scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts`. Prepare each isolated fixture sequentially:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/team-shape-fixture.ts \
  --state-dir <state> --sessions 10000 --runs 8000 --settled-runs \
  --approvals 20 --cron 10 --projects 2 --transcript-mib 1 \
  --seed 967 --now 1791892800000 --port <port>
```

Build the common runtime once before Linux source-entry benchmarking so the canonical native process owner is available. For each concurrent arm, use separate state/ports and its baseline or candidate projection source directory:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts \
  --state-dir <state> --port <port> --mock-port <mock-port> \
  --session-projection-source <owner-source-directory> \
  --scenario memory-soak --clients 66 --exact-clients 12 \
  --viewer-profiles 3 --viewer-roles --viewer-join-batch 6 \
  --session-capability-clients 33,0,33 --roster-body-optional-clients 0,0,33 \
  --sidebar-narration --session-event-ancestors 2 --fixture-plugins 40 \
  --runs 4 --chunks 200 --chunk-interval-ms 10 --stress-tools --stress-subagents \
  --warmup-ms 10000 --duration-ms 60000 --soak-rounds 4 \
  --round-interval-ms 15000 --list-interval-ms 7000 --poll-seed lane1675 \
  --retained-profile-ms 0 --diagnostics --entry src/entry.ts \
  --startup-timeout-ms 600000 --start-file <shared-release-file>
```

Allocation passes add `--allocations --heap-sampling-interval 32768`. Acceptance runs use normal inlining and no source-count/site or consumer-probe instrumentation. The two arms run under one exclusive slot lock with separate low-weight, memory-limited scopes, interleaved CPU assignments, swapped placement and launch order on pair 2, and the unchanged shared guard. Release only after both arms report `PHASE warmed` and the guard clears; publish a timestamp 15 seconds in the future by same-directory atomic rename; preserve failed starts and rerun with matched prepared state. All synthetic Gateway ports are loopback-only and above 40000.

prs.title: fix(daemon): use monotonic clock for launchd stop deadlines
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Gateway runs as a macOS LaunchAgent, stopping it polls launchd until the agent unloads and the gateway port is released, with timeout deadlines anchored to the **wall clock** (`Date.now()`). An NTP step or manual clock adjustment can break an in-progress stop: a forward jump misreports a timeout failure, a backward jump over-extends the wait — either way the Gateway can be left half-stopped, stalling update/recovery flows.

- **Solution**: Anchor both deadlines to the monotonic clock (`performance.now()`), which measures elapsed time and is unaffected by wall-clock adjustments.
- **What changed**: `src/daemon/launchd-stop.ts` — replaced all six `Date.now()` deadline reads with `performance.now()` across the two polling loops; added a regression test in `src/daemon/launchd-stop-deadline.test.ts`.
- **What did NOT change**: timeout durations, polling cadence, error messages, or any other stop behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The codebase already standardizes on the monotonic clock for deadline computation (`createGatewayRestartDeadline`). This change brings the launchd stop deadlines in line. `performance.now()` is consumed through `sleep`'s `resolveTimerTimeoutMs` floor, so no rounding is needed, and the deadlines are process-local so monotonic time is safe. No behavior other than the clock source for deadline expiry changes.

## User Impact

macOS users running the Gateway as a LaunchAgent no longer see stop operations fail or hang when the system clock is adjusted (NTP sync, manual time change, timezone travel). Gateway update and recovery flows that stop the service complete reliably regardless of wall-clock jumps.

## Evidence

Regression test in `src/daemon/launchd-stop-deadline.test.ts` fakes `Date` + timers (so `vi.setSystemTime` moves the wall clock without the real monotonic `performance` clock), jumps the wall clock one hour forward, and asserts the stop does not expire prematurely and still completes:

```console
$ npx vitest run --project daemon src/daemon/launchd-stop-deadline.test.ts
 ✓ |daemon| src/daemon/launchd-stop-deadline.test.ts > does not prematurely expire the stop deadline when the wall clock moves forward
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Adjacent launchd stop/restart suites still pass with the fix (cherry-picked onto current main):

```console
$ npx vitest run --project daemon src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/launchd-deadline.test.ts src/daemon/launchd-stop-deadline.test.ts
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  74 passed (74)
```

**Failing-base regression**: the regression test guards the bug — passes on the fixed `performance.now()` deadline and fails on the old `Date.now()` deadline:

```console
 ✓ fixed (performance.now) ... does not prematurely expire the stop deadline when the wall clock moves forward  1 passed
 × base  (Date.now)        ... does not prematurely expire the stop deadline when the wall clock moves forward  1 failed
```

**Live-system-clock proof**: no live OS clock adjustment is performed; the +1e6 ms step is injected into the OLD variant's deadline reads (equivalent to a real NTP/manual forward jump between seed and reads). See macOS proof above.

**Open PR collision check**: no open PR touches `launchd-stop.ts`.

**macOS real-transport GHA proof (shipped stop path, bounded expiry + port-release)**: drove the shipped `stopLaunchAgent` on a real macOS runner against a real live TERM-resistant child PID (real `process.kill` liveness) and, for port-release, a real TCP port kept busy by a real listener (real `probePortUsage`). A **+1,000,000 ms** forward step is injected into the **OLD** `Date.now()` variant's deadline reads only; **FIXED** `performance.now()` is unmodified. The stop budget was shortened (drain 315s→8s) only to make bounded expiry observable in a fast workflow; the monotonic-vs-wall logic under test is untouched. Headless launchctl/membership wrapping matches merged PR #175204 and is independent of the deadline logic.

Run: https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/40150108893

```console
===== unload scenario (job stays loaded, real live PID) =====
VERDICT[FIXED/unload] wall_jump=+1000000ms observe=40000ms settled_at=33004ms
  rejected: ... is still loaded; PID 4200 is still alive   <- bounded expiry HONORED (full ~33s budget)
VERDICT[OLD/unload]   wall_jump=+1000000ms observe=40000ms settled_at=3ms
  rejected: ... is still loaded; PID 5443 is still alive  <- PREMATURE (clock step cuts budget to ~0ms)

===== port-release scenario (unload completes, real busy port) =====
VERDICT[FIXED/port] wall_jump=+1000000ms observe=40000ms settled_at=27196ms
  rejected: gateway port 49329 is still busy after LaunchAgent stop   <- bounded expiry HONORED
VERDICT[OLD/port]   wall_jump=+1000000ms observe=40000ms settled_at=1263ms
  rejected: gateway port 49332 is still busy after LaunchAgent stop   <- PREMATURE
```

**Before / After** (wall-clock step +1,000,000 ms, real live PID + real monotonic clock + real busy port):

| | Before — OLD `Date.now()` deadline | After — FIXED `performance.now()` deadline |
|---|---|---|
| Deadline source | wall clock (jumps with system clock) | monotonic clock (measures elapsed time, immune) |
| Unload wait under +1e6 ms step | deadline expires at loop start → **premature rejection** (`settled_at=3ms`) | deadline far away → waits the full bounded budget → **bounded expiry honored** (`settled_at=33004ms`) |
| Port-release wait under +1e6 ms step | deadline expires immediately → **premature rejection** (`settled_at=1263ms`) | deadline far away → waits the full bounded budget → **bounded expiry honored** (`settled_at=27196ms`) |
| Stop outcome | misreported as a timeout failure | stop waits the full bounded budget and completes normally |

Under a forward +1,000,000 ms wall-clock step, the `Date.now()` deadlines expire the instant the waits begin (premature rejection); `performance.now()` is monotonic and immune, so both waits run to their full bounded expiry. No local paths, IPs, API keys, or non-public endpoints appear in the output.

prs.title: refactor: remove unused memory host facade exports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The memory host still forwarded 15 symbols through private host modules after all live consumers had moved to their canonical owners, and one same-file implementation helper remained exported without an external caller. Those redundant edges obscured the real ownership boundary and continued to appear as unused production exports.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. Canonical session readers and producers, memory indexing behavior, named `@openclaw/memory-host-sdk` package entrypoints, configuration, persistence, and permissions remain unchanged. The cleanup only makes unconsumed host-internal routes private.

## Why This Change Was Made

Complete caller and package-boundary inspection showed that no selected symbol is imported through `openclaw-runtime-session.ts` or `openclaw-runtime-paths.ts`. Live callers already import the canonical session, agent, heartbeat, provenance, and session-key owners directly. The package is private and exposes ten named runtime, engine, query, and status subpaths; none exposes `host/*` or forwards the selected host-facade routes.

This change therefore removes only the 15 redundant forwarding exports and the `export` modifier from `buildSessionEntryInProcess`. The helper body and its same-file caller are retained, as are every other facade export and all canonical producer exports.

## Evidence

On the pinned base, a focused remote reproduction found all 16 selected private export edges. On the candidate:

- changed-file formatting and lint passed with zero warnings or errors;
- every selected production and test type graph passed;
- the eight existing memory-host test files that literally import the changed modules passed, covering 61 tests; and
- a focused source-boundary check proved the exact three allowlisted file transformations, absence of all 16 selected routes, byte identity for all ten named package entry files and their manifest, preservation of all 14 canonical producer exports, and retention of the helper definition plus same-file call.

Hosted CI, independent exact-head review, and the repository's automated review remain pending after initial publication.

prs.title: fix: prevent terminal recovery test teardown leaks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes terminal-recovery tests that could finish their assertions while the resolver-created reply operation was still waiting on dispatcher finalization. The predecessor operation was already settled, but the successor's queued final-delivery task had no owner running the dispatcher's settlement lifecycle, leaving its watchdog live into later fixture work.

## User Impact

There is no product runtime change. Developers and CI now get terminal-recovery cases that finish only after their reply dispatcher, successor operation, and watchdog have genuinely settled. The existing producer barriers, recovery outcomes, final-reply behavior, timing branches, and assertions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The affected three-case table already owns one dispatcher and already imports the production `withReplyDispatcher` lifecycle used by neighboring cases. Wrapping the existing `dispatchReplyFromConfig` call in that owner runs registered final-delivery settlement tasks before the case completes. The cases also observe the exact resolver-provided operation and verify that its owner has settled and its watchdog is closed when the wrapper returns.

The shared test harness remains unchanged. A broader shared-teardown approach did not quiesce consumers that intentionally retain work, so the correction stays at the one call boundary that owns this lifetime.

## Evidence

- Before the correction, one focused observation of the existing `fresh`, `stalled`, and `terminal-row` cases showed the predecessor settled in all three while the distinct resolver successor remained owner-unsettled, current, and in terminal watchdog phase at case return.
- On the exact committed tree, remote changed-file formatting and lint passed with no warnings or errors.
- The selected `core-test-messaging` type graph passed remotely.
- The full terminal-recovery owner file passed remotely: 32 tests in one file, including the three successor-settlement assertions.
- Hosted CI, independent review, and the exact-head automated review are pending on the newly published head.

prs.title: fix: completed LLM initialization releases prompt buffers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the first completed LLM initialization can keep its caller and prompt buffer alive for the lifetime of the process.

The retained object is a module-level `Error` used only to select the transcript snapshot native-clone fallback. When that module initializes during an LLM call, the cached error stack can inherit and retain the caller's async context.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible workflow or compatibility change. After an initialization call completes, its request-scoped context and prompt can be collected while the process runtime and local provider remain reusable.

Transcript snapshot behavior is unchanged: supported containers still use the fast copy path, opaque structured-cloneable values still fall back to `structuredClone`, shared aliases remain shared, and unrelated errors still propagate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback marker is private control flow, but a single cached `Error` is the wrong lifetime owner because an error carries stack context. The marker is now an unexported error type with a fresh instance at each fallback point. Those instances are caught synchronously by type and released; the module no longer keeps an error object that can own the first caller's context.

This keeps the existing four fallback decisions and the identity boundary in one owner without changing the generic lazy promise cache, LLM dispatch ordering, transcript data, or tests.

## Evidence

The existing production-path lifecycle retention case failed on base `3270e6953055a12ceb9f8ad4a3dad908b5f27972`: only the completed LLM initialization caller and its 1 MiB prompt remained; the provider-child and idle-timer controls collected. Sanitized heap dominator evidence traced that prompt to the module-level transcript clone fallback error.

On final tree `23575f577c1b0aca376428637ce449a89a612ca2`:

| Existing workload observation | Base | Final |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained completed-caller WeakRefs | 2 | 0 |
| Retained 1 MiB prompt | yes | no |
| Retained provider child/timer controls | 0 | 0 |
| Provider child reusable after collection | yes | yes |

Remote focused validation on the same retained Testbox passed:

- changed-file format and lint;
- every selected affected type graph, including core tests and consumers;
- the unchanged lifecycle retention owner;
- existing SessionManager clone fallback, error propagation, opaque-alias, and frozen-graph coverage;
- 58 focused tests across the selected native Vitest shards.

Hosted CI, independent review, and the repository's automated review remain pending at initial publication.

## What Problem This Solves

prs.title: fix(feishu): keep the app registration poll deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Feishu/Lark QR registration keeps polling beyond device-code expiry, or stops early, when the system wall clock changes during pairing.

## User Impact

The registration poll consumes its existing expiry budget using elapsed time, so a clock correction does not extend or shorten the pairing window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The poll owner now uses `performance.now()` for deadline creation and comparison. Provider interval normalization, cancellation, backoff, and registration outcomes retain their existing behavior. The redundant clock explanation was removed; production changes are two substitutions (+2/-2, net 0), with one 24-line regression. Thanks to @mikasa0818 for the fix and regression.

## Evidence

- On main `8c6ad0edc3c9d87f5a5b5a40fad6f84761066348`, the regression remains unsettled after 35 seconds of fake elapsed time when the wall clock rewinds ten minutes. With the fix it returns `timeout`; the entire file plus the temporary runtime probe passed (9/9).
- Real timers and a real local HTTP server through the existing guarded registration transport: a one-second expiry and ten-second wall rewind produced 16 polls over 3202 ms on base (stopped by the probe's safety cap), versus 5 polls over 1043 ms with the fix. The temporary probe was removed after comparison.
- Command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-ct-monoA pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Targeted syntax-only oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent diff review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The isolated leaf-package typecheck could not resolve unbuilt `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` declaration artifacts. Type-aware extension lint then reached the wrapper’s 300-second SDK declaration-generation timeout. Exact-head PR CI supplies broad validation; neither setup failure is a product verdict.
- A real Feishu account/QR round-trip was not live-tested; this proof used synthetic responses from a local HTTP server and required no account credentials.

prs.title: perf(sessions): await the active usage refresh owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent `/usage cost` detail requests retry a busy agent-wide refresh every 25 ms, repeating filesystem identity checks and writer preparation while the existing owner is still working. A waiting request now joins that owner's completion, then refreshes its own requested session so its detail remains fresh. Background refresh requests still return busy immediately, and caller cancellation remains effective.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing refresh owner remains the single owner. Its exclusion entry carries completion for durable and memory callers; the polling loop and delay constant are deleted. Durable admission preserves the existing file identity captured during preparation. A previously missing store may adopt the incumbent's creation only at the same canonical target. Release preserves write settlement ordering. If writer cleanup fails, completion still wakes waiters, the original error remains visible, and cleanup stays retryable. Completion settles once, so retrying old cleanup cannot retire a successor refresh.

Production code grows by 41 lines net for owner notification and cancellation. SQL text, schema, transactions, retention, configuration, and SDK contracts are unchanged; there is no new cache, generation, or fencing protocol. The committed read-only workload probe preserves child IPC and counts initial and post-wait writer preparation.

## Acceptance and Measurements

Acceptance was registered before measurement in #182926 and [`scripts/perf/session-readiness.md`](scripts/perf/session-readiness.md): run an exact-head isolated Gateway through the bundled iMessage adapter and a synthetic loopback bridge, using four distinct synthetic sessions, one cold burst, and five warm bursts. A qualifying baseline must reproduce a busy sleep. Every one of the 24 replies must retain its requested session's fresh token and cost detail. The candidate must eliminate busy sleeps and repeated preparation while preserving cancellation and error behavior. Count filesystem work, SQL, and worker requests across the main thread and workers; busy exclusion precedes dispatch, so no SQL saving is presumed.

Cold and warm results stay separate. All user-facing metrics must hold or improve; a 20% regression is a stop. A latency comparison requires at least five interleaved baseline/candidate samples each, median, p95, and range under the timing lock below load 24. Timing qualification exceeded 60 minutes without meeting that load threshold, so the present evidence is counts and per-thread profiles, with no wall-clock parity, latency improvement, or SQL reduction claim.

The corrected baseline probe confirmed the actual Gateway process independently through its native runtime log and frozen-observer metadata. All 24 requested details were verified.

| Baseline: per four concurrent detail requests | Cold | Warm median [min–max] | Warm p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Busy retry sleeps | 5 | 12 [1–31] | 31 |
| Refresh-path stat calls | 18 | 32 [10–70] | 70 |
| Refresh-path realpath calls | 18 | 32 [10–70] | 70 |
| SQL statements, all threads | 578 | 638 [608–700] | 700 |
| Worker requests | 146 | 142 [133–150] | 150 |
| Main-thread SQL | 0 | 0 [0–0] | 0 |

Busy attempts themselves issue zero SQL statements and zero worker requests. The intended saving is retry timers and repeated preparation.

| Candidate `8c68db484ac`: per four concurrent detail requests | Cold | Warm median [min–max] | Warm p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Busy retry sleeps | 0 | 0 [0–0] | 0 |
| Refresh-path stat calls | 8 | 8 [8–8] | 8 |
| Refresh-path realpath calls | 4 | 4 [4–4] | 4 |
| SQL statements, all threads | 574 | 581 [528–652] | 652 |
| Worker requests | 145 | 136 [125–139] | 139 |
| Main-thread SQL | 0 | 0 [0–0] | 0 |

The candidate passed all 24 fresh-detail checks with no observer errors. Every cold/warm burst had zero retry sleeps, eight stat calls, and four realpath calls. That removes all warm retry wakeups and cuts median filesystem preparation by 75% and 87.5%, respectively. The run captured 29 CPU profiles on each side, covering every observed Gateway thread; profiles are attribution evidence, not calibrated CPU-time or latency measurements.

Across the five warm bursts, cost-origin SQL was 66 [66–68] → 63 [63–68] and cost-origin worker requests 18 [16–19] → 16 [14–19]. Shared exact-entry reads were 30 [25–34] → 25 [22–28], cache-entry reads 19 [19–21] → 18 [18–21], and transcript-event reads 53 [48–65] → 43 [34–64]. None increased. The broader SQL/request totals include concurrent background work, so the lower totals are non-regression evidence rather than an attributed SQL saving. The removed busy attempts themselves perform no SQL or worker dispatch.

## Evidence

The focused regressions fail on unchanged production at the intended boundaries: a durable waiter returns busy instead of remaining cancellable, a cross-session waiter misses its requested fresh detail, and a memory waiter returns busy after incumbent failure. All seven owner suites passed 133 tests: 128 infra tests and five Gateway lifecycle tests. The worker fixture now closes the shared runtime in `finally`; its final test-only lint repair leaves production byte-identical to the previously reviewed head.

Identity coverage verifies existing-file replacement and revocation rejection, rejection of a retargeted missing-store directory alias without creating either target, and allowed first-store creation. The additional cleanup regression is red on the preceding owner: after real execution release followed by an injected close error, the waiter cannot acquire its writer. The repaired owner lets it write fresh detail and preserves its ownership when predecessor cleanup is retried. All seven focused cleanup/cancellation cases passed.

Two isolated Codex full-change review rounds were completed. The first found the preparation-time file-identity regression; that was repaired, and the second was scoped-clean at P0–P2. The separately authorized cleanup-delta review was also scoped-clean at P0–P2. The unchanged paths retain the full-change review coverage.

[Exact-head CI run 40146283242](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146283242) completed successfully for `8c68db484ac99451c631bafc75cf730b1c822304`, including all 25 static gates, nine Node test shards, both browser shards, and the final CI gate. This includes [production types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146283242/job/121028752031), [the repaired core lint stripe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146283242/job/121028752071), [architecture checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146283242/job/121028584067) with zero Madge cycles and passing Kysely guardrails, and [source contracts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146283242/job/121028584113) covering export collisions, session-accessor and SQLite transaction boundaries, and the sessions schema.

Independent Knip 6.40.0 comparison completed successfully in all three scopes: production 70 → 70, full tree 83 → 83, scripts 1,136 → 1,136. Finding sets are identical, with zero new or removed findings and no setup or resolution errors. The controller restored the exact committed source and verified a clean worktree.

PostgreSQL review approved the exact head `8c68db484ac99451c631bafc75cf730b1c822304`: production is byte-identical to the previously reviewed head; the final delta only repairs the worker-test cleanup.

## Overlapping Work

The final-head merge-tree comparison against base `285f5be610fa` adds no conflicts for #182156 (the same one pre-existing path/region), #167275 (clean), or #157922 (the same four pre-existing paths/regions). The aggregation call shape preserves #157922's end-date insertion point. The #132396 overlap is explicitly accepted: its one existing conflict region becomes two because this PR removes the busy-retry loop that it caps. Thanks to @SebTardif for identifying the busy-wait problem.

prs.title: perf(facetime): wake hangup when call registration completes
prs.body:
## Outcome: closed without merging

The registry-only notification candidate is rejected. The real Gateway workload found an added native helper cancellation command in every delayed-alias sample. The acceptance rule requires stopping on a worsened operation count; the gain in polling does not justify ignoring that result.

The underlying polling opportunity remains: an operator hangup can arrive after native dial acknowledgement but before the asynchronous status handler has registered the call or its alias. The existing bounded loop checks every 250 ms. This candidate made the call registry settle waiters on create/alias publication, with the existing 2,750 ms deadline.

## Measured result

The committed opt-in workload in `extensions/facetime/tests/runtime-authority-boundary.test.ts` exercised actual plugin discovery/registration, an isolated authenticated Gateway WebSocket, keyed SQLite and signed synthetic helper TCP. Native/device effects were guarded. Baseline and candidate each completed 18/18 waits: one first prepared wait and five warm waits for each case. First-wait is not process-cold. For the counters below, median = p95 = min = max in both the first-wait and warm groups.

| Case | Registry lookups, base → candidate | Timer allocations | Timer callbacks | Helper commands |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Delayed call | 4 → 3 | 1 → 1 | 1 → 0 | 5 → 4 |
| Delayed alias | 4 → 3 | 1 → 1 | 1 → 0 | 6 → 6 |
| No frame | 13 → 2 | 11 → 1 | 11 → 1 | 0 → 0 |

The delayed-alias total hides a real adverse cell: `safety-mute` falls 3 → 2 but **`cancel-outgoing-call` rises 0 → 1 in every sample**. `leave-call` remains 1 and `inspect-call` remains 2. This is a deterministic change in action ordering, not measurement spread.

Observed full-invocation SQL/request/MAIN counts were 158/645/118 → 157/644/117. Native SQL coverage under Bun is incomplete; these are not complete all-thread totals or a SQL saving claim. The host did not qualify for timing within the allotted hour. No latency or CPU-speedup claim is made. Two Node profiling attempts failed during setup before waits; neither is proof. Further profiling and static repair work stopped when the adverse counter was attributed.

## Why the registry alone cannot own readiness

`handleCallEvent` retains an existing call's aliases before `authorizePendingDial` awaits persistence. Immediate registry notification lets hangup mark that same pending dial as cancelling. The resumed authorization check correctly sends cancellation, adding the command measured above. Removing that check would weaken a real authority boundary.

Publishing only after the entire handler settles is also wrong: active-call handling can await talk/media startup, which hangup must be able to abort. A follow-up needs an explicit event-owner readiness point after authorization/persistence and before carrier/media awaits, while retaining termination and alias behavior. That is a broader contract change than this registry-only optimization. No timer deferral, generation, or weakened safety check was added to hide it.

The candidate had 64 passing focused tests across seven files, including alias-arrival regression, cancellation, timeout and stop behavior, and two completed isolated reviews. Those checks did not detect the new interleaving; the real-flow counters did. CI run 40149487566 also reported fixture lint/type/boundary failures. Those are not claimed inherited or repaired, and the branch is not ready to merge. The production proposal adds 23 net lines (39 added, 16 removed). No SQL/schema/public SDK/config changes are included.

## Acceptance rule — preregistration before first run


Run the opt-in committed workload in `extensions/facetime/tests/runtime-authority-boundary.test.ts` through the repo launcher and database-worker config. It must exercise configured FaceTime plugin discovery/source acquisition, actual plugin registration, a real isolated Gateway WebSocket, real keyed SQLite and authenticated synthetic helper TCP. Only native artifacts, endpoint, supervisor injection and media/device effects are substituted, and native command/spawn guards must remain unused. All fixtures and identifiers are synthetic.

Three cases: dial acknowledged without a UUID followed by a delayed signed ringing frame; an existing call acquiring a delayed alias; and no status frame. Six sequential samples per case separate the first prepared wait from five warm waits; first-wait is not process-cold. Baseline no-frame expectation: 13 registry lookups and 11 periodic timers/fires per wait; candidate: two lookups, one deadline timer/fire and zero periodic timers. Delayed registration/alias must remove timer-driven wakeups while preserving successful hangup. Record helper commands and all SQL/worker requests/MAIN by phase. No added touched-owner SQL/request work or lost cancellation/deadline behavior is accepted.

Counts and per-thread Node CPU profiles are distinct from timing. Normal behavior/count runs use pinned Bun. The profile-only Node exception is recorded in campaign notes before execution. No latency or calibrated CPU-saving claim is allowed on the loaded local host. Any timing comparison requires the campaign mkdir lock, load below 24, interleaved baseline/candidate samples (at least five each), separate cold/warm results, median/p95/range, and a stop for any 20% worsening. If qualification exceeds 60 minutes, report counts/profile evidence and mark latency unmeasured.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This stack consolidates repeated internal implementations across independently revertible cuts. It does not remove features, change public text, add SDK contracts, or change configuration, protocol, dependencies, schemas, or persistence policy. Plugins stay within their own owners and existing SDK contracts. The Phase E standalone memory backend and its factory, registry, expiry, federation, and tests are untouched.

The measured-clone inventory remains open. This is not a claim that all structurally similar code can share an implementation.

## Gateway response construction

Use the existing private `respondError` owner across 47 Gateway handler modules instead of repeatedly constructing the same negative response envelope. Its optional options argument uses the canonical `Parameters<typeof errorShape>[2]` type and forwards existing details/retry metadata unchanged. No second error schema, validator, wrapper framework, or public export is introduced.

All guards, live-authority checks, effect/settlement boundaries, messages, codes, argument evaluation, and synchronous callback delivery remain. Receiver-bound calls, separate fourth-argument response metadata, prebuilt/mapped errors, and computed success/payload responses remain separate. This is the owner-plus-first-Gateway-area slice; further callers can migrate independently.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none newly introduced; the ordinary helper stack frame is already present for existing callers. New imports reach the existing owner's logging/error dependencies; no cold-start or performance improvement is claimed.

## Plugin-local defaults and results

Comfy shares capability defaults within its plugin, FaceTime shares command-action construction within its setup owner, and file transfer uses the existing SDK text-result helper. OpenAI shares pure browser-readiness preparation while keeping separate synchronous/asynchronous auth resolvers and the existing synchronous compatibility deadline.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: a pure OpenAI subscription-model classifier may run before successful platform-auth detection; no credential resolution, permission check, or external effect moves. All default values, setup commands, result text, and capability decisions stay.

## Prepared OpenRouter media facts

Reuse prepared image configuration and the existing base64 decoder, and consume the already normalized video URL. External validation, byte limits, credential stripping, fallback, and provider/model selection remain.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none. This is not a live-provider or billing claim.

## ACP location selection

Use the existing parsed-field selector and remove the repeated location-key membership check already guaranteed by the preceding same-path loop. Keep untrusted location normalization, caps, alias precedence, and insertion order.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; the admitted location domain and existing behavior remain protected.

## CLI and agent-tree grouping

Use the existing record-grouping owner for update-finalization child processes and agent-list trees. Keep ancestry traversal, root selection, ordering, and distinct parent/agent identities.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: an unused private undefined grouping bucket may be constructed. No process-control or authorization behavior changes.

## Catalog expiry arithmetic

Admit positive-safe TTL once, then use arithmetic expiry. Keep pending budget/provider identity, cancellation, settlement, full TTL after success, the 100-entry bound, and close-only lifecycle.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: artificial noninteger, nonfinite, or out-of-Date-range clocks and enormous positive-safe TTLs now cache arithmetically instead of bypassing. Introducing #174361 concerns retention/diagnostics, not a cited human clock-overflow incident; normal 30s/60s/5m/24h durations and #168356's real timeout protection remain. Only tests of the superseded artificial-clock policy change; kept behavior remains covered.

## Previous-head CI attribution and withdrawals

Previous exact head `8d77ba6e66c86f2dce097870601662cdb352df79`, CI run 40136707024, had six failing leaves. Its aggregate ci-gate was a genuine failure, not the unrelated-head misfire.

| Leaf | Attribution and repair |
| --- | --- |
| check-test-types-core-4 | Our two UI grouping changes hit the core test graph's library types. All changed UI paths are now withdrawn. |
| checks-node-compact-small-1 | Our SSH helper extraction violated the eager-import closure. Both changed SSH owners are now withdrawn. |
| checks-node-changed-compact-large-24-1 | Bundled-plugin reload tests expected stale receipts. The bundled lifecycle assertion now matches `restartRequired: true`. Main's subsequent #182962 deliberately converted the channel hot-handoff fixture to a non-bundled plugin; its `restartRequired: false` assertion is preserved unchanged from current main. |
| checks-node-changed-1 | QA control-plane setup timeout. One serial corrected-head/base comparison passed all five cases on both sides, so attribution remained inconclusive. Withdraw all 43 changed production files reachable from the failing test, their associated test changes, and the one necessary outside allocator dependency repair. |
| checks-ui-e2e (4/9) | Mobile chat-motion viewport-Y assertion. The selected case passed on both sides in the same serial comparison; that is not a fix or inherited-failure proof. Withdraw all 13 changed UI files reachable through the browser entry, including dynamic imports. |
| PostgreSQL conformance (2/3) | Inherited missing `standalone-runtime-profile.mjs` in the unchanged reduced-runtime test fixture. A narrow fixture diagnostic reproduces it, and scheduled main run 40138789542 at `87f00b1b5254861d944e524cdd8bb3a65f53b59f`, job 121006161355, independently fails with the same seven PTY/module-loading signatures. |

The union is 66 withdrawn paths, not a whole-PR rollback. Their source is preserved on `deslop/z33-parked-ci-reachable-20261015` at `0f783fb01c5213676b3590136522e569b0ea5d12` without a PR. Eight existing tests were restored when their mechanisms returned; orphaned new helper tests disappeared with those helpers. Neither unknown failure is being waived. The comparison's four test commands exited zero, while its remote wrapper subsequently returned an infrastructure error; these are separate facts. The owned lease was stopped and cleanup reconciled.

## Inherited local catalog test discrepancy

The existing `session-catalog.test.ts` case "keeps a delayed source off the catalog RPC path" fails on this candidate and on clean current main `c2d4264f2e1807bec2f75f1af4d98d71e714b59d`. Both receive a successful host with `sessions: []`, `pending: true`, and `requiresFreshList: true`, while the test expects `error.code: CATALOG_LOADING`. Merged #182242 intentionally introduced the fresh-list pending response; this older Gateway assertion was not updated. The test, fixture helper, and Session Share producer are byte-identical to this PR's original base.

The main replay ran only that case, with 14 other cases name-filtered, in a clean checkout with frozen dependencies and isolated state. It reproduced the same assertion, not a timeout. No test or freshness/security protection was changed. This is an investigated inherited local failure, not a passing test or a waiver for any other exact-head CI failure.

## Exact-head CI attribution

Head `c9c434e9db6857a98653a1a540010f49dafa485f`, CI run [40147249175](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40147249175), attempt 1, has four completed failing Node leaves. All observed cases and error signatures also fail in scheduled main [40142877272](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142877272) at `085076cc8f76c05b58166f85d792d851ac6c6d68`; these are signature comparisons, not shard-name matches.

| Exact-head failing job | Failure and main evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 121031520577, compact-small-3-1 | Delayed-source case expects `CATALOG_LOADING` instead of the pending host introduced by #182242. Main job 121018202179 has the same assertion; the isolated clean-main reproduction above independently confirms it. |
| 121031520648, compact-large-8-1 | Ten budget cases and two reconnect-retention cases use partial fake clients without required `connect`; `client?.connect.scopes` throws. Main jobs 121018202129 and 121018202331 have the same cases/errors, including derivative unhandled errors. |
| 121031520688, compact-small-19-2 | Coalesced phase-diagnostics followers never reach the provider with their invalid fake client and time out at 120000 ms. Main job 121018202129 has the identical case/signature. |
| 121031520659, compact-large-25-1 | Fifteen catalog-progress cases fail with missing `connect.scopes`, the resulting missing host/publication, 3-call versus 2-call assertion, and derivative timeouts/unhandled errors. Main job 121018202099 has the same cases and signatures. |

All five failed test files, the fixture/helper, and the visibility owner are byte-identical between scheduled main, the CI main baseline, and the actual tested merge. The plugin catalog owner is byte-identical between the CI baseline and tested merge; its intervening main-only adopted-session allocation optimization was inspected separately and is not claimed byte-identical to scheduled main. This PR changes only invalid-request response construction in the catalog handlers, not client admission, visibility, provider invocation, or fresh-list behavior; the expanded AST-equivalence check covers those handlers. No defensive production guard is restored to accommodate invalid internal test fixtures.

The actual tested merge is `f04faa8541a390cc6eed66a1e90e8397962d242f`, with ordered parents `479431cbdc53b89b0dc290c575f13aee791d9f08` and this exact head; its tree was independently reconstructed. The coordinator flake list and the last six completed scheduled main runs were checked. All 99 CI jobs are terminal: these four catalog leaves and downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` job 121036318419 fail; every other selected product job passes, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. No cancelled CI suite or missing product-job proof is waived. The gate log identifies the Node-test category as the sole failed category. This PR is being submitted through the native inherited-failure exception under standing scoped landing authority, not relabeled green. Exact-head `security-fast` and lint/type jobs pass; Security Review publisher 40148999245 explicitly enforces PR 182958/head `c9c434…`/CI attempt 1 successfully.

The separate PR-context check rejected the previous body because its descriptive headings did not match the required `What Problem This Solves` and `Evidence` headings. Those headings are corrected here; this was a body-format error, not an inherited product failure. Subsequent exact-head PR-context jobs 121035452029 and 121035646939 pass. Cancelled Auto response/dispatch runs and the older PR-context run are superseded automation, not product proof, and are not relabeled passing.

## Conflict resolution

The previous response head could not produce a merge ref because GitHub reported it conflicting. The surviving stack was coalesced with an independently identical tree, then rebased onto main `6113057491a29b36239ae8f9400617fb1e47729a`. After the one-line lifecycle repair below, the repaired head is `c9c434e9db6857a98653a1a540010f49dafa485f`.

The one textual conflict preserves main's optional `scopes.includes(ADMIN_SCOPE)` predicate and only delegates the error envelope beneath it. Automatic overlaps preserve main's OpenAI transcription options, device/session scope defaults, and lifecycle fixture changes. The first focused lifecycle replay caught our obsolete `true` assertion over #182962's now-external fixture; that one-line hunk was withdrawn, returning the complete channel test file to current main. No production code, assertions for bundled behavior, timeouts, or handoff coverage were weakened. The post-rebase AST comparison again verifies all 47 response handler bodies against main after expanding the helper, with unrelated imports unchanged and no withdrawn or Phase E paths reintroduced. This is source-equivalence evidence, not hosted CI.

## Evidence

Whole candidate: **891 additions / 1,405 deletions = 514 net lines removed**, 63 files. Production: **846 additions / 1,378 deletions = 532 net lines removed**, 58 files. This repaired existing PR remains above the campaign's 500-line floor. No meaningful tests were deleted to reach it.

The 66-path withdrawal is signed, independently reviewed clean at P0–P2, and verified byte-identical to the original PR base. Its 14 suppression-policy tests pass. The new response batch's AST check expands helper calls back to the original form and verifies every handler's non-import AST and unrelated imports; that is source equivalence, not product-test proof. Existing per-cut proof for the retained provider/ACP/grouping/cache changes is unchanged-input evidence, not a claim to have rerun all of it.

Final frozen response proof: format, targeted native typecheck, and typed lint passed (48 files; zero lint warnings/errors). The primary owner/consumer suites passed 773 cases with 20 unchanged platform skips, apart from the single catalog failure reproduced on clean main above. The selected wake cases passed 13 cases (130 unrelated cases name-filtered), and the rich-response/authority suites passed 20 cases. Suppression policy passed all 14 cases; wrapper source closure passed all three. Runtime value cycles and static Madge cycles are both zero. Fresh isolated P0–P2 review found no actionable findings. Final source/input/log hashes were verified unchanged, and isolated proof scratch directories were removed.

No local whole-graph typecheck, broad suite, build, E2E, live deployment, or live-provider/billing claim. PR CI on the repaired exact head is the broad gate; prior-head security/CI evidence does not replace it. No retries, timeouts, skips, suppressions, or baselines were relaxed.

Post-rebase focused proof passed formatting, the targeted 49-source native type graph, typed lint on the four overlapping paths, 49 Gateway owner/scope cases, the selected public permissions case (six unrelated cases name-filtered), and 48 OpenAI browser-auth/routing cases. The corrected lifecycle file passed all three cases (189.89 seconds under current host load). The resumed policy checks passed 14 suppression cases and three wrapper-closure cases; runtime and static cycles remain zero. The first lifecycle failure is retained as a repaired stale expectation, not called inherited or green. A fresh isolated review of the one-line exact-main restoration found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Source/input/log hashes were rechecked and both proof scratch directories removed. Unchanged production proof and review are reused; the inherited catalog failure above remains explicit.

Rejected two findings after inspecting the named remaining owners: `extensions/signal/src/monitor/access-policy.test.ts` tests a phone-primary sender's UUID alias in positive pairing/group authorization and unrelated-UUID denial cases; `src/channels/plugins/contracts/plugin-shape.contract.test.ts` explicitly invokes Signal's outbound sanitizer with hidden tool/reasoning scaffolding and an independent visible-only expected result. Neither proof was removed by this batch.

Hosted run 40137293748 caught batch-caused static issues: `totalTokensVersion` widened from literal `1` in the shared status fixture, a generic selector wrapper failed type-aware lint, the hello fixture omitted required protocol facts, the inferred RPC mock return excluded pagination, and the resolved Signal target's optional source needed validation. Follow-ups contextually type the usage fixture, bind the native DOM selector, provide the complete hello shape, keep unknown RPC responses at their boundary, and require the actual target source.

That run also caught an invalid newly added loading-state assertion in the channel-disposal row. The existing disposal contract retires read receipts without republishing presentation state. All pre-existing disposal assertions remain; the new loading-state assertion applies only to live scope changes. No production contract or assertion on real disposal behavior was weakened. Plain local lint, format, and diff checks passed; fresh-head hosted CI is the verification gate, with no local typecheck or test execution.

Accepted the repository review's status-composition concern: restored the original host-thread SQL observer around both transcript hydration calls and the no-extra-read assertion after committed usage becomes available.
