prs.title: fix(sandbox): toolchain scratch blocks workspace recovery
prs.body:
Related: #182039

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes sandbox preparation and restart recovery getting stuck when a downloaded toolchain or browser under `.openclaw/tmp/` exceeds the 64 MiB workspace-result file limit. Every later preparation retries the same unsynchronizable scratch file.

## User Impact

Checkout-root `.openclaw/tmp/` now stays with the runtime that created it. Commands can continue reading their scratch files locally; ordinary edits synchronize and pending results can settle. Save durable outputs outside this scratch directory. Other `.openclaw` content, adjacent names, and nested project fixtures still synchronize.

User-file size limits and explicit administrator recovery remain unchanged. Exact actionable recovery guidance for genuine oversized user files is owned by the separate existing PR #182039; this PR does not duplicate its error handling or automatically move user data.

## Why This Change Was Made

One entry in the existing canonical runtime-owned exclusion list applies to host capture, serialized remote capture, rsync, reconciliation and historical result recovery. No new cache, state, configuration, schema, or retry mechanism is needed. Production LOC: +1/-1 (net zero); the change removes scratch traversal, hashing and transfer work rather than adding a second path.

## Evidence

- Red on base `4c3bf18daa6c2267aac8c0175d82ce0eed01b9c1`: the capture regression included excluded scratch, and the isolated workspace owner rejected a 100 MiB synthetic Node toolchain with `Cloud workspace result is too large`.
- Green: the same 100 MiB scratch payload contributes zero result payload bytes; source edits synchronize, both runtimes retain their own scratch, restart preparation succeeds and pending custody clears. Older staged result fixtures also include scratch and recover without copying it.
- Focused tests: `workspace-generated-paths.test.ts`, `local-workspace-projection.test.ts`, and `server-methods/worktrees.test.ts`: 48 passed, two environment-specific skips (opt-in Podman and non-UTF-8 filenames), 118.36 s wall including compiler preparation. After consolidating the scratch regression into the existing recovery fixture to respect the file-size lint gate, the three affected recovery cases passed again (51.30 s wall including compilation; individual cases 6.71 s, 2.63 s, 2.74 s).
- The real isolated Gateway recovery-authority test passed: write-only, revoked, replaced-session and rebound-worktree callers cannot move files; the current administrator preserves file bytes and source edits.
- Changed-file formatting and lint, `pnpm tsgo:core` (native tsrs), two-file docs MDX validation, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The configured helper refused its provider route before inference; operator configuration was preserved.
- No Testbox lease, production mutation, live provider call, or production load test. This is a correctness repair with a deterministic removed-work count, not a latency/GC performance claim. PR CI supplies broad validation.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent and auto-reply tests repeat gate waits, fresh data builders, real-session setup and cleanup tails across independent scenarios. This residue consolidates those fixtures onto their existing owners without merging scenarios or removing expectations.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change or operator action. Production code, security boundaries, ordinary write settlement, public contracts and persisted shapes are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each retained cut below removes duplicate test setup. Actual admission, registry publication, native FIFO writes, transport execution and cleanup joins remain at their original boundaries. A small pure Promise-only support leaf owns the existing settlement observer; its callers retain native promise identity and installation timing.

## Size and preservation

45 paths; **300 additions / 449 deletions = 149 net test/support lines removed; production 0**. This is the authorized final 100+ residue allowance, not a LARGE stack. Base: 3f7b7765585ddcd72822d8b4e43ef928d23eecf7.

Whole-file union: **2352 → 2352 assertion expressions; 420 → 420 test/suite/hook registrations; 52 → 52 module-mock targets; 12 → 12 onTestFinished registrations**. Every case, ordered parameter row and expectation remains. These are static call-site inventories, not expanded runtime execution counts. Per-cut whole-file counts overlap and must not be added together. Strict preservation compares ordered assertion/registration/mock ASTs, with only six exact boolean-getter expansions and two exact four-row table-factory expansions. Fresh stores, promises, arrays, nested origins and own undefined fields stay fresh.

The newly opened test-LOC PR #182907 owns subagent-spawn.production-boundary.test.ts. This PR excludes that file completely; its one-line gate consolidation was dropped after the focused run. The remaining 45 files remain byte-identical to the reviewed/tested candidate. Preservation totals decrease only because the unchanged excluded file is no longer in the changed-file union, not because any assertion or registration was removed.

The original mock-before-consumer import order in restart recovery is preserved. An author-found two-import permutation was corrected before runtime/review, with exact before/after hashes and inverse qualification; it changes no assertion or scenario.

### A. Canonical gate-before-settlement waits — 7 net lines

Eight fixed-message races across completion admission, announcement, registration authority, spawn preparation and registry lifecycle reuse existing `awaitGateBeforeSettlement`. Gate-first order, native operation identity/rejection, all diagnostic messages, the result-bearing child-session key and caller-owned release/finally joins remain. Argument-capturing timing callbacks and dynamic-result error diagnostics stay inline; landed #182835 gates are retained.

Formatted LOC: +36 / −43. Whole-file preservation: assertions 807 → 807; registrations 134 → 134; mock targets 21 → 21; cleanup registrations 9 → 9.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; the existing guard behavior is retained, not removed.

### F. Real requester-turn seeding and admission — 10 net lines

Requester-liveness support owns the duplicated real session seed followed by real reply-turn admission, including the same session ID, logical store locator, visible-turn fields and owned-status error. Each invocation performs fresh native setup. Consumers retain attachment, controller-authority scope, completion and owner-settlement joins; the fixture does not fabricate ownership or settle the operation.

Formatted LOC: +27 / −37. Whole-file preservation: assertions 78 → 78; registrations 15 → 15; mock targets 1 → 1; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: ordinary async helper completion/adoption scheduling replaces inline continuation timing; byte-identical microtask timing is not a fixture contract. Native operation ordering and caller settlement remain unchanged.

### G. Fresh native transcript targets — 6 net lines

The existing spawn production-boundary support owns the repeated transcript target object used by command, native and policy fixtures. Every call creates a fresh object with the same agent, bound parent key, session ID, entry, store path and config; entry/config remain direct references. Recorder creation, original-input/adoption assertions, input text, native reply execution and session lifecycle stay with their distinct consumers.

Formatted LOC: +18 / −24. Whole-file preservation: assertions 134 → 134; registrations 5 → 5; mock targets 0 → 0; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; no recorder or lifecycle responsibility moves into the data builder.

### H. Queued-registration listener defaults — 12 net lines

The queued-registration fixture constructs listeners synchronously with its authoritative run map and fresh callback/scheduler defaults per call. The first scenario retains its completion spy; the third retains the exact observed scheduler and does not allocate an unused scheduler. Event-handler capture, `ensure`/`reset`, pending-lifecycle cleanup and all registration sites remain local.

Formatted LOC: +19 / −31. Whole-file preservation: assertions 81 → 81; registrations 14 → 14; mock targets 1 → 1; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: one unused default async completion callback is allocated before the first scenario's explicit override replaces it; this has no observable fixture effect.

### I. Fresh ACP binding registries — 10 net lines

The existing ACP runtime fixture creates the repeated channel-binding registry for the stop-lookup and stop-test IDs. Each call allocates fresh registry/channel/plugin structures with the same test source, base plugin and current-conversation capability. Snapshot capture, active-registry publication/restoration, native bind/unbind, lookup spying, cancellation and owner-settlement behavior remain in the consumers.

Formatted LOC: +22 / −32. Whole-file preservation: assertions 78 → 78; registrations 3 → 3; mock targets 0 → 0; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; the new helper builds data only and performs no registry lifecycle operation.

### M. Shared registry-registration callback type — 12 net lines

Four registry registration drivers reuse the existing requester-completion fixture's exact property-callback type through type-only imports. Optional overrides, mutable draft records, the native `Promise<void>` and the owner's three registration arguments remain unchanged. Local aliases and runtime imports still needed by consumers remain; no runtime dependency edge or shared mutable fixture is introduced.

Formatted LOC: +16 / −28. Whole-file preservation: assertions 135 → 135; registrations 11 → 11; mock targets 0 → 0; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; this cut is erase-only typing consolidation.

### N. Existing synchronous cleanup-error owner — 12 net lines

Completion replay, the control fixture and spawn-authority fixture reuse `throwCollectedErrors` at their three original synchronous throw points. Zero errors return; a sole error, including an unknown or `undefined` value, is thrown by identity; multiple errors retain order and each original aggregate label. Every cleanup call, failure push, await, owner guard and environment restoration stays in place. Async `collectFailure` and cause-bearing `throwBoundFailures` remain separate.

Formatted LOC: +6 / −18. Whole-file preservation: assertions 25 → 25; registrations 11 → 11; mock targets 9 → 9; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

### P. Fresh private-requester route cases — 1 net line

The existing announce fixture returns the repeated four-row requester-origin table from a synchronous factory. Every invocation allocates a new array, rows and nested origins, retaining the channel-less row's own `origin: undefined` property. Both independent `it.each` registrations, titles, callbacks and every scenario/assertion remain. Expected values are still literal fixture data, not generated by production behavior.

Formatted LOC: +20 / −21. Whole-file preservation: assertions 57 → 57; registrations 16 → 16; mock targets 4 → 4; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

### L. One pure promise-settlement observer — 32 net lines

The existing Promise-only `observeSettlement` implementation moves unchanged to a pure test-support leaf and replaces the qualified inline observations. Each call owns a fresh boolean/getter; fulfilled and rejected native `.then` handlers are installed at the original points. Original promises/results, rejection observation and cleanup joins remain; no await, `finally`, `catch` or adoption layer is added. Accepted-stop retains #182835's independent claim/cleanup gates. The held image-tool observer is excluded.

Formatted LOC: +28 / −60. Whole-file preservation: assertions 318 → 318; registrations 63 → 63; mock targets 0 → 0; cleanup registrations 0 → 0. Six exact getter operands use the narrow comparison described above.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; optional-promise, mutable-record, one-arm and three-state observers retain their distinct implementations.

### Q. Canonical fixed-message waits in other agent fixtures — 6 net lines

Six fixed-message gate-first waits in Code Mode swarm, catalog worker pool, CLI policy, inbound registry and app-server recovery reuse existing `awaitGateBeforeSettlement`. Each native promise, original gate, exact message, early rejection and returned parameter value remains the same. Injection/publication/worker retirement/resource assertions and original finish/release/finally joins stay inline; no timeout or retry is introduced.

Formatted LOC: +29 / −35. Whole-file preservation: assertions 356 → 356; registrations 73 → 73; mock targets 6 → 6; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; these retain the existing wait guard rather than remove it.

### T. Canonical pricing-shutdown entered gate — 3 net lines

Remote-publication's void pricing hold uses the existing fresh entered-gate owner. The async callback still resolves entry, waits for release and returns void; it stays in the same `mockImplementation` slot, not `mockImplementationOnce`. Native adoption/start/shutdown expectations, finally release and pricing-spy restoration remain unchanged.

Formatted LOC: +5 / −8. Whole-file preservation: assertions 35 → 35; registrations 9 → 9; mock targets 0 → 0; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; the direct canonical callback ignores the same unused arguments and adds no wrapper.

### V. Canonical patch-context temporary directory — 9 net lines

Patch-context byte tests reuse the existing temp-directory owner with the exact `openclaw-patch-context-` prefix. Every call still creates a fresh directory, returns/awaits the callback result and awaits recursive cleanup in `finally`, preserving creation, cleanup and error ordering. All filesystem bytes, assertions and scenarios remain; filesystem/path imports still required by them stay.

Formatted LOC: +2 / −11. Whole-file preservation: assertions 14 → 14; registrations 8 → 8; mock targets 0 → 0; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; only the duplicate local lifecycle helper is removed.

### Resident microfamily: map seed and rollback — 4 net lines

Two lifecycle scenarios share the synchronous resident-map seed operation. Each call captures its own previous row, installs the same entry and returns a fresh rollback closure; both original caller-owned `onTestFinished` registrations remain at their original sites. Rollback still restores a truthy prior row or deletes an originally absent entry, with the same map/entry references.

Formatted LOC: +14 / −18. Whole-file preservation: assertions 606 → 606; registrations 115 → 115; mock targets 12 → 12; cleanup registrations 6 → 6.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; cleanup registration and per-call capture are retained, not centralized into hidden hooks.

### Yielded microfamily: pending handoff data — 5 net lines

Two lifecycle scenarios reuse a fresh `createRunEntry` builder containing exactly endedAt 4,000, required completion and the pending wake's status/attempt/yield/generation fields. Both scenarios retain their different Gateway/custody/exhaustion operations and assertions. The factory never performs a controller, receipt or settlement action and does not share the wake object between calls.

Formatted LOC: +15 / −20. Whole-file preservation: assertions 606 → 606; registrations 115 → 115; mock targets 12 → 12; cleanup registrations 6 → 6.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; this is fresh literal data reuse, not owner-policy consolidation.

### Suppressed microfamily: delivery-result data — 2 net lines

Two lifecycle scenarios reuse a synchronous fresh six-field suppressed-result object. Both original awaited optional `onDeliveryResult` calls, their `vi.fn` versus inline callback shapes, return values and call-count oracles remain. The direct/false/suppression reason/error/terminal/disposition values are unchanged; no async emitter wrapper is introduced.

Formatted LOC: +14 / −16. Whole-file preservation: assertions 606 → 606; registrations 115 → 115; mock targets 12 → 12; cleanup registrations 6 → 6.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; callback scheduling and suppression semantics remain caller-owned.

### Replay microfamily: collector input data — 5 net lines

Two real spawn calls reuse a synchronous builder for the exact five-field replay input, including task, collect/group settings, replay key and request fingerprint. Each call receives a fresh object rather than a shared constant. Distinct requester contexts, actual spawn operations and generated-ID comparisons remain unchanged.

Formatted LOC: +15 / −20. Whole-file preservation: assertions 132 → 132; registrations 34 → 34; mock targets 0 → 0; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; replay identity/ownership behavior and both scenarios remain covered.

### N extension: two additional cleanup-error tails — 6 net lines

Persistence and restart-recovery fixtures reuse the same existing synchronous error owner at two sites distinct from N's three. Their exact persistence/restart aggregate labels and original throw placement remain; zero/sole unknown-or-undefined identity and ordered multiple-error behavior are retained. Cleanup operations, awaits, restoration and failure accumulation stay local and in order.

Formatted LOC: +5 / −11. Whole-file preservation: assertions 3 → 3; registrations 5 → 5; mock targets 3 → 3; cleanup registrations 0 → 0.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: aggregate construction gains the ordinary shared-helper stack frame, as in N; no failure is suppressed or newly wrapped.

### Former-held K: replacement and sweeper cleanup gates — 7 net lines

Task-replacement and sweeper-recovery use a fresh canonical entered/release pair at each original allocation point. Sweeper allocation remains outside its conditional; only the original branch installs/waits/releases the gate. Direct callbacks, existing waits, finally releases, pending joins and fixture-settlement operations stay intact. The newly orphaned sweeper deferred import is removed; no scenario or lifecycle mechanism is deleted.

Formatted LOC: +10 / −17. Whole-file preservation: assertions 127 → 127; registrations 30 → 30; mock targets 7 → 7; cleanup registrations 3 → 3.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: none; no async wrapper, shared gate, timer or altered settlement ownership is introduced.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

Only the per-cut fixture details above: ordinary async helper adoption scheduling, one inert default callback allocation before override, and a shared-helper AggregateError stack frame. No authorization check, durability mechanism, native FIFO operation, cleanup call, error identity or write-settlement obligation is removed. No new suppression, skip, retry, timeout, ignore or baseline relaxation.

## Evidence

Focused ordinary runtime ran serially through the repository wrapper with nice -n 10 and --maxWorkers=1, under task-owned HOME/OpenClaw/XDG directories: **1277 passed, 0 failed, 0 pending**, across the 46 selected ordinary entrypoints, including the required run/attempt driver and 14-test suppression guard; 2438.971s wall time.

All five touched test graphs (agents-root, agents-other, agents-tools, agents-sessions, messaging), touched lint/format, routing dry-run, runtime cycles 0, Madge cycles 0 and line-cap passed. The existing slow integration files retain real worker replacement, native FIFO writes, admitted session authority, persistence and shutdown/cleanup boundaries. Those are the contracts under test, not fixture allocation assertions; replacing them with mocks would miss the owner/lifecycle behavior. This change adds no test or timeout, and makes no runtime-speed claim.

Fresh post-drop 72-hour collision qualification inspected30test-title and11refactor-title openPRs: no test-LOC campaign overlap across the remaining45paths. The ordinary lifecycle-lock repair137014 is not a test-LOC campaign; its shared tests retain their repair behavior. The peer-owned file remains excluded as described above. The separate open auth/CLI/reply fixture stack is file-disjoint.

Three broad consumers of unchanged ACP exports were not expanded locally: dispatch-acp.test-support.ts, dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test-support.ts and dispatch-from-config.test-support.ts. No local full suite, build, live-provider or E2E run is claimed. Native preflight selected no runtime build. Current head: 31c99de75363b1a542fa4f29d80eeba3fd69326d. Previous head b0dad03d10939983fee17f13f39146cf50d9698f failed [CI40135789934](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40135789934) in two real test jobs. prs.title: perf(infra): reduce worker CPU sampling allocations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Periodic Gateway worker CPU sampling allocates a fresh async frame and its reactions for every worker, even when the native counter read succeeds normally.

## User Impact

Lower allocation while collecting the same CPU counters. Sampling remains once per second when active and once per ten seconds when idle; CPU rates, the residual, unavailable-counter behavior, and the 100 ms sample budget are unchanged. There is no configuration or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each tracked worker now owns reusable fulfillment/rejection reactions. This replaces the async/await/finally wrapper while keeping its one-outstanding-native-request bound and synchronous-throw/rejection recovery. Skipping workers based on task or message activity would miss independent timer/native work; no such inference is introduced.

Production delta: **+10/−6, net +4 lines**. The four-line growth retains native failure handling and pending-request ownership while moving transient async machinery to two worker-lifetime callbacks. The added measurement driver exercises real registered native workers and documents its scope.

## Evidence

Predeclared acceptance: at least 10% lower allocation per fixed sampling batch, equivalent counter availability and existing lifecycle contracts, and no material adverse CPU/GC/tail result. Baseline owner is main `803ad1fdc36e`; both sides use the same new driver and dependencies. Each process creates 50 idle native workers, warms 100 batches, then measures 5,000 batches with 1 ms yields. One batch performs 50 native reads; all measured reads returned counters. Allocation, untraced timing/GC, and traced promotion use separate passes.

Concurrent local pairs on Node 26.12.1/macOS arm64, synchronized to a shared future start, with launch order reversed in pair two. Both Linux quiet slots remained occupied, so these are local paired results without CPU affinity, not quiet Linux or whole-Gateway performance claims. A predeclared third timing pair resolves mixed-sign CPU/GC deltas. Timing-start skews were −1.09, −0.40, and +3.45 ms.

| Metric | Pair 1 before → after | Pair 2 before → after | Pair 3 before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sampled bytes/batch | 67,174.5 → 49,634.0 | 66,844.7 → 50,235.2 | — |
| Main CPU ms/batch, untraced | 0.61123 → 0.60789 | 0.60575 → 0.60849 | 0.53456 → 0.52772 |
| Process CPU ms/batch, untraced | 2.63071 → 2.61126 | 2.69747 → 2.71952 | 2.17967 → 2.17448 |
| Total GC ms / 5,000 batches, untraced | 31.396 → 12.611 | 19.340 → 20.469 | 14.562 → 13.702 |
| Promoted bytes/batch, separate traced pass | 977.23 → 918.08 | 972.72 → 918.60 | — |
| Batch latency p95 ms (5,000/side) | 4.607 → 4.726 | 3.141 → 3.509 | 2.949 → 3.009 |
| Batch latency p99 ms (5,000/side) | 12.763 → 12.939 | 7.480 → 8.452 | 6.531 → 6.516 |
| Maximum batch latency ms (5,000/side) | 49.727 → 57.923 | 123.447 → 120.697 | 37.984 → 30.868 |
| Maximum single GC pause ms, untraced | 3.495 → 1.243 | 2.351 → 6.029 | 1.167 → 3.984 |
| Minor GC collections | 71 → 33 | 61 → 33 | 54 → 33 |
| Minor GC total ms | 30.743 → 11.290 | 18.139 → 18.608 | 13.303 → 12.264 |
| Major GC collections | 1 → 1 | 1 → 1 | 1 → 1 |
| Major GC total/max ms | 0.541 → 1.225 | 1.093 → 1.656 | 1.167 → 1.343 |
| Event-loop p99 ms (samples before/after) | 41.878 → 46.236 (736/747) | 36.307 → 38.175 (634/657) | 36.241 → 36.012 (651/652) |
| Maximum event-loop delay ms | 181.273 → 169.214 | 100.925 → 102.302 | 55.673 → 56.754 |

Mean allocation falls **25.48%**, or **17,075 bytes/batch**. At 50 workers and one batch/second this projects to about 1.02 MB/min less main-isolate allocation; this is a cadence projection, not a measured whole-Gateway saving. Main CPU changes −0.00248 ms/batch (−0.42%) and process CPU −0.00086 ms/batch (−0.03%): effectively unchanged. Promotion falls about 5.8%. Mean batch p99 increases 0.378 ms; p95 increases 0.183 ms, both below the predeclared 1 ms materiality threshold. GC improves overall; the adverse second-pair total is only +0.000226 ms/batch. All candidate GC maxima remain below 50 ms. Event-loop p99 and GC pause percentiles are context only because counts are below their 1,000/200-sample gates; major GC is also below 50 collections per side. No adverse GC/promotion/max-pause rejection was invoked, so A/A rejection controls were not needed.

Reproduce each side from its source with:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worker-cpu-measure.ts \
  --workers 50 --batches 5000 --yield-ms 1 --start-at <shared-epoch-ms> \
  --output <fresh-result.json>
```

Add `--allocations` for the separate collected-object pass; use Node's `--trace-gc-nvp` separately for promotion. Promotion totals include only main-thread trace records between the committed driver's start/end markers. The benchmark artifact-reservation repair is outside the measured window; it preserves existing result/profile pairs on a repeated output path.

Validation:

- Broad PR CI [40134414841](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40134414841) and the required aggregate gate **passed** on exact head `68a1adeded83e2c06451f9dc3e724a904516c70a`. The automated Codex review on that head also completed with no findings.

- Existing worker CPU and Gateway sampling tests: **52 passed** in three focused files, 86.21 s wrapper wall time. Recordings previously read and base64-encoded the whole MP4 without applying the runtime's existing 25 MiB frame budget. They share the existing snapshot projection and keep the existing deferred cleanup.

The regression now checks both the exact raw ceiling, where the envelope causes overflow, and one byte above it, where the early file-size guard rejects the recording. A nearby snapshot assertion uses `#require` instead of a force unwrap to satisfy the current formatter.

## Evidence

- Final regression on baseline `f31072518010` (whose runtime matches integrated main): both 19,660,800-byte and 19,660,801-byte cases returned success and a payload, producing eight expected assertion failures. Tests ran with `sandbox-exec`, private home/temp/state directories, and `swift test --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --skip-build --disable-sandbox --filter MacNodeRuntimeTests`. prs.title: fix(codex): retain persisted user in agent_end observations
prs.body:
Closes #182950

## What Problem This Solves

Codex suppresses a second local transcript write when the Gateway has already persisted the admitted user request. That same suppression also removed the real user message from the current-turn `messagesSnapshot`, so `agent_end` observers received an assistant/tool-only batch even though the user's request existed in the local transcript.

This change restores the already-persisted user message only in the `agent_end` observation payload. It does not write a second transcript row, replay history, or synthesize a prompt.

## User Impact

Post-turn hooks can now associate a successful ordinary Codex turn with the real request that produced it. This removes the deterministic precondition that caused Hindsight to discard the turn before its retain request. The change is limited to the legacy suppression path where a recorder already exposes the persisted message and the native snapshot has no user message.

## Why This Change Was Made

`promptSnapshot()` returns `[]` under `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence`, and `finalizeCodexAttempt()` previously passed the resulting native snapshot directly to `runCodexAgentEndHook()`. The finalizer already trusts `getPersistedMessage()` for restart/plugin handoff, so the hook boundary now uses the same authoritative message and the existing display/Incognito projection.

The first revision skipped restoration whenever the snapshot contained any user message. That still dropped the original request when an accepted steering message was present, because steering is also a user message. The guard now skips restoration only when the persisted request's own `idempotencyKey` or `${turnId}:prompt` mirror identity is already present. Distinct steering messages no longer hide the original request, and an already-observed persisted request is still not duplicated.

## Evidence

- Full target suite: `19 passed` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.hooks.test.ts`.
- Ordinary-turn regression uses the real production attempt, mock native app-server, and real hook runner. It verifies exactly one user observation with the persisted content and one assistant observation.
- Steering regression queues a distinct `Also beta` message through the real production steering path. `agent_end` receives the persisted `Remember alpha` request exactly once, then `Also beta`, then one assistant answer.
- Base-red: with the production change reverted, the hook receives no user message; with only the previous role-only guard, the steering case receives `Also beta` but not `Remember alpha`.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass for all changed files.
- Local evidence: `contributions/pr-evidence-20261025/182977/` (`base-red.log`, `full-vitest.log`).

The unit regressions use a mock native app-server. The linked issue additionally provides the installed Hindsight control showing `0` retains for the old assistant-only payload and `1` retain after the persisted user request is restored.

Real shipped Gateway proof on exact head `938c7cd16`, using the production Gateway, forced `codex` runtime, and a loopback native provider:

```text
transcript rows:
user      Remember alpha
assistant ALPHA-
user      Also beta
assistant BETA-DONE

native provider POST /v1/responses:
request 1  alpha=true   beta=false
request 2  alpha=true   beta=true

agent_end success=true:
user      Remember alpha   (exactly once)
assistant BETA-DONE
```

The first request was observed after the original request had been persisted. The steering RPC was then accepted while that native turn remained open, and the second provider request contained `Also beta`, proving the steering input reached the native transport rather than being reconstructed from the transcript. The final history contains exactly one persisted `Remember alpha` row, the steering row, and both assistant rows; the completion observation restores `Remember alpha` exactly once and does not duplicate it. The separate steering unit regression covers the plugin-refresh handoff, where accepted steering messages are intentionally included in the completion snapshot. Gateway run: `1 passed` in `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/zz-182977-proof.e2e.test.ts`.

## AI Assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance under contributor direction and review.

Replaces https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/120119. Related: #120118.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes mislabeled image attachments when MIME detection or image conversion leaves an old filename extension, including PNG bytes replayed from a `.webp` delivery-queue artifact.

## User Impact

Delivered images have leaf filenames that match their encoded format. Matching aliases such as `.jpeg` keep their spelling. Raw-loader metadata, image bytes, limits, and SQLite-owned artifact paths retain their existing behavior; no migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

On the base commit, `src/media/web-media.ts:487–492` returns preserved image bytes with the source filename, and the non-optimizing path at `579–583` does the same. The old filename helper only runs after encoding. Replace it with one shared image filename reconciler used by the optimizer and public loader, without renaming durable files or re-encoding accepted images. This retains the current HEIC/HEIF preservation, animated WebP, and image-limit behavior and drops the retired QQBot changes from the original PR.

Production delta: +26/−18 (net +8); tests: +106/−3 (net +103); docs: +1/−1. The added production lines cover the previously missed public return paths and matching MIME aliases; there is no new state, fallback, or dependency.

## Evidence

- Base `bb13bcdfb1fe59d506f8b38ba32d9e34794d9bfb`: six selected regression cases failed on the expected filename assertions, including real queue stage → enqueue → source deletion → replay. PNG bytes and MIME retained a `.webp` public name.
- Fixed head: all 66 tests passed across the loader, queue-spool, animated-WebP, and image-understanding suites. The six regressions are green, and the replay test confirms both unchanged artifact custody and a corrected public filename.
- Local wall times: 64.43s for animated WebP, 196.48s for the combined loader/spool run, and 115.65s for image understanding, plus 288.72s of worktree compiler preparation on the loaded host. Per-file test execution was 87.44s for the loader and 46.62s for the spool; the new queue regression took 2.77s; the unchanged HTML-provenance case took 83.41s. The wrapper completed all three shards in 885.61s. The exact-head CI run completed; inherited failure evidence is recorded below.
- Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Isolated Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2; no accepted/actionable findings.
- No live channel send, lease, broad local suite, or full local typecheck was run, per this repair lane's proof scope. Exact-head PR CI supplies the broader checks.

Exact-head CI: [run 40083712451](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40083712451) completed with one inherited test failure and its dependent CI gate. `checks-node-changed-2` fails `pdf-tool.test.ts:397:35` ("reports omitted images for a text-only model and supplies Codex instructions") because `systemPrompt` is undefined. Scheduled main [run 40078639310, checks-node-compact-small-12](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40078639310/job/120827461332) reports the identical title, assertion message, and location. prs.title: perf(reef): skip idle recovery snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reef opens a read transaction and scans peer trust during periodic delivery recovery even when there are no outbound deliveries to recover.

## User Impact

Reduces idle database work for Reef accounts with an empty outbound queue. Populated delivery recovery retains its current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the delivery namespace once in autocommit mode and return immediately when it is empty. A narrow typed `ifEmpty` option on the existing plugin-state operation lets the worker use its existing namespace reader for that shortcut. A populated namespace falls through to the normal snapshot and rereads deliveries plus peers. Both recovery operations retain the same watched namespaces, epoch capture and final authority checks. No cache, schema, SQL syntax or timer change.

Accepted edges: a delivery arriving just after an empty read is picked up on the next periodic reconciliation; an empty recovery scan no longer discovers unrelated malformed peer records. Populated recovery retains peer validation and snapshot consistency, at the cost of one extra SELECT (five statements rather than four). Empty recovery falls from four statements to one, in the same worker request. The generic option preserves namespace and TTL rules and rejects use with writable operations.

## Evidence

Final head: `938d34a9b8ad104ba833a7f39591d98a05759b16`; baseline: `3f7b7765585ddcd72822d8b4e43ef928d23eecf7`.

Three alternating pairs used a real isolated Gateway and loopback Reef relay, no messages, fresh synthetic fixtures and a 125-second steady window with four reconciliation polls. SQL median / p95 / range: **74 / 74 / [74–74] → 50 / 50 / [50–50]**. Worker requests: **29 / 29 / [29–29] in both arms**. MAIN: **0 in both arms**. Each candidate window removes eight namespace SELECTs, eight BEGINs and eight COMMITs; every other SQL shape is identical. That is **24 fewer statements per window, about 11.52 per minute**. All six runs recorded zero unexpected relay requests. Counts and per-thread profile attribution only; no latency or CPU-speed claim.

All 46 focused tests pass: 15 plugin-state operation tests and 31 Reef trust-store tests. The new worker-boundary regression proves empty = one SELECT and populated = SELECT / BEGIN / SELECT / SELECT / COMMIT; substituting the base worker makes it fail. Empty-result receipts invalidate after writes to either watched namespace. Two initial Codex reviews and the coordinator-authorized additional delta-only review of the autocommit revision found no remaining actionable P0–P2 issues. The exact head has PostgreSQL review approval for identical scoping, statement-snapshot consistency, unchanged watch/epoch capture and the documented edge. Production LOC: +43/−4 (net +39), tests +110/−6 (net +104), docs +44. The growth adds one generic typed worker option and its regressions; no second state owner or cache.

Connected-client health reproduces one proactive receipt lookup per minute and its transaction. Replacing it requires a separate cron readiness/configuration lifecycle change, assigned to its owner. Generic multi-read snapshots, real external-writer/effect checks and WAL cadence stay. The proposed plugin `count(*)` target did not reproduce and is rejected here.

Open-main compatibility: complete coverage of 2,670 other currently open-main PRs against main `f0dcb354e45b06d60df466de136f85cd1b7b148e`. The sole overlap, #177691 at `22ea62d40ffb`, touches SDK documentation. Baseline and candidate retain the identical unrelated Discord-test conflict block; no new conflict path or hunk. Candidate integrates cleanly onto that main.

## Frozen control — disclosed count movements

The frozen v3.1.4 control uses the exact same baseline above and the final candidate, matching Node/SQLite versions, options and harness hashes. Both product runs complete shutdown and restart. Ten warm execution windows total **510→512 SQL / 125→124 requests / 0→0 MAIN**. Warm SQL median / p95 / range is **50 / 54 / [50–54] → 50 / 59 / [50–59]**; requests **12 / 14 / [12–14] → 12 / 15 / [12–15]**. Whole run: **3016 / 801 / 94 → 2996 / 800 / 95**.

**The original strict control rule stopped acceptance; the maintainer has now explicitly accepted these unrelated background-count movements under the verified conditions below.** Idle-settle SQL rises **102→145 (+42.16%)** and restart-shutdown requests **6→9 (+50%)**, triggering the written stop rule. Of the idle-settle increase, 39 exact statements move from compaction, but the combined phases still rise 248→252 SQL. Shutdown adds two ordinary `pluginState.entries` requests and one zero-SQL prepared-catalog task; ordinary entries rise 8→10 overall. These use the unchanged ordinary reader, not `ifEmpty`. Warm SQL +2 comprises +4 for an extra unchanged-owner session settlement, +1 catalog read crossing from first-turn, −2 ordinary entries, and −1 WAL checkpoint. The extra settlement invocation and extra ordinary-entry calls remain unexplained. The added MAIN statement is an unchanged device-pairing cold-admission timeout application (`PRAGMA busy_timeout=4999`); warm MAIN remains zero. The maintainer accepted the movements only if no Reef SQL executed in this control and the extra work belongs to unchanged owners. Both conditions are verified: all 2,996 SQL rows have full captured stacks, none contain a Reef path or operation, and 17 relevant owner blob pairs are identical. The frozen workload disables channels. The unexplained invocation-count differences and p95 increases remain disclosed; they are not a claimed non-regression result. The three-pair live-Reef counts above supply target acceptance.

All phase counts are retained below. Counts describe execution windows; dispatch may precede the window. The frozen causal mapper resolves many candidate dist stacks as UNKNOWN, so attribution uses normalized raw shapes, wire command types and unchanged owner blobs. This is one control pair, not a latency/non-regression claim.

## Validation status

Exact-head [CI run 40135566767](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40135566767) passes production/test types, all lint stripes, source contracts, architecture/Madge, T1/dialect/worker ratchets, changed-test jobs and SDK package boundaries. PostgreSQL conformance shards 1 and 3 pass. [Shard 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40135566767/job/120996625090) fails seven interactive-setup fixture cases because its synthetic runtime omits `standalone-runtime-profile.mjs`; aggregate CI is red. The shared actual-main reproduction on `0f6631638b2e` reproduces all seven failures, with one control passing. The fixture repair subsequently landed as #182990 (`27e87016a5e4`); #182996 was closed as its duplicate. This approved candidate remains on the older base and uses the documented inherited-failure exception. Current main is not claimed to retain that defect.

The runtime API guardrail passes all seven tests. All three canonical Knip scans and the SDK surface report are byte-identical between the exact baseline and candidate: zero new findings. The surface report retains the same pre-existing count-limit failures in both arms (3,817 public exports against 3,815; 2,212 callable exports against 2,211), with no unauthorized shipped removals. Both full canonical API renders and their comparison pass: no entrypoint or export is added or removed; the optional `ifEmpty` field is the only declaration addition, propagated through 167 reachable exports (acknowledgement digest `8920e462`). Knip findings remain exactly 67 production / 77 full-tree / 1,136 scripts in both arms. Local formatting/basic lint/diff checks pass. CI supplies successful type/lint evidence; the earlier local type-aware preparation refused the required external virtual store, and no guard was bypassed. A maintainer-approved temporary in-checkout install resolved the canonical API renderer’s physical compiler boundary. The source is restored cleanly to the reviewed, PostgreSQL-approved head.

## Acceptance rule (registered before the first run)

Run the committed `scripts/perf/plugin-state-polling.mts` with a real isolated Gateway, loopback Reef relay, `--messages 0 --seconds 125`, a fresh synthetic fixture, and the frozen v3.1.4 observer. Keep startup and shutdown separate from steady state. Capture V8 CPU profiles per thread for attribution, without claiming a timing improvement.

Count steady SQL statements, worker requests and main-thread statements, including transaction envelopes. Report per-minute rates and per-operation changes. Use three alternating baseline/candidate pairs when host load is below 64 and internal free space is at least 12 GiB; otherwise use one pair and source attribution. The candidate must reduce each empty recovery operation from four statements to one, prove populated recovery uses five statements with its normal snapshot, add no requests or main-thread work, and preserve later delivery visibility and peer changes from supported sibling/external writers. A pattern that does not reproduce on current main is rejected for this change.

Also run the frozen harness warm-turn control. Attribute all count movements; owner-attributed increases stop acceptance. Wall-clock or CPU A/B claims require the timing lock, load below 24, at least five interleaved samples per head, median/p95/spread, and separate cold/warm results; a 20% user-facing regression stops acceptance. This draft claims no timing win.


The autocommit acceptance amendment above was published before the first run of that candidate; the original baseline and draft acceptance are retained in PR history. Exact worker statement-sequence and watch invalidation tests cover the changed boundary.

prs.title: fix(gateway): plugin reloads hang when config changes during Gateway startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `plugins.reload` (or other plugin install/update/reload) request sent while the Gateway is still starting never answers when the config file changed during startup. The client times out (300 s in the reported run), and the Gateway recovers only when its config watcher gives up waiting for the plugin lifecycle lease after 10 minutes. Reproduced live on `9c29902212c5`; on current `main` this trigger is masked, but the reloader still deadlocks under the same conditions (see Reachability below).

## User Impact

Plugin lifecycle requests that arrive during startup now complete. They also apply the config edit that was pending at startup, and startup finishes after them. Later config edits keep hot-reloading through the watcher as before. There is no config change, migration, or new option.

**Reachability on current main:** the field run used `9c29902212c5`. Since #181289 (landed about four hours later), main-session recovery runs as post-ready work, and WebSocket connect admission waits for it. Clients are therefore admitted only after the reloader's startup drain, which masks this trigger on current `main` (a live attempt on `f04709b78a04` could not hit the window, even with a 10 s preparation delay). The reloader itself still deadlocks any caller that holds the lease during its startup drain, as the regression below shows on `main`. This fix removes the reloader's dependency on connect-admission ordering, which another module owns and already changed once.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin request holds the plugin lifecycle lease and then waited for the config reloader's full startup readiness. Since #172266, readiness also drains the reload that initial reconciliation queues for an edited file, and that watcher reload needs the same lease. The request waited for the reload, and the reload waited for the request.

The config reloader stays the single owner; its startup is now split into two stages. Plugin application waits only for **preparation**: the startup baseline, watcher start, and initial reconciliation. The existing `running` flag already serializes it against watcher reloads. It reads the current file, so the pending startup edit is applied together with the plugin change, and the queued watcher reload later sees only its echo. Because the baseline is published before the application reads or commits anything, startup cannot overwrite an applied mutation.

**Readiness** still means nothing is in flight. The startup drain now also waits while an application is running, and the application wakes the drain when it finishes, because it may have consumed the reload timer the drain was waiting on. The startup guarantee documented with #172266 still holds: initial config publication cannot race the first request after startup. No timers, polling, retries, or config were added.

<details>
<summary>Source chain and layout</summary>

1. `src/gateway/server-methods/plugins-mutations.ts` takes the plugin lifecycle lease (`waitMs: 0`) and runs the mutation under it.
2. `src/plugins/management-mutations.ts` calls runtime application, `applyPluginLifecycleChange` in `src/gateway/config-reload.ts`.
3. That application awaited `ready`; `ready` drained the reload queued by initial reconciliation.
4. The watcher's `startTrackedReload` acquires the same lease outside the caller's context, so it waits for the request.

The behavior change is about 20 lines in `src/gateway/config-reload.ts`. That file is over its line cap, and the cap ratchet forbids growth, so five pure candidate-settlement helpers (`isConfigReloadSuperseded`, `candidateApplications`, `settleCandidateApplications`, `transferCandidateApplications`, `createObservedCandidate`) move unchanged into `src/gateway/config-reload-candidates.ts`. Net: `config-reload.ts` +27/−84, `config-reload-candidates.ts` +82. For the same reason, the regression lives in `config-reload.lease-retry.test.ts`, next to the other lease-admission cases.

Docs: `docs/gateway/configuration/hot-reload.md` now describes plugin lifecycle requests during startup.

</details>

## Evidence

- **Field report:** a local-model campaign lane (macOS, isolated Gateway, 2026-10-22) sent `plugins.reload {"plugins":[{"pluginId":"memory-core"}]}` at initial listening while its config had changed during startup. The Gateway log showed `[scheduler] running config:reload` followed by `Waiting for plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global held by …`, and the RPC client was killed after 300 s.
- **Regression** `applies a leased plugin change while startup reconciles a config edit` (`src/gateway/config-reload.lease-retry.test.ts`) uses the real plugin lifecycle lease. The plugin change enters under the lease during deferred startup preparation while a disk edit is pending. The test asserts the plugin receipt, that the startup edit was applied with the plugin lifecycle, that full readiness completes, and that a later watcher edit still applies.
  - main's reloader (`f04709b78a04`) with the new test: **fails** at the 120 s test timeout; on shutdown the stuck application rejects at its `await ready`.
  - this branch: **passes** in 0.7 s; the whole lease-retry file passes 17/17.
- **Affected suites:** all 13 reloader, startup-admission, and plugin-lifecycle suites (`config-reload*.test.ts`, `server.hooks-admission`, `plugins.lifecycle-contention`, `plugins.reload-readonly`, `server-plugins.lifecycle`, `server-reload-handlers`, `server-reload-managed-secrets`, `server-kernel.config-activation`): 13 files, **398/398 passed** on the final tree.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` for `tsconfig.core.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-root.json`: clean. `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and the line-cap ratchet on touched files: clean.
- **Live isolated Gateway, before** (`9c29902212c5`, the field run's commit; isolated state, home, and config; loopback port; macOS, Node 26.12.1): the config was edited right after `http server listening`, and a client then retried `plugins.reload {"plugins":[{"pluginId":"memory-core"}]}` until admitted. A test-only `--import` hook paused the reloader's initial preparation for 10 s so the request deterministically lands inside the window; product files were untouched. The request was admitted 0.12 s into that pause. Gateway log:
  ```text
  23:32:57.519 [scheduler] running config:reload
  23:32:58.619 [state/lease] Waiting for plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global held by f63a1535-…; current lease expires at 06:37:47Z.
  ```
  No response arrived in 120 s, and `[gateway] ready` never appeared.
- **Live isolated Gateway, after** (`9c29902212c5` + this patch, committed locally so the CLI does not rebuild on launch; same sequence and pause): the request was admitted 0.19 s into the pause. No lease wait occurred (0 lines), and the queued startup reload never ran separately; the plugin application consumed it. Gateway log:
  ```text
  04:13:18.471 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (logging.level)
  04:14:32.051 [gateway] Plugin replacement applied: memory-core
  04:14:34.033 [reload] config change applied (dynamic reads: logging.level)
  04:14:34.037 [reload] config source revision 2 accepted (file)
  04:14:43.131 [gateway] ready
  ```
  `plugins.reload` answered `ok` after 94 s, which matches unpatched post-startup reloads on this host (80–130 s): the host's load average was about 50, and loading memory-core took 71.7 s with the main thread stalled. A follow-up `warn` edit started its watcher reload (`running config:reload`) after `ready`, but the harness's 30 s window ended during another 23 s main-thread stall, before acceptance was logged. That post-startup watcher path is unchanged by this patch and is asserted by the regression. The `failed to promote config last-known-good backup: ConfigMutationConflictError` warning in this run also appears in every unpatched run with a startup edit; it is pre-existing.
- **Live on current `main` (`f04709b78a04`):** six natural attempts, plus one with the same 10 s preparation pause, could not hit the window, because connect admission now waits for post-ready work (see Reachability above).

### CI: one pre-existing failure

`checks-node-changed-compact-small-22` failed in [run 40090360372](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40090360372) (attempt 1). `pr-failure-report` classified it **unknown**: main has no comparable job, because main's scheduled CI does not run this changed-file Bun selection. Its Bun shard `agentic-control-plane-runtime-config` timed out with no output after `src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts > openclaw.changes.list preserves an approved include-only operation without a duplicate write`; both Bun processes were zombies. On Linux Bun Testboxes (pinned fork via `scripts/stage-openclaw-bun.sh`, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`), that case's teardown (`server.close`) hits the 180 s hook timeout **with main's `config-reload.ts` (`f04709b78a04`) as well**: 2 of 4 runs ([40142088594](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142088594) passed 1/1; [40145587997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40145587997) failed 2/3, alternating with this head). This head failed 6 of 7 ([40139328854](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139328854), [40143648896](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40143648896), [40145587997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40145587997)). In both variants, the runs after the first on a lease hang almost every time, so this is a pre-existing Bun teardown hang in that test, not caused by this change. The test starts its own Gateway after `startupSettled`, so the reloader's startup drain is already complete when it runs. The remaining 56 cases in that file pass on this head under Bun.

prs.title: fix(codex): recover tool summaries after unfinished earlier work
prs.body:
Related: #128916

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing Codex summaries when a completed tool turn follows an unfinished tool exchange in earlier conversation history.

## User Impact

A turn with complete current evidence can recover its final answer without rerunning completed actions. Recovery may omit earlier conversation and reports that omission; persisted history stays intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

At the verified current-turn boundary, an unfinished prior exchange makes the earlier replay prefix unusable. Omit that prefix as a whole and reuse the existing bounded omission notice. User steering within a completed exchange stays atomic. Current-turn pairing, provenance, call-ID uniqueness, content validation, and recovery eligibility keep their existing guards.

This addresses one recovery failure contributing to #128916; it does not claim to solve that issue in full or explain why a native model/server originally returned an empty final.

## Evidence

- Two new scenarios in the existing native finalizer fixture fail on the base with missing settled-tool evidence and pass with the patch: ordinary unfinished prior work and an oversized omitted prior exchange that still has a pending call.
- The fixture uses the real native process, SQLite transcript reader, context capture, and private finalizer against scripted local provider responses. It verifies the recovered summary is persisted, the original transcript remains unchanged, and the completed action runs once. No real external model or Discord delivery is claimed.
- Six focused files: 88 tests pass. Runner wall time: 32.3 seconds. The changed native file's tests took about 8.1 seconds; it covers native process/auth/persistence boundaries that a projector-only test would miss. The prior-context file's tests took milliseconds. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Existing cases cover current incomplete pairs, provenance drift, duplicate identities/IDs, unsupported content, bounded contiguous history, steering across a completed tool exchange, cancellation, and isolated finalization.
- Full Codex extension attempt: the final shard reports 5,239 tests passed, 2 failed, and 17 skipped (20.2 minutes wall time). Both failures are unchanged `transport-startup.test.ts` descendant-containment cases with `ProcessInspectionError` (`reason: permission`) on macOS. Both exact failures also reproduce on the clean pinned base with an independent frozen install and the same test wrapper: 2 failed, 2 deselected, exit1 in 31.6 seconds. They are baseline-host permission failures; no permission/config changes or unrelated fixes were made. The two new native regressions passed in this run.
- Independent final-candidate rerun of the 88 focused tests: exit 0 in 41.7 seconds.
- Production and test source typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and the changed document MDX check pass. Author simplification is complete; final canonical autoreview is scoped-clean through P0–P2. CI seconds are not yet available.

Validation gaps: no live external provider/channel run or deployment. The first package-boundary typecheck lacked SDK declarations; the documented source typechecks subsequently passed. A missing required fixture option was corrected and the final candidate was reviewed again. The Codex extension lane is not green on this host: both process-inspection failures reproduce without this patch on the pinned base. No live containment claim is made from these failing tests; their finally blocks perform ownership-bound cleanup, but no separate post-hoc descendant-liveness receipt was retained.

## Public CLI boundary proof (2026-10-23)

Addressing the requested entry-point proof on the reviewed head `c7d1b85cefaf230bf5b487ceb3102778ab898173`. Separate normal `pnpm build:runtime` builds of candidate and pinned base `3e4251331e83d844498fc66f70675f97f98616e5` were exercised through **`node openclaw.mjs agent --local`**, with the real pinned **Codex CLI 0.162.1**. The parent independently reran both and inspected the persisted SQLite finalizer record and physical action-count file. The source checkout remains clean at the reviewed head; no code changes were needed.

**Scope and fault injection:** a deterministic local HTTP Responses server supplies model responses; this is not real external-model, Gateway, channel-delivery, npm-installation, or deployment proof. The public CLI first creates isolated state, then a preparation utility seeds a synthetic unanswered earlier tool call through the public transcript SDK. The current turn uses the advertised `openclaw_direct.exec` tool to append one line to a task-owned file. Only after observing its completed tool output and physical count 1 does the provider inject one empty completion. The unmodified native launcher, product CLI, recovery owners, and persistence decide the outcome; no private finalizer is directly invoked for the current turn.

Candidate: CLI exit 0, one recovery request, final answer persisted. Base negative control: CLI exit 1, `incomplete_pairing` / `context_unavailable`, no recovery request or persisted answer. Both perform the action exactly once and preserve the prior event prefix byte-for-byte. Hashes below cover the exact previously stored event text/blob prefix, not the mutable whole database; independent synthetic sessions have different hashes. Observed task-owned processes exit and proof ports close.

Redacted terminal output and read-only persistence measurements from the independent reruns:


A single command-local `logMcpLine` applies the canonical `sanitizeTerminalText` to human report lines; the human error path uses the same sanitizer. JSON and protocol output bypass it. The integration preserves the newer credential-redaction fix in list/show.

prs.title: refactor(plugins): remove redundant async forwarding
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix actions, Copilot isolated completions, and ClickClack HTTP methods wrap existing asynchronous owners in extra async functions.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. These call paths return the owner's promise directly while retaining their current Promise signatures, authorization, cancellation, validation errors, and cleanup behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove 26 forwarding async sites: 13 Matrix callbacks/helpers, 10 Copilot start/cleanup callbacks, and three ClickClack methods. Production delta is +29/-31 lines (net -2); tests are unchanged. Matrix's authorization helper, Copilot's deferred-start and best-effort cleanup owners, and ClickClack's asynchronous request/nonce owners already provide the needed boundary. No SQL, schema, SDK signature, cache, worker placement, or write-order changes.

Keep async wrappers that convert synchronous argument validation into rejected promises, normalize optional cleanup to Promise<void>, or hold an owner lifetime through finally. Copilot starts still defer until the abort listener exists. Authority checks remain at their existing effects. Relative microtask timing of pure forwarding is intentionally reduced; no consumer contract was found that depends on the removed promise identities.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, recorded before measurement: exercise the existing Matrix action/read-policy, Copilot isolated-completion deadline, and ClickClack HTTP owner suites. The simplification wins if all 26 classified forwarding sites disappear with net-negative production lines and behavior remains intact. Run one baseline/candidate pair using the frozen SQL harness v3.1.4 (36/36 hashes verified), including its ten warm turns per run. Report SQL statements, worker requests, and MAIN SQL as warm median [min-max], with operation attribution. Require no added statements or requests from these owners; stop for an attributed increase or a 20% regression in any measured user-facing cell. Counts only on this loaded host: no latency or CPU speedup claim, and cold/warm results remain separate. Any CPU profile is diagnostic sampling, not a timing comparison. The frozen Gateway WebSocket workload (qaRuntime build, channels disabled) is broad runtime non-regression coverage; it does not exercise the Matrix, Copilot, or ClickClack transports directly. Their owning tests cover the changed paths, and no per-wrapper CPU gain or live-traffic SQL saving is claimed.

- Five focused files pass: 103 tests, comprising Matrix action/read policy 65, ClickClack HTTP and Copilot deadline clock 27, and prompt-prefix stability 11.
- Independent Codex review: scoped-clean through P2, one completed round. The final change only narrows that reviewed patch.
- [Exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40143108652): 27 successful jobs, including production/test types, extension type-aware lint, source contracts, ratchets, changed-owner suites, and four QA smoke profiles. No CI failure override.
- Canonical Knip baseline/candidate sets are identical: scripts 1136/1136, production 70/70, full-tree 82/82; zero added/removed findings. Standalone Madge passes with zero cycles. Local formatting/basic oxlint/whitespace and runnable check:changed guards pass; T1 170→170, compatibility T1 15→15, dialect 0→0. The local type-aware lint/typecheck wrappers refuse the required external dependency-store layout before compilation; no containment guard was bypassed. Exact-head CI passes those checks.

### Runtime count pair

Baseline `1a1db5882679`, candidate `29ddad0feca7`: one complete synthetic run each; ten warm turns per arm. Both pass all 14 turns, control-plane, cron, compaction, idle, restart, and clean-shutdown assertions; zero native errors.

| Warm MAIN median [min–max]; p95 | 0 [0–0]; 0 | 0 [0–0]; 0 |
| Whole-run SQL / requests / MAIN | 2989 / 802 / 94 | 2995 / 802 / 95 |

No execution-phase cell increases by 20%. Warm operation totals differ only by one fewer `AsyncWorkScope.enter` checkpoint statement. Whole-run differences are in unchanged owners: checkpoints +3 SQL; native busy-timeout setup +1 SQL/+1 MAIN; session-entry patch +1 SQL; catalog snapshot −1 SQL/−1 request; row reads +2/+1; `runWithAsyncStore` −1 request; `scan` +1 request; session-entry read −1/−1; session-target inventory −1 request; subagent hydration +2/+2; usage-cost −1 SQL. The extra MAIN statement is a boot-time busy-timeout pragma. The changed transports are not enabled in this workload; these counts establish broad runtime coverage, not a measured transport speedup. prs.title: perf(gateway): remove the remaining reload observation lease read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config reload rechecks the durable plugin lease immediately after reading its source snapshot, before observation and bookkeeping. Remove that redundant read. The application owner still checks the lease before reading plugin install records and before credential, runtime publication, acceptance, and transactional effects. Native admission/final checks, heartbeat and recovery stay intact.

This completes the observation-only deletion from #182879, deferred while #89526 was open. #89526 is now closed, unmerged. Accepted edge: retry scheduling, in-process receipt settlement, flushing an already-committed plan, watch registration and audit appends can finish after lease expiry; authoritative application still rejects expired custody.

## Acceptance rule (registered before runs)

Use the existing synthetic isolated Gateway/WebSocket workload `scripts/perf/idle-gateway-measure.ts --config-reloads 5 --settle-seconds 5 --minutes 1`. Count MAIN lease SELECTs in five applied warm reloads separately from boot, settle, idle and shutdown. Expected per reload: 22 -> 21 (five fewer total), with no new worker request or SQL operation. Use current-main 6113057491a as the baseline; the previous 22-read run is supporting evidence only. Report count median/p95/range; do not claim latency or CPU improvement on this loaded host. Boot/idle/shutdown must not add work attributable to the changed owner. Any attributed regression stops the change. One live pair follows the campaign count-only rule; earlier profile evidence applies to the same lease SELECT stack.

The existing real-SQL owner regression must fail on current-main production with checkpoints [0,2], then pass with [0,1]. The expired-observation regression must continue rejecting application before plugin reads. Run the four focused lease/reload owner files with the pinned Bun runtime; use PR CI for broad static gates.

## Evidence

Independent Codex review: scoped-clean P0–P2. Basic oxlint, formatting and diff whitespace pass. Local type-aware wrapper rejects the required external dependency store; exact-head CI will supply that gate. The tightened regression is RED on current-main production 6113057491a: actual [0,2], expected [0,1]. Candidate count and expired-observation regressions both PASS (2/2); expired custody is rejected before plugin reads or application. All four focused owner files PASS: 51 tests across reload, plugin lifecycle, native admission and existing-lease recovery. The fresh isolated Gateway pair is complete: both runs exited 0 with no SQL errors. Its initial wrapper setup failed before Gateway startup (pre-created observer directory), then was corrected without repeating the successful tests or baseline build. pgprep confirmed exact head d97ee0244ab1: resulting production blob is byte-identical to the previously reviewed three-check deletion. Exact-head CI [40146169970](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146169970) passed all 33 executed jobs, including production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts, architecture, changed-owner tests and database ratchets. The local type-aware wrapper limitation is covered by that CI result. Prior #182879 Knip evidence is reused: this follow-up changes no imports, exports, declarations, or dependency reachability (the same callback still has other calls). Production: -1 line; test: one expectation updated, no new test machinery. SQL shape removed once per reload: `SELECT expires_at FROM state_leases WHERE scope=? AND lease_key=? AND owner=? AND expires_at>?`. No schema, SQL dialect, API or worker routing changes.

## Open PR compatibility

Shared prindex yielded five live open overlaps, each fetched and compared base-only versus candidate with git merge-tree: #182125 and #163986 remain clean; #177823, #157558 and #121022 retain the same pre-existing conflict paths and marker counts. Zero new conflict paths or markers across all five exact heads. Closed #89526 and merged #182879 are excluded after live verification. Exact-head PG REVIEW-OK received for d97ee0244ab1.


## Fresh Gateway counts (five reloads per arm)

| Count | Baseline median / p95 [min–max] | Candidate median / p95 [min–max] |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MAIN lease SELECTs per reload | 22 / 22 [22–22] | 21 / 21 [21–21] |
| All MAIN statements per reload | 22 / 25 [22–25] | 21 / 24 [21–24] |
| All SQL per reload | 52 / 56 [51–56] | 53 / 87 [50–87] |
| Worker requests per reload | 16 / 17 [15–17] | 16 / 26 [14–26] |

All five `runReload` reads disappear. Whole-run SQL / requests / MAIN: 1185 / 242 / 192 → 1183 / 240 / 186. Idle: 6 / 3 / 0 → 5 / 2 / 0. Shutdown: 22 / 6 / 5 unchanged. Thread CPU profiles were captured (27 baseline, 26 candidate); no latency or CPU improvement is claimed on the loaded host (one-minute load about 48–55).

The raw p95 rises were a STOP for attribution, not “within spread.” The first-window +32 SQL is exactly −1 target read +12 SQL from two extra pre-callback lease-acquisition attempts +21 relocated startup/cleanup statements. Its +9 requests are +2 acquisition attempts and +7 relocated startup/cleanup requests. The relocated groups are lease cleanup/release, hosted plugin catalog snapshot, catalog/credential snapshot, and memory prewarm. Later reload 2 catches an extra catalog refresh cycle in unchanged owners. Boot/settle SQL shifts 847/45 → 591/269. These raw figures do not support an aggregate speedup claim; the demonstrated saving is exactly one synchronous MAIN read per reload, with unchanged custody and effect checks.

prs.title: fix(migrate-hermes): reject FIFO text inputs without blocking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hermes migration can hang while reading a named pipe as required configuration, an optional profile selector, or an existing memory append target.

## User Impact

Preview and import refuse special-file inputs without waiting for a writer. Ordinary source symlinks, Unicode, optional unreadable-selector behavior, and repeated memory-import dedupe remain supported. Replace an unexpected special file with an ordinary file and retry migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing public regular-file reader at the two existing text policies, and reuse the optional reader for memory dedupe. Strict configuration and credential decoding uses the canonical UTF-8 decoder; optional selectors retain their existing decoding policy. No new filesystem helper, timeout, configuration, or dependency is introduced.

## Evidence

Three production-path FIFO regressions fail on unchanged main readers: optional profile discovery, required configuration planning, and existing-memory dedupe. The optional and dedupe cases prove that the old reader opened the pipe; the required case proves it accepted pipe input into a plan. The required fixture uses `config.yaml` because `.env` is read more than once during planning.

All four affected suites passed: 102/102 tests, including FIFO refusal, supported symlinks, exact Unicode/BOM handling, malformed source preservation, provider routing, credentials, and repeat-import dedupe (294.82 seconds including runner setup and cleanup). Independent Codex autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Targeted typed oxlint, oxfmt, and diff checks passed. After integrating current main, all four FIFO/symlink cases passed again (186.85 seconds including setup and cleanup); the three-file patch is byte-identical to the checked candidate.

Production +17/-9 (net +8); tests +80; docs +6. The small production increase preserves separate optional and strict read policies plus useful source-path/retry errors, while removing the extra byte-reading wrapper and ad hoc UTF-8 validation.

A fresh compiled CLI and installed-stable upgrade were not rerun: the real migration-provider regressions cover file admission and preserved output; a separate runtime build would exceed the bounded live-proof budget. The contributor's compiled Linux CLI and installed-upgrade observations below apply to prior head `c336a0ed26e9b19d2a46c8b00b0a2107a9715caf`, not this revision.

Exact-head CI run 40148332811 passed; dependency, security, and ci-gate checks passed.

Contributor: @Leon-SK668 (Leon-SK668 <0668001470@xydigit.com>).

<details>
<summary>Prior-head compiled CLI and installed-upgrade evidence</summary>

The contributor compared compiled base `e1f4e11918cda015da76ab57b29e59a7c5455d33` with `c336a0ed26e9b19d2a46c8b00b0a2107a9715caf` using synthetic isolated state on Linux, Node 24.22.1. Actual `migrate hermes --dry-run --json --no-auth-credentials` and `migrate apply hermes --json --yes --no-auth-credentials --no-backup --force --item memory:MEMORY.md` processes used no FIFO writers.

prs.title: perf(state): skip unused worker environments in authority reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Placement and agent-registry authority reads rebuild a complete worker environment even though those callers only consume database admission.

## User Impact

Less allocation and CPU work during repeated placement and registry reads. No public behavior, configuration, schema, environment precedence, secret redaction, or allowlist changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing authority-only capture at all three placement admission sites and the registry snapshot admission site. It retains the same database, schema, maintenance, and integrity checks without preparing an unused worker environment. Actual worker initialization keeps its existing capture. No global environment cache: temporary skill credentials, proxy routing, and config publication have independent mutation owners.

Runtime production delta: +6/-6 lines (zero net growth); the unnecessary work disappears at four caller sites. Benchmark tooling adds 70 lines, benchmark documentation 13, and tests 23 net lines. The requested non-test/non-docs-path diff therefore totals +83 lines because it includes the benchmark script and its README. That tooling growth extends the existing harness with real admission, synthetic environment setup, and work counts; there is no new runtime cache or lifecycle machinery. Simplification review retained only these substitutions and their proof.

## Evidence

- Warm real placement-store regression: base enumerates the ambient environment once; candidate zero times. Fails on base for that exact count, passes with the change.
- Synthetic authority probe: 10,000 retained placements, 64 protected records, 200 synthetic environment entries, 1,000 operations; full environment enumerations **1,000 → 0**, identical output hashes.
- Focused tests pass: placement-session-read (5), placement-turn-authority (21), registry-listing.snapshot (11), registry-listing.settled (9). File test durations range from ~0.1 to ~19 seconds; the largest file includes database replacement and live claim revocation. Local total command wall times: 58.76s and 60.51s, including compilation. CI passed on the exact head.
- Changed-file oxfmt and oxlint pass; diff whitespace check and targeted scripts typecheck pass. The full build passed for the isolated Gateway proof. Broad PR CI passed on the exact head.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. The configured autoreview route was rejected before inference because it did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

Paired measurements passed: **CPU/work −57.8%, allocation/work −42.1%, total GC/work −86.0%** (mean of paired percentage deltas). This is a small overall optimization, not a whole-Gateway speedup claim.

| Metric | Pair 1: base → candidate | Pair 2, swapped: base → candidate |

| Sampled allocated bytes/operation | 147,794.5 → 85,467.6 | 147,492.1 → 85,404.6 |

Mean absolute changes: CPU −0.19423 ms/op, allocation −62,207 bytes/op, GC −0.00953 ms/op, loop p95 −0.11571 ms and p99 −1.18118 ms. The first pair's maximum GC pause increased by 0.0153 ms; that is non-gating context, with total GC and collection counts sharply lower. Major GC tails are context only (18 baseline and 15 candidate collections per pair). No adverse gate required A/A controls. Promotion was not measured.

Protocol, declared before measurement: two concurrent pairs per mode, 100,000 operations/side after 1,000 warmups, synchronized future start, 10,000 synthetic retained placements with 64 protected records and 200 synthetic environment entries. Linux Node 26.12.1; exclusive benchmark lock, interleaved 16-CPU sets swapped for pair 2, production guard before/during each pair. All four pairs completed without interruption. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes node-host progress keepalives being delayed or sent early when the operating system adjusts the wall clock during an invocation.

## User Impact

Active node invocations keep their heartbeat interval across wall-clock corrections, avoiding an artificial inactivity timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The progress writer owns this process-local interval. Measuring all three elapsed-time reads with `performance.now()` preserves its existing queue, cancellation, payload, and interval bounds without adding another clock owner.

Thanks @SunnyShu0925 for the fix and regression coverage.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/node-host/node-invoke-progress.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: both added clock-step cases fail on unchanged main (zero heartbeats after a rewind; two after a forward step, each expecting one); all eight tests pass with the fix. The green Vitest run took 317.99 seconds under current host load, primarily worker compilation; the added cases took 8 ms and 194 ms.
- Real production progress writer, real `NodeHostWorkerBridgeClient`, and real timers: after a 1,000 ms wall-clock rewind, a 250 ms heartbeat arrived after **1,251 ms on base** and **252 ms with the fix**. The synthetic probe acknowledges real bridge request frames. A full paired-node/Gateway round-trip was not rerun; this is in-process transport proof.
