prs.title: test(gateway): repair catalog client fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Catalog tests can time out waiting for a provider that never starts because their synthetic clients omit the required connection handshake.

## User Impact

Restores CI coverage for catalog coalescing, progress, budgets and reconnect retention. Production behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regression starts at `219e9181aab075e31903d62a3bb50cf7875ba097` ([#182897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182897)): the visibility owner now trusts the admitted client contract and reads `client?.connect.scopes`. The diagnostic fixture supplied only a connection ID, so the leader rejected while building its visibility key, before snapshot creation or provider enumeration. The test collected that rejection with `Promise.allSettled` and waited indefinitely for the provider's start signal; the follower was never created.

Build catalog clients with the existing `gatewayConnect` fixture and require the real connection shape in the shared test helper. Each caller retains the same client object across requests, preserving the WeakMap identity used for coalescing and retention. Existing assertions and the 120-second timeout are retained.

This predates [#182986](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182986): the failing scope-read commit is already in that merge's parent, `05740a6c078a53fdde9457e783ea8b398472d900`.

## Evidence

Unmodified single-file runs on both requested revisions:

| Revision | Node 26.12.1 | Pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `7b30ad9167e7` | 4 passed, coalesced-follower timeout at 120 s | Same |
| `6188758f^` = `05740a6c078a` | 4 passed, coalesced-follower timeout at 120 s | Same |

Source history narrowed the regression to #182897. Exact adjacent-commit verification under Node passed all five tests on `61164bfcd411` and reproduced the timeout on `219e9181aab0`; the bounded bisect reports `219e9181aab0` as the first bad commit. No test source, assertion or timeout was changed for these runs.

Command for each runtime: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` (or `bun`) followed by `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog-phase-diagnostics.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

With the fix, all five phase-diagnostic tests pass under both runtimes, including the formerly hanging coalesced follower. Focused runs of the five affected test files finish with **54 passed / 1 separately inherited failure** on both Node and Bun. Coalescing, progress, budget, reconnect-retention, permission-scope and caller-identity assertions are retained. Changed-file oxfmt and core-config oxlint pass. Production LOC delta is zero.

The remaining failure is `session-catalog.test.ts` → `keeps a delayed source off the catalog RPC path`: expected `CATALOG_LOADING`, received `pending: true`. The identical single-file run on unchanged base `dde57d3e897e65597b61750b3b431e550f36b04d` fails with **14 passed / 1 failed** on both Node and Bun. [#182242](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182242) (`ae2a9dd8ec74`) introduced fresh authorization, pending progressive pages and awaited non-progressive reads; its plugin tests were updated, but this Gateway integration fixture still assumes the old loading/caching contract. This PR preserves those assertions and does not alter that implementation. That separately inherited failure is not claimed green.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean through P2. The helper's previously observed provider mismatch remains unresolved; operator configuration was unchanged. The fresh reviewer checked scopes, the required handshake type, shared-helper caller migration, object identity and unchanged assertions/timeouts. The simplification pass retained only fixture construction and the shared type correction.


### Exact-head CI and inherited-failure qualification

[Run 40147978172](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40147978172), attempt 1, tested head `2bc9a782be4630eeed6ff3277f6a738151952a06`: **29 jobs passed**. The repaired phase-diagnostic file passed all five tests in the Bun shard; the coalesced-follower case completed in 3 ms. Budget, progress and retention coverage also passed.

The sole non-aggregate failed job is [checks-node-changed-compact-large-17](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40147978172/job/121033597424), solely from the delayed-source assertion described above; `openclaw/ci-gate` is its downstream aggregate failure. The automated comparison labels it **unknown: no matching job on scheduled main**, so attribution rests on the independent unchanged-base Node/Bun reproductions, not a claimed matching-signature table. The producer and relevant test inputs did not change between that baseline and the final rebased parent; this PR's fixture edits preserve the same scope values and object identities. No test assertion or timeout changed.

Security-fast, dependency review and security-sensitive review passed. CI was not rerun. Landing uses the standing exception for this independently proven pre-existing failure; the failed CI result is retained and is not described as green.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PostgreSQL Gateway startup masking an invalid configuration with a main-thread database connection error when shared state already exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

Heartbeat retirement in ec5d369a6f66 (#179387) made the synthetic startup fixture invalid and exposed a missing preparation step. The earlier d0c23802ffb9 (#181224) prepared the first invalid-config pass, but its core-legacy early return can omit plugin metadata. The subsequent legacy-diagnostic pass synchronously loaded plugin discovery policy from PostgreSQL outside admission.

The diagnostics owner now awaits the existing worker-backed policy/inventory preparation before deriving those messages, and both preflight callers await that owner. This completes the diagnostic boundary without a guard exception or another state owner. Production code grows by six lines; the regression adds 65 lines.

## Evidence

- Reproduced at origin/main 418aafaae7e8 with the real CLI, Homebrew PostgreSQL 17.11, and Node 24.22.1, using isolated synthetic state and namespaces. The stack reaches addDoctorLegacyIssues → plugin discovery policy → readConfigMachineState → the PG main-thread guard.

prs.title: fix: preserve automation access for fresh chat after reconnect
prs.body:
Related: #167867

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes incomplete automation lists from a newly submitted administrator message after the Control UI reconnects to an existing conversation.

## User Impact

A fresh message can use the current administrator's automation-management permission. Restored outbox messages, retries, and submissions whose connection changed during preparation keep the existing recovery restrictions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reconnect marker currently describes the resumed session, so it also marks a new foreground submission as recovery. Carry an ephemeral submission-owner check through the existing send path, and omit recovery metadata only for its first, still-current request. The check is never persisted in the outbox. Detached commands use the same distinction.

This changes the UI's classification of new input; it does not remove the Gateway's replay guard or revive an old grant. The change needs the product/security decision discussed in #167867. The issue author's later `automations status` success is useful context; our reproduction exercised an inventory read and observed caller scope after a reconnect, rather than treating scheduler status alone as proof of management authority.

## Evidence

- On the original 2026.10.7 baseline, the foreground regression failed before the fix. Three focused UI files then passed 189 tests (41.61 seconds). An authenticated browser reconnect followed by an actual automation inventory request changed from one caller-visible job to all eight jobs present at that test time.
- On upstream baseline `e1e498602cec224ef4adb16f13512ca6aea26d98`, `pnpm --dir ui test --maxWorkers=1 src/pages/chat/chat-send-submit.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-outbox-transient-recovery.test.ts` passed all 176 tests in 19.46 seconds. The port preserves newer session/admission handling.
- Tests cover fresh text and detached command input, connection replacement during preparation, durable offline restoration, and an explicit retry. No visual layout change.
- Formatting, focused syntax lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent autoreview of the upstream candidate reported no actionable P0-P2 findings. The review did not execute tests.
- Simplification pass: reuse the existing connection, account, and conversation owners; no new persistent state or manager. The forbidden line-limit suppression has been removed. The existing route/settings wait now lives beside its underlying settings-wait owner, and the captured submission scope is reused. Focused syntax lint passes without a suppression.

The live browser evidence applies to the original installed baseline, not to a deployment of current main. Type-aware lint was stopped because its local graph was too costly alongside a serving Gateway; no successful type-aware result is claimed. Broad build/typecheck/test coverage and CI duration remain for PR CI.

## Review follow-up

- Removed the `max-lines` suppression reported by ClawSweeper; no ratchet or baseline exception was added. After the refactor, the same three focused UI files pass all 176 tests (19.97 seconds).
- Added a real browser/Gateway regression with synthetic inference only: after reconnect a fresh administrator inventory request must reveal a foreign-session automation, while offline queued input must remain caller-scoped and hide it. It waits for the original session identity before disconnecting, so the original reconnect classification is exercised.
- Pinned candidate `16dc493f860d18169e0ff4e1a817b447cd3c2e46` passed the [isolated browser CI job](https://github.com/lucafucci/openclaw/actions/runs/40133087221/job/120988800181): max-lines ratchet, formatting, all 176 focused UI tests, runtime build, and the new real-browser/Gateway test (17.33 seconds for the scenario). The foreign-session inventory assertions run before the supplementary request-metadata assertions. Only inference is synthetic; browser pairing, WebSocket reconnect, chat admission, automation tool dispatch, and inventory are real.
- Proof limits: durable restoration and explicit retry are covered by the existing focused UI tests. Browser non-admin and revoked-device denial at the final effect are not newly demonstrated by this browser test. Existing Gateway admission/commit-fence tests support those separate boundaries; no claim of complete end-to-end negative coverage is made.
- Independent review of these follow-up changes found no actionable P0-P2 issue; it was static and did not execute the runtime test.

The second review identified the E2E ownership inventory expectation as incomplete. Commit `b3d87df706b8a9946034755bb61e9f9aa46980ab` adds the serial private-server scenario to `serialGatewayFiles`, which also feeds `realGatewayFiles`; the assertions are unchanged. The isolated VPS run passed all 13 ownership-contract tests and all 176 focused UI tests on that head. It also found a formatting issue, fixed in `7f2acdb440e5d52ae101bc9d9578af5bfd13d617`. The runner now compares the explicit prepared ratchet base without requiring unavailable shallow history. The full runtime build stopped at its memory-admission guard under a 4 GiB job budget; that run is not green. The current head is queued for a 6 GiB job with a 2 GiB host reserve, waiting for capacity. The successful browser runtime evidence above remains explicitly pinned to the preceding head. `openclaw/vps-authority-proof` reports the current result or pending reason.

The classification decision and security-owner review remain required. No maintainer approval is claimed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's production unused-file check reports a retired session runtime-context helper that remained after its last automation callers moved result publication to the conversation-result owner. The orphaned file keeps the dead-code gate red even though no supported runtime, package, or plugin path can reach it.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. Current automation result publication, transcript persistence, lifecycle and current-authority checks, idempotency, configuration, data, dependencies, and public APIs remain unchanged; this PR only removes unreachable internal source.

## Why This Change Was Made

The automation cutover removed both production callers and their test references but left the helper definition behind. Source and history inspection found no remaining internal import, package export, build entry, Plugin SDK surface, generator route, or documented consumer, so deleting the defining file is the smallest complete repair. Adding an analyzer ignore or artificial entrypoint would instead preserve dead code.

## Evidence

- The exact candidate passed changed-file formatting and every selected production and test type graph: core tests, core, UI, extensions, extension tests, scripts, and test root.
- The maintained production unused-file scan no longer reports `src/sessions/runtime-context.ts`. Its remaining entries are pre-existing generator-source roots outside this PR; the full-tree scan also contains no runtime-context helper row.
- The maintained unused-export scans contain no reference to `appendSessionRuntimeContext` or this file. They still expose unrelated baseline backlog, so this PR does not claim the entire dead-code aggregate is green by itself.
- Hosted CI, automated review, and independent engineering review continue on the published head.

prs.title: perf: reuse validated entry facts for cold history accounting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold history accounting rereads the full session entry and participant projection when the actor already holds a valid full entry without a complete transcript snapshot.

## User Impact

The affected accounting request uses six SQL statements instead of eight. Across the complete synthetic Gateway workload, history accounting/display falls from 27 to 25 statements with six worker requests unchanged. A neighboring activity-summary reader adds one projection read in the measured pair, so their combined conservative improvement is 38 to 37 statements, with eight requests unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing full entry receipt through the existing history-worker path. The receiver continues to validate the session, scoped write token, and absence of uncommitted writes. Partial entries remain excluded. There is no new cache, schema, SQL syntax, generation, public API, or transcript identity fold.

## Evidence

### Acceptance rule registered before runtime measurement

Measure the frozen synthetic Gateway workload through its real WebSocket transport:
first turn, ten warm turns, second session with a spawned child, and the first turn
after restart. Keep cold and warm results separate. Count successful SQL statements,
worker requests, and main-thread statements by operation and phase.

The proposed change carries an already validated entry to the history reader when
the actor owns entry facts without a complete transcript snapshot. It must remove
the repeated entry and participant reads in that case (two statements per affected
accounting read), with identical accounting and history results. Transcript payload,
identity, projection, transaction, and write-invalidation behavior must remain intact.
Cold `session.turn.prepare` has six distinct reads; no saving there is presumed.

Use three alternating baseline/candidate pairs when host load is below 64 and
internal free space is at least 12 GiB; otherwise use one pair and report the limit.
For each phase and shared read family, report statement/request/main medians and
ranges. Warm requests and main-thread SQL must not rise. No count reduction means
reject the patch. A 20% regression in any user-facing metric stops the change.

Timing claims require five interleaved samples per arm, the campaign timing lock,
and load below 24. Without those conditions, report counts only; make no latency or
CPU speed claim. The frozen observer's retired causal-context support does not
justify treating background-contaminated window counts as causal counts.


### Measured result

One baseline/candidate pair of the frozen v3.1.4 synthetic Gateway workload completed through real WebSocket transport, including 14 turns, history/control RPCs, spawned child, cron, compaction, restart, and clean shutdown. Baseline `de39463cef3` has unchanged production from `541a09d301b7`; measured candidate `6e0fad57e71` is production-byte-identical to final head `e8cc9e58791`. The final delta only deletes an invalid test assertion.

| Count | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Cold preparation SQL / requests | 18 / 14 | 18 / 14 |
| First turn preparation | 6 / 1 | 6 / 1 |
| Second session preparation, including child | 6 / 2 | 6 / 2 |
| Restart preparation | 6 / 1 | 6 / 1 |
| Ten warm preparations | 0 / 10 | 0 / 10 |
| History SQL / requests | 27 / 6 | 25 / 6 |
| Exceptional second-session accounting SQL | 8 | 6 |
| History plus activity-summary SQL / requests | 38 / 8 | 37 / 8 |
| Warm-turn median SQL [min–max] | 52 [49–70] | 51 [50–70] |
| Warm-turn SQL p95 | 70 | 70 |
| Warm-turn median requests [min–max] | 12.5 [11–20] | 12.5 [12–21] |
| Warm-turn request p95 | 20 | 21 |
| Ten warm turns total SQL / requests | 552 / 138 | 545 / 136 |
| Cold and warm runtime MAIN | 0 | 0 |
| Whole workload SQL / requests / bootstrap MAIN | 3,014 / 802 / 96 | 2,993 / 802 / 95 |

Cold cells each have one sample, so their median and range are the recorded count. Warm distributions describe the ten different warm turns within that pair, not ten independent full-workload samples. The attributable saving is two history statements; the larger whole-workload difference is not claimed as this patch's gain.

The first warm window increases 53→69 SQL and 13→21 requests, crossing the 20% stop threshold. Exact attribution accounts for all +16 SQL/+8 requests: lease bookkeeping +10/+5, plugin metadata refresh +0/+1, plugin metadata read +1/+1, and lease acquire +5/+1. Their respective whole-workload SQL/request counts are identical on both arms: 19/11, 9/1, 3/3, and 5/1. This is a phase-placement change in unchanged background operations, not an added-work or latency claim. The request p95 increase is disclosed for the same reason.

Across the selected cold/warm phases, shared entry-row reads are 86→79, participant reads 14→12, and watermark/projection reads 14→15. Whole-workload actor hydration is unchanged at 83 SQL / five requests. The added activity-summary projection read is conservatively charged against the two saved history reads: net one statement saved across those two readers. Cold preparation's six reads fetch distinct retained-window, full-entry, participant, transcript-version, pending-input, and idempotency facts; they remain intact.

### Design and retained boundaries

Use retained entry facts only when snapshots are full. Carry the entry's existing scoped write token and dependency scopes. The receiver remains the validity owner. Transcript projection, payload, visible-identity reads, and snapshot transactions remain independent; missing transcript facts still use the existing projection reader.

Accepted edge: a cell without projection/context statistics can now supply an entry receipt. The path-alias helper previously assumed such a receipt was absent; its replacement assumption that any retained receipt must still be valid was also too strict. Delete that incidental assertion. The test still requires primary-store receipts to be rejected by the other database and verifies both databases' independent history/accounting. The receiving worker may correctly reject a stale own-store receipt.

Production delta: +6/-6 lines. Final path-alias helper delta: -3 lines. The existing accounting regression is extended to exercise both complete and entry-only actor states, including stale-after-write invalidation.

### Validation

- Frozen harness integrity: 36/36 files match the frozen hashes.
- Regression red on unchanged production: exactly two repeated entry/participant reads in the entry-only case.
- History, replica, projection-fact, entry-residency, and prompt-prefix suites: 70 tests passed.
- Two isolated Codex review rounds completed scoped-clean through P2. Later changes only remove the invalid shared test assertion.
- Focused path-alias SQLite proof passed. Native PostgreSQL proof for the final minimal helper passed (one selected case; six unselected), including schema/trigger parity. Earlier failures were stale test expectations, not classified as inherited.
- PostgreSQL owner approved production `62c2f3330f1a`; coordinator explicitly confirmed approval stands for final head `e8cc9e587911` and instructed landing.
- Baseline CPU profile: three synthetic ingress events, clean shutdown, 29 process/thread profiles; attribution only, no speed claim.
- Canonical Knip 6.40.0 production/full-tree/scripts scans completed on baseline and candidate: 69/83/1,136 findings on both, exact sets identical, zero added or removed. Final-head lint/types/source-contracts/architecture/prompt-snapshot/baseline-ratchet CI jobs passed. Exact final-head CI run [40146854752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146854752) completed successfully: 39 successful jobs / 25 skipped, including all three PostgreSQL shards and `openclaw/ci-gate`. No inherited-failure exception or CI retry used.

### Measurement command and limits

Frozen `sqlharness-v3.1.4/measure.py --repo <lane> --out <proof> --sha <head> --repetitions 1 --scratch-root <internal fixture>` through the ordinary proof slot. Baseline load reached 73 and candidate began at 67, so the preregistered single-pair fallback applies. Counts only; latency remains unmeasured. CPU profiling uses the committed `scripts/bench-ingress-polling.mts --cpu-profile` workload with synthetic events. An earlier QA-channel profile setup failed before any turn and supplies no product verdict.

### Open-PR compatibility

The shared index refreshed at 2026-10-25T00:52:23+00:00 covers 2,671 other open main-targeted PRs and identifies #177242 (`c7f91fb698c4`) as the only overlap across all four changed files. Final-head merge-tree comparison gives 17 existing conflict paths and 15 marker hunks on both base and candidate, with zero added. Release-branch backports are excluded. Current-main merge preview at `bf7cce652226` is clean.

prs.title: fix(feishu): preserve bot mentions across command admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent loses track of which bot was addressed when Feishu strips the receiving bot's own mention from the message in multi-bot conversations.

## User Impact

The agent now receives the full mention context in groups and DMs, while command matching, authorization, debounce admission, sequential routing, and mention-prefixed `/stop` and `/btw` behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared mention renderer mixed the agent-facing message with command parsing, so stripping the bot mention for commands also hid it from the agent. The renderer now keeps all mentions, and only the separate command projection is normalized at the parser consumers and command-decision owners, including transcribed-audio probes. For cross-app bot events, the existing local API verification still decides whether the receiving bot was addressed, and only that verified identity is rendered; the restriction on other recipients and admission policy are unchanged, and the duplicated event clone/reparse path is removed. No config, SDK, protocol, schema, dependency, or authorization-policy change.

This continues closed PR #117906, rebuilt on current main with the missing command, debounce, and verified-identity coverage. Production LOC +28/-33; tests +148/-45; docs +2/-0.

## Evidence

- Red on main: 5 expected failures covering preserved DM and group agent bodies, separate command bodies, and the locally verified cross-app receiving-bot identity.
- Green: 124/124 across eight owning and consumer test files, including existing rejection of unverifiable bot identities and other app-scoped recipients, plus a real receive, debounce, and sequential regression that holds an ordinary turn, admits mentioned `/stop` and `/btw` immediately, and then checks ordinary-message FIFO order.
- Targeted typecheck, oxfmt, the line-cap ratchet, docs listing, and `git diff --check` passed; oxlint reports no new diagnostics (one existing `no-redundant-type-constituents` finding on the broadcast `agentClaim` union reproduces unchanged on main).
- `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen` left all six generated files byte-identical (snapshot token delta 0); per-message content now includes the receiving-bot mention, sized by the incoming event.
- Independent review: clean, no actionable findings.
- Gap: no live multi-bot Feishu or Gateway run; the synthetic tests prove the agent input and control admission but not that a live model answers instead of choosing `NO_REPLY`, so PR CI remains the broad proof.

Fixes #72504

prs.title: perf(plugins): trim metadata refresh lease verification
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-ready plugin metadata refresh makes eight worker round trips to verify the same lease, including checks around observation and completed bookkeeping.

## User Impact

The refresh now uses **24 SQL statements and 7 worker requests**, down from **34 and 12**, while retaining custody checks before publication. No schema, configuration, or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove five observation-only verification calls on fresh acquisition. Keep local cancellation/refusal checks, generic admission and settlement, verification after awaited configuration preparation immediately before registry publication, transaction/commit custody, error-path checks, and runtime invalidation's verification after its awaited loader import.

Nested lifecycle entry retains its original database verification: a retained async resource can carry a completed outer lease whose abort signal remains un-aborted. The existing regression caught this distinction, and the final patch preserves it. Observation and bookkeeping may finish after expiry; protected application cannot.

Production is net **−1 line**, without a cache, generation, identity change, or SQL rewrite. The opt-in startup benchmark now waits for the real post-ready registry task so thread profiles include it.

## Evidence

Frozen observer v3.1.4, exact baseline `241633d2b133` and candidate `f015c0eebe5`. One source-attributed count pair reuses the completed Linux baseline and runs the candidate on macOS under the shared proof slot. All 36 frozen hashes match. No latency or CPU improvement claim; this is not a controlled cross-platform timing comparison.

| Per metadata refresh | Baseline SQL / requests | Candidate SQL / requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Acquire | 5 / 1 | 5 / 1 |
| Verify | 16 / 8 | 6 / 3 |
| Read install records | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
| Protected publication | 9 / 1 | 9 / 1 |
| Release | 3 / 1 | 3 / 1 |
| **Total** | **34 / 12** | **24 / 7** |

Target MAIN is zero in both arms. The actual isolated Gateway passes all 14 turns, control-plane RPCs, cron, compaction, restart, shutdown, and child cleanup.

| Warm ten-turn counts | Baseline median / p95 [min–max] | Candidate median / p95 [min–max] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| SQL | 51 / 68 [50–68] | 50 / 64 [50–64] |
| Requests | 12.5 / 20 [12–20] | 12 / 18 [12–18] |
| MAIN | 0 / 0 [0–0] | 0 / 0 [0–0] |

Whole workload: **2,981 / 801 / 92 → 2,977 / 791 / 94** SQL / requests / MAIN. Whole-workload variation is reported separately from the ten removed target statements. Five-minute connected idle is 106 / 39 / 0 → 106 / 40 / 0, or 21.2 SQL/min unchanged and 7.8 → 8 requests/min.

The two raw phase increases above 20% were stopped for source attribution, not dismissed as spread. Connect is 45 SQL / 14 requests → 235 / 20: unchanged agent-database opening moved from boot into connect (179 → 181 SQL); combined boot/connect/first-turn is 788 / 205 / 47 → 789 / 201 / 48. Idle settling is 7 / 5 → 105 / 15: unchanged memory-index work moved from compaction into settling, including publication (42 SQL), source replacement (27), and vector setup (8). Combined compaction/settling is 247 / 43 / 0 → 253 / 42 / 0. The MAIN increase is exactly the unchanged Darwin-only `PRAGMA checkpoint_fullfsync = 1` once at boot and once at restart; every other MAIN site count is identical. **The coordinator explicitly accepted these cells as phase placement and the MAIN delta as a platform artifact, and authorized landing this reviewed head.**

The frozen observer loses the current async context on this base, so this reports raw phase windows and source/request joins without causal-turn claims. Baseline startup profiling produced 23 nonempty thread profiles through registry-task completion; it is diagnostic evidence only.

Validation on final head:

- All 108 focused checks pass: 54 lease/registry owner tests, 11 prompt-prefix tests, and 43 startup benchmark tests. The deterministic verify-count regression is red on baseline (8, expected 3) and green on candidate. Expiry during config preparation cannot durably publish or invalidate the runtime. SQLite and PostgreSQL post-ready conformance pass all four selected tests, including no MAIN PostgreSQL SQL and custody-loss refusal.
- Formatting and targeted type-aware lint pass. Exact-head CI [40141050101](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40141050101) passes selected types, lint, source contracts, architecture, Madge, and baseline/dialect/worker ratchets. Canonical Knip 6.40.0 completes all three scans on both arms: production 69 = 69, full-tree 83 = 83, scripts 1,136 = 1,136; all 1,235 unique existing signatures match, with zero new findings, zero in changed files, and no resolution failures/timeouts.
- The only behavioral CI failure is the timeout-cleanup retry case in `server-plugins.lifecycle.test.ts`, [job 121013036167](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40141050101/job/121013036167): expected `restartRequired: false`, received `true`. Focused baseline and candidate runs each reproduce the identical assertion (1 failed, 3 skipped); the test and `src/plugins/lifecycle.ts` are byte-identical. The coordinator assigned this inherited failure to the existing main-repair lane. No assertion or timeout was changed here.
- Exact-candidate published-driver update passes in [Package Acceptance 40141160572](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40141160572), using trusted workflow source `a2fbd0305d88` and package source `f015c0eebe5`.
- Two Codex review rounds are clean. The coordinator authorized one additional delta-only review for the CI-required restoration of nested admission; that review is also clean. PostgreSQL owner review approves final head `f015c0eebe5`, including the restored boundary.
- The refreshed open-PR index has only #137014 overlapping these files, at unchanged head `9d9481f94763`. Base-only versus base-plus-candidate comparison has the same 285 inherited conflict paths and zero added paths or hunks. Candidate merges cleanly with current main `55ce216cffd3`.

Reproduction: run the immutable v3.1.4 `measure.py` with `--repo <checkout> --out <proof> --scratch-root <internal-scratch> --sha <exact-head> --repetitions 1`. Fixtures are synthetic; no operator state, rows, messages, or credentials are inputs or published evidence.

<details>
<summary>Acceptance rule recorded before the first run</summary>


# Plugin metadata lease verification

Acceptance rule, recorded before the first run.

Flow: a real isolated Gateway's post-ready `plugin-registry` maintenance with a
synthetic config and derived plugin inventory. Use the frozen campaign v3.1.4
workload, observer and causality instrumentation, pinned to each measured head.
No operator config, state, logs or model credentials are inputs.

Count acquisition, verification, registry publication and release separately.
The baseline attribution is eight `stateLease.verify` requests, two statements
each, per successful refresh. The candidate must use three, removing ten SQL
statements and five requests per refresh. Registry publication, transaction
custody checks, release and runtime MAIN must not increase. Re-run the real
Gateway workload on both heads; failure to reproduce the eight verifies stops
this optimization. Report whole-phase and warm-turn counts separately from the
attributed metadata operations.

Use three alternating baseline/candidate pairs when load is below 64 and at least
12 GiB is free internally, otherwise one pair with explicit source attribution.
Keep cold startup, post-ready maintenance and warm turns separate. Report median,
p95 and min-max for each measured count. CPU profiles cover each Gateway thread.
No wall-clock or CPU A/B claim without the campaign timing lock and load below 24;
if timing is attempted, use at least five interleaved samples per arm. A 20% rise
in any user-facing metric stops landing for attribution and disposition.

The focused regression counts the real worker's verification requests around one
refresh and checks that expiry during configuration preparation cannot publish.
Existing native/worker authority, transaction-custody and PostgreSQL post-ready
conformance tests remain applicable. PostgreSQL review is required before landing.


</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Recurring plugin-policy reads allocate wrapper construction state even on cache hits, while Codex rebuilds all normalized plugin entries for each live config read.

## User Impact

No intentional behavior change. This is a small reduction in recurring plugin overhead. Live enablement, getter/call admission, receiver binding, and retirement checks remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate wrapper construction from primitive/cached returns, using the existing binding cache. Let the existing enablement owner consume `rootConfig` and its publication-owned policy, removing Codex’s explicit fresh normalization. Explicit normalized policy still takes precedence, and public normalization remains mutable.

Runtime production delta: **+3 LOC**, excluding tests, documentation, and the reproducible measurement script. The extra construction boundary prevents closure allocation on cache hits; no new cache or compatibility path is introduced.

## Evidence

Acceptance was recorded before candidate measurement: 40 synthetic plugin entries/policies, 200,000 warm operations per side, two concurrent counterbalanced pairs with swapped interleaved CPUs; timing/GC untraced and allocation in separate passes. Matching results and lower allocation or CPU are required without material adverse deltas. Four matched A/A controls are required before rejecting on noisy GC/promotion/max-pause signals. No such adverse total-GC, loop, or maximum-pause result occurred.

Linux sandbox, Node 26.12.1. Baseline: `5895dc953bae`; the measured owners were unchanged by subsequent main rebases. Each binding operation scans 40 policies. All checksums and config payload identities matched. The shared guard delayed two pair starts for dirty-page pressure; no measured pair was interrupted.

prs.title: fix(telegram): deliver questions during progress draft retirement
prs.body:
Fixes #182624

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native Telegram questions being silently dropped when progress-draft retirement overlaps their delivery.

## User Impact

Native `ask_user` questions arrive once with their buttons and registered message identity, even when the current progress card is being cleared. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Progress retirement and provider delivery now run on Telegram's existing draft-event queue. The queue owns the complete delivery operation, so clearing and reopening a preview cannot interrupt question finalization. The old delivery-internal drain waits are removed. Delivery still propagates errors and settles buffered replies after cancellation; progress retains its existing best-effort behavior.

## Evidence

- **Red on main `f310725180103600d849d6ce94ff0bba7fc40da5`:** the deterministic regression returned `visibleReplySent: false` and sent no question. The stopped-stream window starts at `bot-message-dispatch-draft.ts:231`, between `clear()` and `forceNewMessage()`.
- **Green on local candidate `fe6946b1ad412`:** 126 tests passed across six focused files. The regression checks one question send, visible delivery, its keyboard, question registration, deletion of the old preview, and retention of the question. It uses the real dispatch callbacks, draft stream, and lane deliverer with controlled Bot API promises and fake timers.
- The new regression took **2.67 seconds**. Its complete existing lifecycle suite passed 12 tests in 358.80 seconds including a cold worker build/imports. The baseline filtered run took 55.99 seconds. The other five files passed 114 tests, including unchanged empty-card cleanup, retained progress, queued turns, error propagation, and streaming behavior.
- Changed-file typed oxlint, oxfmt, docs MDX validation, and `git diff --check` passed. `pr-simplify` completed; Codex autoreview is **scoped-clean through P2**, with no findings.
- Fresh main `6113057491a2` was merged after the fixture correction; integration did not alter the affected Telegram source or regression. PR CI validates the integrated head.
- **CI correction:** [the first CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40144345428/job/121023093086) caught TS2532 in the new fixture lookup. An explicit successful factory-result check fixes it. The exact owning test typecheck project (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`) passes locally, and the race regression passes again in 3.09 seconds (399.26 seconds including cold build/imports). Production code is unchanged by this correction.
- **Current-head CI passed:** [run 40146040122](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146040122), head `ce6352706b706ea802eec3d0a682156013be57f4`, including `check-test-types`. All 56 jobs completed successfully or were intentionally skipped; elapsed time from run creation to the final job was 0:09:12.
- Live Gateway/channel end-to-end tests, Crabbox/Testbox leases, and full local typechecks were skipped per maintainer policy. The deterministic owner regression and PR CI supply the intended proof gates.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and change size</summary>

Baseline regression:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.final-delivery-lifecycle.test.ts -t 'delivers a question once'
```

Fixed regression and its existing tests:


Focused sibling files:

```sh

  extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.progress-card.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.progress-lifecycle.telegram-http.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.preview.telegram-http.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/lane-delivery.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.test.ts
```

Production: **+46 / -43 (net +3)**. Tests: **+80 / -0**. Docs: **+2 / -0**. The small production increase preserves distinct delivery error/cancellation settlement and best-effort progress contracts while reusing one queue and deleting the obsolete drain-only path.

prs.title: fix(cron): keep native CLI runs on their own login
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbound native-login CLI automations using host inference credentials restored by environment overrides instead of the CLI's own login.

## User Impact

Native-only jobs exclude Gateway credentials while retaining context, thinking, and generated tool-policy settings. Jobs with saved inference bindings keep using their recorded account.

Paired nodes can update independently. The Gateway sends `nativeAuthOnly` only when the node advertises `claude-cli-native-auth-v1` through node capabilities. Older nodes receive the existing request and retain their node-local credential behavior. Updated nodes also strip their local provider credentials after their new capability is approved.

## Why This Change Was Made

On main `219e9181aab075e31903d62a3bb50cf7875ba097`, `src/agents/cli-runner/execution-env.ts:30–51` can restore credentials through configured or prepared overlays after cleanup. The shared environment owner now filters credentials after every overlay, uses the execution host's provider inventory, and omits prepared secret input for native-only execution. Separate preparation resets preserve Gemini's generated runtime settings and tool restrictions.

The reviewed revision sent the new node field unconditionally (`src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.ts:82`). Released node decoders reject unknown fields (`src/node-host/invoke-agent-cli-claude-params.ts:215`). Reuse the node manifest's capability advertisement and the Gateway registry's effective capabilities to gate that field. Gateway credential withholding applies to every node, independently of this gate. There is no retry fallback or new handshake, configuration option, stored-data schema, or protocol version.

## Evidence

- Regression red on `175883f1e957`: a native-only request to the legacy-node simulation fails with `INVALID_REQUEST`; its supporting-node control passes. The node advertisement assertion also fails before the advertisement is added.
- After integrating main: all 252 tests in eight focused files pass, covering node negotiation and inventory, the node receiver with a real synthetic child process, CLI preparation, spawning, and execution/history ownership. The existing Gemini generated-settings regression remains green. Gateway negotiation cases take 2 ms each; the inventory advertisement case takes 16 ms. Full local groups took 30.25 s (Gateway), 476.13 s (infrastructure), 172.94 s (spawn), and 190.00 s (native execution/history), plus 115.94 s compiler preparation on the loaded macOS host.
- Independent Codex review of the compatibility correction is clean at P0–P2. Targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass after integrating main.
- Full PR delta against integrated main: production +108/−37 (net +71), tests +172/−19 (net +153), docs +13. The compatibility correction itself adds 12 production lines and 25 test lines.
- Exact-head CI is green for `b646c1465541136d0ce04de04b11bd8c9fe1de3d`: [run 40143359797](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40143359797). No rerun or inherited-failure exception was needed.

No live vendor-login, installed-stable upgrade, production Gateway, or lease was used. Focused boundary regressions and exact-head PR CI are the requested validation scope; this does not claim live provider or upgrade proof. ClawSweeper's exact-head review reports no discrete code defect and confirms the compatibility repair. It retains a needs-human/security proof hold for live account-isolation and installed-stable upgrade traces; these remain deferred under the requested focused-regression and PR-CI scope. No stored data format changed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Git backup reports that emit terminal controls from repository paths, commit subjects, restore metadata, or diagnostics.

## User Impact

Human-readable reports preserve printable Unicode and deliberate tab/newline separators while escaping control-bearing fields. Git operations, JSON values, returned results, and recorded diagnostics remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the canonical `sanitizeTerminalText` at each terminal report boundary. The shared backup-outcome helper also sanitizes its ledger-failure warning once, covering the same path for Git and archive backups. The snapshot mock now preserves real exports; the owning generator removes its obsolete baseline exemption.

Thanks @Alix-007 for the fix, regression tests, and original real-CLI proof.

## Evidence

- Both new command regressions fail on unchanged main production code (2 failed, 17 skipped; 224.27s runner duration): raw repository and restore paths reach terminal output. All 19 command tests pass with the fix (222.97s runner duration).
- Regressions preserve raw JSON, result identities, Unicode, and report separators. The existing push-diagnostic test checks safe terminal output alongside unchanged credential-redacted persistence. The existing archive-failure regression now uses a control-bearing ledger error.
- Targeted typed oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. The focused snapshot diagnostic/persistence test passes (1/1), all archive tests pass (3/3), and the existing corrupt-SQLite outcome-warning test passes (1/1). Independent Codex review through P2 is scoped-clean. After integrating current main, all 22 command/archive tests pass (255.26s runner duration), the snapshot diagnostic/persistence test passes (1/1), and the corrupt-SQLite outcome-warning test passes (1/1). prs.title: perf(workboard): fold placement precondition into write
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every successful Sessions-board move reads its placement revision immediately before writing, although the caller already supplies the expected revision. This removes that redundant read from the storage owner.

## User Impact

Moves retain their results and conflict handling with one fewer SQL statement per successful move. This is an on-demand Workboard improvement: the retained live-traffic extracts do not show this statement shape, so no steady-traffic reduction is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expected absence uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(board_id, session_key) DO NOTHING`; an expected revision uses `UPDATE ... WHERE board_id = ? AND session_key = ? AND updated_at = ?`. Both consume the affected-row count. The existing transaction, board/spec/column validation, write authority, notification behavior, and monotonic revision remain. Rejected moves still execute one conditional statement. There is no schema, SDK, permission, retention, or transaction-boundary change, and no new cache or retry. Production is seven lines smaller.

## Evidence

The acceptance rule was published before measurement and is committed in `scripts/perf/workboard-placement.md`. Run the existing workload with `--placements --prepare --root <fresh-root> --output <report> --waves 10 --clients 1`: one cold insertion and ten warm moves through authenticated loopback WebSocket transport to an isolated synthetic Gateway. The target is one fewer placement point SELECT per successful move, unchanged owner requests/MAIN, and every requested column visible.

Both revisions completed all eleven moves. Counts below use the unchanged frozen v3.1.4 observer; warm cells are median / p95 [min–max]. MAIN means SQL on the Gateway main thread.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Placement point SELECTs, eleven moves | 11 | 0 |
| Placement writes, eleven moves | 11 | 11 |
| Cold move SQL / requests / MAIN | 11 / 7 / 0 | 10 / 8 / 0 |
| Warm move SQL | 9 / 12 [9–12] | 8 / 12 [8–12] |
| Warm move requests | 5 / 5 [5–5] | 5 / 5 [5–5] |
| Warm move MAIN | 0 | 0 |
| Ten warm moves, total SQL | 93 | 84 |
| Frozen control, whole SQL / requests / MAIN | 2,936 / 760 / 96 | 2,928 / 764 / 94 |
| Frozen control, warm SQL | 50.5 / 69 [50–69] | 50 / 63 [50–63] |
| Frozen control, warm requests | 12 / 19 [12–19] | 12 / 15 [12–15] |
| Frozen control, warm MAIN | 0 | 0 |

The control completed startup, all turns, compaction, restart, and shutdown. Per-thread CPU profiles include the placement writer (47 baseline and 42 candidate profiles). One baseline/candidate pair uses the campaign's loaded-host count allowance. No CPU-speed or latency claim is made; no qualified timing samples were collected.

Raw increases were investigated rather than discarded:

- Cold requests 7→8: the same single ACP batch read shifted from setup into the cold phase; whole placement-run task requests are 82→82.
- First warm move SQL 9→12: an unchanged four-statement transcript-projection transaction shifted into this phase. Whole projection read/write counts remain 1→1; BEGIN IMMEDIATE 55→55 and COMMIT 76→76. The placement itself saves one statement.
- Placement shutdown SQL 17→24: seven schema/config reads occur during the unchanged Gateway owner-lease release in a native child process, not Gateway MAIN.
- Control boot SQL 309→534 and compaction SQL 109→142: schema/admission initialization shifts between phases; boot adds 100 DDL statements and compaction adds 19, with identical whole-run DDL counts. Control connect requests 17→29 are execute requests shifted between phases; whole execute requests remain 405→405.
- Control's net four extra requests are unchanged background tasks: session-entry-list +3, lifecycle-artifact-plan +1, prewarm +1, pending-archives +1, prepared-model-catalog +1, proactive-jobs +1, deletion snapshot −1, scan −1, and plugin-state entries −2. The control executes no placement writes. All core source files are unchanged; no caching, invalidation, or routing path changed. This follows the campaign's per-operation attribution rule, not a claim that raw totals are equal.

The first candidate attempt stalled during model-catalog preparation before any placement. It was stopped and retained as a setup failure; a fresh-state run on the identical head/workload succeeded, as did the control. The cause is not established and this PR does not claim to fix it.

The deterministic SQLite count regression fails on the baseline and passes on the candidate. SQLite owner tests pass 9/9. Native PostgreSQL 17 passes all six applicable behavior/authority cases, with three SQLite-specific fixtures skipped; schema conformance passes. PostgreSQL review explicitly approves this exact head. Two Codex review rounds completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Exact-head [CI 40142781126](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142781126) succeeds: 39 jobs passed, 26 skipped, including all three PostgreSQL shards, types, lint, source contracts, Madge, and T1/dialect ratchets. T1 is 170→170; dialect findings 0→0. The three canonical Knip scans match exactly: 1,136 script, 69 production, and 81 full-tree findings, zero new. Local type-aware lint refused the mandated external virtual-store layout; passing CI supplies that gate without bypassing it.

The refreshed complete open-main PR index lists no other PR touching these four files, so there are no new overlap conflicts. Existing validation and authority checks remain; no new accepted concurrency edge is introduced.

prs.title: fix(openai): realtime voice sockets bypass the managed proxy on Bun
prs.body:
Related: #175794. The landed #175886 repaired the media worker; this follow-up repairs the three realtime sockets owned by the Gateway process.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes OpenAI realtime voice bypassing `proxy.proxyUrl` on Bun Gateways, which breaks voice on hosts that require a managed proxy for internet access.

## User Impact

Realtime voice and its browser and Gateway sidebands follow the configured managed proxy on Bun. A refused tunnel fails without a direct connection. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bun substitutes its native adapter for bare `ws` imports, bypassing the Node HTTP hooks used by the managed proxy. The three socket constructors now use the existing SDK WebSocket loader, which loads the installed implementation. Proxy routing remains owned by the managed proxy lifecycle.

The affected voice, FaceTime, and native Talk tests retain their existing behavior coverage by mocking the SDK constructor. The real-proxy regression additionally resolves the runtime's native bare package entry: Vitest otherwise aliases `ws` to the installed implementation and hides this production defect.

Original fix and live Gateway evidence by @MertBasar0.

## Evidence

- Current-main baseline `f31072518010`, pinned Bun: both real managed-proxy regressions fail for the intended reasons. The proxy-only hostname is resolved directly (`ENOTFOUND`), and the refused loopback tunnel is bypassed (`connect()` resolves). The original test passed on the base until its Vitest alias masking was removed.
- Head: admitted CONNECT reaches the synthetic server and completes session readiness; refusal rejects with no direct connection. All 162 targeted native Talk, voice, sideband, proxy, and FaceTime tests passed across 11 files (1339.47 s runner wall time on the loaded host). After merging current main, all 14 affected files matched those tested inputs; the four proxy/sideband tests passed again.
- Typed oxlint for all changed extension/core files, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent diff review through P2 found no actionable issues.
- Exact-head [CI run 40146163501](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146163501) is green. Supplemental `check-changed` passed its typechecks, ratchets, formatting, and targeted lint; its whole-tree dead-export scan reported unused exports across 101 unchanged files, with no reported file in this patch. That local scan is recorded as failed.
- Production: +3/-3, net 0. Tests: +322/-15, net +307. The added tests protect real proxy admission/refusal and the two distinct private sideband constructors; no production test seam was added.
- Contributor [live Bun Gateway proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176567#issuecomment-6336966992): isolated Gateway `talk.session.create` bypassed a refusing proxy on the parent; the contributor head used CONNECT for admission/refusal with zero direct external sockets. The admitted tunnel returned OpenAI's placeholder-key rejection.

A completed authenticated voice conversation and live browser/WebRTC sidebands were not repeated locally; local proof uses real sockets and the real managed-proxy lifecycle with synthetic endpoints. The contributor's live proof establishes external TLS routing, not a completed voice conversation.

prs.title: fix(daemon): keep schtasks SQLite lease-read retry deadline monotonic across clock jumps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, when the gateway process resumes a scheduled task while a sibling process is still unmapping SQLite shared memory, `retryScheduledTaskLeaseRead` reads the owner lease through a 15s retry budget. The deadline was computed with the wall clock (`Date.now()`), so an NTP/clock jump forward expired the budget mid-retry and discarded a healthy lease that was still within budget. The deadline now uses the monotonic clock (`performance.now()`), so the retry budget measures elapsed time independent of wall-clock jumps.

- Problem: the retry deadline was seeded with `Date.now() + 15_000` and the remaining budget read again with `Date.now()` across an `await sleep(...)` tick. A wall-clock jump forward makes `Date.now() >= deadline` true on the next retry, so a transient SQLite sharing error is thrown without being retried. A jump backward inflates the effective retry window.
- Solution: seed, expire, and consume the budget all on `performance.now()`, which is monotonic and unaffected by wall-clock jumps.
- What changed: `src/daemon/schtasks-sqlite.ts` — `retryScheduledTaskLeaseRead` now uses `performance.now()` in all three places (deadline seed, expiry check, remaining-time read).
- What did NOT change: the retry policy itself (15s budget, 100ms steps, sharing-error classification), and no code outside `retryScheduledTaskLeaseRead` was touched.

## Why This Change Was Made

`retryScheduledTaskLeaseRead` is a pure in-process retry loop: its deadline is never serialized, persisted, or reported to the UI, and it is only compared against the same clock that computes the remaining budget. The monotonic clock is therefore the only correct clock here. The alternative — retaining `Date.now()` and guarding against jumps — would needlessly add complexity to a function whose only job is to wait a bounded time. This is the standard wall-clock→monotonic fix already merged across the codebase for deadline budgets (e.g. the monotonic-clock retry family).

Best-fix: replacing all three `Date.now()` reads with `performance.now()` is the minimal, complete change; the loop's deadline, expiry check, and remaining-budget read now all share one monotonic clock.

Risk / boundaries: the backward-jump direction inflates the effective window, which is bounded by `Math.min(100, ...)` on each step and is strictly less harmful than the forward jump (which discarded healthy leases). No Windows runtime was available, so the test forces the `win32` platform branch to exercise the sharing-error classification; the deadline logic itself is platform-agnostic.

## User Impact

On Windows, gateway startup/resume and scheduled-task activation can no longer have a healthy SQLite owner-lease read wrongly discarded by a wall-clock jump during retry. The 15s retry budget now reliably measures elapsed time, so transient SQLite sharing errors (sibling process still unmapping shared memory) are retried for their full budget as intended instead of failing early.

## Evidence

**Windows-native before/after proof (GitHub Actions, `windows-latest`, Node v24.22.1)** — drives the shipped `retryScheduledTaskLeaseRead` wrapping the shipped `readGatewayOwnerLease` against a real SQLite state database while a sibling process holds a real `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` write lock (DELETE journal mode), producing a real `SQLITE_BUSY` (errcode 5). A wall-clock NTP correction is simulated by skewing only `Date.now` mid-retry.

**Behavior before/after (same script, same cases; only the deadline clock differs)**

| case | before (`Date.now`) | after (`performance.now`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no wall-clock jump (control) | ✅ SUCCESS ~6.7s | ✅ SUCCESS ~6.8s |
| `+20000ms` forward jump (NTP) | ❌ FAILED ~6.6s — healthy lease **discarded** | ✅ SUCCESS ~6.7s — **recovered** |

Only the forward-jump case differs: before, the wall-clock deadline expires mid-retry and the healthy lease read is discarded; after, the monotonic deadline ignores the jump and the read recovers once the lock is released.

**Before (pre-fix, `deadline line: for (const deadline = Date.now() + 15_000; ;) {`)**

```console
--- no jump (control) ---
[proof] RESULT=SUCCESS lease=undefined monotonicElapsedMs=6681
--- +20000ms forward jump ---
[proof] RESULT=FAILED err=database is locked errcode=5 monotonicElapsedMs=6602
```

**After (post-fix, `deadline line: for (const deadline = performance.now() + 15_000; ;) {`)**

```console
--- no jump (control) ---
[proof] RESULT=SUCCESS lease=undefined monotonicElapsedMs=6791
--- +20000ms forward jump ---
[proof] RESULT=SUCCESS lease=undefined monotonicElapsedMs=6677
```

The before/after code change is exactly the three `Date.now()` → `performance.now()` reads in `retryScheduledTaskLeaseRead` (deadline seed, expiry check, remaining-time read); the control cases confirm both versions recover, isolating the wall-clock jump as the trigger.

**Unit regression test** — `src/daemon/schtasks-sqlite.test.ts`:

```console
$ npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.daemon.config.ts src/daemon/schtasks-sqlite.test.ts
 ✓ keeps the lease-read retry deadline on the monotonic clock across a forward wall-clock jump
 ✓ keeps the lease-read retry deadline on the monotonic clock across a backward wall-clock jump (budget not inflated)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

Pre-fix the backward-jump case fails with `expected 35000 to be less than 16500` — the `Date.now` deadline is inflated to 35s by the 20s backward jump instead of exhausting at ~15s of monotonic time.

Related daemon suites pass with no regression: `schtasks-runtime.deadline.test.ts` and `schtasks-process.windows.test.ts` (24 tests, 1 Windows-only skip). `oxfmt --check` and `tsc` are clean.

Open PR collision check: scanned 300 open PRs' changed-file lists plus module-keyword search (`schtasks`, `monotonic`) for `src/daemon/schtasks-sqlite.ts`; no open PR touches it, and `origin/main` still contains the `Date.now()` deadline (not already fixed).

prs.title: perf(ui): construct live Markdown tails directly as DOM
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Live chat tails repeatedly serialize Markdown to HTML, parse it through DOMPurify, then parse it again for reconciliation. This change constructs supported Markdown syntax directly as allowlisted DOM only for the mutable streaming tail and carries that fragment through the existing reconciler.

## User Impact

Settled messages, reload, history load, session switch, completed prefixes, and completion retain the existing HTML + DOMPurify path and string cache. Raw HTML, unsupported plugin tokens, and specialized renderers keep the full sanitizer boundary. Prepared fragments are cloned before consumer mutation. Appearance, links, reader controls, and lazy boundaries remain unchanged.

Peter accepted the additional code and chat bytes after the original experiment measured streaming script CPU −8.6% and HTML assignments 2,129 → 178. The broad direct-rendering candidate was rejected after a reload p95 regression, so this revision restricts direct construction to streaming. Three base and three broad-candidate diagnostic profiles did not establish per-node construction as the cause of that tail; no causal claim is made from those samples.

## Evidence

Security proof is against the original pipeline at main `368b9dc52b98985dda08c2579fa1bff3e1809485`; the newer fetched main has identical Markdown owners and budget inputs. All differential inputs match the current source hashes.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Independent explicit XSS/mXSS autoreview | Scoped clean at P0–P2; allowlists, URL policy, raw HTML fallback, fragment isolation, callers, promotion, and completion reviewed |

| Narrowed streaming security differential | 71 cases, 2,487 updates, 71 completions; zero differences, unsafe DOM, or alerts |
| Completion parity | Actual settled chat preparation returns strings and matches bulk DOM byte-for-byte, removing only empty reconciler comment markers |
| Final API/test-cutover autoreview | Scoped clean at P0–P2; deleted string API and real-DOM retention proof reviewed |
| Fragment ownership | Mutating one consumer leaves the prepared fragment and a second consumer unchanged |
| Focused tests | 85 security/chat tests plus 26 cutover tests pass; three cutover files exercised the real streaming API, stable-prefix budgets, node retention, and attachments |
| UI typecheck / targeted lint / production build | Pass; lint uses boundary-free `tsconfig.ui.json` |

| New Session gzip | 767,623 → 767,376 B; 16 JS + 3 CSS unchanged |
| CSS | 303,561 B on both builds; inherited absolute cap overage retained |
| Exact-head `ci:full` | [40145767702](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40145767702), success on `f01cc6fd4d3a66ba00d8a4ad63b7e89958a8ea0f` |
| Final streaming workload | All 60 cells delivered 645 deltas/writes; one normalized final DOM across all variants; no harness warnings |

Startup raw bytes are identical; its gzip movement is build variation, not a causal win. The supported `--update-baseline --reason` command records the accepted CPU/bytes tradeoff and measured startup baseline. Chat's cap is 1,274,861 B: measured head plus the existing 811 B headroom.

Final same-machine timing uses 20 serial base/base/head triplets (60 cells). Values below are median / nearest-rank p95 / min–max, in milliseconds unless noted.

| CPU / work | Base | A/A control | Streaming-only head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Streaming script CPU | 1,838.361 / 2,025.458 / 1,681.824–2,154.721 | 1,823.193 / 1,883.413 / 1,737.818–2,144.218 | 1,712.024 / 1,780.806 / 1,629.428–2,100.217 |
| Reload script CPU | 528.444 / 556.223 / 445.246–557.612 | 521.883 / 611.013 / 460.011–621.389 | 530.238 / 591.923 / 446.782–613.996 |
| Reload task CPU | 1,102.911 / 1,355.079 / 997.925–1,418.720 | 1,105.361 / 1,331.230 / 1,041.008–1,378.931 | 1,138.467 / 1,287.940 / 1,012.920–1,307.421 |
| Streaming HTML assignments (count) | 2,114 / 2,191 / 2,005–2,254 | 2,113.5 / 2,177 / 1,936–2,252 | 236.5 / 317 / 229–824 |

Streaming script median improves **6.87%** (A/A −0.83%) and p95 improves **12.08%**. HTML assignments fall **88.81%**. Reload script median changes **+0.34%**; its p95 is **+6.42%**, while the unchanged A/A p95 is **+9.85%**. Reload total-task median is +3.22% and p95 −4.95%. The shared host's one-minute load ranged **35.14–77.36**; wall readiness is noisy (A/A median +30.26%) and is not treated as a speedup or regression. The raw p95 increase is disclosed: the unchanged control has a larger tail, so it does not establish a candidate-specific reload regression. Bulk source/cache behavior is restored, and reload script/task medians remain inside the 5% band. Reload style CPU is a disclosed exception among subphases: median +6.26%, p95 −2.08%; there is no CSS change and the bulk DOM path is unchanged. This is not a claim that every CPU submetric improved.

Touched UI production source: 1,999 → 2,444 lines (+445). All touched production/config/scripts: 2,795 → 3,241 (+446). Tests/support: 3,527 → 3,599 (+72). The simplification removes static prepared caching and the obsolete string-streaming production API; string assertions now serialize the real streaming result in test support. Effects 1 → 1, listeners 0 → 0, DOM queries 2 → 2, cleanup 1 → 1; owner APIs and reactive state counts unchanged. No Worker or dependency added.

Synthetic-only before/after captures were inspected. Both show the final streamed reply with identical code blocks, tables, and links.

![Before: synthetic streamed Markdown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57260fc2-d875-4a10-8986-7baf417a3683)

![After: synthetic streamed Markdown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/475a6f9b-7ed1-4f0d-8c08-4c59b4911afa)

<details>
<summary>Workload, acceptance, and limits</summary>

The final acceptance run uses a 400-message synthetic chat and 645 deltas at 30/s: 20 serial base/base/head triplets, untraced renderer thread CPU, host load recorded. The second base copy is an A/A control. Reload uses persisted state and HTTP cache; it does not model a cold-network first visit. Acceptance requires streaming improvement and reload median regression ≤5% with no real p95 regression. On a noisy host, A/A and CPU over 20 pairs take precedence over wall timing. The original −40% / ≤1.0 s streaming and −40% settled targets are not achieved or claimed.

The corpus includes transcript Markdown, DOMPurify historical XSS/mXSS payloads, hostile attributes/language labels, URL schemes and decoded control bytes, generated links/favicons, nested grammar, deterministic prefixes, and syntax-boundary/random streaming splits. Raw authored HTML still uses DOMPurify.

Reproduce with `scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts --bundle-dir <base> --compare-bundle-dir <base-copy> --compare-bundle-dir <head> --runs 60 --streaming-reply --transcript-messages 400 --face chat --untraced --thread-cpu-time`. Builds use `pnpm ui:build`; strict asset comparison uses both same-machine bundles. No broad local E2E, Docker, or remote lease was used.

The first lint attempt used the editor UI graph and timed out in unrelated SDK declarations; the corrected documented lint graph passes. Knip's four inherited files are `extensions/codex/src/app-server/protocol-validator-schemas.ts`, `src/gateway/mcp-app-standalone-host.ts`, `src/gateway/worker-environments/repository-node-requirement.ts`, and `src/sessions/runtime-context.ts`.

</details>
