prs.title: perf(gateway): preserve session row identity across unchanged reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sidebar reads rebuild search fields and presentation graphs when unchanged session rows are reacquired or materialized. The row owner now keeps equal entry, selection, parents, membership, materialized, fallback-model, and facts-reader identities. Installation and publication share one change decision, so unchanged materialization no longer retires presentation sharing.

Fresh rows and merged writer patches use the existing sparse-field normalizer before freezing. Undefined patches still clear previous values, and retained snapshots stay immutable. This removes the divergent handwritten normalization loop and reverses the dense representation's retained-memory growth. Full deep-freeze semantics remain unchanged; committed-snapshot reuse is separate work in #182210.

The cold-load investigation and parked read-side patch in #182686 supplied the analysis and starting point. This PR completes the materialization half. Production delta is **+92 lines**. A second simplification review found no safe structural deletion: the growth records the complete static-search dependencies and facts reader's captured-input equality contract, needed to avoid stale output. There is no new cache or invalidation owner.

## Evidence

- **Board changes retire sharing:** the real Board widget publication/list flow checks a new sharing revision.
- **Real visibility, sharing, and run-state changes replace materialization:** the owner integration test covers label/model changes, read-only/shared visibility, terminal failed/done state, and membership additions/removals. The membership test exposed stale reuse despite correct sharing retirement; reuse now requires unchanged membership. Runtime activity remains live; regressions also cover dirty rows and pending category reconciliation.
- **Unchanged materialization retains identity:** red/green owner tests cover materialized objects, facts readers, sharing tokens, and timestamp-only search identity. Sparse-shape and transcript-clearing regressions failed before repair and preserve old snapshots after clearing.
- Final affected suites passed: projection 18, backfill 18, materialization golden 2, publication snapshots 3. Earlier focused record/presentation/facts proof, export-name guard, 22 closure tests, changed-file lint/format, and one targeted core typecheck passed. Broad proof comes from PR CI.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) is clean after the sparse, membership, runtime-summary, and harness repairs. The helper refused the provider route; operator configuration was unchanged.

## Measurement

**The requested 15 primary pairs are complete. The final decision, including the predeclared extra pair 16, follows this primary report.** Each side completed 3,000 timestamp writes and 2,925 sidebar searches, with zero RPC failures. Static search facts did not change; the candidate rebuilt no repeated search fields in any pair.

| Metric | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Paired absolute Δ | Δ / baseline mean |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Repeated search-field rebuilds | 110.93 | 0.00 | -110.93 | -100.00% |
| Main-thread CPU per wave, ms | 3204.94 | 3106.72 | -98.22 | -3.06% |
| Session-row consume task time per wave, ms | 189.94 | 95.64 | -94.30 | -49.65% |
| Consume calls per wave | 27.73 | 5.60 | -22.13 | -79.81% |
| Sidebar search RPC p90, ms | 165.50 (n=195/pair) | 166.99 (n=195/pair) | +1.49 | +0.90% |
| Agent-roster task p90, ms | 22.00 (n=6–8/pair) | 22.19 (n=6–13/pair) | +0.19 | +0.86% |
| GC time, ms/min | 704.86 | 695.40 | -9.47 | -1.34% |
| Event-loop p95, ms | 12.96 (n=892–913/pair) | 12.41 (n=898–917/pair) | -0.55 | -4.22% |
| Event-loop p99, ms (context) | 29.34 (n=892–913/pair) | 27.95 (n=898–917/pair) | -1.38 | -4.72% |

CPU improved in 13/15 pairs and consume time in 15/15. The mean of individual paired relative changes was −3.04% CPU, −49.07% consume, and +1.06% search p90; the decision uses signed absolute means. Event-loop p95 has enough observations; p99 does not reach 1,000 per side/pair and is context. Agent-roster task p90 has only the small counts shown. Both swapped-placement groups remain below adverse thresholds.

<details><summary>Per-kind GC and both maximum pauses for all 15 primary pairs</summary>

| GC kind | Baseline collections / total ms | Candidate collections / total ms | Absolute total Δ | Relative total Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| minor | 694 / 1737.53 | 666 / 1700.53 | -37.00 ms | -2.13% |
| major | 1 / 15.74 | 2 / 31.31 | +15.57 ms | +98.92% |
| incremental | 1 / 2.10 | 0 / 0.00 | -2.10 ms | -100.00% |
| weak | 0 / 0.00 | 0 / 0.00 | +0.00 ms | — (both zero) |

| Pair | Baseline max GC pause, ms | Candidate max GC pause, ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.987 | 9.186 |
| 2 | 8.111 | 16.705 |
| 3 | 4.923 | 4.621 |
| 4 | 6.530 | 3.898 |
| 5 | 6.946 | 5.378 |
| 6 | 6.622 | 14.606 |
| 7 | 15.741 | 7.686 |
| 8 | 5.040 | 5.642 |
| 9 | 10.483 | 9.987 |
| 10 | 9.083 | 7.221 |
| 11 | 4.885 | 6.263 |
| 12 | 6.506 | 5.322 |
| 13 | 6.691 | 6.703 |
| 14 | 5.764 | 14.208 |
| 15 | 7.943 | 6.456 |

Mean maxima were 7.350 → 8.259 ms (+0.908 ms, +12.36%); the mean of individual relative changes was +21.01%. No candidate exceeded `max(50 ms, 2 × its paired baseline maximum)`. Minor collections remain below 200 per run, and major collections are 0–1 per run, so collection pause percentiles are context. Total GC cost fell. Promotion was not measured in this untraced pass. No GC rejection gate or corresponding A/A-control requirement has been triggered.


Minor pause percentiles (context; insufficient per-run collection counts):

| Tail | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Paired absolute Δ | Relative Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Minor p95 | 4.330 ms (n=44–50/pair) | 4.107 ms (n=42–49/pair) | -0.222 ms | -5.14% |
| Minor p99 | 6.950 ms (n=44–50/pair) | 7.526 ms (n=42–49/pair) | +0.576 ms | +8.29% |

Major collections: pair-2 fix: 16.705 ms (n=1); pair-6 fix: 14.606 ms (n=1); pair-7 base: 15.741 ms (n=1). No pair has major collections on both sides, so a paired major-percentile delta is unavailable.

</details>

Detailed identity tracking is disabled in timing runs. Materialized/facts replacement and live-presentation counts below come from the separate five-wave retention pass.


### Declared extra pair and final decision

**Acceptance passes at the fixed stop of 16 valid pairs.** Pair 16 completed 200 writes and 195 searches per side without RPC errors; repeated field rebuilds were 109 → 0. The primary 15 results above are preserved. Across all 16 pairs, each side completed 3,200 writes and 3,120 searches. The two CPU placements have eight pairs each.

| Metric, all 16 pairs | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Paired absolute Δ | Δ / baseline mean |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Repeated search-field rebuilds | 110.81 | 0.00 | -110.81 | -100.00% |
| Main CPU per wave, ms | 3237.01 | 3122.90 | -114.11 | -3.53% |
| Consume task time per wave, ms | 189.95 | 96.15 | -93.80 | -49.38% |
| Sidebar search RPC p90, ms | 165.95 (n=195/pair) | 167.08 (n=195/pair) | +1.13 | +0.68% |
| Agent-roster task p90, ms | 21.94 (n=6–8/pair) | 21.99 (n=6–13/pair) | +0.05 | +0.21% |
| GC time, ms/min | 709.12 | 695.17 | -13.95 | -1.97% |
| Event-loop p95, ms | 13.00 (n=892–913/pair) | 12.42 (n=896–917/pair) | -0.58 | -4.45% |
| Event-loop p99, ms (context) | 29.70 (n=892–913/pair) | 28.03 (n=896–917/pair) | -1.66 | -5.60% |

CPU improved in 14/16 pairs; consume time improved in 16/16. No eligible metric crosses either the overall 20% adverse threshold or the 10% threshold in both placement groups. Total GC cost fell, and no pair crosses the maximum-pause safeguard. The requested identity correction therefore meets its no-regression rule with a clear work-count/consume-time benefit and modest CPU improvement. Independent review confirmed the arithmetic and gate decision. No additional measurements were run after pair 16.

Pair 16 maximum GC pauses: **11.227 → 6.054 ms**. Across all pairs, the largest observed pauses were 15.741 → 16.705 ms.

| GC kind, all 16 | Baseline collections / total ms | Candidate collections / total ms | Absolute total Δ | Relative total Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| minor | 740 / 1865.87 | 710 / 1815.40 | -50.47 ms | -2.71% |
| major | 1 / 15.74 | 2 / 31.31 | +15.57 ms | +98.92% |
| incremental | 1 / 2.10 | 0 / 0.00 | -2.10 ms | -100.00% |
| weak | 0 / 0.00 | 0 / 0.00 | +0.00 ms | — (both zero) |

All-16 minor pause tails remain context: p95 4.353 → 4.097 ms (Δ -0.256 ms, -5.89%); p99 7.217 → 7.434 ms (Δ +0.217 ms, +3.00%). Counts are 44–50 baseline and 42–49 candidate collections per pair.

The per-run sample limitations remain: loop p99 and collection pause tails are context, and promotion is unmeasured. Major-GC relative changes on the small collection count do not override the lower total GC cost. The separate retention pass and real-Gateway coverage limits below remain unchanged.

### Five-wave settled retention

Exact source pair: baseline `8c6ad0edc3c9d87f5a5b5a40fad6f84761066348`, candidate `1e525e8e9a4b2d80c3f405d9a73e407b28c6cd92`, identical current dependency graph, swapped interleaved 16-CPU placement from process startup, absolute nice 10. Each side completed 1,000 timestamp writes and 975 searches across five waves with zero RPC failures.

| Wave | Live base → fix | Presentation/consume MiB base → fix | Index/trim MiB base → fix | Sidebar sharing MiB base → fix |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 659 → 659 | 2.877 → 3.000 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 4.005 → 3.912 |
| 2 | 658 → 658 | 3.066 → 2.610 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 3.254 → 3.224 |
| 3 | 658 → 658 | 2.981 → 2.991 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 3.160 → 3.287 |
| 4 | 658 → 658 | 3.172 → 2.741 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 3.192 → 3.193 |
| 5 | 659 → 658 | 3.301 → 3.267 | 0.000 → 0.000 | 3.286 → 3.892 |

**Mean presentation/consume: 3.079 → 2.922 MiB (−5.11%).** Sidebar sharing: 3.380 → 3.501 MiB (+3.61%). These are inclusive sampled surviving JavaScript families after settlement and GC; they overlap and cannot be summed. Native bytes are not attributed. Mapping was valid on both sides. The presentation-family decrease is modest and varied by wave (lower in three of five); the earlier dense growth has reversed against the new concurrent baseline.

Materialized and facts-reader replacement counts were identical on both sides: 63 in wave 1, then 200 per later wave. Every repeat changed `updatedAt`; identical-source and unchanged-graph replacement counts were zero. The real-Gateway workload did not reproduce the original unchanged-source rematerialization path; the red/green owner regression covers it. Initial search construction was 4,000 on both sides; baseline then reconstructed 110 repeated fields in wave 1 and 200 newly keyed fields per later wave, versus zero candidate reconstructions. Real source-field changes were zero.

The predeclared below-baseline staging condition passed, so the same lock custody proceeded to all 15 untraced timing pairs. All 15 primary pairs and the single predeclared extra pair are complete; final acceptance passed.

## Provenance and limits

Measurements use baseline `8c6ad0edc3c9d87f5a5b5a40fad6f84761066348` and candidate `1e525e8e9a4b2d80c3f405d9a73e407b28c6cd92`, with identical reconciled dependencies. Production and test files on the final rebased PR head are byte-identical to that measured candidate. The only later harness change reads Gateway ports from each prepared fixture instead of duplicating hardcoded ports, and records them in pair metadata. The README section was moved alongside related documentation and updated to describe fixture-owned ports. Results do not measure unrelated upstream changes introduced by rebasing.

Attempted timing pair 10 is invalid setup evidence: sandbox bind on 41670 failed; baseline completed 11 writes, no searches and 65 failed Board reads. Candidate completed 200 writes/195 searches, but neither side counts. The guard was healthy. No conflicting listener remained when inspected, so its ownership/cause is unproven and no process was killed. The replacement and remaining pairs use 62669/62679 (sandboxes 62670/62680), outside the host's ephemeral range, fresh fixtures, and the same protocol. Nine earlier valid pairs are retained. Earlier smoke with colliding Gateway/sandbox ports and measurements starting before final CPU placement are also excluded.

An earlier root-help metadata build timed out after 120 seconds. Its log was fetched once; the CSS budget warning was advisory. Exact-base CI had been cancelled and nearby main built successfully, so inherited/flaky attribution is **unproven**. The measured candidate and the current head subsequently passed build-artifacts jobs ([current build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142990562/job/121018434622)) without a renderer or timeout change; no CI rerun was requested. The renderer imports its compiled help module, renders command descriptors, and explicitly exits; it does not directly invoke the changed row functions. Its 120-second timeout covers the whole child lifetime and the saved terminal error omits captured output, so import, rendering, and shutdown cannot be distinguished. Historical cause remains unknown. Current-head CI completed with the one proven inherited fixture failure and downstream gate described below; other jobs passed or were skipped. Performance acceptance passed after the fixed 16-pair stop.

## Inherited CI failure

Current CI [run 40142990631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142990631) has one non-aggregate failed job: `checks-node-changed-compact-large-24`, with the downstream `openclaw/ci-gate` failure. The coalesced-followers case in `src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog-phase-diagnostics.test.ts` times out after 120 seconds. The exact same single-file command on PR head `8134942448b90349b1bbdb4e5da2cb7f94bd8cfc` and CI's unchanged main parent `d26ed20767956a1eaca9cc8caa8c04b4fdf62e3d` produced **4 passed / 1 failed**, with the identical timeout:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog-phase-diagnostics.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The test supplies `{ connId: "shared-caller" }` without `connect`. Upstream [#182897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182897) changed the trusted client read to `client?.connect.scopes`; the malformed fixture therefore rejects before its provider starts. The test absorbs the rejected completion and waits indefinitely for that provider. Both relevant files are unchanged by this PR; its empty store and mocked readiness do not execute our changed row branches. Head/base replay durations were 162.44/157.67 seconds including compilation; the failing test's own timeout was 120 seconds on both. No CI rerun was requested. Landing uses the standing exception for proven inherited failures after performance acceptance; CI is not claimed green.

### Predeclared performance acceptance

Use the committed real-Gateway churn harness: 5,000 synthetic sessions, 6,000 settled runs, 65 reader clients, and 200 timestamp-only writes at 50ms submission spacing. Each wave includes 195 sidebar searches overlapping committed writes. Baseline and candidate use fresh identical fixtures, concurrent synchronized starts, exclusive shared quiet-slot custody, interleaved 16-CPU placement from process startup and counterbalanced launch order. The final fixture epoch is the original rig reference time, `1791892800000`; both sides use the same post-connect start barrier. Run 15 valid paired samples; preserve invalid setup/guard attempts and replace the whole pair. No production database or Gateway is used.

The five-wave retention pass runs first and validates baseline repeated search-field rebuilds and zero candidate rebuilds. Before seeing the new results, the staging rule is to continue automatically to all 15 timing pairs only if mean sampled presentation/selection/consume bytes falls below baseline across the five settled waves. Otherwise preserve all outputs and repair the representation before spending the timing campaign. This is a directional staging rule, not a statistical acceptance verdict. Report materialized/facts replacements, live presentations and sampled surviving JavaScript bytes for the presentation/consume, index/trim, and share/sidebar families after each of five post-GC waves. Retention profiling stays separate from timing. Also report agent-roster search p90, session-rows:consume task time, main-thread CPU, event-loop counts/tails, per-kind GC time/counts/tails and both maximum pauses.

Decide on paired signed absolute means alongside relative differences. Adverse gates use mean >=20% or >=10% in both swapped placements, subject to the campaign amendments: GC increases need >=50ms/min or >=1ms/operation absolute materiality; sub-ms GC pause percentile changes are context; sub-ms event-loop changes are context when CPU/allocation improves >=10%. Qualified p99 needs 1,000 observations per side, p95 needs 200, and major-GC tails need 50 collections. Before rejecting on GC/promotion/max pause, require at least four matched A/A controls; noisy controls make the protocol inconclusive and require a longer fixed-work experiment. Mixed-sign gated results get one predeclared extra pair. A consistent >=5% CPU/allocation gain can land when only inconclusive GC/max-pause controls remain. Maximum-pause safeguard remains max(50ms, 2x baseline). Promotion is not measured by the untraced timing pass.


**Mixed-sign rule, declared before the remaining results:** at 23:29Z on October 24, the first nine valid timing pairs contained mixed-sign deltas in sample-qualified gating metrics. Run the requested 15 pairs, then exactly one extra pair 16 with the same protocol and swapped placement. Report the primary 15 separately and decide on the signed absolute mean over all 16. Stop there; no further result-dependent samples.

prs.title: test(memory): prune duplicate embedding retry cases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The memory manager's embedding retry wrapper repeats the provider error-message matrix already covered at the policy owner and real HTTP boundary. Remove 20 redundant expanded cases from one test file (41 → 21 cases; net 68 test lines removed). Production code is unchanged.

Both text and structured wrapper paths retain ordered split results, exact request sizes, no retry/degradation on success, terminal error wrapping, unchanged input forwarding, and the single-item rejection stopping condition. Query formatting, cancellation and deadline coverage stays intact. No SQL, schema, SDK, migration, security, channel e2e or live-proof tests change.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. This reduces repeated CI test execution while retaining the embedding retry contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared policy and HTTP boundary already protect error classification and recovery, so the manager wrapper needs only its distinct input and error behavior.

## Retained contracts

| Removed wrapper rows | Retained proof |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit numeric maximum, max-input-length, input-array cap | `manager-embedding-policy.test.ts`: numeric embedding item limit matrix and paired-input persistence/split matrix; `generic-embedding-provider.integration.test.ts`: ordered HTTP embedding matrix |
| Nonnumeric row cap, item length, indexed element, token limits and fractional limits | Policy negative matrix; HTTP terminal rejection matrix for item/token/fractional limits |
| Ordinary under-cap success | Existing wrapper formatting cases and HTTP ordinary batch / Qianfan declared-cap tests |

The DashScope success fixture and both generic-validation and single-item rejection fixtures remain for both input forms. The shared policy owns parsing; the wrapper retains its distinct input and error contracts. No test-only production seam is introduced or removed.

## Acceptance rule (registered before execution)

Flow/workload: run the affected wrapper suite and the unchanged policy and HTTP keeper suites on this machine with the pinned Bun Vitest runtime, one worker, identical inputs and dependency installation. Primary metric: 20 fewer expanded wrapper cases, with every retained case green, no production changes, and no new static-analysis findings. Any lost unique contract or newly failing retained test rejects the change.

Record local test-run elapsed time and host load for baseline and candidate as execution evidence. A performance claim requires the campaign timing lock, load below 24, alternating baseline/candidate samples (at least five each), cold and warm samples separate, and median/p95/range. Any user-facing metric regression or 20% cell movement stops acceptance. If host load never qualifies for 60 minutes, report counts without a wall-clock speedup claim. Test-only edits have no production SQL/request delta; no Gateway workload change is asserted.

## Evidence

Isolated Codex P0–P2 preservation review: scoped-clean; no actionable coverage loss. Focused proof passes: baseline wrapper 41/41, retained wrapper 21/21, policy keeper 61/61, and real HTTP keeper 25/25. That is 107 retained cases green, with no production edits.

Raw wrapper command times were 303.46s baseline and 80.25s candidate, at one-minute loads 74.75 and 61.84. The baseline included 167.5s of cold worker compilation; the candidate reused compiler artifacts. Qualification waited more than 60 minutes without load below 24, so these are execution records, **not a speedup measurement**. Zero qualified timing samples; counts are the result.

Exact-head CI [40141864976](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40141864976) passed types, lint, architecture, source contracts, ratchets and changed tests. The only failing test job was [PostgreSQL shard 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40141864976/job/121015372510): seven synthetic-runtime missing-module cases in `interactive-setup.integration.test.ts`. These were reproduced on main and fixed independently by #182990; the duplicate fix #182996 passed all three PostgreSQL CI shards. The aggregate gate reports that same inherited failure. No affected-file failures.

Local `check:changed` passed the runnable guards, including T1 170→170 live / 15→15 deprecated-only and zero dialect growth. Its type/lint preparation refused the campaign-mandated external-to-checkout dependency store; exact-head CI supplies those passing checks. Its parallel full-tree Knip scan timed out at the unchanged 600-second limit. The completed serial canonical Knip scans match exactly: production 70→70, full-tree 83→83, scripts 1,136→1,136; zero added or removed findings and zero resolution errors. ## What Problem This Solves

Agent and Gateway CI repeatedly executes contracts already covered by their owning suites, including a standalone file with no distinct behavioral coverage.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. This removes 12 duplicate test cases and 307 net test lines across five files; production code, security checks, migration tests, and PostgreSQL conformance remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one strong proof per contract. The CLI parser delegates to the same streaming parser, replay cases directly exercise the repair owner rather than endpoint compaction, and announcement output cases duplicate the output suite. Metadata readiness is already checked through the registered handler with the same held model-list fixture.

Only test deletions and unused test-import/fixture-parameter cleanup are included. No production seams are changed. The neighboring non-object schema rejection and endpoint quality-guard cases are retained because they protect distinct behavior.

prs.title: perf(gateway): allocate session group positions in the insert
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Registering a new session category reads its greatest position in a separate SQL statement immediately before inserting the category. The position is needed only by that insert. The insert now computes that value itself, removing the extra statement and materialized row.

## Design

Keep the existing catalog owner, serialized mutations, names admission, transaction and final snapshot. Compute the next position inside the single-row INSERT with a dialect-neutral ordered scalar subquery. No schema, cache, identity, SDK, cross-store transaction or authority change.

Before:

```sql
SELECT position FROM session_groups ORDER BY position DESC LIMIT 1;
INSERT INTO session_groups (name, position, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?);
```

After (logical shape):

```sql
INSERT INTO session_groups (name, position, created_at)
VALUES (?, COALESCE((SELECT position FROM session_groups ORDER BY position DESC LIMIT 1), -1) + 1, ?);
```

Names admission and the committed snapshot remain. Empty and gapped catalogs retain their current ordering; duplicate registration remains unchanged. Direct external corruption receives no new recovery guarantees. Position has no unique constraint: PostgreSQL allocation relies on READ COMMITTED and the existing per-store advisory lock acquired before authoritative reads; SQLite relies on BEGIN IMMEDIATE. REPEATABLE READ would not provide the required post-lock statement snapshot.

## Acceptance rule — recorded before first run

Workload: committed `scripts/perf/session-group-registration-measure.ts`, isolated synthetic state and workspace, loopback Gateway on the tested head, actual token-authenticated WebSocket. One `sessions.create` with a new category (cold); twenty `sessions.patch` calls with unique categories (warm); twenty assignments of an existing category (warm control). Verify the returned category and immediate ordered `sessions.groups.list` results. No model calls or private data.

Rerun command (new synthetic directory each time):

```sh
NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-group-registration-measure.ts --state-dir <new-directory> --registrations 20
```

Counts first, with the frozen SQL observer: standalone greatest-position SELECT must change from one to zero for each new category. Total SQL must decrease by exactly one per new registration; worker requests and MAIN work must not increase. Warm existing-category registration must retain zero catalog worker work. Explain all other changed operations. Preserve empty/gapped ordering, duplicate/concurrent registration, rollback/rejection, publication and post-commit repair behavior. The count regression must fail on base and pass on the fix.

Profile the real Gateway flow with `node --cpu-prof` on the main thread and every worker; report main and total work. For latency/CPU A/B runs use the serialized timing lock and one-minute load below 24. Interleave baseline/candidate ABAB with at least five samples per head, separate cold and warm results, and report median, p95 and min–max spread. All user-facing metrics must hold or improve; any adverse 20% cell stops the change for investigation. No latency claim from a loaded host. If the quiet-host wait exceeds 60 minutes, explicitly report count/profile evidence and the missing timing result.

Frozen standard workload: three alternating baseline/candidate pairs when host load is below 64 with at least 12 GiB free; otherwise the authorized single pair or source attribution, including warm non-regression. Counts and profiles are distinct from latency evidence. New heavy runs wait for at least 12 GiB internal free.

## Evidence

The regression failed as expected on the base: two registrations issue two standalone highest-position SELECTs. Both real Gateway arms passed all 41 category operations and immediate ordered readback, using the same Mac and source tree. The baseline restores only the old allocator from `085076cc8f76`; the candidate uses the final allocator from `b9be2c4ae08e`. The frozen observer hashes were verified; runtime state, workspace and ports were isolated and synthetic.

| Phase | Samples per arm | SQL median; p95 [min–max], base → head | Requests median; p95 [min–max], base → head | MAIN |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| Cold new category | 1 | 179 → 178 | 46 → 45 | 0 → 0 |
| Warm new category | 20 | 16; 16 [16–17] → 15; 15 [15–16] | 4; 4 [4–4] → 4; 4 [4–5] | 0 → 0 |
| Warm existing category | 20 | 10; 10 [10–10] → 10; 10 [10–10] | 3; 3 [3–4] → 3; 3 [3–3] | 0 → 0 |

Standalone position reads change from 1 to 0 on every new registration. Across all 40 warm actions the only SQL-shape delta is twenty standalone position SELECTs removed and twenty INSERTs changed to compute the position. Catalog worker requests are unchanged. Immediate readback is 4 SQL / 0 requests / 0 MAIN in both arms; shutdown is 16 / 4 / 6 in both. Whole-run counts are 1,517 → 1,494 SQL, 296 → 296 requests and 530 → 529 MAIN. Claim only the 21 removed allocation statements; two other SQL differences are startup busy-timeout/initialization variation, with boot 797 → 795 SQL and cold 179 → 178. Startup work interleaves across those two phases.

**20% stop investigated; coordinator disposition accepted:** warm-new request maximum rises 4 → 5 (+25%). The frozen request trace identifies exactly one identical background provider-catalog task moving from baseline `warm-existing-16` to candidate `warm-new-20`; the full origin stack matches. Warm-new total requests move 80 → 81 and warm-existing 61 → 60, with whole-run requests exactly 296 in both. This is recorded explicitly rather than described as spread. The coordinator accepted this single-sample change on 2026-10-25: median/p95 requests stay 4, existing-category work is unchanged, MAIN is zero, and the SQL change is exactly the designed reduction. The full-stack match and conserved total requests establish the background-task placement.

The prior Linux baseline independently reproduced 16 SQL / 4 requests / 0 MAIN for warm new categories and 10 / 3 / 0 for existing ones. It is not mixed into this Mac pair. The Mac baseline/candidate captured 42/36 per-thread CPU profiles (1,339,513/1,141,601 samples). These are profile evidence, **not** a calibrated CPU-time, latency or memory saving. The general census harness uses the authorized source-attribution/next-census route after host load exceeded 64; no ABAB latency result is claimed.

Two isolated Codex reviews passed at P0–P2. Changed-file type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Final-head CI [40145894486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40145894486) completed successfully, including types, lint, architecture/Madge, source contracts, guards/ratchets, changed-test jobs and all three actually executed PostgreSQL conformance shards. Canonical Knip 6.40.0 scans completed on both base and candidate: production 70 → 70, full-tree 82 → 82 and scripts 1,136 → 1,136; zero new findings, zero removed findings and no setup errors. PostgreSQL semantic approval explicitly carries to the final comment-only head. The allocator is **+4 production LOC** including the lock-dependency comment; tests net +40 and the committed workload +138, plus two executable-root registration lines. The only retired production path is the standalone position read/result handling; no cache or new owner machinery is added.

Release-note context: session category registration performs one fewer SQL statement while preserving category order and publication behavior.

## PostgreSQL checklist

1. Existing READ COMMITTED write transaction and eager store advisory lock remain before authoritative reads. No writable CTE lock, string batching or multirow conflict input.
2. The scalar LIMIT 1 stays bounded; no larger payload or buffered iterator.
3. No cache or read-skipping revision is added. Existing catalog/write-receipt lifecycle remains.
4. No schema, PRAGMA, identity or admission change.
5. Same worker path and MAIN work; no relocation.
6. All three final-head PostgreSQL CI conformance steps actually executed and passed in run 40145894486. PG semantic review approved the executable head and explicitly carries to the comment-only final head.

## Open-PR compatibility

Shared prindex snapshot 2026-10-25 00:21:38 UTC: 2,682 open PRs targeting main; all 44 overlapping external heads compared using base-only versus base-plus-candidate merge-tree. Every comparison passes: zero added conflict paths, normalized blocks or messages. Existing conflicts are retained, including #164857's one path/block. The sole newly indexed overlap, #183044, is clean in both arms. Comment-only reuse was limited to verified identical merge inputs; the affected allocator overlap was recomputed.

All PASS: #183044, #182127, #180139, #167717, #167471, #164893, #164857, #163964, #163405, #162160, #162144, #162132, #162126, #161524, #161344, #160325, #160209, #159569, #158419, #155467, #154240, #152205, #151441, #150381, #150246, #148581, #147026, #145117, #138385, #137834, #137788, #137014, #136476, #136474, #135480, #131891, #130745, #129388, #128872, #126924, #118555, #117734, #117074, #89040.

prs.title: improve(database): load PostgreSQL agent sessions without reconnecting each time
prs.body:
Closes #182805

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with agent databases on PostgreSQL, every read-only agent database open, including each full session load (`SessionManager.openAsync` / transcript hydration), connects a new PostgreSQL backend and tears it down. A full session load takes about 115 ms where SQLite takes about 4 ms.

## User Impact

User impact: in a long-lived process such as the Gateway, repeated session loads on PostgreSQL-backed agents drop from about 115 ms to about 9 ms, with no new server connection per load. One-shot CLI commands open one fewer backend per repeated read and show no wall-time change. Agent database owners, agent creation and maintenance opens (doctor, port, lifecycle probes) keep their current connection behavior. No config, schema or SQLite change.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openOpenClawAgentDatabaseReadOnly` is the owner of short, exclusive, read-only agent leases, the agent counterpart of the existing-state opens that already use the per-worker idle connection cache from #175146. It now passes the existing engine option `reusePostgresConnection` through `openAgentEngineStore`. No other caller changes. The cache already keys by DSN, namespace and store id, gives each caller exclusive use, and discards any connection that is still inside a transaction. Agent PostgreSQL locks are transaction-scoped. The PostgreSQL docs paragraph on the cache now names read-only agent opens.

The first revision opted in every existing-only agent open. CI's `doctor-database-diagnostics.postgres.test.ts` then caught a real tradeoff: doctor's port admission left an idle backend in the cache, so a `DROP DATABASE` right after it failed with `database ... is being accessed by other users`. Maintenance opens therefore stay off the cache, and that existing test guards the boundary.

## Evidence

Head `bce2640dc81`, local PostgreSQL 17 over a Unix socket, throwaway schemas in a CI database.

**Regression test** (`src/state/openclaw-agent-db.postgres.test.ts`): two sequential `openOpenClawAgentDatabaseReadOnly` opens of a real agent store must get the same `pg_backend_pid()`.

```
# base a548e97016f production code
 ×  ... > PostgreSQL agent database owner > reuses one idle PostgreSQL backend across sequential read-only session opens
   → expected 19687 to be 19688 // Object.is equality
# bce2640dc81
 ✓  ... > reuses one idle PostgreSQL backend across sequential read-only session opens 331ms
 Test Files  8 passed (8)   Tests  49 passed
```

The other 7 files: `openclaw-agent-db-engine`, `postgres-sync/reuse`, `postgres-sync/transcript-hydration`, `session-accessor.sqlite-read-hold`, `session-turn-resident`, `database-engine/agent-port`, `openclaw-agent-doctor-media` (`*.postgres.test.ts`).

**Shipped CLI, base vs fix.** Setup:
- The CLI was built from this worktree with `node scripts/run-node.mjs`, once with the two production files at base and once at head.
- It ran as `openclaw` against an isolated state dir (`OPENCLAW_PROFILE=prreuse`, own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / config, scratch schema prefix).
- The data is a synthetic PostgreSQL agent with a 400-message session.
- Backends were counted by polling `pg_stat_activity` for the CLI's `application_name`.

3 runs each:

| command | base backends | fix backends | wall s (base → fix) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sessions export-trajectory --session-key agent:<id>:hist --json` (full session load) | 6 / 6 / 6 | 5 / 5 / 5 | 1.69–1.77 → 1.75–1.83 |
| `sessions --agent <id> --json` | 6 / 6 / 6 | 6 / 6 / 6 | 2.50–2.57 → 2.66–2.70 |
| `sessions tail --session-key agent:<id>:hist --tail 20` | 2 / 2 / 2 | 2 / 2 / 2 | 1.06–1.07 → 1.11–1.13 |

The results are equivalent: the exported `events.jsonl` (400 events) and `session-branch.json` are byte-identical between base and fix, and `manifest.json` differs only in `generatedAt`. A one-shot CLI does few repeated read-only opens of one agent, so it saves one backend and no measurable time. The per-run wall-time spread on this shared host is about ±0.1 s.

**Long-lived caller (Gateway-role process).** Setup: the same tree at base vs fix, 3 interleaved rounds, process role `gateway` with the engine installed through `installGatewayDatabaseEngine`, fresh PostgreSQL agents and a 200-turn session.

| op | base p50 / p95 ms | fix p50 / p95 ms |
|---|---|---|
| `SessionManager.openAsync` | 113 / 119 | 8.63 / 12.8 |
| `openModelContextAsync` | 17.6 / 24.5 | 17.8 / 25.8 |
| history tail (20) | 4.00 / 4.85 | 4.18 / 4.99 |
| session list | 0.70 / 0.83 | 0.69 / 0.83 |

Per `openAsync` call, `pg_stat_database.sessions` goes from 1 to 0 and `xact` from 3.9 to 2.9.

**Several agents in one Gateway-role process.** Base vs fix, 3 interleaved rounds, 6 PostgreSQL agents with 100-message sessions, `SessionManager.openAsync`. Each load was checked to return the full 100 entries. Per-round p50, ms:

| pattern | base | fix |
|---|---|---|
| same agent repeatedly (work removed: 1 → 0 new backends per load) | 121 / 128 / 127 | 3.4 / 3.9 / 3.7 |
| round-robin over 6 agents (more than the 4 idle slots per worker) | 127 / 120 / 125 | 119 / 134 / 124 |
| 6 concurrent loads (batch wall time) | 6459 / 6152 / 6615 | 6181 / 6554 / 6485 |

Neither the cache-thrash nor the concurrent pattern regresses, and neither gains. With more agents than idle slots in round-robin, every load still reconnects, exactly as on base. Concurrent loads each take their own exclusive connection. The cache's three-minute idle release is unchanged and was not measured: after it expires, the next load pays the base connect cost once.

**Accepted tradeoff:** a worker keeps up to 4 idle backends for up to three minutes, the cache's existing limits, which agent read leases now share with state reads. We did not measure many-agent concurrency against those limits.

**Gaps:**
- We did not start a Gateway on this shared host, which runs a production Gateway, so the long-lived numbers come from the Gateway-role bench above, not from a running Gateway.
- `doctor-database-diagnostics.postgres.test.ts` needs `CREATEDB`, which our local test role lacks, so this head relies on CI for it.

CI on `bce2640dc81`: PostgreSQL conformance shards 1/3 and 3/3 pass, and 3/3 includes `doctor-database-diagnostics.postgres.test.ts`, which failed on the first revision. Shard 2/3 fails only in `src/infra/database-engine/interactive-setup.integration.test.ts`, for both its SQLite and PostgreSQL cases, with `Gateway failed to start: Cannot find module '.../runtime/standalone-runtime-profile.mjs' imported from .../runtime/packages/llm-core/src/validation.ts`. That module and import arrived on main in #182856, merged at 21:30 UTC, after this branch's base. This PR does not touch them, and the same shard passed on this PR's first CI run, which predates that merge. We left it alone.

Local checks: `oxfmt --check`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` and `git diff --check` are clean. `pnpm lint` reports only pre-existing `max-lines` errors in files this PR does not touch. Autoreview was scoped-clean with no actionable findings.

pr-simplify was run on the final diff, asking whether the fix could use fewer concepts:
- The first revision's broad opt-in was replaced by the single owner that needs it, the read-only opener, passing the existing engine option.
- A bespoke engine-level test was dropped in favor of one regression on the existing agent-database PostgreSQL fixture. The maintenance boundary stays covered by the existing doctor diagnostics test.
- Net production change: +14/−4 across two files (mostly reformatting one call), with no new types, options or helpers. The +1 line in the test support module only exposes the read-only opener to the fixture.

prs.title: improve(database): speed up PostgreSQL agent session loads
prs.body:
Closes #182805
Supersedes #182845 (thanks @etzelm)

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL agent session loads reconnect and authenticate on every transcript hydration, adding avoidable latency.

## User Impact

Repeated session loads can reuse an idle PostgreSQL connection. SQLite behavior, database schemas, configuration, and the existing four-connection/three-minute idle-cache limits are unchanged.

Release-note context: PostgreSQL agent session loads reuse idle read-only connections to reduce repeated connection overhead. Thanks @etzelm.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose the existing connection-reuse option through the agent-store owner and opt in only from the read-only opener. Writable agent owners and maintenance opens keep dedicated connections. The change adds no new cache or connection manager.

The session-state audit found no read-only setting leaking between leases: read snapshots use transaction-scoped `BEGIN ... READ ONLY` and end with `ROLLBACK` (`src/infra/postgres-sync/transaction.ts:30-47`). Persistent lock/statement timeouts and search path are established at connect (`bridge.worker.ts:73-76`) and all their inputs, including URL, schema and store ID, are in the reuse key (`bridge-prestart.ts:24-32`). Only an idle server transaction status can be retained (`bridge.worker.ts:92-98`); queries use unnamed statements (`bridge.worker.ts:110`). No reuse-key or reset change is needed.

## Evidence

Real `prepareSessionTranscriptHydration(target).read()` on Homebrew PostgreSQL 17.11, Node 26.12.1, a synthetic 200-turn/400-message transcript, and 30 warm calls per arm:

| Measurement | Reuse disabled | Reuse enabled |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Hydrate p50 | 229.5 ms | 61.0 ms |
| Hydrate p95 | 418.2 ms | 188.1 ms |
| New connections per call | 1 | 0.033 (1 total; final 29 calls opened none) |

All 62 cold/warm reads returned identical full transcript SHA-256 `e09b26bcc8a195faff6facbefd2a6078046c41710ecf8ac1f69823f8f702c82f`. Timing is from a heavily loaded development host (load averages approximately 61–73), not a throughput claim. The first warm candidate sample took 30.1 s and opened the only new connection; the remaining 29 reused connections. The earlier unchanged-main reproduction measured 296.9/822.0 ms p50/p95 and one connection per call.

The real PostgreSQL backend-PID regression was RED on main (different backend PIDs) and GREEN with this change. Focused command: `pnpm test src/state/openclaw-agent-db.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'reuses one idle PostgreSQL backend'`, with the documented PostgreSQL conformance preload. Test execution: 39.89 s; first worker compilation: 224.63 s. Core type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

Final-head CI [40142873505](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142873505) passed on `91edc2cecca72ceb3ed56a58158831fc0bd36d1e`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. A real isolated Gateway using a fresh valid config and the existing synthetic PostgreSQL store passed five authenticated WebSocket `chat.history` calls. Every response contained all 400 messages with exact expected roles/text and identical content hashes. Durations: 172.7, 38.6, 45.9, 39.3, and 33.0 ms. The Gateway stopped cleanly. No model inference was needed for this history-only proof.

<details>
<summary>Proof setup limitation</summary>

Two QA-helper attempts stopped in the configured 90-second seeding subprocess (including a two-turn fixture); no history request ran in either attempt. Both Gateways became ready and were confirmed stopped. The successful proof used the supported CLI with the already-seeded 400-message store, preserving the same readiness/request deadlines and avoiding that seeding subprocess.

</details>

prs.title: perf(plugins): defer unused capture resolvers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin preparation workers retain a Jiti resolver even when their captured package modules never need import resolution.

## User Impact

Node Gateways with these plugins retain less worker heap. Artifact workers remain separate, and configured TypeScript path mappings retain their existing capture-time behavior. No configuration, migration, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Construct the existing capture-owned resolver at its actual resolution/source-inspection use sites. Keep eager initialization when `JITI_TSCONFIG_PATHS` is configured so a later tsconfig edit cannot alter a retained artifact's mapping. Bun's required source inspection remains eager.

A shared-worker experiment exposed stale dependency package-resolution caches across artifacts, including deferred package imports after a filesystem edit. This change preserves artifact isolation instead. Runtime production code is +12/-4 (net +8 lines); the configured-mapping capture contract accounts for the explicit early-initialization branch. There is no second cache or lifecycle owner. The reusable benchmark adds 59 net lines for the 40-plugin fixture, readiness timing, and verified source-update measurement; tests add 54 and documentation adds 14. The requested non-test/non-docs diff filter totals +84/−7, including the benchmark and its README.

## Evidence

- Focused resolution and conditions tests: 74 pass on Node; resolution tests: 18 pass on Bun.
- New Node work-count regression fails on the unchanged base (one unused resolver construction instead of zero) and passes with the change. Deferred import still captures the expected source and reuses the resolver.
- Configured-tsconfig regression prepares a module, edits its original mapping, then verifies the deferred import still selects the captured mapping.
Local built Node Gateway, with 10,000 synthetic sessions, 6,000 settled runs, 40 synthetic plugins, and four mock-provider turns. Ten-minute natural-idle endpoints on base `397807c7374c41ffe434215e1e091edba2997474` versus that base plus this change (the reviewed patch was unchanged by its subsequent rebase onto current main):

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Preparation workers | 40 | 40 | unchanged |
| Preparation-worker heap | 581.60 MiB | 543.86 MiB | −37.74 MiB (−6.49%) |
| All-worker heap | 992.27 MiB | 950.48 MiB | −41.79 MiB |
| Process RSS | 2248.85 MiB | 2250.59 MiB | +1.73 MiB (+0.08%) |
| Process CPU per idle minute | 979.18 ms | 951.02 ms | −28.16 ms |
| Main GC per idle minute | 14.57 ms | 11.99 ms | −2.58 ms |

Both endpoints sampled all 50 resident workers. This is a small retained-heap improvement, not a worker-count or demonstrated RSS reduction. Main GC maxima were 29.02→14.88 ms. Minor GC: 174→161 collections, 85.26→93.86 ms total, max 2.14→2.01 ms; major GC: 3→2 collections, 58.69→24.79 ms total, max 29.02→14.88 ms. Major tails are context only; no promotion tracing was performed. Loop p99 was 22.774→22.741 ms (28,865/28,719 samples); loop maximum was 426.77→626.00 ms. Main-GC telemetry does not measure worker GC.

The counterbalanced 120-second idle A–B–B–A repeats confirm the target heap result: 577.872→540.386 and 577.875→540.676 MiB (mean −37.343 MiB, −6.46%). RSS was 2613.381→2609.913 and 2582.519→2546.127 MiB (mean −19.930 MiB, −0.77%). All preparation-worker samples were present. Initial snapshots have different collection phases and are not a settled-heap comparison.

Edited-plugin update A–B–B–A: five measured edits per run, all 20 revisions verified. Edit-through-verified-RPC medians were 1455.890→1199.898 and 1422.046→1098.502 ms; mean paired reduction 289.768 ms (−20.14%). Process CPU/update was 1967.981→1532.723 and 1658.677→1376.227 ms (mean −19.79%); main CPU/update fell 22.96%. Main GC/update was 20.572→17.733 and 19.758→17.592 ms (mean −12.41%). GC maxima were 10.924→4.962 and 4.790→10.317 ms, with 76→73 and 75→72 collections. Loop maxima were 1075.84→461.64 and 1267.73→551.55 ms. Per-round loop sample counts were only 74–137; update tails and major-GC tails are context, not gates.

Whole-Gateway startup had opposite-sign first-pair deltas, so one further matched A3→B3 pair was declared before its results. Three pairs: 18.845→25.219, 20.193→17.868, and 19.987→18.412 seconds. Signed mean difference +0.825 seconds (+4.19%); no startup speedup is claimed. The logged `plugins.runtime-post-bind` phase averages 6.063→5.824 seconds (−3.95%); this is a broader plugin phase, not pure preparation time. Across all three natural-idle pairs, preparation heap averages 577.896→540.485 MiB (−37.412 MiB, −6.47%) and process RSS averages 2595.536→2573.160 MiB (−22.376 MiB, −0.86%).

Local measurements share a contended Mac; these are fresh-process starts with warmed compile caches, not cold filesystem-cache measurements. A missing launcher failed a saved-baseline setup before readiness; that attempt was not counted. A separate layout/cache warmup was excluded before its values were inspected. Active inventories match (40 synthetic plugins plus memory-core and openai); the candidate also discovers two disabled, unloaded QA entries absent from the saved baseline's layout. No production data or Gateway was used.

Short-idle context across three pairs: process CPU was +11.29% on the signed mean, compared with −2.9% in the ten-minute interval; no idle-CPU win is claimed. Main GC rose 14.91 ms/min in the short repeats, while it fell 2.58 ms/min over the ten-minute interval. GC counts were 77→108, 82→111, and 78→111; major counts were three per run. GC maxima were 15.25→12.46, 17.01→27.21, and 14.70→14.32 ms. Loop p99 rose 0.726 ms (+3.17%, 5,714–5,782 samples/run), with maxima 543.69→784.86, 781.71→858.78, and 544.21→693.11 ms. Loop p95 was not captured. Initial total worker heap was +5.51% across the repeats because natural collection phases differed; settled total worker heap was −2.49%. The primary repeatable improvements are retained preparation heap and verified update work.

- Changed-file formatting, repository type-aware lint, and diff checks passed; PR CI provides broad validation.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable findings.

The source-update benchmark edits a plugin, reloads it through the Gateway, then invokes its RPC and checks the new revision. Its edit-through-verification latency is separate from reload-only RPC latency. Warmups are excluded. The benchmark flags and procedure are documented in scripts/perf/README.md.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reduce compression work for short frame segments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compressed broadcast fanout repeatedly resets large zlib tables for tiny per-recipient envelope segments.

## User Impact

A small reduction in synchronous send CPU, with unchanged payloads, negotiation, the 1 KiB compression threshold, context-takeover policy, and worker-precompressed history reuse. No configuration or migration is needed. This is a CPU optimization, **not a memory reduction**: the usual 15-bit window gains one lazy shared compressor, approximately 144 KiB of [native workspace](https://nodejs.org/api/zlib.html#for-zlib-based-streams) plus stream overhead, regardless of connection count.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `memLevel: 5` only for pieces smaller than the existing threshold. Larger pieces retain zlib's default `memLevel: 8`: an exploratory varied-data control showed that lowering it globally increased compression CPU for large payloads. Shared contexts are keyed by both negotiated window and memory level. Cached large segments still always use level 8.

Production delta: +10 lines. The small additional context and selector avoid the measured large-payload regression from a global setting change. The existing compression owner still handles every frame; no user option or competing transport path is added.

## Evidence

Four concurrent local baseline/candidate pairs, alternating launch order and synchronized warm/start deadlines; 65 real negotiated WebSocket clients, 65 distinct recipient envelopes, 3,000 fresh broadcasts per side. The existing workload uses varied JSON, with one quarter of events below the compression threshold and the rest targeting 16 KiB. Four identical-source A/A controls used the same protocol. Node 26.12.1 on macOS; no CPU-affinity claim. Baseline source: `5895dc953bae861eb1f410b5f99075c1daeaecc3`.

| Metric per broadcast | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Mean paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Synchronous send CPU | 481.825 μs | 438.452 μs | −9.03% |
| Benchmark main-thread CPU | 2,926.615 μs | 2,884.671 μs | −1.48% |
| Total process CPU | 6,619.626 μs | 6,572.613 μs | −0.81% |
| GC time | 0.076195 ms | 0.078337 ms | +0.002142 ms absolute |
| Delivery p95 | 5.5005 ms | 5.4175 ms | −1.64% |
| Delivery p99 | 12.4936 ms | 11.8530 ms | −3.98% |
| Event-loop p95 | 2.0329 ms | 1.9704 ms | −3.11% |
| Event-loop p99 | 3.1729 ms | 3.0679 ms | −3.11% |

Send CPU improves in every pair (7.05%, 10.25%, 8.60%, 10.22%); A/A changes range from −0.38% to +0.93%. **No whole-process or production CPU improvement is claimed**: total-process results have mixed signs and are comparable to A/A variation. Clients inflate in the benchmark process; the synchronous send interval is the directly attributable result. Windows lasted 7.86–12.43 seconds, with paired starts within 1 ms. The Linux quiet-slot comparison did not obtain a slot; the queued task was stopped before any measurement window began. Linux performance remains an explicit gap.

Each side delivers 195,000 measured frames: **406,231,375 wire bytes and 2,488,264,185 decoded bytes**, with all 65 decoded SHA256 hashes matching. These are equal wire byte counts, not a compressed-byte hash comparison. Latency has 3,000 samples/side; event-loop counts are 7,579–10,461. Both p95/p99 improve in every pair. Maxima are noisier: pair 1 delivery max increases 119.55→142.27 ms and loop max 38.24→68.42 ms; A/A maxima also vary.

GC's largest paired rise is 0.009046 ms/broadcast, below the 1 ms/operation materiality floor. Baseline→candidate maximum GC pauses by pair: **14.17→11.26, 6.69→24.64, 1.98→2.33, 1.66→1.74 ms**; all satisfy `candidate ≤ max(50 ms, 2×baseline)`. A/B major-GC counts are 117–132 and minor counts 17–34 per side; per-kind p95/p99 are context only, not eligible tail gates. Major p99 rises 2.88/1.61 ms in pairs 1/2 with insufficient samples. No pauses were removed and no collections forced. Promotion was not measured.

Reproduce the transport workload with the committed harness:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/ws-compression-measure.ts \
  --clients 65 --profiles 65 --batches 3000 --port 41711 \
  --codec /absolute/path/to/saved-compression-owner.ts \
  --warm-start-at <epoch-ms> --start-at <later-epoch-ms>
```

The new `--codec` option keeps the broadcaster, transport, dependencies and fixtures identical while selecting a saved baseline or candidate owner. Preserve relative imports when placing the saved owner beside its source.

The deterministic frame-size sweeps also kept wire byte counts unchanged. At nominal payload sizes 512 B, 2 KiB, and 64 KiB, wire/decoded ratios were 100.64% (raw frames plus headers), 28.99%, and 15.13%. Larger sweeps retain the same quarter-small-frame mixture. The main 16 KiB mix was 16.33%. These are synthetic corpus ratios, not a production egress forecast.

Additional proof:

- Built isolated Gateway, synthetic 10,000-session / 6,000-settled-run / 40-plugin fixture, 65 authenticated compressed Control UI connections and 10 successful mock-provider turns on both baseline and candidate. Main-thread factory census found baseline **one deflater + one inflater**, candidate **two deflaters + one inflater**; contexts did not scale with 65 connections. Native workspace is an estimate, not an RSS delta. The current shared-context design already eliminates the historical per-socket premise.
- `pnpm build` and candidate `pnpm build:runtime` passed. Focused real-WebSocket checks: 9 serialized-frame tests plus 22 request-start/broadcast serialization tests passed. No new behavior test duplicates these contracts; the paired workload proves the performance change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the scheduled-main parent Stop test crashing when it tries to rewrite a kill record that controller settlement has already cleared.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior, production code, or migration changes. The existing product test continues to verify that stopping the parent settles its child without sending the parent a redundant notice.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commit 36e277d76147 (#175837) made controller settlement confirm provisional kills immediately. The ordinary parent-stop fixture still waited for the transient record, rewrote its timestamp, and forced a sweep; confirmation could clear the record before that rewrite. Remove that obsolete fixture machinery and its unused import. The public `sessions.abort` call and every terminal-cleanup, obligation-retirement, and no-notice assertion remain unchanged. The separate overlapping-confirmation/sweeper test is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Scheduled main [run 40125377367, job checks-node-compact-small-23](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40125377367/job/120965783750) fails at the old line 617 with `row.killReconciliation.killedAt` undefined. - The fixed local probe reached the unchanged 120-second test timeout on a loaded host (495.46 seconds wrapper wall time); this is inconclusive, not passing proof or a product verdict. - Scoped oxlint with the core configuration, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. The lint wrapper's artifact-preparation lock prevented its run; the explicitly permitted direct oxlint route passed.
- Author pr-simplify pass retained the minimal deletion: production +0/-0, tests +0/-11, docs +0/-0.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the parent Stop product test can fail when the real cleanup owner settles a child between the fixture's initial observation and its later atomic mutation.

## User Impact

User impact: there is no production behavior change; CI continues to exercise the complete Stop, settlement, cleanup, notice, and owed-input contract without failing on already-settled fixture state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture waited until a reconciliation marker existed, then assumed a later atomic read still contained that marker. Cleanup is allowed to remove it during that interval. The mutation now ages the marker only when the atomic snapshot still owns one; otherwise it makes no synthetic write and lets the existing settled-state assertions verify the completed outcome.

## Evidence

On the pinned base, the complete owner file reproduced the failure with 10 passing cases and the parent-Stop case throwing while reading the removed marker. On the corrected tree, remote changed-file format/lint and the affected gateway-server test type graph passed, and the same complete owner file passed all 11 cases. Hosted CI and repository review automation begin with this non-draft PR.

prs.title: perf(plugins): reuse bounded retention owners across references
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin invocations repeatedly copy and freeze the same acquisition-owner IDs for retained-reference diagnostics, even though the turn scope already owns a bounded, immutable copy.

## User Impact

This is a small allocation improvement: **1.18% less allocation per synthetic turn**, saving **12,455 bytes (12.2 KiB) per turn**. Final CPU results were mixed, with a **+2.04% mean paired change**; this is not a CPU-speedup claim. Diagnostic output and plugin lifetimes remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Administrator `plugins.inspect` and reload-blocker diagnostics must explain work acquired before inspection, so gating all recording on an active reader would lose acquisition facts. Reuse the frozen scope owner instead. Explicit consumer overrides still cross the existing copy/bounds boundary, including empty overrides.

Production delta: **+4 lines**, needed to distinguish immutable scope facts from explicit caller overrides that still require sanitization. No cache, subscriber lifecycle, configuration, or sampling policy. The existing benchmark now supplies a synthetic turn owner so it exercises this path.

## Evidence

- Baseline regression failed because two acquisitions copied the same immutable owner; candidate passes. Explicit override mutation isolation, 256-character bounds, and empty overrides remain covered.
- **62 focused tests passed** across recorder, administrator inspection, reload diagnostics, and instance/consumer lifecycle. Recorder: 7 tests, 46 ms test time; combined focused runs including compiler preparation: 65.35 s and 41.65 s.
- Changed-file oxfmt/lint, targeted `pnpm tsgo:core`, and `git diff --check` passed. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40145901484) and the required aggregate gate passed on `a63d1aaa1c8bdbfe726460215061187de66f6eec`.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean through P2. The scope-entry helper is the sole production writer of retention owners. GitHub Codex review also completed without findings.
- Built-Gateway proof: 10,000 synthetic sessions (2,000 archived), 8,000 settled runs, 40 active fixture plugins, and 10 successful mock-provider turns across five dashboards. Administrator inspection found the session-owned lease acquired before inspection while the provider response was held; after release, its reference disappeared and retention total fell from 3 to 0. All task processes stopped. Build passed in 4m17s. Build metadata retained the pre-rebase candidate ID; runtime compilation occurred after the patch-identical rebase and the intervening runtime change was verified in output. This is correctness evidence, not timing evidence.

### Measurement and decision

The Linux quiet slots were unavailable; no Linux measurement ran. Before local capture, the protocol was reduced to **4,000 turns / 200 warmup turns per side, 40 plugins, 16 calls/turn, 1 ms yield**. Both sides used the same committed workload and dependency closure, with only the diagnostics module switched between baseline and candidate. Runs were concurrent, nice 19, synchronized at warmup and measurement barriers, with counterbalanced launch order and source hashes verified before/after. Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64; **no Linux CPU affinity**, so these are local owner-workload measurements, not production-wide claims. Each measured side ran for less than 10 seconds.

Two allocation pairs both improved (-0.76%, -1.60%). Two initial scoped timing pairs were followed by the one predeclared extra pair for mixed GC results. Final scoped CPU signs were mixed (-1.60%, -0.55%, +8.27%): signed mean +0.01832 ms/turn, +1.71% of mean baseline, +2.04% mean paired percent. The owner-absent control had CPU changes -0.94%/-0.01% and lower GC/turn in both pairs.

Scoped GC increased by **0.02555 ms/turn** on the signed mean, below the agreed **1 ms/operation** absolute materiality threshold for this fixed-work workload. Rate-normalized GC increased **844.55 ms/min** and is reported explicitly below. We do not claim that noise was proven: no A/A controls or traced promotion pass ran. Maximum pauses stayed below 50 ms; latency p99 mean paired change was +13.84% (+0.142 ms signed mean), below the 20% adverse threshold, and event-loop p99 signed mean was -0.006 ms. Major-GC tails have fewer than 50 collections per side and are context only. This lands as a small allocation win under the stated per-operation thresholds, with mixed CPU and increased GC time disclosed.

Reproduce the measured workload on each revision (use separate state/HOME/TMPDIR and synchronized start barriers):

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/plugin-invocation-scope-measure.ts \
  --mode timing --operations 4000 --warmup 200 --plugins 40 --calls 16 --yield-ms 1 \
  --state-dir <isolated-state> --output <result.json>
```

Run allocation separately with `--mode allocation`; timing was untraced. The owner-absent control used the original committed harness before this PR's owner-scope addition, identically on both diagnostics revisions.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): reuse completed admission scope sweeps
prs.body:
Related: #172886, #174395, #182900

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated SQLite admission installs traverse retained session receipt scopes even when only references or facts changed.

## User Impact

Less CPU spent on admission bookkeeping. This is a small subsystem improvement, with no schema, configuration, stored-data, permission, settlement, or fencing changes. New-scope installs still perform their required sweep.

## Why This Change Was Made

Install already publishes only changed database records. The remaining work was a complete scope traversal inside each changed record. The publication owner now remembers the shared revision of its last complete sweep in a weak map keyed by the exact Admission object. Scope imports invalidate that result, and keyed publication never certifies a full sweep. Recording the revision before traversal preserves detection of concurrent remote retirement.

The existing fencing revision cannot stand in for that fact: keyed publication can acknowledge a revision without inspecting unrelated retired scopes. Production growth is **8 lines**, needed for this separate completion marker and its invalidation; no new publication path or caller-specific cache is introduced. Generation replacement naturally gets a different key.

## Evidence

Acceptance was declared before candidate measurement: 40 synthetic databases with 3,000 scopes each; zero, one, and 40 affected records; reference-only installs avoid repeated scope visits, scope imports retain exact publication/retirement behavior, and CPU or allocation improves without a material controlled regression. CPU/GC and sampled allocation use separate processes.

- Regression fails on the base with 256 unwanted scope visits, then passes with zero. Additional proof covers remote retirement followed by keyed publication, imported cells, reference deltas, and immutable earlier snapshots.
- Four focused files pass: **43 tests**, approximately 45 seconds including wrapper preparation. The receipt file itself takes under 0.6 seconds. Native worker cases cover settlement, stale snapshots, final-reader retirement, sibling references, and bounded task publication.
- Formatting, narrow core/test/script lint, and diff checks pass. Targeted core typecheck (`pnpm tsgo:core`, native tsrs) passes.
- Runtime built with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build`; declarations omitted for runtime proof. The final build completed in 90.2 seconds.
- Final built, isolated loopback Gateway: **10,000 synthetic sessions, 8,000 settled runs, 2,000 archived sessions, 41 loaded plugins**, ten completed mock-provider turns, roster/history and label churn, successful snapshot capture, clean shutdown in **225 ms**. This is correctness proof, not a paired whole-Gateway speedup claim.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. The helper refused its provider/configuration mismatch; operator configuration was preserved.
- Rebased onto current main before pushing; the measured owner source hash is unchanged. PR CI validates the integrated head.
- [CI run 40146450842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146450842) passed on exact head `2af14871197ca421ff7d8ae37a56c270ef26dead` in 479 seconds (7m59s). Both required CI-gate publications passed; no CI failures or reruns. GitHub code review also completed on this head with no findings. Merged as `688febc23436f7686f994cd88fe1c50f2b4217aa`.
- No Testbox/Crabbox lease. Both shared timing slots were occupied on immediate checks; one check also exceeded the shared dirty-page guard. Timing below uses five serial counterbalanced pairs of tiny local processes, each limited to 29 seconds. No production Gateway was exercised.

prs.title: fix(ui): stop offering admin upgrades above a member role ceiling
prs.body:
Related: #157182

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Control UI offering **Request admin** when the authenticated person's role cannot grant administrator access.

## User Impact

Role-limited people see guidance explaining that device approval cannot lift their role ceiling. Pairing-limited administrators retain the existing request and approval flow. No permissions, role assignments, configuration, or protocol version change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing handshake carries an optional presentation fact derived from the Gateway's actual role policy. The UI consumes that fact instead of guessing from role names, session access, or current device scopes. Role guidance has a separate dismissal identity so it cannot hide a later actionable pairing upgrade. One policy read supplies both the existing session cap and the new fact; no new owner, cache, RPC, or authorization path.

The handshake is a connection snapshot. After a role change, reconnect to refresh its presentation; request and approval-wait RPCs still check the current role. This fix does not force reconnects or revoke accepted work merely to refresh a notice.

## Evidence

- Real isolated Gateway regression: red on the base for the missing role-ceiling fact; repaired role, request/wait authorization, and session-cap checks pass, 23 selected cases across three files (121.06 seconds wall including compiler preparation).
- Faithful source-browser regression: red with the pre-fix availability owner and the actual forwarded role fact; the fixed owner was restored byte-for-byte. All 15 current browser scenarios pass (44.80 seconds), including capped-member guidance without an upgrade request and the preserved pairing-limited admin approval flow.
- Owner retirement and existing notice consumers: 24 cases across three files pass (5.52 seconds). Retired requests cannot replace role guidance, and a fresh eligible snapshot restores the action.
- Targeted Gateway/protocol and UI/test types, scoped type-aware lint, English catalog verification, documentation lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Protocol/native generators were run; no tracked generated delta is needed.
- Inspected synthetic Before/After screenshots from the actual source Control UI are embedded below. Final canonical source-bound Auto Review completed all six passes: scoped-clean at its configured P0-only threshold, no findings (openai/gpt-6.1-sol).

Production delta: +33/-7 lines; tests and fixtures: +84/-0; documentation: +8/-0. Growth is limited to the authoritative presentation fact, its guidance/dismissal consumers, and distinct wire/render/retirement regressions.

No live Team Gateway, real user-role mutation, provider call, full build, merge, or deployment was used. CI seconds are not yet available; no CI was dispatched or rerun for proof.


### CI follow-up

The first head’s `checks-node-changed-compact-large-20` job exposed one stale exact hello-auth expectation (`connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts:667`). The follow-up adds the intentional `roleAllowsAdmin: true` field and preserves deep equality plus the exact effective-scope, recovery, token, and telemetry assertions. The full 47-case file passes locally (48.67 seconds wrapper wall); targeted types, one-file lint/format, and whitespace checks pass. This addresses the hosted review’s sole P2 finding. Production code and visual proof are unchanged; the completed production review is retained, with this one-line expectation correction independently inspected. The original failed CI is not relabeled green; new-head CI remains pending.

### Before

![Before: role-limited member is offered an impossible admin request](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/967f5a54-ca22-4154-a03d-b91476e647d0)

### After

![After: role-limited member receives role guidance without an upgrade action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec0dec94-442d-49ff-8668-6a472562ec31)

@etzelm
