prs.title: perf(plugins): reduce request scope enumeration work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin invocations repeatedly copy Gateway request scopes and recheck whether every string field is enumerable, even though the runtime can provide those enumerable keys directly.

## User Impact

A small reduction in allocation during plugin calls. No intended user-visible behavior change or configuration action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `Object.keys` for string fields and preserve the separately filtered symbol fields. Every child still receives its own scope, with unchanged weak registry borrowing, expiry, replacement, identity isolation, and authority callbacks. Sharing the whole scope would be incorrect: suspended wizard continuations refresh request authority, and plugin children have independent mutable fields.

Production delta: **+5 lines**. The separate symbol pass preserves the existing public scope copy contract; no cache, new owner, or parallel implementation is introduced. Extend the existing isolation test for enumerable and hidden symbols, and give the existing invocation benchmark the request field shape used by Gateway method dispatch.

The profiling build already included #181771 and #182676 (both verified ancestors of `fe6f5c21`); this targets residual cost after those fixes.

## Evidence

Acceptance was recorded before measurements: preserve isolation and lifetime behavior, count small CPU/allocation gains, use absolute paired deltas and the campaign's GC/tail sample rules, and run matched identical-source controls before rejecting noisy GC or promotion results.

Local measurement results, three counterbalanced serial pairs, 1,000 synthetic turns per side with 16 prepare/execute calls per turn, collected-object heap sampling, untraced timing:

| Metric per synthetic turn | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sampled allocation | 344,682 bytes | 334,640 bytes | -2.91% |
| CPU | 0.50746 ms | 0.51058 ms | +0.00312 ms (+0.61%) |
| GC | 0.01437 ms | 0.01691 ms | +0.00254 ms (+17.69%) |

Allocation improved in all three pairs (-1.29%, -4.28%, -3.16%). CPU was mixed-sign, so the third pair was run as predeclared; no CPU win is claimed. GC's absolute rise is below the 1 ms/operation materiality threshold. Maximum GC pauses, baseline → candidate: 4.72→9.24 ms, 2.80→5.08 ms, 2.62→3.04 ms. Each latency distribution has 1,000 samples; event-loop p99 has only 999 samples and is context. These busy-Mac probes do not establish whole-Gateway or model latency.

Command: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/plugin-gateway-scope-measure.ts --turns 1000 --output <result.json>` under isolated state and home directories. Shared quiet slots had long queues; the queued job was cancelled and the authorized local fallback was used. No quiet-host result or traced promotion claim is made. Built-Gateway RPC proof passed on Linux and locally on macOS: 10,000 synthetic sessions, 6,000 settled runs, 2 clients, 2 warmup + 20 measured plugin-scope calls, preserving plugin identity, provenance, registry, client, and scope identity across await.

- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-instance-invocation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 21 tests passed; 45.90 s including cold compiler preparation, test execution under one second.
- Changed-file oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed. Broad validation belongs to PR CI. No Testbox allocated.
- Additional local built-Gateway proof: 40 synthetic startup plugins plus `openai` and `memory-core` (42 loaded), 10,000 sessions and 6,000 settled runs; a mock-provider chat turn completed and delivered 14 session events. No production Gateway or paid provider was used.
- Remote runtime-only build passed with the supported `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build:docker` route. Full declarations were not run: the declaration builder correctly refuses a borrowed dependency installation.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. The configured autoreview route was refused for not matching the operator configuration; no configuration was changed.
- Baseline source: `5895dc953bae861eb1f410b5f99075c1daeaecc3`. The pre-push rebase onto `673e524ee6a3` changed none of the affected scope, invocation, or benchmark owners; the reviewed patch is unchanged.
- This is a behavior-preserving optimization: existing baseline behavior tests remain green; measured allocation is the performance evidence, rather than a timing threshold in unit tests.

<details>
<summary>Paired tails and collection details</summary>

All timing runs were untraced. Entries are baseline → candidate. Latency tails have 1,000 samples per side; loop tails have 999 (p99 context only). Major-GC tails are context only (one collection per side). The mixed-sign latency mean is evaluated by the signed absolute delta; no metric crosses the material adverse threshold.

| Pair | Latency p95 ms | Latency p99 ms | Loop p95 ms | Loop p99 ms | Minor GC count | Major GC count | Minor total ms | Major total ms | Max GC ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.540 → 0.289 | 0.685 → 0.575 | 1.879 → 1.656 | 2.012 → 2.652 | 12 → 12 | 1 → 1 | 11.507 → 11.382 | 4.716 → 9.237 | 4.716 → 9.237 |
| 2 | 0.294 → 0.563 | 0.371 → 0.740 | 1.613 → 1.909 | 1.717 → 2.204 | 12 → 11 | 1 → 1 | 10.662 → 11.245 | 2.805 → 5.075 | 2.805 → 5.075 |
| 3 | 0.288 → 0.282 | 0.410 → 0.366 | 1.592 → 1.583 | 1.723 → 1.657 | 12 → 11 | 1 → 1 | 9.920 → 9.812 | 2.625 → 3.043 | 2.625 → 3.043 |

GC p95/p99 have too few collections to gate; the totals and both maxima are reported above. No raw-Gateway CPU, throughput, or model latency improvement is claimed.

</details>

## Inherited CI failure

[CI run 40146265480](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40146265480), job `checks-node-changed-compact-large-7`, fails the two reconnect cases in `src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog-list-retention.test.ts`. Both throw `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'client?.connect.scopes')` at `session-catalog-visibility.ts:45`. The fixture provides `connId` and `connectionSignal`, but no `connect`; the changed scope-copy loop is not involved in that failing access.

The single failing file was reproduced on PR head and with the exact baseline scope implementation from its main parent (`673e524ee6a3`) restored in the same checkout. All other production inputs were unchanged; the remaining PR differences were its scope test and benchmark fixture, neither used by this file. Both runs: **2 failed, 2 passed**, with the same exception and stack (46.83 s on head; 37.01 s with baseline). No CI rerun or unrelated repair was used to chase green. Landing uses the explicitly authorized inherited-failure exception once the remaining checks finish.

prs.title: perf(agents): reuse frozen hydrated history fingerprints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prompt-cache diagnostics retain mutable revision maps and repeatedly hash messages that transcript hydration already shares as deeply frozen data. In the synthetic owner workload, switching from cloned to shared hydration with unchanged prompt-cache code increased retained main-isolate memory 3.06×. This PR removes 58.2% of that shared-path footprint while preserving history-rewrite detection, changed-field reports, and provider request bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The append path normalizes a message's children and freezes its envelope. The envelope is deeply frozen but does not carry the transcript-owned-root marker. `cloneTranscriptView` recognizes and shares it; prompt-cache preparation and fingerprinting previously did not. Both now consume the existing frozen-plain-data proof, including frozen content under mutable projections.

The existing worker prepares newly admitted messages; subsequent observations reuse their packed fingerprints. Mutable messages still undergo revision checks. No new cache, retained payload, configuration, migration, or hydration-owner change. Full diagnostic history remains: a WeakRef-only field-diff design would lose information when prior payloads disappear. Runtime source is +8/−3 lines (**+5 net**), aligning the existing admission boundaries; the separate benchmark is proof tooling.

## Measurement

Pinned base `8b46672f4762d8c76237ad678b88b5f7201e0609`, head `a3efa15ba6b28b0a1e9e7f9099447caea992bbfa`. Node 26.12.1, synthetic append-shaped frozen transcripts through the actual `cloneTranscriptView → convertToLlm → onModelRequest` path. Each independent process has **16 sessions × 128 messages, 16 first observations + 320 warm observations = 336 calls**. All fixtures and call counts match; stable-prefix assertions pass. Five samples per variant, alternating base/head launch order and swapping interleaved CPU sets under the exclusive quiet slot and shared production guard. These are sequential owner samples, not concurrent whole-Gateway pairs. The guard delayed starts for dirty pages; no measured process was interrupted. No history-worker fallback warnings occurred.

Forced GC before, after first observations, and after 20 further rounds. The following are five-run means; percentages below are changes of those means. The signed paired mean gives the same decision (warm CPU mean paired percentage −33.6%).

| Metric | Cloned hydration, unchanged owner | Shared hydration, before | Shared hydration, after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Final retained main-isolate bytes/session | 62,204 | 190,453 | **79,690 (−58.2%)** |
| Final retained bytes/resident message | 486.0 | 1,487.9 | **622.6** |
| Final retained bytes/model call, amortized | 2,962 | 9,069 | **3,795** |
| First-observation process CPU, ms/call (80 calls/variant) | 1.892 | 2.194 | **4.049 (+1.856 ms)** |
| Warm process CPU, ms/call (1,600 calls/variant) | 1.587 | 0.316 | **0.209 (−33.8%)** |
| Cold + warm process CPU, ms/call (1,680 calls/variant) | 1.602 | 0.405 | **0.392 (−3.3%, mixed signs; inconclusive)** |
| Warm main-isolate GC, ms/call | 0.114585 | 0.017464 | **0.013940 (−0.003524 ms)** |

**Tradeoff:** worker admission raises first-observation CPU by 84.6%; the repeated resident-history path is cheaper. Total CPU over the declared workload is roughly neutral, not a claimed CPU win. The acceptance result is the consistent 58.2% retained-memory reduction. CPU includes process worker threads but excludes hydration/projection; GC covers the warm hydration/projection/observation interval. Retained bytes/call amortize resident state over 21 observations/session; they are **not** allocation turnover or newly retained bytes per request. This fixture supports the mechanism, not an exact attribution of a production survivor-profile ratio.

<details>
<summary>All five base/head samples and GC counts</summary>

| Sample | Retained bytes/session, before → after | Warm CPU ms/call, before → after | Cold + warm CPU ms/call, before → after | GC ms/call, before → after | Max single GC ms, before → after | Minor collections, before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 191,003.5 → 77,175 | 0.325013 → 0.219275 | 0.413411 → 0.400357 | 0.017691 → 0.014655 | 2.624 → 1.964 | 4 → 3 |
| 2 | 191,000 → 81,366 | 0.310447 → 0.209350 | 0.399185 → 0.393417 | 0.017815 → 0.013381 | 2.472 → 1.640 | 4 → 3 |
| 3 | 188,249 → 81,366 | 0.297113 → 0.236869 | 0.387060 → 0.414235 | 0.016051 → 0.015260 | 2.115 → 1.803 | 4 → 3 |
| 4 | 191,007.5 → 77,175 | 0.312738 → 0.192369 | 0.403098 → 0.377068 | 0.017850 → 0.014127 | 2.653 → 1.988 | 4 → 3 |
| 5 | 191,007 → 81,366 | 0.333863 → 0.187166 | 0.423482 → 0.374298 | 0.017914 → 0.012278 | 2.547 → 1.554 | 4 → 3 |

Untraced pooled GC: cloned hydration 100 minor collections / 183.336 ms; shared before 20 / 27.943 ms; shared after 15 / 22.304 ms. Major/incremental/weak-callback events: zero in each warm interval. Pooled minor p95/p99: clone 2.138/2.287 ms (n=100), before 2.624/2.653 ms (n=20), after 1.988/1.988 ms (n=15). All tails are context-only below the required sample counts. Both per-sample maxima are reported above; none approaches 50 ms. No adverse GC decision requires A/A controls here. Event-loop tails were not measured in this owner workload.

</details>

### What remains resident

Separate before/first/final heap snapshots, one process per variant, each with the same 16 sessions and 2,048 messages. These are restricted diagnostic-reachable **shallow bytes**, not dominator retained sizes or the heap-used deltas above. Named context/module bindings and V8 ephemeron edges identify the maps; final snapshots have no discovery warnings. Transcript keys, primitive payload values and string-memo text are excluded. Shared nodes are deduplicated in the union.

| Main-isolate diagnostic graph | Cloned hydration | Shared before | Shared after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Observation-history bytes (2,048 roots each) | 853,104 | 853,392 | 824,432 |
| Record-memo bytes / roots | 0 / 0 | 1,871,632 / 3,584 | 114,688 / 512 |
| String-memo bytes / roots | 0 / 0 | 61,440 / 512 | 0 / 0 |
| Immutable-value memo bytes / roots | 0 / 0 | 29,504 / 512 | 0 / 0 |
| Message-memo bytes / roots | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 647,440 / 1,536 |
| Deduplicated union, including map storage | 1,149,400 | 2,951,624 | **1,071,576** |

The after history and message memo share all 1,536 cached fingerprint roots (647,440 bytes), counted once. The remaining 512 record memos belong to shared frozen content beneath the fixture's 25% mutable custom-message projections. Diagnostic union growth from first to final observation is **448 bytes on both shared variants**, supporting bounded state across repeated requests rather than accumulating request history. The packed diagnostic history is preserved.

Separate collected-object sampling (512-byte interval, 336 calls each) estimates main-isolate allocation at **172,718,168 → 114,327,424 bytes (−33.8%)**, or 514,042 → 340,260 bytes/call; 296,667 → 193,187 sampling records. Exclusive stable-stringify stack family: 36,122,808 → 26,312,872 bytes (−27.2%); other fingerprint-family allocation: 95,580,504 → 39,713,304 bytes (−58.5%). A heap snapshot cannot recover stable-stringify allocation provenance, so this origin breakdown comes from sampling, not invented retained-string attribution. Worker allocation is outside this main-isolate profile.

Separate whole-process traced promotion: **105,081,872 → 114,402,392 bytes (+9,320,520; +8.9%)**, one pass each. Minor trace records 45 → 59 (93,599,944 → 102,517,912 promoted bytes); major records 12 → 14 (11,481,928 → 11,884,480 bytes). This includes startup, warmup, forced GCs and all emitting isolates; it is **context only**, not a matched steady-state per-call promotion gate. Instrumented timings do not enter the untraced decision table.

## Proof and review

- Base-failing regression exercises frozen unbranded hydration through conversion and request observation; candidate avoids main-thread history hashing and retains exact changed-field diagnostics. Existing fingerprint-byte assertions are unchanged.
- Focused files: `prompt-cache-observability.history.test.ts`, `prompt-cache-observability.test.ts`, `prompt-cache-request-observer.test.ts`, `provider-prompt-state.test.ts`, and `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` (128 distinct tests including the new retention regression).
- Retention test: 4 sessions × 512 messages × 21 calls/session. Original owner retains 2,930,152 bytes against the unchanged 2,228,224-byte budget (red); candidate passes on Node 24.22.1 and Node 26.12.1. Growth limit remains 262,144 bytes.
- `eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts`: 22 tests passed. Export-name collision guard passed. Targeted `pnpm tsgo:core`, changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed.
- [Exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40143109862) is green, including the required aggregate gate. Initial CI exposed negative warmup fixture indices skipping assistant/tool-result cases. Reproduced, fixed by warming the full mixed history 100 times, and reran the focused failing test with the same memory limits; no rerun-for-green or threshold widening. The production fix did not change.
- **Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**: no actionable P2+ findings, including review of the warmup repair. The helper rejected a provider-route mismatch; no operator configuration was changed. GitHub Codex review also completed with no findings on this head.

## Deployment signal and remaining limits

Look for fewer main-isolate `fingerprintRecord` / `fingerprintMessage` / stable-stringify-family survivors per model call at matched observation phases, while history-rewrite and field-diff output remain unchanged. Synthetic owner proof does not establish whole-Gateway latency, total worker-inclusive allocation, or the exact production survivor ratio; the first-observation CPU increase is the principal tradeoff. No production profiling was performed.

Ready for lead review; **this lane must not merge the PR**.

prs.title: test(sessions): avoid duplicate conformance executions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session-accessor conformance matrix executes five SQLite scenarios twice through identical functions and fixture scopes.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The suite executes 37 cases instead of 42 (-11.9%), preserving every assertion. Five registration lines change; no test declarations, source lines, production seams, SQL, schemas, or PostgreSQL conformance cases are deleted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct SQLite adapter inherits every method from the public adapter except entry listing and entry updating. Keep the CRUD scenario on both adapters because it exercises those two distinct entry points. Register the five scenarios that use only inherited methods once through the existing SQLite-only registrar, as the rest of the suite already does.

The bounded audit covered 24 complete test files and 201 expanded cases. It retained the other 196 cases, including worker settlement, cancellation, authority, cache invalidation and upgrade regressions. Five duplicate executions are below the requested batch target; there is no safe reason to delete distinct contracts to fill a quota.

| Duplicate scenario | Retained proof |
| --- | --- |
| Exact persisted-key lookup | Same callback once: canonical lookup, exact miss and exact hit |
| Lifecycle cleanup | Same callback once: age/segment filtering, retained history and archive content |
| Raw event append/read | Same callback once, including sync and async reads |
| Raw message rejection | Same callback once, retaining the message-write integrity boundary |
| Message append/idempotency/publication | Same callback once: durable message, idempotency conflict and emitted update |

## Evidence

Acceptance recorded before the first test or benchmark execution: run the complete conformance suite on baseline `349369c020470a2184304c35f99ab3fc45f13726` and candidate with the default pinned Bun runner and one worker. Primary result must be 42 passing baseline cases and 37 passing candidate cases; the five removed executions must retain their unchanged callbacks, and production must remain untouched. Require no new static findings.

Timing is secondary: acquire the campaign timing lock, require host load below 24, keep cold and warm cohorts separate, alternate baseline/candidate with at least five samples per arm, and report wall-clock median/p95/range. Any >20% adverse cell stops a performance claim. If no qualified window appears after 60 minutes, report counts and unqualified observed durations without a speedup claim. Correctness runs do not require the timing lock. No application SQL saving is claimed or SQL harness pair needed for this test-registration change.

Formatting, basic lint, type-aware core lint and diff whitespace checks pass. One isolated Codex preservation review found no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings. The complete affected suite passed on both revisions: baseline 42/42 and candidate 37/37. Observed command durations were 310.026 s and 197.963 s, respectively. These are unqualified high-load observations: the baseline built worker bundles, and the candidate reused them; no wall-clock speedup, median/p95, or application SQL saving is claimed.

prs.title: fix(android): keep model catalogs responsive during refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Scope: Android catalog refresh and warning recovery.**

This PR fixes two Android catalog-consumer defects:

- Repeated metadata or health notifications can supersede valid in-flight reads before their successful results reach the UI, leaving model choices empty.
- Provider-status settlement can leave a refresh warning visible after the catalog has recovered.

## Changes

The changes stay within the existing general, provider-settings and chat catalog owners and their shared result parser:

- Preserve valid same-scope in-flight reads and accepted model choices.
- Coalesce legacy unflagged metadata hints into an immediate-first refresh followed by fixed 30-second windows with pending catch-up. Continuous hints cannot postpone progress indefinitely.
- Join active reads for health/status observations and perform status catch-up when needed, clearing recovered warnings without hiding genuine failures.
- Preserve immediate invalidation for genuine catalog, authentication, configuration, agent/session and manual changes, including rejection of obsolete responses.

The 30-second window applies to legacy unflagged hints, not to all refreshes.

## Evidence

Exact Android head: `7a5e0bda258ac938456e42cfcb6b4f2b2fa23a30`.

[Immutable Android source, regression and native retained-upgrade evidence](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/eab6eb823e6993152c11341d733498df2df8cf9b/README.md):

- 147 focused tests passed. Failing/passing owner regressions isolate sustained-hint starvation and bounded cadence; additional regressions cover status-only catch-up. All five published source/test hashes match this head.
- Two completed native captures used the exact installed APKs with official Gateway 2026.9.6 and audited Gateway build `a7f5cc2`. Actual app-UI sends completed and rendered.
- All three catalogs retained 732 rows through provider failure and recovery; warnings appeared and then cleared. The native transition combined semantic and status events; owner regressions isolate status-only behavior.
- The same APK, pairing and conversation survived the supported Doctor migration and Gateway upgrade.

These captures used synthetic provider/inference data. They demonstrate Android catalog retention, warning recovery, and app-UI sends.

## Compatibility and non-goals

- This is an Android-only change; no Gateway implementation changes are included.
- The legacy compatibility path has a removal condition: all supported Gateways must publish semantic change flags.

prs.title: fix(doctor): refuse malformed UTF-8 before claiming node state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can move a malformed interrupted node-host claim before reporting its encoding error, or discard a distinct claim whose invalid bytes replacement-decode like the source. Web Push claim recovery shares the same gap. Ordinary malformed-file imports are already refused on main by #180861.

## User Impact

Malformed retired node-host and Web Push files produce a recoverable UTF-8 warning before text-based claim recovery changes their contents or paths. After backing up and correcting the affected files, operators can rerun `openclaw doctor --fix`. Valid Unicode, literal replacement characters, and existing canonical state remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate text in the existing snapshot owner before hashing or claim recovery, using `decodeUtf8Input`. Its error retains the backup, corrected-copy, and retry guidance. Node-host and Web Push consume that validated text instead of decoding again later. Byte-hashed migration callers, snapshot fingerprints for valid input, database schemas, and locking remain unchanged.

## Evidence

The new claim cases fail on unchanged main owners: four failures, three passing controls. They expose missing claim paths for node-host and both Web Push inputs, including distinct invalid bytes with equal replacement-decoded text. The corrected Unicode retry also checks canonical node readback and cleanup.

Full node-host, Web Push, and shared snapshot suites: 67/67 passed (343.32 seconds including compilation and cache verification). After integrating main, all seven malformed-input cases passed again (38 unrelated cases skipped). The guidance follow-up reran all seven malformed-input cases successfully, and all seven passed again after final main integration. Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, MDX, and diff checks passed. Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

Fresh compiled Doctor and installed-stable upgrade were not rerun: the source-owner regressions cover recovery and SQLite readback; preparing another runtime build would exceed the bounded live-proof budget. Contributor-provided Linux compiled Doctor and installed-stable upgrade evidence applies to prior head `6554e11735cfe3b2da62f792d65d36a24109b337`, not this revision.

Production +11/-11 (net 0); tests +56/-17 (net +39); docs +5. The smaller production path removes duplicate late decoding. No generated files or changelog changes.

Contributor: @Leon-SK668 (Leon-SK668 <0668001470@xydigit.com>).

Local broad `check-changed` reached its dead-export audit after passing core production and all selected test typecheck graphs. Its only failure was the dead-export audit, which reported unused exports in untouched generated protocol declarations and unrelated files, with no changed Doctor file in the findings. This local audit is not reported as green; exact-head PR CI remains the broad gate.

<details>
<summary>Prior-head compiled Doctor and installed-upgrade evidence</summary>

The contributor ran `node ../node-import-utf8-proof-20261023.mjs` against the node-host migration at `6554e11735cfe3b2da62f792d65d36a24109b337`, on Linux with Node 24.22.1 and synthetic isolated state. A main-owner comparison moved a malformed interrupted claim away from its original path; correcting only that retained path did not migrate it. At the contributor head, the original claim and bytes survived refusal, and correcting that file let Doctor import the exact Unicode configuration and remove the retired names.

A paired-input probe used different invalid bytes (`e9` and `ea`) that replacement-decode identically. The main-owner comparison deleted the distinct claim; the contributor head retained both original files, with zero canonical rows until corrected retry. Both kept the existing recoverable Doctor exit contract.

The contributor also installed the official 2026.10.6 package in an isolated prefix, seeded canonical node state, and installed the `6554e11735cfe3b2da62f792d65d36a24109b337` package over it. Malformed-source refusal preserved the source and canonical settings; corrected retry succeeded. The actual stable and candidate node CLIs both reached the synthetic loopback recorder at `/proof`; the recorder returned 503, so this was endpoint-consumption evidence, not a completed pairing session.

Those observations predate this revision and cover the node-host path. They do not constitute current-head runtime or Web Push upgrade proof.

</details>

prs.title: perf(sessions): share resident actor entries across projections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Durable session actors retained two decoded copies of their session entry: one in the stored-row map and another in hot state. Each copy includes nested skill and system-prompt snapshots. Hot-state projection cloned that entry again after mutations.

## User Impact

Active durable sessions retain less worker memory, especially when skill and system-prompt snapshots are large. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one actor-owned entry across those internal views. Incoming postimages still detach once, writers replace entries, transaction forks preserve the previous entry for rollback, and public reads/commit receipts remain detached. The existing cache limits, persisted representation, transcript contents, and public APIs are unchanged. Runtime production code is net −2 lines; tests are +2, the reproducible benchmark is +208, and documentation is +35. The broad non-test/non-doc diff is +236 because it includes the benchmark and its README. This tooling growth supports the requested owner-level proof; it adds no production instrumentation hook.

Release-note context: lower retained worker memory for active sessions with large entry snapshots.

## Evidence

Node 26.12.1; a synthetic Gateway fixture with 5,000 sessions and 6,000 retained runs. Four real synthetic-provider child sessions were warmed through agent/tool turns, producing 36,514-byte session entries. Five fresh-process pairs used alternating launch order, identical source-replacement instrumentation, and forced GC in the native worker. Snapshots were captured outside timing windows.

| Metric (5 samples per side) | Base mean | Candidate mean | Paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Four-actor resident graph | 1,060,800 B | 860,948.8 B | −199,851.2 B (−18.84%) |
| Whole native worker post-GC heap (context; mixed signs) | 166,720,547.2 B | 166,542,936 B | −177,611.2 B (−0.11%) |

The comparison uses base `803ad1fdc36e3473b4a9c538fd3dfb4a15f4431a` with only the three runtime owner files replaced for the candidate. Their measured bytes match the current PR head; rebasing did not change those runtime files. The resident-owner saving is consistent. In the initial source-loaded SQLite worker snapshot, 50,258,296 bytes belonged to tsx’s in-process transform cache; this does not establish that deployed builds retain that cache. Loaded code and source-runtime machinery dominate the whole worker, so this is not a claim of a large whole-worker reduction. Transcript history windows, actor residency, statement caches, and reply-transfer lifetimes were audited; this patch changes only the demonstrated duplicate actor entry.

### Latency and correctness

The candidate completed a full synthetic Gateway memory-soak run: 4 clients, 2 measured rounds, 8 completed measured turns and 8 session resets, plus warmup. The driver verified its edit-visibility control. Two simultaneous, CPU-swapped native-owner pairs completed with identical command identities and separate synthetic fixtures. Each side performed 1,200 native reads and 1,200 real patch commits. Shared quiet-slot and production guards remained healthy. The following are untraced results; percent changes are the mean of the two paired percentages.

| Metric | Base mean | Candidate mean | Signed paired delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Worker CPU, ms/operation | 1.5354 | 1.4334 | −0.1020 (−6.66%) |
| Total GC, ms/operation | 0.1205 | 0.1084 | −0.0121 (−9.83%) |
| Read mean, ms | 0.9920 | 0.9762 | −0.0157 (−1.46%) |
| Read p95, ms | 1.6221 | 1.5274 | −0.0948 (−5.85%) |
| Read p99, ms | 5.0419 | 5.0535 | +0.0116 (+0.36%) |
| Commit mean, ms | 3.7628 | 3.5888 | −0.1740 (−4.69%) |
| Commit p95, ms | 6.0186 | 5.5173 | −0.5013 (−8.42%) |
| Commit p99, ms | 10.2503 | 10.1863 | −0.0641 (−0.39%) |
| Worker event-loop p95, ms | 4.4114 | 4.1953 | −0.2161 (−4.92%) |
| Worker event-loop p99, ms | 6.6191 | 6.1440 | −0.4751 (−7.21%) |

Every read/commit tail has 1,200 samples per side per pair. Event-loop sample counts were 2,660→2,697 and 2,387→2,461. Read p99 deltas were −0.0731/+0.0964 ms; commit p99 deltas were +0.9084/−1.0365 ms. These mixed-sign tails are context, with no adverse paired-mean gate; CPU fell in both pairs (−6.27%/−7.05%).

| Untraced GC kind | Pair 1 base→candidate count; total ms; max ms | Pair 2 base→candidate count; total ms; max ms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scavenge | 166→153; 265.892→231.736; 4.603→3.167 | 168→152; 246.896→224.010; 2.870→3.684 |
| Incremental marking | 6→5; 3.813→3.502; 0.781→0.819 | 5→5; 2.857→3.156; 0.689→0.711 |
| Major | 6→5; 35.250→27.486; 7.342→6.094 | 5→5; 23.882→30.545; 5.207→8.346 |
| All GC | 178→163; 304.955→262.723; 7.342→6.094 | 178→162; 273.634→257.712; 5.207→8.346 |

GC pause percentiles are context: fewer than 200 collections per kind/side and fewer than 50 majors. Neither maximum GC pause reaches the max-pause safeguard. Loop maxima were 59.507→58.032 and 38.896→66.224 ms. Separate traced pairs, with identical instrumentation on both sides, measured allocation and promotion. Allocation sampling used a 32 KiB interval and included objects collected by both minor and major GC. Promotion came from complete, isolate-matched V8 trace windows; 75 collections from other isolates were excluded on each side in each pair. Both pairs completed all 1,200 reads and 1,200 committed writes per side.

| Traced owner metric (2 swapped pairs) | Base mean | Candidate mean | Signed paired delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Estimated allocation, bytes/operation | 760,658.1 | 683,869.7 | −76,788.4 (−10.09%) |
| Promotion, bytes/operation | 108,350.5 | 84,950.0 | −23,400.5 (−21.59%) |

Allocation sample counts were 54,389→48,866 and 54,552→49,027; allocation fell 9.93% and 10.26%. Target-isolate trace GC counts were 171→157 and 172→158; promotion fell 22.34% and 20.84%. Traced timings are not used as gates. One temporary traced-preload launch failed syntax parsing before the workload and is preserved as setup failure; the corrected probe passed independent review, and both complete measured pairs are included.

Decision: the owner retains 18.84% less memory, CPU falls consistently by 6.66%, estimated allocation falls 10.09%, and promotion falls 21.59%, with no adverse untraced latency or total-GC gate. No adverse GC/promotion/max-pause result required A/A rejection controls. Whole-worker retained-heap variation remains inconclusive. This is a small production simplification, ready for the lead's landing decision; it is intentionally unmerged.

The exact PR head `d89f3ecd709c30c526d88cfe7e13f7d2fafbdb4e` has an inherited PostgreSQL conformance (2/3) failure: seven `interactive-setup.integration.test.ts` cases fail before Gateway readiness because the isolated runtime omits `standalone-runtime-profile.mjs`. All seven test signatures and the missing-module cause match the newest scheduled main run at attribution time: [main job 121006161355](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138789542/job/121006161355), main head `87f00b1b5254861d944e524cdd8bb3a65f53b59f`; compare [PR job 121006359977](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138813188/job/121006359977). Both report 7 failed / 271 passed in that batch. The failing test, its fixture builder, the importing module, and the root helper have identical blobs on both heads. The root helper/import arrived in upstream #182856; the fixture's explicit copy list omits it. This lane does not change those files. Logs were fetched once per completed job; no CI reruns were requested. All other code checks completed successfully (62 successful check runs; skipped/neutral checks recorded separately). The aggregate CI gate remains red because of that shard. Its automatic classification used the older successful main run `40134490303`, which predates the upstream import; the newer matching main job above is the current attribution evidence.

Focused proof: actor kernel and native worker tests (24 tests), export-name collision guard, and both eager-import/PR-wrapper closure files (22 tests) passed. Participant-repair and entry-residency consumer tests also passed (18 tests). Changed-file formatting/lint and the targeted scripts typecheck (`pnpm tsgo:scripts`, native checker) passed.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): production/test/docs and the benchmark were reviewed in separate scopes, with no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings. The configured autoreview provider did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

Reproduction is documented in `scripts/perf/README.md`; the new owner probe measures native reads after host-replica invalidation, real patch commits, operation counts, worker CPU/GC/event-loop samples, and post-GC heap. Promotion requires a separate traced pass and is not inferred from retained bytes.

<details>
<summary>Worker attribution and cache bounds</summary>

| Owner | Bound/lifetime and observed attribution |
| --- | --- |
| Transcript worker source loader | 12,644,352 B in tsx's transform cache; Node ModuleLoader retains 15,784,328 B, including its LoadCache and ResolveCache. These are source-loaded fixture costs, not a production-memory estimate. |
| Transcript database scopes/history | 64 database scopes; reader idle expiry is 30 minutes. Recent history retains 16 windows, each admitted at ≤1 MiB serialized. Visible history projections retain 16 sessions per connection; boundary collections have no independent byte cap. Connection disposal clears them. |
| Model-context navigation | One snapshot per connection, with maxEvents decoded requests and boundary/model/thinking facts; prefix membership scales with history pages. Identity changes and disposal invalidate it. |

prs.title: refactor(mentions): keep Inbox database work off the Gateway thread
prs.body:
Related: #153801
Backend prerequisite for #153812.

## What Problem This Solves

Mention delivery and Inbox policy checks need to leave the Gateway thread without losing access checks, durable state, or notifications; prefix-only excerpts also hide selected names in long messages.

## User Impact

The existing Inbox and personal session visibility use database workers, and new entries retain recipient-specific context. Message-commit ordering, current access checks, dismissal, replay suppression, and retention limits remain intact. Transient notification failures do not suppress unrelated recipients or strand other connected views.

No new setting, permission, table, column, index, or database version is introduced. Older writers may discard the optional preview/highlight metadata when rewriting a source; retained IDs, dismissal and expiry survive, and the candidate uses its plain-text fallback. [Accepted excerpt design](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153812#issuecomment-5766660909).

The earlier compatibility proof covered the **shared Inbox store at `5e74fbbcf71`**, not whole-installation rollback. It used version-local agent metadata without bypassing schema guards. The current rebase inherits newer main schema versions; that historical roundtrip is not a downgrade test of this new head. This feature adds no further database version.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Inbox remains the owner of ordering and retention. The existing shared-state broker owns writes; read-only workers prepare policy facts. Cache lifetime now retains canonical target-revocation authority, and synchronous guards revalidate permissions at transaction and commit. Committed-input observers join accepted asynchronous work before acknowledgment.

This separates the backend prerequisite from the notification-card UI, keeping the presentation change independently reviewable.

## Evidence

Current head: `51e8c1ae26a5b5f2e587e8ba17da47115de2b637`, based on main `4d1c5d19ecc893ecef7b52cf7b3be002c794e770`. Both related PRs remain open; **no merge or auto-merge is requested**.

- Resolved current-main conflicts without restoring retired APIs. Recipient aliases are reconciled inside the authoritative transaction, and failed view publication recovers at FIFO settlement. Mixed-cohort expiry and record/list/dismiss recovery have failing-original regression controls.
- Final owner batch: **40 tests / 4 files passed**, 84.24 s. Earlier current-main boundary and sibling batches passed **273** and **340** tests; these overlap and are not a unique combined count.
- The preceding rebase `fd768fec797` passed core types, all 25 test-type groups, generated Swift parity, packaged worker syntax, and full build (**302.19 s**), with a scoped-clean whole-candidate P0–P2 review. Current CI repairs additionally pass core/scripts/Gateway test types, typed lint, and two scoped-clean independent reviews. No new full-build result is inferred from the earlier build.
- The full local changed macro reports an unchanged-main max-lines error in `context-engine-maintenance.ts` (710/700). The file matches main exactly. Existing hosted-CI policy treats limit diagnostics as warnings; no rule, assertion, deadline, or limit was weakened here. The upstream Mermaid 12 size excess is likewise retained, not claimed as a local performance pass.
- Reproduced and repaired the first hosted-CI failures: moved unchanged DTOs/codecs into leaf contracts, removed worker imports through the host validator registry, registered the exact required SQLite binder ABI, sorted the canonical test inventory without changing membership, and retained canonically regenerated Workboard assets. Madge and runtime-value graphs both report zero cycles; 41 export-guard tests retain unrelated-module rejection.

prs.title: fix: restore standalone helper launches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Standalone update, MCP, and file-transfer helpers could launch JavaScript paths or inline programs that were unavailable after packaging.

## User Impact

Packaged helpers use declared entries and the existing worker/child dispatcher. Source Node/Bun launches keep their package roots, runtime flags, and lifecycle behavior. No configuration change or new dependency is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime-process manifest now owns the remaining helper entries and copied programs. Explicit modules replace inline native-gate, cleanup, and file-transfer programs. Dependency entries resolve relative to their calling package; path resolution does not impose an execution policy.

The update canary distinguishes CLI launches from worker dispatch. Retained generations preserve embedded executable identity, and native-gate bytes are staged even when complete rollback retention is unavailable. Existing admission, cancellation, environment, and cleanup protections remain at their owners.

This completes the runtime cutover following #182405. It removes inline helper programs and repeated caller-owned paths; added code consists of explicit entry modules, manifest projections, and regressions for their distinct launch/lifecycle boundaries. Build-time source enforcement follows separately.

## Evidence

Targeted source, script, and tooling typechecks; production, script, and test lint; formatting; and line-count checks pass. Native declaration preparation for the five touched package-boundary plugins passes (697.54s). Full package/platform checks remain with PR CI.

- Entry resolution and canary routing: 32 tests pass under Bun, 158.50s wall.
- Runtime asset/build suites: pass, 119.82s. Generated-source check passes in 0.89s.
- Native PR wrapper inventory: passes, 110.03s.
- Admission: all 25 tests pass under Node, 202.97s; focused Bun case passes, 414.82s. A fixture now creates its tracked directory through the secure-temp owner so an external scratch volume does not invalidate the test before admission runs.
- The unchanged native-gate/cleanup and retained-generation sources retain their Node/Bun boundary proof: 34/34 (Node 26.31s, Bun 16.81s) and 52/52 (Node 32.85s, Bun 29.31s), respectively. Source hashes were compared when assembling this candidate.
- Independent Codex review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Small probes compiled with Bun revision `5d8fe974f` reproduce missing-entry and wrong-dispatch failures, then pass with declared entries and source directories hidden. They cover file-transfer, native-gate/cleanup, retained embedded generation identity, MCP selection, and copied secret-provider programs with synthetic inputs. Loose Node/Bun comparisons pass too. These are entry-routing proofs; no whole-application or database qualification is claimed, and no interpreter tripwire is used.

## CI Repairs and Local Limits

CI exposed native Node source imports that referenced emitted `.js` paths, and a Doctor capability check that treated argv[1] as a worker path after Bun added `--no-install`. Source tooling now imports the actual TypeScript modules; Doctor receives an explicit worker URL separately from argv. Update fixtures recognize declared worker and retained-script entries while preserving lifecycle assertions.

- The four npm/source-import suites pass in 56.99s wall; the build-cache suite passes all 54 tests in 235.89s.
- Nine selected update/platform regression cases pass, 55 unrelated cases skipped, in 806.92s wall. This includes 190.97s cold compiler preparation and real Doctor/SQLite custody. The pre-fix post-core replay had three failures and one passing control.
- All ten Doctor capability cases pass under Node and Bun, including malformed contracts and revoked authority. Targeted types, source/test lint, formatting, whitespace, and line-count checks pass. Fresh Codex review reports no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Two memory packaging tests fail because their synthetic install lacks `@openclaw/fs-safe`; both reproduce on main `dd155be2`, with unchanged relevant inputs through `6c33f5ff`.
- A broader local Node admission run was stopped after 12 passing cases and four earlier-refusal failures. All four failures were independently reproduced on main `6c33f5ff` (251.04s for the first case; 140.92s for the other three). No complete Node CLI-admission-suite pass is claimed.
- The local Bun fresh-runtime admission case also fails on unmodified main `6c33f5ff` (144.71s). An observation-only replay shows its provisioning spy stops before the native-gate call because no admission context was observed. Original CI reached a later point (`admission` was recorded); that distinction remains explicit. The temporary observer was removed byte-for-byte, and fresh-head CI must qualify the normal CI path.

## Current-Head CI

[CI run 40142694288](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142694288) completed at the current head. Its only failing root job contains the two Docker-selected memory packaging cases above; the aggregate gate fails because of that job. Both cases reproduce on main, and their determining sources, package manifest, lockfile, and test block are unchanged through the actual CI base and tested merge. The same-named scheduled main job ran different test partitions, explaining the informational new classification. Landing uses the native inherited-failure route and preserves these failures; no CI rerun was requested.

prs.title: feat(ui): show session mention notifications
prs.body:
Closes #153801

Stacked on backend prerequisite #155419 so this diff remains UI-only while both PRs stay unmerged. **No merge or auto-merge is requested.**

## What Problem This Solves

People working in another session can miss a new mention unless they open the Inbox.

## User Impact

New mentions show a compact card with a side avatar, sender and session, the highlighted selected username, immediate message context, and **View session**. Long messages use context around the mention—not the beginning of the message.

Each tab stays quiet for sessions already visible there, including desktop split panes. Hidden narrow-screen panes can notify; making the pane visible retires its active or queued card. Closing or timing out a card leaves the shared Inbox entry intact. Hover and keyboard focus pause the five-second timeout. The first accepted Inbox snapshot is the baseline: it never toasts; subsequent fresh IDs notify. Reconnect and temporary loss/restoration of session visibility do not replay retained mentions.

The Inbox and notifications share escaped, recipient-specific excerpts and explicit selected-name spans. The backend prerequisite supplies optional excerpt metadata in existing retained records; old records remain plain text. No new setting, dependency, permission, retention rule, or database table is introduced. [Accepted persistence design](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153812#issuecomment-5766660909).

## Why This Change Was Made

Matches the approved side-avatar reference, with compact mobile actions and the selected username using the active theme’s accent rather than a fixed color. The existing mention capability owns arrivals and the shared toast owner owns timing, cancellation, and FIFO. Notification presentation loads lazily without activating unrelated Inbox health or model-auth work on Settings pages.

## Evidence

Current UI rebase: `75fb106050544a5f2ea04bac025aa68084892058`, on backend `51e8c1ae26a5b5f2e587e8ba17da47115de2b637` and main `4d1c5d19ecc893ecef7b52cf7b3be002c794e770`.

- **202 focused UI tests across 12 files passed**, 20.19 s, covering shared Inbox ownership, arrival/reconnect behavior, notification cancellation, toast timing, and split panes.
- **18/18 bundled Control UI browser cases passed** on [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35929875580): the seven mention scenarios plus all eleven plugin-Settings scenarios. The four previous 16-pixel alignment failures now pass. The actual source tree was verified inside the runner; the command exited 0 and its lease was stopped. Browser test duration 48.06 s; complete remote command 131.819 s.
- The Settings stylesheet and its plugin overrides now share one bundle boundary, preserving their cascade order while keeping the dense boot CSS within the existing limit. No selector, assertion, timeout, or budget was weakened.
- Preserved current-main sidebar-card rendering, deferred health refresh, extracted fixtures, and split-pane behavior during conflict resolution. Production UI types and all 25 test-type groups pass after composing the backend protocol. Typed lint, styles, formatting, and i18n checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. A mechanical fixture deduplication preserved the same response and assertions; all 35 cases in that file passed in 3.26 s and remain part of the earlier 202, not additional unique tests.
- Measured startup JS **371118 B / 7 requests**, startup CSS **51144 B / 1 request**, largest CSS **51144 B**: all within their existing limits. The unchanged Mermaid 12 asset exceeds the local deferred-size check exactly as on untouched main; upstream #156363 documents it and existing hosted-CI policy reports size excess as a warning. No local performance pass or limit increase is claimed.
- The UI patch is byte-identical after rebasing onto the repaired backend; production UI types and the exact generated-plugin asset check pass on the composed head. The previous backend CI failures were reproduced and repaired. Fresh exact-head [UI CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35938291761), including its CI gate. The matching Security Review run passed; skipped native lanes are not counted as proof. Both PRs remain intentionally unmerged. No live Web Push or native notification transport was changed or claimed as tested.

### Current browser proof

Synthetic mock-Gateway data rendered by the actual bundled app. Images are cropped to the session and notification context.

Before

![Before: another session is visible before the fresh mention](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9258f4d8-fe0b-4579-819b-36a3669d182b)

After

![After: fresh mention card with selected-name highlight and View session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9150d06a-3d15-43f3-9109-5773ca9e9c20)

<details>
<summary>Historical feature verification and design captures</summary>

- **145 focused regressions passed**: 69 Gateway tests and 76 UI tests, including actual message commit, selected-recipient excerpts, restart/redaction behavior, arrival ownership, cancellation, FIFO, and lazy loading.
- **7/7 real Control UI browser scenarios passed** on [Blacksmith Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35670838532), lease `tbx_01m3376dwe8vqh1gh6a6f5at85`. Includes tabs/splits, local dismissal/navigation, desktop/light mode, 390px/320px layouts, and tapping the expanded target outside the smaller visible mobile button. The one-shot command exited 0 and stopped its lease; this is separate from the PR CI gate.
- **24 Chromium stylesheet checks passed**: all 11 built-in themes plus a custom palette, each in light and dark modes. Notification surfaces and selected-name colors follow their existing theme tokens. This focused color check adds no per-PR test suite.
- The code/test audit removed duplicate helper coverage, markup-specific assertions, an unused type export, redundant lifetime state and duplicate checks. Remaining privacy, replay, lifecycle and split-view boundary tests were kept. P0–P2 autoreview and repository changed-code gates passed.
- Exact-head CI and main-branch integration remain required before merge; this is not a merge-ready claim.

<details>
<summary>Verification scope and measured cost</summary>

The focused nine-file regression invocation took 91.67 seconds including shared preparation. The browser file took 38.77 seconds; its app boot, Gateway handshake, routing and visible-pane interactions require the browser boundary. The color matrix used real Chromium with the production stylesheets and canonical theme inventory, independently of the full-app browser flows.

</details>

prs.title: fix(cli): route config mutations through a running Gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set`, `config patch`, and `config unset` exit 1 with `Cannot admit config set ... This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership` whenever a Gateway is running. This started in v2026.10.10-beta.3; v2026.10.9 did not refuse.

The Windows companion app (openclaw/openclaw-windows-node, every published version including stable v2026.9.8-1) runs these commands inside WSL while its own Gateway is running:

- Setup fails at its first step, `openclaw config set gateway.reload.mode off`, which runs right before the onboarding wizard.
- Later steps also fail: restoring the reload mode, the Tailscale device-pair URL, and the local AI `--batch-file` and `config unset` writes from setup and the tray.

## User Impact

Config writes from the CLI work again while a Gateway is running, and they still go through the Gateway as the only writer.

- Output and exit codes match the offline command.
- Unsetting a path that is not set still fails with the same error text.
- The Gateway applies each change under its own reload policy. Switching `gateway.reload.mode` does not restart it.

Two kinds of change still need the Gateway stopped, with the same stop-then-rerun guidance as before:

- `database.*` settings, which choose the state database the running Gateway holds open.
- Changes a merge patch cannot express, such as an authored `null` value.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **CLI:** When another process owns the state, `runWithLocalStateOwner` now passes `requestOwner` to its `onForeignOwner` callback. This sends one request to the Gateway that owns the state, checking that owner again right before sending, the same way the existing routed path does.
- **`config set`, `config patch`, `config unset`:** The command calls `config.get` first to get the current hash, then prepares the change exactly as it does offline (validation, roster mapping, auth-mode cleanup, the missing-path error). Then it sends the authored before/after diff as one `config.patch` with that `baseHash`.
  - Arrays the patch replaces are listed in `replacePaths`. So are base arrays that disappear when a subtree is deleted or replaced by a scalar or array, for example `config set tools.toolSearch false` over `{include:[...]}`.
  - Before sending, the CLI replays the patch with the Gateway's merge rules. If the result does not match the prepared config, it refuses instead of sending an approximation.
  - A failure after the request was sent is reported as an uncertain outcome and is never retried locally.
- **`--dry-run`:** Still never contacts the Gateway.
- **Removed:** The old `openclaw gateway call config.patch` workaround text, from the refusal and from the docs.
- **Gateway fix:** `config.patch` with `gateway.reload.mode: "off"` answered `UNAVAILABLE: config.patch persisted but was not applied (failed)`. This happened even for the reload-mode write itself.
  - Cause: when reload is off, the reloader intentionally leaves every non-plugin change unapplied, so waiting for it to apply could only ever report a failure.
  - Fix: `shouldAwaitGatewayConfigApplication` now stops waiting when the resulting mode is `off`. The write is acknowledged once saved. A change that needs a restart still schedules one.
  - The existing unit expectation that cold-storage settings are awaited under `off` is updated to match.

**Write target and immutable config (review follow-up):**

- **Bound to one file:** a routed write only proceeds when the Gateway's `config.get` `path` and this command's config file resolve to the same file. Otherwise it refuses before sending anything, so a CLI pointed at a different `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` under the same state directory can't have its diff land in the Gateway's file.
- **Immutable config:** `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1` and `OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1` are now enforced at the routed commit with the same `assertConfigWriteAllowedInCurrentMode` guard the local writer uses at its write. This keeps the immutable-config enforcement from #140719 intact on the routed path.

**Data model and upgrade compatibility:** this PR adds no stored data, schema, migration, or config shape. Routed writes are persisted by the Gateway's existing `config.patch` writer, the same path the Control UI and the companion app's RPC writes already use. Offline writes are unchanged. Upgrading from the latest stable needs nothing, including the window where an updated CLI runs while the old Gateway is still serving. The routed request carries only `raw`, `baseHash` and `replacePaths`. Those fields are all inside v2026.10.7's closed `config.patch` schema, and that release already advertises `local-state-owner-routing-v1`. An earlier head also sent `response: "summary"`, which stable rejects. ClawSweeper flagged it and it has been removed (see below).

**Stable Gateway request contract (review follow-up):** `buildConfigOwnerPatch` now owns the whole `config.patch` request, including `baseHash`. It no longer sends `response: "summary"`, so a v2026.10.7 Gateway that is still running after a CLI update accepts the write. The CLI only reads `restart` from the full response, which every version returns.

**Accepted edge cases:**

- With `gateway.reload.mode: "off"`, a routed write that needs a restart makes the Gateway schedule a restart. An offline write would only have printed `Restart the gateway to apply.`. The CLI now prints `The Gateway is restarting to apply it.`
- **Mixed versions, reload off:** an updated CLI talking to a still-running v2026.10.7 Gateway that sets `gateway.reload.mode off` gets that Gateway's own `UNAVAILABLE ... persisted but was not applied` answer. The value is saved; the command exits 1 and says to inspect it. The reload-off acknowledgement fix is Gateway-side, so it applies once the Gateway runs this version, which every update does when it restarts the Gateway. Other writes to a stable Gateway succeed (see Evidence).
- If the owner has no Gateway listener, for example another CLI holding offline custody, the command is refused with the existing `The state owner has no Gateway listener` message.
- The Gateway does not check `expectedOwnerId` for `config.patch`, because its request schema is closed and this PR avoids a protocol change. The CLI checks the owner lock right before sending, and `baseHash` ties the write to the exact config the CLI read.

**Backport:** this needs to go to `release/2026.10.10` for beta.4.

## Evidence

- **`src/cli/config-owner-route.process.test.ts` (new):** Starts a real in-process Gateway that owns the state lock, then runs the real CLI entry as child processes using the app's exact command shapes. Wall time is 13.6–15.2s with `--maxWorkers=1`; most of that is Gateway boot plus 11 CLI child processes. No cheaper layer covers routing, auth, the merge, and runtime application together.
  - Set `gateway.reload.mode` to `off`, then back to `hybrid`. Both succeed, the Gateway reports the new value, and there is no restart request, no hot-reload recovery, and the observer WebSocket stays open.
  - Set `gateway.nodes.commands.allow` to an array with `--strict-json`, then to a shorter array. The Gateway reports the replaced value.
  - Set `tools.toolSearch` to `{include:[{source:"mcp"}]}`, then to `false`. The Gateway reports `false`. Before the descendant-array fix, this failed with `config.patch would remove entries from array path(s): tools.toolSearch.include`.
  - `config set --batch-file f --dry-run` leaves the file unchanged, then `config set --batch-file f` succeeds (provider plus primary model). `config unset` then removes both paths.
  - `config unset` of an absent path exits 1 with `Config path not found: <path>. Nothing was changed.` and leaves the file unchanged.
  - `config set database.postgres.schemaPrefix ...` still refuses with offline guidance and leaves the file unchanged.
  - Before the Gateway fix, the reload-mode test failed with the `UNAVAILABLE ... not applied (failed)` error above. On `main`, every write case fails with the offline-only refusal.
- **Review follow-up cases** (same file): a CLI pointed at a different config file refuses and neither file changes. `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1` and `OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1` each refuse, the file is unchanged, and the Gateway still reports the old value. All three fail when their guard is removed.
- **Built CLI against a real installed v2026.10.7 Gateway** (`npm install -g openclaw@2026.10.7` into an isolated prefix; `openclaw gateway run` with isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`/state/config, loopback port, token auth, reload `hybrid`; this PR's built `dist` run as `node openclaw.mjs`):
  - `release/2026.10.10` (`8d18f82`) CLI: `config set logging.level warn` refuses with `This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership`, file unchanged.
  - PR CLI: `config set logging.level warn`, `config set models.providers.local --strict-json '{...}'`, `config set gateway.reload.mode hybrid`, `config unset logging.level` and `config get gateway.reload.mode` all exit 0. The file and the Gateway reflect each change. The Gateway logs `config.patch write actor=cli` for each one, and its pid is unchanged (no restart).
  - PR CLI: `config set gateway.reload.mode off` saves the value but exits 1 with the stable Gateway's `UNAVAILABLE ... not applied` error (the accepted mixed-version edge case above).
- **`src/cli/config-cli-owner-patch.test.ts` (new, under 1s):** Checks that the patch body and `replacePaths` are correct for array replacement and subtree deletion, and that an authored `null` is refused. It also checks that the request carries `baseHash` and no field outside v2026.10.7's `config.patch` schema. Re-adding `response: "summary"` makes it fail.
- **`src/cli/config-state-owner.process.test.ts` (updated):** Previews are unchanged. A lock without a listener still refuses before any write. The offline writes for set, patch, unset and the fast unset route are unchanged.
- **Regression runs, all passing:**
  - `local-state-owner.process.test.ts`: 18 tests
  - `local-state-owner.test.ts`, `models-cli.state-owner.test.ts`, `config-cli.test.ts`, `claws-cli.state-owner.test.ts`, `config-write-flow.test.ts`: 116 tests
  - `server.config-patch.test.ts`, `server-methods/config.test.ts`: 88 tests
- **Static checks:** `pnpm check:changed` passes, run with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1`. The dead-export scan's findings, for example `isCapabilityConsentErrorDetails` and `assertGatewaySuspendingError`, are all in files this PR does not touch.
- **App compatibility:** I read the app's call sites as data, without running them. None use `config patch`, `--merge`, or `--replace`. One uses `--strict-json`. Batch writes use `--batch-file` with `--dry-run` first. The app treats exit 0 as success. `GatewayConfigCliCompatibility` parses `config get` error text, which this PR does not change.

prs.title: fix: CLI runs stall for minutes scanning an agent database the Gateway already opened
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: CLI processes such as `openclaw agent exec` (used by the Auto Review tool for every pass) spend up to several minutes in a full SQLite `integrity_check` when they open an agent database that the running Gateway already holds.

## User Impact

Auto Review passes and other CLI commands that open a large, Gateway-held agent database start in seconds instead of waiting minutes, and the Gateway no longer stalls on its own rescans after one of those processes is killed mid-open.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the Gateway holds a lease on an agent database, any second process opening the same file was refused reuse of integrity proof (`integrityGateReason=lease-class`) and ran a full scan. A live process that already finished admitting that exact file has verified it, and a second process rescanning a file the Gateway is actively writing adds no protection.

Now a claimant reuses that admission when another lease on the exact same path has completed admission and its PID start time still matches. Schema and canonical-index validation still run. Migrations, alias paths, unfinished admissions, and stale or revoked leases keep the full check. Doctor and updater quick-check handles hold the maintenance lease, which refuses all lease claims, so they cannot lend admission.

Named edge case: the borrowing process never verified the file itself, so if it is the last process to close it does not publish a clean-close seal, and the next opener runs one full check. That is still strictly fewer scans than before, where every borrower scanned at open. Documented in `docs/reference/database-schemas/integrity-and-recovery.md`.

## Evidence

**Production (OpenClaw Team Gateway, 2026.10.7, read-only log analysis, 2026-10-24):** the main agent database is 43 GB. Auto Review's `agent exec` passes produced 97 `lease-class` full scans totaling 7,465 s that day (about 2.1 hours), 50–321 s per open. Two of those processes were killed mid-scan; their unfinished leases then forced Gateway-side `stale-lease-full` rescans (4 scans, 280 s total, one 89 s scan that stalled all of that agent's sessions for about 55 s).

**Local reproduction through the real entry point:** isolated dev Gateway on this branch's base, main agent database grown to 1.98 GB with synthetic rows, a synthetic API-key profile so `agent exec` reads the agent database the same way production does.

| Build | Separate `agent exec` open of the Gateway-held agent DB |
| --- | --- |
| main (`52068cf86d6`) | `integrityGateReason=lease-class`, `mode=full`, 967 ms integrity scan |
| this PR | Opens the same file (confirmed with `lsof`), no integrity gate event, no slow-open warning |

Scan time scales with file size, which matches the minutes observed at 43 GB.

**Tests:**
- New `reuses a live peer process admission instead of rescanning the file` (real child process holds the database): fails on main with `integrityGateOutcome: "healthy"` (a full scan ran), passes with the fix. It also asserts that a borrower closing last publishes no seal.
- New lease unit cases: an admitted live peer lends admission; a peer with unfinished admission or on an alias path does not.
- `openclaw-agent-db.integrity-lease`, `openclaw-agent-db-lease`, `openclaw-agent-db.integrity-cache`, `openclaw-agent-db.open-timing`, `server-close.agent-databases`, and `sqlite-integrity` suites pass. The existing clean-close test now has its last closer verify the file itself, since a borrower intentionally cannot certify it.
- `tsgo:core` and the core oxlint shard pass; independent Codex review (P0–P2) was scoped-clean.

**Not covered:** the effect on the production Gateway itself, which needs this change deployed and the same log query repeated.

prs.title: perf(sessions): avoid copying catalog rows for adoption lookup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated native-session catalog listings allocate a full selected-agent array just to find a handful of adopted sessions. This remains after shared catalog snapshots and #182986. Both earlier snapshot-sharing changes (#159900 and #114829) are ancestors of the profiled build; this fixes their residual adoption cost.

## User Impact

Less allocation during adopted-session discovery, with the same bindings, agent scope, privacy checks, and refresh cadence. No configuration or migration changes. This is a small production optimization; the percentages below describe the isolated catalog workload, not overall Gateway performance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The adoption helper consumes the existing frozen catalog snapshot directly, combining agent scope, plugin ownership, and initialization checks in one indexed pass. It decodes source markers only for eligible rows. Indexed iteration also avoids the frozen-array iterator allocations observed during profiling. The public all-entry listing API and no-snapshot SDK path remain supported.

Production runtime delta: **+13 lines**. That small growth preserves the distinct public all-entry API while removing its intermediate array from adoption lookup; no cache, index, or invalidation state is added. Acpx has no independent adoption poller: the visible sidebar refreshes 120 seconds after completion, with extra listings for navigation, pages, and continuation. External native changes have no reliable Gateway event, so cadence stays unchanged.

## Evidence

The committed `scripts/perf/session-catalog-selection-measure.ts --adopted` workload uses the real handler and 10,000 persisted synthetic rows split between two agents. One provider exposes 32 native rows; exactly the selected agent's 16 rows bind. Every complete ordered entry/response hash matched across all eight runs. Baseline uses main's unchanged helper (blob `89219603235bccb7d247b1b365f39e2f532d393c`); candidate uses this patch. Same workload and runtime, 4,000 calls/run, counterbalanced A/B then B/A order on the authorized local host.

| Mean per call | Before | After | Absolute delta | Relative delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Total sampled allocation | 264.82 KB | 108.39 KB | −156.43 KB | −59.1% |
| Adoption-helper allocation | 160.25 KB | 3.44 KB | −156.82 KB | −97.9% |
| Source-marker decodes | 5,000 | 16 | −4,984 | −99.7% |
| CPU, untraced | 0.674 ms | 0.319 ms | −0.355 ms | −52.6% |
| Total GC, untraced | 0.00621 ms | 0.00338 ms | −0.00283 ms | −45.6% |

Allocation passes include objects collected by minor and major GC. Timing/GC passes use neither heap sampling nor GC tracing. Each pair improved allocation, CPU, total GC, latency tails, and event-loop tails. Local scheduling limits throughput claims; remote quiet slots were occupied, and no remote measurement is claimed. Major GC/promotion and long-running retention are not established by these short runs; there is no new retained state.

<details>
<summary>Per-pair measurements and reproducible workload</summary>

| Pair | Total allocation B → C, bytes/call | Helper allocation B → C, bytes/call | CPU B → C, ms/4,000 calls | Total GC B → C, ms | Minor collections B → C | Maximum GC pause B → C, ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| B/A | 265,107 → 108,235 | 160,802 → 3,406 | 2,568.77 → 1,251.19 | 24.294 → 13.483 | 39 → 16 | 1.388 → 0.964 |

All observed collections were minor; major count/time was 0 on both sides. Per-collection p95/p99 are context only (39/16 samples per pair): pair 1, 0.963/1.069 → 1.034/1.034 ms; pair 2, 1.134/1.388 → 0.964/0.964 ms. No pause exclusions or major-cycle normalization.

| Pair | Handler p95/p99 B → C, ms (4,000 samples/side) | Loop p95/p99 B → C, ms | Loop samples B/C | Loop max B → C, ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A/B | 1.322/1.511 → 0.358/0.690 | 2.660/2.853 → 1.667/2.035 | 4,395/4,256 | 3.557 → 2.972 |
| B/A | 1.273/1.415 → 0.306/0.398 | 2.574/2.798 → 1.621/1.731 | 4,359/4,277 | 3.142 → 2.058 |

```sh

  scripts/perf/session-catalog-selection-measure.ts \

```

Use the same benchmark script on both revisions; the baseline run supplies main's unchanged `src/plugins/session-catalog.ts`. Setup and 20 warmups precede measurement. Counterbalance launch order; compare all golden hashes.

Acceptance was declared before paired results: preserve ordered outputs and ownership; accept modest allocation/CPU reductions without a material controlled regression, with undersampled tails treated as context. No adverse metric required A/A rejection controls.
</details>

Built loopback Gateway proof used approximately 10,000 synthetic sessions, 40 enabled plugins including acpx, 20 Pi adoptions, and three mock-provider turns interleaved with catalog reads per replay. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Remove six redundant test executions and four duplicate assertions across CLI startup policy, host tool metadata parsing, channel registry lookup, and reply queue policy. Production code is unchanged. The smaller final batch follows a bounded audit: distinct recovery, security, migration, storage and SDK contracts were retained rather than padding a deletion target.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Production code, public contracts, security checks and runtime behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- CLI: remove browser native-host and cloud-worker catalog replay from startup policy. `command-path-policy.test.ts` retains the catalog assertions; startup policy still tests the common mapping through node-worker/onboarding/protocol cases.
- Plugins: remove the repeated Add/Update/Move/Delete and sandbox path fixtures from the parser suite. `agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts` exercises those exact paths through the public callback boundary. Keep immutable snapshots, whitespace/default-cwd, invalid inputs and prototype-key tests.
- Channels: remove four duplicate calls to the same function imported under a second name. The public re-export retains exact-ID precedence and registry invalidation assertions.
- Reply queue: replace three labels that all pass identical boolean inputs with one identical-input test. Every distinct admission branch stays covered.

Changed-file cases: 31 → 25. Four files; test +9/−88, net −79 lines; production 0. No SQL, schema, runtime, SDK surface, security, update or lifecycle change. No test-only production seam was found.

## Coverage retained

| Removed duplicate | Surviving proof |
|---|---|
| Browser native-host and cloud worker catalog replay | `src/cli/command-path-policy.test.ts`, “resolves mixed startup-only rules”; generic startup mapping remains in `command-startup-policy.test.ts` |
| Add/Update/Move/Delete path parsing | `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts`, “passes host-derived apply_patch paths to before_tool_call hooks” |

| Queue mode-label rows | Same `resolveActiveRunQueueAction` input and assertion, once; mode strings never reached production |

## Acceptance rule (published before timed runs)

Primary metric: remove exactly six duplicate executions and four duplicate calls with every distinct contract above still passing. Workload: the four changed Vitest suites, same machine, pinned Node/Bun/dependencies, one worker and fixed sequential commands. For a timing claim, acquire the campaign timing lock with load1 <24; warm baseline/candidate ABAB with at least five samples each, report median/p95/min/max, keep cold runs separate, and stop any speed claim on a ≥20% adverse cell. If no qualified window is available after 60 minutes, report counts only and make no wall-time/CPU claim. No SQL performance claim: runtime code is byte-identical.

## Evidence

Baseline: 31/31 changed-file cases pass. Candidate: 25/25 pass, plus 14 retained CLI/channel cases and all four retained hook-boundary cases (43 candidate/keeper cases total). Commands:

```text
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/queue-policy.test.ts src/channels/registry.helpers.test.ts src/cli/command-startup-policy.test.ts src/plugins/host-tool-param-parsers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

```

The default hook E2E setup refused the external dependency store during declaration preparation before executing any cases. The documented focused-suite switch above is appropriate after source inspection: these four cases use source aliases, synthetic patches and the real source hook policy with a mocked receiver/bridge, with no packaged CLI or dist consumer. Normal test setup/cleanup remained active; all four cases executed and passed.

Diagnostic single-run elapsed times, baseline/candidate: unit-fast 1.31/1.68 s, CLI 3.11/6.45 s, channels 173.12/198.69 s; complete selected run 216.88/233.88 s. These are correctness runs on a loaded host, dominated by separate cold worker-cache generation, not qualified ABAB performance samples. They establish no wall-time or CPU improvement or parity. Qualification ran from 23:08:04 to 00:08:22 UTC (over 60 minutes), with zero qualified samples; the latest observed load1 was 57.88 against the required <24. The counts-only fallback applies. No timing lock was acquired, and no wall-time or CPU-speedup claim is made.

Formatting, basic lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Two isolated Codex P0–P2 preservation reviews found no actionable findings; the final review includes complete retained owner suites. Exact-head CI [40142644622](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142644622) is successful, including selected type, lint, source-contract, architecture, changed-boundary and ratchet jobs; the watcher reports GREEN. The redundant standalone local Madge run was canceled and its successful exact-head CI architecture result reused; no local Madge pass is claimed. No CI reruns or gate bypasses were needed.

Final shared index completed at 2026-10-25 00:21:38 UTC: 2,682 open-main PRs, sole other overlap #153405 at `87df87168f7477812b67e478c2609e12cedf2f10`.
