prs.title: fix(health): surface restart-required runtime config drift
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw health` reports `ok` when the running Gateway still uses an older model, provider, auth or secrets config than the one on disk, for example after an edit under `gateway.reload.mode: "off"`, a failed reload, or while a required restart is pending.

The diagnostic also compared only `secrets.providers`. Changing `secrets.defaults.env`, which selects the active provider alias, therefore produced a false `ok` result even after the reloader completed the new source observation.

## User Impact

`openclaw health --json` includes optional `runtimeConfig` state:

- `ok`: monitored runtime values match the latest completed reload observation.
- `drift`: they differ, with redacted path names and default-model labels.
- `unknown`: one authoritative source is unavailable.

Text health prints a warning for `drift` or `unknown`. The diagnostic never emits config fingerprints, secret values, source paths, parse excerpts, or observation errors.

`openclaw health` advertises `runtime-config-health`. Every other client (Control UI, native apps, nodes, third-party v4 clients) receives hello, `health` events, and `health` responses without `runtimeConfig`, the same shape as main.

Since #111527, `hot` and every mode other than `off` resolve to `hybrid`, so lasting drift now mainly comes from `mode: "off"`, failed reloads, writes whose writer skipped runtime application, and restarts that are still pending.

Update behavior: no config, default, SQLite, migration or protocol-version change. A new CLI talking to an older Gateway sends a capability that Gateway ignores, so the field and the text line are simply absent; an older CLI talking to a new Gateway doesn't advertise it and sees today's payload.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config reloader owns one generation-fenced, immutable latest-completed source observation. The shared health owner compares that observation with the published runtime source snapshot. RPC, connection hello, broadcasts, cached health, and CLI text all read the same redacted projection. Monitoring canonical parent `secrets` covers provider declarations, provider-default selection, and the restart-owned egress proxy without adding another config or API surface.

Every reloader transaction that reads the source publishes that read when it finishes, and only while its source revision is current. A write's own same-source watcher echo is published by the echo's reload pass: main removed the in-transaction echo catch-up in #168980. That covers watcher reloads, in-process writes (which publish the canonical reread their notification carries), and plugin lifecycle applications.

The alternative was to read disk or reconstruct reload state in each health consumer. That would duplicate policy and recreate mixed-generation results during debounce, in-flight reads, supersession, and bootstrap awaits.

`runtimeConfig` is sent only to clients that advertise the `runtime-config-health` client capability, so existing strict v4 decoders never see it (details under Protocol compatibility).

## Protocol compatibility

An ungated field is rejected by the pre-change strict v4 decoder. Measured at `a78f6e3c2fd` with its own lockfile: that head's `sendGatewayHello`, carrying a drift value from its real `buildRuntimeConfigHealth`, validated with TypeBox `Value.Check` against the pre-change strict v4 decoder (`snapshot.ts` byte-identical to `bf83a4dde8f`; `frames.ts` has no diff between base and head, so `HelloOkSchema` is the same with the base snapshot swapped in):

```text
head HelloOkSchema, drift hello                      : true
base HelloOkSchema, control hello (no runtimeConfig) : true
base HelloOkSchema, drift hello                      : false
  /snapshot/health  additionalProperties  "must not have additional properties"  {"additionalProperties":["runtimeConfig"]}
base SnapshotSchema, drift snapshot                  : false
  /health           additionalProperties  "must not have additional properties"  {"additionalProperties":["runtimeConfig"]}
```

So the field is capability-gated. It uses the negotiation the protocol already has (`GATEWAY_CLIENT_CAPS` in `client-info.ts`, `ConnectParams.caps`, `hasGatewayClientCap`) and adds one entry, `RUNTIME_CONFIG_HEALTH: "runtime-config-health"`. The field is projected per connection on all three surfaces:

- hello-ok: the cached snapshot is projected per connection; on the uncached path the diagnostic is read only for advertising clients.
- `health` events: through the broadcaster's existing per-recipient projection hook in `server-connection-state.ts`. The node-subscription fanout has no per-client caps in scope, so it always drops the field.
- `health` RPC: both the cached and the refreshed response.

The shared health cache is never mutated by the projection. The closed `HealthSnapshotSchema` is reachable only through hello-ok's `snapshot`: the `health` RPC result already carries `modelRuntime`, which no schema in `packages/gateway-protocol` declares, and I found no payload schema there for the `health` event. I gated all three anyway so a client never sees the field without asking for it; a hello-only gate would be about 20 production lines smaller.

Which contract to keep is the Gateway owners' call, and nothing here claims that decision. One set of data points for it, each measured with `git show <sha> | grep -E 'GATEWAY_CLIENT_CAPS|hasGatewayClientCap'` (0 hits each): main has added optional fields to closed v4 hello-snapshot objects without a capability gate, for example `suspension` in #136220 (`e0ab9907621`), presence `clientId` in #145559 (`0141569e798`), health `ingressFailed`/`ingressPressure` in #123234 (`b233ea79575`), and, since the last review, health `childRuntime` in #157190 (`92c86fefcd4`).

## Evidence

### Current revision: October 24

Pushed [`74a5bb3048320571d7be4f5234ffabcb1c1c9a64`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/74a5bb3048320571d7be4f5234ffabcb1c1c9a64), tree `3e50c559c9bd4a15d57f2dfd5130e6d6fcb021de`, by a normal push after verifying the remote still held `24431ac4acf68f7508e389126588782e33004ca6`. The merge preserves that head and upstream `1d9da0d5dce9ea92065015cb5de0671d2e68db8b` as parents. It picks up the public-startup readiness fixture repair in [#181700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181700) and the worker-recovery fixture repair in [#181816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181816).

The previous [CI run 39971742215](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39971742215) executed merge `43cbeb2d78a66105d5293779dd0f75581e3ef5ce` with actual base `be6b43f3c52b5e6b53504312554287135c302283`. Replayed the original selected groups on those exact sources before testing the candidate:

| Proof | Complete result |
| --- | --- |
| Original seven-file hook group, exact base and exact CI merge | Both runs: 53 passed, 2 failed. Both named hook cases failed `hello.ok` with `UNAVAILABLE`, reason `startup-sidecars`. |
| Same hook group, candidate | 55 passed, 0 failed. Both original failures passed. |
| Original worker-startup group, exact CI merge | 171 passed. The hosted worker-recovery failure did not reproduce in this one-worker replay. |
| Same worker group, candidate | 173 passed across 18 files. |
| Original runtime-config group, exact CI merge | Five individual passes, then the unchanged 300000 ms no-output watchdog; exit 143, no suite total. |
| Same runtime-config group, exact base | 56 passed, 1 failed, 10 skipped, plus one failed suite. The include-only operation's teardown timed out at `server.close`; a later suite could not acquire plugin metadata while shutdown remained pending. This is a baseline cleanup failure, not a reproduction of the watchdog termination. |
| Same runtime-config group, candidate | 67 passed, 0 failed. The include-only case completed in 5508 ms, versus 292905 ms before the base reported its hook timeout. |
| Candidate PR contract tests | Nine files, 127 passed, 0 failed: CLI projection, reload observations, health cache/publication, RPC, hello, event projection, and protocol schema. |
| Candidate static checks | Format parity on 28 files passed; typed lint on 26 files reported 0 warnings and 0 errors; `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` exited 0. |

These runs used Linux, Node `24.22.1`, pnpm `12.15.0`, pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`, frozen installs, and one test worker. The base and merge have byte-identical dependency inputs and used Vitest `5.0.3`; the candidate's integrated main uses `5.0.5`. The candidate passed the replay, but the watchdog's cause has not been isolated. Hosted CI used two workers, so the local controls do not reproduce its concurrency. Source-tree guards passed around every candidate run.

The original group plans are recorded in [hook job 120476682644](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39971742215/job/120476682644), [worker job 120476682315](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39971742215/job/120476682315), and [runtime-config job 120476682472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39971742215/job/120476682472). Replays used each logged `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_GROUPS_JSON` through `node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts`, with `OPENCLAW_CI_TEST_RUNTIME_POLICY=bun-all`, `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONCURRENCY=1`, the one-worker override, and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000`.

The focused candidate command was:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/health-runtime-config.test.ts \
  src/commands/health.snapshot.runtime-config.test.ts \
  src/commands/health.plugins.test.ts \
  src/gateway/config-reload.observation.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-connection-state.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/health.runtime-config.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts \
  packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/snapshot.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Fresh source review covered all 29 complete patches and 70 hunks against pinned main, with no actionable P0-P2 finding. It used patch context and did not execute these tests. The committed tree matches the reviewed and tested tree.

[Current-head CI run 40126705412](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40126705412) is running. At `2026-10-24T19:46:10Z`, the complete capture contained 49 check runs: 13 successful, 21 skipped, 15 in progress. These are incomplete CI results. The separate `openclaw/ci-gate` and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` commit statuses require fresh maintainer approval; the [notice](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89526#issuecomment-5791961319) names this exact head. The [Gateway-owner contract decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89526#issuecomment-5791658271) remains open.

Earlier measurements below are historical author reports at the SHAs they name. They are not current-head proof.

### Historical revision: October 20

Pushed [`426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2), tree `9190bd4b0c36a0219455cec5566bedf0b9b65b4c`, as an additive merge of `832a0c2cffae34863248e9d29a44925995148a04` and upstream `f629720edbb9f4b458adae30c7506c1dc5d1adc6`. The normal push and remote head were verified. [CI run 39499291024](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39499291024) completed successfully: **112 jobs, 89 successful and 23 skipped**, with no failed, running or queued jobs. The fully paginated capture at `2026-10-20T23:42:26.369785+00:00` records `filter=all`: 180 completed checks (1 neutral, 57 skipped, 122 success); `filter=latest`: 180 completed checks (1 neutral, 57 skipped, 122 success). The [preflight job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39499291024/job/118892385712) checked out merge [`5c19327872dac9e8382503fe89163559452f54b4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5c19327872dac9e8382503fe89163559452f54b4), tree `29fc941f9313770bccb92a973fad06d5fdd00492`, with parents `8f0973e37405d683e242e217f4d7c30a1efc4118` and this head `426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2`. That executed merge differs from the locally validated integration tree. The [last queued shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39499291024/job/118912285234) is included in the terminal result.

The integration preserves upstream health-summary and hello-on-demand behavior alongside the optional runtime-config capability. It also fixes two demonstrated defects:

- The runtime-config event projection could restore `agents` and `sessions` after the broadcaster had removed them for a summary-only client. The existing per-recipient callback now applies both projections before serialization. The generic broadcaster matches pinned main. [Production callback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2/src/gateway/server-connection-state.ts#L137-L153), [eight serialized-event combinations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2/src/gateway/server-connection-state.test.ts#L730).
- Clearing and republishing the runtime snapshot can reuse a numeric revision. The cache key now compares the reload-observation generation and the runtime owner's stable publication object identity, so a different publication cannot reuse stale cached or in-flight health. The key remains internal. [Freshness checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2/src/gateway/server/health-state.ts#L137-L162), [cached and pending reset cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2/src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts#L390). These cases call the actual runtime reset/publication owner and summary builder with controlled collection and reload observations; they are not a full Gateway restart test.

The [hello table](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2/src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts#L442) covers all 16 combinations of cached health, runtime-config capability, hello-on-demand and health-summary capability.

Executed on the private Linux builder with Node v26.8.2, pnpm 12.12.1, frozen dependencies and one Vitest worker:

| Control | Result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Event-composition regression before the repair, tree `f84da04ee18080546e35ac732673768b22516d81` | One intended payload assertion failure with `runtimeConfig` present; the absent case passed, eight unrelated cases skipped. The loop stopped at its first affected recipient, so this is one observed failure. Exit 1, 144.13 seconds, no timeout. |
| Actual reset/republication regressions with the old numeric key, tree `de0fdb18b3033c0876e41a261bb4d65e1d89ee62` | Two intended failures: stale cache returned instead of invalidation, and stale pending collection returned instead of recollection. 24 skipped, exit 1, 57.23 seconds, no timeout. |
| Final tree `9190bd4b0c36a0219455cec5566bedf0b9b65b4c` | Five suites, 114 tests passed, exit 0, 79.31 seconds. Both reset cases, all event and hello combinations, RPC controls and broadcaster serialization are included. |
| Scoped static checks on final tree | Incremental core TypeScript: exit 0, 6.26 seconds. Gateway-server test TypeScript: exit 0, 7.55 seconds. Seven-file typed lint: zero warnings/errors, exit 0, 13.82 seconds. |
| Source identity and review | Before/after index trees and all 58,328 tracked blob hashes match the final tree. Two separate source reviews found no actionable P0-P2 issue; the reviewers did not execute target tests. The peer review independently inspected the complete positive/negative logs and identity receipts. |

Reproduce the positive set:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts \
  src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-connection-state.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/health.runtime-config.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-broadcast.serialization.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

For the event negative control, retain the final tests and remove only summary composition from the runtime-config per-recipient replacement, then run the connection-state cases. For the reset control, retain the tests but replace publication-identity comparison with the old observation-generation/numeric-revision key, then run the two reset cases. Restore the exact production bytes after each control. Neither mutation is in the branch. The final runs reported no remaining process-group children; tracked-blob checks do not certify untracked files or the entire runtime environment.

The integration includes upstream [`b6bd9e8bd0cad400b31a223a0c44f8494f5cfb87`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b6bd9e8bd0cad400b31a223a0c44f8494f5cfb87), which fixes the missing `createDeferredCore` import reported by the previous head's static jobs. Those old failures also occur in the exact-base main CI; the old runtime jobs completed. The earlier SIGKILL/137 remains unexplained and is not classified as OOM.

The [fresh hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89526#issuecomment-4604300916) completed October 20 at 21:30 UTC on `426d7295459be24e2d18d968f6dc8f1411e4abf2`, against main `4b065f50d724f380dca1fa09b387c2b0e42a80a0`, with zero findings. It accepts the supplied historical Gateway proof and current regression evidence. This was source inspection, not an independent execution of the target code. Its two remaining items are Gateway-owner acceptance of the capability-gated health contract and current-head maintainer security approval. Primary CI is now complete as recorded above. The separate `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` commit statuses remain failure; `openclaw/dependency-review` is success.

Maintainer security approval and Gateway-owner acceptance of the optional `runtimeConfig` contract remain open. A successful Security Review workflow does not grant the required approval. The historical sections below retain their original heads and are not new executions at `426d7295`.

### Historical integration: October 19

Head [`832a0c2cffae34863248e9d29a44925995148a04`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/832a0c2cffae34863248e9d29a44925995148a04) is an additive merge of the previous head `56b8e57fe36d33313e80af541820b11e02ab9a2e` and upstream main `2cd23b665868c75bfb02537cef9eb9f2b329667a`. GitHub reports the conflicts resolved. No rebase or force-push.

The six conflict resolutions retain main's health-event deduplication, pinned config paths, connection-row delivery-loss handling, and `hello-health-on-demand` behavior alongside this PR's runtime-config capability gate. Clients advertising both health capabilities receive an empty hello health snapshot; requests and events still carry the opted-in diagnostic. The [hello tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/832a0c2cffae34863248e9d29a44925995148a04/src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts) cover all eight combinations of cached health, runtime-config capability, and hello opt-out.

A new [health-owner regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/832a0c2cffae34863248e9d29a44925995148a04/src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts) reproduced an old `ok` diagnostic being broadcast after its observation was superseded. The pre-fix resolved tree was `022244e3589d615e8b58745e6ab6ca9cd7edb9c8`; it failed with `expected generation: 7, received generation: 8` while both values carried `state: ok`. The fix removes the async helper hop between the final config check and publication. A separate regression checks that an equivalent diagnostic at a newer generation refreshes the cache key without another event.

Local author-run validation of the current tree (`a08c6662c26a9fb90f366284fadae4dceec13144`):

- Four focused Gateway suites: **88 passed**, wrapper wall time 266.55 seconds. This includes the red-to-green publication regression, strict legacy decoder controls, capability projection for hello/events/RPC, and main's health deduplication tests.
- Core production TypeScript: passed, 47.75 seconds. Gateway-server test TypeScript shard: passed, 48.38 seconds.
- Targeted type-aware lint and formatting on the repaired files: passed. `git diff --check` against pinned main: passed.
- Workboard's asset build, the consumer previously affected by capability-registry changes: passed, 5.14 seconds. This is a focused consumer build, not a full build claim.
- Independent canonical `autoreview`: three completed passes, `scoped-clean` through P2 on the full candidate diff against pinned main. The reviewer assessed supplied patches and did not execute tests. Helper SHA-256: `b95e51b79d9f68fe445cdc9d6c1e07b01507188bba1bfe8a59f14c378e5ac3a5`.

Reproduce the focused runtime checks from this head with its frozen dependencies and repository test wrapper:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts src/gateway/server-connection-state.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/health.runtime-config.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json --incremental
```

Exact-head CI [run 39320268759](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39320268759) finished with two failing jobs plus the aggregate gate, both in a file this PR does not touch. `check-test-types-core-4`: `src/gateway/local-http-probe.test.ts(154,25): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'createDeferredCore'`. `check-lint-core-1`: `src/gateway/local-http-probe.test.ts:178:53` (`prefer-promise-reject-errors`). #177670 (`2cc639d7023`) broke that file on main and `b6bd9e8bd0c` fixed it at 2026-10-19 21:24Z; the run's base `0548086d6a95` predates the fix. Every other job passed or was skipped, so the earlier SIGKILL in `checks-node-changed-compact-large-22` (run 39007736518) did not repeat. `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` is the open approval gate below, not a test result.

The Gateway-owner contract decision below and the maintainer security approval remain open; this update claims neither approval nor landing readiness with green CI.

### Historical author-reported evidence

The evidence below belongs to the named earlier heads and has not been promoted to current-head proof.


Head `8606a2df718`: six commits on the earlier head `5d5ad44f5f6`. `6d62aefe5a1` merges `main@6b2afbfe981` (the branch was CONFLICTING), `32548a164ba` moves the external-change audit appender out of `config-reload.ts`, `82be5c6edc6` fixes the plugin lifecycle publication gap, `759130f4cc7` brings the health mocks inside main's mock-export ratchet, `3ee3413ef5e` rechecks cached health after its awaited reads, and `8606a2df718` removes three mock-shaped tests. `git merge-tree --write-tree` against `main@f3f9bf90c69` (2026-10-09) exits 0.

Since then, `615fde1ef66` merges `main@bb642e181e1` and `56b8e57fe36` merges `main@4af30f64ca7`. Neither changes an added or removed line of this branch's own diff; the merge notes below cover both.

### Plugin lifecycle publication (the P2 from the last review)

`applyPluginLifecycleChange` reads and applies the source outside `runReload`. It could consume a pending write and accept that write's watcher echo, and accepting the echo cleared the queued reload, so nothing published the source it applied. It now publishes through the same per-transaction tracker. Regression in `config-reload.observation.test.ts`, run on the same tree with and without the three production lines:

```text
without the fix   publishes a plugin lifecycle read that consumes a pending write and accepts its echo
                  AssertionError: expected { generation: 15, …(1) } to deeply equal { generation: 16, …(1) }
                  observation still agents.defaults.model = openai/gpt-5.6-sol; readSnapshot called twice, onHotReload once
                  Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)
with the fix      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

### Cached health after awaited reads (the P2 from the re-review)

The cached branch of the `health` RPC read the shared snapshot, awaited the delivery-queue and context-engine summaries, then answered from the captured copy even when a config observation had retired that snapshot in between. It now rereads the shared cache after the awaits and answers from a refresh when the snapshot is no longer the current one. Regression in `health.runtime-config.test.ts`, run with and without the production change:

```text
without the fix   refreshes when the cached snapshot is retired during its diagnostic reads
                  AssertionError: expected { state: 'ok' } to deeply equal { state: 'drift', …(3) }
                  Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
with the fix      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Tests and gates on `8606a2df718`

Run on an M4 Pro, Node 26, on the tree CI tests: `main@f3f9bf90c69` merged with this head.

- 20 affected test files (`config-reload`, `config-reload.observation`, `config-reload.plugin-drain`, `config-reload.lease-retry`, `server-reload-handlers`, `health-state`, `connect-hello.update-scope`, `connect-hello.setup-completion`, `server-connection-state`, `server-methods`, `health.owner-routing`, `health.runtime-config`, the seven commands health suites, and the protocol snapshot schema): 601 passed, 0 failed.
- The CI ratchet step with `--base` at that main: max-lines, line-cap ("OK: 26 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth"), assertion-safety, database-worker, test-timeout-race and test-mock-exports ("Mock factory ratchet OK: 10238 grandfathered factories") pass, as do `config:docs:check` and `plugins:inventory:check`.
- `run-tsgo.mjs` 0 errors on `tsconfig.core.json` and the gateway-root, gateway-server, gateway-other, gateway-methods, commands and packages test shards.
- oxfmt clean and oxlint 0 warnings, 0 errors on the 26 changed code files. `plugins:assets:check`: generated assets match the committed bytes. Import cycles: 0 (measured at `82be5c6edc6`; no import changed since).
- Not run: the full `check-changed`, the other core test shards, full `lint:core`, knip, and the docs MDX and link checks.

Test cost. Wall is `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on the M4 Pro with the compiled-worker cache warm. CI is the sum of per-test times for that file in run 37976193929 (`82be5c6edc6`).

| Test file | Tests | Wall | CI |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `src/gateway/config-reload.observation.test.ts` (new) | 11 | 7.10 s | 2.49 s |
| `src/commands/health-runtime-config.test.ts` (new) | 5 | 1.24 s | 1 ms |
| `src/commands/health.snapshot.runtime-config.test.ts` (new) | 5 | 1.23 s | 4 ms |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/health.runtime-config.test.ts` (new) | 3 | 8.36 s | 0.64 s (2 tests) |
| `src/gateway/server/health-state.test.ts` | 30 | 9.12 s | 10.18 s (33 tests) |
| `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts` | 43 | 6.23 s | 0.27 s |
| `src/gateway/server-connection-state.test.ts` | 8 | 15.93 s | 7.52 s |
| `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/snapshot.test.ts` | 13 | 1.60 s | 0.10 s |

The two rows with a test count in the CI column changed after that run: one case added, three removed. The observation suite runs on main's shared reload harness with fake timers and deferreds; it adds no real timers, sleeps or Gateway boot.

### Process proof at `82be5c6edc6`

Isolated Gateway on an M4 Pro: `env -i` with a temp `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`, loopback port 28797, token auth, `gateway.reload.mode: "off"`, started with `pnpm openclaw gateway run --port 28797 --bind loopback --verbose`. Clients: `openclaw health --json` (advertises the capability) and `openclaw gateway call health --json` (does not).

```text
before the edit
openclaw health --json               16 top-level keys | runtimeConfig = {"state": "ok", "liveDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "observedDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5"}
openclaw gateway call health --json  15 top-level keys | runtimeConfig absent

an unused gateway.auth.password added on disk, a restart-required path
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.auth.password)
[reload] config reload disabled (gateway.reload.mode=off)
[reload] config source revision 1 accepted (file)

after the edit
openclaw health --json               16 top-level keys | runtimeConfig = {"state": "drift", "liveDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "observedDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "driftPaths": ["gateway.auth"], "message": "Live gateway runtime config differs from the latest completed reload observation for model/provider/auth paths; restart is required or pending."}
openclaw gateway call health --json  15 top-level keys | runtimeConfig absent
openclaw health (text)               Runtime config: warning (live gateway differs from latest completed reload observation for gateway.auth; restart required or pending; live=openai/gpt-5.5 observed=openai/gpt-5.5)
```

Neither the token nor the password appears in the 9,401 bytes of captured client output. The Gateway was stopped by the pids recorded at launch (`[shutdown] completed cleanly in 193ms`).

This run covers the `health` RPC for one advertising and one non-advertising client after the merge. The hello and event projections, the echo and reread races, and the plugin lifecycle case are covered by the regressions, not by this run. The earlier process run at `59271bb6847` also captured hello-ok with and without the capability (absent without it); that part was not repeated here. Not rerun at `8606a2df718`: the three later commits change tests and the cached branch of the `health` RPC, which the regression above covers.

### Observation publication (the two P2s from the review before that, measured at `59271bb6847`)

Each regression failed on the rebased pre-fix code and passed at `59271bb6847`; `config-reload.observation.test.ts` went from 6 passed / 5 failed to 11/11:

```text
slow in-process write accepts its own watcher echo   before: generation 13, expected 14; observation still held the prior model
reread after a read failure                          before: published the queued model, expected null
reread after a missing file                          before: same
reread after an invalid file                         before: same
reread after replaced bytes                          before: published the queued model, expected the replacement
```

Not re-measured as before and after at this head. Main changed the contract under the four reread cases: a write notification now carries the writer's canonical reread, and the reloader no longer rereads. They are now three cases that drive the notification's snapshot (missing, invalid, replaced bytes) and pass. The read-failure case is deleted with the reread it covered. The echo case passes unchanged apart from building its write with `makeWrite`.

### Regression with the pre-change strict v4 decoder

`connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts` builds the decoder a client had before this change (the current closed `SnapshotSchema` with `runtimeConfig` removed from the closed health object). On both the cached and uncached hello paths it accepts what a non-advertising client now receives, and that client's health has no `runtimeConfig`. An advertising client still gets `runtimeConfig`, which the current schema accepts and the pre-change decoder rejects. `server-connection-state.test.ts` and `health.runtime-config.test.ts` pin the event and RPC projections.

Pre-gate control, measured at `183d408dcee` with the gate commit's six production files reverted and `runtime-config-cap.ts` removed: 4 failed, 37 passed (the hello, broadcast, and cached and uncached RPC cases). With the gate, all four pass.

### Merge notes (`6d62aefe5a1`)

- `config-reload.ts`: main moved source observation into `src/config/source.ts` (#157372), and a write notification now carries the writer's canonical reread (#161868). The tracker keys on `source.observation.revision`. Main's #168980 removed the in-transaction echo catch-up, so the accepted-echo marker this PR had added is gone too. The echo's own reload pass publishes that read, one pass later; both echo regressions still observe the next generation. The pending-write path records the notification's snapshot because the reloader no longer rereads it. `config-reload-watcher.ts` is deleted: main dropped the polling resolver it held.
- `server-connection-state.ts`: main's per-recipient projection hook returns `{ payload }`, so the health projection returns that shape. This file merged without a textual conflict and failed typecheck until adapted.
- `server-methods/health.ts`: the capability projection wraps main's inlined cached-health object and its live `childRuntime` read.
- `snapshot.ts`: `runtimeConfig` sits beside main's `childRuntime`. `health.ts`: the text line joins main's formatter loop.
- Tests: `makeContext` in `connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts` takes `{ caps, client }`. The observation suite uses main's `makeWrite`. The four pending-write "reread" cases became three that drive the notification's snapshot; the read-failure case is deleted with the reread it covered.
- Line cap: the ratchet rejects any growth in `config-reload.ts`. The observation wiring adds nine counted lines and the resolver that used to pay for it is gone from main, so `32548a164ba` moves the external-change audit appender (it only reads the watched path) verbatim to `config-reload-audit.ts`.
- `health.plugins.test.ts` (`56b8e57fe36`, `main@4af30f64ca7`): main's shared `health.test-fixtures.js` import sits beside this branch's `installHealthConfigMock` import. `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` auto-merged; it is main's baseline minus this branch's three entries.

### CI on `82be5c6edc6` (run 37976193929)

Four jobs were red.

- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: this PR. `check:test-mock-exports` rejected six mock factories the branch adds or changes. Fixed in `759130f4cc7`.
- `checks-ui-e2e (7/8)`, `chat-flow.history-recovery.e2e.test.ts` ("Timed out waiting for 1 chat.history requests"): red on main. The scheduled main runs at 18:38Z, 19:31Z and 20:33Z failed the same test at the same line, as did 21 other PR runs on 14 branches between 18:28Z and 20:39Z. This PR does not touch `ui/`.
- `checks-node-changed-5`, `gateway-node-exec-approvals.e2e.test.ts`: the test passed and the job failed on an unhandled rejection of `node returned invalid exec approvals payload`. The test attaches `.rejects` to that request two awaits after starting it (lines 168-181). Neither the test nor the exec-approvals path is in this diff. 3 of 3 local runs passed without the error.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-14-1`, `src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts`: 9 failed of 254, starting with three fake-timer cases that timed out at 120 s waiting on a write-triggered reload. Not reproduced: the same 18 files on the exact tree CI tested (`164210c355e` merged with `82be5c6edc6`) pass 254/254, the base alone passes 253/253, and the file passed 8 more times in a row on a later main merged with this branch, 4 of them under background QoS. The test file is not in this diff and did not fail in the 10 scheduled main runs or the 99 other failed PR runs I checked from that day. This branch changes `config-reload.ts`, which those cases drive, so I can't rule it out; I have no mechanism and no reproduction.

`openclaw/security-sensitive-review` is the maintainer approval gate for `connect-hello.ts`.

### Review metrics

- Against `main@4af30f64ca7`: production +470/-76 in 14 files; tests and test support +1155/-21 in 12 files; docs +23/-3; the mock-export baseline -3. One optional, read-scoped health field behind one new client capability.

## Decision needed

For Gateway owners (CODEOWNERS has no entry for these paths): accept the additive, capability-gated `health.runtimeConfig` field, accept it with the gate on hello only, or close. With #89517 closed, this is the only place an operator sees reload-disabled or restart-pending drift.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes managed-worktree reports that emit terminal controls from repository paths, branch names, IDs, or operation diagnostics.

## User Impact

Human-readable tables and acknowledgements preserve printable Unicode and visibly escape control-bearing fields. Git paths, registry records, JSON values, and intentional report separators remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `renderTerminalSafeTable` for the list table and the canonical `sanitizeTerminalText` at non-table output boundaries. The shared garbage-collection formatter keeps its existing nonterminal contract.

Thanks @Alix-007 for the fix, regression tests, and original real-CLI proof.

## Evidence

- Both new command regressions fail on unchanged main code: table output and creation acknowledgement (2 failed, 23 skipped; 330.03s command wall time). With the fix all 25 owner tests pass (205.05s runner duration).
- Tests cover escaped controls, printable Unicode, preserved acknowledgement tabs, raw JSON values, and unchanged records. The redundant restore test was removed because create and restore share `printRecord`.
- After integrating current main, all 26 tests in the owner and import-boundary files pass (292.61s runner duration). Targeted typed oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review through P2: scoped-clean; the integrated patch matches the reviewed candidate.
- Against main: production +18/−12 (net +6), tests +42/−0, docs +2/−0. The small production increase is the safe-table import and the field escaping needed to retain deliberate separators.
- A fresh standalone CLI live replay was not repeated on this source-only, heavily loaded Mac. Inspected prior contributor proof used the built Linux CLI for real Git worktree creation and registry/Git readback: list controls changed from 4 to 0, with raw paths preserved. That evidence predates the current integration; it is not an exact-head live claim. Gateway-owned GC and restore/removal were not live-tested.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Batch d500 removes repeated test setup, assertions, and duplicate proof layers from the test-reduction campaign, replayed onto main at `6c33f5ff5ee0b7d438238edfdebb2762acd72503`.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Production LOC: **+0 / -0**. Test/support diff: **+2533 / -4294**, or **1761 net lines removed**, across **34 test/support files**. Shrink-only mock-baseline maintenance removes 3 additional lines: **+2533 / -4297 overall**, or **1764 net lines removed across 35 files**. The shared test-support file is +27 / -50; test files are +2506 / -4244. Runtime and coverage improvements are not claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the existing boundary contracts while consolidating fixtures and redundant checks. This is a conservative replay: current main wins wherever the older campaign shape conflicts with newer behavior or ownership proof.

prs.title: feature(presence): add presence query CLI for Gateway RPC
prs.body:
Implements #182758

## What Problem This Solves

Docs already document `openclaw gateway call presence.query` for the people/devices roster used by the agent `presence` tool. Operators still have to hand-craft RPC JSON. Distinct from `openclaw system presence` (`system-presence` beacon list) and from the Control UI Devices page (which joins `system-presence` with pairing/node inventory).

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw presence query [--action list|person|device] [--person …] [--device-id …] [--include …] [--limit …] --json` returns the same `presence.query` payload. Registered `--port`/`--url` targeting works. Unreachable Gateway fails closed like sibling Gateway-backed CLIs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Thin Alix-style CLI adapter only: register `presence query`, forward validated params through `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport("presence.query", …)`, document next to system presence, and replace the docs `gateway call` example. No new Gateway methods, schema, or permissions.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/commands/presence-query.ts`, `src/cli/program/register.presence.ts`, `src/cli/command-catalog.ts` (PASSIVE_STARTUP_POLICY), registry/descriptors, colocated tests, `docs/cli/presence.md`, `docs/concepts/presence.md`, `docs/cli/index.md`
- ClawSweeper author follow-up: passive startup policy, root-command JSON_NOT_APPLICABLE + description alignment, docs distinguish agent presence.query from Devices page `system-presence` inventory
- Unit: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/presence-query.test.ts` — **3 passed** (CLI `--port`/`--url` registration + failure envelope)
- Packaged CLI proof below (Node 24.22.1, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, local Gateway token auth on port 18801)

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Operators need native `openclaw presence query` that calls existing `presence.query`; targeting via `--port`/`--url`; person/device selectors; unreachable Gateway must fail closed. Distinct from `system presence`.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw presence query` → `presenceQueryCommand` → `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport("presence.query", …)` → `src/gateway/server-methods/presence.ts`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses `addGatewayClientOptions` + `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport`. No new presence owners.

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI after `qaRuntime` build on Node 24.22.1; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`; local `openclaw gateway run --port 18801` with token auth.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node openclaw.mjs presence query --url ws://127.0.0.1:18801 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs presence query --port 18801 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs presence query --action person --person me --include devices --url ws://127.0.0.1:18801 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs gateway call presence.query --params '{"action":"list"}' --url ws://127.0.0.1:18801 --token "$TOKEN" --json
# negative unreachable → exit 1
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
# presence --help lists query
  query       Query connected people and devices (presence.query)

# presence query --url … --json (exit 0)
{
  "observedAt": 1792865187469,
  "status": "ok",
  "people": [],
  "totalPeople": 0,
  "truncated": false
}

# presence query --port 18801 … --json (exit 0) — same shape
{
  "observedAt": 1792865189290,
  "status": "ok",
  "people": [],
  "totalPeople": 0,
  "truncated": false
}

# gateway call presence.query list parity (exit 0)
{ "observedAt": 1792865185537, "status": "ok", "people": [], "totalPeople": 0, "truncated": false }

# person me without authenticated person identity (exit 0, status identity-unavailable)
{
  "observedAt": 1792865191033,
  "status": "identity-unavailable",
  "people": [],
  "totalPeople": 0,
  "truncated": false,
  "message": "This caller has no authenticated person identity. Select a person returned by list."
}

# unreachable Gateway (exit 1)
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Gateway not reachable at ws://127.0.0.1:1 (ECONNREFUSED).…"
  }
}
```

## Notes for reviewers

- Distinct from `system presence` / `system-presence`.
- AI-assisted. Maintainers can edit.

prs.title: perf(gateway): skip stale placement replica scans during maintenance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session maintenance repeatedly scans every retained worker placement replica even when the preservation read's sequence fence proves none can change its snapshot.

## User Impact

Less temporary allocation and CPU work during maintenance on large session stores. No changes to which sessions are protected, stored data, configuration, or public interfaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every committed or read-replica postimage has a sequence at or below the owner's sequence. Until that sequence reaches the preservation read's fence, the entire replica traversal is unnecessary. Skip that traversal at the existing owner; keep per-use authority checks, the committed overlay after writes, additive pending protection, and caller-owned snapshot cloning.

Runtime code grows by three lines. The existing overlay remains necessary for publications that arrive after preparation; no new cache, revision, invalidation path, or retained snapshot is introduced. The rest of the diff is a rerunnable benchmark/runbook and five assertions extending the existing preservation test.

## Evidence

- Current-main built Gateway, synthetic 10,000 sessions/local placements, 6,000 settled subagent runs, and 40 synthetic plugins: each of five `sessions.cleanup` RPCs makes four getter calls, scanning 10,003 replica entries per call while returning an empty protected inventory. That is 40,012 unnecessary replica visits per RPC. All 10,003 resulting session rows remain unchanged.
- Production-owner count probe, 10,000 replicas and 64 protected placements: two captures visit **20,000 → 0** replica entries, with identical returned records. This is owner-level evidence, not a throughput claim.
- Candidate built Gateway: five RPCs again prepare one reader and capture four times, with **zero actual replica traversals**. All 10,003 sessions remain; no pruning/capping/archiving/mutation. Local baseline and candidate use the same current package builds and platform dependencies. The candidate also passed two measured mock-provider turns (plus warmup), each with one tool call/result and one primary response stream; owned Gateways shut down cleanly.
- Measurement acceptance: repeatable CPU/allocation savings with equivalent behavior and no material adverse result, evaluated using absolute tail/GC deltas and sample counts. Both shared Linux quiet slots remained unavailable, so the queued Linux protocol did not execute. The authorized local fallback used two concurrent pairs with shared future starts and reversed launch order, **4,000 preparations per side, 200 warmups, two captures per preparation**, and separate untraced timing/allocation passes. Each process was a short microbenchmark; no CPU affinity was applied on macOS. These owner-operation results are not whole-Gateway throughput or production savings claims.
- Focused worker tests: **51 passed** across placement read cache, read projection, and turn claims (55.46 s command wall time). Consumer tests: **27 passed** across disk space and session retirement (15.57 s). Import-closure tests: **22 passed** (33.10 s). Export-name collision guard, changed-file lint/format, and targeted script typecheck pass.
- Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**, clean through P2 after fixing benchmark output verification and keeping it outside every measured interval. Broad validation is delegated to PR CI; no Testbox was allocated.

The benchmark verifies the actual final output against the independent fixture and reports its digest. Count-instrumented runs do not provide timing claims; the isolated mock-provider Gateway provides maintenance boundary proof separately.

### Local paired owner results

Node 26.12.1, 10,000 replicas. A benchmark operation contains two captures; the real cleanup RPC contains four. Means below are paired reductions, with before/after values averaged across the two pairs. Returned-record hashes match in every run.

| Protected placements | Sampled bytes/operation | CPU ms/operation | Total GC ms/operation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 1,372,996 → 84,267 (**−93.86%**) | 0.2483 → 0.1695 (**−31.71%**) | 0.008895 → 0.001453 (**−83.67%**) |
| 0 (all local) | 1,293,164 → 5,844 (**−99.55%**) | 0.1071 → 0.0162 (**−85.11%**) | 0.011427 → 0.000278 (**−97.59%**) |

<details>
<summary>Paired tail/GC details and limits</summary>

- **64 protected, pair 1:** minor GC 493→51, 35.447→5.835 ms total; major 1→0, 0.657→0 ms; incremental 1→0, 0.068→0 ms. Maximum pause 0.657→0.158 ms. Operation p95/p99 0.241/0.266→0.178/0.191 ms (4,000 samples/side). Loop p95/p99 1.184/1.236→1.114/1.167 ms (986/721 samples).
- **64 protected, pair 2:** minor GC 494→51, 34.278→5.786 ms total; major 1→0, 0.630→0 ms; incremental 1→0, 0.079→0 ms. Maximum pause 0.630→0.173 ms. Operation p95/p99 0.234/0.255→0.173/0.187 ms (4,000 samples/side). Loop p95/p99 1.194/1.243→1.099/1.144 ms (968/707 samples).
- **All local, pair 1:** minor GC 670→3, 47.879→1.345 ms total; no major/incremental collections. Maximum pause 0.413→0.588 ms (+0.175 ms). Operation p95/p99 0.200/0.257→0.024/0.044 ms (4,000 samples/side). Loop p95/p99 1.164/1.328→1.059/1.114 ms (459/151 samples).
- **All local, pair 2:** minor GC 671→3, 43.535→0.877 ms total; no major/incremental collections. Maximum pause 0.287→0.319 ms (+0.031 ms). Operation p95/p99 0.184/0.230→0.008/0.017 ms (4,000 samples/side). Loop p95/p99 1.125/1.306→1.019/1.027 ms (393/80 samples).
- No weak-callback GC events. Major-GC counts, loop p99 (<1,000 samples), and candidate minor-GC tails (<200 samples) are context only. The two small all-local maximum-pause increases are below the absolute safeguard while total GC falls sharply. No control-valid adverse gate was observed, so no rejection/A-A escalation was needed. Promotion was not separately traced; this change introduces no retained state. No long-running soak or production throughput estimate is claimed.
- Full cleanup response-byte equality is not claimed: disk/WAL telemetry differs between launches. Session counts, retention/mutation outcomes, and the owner benchmark's complete placement records match.

Reproduce an owner pass with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/placement-preservation-measure.ts --mode timing --operations 4000 --protected 64 --captures 2 --start-at <shared-epoch-ms> --output <result.json>`; repeat using `--mode allocation` and `--protected 0`, selecting the preserved baseline source through `--owner-source` as documented in the runbook.

</details>

prs.title: fix: honor reasoning capabilities on compatible model routes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes operator-declared reasoning efforts being replaced by live catalog guesses, and utility/title requests sending unsupported `reasoning.effort: "none"` to OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoints.

Closes #165119. Closes #177425. Thanks @tre1d and @eulrich101618 for the reports and reproductions.

## User Impact

Explicit reasoning lists and maps survive catalog preparation. Off sends a disable value only when the selected route declares it; an unknown disable contract omits scalar effort and leaves the server default in effect. Explicit opt-outs and accepted effort lists remain authoritative. Saved thinking preferences stay intact, with the existing runtime clamping policy.

Custom Ollama `/v1` users can declare `none` through existing compat metadata to disable thinking on models that support it. Declared binary formats retain their disable field. No new configuration field is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared request resolver owns scalar off/none mapping across Completions and Responses, replacing the separate Completions off-default hint. The catalog merge retains operator reasoning declarations while leaving unrelated capabilities catalog-owned. Map-only declarations no longer inherit a catalog veto or lose their disable value in the Responses payload policy; partial maps stay partial. Native model-name disable defaults apply only on known native routes.

When a managed request has disabled intent and no scalar effort, its declared DeepSeek/Z.AI binary dialect supplies the disable field. Enabled/default behavior and explicit scalar mappings stay unchanged. The PR tooling extraction inventory includes the shared query's new dependency. Model-level off mappings also participate in the inferred Z.AI declaration check; binary disable remains available when scalar effort is disallowed. Undeclared inferred Z.AI off controls remain omitted, preserving #172580's policy while honoring explicit model/compat mappings.

Production: +100/-58 lines (net +42, including one inventory entry). Tests: +165/-29. Docs: +14/-7. The remaining growth preserves declarations and shares mapped-value capability checks; the obsolete transport-specific off policy was removed. The assertion baseline shrinks by one cast.

## Evidence

- Baseline regressions fail at the owning boundaries: six request cases, declared catalog ladders/disable support, and map-only catalog/wire controls. An isolated CLI call reproduces the original Responses HTTP 400.
- 197 focused tests passed across request, catalog, preparation, utility, prefix-stability, and OpenRouter consumers (1,079.73 s including cold compilation). Native provider siblings: 66/66 in 19.51 s. Reasoning/ChatGPT siblings: all 38 cases covered; an obsolete explicit-map expectation was corrected and its two controls passed in 19.47 s.
- Initial PR CI found two attributable gaps. Both reproduced locally and were repaired together: managed binary-disable coverage and the tooling extraction inventory. All 154 affected request tests pass in 14.23 s; the two failed extraction tests pass in 84.37 s. The binary tests also protect enabled/default requests and scalar mappings.
- A subsequent review exposed a model-level Z.AI mapping gap under production endpoint attribution. Both direct/managed regressions failed before the fix; all 156 request cases now pass in 14.36 s. A real attribution-resolver → managed transport → owned HTTP fixture probe changed from two HTTP 400 errors to two normal visible answers, with scalar support unset/false. Null-map and explicit scalar controls remain covered.
- Core/scoped test types, changed-file lint, all seven ratchets, and isolated Codex review pass. Review is scoped-clean with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The full setup build passed (36m 26.9s); the final head's runtime rebuild passed (9m 21.8s).
- Final-head live macOS Gateway `agent` requests returned `4` with zero reasoning characters on Ollama `qwen3:8b` and `qwen3.5:4b`, LM Studio `google/gemma-4-e4b`, and managed llama.cpp b10809 reusing the existing Qwen3 GGUF read-only. Captured controls: scalar `none` for Ollama/LM Studio and `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false` for llama.cpp. End-to-end times: 10.357 s, 0.497 s, 1.114 s, 4.353 s; functional probes, not benchmarks.
- Owned fixtures reject unsupported controls. Responses off/title omit effort; medium remains medium; a map-only route sends its required `none`. The two binary fixtures receive `thinking.type: "disabled"` without scalar effort. All ten Gateway cases return HTTP 200 with no fallback. Title generation returns `Synthetic title` in 0.385 s.

Final-head CI passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40144165466)). ClawSweeper found no actionable code defects on this head; its only remaining hold is the latest-stable upgrade proof gap below.

Limits: no latest-stable upgrade run; existing config fields and data shapes are retained. Local macOS proof only; no hosted OpenRouter/Muse inference. Ollama was 0.40.10, whose [OpenAI adapter is byte-identical to 0.40.8](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/v0.40.8/openai/openai.go#L582-L620). LM Studio used an 8K loaded context with small prompts. The mandatory-thinking Qwen3 4B model was not an off control. Unknown custom routes still need a verified disable declaration. The full build reports an existing CSS budget overage (296.4 KiB vs 296.3 KiB); its UI/checker inputs match the exact base and this branch does not change them.

prs.title: fix(web-fetch): balanced link URLs leak into extracted text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: text-mode `web_fetch` results leak URL suffixes when Markdown link destinations contain nested parentheses.

## User Impact

`[Cassini](https://example.com/a_(b(c)))` becomes `Cassini`, without stray closing parentheses. Images stay omitted from web text, while one-line previews keep their existing image labels. HTML anchor labels remain readable even with spaces or unmatched parentheses in the destination. No configuration or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the two first-closing-parenthesis regexes with the existing balanced-link parser. The shared parser retains its preview default and supports omitting images for web extraction. Basic HTML text extraction keeps anchor labels directly instead of serializing arbitrary HTML URLs as Markdown and parsing them again. Thanks @AmelioMansour for the fix and its regression cases.

## Evidence

- The owner regression fails on current main with `Read Cassini)) and .png).`, then passes with this repair. The full extraction, normalizer, and Readability suites pass: 46 + 23 + 7 tests. Vitest durations were 4.04s, 7.70s, and 11.16s; combined wrapper wall time was 34.96s on a busy host.
- Real HTTP through `createWebFetchTool().execute` in isolated process state reproduced leaked Markdown/HTML suffixes and malformed-Markdown rewriting on base. All seven head fixtures pass: balanced links, unmatched HTML parentheses, a space-bearing HTML URL, a trailing label backslash, unchanged HTML Markdown output, and malformed Markdown preservation. The synthetic server was stopped. A full Gateway/model session was not run; the HTTP tool invocation exercises the changed extraction boundary.
- Targeted package typecheck, type-aware oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad proof is provided by exact-head PR CI.
- Simplification removes the two inadequate link regexes and reuses one maintained parser. Production delta is +14 lines, tests +22: the remaining growth preserves the distinct image policies and avoids lossy HTML-to-Markdown round-tripping.
- Independent diff review through P2, with full parser and extractor source, found no actionable findings.

## Current CI limitation

Exact-head run [40140057766](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40140057766) finished red in two Gateway recovery cases: `gateway-widget-restart.e2e.test.ts` (widget revision stayed at 1) and `gateway-restored-requester-settle.e2e.test.ts` (three restored wakes instead of two). Their classification is unknown because the scheduled-main run uses different shard coverage; no matching main failure has been established. The extraction regressions and targeted checks above pass. These failures have not been rerun merely to obtain green CI.

A bounded local baseline attempt on main `085076cc8f76c05b58166f85d792d851ac6c6d68` used `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/oc-ct-webfetch OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/gateway-widget-restart.e2e.test.ts test/gateway-restored-requester-settle.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Runtime preparation took 23m19s and worker preparation another 213.5s; the attempt was stopped after 30 minutes without a test verdict. The completed build was not interrupted. This establishes an environment/proof limitation, not an inherited-failure classification. No CI rerun was requested.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces duplicated fixtures, overlapping scenarios, and implementation-coupled assertions in eight test files while retaining their distinct behavior contracts. This is the replayed test-only portion of batch d498.

## User Impact

No production behavior, runtime configuration, API, or runtime support code changes. The only non-test edit removes four obsolete CI mock-export exceptions. The retained changes consolidate test setup and owner-level assertions; hosted CI is the behavioral proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replayed 21 of the 30 supplied commits onto pinned main `51400ac59921960ccaf335f99919a23f51e390a4`. The other nine were omitted to preserve main's newer tests or because their deletion was already present.

### Retained shard scope

Counts compare the pinned main tree with this PR. Declarations are static test declarations (parameterized declarations counted once), not executed case counts.

| Shard | File | Test LOC before → after | Declarations before → after | In-shard coverage evidence |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| r0292 | `extensions/qa-lab/web/src/app.browser.test.ts` | 842 → 561 | 18 → 12 | Tests and coverage not run, per CI-only instructions. |
| r0295 | `src/cli/node-cli/daemon.test.ts` | 837 → 556 | 22 → 14 | Tests and coverage were not run, per CI-only mode. |
| r0296 | `ui/src/lib/cron/index.test.ts` | 837 → 550 | 27 → 19 | Tests and coverage were not run, per CI-only mode. |
| r0298 | `ui/src/lib/board/provider.test.ts` | 830 → 768 | 27 → 23 | No tests, coverage, or builds ran under CI-only mode. |
| r0299 | `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-keyword-retrieval.test.ts` | 770 → 538 | 22 → 17 | Tests and coverage deferred to hosted CI as instructed. |
| r0300 | `extensions/onepassword/src/secret-ref-resolver.test.ts` | 827 → 711 | 19 → 17 | Tests and coverage intentionally not run under CI-only mode. |
| r0301 | `extensions/workboard/src/sessions-board.test.ts` | 827 → 785 | 19 → 20 | Tests and coverage were not run, per CI-only mode. |
| r0302 | `src/infra/database-engine/session-entry-write.conformance.test.ts` | 815 → 769 | 5 → 5 | Tests and coverage were not run, per CI-only instructions. |

The shard reports contain no measured coverage totals. Some describe an earlier intermediate reduction rather than the complete supplied commit chain; the line/declaration counts above are freshly measured from the actual replay. No coverage-preservation percentage is claimed.

### Replay decisions

- Dropped `39325ed741f1` (r0293): FaceTime's current fixture/lifecycle structure differs substantially from the prerequisite campaign version. Preserved main's startup, carrier, cancellation, and shutdown tests.
- Dropped `208ae3a5d946` and `c82334ed18bf` (r0301 follow-ups): conflicts with main's parameterized Home-session, new-session notification, projection/authority, and explicit store-cleanup changes. Retained the cleanly replayed initial Workboard cleanup.
- Skipped `41579751abef` (r0305) as empty after preserving main's current mock names: its duplicated custody cases were already absent.
- Dropped `729b90e5cb17` (r0305): depends on missing campaign helper aliases and conflicts with current prepared/durable/finalized delivery contracts.
- Dropped `941de1be9314`, `3092b06a520c`, and `6735e095eb87` (r0306): main already has local panel helpers and has moved sizing coverage; the dependent chain conflicts with current fixtures and lifecycle coverage.
- Dropped `6daffc27fcab` (r0304): prerequisite pricing fixture refactors are absent and current startup/cache/metadata tests differ. Preserved main's pricing proof.

### Review and CI repair

Accepted review findings restored the resolver's real process-tree cleanup tests, full cross-engine actor write/rollback conformance, queued disabled/deleted job coverage (ultimately by dropping all r0303 changes), composer-draft and selected-tab polling, explicit-zero cron timeout/cooldown values, unpinned Node and automatic Bun selection, restricted command selection, returned Workboard columns, memory-import recovery details, and late initial plans after an agent switch. All repairs are staged together; findings about the previous index-only snapshot were resolved by staging those repairs.

The successful cron conflict-recovery finding was declined after inspecting unchanged `ui/src/pages/cron/cron-page.conflict.test.ts`: its save/toggle cases cover exact `cron.get` refresh outside active filters, authoritative editor revision, and deliberate retry with that revision.

The second run ([40140934923](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40140934923)) exposed a memory-import readiness helper that accepted an empty match without asserting button existence, a type-aware lint error in the QA Lab generic query helper, and three relocated partial mocks caught by the mock-export ratchet. The repair adds the missing non-null readiness assertion, uses typed DOM queries directly, and preserves actual exports in those mocks. Focused independent review of these repairs is clean.

The third run ([40141944687](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40141944687)) cleared extension lint and eight readiness-related UI failures, but two memory-import consolidation failures remained. Dropped the entire r0297 file change rather than weaken either assertion. The baseline only shrinks; no new exceptions were introduced.

Commits `2bf1db19312f` and `9d5ec83d8fc2` were neutralized after review; all r0303 commits (`38df1ad5024a`, `352d9f1c6c51`, `e32e9f2e5b24`) were neutralized during review/CI repair. The original replay history is retained, followed by repair commits.

No conflict markers or partial hunks from omitted commits remain. No CODEOWNERS-owned paths are changed.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` — passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write <8 changed test files>` — passed, no residual changes.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <8 changed test files>` — exited 0.

Reduces CPU and temporary allocation in history preparation without changing provider payload bytes or stored transcripts. There are no configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Memoize message-local normalization by the existing immutable transcript publication identity. Keep mirror detection and failed-tool completion repair outside the memo because later messages can change those decisions. Reuse image-free content cleanup by immutable content identity and the finite role/signature policies, including when tool-result envelopes are rebuilt. Image-bearing messages still enter the image sanitizer on every attempt: transient decoder failures and unavailable backends must remain retryable.

Both caches have weak source keys; replacement publications miss naturally and derived cached results are frozen. This replaces repeated content work rather than caching the complete history pipeline. Runtime production delta: +41 lines (85 added, 44 removed), plus a 273-line benchmark harness and 62 test lines; the growth implements the immutable admission and policy separation needed for safe reuse. The remaining whole-history pairing, model-switch, compaction and provider-hook passes are unchanged.

## Evidence

Baseline replay owners: `219e9181aab075e31903d62a3bb50cf7875ba097` (unchanged through rebased main `05740a6c078a53fdde9457e783ea8b398472d900`). The refreshed pairs use that common source/dependency tree with only the two replay owners swapped. The committed `scripts/perf/replay-history-measure.ts` uses real in-memory SessionManager publications: 1,000 retained messages, metadata cleanup on 10% of assistant messages, and one new user tail per attempt. Matching input and serialized output hashes are required. Two concurrent local macOS pairs use synchronized warm starts and reversed launch order; they are source-owner measurements, not complete Gateway latency or isolated Linux CPU-placement results. Allocation sampling runs separately and includes collected objects.

| Full history preparation | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| CPU / 5,000 attempts | 7,010 → 2,082 ms | 7,229 → 2,197 ms |
| Sampled allocation / 500 attempts | 2,208,055,528 → 733,131,248 B | 2,206,205,952 → 733,440,328 B |
| Total GC / 5,000 attempts | 236.28 → 50.39 ms | 275.59 → 60.44 ms |
| Maximum GC pause | 1.965 → 0.684 ms | 1.460 → 0.808 ms |

Paired mean reductions: CPU 70.0%, allocation 66.8%. All input/output hashes match. Warm heap is about 0.08 MiB higher for the memoized 1,000-message fixture; final post-GC heap was lower in both pairs. Those heap readings include runtime state and are not a precise cache-size attribution.

All measured collections were minor (667 → 250 per pair); major GC had zero samples and is not a percentile gate. Latency p95/p99 improved in both 5,000-sample pairs (p95: 1.658 → 0.424 ms and 1.847 → 0.555 ms; p99: 1.823 → 0.476 ms and 2.979 → 0.964 ms). Minor-GC p95 also fell (0.446 → 0.267 ms and 0.678 → 0.401 ms); GC p99 has fewer than 1,000 samples and is context only. Event-loop p95 improved (14.31 → 4.17 ms; 17.20 → 5.52 ms; 499–500 samples/side); p99 lacks the required 1,000 samples and is context only. Both maximum GC pauses improved. No adverse acceptance gate triggered; no A/A rejection was inferred.

Attribution smoke (200 attempts): normalization reuses all 1,000 historical output messages instead of 950; image cleanup no longer recreates all 200,200 envelopes/content arrays. Full-history historical output reuse increases from zero to 199,000 across successive attempts. The history array is still traversed for contextual repairs; these counts do not claim zero message iteration.

Validation: both new reuse regressions fail on the baseline; 118 tests in five focused files pass, including replay hygiene, malformed/signed image content, late tool results, mirror ordering, provider payload/cache stability and stable tool prefixes. The focused run took 81.5 s including compiler preparation. `pnpm tsgo:core` and the local built-distribution build pass. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) is clean at P0–P2.

Built-distribution Gateway proof passed on isolated loopback ports with 10,000 background sessions, 6,000 settled runs, 40 synthetic plugins, and two foreground histories of 250 seeded turns each. Three rounds completed six foreground turns with real tools and concurrent history/list/diff RPC traffic; all six historical replay checks passed. This verifies synthetic provider-facing behavior, not real-provider latency or billing. Changed-file lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks pass; PR CI supplies broad validation. No Testbox lease was allocated.

The first CI pass found broad-union type accesses in the new benchmark/test assertions and required the cast-count baseline to shrink from 6 to 3. Fixed together; the three failed typecheck leaves, both changed test files (65 tests), and the assertion ratchet were rerun locally. Production behavior did not change. Matched measurements above were refreshed after the benchmark bookkeeping type fix.

The complete CI and applicable security-review gates passed on `088ba04ae0c01a125da6bb5bcec8cdbda070502d`. Main then added another benchmark description at the same README insertion point. Rebased and preserved both sections; runtime code, tests and benchmark remain identical to that passing head. Formatting and whitespace checks and independent review pass on the resolution. The complete current-head CI run [40144023563](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40144023563) passed on `38f89d066e5d46a805aeffe30f48ecdc37b03298`. The Team quiet-slot measurement never started, so its waiter and sandbox were removed; no Team performance result is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated fixture constructors, held promises, wire responses and cleanup blocks give the same test setup several owners. This consolidates that setup without deleting any kept assertion, scenario, registration or table row. No production behavior, public SDK export, config, schema, protocol or dependency changes.

Whole diff: **251 net test/support lines removed across 58 paths in 23 cuts; production 0** (224 additions, 475 deletions). This is an explicitly authorized 100+ residue PR, **not LARGE**, and does not count toward the LARGE-PR target. Shared fixture ownership stays local to equivalent families; existing owners are reused first. Each cut is independently droppable, except the named storage follow-on within the collector family.

The independent MCP connection-fixture slice remains (10 net lines). prs.title: fix(browser): stop Playwright downloads past 10 MiB
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A page the browser tool visits can download a file of any size. The Playwright save copied that body into the managed download directory and published it. The browser node proxy already rejects a file over 10 MiB, but only after the bytes are on disk. A direct Playwright save had no byte budget at all.

## Evidence

Local Chromium on macOS downloaded two attachments from a loopback HTTP server through production `saveBrowserDownload`. The oversized attachment was rejected and was not left in the output directory. A 13-byte attachment was published.

```console
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-download-byte-cap.mts
budget=10485760 large=10551296
large rejected message=Browser download exceeds 10485760 bytes outputEntries=chromium-profile ms=28
small published bytes=13 path=small.bin ms=11
```

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: After Chromium finishes a download, OpenClaw publishes the managed copy only when it is at most 10 MiB. A larger file is cancelled and is not published.
Real environment tested: macOS 27.0.1, Node v26.10.0, headless Chromium from playwright-core, loopback HTTP attachments, worktree /tmp/oc-f083 at 5725211f014.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: Started a local HTTP server that served a 10551296-byte attachment and a 13-byte attachment. Launched headless Chromium with downloads accepted, navigated to each attachment, and passed the Playwright download to saveBrowserDownload.
Evidence after fix: terminal output copied below.

```console
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-download-byte-cap.mts
budget=10485760 large=10551296
large rejected message=Browser download exceeds 10485760 bytes outputEntries=chromium-profile ms=28
small published bytes=13 path=small.bin ms=11
```

Observed result after fix: The 10551296-byte download was rejected with Browser download exceeds 10485760 bytes in 28 ms, and the output directory did not contain large.bin. The 13-byte download was published as small.bin.
What was not tested: A remote browser node, and a download that is still transferring when it crosses 10 MiB. Playwright exposes the body stream after the browser finishes, so this run covered a finished local attachment.

## Summary

The cap is the existing `BROWSER_PROXY_MAX_FILE_BYTES` value, 10 MiB. Files at that size still publish. One byte over cancels the download, deletes the Playwright artifact when that method exists, and leaves the managed path unpublished.

Ref https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/127497

That issue also asks for a retention owner for successful downloads. This pull request does not change how long a download under the limit is kept.

## Chromium cancellation fixture

The caller-abort case in `pw-download-cancel.chromium.test.ts` used to resolve only inside `download.saveAs`. Real Playwright downloads take `createReadStream`, so the abort waited until the five-second capture deadline. Production now always reads `createReadStream`. Test doubles that only implemented `saveAs` yield the same bytes on that stream, and the `saveAs` copy path is gone.

Headless Chromium on this Mac, with `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD_E2E=1`, ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-download-cancel.chromium.test.ts -t "cancels a streaming download"`. Both matching cases passed: caller abort in 517 ms, and invalid output directory in 282 ms. This commit does not change whether a direct-host download uses the 10 MiB budget. That choice remains a maintainer decision.

prs.title: fix(ui): limit Details to running processes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Details mixes finished process history with current work and opens the whole collection when a user selects a process. ## User Impact Details shows up to three running processes on desktop and two on mobile, with a separate Stop action. Desktop shows command names without elapsed time; mobile keeps elapsed time and uses the same square-terminal icon and running spinner as desktop. Mobile rows preserve the panel’s side insets and inset divider before the overflow link. The Processes heading has no counter. When more running processes exist, the link reads “Show N more” with tabular numerals; otherwise it reads “View all processes.” Both open the full Running/Finished history. Selecting a row opens its exact output; Back returns to the previous Details position. ## Before and after Before is the original main baseline captured before this PR. After represents head 4cf136f20e5b1ac6e9dccdaa0f6dc1a1dbb84caf, using the same synthetic Gateway fixture, view, theme, and image scale.
