prs.title: fix(claws): refuse malformed UTF-8 before adding agents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Claw inspection and Add accepting malformed JSON or YAML bytes as altered names, manifest paths, or policy text.

## User Impact

Malformed UTF-8 is rejected with the existing source diagnostic before Add plans or creates an agent. Valid Unicode, JSON BOM rejection, YAML BOM support, legacy profile pointers, and byte-based integrity checks retain their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both text intake owners use the existing `decodeUtf8Input` before parsing, while retaining the original bytes for integrity hashing. The profile reader also reuses its existing filesystem root instead of creating it twice.

Thanks to @Leon-SK668 for the original fix and Linux CLI reproduction.

## Evidence

- Four regressions fail against the unchanged current-main readers: package metadata can select a replacement-character filename, JSON manifests accept altered names, and conventional/legacy YAML profiles accept altered policy text. All four pass with strict decoding, including repaired Unicode controls.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/claws/reader.test.ts src/claws/openclaw-profile.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all 40 tests pass, including BOM, bounds, integrity, link admission, and legacy-profile controls. After merging current main, all 40 tests passed again (277.22 s wrapper / 225.79 s Vitest). The earlier green run took 251.83 s / 201.81 s; the base red run took 241.81 s / 209.15 s. Most time was module compilation (98% of the green Vitest duration), not test execution.
- Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and diff checks pass.
- Production +6/-4 (net +2), tests +55/-1 (net +54), docs +3. The small production increase validates text once while preserving raw-byte integrity; redundant root creation and comments were removed.

The contributor's original PR includes compiled Linux CLI proof pinned to `c52cfbb5ce46d8dc4142d3152b663aff148018bc`. This revision exercises the real filesystem and inspection owner; the built CLI and live Gateway were not rerun because a separate full build was not proportionate. The Add caller returns on a failed source read before planning or creating resources.

Independent P0–P2 autoreview completed with no actionable findings.

The previous head passed all 68 CI jobs (run 40139956445), but the separate security-review workflow failed on inconsistent GitHub diff metadata (13,906 reported files versus the five-file local diff). A normal merge of current main preserves the reviewed five-file patch byte-for-byte and refreshes that required check.

<details>
<summary>Prior-head compiled CLI trace (contributor evidence)</summary>

The following captured Linux output predates this revision. The contributor ran `node ../claw-source-utf8-proof-20261022.mjs` against base `ce54bc879ad922006023cf889f1f38df9efd689d` and candidate `c52cfbb5ce46d8dc4142d3152b663aff148018bc` on October 22, using Node 24.22.1 and isolated synthetic state. It is retained for inspection, not claimed as runtime proof of the current head.

### Captured native output and independent readback

The malformed manifest contains byte sequence `c3 28` inside the agent name. These are captured output excerpts; only temporary roots are redacted as `<proof-root>` and unrelated fields are omitted.

Base `claws add ... --json` exits **0** and reports:

```json
{
  "status": "complete",
  "agent": {
    "requestedId": "utf8-import",
    "finalId": "utf8-import",
    "workspace": "<proof-root>/manifest/rejected-workspace",
    "config": {
      "id": "utf8-import",
      "name": "Caf�(",
      "workspace": "<proof-root>/manifest/rejected-workspace"
    }
  },
  "workspaceCreated": true,
  "configCommitted": true
}
```

A subsequent `agents list --json` process reads the stored agent back with `"id": "utf8-import", "name": "Caf�("`. For the profile variant, a subsequent `config get agents.entries.utf8-import.groupChat.mentionPatterns --json` exits **0** and reads:

```json
[
  "@caf�("
]
```

At the candidate head, the identical malformed manifest Add exits **1** with this complete stdout:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "openclaw.clawAddPlan.v1",
  "stability": "experimental",
  "valid": false,
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "level": "error",
      "code": "invalid_json",
      "phase": "parse",
      "path": "$",
      "message": "Could not parse <proof-root>/manifest/source/openclaw.claw.json: <proof-root>/manifest/source/openclaw.claw.json must be valid UTF-8."
    }
  ]
}
```

Fresh agent-list readback contains only `main`; the rejected workspace is absent and config/source bytes match their pre-Add hashes. The profile variant reports `openclaw_profile_read_failed` at `$.profiles.openclaw` with `profiles/openclaw.yml must be valid UTF-8.` The package variant refuses before a replacement-decoded manifest path can select a different file.

Re-encoding the sources and retrying Add exits **0**, creates exactly one agent per isolated case, and fresh `agents list --json` reads `"name": "Café �( 😺"`. The repaired BOM-prefixed profile's fresh config readback is:

```json
[
  "@café �( 😺"
]
```

This distinguishes legitimate U+FFFD from invalid input bytes rather than rejecting a character in the decoded string.


</details>

prs.title: perf(gateway): bound failed orphan workspace discovery retries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The remaining background workload repeatedly reads exact session entries and live worktree ownership. Source tracing points to minute reconciliation retrying workspace discovery for startup placements whose workspace cannot resolve. Successful roots are already retained. Failed resolutions intentionally remain retryable after #169223; any fix must preserve that recovery.

The existing orphan-cleanup owner now discovers the startup set once, retains successful roots, and rotates at most eight failed workspace resolutions in each later minute sweep. Every failed identity remains eligible for recovery. Only synthetic state was used for reproduction.

## User Impact

Gateways with many unavailable historical workspaces avoid re-reading every session and bound worktree each minute. Cleanup of settled orphan refs retries each unresolved workspace within `ceil(F / 8)` minute sweeps for F unresolved workspaces, with additional deferral while sessions are busy. Foreground workspace resolution, pending-result recovery, lease expiry and heartbeat handling remain independent.

## Why This Change Was Made

The smaller earlier fixture did not reproduce sustained exact-entry polling. The retained-placement workload crosses the current 128-entry replica capacity without changing that cache. The 177-placement real Gateway workload reproduced the same sustained shape, and the zero-placement control removed it. The change bounds background retry work at its existing owner; it adds no cache, timer, generation, schema, SQL text, or permanent error classification.

## Acceptance rule (registered before the first run)

Flow: an isolated built Gateway at the recorded head, three configured agents, 2,600 synthetic sessions, 177 retained local placements, 46 with missing bound worktrees, the bundled iMessage plugin with a synthetic JSON-RPC bridge, and a connected loopback operator client subscribed to sessions. Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-ingress-polling.mts --session-polling --observer <frozen-v3.1.4>/observer.cjs --out <isolated-output> --idle-seconds 180 --sparse-events 3 --cpu-profile`.

Count operations first using the frozen observer, causality module, and background roots. Separate boot/settle (90 seconds), warm idle (180 seconds), each sparse real channel turn, and shutdown. Run a zero-placement control. Reproduction requires sustained repeated exact-entry reads and bound registry reads at approximately 177 and 46 per minute with the observed worker stack; a startup-only burst is insufficient. If that pattern does not reproduce, reject the item rather than make a speculative production change.

Once reproduced, the win is eliminating unchanged-placement minute reads and worker requests, keeping MAIN at zero in the warm target path, and preserving fresh workspace resolution after owner writes plus transient-error, lease, heartbeat, and cleanup recovery. A bounded slow recovery path must be counted and disclosed. Shared read families (exact entries, actor hydration, entry-cache snapshots, row facts, watermarks), all statements/requests, and MAIN are reported so cost cannot hide in another worker or phase.

Use five interleaved baseline/candidate samples for the reproduction workload, keeping cold and warm separate; report median, p95, and min–max. Frozen general-workload validation uses three alternating pairs if host load is below 64 and internal free space is at least 12 GiB, otherwise one pair with the limitation stated. Profiles use `node --cpu-prof` for every thread. Wall-clock/CPU A/B runs require the campaign timing lock and load below 24; no latency or CPU-time claim from unqualified runs. A 20% adverse movement in any user-facing cell stops acceptance for attribution or repair. If no qualified window is available after 60 minutes, report counts/profile attribution only.

## Design and acceptance of the slow path

Initial discovery still attempts every startup identity. Later sweeps attempt at most eight unresolved identities, fairly rotating failures; successful roots leave that queue. Admission groups are always rebuilt from all known roots, so a newly resolved sibling cannot bypass an already-known busy session. Cleanup keeps its final retained-ref read and Git serialization. An empty unresolved queue plus completed root cleanup ends the pass; unresolved identities are not dropped when known roots complete.

Expected candidate target: at most eight exact-entry reads and eight bound-owner reads per minute after initial discovery, lower total statements and requests, zero warm MAIN, and all synthetic channel turns delivered. This is a bounded retry-rate reduction, not permanent elimination of recovery reads. The delay concerns settled orphan refs; no lease or live claim is retained longer by this change.

## Evidence

Five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs completed on built heads `b46707af923647da66832fc356462f6afb758e46` and `9fedb5c7b7ea73ae5ba65d415a74365fd60b7954`; production base `3f7b7765585ddcd72822d8b4e43ef928d23eecf7`. All 30 synthetic channel turns replied. The baseline reproduced 177 exact-entry and 46 bound-owner reads/minute, close to the live normalized shape (about 169 and 44/minute). The zero-placement control recorded 30 SQL / 13 requests / 0 MAIN over 180 seconds, with neither target family.

| Warm idle, 180 seconds | Baseline median [min–max]; p95 | Candidate median [min–max]; p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| SQL statements | 699 [699–699]; 699 | 58 [56–273]; 273 |
| Worker requests | 682 [682–682]; 682 | 41 [39–259]; 259 |
| MAIN SQL | 0 [0–0]; 0 | 0 [0–0]; 0 |
| Exact-entry reads | 531 [531–531]; 531 | 24 [24–193]; 193 |
| Worktree-owner reads | 138 [138–138]; 138 | 4 [2–50]; 50 |

All 641 median removed statements and 641 removed requests are explained by the target families: exact-entry −507 and bound-owner −134. Residual idle work stays 30 SQL / 13 requests. No cost is moved to MAIN or another worker. C5 delayed the initial full discovery into idle: its settle phase had no target reads, and idle contained the initial 177/46 discovery plus two bounded retries (193 exact-entry / 50 bound-owner total). This sample is kept in the candidate idle p95/spread (273 SQL / 259 requests), still below baseline p95 (699/682). This is a 91.7% idle SQL reduction and 94.0% request reduction in this fixture. The candidate retries eight identities/minute, not every unavailable identity; the measured target is about 9 reads/minute. That is not a universal nine-read cap: each bound identity can require both an exact-entry and a registry read.

Thirty-three CPU profiles per arm were captured on B1/C1. Host load did not qualify for the timing lock's load-below-24 condition within 60 minutes; these are counts and profile-attribution results, with no latency or CPU-speedup claim. Cold boot/settle, individual turns, shutdown, and whole-run counts are reported separately below.

### Accepted retry overlap

The raw sparse-2 exact-entry cell reaches 9 on the candidate versus 1 on the baseline. The extra eight reads are one bounded background minute retry (`kind=session-exact-entries`, `background:no-turn-context`), while the foreground cohort read stays one. Some candidate windows also contain one bound-owner read. This is disclosed rather than treated as measurement noise. The campaign coordinator explicitly accepted this overlap on the reviewed head: “the sparse-2 exact-read family cell (median 1 -> 9) is ACCEPTED as the documented, approved bounded minute retry (<= 8 failed identities/min) overlapping that measurement window.” That quote refers to the first three pairs; the final five-pair exact-read median is 1 in both arms, with p95 1 → 9. The corresponding sparse-2 task-request median/p95 is 10/11 → 17/21. Aggregated turn-family p95 also includes that same retry; it is not a second increase. The final five-pair statistics are retained in the full table. The retry-related increase remains covered by that disposition; idle and full-run target reads fall substantially.

One baseline/candidate pair was used because host load exceeded 64. Both arms passed the 14-turn workload, cron, compaction, control-plane, shutdown, and restart assertions. These are physical window counts; the frozen harness did not provide complete causal labels for this build, so no turn-causal count or latency claim is made. The warm statistics below describe ten sequential warmed turns within each arm, not ten independent runs.

| Warm window metric | Baseline median [min–max]; p95 | Candidate median [min–max]; p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| statements | 51 [50–71]; 71 | 50.5 [50–69]; 69 |
| requests | 12 [12–18]; 18 | 12 [12–17]; 17 |
| main | 0 [0–0]; 0 | 0 [0–0]; 0 |

Whole-workload SQL / requests / MAIN: 2986 / 796 / 96 → 2991 / 798 / 96.

The individual adverse windows were stopped and attributed before acceptance; the improved aggregate is not used to hide them:

| Physical window | SQL, baseline → candidate | Requests, baseline → candidate | Attribution |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| turn 7 | 50 → 62 | 12 → 16 | Six lease-expiry reads, one lease-acquisition transaction, one passive checkpoint. |
| turn 8 | 50 → 54 | 12 → 15 | Four lease-expiry reads, one plugin-metadata read, one fewer audit write. |
| turn 9 | 50 → 69 | 13 → 17 | Ten lease-expiry reads plus existing plugin-refresh/audit/transaction and handle-admission work. |
| idle settle | 64 → 125 | 16 → 20 | Memory indexing/publication work moves into this window; exact-entry and watermark work moves out. |
| restart shutdown | 22 → 23 | 6 → 8 | One upstream-link monitor read and one zero-SQL prepared-model-catalog task. |

Across the whole run, lease-expiry SELECTs are exactly 20 in both arms: baseline first turn/turn 1 has 10/10; candidate turns 7/8/9 have 6/4/10. Memory SQL is 127 → 129; the only whole-run memory shape difference is two source-file-state reads. Memory publication shapes are identical in total. The shutdown additions come from `session-upstream-monitor.ts` and `prepared-model-catalog.worker.ts`. All 135 source files appearing in the adverse SQL stacks are byte-identical between production base and candidate, including the lease, plugin, memory, transcript and monitor owners. These are unchanged background operations appearing in different physical windows. Per the campaign's attribution-over-raw rule, they do not establish a regression caused by this change; no general-workload saving is claimed.

The same stack-based shared-family classifier gives whole-run exact-entry 19 → 18, bound-owner 1 → 1, actor hydration 10 → 10 and watermark 35 → 35; entry-cache-snapshot and row-facts markers are absent in both. Exact-entry/watermark reads shift from idle settle to connected idle together (2/8 in each arm). No shared-family increase is hidden by the window totals. Because baseline origin labels are incomplete, these are physical SQL/stack comparisons, not a causal-request comparison.

### Validation

The regression is red on unchanged production: ten unavailable identities cause ten repeated resolutions instead of the permitted eight; the one-identity case passes. The candidate passes fair rotation and later recovery. The busy-sibling regression passes and proves that a newly resolved sibling cannot bypass an already-known busy session. The recovery suite passes all 60 tests, with focused lease-expiry and heartbeat-at-delivery tests also passing.

Exact-head CI [40135797981](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40135797981) completed successfully: 46 successful jobs and 28 skipped, including changed-owner tests, types, lint, source contracts, Madge, T1/dialect/worker ratchets, and the required CI gate. Basic local lint/format and `git diff --check` passed. Local type-aware preparation rejected the mandated external-to-checkout internal virtual store (`Declaration input escapes checkout`); no bypass was used, and exact-head CI supplied the authoritative type/lint proof.

Knip's baseline and candidate finding sets were compared by scan and exact file/export; there are no new findings. Existing findings in all three scans are inherited from the production base (script 1,136; production 67; full-tree 77, with identical file/export sets). Two independent Codex review rounds completed with no unresolved actionable finding. PostgreSQL review approved the exact head (`REVIEW-OK SESSPOLL #182871 9fedb5c7b7ea`): no SQL, transaction, schema, or identity changes; the final current retained-reference read still protects cross-process commits immediately before deletion.

The production change is +9 net lines. The extra state is one first-discovery flag; the existing placement queue and resolved-root map carry retries and successful facts. No new cache, timer, generation, option, or permanent-failure classification. The committed workload is reusable; test additions cover bounded retry/recovery and sibling admission. Frozen harness integrity: 36/36 hashes match v3.1.4.

## Permanent failures and compatibility

The current workspace resolver uses the same error for missing sessions, unbound workspaces, missing/removed live worktree registrations, and changed identities. Its live-registry projection carries no permanent tombstone; removed worktrees can be restored, and the existing target test proves an unbound session can later acquire a worktree. The resolver does not test filesystem existence. Retiring these failures permanently would need an owner-defined outcome and a wakeup after later binding/restoration writes. That is a follow-up; the bounded retry preserves recovery without adding a probe.

## Open pull request compatibility

Final census: all 2,678 open PR heads targeting main (2,677 other PRs), against `355a5ae8bc8e33e1d6590c831b79d667cd0bc60b`; 44 new/moved file lists refreshed, full pagination included. Only #144351 (`25704f50a9d3c0894799a5fcd3693db5b654183b`) and draft #170160 (`ee6003da2db0578eedc8ea07a3410bbabc04a954`) overlap. #144351 retains the same 40 conflict paths/four regions, with no new conflict. #170160 gains the previously accepted contextual cleanup-loop conflict (current-main comparison: 73 → 74 paths); its sole overlapping semantic change is already on main. The coordinator explicitly accepted that superseded-line conflict. #180741 moved to a head with no overlapping files; #182979 is merged. Candidate merges cleanly into current main.

prs.title: fix(memory): rebuild reuses cached embeddings instead of evicting them first
prs.body:
Fixes #182886. Thanks @etzelm for the reproduction and provider-input counts.

## What Problem This Solves

Full memory rebuilds at the embedding-cache cap evict cached vectors before later rebuild batches read them, turning a few misses into provider calls for the whole index. Forced indexing and the rebuild after an agent database-engine port share this path.

## User Impact

Rebuilds reuse cached vectors and embed only the misses. The cache may temporarily grow by newly generated vectors during a rebuild; publication, failure, and abandonment trim it back to the existing cap. Suspended background rebuilds retain their vectors until resumption or discard. A process interruption can leave excess rows until the next synchronization prunes them. Incremental writes retain their per-commit capacity bound. No configuration, schema, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing rebuild owner tracks pending cache cleanup alongside its staged index. Generated-cache writes defer eviction while that rebuild exists, and the same pruning owner handles SQLite and PostgreSQL cleanup. This avoids another corpus pass or holding a full vector-cache snapshot in JavaScript. Failed rebuilds preserve the published index and retain generated vectors under the normal cache policy.

The separate PostgreSQL query-plan issue #182808 already has PR #182821; this PR leaves its eviction query unchanged. A bounded nearby test repair captures SQL while native statements are live, preserving existing cache-capacity assertions after Node finalizes those statements.

## Evidence

Acceptance: with 8 reusable vectors and 4 missing vectors in a cache at capacity, embed exactly 4 inputs, keep all 12 indexed chunks, and settle back to the cap. Cover both populated and empty published indexes, plus failed publication and suspended shutdown.

- Base `dc3a0a6a3d7a`: the original manager regressions sent 12 inputs instead of 4, for both populated and empty published indexes. The extracted focused suite passes both cases, failure cleanup, and incremental commit bounds: 4 tests, 9.55s of test time. These need the real manager/cache/publication composition; cache-helper tests alone miss the cascade.
- Real CLI with a loopback HTTP embedding stub and a 50,000-row cache containing 8 needed vectors: SQLite `memory index --force` embedded exactly **4 inputs**, published **12 chunks**, and finished with **50,000 cache rows**.
- Real PostgreSQL CLI `memory index --force`, with the same 50,000-row/8-hit/4-miss fixture and an empty derived index: exactly **4 inputs**, **12 chunks**, and **50,000 cache rows** afterward.
- Node focused replay: **74 tests passed across the other five files**. The raw-cache suite initially had 4 failures because its observer read `StatementSync.sourceSQL` after disposal; after repairing that observer, **19/19 passed** in 10.20s wall time (0.2s tests). Query counts, query plans, storage, and rollback assertions remain intact. Together these cover 93 distinct passing cases.
- The six-file replay took 527.46s wall time, including 138.145s shared worker compilation and additional module preparation. The earlier recovery run passed 30 tests in 357.22s wall time (53% test time), with repeated pre-existing manager/worker startup. No individual test exceeded 30s. The shutdown case verified 8 suspended cache rows trim to 2 on close (2.268s).
- Touched-file `run-tsgo`, oxlint, oxfmt, Madge (0 cycles), and `git diff --check` pass. Isolated Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

All product invocations used isolated HOME/state, distinct service profiles, and synthetic data. PostgreSQL uses a disposable local UTF8 PostgreSQL 17 database with the documented search extensions. A remote attempt failed authentication before returning a lease; no remote proof is claimed.

The full `database port` attempt stopped during preparation: the fresh server initially lacked `unaccent`, and the retained manifest then refused resume/rollback with “observed changed source data; required captured original SQLite image.” No engine switch or successful port is claimed. Captures remain intact. PostgreSQL cache proof uses a fresh PostgreSQL-backed CLI rebuild with an empty derived index instead.

The full `check:changed` SQLite-inventory step was omitted under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI is the broad proof. CI seconds are not yet available. Diff: production +25/-9, tests +194/-58 (including moving the existing capacity case), docs +9/-3.

prs.title: perf(agents): release skill catalogs retained by prompt reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

System prompt reports can keep discarded skill catalogs alive through their short skill-name strings.

## User Impact

A small retained-memory improvement with identical `/context` and usage reports. No configuration, schema, or provider-request changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Regex captures were slices into the entire skills catalog. Find the same valid name without allocating a capture result, then detach it into a name-sized backing string. This keeps the latest run report available after the run without adding a cache or changing persistence. Production delta: **+5 lines**; the copy protects the report's independent lifetime, and removing capture allocation pays for it.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before measurements: identical reports, release discarded catalogs while reports remain alive, and no material construction regression. Baseline: `219e9181aab075e31903d62a3bb50cf7875ba097`. Five alternating local Node 26.12.1 pairs use 200 distinct 80-skill catalogs and 40 tool definitions for retention; timing uses 10,000 warmed constructions per process; allocation uses a separate 1,000-construction sampled pass including collected objects.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Retained heap, 200 reports | 16.40 MiB | 2.98 MiB | −81.85% (13.43 MiB) |
| Sampled allocation/report | 46,823 B | 43,243 B | −7.65% |
| CPU/report | 156.34 µs | 158.73 µs | +2.40 µs (+1.54% paired mean) |
| Wall time/report | 155.77 µs | 158.82 µs | +3.05 µs (+1.99% paired mean) |

Heap snapshots show **201 → 1** large catalog backing strings (the remaining one is the intentional warm fixture), releasing 14,718,400 backing bytes. All report digests match. `--expect-detached` fails on baseline and passes on candidate. Releasing reports also releases their retained storage. These are owner-level synthetic savings; another live owner may independently retain a catalog, so this is not a production-wide memory estimate.

<details>
<summary>GC context and reproducible commands</summary>

Untraced timing, minor GC only; no major collections occurred in these short windows. Per pair, baseline → candidate total GC ms / collection count / maximum pause ms:

1. 10.559 / 114 / 0.142 → 10.495 / 105 / 0.233
2. 11.007 / 114 / 0.211 → 9.242 / 104 / 0.151
3. 10.910 / 114 / 0.148 → 10.489 / 104 / 0.227
4. 12.194 / 113 / 0.243 → 10.239 / 104 / 0.141
5. 13.947 / 113 / 0.495 → 11.081 / 104 / 0.183

No pause-percentile claims (sample counts below the required threshold). Promotion and event-loop tails were not measured. Shared remote measurement slots were unavailable; these are short local probes, not swapped-CPU remote acceptance evidence.

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/system-prompt-report-retention.ts --expect-detached
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/system-prompt-report-retention.ts --mode timing --operations 10000
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/system-prompt-report-retention.ts --mode allocation --operations 1000
```

Use `--owner /absolute/path/to/saved-owner.mjs` for each baseline/candidate bundle and `--snapshot /path/to/synthetic.heapsnapshot` for backing-string inspection. No snapshots or private runtime data are included in this PR.

</details>

Focused report tests pass (20 tests; 44.18 s wrapper time, including compiler setup). Eager-import and PR-wrapper source-closure guards pass (22 tests); export-name collision guard passes. Formatting and targeted lint checked. Independent subagent review is clean through P2 (**autoreview route unavailable**: provider selector did not match operator configuration).

Built-Gateway smoke passed on exact head `e23c4298ab6a9cc58eb93592aaab039480264356` after `pnpm build` (3m33s). The isolated loopback fixture contained 10,000 synthetic sessions (mostly idle subagent-shaped keys plus archived dashboard rows), 40 synthetic plugins, and 80 skills. A two-minute workload completed nine turns, including two child runs, two attachment/artifact flows, and one cron run. `sessions.usage` with `includeContextWeight` returned the persisted `source: run` report with all 80 expected skill names (19,548 rendered catalog characters). All task-owned Gateway/mock processes stopped cleanly. A fixture-only archive request initially omitted `expectedSessionId`; it was corrected before this successful run. PR CI supplies the broad gates.

CI follow-up: [run 40142220964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142220964) caught this PR's benchmark lint-suppression comment in `test/scripts/lint-suppressions.test.ts`. Removed the exemption while preserving the RegExp cleanup; the focused guard now passes (14 tests, 7.89 s wrapper time), and the retention assertion and independent re-review pass. Head `81c85a772ab7f2fe7038ed8c785bb670ea1b7e96` keeps the report implementation and report tests identical to the built-Gateway proof above; only the benchmark cleanup expression changed. All required checks passed on `81c85a772ab7f2fe7038ed8c785bb670ea1b7e96` ([gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40143550778)); the optional artifact-build job was still running at landing.

prs.title: perf(sessions): share retained summary identity strings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Retained session observer digests and restart-recovery source records carry separate copies of identifiers already held by their session entry after JSON decoding and worker transport.

## User Impact

A small retained-memory reduction for Gateways with many session summaries. Session data, stale-lifecycle rejection, recovery authority, and wire/storage formats are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker-reader adoption boundary now reuses equal immutable identity strings before its received objects are retained. It preserves unequal identities and absent optional fields. There is no global interning table, cache, or reference that extends a session row's lifetime. Actor postimage adoption is outside this change.

Runtime production delta: +57 lines. The existing wire/storage contracts retain these fields, and transport recreates primitive strings, so this adds the missing receiving-side reuse rather than another owner. The larger addition is a rerunnable synthetic Gateway workload.

## Evidence

Final built-Gateway comparison: baseline runtime source `18503f69a904a94eeb7571141d9db6be47e0ee3d`, candidate runtime source `482c7f3b2841861158a96442dd86ad74f15d6267`. The subsequent rebase did not change this runtime module. Workload: 10,000 synthetic sessions, 8,000 settled runs, 2,000 archived sessions, 40 synthetic plugins, and ten successful mock-provider turns. Both snapshots contain 12,000 observer digests and 12,000 recovery sources.

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Physical family ID string nodes | 120,000 | 73,025 |
| Family ID string shallow bytes | 4.942 MiB | 2.983 MiB |
| Duplicate ID string bytes within the families | 3.112 MiB | 1.153 MiB |
| Family dominator-union retained bytes | 14.457 MiB | 11.180 MiB |

The small reduction is **3.277 MiB (22.7%)** in family retained bytes and **1.959 MiB (63.0%)** in duplicate ID bytes. These are overlapping views of the same savings, not additive. A prior independent capture reproduced the target counts and savings exactly. The final baseline includes #182906 (verified by ancestry), so this measures its residual cost.

Whole-Gateway heap was inconclusive across captures; forced-GC snapshots do not establish CPU, latency, or GC-throughput improvements. Among each family’s 12,000 records, 8,995 now share session/lifecycle string nodes with their entry; 3,005 remain duplicated through other retained ownership paths. This does not extrapolate the synthetic saving to production.

Reproduce with `scripts/perf/session-summary-id-retention.ts --prepare --state-dir <new>` then `--capture --state-dir <new> --output <new>`, after building each revision. Compare snapshots with `scripts/heap-snapshot-diff.mjs --independent-ids --json`; a property-edge census measures the family-specific string nodes and dominator unions. Physical heap-node census establishes string sharing; JavaScript equality alone cannot.

Focused proof: worker-readers tests (24 tests, 1.96 s final file duration) and entry-readonly worker tests (18 tests) pass. The new isolated-process heap-node regression fails against the baseline runtime with “sessionId retained a duplicate string node” and passes with this fix. Value tests also cover stale identities, absent optional fields, and caller isolation. Core typecheck, changed-file formatting/lint, export-name collision guard, and both eager-import/PR-wrapper closure guards (22 tests) pass. Both final built Gateways complete all ten mock-provider turns. Broad proof is PR CI; no remote test lease was used.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings. The configured autoreview provider selector was refused; no configuration was changed. Review covers the runtime, workload, and physical-sharing regression; no actionable findings remain.

## CI and inherited failure

Final head `b48f2d257088c2b03e81bda31565415f8ad1812c`: the changed-code tests, build, lint, type checks, boundary checks, UI E2E, and security review pass. PostgreSQL conformance shard 2 fails seven cases in `src/infra/database-engine/interactive-setup.integration.test.ts`: the fixture runtime omits `standalone-runtime-profile.mjs`, which `packages/llm-core/src/validation.ts` imports. The Gateway exits before the onboarding-ready marker.

The [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40141688438/job/121014904329) and [scheduled main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138789542/job/121006161355), main `87f00b1b5254861d944e524cdd8bb3a65f53b59f`, show the identical seven failures and missing-module signature. The test, `doctor-config-preflight.process.test-support.ts`, and `packages/llm-core/src/validation.ts` have no diff between that main build and this PR. This is an inherited fixture failure; no CI rerun was requested.

prs.title: perf(ui): defer optional transcript renderers and session copy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold chat loads renderers for optional transcript content and the full session-management English catalog even when the first screen does not use them.

## User Impact

Chat loads 13,992 B less preloaded JavaScript gzip (49,958 B raw). Ordinary messages, active answers, the composer, and run frames remain eager. Optional content retains its current selectors, behavior, error boundaries, and CSS order.

## Why This Change Was Made

Load activity details, source previews, question summaries, system notices, typing rows, and browser-card renderers when their content is present. Move the work-summary implementation intact into its own module. Seven cold-chat consumers register a shared catalog with their 25 additional labels instead of loading management copy; the full catalog references the same literals in its original order. All 378 catalog leaves, namespace identity, and active foreign translations are retained.

Completed-work summaries remain eager: the first CI attempt showed that deferring the header hid duration metadata on the first cached frame. The repair restores that first-frame contract. Optional activity and raw-detail bodies still load when needed.

The whole-run-frame lazy prototype was rejected after a 133 ms active-text delay at 100 ms RTT. This change retains the frame and text stream synchronously. A redundant recap lazy wrapper was also removed because that renderer was already eager through message rendering.

## Evidence

Asset base: `285f5be610f`. Head: `f78992cc400`. Node 26.12.1 on the same Mac. Current-main integration preserves its saved-conversation media gate in the extracted work summary and frame previews; a focused regression passes denied/allowed/denied preview access while completed-work text stays visible. Full CI passed on this exact head: [40142398817](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142398817). Measurements use production bundles, the production Gateway HTTP entry, and synthetic RPC data; they do not claim real-provider latency.

| Asset surface | Base | Head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip / raw | 281,411 / 870,677 B | 281,589 / 870,946 B | +178 / +269 B |
| Chat preload JS gzip / raw | 1,271,676 / 4,094,983 B | 1,257,684 / 4,045,025 B | −13,992 / −49,958 B |
| New Session preload JS gzip / raw | 767,357 / 2,493,324 B | 763,067 / 2,478,707 B | −4,290 / −14,617 B |
| Observed cold-chat JS gzip / raw | 1,373,526 / 4,323,615 B | 1,359,627 / 4,273,924 B | −13,899 / −49,691 B |
| V8 executed / unused raw | 1,923,763 / 2,399,852 B | 1,902,041 / 2,371,883 B | −21,722 / −27,969 B |
| Total CSS gzip / raw | 303,561 / 1,595,121 B | 303,490 / 1,595,121 B | −71 / 0 B |

The strict base/head comparison passes. Startup remains within its current budget; the 178 B gzip growth accompanies the split shared labels/lazy bindings. Startup/Chat/New retain 7/19/16 JS and 1/3/3 CSS requests. The existing aggregate CSS cap excess does not grow. Refreshed coverage on the integrated bundles includes 53 scripts on each side. Gzip totals use the Gateway sidecars, falling back to identity bytes for uncompressed assets, matching the performance checker.

After full CI exposed missing first-frame duration, synchronous lazy-content assertions, and a missing required fixture option, the repaired head passes UI and chat-test types, 81 unit cases, and five production E2E cases across cached boot and desktop/mobile delegated-work history. The E2E opens Worked, waits for the nested Raw details control, and verifies retained tool results. A second CI run exposed the remaining standalone preview/typing/retry assumptions plus missing browser-card fixture CSS; all 23 affected cases pass locally, including dark/light menu geometry. Formatting and affected chat-test types pass. Both failed full CI attempts and their repairs remain explicit evidence: [40136445254](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136445254), [40139345164](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139345164). The repairs add no preloads or longer timeouts and remove no assertions. Prior unchanged-input proof also passed: integrated UI typecheck; lazy transcript lifecycle (1), streaming (9), message groups (11), activity disclosure (28), optional English loading (4), and two browser files (12). The lifecycle case preserves adjacent message identity, Reply focus, current callbacks through row changes, and the completed frame. Production Knip on the integrated head reports four unused non-UI files, 33 export entries and 12 type entries, with no UI findings or new ignores. Its output is byte-identical to current main. The extra export compared with the original measured base is an untouched OpenAI-plugin export from main. Independent current-diff P0–P2 autoreview found no actionable issues.

Solid refactor census: effects 1→1, untrack 1→1, owner API calls 3→3, onSettled 6→6, lazy declarations 4→13; controllers, render effects, direct listeners, DOM queries, flush, and onCleanup remain zero. Touched production UI LOC: 4,696→4,798; tests: 10,593→10,838; tooling/generated: 2,791→3,077. Added production lines are local lazy boundaries and the shared catalog; the moved renderer is not duplicated. Test LOC now includes the additional consumers repaired after full CI exposed their synchronous readiness assumptions.

This follow-up is an incremental measured step toward the −30% boot goal. It does not reach that target. The first step landed as #182813.

### Readiness and renderer CPU

Readiness proof was captured before current-main integration, on base `3df26eebaf4` and the corrected production candidate committed as `d3533cf7c0c`. The integration preserves those lazy boundaries and adds the current-main media gate; its focused regression and UI types pass, and exact-head full CI passed on the combined code. These timings are retained evidence, not a rerun on the final merge. Twenty interleaved base/control/head observations per cell, with ten additional rich-RTT pairs (30 total). Each control uses the identical base bundle. Entries are **median / p95 (min–max), ms**. RTT uses 100 ms latency and 10 Mbps.

| Workload/profile | Visible outcome | Base | A/A control | Head |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary / local | Composer | 265.6 / 598.6 (219.6–925.1) | 248.5 / 377.3 (220.5–487.6) | 280.8 / 491.8 (208.1–815.8) |
| Ordinary / local | Transcript | 515.3 / 760.2 (413.6–1244.9) | 498.7 / 567.3 (431.5–742.6) | 524.9 / 706.5 (418.7–1065.2) |
| Ordinary / 100 ms RTT | Composer | 1500.8 / 1593.2 (1449.5–1611.1) | 1506.0 / 1603.0 (1442.5–1710.0) | 1499.4 / 1631.3 (1446.7–1641.7) |

prs.title: fix(markdown): inline backticks swallow following prose in chunking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes replies beginning with inline triple-backtick code being split as an unclosed code block, repeating the label and formatting following prose as code.

## User Impact

Following prose splits normally, while actual backtick and tilde code blocks keep their existing protection. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the CommonMark restriction on backticks in a backtick-fence opener's info string at the existing shared scanner. Preserve AmelioMansour's four-line fix, replace the duplicate scanner regression with a public `chunkMarkdownText` regression, and retain the distinct tilde-fence control. The scanner remains the sole fence owner; no new parsing path or state is added.

Thanks @AmelioMansour for the fix and original channel-boundary proof. Production +4 lines, tests +14, documentation +1 against main. The four production lines express the missing grammar rule; no unrelated cleanup is needed.

## Evidence

- Current-main regression is red: the chunker repeats `literal` and injects closing/reopening fences around ordinary prose. The identical input on the fix returns `['```literal```', 'Paragraph outside code with', 'ordinary words.']`.
- Direct production reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /private/tmp/oc-ct-webfetch/chunk-proof.mts` exits 1 on base and 0 on the fixed scanner. No helper mocks or live state.
- Full selected consumer and extraction suites: 343 tests pass across ten files (241.90s wrapper wall time, including a one-time 120s test-worker build). The public chunker/fence/code-span group took 2.27s Vitest. After integrating current main, all 188 tests in the six focused fence/chunker/extraction files pass (29.06s wrapper).
- Targeted type-aware oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex review through P2 is scoped-clean, with no actionable findings.
- Broad proof: exact-head CI [40142901202](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40142901202) passed on `67d05e32ddb990cceae9705177edda38968c1be0`. Fresh ClawSweeper review on this head reports zero findings.
- No live Slack UI or full Gateway/model session was exercised in this pass. The direct chunker proof covers the changed owner; the contributor's prior real sender/HTTP proof is preserved below.

### Contributor's sender-to-HTTP evidence

On original head `0b18f1aad38cf67d8a742a8a629795908f3b5fe6`, the contributor exercised production `sendMessageSlack`, `createSlackWriteClient` and the real Slack WebClient against a temporary synthetic HTTP server, with newline chunking and `textChunkLimit=32`. The base sent five malformed `chat.postMessage` payloads with repeated inline labels and invented empty code blocks; the fix sent three payloads containing one inline label and ordinary prose. Real-fence and ordinary-prose controls passed. This is sender-to-HTTP proof, not live Slack receipt or a full Gateway/model session. See the [original verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180588#issuecomment-6356395793).

prs.title: fix(lobster): validate workflows without runtime code generation in AOT
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Lobster workflow validation failing in standalone AOT builds.

## User Impact

Lobster can request input, resume workflows, and validate LLM output on AOT hosts. Fixed schemas no longer compile during startup on any host; Node and JIT Bun retain native Ajv for dynamic schemas. No new configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lobster compiled two fixed schemas during import. The narrow dependency patch generates those checks with Ajv at build time, including its Unicode-length helper. The existing host profile selects dynamic validation once, when the runtime is first acquired: native Ajv for JIT, the shared codegen-free provider for AOT. Request-local compiler selection and dependency-owned reference namespaces preserve concurrent requests and schema references across recreated runners.

The profile and AOT compiler load lazily, so the plugin's native static import list is unchanged. Narrow typed SDK subpaths expose the shared validator and the existing profile getter without loading the broader runtime/logging surface on first use; that broader surface was measured and would regress first acquisition. CI's existing generated-validator check covers the patched output, Ajv version, and helper hash.

## Evidence

- **36 owning/sibling tests passed in 37.92s**; after the typed-entry correction, all **24 affected runner/profile/compiler cases passed in 31.17s**. Both profiles exercise workflow resume rejection, LLM output rejection/recovery, and references across recreated runners.
- The corrected `pnpm build` passed, including **160 public SDK subpaths** (7m05.2s in build phases, following artifact-lock preparation). It reported the same inherited UI CSS warnings (296.5/296.3 KiB gzip; 1558.7/1558.1 KiB raw).
- After replay onto the merged dynamic-validator base, the reviewed patch ID is unchanged. All 36 owning/sibling tests passed again in 118.85s wall time (including worker-cache rebuilding), and generated-validator freshness passed.
- Targeted core, extension, script and test types/lints, mock-export guard, SDK exports and generated-validator freshness passed. Independent Codex review is clean.
- The public SDK API comparison passed: two added entrypoints (`json-schema-validator` and `runtime-profile`), four added exports, and no removals. Acknowledgement digest: `6c875951` (`--require-acknowledgement --acknowledge 6c875951`).
- The committed-head native import profile passed with clean source/build provenance, no qualification gaps, and 106.9 MiB peak RSS.
- A strict NodeNext consumer imports the getter and exhaustively checks its published profile type through actual package exports, with no source aliases; its emitted JavaScript passes with string compilation disabled.
- The packed plugin includes the patched dependency. Its five changed files match installed bytes, and the extracted plugin imports the built SDK and validates Unicode with Node string compilation disabled.
- A small experimental Bun AOT probe fails before the change with `EvalError` and passes afterward, including real ask/workflow valid and invalid resumes plus compiler scope/cache checks. The final public-import probe compiled **437 modules in 3.982s**. This is not a whole-application AOT build or an interpreter-free claim.

### Exact-head CI

Run [40135040447, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40135040447/attempts/1) completed on `0d32d99a9d400d389d5b1f3bc9552f6a74b58786`: **147 jobs passed, 21 skipped, six primary jobs failed plus their aggregate**. Security and all selected Android jobs passed. CI remains failed; it was not rerun.

All six failures are attributed to baseline behavior. The Docker memory-store cases fail to resolve `@openclaw/fs-safe`; both reproduce on clean exact CI base `90d9772` with the same generated chunk (2 failed, 60 skipped; 119.75s total). The hooks newline and sandbox agent assertions match retained clean-main reproductions. Codex fixtures omit the unchanged producer's reasoning flag; model-discovery and delayed-catalog assertions match retained main failures. Their causal input blobs match the current CI base and tested merge. The failure report labels five jobs unknown and the packaging job new; the independent exact-base proof supplies the attribution rather than relabeling CI green.

CI tested merge `c13c7f9` has the exact PR head and recorded main baseline as parents. Its 22-path authored change record is byte-identical to the reviewed branch patch. Native inherited-failure admission retains this evidence and does not waive security or review gates.

### Performance

Fifteen paired fresh processes importing native packaged plugin entries, on a shared host:

| Cold import | Node before → after | Bun before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| CPU median | 261.874 → 259.031ms | 342.911 → 342.012ms |
| Wall median | 212.469 → 212.118ms | 99.599 → 97.709ms |
| CPU p95 | 291.748 → 331.739ms | 924.046 → 1649.392ms |
| Wall p95 | 254.297 → 283.863ms | 172.692 → 160.702ms |

Medians are within noise; tail regressions remain visible. The earlier eager-profile version and all samples with increases of at least 20% are retained in the task evidence. No startup speedup is claimed.

At the package boundary, removing import-time compiler warmup moves cost to the first dynamic compilation: Node **9.509 → 16.846ms**, Bun **22.141 → 33.082ms**. Total import plus first validation CPU decreased from **179.281 → 170.835ms** on Node and **159.675 → 109.179ms** on Bun. The longer Node warm-validation run measured **2296.438 → 2256.982ns** median and **2328.055 → 2419.240ns** p95 (+3.92%). These are scoped validator measurements, not whole-application startup claims.

### Dependency and follow-up

Ajv 8.20.0 was already Lobster's pinned runtime dependency; the new direct declaration is build-only. It is MIT-licensed, was released April 24, 2026, and its repository is active/not archived (last push September 6; latest commit `f177fe323420ccb23e1a79445fd470cbf80aee7c`). npm reports 249,308,485 downloads for October 16–22.

Port the generated fixed validators and scoped compiler hook to [openclaw/lobster](https://github.com/openclaw/lobster). Remove the patch when a published version passes the same runner and AOT/codegen-ban proof. No new runtime dependency is introduced.

prs.title: fix(sessions): align reply barrier extension deadline with monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The extendable reply-barrier settlement budget was seeded and consumed with wall-clock elapsed time while feeding a monotonic `setTimeout`. A backward wall-clock jump inflates `remainingMs`, so a healthy run settles late; a forward jump can force an early finish. Seed and consume now both use `performance.now()`, matching the timer's monotonic domain.

- Problem: `waitForReplyBarrierSettlement`'s object-timeout branch mixed `Date.now()` with a monotonic timer.
- What changed: two lines in `src/sessions/session-controller.settlement.ts`, plus a regression in the existing `reply-run-registry.successor-barrier.test.ts` suite.
- Not changed: numeric timeouts, extension policy, public signatures, schema, or runtime mechanisms. Production changes are +2/−2.

## Why This Change Was Made

The owner already bounds this work with a wall-clock-independent `setTimeout`. Measuring that budget from the wall clock makes the declared limit depend on an unrelated clock adjustment. Both readings use the monotonic clock the timer consumes, so this is the smallest owner-local correction. The policy is optional and normally unset by bundled callers; the fix matters for callers supplying it.

## User Impact

An active follow-up is no longer held beyond its stated budget or released early solely because the host clock changes. Without a clock jump, settlement behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Each run used an isolated same-process `startGatewayServer` and token-authenticated `GatewayClient` WebSocket. The real `enqueueFollowupRun` path was first blocked by `followup-barrier`, then released. The original barrier and delivery were deliberately left pending. Only the proof process's `Date.now()` rolled back 1 s; host time and the production Gateway were untouched. Same 5 s extendable budget in both columns.

| Observed result | Before: `Date.now()` | After: `performance.now()` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Barrier installed | 67,268 ms | 66,487 ms |
| Wall clock stepped back | −1,000 ms at 67,272 ms | −1,000 ms at 66,491 ms |
| Initial admission | blocked, `followup-barrier` | blocked, `followup-barrier` |
| Requested budget settled | 73,268 ms | 71,488 ms |
| Queued runner entered | 73,275 ms | 71,493 ms |
| Admission released | 73,276 ms | 71,494 ms |
| Barrier install → admission | 6,008 ms | 5,007 ms |
| Original barrier / delivery | pending / pending | pending / pending |

Before waited about one extra second after its budget; After released at the budget despite the rollback. Both records show the runner and admission while the original barrier and delivery were still pending, ruling out normal delivery completion.

```console
# Before: budget reached, original barrier still pending
PROOF-SCENARIO-BUDGET requested settled atMs=73268
PROOF-SCENARIO-ADMISSION released atMs=73276
PROOF-SCENARIO-STATE {"rawBarrierPending":true,...}
# After: same scenario, monotonic budget
PROOF-SCENARIO-BUDGET requested settled atMs=71488
PROOF-SCENARIO-ADMISSION released atMs=71494
PROOF-SCENARIO-STATE {"rawBarrierPending":true,...}
```

Regression installs a 500 ms extendable barrier first, then steps the wall clock by 30 s in either direction while its underlying promise stays pending. Advancing 1,000 ms of monotonic time releases it in both cases.

| Regression | Result |
|---|---|
| Before source, rollback / forward step | ✗ late release / ✗ early release |
| After source, both directions | ✓ 2 passed, 5 skipped |
| Existing test file | ✓ 7 passed |

- Not tested: a forward wall-clock jump through the full Gateway entry; the regression covers that direction.
- The owner settlement remains pending after the observed admission; this PR does not change its later completion.
- Open PR collision check: no open PR touches the settlement source or successor-barrier tests. Current `main` still contains the defect.

prs.title: perf(plugins): reduce retained preparation-worker memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Retained plugin-preparation workers load the Kysely query-builder graph solely because their private SQLite staging lock uses it to execute fixed transaction and PRAGMA commands.

## User Impact

Reduces the memory retained by each plugin-preparation worker. Plugin loading, lazy imports, recovery, and the plugins-once behavior are unchanged. No schema, configuration, stored-format, durability, or locking change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing native statement owner for the lock's two PRAGMA reads and the already-wrapped connection for fixed transaction commands. The staging lock retains its file-identity checks, journal-mode check, reader/exclusive custody, and persisted retirement marker. The narrow raw-SQL guardrail entry covers this lock primitive only.

Do not terminate the worker after preparation: the host still invokes its artifact methods for lazy imports and recovery. It already closes when its last resource and pending request are released. This removes an unnecessary dependency instead of adding an idle-retirement or recreation path.

Runtime production LOC: −1. The extra lines are the guardrail entry, baseline-harness support, and benchmark documentation.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule declared before candidate measurement: real worker-task protocol, synthetic plugin and shared admission facts for 100 roots / 5,000 files, five alternating baseline/candidate samples, forced GC in each worker, lower retained heap with preserved capture/resolve/close behavior. Node 26.12.1; source workers, not a whole-Gateway benchmark. No production snapshots or production workload were used.

| Pair (one fresh worker per side) | Baseline bytes | Candidate bytes | Delta bytes | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 39,976,160 | 36,824,888 | -3,151,272 | -7.88% |
| 2 | 39,940,696 | 36,814,696 | -3,126,000 | -7.83% |
| 3 | 39,965,328 | 36,821,968 | -3,143,360 | -7.87% |
| 4 | 39,964,288 | 36,815,040 | -3,149,248 | -7.88% |
| 5 | 39,965,952 | 36,814,736 | -3,151,216 | -7.88% |
| Mean (n=5 per side) | 39,962,484.8 | 36,818,265.6 | -3,144,219.2 | -7.87% |

Mean post-GC retained heap: **38.11 → 35.11 MiB (−3.00 MiB, −7.87%)**. All five pairs had **981 → 725** loaded script URLs and **254 → 0** Kysely scripts. Five alternating samples used fresh worker processes, ten warm resolve calls, one workload call, and forced worker GC before inspection. Every capture/resolve/content/close assertion passed.

The shared Linux quiet-slot allocator remained queued, so this uses the lane-authorized local owner-heap proof on macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1. The unused remote wait was cancelled. This is memory evidence, not a latency, GC-rate, promotion, or cold-restart benchmark; the worker lifecycle is unchanged. One earlier incomplete pair was discarded for a Bash 3.2 empty-array setup failure (baseline 39,856,896 bytes; no candidate ran), before all five fresh pairs above.

Reproduction: run `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worker-module-graphs-measure.mjs --state-dir <fresh-owned-dir> --output <result.json> --worker plugin-generation-preparation --samples 1` five times per side, alternating baseline and candidate. Baseline adds `--baseline-dir <baseline-dir>` containing the parent's `src/infra/sqlite-staging-token.ts` and unchanged `src/plugins/plugin-generation-preparation.worker.ts` at those relative paths.


Local Node 26.12.1 diagnostic snapshots show 981 → 725 loaded script URLs, including 254 → 0 Kysely scripts; retained V8 heap after the workload was 39,868,864 → 36,830,224 bytes. Snapshot analysis preserves the shared admission facts; the removable cost is the query-builder import graph.

Focused validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-staging-token.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-generation-worker.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-source-capture-directory.test.ts src/plugins/plugin-source-capture-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 68 tests passed across four files. Staging lock: 3.43 s including startup; plugin files: 384.60 s including cold worker compilation.
- Changed-file oxfmt and scoped core/scripts oxlint passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Autoreview refused the requested provider because it did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

Exact-head CI (`a2c6d822aedb742843d98a4f22ed5367f0ab5bcb`): [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133216039) passed (48 successful jobs); [build artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133215994) passed; [security](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133215995) passed (seven jobs). No failed-job reruns were needed.

Limits: the source-worker retained-heap fixture is synthetic, and built Gateway heaps may differ. PR CI owns broad type/build/test proof. No new lifecycle cache or worker restart cost is introduced. Post-deploy, compare plugin-preparation worker heap at the same loaded-plugin count and after GC; verify lazy imports and reload recovery still work.

prs.title: refactor: remove redundant timer cleanup guards
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Timer cleanup repeatedly checks whether a handle exists even though Node's `clearTimeout` and `clearInterval` already treat absent or previously cancelled handles as a no-op. Remove 20 such branches across Gateway cleanup, request deadlines, realtime transcription, uploads and backup streaming: **40 fewer production lines**, with no new helper or state.

Keep the existing handle resets, abort listeners, admission/settlement checks, stream closure and error propagation. This only delegates timer cancellation to its existing owner. Real error translation and resource cleanup remain; there is no SQL, schema, identity, SDK or public behavior change.

## Acceptance rule (before measurement)

Run one baseline/candidate pair of the frozen v3.1.4 synthetic Gateway workload, with ten warm turns over its real transport, separate cold/first-turn results, and one sample per revision. Report statements, worker requests and MAIN counts, plus per-operation attribution; no latency or CPU speedup claim. Use zero idle observation time because this batch does not alter periodic scheduling. The win is 20 eliminated cleanup branches and net-negative production code while preserving behavior. Reject any new statement/request attributable to the changed owners; investigate any warm cell moving 20% or more rather than calling it spread. Background-only count variation must be identified explicitly. Existing boundary tests remain unchanged and PR CI supplies broad validation.

## Evidence

- Formatting: passed for all 13 changed files.
- Core type-aware lint: passed for all 13 changed files using the repository core tsconfig.
- Isolated Codex review: both actual review rounds scoped-clean; no accepted/actionable findings. The final round covers the preamble substitution and retained admission guard.
- Frozen v3.1.4 synthetic Gateway pair: both complete workflows passed. Ten warm turns: **552 → 547 SQL**, **138 → 136 requests**, **0 → 0 MAIN**. Warm SQL median **51 → 50**, p95 **67.85 → 67.10**, range **50–71 → 50–68**; request median **12.5 → 12**, p95 **17.55 → 18.20**, range **12–18 → 12–20**. Whole workflow: **2,903 → 2,911 SQL**, **760 → 765 requests**, **96 → 95 MAIN**. Cold/startup, first-turn and restart counts remain separate in the evidence.
- **Coordinator disposition accepted (2026-10-24, exact head `11bedd0366dfbff8b6a85bcd6ffda13810682289`):** raw cells moving 20% or more are accepted as phase placement under the campaign's attribution rule. Warm turn 3 rises **51/13 → 66/20 SQL/requests**, while turns 2+3 combined are **115/31 → 116/32**: the same metadata read, stateLease acquisition and UNKNOWN batch move from turn 2 to 3, plus one run record. Across all warm turns, every per-operation delta decreases: AsyncWorkScope −2 SQL, session-identity-evidence −2 SQL/−1 request, worker-placement read −1/−1. Compaction **99/12 → 109/19** and restart-connect **14/6 → 20/9** reflect health/delivery/indexing checks moving between neighboring phases. The diff only removes timer-existence guards; it changes no SQL, scheduling, awaits or handle resets. The frozen harness reports causal attribution unavailable; no latency, CPU or SQL-saving claim is made. Both runs used the same synthetic fixture; admission load averages were 62.85 and 86.67. The coordinator explicitly authorized landing after the completed Knip comparison, retaining the media-understanding and PG2 failures as inherited.
- Open-main-PR conflict comparison: initial 2,696-PR census and refreshed complete shared index (2,680 PRs). Five remaining overlapping heads are unchanged; base-only versus base+candidate `git merge-tree` adds zero conflict paths or hunks: #180921 at `5978f3841f50`, #177257 at `aa973a461027`, #159326 at `8db89e068292`, #155378 at `5a4a5923953a`, #118977 at `0a348e273357`. Previously compared #182955 is now closed.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138085135): production/test types, all lint shards, source contracts, architecture guards, baseline/worker/dialect ratchets, build, selected owner tests, and PostgreSQL shards 1/3 and 3/3 passed. The separate Knip 6.40.0 export/type scan has 35 identical findings on baseline and candidate (26 exports, 9 types), zero new or resolved findings, and none in the changed files.
- CI is not all green: [extension bundle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138085135/job/121004093044) has two stale media-understanding config expectations. Both reproduce on clean base `fe6f5c2119ae` with the identical extra `features.reasoning_effort_override: true` field (2 failed / 13 skipped); this patch does not touch the test or its producer. The coordinator assigned that inherited failure to the existing main-repair owner.
- [PostgreSQL shard 2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138085135/job/121004092376) has the same seven interactive-setup fixture failures already attributed to main: synthetic runtimes omit `standalone-runtime-profile.mjs`; its remaining 274 tests pass. The aggregate gate consequently fails. The campaign's explicitly approved inherited-failure route applies under coordinator RED-MAIN NOTE 1. Its fixture repair has since landed in #182990 (`27e87016a5e4`); this PR retains its exact approved head and older base, as explicitly instructed. The media-understanding failures remain covered by coordinator RED-MAIN NOTE 2.
- The initial PR-context failure was only the authored section headings; correcting this body made the replacement check pass. No code rerun or retry was used.

No new regression test asserts a removed implementation guard; existing timeout, abort, stream, and cancellation behavior suites exercise the retained contract. No update/Doctor/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle policy changes, so no published-driver update cell is required.

The admission-timer guard in `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts` was deliberately left intact to avoid a new merge conflict with #168545. The equivalent preamble cleanup site keeps the batch at 20 removed guards.

prs.title: perf(gateway): release archived page budget after reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A large archived session page raises the Gateway's archive materialization budget, which stays elevated after the read pins release. In the synthetic 10,800-session workload, a 4,813-row archive visit leaves all 4,813 archived display graphs resident after clients close, response TTL expiry, and major GCs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The archive owner now raises its existing budget while rows are pinned for preparation and recomputes it from the 100-row default and remaining live pages when pins release. Existing trim/demotion rules still own eviction. Search requests page capacity inside its acquired read scope, so abandoned searches cannot leave an unowned budget.

The preparation window and other concurrent pages must remain protected. That contract requires **+6 production LOC** (10 added / 4 deleted across two files). Existing manual archive-warming test setup is removed. No new cache, configuration, schema, durable-record shape, or protocol; cold-row semantics and demotion rules are preserved.

## User Impact

Completed archive discovery releases unused display graphs. Durable metadata remains discoverable, and exact archived reads, search hits, overlapping pages, archive transitions, and archived board/event preparation retain their behavior. Nonarchived materialization remains outside this change.

## Evidence

Final head: `29b25c25f72339c976557c521899dbf92e573871`; baseline production source: `04fa634c63b0e7584886b530d6d23468f4ab1605`. One quiet **AWS c7a.4xlarge**, lease `cbx_6bbd994e17f4`, Node 26.12.1. L196 synthetic real-Gateway rig: 10,800 durable sessions, 65 clients, five reconnect/churn waves and 1,000 injected updates per case, with retention disabled in scratch fixture config. Fresh state per variant; identical build recipe and canonical `dist/entry.js`. One matched snapshot pair followed by **seven unprofiled interleaved baseline/candidate pairs**. All recorded RPCs succeeded and all five waves completed in every timing case.

Snapshot attribution after the large archive page is served and released:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Materialized archived rows | 4,813 | 100 |
| Materialized nonarchived rows | 5,059 | 5,059 |
| Durable metadata records | 10,800 | 10,800 |
| Rows Map retained MiB | 43.8843 | 34.6920 |
| Publication witnesses retained MiB | 45.5957 | 25.1396 |

Rows Map releases **9.1923 MiB**; witnesses release **20.4561 MiB**, reported separately because retained graph families can overlap. Before archive discovery, both variants materialize 396 rows with zero archived rows; rows Map is 12.5803 / 12.5846 MiB and witnesses 2.7110 / 2.7110 MiB.

Seven unprofiled pairs, median (inclusive IQR):

prs.title: fix(failover): do not default a redaction-destroyed 400/422 body to format
prs.body:
fix(failover): do not default a redaction-destroyed 400/422 body to `format`

Closes #183005

## What Problem This Solves

The failover classifier decides `reason=format` for a 400/422 **from redaction-destroyed text**. `projectProviderError()` runs `redactDiagnosticText()` on the provider body *before* the classifier sees it (`packages/ai/src/utils/provider-error.ts`: *"Redact complete structured data before clipping its message/body projections"*). When the body is oversized or a balanced JSON fragment fails `JSON.parse`, the redactor replaces the **entire** body with a placeholder (`[Oversized diagnostic JSON redacted]` / `[Malformed diagnostic JSON redacted]` / `[Unserializable]`). The `400/422` branch in `classification-rules.ts` then finds no classifiable signal and **defaults to `format`**.

`format` is a terminal format failure (`isTerminalFormatFailure` in `failover-policy.ts`), so the run does a **model-swap** (next configured fallback) instead of the **token-budget overflow recovery** (auto-compaction) that fits a context/request-size 400. Context/request-size 400 bodies are exactly the ones most likely to be oversized (vLLM embeds the offending prompt verbatim), so this is the common case.

This is the 400-path analog of #179962 / #179967 (429 path, "the long-window check reads the redacted text").

## User Impact

- A healthy primary is abandoned for a smaller-window fallback, which then fails for a different reason (real overflow) and can cascade — e.g. a 65k-token content loop on the fallback (2026-10-24 incident).
- The real 400 error is hidden from the user and telemetry (only the placeholder is logged), making diagnosis hard.
- The correct recovery (token-budget compaction, which does not depend on the error text) is never reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

A redaction-destroyed body carries **no classifiable signal** — the same situation the code already handles for the no-body case (`isUnclassifiedNoBodyHttpSignal` returns `null`, with an explicit comment that defaulting to `format` *"triggers a compaction loop that cannot recover"*). This change extends that safe handling to the redaction-placeholder case: classify `null` and let the caller choose recovery.

## Evidence (verified against the real compiled code)

Real shipped redactor + classifier (`packages/ai/dist/provider-error-*.mjs`, `dist/classify-*.mjs`):

```
raw overflow 400 body (112 KB)
  classify(raw)            = context_overflow   (correct)
  redactDiagnosticText()   = [Oversized diagnostic JSON redacted]
  projectProviderError().errorMessage = "400: [Oversized diagnostic JSON redacted]"
  classify(projected)      = format             (wrong, before)  -> null (after)

classify("400: [Malformed diagnostic JSON redacted]")  -> format (before) -> null (after)
classify("400: [Oversized diagnostic JSON redacted]")  -> format (before) -> null (after)
classify("400: [Unserializable]")                       -> format (before) -> null (after)
classify("400 status code (no body)")                   -> null (unchanged — precedent)

A real classifiable 400 body keeps its semantics (unchanged):
  classify('400 {"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Unsupported parameter: logprobs"}}')
    -> format (before and after)
```

## Changes

- `src/agents/failover/classification-rules.ts`: add `isRedactionDestroyedHttpBody(message, status)` (400/422 only, full-body placeholder only) and, in the `400/422` branch, return `null` when the body is a redaction placeholder — before the `format` default.
- `src/agents/failover/classify.ts`: re-export the helper.
- `src/agents/failover/classify.test.ts`: cover all three placeholders across `400:` / `400 ` / bare forms and the signal path, the 422 path, the status scoping, and that a real classifiable 400 body still reads `format`.

## What was not tested

Ran the targeted `src/agents/failover/classify.test.ts` suite and the extracted-function reproduction above. Did not run the full repo typecheck/test suite (no full build in this environment) — the change is confined to the failover classification module and its test.

prs.title: fix(android): bind chat to an allowed agent roster
prs.body:
Fixes #182638

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Android Chat targeting an excluded Gateway default after restart, even though the operator's agent picker contains only an allowed agent.

## User Impact

On startup Android waits for the role-filtered roster, then chooses the allowed default or the first selectable agent. An empty roster shows “No agents available for this role” and keeps Chat unavailable. Failed discovery stays visible and can be retried through the existing Gateway connection action. A remembered explicit selection retains its existing reconnect behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hello and `agents.list` routing metadata remain Gateway-wide, preserving the shipped contract from #161019. Android owns choosing a usable target from discovery.

The maintainer rewrite preserves @xiaopan-xydt's commits and regression intent while removing the extra connection epoch, retry loop, bootstrap flags, and unchecked `mainKey` fallback. Discovery uses the existing connection-catalog lifetime, propagates cancellation, and initializes Chat on a successful retry even when its canonical session key is unchanged. Chat's production transport waits for runtime readiness so manual history refresh cannot bypass failed or empty discovery.

## Evidence

**Final head `571716ebe65d7b069e4df311d574c05c99d599ea`: all selected CI jobs passed.** [Play tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139347410/job/121007794327) passed in 10m07s job wall time; [third-party tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139347410/job/121007794296) passed in 10m06s. Wear, both native-access jobs, Android ktlint, localization, docs, security-fast, and the CI gate also passed.

- Confirmed the original defect on main: `NodeRuntime` bound `hello.mainSessionKey` before discovery and later accepted a fallback absent from the returned roster.
- Owner regressions cover excluded hello defaults, cancellation before readiness, failed-discovery retry with the same session key, an empty allowed roster, and a newer notification conversation selected during initial discovery. The first exposes main's premature binding; the retry and cancellation cases expose the original contributor bootstrap defects. Regression execution is delegated to PR CI; no local red/green run is claimed.
- Updated the synthetic Gateway roster responses used by Android lifecycle, appearance, UI, and Wear tests without weakening their original assertions or timeouts.
- Static Kotlin formatting and lint use the repository-pinned ktlint 1.8.0 and Android `.editorconfig`; documentation formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Contributor Gradle/build/test code was not executed locally.
- Live Gateway/Android e2e and upgrade proof were skipped per maintainer policy. PR CI is the broad gate, including both Android test flavors.
- Independent P0–P2 autoreview completed with no accepted findings. Its one omitted-catalog finding was rejected after checking `replaceGatewayMethods(hello.methods)`: the existing owner marks the connection present even when the optional catalog is null. The incremental repair autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2; the final matching Wear fixture update also received independent source review. Exact-head [CI 40139347410](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139347410) is green at `571716ebe65d7b069e4df311d574c05c99d599ea`, including both Android test flavors and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- Change versus integrated main: production +97/−46, tests +227/−23, docs +5/−2. Local test timing is unavailable because contributor code was not executed; hosted timings remain in CI.

The rewrite removes the new epoch/backoff machinery. Necessary production growth covers readiness, visible discovery failures, and the Chat transport hold; no Gateway, protocol, config, or persistence schema changes.

The first maintainer-head CI run ([40134316442](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40134316442)) reached the Android job limit after fixture readiness failures: those synthetic Gateways returned `{}` or unsupported-method for the newly required discovery request. The repair gives those fixtures their existing `main` roster and preserves every assertion. This was PR-caused fixture fallout, not an inherited failure; no blind rerun or timeout increase was used. The discovery hold also uses the existing not-enqueued error classification so unsent messages remain queued.

ClawSweeper reviewed the complete Android rewrite at `1d7692c379c2e775bfb6ac47755eb427f5d4784e` with zero code findings and confirmed the prior P2s resolved. Its remaining live-proof-only hold is superseded by the maintainer validation policy above.

The second run ([40137760546](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40137760546)) completed with Play **3,583 passed / 1 failed** and third-party **3,715 passed / 1 failed**. The remaining notification-reply failures exposed an initial-discovery ordering bug: selecting a conversation after socket admission retired the pending roster result, leaving startup incomplete. Initial discovery now completes while the existing binding owner preserves the selected conversation; ordinary later refreshes still reject stale selection results. The held-roster regression would fail on `94efb23e6897` at its Connected assertion because that head discards the initial roster; it covers this path, and the unchanged notification tests remain the receiving proof. This incremental repair passed static lint and scoped-clean P0–P2 autoreview.
