prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid startup restart loops while Tailscale needs login
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A supervised Gateway can repeatedly fail startup while Tailscale needs login or machine approval. Restarting the Gateway cannot satisfy that operator prerequisite.

Related: #167072

## User Impact

After a supervised Tailscale Serve startup fails, the Gateway finishes cleanup and waits without listeners. It tells the operator to sign in or approve the node. Once Tailscale reports Running, it attempts normal startup once. The Serve claim and Gateway readiness checks must still pass before service starts.

Foreground startup, Funnel, unknown failures and route conflicts retain their existing failure behavior. The change does not sign in to Tailscale, modify routes, or change Gateway authentication.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Gateway run loop owns recovery. A typed error identifies the missing Tailscale prerequisite. Status checks use increasing intervals capped at 30 seconds. Shutdown cancels the wait and waits for its cleanup. A completed authentication-prerequisite failure does not count toward the crash-loop breaker. Other startup failures and unfinished boots still count.

Recovery restores transport availability. Gateway authentication and personal-identity rules continue to govern access.

## Evidence

### Current revision: duplicate-test cleanup, October 24

Head [`daeb4f01344bcf3bd46762270a7706693b24ca41`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/daeb4f01344bcf3bd46762270a7706693b24ca41) appends one test-only commit to `943f572bf15eb8c9125f9c23cac5be0c6530b995`. It removes exactly 26 lines: the helper-only second-failure preservation test and its now-unused local setup, as requested by the completed ClawSweeper review. Both immediately following production `runGatewayLoop` distinct-failure drain-path cases remain, along with additional-error, undefined-rejection, cancellation and cleanup coverage. Fresh native P0–P3 review on candidate tree `4ff06c4e4274cb0d0a27ddb7cebfd5029628e2da` was scoped-clean with no findings and confirmed the stronger retained owner coverage. The published tree matches exactly, the commit parent is `943f572`, and the required human coauthor credit is retained.

The earlier source/review/runtime/CI evidence below retains its actual head. In particular, the current ClawSweeper assessment reviewed `943f572`, not this deletion-only successor; no duplicate re-review request was sent. The scratch integration preparation also remains pinned to `943f572` and main `f7e2eed98468b80ed091cf5ed4a7554aaf00c8ef`; its helper-removal hunk is already incorporated by this successor, so the old patch must not be blindly replayed. No main integration was published. Merge conflicts, broad merge-ref CI, Core waiting-policy acceptance, authenticated restoration and latest-stable upgrade/platform proof remain outstanding.

### Published repairs, October 24

Earlier published head [`943f572bf15eb8c9125f9c23cac5be0c6530b995`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/943f572bf15eb8c9125f9c23cac5be0c6530b995) appends to original head `2ca59ca9e667907432836f290e9288d1058bd728`, preserving history and contributor credit. ### Previous revision, October 21

Previous head was [`2ca59ca9e667907432836f290e9288d1058bd728`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2ca59ca9e667907432836f290e9288d1058bd728), including main `2ad4d4c` through ordinary merges. The evidence below is historical and retains its tested revisions. It does not establish current-head CI or installed-runtime success.

On its parent `74007b`, the canonical type/lint gates and the recovery run-loop tests passed, including joined cancellation and listener-free parked retry. That partial result is not a full current-head CI pass.

prs.title: perf(sessions): lazily wrap catalog entry snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Catalog snapshot rebuilds create a frozen per-agent wrapper for every session and then copy each wrapper into a second catalog row, even when providers only request the catalog.

## User Impact

This is a small allocation and retained-memory win for catalog rebuilds, with no user-visible or Plugin SDK behavior change. Unchanged-revision requests remain effectively flat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the selected entry pairs in the existing revision-owned snapshot, construct catalog rows directly, and create per-agent wrappers only when a caller requests them. Lookup indexes also consume the captured pairs. Both public row shapes, all freezes, ordering, alias normalization, revision invalidation, and entries captured before provider awaits are preserved.

Production code grows by 13 lines (+26/-13) to preserve the distinct public shapes while removing their eager double wrapping; the regression adds 44 test lines. There is no new cache or configuration.

## Evidence

A synthetic isolated Gateway with 10,000 sessions and four clients observed **4.15 catalog requests/minute and 0.92 snapshot rebuilds/minute**: 18 requests over 260 seconds, 4 rebuilds and 14 revision-cache hits (77.8%). The mix used two sidebar refreshers at 120 seconds, navigation every 30 seconds, roster reads every 5 seconds, and an active phase with a metadata patch every 10 seconds. Initial request bursts are included. Baseline and candidate produced the same counts and expected responses. This is a synthetic traffic census, not a production request-rate measurement.

Two concurrent, CPU-swapped pairs per allocation mode, 1,000 requests per side, 10,000 persisted synthetic sessions:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Catalog allocation per rebuild | 5.786 MB | 4.252 MB | -26.5% |
| Retained sampled snapshot | 2.239 MB | 1.494 MB | -33.3% |
| Catalog allocation per unchanged request | 0.4267 MB | 0.4239 MB | -0.65% |

MB is decimal. Retained values are sampling estimates after collection, not exact heap dominator sizes. The rebuild allocation pairs improved 26.39% and 26.63%; unchanged pairs were -1.31% and +0.01%. Applying the rebuild saving to the synthetic census gives approximately 1.42 MB/minute, an extrapolation rather than measured production savings. Further reductions in revision churn would reduce the absolute benefit.

Allocation and real-Gateway census evidence came from the original experiment on `3729046a10db`. The restored implementation was rebased for the current correctness and untraced checks; both baseline and candidate snapshot-owner files are byte-identical to their original experimental versions. The final patch-identical rebase is covered by exact-head PR CI. Exploratory measurement scripts extended the existing `scripts/perf/session-catalog-selection-measure.ts` workload locally for 10,000 sessions and catalog-only providers. All six allocation/survivor pairs preserved full ordered-entry and response hashes. Maintenance remained enabled; preparation and measurement used separate CPU placements, exclusive quiet-slot locking, synchronized starts, and the shared production guard.

**Untraced CPU/GC qualification passed.** Two synchronized, CPU-swapped pairs each for rebuilds and unchanged reads, 1,000 requests per side, on base `0a3d2dc31216`. Mean paired CPU deltas were **-20.26% / -1.968 ms per rebuild** and **-5.90% / -0.0491 ms per unchanged request**. GC signs were mixed; the positive individual deltas were only +0.001716 and +0.000134 ms/request, below the predeclared +1 ms/op materiality gate. These short runs show no adverse GC result, not a robust GC improvement. Handler and loop tail means improved, with 1,000 handler samples and 1,341–2,626 loop samples per side. The largest candidate GC pause was 30.245 ms, below the maximum-pause safeguard. All four pairs preserved complete response and entry hashes, with no guard interruptions.

Each rebuild side recorded exactly 1,000 rebuilds and zero revision-cache hits; each unchanged side recorded zero rebuilds and 1,000 hits. No allocation inspector or GC tracing was enabled. Per-kind GC tails are context only because collection counts are insufficient; promotion was not measured. Windows lasted 1.73–9.07 seconds, so this requested short safety screen does not qualify rare long-run pauses.

Validation: 15 focused tests passed across `session-catalog-entry-snapshot.test.ts`, `session-catalog-selection.test.ts`, and `session-catalog-resident-entries.test.ts`. The new work-count regression failed on the original baseline (two wrappers instead of one), and checks lazy wrapping, exact public fields, freezes, same-revision reuse, and old-entry isolation after a projection update. Changed-file oxfmt and core-config oxlint passed; exact-head [PR CI run 40140075706](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40140075706) passed on `1aab639b21b7067b35cf5e6d39aab2e5346aab7b`, including lint, production/test types, changed-node tests, architecture/boundary guards, UI e2e, and the aggregate CI gate. Dependency and security-sensitive statuses also passed.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean through P2. The configured autoreview helper refused a provider mismatch; operator configuration was left unchanged. The reviewer independently checked retained-pair lifetime, both public shapes, alias/order preservation, revision reuse, lookup behavior, and isolation across awaits. The simplification pass retained only the two-shape lazy wrapping change.

prs.title: perf(diagnostics-prometheus): reuse unchanged series bytes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large Prometheus scrapes repeatedly spend CPU rendering metric series that have not changed.

## User Impact

CPU per scrape improves 64.42% and HTTP p99 improves 21.97%, with byte-identical exposition. The promotion increase is real (four matched A/A controls are clean), but its absolute magnitude is approximately 9 KB per scrape; retained heap plus array-buffer memory increases 2.63 MiB. The maintainer accepts these small, expected costs of reused render state in exchange for the large CPU/latency improvement. This is an explicit acceptance of the absolute cost, not a claim that the measured increase is noise.

The rendered blocks remain live across scrapes so unchanged series do not need formatting again. Keeping that reusable state alive explains the retention and associated promotion tradeoff; the trace totals are not a per-object attribution of every promoted byte. A separate 1,000-scrape churn proof now verifies that retained cache state tracks current series and current serialized bytes, and removal/reset releases it. Details are below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prometheus scrapes repeatedly sort admitted series and reformat unchanged values. This candidate keeps writer-invalidated rendered blocks, sorts only when membership changes, and uses private scratch storage to format changed series. Equal-length refreshes refill an existing block; different lengths get an exact-size replacement. Each response retains its own backing buffer so successful HTTP completion can detach it safely. Removal/reset releases cached series.

The change builds on #182804 and replaces the previous fragment renderer. Production LOC: +38. The growth implements incremental reuse, invalidation, and the independent-response contract. Retention increases by approximately one scrape of cached bytes plus scratch capacity; it is reported separately below. Equal-length refreshes refill existing arrays. The extra retained state serves current series; it is not a second unbounded history of prior scrapes. The churn/removal proof below verifies that lifecycle directly.

## Evidence

- Base work-count regression reproduces 3 redundant floating-point formatting calls; candidate performs 0 on unchanged interleaved stores.
- Store/service/HTTP-scope focused tests: 33 passed. Revised owner tests: 6/6, including equal-length/growing/shrinking numbers, histogram digit transitions, older response stability, response detachment, UTF-8, admission/drop limits, removal/reset, and unrelated Buffer slab lifetime.
- Changed-file formatting/lint and targeted plugin typecheck passed.
- Synthetic dist-Gateway confirmation: 10,000 seeded sessions, 8,000 settled runs, 40 active plugins (38 synthetic fixtures plus two bundled plugins), 12 archived dashboards, four completed mock-provider turns with persisted replies, expected unauthenticated 401, and 20 correct authenticated scrapes. Maintenance remained enabled. Revised-run median 2.41 ms/max 6.47 ms and 985,637-byte output are functional context only. The previously successful full core build was reused with a fresh native narrow build of the changed plugin; this is not a whole-Gateway paired performance claim.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0–P2 findings, including the allocator integration and equal-length refill revision. Current-head automated code review also reports no findings.
- CI [40141397307](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40141397307) succeeded on exact rebased head `51968d07ea490707e113fc22992f58da018c5e15`; the combined CI/security requirement passed. Current-head automated code review and the refreshed ClawSweeper review have no actionable findings.

## Measurement protocol and acceptance

Baseline `d147fa35ba33` from #182804; candidate source identical to published `7b82af10132e`. The owner, formatting, family budget, HTTP service, and committed workload sources were unchanged across the final rebase onto main. Both benchmark bundles used the same committed harness and canonical helper implementations.

Workload: `extensions/diagnostics-prometheus/src/metric-store.benchmark.test-support.ts` with `benchmarks/render-shape-2026-10-23.json`: 2,982 synthetic series / 38,779 sample rows, 100 rotating existing-series updates per request. Per side: 1,000 untraced HTTP requests plus a separate 200-request heap-sampling phase. Two concurrent pairs swap interleaved 16-CPU placements and counterbalance launch order, with synchronized warm starts. Promotion uses two separate traced pairs with the same workload and its own baseline. Four additional baseline/baseline traced A/A controls use the same protocol. The shared guard remained enabled and did not interrupt any measured pair. No pauses were trimmed, windows discarded, or results normalized by collection count.

Rerun the committed workload using `--http-only --flush-headers --http-port <distinct-port> --shape <shape-path> --updates-per-render 100 --render-samples 1000 --allocation-renders 200 --phase-ms 30000 --start-at <shared-future-epoch-ms> --output <result.json>`, with Node `--expose-gc`; add `--trace-gc-nvp` only for the separate promotion passes. These runs used bundled copies of that source. Compare initial, escaped, and final exposition files outside timing. All such byte comparisons passed in every pair, with equal aggregate received bytes.

Predeclared acceptance: byte equivalence, consistent approximately 5% or greater CPU/allocation improvement, and no material adverse controlled metrics. Total-GC timing changes below +1 ms/op and sub-ms tails are context when CPU/allocation improves at least 10%. Percentile sample thresholds remain in force. Promotion retains its threshold: adverse mean at least 20%, or at least 10% adverse in both swapped pairs; matched A/A controls are required before rejection. The maintainer has explicitly superseded the relative promotion rejection for this candidate after reviewing its absolute cost, CPU/latency improvement, and expected retained reuse state. Raw results and controls remain unchanged below.

## Untraced timing and allocation

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate | Absolute paired mean delta | Mean paired relative delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CPU ms/op | 3.504998 → 1.077283 | 4.302859 → 1.739538 | −2.495518 | −64.42% |
| Total GC ms/op | 0.035216 → 0.027287 | 0.030850 → 0.032261 | −0.003258 | −8.97% |
| Sampled heap B/op | 379,304.60 → 387,782.96 | 386,215.56 → 391,623.60 | +6,943.20 | +1.82% |
| HTTP p50 ms | 3.549473 → 1.145130 | 3.824385 → 1.411752 | −2.408488 | −65.41% |
| HTTP p95 ms | 4.647413 → 3.179577 | 7.051465 → 4.635254 | −1.942024 | −32.92% |
| HTTP p99 ms | 5.526112 → 4.313340 | 9.230067 → 7.199427 | −1.621706 | −21.97% |
| HTTP max ms | 7.994071 → 6.366555 | 12.073710 → 12.103355 | −0.798935 | −10.06% |
| Loop p95 ms | 4.198399 → 1.830911 | 6.840319 → 3.868671 | −2.669568 | −49.92% |
| Loop p99 ms | 5.742591 → 2.347007 | 9.027583 → 6.873087 | −2.775040 | −41.50% |
| Loop max ms | 7.966719 → 4.014079 | 11.755519 → 11.239423 | −2.234368 | context |

HTTP p95/p99 have 1,000 samples on both sides of both pairs. Event-loop sample counts are 1,079 → 1,263 and 1,107 → 1,158; both percentiles are eligible. All eligible latency and loop tails improve in both pairs. CPU declines by 69.26% and 59.57%. Sampled heap rises by 2.24% and 1.40%, below an adverse threshold; this remains a CPU optimization with a small measured heap-allocation tradeoff, not a rotating-workload allocation win.

Total GC has opposite-signed changes, so its small mean reduction is descriptive rather than a consistent improvement claim. Pair 2's +0.001412 ms/op increase is far below the +1 ms/op materiality threshold, and the signed mean is negative. It therefore does not gate under v5.6 and does not need a third pair under v5.2/v5.4. HTTP maximum's pair-2 change is +0.029645 ms, with a negative mean; it supplies no adverse tail gate.

## Untraced per-kind GC and both maxima

| Pair/kind | Count baseline → candidate | Total ms baseline → candidate | p95 ms baseline → candidate | p99 ms baseline → candidate | Maximum ms baseline → candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 minor | 223 → 76 | 33.866757 → 16.984287 | 0.237597 → 0.341283 | 0.346150 → 0.422084 | 0.706932 → 0.422084 |
| 1 major | 1 → 10 | 1.136958 → 8.556983 | 1.136958 → 1.366823 | 1.136958 → 1.366823 | 1.136958 → 1.366823 |
| 1 other | 1 → 10 | 0.211948 → 1.745893 | 0.211948 → 0.185238 | 0.211948 → 0.185238 | 0.211948 → 0.185238 |
| 2 minor | 250 → 72 | 29.646129 → 20.242585 | 0.179790 → 0.439340 | 0.217186 → 0.706982 | 0.305108 → 0.706982 |
| 2 major | 1 → 10 | 1.024279 → 10.121817 | 1.024279 → 1.419473 | 1.024279 → 1.419473 | 1.024279 → 1.419473 |
| 2 other | 1 → 10 | 0.179189 → 1.896919 | 0.179189 → 0.213150 | 0.179189 → 0.213150 | 0.179189 → 0.213150 |

Overall counts are 225 → 96 and 252 → 92. Overall maxima are **1.136958 → 1.366823 ms** and **1.024279 → 1.419473 ms**, both well below max(50 ms, 2× baseline maximum). Candidate minor counts are below 200 and major counts below 50; pause percentiles are context. All paired-mean per-kind pause-percentile increases are also below 1 ms, independently invoking v5.3. Major collection counts rise but are not a separate declared rejection criterion; aggregate GC time/work remains the applicable timing metric.

## Promotion: measured cost with clean controls

Raw Node 26 JSON traces were independently parsed with balanced start/end phase assertions, summing numeric promoted bytes for every in-phase GC event. Timing from these traced runs is context only.

| Traced phase | Pair 1 B/op baseline → candidate | Pair 2 B/op baseline → candidate | Absolute paired mean B/op | Mean paired relative delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Unprofiled HTTP, 1,000 ops/side | 949.416 → 10,235.896 | 1,349.168 → 10,071.744 | +9,004.528 | +812.32% |
| Allocation-profiled HTTP, 200 ops/side | 1,497.24 → 16,083.40 | 1,475.56 → 15,108.96 | +14,109.78 | +949.08% |

Unprofiled per-pair increases are +9,286.480 B/op (+978.13%) and +8,722.576 B/op (+646.52%). They agree in sign and baseline costs differ by only ~1.42×, so this is a real measured increase, not an inconclusive result. Baseline unprofiled trace collection counts are 28 minor / 0 major and 245 minor / 1 major; candidate counts are 73 minor / 9 major and 72 minor / 9 major. The first baseline's different natural GC cadence is retained as observed, not removed or normalized away. The separate allocation-profiled phases contain baseline 60/52 minor and no majors versus candidate 43 minor plus 3 majors in each pair.

The four matched baseline A/A unprofiled promotion deltas were −0.349%, −0.569%, +5.609%, −4.953% (signed mean −2.916 B/op), with all profiled deltas within ±0.75%. Neither any individual pair nor either consecutive swapped-pair group trips a promotion gate. These controls establish that the promotion increase is real. The revision reduced absolute candidate promotion compared with the original implementation but leaves it far above baseline; The maintainer accepts this candidate-specific tradeoff on absolute magnitude; the measurements are not being relabeled as noise.

## Retained memory and host context

Responses still have exactly 3,389,076 useful bytes and exactly 3,389,076 backing bytes. Warmed array-buffer retention is 3,399,744 → 6,780,706 bytes in both pairs: **+3,380,962 bytes (~3.22 MiB)**. Mean warmed heapUsed is 7,473,768 → 6,848,528 bytes: −625,240 bytes. Heap plus array-buffer accounting rises **2,755,722 bytes (~2.63 MiB, +25.34%)**. External and arrayBuffers overlap and must not be summed together. After reset, arrayBuffers agree at 131,152 bytes. The cache has a retained-memory cost despite preserving exact response ownership.

CPU64–95 sampled mean idle during whole captured windows is 94.83% / 94.67% for untraced pairs and 80.05% / 93.06% for traced pairs. These windows include phase waits and are context only; they do not invalidate runs. The lower traced pair-1 idle is reported without post-hoc exclusion.


## Current-main and bounded-retention verification

Rebased onto main `6c33f5ff5ee0b7d438238edfdebb2762acd72503`; current head `51968d07ea490707e113fc22992f58da018c5e15`. The #182804 squash commit `6e5465a1c3a3bdebc5219c92508569f6de75d9ca` is an ancestor. The metric store, formatter, family budget, HTTP service, and committed benchmark sources are byte-identical to the previously measured candidate. All 33 focused store/service/HTTP-scope tests pass after rebase; the final pre-push main refresh leaves the entire plugin directory unchanged. New-head CI and applicable security review requirements passed. The retained-object proof passed on this current source, and its saved snapshot summaries were independently checked.

The proof uses the committed representative family/bucket shape (1,462 histograms, 961 counters, 559 gauges), with fixed-width synthetic generation labels and primed numeric widths to separate leaks from legitimate output-length changes. It performs 1,000 scrapes, 100 rotating updates per scrape, and a complete 559-gauge replacement every 25 scrapes (40 replacements), without any reset inside the window. Responses are detached after consumption. This is a lifetime proof, not a new latency benchmark; its extra labels explain the different byte total from the performance fixture.

V8 heap snapshots enumerate actual sample→rendered-array→ArrayBuffer backing objects. They also census every Uint8Array in the process and track heap identities. No production hook or test seam was added.

| Checkpoint | Live cache arrays | Cache backing bytes | All Uint8Array objects |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial | 2,982 | 4,642,941 | 2,990 |
| Scrapes 100, 250, 500, 750, 1,000 (each) | 2,982 | 4,642,941 | 2,990 |
| All gauges removed | 2,423 | 4,584,535 | 2,431 |
| Reset | 0 | 0 | 8 |
| Refilled | 2,982 | 4,642,941 | 2,990 |
| Final reset | 0 | 0 | 8 |

Cache bytes equal current emitted sample bytes at every checkpoint. No obsolete gauge cohort sample or previously observed retired cache array remains reachable; total typed-array population tracks live cache count plus a constant eight other objects. All 2,423 persistent histogram/counter cache arrays retain their identities throughout the window. Clearing gauges removes all 559 gauge caches. Reset removes every sample cache.

Scratch remains 6,848 bytes and the current private prefix chunk remains 4,096 bytes through the window and gauge removal; these are fixed exporter workspace. Both become zero bytes after reset and return to the same bounds after refill. There is one exporter workspace in every snapshot. The memory bound is current series × their current bucket/label/number byte sizes, plus scratch high-water capacity until reset—not an unlimited history of scrapes. Cardinality alone does not cap arbitrary-sized input strings.

The proof, full typed-array census, historical identities, and workspace release were checked against all ten saved snapshots. This establishes the bounded reuse lifetime requested for landing. It supports the expected lifetime cost of keeping render state alive, while aggregate GC traces do not identify every promoted object's V8 path.

prs.title: fix(gateway): apply reloaded config to new native approvals
prs.body:
Closes #138552
Related: #138112

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes new native approval cards continuing to use the startup origin and forwarding accounts after a Gateway configuration hot reload.

## User Impact

New approvals use the applied public origin and exec/plugin forwarding accounts. An approval already being delivered keeps its admitted configuration through resolution and cleanup. Standalone handlers keep their explicitly supplied configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

On the refreshed main base, `src/infra/approval-handler-runtime.ts:435` captures `params.cfg` for the lifetime of a retained handler; `src/infra/approval-native-runtime.ts:120` and `:203` also classify and plan delivery with startup config. These paths outlive hot application of `gateway.publicOrigin` and `approvals.exec`/`approvals.plugin`.

The Gateway instance exposes its existing configuration owner to native approval handlers. Each handler captures that owner once and uses one configuration snapshot per request for eligibility, route classification, presentation, delivery planning, transport, and cleanup. The snapshot follows the stable request payload across normalization. Existing authority and scoped-reviewer checks stay in their owning paths. No public SDK option, config setting, retry generation, or extra runtime owner is added. The existing channel-manager approval fixture moves unchanged into its shared test-support owner so the oversized consumer file shrinks.

## Evidence

The exec and plugin forwarding regressions failed on base `7c727c540b4927008f085075f43481bec18ce468`: both delivered to the old `first` account instead of the expected `second` account. Both pass with the fix. The standalone explicit-config case also passes.

Two additional cases retain a handler, apply config B before admission, then apply C while presentation waits. Both pass and verify that the delivered origin, delivery plan, and finalization keep config B. The Gateway-instance getter test passes and verifies config replacement and rejection after instance closure. All six new behavioral cases pass across the focused runs.

Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace validation, and two independent Codex reviews passed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Production delta is +50/−18 lines; tests +276/−6; docs +5/−0. The final snapshot file took 139.92 seconds wall time (1.299 seconds of test execution); the selected Gateway getter file took 798.08 seconds (53 ms of test execution), dominated by module transformation/loading on the shared host. The combined final command exited 0 after 997.15 seconds wall time. Exact-head PR CI provides the broad check: [run 40082935315](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40082935315).

No live Gateway, Telegram, model, or network proof was run, per the phase-1 scope of focused local regressions and PR CI. Native Telegram forwarding and the system-agent Review URL were not live-tested.

ClawSweeper's [exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138553#issuecomment-5545709920) reports zero code findings and retains a security/live-proof hold for Telegram delivery and reviewer revocation. Source inspection confirms that resolution prepares reviewer custody from current Gateway config (`src/gateway/server-methods/approval-shared.ts:520`) and rechecks it in the final commit guard (`:613-629`); the unified approval path does the same (`src/gateway/server-methods/approval.ts:344-419`). Those owners are unchanged by this patch. The delivery snapshot does not replace their current authority checks. This is source evidence, not the requested live proof; the remaining hold is explicitly preserved for the maintainer's land decision.

prs.body:
Closes #180719

## What Problem This Solves

Codex rejects OpenClaw's default managed proxy environment before preparing the ChatGPT subscription relay.

## User Impact

The existing `gateway-only` proxy defaults work with Codex subscription sharing. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Accept the exact `localhost.` and `127.0.0.0/8` loopback entries already emitted by the managed proxy. The existing proxy-selection and trust checks remain in place. The regression crosses the real proxy producer and Codex relay-preparation boundary through the plugin's lazy test API.

Thanks to @indra622 (Hosung Park) for the fix and original evidence.

## Evidence

- On base `90d9772045f98`, the host regression fails at `ownCodexInferenceClient` for `gateway-only`, while the incompatible `proxy` and `block` controls pass. With this fix, all three pass; the routing suite also passes, for 49 focused tests total. The direct qualification reproduction likewise changes from `managed false` to `managed true`.
- The integration test verifies relay preparation, ownership revocation, and restoration of the original proxy environment. Targeted type-aware oxlint and formatting pass. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- After merging main `8c6ad0edc3c9`, the same 49 tests pass (418.17 s wrapper time on the loaded host). Changed-file validation passes every other check, including typechecks, targeted lint, import cycles, and 10 doctor boundary tests. Its broad unused-export scans report 1,136 script, 69 production, and 83 full-tree findings across 102 files; none is in this PR, and all 102 files are byte-identical to that main revision. prs.title: fix(setup): preserve the current model when activating saved auth
prs.body:
Related to #167381

## What Problem This Solves

Activating a previously saved auth profile failed with `The candidate route does not match the selected model` when the saved credential's starter model differed from the current agent model. The activation path staged the stored starter model instead of the model the agent was already using, so route verification rejected the candidate. If the models happened to match, activation could also overwrite the user's current model with the starter model. Discovery had the same mismatch: Model Setup forwards the discovered candidate model explicitly, so fixing activation alone was bypassed by the normal UI flow. Provider-qualified aliases such as `openai/Fast` must also be resolved to their canonical model identity or the same route check rejects a valid current model.

## Why This Change Was Made

Saved-auth discovery and `stageSavedAuthCandidate` now share the same model-selection decision:

1. An explicitly supplied `modelRef`.
2. The canonical current agent route model, when it belongs to the same provider as the saved credential.
3. The saved credential's stored model, preserving the existing cross-provider fallback.

Both paths call `resolveCurrentModelRefForSavedAuth`, which uses the existing setup route resolver. Configured aliases therefore resolve to the same concrete model identity used by the model-selection updater, and discovery advertises that canonical current model to Model Setup. The trailing auth-profile suffix is removed before comparing providers. API-key header configuration is applied to the provider of the resolved model rather than always using the saved starter model's provider. Credential and auth-profile binding behavior is unchanged.

The saved-auth route lookup is also scoped to the setup target. Previously it always resolved the primary route and cached by provider alone, so a credential chosen for the utility target could advertise the primary model and ordinary activation could promote a utility-only model to primary. Discovery and `stageSavedAuthCandidate` now pass `modelTarget` (`primary` or `utility`) into the shared resolver, and the discovery cache is keyed by provider plus target. A utility-only configuration therefore keeps its utility model while saved-auth activation still persists the selected starter model as primary.

## User Impact

Users can switch back to a saved sign-in without a spurious route mismatch, and activation no longer resets their current model to the provider's starter model. Cross-provider saved credentials retain the previous fallback behavior.

## Evidence

- Full target suites on the final head: `43 passed` across `setup-inference-activate.test.ts` and `setup-inference-saved-model.test.ts`, including both `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and the configured `openai/Fast` alias; `19 passed` in `setup-inference-detect.test.ts`.
- Discovery-to-activation regression: both cases call `setup.detect()`, assert the saved-auth candidate advertises the canonical current model, activate that candidate as Model Setup does, and verify the persisted model and inference call.
- Discovery base-red: with the previous discovery selection restored, both cases advertise `openai/starter-model` and fail before activation.
- Role-isolation regression: with only `agents.defaults.utilityModel` configured, detection advertises the saved starter model and activation persists that model as primary while leaving `utilityModel` unchanged.
- Type-safety hardening: the API-key header target uses the resolved model provider when a model is present and otherwise falls back to the saved provider, so `parseInferenceRef` never receives an optional model reference. The final-head model regressions pass (`2 passed | 40 skipped`).
- Formatting and lint: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` passed for all changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- Logs: `180832-final.log` (43 + 19 passed) under `contributions/pr-evidence-20261025/180832/` in the contributor workspace. Earlier logs remain under `contributions/pr-evidence-20261023/`, and the upgrade readback files are under `180832-live-proof/upgrade-20261023e/`.

### Real CLI behavior proof

On 2026-10-23 I exercised the shipped `openclaw` CLI in an isolated state directory against a local loopback OpenAI Responses provider. The state had an active `openai:baseline` credential and a saved replacement `openai:saved-proof` credential whose recorded model was `openai/starter-model`; the current agent model was `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`.

- A baseline `openclaw agent --local` turn authenticated with the baseline credential and returned `LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_1` on `gpt-5.4-mini`.
- `openclaw models auth activate openai:saved-proof --agent main` printed `Inference verified: openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and `Sign-in verified and saved.` It authenticated the probe with the saved credential, not the baseline credential.
- A subsequent `openclaw agent --local` turn returned `LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_3` from `gpt-5.4-mini` and used the saved credential.
- Persisted config after activation: `agents.defaults.model.primary` remained `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, while `agents.entries.main.model` became `openai/gpt-5.4-mini@openai:saved-proof`.
- The saved profile remained present in the migrated auth store with its original key; only its consumed setup marker was cleared.

Provider-side request sequence, with keys redacted:

```text
baseline warmup   Bearer <baseline>  gpt-5.4-mini     LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_1
activation probe  Bearer <saved>     gpt-5.4-mini     LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_2
follow-up turn    Bearer <saved>     gpt-5.4-mini     LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_3
```

The discriminating latest-stable run used the published `openclaw@2026.10.6` package with the same fixture. It activated the saved credential as `openai/starter-model` and persisted `agents.entries.main.model = openai/starter-model@openai:saved-proof`, reproducing the reported drift. The head above instead persisted `openai/gpt-5.4-mini@openai:saved-proof`.

### Existing-state compatibility

The fixture initially used the legacy `auth-profiles.json` layout. The reviewed head's `doctor --fix` migrated it to the current state SQLite database, retained both profile IDs and credentials, and the CLI listed and activated both afterwards. This PR adds no persisted-format change.

### Latest-stable upgrade readback

The readback was verified on `a8b7787e`, rebased onto current `main` (reports `2026.10.6`). The branch was then rebased once more to `e3d624de` solely to pick up upstream `82c46546`, a test-fixture typecheck fix; the source diff is unchanged. I seeded an isolated state with the published `openclaw@2026.10.6` (fe06181) package: its `doctor --fix` migrated the legacy store and stamped `meta.lastTouchedVersion=2026.10.6` with schema v20, and one baseline turn ran against that state (`LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_1`, baseline credential, `gpt-5.4-mini`).

The candidate head then opened the same state. Its `doctor --fix` advanced schema v20 -> v31 and retained pre-migration SQLite backups. `models auth activate openai:saved-proof --agent main` printed `Inference verified: openai/gpt-5.4-mini` and `Sign-in verified and saved.` with no downgrade-guard warning. The follow-up turn returned `LIVE_PROOF_REPLY_3` on `gpt-5.4-mini` using the saved credential. After the upgrade, `agents.defaults.model.primary` remained `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, and only `agents.entries.main.model` became `openai/gpt-5.4-mini@openai:saved-proof`.

Machine-checkable result: `upgrade-20261023e/upgrade-verification.json` (13/13 checks), with logs in `upgrade-20261023e/` under `contributions/pr-evidence-20261023/`.

Command:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts \

```

`tsgo` could not be run on this host because the available glibc is older than the installed TypeScript native binary requires, so this PR does not claim a local typecheck result.

## CI note

`check-test-types-core-1` failed only in `src/hooks/loader.cache-invalidation.test.ts` (`managedHooksDir`), which this PR does not touch; it is a pre-existing failure on `main` already fixed by upstream `82c46546`. The final rebase includes that fix.

prs.title: perf(runtime): reduce idle worker GC profiler churn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workers with active GC telemetry restart Node's native GC profiler ten times per second, including while idle. Each restart creates another native profiler whose cleanup depends on garbage collection.

## User Impact

Worker GC diagnostics now batch once per second, matching the main thread. Collection counts, durations, reclaimed bytes, attribution, and the Code Mode safety subscriber keep their existing meanings. Worker notifications can arrive up to 900 ms later; orderly retirement still explicitly flushes pending records within its existing best-effort deadline. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing sampler owner and retirement flush to remove nine scheduled stop/start cycles per second per subscribed worker. Ordinary worker subscriptions already follow live telemetry demand, so disabling more profilers would discard useful metrics. Creating a fresh public profiler each cycle does not avoid Node's native restart lifecycle. Production LOC delta: −1.

## Evidence

- The extended existing worker-port regression fails on the base because a periodic batch is delivered before 900 ms. It passes with this change and still proves final flushing without duplicate collection counts.
- Focused diagnostics/worker-retirement tests: 2 files passed; Code Mode GC contract: 1 file passed. Changed diagnostic file: 8 tests, 3.65 s runner duration on the green run. Targeted core typecheck, changed-file lint/format and diff checks passed. PR CI run 40140433409 passed all 62 jobs on head `607c17d13da5f681527e71bb3de1c6b208985a5f`. No retry was used.
- Node 26.12.1 with jemalloc 5.3.0: 10,000-cycle worker diagnostics, five fresh-process runs per mode, comparing one public instance, a fresh instance per cycle, and no profiler. Both profiler variants incur native restart churn; fresh wrappers do not provide a lifecycle fix.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings. The configured helper refused its provider route; no operator configuration was changed.
- Real-worker queued-batch proof: 24 cases across baseline/candidate and 1, 25, 100, or 500 major collections. Periodic timers could not drain the batch first; all requested majors were delivered. Candidate maximum native drain 22.06 ms and signal-to-return 24.10 ms; baseline 54.93/57.13 ms. Both fit the unchanged 100 ms retirement budget. Forced GC was used only in this isolated diagnostic, outside Gateway measurement windows.
- Built Gateway on Node 26.12.1/jemalloc 5.3.0: two counterbalanced sequential comparison pairs, 10,000 synthetic sessions, 40 synthetic external plugins, 40 compressed clients, 60 s warmup and 180 s windows. All four runs completed 144 turns. Profiling/tracing and forced collection were disabled in these windows; identical thin instrumentation collected native stats and sampler counts. The generated fixture was reused with the benchmark's session resets. This is an isolated shared-Linux-host comparison, not production attribution.

| Metric | Baseline → candidate, pair 1 | Baseline → candidate, pair 2 | Mean paired change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Process CPU / turn | 1344.4 → 1278.1 ms | 1338.8 → 1283.3 ms | **−4.5%** |
| Native profiler starts / second | 599.9 → 60.6 | 593.7 → 60.9 | **−89.8%** |
| Native allocated, warm mean | 651.9 → 667.6 MiB | 658.0 → 661.0 MiB | +9.4 MiB (+1.4%) |
| Allocator resident, warm mean | 860.2 → 834.0 MiB | 816.3 → 805.1 MiB | −18.7 MiB (−2.2%) |
| Process RSS, warm mean | 3199.0 → 3173.4 MiB | 3254.9 → 3235.0 MiB | −22.8 MiB (−0.7%) |
| Native-reported GC time / minute | 2374.8 → 2100.8 ms | 2372.4 → 2121.9 ms | **−262.3 ms (−11.0%)** |
| Mean 30 s loop p99 | 47.00 → 47.70 ms | 44.66 → 44.49 ms | +0.26 ms (+0.6%) |
| Maximum loop delay | 137.10 → 121.90 ms | 103.02 → 89.78 ms | lower in both |

The win is less sampler churn and CPU, not a reduction in standing native allocation. Mean loop p95 changed −0.02 ms. Each reported loop window contains 1,308–1,365 samples (five windows per run); each memory mean has six samples. CPU fell consistently by about 4–5%, GC cost fell in both pairs, and the small native-memory increase is disclosed. No GC rejection or inconclusive-control exception was needed. JS allocation/promotion was not separately profiled.

<details>
<summary>GC counts, per-kind time and pause maxima</summary>

Counts and total times below cover the measured windows from periodically sampled cumulative counters. Maximum single pauses are conservative lifetime maxima including warmup; no pauses were trimmed. Columns are baseline 1 / candidate 1 / baseline 2 / candidate 2.

| Kind | Collections | Total ms | Max single pause ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scavenge | 1889 / 1911 / 1910 / 1846 | 3671.8 / 3664.2 / 3350.6 / 3327.8 | 26.57 / 50.87 / 13.04 / 15.34 |
| Major | 359 / 387 / 480 / 465 | 2352.4 / 2291.1 / 2685.5 / 2733.6 | 150.79 / 154.00 / 67.41 / 76.45 |
| Incremental | 356 / 382 / 462 / 443 | 1207.8 / 430.0 / 1199.7 / 426.7 | 23.76 / 9.46 / 22.07 / 5.98 |

GC pause percentiles were not collected. Neither candidate maximum exceeds the max(50 ms, twice baseline maximum) safeguard. Much of the measured GC reduction is incremental work; collection conversion and native-reported duration semantics remain unchanged.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): keep the attempt budget for runtime plugins without a monotonic start
prs.body:
Fixes #181619

## What Problem This Solves

After upgrading to 2026.10.6+, every Codex turn silently falls back to another model when the older 2026.10.5 `@openclaw/codex` runtime plugin is still installed. That plugin passes only `startedAtMs` to `createAgentHarnessAttemptDeadlineController`; since #155801 the host computes the execution deadline from `startedAtMonotonicMs`, which is `undefined`, so the remaining budget is `NaN`, the timer fires after 1 ms, and the attempt reports a timeout with `elapsedMs=null`.

## Solution

`startedAtMonotonicMs` becomes optional. When it is absent or non-finite, the controller anchors it once to the epoch admission time (`performance.now() - (Date.now() - startedAtMs)`). Current callers, which pass the monotonic start, are unchanged. The official runtime-plugin floor stays at 2026.9.7, so older plugins keep working instead of being marked unavailable; the fallback can be removed once that floor reaches 2026.10.6.

## Evidence

- New regression case in `src/agents/harness/attempt-deadlines.test.ts`: a caller that omits the monotonic start keeps its full 60 s budget (fails on main with an immediate timeout, passes with the fix).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/harness/attempt-deadlines.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 11 passed.
- Needed for the 2026.10.8 stable patch (same code and floor on the stable line).

prs.title: perf(agents): wake media completion waits from owner changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completion-required media tasks currently wake the waiting cron turn every 500 ms to reread process-local task state and its deadline. Replace that polling with notifications from the media operation and attempt deadline owners. Keep queued-delivery release, late task IDs, approval pause/resume, abort, and the existing 500 ms early timeout margin. No SQL, schema or public configuration changes.

## Acceptance rule — registered before the first run

Workload: `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-media-completion-wait.mts --samples 5`. Five sequential warm in-process synthetic image completions, each published after 1250 ms. Count deadline reads and main-thread timer creation during each wait. Baseline expected: 3 deadline reads / 4 timers including the completion stimulus; candidate: 1 read / 1 stimulus timer, zero periodic timer wakeups. No worker relocation. Any additional operation count or loss of completion, queued-delivery, late-ID, abort or timeout behavior is a regression.

Wall-clock/CPU comparison, if run: same owner workload, baseline/candidate interleaved ABAB with at least five each, cold and warm separate, campaign timing lock and one-minute load below 24. Report median/p95/range; any 20% worsening stops publication of the performance claim. A busy host is not evidence of latency parity. CPU profiles and deterministic fake-clock reaction tests supplement operation counts; neither is a real Gateway end-to-end latency measurement.

Real-flow acceptance, registered before its first run: `scripts/bench-media-completion-gateway.mts --out <new-fixture> --samples 5 --image-delay-ms 1250 --count-waits --cpu-profile --observer /path/to/frozen/observer.cjs`, against each exact-head source build. One cold and five warm scheduled image-generation turns use a real isolated Gateway WebSocket and loopback model/image provider. Each must finish successfully with one image request, a detached media tool result, and the synthetic final reply; record model requests, media-wait timers, SQL/worker requests/MAIN by phase, and per-thread CPU profiles. Candidate must remove periodic media-wait timers without increasing per-action model/image work or touched-owner SQL/requests. Counts/profiles on a loaded host support no latency claim. Separate uninstrumented ABAB timing runs need the campaign timing lock and load below 24; cold and warm remain separate, median/p95/range with no 20% regression accepted.

## Evidence

Head `6c3432d3d8eea5f78c689c35a1caf9a0f2a5a69c`; runtime implementation `57cd2c3532b`. Later commits repair only the synthetic workload and remove an unconsumed result-type export. The mapped baseline and candidate builds contain their respective wait implementations. Source-owner reproduction preceded implementation; the complete Gateway reproduction followed implementation after fixing fixture setup/routing issues, so it is not claimed as a pre-edit end-to-end reproduction.

Both real Gateway arms completed one cold plus five warm cron media turns, with one image request, three model requests, a detached tool result and the expected final response in every sample. Each sample uses an independent disabled cron job and provider marker because completion replies can outlive cron.run. No retry or settling sleep is added.

| Count per wait | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Owner workload: deadline reads, median/p95 [min–max], n=5 | 3/3 [3–3] | 1/1 [1–1] |
| Owner workload: periodic timers, median/p95 [min–max], n=5 | 3/3 [3–3] | 0/0 [0–0] |
| Gateway warm: media timer allocations, median/p95 [min–max], n=5 | 2/2 [2–2] polling | 1/1 [1–1] bounded deadline |
| Gateway cold: media timer allocations, n=1 | 3 polling | 1 bounded deadline |
| Image / model requests per Gateway sample | 1 / 3 | 1 / 3 |
| Observed warm SQL, median/p95 [min–max], n=5 | 502/629 [498–629] | 533/662 [399–662] |
| Observed warm worker requests, median/p95 [min–max], n=5 | 133/174 [131–174] | 144/179 [104–179] |
| Observed warm main-thread SQL | 0 | 0 |
| Observed whole workload SQL / requests / MAIN | 3949 / 977 / 66 | 3916 / 962 / 66 |

The source-owner completion stimulus timer remains one per sample in both arms. Gateway instrumentation counts allocations, not fired callbacks. The candidate removes the periodic path and retains one bounded timeout. No worker relocation occurs.

**Coordinator accepted the raw count shifts as phase placement (2026-10-24, exact head `6c3432d3d8e`).** Boot SQL moves 590→766 (+29.8%) while cold moves 697→432; warm-3 moves 502→631 SQL (+25.7%) and 133→168 requests (+26.3%). These cross the registered 20% stop threshold. Warm aggregate is 2633/705→2690/714 SQL/requests. Whole-run operation deltas are execute 2443→2420, entry-read 9→7, exact-entries 43→42, proactive jobs 33→30, identity evidence 22→20, unattributed 98→94, generic task 37→39 (session-count SELECT 13→15). Model-context and transcript-hydration totals are unchanged. Phase labels are execution windows and can include prior asynchronous completion replies; they do not prove per-turn causality. The coordinator attributes these shifts to earlier completion-reply visibility after replacing the 500 ms poll; the +2 session-count reads remain explicitly recorded. This accepts the raw-window changes, not a SQL or timing performance claim. No SQL reduction, latency parity or CPU speedup is claimed.

Frozen observer v3.1.4 hashes pass. CPU profiles cover Gateway main plus 41 baseline / 40 candidate worker threads; both include the actual media wait functions. The heartbeat worker clears its environment and therefore does not load the frozen SQL observer, but it is profiled. Bootstrap thread 1 is also profiled without SQL records. The SQL table is explicitly observed work, not an all-thread census. Heartbeat code is unchanged. Timing qualification exceeded 60 minutes without load below 24; these loaded-host instrumented runs establish counts and profile coverage only.

Validation: 131 focused owner/caller/prefix tests across 10 files pass with pinned Bun, including late IDs, queued delivery, deadline pause/resume, abort cleanup, timeout margin and settlement. Immediate-wakeup/count regressions fail on the base. Two Codex review rounds completed; the final round found only INDEX-only red preparatory tests without the implementation, resolved by the complete implementation commit. No other actionable working-tree finding. Basic lint/format/diff pass. Local type-aware tooling refuses the mandated external virtual store; CI owns those checks. prs.title: perf(gateway): prepare the default state root at startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Default-home Gateways repeatedly derive the same home and state paths during agent database admission. Startup normalized existing overrides but never prepared the implicit default root, bypassing the existing absolute-root and SQLite-path caches.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare the ordinary default root at the existing bootstrap boundary after config environment selection. Admission and other runtime consumers then use the existing path caches. Admission decisions remain live; standalone callers and tests with explicit environments remain independent. The early normalizer stays unchanged because trusted dotenv/config can still select a root there.

## User Impact

The pin applies only to unnamed default roots whose config directory already matches. Separate config roots and env-only named profiles retain their existing config precedence, dotenv selection, and socket defaults. Foreground child restarts inherit the selected default root; selecting a different root requires a fresh launch with that environment. Windows retains its existing path-resolution behavior.

Runtime production delta: **+9 lines**, required to preserve those public selection contracts at startup. No new cache, manager, schema, config option, hot-path branch, or compatibility reader. The requested non-test/non-doc filter totals +40 lines: runtime +9, measurement tooling +21, benchmark README +10. Existing test and benchmark files are extended; no new module/export/test file.

## Evidence

Owner probe: five samples of 20,000 reads per case.

| Metric | Home-selected root | Prepared root |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `path.resolve` calls / 20,000 reads | 40,000 | 0 |
| `path.join` calls / 20,000 reads | 20,000 | 0 |
| Sampled allocated bytes/read, mean | 1,194.71 | 71.91 |
| Time/read, median | 526.63 ns | 66.17 ns |

**Admission-site allocation falls 94%; median site time falls 87%.** These are site-level results, not whole-Gateway improvement claims.

Final built-Gateway proof compares main `4c3bf18daa6c2267aac8c0175d82ce0eed01b9c1` with candidate `0e7dbb9bd91d1449184492e7f4ea3df1e3a8f1a2` on the same base. Fresh synthetic fixtures have 10,000 sessions, 6,000 settled runs, 40 startup plugins plus a mock provider, isolated state and loopback ports. The generated config sits in the state root so the final eligibility guard is exercised. Both builds and all turns completed.

Separate allocation capture, five rounds/two turns each: the targeted path-resolution stack under `readAgentDatabaseAdmissionRefusal` has **328,080 sampled bytes on baseline → zero on candidate**. Admission itself remains sampled in the candidate, confirming the missing path frames are not caused by missing admission entirely. Promotion is 7,321,322 → 7,786,324 bytes/turn (+6.4%); this single traced pair is context. Traced maximum pauses are 4.58 → 37.88 ms, minor/major counts 27/0 → 47/2; traced GC timing is not a gate.

Untraced timing uses two counterbalanced serial pairs (ABBA), each 25 rounds/two turns = 50 turns per side. Work count was fixed before results; maintenance remained enabled and no samples were trimmed.

| Pair | CPU ms/turn, base → candidate | GC ms/turn, base → candidate | Max GC ms, base → candidate | Minor/major counts, base → candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 195.54 → 228.85 | 9.62 → 12.31 | 31.32 → 43.03 | 140/9 → 168/11 |
| 2 | 217.90 → 214.99 | 11.05 → 9.86 | 34.24 → 31.06 | 148/9 → 150/10 |

CPU paired deltas are +33.31 ms (+17.0%) and −2.91 ms (−1.3%); signed mean +15.20 ms/turn (+7.4%). GC deltas are +2.69 ms (+28.0%) and −1.19 ms (−10.7%); signed mean **+0.75 ms/turn (+7.3%)**, below the predeclared 1 ms/operation materiality floor. Neither metric is ≥10% worse in both pairs or ≥20% worse on the signed mean. All maximum pauses remain below 50 ms. Minor/major total GC milliseconds are 271.89/199.33 → 333.58/265.23 in pair 1 and 333.88/208.88 → 286.63/195.22 in pair 2; totals also include other collection kinds.

ACK sample counts are 50/side/run, and event-loop windows contain 109–156 observations. Their p95/p99 values cannot gate under the declared sample minima. Major collections are below 50/side/run. These are saturated-Mac local comparisons without CPU isolation, so there is **no whole-Gateway CPU, latency, or allocation improvement claim**. The strong site-level reduction and live removal of the target stack support the requested change; whole-Gateway measurements show no material paired gate violation.

Earlier live captures are superseded: the driver initially generated a split-root config and measured the original unconditional implementation, which the final compatibility guard intentionally excludes. That mismatch was discovered, documented, and the PR returned to draft before these fresh captures. Earlier short-window GC/control results are not used for the final decision.

## Correctness and review

The startup work-count regression fails on original main with 20 path resolutions for ten admission reads. Split-config and named-profile regressions fail on the initial unconditional PR implementation. The corrected `server-startup-minimal-boot.test.ts` passes all four cases (252.27 s): default-root admission work counts, separate config roots, named profiles, and two full starts.

Changed-file oxfmt, targeted core/test/scripts lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Baseline and candidate runtime builds pass; the existing CSS gzip budget warning is informational (296.4 KiB vs 296.3 KiB). No remote test lease was allocated. Broad validation belongs to PR CI.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): fresh reviewers inspected the diff and ownership contracts, corrected a Windows-only assertion, and confirmed no actionable P0–P2 findings. GitHub review identified split-config precedence; the correction preserves that and named-profile semantics, with red/green regressions and a fresh scoped-clean review. The final measurement-driver correction also received scoped-clean review. Operator review configuration was not changed.

The final pre-push rebase onto `76920c13a1f6` was conflict-free. The bootstrap/path owners and inherited-failure source files had no delta from the measured base; exact-head PR CI covers the updated base.

Reproduce the site probe:
`node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/state-path-resolution-measure.ts --iterations 20000 --rounds 5`

Built Gateway driver: `--default-state-dir --scenario chat.send --clients 1 --runs 2 --rounds 25 --chunks 4 --chunk-interval-ms 1 --round-interval-ms 1 --diagnostics`. Allocation capture uses `--rounds 5 --allocations`. Fixtures: `--sessions 10000 --runs 6000 --settled-runs --approvals 0 --cron 0 --projects 0 --transcript-mib 1`, with the existing synthetic plugin fixture helper.

## Prior-head CI attribution

Prior head `41cca7bb62cf0b3fe9e34fe5a325f4382c760e6f` had two failures in [run 40136422879](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136422879). Both were reproduced on unchanged main `4c3bf18daa6c2267aac8c0175d82ce0eed01b9c1`; no main source was edited and no CI rerun requested. Final-head CI remains authoritative for landing.

1. [Compact-small-2 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136422879/job/120999097164): `server-plugins.lifecycle.test.ts`, “keeps Gateway available after timeout cleanup refuses replacement,” expects `restartRequired: false`, gets `true`. Baseline command `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` reproduces the same assertion: one failed, three passed, 70.17 s. [#182403](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182403), commit `ae81c0703e7ca223cb671612e74834e414670a0c`, made explicit bundled reloads require restart; the sibling installed-package test correctly expects true. This fixture explicitly sets the state directory, skipping the new branch.

2. [PostgreSQL conformance 2/3 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136422879/job/120999097122): seven `interactive-setup.integration.test.ts` cases fail before PTY readiness because the synthetic source runtime lacks `standalone-runtime-profile.mjs`, imported by `packages/llm-core/src/validation.ts`. [#182856](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182856), commit `4a38dbdb6b1de4024abab8aca0ddc3c8cb0f9e73`, added that import; `createSourceRuntime` omits the root file from its copied fixture. The identical shared import failure reproduces on main with the single SQLite onboarding case: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/database-engine/interactive-setup.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'sqlite interactive setup.*onboard saves'` (one failed, seven filtered, 46.46 s; 138.65 s including required runtime build). It fails before bootstrap; this fixture also sets an explicit state override.

## Final-head CI evidence

On final head `3211cce3ee2158fbeefe97d6fa8668d629c15ee5`, [run 40139933686](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139933686) reproduces exactly the two inherited signatures above: [compact-small-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139933686/job/121009711526) has the same stale restart assertion; [PostgreSQL 2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139933686/job/121009711152) has the same seven missing-fixture import failures. The unchanged-main reproductions and source attribution above apply; those inputs did not change in the final rebase.

The final-head startup group passes all five files/26 tests, including all four changed default/split/profile/two-start cases. Production/test typechecks, lint, security checks, and the other completed test lanes pass. The body-validator failure was caused by renamed template headings; restoring the required headings passed [the replacement body check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40140381125/job/121010682071), with no code push or CI rerun.
