prs.title: refactor: deslop gateway, config and infra fixtures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Duplicated test setup across Gateway, configuration, infra, state and daemon tests makes fixture ownership harder to follow and leaves a few redundant internal operations behind.

Measured complete diff: **78 paths, +416/-920 = 504 net lines removed**, including **2 net production lines** (+1/-3 in source-file.ts). These are disjoint changed paths, including all three new test-support owners, not cumulative counts of predecessor packets. The workspace-projection fixture and its two changed-reachable production files were conservatively excluded after a timing-sensitive local failure; all three are unchanged from the base.

## User Impact

No feature, public API/config/protocol or persisted schema changes, and no required user action. Tests retain every scenario, assertion and registration. The only accepted runtime edge-case change is best-effort overlapping pre-refresh watch selection, described explicitly below; security/effect authority, common-path durability and write settlement remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each independent cut gives repeated fixture data or setup one owner without moving assertions into production or sharing state that was previously fresh. The only production simplification removes a pre-refresh watcher counter. The following sections separate their ownership and tradeoffs for review.

### Preservation and size by independent cut

For the original rows, assertion counts are direct `expect(...)` source calls; test counts are lexical callbacks, with custom setup/registration calls shown separately. W counts terminal expect/assert expressions instead; D separately records 144 direct expects and 294 rooted expression entries. T records direct expects plus Vitest assert calls. **These methods are not added into a single assertion total.** Parameterized rows, hook/mock signatures and complete assertion bytes are preserved; registration counts are not expanded runtime test counts. Rows with zero assertions/tests change production/support only, not tests.

| Cut | Net LOC | Assertions before→after | Tests / custom setup before→after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fixed session-store configuration | 59 | 479→479 | 152→152 / 18→18 |
| Model fixture defaults | 12 | 48→48 | 11→11 / 1→1 |
| Outbound target registry defaults | 7 | 15→15 | 7→7 / 0→0 |
| Scheduled-task spawn results | 21 | 10→10 | 1→1 / 0→0 |
| Eager test gates | 18 | 49→49 | 12→12 / 0→0 |
| Requester test gates | 12 | 33→33 | 10→10 / 1→1 |
| ACP startup metadata | 24 | 36→36 | 6→6 / 0→0 |
| Config promotion listeners | 16 | 89→89 | 12→12 / 3→3 |
| PostgreSQL bootstrap defaults | 13 | 126→126 | 27→27 / 1→1 |
| Pending-input history | 35 | 36→36 | 9→9 / 0→0 |
| Held migration locks | 18 | 325→325 | 52→52 / 0→0 |
| Avatar response bytes | 6 | 5→5 | 1→1 / 0→0 |
| Source watch selection | 2 | 0→0 | 0→0 / 0→0 |
| Package publication setup | 54 | 203→203 | 26→26 / 0→0 |
| Unused validation observer | 17 | 0→0 | 0→0 / 0→0 |
| Cron process-exit values | 13 | 0→0 | 0→0 / 0→0 |
| Cron read-service fixtures | 13 | 22→22 | 8→8 / 1→1 |
| Inert socket fixtures | 25 | 112→112 | 14→14 / 3→3 |
| Placement claim/runtime fixtures | 38 | 234→234 | 28→28 / 0→0 |
| Repository harness fixtures | 8 | 52→52 | 8→8 / 5→5 |
| Codex harness fixtures | 8 | 71→71 | 30→30 / 4→4 |
| Pending reclaim runtime | 8 | 8→8 | 1→1 / 0→0 |
| Scheduled-task settlement result | 7 | 78→78 | 22→22 / 0→0 |
| CLI registry entries | 9 | 218→218 | 35→35 / 4→4 |
| Compaction result fixtures | 11 | 3→3 | 0→0 / 2→2 |
| Archive snapshot fixtures | 7 | 111→111 | 35→35 / 0→0 |
| Managed-worktree records (W) | 19 | 222→222 (terminal) | 54→54 / not separately tallied |
| Device request/mutation helpers (D) | 14 | 144→144 | 29→29 / 0→0 |
| Transcript event records (T) | 10 | 95 expects + 2 Vitest asserts→same | 6→6 / 0→0 |

The retained original 68-path census additionally preserves 2,363 direct expects, 2,366 expect entries, one assert-root call and all 4,967 rooted assertion-expression texts; those are separate representations, not additional assertions. Its aggregate is 507→507 test callbacks, 51→51 suites and 102→102 hooks. W retains 5→5 suites/9→9 hooks/16→16 mock-fn signatures; D retains 2→2 suites/6→6 hooks/2→2 mocks. All owner/consumer byte or inverse-AST checks remain supporting evidence, not substitutes for product-path tests. Shared support files and the composed claim/runtime file are counted once.

### Fixed session-store configuration

Replace ten copies with existing fixed-store configuration owners; preserve the original store expression, roster and fresh nested values.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: Incidental property order in the tools/Talk fixtures follows the existing owner; values, own fields and evaluation timing remain unchanged.

### Model fixture defaults

Reuse the existing model-definition fixture in authority, agent and fallback-transport tests, retaining explicit capabilities, limits, absences and the agent input alias.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: Model enumeration order follows the existing fixture owner; no provider request, fallback behavior or security boundary changes.

### Outbound target registry defaults

Reuse the existing registry defaults within the same beforeEach allocation/reset scope.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. Forum identity and registry/plugin/metadata freshness remain explicit.

### Scheduled-task spawn results

Reuse the typed spawn-result owner and retain the positional stop adapter's stdout/output coupling and hoisted fixture.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: The general factory allocates a tiny default output array that explicit overrides discard; process result values, freshness and settlement behavior remain unchanged.

### Eager test gates

Replace captured promise/resolver boilerplate with the existing deferred owner without moving allocation or release sites.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: Deferred also supplies an unused reject field. No consumer relies on the old object's exact key set; scheduling assertions stay.

### Requester test gates

Reuse that deferred owner for four eager requester gates; keep binding order, releases and requester authority local.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: An unused reject field is supplied by the shared owner; no scheduling or authorization guard is removed.

### ACP startup metadata

Construct repeated ACP metadata through the existing test fixture owner while retaining scenario-specific fields and startup paths.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None in metadata values, allocation lifetime or migration behavior.

### Config promotion listeners

Share the repeated failing-runtime-overlay listener setup, allocating a fresh listener closure at every original call.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: No listener loss: three original registrations remain three helper invocations. The raw broad name screen gains the helper's own registration site; expansion restores the original module AST.

### PostgreSQL bootstrap defaults

Move repeated bootstrap callbacks to the existing engine-store support owner; keep custom vector-search setup distinct.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None in engine selection, callback freshness, schema/admission or cleanup. Real PostgreSQL conformance proof remains required; skip-only collection is not acceptance.

### Pending-input history

Reuse existing pending-input support for repeated history setup without sharing stores or moving assertions.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. Each scenario retains its own state, inputs and history expectations.

### Held migration locks

Reuse the existing held-Gateway-lock fixture rather than reconstructing its held promise and native import graph.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None in lock admission, release/settlement or native-cohort import timing; the existing owner remains the lifecycle authority.

### Avatar response bytes

Reuse the existing response fixture while retaining exact byte content and response ownership.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: One additional bounded setup-time byte copy; no avatar admission or response behavior changes.

### Source watch selection

Remove only the pre-canonicalization selectionRevision counter. Current/stopped watcher, admitted-root, publication and durability checks remain. Introducing PR #159226 supplies no human inversion incident; related write-effect guards are untouched.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: Overlapping pre-refresh selection no longer guarantees latest-invocation-wins. The pinned filesystem dependency has synchronous canonicalization work; a future delayed inversion may briefly select an older watch plan and cause an extra notification/reload that rereads current config. This is not authorization to publish old config or write state.

### Package publication setup

Reuse existing publication-swap transaction capture and fence scopes in boundary/durability tests; keep aliases, explicit authority, refusal callbacks and custom transaction/journal scenarios local.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. Fresh runtimes/executors, error identities, native admission, FIFO settlement and durability assertions remain unchanged.

### Unused validation observer

Delete only the unimported test-only PRAGMA observer and its unused counter import, after the final callers were removed in merged #182687.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None for retained behavior. Live validation fixture APIs, the general counter owner and native/schema/security/durability behavior remain.

### Cron process-exit values

Delete the local duplicate runExit constructor and import the existing process-test owner; leave stronger watched-run extinction behavior local.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. Fresh result objects, overrides, mocks and lifecycle registrations retain their original sites.

### Cron read-service fixtures

Reuse the existing createReadService owner at three construction sites with the same scheduler, clock and logger.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: Incidental logger property/spy-allocation order follows that owner; scheduler identity, clock values, fresh spies and every consumer assertion remain.

### Inert socket fixtures

Give five inert socket literals one narrow test-support owner, preserving send identity/callbacks, numeric OPEN and fresh mock functions; remove only imports made unused by the move.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: Only incidental fixture construction is centralized. No live socket behavior, registration, transport callback or expectation changes.

### Placement claim/runtime fixtures

Reuse the existing claim and runtime owners across three suites. Explicit active remote-exec versus worker-turn seed modes and claim/run IDs remain distinct. The same-file cuts are counted together once.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: Only internal fixture property-order normalization; owner identities, per-call freshness, store/resolver bindings, cancellation and effect checks remain.

### Repository harness fixtures

Use a pure constructor in the already-imported session-test owner for the repository selection/projection pair; keep distinct failure messages and registry activation local.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. Repository provider identity, priority-free support result and fresh rejecting attempt remain.

### Codex harness fixtures

Use a separate pure constructor in the existing dispatch-test owner; keep the provider list, priority, command protocol and registration timing distinct from repository fixtures.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. No universal provider factory or production registry seam is introduced.

### Pending reclaim runtime

Reuse the existing sessionRuntime projection while explicitly overriding managedWorktrees with the scenario's original workspace closure.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: The helper creates an unused pure default closure before replacement. Workspace reference identity, fresh loader methods, canonical resolver and cancellation-failure scenario remain.

### Scheduled-task settlement result

Replace the remaining literal with the existing positional spawnSyncResult adapter, retaining status, signal, output and error semantics.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. The current suite's 78 direct expectations and 22 registrations are preserved; native settlement and security authority are untouched.

### CLI registry entries

Put identical CLI-backend entry data in the already-imported registry fixture owner; leave registry push, activation, callbacks and cleanup at each original site.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. The nested command configuration remains fresh and registration lifetime is unchanged.

### Compaction result fixtures

Share the nested success result through the existing runtime-state owner at initialization, reset and held-result default sites.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. Each call creates fresh outer/nested data; supplied results, getters, held signals and write-capable settlement remain unchanged.

### Archive snapshot fixtures

Add one type-only archive test-support owner for repeated cold snapshots; preserve the index fixture's singleton lifetime and per-page callback freshness.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. Own-undefined fields, key order, cursor/generation identity and all bounded-reader/recovery scenarios remain.

### Managed-worktree records

Reuse the existing makeWorktreeRecord owner at five sites. Preserve real versus synthetic repository identity, UUID call timing, zero clocks, own optional fields, explicit paths/refs and fresh records.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: Incidental own-property insertion order follows the existing fixture owner. The local-workspace-projection substitution was dropped: saving two lines did not justify widening its initialization graph. The review concern is resolved by retaining that suite's original literal, not by claiming the import caused every timing-sensitive failure. Zero-net publication/abandonment proposals and the broad launcher-support proposal are excluded.

### Device request/mutation helpers

Share repeated request defaults, required-value checks and paired-record mutation helpers in one infra test-support owner; retain the main suite's call-time default state directory adapter.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None in device identity, fresh request arguments, store transactions, error text, credentials or mutation persistence. No production auth/approval seam changes.

### Transcript event records

Add two fresh record constructors to the existing transcript-message test-support owner and migrate the actor-kernel suite as the first area. Every original field, message reference, timestamp and allocation site remains; the complete helper-expanded kernel AST and assertion/registration texts match. This is the owner-first stage, not a migration of every transcript suite.

Best-effort tradeoffs accepted: None. The existing owner's import graph is inert (type imports and pure fixture constructors); no hooks, native initialization or asynchronous work is introduced. Its existing 19 direct consumers remain unchanged. The kernel retains 95 direct expects, 2 Vitest assert calls, 6 lexical callbacks, 2 mock registrations and 192 rooted assertion entries, each before→after.

## Evidence

The original 77-file focused selection completed with **1,458 passed and one existing platform skip**. The added selection completed with **Gateway: 140 passed, two failed, two existing skips** across six files, and **infra: 34 passed** across two files. The added-eight driver exited 1 after 763.602 seconds; its canonical test run reported 759.24 seconds. These are focused-suite results, not a whole-suite or exact-head hosted-CI claim.

Both original failures are in local-workspace-projection's checkpoint-resume cases, for stopped=false and stopped=true: lease caller-abort results at approximately 1,002/999 ms differed from the expected outcomes. One serial full-file comparison completed: original candidate **33 passed, one failed, two existing skips** (stopped=true again received the approximately 1,001 ms lease abort); untouched pinned base **34 passed, two existing skips**. Canonical durations were 250.09/221.73 seconds and driver durations 274.667/250.676 seconds. All 79 changes were reversed for the base, with 302 bindings verified and a clean worktree; this was not a cut-only control. The varying false row is not labeled a proven inherited or load-only failure. No timeout, retry or expectation changed.

The initial review's P2 concern about that suite's new non-pure service.test-support import was accepted on import-footprint grounds and the entire fixture substitution was dropped. The one post-repair full-file run still failed: 33 passed, one failed, two existing skips; stopped=true received the same approximately 1,001 ms lease abort (238.58 seconds canonical / 271.818 seconds driver). Thus removing the import is not a proven timing fix. Both remaining changed production dependencies reachable from that suite, systemd-service-files.ts and openclaw-state-read-worker.ts, were then conservatively restored to base. Their hunks are excluded and retained separately, not attributed as the cause. Projection and both production files are now byte-exact base. The static/literal closure covers 12,209 modules with five parser gaps closed; 18 computed-loader boundaries remain explicit limitations, not a claim of complete runtime reachability. The two added transcript files are outside that closure. Final source guards verify 304 inputs and 20 unchanged boundary files.

A fresh independent final-candidate review reported one P2 claiming the new event helpers lose a required literal discriminator. Rejected after checking the actual API: appendTranscriptEventsInTransaction accepts Iterable<TranscriptEvent>, and session-accessor.types.ts defines TranscriptEvent = unknown. The owning agents-sessions type program passed. No cast or speculative type constraint was added. The engine's status remains findings, not scoped-clean; there are no accepted unresolved findings.

Scoped static checks passed: original 70-path lint/format took 103.177/6.155 seconds; added nine-path lint/format took 52.426/8.989 seconds. The actual mock-export ratchet passed with 7,067 grandfathered factories. A fresh final-candidate collision census observed at 2026-10-24 22:28:09Z covered 42 complete open manifests with zero intersections and zero errors (62 calls, at most three in flight). This includes both new transcript paths and is title-routed, timestamped collision evidence, not permanent clearance, mergeability or CI proof.

The retained added seven files account for 142 passing cases, with no overlap with the original 77-file selection. The new kernel passed all 6 cases (104.92 seconds canonical / 123.93 seconds runner / 125.506 seconds driver); the two new-file lint/format checks passed in 22.747/5.286 seconds. All eleven targeted type programs passed. Real PostgreSQL proof passed all 6 files and 45 cases (24.75 seconds canonical / 94.51 seconds runner / 104.405 seconds driver), against an isolated task-owned PostgreSQL 18 database. Final runtime cycles (zero), Madge cycle ratchet, all 14 lint-suppression tests, changed-file classification and diff checks passed. Exact-head hosted CI remains the broad proof. The unchanged conditional real-Podman scenario in the excluded projection suite is unrun and is not proved by default selection. These existing native/database-heavy suites retain their original policies and real storage boundaries; no timeout was inflated to accommodate shared-host setup time.

Local proof uses the canonical runner, serial nice10 execution, one Vitest worker and task-owned HOME/OpenClaw/XDG state. No new skips, weakened expectations or manual prerequisite bypasses are part of these cuts. No user-visible UI change or screenshot requirement is introduced.

### Conflict-only integration

GitHub reported CONFLICTING on the first published head, so the branch was rebased onto main d2d935290de6. The sole conflict was pending-input-history's new upstream context/id table from #182883. Both rows, its stronger statement counter, every assertion and cleanup are retained; only the same eight setup literals are replaced. Expanding the eight fixture calls reproduces the complete current-main module AST, with 36→36 direct expectations and identical table/registration AST. The full diff remains 78 paths,+416/-920=504 net. The signed rebased head is 2ee8af0bd0b2edb9d896756f9f9bffc360a18373. Frozen dependencies were reinstalled successfully. The full affected suite passed 10/10 (169.33 seconds canonical / 190.39 seconds runner / 193.641 seconds driver); owning types, scoped lint/format, runtime cycles (zero), Madge cycles (zero), all 14 suppression tests and diff checks passed. Earlier proof remains prior-head evidence, not a claim of current-head hosted CI.

### Exact-head CI failure attribution

Run [40139494507](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139494507), attempt 1, tests head 2ee8 through actual merge ad66967deb3af510628a7eb72401c36a1389949f. Its ordered parents are main 0a3d2dc31216ccb66291a327c128ae87dbe57564 and this PR head; the retained merge tree equals a fresh merge of those parents. The following are failure witnesses, not a claim of green CI or repairs to the failing behaviors.

The small-3 lifecycle job fails two cases: webhook handoff with cleanup rejects=false at channels.test.ts:405:43, and timeout cleanup refusing replacement at lifecycle.test.ts:459:45. Both expect restartRequired=false and receive true. One serial complete-two-file comparison reproduced exactly those failures on the clean PR head and untouched parent d2d935: **5 passed / 2 failed on each**. Canonical/runner durations were 141.97/158.96 seconds on head and 203.37/225.39 seconds on base. Both use the same Node26 launcher and pinned Bun on macOS, not Linux CI runtime parity. The local base differs from actual CI base; all 22 specifically inspected lifecycle/test/owner/frontier blobs match local versus CI base and PR head versus tested merge, but this is not a full dynamic import-closure claim. The webhook case additionally matches all six preceding completed scheduled-main runs, most recently [40134490303/job120993216566](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40134490303/job/120993216566).

PostgreSQL (2/3) fails seven interactive-setup cases: sqlite onboard/setup/crestodian, PostgreSQL onboard/setup/crestodian, and PostgreSQL malformed-config onboard. Every full tail reports missing staged runtime/standalone-runtime-profile.mjs imported by runtime/packages/llm-core/src/validation.ts. prs.title: fix(sessions): reset detaches a project folder that has no worktree
prs.body:
Fixes #182474

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: text `/reset`, text `/new`, and idle rollover detach a registered project conversation that has no managed worktree.

## User Impact

The conversation keeps its project association, working directory, and containment root after reset, matching the existing `sessions.reset` behavior. Plain Control UI **New Chat** keeps its existing explicit detachment behavior. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reply initialization rebuilds the conversation entry on reset, but the rollover owner preserved `projectId`, `spawnedCwd`, and `sessionRoot` only when `worktree` was present. Extending that existing condition to registered projects preserves the missing fields without copying runtime state or adding another state owner.

Maintainer review retained Eric Curtin's implementation and regression unchanged: it is the smallest complete fix. The existing managed-worktrees documentation already describes this reset contract. Recent main drift only changes automation timestamps when an existing conversation is reused and consolidates unrelated fixtures; it does not affect this reset path, so no merge-only refresh was needed.

## Evidence

- Source-confirmed on main [`7221ce54924a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7221ce54924ac848aa14ac75c5a74b269102d280): the omission is at [`session-rollover-state.ts:65`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7221ce54924ac848aa14ac75c5a74b269102d280/src/auto-reply/reply/session-rollover-state.ts#L65); [`session.ts:572–591`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7221ce54924ac848aa14ac75c5a74b269102d280/src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts#L572) selects that projection after dropping `baseEntry`.
- The new table in `session.test.ts` exercises real reply initialization and reads the committed entry for `/reset`, `/new`, and idle rollover. On the defective base, its project/directory assertions fail because those fields are omitted. The contributor reported red-on-base/green-with-fix results; those local runs were not repeated during maintainer review.
- [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40083413328) for `dc679280af90e43a1b87679517863aecb26744a2`, including the CI gate, type checks, lint, and selected test lanes. The [test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40083413328/job/120841646950) explicitly passed all three new regressions: `/reset` **86 ms**, `/new` **68 ms**, and idle rollover **79 ms**. The full session suite passed **98 tests** in **25.51 s** (**27.57 s** including its runner); the existing worktree-reset sibling suite also passed all three cases. Local runtime was not measured because target execution was prohibited.
- Maintainer static checks passed: oxlint with trusted-main core rules on both changed files, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`. Independent autoreview: **scoped-clean through P2**, with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Simplification review found no extra helper, guard, or state machinery to remove. Exact introduced diff: production **+4/-3** (net +1 from comment wrapping), tests **+37/-0**, docs **+0/-0**.
- Per maintainer proof policy, contributor code was not executed locally. Live Gateway/channel e2e and a latest-stable upgrade run were skipped; PR CI is the broad gate. ClawSweeper found no concrete code defects. Its live-behavior and upgrade-proof holds are overridden by that policy; this patch changes no stored schema or format.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reduce repeated task PR subscription work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI task PR subscriptions rebuild and sort the same task audience on every currency check, including unrelated session publications. This is the residual `assertCurrent` work after #181890, which already removed repeated parent-index selection.

## User Impact

Less background allocation for task PR subscriptions, with unchanged snapshots and live viewer-permission checks. No configuration, API, or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The task-publication owner now retains its existing lineage revision and compact visited-node decisions. Each assertion reads current sharing rows and rechecks live permissions; it rebuilds and compares the selection only when lineage or an inclusion decision differs. Denied frontiers, duplicate visits, pending row facts, lazy lineage publication, and lifecycle/permission withdrawal retain their existing behavior. The caller's repeated selection/comparison is removed.

Production code grows by 47 lines to preserve that permission contract: retaining selected sessions alone would miss a previously denied descendant becoming visible. This reuses the existing producer index and revision lifecycle, without retaining a sharing-map revision or adding another index. Tests grow by 24 lines. The measurement harness now separates untraced GC timing from opt-in traced promotion and supports a fixed warmup. Its initial ready wait honors a later explicitly declared paired start, while missed-start and measurement checks remain unchanged.

## Evidence

**Decision: land.** The two counterbalanced untraced pairs reduce sampled allocation by **15.40%** (1.570 MB/op), main-thread CPU by **6.93%** (1.999 ms/op), and total GC/work by **11.42%** (0.096 ms/op; 56.6 ms/min). The predeclared extra pair confirms the improvement: allocation −15.03%, main CPU −7.12%, GC/work −9.70%. Separate traced promotion falls **6.18%** (13.472 KB/op). These are synthetic subscription-workload results, not a claim of the same percentage reduction in whole-production CPU.

The mixed-sign latency metrics resolve on the signed absolute three-pair mean: subscription p95 −0.813 ms, update RPC mean −0.070 ms / p95 −0.345 ms / p99 +0.275 ms, settlement p99 −0.758 ms. The only positive eligible tail mean is update-RPC p99, approximately +0.99% of mean baseline cost, below the adverse gate. Loop p99 improves in every pair. GC pause p95 increases are below 1 ms absolute; maximum GC pauses are 37.75→38.87, 36.07→28.86, and 33.96→35.64 ms, all within the max-pause safeguard. No GC/promotion/max-pause rejection signal requires A/A controls.

Tradeoffs/context: individual subscription maxima rise (70.08→94.89, 64.10→71.13, 65.82→128.46 ms) while subscription p95 improves on the signed mean. Loop maxima also rise by 8.0–14.8 ms while loop p99 falls. Subscription p99 (256 samples) and sidebar tails (125 samples) are undersampled context; major GC has only two collections per side and is context. These observations are retained in the tables rather than trimmed.

An isolated built Gateway used 10,000 synthetic sessions, 6,000 settled subagent runs, 40 synthetic plugins, eight signed clients with 50 subscribed keys each, label updates, sidebar reads, and mock-provider turns. Main baseline: `7221ce54924ac848aa14ac75c5a74b269102d280`.

Each selected task had four lineage nodes; the residual was repeated selection construction, not scanning all 10,000 sessions. All 400 snapshots stayed identical, and all 12 provider turns completed with verified responses. Live permission work remains; zero full selections does not mean zero guard cost.

These instrumented sequential runs on a shared Mac establish work counts and context, not paired timing acceptance. prs.title: improve: skip redundant expiry probes in plugin-state writes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin-state operations issue a redundant expiry query when the namespace aggregate has already found expired rows in the same transaction.

## User Impact

Plugin-state writes with expired siblings perform one fewer SQL statement. Quotas, TTL visibility, bounded cleanup, cross-process reads, and the Plugin SDK contract are preserved. There is no schema migration or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the aggregate's existing expiry fact to the cleanup owner. Distinguish known expiry from a live-only scan or a full 1,024-row cleanup batch; those unknown cases retain the indexed existence probe. The fact lives only in the existing transaction-local view. No cache, generation, additional transaction, new SQL shape, or public signature change is introduced.

The apparent two aggregates beside a Reef audit delete actually describe different namespaces (`audit` and `audit-head`). Both are needed for quota/TTL accounting. Ordinary compare/update probes also remain: their covering expiry index avoids scanning large clean namespaces. This change does not claim to eliminate the entire live expiry-probe family.

## Evidence

### Acceptance rule (registered before the first run)

Use the committed Reef boot workload with 173 signed synthetic receipts, a full 30,000-entry audit window, and real loopback transport. Include one expired orphan and a clean control; split boot from 60 seconds of warm polling. Remove one expiry probe per aggregate-confirmed sweep, retain the audit chain/quarantine result, quota/TTL/read-own-write behavior, and add no warm statements, requests, or MAIN SQL. Frozen observer v3.1.4 verified 36/36 hashes.

Any timing claim requires at least five alternating samples per arm, the campaign timing lock, and load below 24, reporting median/p95/range; an adverse 20% cell stops the candidate. Local load was 67.59, selecting the one-pair fallback. These results are statement counts, not a latency/CPU speedup claim.

Command on each arm:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/plugin-state-polling.mts \
  --output <isolated-proof-dir> --observer <frozen-observer.cjs> \
  --messages 0 --receipts 173 --audit-prefill --expired-audit-orphan \
  --seconds 60 --profile
```

Repeat without `--expired-audit-orphan` for the clean control.

Baseline production: `61deaaef587`; baseline workload: `124015bbea3`. Blacksmith Testbox, Node 24.22.1, four observed CPUs, 15.4 GiB RAM. Both baseline scenarios verified 30,000 retained audit entries, sequence 30,346, and 173 quarantines. Per-thread CPU profiles captured across 23 threads; the plugin-state worker owns the aggregate/registration work.

| Scenario / phase | Base SQL / requests / MAIN | Candidate SQL / requests / MAIN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expired orphan, boot | 5,363 / 858 / 52 | 5,362 / 858 / 52 |
| Clean control, boot | 5,361 / 858 / 52 | 5,362 / 858 / 52 |
| Expired orphan, warm 60s | 33 / 13 / 0 | 33 / 13 / 0 |
| Clean control, warm 60s | 33 / 13 / 0 | 33 / 14 / 0 |

Baseline plugin-state boot: 865 aggregates, 867 multi-key reads, 346 keyed deletes, 1,211 upserts, one expiry probe, one bounded expiry delete. prs.title: perf(memory): batch source headers during publication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory index publication writes each source header separately even when the same publication already batches its chunk, recall, and provenance rows.

## User Impact

Multi-source indexing performs fewer SQL statements. Stored content, search results, rollback, tombstones, revision publication, and the worker request contract stay unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required; latency improvement is not claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Batch source headers at the existing `MemorySourceIndexKernel.replaceGroup` owner and remove the per-source UPSERT. Each statement carries at most 128 distinct `(path, source)` keys and an estimated 64 KiB of UTF-8 header data. Deduplicate pending keys so the final header wins and PostgreSQL never updates the same conflict key twice in one statement. A single oversized header retains its existing single-row behavior.

The existing transaction, source checks, chunk/vector ordering, and mutable vector-rebuild reads remain authoritative. No cache, generation, schema, extra request, or additional main-thread work is introduced. Production changes are +49/-19 lines (net +30): the bounded, deduplicated batch replaces the scalar writer. Tests are +122/-70 lines, primarily extending existing fixtures.

## Evidence

Acceptance was published in d86e145ebc480942d1b07d43ee4065aa305c39b0 before new measurements. The committed acceptance and workload instructions are in `scripts/perf/memory-source-header-batching.md`.

| Sources per publication | Baseline header UPSERTs | Candidate header UPSERTs |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 100 | 100 | 1 |
| 129 | 129 | 2 |
| Large UTF-8 headers with a repeated final key | 3 | 2 |

All 33 SQLite owner tests pass, covering stored/searchable rows, vectors, ordering, rollback, duplicate keys, and byte bounds. The corrected baseline fails the 100/129-source assertions with actual counts 100/129 versus expected 1/2; the one-source case passes. An initial enlarged fixture exceeded the allowed importance value; those setup failures were discarded and the corrected fixture was rerun on both revisions. Other chunk/recall/provenance insert counts remain unchanged.

Two retained synthetic Gateway runs each recorded three header UPSERTs inside one `source.replace.group` request and zero target MAIN SQL. The later run used 3f7b7765585ddcd72822d8b4e43ef928d23eecf7; the kernel, worker, PostgreSQL adapter, and transfer modules are byte-identical at production base 90d9772045f. This is source-attributed baseline evidence under the campaign's busy-host exception: the new baseline build was canceled before execution with load above 80 and six jobs queued ahead. No fresh-head Gateway A/B, latency, CPU, p95, or whole-workload saving is claimed. The frozen observer's retired causal labels are not used; attribution uses phase/request identity.

PostgreSQL review approved head `64b57f9e221c`; both native PostgreSQL owner/publication suites now pass (22 tests), satisfying that review condition. The temporary PostgreSQL server stopped cleanly. Basic lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Exact-head CI run [40136165351](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136165351) has 36 successful jobs, including production/test types, lint, source contracts, architecture/ratchets, and PostgreSQL shards 1 and 3. A focused current-main baseline at `0f6631638b2e3b6dd5fcbc1ad94a46ed4fe5ae47` independently reproduced the same seven failures (one other case passed). prs.title: perf(gateway): reduce repeated profile reads during restart recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restart-recovered operator runs repeatedly rebuild unchanged profile facts during authority checks.

## User Impact

Recovery performs less allocation and CPU work while preserving every privileged-use authority check. There is no permission, configuration, schema, or persistence change and no required user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original prepared profile identity now exposes its existing canonical row identity as an opaque access-fact revision. Reading that revision still checks the exact bound catalog owner, admission/settlement, profile lifetime, and required email-binding lifetimes. Native and worker profile publications, including email changes, already replace that row. Recovery retains validated facts privately until the revision changes; both checks around plugin policy execution remain. Pending, uncertain, missing, replaced, and revoked authority still fail closed.

Runtime production code grows by 13 lines: the small retained revision/fact pair preserves the security boundary while eliminating repeated full projections. The existing owner remains the only authority; no new cache manager or invalidation mechanism is introduced. The requested non-test/non-doc-path diff totals +300 lines: +13 runtime, +233 benchmark tooling, and +54 in the benchmark README. Tooling growth provides the requested per-recovery counters and separate allocation/GC evidence; it removes the duplicated transcript observer instead of keeping parallel instrumentation.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the baseline with 10 full-fact reads during restoration instead of one. Focused recovery/resident tests pass (62 tests across three files), including pending/uncertain mutations, unrelated-profile stability, changed-profile refresh, and permanent refusal after original email revocation. The final four-file consumer run passes all 123 tests, including the extracted existing recovery fixtures. Core typecheck, changed-file format/lint, export-name collision guard, and both source-closure test files passed. Baseline full build and candidate runtime build both exited zero; both emitted the identical CSS-size advisory (303,542 versus 303,372 bytes).

Baseline: `3f7b7765585ddcd72822d8b4e43ef928d23eecf7` on Node 26.12.1. Five alternating local baseline/candidate pairs, each with 100,000 warmup and 1,000,000 measured restored-authority checks, use the same dependencies and hash-attested source overlays. Every allocation and CPU pair improves:

| GC/check | 0.001183302 ms | 0.001026929 ms | −0.000156373 ms |

A separate 20,000-check counter pass reduces warm full-fact reads and GitHub projections from 40,000 to zero. Exact owner and settlement checks remain 40,000 each. Plugin/config revocation controls fail on the next check as expected.

GC signs vary across pairs and baseline cost spans 5.16×; its relative mean is inconclusive on this shared Mac. The signed absolute mean falls, and the largest adverse pair is +0.000940933 ms/check, well below the +1 ms/check materiality threshold. No max pause exceeds max(50 ms, 2× its paired baseline). Major-GC counts are one per side; candidate minor counts are below 200, so pause percentiles are context only. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable findings after reviewing the full diff, authority owners/callers, tests, and measurement harness.

Built Gateway proof: a fresh synthetic fixture contains 10,000 sessions (2,000 archived), 6,000 settled runs, and 40 active plugins verified on both boots, including all 19 synthetic registration markers. After deliberately interrupting one held mock-provider operator request, the restarted candidate Gateway dispatched the exact cohort and recorded terminal `status=ok reason=completed`. The baseline also completed its exact cohort on the earlier 21-active-plugin fixture. The initial candidate fixture discovered but did not activate its external plugins; explicit synthetic selection corrected that setup before the 40-plugin proof. The 40-plugin driver exited zero with one initial/held/recovered request, one reconnected client, and no connection errors. Separate source-counter runs also exit zero and complete recovery. The candidate's extra owner check is its initial full-fact read. Both source overlays were verified against their pinned hashes in the restarted child. These windows include startup and polling; baseline snapshot was just before terminal completion, candidate snapshot after it. They are counts per recovered provider arrival, not matched complete-turn or latency measurements. All isolated Gateways and mock servers were stopped.

The retained-child filesystem test now covers original email reassignment and reassignment followed by restoration, alongside device revocation. Each case first completes an allowed write after the recovered requester settles, then pauses a second production write after directory preparation. The original email is moved to another profile (and optionally back) before the write resumes. The retained tool rejects, the write callback remains at one call, and the file still contains only the allowed content. A second alias keeps the original profile independent; the restoration case asserts that the returned canonical ID is the original profile, preventing a merge-tombstone fixture from passing accidentally.

The final focused command passes 43 recovery tests and 22 source-closure tests:

Changed-file formatting/lint and the export-name collision guard also pass. Fresh independent review found and corrected the initial single-alias fixture mistake, then reported no remaining findings. This follow-up changes tests only; runtime production delta remains +13 lines and the measured runtime patch is unchanged.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): trust admitted client scope arrays
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway connections validate optional string-array scopes at admission. Downstream handlers repeatedly call `Array.isArray` on the retained, typed value. Remove 20 of these repeated shape checks across 14 Gateway files (22 additions, 34 deletions; net -12 production lines).

## User Impact

No user-visible authorization change. Gateway handlers do less repeated validation after admitting a connection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The WebSocket `ConnectParams` schema and admission validators remain the boundary owners. In-process constructors accept or produce typed arrays. Scope membership, revocation, per-effect authorization, nullable clients, and the original pre-/post-await capture positions are preserved. No SQL, schema, database identity, SDK surface, provider request, or configuration changes.

Retained checks include untrusted token-scope normalization, unknown-valued approval-client scopes, agent-tool input decoding, and WebSocket admission. Arbitrary JavaScript violating an internal TypeScript constructor contract is not a supported input boundary; existing array operations already rely on that contract.

## Acceptance rule (registered before measurement)

Use frozen SQL harness v3.1.4 with synthetic state and real loopback Gateway transport. One baseline/candidate pair with matching default options; analyze ten warm turns separately from cold/startup/restart phases. Require successful turns, spawn, cron, control RPCs, compaction, restart, and shutdown. Compare statement, worker-request, and MAIN counts, including per-operation execution-window counts; no increase caused by changed scope consumers. Report warm median, nearest-rank p95, and min–max, plus raw phase changes. Any 20% adverse metric is a stop pending disposition. No latency or CPU speed claim is made. Counts-only runs do not use the timing lock.

The frozen v3.1.4 causal hook predates the shared AsyncContext migration: causal phases are empty and requests classify as background on current main. The comparison therefore uses native warm execution windows, not causal turn counts; the frozen harness is unchanged. This limitation is recorded before the first run.

The simplification gain is 20 removed runtime array-shape checks, with no new validation owner, state, cache, copying, or fallback.


## Preserved authorization checks

| Removed shape check | Preserved permission or effect check |
| --- | --- |
| operator-scopes; operator-approval-authorization (three sites) | Admin/approval scope membership and device/connection binding in the same functions |
| approval-record-lookup | Admin/approval membership, requester identity, visibility filter, revocation and effect-time authority |
| health (two sites) | Admin membership at its existing capture point |
| server-broadcast-scopes; server-request-context | Event scope policy, invalidation and approval-delivery membership |
| session-catalog-visibility; client-human-presence | Operator scope policy and authenticated UI identity |
| environments (three sites) | Admin policy before projection, with current scopes re-read at the same post-await sites |
| sessions-mutations (two sites); sessions-patch-engine | Permission-mode/admin authorization and the existing internal null-client contract |
| device-scope-upgrade; nodes.pairing | Role-scope policy and pending-pairing ownership enforcement |
| talk handlers | Admin or talk-secrets scope membership before secret disclosure |

## Admission regression

The existing `ConnectParamsSchema` (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/frames.ts:61`) owns scope shape. WebSocket admission applies `validateConnectParams` at `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts:286`. The suspension-admission suite now sends actual connect frames with both `"operator.admin"` and `"xoperator.adminx"` as string-valued scopes, and requires `INVALID_REQUEST`, socket close, and no admitted client. Downstream `includes` can therefore only receive an admitted array.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated setup and overlapping assertions make these test suites harder to maintain. This batch consolidates fixtures and behavior scenarios across seven test owners.

## User Impact

No production or user-visible behavior changes. All changes are in existing test files; no production seams, dependencies, configuration, or baselines change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared fixtures and table-driven cases retain the meaningful owner-boundary scenarios while removing duplicate proof. This replays 24 of the 30 requested campaign commits onto main at `541a09d301b7a5603924d110d9dde0e925c288c0`; review and CI then reverted seven of those commits' effects (Copilot, report-scheduler, and Claws home), leaving 17 effective campaign commits across seven files.

Conflict decisions: skipped terminal commit `3d2aba36d07f` because its whole-file rewrite conflicts with main's current session fixtures and lifecycle proof. Skipped Voice Call `9dd1bab5d09a` because its duplicate media-stream suite is already absent on main. Skipped decisions `fdd50f5e4b8c` and `64b245254677`: main already reorganized this coverage (including `b429fdd74d69`), and the campaign rewrite assumes a different fixture/API shape. Skipped FaceTime `6b67c89e65f2` and `125c80251809`: the campaign depends on support helpers absent from current main and conflicts with the current explicit lifecycle fixtures. All other commits applied without conflicts; no conflicting hunk was forced through.

Independent review found six actionable issues, all accepted: incomplete Copilot runtime mocks, an incomplete non-interactive auth context, lost configured-secret failure coverage, lost filesystem traversal rejection, lost error-serialization redaction, and lost admitted-report-write shutdown proof. Restored the MXC traversal and gateway-client redaction assertions. Dropped the complete Copilot and report-scheduler changes instead of rebuilding their fixtures here; those files now match pinned main exactly, preserving their existing contracts.

Final review added one accepted issue: restore the exact approval.resolve `{ id, kind, decision }` assertion, now present with the request mock typed to the real Gateway handler contract. One finding was rejected after source verification: QA-channel already calls `vi.restoreAllMocks()` inside its suite-wide `afterEach` `finally`, restoring HTTP spies between every parameterized case. No accepted findings remain unresolved. Superseded intermediate review attempts were stopped when new CI results required changing their captured candidate.

The first-head CI run also exposed batch-caused fixture/static failures, repaired before publishing the replacement head: forward LM Studio wizard text arguments and retain the original optional model-ID normalization; copy readonly expected values for MXC's matcher and retain method binding; preserve cron's undefined-value checks using property reads rather than requiring serialized absent properties to be present. Dropped Claws home's complete rewrite after its fixture/navigation tests failed, also removing its generic-lint defect. No assertions, retries, or timeouts were weakened to get green. Failed-job logs were inspected once; no local runtime tests or typechecks were run.

## Evidence

- First-head failures: [LM Studio fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138161936/job/121004413328), [cron undefined-property assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138161936/job/121004413379), [MXC readonly matcher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138161936/job/121004959749), and [UI generic lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138161936/job/121004959761). - Additional first-head findings: [Claws fixture/navigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138161936/job/121004413072), [Copilot mock-export guard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138161936/job/121004413279), and [extension type-aware lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138161936/job/121004959815). prs.title: feat: manage channel identity links in the existing Profile
prs.body:
Related: #162164 — this is the separate Profile-management slice for channel identity links.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway administrators currently have no Profile UI for explicitly associating a channel sender with a personal OpenClaw Profile.

## User Impact

A connected administrator with the negotiated `operator.admin` scope can view, add, and remove exact channel/account/sender identity links for their currently authenticated personal Profile. The Shared Gateway Owner is not a link target. A link is an administrator-entered association; it does not verify control of the external account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Profile page now exposes the Gateway's existing list/link/unlink methods. It adds no backend method, identity store, or automatic name/email matching. Failed writes preserve entered identifiers, and stale results cannot update a replaced Profile or connection. Linking does not merge people, rewrite transcript attribution, assign session ownership, or change session visibility.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @TheAngryPit](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/79137be2-2b05-499c-89c9-d70c38ec03e5)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/578e501f)

## Evidence

### Incremental first-link rendering repair — `e0699a0d322f465918dbd9fe8a4cccaf9449b80d`

[Published repair `e0699a0d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e0699a0d322f465918dbd9fe8a4cccaf9449b80d), based on `27a731b2a5c783880cf5a8ab47c149bcd2fa9cdb`, repairs a reproduced Solid rendering defect: after adding the first channel link, Profile reported success but retained the empty-list message. The existing `<For>` now owns its empty fallback instead of a conditional evaluated once outside tracking. Authorization, requests, domain state, existing link rows, and stale-result retirement are unchanged.

The existing single-flight regression now asserts first-link and last-unlink rendering while preserving its same-turn duplicate-RPC and enabled-control waits. The new first-link assertion failed on the imported source (1 failed, 11 passed). On the fixed source, the focused channel/Profile run passed all 33 tests, zero failures/skips, with exit 0 in 4.93 seconds wall time; Vitest reported 1.75 seconds. CI seconds for this candidate are not available. Scoped formatting, type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), production UI typecheck and diff whitespace checks passed. A frozen complete-candidate P0–P3 Auto Review against `4445492de48b6650c3ce3272a68e8ac697cb0a54` returned no findings; the reviewer did not execute tests or certify current-main/browser behavior.

Additional verification of the unchanged published candidate: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-pages.json` passed (exit 0, 3.81 seconds wall time). The existing `src/gateway/server-methods.channel-identities.test.ts` also passed all three cases (exit 0, 56.34 seconds including cold worker compilation), exercising registered in-process Gateway authorization and real isolated storage for denied scopes, permitted administration and conflicting/malformed assignments. This is not WebSocket/browser, persistence-across-page-reload, or current-main integration proof.

**This is an incremental bugfix, not completion or merge readiness.** Current real-browser/Gateway persistence, authorization-denial execution and before/after screenshots remain missing: Chromium downloaded, but Linux shared libraries are absent, and supported dependency installation failed at sandbox privilege setup. No root/sandbox workaround was used. Integration with current main also remains blocked: managed `refresh_base` refuses this existing-PR binding and `prepare_pr` returns the unchanged older review base. Historical CI, browser and screenshot receipts below remain pinned to their actual revisions and do not establish this candidate. Product/design acceptance remains a separate maintainer decision.

Simplification: the renderer loses its competing empty/list conditional; production net -1 line and the existing regression net +21 lines compared with the imported PR source. No new state, effect, backend method, stored-data format, migration, grant or external-account ownership claim is introduced.

Previously published head `27a731b2a5c783880cf5a8ab47c149bcd2fa9cdb` integrates main `4445492de48b6650c3ce3272a68e8ac697cb0a54` and repairs the channel-test readiness failure. The diagnostic showed a click while Add was still disabled and busy, before any link RPC. The test now waits for the actual Add and Remove controls to become enabled using the existing wait defaults. It retains all twelve cases and their original RPC, row, status and error assertions. Production busy guards and authorization are unchanged.

The repaired twelve-case channel suite passed with zero failures or skips under Node24.20, Vitest5.0.3 and Solid2 rc.14 before the main integration. Those source bytes remain identical. This is revision-pinned proof, not a fresh run against the merged lockfile or hosted custom Bun runtime. prs.title: test(perf): add synthetic session readiness workloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Investigates repeated waiting work when history reads overlap transcript projection repair, and when concurrent `/usage cost` requests share the agent's refresh writer.

## User Impact

This PR adds synthetic real-Gateway workloads. There is no production behavior change yet. A fix will follow only for waiting work reproduced on the current main baseline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The projection owner already knows when each session is ready. The usage refresh owner already knows when its writer is released. Readers should consume those completion facts while preserving early per-session readiness and the requested session's fresh cost detail.

The cost busy branch returns before SQL or worker dispatch. Its expected waste is repeated filesystem preparation and timer wakeups; it must not be advertised as a SQL saving.

## Evidence

### Acceptance registered before the first measurement

Baseline source: `4a38dbdb6b1`. Both workloads use newly created synthetic state, an isolated Gateway, and real transports. No operator state or logs are read. No production delays or forced branches are injected.

- Projection: `scripts/bench-session-projection-ready.mts`, six durable sessions, 5,000 messages per session, 256 payload bytes, target session index two. Request `chat.history` over an authenticated WebSocket while startup reconciliation runs, then five warm reads. Reproduction requires more than one projection-status worker request during the cold read. The candidate must reduce this to at most one and preserve readiness before unrelated sessions finish.
- Cost: `scripts/bench-session-cost-ready.mts`, four distinct sessions with 16 MiB synthetic transcripts and 2,000 long-transcript entries, one concurrent cold `/usage cost` burst and five warm bursts over the bundled iMessage adapter's loopback bridge. Verify each reply's distinct requested-session token and billed-cost totals. Count busy sleeps and filesystem identity work with the optional read-only probe. A qualifying reproduction requires actual busy sleeps; a candidate must remove those sleeps and repeated preparation while retaining each requested session's fresh detail.
- Count SQL statements, worker requests, and main-thread SQL with the unchanged frozen SQL observer and analyzer. Record operation families and separate cold from warm. Report count windows honestly if causal attribution is unavailable. Capture Node CPU profiles on the Gateway and its workers before optimizing.
- Timing, if available, uses at least five interleaved baseline/candidate samples each, cold and warm separated, under the campaign timing lock with initial one-minute load below 24. Report median, p95 and range. Every user-facing metric must hold or improve; a 20% regression stops landing. If the quiet-host wait exceeds 60 minutes, report counts/CPU evidence only and make no latency-improvement claim.
- Re-run the frozen warm workload for non-regression under its host-capacity policy. Preserve cancellation, worker failure settlement, early readiness, and different-session cost freshness in focused owner regressions. No schema changes, new generations, or cross-store transactions.

### First execution and workload repair

Production remains unchanged. The six-by-5,000-message projection fixture reached the real history wait and issued **130 projection-status worker requests** before the Gateway returned its bounded `UNAVAILABLE` rebuilding response. The cold-read window contained 2,677 SQL statements / 151 worker requests / 0 main-thread SQL. This demonstrates repeated polling, but that failed history request does not establish successful or early readiness.

The cost workload delivered and validated all **24/24 replies**, including each requested session's distinct usage details. Its initial wait counts are invalid: bridge subprocesses inherited the optional probe and overwrote its shared file. The repair uses a separate file per process; a parent/child smoke confirms independent records and exact timer/stat/realpath counts. Analyzer child metadata and the three CI script-type errors are repaired in the same benchmark-only change. No cost wait or savings claim is based on the overwritten file.

### Follow-up acceptance, registered before execution

Run the same projection workload with the existing `--messages 1000 --target-index 0` options, leaving six sessions and five warm reads. This bounds the requested session's work below the normal history readiness deadline while retaining unrelated backlog. Require a successful one-message history response, more than one projection-status request for reproduction, and remaining pending sessions to prove early readiness. The original 5,000-message result stays separately reported.

Rerun the same four-client cost workload after the per-process probe repair. The Gateway's own PID-specific record is authoritative; bridge records must never overwrite it. All other acceptance rules above remain unchanged. No production candidate will be applied for an unreproduced target.


### Workload review and static validation

Exact-head CI [40137380314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40137380314) passes at `5e768e47b9cb4b29b3eb7fe895eae897d727cc76`, including production/test types, type-aware lint, source contracts, architecture and database ratchets. Two independent Codex review rounds completed. The actionable findings were fixed: probe output is PID-specific and detached Gateways are stopped on interruption. No unresolved actionable finding remains.

The open-main conflict census covers 2,695 other PR heads (2,696 including this PR); 21 new or changed heads were refreshed before readiness. None touches these five workload files, so there is no overlapping PR for a base-only/base-plus-candidate merge-tree comparison. Production LOC and SQL remain unchanged; this PR adds 1,041 workload/documentation lines. The owner implementation and corrected runtime attribution follow separately.


### Second projection result and smaller-fixture acceptance

The 1,000-message/target-zero run again reached the bounded rebuilding response: 142 projection-status requests, with no successful history sample. This reproduces polling but does not prove early readiness. Before the next run, reduce only the existing workload size to --messages 100 --target-index 0 (still six sessions and five warm reads). This tests whether the requested projection can finish within the product's unchanged readiness deadline on this loaded host. Require the same successful one-message reply, more than one baseline status request, and other sessions pending; do not increase a product timeout or inject a delay. If it does not qualify, report the evidence gap rather than claiming successful early readiness.


### Corrected cost probe follow-up acceptance (before execution)

The second baseline validated all 24 requested details, but its exit-only probe was lost: the probe IPC listener kept the real Gateway alive until forced teardown. No busy-retry count is claimed from that run. The observer repair unreferences IPC and saves per-PID checkpoints on phase changes and each second; natural-exit and forced-kill subprocess checks preserve exact counters.

Rerun the same committed four-session cold burst and five warm bursts with this observer repair, counts-only and per-thread profiles, against unchanged production source `4a38dbdb6b1`. Accept attribution only from the Gateway PID identified by both frozen process metadata and its synthetic native-runtime log. All 24 replies must retain requested-session token and cost details; at least one busy sleep must reproduce before implementing the cost optimization. Report per-phase busy sleeps, refresh-path stat/realpath calls, SQL, requests and MAIN; absent probes remain missing evidence, never zero. The candidate must remove timed busy sleeps and repeated refresh preparation while retaining every requested detail and all existing cancellation behavior. No latency claim will be made from this loaded host.



### Corrected cost-probe baseline

The previous probe changed IPC liveness in inherited child processes, causing startup failure before any measured cost request. That run is excluded. The corrected probe reads the workload's existing phase file and never installs IPC listeners or changes IPC references. A small process-lifetime reproduction, phase counter checks, and forced-kill checkpoint checks validate the repair.

The next baseline uses the unchanged cost workload and production baseline, four distinct sessions, one cold burst and five warm bursts. The acceptance rule above is unchanged: at least one observed busy retry, correct detail for all 24 requests, then zero timed retries on the candidate. Counts and per-thread profiles only; host timing qualification was not met.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): avoid copying complete worker transfer records
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Receiving a complete SQLite worker record allocates and copies a second full-size byte buffer immediately before deserializing the bytes the receiver already owns.

## User Impact

Complete framed replies use less CPU and avoid one byte-buffer allocation/copy. Decoded values, validation, error handling, fragmented transfers, and SQLite admission/transaction behavior are unchanged. Measured receiver CPU improves 39.8%, 13.8%, and 6.4% for the tested 1/16/128 KiB records; this is not a whole-Gateway latency claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the received bytes when the first frame completes the record. Keep the owned assembly buffer for genuinely fragmented records. The final production diff is **+8/−2 lines (net +6)**: the supported fragmented-record contract requires both ownership cases in the same receiver. The 9 MiB control exercises that retained path. A representative 16 KiB record avoids a 16,670-byte assembly buffer and copy per decode.

Ordinary replies already transfer serialized ArrayBuffers. v8 serialization remains because structured clone changes Buffer values to Uint8Array and does not preserve the encoded-size budget. The accompanying synthetic-only census identifies reply counts/bytes by method; the benchmark loads the complete receiver source and records its source hashes.

**An earlier ordinary-reply narrowing is excluded from the final diff.** It improved CPU but failed the qualified loop-p95 gate; details below. Session mutation producers, receipt fallback, provider review, maintenance results, and their tests remain unchanged from main.

## Evidence

An isolated Gateway used 10,000 synthetic sessions (2,000 archived), 6,000 settled runs, and 40 synthetic plugins plus memory-core. Four measured mock-provider turns over two rounds with four clients completed successfully. Successful entry-patch commits consume framed publication envelopes through the admission MessagePort, exercising this receiver. The ordinary-reply census excludes that separate port. Baseline used a built Gateway; candidate used source with a longer startup allowance. These instrumented runs establish behavior/applicability, not comparable end-to-end timing.

Two concurrent, CPU-swapped fixed-work comparisons on an isolated Linux sandbox, Node 26.12.1:

| Record shape | Mean paired CPU/op delta | Mean absolute CPU/op delta |
|---|---:|---:|
| Complete 1 KiB | −39.76% | −2.309 µs |
| Complete 16 KiB | −13.76% | −1.552 µs |
| Complete 128 KiB | −6.42% | −4.540 µs |
| Fragmented 9 MiB control | −1.41% | −47.262 µs |

No material adverse receiver gate. The fragmented control's mean GC rise is **+0.00423 ms/op**, below the v5.6 +1 ms/op materiality threshold. Separate 16 KiB receiver heap-sampling passes are roughly neutral (−0.62%); they exclude external backing buffers and cannot count the eliminated byte-buffer allocation. Separate traced promotion totals fell in both pairs: 2,685,069,912→2,677,748,112 bytes and 2,748,398,352→2,664,898,504 bytes (−0.27%, −3.04%).

Protocol: exclusive slot B; interleaved CPUs 64,66,…,94 versus 65,67,…,95, swapped per pair; shared production guard; prepared fixtures, synchronized warm start, and fixed operation counts. Untraced runs supply CPU, GC, maxima, and loop gates. Tracing and allocation sampling run separately. Traced promotion includes process setup and 200 warmup operations; no traced timing gates. Receiver passes recorded load-average context. The original trace JSON mislabeled its mode, but separate filenames/launch commands identify it; the harness now labels traced runs correctly. No pause trimming, maintenance exclusions, forced GC, or major-cycle normalization.

<details>
<summary>Receiver pairs: CPU, per-kind GC, both maxima, and tail sample counts</summary>

</details>

<details>
<summary>Rejected ordinary-reply candidate — not included in this PR's final code</summary>

The census found 120 sessions.patch replacement replies totaling 672,744 bytes (maximum 6,026), although the caller consumes only maintenance plans. A candidate relying on native publication receipts reduced these to 19,320 bytes / 161-byte maximum (−97.1%), with equal maintenance plans and matching retained RPC response samples apart from timestamps. All focused correctness tests passed.

Captured 5,591-byte baseline and 161-byte candidate replies were replayed for 2,000,000 operations per side, in two concurrent swapped pairs:

| Pair | CPU µs/op B → C | GC µs/op B → C | Max GC ms B → C | Loop p95 ms B → C (samples B/C) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 25.461 → 1.876 | 2.270 → 0.240 | 4.301 → 7.424 | 11.977 → 14.361 (3494/263) |
| 2 | 26.245 → 1.923 | 2.329 → 0.229 | 3.896 → 7.338 | 12.239 → 14.508 (3570/268) |

CPU improved 92.65%, but loop p95 rose **+2.384 ms (+19.9%)** and **+2.269 ms (+18.5%)**. Both candidate sides exceed 200 samples, and both deltas exceed the 1 ms exemption and 10% paired threshold. Reject under the loop rule. Both sides use batchSize 64; the faster candidate produces a much shorter saturated window. This result describes saturated decoding, not equal offered Gateway request rates; it is retained rather than dismissed.

Minor GC counts fell 1847→102 in both pairs; totals fell 4539.944→480.756 ms and 4657.943→458.208 ms. Minor p95/p99 were 3.173/3.626→5.737/5.905 ms and 3.124/3.320→5.382/5.963 ms. Candidate pause tails have insufficient samples and qualify for the fewer-collections exemption. Major/incremental/weak GC counts were zero. Loop p99 was 13.074→14.918 and 13.296→15.057 ms, ineligible because candidate sides lack 1,000 samples. No maximum-pause safeguard fired.

Optional A/A controls and allocation-attribution probes were queued, then cancelled **before acquiring the slot or producing any result** once independent review confirmed the qualified loop rejection. v5.4 requires controls before rejecting GC/promotion/max-pause results; this rejection uses loop p95. The ordinary allocation filter under-attributed the decode and is not used for a total-allocation claim. Its replay helper and all ordinary-result production/test changes were removed from the final diff. The ignored ordinary reply fields remain an identified follow-up opportunity.

</details>

Validation: existing transfer/framing tests pass (8/8 on baseline and candidate); operation-admission and affected caller/recovery files also passed during investigation (97 focused tests total). The receiver is byte-identical to the version used for those tests, Gateway turns, and paired measurements. No new implementation-coupled test was added for the allocation elision. Export collision guard and eager-import/PR-wrapper closure files pass (22 tests). Changed-file lint, formatting, and core typecheck passed; final helper reduction passed focused lint/format. No Testbox lease was used under the task's focused-local/PR-CI rule.

CI run 40135169314 found two unbound-method errors in the diagnostic preload. Both captured Worker methods explicitly preserve the original receiver. Inline suppressions appear unused in focused JS lint, so this file joins the existing receiver-preserving diagnostic exception in `.oxlintrc.json`. The narrow exception is source-verified and independently reviewed; runtime code is unchanged. The following head passed that lint gate. Final-head CI completed; the inherited failure and passing gates are recorded below.

Author simplification pass and final reduced-patch independent review are clean. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) was used because the requested route did not match operator configuration; no configuration was changed. GitHub Codex review also completed without findings on the earlier head. The final review confirms the rejected path and helper are absent.

## Final CI disposition

Exact head `e6bf5e16f83ab21aafcaa8f93c18489ddaad897c`, [CI run 40138374774](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138374774), attempt 1: all selected non-aggregate jobs passed except [PostgreSQL conformance 2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138374774/job/121005107872). Shards 1/3 and 3/3 passed, as did security, lint, types, and the selected test shards. The aggregate CI gate remains failed; it is not claimed green.

The failed shard has seven failures in `src/infra/database-engine/interactive-setup.integration.test.ts`: SQLite and PostgreSQL onboard/setup/crestodian, plus PostgreSQL malformed-config onboard. Every case exits before onboarding authentication because the isolated fixture omits `standalone-runtime-profile.mjs`, newly imported by `packages/llm-core/src/validation.ts` in #182856. The exact same seven cases and missing-module signature fail on [scheduled main run 40138789542, job 121006161355](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138789542/job/121006161355), main `87f00b1b5254861d944e524cdd8bb3a65f53b59f`. The failing test, runtime fixture helper, validation module, and standalone profile are byte-identical between that main revision and this PR. Both job logs were inspected; their failed-case lists match exactly.

The automated classification says “new” because it compared against the preceding hourly run 40134490303, whose main revision predates #182856. The newer scheduled run above supplies direct inherited-failure evidence. A local single-case baseline attempt was stopped during automatic build preparation to honor the compute limit; it provides no test verdict. No CI rerun or unrelated source repair was used to chase green.

Landing uses the authorized inherited-only CI exception. Native workspace preflight would create another checkout outside this lane, conflicting with the task's explicit one-worktree rule, so the authorized fallback is a squash merge pinned to the exact reviewed head. Independent review is clean; there are no unresolved review threads.
