prs.title: fix: clarify pending agent startup admission messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading repair advice when a Gateway listener is available but an agent is still completing normal startup preparation.

## User Impact

Operators see that startup preparation is pending, its current phase and elapsed background-preparation time, and a request to retry when preparation finishes. Actual failures retain their repair guidance.

This does not speed up startup or change readiness, queueing, retry policy, configuration, or database schemas. It does not claim that rejected input was queued. No migration or operator configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pending admission currently suggests stopping the Gateway and running `doctor --fix`, even when no failure has occurred. The existing startup owner already tracks phase and elapsed time; this change reuses its phase transitions and progress timer to update the pending refusal instead of introducing another state owner or timer. Elapsed time is refreshed at those existing progress points, not continuously.

## Evidence

- Regression on the base: 23 tests passed; the new pending-message assertion failed against the old startup reason.
- Patched focused suites: **51/51 tests passed**, covering pending retry metadata, phase/elapsed updates, successful admission, and actual failure repair guidance.
- Targeted format, lint (0 warnings/errors), and whitespace checks passed.
- Core plus Gateway-server and state-logging test typechecks passed.
- Independent supplied-diff review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; source-owner context was inspected separately.
- Gateway preparation suite: 24 tests in 2.93s. Combined focused run: 117.14s including compilation and existing native SQLite integration suites. CI timing is not yet available.

The focused tests exercise the production admission/startup owners with controlled external preparation and native database integration. Separately, an installed-runtime backport was activated and verified through a clean Gateway start. That runtime check is separate from the exact-head isolated RPC proof below; it does not claim that pending or genuine failure responses were captured on the live Gateway.

## Additional real Gateway operator-facing proof

Exact head: `80ddc37d056e5939341bbdcbc22c779502188254`. Full `pnpm build` passed (4m4.5s); previous focused tests were not rerun.

Ran the built Gateway in isolated synthetic state with channels, cron and providers disabled. A supported index-repair fixture (40 queued agents plus the probe) kept real background preparation pending; a separate agent had a required table deliberately removed. No production admission hooks, fabricated refusals, or copied helper implementation were used.

**Authenticated `sessions.create` WebSocket response while pending:**

```json
{
  "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
  "message": "Agent probe is still preparing (phase: open-wait; background preparation elapsed: 4s).\nStartup inspection and preparation are still running. Retry the request after preparation finishes; no repair action is needed while it is pending.",
  "details": {
    "reason": "startup-sidecars",
    "method": "sessions.create"
  },
  "retryable": true,
  "retryAfterMs": 250
}
```

**Genuine schema failure through the same RPC:**

```json
{
  "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
  "message": "SQLite schema is incomplete or noncanonical for <isolated-state>/agents/broken/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: missing table session_key_contract; missing or drifted index idx_agent_session_nodes_active; run openclaw doctor --fix to repair it.\nSessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, run \"openclaw doctor --fix\" to inspect and repair this agent database, and restart.",
  "retryable": false
}
```

Captured 35 pending error frames across phases `open-wait`, `open`, `migration`. Every pending frame retained `retryable: true`, `retryAfterMs: 250`, phase/elapsed text, and no Doctor/stop/restart advice. Genuine failure frames retained `retryable: false`, no retry delay, and Doctor repair guidance. The real GatewayClient retried the pending request and `sessions.create` succeeded after admission (`runStarted: false`; no model call).

Capture used an unchanged-byte loopback WebSocket forwarder because GatewayClient intentionally hides retryable startup refusals behind automatic retry. Raw responses were inspected before sanitization; only isolated filesystem roots were replaced in the failure excerpt. Gateway runtime: Bun1.4.4/Linux; observer: Node24.22.1.

**Limits:** This adds current-head RPC/operator-message proof, not a base-runtime before/after recording, channel/UI screenshot proof, or a restart-performance claim. The large synthetic queue is a fixture, not a proposed production configuration.

## Consumer-test correction after CI review

Correction head: `e0b67835fc9d11643c8241c5d0f1ef138839a0c9`.

Updated six stale pending-error expectations across `server-request-context.test.ts` and `session-row-prepared-read.test.ts`. They now assert the preparation phase, numeric elapsed seconds and retry guidance. The copied-context test explicitly checks the transition from `inspection` to `readiness`. Existing handler-wait, eventual success, authority, cancellation and genuine-failure checks remain intact.

Exact-head CI on `80ddc37d` reproduced the obsolete-message failures in `checks-node-changed-compact-small-8` and `checks-node-changed-compact-large-11` (run 39864296549). After the test correction, this focused command passed **85/85 tests** across all four files:

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The webhook hot-handoff lifecycle check installed its synthetic plugin as bundled while expecting the non-bundled reload receipt. Production correctly marked that reload as requiring a restart, so the fixture failed before it could validate the intended channel handoff behavior.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. The lifecycle check now exercises the operator-managed plugin path it was designed to cover, while production bundled-plugin restart behavior, plugin trust restrictions, channel handoff assertions, timeouts, and configuration contracts remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture now keeps the bundled discovery root empty and selects its synthetic plugin through the existing `plugins.load.paths` contract. Because ordinary load-path plugins are intentionally not trusted to issue scoped Gateway requests, the fixture observes the same reload-settlement fact through its already-authenticated admin RPC before starting the manual reload. This keeps the security boundary intact without manufacturing official provenance or changing shared helpers.

## Evidence

- On the base revision, the [historical owner job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40098379185/job/120885426791) reached the successful webhook handoff receipt and failed with `restartRequired: true` instead of the fixture's unchanged `false` expectation; the other two cases passed.
- On the corrected exact head, the [hosted owner-file job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136966373/job/121000716891) passed all 3 cases, including both webhook cleanup variants and the sibling lifecycle control.
- Changed-file formatting and lint passed with no warnings or errors.
- The affected `core-test-gateway-server` test type graph passed.
- Both exact-head independent reviews concluded clean.
- Hosted changed-node, source-contract, guard, security, plugin-trust, lint, and test-type checks passed. An unrelated PostgreSQL interactive-setup fixture row failed because its isolated runtime omitted `standalone-runtime-profile.mjs`; the same seven failures reproduced on current `main`, while this PR changes no database, onboarding, PTY, or runtime-copy input.

prs.title: fix(telegram): large media sends time out after 30 seconds
prs.body:
Related: #112116 (closed, covered the unhandled rejection after a media upload timeout, not the deadline itself)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a large video or document sent to Telegram fails with `Network request for 'sendVideo' failed!` after 30 seconds when the file needs longer than that to upload.

## User Impact

Media sends get a deadline that grows with the file instead of a flat 30 s. An upload keeps its current guard until its transfer estimate outgrows it (30 MiB for the 30 s methods), and the longest guard is 30 minutes. Operators have no knob for this today: `timeoutSeconds` is in `RETIRED_TUNING_KEYS` (`extensions/telegram/src/doctor-contract.ts:29`), and neither client passes a timeout to `createTelegramClientFetch`.

Tradeoff that needs a maintainer call: the account throttler runs one request at a time per chat, and in a group one at a time across all of its forum topics (`GroupRequestScheduler.drain` in `account-throttler.ts`). A slow upload now holds the requests queued behind it in that chat for as long as its guard, up to 30 minutes, where today they wait at most the 30 s guard (60 s for albums) for it to fail. Other chats are not held.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveTelegramRequestTimeoutMs` gives `sendvideo`, `senddocument`, `sendphoto`, `sendanimation`, `sendaudio` and `sendvoice` a fixed 30_000 ms, and `sendmediagroup` gets the 60_000 ms default. Pinned main `2e7668b2eaad` still uses that table. The Bot API answers an upload with the sent Message, so the response cannot arrive before the file has been uploaded, and a big enough file always loses.

The resolver now takes an optional upload size and returns the larger of the table value and `ceil(bytes / 2 MiB/s)` seconds plus 15 s, capped at 30 minutes. 2 MiB/s is an assumed floor, not a measurement.

The size comes from the InputFile that `prepareTelegramOutboundMedia` builds (recorded in a WeakMap); direct sends, reply media and albums all take their files from it. A grammY transformer installed inside the account throttler, in both `send-context.ts` and `bot-core.ts`, reads the size off the payload (including `sendMediaGroup`'s `media[]`) and hands it to the client fetch through AsyncLocalStorage. I did not take the size from the caller's async context because the throttler runs queued requests from its own drain loop. In a probe on an earlier base, a second request enqueued under its own AsyncLocalStorage value ran under the first request's value, for both a group chat and a private chat.

Two more timers sat under that guard. grammY 1.46.0 races every call against one client timer, `options.timeoutSeconds ?? 500` (`out/core/client.js:77`), with no per-call override, and neither client set it. undici 8.11.2 waits `headersTimeout` for response headers, `300e3` by default (`lib/dispatcher/client.js:317`), and refreshes that timer when a streamed body ends, so it counts from the end of the upload. A self-hosted Bot API server answers only after it has relayed the file to Telegram. Both clients now set grammY's `timeoutSeconds`, and the Telegram dispatchers set `headersTimeout`, to 1860 s (the 30-minute cap plus 60 s), so the per-method guard is the deadline. Every other consumer of the Telegram transport keeps a shorter deadline of its own (getUpdates 45 s, file downloads 120 s to headers, probes through `fetchWithTimeout`).

## Current revision and fixture repair

Head: [`44411bc979e3f8aab896aa154036769bedde0737`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/44411bc979e3f8aab896aa154036769bedde0737), tree `8abfeb27059dab4f917a1818a34a495c1e303af3`.

This fixture-only commit disables persisted thread bindings in the upload-deadline fixture and registers `bot.stop()` for cleanup. The real bot, send stack and all four upload assertions remain. Upstream #175379 deliberately acquires runtime when thread bindings start; the upload fixture does not initialize that unrelated runtime. Production binding behavior is unchanged.

The preceding head `0afce1f7d17e08adbf2d3818122e9ebb6420cecd` merged main `2e7668b2eaad12171ef4421b68286de6063b7e77`, retaining main's one-argument account-throttler constructor and the upload transformer before the throttler. The sequential transformer/WeakMap/context test requested removed in [the review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151923#issuecomment-5733461410) is removed; the four independent size-boundary cases remain.

[Previous-head CI 40121818105](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121818105) finished with 27 successful jobs, 31 skipped and two failures: the Telegram job failed both polling-bot rows with `Telegram runtime not initialized` before their upload assertions, and the aggregate gate propagated that failure. The four boundary cases, two other send cases and loopback case passed.

## Evidence: reproducible fixture validation

A separate Linux x64 runner tested the exact published tree using Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, frozen dependencies, Vitest 5.0.5 and pinned OpenClaw Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`. Lockfile SHA-256: `21592b379203de7ecd8661cfd6e412daf6546f94b203f28c314579db20f76594`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Upload-deadline fixture | Four cases passed; 122.03 s. |
| Independent size boundaries plus loopback transport | Five cases passed; 105.10 s. |
| Restore only the upload fixture from `0afce1f7`, same environment | Exactly the 100 MiB and 1 GiB polling rows failed with the runtime-initialization error; both send rows passed; 125.27 s. |
| Boundary and loopback controls after reversal | All five passed; 129.37 s. |
| Restoration | Exact candidate tree restored; validation processes and allocation drained. |

```sh
CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/send.upload-timeout.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/send.upload-real-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Tested fixture SHA-256: `142a7e49383fc875bed18b2774b39bb862f77c363680890bf953bf54a90ab530`. Validation receipt SHA-256: `181295d70e37bcc0cb488ed9c0728241e315881072b5041d1a6cb6e10663425c`. Independent source review found no actionable issue in this fixture change.

These are fixture results. The loopback case uses a 64 KiB payload tagged with a larger upload size and a fake clock. It proves timer ordering through the local transport; it does not deliver an approximately 893 MiB file to Telegram.

## Historical product regression evidence

At `34a6f9e42fb`, the three upload files and neighboring bot/fetch suites passed 94 cases. Replacing only the four production wiring files with main `4db022470af6` caused all four upload fixture cases and the loopback case to abort at 30,000 ms. Earlier timer probes distinguished grammY's 500-second client deadline and undici's response-header deadline. These remain historical evidence, not a current-head live-platform result.

## Remaining gates

[CI 40138561883](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138561883) completed successfully for this head: 29 jobs passed and 31 skipped. Its merge checkout `bd77e2ea717464e780e0a5777fa21633727576ff` has parents main `418aafaae7e8d13792b9095c010a114ca4e058ea` and this head; the upload fixture is byte-identical. All four upload cases, four size-boundary cases and the loopback case passed. The latest dependency, security and aggregate statuses are success ([status publisher 40139326205](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139326205)).

The later PR-context check rejected the previous body because its validation heading did not start with `Evidence`. This body restores that required heading. The product and live-proof gates below remain open.

- Maintainer acceptance of the assumed 2 MiB/s budget and up-to-30-minute per-chat wait remains open.
- Fresh-install and latest-stable upgrade proof with Telegram settings preserved is unperformed.
- The approximately 893 MiB send through a self-hosted Bot API must still demonstrate an unpatched timeout and a delivered message on the patched build, with size and elapsed time. No live upload or two-bot proof was performed in this fixture validation.
- The 2 MiB/s floor remains an assumption. Loopback and fake-clock results do not establish real transfer rates.

We're from the MiniMax team.

## What Problem This Solves

The official MiniMax M3.1 model id is `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`. This renames the catalog entry, thinking profile, docs and tests from `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` (name "MiniMax M3.1 Flash") so the id matches the official one. It also marks `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` and `MiniMax-M3` `supportsTemperature: false` in their catalog compat (open-weights models; temperature is not a supported knob).

It also keeps `/think xhigh` and `/think max` intact for M3.1: the runtime stream caps `options.reasoning` at `high`, so the MiniMax wrapper now uses the session level when it is `xhigh`/`max` (previously both were sent as `output_config.effort: "high"`).

## Evidence

- `vitest run extensions/minimax/index.test.ts extensions/minimax/provider-catalog.test.ts extensions/minimax/model-definitions.test.ts`: 35 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` on `extensions/minimax` and `docs/providers/minimax.md`: clean.
- Real run (`openclaw agent --local`, MiniMax CN API key, `minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`): `--thinking low|medium|high|xhigh|max` send `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` with `output_config.effort` low/medium/high/xhigh/max, all HTTP 200; default sends `max`; `off` is rejected locally as unsupported; multi-turn tool use and image input work; no `temperature` sent. `MiniMax-M3` still offers off/adaptive.
- `vitest run extensions/minimax`: new xhigh/max tests pass; the only failures are 4 `tts.test.ts` music cases that fail identically on the base (SSRF guard in this sandbox).


## Maintainer follow-up

Fixes #177387. Both `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` and `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` now retain the M3.1 five-level thinking profile, adaptive request shaping, output limits, and multimodal catalog metadata on API-key and OAuth routes. GA is the recommended ID for new configurations. The original GA pricing, temperature metadata, and xhigh/max effort fixes remain.

The Preview ID is intentionally retained: released configurations and saved selections reference it. Removing support would require a migration and a separate compatibility decision. This preserves OpenClaw's handling of the ID, without promising that MiniMax will keep serving it. Preview keeps its previous Token Plan cost metadata.

Thanks @Hansen1018 for the original report, @bit-777 for the additional reproduction and upgrade warning, and @php737 for the dual-ID analysis and payload evidence. All @SaladDay contributor commits are preserved; current main was merged without rebasing or force-pushing.

### Additional maintainer evidence

- Original-main regression: 3 GA cases failed and 30 existing cases passed. The affected MiniMax sources are unchanged between that baseline and the merged main base. The adapted regression now covers both IDs, cold dynamic resolution, pricing, five-level thinking, signed replay, and outbound request assembly; the six focused files pass all 60 tests (524.98 s total wrapper wall time, including 244.30 s cold worker compilation).
- A rebuilt CLI, isolated configuration, synthetic credential, and owned loopback SSE fixture captured all four combinations below. Each command exited 0 and returned the fixture's `OK`. GA previously emitted manual-budget thinking with no effort; Preview previously emitted the correct adaptive/low payload.

Every capture retained `max_tokens: 131072` and omitted manual thinking budgets. This proves the built OpenClaw request-assembly path on macOS; the responses are deterministic fixtures, not hosted MiniMax inference. No paid call or real hosted key was used, and Preview service availability was not tested.

The full build passed in 37m 22.1s after the old-branch refresh. Its unchanged UI emitted an advisory total-CSS report (296.4 KiB versus 296.3 KiB); the owning build intentionally runs this report with `--report-only`. No UI source, toolchain, or budget input changes in this PR.

prs.title: perf(gateway): bound selected PR facts to retained rosters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selected session PR facts accumulate for every session ever selected, even after those sessions leave all retained reader rosters.

## User Impact

Bounds the retained PR-facts cache to sessions used by retained read scopes or acquisitions still in flight. Re-entering a previously evicted session reads its current facts again; selected rows keep their existing retry/backoff and last-confirmed PR behavior. No configuration or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prune the shared cache after roster changes against the union of retained selections and in-flight acquisitions. Human and service readers retain independent membership within the existing 64-scope cap. Service membership uses the connection/run identity when available and a weak caller-object identity otherwise; those callers still rebuild authorized results and never share snapshots. Unchanged human reads avoid a cache-wide pruning pass. Projection ownership and publication files are unchanged.

Runtime production LOC: +94/-49 (net +45). The growth preserves existing cross-reader retry sharing, separates service-reader membership without caching their authorized snapshots, and protects acquisitions that yield between batches. The weak caller IDs live with the existing capped scope owner and do not retain clients. The PR also adds a 301-line rerunnable benchmark capsule and its guide. No new facts cache or public API.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before measurement: rotate 10,800 synthetic sessions through two 40-row rosters using the actual selection and facts-read owners; candidate must retain only the 80 live entries, reduce forced-GC retained heap, preserve PR output, use one facts read on re-entry and zero on the next unchanged read. Five fresh-process pairs, alternating launch order and swapped interleaved CPU sides, synchronized after warmup. Owner-only proof; no whole-Gateway throughput, promotion, or latency claim.

All five pairs passed on Node 26.12.1, comparing parent `721cdadccb93b9c185d367f0e8082b2338553c81` with head `f314b80faf9636ce5bbc26d1c639260925458698`. Each side visited 10,800 sessions through two 40-row scopes. Source hashes matched the pinned owners in all ten fresh processes. Four forced collections with event-loop yields preceded and followed each rotation.

| Metric (5 samples per side) | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Retained PR-facts entries | 10,800 | 80 | −10,720 (−99.26%) |
| Post-GC retained heap growth from warm fixture | 25.803 MiB | 0.945 MiB | −24.858 MiB (−96.34%) |
| Facts reads during rotation | 10,720 | 10,720 | 0 |
| Prepared PR reads during rotation | 10,720 | 10,720 | 0 |
| Facts reads on re-entry | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Facts reads on next unchanged read | 0 | 0 | 0 |

All retained-heap samples, in bytes (candidate minus baseline):

| Pair | Baseline | Candidate | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 27,056,640 | 990,400 | −26,066,240 |
| 2 | 27,056,784 | 990,872 | −26,065,912 |
| 3 | 27,056,792 | 990,408 | −26,066,384 |
| 4 | 27,058,192 | 990,408 | −26,067,784 |
| 5 | 27,053,944 | 990,408 | −26,063,536 |

The baseline retained 80 → 2,720 → 5,400 → 8,120 → 10,800 entries at successive checkpoints; the candidate retained 80 throughout, with its bound asserted after every page. The separate cache-clear diagnostic released a mean 25,689,724.8 bytes on baseline (range 25,689,688–25,689,872) versus 13,440 bytes on candidate (all five), after the re-entry check. That diagnostic excludes objects still held by retained scopes; it is not an exact dominator measurement.

Within each of the five pairs, baseline and candidate ran concurrently under the exclusive slot-B lock, with interleaved CPU sides and launch order swapped on successive pairs, synchronized after warmup. Every pre/post guard check passed, and the shared watcher did not abort a pair. Admission used native blocking `flock` after the nonblocking helper repeatedly missed queued releases; measurement conditions were unchanged. One earlier setup attempt exposed an empty start file and failed on both sides before capture or measured work, producing no result samples. Atomic timestamp publication fixed the private runner, passed setup verification, and all five counted pairs were fresh. No measured sample was discarded.

The benchmark deliberately releases materialized row wrappers after each read, representing archived pages that can leave the projection. Its heap result is whole-process post-GC growth from the warmed fixture; production can share retained objects through live rows and other scopes. It proves the owner retention bound, not an exact production heap reduction, throughput improvement, or allocation/promotion/GC-pause result. The committed benchmark and guide contain the rerun recipe and limitations.

Validation:

- New eviction regression fails on baseline at the retained-key bound.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-plugins.session-facts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed; 48.05 s Vitest duration, 60.22 s wrapper wall time (most time was compiler setup). Covers service-only backoff plus interleaved connected/connectionless service readers; these cases were reproduced red before their correction.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed using the repository's native typechecker.
- Changed-file oxfmt and oxlint: passed.
- Export-name collision guard: passed. Eager-import and PR-wrapper source-closure tests: 22 passed (35.63 s wrapper wall time).
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped clean after resolving service-reader retention findings. The configured review helper refused the requested provider route; operator configuration was unchanged. The service-reader correction received a fresh independent review with no remaining actionable findings.
- Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40131664963) passed on `f314b80faf9636ce5bbc26d1c639260925458698`, including the aggregate, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review gates. No CI reruns or Testbox/Crabbox leases were used.

After deployment, watch the selected PR-facts map's retained entry count/bytes as roster churn grows: it should track retained roster membership, not cumulative session selections. A scope that deliberately retains a broad roster still retains its facts. Synthetic owner measurements do not predict whole-process memory savings exactly.

Prepared for maintainer review; this lane does not merge its PR.

prs.title: fix(openai): restore Azure realtime Talk on GA deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Azure Realtime Talk connections to GA-only deployments and input transcription when the transcription deployment is not named `whisper-1`.

Closes #166773
Closes #166776

## User Impact

Azure Realtime uses the GA endpoint and session payload when `azureApiVersion` is omitted. Explicit preview configurations retain their existing URL and payload. Users can set optional `inputTranscriptionModel` under `talk.realtime.providers.openai` or `plugins.entries.voice-call.config.realtime.providers.openai`; omitting it preserves the transcription default. This additive setting requires no Doctor migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge previously defaulted Azure to the retired preview API and hard-coded its transcription deployment. Connection setup now selects the Azure protocol once; session updates use that selection and share the existing GA policy builder. GA endpoints normalize optional `/openai` or `/openai/v1` suffixes. Explicit preview URLs retain their original path bytes, including an existing duplicated `/openai` segment. OpenAI Platform retains its behavior and default transcription model unless the override is configured.

The option is declared and validated in both configuration owners and the Voice Call plugin manifest. Documentation and generated config baselines are updated.

## Evidence

- Regression tests fail on main for the GA URL/session payload, the Azure transcription override, and non-string configuration values. The repaired bridge tests cover GA default/override, exact preview URL/session compatibility, the endpoint-plus-model deployment fallback, and the OpenAI Platform override.
- Targeted tests: **199/199 passed** across bridge connection, event handling, response control, provider routing, Talk schema, and Voice Call schema suites (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <six files> --maxWorkers=1`).
- Targeted syntax lint, core typed lint, formatting, config-baseline generation/check, and all 1,357 documentation config fences passed. Extension typed lint was blocked by the repository's shared-install guard (`Declaration input escapes checkout`); exact-head PR CI provides broad validation.
- Net change versus integrated main: production **+28 lines**, tests **+156 lines**, documentation/generated metadata **+68 lines**. Duplicate Azure connection logic and the duplicate GA payload builder were removed; remaining production growth declares and describes the supported setting in both schema owners.
- No fresh live Azure test was run because Azure credentials are unavailable. Cameron's October 7 live GA evidence below is retained. Earlier October 23 isolated released-Gateway evidence used a synthetic WebSocket peer: it observed preview/`whisper-1` on `openclaw@2026.10.6`, GA/configured transcription on the contributor head, and successful `talk.session.create` in all six cases. That older-head synthetic proof is supplementary, not exact-head Azure acceptance. The suffix compatibility issue it identified is now covered by the exact-path regression.
- Exact-head [CI run 40133878991](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133878991) passed on `66f23694c423e3f89ac3d3bfe366464a808402df`; the CI watcher reported GREEN. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issue.
- [ClawSweeper's final review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166772#issuecomment-6048157427) found no code issues. Its additional latest-stable upgrade proof remains unperformed; no stored-data schema or migration changes are introduced, existing configuration is preserved by the schemas, and explicit-preview wire compatibility is covered by regression tests.
- Microsoft documents the April 30, 2026 preview deprecation and GA URL/session changes in the [migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/realtime-audio-preview-api-migration-guide).

Implementation and live Azure evidence contributed by @CameronVetter.

<details>
<summary>Contributor live Azure GA proof — October 7, 2026</summary>

Manual end-to-end run against the existing Azure resource using short synthetic English speech. Private endpoint and credentials were redacted; the utterance, transcript contents, and audio payloads were not included in the evidence.

**Separate deployments, configured transcription override**

prs.title: fix(gateway): isolate scheduled runs from worker refresh scope
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Workboard automation nudges fail with "Plugin runtime changed" when a script-payload cron job runs after the worker that nudged it has ended.

In plain terms, a card-completion event could schedule the board's owner job, but that job inherited a permission lifetime from the worker that had just finished. The job therefore started and immediately lost permission to call its first tool. Scheduled and manually started runs were unaffected.

## User Impact

Event-driven Workboard automations now start with their own scheduler-owned lifetime instead of inheriting the ended worker's refresh scope. Scheduled runs, manual runs, tool restrictions, cancellation, and stale-tool rejection keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler already replaces Gateway caller, plugin registry, and request scopes, but it intentionally preserved unrelated ambient async context. One of those inherited contexts was the agent plugin-runtime refresh owner, so a queued run captured the closing worker's owner and every tool call rejected it.

The scheduler boundary now clears only the plugin-runtime refresh field before running detached work. A real agent run still creates its own refresh owner through the existing embedded-runner path.

## Evidence

Base-red behavior probe using the production refresh and scheduler owners:

```text
refresh_assert=Error: Plugin runtime changed. Continue with the refreshed tool catalog; do not repeat completed actions.
```

Head-green with the same probe:

```text
refresh_assert=ok
```

Focused regressions:

```text
src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts                    2 passed
src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.plugin-runtime-refresh.integration.test.ts  17 passed
```

The new regression holds the scheduled callback until the originating refresh owner closes, then verifies the callback no longer inherits that closed owner. The adjacent integration suite verifies real agent runs still reacquire generations and preserve run authority, committed work, and terminal results.

- `pnpm test src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.plugin-runtime-refresh.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/agents/plugin-runtime-refresh.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/plugin-runtime-refresh.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.ts src/gateway/scheduled-run-gateway-context.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

Focused typecheck remains unavailable in this container because the pinned `tsrs` binary requires `GLIBC_2.34`; the host loader fails before project checking starts. A full Workboard card lifecycle was not run against a live Gateway, but the regression and production probe exercise the exact scheduler/refresh boundary that produced the reported error.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Codex). The scope came from #170985 and was validated against the real scheduler and refresh owners. No production data, credentials, or external services were used.

Closes #170985

prs.title: fix(update): report corrupt restart sentinel rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A present-but-unreadable restart sentinel row was treated as absent by the managed update helper. Operators lost the recovery context without any corruption-specific guidance. The helper now reports the shared reader's `invalid` state, keeps the row intact, and does not replay unverified context.

Closes #153501

## User Impact

After a failed managed update, corrupt JSON in `continuation_json` or `stats_json` now produces an actionable warning instead of silently dropping recovery context. Safe service recovery still proceeds, the malformed row remains available for inspection, and the warning is persisted in update history.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared reader already distinguishes `missing`, `valid`, and `invalid` rows. The helper consumed that state but returned silently. This change reuses the existing owner result rather than parsing or rewriting the corrupt payload.

The warning is logged and recorded as a run warning:

`Restart sentinel metadata is unreadable; preserved the row and skipped its unverified recovery context. Run openclaw update repair on the Gateway host, then retry the update.`

For a failed standalone CLI handoff without notification or exported triage metadata, outcome recording can finish before failure triage reads the sentinel. The helper now performs that existing failed-update capture before the terminal writer snapshots `runWarnings`, so the corruption diagnostic is included in the persisted run steps instead of only appearing in console output. That pre-terminal capture is best-effort: if reading the sentinel fails, the helper logs the diagnostic failure and still finalizes the recorded updater outcome instead of replacing its exit code.

## Evidence

- Added a managed-handoff regression test that writes truncated `continuation_json`, asserts the repair hint appears, and verifies the sentinel row is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The terminal-ordering regression asserts the persisted update run contains `warning:restart-sentinel-unreadable` with the repair guidance before the run is finalized.
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-triage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14 passed. Both before- and after-recovery diagnostic read failures retain updater exit 7, finalize terminal state, and skip unavailable triage.
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "persists a corrupt restart-sentinel diagnostic"`: 1 passed, 70 skipped.
- `pnpm test src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 13 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm test src/infra/restart-sentinel.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 39 passed.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap ratchet pass.
- Test and core typechecks report only the pre-existing unrelated `src/snapshot/local-repository-directory-policy.ts:351` (`isVolumeRoot`) failure on `main`.

prs.title: fix(text): bound brace checkpoint activation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A bare `{` in any streamed final answer activated whole-reply plain-tool-call checkpointing. Every model delta then re-projected the complete reply, so ordinary pretty-printed JSON and brace-heavy prose blocked the Gateway for seconds.

Closes #182562.

## User Impact

On the same 32 KiB inputs and 4-character deltas, the shipped `createAssistantVisibleStreamText("final_answer")` path improves from:

| Shape | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Pretty-printed JSON | 45,793 ms | 221 ms |
| Brace-heavy prose | 6,905 ms | 61 ms |

Visible output is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the bare `{` activation token and replace it only for bracket JSON calls with a bounded incremental probe. The probe:

- consumes every appended character before retaining state;
- recognizes a line-start bracket header followed by a JSON payload marker;
- preserves unresolved headers across grammar-permitted whitespace, including split chunks and line breaks;
- keeps only a capped header and no unbounded reply tail.

Existing activation tokens continue to own Harmony and XML-like calls.

## Evidence

- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts`: 38 passed
- `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.streaming-work.test.ts`: 29 passed
- `src/shared/text/plain-tool-call-text.test.ts`: 44 passed
- Added parity coverage for a 600-byte payload in a single chunk, a header split across permitted whitespace, and a full source replacement; each matches `sanitizeAssistantVisibleStreamText`.
- Base-red regression: ordinary 4 KiB pretty-printed JSON called the canonical projector 2,048 times on base and fails the zero-checkpoint assertion.
- `oxfmt --check` and targeted `oxlint` passed for all changed files.

## Shipped-path proof

`openclaw agent exec` was run through the shipped `src/entry.ts` entrypoint against one local OpenAI Responses SSE provider. The 24-delta stream split `[tool:`, `read]`, and its JSON payload across different chunks. Result:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "streamingRequests": 1,
  "chunkCount": 24,
  "braceProsePreserved": true,
  "splitToolCallHidden": true,
  "fencedExamplePreserved": true,
  "matchesExpected": true,
  "finalText": "Ordinary brace prose: {\"mode\":\"fast\",\"items\":[{\"id\":1}]} stays visible.\n\n\nVisible after call.\n\n```text\n[tool:read] {\"path\":\"example.txt\"}\n```"
}
```

The visible result retains ordinary brace prose and the fenced example, while the split, unbracketed tool call is removed. The complete captured run is in `agent-exec.log`.


### Review follow-up

Removed the helper-only complete-large-chunk probe case flagged by ClawSweeper. The shipped visible-stream large-first-chunk regression already exercises that boundary and asserts the sanitized output. Re-ran `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts` (37 passed) plus the related `assistant-visible-text.streaming-work` suite (29 passed); `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass on head `3cb4932a6`.

prs.title: fix(ui): replace stored secrets from config forms
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI Form mode can type a new sensitive value, but a stored secret arrives as the server redaction sentinel and remains read-only. The disabled reveal button leaves no way to replace that credential from Form mode.

Sensitive scalar fields now offer an explicit **Replace stored value** action. It opens an empty, masked input without revealing or committing the sentinel. Abandoning the replacement restores the concealed state; typing replaces the stored value normally.

## User Impact

Operators can rotate a stored token from Settings and channel forms without switching to Raw mode or exposing the existing secret. Opening and abandoning the replacement does not clear the credential.

Structured `SecretRef` values remain raw-mode-only, and non-masked reveal behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`getSensitiveRenderState` intentionally prevents the redaction sentinel from becoming editable. The scalar renderer now tracks a local replacement transition: the sentinel stays concealed, the input renders empty as `type=password`, and the first input marks the replacement as intentional. Blur without input cancels the transition.

The existing sensitive-field button becomes the explicit replacement entry point when the value is sentinel-redacted; otherwise it keeps its reveal/hide behavior.

The secret wrapper now also remains mounted while that replacement transition is active. Channel forms configure masking without a reveal callback, so deriving the wrapper only from `sentinelRedacted` removed it after the first character and replaced the focused input. The regression types a two-character credential and asserts that the same input remains focused and both characters reach `onPatch`.

## Evidence

Base-red on `origin/main` with the new browser coverage: 3 failures. The replacement action was absent, and the sentinel remained locked. The new no-reveal regression additionally failed on the previous head after the first replacement character.

Head-green:

```text
config-form-scalar-integrity.browser.test.ts  37 passed
config-form.browser.test.ts                   43 passed (adjacent suites, 2 files)
```

Browser proof covers replacement, masked keystrokes, focus retention, no sentinel disclosure, no reveal callback, and cancellation without clearing. The focused no-reveal regression verifies `onPatch` receives the complete two-character value and `document.activeElement` still points at the same input.

- `pnpm test ui/src/components/config-form-scalar-integrity.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm test ui/src/components/config-form.browser.test.ts ui/src/components/config-form-union-integrity.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json ui/src/components/config-form.node.scalar.tsx ui/src/components/config-form.node.shared.tsx ui/src/components/config-form-scalar-integrity.browser.test.ts ui/src/i18n/locales/en-settings.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/components/config-form.node.scalar.tsx ui/src/components/config-form-scalar-integrity.browser.test.ts`
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base origin/main`
- `git diff --check`

Focused UI typecheck reached unrelated existing errors in `src/snapshot/local-repository-directory-policy.ts:351` and a missing local `libdeflate` declaration; neither changed file is involved.

Closes #163393

prs.title: feat(models): operator text for a provider's own refusals, such as an empty prepaid balance
prs.body:
Related: #167341

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: people are told to sign in again when a provider or proxy refuses a request with an error type of its own sent as a 401 or 403, such as an empty prepaid balance.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator can set the text people see for a provider's own error types, keyed by the `type` in the provider's error body:

```json5
{
  models: {
    providers: {
      "acme-proxy": {
        failureCopy: { insufficient_balance: "Your balance is empty. Top it up on the billing page." },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

Channel replies, Control UI replies and the run's error event then show that text, with a leading ⚠️ like the built-in messages, instead of "Couldn't sign in to the AI service…". Nothing changes without the setting. The copy is static operator text and never includes the provider's message.

Unchanged: classification, fallback and cooldowns. The refusal still counts as `auth`. Known gaps:
- Chat history rebuilds a failed reply with the built-in copy.
- While the key or auth profile cools down after the refusal (30 s, then 1 min, then 5 min), requests fail before reaching the provider and show the built-in message.
- When every model of a fallback chain refuses, the reply and the run result show the last attempt's provider copy, but the run's error event keeps the summary of every attempt it shows today ("All models failed (2): …"), which includes each provider's own message. 2026.10.5 shows the same summary (below).

## Why This Change Was Made

Any 401 or 403 is classified `auth`, and the copy follows the class. A proxy can't make OpenClaw say the balance is empty:
- Rewriting the reply in a `reply_payload_sending` plugin misses the run's error event. Registering that hook also turns off Telegram preview streaming for every reply.
- Sending it as a billing failure would disable the auth profile for 10 minutes to 24 hours, so a top-up wouldn't take effect.

How it works:
- The provider's `errorType`, already on the failed assistant message, now travels on `FailoverError`. It goes through `describeFailoverError`, the reply's failover facts and fallback attempts, so the last attempt of a fallback chain carries it.
- `renderProviderFailureCopy` looks up `failureCopy` for the failed request's provider and error type. The run's error text (`formatUserFacingAssistantErrorText`) and the auto-reply error handler (channel and Control UI replies) use it before the class's copy.
- When profile rotation for an overloaded provider reaches its cap and model fallback takes over, that failure keeps the provider's error type and uses its copy too, so a capped provider that is a chain's last attempt still finds its text.
- Only static operator text is shown:
  - at most 300 characters, so the run error event's 400-character text preview carries it whole;
  - keys are up to 64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`, looked up with `Object.hasOwn`.
- The new field's label goes in `schema.labels.models.ts`, where `main` now keeps the `models.*` labels.

#167341 proposes `messages.failureCopy` keyed by failover reason. This change keys the copy per provider by the provider's own error type instead. A refusal the provider names gets its own text, and real sign-in failures keep theirs.

**Needs a maintainer decision:** this adds a config option. Is per-provider copy keyed by error type the shape you want, or a global map keyed by reason as #167341 proposes?

## Evidence

### Through the CLI, upgrading from the latest stable release

A local harness (not part of this PR) runs `openclaw gateway run` from the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` (npm `latest`), then from this branch's `pnpm build` at `1ed01ac776`, on one state directory. Config changes go through `openclaw doctor --fix` and `openclaw config patch`. One local server stands in for eight OpenAI-compatible providers, and each refuses every request with HTTP 401 and an error type of its own (synthetic: `{"error":{"message":"Your balance is empty. Top up to continue.","type":"insufficient_balance","code":"401"}}`). A backend client sends with `chat.send` and reads the run's `chat` error event and its `agent.wait` result. A refusal cools the key down across restarts, so each check uses a provider nothing has called yet.

1. **Latest stable:** 2026.10.5 shows the built-in copy, and an exhausted fallback chain's error event is the per-attempt summary.
2. **Upgrade with existing settings:** after `doctor --fix`, this branch loads the same config and behaves as before.
3. **Configured refusal:** `config patch` adds `failureCopy` to providers the config already had. The error event and the run result read the operator's text, `failoverReason` stays `auth`, and the provider's message does not appear.
4. **Unconfigured type:** a type the provider's `failureCopy` doesn't name keeps the built-in copy.
5. **Fallback exhausted:** when both candidates refuse, the run result carries the last attempt's provider copy, and the error event keeps the summary (the gap above).

```text
[01] openclaw 2026.10.5 (npm): openclaw gateway run, providers without failureCopy
     chat error event: errorMessage="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="acme-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     PASS acme-proxy refused with insufficient_balance: built-in copy (released behavior)
[02] 2026.10.5: agent released-chain -> echo-proxy, then fallback foxtrot-proxy; both refuse
     chat error event: errorMessage="All models failed (2): echo-proxy/model: 401 Your balance is empty. Top up to continue. (auth) | foxtrot-proxy/model: 401 Your balance is empty. Top up to continue. (auth). Re-authenticate with: openclaw models auth login --provider 'foxtro..."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="foxtrot-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     PASS released behavior: an exhausted chain's error event is the per-attempt summary
[03] stop 2026.10.5: exit 0
[04] this branch (1ed01ac776): openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive: exit 0
[05] this branch: openclaw gateway run, same state directory and config
     chat error event: errorMessage="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="bravo-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     PASS the existing config loads and behaves as before: built-in copy in the event and the run result
[06] stop: exit 0
[07] openclaw config patch (failure-copy): exit 0
[08] this branch: openclaw gateway run with failureCopy on charlie-proxy, beta-proxy and delta-proxy
     chat error event: errorMessage="⚠️ Your prepaid balance is empty. Top it up on the billing page."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="charlie-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ Your prepaid balance is empty. Top it up on the billing page."
     PASS configured refusal: the operator's text in the error event and the run result
     PASS classification stays auth, and the provider's own message is not shown
[09] agent typed -> beta-proxy, which refuses with quota_exceeded (its copy names insufficient_balance)
     chat error event: errorMessage="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="beta-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`."
     PASS unconfigured type: built-in copy
[10] agent chain -> gamma-proxy (no failureCopy), then fallback delta-proxy (failureCopy); both refuse
     chat error event: errorMessage="All models failed (2): gamma-proxy/model: 401 Your balance is empty. Top up to continue. (auth) | delta-proxy/model: 401 Your balance is empty. Top up to continue. (auth). Re-authenticate with: openclaw models auth login --provider 'delta-p..."
     chat error event: errorDetail.provider="delta-proxy" failoverReason="auth"
     agent.wait: status="error" error="⚠️ The backup provider's balance is empty too. Top it up on the billing page."
     PASS fallback exhausted: the run result carries the last attempt's provider copy

[11] stop: exit 0

prs.title: fix: restore the Gateway when Doctor receives SIGHUP
prs.body:
Related: #182683

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the managed Gateway remaining stopped when a terminal hangup (SIGHUP) interrupts `openclaw doctor --fix` during repair.

## User Impact

Doctor settles admitted repair work and restores the managed Gateway it stopped before exiting on SIGINT, SIGTERM, or SIGHUP; restoration failures retain the existing actionable warning. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main already restores the Gateway in the existing SIGTERM repair/progress, approval, and restoration tests. The remaining gap in the interruption contract was SIGHUP: [Doctor’s signal installer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/721cdadccb93b9c185d367f0e8082b2338553c81/src/cli/signal-exit-barrier.ts#L177) did not register it, and the shared exit gate could not preserve its exit code. The new process regression reproduces that gap through the real command registration, maintenance, archive-repair, and restoration owners. The original 2026.10.7 SIGTERM incident has not been reproduced or proven resolved by this patch; this PR completes the SIGHUP part of the requested interruption invariant. The requested closing reference is retained for the maintainer landing decision; ClawSweeper recommends changing it to a related reference for that distinct incident.

Doctor now registers SIGHUP with its existing signal owner and the common drain preserves exit code 129. The updater can use that same path, removing its separate HUP workaround. Service selection, live ownership checks, restoration failure reporting, and launchd/systemd/Windows adapters remain with their existing owners. Candidate Doctor must contain this fix; it cannot change an older Doctor process already running. SIGKILL and process loss remain uncatchable.

## Evidence

- Base `721cdadccb93b`: new SIGHUP repair regression failed with only `stopped` and `archive-started` recorded, with no resource cleanup or service restart. All seven existing interruption cases passed, including SIGTERM during repair, approval, and restoration.
- Base: new one-shot exit regression failed with exit 143 instead of 129. Its existing proxy-command child test also timed out on the unchanged base; this is a separate local failure.
- Fixed: all 8 cases in `doctor-maintenance.interruption.process.test.ts` pass; the SIGHUP case records cancellation, stores closed, exactly one restart, healthy verification, and exit 129. File wall time: 107.16s; new process case: 10.771s. Existing compiled process startup dominates this suite.
- Fixed: the new `one-shot-exit.test.ts` SIGHUP case passes (19ms); the file has 17 passed / 1 pre-existing proxy child timeout (42.72s wall time). `signal-exit-barrier.test.ts`: 10 passed. `update-command-mutable-signals.test.ts`: 15 passed / 3 local 60-second timeouts (publishing-compensation, rollback-compensation, accepted-compensation); no assertions or timeouts were weakened. The combined signal/updater invocation took 755.00s including runtime preparation. These timeout results are retained as unresolved local evidence, not claimed as passing or attributed to main CI.
- Commands used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with the explicit files above. Changed-file core lint, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` pass. Codex autoreview: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. GitHub Codex review and ClawSweeper found no actionable code defects on `b73be46f4de2a`; ClawSweeper’s scope and live-proof notes are addressed above and below.
- Diagnostic rerun of only the proxy timeout with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` passed (28.597s test, 36.15s file wall time); the original pinned-Bun timeout on both base and fix remains recorded.
- Fresh main `aaecd52e6bffc` was merged without conflicts; the five-file patch is unchanged from reviewed commit `129778f1404d0`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133439474) passed on `b73be46f4de2a`: 54 successful jobs, 26 skipped, zero failed; workflow wall time 1394s. No CI rerun was needed.
- Per the maintainer proof policy for this repair, live Gateway/channel e2e, latest-stable upgrade runs, and Crabbox/Testbox leases were intentionally skipped; native service effects use synthetic adapters, and PR CI provides broad proof. No operator Gateway was touched.

Author simplification removed the updater's obsolete HUP branch and consolidated signal code selection. Exact production delta: +18/-19 (net -1); tests: +15/-7 (net +8); docs: +3/-3 (net 0).

prs.title: perf(ai): avoid loading Google SDK for generic Gateway work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An OpenAI-only Gateway eagerly initializes the Google SDK through the generic AI transport barrel. Catalog listing also restores that dependency later through Anthropic history's import of the broad provider transport SDK, even when no history is imported and no Google generation helper runs.

## User Impact

Generic transport and catalog work no longer load the unused Google SDK graph. Across two complete, CPU-swapped ten-minute dist Gateway pairs, the fix removes 71 main-isolate scripts and 1.869 MiB of retained code on average. Startup and first-turn means improve. Existing public Plugin SDK Google helpers and provider request behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the two Google generation helpers from the generic AI transport barrel into the existing private-entry pattern, with aligned package exports, build entries, TypeScript paths, and native source resolution. Keep their existing Plugin SDK exports. Anthropic catalog history now imports its identical canonical zero-usage helper from the already-resident shared-stream SDK entry.

Extend the existing heap rig with a private main-isolate script census, separate precise coverage, binary byte counts, idle observations, and synchronized starts. Fix the startup benchmark's silent exit through a symlinked scripts directory using the existing entrypoint owner. The diagnostics runbook matches the rig's high default ports.

## Measurement

Fixed baseline `751f8910c9017a25cb128fcbe15cfd36baf7194c` versus that baseline plus this PR's reviewed application patch, using isolated dist/package trees and equal instrumentation. These measurements are not full builds of the later rebased head; exact-head CI validates that integration. Synthetic state only: 500 sessions, four clients, two agents, and text/code/subagent/artifact/session-churn/cron work. Each of four windows completed 29 successful turns, six children, six artifacts, and five cron runs with matching receipts/history/counts.

Two concurrent ten-minute pairs used one exclusive slot, interleaved CPUs with swapped placement/launch order, and the unchanged shared guard. Timing has no precise coverage; retained snapshots are serial after five natural idle observations, with capture order reversed. Source bytes and retained code are distinct measurements; retained totals count unique code objects rather than adding overlapping script groups.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Paired mean delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Main scripts, both pairs | 8,312 | 8,241 | −71 (−0.85%) |
| Script source MiB | 73.965 | 72.329 | −1.636 (−2.21%) |
| Retained code MiB | 228.969 | 227.100 | −1.869 (−0.82%) |
| First turn, ms; n=2/side | 2,319.5 | 2,149.5 | −170 (−7.33%) |
| Startup completion, ms; n=6/side | 20,568.966 | 20,424.458 | −144.508 (−0.70%) |
| Startup CPU, ms; n=6/side | 34,833.333 | 34,000 | −833.333 (−2.39%) |

Retained-code pairs: **229.274269 → 227.416664 MiB** (−1.857605), **228.663689 → 226.784195 MiB** (−1.879494). First turns: **3,043 → 2,759 ms**, **1,596 → 1,540 ms**.

Six process-cold startup pairs use the existing `teamBoot` fixture: 5,000 sessions, eight agents, and 44 synthetic startup plugins. Prepared fixtures are reused symmetrically without disk-cache eviction; build-qualified worker caches may warm after pair one. No samples are trimmed. Startup completion includes successful health/readiness probes and seeded `sessions.list`:

| Pair | Baseline ms | Candidate ms | Delta ms | CPU ms baseline → candidate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 22,506.088 | 22,368.030 | −138.058 | 36,000 → 36,000 |
| 2 | 20,073.699 | 19,914.180 | −159.519 | 34,000 → 33,000 |
| 3 | 19,967.132 | 19,767.863 | −199.269 | 34,000 → 33,000 |
| 4 | 20,038.980 | 20,017.649 | −21.331 | 35,000 → 34,000 |
| 5 | 20,561.181 | 20,309.500 | −251.681 | 35,000 → 34,000 |
| 6 | 20,266.715 | 20,169.527 | −97.188 | 35,000 → 34,000 |

Readyz mean: 20,568.912 → 20,424.407 ms. Seeded RPC mean: 20,507.675 → 20,384.412 ms; pair four is +2.020 ms (+0.010%), the other five improve. These sample counts support paired means, not tail-percentile claims. CPU counters have 1-second granularity. This is representative synthetic runtime breadth, not the exact private production configuration or its full code-residency graph. Cumulative main GC time and promotion were not available in this fixture; no such improvement is claimed.

### Discovery and idle behavior

The separate coverage census classifies 8,316 scripts: 3,184 with observed main execution, 5,128 without observed execution in the window, one confirmed worker implementation leak, two mixed native-node plugin entries, and one Wasm script without execution coverage. Largest retained scripts include actual main-thread agent/tool/protocol owners; inactivity in this window alone does not justify removing them.

The initial candidate only split the generic barrel. Its complete coverage run found 120 catalog listings restored Google residency, with no history-import or Google-helper calls; retained code was neutral (250,264,424 → 250,190,872 bytes). Its incomplete timing pair was stopped and excluded. The caller migration above fixes the second edge; all reported paired results use that complete fix.

Between idle minutes one and five, bytecode+metadata bytes were 15,679,976 → 15,680,984 and 15,644,776 → 15,664,512 on baseline; 15,608,784 → 15,609,792 and 15,550,256 → 15,570,440 on candidate. Code+metadata also rose slightly in all four windows. There was no aggregate idle reclamation. Node 26.12.1/V8 14.6.202.34 defaults enable bytecode flushing after six GC ages, but disable time-based and baseline-code flushing. No forced GC occurred in these observations; this does not prove that V8 can never flush idle code.

## Evidence

- Import regressions fail before and pass after the generic-barrel and catalog fixes. Google helpers (46), Google transport (115), native resolver (8), heap rig/census (6), startup benchmark (44), Anthropic history (12), and SDK identity (1) tests pass. Wasm-byte-count and symlink-CLI regressions were also red before their fixes.
- Changed-file lint/format, export collision, eager-import closure, PR-wrapper closure, and CI planner guards pass (178 tests in the latter guard group).
- Dist builds pass. Original baseline/candidate builds share five inherited UI `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` warnings; the final candidate introduces none and has zero runtime import cycles.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): accepted integration findings fixed; complete final-head review clean. The configured route refusal did not result in configuration changes. Hosted code review also completed on `d7885b8abe28c31c0636087cc5cf68b113f8cb79` without findings.
- No Testbox lease was used under the lane's light-local/PR-CI rule. Builds and measurements ran in the isolated sandbox. No production Gateway or state was changed.

Exact-head CI completed with 105 successful CheckRuns and two successful commit statuses. The sole failing test job and aggregate CI gate are inherited: both Docker memory-store variants in `test/scripts/tsdown-config.test.ts` fail with missing `@openclaw/fs-safe` from `file-lock-B53vmz6H.mjs`, identical on scheduled main `52068cf86d6a78fe05625f1d771554ad4d87e21d`. The unchanged dependency chain was introduced by #182530. [Main evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40134490303/job/120993216399), [PR evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40135235227/job/120995644163). A canceled Labeler has a successful replacement. No CI rerun was requested; landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception.

## Change Size

The prescribed non-test LOC filter reports **+237/−17 = +220**: +10 application/package declaration lines, +181 diagnostic code lines, and +29 diagnostic README lines. The private entry and aligned declarations preserve the existing SDK contract; the catalog caller migration is LOC-neutral. The requested census and measurement support account for the diagnostic growth. No runtime cache, fallback, or duplicate implementation is added. This explicitly requested boundary repair delivers a small, repeatable residency reduction without a measured startup or first-turn regression.

prs.title: perf(sessions): share immutable replica publication entries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session metadata notifications clone the complete committed entry into the actor replica even when its producer already owns an immutable snapshot.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Session updates avoid allocating and freezing another full entry graph; snapshot mutation protection and publication freshness checks remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain `prepared.fullEntry` directly. Native producers already freeze their decoded/committed snapshots. Decoded worker facts still pass through the replica's existing deep-freeze boundary, as they already do on first installation. Mutable caller results remain separate from retained publication facts. No additional cache, configuration, schema, or compatibility path.

Runtime production LOC delta: 0 (+1/−1), removing the redundant clone expression. The other changes are a 37-line native regression, 243 lines of rerunnable benchmark tooling, and 29 lines documenting that workload.

## Evidence

The new regression fails on unchanged main (`721cdadccb93`) because published and retained entries have equal serialized contents but different identities. With the change, all 36 focused replica, entry-residency, and row-publication tests pass; the new regression takes 429 ms. The three-file invocation takes 201.7 s on the busy host, mostly compiled-worker preparation. Both import-closure guards pass (22 tests, 123.0 s), and the export-name collision guard passes. The targeted core typecheck passes. Formatting and targeted lint pass. No Testbox lease was used.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped-clean, no actionable P1/P2 findings. The configured autoreview route refused its provider/config preflight; configuration was unchanged. The reviewer inspected publication ownership, decoded worker freezing, freshness/invalidation, caller mutability, the regression, and the benchmark's scope.

### Deterministic notification/install diagnostic

32 prepared frozen full entries, passed through the real row-change dispatcher and replica installation owner:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full-entry clones | 32 | 0 |
| Full-entry serialized clone bytes | 1,192,364 | 0 |
| All serialized clone bytes | 1,222,082 | 29,718 |
| Shared full-entry identities | 0/32 | 32/32 |

This removes 37,261 bytes of full-entry copying per install, and 97.57% of total serialized clone payload bytes. The separate sharing-projection clones remain unchanged. Serialized payload size is not V8 allocation. Both versions preserve exact contents and frozen nested values; mutation attempts are rejected.

### Isolated built Gateway

Synthetic fixture: 10,000 sessions, 8,000 settled child runs, 2,000 archived rows, 30,000 participants, and 40 configured plugins. The baseline built Gateway completes four measured mock turns, 119 connects, 119 `sessions.list`, 118 `chat.history`, and 118 `sessions.diff` calls, delivering 252 session events, then shuts down cleanly. The reported full-entry notification stack reproduces with 50 clones / 764,465 serialized bytes across startup, warmup, and the measured flow. The candidate completes four primary turns, 29 connects, 30 `sessions.list`, 31 `chat.history`, 32 `sessions.diff`, and four `agent.wait` calls, delivering 208 session events. The targeted full-entry notification clone path is absent: 0 calls / 0 bytes. Both runs exit successfully, close their children, and release their ports. RPC counts differ because that background traffic is time-bounded on a busy host; this proves functional flow and clone removal, not a full-Gateway timing improvement.

The full `pnpm build` passes (22m39s), and the candidate `pnpm build runtime` passes (6m14s). Baseline runtime bundle source was captured before the one-line edit; candidate Gateway proof is pinned to `cad78cf05f0d`. The production owner bytes are identical on the current rebased head; subsequent benchmark-only repairs do not change the Gateway code. A baseline memory-core standing-intent maintenance warning reports an unresolved source-worker module; it does not prevent the measured flow and is outside the changed owner.

### Paired measurement protocol

Declared before timed pairs: 32 prepared frozen entries, 100,000 installations per side, concurrent baseline/candidate with synchronized warm starts, swapped interleaved CPUs, one exclusive quiet-slot lock and shared host guard. Allocation sampling runs separately; CPU, latency and GC acceptance use untraced passes. Accept exact immutable contents, reduced copying/allocation, and no material CPU or tail regression. Apply sample-count and absolute-delta thresholds: p99 needs 1,000 observations, p95 needs 200, major-GC tails below 50 collections are context; sub-millisecond pause/tail shifts are context when allocation/CPU improves materially, and total GC needs at least +1 ms/operation to be a material per-operation regression. Adverse GC/promotion requires matched A/A controls before rejection.

The final paired results support landing. All four pairs completed without interruption or exclusion. The runtime owner bytes measured below are unchanged on the current rebased head.

The harness emits 32 prepared frozen native-style entries through the real row-change dispatcher/replica installation path. Each entry includes saved instructions and nested plugin results. Exact contents, frozen nested values, and mutation rejection pass on both sides. Shared entry identities rise from 0/32 to 32/32. This isolates notification installation; producer decoding, worker cold-freezing, Gateway traffic, RPC latency, and promotion are not measured here. No claim about whole-production allocation share follows from this owner workload.

| Metric | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Mean paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Full-entry clones/install | 1 | 0 | −100% |
| Full-entry serialized clone bytes/install | 37,261.375 | 0 | −100% |
| All structured clones/install | 2 | 1 | −50% |
| All serialized clone bytes/install | 38,190.063 | 928.688 | −97.57% |
| Sampled allocation bytes/install | 59,188.010 | 17,614.735 | −70.24% |
| CPU ms / 100,000 installs | 3,014.877 | 1,552.717 | −48.49% |
| Elapsed ms / 100,000 installs | 2,745.705 | 1,280.878 | −53.35% |
| Total GC ms / 100,000 installs | 134.924 | 38.972 | −71.06% |
| Total GC ms/install | 0.001349244 | 0.000389719 | −0.000959526 ms/install |

Serialized clone bytes are copied payload sizes, not V8 allocation. Allocation is a separate sampling pass with objects collected by minor/major GC included; its timing and GC values do not gate. Allocation pairs are 59,173.681→17,689.241 and 59,202.338→17,540.229 bytes/install (−70.11%, −70.37%).

#### Untraced paired tails and GC

All installation latency tails have 100,000 samples per side. Loop p95/p99 qualify by sample count; scavenge p95 qualifies, while scavenge p99 and all major-GC tails are context only.

| Metric | Pair 1 baseline → candidate | Pair 2 baseline → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU ms | 3,030.596 → 1,512.241 | 2,999.157 → 1,593.192 |
| Install p95 ms | 0.027421 → 0.013941 | 0.027731 → 0.017607 |

| Loop max ms | 5.705727 → 6.635519 | 5.287935 → 4.304895 |
| Scavenge count | 237 → 396 | 237 → 370 |
| Scavenge total ms | 122.937876 → 30.070556 | 135.399600 → 30.665944 |
| Scavenge p95 ms | 0.864238 → 0.103485 | 0.939362 → 0.145479 |
| Scavenge p99 ms (context) | 1.117240 → 0.196295 | 1.107890 → 0.231148 |
| Scavenge max ms | 1.332940 → 0.295344 | 1.196750 → 0.274272 |
| Major count | 2 → 2 | 2 → 3 |
| Major total ms | 5.398030 → 8.476360 | 5.207820 → 7.626330 |
| Major p95/p99/max ms (context) | 2.944380 → 5.947800 | 2.867500 → 3.026100 |
| Incremental marking count | 2 → 2 | 2 → 3 |
| Incremental marking total ms | 0.456576 → 0.448955 | 0.448975 → 0.655557 |

| Overall max GC pause ms | 2.944380 → 5.947800 | 2.867500 → 3.026100 |

No minor-mark-sweep collections occurred. Major collections are below 50 per side and remain context. Total GC falls in both pairs; both GC maxima stay below the 50 ms safeguard. Loop p99 improves by 1.240064 and 1.149952 ms. Loop maxima move oppositely with signed mean −0.026624 ms; no adverse qualifying metric remains. No rejection or A/A escalation is warranted by these measurements under v5.6.


CPU means fall by 1,462.160 ms per 100,000 installs; sampled allocation falls by 41,573.275 bytes/install; total GC falls by 95.952 ms per 100,000 installs. All relative changes above use the mean of the paired changes.

Host context: five-second CPU samples cover all four windows; mean busy CPU is 8.98%, 9.46%, 15.22%, and 6.99%, including benchmark work, with no steal. These are context, not exclusions. The measurements ran on 2026-10-24 at 21:44–21:45 UTC, outside the predeclared deployment exclusion. The shared guard did not interrupt any run. The task-owned remote sandbox and monitor have been removed.

The first CI run found three benchmark-only TS18048 diagnostics because an optional-chain assertion did not narrow the database identity. A reviewed explicit `identity &&` assertion fixes that without changing runtime acceptance; `check-test-types` now passes on `a494ed3ba0e844ab7e7c91040b05e84037d45229`. Production owner bytes remain unchanged from the passing Gateway replay and focused tests.

Conflict repair: rebased onto main `83c4da899710` as `b3dea40099bf4d3511b5dd93f66019d14b5d61b0` because another benchmark appended documentation at the same README location. Both sections are preserved. Production, regression, and benchmark files are byte-for-byte unchanged from the reviewed/tested head; the README passes formatting and `git diff --check`. The code review on that head completed without findings; CI passed all checks except PostgreSQL conformance (2/3).

A second README append conflict required rebasing onto main `8c6ad0edc3c9` as `6b22c1fe4f34f48b0337fec3c3663712a85802ef`. The listener section now precedes an existing section to avoid repeated end-of-file conflicts. Runtime, regression, and benchmark files remain byte-for-byte unchanged; formatting and diff checks pass.

CI investigation: [run 40136113132](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136113132/job/120998277053) failed seven interactive onboarding cases in `src/infra/database-engine/interactive-setup.integration.test.ts`. Each child Gateway failed to import the omitted `runtime/standalone-runtime-profile.mjs` from `packages/llm-core/src/validation.ts`. The fixture root-file list omits that module. prs.title: fix(gateway): serve readiness probes through trusted proxies
prs.body:
Closes #182798

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: reverse-proxy readiness and startup checks return `403 proxy_attribution_required` when a configured trusted proxy cannot supply a forwarded client address.

## User Impact

Operators can health-check healthy Gateway backends from Traefik, ALB target groups, and other trusted proxies without fabricating an `X-Forwarded-For` header. Public probe responses stay aggregate-only; detailed readiness/startup diagnostics still require a local or authenticated caller, and every non-probe route retains proxy-attribution rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Headerless health checks have no client identity to attribute. The Gateway now serves the existing bounded ready/startup handlers before rejecting unattributable proxy ingress. `/livez` is also accepted as a liveness alias, matching the path reported in the issue and the documented liveness behavior.

## Evidence

- Base-red: the new trusted-proxy regression failed with `GET /ready: expected 403 to be 503`; see `contributions/pr-182798-evidence/base-red.log`.
- Fixed: the regression covers GET/HEAD for `/ready`, `/readyz`, `/startup`, `/startupz`, `/health`, `/healthz`, and `/livez`, including reduced bodies and `Content-Length`; a protected node route still returns `403 proxy_attribution_required`.
- Real listener proof: the shipped `startGatewayServer` was started on a loopback TCP port with a trusted loopback proxy entry. Requests carried a loopback `X-Forwarded-For` value, so ingress was classified as unattributable. All 14 GET/HEAD probes returned 200; `/ready` and `/readyz` returned `{"ready":true}`, `/startup` and `/startupz` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"started"}`, and the liveness aliases returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`.
- The same listener rejected the protected `/api/nodes/watch/node-1` request with `403` and `proxy_attribution_required`, proving the probe exception did not widen authenticated routes.

```json
{
  "entrypoint": "shipped startGatewayServer with a real loopback TCP listener",
  "probeCount": 14,
  "probeStatuses": { "GET": 200, "HEAD": 200 },
  "protectedRoute": {
    "path": "/api/nodes/watch/node-1",
    "status": 403,
    "type": "proxy_attribution_required"
  }
}
```

- Focused suites: `server-http.probe.test.ts`, `ingress-attribution.test.ts`, and `auth.test.ts` passed, 83 tests total; see `contributions/pr-182798-evidence/final-tests.log`.
- `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `check:changed` passed all runnable gates. Its typecheck lanes cannot run on this host because the bundled `tsgo` requires glibc 2.29 while the host provides 2.28; the dead-export lane also reports the existing repository-wide Knip baseline unrelated to these files. See `contributions/pr-182798-evidence/check-changed.log`.
