prs.title: fix(msteams): a code block in a list item swallows the following items
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Microsoft Teams, a reply with numbered steps that contain code blocks loses the steps after the first code block, when the model formats them as a normal Markdown list.

`formatMSTeamsMarkdown` (`extensions/msteams/src/format.ts`) writes a code block as fence, code, fence and adds a line break after the closing fence only when quoted text follows. Inside a list item the next item follows the code block directly, so it lands on the closing fence line (```` ```2. Run: ````). A closing fence with text after it does not close the block, so Markdown readers keep the rest of the reply inside the code block.

## User Impact

Step-by-step answers ("1. Install … 2. Start … 3. Open …") are among the most common replies. In Teams the second step and its command render as code inside the first block, and the third step vanishes into the language label of an empty block. The same happens with bullets (```` ```• Step two ````), with text that continues an item after its code block, and with a table inside a list item when `tableMode` is `code` (everything after it renders as code). Normal replies, streaming finals, proactive sends and edits all go through this formatter.

## Why This Change Was Made

The formatter already adds the line break when quoted text follows a code block (`format.test.ts` asserts `not.toContain("```> ")`), and code blocks outside lists get one from the IR. A code block followed by any text now gets the same line break. The fixture `raw table after list-fence outdent` pinned the glued fence (```` ```>   | A | B | ````, where markdown-it hides the table header inside the fence); it now expects the fence on its own line.

## Evidence

**Real behavior: a built Gateway delivers an agent reply to a loopback Bot Framework Connector.** I ran `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --bind loopback --auth none` (which builds `dist` first) once on this branch (`05909f3c4`) and once on its base (`3fe99086c0`). The base run used the same checkout with only `extensions/msteams/src/format.ts` reverted. The bundled msteams plugin ran on the private QA runtime that the Teams QA lane uses: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1`, plus an `--import` bootstrap that sets `Symbol.for("openclaw.msteams.privateQaRuntime")` (connector URL, nonce, bot token) as `extensions/msteams/src/qa/adapter.runtime.ts` does. Connector requests therefore went to a local server that records them, instead of `smba.trafficmanager.net`. The config had `channels.msteams` with the QA lane's app and tenant ids, `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, and a `models.providers` entry (`api: "openai-completions"`) pointing at a local stub that streams this fixed answer:

````
To get started:

1. Install the dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```
2. Start the server:
   ```bash
   npm start
   ```
3. Open http://localhost:3000
````

An allowlisted user sent one DM to `/api/messages`. The agent answered through the normal reply path, and the Connector received four authorized requests per run: typing, two streaming updates, and the final `message` activity (`streaminfo: final`). That final activity, as recorded (no credentials or private endpoints in it), and how markdown-it (the parser `format.test.ts` uses) reads its text:

````
base 3fe99086c0: POST /qa/v3/conversations/19:qa-proof-dm@thread.tacv2/activities, type message, streaminfo final
text:        "To get started:\n\n1. Install the dependencies:\n```\nnpm install\n```2. Start the server:\n```\nnpm start\n```3. Open http://localhost:3000"
code blocks: "npm install\n```2. Start the server:\n" and "" (info string "3. Open http://localhost:3000")
list items:  "Install the dependencies:"

this PR 05909f3c4: same request
text:        "To get started:\n\n1. Install the dependencies:\n```\nnpm install\n```\n2. Start the server:\n```\nnpm start\n```\n3. Open http://localhost:3000"
code blocks: "npm install\n" and "npm start\n"
list items:  "Install the dependencies:", "Start the server:", "Open http://localhost:3000"
````

On the base, step 2 is rendered as code inside the first block, `npm start` becomes plain text, and step 3 ends up as the info string of an empty block. Both runs drop the `bash` label and the item indentation; that is existing formatter behavior and this PR does not change it.

**In process (the earlier check):** the same reply through `renderReplyPayloadsToMessages` (core chunker, `tableMode: "code"`) and `buildMSTeamsMessageActivity` places the closing fence the same way: ```` ```2. Start the server: ```` on main, and on its own line with this PR.

Tests: new `ends a code block inside a list item before the next item` (`format.test.ts`) fails on main. `format.test.ts` 14, `messenger.test.ts` 20, `reply-stream-controller.test.ts` 18 and `send.threaded-attachments.test.ts` 12 pass. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the changed files.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The state-read transport tests repeat command-by-command snapshot and byte-accounting scenarios after those operations moved to generic structural owners in #169379 and #169754.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. This removes 17 redundant cases from two test files (41 → 24, −41.5%) and 215 net test lines (1,104 → 889).

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep four representative capture cases for nested Unicode fields, arrays, booleans/numbers, prepared/queued mutation, and ACP batches. Remove command-name variants that exercise the same generic structured clone and byte walker. All lifecycle, authority, storage, migration, and PostgreSQL proof remains. There are no production changes or new seams.

The owner audit covered 36 test files and 340 expanded cases, including a final bounded session/transcript pass. This batch is smaller than the 30–150 target: the remaining worker tests protect distinct failures and were retained rather than used to fill a quota.

<details>
<summary>Removed rows and surviving proof</summary>

All removed rows exercise the same generic command snapshot and byte-charge owner; their mocked replies do not test domain reads.

| Removed rows | Retained capture/charging proof |
| --- | --- |
| onboardingRecommendations.read; workspace.snapshot; pluginBlob.lookup/entries; sandboxRegistry.get/runtimeIds; updateRuns.get (7) | githubPublications.sharedObservation: nested objects and UTF-8 selectors |
| updateRuns.list (1) | updateRuns.reconciliationCandidates: arrays, booleans, numeric fields and mutation |
| subagents.runs descendants/maintenance; skills.library.manifests (3) | acpSessions.metadata batch: arrays of objects, nested arrays and optional entries |
| abbreviated audit.run.inspect queries (2) | Full audit.run.inspect query: prepared capture and mutation while queued |
| mcpOAuth.statuses; userPreferences.values (2) | acpSessions.metadata batch: complete batch capture and incremental byte charging |
| workerPlacements.changeSnapshot; agentDeletionJournal.status (2) | Retained generic transport tests above, through the same captureOpenClawStateReadSource owner |

</details>

## Evidence

Acceptance rule recorded before the first run: run the two changed suites on pinned base `a31e54a90d6` and candidate; count 41 → 24 expanded cases with zero lost distinct contracts and all retained tests passing. No new static findings. Warm timing requires the campaign lock, load <24, at least five interleaved samples per revision; cold runs stay separate. Report median/p95/range; a >20% regression stops acceptance. If the host stays busy for 60 minutes, report counts and test outcomes with no wall-time claim.

Codex review found no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings. Formatting, type-aware core lint and diff whitespace checks pass. The initial default lint command attempted plugin declarations and refused the external virtual store; the supported core configuration passed without that unrelated preparation. Focused baseline: 41/41 cases pass; candidate: 24/24 pass. Exact-head CI run 40135535259 passed changed tests, types, lint, source contracts, architecture and baseline ratchets. PostgreSQL shards 1 and 3 passed; shard 2 failed seven unrelated interactive-setup cases because its synthetic runtime omitted standalone-runtime-profile.mjs. The maintainer has attributed this to the main-branch fixture regression introduced by #182856 (4a38dbdb6b1): createSourceRuntime omits the newly required root file. The failing test and fixture helper are untouched by this PR; their blobs match the CI main parent. The coordinator has authorized inherited-failure landing while the separate repair is in progress. Exact failure: [run 40135535259, job 120996441483](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40135535259/job/120996441483); the aggregate ci-gate is red for the same failure. Every other executed CI job passed. This lane does not claim a separate main execution. Local baseline/candidate dead-code comparisons are identical: 48 dependency, 63 unused-file, and 1,233 export finding lines, zero new findings. Refreshed census covers 2,691 other open main-target PRs with zero overlapping files, so no merge-tree comparison is applicable. No SQL harness is needed for this test-only change.


Timing fallback: after more than 60 minutes waiting (21:41:48–22:41:52 UTC on 2026-10-24), host load remained above the required <24 threshold and no qualified samples were collected. Correctness-only Vitest durations were 101.41 seconds baseline and 24.96 seconds candidate, but these runs had different cache state and heavy host contention; they are not an A/B result. Acceptance uses counts and passing retained contracts. No speedup, median/p95, or CPU saving is claimed.

prs.title: fix(plugins): reject pipe-backed authoring metadata without blocking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin metadata builds and validation hanging when `package.json` or `openclaw.plugin.json` is a FIFO with no writer.

## User Impact

Authoring commands reject pipes and special files promptly without rewriting project metadata. Regular files, supported symlinks, valid Unicode, and malformed-JSON diagnostics retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared authoring reader resolves symlinks and delegates admission to `readRegularFileSync`. It also uses `decodeUtf8Input` for the existing strict UTF-8 requirement, removing the duplicate byte check and the proposed custom descriptor-management code.

Thanks to @Leon-SK668 for the original fix and Linux CLI reproduction.

## Evidence

- Red on the unchanged main reader: the special-device package regression reached JSON parsing instead of rejecting the nonregular input. Green with the fix.
- Real-filesystem FIFO regressions cover both metadata files, without I/O mocks, and verify that the pipe and sibling metadata remain unchanged.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/plugins-authoring-command.utf8.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all 7 tests pass, including existing malformed UTF-8 refusal, metadata preservation, and valid Unicode controls. Wrapper wall time 25.37 s; Vitest duration 13.10 s. These tests import a synthetic plugin through the production build/validation owners.
- Production +5/-6 (net -1), tests +33, documentation +3.

The contributor's built Linux CLI evidence at `c023e6b5c3a04c8dddb7a2c042ba5d158ea42b62` reports baseline timeouts, prompt FIFO refusals after the fix, successful regular-file builds, and validation through a linked package file. This revision was exercised through real filesystem/build/validation owners; the built CLI and live Gateway were not rerun because they require a separate full build, and this path does not use a model or channel.

Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and diff checks passed. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defects. Additional authoring controls passed for stable JSON and malformed JSON. The symlink-root permission control fails identically with the unchanged reader and this change on macOS: directory mode is `01770`, expected `03770` (`plugins-authoring-command.test.ts:564`). This reader does not change directory permissions; the failure is retained as baseline evidence rather than weakened.

After merging current main, the final diff remained byte-identical to the reviewed candidate. All 7 encoding and special-file tests passed again (21.09 s wrapper wall time; 12.14 s Vitest duration).

Known diagnostic limitation: the canonical reader's nonregular-file error does not name which metadata file was rejected. The P3 suggestion to add authoring-specific error wrapping is left as a follow-up to keep this fix at the shared admission boundary; FIFO refusal and file preservation are covered above. Fresh built-CLI proof remains unrun as noted above.

prs.title: fix: bound stalled session archive and reconciliation work
prs.body:
Related: #176080

## What Problem This Solves

Stuck archive work can hold its FIFO indefinitely, and timed-out archive or transcript-reconciliation workers can retain native/database custody forever if termination never finishes. This completes the reporter's requested bounded retirement and recovery through the existing Gateway service lifecycle.

## User Impact

Archive admission is bounded to 128 outstanding claims. Active archive and reconciliation tasks request retirement after 180000ms. FIFO and database ownership remain held until physical settlement; expiration never admits overlapping replacement work.

If native settlement remains pending after the existing 5000ms retirement grace, the Gateway recovery owner verifies its live native service and Node command, then requests forced fresh-process recovery through the existing shutdown and hard-exit path. Required fresh-process recovery cannot fall back to an in-process restart. Concurrent requests coalesce and a worker that settles during verification cancels recovery. Unmanaged, external-supervisor, embedded, disabled-respawn or unavailable-native-service instances remain report-only.

The accepted native recovery records and awaits the existing boot-lifecycle completion before shutdown watchdogs or teardown. That native reason survives forced process death, so a successor with another stuck worker within five minutes remains report-only. The existing consumed boot ID prevents a later generic shutdown deadline overwriting the native reason.

Native systemd capability is prepared before workers start: lazy dependency initialization otherwise calls Node's diagnostic-report API, which waits for the stuck worker and deadlocks recovery. Actual service/Node verification remains live at recovery time.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair reuses the archive FIFO, scoped archive worker, reconciliation WorkerTaskPool and Gateway process lifecycle. Schemas, canonical transcript bytes, retention and final archive-publication rules are unchanged. Whole-process death may leave an unreferenced staging artifact; no new orphan-cleanup policy is introduced. Existing best-effort boot-history persistence policy is preserved.

## Evidence

Final source and actual runtime build: `989b30680025e029885e77e6aeefb3c1cc7626a5`.

[Immutable evidence index, complete logs, drivers, receipts, hashes and limitations](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/README.md).

- **Permanent archive recovery:** real native fsync remains blocked through the unchanged 180-second budget and five-second grace. FIFO/native/staging custody remains held. The service replaces PID 629111 with 632652 without releasing the fault; both archive retries match exact canonical rows, retained history is readable and SQLite integrity passes.
- **Forced-death cooldown RED/GREEN:** the pre-repair production baseline kills its successor again 225.2 seconds after the first death and queues another service restart. Final head records the native planned-restart row durably while the old process is still alive. After its physical death, the successor holds a second permanent native fsync for 205.125 seconds without restarting, logs the five-minute report-only cooldown, and retains native custody and canonical rows. [Baseline failure](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/native-baseline/cooldown-successor.json), [pre-kill durable row](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/native-archive/durable-native-recovery-before-kill.json), [successor result](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/native-archive/cooldown-successor.json).
- **Permanent reconciliation recovery:** startup SQLite pread stays blocked, and the durable lease/canonical rows remain held without cleanup overlap. After physical death, PID 629566 is replaced by 632844; the dead lease is reclaimed, successor reconciliation and authenticated history rebuild the index, and canonical rows and SQLite integrity remain intact. A separate pre-fault credential migration restart is explicitly distinguished in the receipts.
- **Official stable upgrade:** verified npm `2026.10.6` creates two conversations/four canonical rows and non-default settings. Candidate Doctor succeeds. Both candidate boots retain every original JSON/compressed transcript byte and selected settings; authenticated history works, and a third conversation's two new rows survive another clean restart. [Stable package identity](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/stable-install/install.receipt.json), [upgrade/restart receipt](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/stable-upgrade/upgrade-v2.receipt.json), [final settings/history/integrity](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/1dfe0de7623a8ef25ed67a11dbbb807a90382f23/cooldown-upgrade/stable-upgrade/candidate-restart-v2-integrity.json).
- The new ordering regression fails before the repair and passes after; all six runtime-unavailable cases pass. Scoped type-aware core lint, config-cli types, formatting and diff checks pass. Independent P0-P2 review of the final delta is scoped-clean, with its context/execution limitations retained. Earlier custody, retirement, FIFO, import-closure and service-recovery validation remains linked in the evidence index.
- Failed fixture admission, a lint prerequisite timeout, and the first upgrade comparison's null-prototype-object mismatch are retained and explained. The corrected upgrade comparison normalizes representation while still comparing every original byte; no product code or expected data was changed for that proof correction. Final native scenarios use unchanged production timeouts and never release injected faults to obtain a passing result.

The actual main merge conflict is resolved using exact current-main hook-fixture bytes; that fixture is no longer part of this PR's diff. The final cooldown repair adds 10 production lines and 48 test lines. Permanent recovery and its cooldown remain one coherent availability repair.

## Maintainer Decision

The contributor recommends bounded admission, retirement and verified-service recovery. Upstream acceptance of the fixed limits and automatic escalation remains outstanding: overload can be rejected and slow healthy work can be retired. This PR does not claim authority to grant that owner decision.

The incident's underlying memory-growth cause is not established by this availability repair. Final-head CI and ClawSweeper's verdict remain separate gates, not implied by evidence publication.

Related: #182558

## What Problem This Solves

Update settings mix everyday controls with build details, while failed-update dialogs hide useful recovery actions on a separate page.

## User Impact

A compact status/version/action card is followed by Preferences and a concise latest-attempt summary. View result opens existing progress and recovery; terminal details stay optional. Refresh status, Try again, Report failure and Diagnose stay visible, with Diagnose primary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the presentation-only slice of #182558. Existing update, retry, diagnostic and report owners retain confirmation, live permissions and attempt identity. Report and Diagnose leave the dialog for their working surface; closing does not cancel the update.

Refresh status does not promise fresh package discovery (#182567). Companion inventory/release indicators (#182568) and separate Mac installation policy (#160530) remain outside this PR. The Apps tab exposes only existing bridge capabilities and accurately labels combined automatic checking/downloading.

The initial screenshots and layout were rejected and have been replaced by the corrected card/detail hierarchy below.

Focused replays of the exact CI merge revision and a local Bun replay of shard 2/3 do not reproduce that failure. The shard has three other local assertion failures, all reproduced on its unmodified main parent. The original hosted failure remains unclassified; a passing replay is not a repair or evidence of green CI.

- Final-base production UI typecheck and performance pass; chat startup gzip decreases 77 B, CSS grows 62 B raw / 15 B gzip, with no budget changes.

Fixture captures do not prove native installation or model-backed diagnosis. Captures precede the nonvisual sidebar simplification and test-only rebase resolution.

Completed independent source/visual reviews provide separate coverage. Hosted review at `e421d3ed` completed with no actionable code findings; product acceptance remains with the area owner.

### Real recovery handoff on the reviewed runtime

prs.title: perf(runtime): avoid pooled slabs in retained buffers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Small cached JSON and queued process/audio buffers can pin mostly unused process-wide Buffer slabs for the lifetime of their owners. Logical byte limits therefore understate retained storage when unrelated allocations occur between inserts.

Related: #182804. That exporter repair is already in the measured baseline; this fixes separate residual owners.

## User Impact

Retained buffers now own their storage. JSON wire bytes, UTF-16 process output (including split/lone surrogates), audio source-copy isolation, queue limits, polling, and cleanup remain unchanged. The voice worker transfers the queue's owned buffer directly, removing a second copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

A small shared allocation utility encodes UTF-8/UTF-16LE directly into exact storage or copies producer bytes once. The existing JSON frame owner assembles its retained contiguous buffer directly into unpooled storage. No arena, cache, configuration, schema, or alternate rendering path was added. Transient buffers remain pooled; discarded string process output no longer needs a buffer at all.

Runtime production delta is **+31 lines** across the owners and shared utility. The growth implements the explicit storage-ownership contract and one-pass segment assembly; the voice transfer removes its obsolete allocation/copy. The requested stat filter (excluding tests/test-support/docs) is +672/−23, net +649: it includes 575 lines of rerunnable measurement scripts, 42 lines of their README, and one required wrapper-inventory entry. Runtime code itself is +54/−23, net +31.

Presence was investigated and left unchanged: the real Gateway retains no presence fragments between publications. Its newly allocated roster arrays are weak cache keys. A probe that deliberately held those arrays alive overstated their production lifetime and was excluded from the fix. Fixed-cardinality module constants, the one-per-Gateway config revision key (65,600 backing bytes for 32 logical bytes here), and bounded parser fragments remain outside this change.

## Evidence

Acceptance: identical outputs and source-copy isolation; repaired owners retain no unrelated pooled slabs; normal release boundaries collect their storage. These are retention proofs, not CPU/latency/GC-rate claims or guaranteed production savings. Node 26.12.1 reports `Buffer.poolSize=65536`; observed pooled backing stores are 65,600 bytes. Measurements use that observed size.

| Synthetic live owner | Logical workload | Retained backing before | After | Pooled stores before → after |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Running process registry | 16 processes × 32 sparse UTF-16 callbacks | 32.03125 MiB | 0.03223 MiB | 512 → 0 |
| Voice readiness queue | 320 × 960-byte PCM frames | 20.01953 MiB | 0.29297 MiB | 320 → 0 |
| Meeting input queue | 200 × 4,096-byte chunks | 12.51221 MiB | 0.78125 MiB | 200 → 0 |
| Transcription reconnect queue | 1,024 × 960-byte PCM frames | 64.06250 MiB | 0.93750 MiB | 1,024 → 0 |
| Running buffered command / string captures, each | 32 sparse outputs | 2.00195 MiB | 704 B | 32 → 0 |
| Clipped head / tail, each | 32 × 16-byte captures | 2.00195 MiB | 512 B | 32 → 0 |
| Partial tail | 32 × 32-byte captures | 2.00269 MiB | 1,024 B | 32 → 0 |
| Registered JSON arrays | 70 retained small arrays | 4.37927 MiB | 28,670 B | 70 → 0 |
| Shared payloads, ordinary / segmented, each | 16 retained responses | 1.00098 MiB | 982 B | 16 → 0 |

Sparse insertion interleaves disposable pool allocations; this measures amplification when other work separates retained values. Adjacent values can share slabs efficiently. The audio workloads represent 6.4 seconds of readiness backlog, about 17 seconds of meeting input, and 20.5 seconds of reconnect backlog. Process/audio probes verify exact output and release controls; synthetic heap snapshots confirm the backing-store shapes.

Rerunnable workloads and scope limits are documented in `scripts/perf/README.md` under “Retained Buffer pool storage.”

### Built Gateway proof

An isolated loopback Gateway uses 10,000 synthetic sessions, 8,000 settled runs, 2,000 archived rows, 24 profiles, 100 cron jobs, 200 approvals, two synthetic worktrees, and 40 synthetic plugins. The replay connects 24 signed UI clients, declares 24 viewers, reads five session lists and nine cron lists, and completes two turns against a local mock provider before capturing a main-isolate heap snapshot. No production state is used. Allocation-stack tagging is diagnostic only and invalidates timing comparisons.

| Live Gateway owner | Logical bytes, baseline → candidate | Backing bytes, baseline → candidate | Pool slabs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cron arrays | 2,819 → 2,819 | 65,600 → 2,819 | 1 → 0 |
| Shared payloads | 71,350 → 72,160 | 135,636 → 72,188 | 1 → 0 |
| Session array | 65,950 → 66,750 | 65,950 → 66,750 | 0 → 0 |
| Config revision key, unchanged | 32 → 32 | 65,600 → 65,600 | 1 → 1 |
| Presence fragments, unchanged | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

The changed owners' deduplicated backing union falls **267,186 → 141,757 bytes (−125,429 B / −0.1196 MiB / −46.94%)**, with **2 → 0** pooled slabs. This is the residual steady-state cost in this fixture, not the much larger exporter saving in #182804. Whole-snapshot pool slabs fall 42 → 40; this single pass does not establish whole-heap/RSS improvement.

Candidate state was freshly seeded with the same population/seed/date. Cron response sizes match exactly. Session payload sizes differ because of fixture paths and baseline pilot history, so these live responses are not a byte-equivalence comparison for identical inputs; focused tests establish that contract. Both replays completed exactly two mock-provider requests/turns before capture. Gateways and mock servers were stopped afterward. An unrelated memory-core worker import warning appeared during synthetic startup; it did not prevent either completed-turn replay.

### Validation

- Owner retention regressions are red on the unchanged baseline and green after the fixes; exact JSON, UTF-16, and audio bytes are checked.
- Final focused batch: **104 tests passed** across ten JSON-sharing, session-list/cron projection, process-command, transcription, voice transport, and SDK files (374.94 s wrapper wall time including cold compiled-worker preparation). Separate bash-retention **30/30** (final rerun 8.19 s wrapper / 4.93 s file duration) and meeting-audio **23/23** passed. The mechanical final voice-test lint fix was rerun: **2/2**, 8.23 s wrapper / 4.42 s file duration. Earlier overlapping source edits invalidated compiled-worker inputs; the final frozen batch replaces those setup failures.
- Export-name collision guard passed. Closure guards found the new helper missing from the selective PR wrapper inventory; adding its actual runtime import path repaired both failing checks. The other **20** checks passed initially; the **2** repaired checks passed in 126.95 s. No new test file or CI planning exemption was added.
- Rebased onto current main before push; only an append/append README conflict needed resolution. All changed production modules are byte-identical to the measured and reviewed versions.
- Baseline `pnpm build` and candidate `pnpm build:runtime` passed. `pnpm tsgo:core` passed using the native typechecker. Changed-file formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Targeted core and script lint passed after mechanical test/harness lint repairs (no production changes).
- Initial CI found and repaired two measurement-fixture issues: removed a readonly child-process exit-code assignment (queued exit/close events already settle teardown), and explicitly inventoried the two static Buffer factory references needed for exact instrumentation restoration. The suppression inventory now passes **14/14**; the meeting retention probe again reports zero pooled stores and zero markers after release. No runtime code changed in this repair.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean, no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings. The configured provider did not match the operator configuration; no configuration was changed.
- The initial build emitted an existing Control UI CSS budget warning (296.4 KiB vs 296.3 KiB). No UI source changes are included.

### CI and inherited failures

Exact reviewed head: `30c2ec7f4f5d85ca6f47a3d4e2f2adad584b4f36`; [CI run 40138631855](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138631855). Production/test typechecks, lint, the repaired suppression inventory, code review, and all applicable security checks passed. Three test jobs remain red, with these four cases reproduced against unchanged main parent `4298fe6550fb846e7bf7feff630d818db4ed57e3`:

| Test | CI signature | Main-base evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ClawRouter managed Gateway | Empty model catalog, line 109 | Same failure with rebuilt main-base runtime, pinned Bun, prebuilt dist, one worker |
| Widget restart | Revision `1 > 1`, line 366 | Same failure with rebuilt main-base runtime and identical command |
| Restored requester settlement | Three restored wakes where two are expected | Same failure; the other four tests pass on main-base runtime |
| Exec process lifecycle | `missing spawned child <pid>` | Same failure on head and unchanged main sources through the actual service-relay path, selected by test-local service identity on macOS |

The three built-Gateway files ran individually, sequentially, with `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1`, the repository-pinned Bun fork, and `--maxWorkers=1`. The baseline build used source bytes equal to the pinned main parent; the branch source was restored afterward. The shared `origin/main` ref advanced during preparation, so these results are explicitly pinned to that parent, not described as latest-main evidence.

The lifecycle case needs a platform qualification: Linux's default exec memory limit selects the service relay. Its public PID belongs to the relayed command, while the test records only parent-isolate `ChildProcess` instances. The default macOS case passes because it uses direct spawning. For the head/base comparison, a temporary test-local `vi.stubEnv("OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER", "synthetic-lane1693")` selected the same existing relay/PID contract after normal test isolation. Both versions fail the same lookup; no implementation was mocked, no assertion was changed, and the temporary setup was removed. This is source-regression attribution through the real relay boundary, not a claim of Linux runtime reproduction. The relevant test and routing sources are unchanged by this PR.

Failed jobs: [changed-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138631855/job/121005815235), [changed-10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138631855/job/121005815114), and [changed-9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40138631855/job/121005815362). Their downstream CI gate remains red; no CI rerun was requested. A real README append conflict required rebasing; the section now sits beside the existing heap-retention guide to avoid recurring EOF conflicts. All 25 lane-owned non-README files are byte-identical to the prior reviewed head, and fresh CI on the rebased head confirms precisely the same four inherited failure cases. The listed test files and lifecycle routing sources are byte-identical to the pinned main baseline. Independent review found no blocking source or attribution findings. Landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception; CI is not represented as green.

## Tradeoffs and Limits

Dedicated backing storage replaces pooled suballocation only for retained values. A short allocation-only pilot was noisy (greater-than-5× baseline spread) and showed sub-microsecond extra encoding cost for small values; it is not a measured Gateway CPU regression or a throughput claim. The owner and live probes here measure retention and correctness, not matched CPU/GC/promotion/event-loop gates. The voice worker removes one additional allocation/copy per transferred frame. No production heap was captured or copied.

prs.title: feat: preview Control UI themes before applying them
prs.body:
Related: #151479 (reuse of shared radio/option-card controls; this does not complete the consolidation tracker).

## What Problem This Solves

Choosing a Control UI theme needs a compact, keyboard-friendly way to try it across the window before saving, including matching colors in the embedded terminal.

## User Impact

Users can hover, focus, or tap a theme to preview the current window; Apply theme or Enter saves it, while Cancel, Escape, or leaving Appearance restores the current selection. Other windows and saved preferences are unchanged during preview. All 11 built-in names/IDs are preserved, with palette descriptions and Beacon identified as the high-contrast option.

Arrow keys browse, Home/End jump, and Space previews without saving. The visible keyboard guide is scoped to the picker, not text fields. Plugin and personal palettes use the existing catalog, including cancellation when a previewed plugin disappears.

Themes may optionally author 16 ANSI colors. Existing terminals and scrollback repaint without restarting the shell; explicit true-color output remains application-owned. No database migration or operator configuration change is required. The approved temporary ghostty-web 0.4.0 repair includes rebuilt embedded WASM and generated ESM/CJS/declarations, with pinned sources, hashes, rebuild instructions, and removal gates in patches/README.md and the packaged source patches.

This is Omarchy-inspired groundwork, not an official collaboration or an installed Catppuccin/Tokyo Night theme pack. New wallpapers, continuous animation, and external CLI theming are outside this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing application theme owner now holds transient preview state separately from canonical preferences and rejects stale palette completion after cancellation. The picker reuses shared native radio navigation instead of adding a second keyboard model; the real window is the preview surface rather than a floating miniature. Preview and commit share the font/accent reset policy.

The terminal updates native color defaults directly rather than injecting OSC into the PTY parser, preserving split escape sequences and active-theme reset baselines. The canvas also paints literal-black cell backgrounds correctly. Existing clipboard-success and disposal repairs remain intact. Most patch bytes are reproducibly generated dependency output, not a second terminal implementation.

## Evidence

- Real Control UI browser flow: window preview, all scoped navigation keys, explicit Apply/Enter, Escape/Cancel/route exit, no writes before Apply, a second window retaining its selection, touch, plugin preview/withdrawal, and saved-profile persistence.
- Chromium Appearance consumer suite: 20 tests. Focused keyboard/preview consumer also passed in WebKit. Focused owner/preference/configuration suites: 169 tests, including late palette completion and Gateway-scope retirement. Contrast matrix retains AA, with Beacon AAA for the sampled text pairs.
- Full terminal browser suite: 6 cases, including cold authored palettes, live reload/fallback, clipboard outcomes, input, memory isolation, and disposal. Native regressions cover all 16 colors, scrollback, explicit RGB, cursor preservation, fragmented CSI/OSC, and reset defaults.
- The literal-black canvas regression was red before the renderer repair and green afterward: SGR 40 paints [0,0,0], while untouched default background remains [30,30,46]. A fresh-store frozen install reproduced both generated runtime formats and the native WASM hash.
- UI production typecheck, scoped lint/style/format, docs MDX, and i18n verification passed. Independent P0-P2 review is scoped-clean after resolving the black-background finding. PR CI provides the broad suite; no remote CI or whole-repository typecheck success is claimed.

- After GitHub reported an actual conflict, integrated main at `c64eaf54ad0b609a114d580e29135acd93433bfd`. Kept the new canonical Settings preference owner rather than restoring duplicate bindings. On that exact base, all 9 browser cases, affected Settings/preview owner regressions, UI production typecheck, scoped lint/format, and fresh P0-P2 review passed. The integrated After capture is byte-identical to the image below. Earlier unchanged-contract proof is retained, not relabeled as remote CI.

- Hosted-review follow-up: completed the remaining browser-only `ApplicationTheme` fixture and corrected the radio test callback's return contract. The UI-components test typecheck leaf now passes, along with that browser test and all 5 shared-radio tests. These follow-up edits are test-only; production behavior and the inspected images are unchanged.

Existing persisted preference and theme-definition shapes are unchanged, and ANSI tokens are optional. A full v2026.10.6-to-candidate upgrade run was not performed; it remains an explicit qualification gap rather than a claimed pass.

The earlier editor/test type graph (before base integration) reported errors in untouched native-desktop, quota-reset, and regexp declaration inputs. That broad graph was not rerun or claimed fixed; this is not a clean full-project gate run. No live Gateway was modified or deployed. Browser evidence uses synthetic Gateway fixtures.

### Visual walkthrough

**Revision provenance for every Before/After comparison below:**

- **Before = main at [d75915ee88343c26565b6855fde235525d112ba3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d75915ee88343c26565b6855fde235525d112ba3)**, fetched into an isolated, clean checkout for this recapture.
- **After = pushed PR head [da36d69fe3933fe1675201b26622972a7327b066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/da36d69fe3933fe1675201b26622972a7327b066)**. The capture checkout's Git tree exactly matches the published commit tree (777b6ea8a27dab54d4656a994a92fe40f70177fc); it contains no unpublished product changes.

Both revisions ran the same scenario script and synthetic Gateway fixtures with matching viewport, locale, color scheme, and reduced-motion settings. Each used its own dependency installation and lockfile. These are real rendered Control UI captures, not design mockups or previous design iterations. Fixture footer version/build strings are synthetic; the source revisions above identify the code being compared. No code was pushed for this description/evidence update.

**How to read the picker:** the checkmark identifies the saved theme; the highlighted/focused radio identifies the preview target. “Previewing … — not saved” is an unsaved window-local state. “Current: …” and disabled Apply/Cancel mean there is no pending theme choice.

#### Main versus PR: hover Tide while Claw is saved

Identical action on both revisions: open Appearance with Claw selected, then hover Tide. Both use a 1440 × 1200 viewport.

**Before — main d75915ee: hover/tooltip only; the window stays Claw**

![Before on current-main snapshot d75915ee: hovering Tide leaves the window in Claw](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f2e11f8-783a-498c-880c-bfc786c8bffc)

**After — pushed PR da36d69: the whole window previews Tide, with Claw still saved**

![After on pushed PR da36d69: hovering Tide previews the whole window without saving](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efeee2cf-26ea-48d6-b44d-74f88b96d688)

| Same action | Main d75915ee | Pushed PR da36d69 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hover Tide | Window remains Claw; 0 theme-selection requests | Window previews Tide; 0 theme-selection requests |
| Click Tide | Window changes to Tide and sends 1 theme-selection request | Window previews Tide but sends 0 theme-selection requests |
| Separate commit step | None: selecting the theme commits it | Apply/Enter commits the preview; Cancel/Escape restores the saved theme |

The comparison scenarios asserted these rendered states and request counts on both revisions. The PR preview includes typography as well as colors, so surrounding copy can rewrap; the captures do not normalize away that layout change.

#### PR-only state and persistence walkthrough

The following gallery and state sequence are **all from pushed PR head da36d69**. They illustrate individual PR interaction states, not additional main-versus-PR comparisons. This separate PR-state capture checked the rendered window, browser preference mirror, and outgoing **themes.set** requests:

| Action | Window displays | Saved theme | Theme-selection writes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Start | Claw | Claw | 0 |
| Hover/focus Tide | Tide, unsaved | Claw | 0 |
| Escape | Claw restored; focus retained | Claw | 0 |
| Preview Tide again, then Apply | Tide, current | Tide | 1 |
| End from the picker | Miami, unsaved | Tide | still 1 |
| Escape from that keyboard preview | Tide restored | Tide | still 1 |
| Tap Tide in a fresh mobile scenario | Tide, unsaved | Claw | 0 |

Cancel and leaving Appearance use the same saved-selection restoration path. Applying uses the existing preference owner; it does not create a separate theme engine. Other browser windows do not inherit the transient preview.

**Important scope distinction:** Light/Dark/System retain their existing immediate preference behavior; the new Apply button stages the **theme choice**, not every Appearance setting. The light-mode image below is after explicitly choosing Light, not a claim that Cancel rolls color mode back.

**Observed interaction edge for review (not fixed by this metadata-only update):** after Escape, leaving and returning to the exact previous pointer coordinates can leave the saved theme visible until another in-card movement, focus change, or click. The capture reproduced this, then explicitly clicked Tide to continue. It is not presented as repaired behavior.

<details>
<summary>PR-only gallery: saved, Cancel/Escape, and applied states</summary>

**New picker at rest — Claw saved, no pending choice**

![New picker at rest with Current Claw and Apply/Cancel disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6a58fa5-acfd-44fc-97a9-44ca1a691949)

**Escape state on the PR — Claw restored, Tide still has keyboard focus**

The focus outline is not a saved-selection indicator. The Claw checkmark and “Current: Claw” remain authoritative; no theme-selection write occurred.

![Escape restores Claw while retaining focus on Tide](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c23b668-56ef-4534-bbef-9b9bd08b46c5)

**Applied state on the PR — saved checkmark moves to Tide**

“Current: Tide” replaces the unsaved-preview status. Apply/Cancel are disabled again. The capture observed one theme-selection request and the saved mirror changed to Tide.

![Applied Tide with saved checkmark and Current Tide status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b8d31de4-37f6-4de2-98b2-cbb7f9950554)

</details>

<details>
<summary>PR-only gallery: keyboard navigation, light mode, and touch layout</summary>

**Keyboard — End previews Miami while Tide stays saved**

The actual window and typography change, the Miami focus/preview target is visible, and the saved checkmark remains on Tide. The same run exercised Home, ArrowRight, and Escape and verified no additional theme-selection request.

![Keyboard End previews Miami while saved selection remains Tide](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d17a31d-f249-42e5-b1db-5273a3d37d00)

| Key, with focus in the picker | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Move through choices and preview |
| Home / End | First / last choice |
| Space | Preview without saving |
| Enter | Apply the focused choice |
| Escape | Restore the saved theme, retaining focus |
| Tab | Normal navigation into/out of the native radio group and actions |

These bindings do not intercept the import URL field or other text inputs; that boundary is exercised by the browser flow.

**Light mode — applied Tide, with real light palette swatches**

![Applied Tide in Light mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/168e1254-8cbf-483a-9df6-98c6daf51bd7)

**Touch — 390-pixel viewport, Tide preview with Claw still saved**

The choices form two columns and actions wrap below the status. One tap previews; Apply is still explicit. This is the actual responsive layout, including the keyboard hint that remains visible on mobile.

![Mobile Tide preview with Claw saved and explicit Apply and Cancel buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69aee76a-e415-46a8-855f-f84ff9b8d89e)

</details>

#### Main versus PR: identical authored ANSI fixture

These are **two revision-specific captures**, not one PR implementation with its palette toggled. Both revisions received the same synthetic desired palette and the same four-row terminal output, in a 1280 × 900 viewport. The images crop the same header/output region without altering pixels.

**Before — main d75915ee: terminal retains its fallback indexed colors**

![Before on main d75915ee: identical ANSI fixture renders fallback indexed colors](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f83fae33-995b-4d93-866e-2e4196586c4c)

**After — pushed PR da36d69: terminal uses the authored ANSI colors**

![After on pushed PR da36d69: identical ANSI fixture renders the authored palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f15d45b-55f8-44dc-87bc-fe9d9b59e5ed)

The sampled red background was RGB (255,107,107) on main and the authored RGB (243,139,168) on the PR. The synthetic UI fixture supplies the desired optional ANSI fields to both clients; it is not a claim that main's server accepts the new theme-import fields. Import/schema acceptance is tested separately.

Live-update behavior is also tested separately on the PR: the existing canvas/session is retained, terminal.open is called once, removing authored tokens restores defaults, and palette changes emit no terminal.input. Native checks cover all 16 indices, scrollback, explicit-RGB preservation, fragmented escape sequences, and reset baselines. The pictures above compare main with the pushed PR; they do not substitute two states of the same revision for a Before/After comparison.

Concept, UX direction, and feature request: Chris Eckert (@ceckert).

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5c6bc88f-6d89-40f8-9bad-41b563880ac3)

## Worked on by

- @ceckert

prs.title: perf(ui): show saved conversations before reconnecting
prs.body:
Related: #182825

## What Problem This Solves

Warm reloads could leave a saved conversation blank until the connection request was sent, even though its scoped snapshot had already arrived. A slow IndexedDB read could also hold the first history request for two seconds.

## User Impact

Saved conversations become readable earlier and are marked **Saved conversation · reconnecting**. Drafts keep their existing behavior; remote media, embeds, and plugins wait for connection and route admission. Workspace icons also wait for connection and route admission, including after disconnect. Saved text remains accessible to screen readers and can be selected/copied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prewarming now follows the current route rather than blindly reading the last selected session, and skips unrelated pages. The normal pane renderer paints saved rows after yielding for the initial composer, without waiting for connect. Live history uses an already-restored cursor when available, starts independently of browser storage otherwise, and retires pending snapshot publication before applying its result.

The existing identity, invalidation, retention, and reconciliation owners remain in charge. The connect-before-transcript flag and two-second snapshot wait are removed; cached board startup keeps its separate timing. The design note is updated at `docs/reference/control-ui-warm-transcript-design.md`.

## Evidence

Production bundles on the same shared Mac; synthetic 240-message / 390-session workload, 20 interleaved base/head pairs per profile. Remote means the existing `live-fast` RPC profile plus 100 ms HTTP latency and 10 Mbps, not an Internet deployment.

| Milestone | Base median / p95 | Head median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local visible transcript | 212.5 / 265.6 ms | 203.7 / 235.4 ms |
| Local enabled composer | 207.8 / 232.1 ms | 201.9 / 234.8 ms |
| Remote visible transcript | 509.3 / 515.0 ms | 304.7 / 322.4 ms |
| Remote enabled composer | 250.7 / 256.9 ms | 247.8 / 260.0 ms |
| Remote live-history response | 966.3 / 979.1 ms | 940.8 / 945.7 ms |
| Local scripting CPU | 416.0 / 455.6 ms | 421.7 / 449.6 ms |
| Remote scripting CPU | 434.8 / 457.7 ms | 429.1 / 466.8 ms |

The shared-host A/A control had noisy tails: identical-code scripting CPU p95 moved +7.8% and task CPU p95 +16.2%. The 20-pair CPU comparison is inside that noise. Connection dispatch remains at the profile's approximately 449 ms boundary; no extra history request is needed in the warm fixture.

The remote median misses the 300 ms goal by **4.7 ms**. Diagnostic filmstrips show **zero duplicate row keys**, visible-anchor movement below **0.04 px**, and **zero CLS during live adoption**. Whole-page CLS remains approximately **0.112**, including earlier virtualizer/sidebar/details updates; this PR does not establish zero whole-page CLS.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Targeted bootstrap, hydration, warm reload, routes, and media tests | 100 initial cases passed; 35 focused CI-repair cases passed |
| UI typecheck | Passed |
| Controller/reactivity guard | Passed; effects 2→2, untrack 3→3, owner APIs 2→2, DOM queries/listeners/render effects/flush remain 0 |
| Changed leaf lint / formatting / diff check | Passed; whole touched-file lint also reports the existing `bootstrap.ts` max-lines finding (its line count is unchanged) |
| Production Knip | 3 unused files, 30 export groups, 11 type groups outside this change; no UI findings; retained for CI attribution |
| Strict performance comparison against built base | Passed; no added requests |
| Startup gzip | **281,184 → 281,367 B** (+183 B), 7 JS + 1 CSS request |
| Chat / New Session boot gzip | **1,274,797 → 1,274,888 B** / **770,888 → 771,094 B** |

The final media-admission follow-up passes all 24 warm-startup cases and UI typecheck; its new workspace-icon test fails on the prior head. Timing values above precede that small request-gating follow-up. The production byte counts in the table include it.

The startup baseline is ratcheted to the measured 281,367 B. The base already exceeds the total CSS ceilings by 155 B gzip / 1 B raw; this change leaves those bytes unchanged.

Touched production UI LOC against the integrated main: **12,868 → 12,911 (+43)**. Touched tests: **4,077 → 4,263 (+186)**. Growth is the route-aware selection, explicit passive-media propagation, and coverage; there is no second cache, renderer, storage identity, or new dependency. `ci:full` requests the complete UI and Gateway selection.

Reproduce the remote timing comparison (use `--latency-ms 0 --frame-gap-ms 0` for local):

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
  --gateway-http --bundle-dir /path/to/base/control-ui \
  --compare-bundle-dir dist/control-ui --runs 40 --untraced --thread-cpu-time \
  --face chat --latency-profile live-fast --network-latency-ms 100 --download-kbps 10000
```

Inspected synthetic-only frames: before is the last unchanged frame before 425 ms (307.9 ms; no new frame until 526.9 ms), after is 422.4 ms. The after transcript first painted at 356 ms in this diagnostic run.

![Before: saved transcript still blank during reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/861a2f02-b02b-4cbf-9bca-ef740cf1e7a5)

![After: saved conversation visible while reconnecting](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d089cf8-8606-4d8c-b786-2cd55599cc94)

## CI repair

Run 40130583989 exposed five PR regressions; the matching jobs passed in scheduled main run 40125377367. All are treated as ours: header subagent rendering read transcript history, the new workspace fixture omitted its required kind, two timer executors returned timer IDs, passive widgets lost their saved shell/height, and the new composer yield split dashboard board/transcript first paint.

The repair short-circuits the saved label for established live headers, fixes the fixture and executors, preserves the normal passive widget shell/learned height, and keeps the dashboard restore atomic. The three focused unit files pass 35 cases; both UI and UI-chat test typechecks pass. Full E2E proof belongs to the replacement CI run. Timing measurements predate these bounded repairs; the final byte counts above include their production changes.

The replacement run 40132282378 passed 48 jobs, including the widget E2E and both real-Gateway shards, but still exposed one empty first frame in the dashboard name-alias case. Bootstrap had treated the ambiguous name as an exact literal cache key. The final repair warms one same-agent last-viewed dashboard candidate; exact route/cache-key consumption remains authoritative, with one unused scoped read accepted if the alias resolves elsewhere. Forced literals, other agents, and chat routes remain unchanged. All 15 prewarm cases and the exact unchanged dashboard E2E (`restores /dashboard/main/mission-control before hello`) pass locally; UI types, leaf lint, and final bundle comparison pass.

Final run 40133980199 exposed an unrelated timing race in `returns Escape to its trigger after pointer and keyboard reopening with title tooltips` (`chat-effort-picker.browser.test.tsx`). The test queries the lazily mounted range once before polling focus; CI captured `null` even though the failure DOM contains the range. That test and its production owners are unchanged here, and the previous two PR runs and latest completed scheduled main run passed it. The exact case passed in a focused local diagnostic. This is a diagnosed flake, not an inherited-failure claim or a repaired test; The final run completed with 48 jobs passing, including dashboard E2E and both real-Gateway shards. The single diagnosed-flake rerun passed. Final run 40133980199, attempt 2, completed successfully with all 50 jobs that ran passing (non-applicable jobs skipped). No source changes were made for this flake.

## Final main integration

Native recovery found a startup-budget conflict after the green run. Merged current main (0bba2a4f976) without replaying commits; only the budget record conflicted. The combined build measures startup **281,702 B**, chat boot **1,271,675 B**, and New Session **767,609 B**; request counts remain unchanged. Startup is +403 B against incoming main’s recorded 281,299 B, within the approved sub-0.5 KB allowance for measured latency/CPU wins. The baseline is ratcheted to the measured combined artifact. UI typecheck and the strict comparison against the original built base pass. The timing table predates this integration. Current-head CI **40137609860**, attempt 1, completed successfully: **all 49 jobs that ran passed**; non-applicable jobs skipped. The final head required no rerun.

prs.title: feat: show paired companion apps in Updates settings
prs.body:
Related: #182568. Depends on #182590.

## What Problem This Solves

Browser users cannot see their paired companion apps from Updates; the existing Apps panel is visible only inside a native app.

## User Impact

Updates → Apps lists paired native installations with their reported app version and connected/offline state. Remote entries say **Update on device** and offer no remote update action or release-available indicator. The current native app retains its existing local controls, even while the inventory request is pending or fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the read-only initial inventory slice discussed in #182568, not a fleet updater. It reads existing `node.list` facts, excludes unapproved and non-native clients, preserves separate installations, and deduplicates the local app only by exact node ID. Gateway remains the default tab. Native lifecycle, release discovery and the Mac automatic-installation policy (#160530) are unchanged.

**Stack:** this branch includes the unmerged presentation-only parent #182590. Review the [inventory-only diff](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/compare/e54dc02de6abe36d3ed37e7d8ab9fb55dba8dfc9...75823680136e5417f3bf0c9174fbff755e5e1e48): 12 files, +425/-130 (including the five-file test-only CI repair). Do not merge independently of the parent; its presentation decision remains with maintainers. No backend, protocol, native-app, dependency or CSS changes are added by this slice.

## Evidence

**Current CI caveat (2026-10-25):** [checks-ui-e2e (6/9)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40137666909/job/121002814403) is red in the unchanged compact agent-picker test: after selecting Writer, its checkmark has no bounding box at 390px. Both viewport cases pass unchanged locally. The matching main job failed a different test, so its coarse pre-existing classification does not establish this failure as inherited. Cause remains unclassified; the passing replay is not a repair or evidence of green CI.

- 60 focused UI tests,42 confirmation-runtime tests and all5 native-device browser scenarios pass. A deferred-read regression fails before the repair and passes afterward: local Check now stays usable while `node.list` remains pending; choosing a remote app removes the local action. Tests also cover filtering, exact-ID deduplication, unknown version, read failure and stale-connection retirement.
- Production UI typecheck, focused lint/format, keyless i18n, Solid guards and UI build pass. Build reports the same inherited CSS budget warnings as the parent (296.5 vs296.3 KiB gzip); no CSS or budget changes are included. Independent source review found the pending-read issue; it was fixed and re-reviewed.
- **Real Gateway proof:** shipped browser Updates → Apps → actual WebSocket `node.list` (no RPC interception), with synthetic paired offline iOS/Android/node-host identities created through the production pairing APIs in separate secretless state. Both native apps rendered; node-host was excluded. Desktop/narrow views had no overflow or browser errors; all 106 fetched assets matched the tested UI build. Temporary Gateway stopped and its port verified free.
- **Fixture proof:** separate connected/offline scenarios cover both widths; settled card opacity verified as1. These are not physical-device or native-updater demonstrations.
- Provenance: tested UI source was the final inventory tree atop `e421d3ed`; the published stack moves it onto the parent's test-only `e54dc02` cleanup. prs.title: fix(sessions): context token count stays stale for the whole of a long agent turn
prs.body:
Related: #164550

## What Problem This Solves

The session's context count (`totalTokens`) can stay at its pre-turn value throughout a long embedded agent turn. This change publishes the latest settled model call's prompt context while the turn is running. Turn completion still writes the final accounting result.

The writer serializes writes, fences them to the admitted session/run, closes before final accounting, and drains before settlement returns. Detached and incognito attempts, and follow-ups that preserve user-facing session state, do not use it. This covers the embedded runner; mid-turn reporting for the separate Codex app-server and CLI backends is not established.

## Current revision and integration

Head: [`633860da372bfa96638235cde41244f853357115`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/633860da372bfa96638235cde41244f853357115), tree `bddbf5bc79f6a022eb56264f504eb0c6b9404185`. This merges fixture head `0fee8253e66c0ea50ab7c5b6f3608464fd510a04` with pinned main `418aafaae7e8d13792b9095c010a114ca4e058ea`, preserving both parents.

Main's on-demand fork change (#182844) conflicted with the context-writer import in `attempt-stream-prepare.ts`. The resolution retains both imports and all upstream fork-boundary, message-projection and guarded read changes. The context writer still receives settled model calls, closes before final accounting, and drains in settlement cleanup.

Main also removed the cron writer's `resultTarget` and `cronSession` parameters in [#182262](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182262), commit `721cdadccb93b9c185d367f0e8082b2338553c81`. The integration follows that new owner contract: it removes the now-obsolete fixture arguments and generation import while preserving every final-accounting assertion. The earlier fixture fix below was needed on its older base; carrying those arguments into current main would be wrong. This avoids duplicating or reversing the upstream change.

An independent source review checked the full 20-path delta, every resolved blob and the complete tree. It found the obsolete arguments before publication; the revised candidate has no remaining source finding. Source review is not an executed test or maintainer policy approval.

[CI 40139208391](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40139208391) is running for this head. The PR is mergeable; broad checks and the aggregate gate are not yet complete.

## Evidence: earlier fixture validation at `0fee8253`

A separate Linux x64 runner tested tree `2f7b14302b4298d6cd677db3c71884614b90e275`, published as `0fee8253e66c0ea50ab7c5b6f3608464fd510a04`, using Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, the frozen lockfile, Vitest 5.0.5 and pinned OpenClaw Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`. The lockfile SHA-256 was `21592b379203de7ecd8661cfd6e412daf6546f94b203f28c314579db20f76594`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Services/cron test typecheck | Exit 0; 40.28 s. |
| Final cron context runtime fixture | Both cases passed; 161.98 s. |
| Restore only the fixture from `793bd7ed`, leaving the environment unchanged | Typecheck exit 2; exactly one `TS2739` at line 46 for missing `resultTarget` and `cronSession`; 12.68 s. |
| Runtime fixture with that reversal | Both cases still passed; 84.69 s. Runtime success alone does not prove this type repair. |
| Restoration | Exact candidate tree restored; validation processes drained. |

```sh
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental
CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts \
  src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.context-total.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

These results are prior-tree evidence: current main has a different writer contract, so the merged head needs its own validation. The earlier tested fixture's SHA-256 is `0197027e9c17c8044f27707c6b22cd4599717c627c7f5ecea8c50766fb8edd46`. The exact-source validation receipt SHA-256 is `ed46230f8829459015ae408653e10a053cc1c4f0a7501da6225016597cd4455d`. Independent source review found no actionable issue in the fixture change; that is not maintainer policy approval.

## Goal budget decision

Goal accounting retains its existing peak-usage policy. The store-backed regression starts a Goal with a 50,000-token budget and publishes 40,000, 60,000, then 30,000 tokens. Current context finishes at 30,000; Goal usage remains 60,000 and `budget_limited`. The lower snapshot goes through the real writer and store; the test does not execute the compactor.

Publishing intermediate observations can expose a peak that turn-end accounting alone would not have seen. Whether those intermediate peaks should count toward Goal budgets remains a maintainer decision. My recommendation is to preserve the existing peak reducer. Explicit resume starts a fresh budget window at the current context and resets `tokensUsed` to 0. Automatically crediting the Goal after compaction would change budget semantics; this PR does not do that.

## Remaining gates

Fresh-head hosted CI and its aggregate gate are pending. The import conflict is resolved; no broad CI success is claimed. Security and dependency gates are not waived.

The earlier real-provider `agent --local` measurements and [successful October 20 CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39497256630) remain historical, tied to `a1bdfb50d5d45e742582c399f47c9a1ac5b5df33` and its recorded merge checkout. This fixture validation adds no shipped Gateway, channel, compactor or live-provider execution of the current head. The Goal policy decision remains open.

prs.title: fix(fs): prevent runaway symlink traversal in directory scans
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes runaway memory consumption when a recursive directory inventory reaches checkout symlinks that point back to ancestor directories.

## User Impact

Directory scans terminate without traversing discovered symlinks. Worker Corepack preparation no longer chmods files or directories outside its copied package. Session-log discovery ignores linked files and directories instead of counting outside transcripts.

## Why This Change Was Made

An incident investigation reproduced directory-symlink following with name-only recursive readdir on Node 26 and Bun 1.4.4. An affected checkout had at least 43 dependency links back to the repository root; a QA scan repeatedly expanded that graph, reached roughly 83–100 GiB anonymous RSS, and triggered two host OOM outages.

- Add async/sync iterative Dirent inventories using incremental opendir reads, deterministic relative-path sorting, and typed maxDepth/maxEntries errors (defaults 64 / 100,000). Symlinks are reported but never descended into; symlink roots are rejected and missing roots retain ENOENT.
- Migrate runtime scans and script inventories; keep workshop regular-file filtering and restore rejection of symlinks. QA treats only ENOENT as an empty inventory, so real failures and exhausted budgets remain visible.
- Expose the helper through the existing file-access-runtime SDK entrypoint. Remote bootstrap and historical-release installer snippets cannot import current host modules, so use small bounded local Dirent loops there.
- Ban recursive readdir/readdirSync calls through normal and focused oxlint across all linted source, tests, test-support, e2e, tooling, UI, packages, and root scripts. Resolve lexical const bindings and filesystem aliases; report unverifiable options. Embedded JavaScript snippets are manually migrated.

This is an inventory API, not a race-proof authorization mechanism for subsequent filesystem mutations. No runtime/config migration or live deployment is included. Release-note context stays here; CHANGELOG files are release-owned.

## Evidence

- Real filesystem fixtures: ancestor loop, external directory link, file/dangling links, exact relative paths/types, deterministic order, typed entry/depth limits, missing/non-directory/symlink roots. Passed on Node 26.12.1 and the repository-pinned Bun 1.4.4 fork.
- Real worker bootstrap regression: on the original production module, copied Corepack symlinks changed outside directory mode from 0755 to 0700; the same test passes with the fix and also preserves outside file mode 0644. QA session counting and workshop listing have link regressions.
- Focused owner suites passed for walker, worker toolchain, workshop, Doctor proposal retirement, QA fetch/session/tool-search, package bundling, changelog attribution, icon inventories, native protocol artifacts, database conformance, lint, and installer smoke. The installer integration suite passes; its filesystem fixture now exercises real opendir and asserts the actual refusal reason.
- Normal oxlint deliberately rejected a scratch recursive readdir call with exit 1 and the walker guidance; the scratch file was removed. Six call shapes plus the explicit suppression mechanism are covered in executable lint fixtures. Production guard scan: zero violations.
- Passed pnpm build; tsgo:core, tsgo:scripts, tsgo:extensions, tsgo:core:test, tsgo:extensions:test, and the root tooling typecheck. Targeted core/script/extension/root-test lint and diff/format checks pass.

Known local baseline failures: two control-ui-session-prs-branch cache-work-count assertions fail identically with the original production module restored (unexpected checkout.context reads; two merge-base calls). Other exercised PR suites passed. Full check:changed was run: its unrelated pre-existing dead-export and oversized-file findings remain; this change's lint findings were repaired and targeted lanes rerun. The requested global virtual store was tried first, but current declaration tooling rejects compiler inputs outside the checkout; a task-owned local virtual graph using the same canonical pnpm store fixed that tooling prerequisite. No guard was bypassed.

Initial implementation touched-test audit: read the then-modified test/support files in full. Retained independently useful boundary, recovery, authority, process-lifecycle, and static packaging contracts; no dead tests were removed. Strengthened installer refusal assertions rather than accepting an arbitrary failure. New walker/QA tests take well under one second of test execution; existing workshop and installer integration files take about 48s/33s and retain their real mutation/process boundaries. Exact-head CI results are recorded below. The first CI run found missing lifecycle/PR-wrapper source closure entries and a lint fixture that assumed its scripts directory did not exist. The closure inventories and fixture setup are now repaired; all 43 focused CI-repair tests pass locally.

Author simplification pass complete: one core inventory owner, no new configuration/state/dependencies, with only the two unavoidable standalone transport loops. Independent review and merge are owned by the requesting maintainer; this child does not merge.

## Review round 2 — historical findings and CI

**Head: a6ab88e95583778fa38829b2f6c6d1efc8cd40cf.** Published once for this round. Rebased onto main f2fccfab05f36f400a671026d95263db790affd2 after resolving the originally reported conflicts and one later observed Copilot import conflict. Upstream staging owners, native .js input coverage, and consolidated/deleted tests were preserved rather than overwritten with older copies. No merge is authorized for this child.

### Requested repairs

1. **Current-main traversal coverage:** migrated all 11 recursive calls exposed by the rebase. A complete source/test/script/UI/package/root-script guard scan has zero non-fixture violations; a separate embedded-program inventory finds only the deliberately link-free compatibility oracle.
2. **Mutation/escape safety:** constant options are no longer trusted after member writes, delete/update operations, unknown calls, alias/publication escapes, exported bindings, or unknown captured use. Invocation position is carried through option aliases so a later Object.assign cannot hide behind an earlier initializer. Known nonmutating filesystem reads can reuse options. Nine mutation/escape fixtures are rejected; negative cases stay clean.
3. **Lint cost:** source text is checked before registering visitors or materializing scopes. Files without readdir do no scope/listener work; a regression test enforces that property. Measurements below satisfy the recorded acceptance rule.
4. **Canonical CI coverage:** added scripts:resource-safety to createOxlintShards. CI's existing --only=scripts selection now owns test/ and automatically discovered root source files through a rule-only config, without adding a full semantic lint pass. Its integration test obtains targets from the canonical selector, then runs native oxlint against an owned fixture; no source paths are manually supplied to the selector. The actual shard entrypoint completed with zero diagnostics across 2,310 files. Only deliberate lint-rule fixtures are excluded.
5. **Workshop pruning:** skipDirectory retains a directory entry while omitting descendants before budget consumption. Workshop list/view prunes hidden metadata and node_modules. A real deep .git/.venv/node_modules fixture failed on the original code with ERR_DIRECTORY_WALK_LIMIT, then passed; async/sync walker tests cover pruning at exact entry/depth budgets.
6. **Repository-absence proof:** both candidate-state checks now inspect every reported symlink's real target and reject targets inside the source repository or pointing to its ancestors, in addition to checking for copied unrelated.txt. They no longer rely on a nonfollowing inventory alone. All 19 candidate-state tests pass.
7. **Remaining source checks:** renamed and annotated timeout-adapter and frozen-payload assertions as static packaging contracts. They protect packaged ownership/dependency wiring; they explicitly do not claim runtime timeout enforcement or filesystem mutation proof. Existing executable installer proof remains intact (67 tests pass on the new main baseline).

**Nits:** known callback functions/aliases are accepted as the second readdir argument. Corrected the packaging-closure comment: published installs skip source-only generation. Removed redundant String projections in declaration-stage. Added process.getBuiltinModule, createRequire aliases, and literal dynamic-import default support. Rule header documents let/reassigned aliases, computed names and cross-module wrapper limitations; this is not whole-program dataflow analysis.

### Lint proof

The real lint fixture suite checks **33 expected resource-safety diagnostics**: 18 existing unsafe/unknown cases, nine mutation/escape cases, and six builtin/createRequire/dynamic-import cases. Local callbacks, stable nonrecursive options, and unrelated receivers produce none. Before this repair, the mutation cases were missed and two callback negatives were incorrectly reported. The canonical selector/native-CLI coverage test passes; the actual command below exits 0:

    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=scripts:resource-safety --format=json

### Performance acceptance and results

Acceptance recorded before measurement: identical normalized native diagnostics, lower median wall time and peak RSS. Same final rule with only the prefilter removed (A) or enabled (B); five serial interleaved AB pairs, warm filesystem caches, oxlint 1.88.0, eight threads, 47,995 files. No concurrent task-owned check ran; unrelated host load was present and recorded. This is a paired comparison, not an idle-host absolute benchmark.

    /usr/bin/time -l node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=8 --format=json src ui packages extensions scripts

| Metric | A: no prefilter | B: prefilter |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median wall time | 28.42 s | 9.75 s |
| p95 wall time (nearest rank, n=5) | 28.57 s | 11.84 s |
| Median peak RSS | 8.93 GiB | 3.29 GiB |
| p95 peak RSS | 9.06 GiB | 3.68 GiB |

All ten runs produced **241 identical normalized diagnostics**. Their nonzero native exit reflects existing whole-repository max-lines failures, not altered rule behavior. The final rule was measured on the 1d5d26784447-based tree; its bytes did not change during the final ten-commit conflict refresh. No additional cache or disabled rule was introduced.

### Verification and CI

Passed: pnpm build; pnpm tsgo:all; scoped core/script/root-test lint; formatting and diff checks; line-cap ratchet; 40 walker/workshop tests; 19 candidate-state tests; 35 lint-runner tests; guard and canonical-lane tests; 80 installer/package-staging tests; 31 declaration/PR-closure tests. The conflict-refresh Copilot suite passes all 38 tests with ambient profile/config/state variables cleared; an initial ambient-profile setup failure was discarded, not treated as a product regression. Build completed with advisory upstream CSS-size warnings.

### Terminal CI result and attribution

[CI run 40120977526](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40120977526) completed on **a6ab88e95583778fa38829b2f6c6d1efc8cd40cf**: **169 successful jobs, 20 selected skips, 12 failed jobs plus the aggregate gate**. Both required openclaw/ci-gate records are FAILURE. Security Review succeeded. **This is not ready to land and does not qualify as an inherited-only red.**

The repository's own pr-failure-report and pnpm test:ci-failed classified against the newest completed scheduled main available at settlement, run 40116354100. It reported check-docs new, the UI shards pre-existing by job name only, and the remaining failed jobs unknown. Individual logs supplied the missing signatures; completed jobs in the newer same-base scheduled run 40121287574 provide stronger evidence below.

| Failed PR job | Native class | Investigation / evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [check-docs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40120977526/job/120952665892) | new | **PR-caused:** formatter rejects scripts/lib/package-bundled-links.mts after conflict resolution. Reproduced locally with the repository formatter. Earlier local formatting covered the working delta and missed this already-rebased file. |
| [check-lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40120977526/job/120952988503) | unknown | **Same PR-caused formatting issue.** Actual lint subchecks report zero errors. |
| [checks-node-compact-small-6-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40120977526/job/120952668631) | unknown | **PR-caused:** lint-status.test.ts still expects three canonical shards; the new resource-safety shard makes four. Its stub/expected shard inventory needs the new lane. No assertion was weakened. |
| [checks-node-changed-16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40120977526/job/120952668512) | unknown | Baseline-reproduced on main f2fccfab05f3: cli-json-stdout.e2e.test.ts fails the same sandbox diagnostic assertion (1 failed / 38 passed). |
