| [checks-node-compact-small-2-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40120977526/job/120952670542) | unknown | **Unattributed:** PR-wrapper overlapping-install test timed out at 120s in CI. The exact focused case passed locally on main f2fccfab05f3 (~3.45s) and this head (~2.89s). Different-host passes do not establish a flake or baseline failure. |

Main reproductions used the same repository runner with --maxWorkers=1 and cleared profile/config/state environment. No main files were modified; the PR branch was restored cleanly.

**Handoff:** per the one-push/stop instruction, the published head remains unchanged after CI. Parent re-review owns the next source pass: format the rebased package-staging file, update the lint-status fixture for the additional canonical lane, and retain the wrapper timeout as an unresolved attribution gap. No second push, manual CI rerun, skip, timeout bump, or merge was performed.


## Review round 3 — CI repair

Head: **88a48221c8be5f04357530346627c123516cb51d**. One scoped push; no merge. The round-2 CI table above is historical, not this head's result.

- Fixed the rebased package-staging file with the canonical formatter. Whole-repository `CI=true node scripts/run-format.mts --check` now exits 0, including oxfmt/Bun parity. It exited 1 on the preceding head with that exact file.
- Updated the lint-status fixture's tool identity and exact expected inventory to include `scripts:resource-safety`. The actual failure reproduced locally (1 failed / 16 passed) before this repair; all 17 cases now pass. Its existing copied-source compiler keeps linked JSON5 external using the established externalModules option, avoiding a relocated CommonJS dependency resolution failure in this local install. No mock, assertion, skip, or timeout was weakened.
- Focused boundary/sibling proof: **66 tests passed in four files**, 19.97s Vitest / 21.21s wrapper wall time (lint-status, package-bundled-links, run-oxlint, oxlint-resource-safety). Tooling-test typecheck and both affected lint scopes pass. Full-file test audit retained the distinct exit, signal, watchdog, parallel-drain, and ownership-release contracts. Delta: formatting-only tooling +3/-1; test fixture +4/-2.

### Wrapper-timeout investigation

Decoded the exact failed job's compressed plan, preserving all **23 files in three sequential plans**, the CI `bun-all` policy, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2`, and the repository `ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` wrapper. Both local runs used pinned Bun revision `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de` and the same dependency installation; the runner reported inner plan parallelism 1, as in CI. Profile/config/state variables were cleared. Main was restored without changes after the comparison.

| Measurement | Previous PR head a6ab88e9558 | Exact main base f2fccfab05f3 |

| Complete 23-file job wall time | 583.30s | 564.81s |

The timed-out test and its helpers are unchanged. The actual overlap path creates two wrapper dependency stages through the unchanged shell/materialize-dependencies owner and a fixture pnpm process; it does not execute the lint runner or walker before readiness/publication. The PR does add the walker to the copied wrapper source inventory, so the input closure was **not** assumed disjoint. Two other files in the full job were directly changed by this PR (installer smoke and migration-order tests); both completed in their original plans.

**Verdict:** no reproduced hang or material overlap-case slowdown on head. Total local job time differed by 3.3%, wrapper-file time by 0.8%, and the failing case was slightly faster on head. prs.title: fix: trusted proxy readiness probes return 403 without forwarded headers
prs.body:
Fixes #182798

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: configured reverse proxies receive `403 proxy_attribution_required` from Gateway readiness and startup checks when their backend health probes omit forwarded client headers.

## User Impact

Trusted proxies can use the existing aggregate readiness/startup checks without inventing a client address. Healthy backends return 200 and pending backends return 503. Diagnostic details still require attribution and authorization; protected routes and untrusted proxy-shaped sources retain their existing rejection behavior. No new route or configuration option is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dispatcher rejected unattributable ingress before reaching the probe handler that already separates public aggregate status from authenticated diagnostics. The repair moves that existing handler before rejection and removes its former stage registration.

The maintainer rewrite preserves Eric Cai's implementation and regression, adds the existing CIDR-aware trusted-source check so the exception cannot admit untrusted proxy-shaped sources, extends the existing rejection test, and documents the boundary. Contributor commits remain in the branch; credit: @ericcaiwx-star (Eric Cai).

Simplification: one probe owner and one dispatch call, with no new helper or state. Against main, production is +23/−17 (net +6), tests +45/−2, and docs +5/−0. The small production growth is the early return and explicit trusted-source boundary; unrelated cleanup would obscure this repair.

## Evidence

- Source-confirmed on main `3f7b7765585ddcd72822d8b4e43ef928d23eecf7`: [`server-http-request.ts:279`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f7b7765585ddcd72822d8b4e43ef928d23eecf7/src/gateway/server-http-request.ts#L279) rejects before probe dispatch, after [`ingress-attribution.ts:282`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3f7b7765585ddcd72822d8b4e43ef928d23eecf7/src/gateway/ingress-attribution.ts#L282) classifies a headerless trusted proxy as unattributable.
- The regression covers existing ready/startup aliases, GET/HEAD, healthy/pending status, reduced bodies, Content-Length, and protected-route rejection. On base, the first `GET /ready` assertion would receive 403 instead of 200. The extended untrusted-source assertion would fail on the original contributor head, which returned 200 instead of 403. These are source-based failure predictions; no local execution is claimed.
- Exact-head [probe-suite CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133300992/job/120989739188) passed all 16 cases, including the trusted headerless-proxy regression (18 ms) and untrusted-proxy rejection (7 ms).
- Static oxlint with the core configuration, oxfmt on all three changed files, and `git diff --check` passed. `pr-simplify` completed.
- Independent Codex autoreview: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings on repair commit `20ec0cae599a60b041cb6ac87b587064ffe8b4da`. The final main merge leaves all reviewed owner files and the repair diff unchanged.
- Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133300992) passed on `25423214cdf6ada3209aa364a14b0f2ec4ba06fe`: 35 successful jobs, 29 skipped, no failures or retries.
- [ClawSweeper revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182823#issuecomment-6389054456) reviewed that exact head and reported no code findings. Its remaining live-proof-only hold is overridden by the maintainer policy below.

Local regression execution, broad suites, and full typechecks were not run because contributor source is untrusted. Live Gateway/channel e2e and remote leases were skipped per maintainer policy; PR CI owns regression execution and broad proof. The maintainer's proof waiver is recorded in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182823#issuecomment-6389619932). No deployed Traefik/ALB or live Gateway acceptance is claimed. Local file wall time was not measured under this policy; CI case timings are reported above.

prs.body:
## Outcome: merged after measurement attribution

This behavior-tested cleanup merged as `8b31c36236f2ab1f7121e24f2a66afa255c2e633` from reviewed head `179aa1ce881f8d77accd10ae649c0ffb9639d870`. It was initially closed when the single frozen-harness pair exceeded the preregistered warm-window threshold. The maintainer disposition on 2026-10-24 accepts the measured spikes as background placement: the exact same 34-SQL / 12-request / 13-shape bootstrap block moved between execution windows, all 65 captured stack source files are unchanged, and none overlaps this patch. It was reopened and merged under that explicit disposition; the original measurements remain below. No SQL, CPU or latency saving is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

Native date/time consumers carried alternative implementations for missing explicitly requested Intl parts. The patch removes 22 fallback/guard expressions at 17 source locations, including the private session-memory part wrapper and the UTC envelope's no-weekday recovery. Production diff: +18/-42 (net -24); tests: +10/-10 (net 0). No SQL, schema, public signature, security authority, cache, plugin-loading, migration or lifecycle change.

Keep real invalid-date/timezone handling, failed OS preference probes, filesystem recovery, and type-narrowing guards. Hosted review identified a genuine native exception: Node with `TZ=UTC0` can omit the host timezone identifier. The original UTC fallback was restored and verified through `resolveCronStyleNow`, with an owner regression. Deliberately mocked partial `formatToParts` output is not a supported native-runtime contract.

## Acceptance Rule (recorded before measurement)

This is a defensive-code simplification, with no SQL or latency improvement claim. Compare one baseline/candidate warm pair with frozen SQL harness v3.1.4 on synthetic isolated Gateways, using the real transport and identical workload. Report statements, worker requests and MAIN counts for ten warm execution windows and by operation; preserve all expected replies and shutdown completion. No new query/request operation or warm MAIN work is accepted. Investigate any adverse total count and stop on a 20% per-cell change until attributed. This single pair is count evidence, not a statistically qualified timing result; cold and warm counts remain separate. Do not draw latency or CPU conclusions from a loaded host. The shared harness audit found that frozen v3.1.4 causal labels are unavailable on current main; use valid phase-file execution-window counts only, not causal attribution.

## Results

One baseline/candidate pair, ten warm execution windows each; frozen harness v3.1.4 (36/36 hashes verified). Both real synthetic Gateway runs passed, including expected replies, cron, compaction, restart and shutdown. No operator state or logs were read.

| Warm execution-window count | Base median [min–max], p95 | Candidate median [min–max], p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| sql | 51 [50–54], 54 | 51 [50–84], 84 |
| requests | 12.5 [12–13], 13 | 12 [12–23], 23 |
| main | 0 [0–0], 0 | 0 [0–0], 0 |

Warm totals: **512 → 545 SQL**, **125 → 135 requests**, **0 → 0 main-thread SQL**. Whole-workload totals: 3,027 → 3,047 SQL; 806 → 810 requests; 96 → 96 main-thread SQL. SQL p95 increased 55.6% and request p95 increased 76.9%: both exceed the 20% stop rule. No SQL saving or latency claim.

Attribution found an identical bootstrap block of **34 SQL / 12 requests / 13 SQL shapes** in baseline `01.connect` and candidate `03.turn-01/02`: state-lease setup, plugin metadata read/index refresh, and their internal worker operations. The SQL-shape multisets are identical; all 65 source files in captured origin/worker stacks are byte-identical across revisions; none is changed by this patch. All newly warm operations already existed in the baseline workload. A model-catalog statement also crossed an execution-window boundary. The frozen v3.1.4 causal hook is unavailable on this source, so these execution-window counts cannot establish causal per-turn non-regression. The raw threshold was exceeded and the initial stop was honored. prs.title: fix: align bootstrap hardlink safety fixture
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the bootstrap publication test that expected readable content while its own fixture deliberately held the published file in a two-hardlink interval. The production reader correctly rejects that transient state, so the stale expectation made the JavaScript publication fallback fail even though publication later settled to one complete, single-link file.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible product change. The test now preserves the production hardlink-safety policy and distinguishes the states it is responsible for checking: where the async reader can observe both names it fails closed, while Windows synchronously removes the staging name before the reader resumes. A fresh read after publication settles returns the complete bootstrap bytes with one remaining link on every platform.

Production publication and reading code, `@openclaw/fs-safe`, hardlink policy, dependencies, configuration, workflows, timeouts, and adjacent scenarios are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture intercepts the real hardlink creation and starts a workspace read before the publisher removes its temporary name. Current `@openclaw/fs-safe` deliberately yields during that interval as part of its destination-descriptor handoff on supported POSIX platforms, so the reader sees `nlink === 2` and returns the existing hardlink-rejection diagnostic. On Windows that handoff is disabled and cleanup is synchronous, so the async read correctly sees the complete single-link file instead.

This change corrects only that case's oracle. It expects the existing rejection when the injected read observes the two-link interval, preserves the successful overlapping Windows read, retains the terminal `nlink === 1` assertion, and adds a fresh post-settlement workspace read that must return `COMPLETE`. This keeps the proof at the production owner boundary without adding a test-only seam or weakening a guard.

## Evidence

The exact case failed on the base revision because the interval read returned `[UNREADABLE: path must not be hardlinked]` where the stale oracle expected `COMPLETE`.

On the corrected candidate, remote Linux verification passed:

- changed-file formatting and lint: clean, with zero warnings or errors;
- affected test type graph (`core-test-agents-root`): passed;
- full `src/agents/workspace-bootstrap-publish.test.ts`: 7/7 tests passed in 3.91 seconds.

After the cross-platform correction, the same remote Linux gates passed again: formatting/lint clean, affected types passed, and the full owner file passed 7/7 in 3.86 seconds. The Windows ordering is source-qualified against the installed `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.26.13 implementation; exact Windows execution remains pending.

Hosted CI, independent review, and exact-head ClawSweeper reassessment continue on the corrected revision.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope agents.list defaultId to the caller's allowed agents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`agents.list` filters the returned roster to the caller's operator-role allowlist, but spreads the rest of the roster unchanged, so `defaultId` keeps naming the Gateway default agent even when the caller's role forbids it. Every client that falls back to `defaultId` then targets an agent it must not use: the Control UI selection resolves `next.agentId || agentsList?.defaultId` (`ui/src/plugins/control-ui-components.ts:133`), and any picker bootstrap that trusts the field does the same. The picker shows only the allowed agents while the actual send goes to the hidden default and is rejected. Reported with a source repro in #182638.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner, one place: the handler that already filters `agents` also owns the projection of the remaining roster metadata. After the allowlist filter, if the response's `defaultId` is not among the returned agents, the first returned agent becomes `defaultId`. Roster order is already deterministic (default first when present, then alphabetical), so the projection is stable and needs no extra configuration or client change.

Untouched: the `agents` list itself, `mainKey`, `scope`, `ownership`, `selectionRequired`, model-policy presentation, catalog preparation, and the empty-allowlist path (no agents to project, so the previous value is returned unchanged).

Production is `+6/-0` lines; the two suites are `+17/-2` and `+4/-1`, the latter flipping an expectation that pinned the old projection.

## Evidence

Two suites against the same tree, both exercising `agents.list`:

1. **RPC-level, real roster** — `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read.test.ts` calls `agents.list` through the request handler with the real agent roster; its `revoked` case narrows the role to `["research"]` while the response is being prepared, so the default agent disappears from `agents` mid-flight.

`pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-read.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

- main `ae180dc0ad6` + the flipped expectation: **1 failed | 12 passed (13)** — `expected { defaultId: 'ops', …(5) } to match object { defaultId: 'research', …(5) }`.
- candidate `479436a592b`: **13 passed (13)** in 117.3 s.

2. **Handler-level, role policy real** — `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-list.test.ts`; only the roster read (`listAgentsForGateway`) is stubbed.

`pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/agents-list.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

- main + the regression: **3 failed | 5 passed (8)**, all three the same defect (`expected "defaultId": "research"`, `received "defaultId": "ops"` for a role whose `agents` list is `["research"]`).
- candidate: **8 passed (8)** in 98.0 s.

`scripts/run-format.mts --check` on all three changed files: clean.

Reachability chain:

- `src/gateway/agent-list.ts:44-70` — `resolveGatewayAgentSelectionState()` picks `defaultId` as the first configured agent under `agents.ownership: "explicit"`; nothing there knows about operator roles.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/agents.ts:167-171` — the handler filters `agents` by `resolveOperatorRolePolicy(client, currentConfig)?.agents` but previously reused the unfiltered `defaultId`/`mainKey`/`scope` projection.
- `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-components.ts:133` (and `:148`) — the Control UI resolves the active agent as `next.agentId || agentsList?.defaultId || ""`, i.e. it trusts the field when the client has no explicit choice.

## Not tested

No role-authenticated live Gateway run: exercising `agents.list` over WS as a role-bearing user needs `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"` plus forwarded identity headers from a trusted address, which this offline proof host cannot present. The regression above exercises the real handler and role policy; the stubbed layer is the roster read, not the authorization or the projection. The Control UI path was not re-rendered, and the Android client was not run.

prs.title: perf(ui): remove redundant first-screen boot work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat boot still creates avoidable first-screen work and repeatedly collapses displayed pins while their query is replaced.

Related: #182814, #182825. Measured on current main `3df26eebaf4`, including #182813.

## User Impact

The synthetic desktop chat workload now reaches **136.5 ms median boot long tasks**, below the 150 ms target. The final viewport, selectors, retained content, and saved-reader behavior are preserved. Displayed pins remain stable while their authoritative descriptor loads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Create pane field signals only when a tracked reader first needs them, preserving synchronous plain-owner reads. Admit cold authenticated avatars in the next task and recheck the existing credential-scoped cache entry before fetching. Remember live displayed pins through the existing connection-scoped descriptor seed; a missing descriptor still removes the row. During hidden transcript fill, measure rows and decide whether to admit the next row in one pass instead of short-circuiting into another render/geometry pass.

No transcript scheduler, new cache, dependency, owner, or public API was added. The pin seed parameter now names only the descriptor fields it already copies.

## Evidence

Acceptance recorded before measurement: twenty serial interleaved base/control/head triples; identical production bundles for the A/A control; fresh application storage, warm immutable server assets; 390 sessions, 30 pins, 240 messages, avatars enabled, 1719×1179. Production Gateway HTTP/assets with synthetic WebSocket RPCs and media. Untraced timing with renderer thread CPU; no concurrent local checks or builds. Host load was 60.9–79.1, so the A/A readiness spread is material. The retained head is within the 5% timing/CPU band against the faster control; no cell approaches a 20% regression.


### Remaining long-task owners and measured attempts

The following single CPU-profile captures identify owners; profiler overhead inflates their times, so they are **not** the acceptance timings above. Whole-task times are disjoint; source owners within each task overlap.

Rejected prototypes were removed: progressive overscan had 193 → 196.5 ms long tasks; one-row scheduling reached 114.5 ms but delayed transcript readiness by 20.1%; two-row scheduling reached 71.5 ms but delayed it by 11.9%. These were separate paired experiments on the earlier base and are not compared numerically with the current-main run.

- Passed `pnpm tsgo:ui`, focused avatar/field/pin/rail/transcript-geometry tests, scoped oxlint, oxfmt, and the Control UI controller guard. Focused proof was reused across the disjoint main update; final type checking and broad PR CI cover the integrated head.

prs.title: fix: rate-limited runs fail within seconds and stack identical error cards
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: rate-limited turns give up within seconds ("Rate-limit recovery stopped after 9 automatic retries…") while the provider is still saturated, and every automation wake of that session leaves another identical "Unable to finish this reply" card in the chat.

## User Impact

User impact: rate-limited runs now wait patiently (up to roughly ten minutes of backoff) before failing, and a run of identical failures shows as one card with a repeat count ("· 5 times") instead of a stack of duplicates. Try again still sits on the newest failure. Transcripts are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same-model rate-limit retries waited exactly the provider's hint. OpenAI tokens-per-minute 429s say "try again in ~1s", so under sustained org saturation all nine retries fired about a second apart, concurrent sessions retried in lock-step, and the budget was gone almost immediately.

- The failover retry controller now treats provider timing as a minimum wait under jittered exponential backoff. For rate limits the backoff caps at 60 seconds (other transient failures keep 30 seconds, eight retries, and the 90-second window). Longer provider floors are still honored, subject to the existing `retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs` failover check.
- The rate-limit budget grows from 10 to 16 attempts (15 retries) per consecutive outage, including the ceiling for `retry.provider.maxRetries` overrides. A completed model response still resets the budget.
- The Control UI collapses consecutive run-failure notices with an identical summary into the latest one and shows the count. Only real user input breaks a streak; agent updates, automation wakes, internal retry prompts, tool rows, and partial output do not. Different errors still show separately. This is display-only.

Accepted edge case: the first retries still follow a short provider hint closely; the backoff only takes over once it exceeds the hint. Not changed here: automation updates can still wake a session that is cooling down. That scheduling change is a possible follow-up if patient retries alone don't cover it.

Docs: `docs/concepts/retry.md` and `docs/concepts/model-failover.md` describe the new budget, cap, and floor semantics.

## Evidence

Before (five identical failure cards between synthetic automation updates):

![Before: five stacked identical failure cards](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d79d6ff8-a467-46aa-a4c4-644e141cf50f)

After (one card, "· 5 times", Try again on the newest run):

![After: one failure card with a repeat count](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b8ae0696-fcfb-4b9d-ace9-ed19d93e8f57)

Screenshots are from the Control UI e2e harness with a mocked, synthetic transcript.

- New and updated retry-controller tests fail on the base controller (6 failed; the unchanged explicit `budget=3` case passes) and pass with the fix: `failover-retry-controller.test.ts` 40/40.
- `run.shared-integration.test.ts` 160/160; `model-fallback.reply-entry.e2e.test.ts` + `model-fallback.run-embedded.e2e.test.ts` 38/38.
- UI: failure-streak projection, run-failure notice render, and chat-thread build tests 94/94 (normal and search views). The streak/render checks failed before the change.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, format, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `git diff --check` passed.

- CI-found consumer expectations updated in `attempt-recovery.test.ts` and the OpenRouter classification integration; affected tests pass 128/128 and 9/9.
- Cached-history repeat counts fixed in `a7637c585f77`: the history-prepend regression fails without the notice equality field and passes with it; streak/thread/notice tests pass 95/95.

## What Problem This Solves

The disabled-restart regression fails when owner authorization reads an existing shared-state database, because the test counts an idle database-reader timer as restart work.

## User Impact

There is no runtime behavior change. The restart policy tests remain deterministic when prior Gateway state exists, and still check refusal, deferred authority revocation, and persistence of the completion notice before restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture now creates prior state through the existing restart-sentinel owner before installing fake timers. The refusal cases advance the coordinator's immediate deadline and assert that no `SIGUSR2` is emitted, instead of requiring every subsystem to have zero timers. Exact rejection reasons and the remaining cancellation and notice assertions are retained.

This introduces no production code, mocks, real sleeps, schemas, or new configuration. Simplification retained one suite-level state seed and changed only the invalid refusal assertion: production +0/-0, tests +9/-4, docs +0/-0.

## Evidence

- Scheduled main [run 40130094950, job 120979998415](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40130094950/job/120979998415) fails `refuses disabled before scheduling` with one timer instead of zero, matching the earlier scheduled run.
- The initial isolated Node run passed 6/6 with no prior shared-state database. On main's unchanged assertion, adding the real prior-state fixture reproduces the exact disabled-case failure: **1 failed, 5 passed**, 28.39s Vitest / 35.38s wrapper. This isolates the missing fixture condition instead of treating a passing replay as a fix.
- With the assertion repair and the same state fixture, the full file passes **6/6** on Node 26.12.1: 15.06s Vitest / 21.03s wrapper. Command: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/restart-owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Scoped oxlint using `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Named test, authorization, and reader-owner inputs are unchanged between the initial main checkout `721cdadccb93` and fresh main `fd0eee8790b6`, merged before publication.
- Independent Codex autoreview through P2: **scoped-clean**, zero findings.
- Live e2e, remote leases, broad local suites, and full local typechecks were skipped per maintainer policy.
- Exact-head [CI run 40134160323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40134160323) passed on `87fd08df23f94d469776f23b14a185012b2d9898`: **20 successful jobs, 31 skipped**. The targeted Gateway test job took 80s. Final PR checks are **42 passed, 63 skipped**, with none pending or failed. The native watcher reported GREEN after excluding 79 superseded check contexts.
- Automatic GitHub Codex review completed on that exact head without findings. ClawSweeper has acknowledged the PR but has not published findings.

prs.title: fix(ingress): bound pre-adoption abandonment with the existing retry budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An ingress row can defer its turn to the reply queue and then end without ever being admitted. When that happens, the row is released with `lastError: "turn-abandoned"` and an attempt recorded, but the retry policy is never consulted. Such a row can therefore retry forever:
- `attempts` climbs past `maxAttempts`;
- the row never dead-letters;
- it holds the head of its lane, so the messages behind it never run.

Sending abandonment through the shared retry disposition takes a single hunk, but that is only safe once intentional cancellation stops arriving as abandonment. On main, the reply queue settles every unadmitted turn through `onAbandoned`:
- `TurnAdoptionLifecycle` has no `onCancelled`;
- the ingress binding omits it;
- the inbound debounce flush drops it.

Bounding abandonment on its own would therefore charge these as failures: queue clears, Stop cleanup, drops of aborted followups, collect-group aborts and gateway shutdown. That was the P1 on the earlier head of this PR.

This PR lands both halves:
- **`fix(reply)`** makes `onCancelled` part of the reply terminal contract:
  - every intentional relinquish site uses it;
  - both dedupe owners release on either terminal callback;
  - fan-in always offers `onCancelled`.
- **`fix(ingress)`** settles `onAbandoned` through `applyFailureDisposition`. It records one attempt, respects `maxAttempts` and `deadLetterMinAgeMs`, and dead-letters as `retry-limit-exceeded`.

There is no AsyncLocalStorage compatibility flag. Every lifecycle that reaches a fan-in carries `onCancelled`, so the consumer makes the flag unnecessary.

## Since Revision 20 → Revision 21 (head `9fd80c6cdbd`)

**Change:** a merge of upstream `main` `93a9fa4562b`, which was 631 commits ahead, into `cd8a6e26fe`. It had no conflicts (`diff-filter=U` and a marker grep were both empty), and nothing in this PR's own diff changed. The history is kept: a merge commit, then a fast-forward. Nothing was rebased.

**Gate at exact head `9fd80c6cdbd`** (Linux x86-64, Node 26.12.1):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:test:src` exit 0.
- Vitest: 67 files and 884 tests pass. The set is this PR's changed tests plus every test that imports a changed module from the same directory.
- The Telegram cancellation e2e (`telegram-ingress-coalescing.cancellation.e2e`) passes 1/1.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and `check-line-cap-ratchet --base 93a9fa4562b` are clean.
- The tree was clean at the start and at the end.

**New:** the shipped-Gateway proof that the last review asked for. It is the `## Evidence` section below. The earlier boundary-harness evidence stays, under "Earlier evidence".

## Evidence

**Behavior or issue addressed:** an ingress row that defers to the reply queue and is then released without being admitted. Two halves:
- Intentional relinquish (Stop / queue clear, Gateway shutdown) must release the row **without spending retry budget**.
- Genuine abandonment (for example a `queue-cap` rejection) must go through the shared retry disposition, so `maxAttempts` bounds it.

**Before evidence:** shipped Gateway at upstream `main` `93a9fa4562b`, same harness and steps as the after-fix runs (3/3 runs per scenario):
- After `/stop`, the queued row that Stop relinquished has spent one attempt (`attempts=1`).
- After a clean Gateway shutdown, the queued row is `pending attempts=1 last_error=turn-abandoned`. A shutdown is charged as a failed attempt.
- A `queue-cap` rejection releases the row with `attempts+1` and `last_error=turn-abandoned`, and logs no retry-disposition line.

**Real environment tested:** the shipped Gateway (`node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway`) on Linux x86-64 with Node 26.12.1, from a clean worktree at the head and one at the base. Everything else was loopback-only:
- **Channel:** the production Discord plugin, reaching a loopback mock of Discord REST plus WebSocket Gateway through the production `DISCORD_API_URL` override. The mock was adapted from the #121204 proof corpus.
- **Agent:** the bundled Codex 0.162.1 app-server as agent runtime (`agentRuntime.id: "codex"`), pointed at a scripted Responses endpoint.
- **Isolation:** its own state directory, config and ports. No real Discord, model provider, credential or host Gateway was involved.
- **Message flow:** messages enter as `MESSAGE_CREATE` frames and pass through the production listener, ingress monitor, SQLite ingress queue, drain, reply queue and agent turn. Replies leave as REST sends, recorded by the mock with their text.
- **Busy turn:** a `HOLD-1` message keeps one turn busy through repeated `sleep` tool calls, so later messages queue behind it.

Config:
- `messages.queue`: `followup`, `cap: 1`, `drop: old | new`; one run used `collect`, `cap: 2`, `drop: old` in a guild channel.
- `messages.inbound.debounceMs: 0`.
- Discord DM allowlist plus one open guild.
- Discord's production ingress policy: `maxAttempts: 8`, `deadLetterMinAgeMs: 0`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
- Head: `9fd80c6cdbd`, which is this PR's `cd8a6e26fe` with upstream `main` `93a9fa4562b` merged in. The merge was clean; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:test:src` all exit 0.
- Each run (`scenario.sh <scenario> <side> <n> <tree>`):
  1. starts the mock, the scripted provider and the Gateway;
  2. sends `HOLD-1`;
  3. sends one or more `MSG-*` while the turn is busy;
  4. does the scenario action (below);
  5. snapshots `channel_ingress_events` from a copy of the state database (status, attempts, `last_error`, `failed_reason`).
- Scenario actions:
  - **cancel:** `/stop` while `MSG-A` is queued.
  - **restart:** SIGTERM the Gateway while `MSG-A` is queued, then start it again on the same state.
  - **abandon:** `drop:new` with the one slot held by `MSG-A`, then `MSG-B`. Variants: `drop:old`, and a 12-message guild burst under `collect`.

**Evidence after fix:**

| Scenario (runs) | Head `9fd80c6cdbd` | Base `main` `93a9fa4562b` |
|---|---|---|
| Stop clears the queued `MSG-A` (3 + 3) | `completed attempts=0`, 3/3 | `completed attempts=1`, 3/3 |
| Shutdown with `MSG-A` queued (3 + 3) | `pending attempts=0`, no `last_error`, 3/3 | `pending attempts=1 last_error=turn-abandoned`, 3/3 |
| Restart redelivery of that row (3 + 3) | delivered once, one `ack MSG-A`, `completed attempts=0`, 3/3 | delivered once, one `ack MSG-A`, `completed attempts=1`, 3/3 |
| First `queue-cap` rejection (5 + 3) | `[discord] ingress: spooled update msg#04 failed; keeping for retry: turn-abandoned`, then `attempts=1` | silent release, `attempts=1 last_error=turn-abandoned` |
| Guild burst, `collect` cap 2 (1 + 1) | 5 `keeping for retry: turn-abandoned` lines, all 14 rows `completed`, every message answered | 0 such lines, all 14 rows `completed`, every message answered |

**Observed result after fix:**
- Stop and Gateway shutdown now release the row without spending an attempt, and the restart still redelivers it exactly once.
- A genuine `queue-cap` abandonment is now settled through the retry disposition, bounded by `maxAttempts`.

**Additional real-environment observation (production seat, fork build; not this exact head).** This was observed on a long-running production Gateway, not run by the harness above.

- **Setup:** real Discord, a real native-Codex agent, and real room traffic. No production state was changed to collect this.
- **Build:** the fork build `7d8a1a91c6`. It contains this PR at an earlier revision, `51631e61a2`, merged as `3d05df8b5f5` (verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`).
- **Same settlement:** its `onCancelled` / `onAbandoned` settlement in `src/channels/message/ingress-drain.ts` is semantically the same as this head `9fd80c6cdbd`, differing only in formatting: `releaseClaim(…, { recordAttempt: false })` and `applyFailureDisposition(…, new Error("turn-abandoned"))`. The surrounding files differ by later upstream merges. This is therefore evidence about the settlement path, not a receipt for this SHA.

**What happened:** on 2026-10-24 a burst of room messages overflowed the seat's reply-queue cap (`drop: "old"`). The queue-cap drop then re-dispatched ingress, which is a separate defect (#182252). That produced quick, repeated pre-adoption abandonment, the shape the loopback harness above could not reproduce.

**Gateway journal**, one process lifetime from 20:07:31Z to about 22:03Z (redacted):
- **1,006 events:** `[discord] ingress: spooled update <id> failed; keeping for retry: turn-abandoned`.
- **0 `handler-timeout` lines observed in that window.** This means none was observed in that window; it is not a claim that the watchdog can never take this path.
- **254 lines** of the shapes `spooled update <id> failed with non-retryable retry-limit-exceeded: turn-abandoned; dead-lettered` and `spooled update <id> on lane channel:<id> reached retry limit after 8 attempts; dead-lettered` (`maxAttempts: 8`).

**State DB**, read from a consistent copy at about 22:03Z, counting rows (not events) received from 19:30Z on that lane:
- **119 rows** ended `failed / retry-limit-exceeded`;
- **121 rows** completed after the first dead-letter at 20:09:41Z, so the lane kept making progress.

**What this supports:** abandonment retries were bounded at `maxAttempts`, and later messages on the same lane went on to complete.

**What this does not prove:** that each abandoned attempt settled correctly, or that this PR alone caused the recovery.

**Telegram** interactive-submission cancellation remains **untested**.

Redaction: no message, channel or session IDs; no host name, content or credentials; no raw journal or DB attachment.

**What was not tested:**
- **Dead-letter through abandonment.** In every Discord shape above, the redelivered row waits behind the busy turn on its channel. After the first abandonment, each further attempt is therefore settled by the 300 s claim→adoption watchdog (`handler-timeout`), and that path applies the retry policy on head and base alike.
  - A 42-minute run on each side ended identically: `spooled update msg#04 on lane channel:<dm-channel> reached retry limit after 8 attempts; dead-lettered` within 0.3 s of each other, then `MSG-C` was answered.
  - So the base defect (abandonment re-dispatching past `maxAttempts`) was not reached in this harness. The proof shows the disposition change, not a lane that main leaves blocked.
  - The production observation above shows the bounded path and lane progress on a fork build that carries this settlement. It is not a base-side contrast: every observed seat already carried the fix.
- **Telegram** interactive-submission cancellation: this needs a Telegram Test Server bot token, which this run did not have.
- Other channels (Slack, SMS, LINE, Twitch, Feishu) and native Discord commands.
- A real model and real Discord.

Redacted receipts (21 runs, the harness, the gate): https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/fe333eff401c78b165b06e7ad77af99bcc654baf/PR-124337/PROOFS/9fd80c6cdbd8d67ea6b27ac1b1bf19471eef225f/GATEWAY-DISCORD. Each run has `meta.txt`, `rows.txt`, mock Discord and provider JSONL, and Gateway logs. They use synthetic snowflakes only, with the home path and host name removed.

## Since Revision 20 (head `cd8a6e26fe`)

**Change `cd8a6e26fe`** (test only): drops the helper-only "pre-retry release ahead of both terminal callbacks" case from `queue/lifecycle.test.ts`, as the review at `8da32c408e` suggested. The wrapped-rejection cases keep the release-before-callback coverage.

**Upgrade / data-model compatibility.** Corpus: [`UPGRADE-v2026.10.6`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/1d38ccd0333be93e8775193c4cfb1d63ea20aa86/PR-124337/PROOFS/cd8a6e26fecc7a256533c4bcf79219d63f8d7344/UPGRADE-v2026.10.6).
- **Seeding:** the latest stable release, v2026.10.6, writes seven ingress rows into a fresh state: pending, released with 2 attempts and a last error, abandoned under the limit, over the limit (6 attempts, limit 3), a cancel case, dead-lettered, and a dead-owner claim.
- **Migration:** upstream's `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates the state schema from 20 to 31. This PR changes nothing in `src/state`.
- **Drain:** this head drains the migrated state. As controls, stable drains an unmigrated copy and upstream `7ab64536d3` drains a migrated copy, all with the same retry policy.
- **What carries over:** the retry facts stable wrote. The head reads attempts and the last error as stored and counts attempts on from there, without resetting them. A later successful completion clears `last_error`, exactly as it does upstream.
- **Cancellation and settled rows:** the cancelled row spends no attempt, the dead-lettered row is never dispatched, and the dead-owner claim is recovered as stale.
- **The one difference from both controls is the over-limit row.** At this head it is dispatched once, then dead-lettered as `retry-limit-exceeded` with its attempts and last error kept. Both controls keep re-dispatching it (still pending at 18 attempts after 12 passes). That is the defect this PR fixes.
- **Schema:** the ingress table schema and index are identical across stable, this head and upstream.

**Checks at `cd8a6e26fe`:** `queue/lifecycle.test.ts` 17/17, oxfmt and oxlint clean. Everything else is as at Revision 19 (`8da32c408e`); the only difference is this one test file.

**Still open:** shipped-Gateway / real-transport cancellation, restart and abandonment, and the Telegram Test Server interactive-submission case.

## Since Revision 19 (head `8da32c408e`)

This revision brings the branch up to upstream main `7ab64536d3` (2026-10-23). History is kept: merges and fast-forwards only.

**Back-merge `8da32c408e`** (merge of `7ab64536d3`):
- Upstream folded `queue/recent-message-ids.ts` into `queue/enqueue.ts` (#181498). The recent-source release there now goes through `releaseBeforeTurnAdoptionRetry`, so a cancelled queued turn also forgets its recent message id, as before.
- `dispatch-from-config.prepare-context.ts`: kept the `releaseBeforeTurnAdoptionRetry` import. `waitForReplyDispatcherIdle` is unused after #181105, so it is dropped.
- Upstream removed `createTwitchIngress`'s `pollIntervalMs` option (#180700). The aged-cancelled Twitch test no longer passes it. That was the `check-test-types` red at Revision 18, since CI type-checks the PR merged with main.

**Test added: `3fbec00bb7`.** When `onCancelled` starts a Feishu flush's settlement and `onAbandoned` and `onAdopted` overlap it, the transport settles once through `onCancelled` (no retry budget). The logical claim is released once, and nothing adopts or commits. As a mutation control, setting `settled` after the await makes it fail on the intended assertion.

**Checks at `8da32c408e` (Linux x86_64, Node 26.12.1):**
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test` and `tsgo:extensions:test` are clean. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the PR's changed files.
- One grouped run of 619 test files: 30 tests in 3 files failed. Run alone 3 times a side, each matches upstream main `7ab64536d3`:
  - `dispatch-from-config.delivery`: 27 fail on both sides, with identical test names ("Physical session already has a different controller owner").
  - `dispatch-from-config.lifecycle`: 1 fails on both sides, the same test as at Revision 18.
  - `progress-narrator-model`: passes 4/4 on both sides, a grouped-load flake.
- `db:worker-inventory:check` is stale at upstream main itself. A regen changes rows only for files this PR doesn't touch.
- The Telegram cancellation e2e passed.

## Since Revision 18 (head `2407313ae0`)

This revision brings the branch up to upstream main `827aae9c0b` (2026-10-22). It adds one fix that upstream needs as well. History is kept: these are merges and fast-forwards only, no rebase.

**Back-merges.**
- `e7ef059e18`, `15499d136a` and `1add83f4a1` merge upstream `9c87c4e826`, `646647245f` and `79ab1c4907`.
- `3cd32643c6` merges upstream main `827aae9c0b`.

Upstream rebuilt the follow-up queue on the session controller (#175837), so `1add83f4a1` re-applies this PR's cancellation onto upstream's shapes rather than merging textually:
- `queue/lifecycle.ts` adds `releaseBeforeTurnAdoptionRetry`, `cancelFollowupRunLifecycle` and a `"cancelled"` disposition.
- `session-controller.mailbox-source.ts` routes a cancelled disposition, or an aborted lifecycle signal, to `onCancelled`. A committed `abortSessionControllerInput` counts as cancellation.
- Queue clear, Stop cleanup and restart-cleared waiting inputs settle as cancelled.
- The adapters (Feishu, LINE, MS Teams, Telegram, Twitch, inbound debounce) carry `onCancelled` through upstream's shared bindings.

**Fix, `493d5bf21f`: release unadopted sources when a drained run returns.** This bug exists on upstream main as well.
- Upstream's `executeClaim` marks every source of a run that returns normally as consumed. A source that was never adopted is included, and consumed suppresses its terminal callbacks.
- Its durable ingress claim is then held until the adoption-stall watchdog fails it as `handler-timeout` (5 min). That charges an attempt even to a source whose owner aborted.
- Reproduced at `79ab1c4907`: both claims stay held, then are dead-lettered under a one-attempt policy.
- Now a normal return completes an unadopted source without the consumed disposition. An aborted owner cancels (no attempt); a live one abandons (one attempt). Adopted sources stay consumed. Throws keep upstream's no-replay rule unless the producer refused before execution.
- The collect-group cancellation test is restored on upstream's fixtures.

**Tests added.**
- `c7f27a7410` drives `bindSessionControllerMailboxRestartDrain` through the durable boundary. A waiting ingress claim is released on gateway restart with no attempt charged: `onCancelled` fires once, `onAbandoned` never fires, and nothing is dead-lettered.
- `2407313ae0` follows upstream's narrowed test seams (#180003): the Slack duplicate-wait test stubs the replay guard by module mock, and the Twitch test-message helper takes the id as a string.

**Not carried 1:1** (the reviewers' rulings are in the thread):
1. `containSettlement` is dropped. Upstream now awaits async `onAbandoned`/`onCancelled` and records a rejection as that input's settlement failure.
2. A run whose own abort signal fired and that completes unconsumed counts as cancellation (`completeFollowupRunLifecycle`).
3. Twitch shutdown/`handedOff`: upstream's adapter no longer has this handling, and upstream's choice is kept.

**Checks at `2407313ae0` (Linux x86_64, Node 26.12.1):**
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test` and `tsgo:extensions:test` are clean.
- `db:worker-inventory:check` is current. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the PR's changed `.ts` files.
- One grouped run of 619 test files: this PR's suites plus everything under `src/auto-reply/reply`, `src/sessions` and `src/channels/message`, and the adapter suites the merges touched. 3 tests in 2 files failed, and both match upstream main `827aae9c0b` when run alone (3 runs per side):
  - `dispatch-from-config.lifecycle` › "audits an aborted prepared-runtime wait as a skipped reply operation" fails 3/3 alone on both sides with the same test.
  - `progress-narrator-model` passes alone in 3 of 3 runs on both sides (4/4 tests each); its two grouped reds are a load flake.
  - The run started at the merge `3cd32643c6`. The two test-seam files were committed mid-run as `2407313ae0`; they pass alone at this head, 10/10 and 1/1.
- The Telegram cancellation e2e: passed (1/1).
- Three fork reviewers re-reviewed `493d5bf21f` at that exact head and found no blockers.

**Still open:**
- The boundary harness has not been rerun at this head. The last proof corpus is at `ee2f6dfdf6` (Revision 17).
- ClawSweeper's request for shipped-Gateway / real-transport cancellation and restart evidence, and for Telegram Test Server proof, is still outstanding.

## Since Revision 17 (head `ee2f6dfdf651a8bd4416edb435335c5393190c5e`)

This revision addresses ClawSweeper's review of `e682f7cc17` (fast-forward; no rebase):
- **`7cab4e61eb`, [P1] cancel LINE's unhanded delivery when shutdown returns ownership.** In `extensions/line/src/webhook-spool.ts`, the stop branch for a delivery that returned without `onAdopted` or `onDeferred` now ends ownership through `fannedIn.cancel()` instead of `fannedIn.abandon()`. A row at the retry ceiling is no longer dead-lettered as `retry-limit-exceeded` on stop. The new test "keeps an aged row at the retry ceiling recoverable when shutdown ends an unhanded delivery" covers the active-delivery-return case. It passes (16/16) and fails with only this fix reverted (15/16).
- **`2b67393ddd`, `5c214fa2a4`, `cd45f79821`, [P3] await owned settlement signals instead of polling.** Every `vi.waitFor` this PR added, across 10 test files, is gone. The tests now await one of three signals:
  - the queue's committed write, through `observeChannelIngressQueueWrite`, or the new `observeChannelIngressQueueWrites`, which wraps each queue method once so several observers can't stack;
  - the drain's own `claimNext` commit;
  - deferreds that the owned turns resolve.
  
  These commits are test-only.
- `ee2f6dfdf6`: two lint fixes in the Slack tests (a bound `claimNext`, an unused import).

**Checks at `ee2f6dfdf6` (Linux arm64):**
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test` and `tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- 35/35 focused test files pass.
- `pnpm check` fails only in its lint step. None of the reported files is in this PR's diff against `042db1e706`; the remaining errors (max-lines, ui) are in files this PR doesn't touch.
- The Telegram cancellation e2e passed 3 of 3 repeated runs.

**Proof.** The boundary harness was rerun at this exact head with the same bytes, against control `042db1e706`. Every verdict and final SQLite row matches the `0cb65da5f2` corpus. The corpus is at https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/615595b9fcc318c8c6d45d4a4f0db2ad9069a7a9/PR-124337/PROOFS/ee2f6dfdf651a8bd4416edb435335c5393190c5e

**Still open:** ClawSweeper's request for shipped-Gateway / real-transport cancellation and restart evidence, plus Telegram Test Server proof for cancelled interactive submissions. That needs a Telegram test bot and account, and is not covered by the harness above.

## Since Revision 16 (head `e682f7cc17fdbc34f299b6703e11aa23d90c120c`)

Revision 16 had no findings; the branch had since gone conflicting with main. This head merges upstream main `042db1e706` into `51631e61a23` (merge `8853b1ae51c`; no rebase) and adds two test-only commits. Upstream had refactored the follow-up queue and Feishu settlement, so the cancellation half is re-applied onto upstream's shapes rather than merged textually:
- `completeFollowupRuns` forwards an optional disposition; stop, clear and aborted collect/summary sources settle as `cancelled` through it.
- `consumeQueueSummaryDelivery` keeps its settlement argument; upstream's boolean `false` calls are `"retained"`.
- `dropAbortedFollowups` stays in `aborted-followups.ts` (re-exported from `drain.ts`) and settles through `completeFollowupRuns(…, "cancelled")`.
- Feishu broadcast: a `cancelled` lane state on upstream's pending/deferred/completed/failed model. Feishu flush and delivery, Slack and Telegram regain `onCancelled`; Telegram's abort-reason mapping now lives in `abortedProcessingResult`.
- `c6cfd25c543`: the ingress-cancellation test follows upstream's dispatch fixture move to `dispatch-from-config.test-support.ts`. `0cb65da5f22`: the Slack cancellation test's mocks spread the real modules (first-party mock export ratchet).

- `e682f7cc17f`: oxfmt only. It folds one `if` condition in `bot-handlers.callback-router-controls.ts` onto one line, so behaviour is byte-equivalent to `0cb65da5f2`, where the checks and proof below ran.

Checks at `0cb65da5f2` (Linux arm64): `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; 35/35 focused test files (this PR's suites plus the queue, drain, Feishu, Slack and Telegram suites the merge touched). `pnpm check` fails three ratchets (line-cap growth, max-lines suppression, assertion SAFETY comment) that fail identically on main `042db1e706` and name no file in this PR. The boundary proof below was rerun at `0cb65da5f2`. CI note: `src/plugin-sdk/channel-inbound.test.ts` › "dispatches a published inbound event before automatic session maintenance" fails on main `b3c7dc2af7` itself (3 of 3 local runs), but passes at this branch's tree (`042db1e706` base). It touches nothing in this PR.

## Since Revision 14 (head `51631e61a238de75ae0207af541b341e6edeac0e`)

The branch is rebased onto main `2983dfcfb3` and merges cleanly into main `f986a7aaf1`. The two original commits change only in rebase-conflict hunks: upstream's new `readLaneBacklog` stays drain-only, the vitest path list keeps both entries, and Telegram uses upstream's participant heartbeat. On top of them:

| commit | addresses | change |
|---|---|---|
| `4dd7877d56a` | [P1] carry cancellation through custom channel lifecycle adapters | Telegram, Twitch, and Feishu's merged and broadcast lifecycles forward `onCancelled`. Feishu's pre-flush cleanup runs on cancellation too. |
| `06cd20afc87` | [P1] preserve Slack replay and migration cleanup on cancellation | Both Slack owners wrap cancellation: `releaseClaims()` and `settleTurn()` run, then cancellation is forwarded budget-free. |
| `6ff545fd490` | [P2] clean up deferred MMS attachments on cancellation | The MMS lifecycle has its own cancellation wrapper that cleans up before forwarding. |
| `784a1f1f437` | same class | LINE ends shutdown-rejected ownership by cancellation, not abandonment, because the core types define shutdown as cancellation. |
| `5f713b6bd7d` | same class | Feishu message and comment paths whose abort already fired cancel instead of abandoning. Real dispatch failures still abandon. |
| `3cd7de6f3d4` | found in review | SMS: a rejected MMS unlink no longer skips settlement. Cleanup failure is logged, and the owner settles once, for both cancel and abandon. |
| `d1c4823226e` | found in review | Core `completeFollowupRunLifecycle` contains a rejected async `onCancelled` or `onAbandoned` (logged via the runtime error log). The callback still starts synchronously, and `onSettled` still runs right after it. |
| `bcbc2837f4e` | found in review | Telegram albums: cancelling a coalesced turn settled every participant as `failed-retryable`, which dead-lettered non-head members at the ceiling. A `{ kind: "cancelled" }` result now routes to each member's own `onCancelled`, and the update tracker treats cancelled like retryable (not completed), so dedupe cannot swallow the redelivery. |
| `53cb34f058` | found in review | The dedupe wrapper `releaseBeforeTurnAdoptionRetry` now returns `onAbandoned`'s result, so core can contain its rejection on the wrapped path. |
| `cb1cd8a1d0f` | Revision 15 [P3] mock isolation | The two new Telegram dispatch mocks spread the real module (`importOriginal`) and override only `buildTelegramMessageContext` and `dispatchTelegramMessage`. |
| `4a6c265fa80` | Revision 15 [P3] `drain.ts` line cap | `dropAbortedFollowups` moved verbatim into the sibling module `queue/aborted-followups.ts`; only the parameter type changed, to a named subset alias. `drain.ts` re-exports it, so existing `drain.js` module mocks still catch the call. The baseline is unchanged. |
| `51631e61a23` | Revision 15 [P3] e2e line cap | `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` is restored to its upstream content. The aged-album cancellation regression moved unchanged into `telegram-ingress-coalescing.cancellation.e2e.test.ts`, which uses the shared fixtures; the bundled-plugin e2e glob includes it. |

**New tests.** Each new test failed before its fix and passes after it.
- The aged-row tests seed a row at 7/8 attempts with `lastError` "prior failure". They cancel the deferred turn, then assert that nothing is dead-lettered and that the row returns with attempts and error intact. These run on the real durable SQLite queue for Telegram (single update and a two-member album), Twitch, Feishu (merged turn and handler-entry abort) and LINE (late deferral at shutdown).
- Slack migration fence: a cancelled deferred turn lets a queued `channel_id_changed` run. Before the fix, `stop()` waited on it indefinitely.
- Rejection tests run the failing callback directly and behind the dedupe wrapper. They assert the order release → callback → `onSettled`, that there is no unhandled rejection, and that the error is logged. They check the error text, not a count of log calls.

## Known boundary

- Reply-queue cap evictions still settle as genuine abandonment, which is one bounded attempt. That is intended.
- IRC forwards `onCancelled`, but it does not update its local handoff state on cancellation. That would only matter for a cancellation before `onDeferred`, which the reply lane does not send.
- Channels that call `onAbandoned` on real dispatch failures (Mattermost, MS Teams, Signal) are unchanged. Those failures are charged attempts, as intended.

## Earlier evidence (boundary harness, head `0cb65da5f2`)

**Real behavior** (central fix). I ran a production-module boundary harness at this exact head `0cb65da5f2283965905abe1c55aca505e8139550`, with main `042db1e7064930a08c534c4487864d7bfb8c5287` (the merge's second parent) as the control. The chain is the channel ingress monitor → the durable SQLite ingress queue → the drain → the bound reply/followup queue. There is no vitest and nothing in the chain under test is mocked. Each scenario ends with a projection of the SQLite row. Every verdict matches the earlier run at `b2d5e48e5b`.

| scenario | this PR | main (control) |
|---|---|---|
| queued message, then gateway stop (restart-drain clears the followup queue) | **budget-free**: `attempts=0`, no `lastError` | **charged**: `attempts=1`, `lastError=turn-abandoned` |
| restart in a fresh process | redelivered, adopted, completed | redelivered, completed |
| genuine pre-adoption abandonment (reply queue at cap), `maxAttempts=3` | **dead-lettered** `retry-limit-exceeded` / `turn-abandoned` on the 3rd delivery, and the next row in the lane completes | **not dead-lettered** at `attempts=6` (2× the limit) when observation stopped, and the lane stayed blocked |

- Corpus, README and method: https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/a499e4a22b/PR-124337/PROOFS/0cb65da5f2283965905abe1c55aca505e8139550 (earlier corpus at `b2d5e48e5b`: https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/a2cf9d60fabd7ddb5ee6a985365d60c16eb99bf1/PR-124337/PROOFS/b2d5e48e5b59da6d1d29b2bfb7b2af51aee58f0a)
- Raw logs: `logs/{head,control}-{A1,A2,B}.log` in that directory.
- What this is not: there is no gateway server and no transport socket. The channel plugin is a minimal stand-in, and the agent turn is a stub that adopts through `admitFollowupRunLifecycle`. `METHOD.md` lists every limit. The adapter fixes in this revision are covered by the real-queue tests above, not by this harness.

**Failing control (unit).** At the earlier head, with the production files reverted to main and the tests kept at head, 11 assertions across 6 files fail. They pass at head.

**Tests** (focused, Linux): at `bcbc2837f4e`, 335/335 across 30 files. The set covers the adapter suites above, `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e`, the reply lifecycle, the ingress drain and lifecycle, and the ingress-cancellation dispatch suite. The final commit `53cb34f058` changes only `lifecycle.ts` and its test, which were re-run at that head: lifecycle 14/14, cancellation 4/4.

**Revision 15 policy checks at `51631e61a23`:**
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base 2983dfcfb3`: OK.
- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base 2983dfcfb3`: OK.
- lifecycle + ingress-cancellation: 18/18 (`--maxWorkers=1`, 15 s).
- telegram-ingress-drain + coalescing e2e: 57/57 (`--maxWorkers=1`, 70 s).
- the new cancellation e2e suite on its own: 1/1. Vitest itself took 35 s; the first run's plugin-SDK rebuild is the rest of the wall time.
- queue suites and the gateway tests that mock `drain.js`: 247/247.
- `check:import-cycles`: 0.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.

**Typecheck:** `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` are clean at `bcbc2837f4e`. `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` are clean at `53cb34f058`. `oxfmt` is clean.

prs.title: fix(macos): keep the latest Browser toggle when clicks overlap
prs.body:
Closes #127616 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the macOS menu bar's Browser button silently reverts to the older value (and saves it) when it is clicked twice within one config save round trip. ## User Impact Turning Browser Control off and back on quickly now ends with Browser on, both in the menu and in the Gateway config. A single click behaves exactly as before. ## Why This Change Was Made Each Browser click started its own untracked `Task` that loaded the whole config, flipped `browser.enabled`, and saved it with that read's `baseHash`. Two quick clicks read the same revision, the Gateway correctly rejected the second save as stale, and the catch block reloaded and published the older persisted value over the newer click. The fix keeps the existing `ConfigStore` load/save and the Gateway's compare-and-swap (CAS) unchanged. It moves the menu's two private Browser functions into one small owner, `BrowserControlSetting`, beside the view: - a click updates the shown value and bumps an intent counter; - only one save runs at a time, claimed synchronously so clicks delivered in the same turn cannot start a second one; - after a save settles, the same task saves again from a fresh read if a newer click arrived; - loads and failed-save reloads publish only when no newer click arrived meanwhile; - each click records the Gateway selection it was made on (`ConfigStore.Selection`: endpoint revision, connection mode, and config path, the same source identity #137502 binds documents to). A save writes only to a document from that same selection. Any other Gateway shows its own value and receives nothing, so a choice made on one Gateway is never written to another, however many switches happen while a save is in flight. `ConfigStore.Selection` is the selection `ConfigStore.Origin` already compared field by field; `Origin` now holds it, so `ConfigStore` stays the one owner of what "the selected Gateway" means, and `Document.isCurrent` is unchanged for its other caller (Tailscale settings). This follows the Gateway contract in `config.patch` ("only the client can replay fresh intent after a lost race"). The client replays the newest click and never retries a failed write on its own.
Root cause - `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/StatusMenuHeaderView.swift:122-124` (base): `Task { await self.saveBrowserEnabled(enabled) }` per click, with no ordering. - `:324-334` (base): independent `ConfigStore.load()` → `save()`; `catch { await self.loadBrowserEnabled() }` publishes unconditionally. `isCurrent` (#137502) fences Gateway origin, not intent order. - Introduced in #130041 (single-owner status menu). #137502 added origin checks but kept independent saves (see the ClawSweeper analysis on the issue). - Gateway side is correct: `config.set` rejects the stale `baseHash` (`src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts`).
Not changed: a save that fails with no newer click still shows the value the Gateway has, as before. The button visibly flips back. No new message or option was added. Accepted edge: the selection revision changes only on configured-client retirement (Gateway replacement, credential/TLS/route change, or endpoint loss in `GatewayEndpointStore`), never on a socket reconnect (`GatewayConnection.swift:924`, "Durable intents survive socket reconnects, but not configured-client retirement"). A click still pending across such a retirement is dropped and the button shows the Gateway's value, the same way `ConfigStore` already retires documents loaded before it. ## Evidence Main = upstream `6290fb26c9f`; candidate = the same commit plus this PR. Scenarios 1–7 ran on the first commit (`7d9066a`); scenarios 8–10 and the scenario-3 rerun ran on the final head (`c91324b`; that app was packaged from the working tree committed unchanged as `c91324b`). Each was packaged as the real macOS app (`scripts/package-mac-app.sh`, ad-hoc signed, Node 24.22.1). An isolated named profile was pointed (`configure-remote --direct-url`) at an isolated `openclaw gateway run` with private HOME/state/config and a synthetic token. The app reached the Gateway through a local WebSocket proxy that holds each `config.set` frame for 1.5 s, so two clicks deterministically overlap one save round trip. Clicks were macOS Accessibility `AXPress` on the menu's Browser button. Persisted values were read back with `openclaw gateway call config.get`. Traces show config frames only; hashes are truncated to the last 8 chars. 1. **Main, on → off → on (RED):** latest intent On; the menu shows Off and the Gateway keeps `false`. ``` button before: On $ AXPress Browser; delay 0.2; AXPress Browser button after settle (6s): Off persisted (openclaw gateway call config.get -> browser.enabled): False app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=false app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=true gw -> config.set ok=true hash=BWyfh5qE gw -> config.set ok=false error="config changed since last load; re-run config.get and retry" gw -> config.get ok=true hash=BWyfh5qE browser.enabled=false ``` 2. **Main, off → on → off (RED, inverse):** latest intent Off; the menu shows On and the Gateway keeps `true` (same stale rejection on `BWyfh5qE`). 3. **Candidate, on → off → on (GREEN):** the second save waits for the first and uses the new hash; the menu shows On and the Gateway has `true`. ``` button before: On $ AXPress Browser; delay 0.2; AXPress Browser button after settle (6s): On persisted (openclaw gateway call config.get -> browser.enabled): True app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=false gw -> config.set ok=true hash=BWyfh5qE gw -> config.get ok=true hash=BWyfh5qE browser.enabled=false app -> config.set baseHash=BWyfh5qE browser.enabled=true gw -> config.set ok=true hash=5GSf1Enc ``` 4. **Candidate, back-to-back clicks with no delay (GREEN):** serialized the same way (`set false` on `5GSf1Enc`, then `set true` on `BWyfh5qE`); the menu shows On and the Gateway has `true`. 5. **Candidate, off → on → off (GREEN):** both clicks land before the save reads, so exactly one `config.set ... browser.enabled=false` is sent, ok; the menu shows Off and the Gateway has `false`. 6. **Control, single click, main and candidate:** On → Off, one `config.set`, the Gateway has `false` in both; unchanged. 7. **Screenshots (same setup, 150 ms hold):** after on → off → on settled, the menu was reopened and captured by window ID. | Main: Browser off, latest choice lost | Candidate: Browser on | |---|---| | | | ``` main: app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=false app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=true gw -> config.set ok=true hash=BWyfh5qE gw -> config.set ok=false error="config changed since last load; re-run config.get and retry" persisted False; reopened menu Browser button: Off candidate: app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=false gw -> config.set ok=true hash=BWyfh5qE app -> config.set baseHash=BWyfh5qE browser.enabled=true gw -> config.set ok=true hash=5GSf1Enc persisted True; reopened menu Browser button: On ``` 8. **Authority-chain proof: a click queued on Gateway A is never written to Gateway B.** Two isolated Gateways (A and B, separate tokens and state), each behind its own proxy. A's proxy holds `config.set` for 15 s and B's passes through and logs every config frame. The app starts on A. Browser goes Off (save in flight to A), then On (queued), then the app is switched to B with `openclaw-mac primary set --direct-url --token-stdin` while A's save is still held. Before: A `true`, B `false`. PR head `7d9066a` (RED): the replay loop read B's document and wrote A's queued click to B. ``` Gateway A: app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=false (held) Gateway B: app -> config.get gw -> config.get ok=true hash=qLPHCpJw browser.enabled=false app -> config.set baseHash=qLPHCpJw browser.enabled=true gw -> config.set ok=true hash=GpJF-RN8 after: Gateway B browser.enabled=True (B config.set count: 1) ``` Candidate (GREEN, rerun on the final head): the queued click was made on A, so B's document is not its selection. B only receives reads, and its value is shown. ``` Gateway A: app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=false (held) Gateway B: app -> config.get / gw -> config.get ok=true hash=PPKVRTX4 browser.enabled=false (x4) after: Gateway B browser.enabled=False (B config.set count: 0) ``` Allowed principal (`838834c`): after the switch, one click made on B saves to B. Item 9 GREEN is the same allowed write to B on the final head. ``` Gateway B: app -> config.set baseHash=PPKVRTX4 browser.enabled=true gw -> config.set ok=true hash=GpJF-RN8 after: Gateway B browser.enabled=True ``` 9. **A click made on Gateway B while A's save is still settling is saved to B.** Same two Gateways; B's proxy also holds `config.get` for 1.5 s, which widens the window where the save task is still finishing after the switch. Browser goes Off (save in flight to A), the app is switched to B, and Browser is clicked On 0.5 s later. Before: A `true`, B `false`. Previous head `838834c` (RED): the click on B was dropped. B only received reads and kept `false`, while the menu had shown On. ``` Gateway A: app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=false (held) Gateway B: app -> config.get / gw -> config.get ok=true hash=PPKVRTX4 browser.enabled=false (x5) after: Gateway B browser.enabled=False (B config.set count: 0) ``` Candidate (GREEN, rerun on the final head): the click was made on B, and the save writes it to B's document. ``` Gateway A: app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=false (held) Gateway B: app -> config.get / gw -> config.get ok=true hash=PPKVRTX4 browser.enabled=false (x3) app -> config.set baseHash=PPKVRTX4 browser.enabled=true gw -> config.set ok=true hash=GpJF-RN8 after: Gateway B browser.enabled=True (B config.set count: 1) ``` 10. **A click made on Gateway B is never written to Gateway C.** Three isolated Gateways. Browser goes Off (save in flight to A, held 15 s), the app is switched to B, Browser is clicked On on B, and the app is switched to C before the save settles; nothing is clicked on C. Before: A `true`, B `false`, C `false`. Previous head `69f6fd7` (RED): B's choice was written to C. ``` Gateway A: app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=false (held) Gateway C: app -> config.get gw -> config.get ok=true hash=mZKVEYFM browser.enabled=false app -> config.set baseHash=mZKVEYFM browser.enabled=true gw -> config.set ok=true hash=7EODvSH8 after: Gateway C browser.enabled=True (C config.set count: 1) ``` Candidate (GREEN): C's selection is not the one the click was made on, so C only receives reads. ``` Gateway A: app -> config.set baseHash=5GSf1Enc browser.enabled=false (held) Gateway C: app -> config.get / gw -> config.get ok=true hash=mZKVEYFM browser.enabled=false (x4) after: Gateway C browser.enabled=False (C config.set count: 0) ``` The same-Gateway on → off → on case (scenario 3) was rerun on the final head: `set false` on `5GSf1Enc`, then `set true` on `BWyfh5qE`, both ok; the menu shows On and the Gateway has `true`. Tests (`apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/BrowserControlSettingTests.swift`), driven through `ConfigStore` with a revisioned fake that rejects stale saves like the Gateway: - `overlapping clicks persist and show the newest choice`: fails with the base logic (two writes in flight, newest choice lost, shows Off). It also fails with an intermediate candidate that claimed the save inside the task. - `a read in flight when the user clicks does not undo the click`: fails with the base logic (the reload shows the pre-click value). - `a click queued on one Gateway is never written to its replacement`: fails on PR head `7d9066a` (Gateway B receives the queued click and the menu shows it); passes with the fix (B gets no write and the menu shows B's value). A changed config path changes the `ConfigStore.Selection`, as a remote-to-remote switch changes its endpoint revision. - `a click made on the replacement Gateway while the old save settles is saved there`: fails on `838834c` (B gets no write and the click is lost); passes with the fix. - `a click made on one replacement Gateway is never written to the next one`: fails on `69f6fd7` (C receives B's click); passes with the fix. - Focused run `BrowserControlSettingTests|ConfigStoreTests|StatusMenu|Tailscale` on the candidate: 61 tests in 10 suites pass, including both Tailscale suites (the other `ConfigStore` caller). Checks on the candidate: - `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` passes, and `swiftformat --lint` on the new test passes. - `swiftlint --strict` on the three touched files: 0 violations. - `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` reports one existing `file_length` violation in `DashboardManager.swift`, which this diff does not touch and which is identical on main. - `git diff --check` is clean. Production delta +80/-28; test delta +217/-0. Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous per-click saves with no config, state or protocol change. Blast radius is the Browser button in the macOS status menu, including its writes across a Gateway switch.
