prs.title: fix(memory): PostgreSQL embedding cache eviction scans the whole cache on every write at the cap
prs.body:
Closes #182808

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on PostgreSQL, memory embedding cache eviction seq-scans and sorts the whole cache on every write batch once the cache is at its cap.

## User Impact

User impact: agents whose memory is on PostgreSQL stop paying an O(cache size) scan per memory write at the cap. At the default 50,000 rows that is about 6–8 ms down to about 0.2 ms per eviction. Eviction order, eviction count and the schema do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generated PostgreSQL index is `idx_memory_embedding_cache_updated_at (updated_at ASC NULLS FIRST)`, because the generator emits every ascending key with SQLite's null order. The PostgreSQL eviction ordered by plain `updated_at ASC`, which is `NULLS LAST` there, so the planner could not use the index and sorted every row instead. The query now orders by `updated_at ASC NULLS FIRST`, the same way `src/transcripts/store-read.ts` matches these indexes. `updated_at` is `NOT NULL`, so the order is the same. PostgreSQL then walks the index and uses an incremental sort for the remaining tie-break keys. The SQLite branch is unchanged.

No index or schema change is needed, so this is a bounded query-plan change with no write or disk trade-off.

## Evidence

All evidence is at exact head `a51492ba32f`.

New test in `manager-embedding-cache.postgres.test.ts`: `walks the generated updated_at index for oldest-first eviction`. It seeds 2,000 rows, captures the eviction statement that `pruneMemoryEmbeddingCache` actually sends, and asserts that its plan uses `idx_memory_embedding_cache_updated_at` and that the oldest rows were the ones removed. The fixture index now matches the generated DDL (`ASC NULLS FIRST`). Before this, the fixture used the PostgreSQL default order, so it could not see the mismatch.

With `manager-embedding-cache.ts` from `origin/main` (the test fails):

```
 × walks the generated updated_at index for oldest-first eviction
+                           ->  Sort  (cost=92.22..97.22 rows=2000 width=39)
+                                 Sort Key: memory_embedding_cache_1.updated_at, memory_embedding_cache_1.provider COLLATE "C", ...
+                                 ->  Seq Scan on memory_embedding_cache memory_embedding_cache_1  (cost=0.00..49.00 rows=2000 width=39)
 Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
```

This branch:

```
 ✓ walks the generated updated_at index for oldest-first eviction
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

Measured on a copy of a real 50,000-row cache (PostgreSQL 17, `BEGIN; DELETE … \bind <limit>; ROLLBACK`, 15 runs each, cold first run excluded):

| limit | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 6.0–10.2 ms | 0.13–0.26 ms |
| 100 | 7.7–12.1 ms | 0.70–1.33 ms |

Shipped CLI at the cap: `openclaw memory index --force --agent main` on a scratch state with the agent and state stores on PostgreSQL 17. The workspace has 3 small files (4 chunks, so 4 real embedding calls). Before each run the agent's `memory_embedding_cache` was reset to 50,000 rows with distinct older `updated_at` values, so every write had to evict. Table and index counters were read before and after each run:

| run | cache `seq_scan` | `seq_tup_read` | `idx_memory_embedding_cache_updated_at` scans | rows deleted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| installed 2026.10.6 (main 98f1a668) | +7 | +350,000 | +0 | +4 |
| this branch (a51492b), run 1 | +4 | +200,000 | +3 (10 tuples read) | +4 |
| this branch, run 2 | +4 | +200,000 | +3 (32 tuples read) | +4 |

Both builds printed `Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed.`, and both did the same 4 deletes, 4 inserts and 17 primary-key scans. The difference is 3 eviction statements per run. Before, each was a 50,000-row seq scan; on this branch, each is a scan of the `updated_at` index. The 4 remaining seq scans are the same in both builds and are not eviction (likely the cache size count). After each run the cache was back at 50,000 rows, and the oldest rows were the ones removed. The two builds ran on separate fresh scratch states with the same config and reset, because the newer branch build refuses agent state created by 2026.10.6 until `doctor --fix` runs.

Result equivalence:
- `updated_at` is `NOT NULL`, so `ASC NULLS FIRST` and `ASC` give the same order. To check this, I compared the first 1,000 keys from both orderings on a 50,000-row table with heavy timestamp ties (500 distinct values, 3 providers, 7 keys): there were 0 differing positions.
- In the CLI runs, both builds deleted the same number of rows and removed the oldest rows. The final cache size was the same (50,000) in every run.
- No other cache statement changes. The load path (primary-key `IN` lookup), the upsert (`ON CONFLICT` on the primary key), the identity clear and the SQLite branch all send the same SQL as before, so their plans cannot change.

Checks:
- `manager-embedding-cache.test.ts` (SQLite) passes, 19 tests.
- `oxfmt --check`, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the touched files, and `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` are clean.
- pr-simplify: no change. The diff is one production line plus one comment, the fixture index fixed to match the generated DDL, and one regression test. The test's two assertions each catch a distinct failure: the index plan, and the oldest rows being the ones removed. A smaller fix would need a schema change (a `NULLS LAST` index), which adds a concept instead of removing one.
- autoreview (shared helper, `--mode branch`, max priority P2): `scoped-clean`, "patch is correct (0.88)", no P0–P2 findings. It ran on the Claude engine because Codex CLI is not installed here.

Gaps:
- The PostgreSQL test ran through `scripts/test-projects.mts` with the conformance preload. I skipped the catalog pre-check of `test-database-conformance.mjs`, because our local role cannot set `track_functions`.
- This is not the main cost of the slow post-port memory rebuild we saw. By our counters the eviction was about 1% of wall time. The large cost is re-embedding, tracked in #182886.

prs.title: perf(agents): skip unconsumed model stream byte statistics
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model streaming still sizes request/response diagnostics without a consumer and allocates a fresh iterator callback for every chunk, even after #182672 removed unconsumed prompt statistics.

## User Impact

No model-visible prompt, stream, result, or diagnostic-consumer changes. This removes unused sizing work and modestly reduces allocation during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The request lifecycle now decides byte-stat interest once, independently of prompt-stat interest. Metrics-only completed/error listeners, trace propagation, and unsuppressed `model_call_ended` hooks retain byte statistics. The iterator reuses its bound callback while still entering transport context on **every** `next()`; entering once does not preserve identity on later resumptions.

For the 100-delta fixture, two requests require 204 `next()` entries per turn. Fresh callbacks fall from 204 to two bound callbacks. The context object was already allocated once per request; per-entry async context frames and iterator promises/results remain. Capturing every ambient context once could hide the live caller-admission check that precedes the provider iterator’s existing captured context. Delta byte counting creates no payload copy; unconsumed non-delta sizing/rest-object/JSON work is now skipped. Progress-event payloads are already throttled, and terminal content copies remain opt-in.

Usage already parses only terminal events/results. Both observations remain because result decorators can mutate or replace the message after `done`. Iterator ordering, cleanup, watchdog progress, and caller admission remain intact.

Runtime production delta: **+17 lines**; focused tests: **+152 lines**. The rerunnable measurement harness is 350 lines. This growth carries the separate byte-interest decision through both lifecycle callers and preserves the distinct consumer contracts; no cache, new option, or parallel observation path was introduced.

## Evidence

Baseline `fd0eee8790b6` includes #182672. Rebased before publication; the affected production owners were unchanged on the new base. The only conflict was adjacent README additions, both retained.

Five alternating allocation pairs, 500 turns/side, two requests/turn, 100 text deltas/request, Node 26.12.1, 4 KiB collected-object sampling:

| Consumers | Baseline bytes/turn | Candidate bytes/turn | Paired mean change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| None | 514,765 | 502,151 | −12,614 (−2.45%) |
| Metrics, no prompt stats | 534,797 | 523,498 | −11,299 (−2.11%) |

All ten allocation pairs improved. A separate count pass removes **20 → 0 terminal JSON serializations per 20 requests** without consumers; metrics/full consumers retain their original counts and exact byte/usage fields. The owner harness includes downstream observer work, but not request-payload sizing because its fixture does not call `onPayload`.

An isolated built Gateway, mock provider, 10,000 synthetic sessions, 9,000 settled runs and 40 synthetic plugins completed five rounds/ten turns per revision. Inclusive diagnostic-`next` allocation was **1.835 → 1.827 MiB/turn (−0.45%)**, neutral within sampling noise. Most of that stack is transport/context machinery, not optional diagnostic sizing. This is a small owner-level improvement, not a whole-Gateway speedup claim.

Separate untraced local timing used five alternating pairs of 10,000 turns/side. CPU signs vary on the shared host; these means are context, not a confident speedup:

- none: CPU 0.2413 → 0.2303 ms/turn (-0.0110, -4.57%); total GC 0.01854 → 0.01404 ms/turn (-0.00450, -24.29%).
- metrics: CPU 0.2728 → 0.2598 ms/turn (-0.0129, -4.73%); total GC 0.01456 → 0.01393 ms/turn (-0.00063, -4.34%).

No candidate maximum GC pause exceeds 50 ms. Major-GC counts are only 1–3 per side/window, so their tails are context. Loop samples are shown below; p99 is context when either side has fewer than 1,000 samples. No pauses were trimmed and no maintenance windows excluded. Promotion was not measured. Baseline/candidate Linux sanity runs passed all three listener modes. Both guarded quiet slots remained occupied, so the queued run was stopped before any measurement; there are no guarded Linux timing results. Local timing remains context on a shared host.

prs.title: fix(update): candidate admission falls back to installed checks when console logging is raised
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` ignores the candidate's admission verdict and falls back to installed admission (`malformed-json`), and Doctor's pre-repair recovery copy fails with `Unexpected token … "[state/sqli"`, when the console log level is raised (`logging.consoleLevel: "debug"` or `OPENCLAW_LOG_LEVEL=debug`).

## User Impact

User impact: updates with a raised console level get the candidate-owned admission checks again, including from already-published updaters (2026.10.6 verified), and Doctor's recovery capture works under debug logging. When a candidate's admission output is still not JSON, the update ledger now records what it printed. Docs also tell operators that older updaters' `updater-runtime-retention` step can take minutes on busy disks and should be allowed to finish. No config, schema, or state change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Route console logs to stderr at the protocol owners: the `update admit` fast path and the three one-shot JSON workers. Each module already loads the logging graph, so this adds no imports to CLI startup (`entry.ts`'s static graph is unchanged; the fast path imports `console.js` dynamically). Because published drivers launch the candidate's own `update admit` and state workers, this repairs published-driver × candidate updates without patching the driver.
- The installed admission parser now appends an excerpt of the first stdout line, redacted in full and then bounded to 160 UTF-16 units, to the `malformed-json` warning, since admission otherwise discards stdout and this failure was undiagnosable from the ledger.
- Docs (`docs/cli/update.md`): the `update admit` stdout contract and the new excerpt, plus operator guidance that older updaters' `updater-runtime-retention` can take several minutes on busy disks and should be allowed to finish.

No retention code change: proportional to the finding (no copy regression, candidate cannot influence the step, `main` already fixed the design for future drivers).

The installed updater still runs first and cannot be patched. Candidates with this change return a clean verdict to every published driver that supports candidate admission (protocol 1), so a raised console level no longer forces the installed-admission fallback. Future drivers additionally record what a misbehaving candidate printed.

<details>
<summary>Original report and root cause</summary>

An isolated published-driver upgrade cell on a macOS arm64 Mac Studio (npm-installed `openclaw@2026.10.6` updating to a locally packed candidate) failed two ways:

1. **Candidate admission fell back with `malformed-json`.** The installed driver (`src/infra/update-candidate-admission.ts`) parses the candidate's `update admit` stdout as one JSON verdict. A separate Doctor capture in the same run failed with `Unexpected token 's', "[state/sqli"... is not valid JSON`.
2. **`updater-runtime-retention` crawled** and was interrupted after ~770 s in that step (2407 s total).

**(1)** With a raised console level (`logging.consoleLevel: "debug"` in the cell's config, or `OPENCLAW_LOG_LEVEL=debug`), subsystem debug logs such as `[state/sqlite] SQLite read-only snapshot for …: 1.4 MiB, budget 302 seconds` are written through `console.log`, i.e. **stdout**, unless `routeLogsToStderr()` ran. Regular `--json` commands get that routing from Commander preaction, but protocol paths that own stdout never did:

- `openclaw update admit` runs through the pre-startup fast path `tryRunUpdateAdmissionBeforeStartup` (from `entry.ts`, `index.ts` and `run-main.ts`), which bypasses preaction.
- One-shot JSON child workers: `update-candidate-state.worker` (the Doctor/update state inspection that printed `[state/sqli`), `sqlite-readonly-location.worker`, and `openclaw-state-ownership.worker`.

Reproduced directly against the published 2026.10.6 package: `update admit` exits 0 with an `admit` verdict, but stdout begins with four `[state/sqlite]` lines, so `JSON.parse` fails with the exact `"[state/sqli"` prefix. At the default `info` level stdout is clean.

**(2)** Not a regression to copying. The published retention retains the *installed* (running) package before any candidate code runs; measured with the shipped retention chunk against its own 2026.10.6 install (43,184 files, 609 MB) on the same host: 40,234 files hard-linked, 1,522 byte-copied by design (every `package.json` plus plugin-safety-inspected files, via fs-safe `copyIn` + `clonefile` + `rename_no_replace` — the frames in the original sample). Throughput was 198–601 entries/s depending on host load, against a raw `fs.link` baseline of 710 entries/s on the same tree. The host was heavily contended (load 35–65, `fseventsd` ~109% CPU, dozens of Spotlight workers). The shipped step also re-walks the whole retained tree after every quiet second; the failed cell logged 19 such re-budgets. It was still progressing when interrupted. A candidate cannot change that step, and `main` already replaced it (#175626 deadline-bounded retention worker without the per-second probe; #175757/#177877 dropped per-entry pre-checks).

</details>

## Evidence

**Published-driver × candidate cells** on the same Mac Studio (macOS 27, APFS, Node 26.12.1, load 30–65 from unrelated agent builds). Each cell: `npm install -g openclaw@2026.10.6` into an isolated prefix, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/config/`TMPDIR`, unique `--profile`, config seeded by the published CLI with `logging.consoleLevel: "debug"`, then `openclaw update --tag file:<tgz> --yes --no-restart --json`. No Gateway, LaunchAgent, or `~/.openclaw` was touched (service reconciliation is skipped for non-default state).

| Cell | Candidate | Admission | Retention | Validating | Activating | Total | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | published `2026.10.7` | `owner: installed`, **`fallbackReason: malformed-json`** | — | 325 s | 411 s | 13 m 43 s | succeeded via fallback |
| fix | this branch, packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mts` (sha256 `6aabb3f0…24f6`, integrity check passed) | **`owner: candidate`**, `config`/`database-schema`/`node-runtime`/`plugin-availability` all `ok` | 158 s (40,234 linked, 1,522 copied) | 397 s | 190 s | 13 m 19 s | succeeded, `2026.10.6 → 2026.10.7 (820c30a)` |

Both drivers' `--json` stdout parsed as one document; the published driver's own debug lines went to stderr. An earlier cell whose seed never created a state DB before admission got a candidate verdict even from published 2026.10.7, which is consistent with the cause: the leaked line is the SQLite inspection budget log.

Retention measurements of the shipped step (exact published chunk, run against its own install; details in the root-cause section):

| Run | Host load | Inventory | Materialization | Entries | Linked / copied | Entries/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| published, harness | ~50 | 36.9 s | 224.3 s | 44,466 | 40,234 / 1,522 | 198 |
| published, harness | ~35 | 31.0 s | 74.0 s | 44,466 | 40,234 / 1,522 | 601 |
| published, in cell | ~35–40 | 49.7 s | 108.7 s | 44,465 | 40,234 / 1,522 | 409 |
| raw `fs.link` baseline, same tree | ~50 | 24.6 s walk | 64.9 s | 46,069 | 43,184 / 0 | 710 |

For comparison, `main`'s retention (the worker-based design future drivers ship) against the installed candidate on the same host at load ~28–40: inventory 13.8 s, materialization 23.1 s for 44,896 entries (40,517 linked / 1,592 copied), **≈1,945 entries/s, 38 s wall** — about 3× the published step at comparable load. No further retention change is warranted here.

Observed, not in scope: both baseline cells (candidate = published 2026.10.7) recorded `Automatic database restoration unavailable: databases changed after snapshot capture; the writer is unknown`; the candidate cell from this branch did not.

Regression tests, each red on the original code and green with the fix:

| Test | Contract | Red on original | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/cli/run-main-update-admission.test.ts` | the `update admit` fast path routes raised-level console logs to stderr; stdout is only the verdict | `JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "state"` | 79 ms (5.5 s file wall) |
| `src/infra/update-candidate-state.budget.test.ts` (new case) | real one-shot state worker subprocess with `OPENCLAW_LOG_LEVEL=debug` returns parseable JSON | `State schema inspection failed … during shared database snapshot … Unexpected identifier "state"` (the original Doctor signature) | ~6.4 s case (27 s under load); file 34 s |
| `src/infra/update-candidate-admission.test.ts` (new case) | `malformed-json` warning carries a bounded excerpt of the first stdout line, redacted before bounding (a synthetic JWT straddling the 160-char cut stays masked), alongside the stderr diagnostic | excerpt missing; the earlier slice-then-redact revision leaked the JWT header (review fix 9e857e7cbdb7) | 12 ms |

Local checks: oxlint (core config) and oxfmt on all changed files, `tsgo` for `tsconfig.core.json`, `tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json`, `tsconfig.core.test.infra.json`, `tsconfig.core.test.services.json`; `src/index.entrypoint.test.ts` (admission fast-path entry cases) passes.

Release-note context: `openclaw update` now gets a valid candidate admission verdict when `logging.consoleLevel` (or `OPENCLAW_LOG_LEVEL`) is raised; previously candidates printed debug logs ahead of the verdict and the updater fell back to installed admission (`malformed-json`). Doctor's pre-repair recovery copy no longer fails with `Unexpected token … "[state/sqli"` under debug logging.

auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix(update): keep JSON protocol stdout clean under raised log levels

With logging.consoleLevel or OPENCLAW_LOG_LEVEL raised to debug, subsystem
logs went to stdout in paths whose stdout is one JSON document: the
`update admit` pre-startup fast path (which bypasses preaction routing) and
the one-shot state, SQLite read-only, and state-ownership workers. Published
drivers then fell back with malformed-json and Doctor's recovery capture failed
on a "[state/sqli" prefix.

Route console logs to stderr at those owners, and record a bounded, redacted
stdout excerpt in the installed driver's malformed-json admission warning.

* fix(update): redact the admission stdout excerpt before bounding it

A credential straddling the 160-character cut no longer matched its redaction pattern. The shared diagnostic redactor now sees the whole first stdout line before truncating, and the excerpt stays outside the stderr diagnostic's own bound.

* test(update): keep admission regression tests CI- and scanner-clean

Place the mock-isolation note directly above vi.mock for the mock-exports ratchet, strip ANSI before asserting colorized CI stderr, and assemble the artifact URL fixture's credentials at runtime so the PR input-safety scanner no longer rejects the touched file.

prs.title: perf: avoid extra transactions for pending input lookups
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`chat.message.get` opens an explicit read transaction when retrieving one retained pending input. The lookup is already one SELECT, including the current-session scalar and a byte-bounded payload, so BEGIN and COMMIT add two unnecessary SQL statements.

## User Impact

Retrieve retained pending inputs with the same content, payload limits, current-session checks, missing-ID behavior and authorization, using one SQL statement instead of three. Count-and-page listings retain their snapshot. There is no schema, cache, write-transaction or worker-routing change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route ID lookups through the existing count-free page path and remove the now-redundant conditional around the listing count. Production diff: +5/−7 lines, net −2; the existing test is +60/−53 (net +7), and the reusable workload/protocol add 126/29 lines. The existing owner regression now covers both count-free context and ID lookup, including visibility of an input committed after an empty read; its SQL counter also captures native `exec` transaction envelopes. A committed synthetic WebSocket workload reproduces the public flow.

## Evidence

Acceptance registered in this PR before the first run:

- Flow: synthetic retained pending input retrieved over a real isolated Gateway WebSocket using `chat.message.get`; also check a missing ID.

- Latency/CPU comparisons require five interleaved samples per arm under the timing lock. Counts-only evidence makes no latency or CPU claim. All user-facing metrics must hold or improve; a 20% regression in any measured cell stops the change.

One committed baseline/candidate pair passed all 12 lookups per arm with zero SQL errors: baseline `8704e103e12`, candidate `df661e7d663`. Counts use frozen observer v3.1.4; its 36 frozen files were verified. The observer's causal hook misses the current AsyncContext, so these are phase-file execution windows, not causal-turn attribution. Host 1-minute load was 75.09/86.43; 41/40 per-thread CPU profiles were captured for attribution only. No latency, CPU-speedup or memory claim.

| Target SQL per cold / warm / missing lookup | 3 / 3 / 3 | 1 / 1 / 1 |
| Target worker requests per lookup | 1 | 1 |

prs.body:
Closes #181686

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes offline `models status --probe` reporting `unknown` for account-owned SecretRefs even when the referenced credential is available.

## User Impact

Operators can check environment- and protected-store-backed account credentials offline, while unresolved references remain unsent and resolved credentials stay out of persisted profiles.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing local account-secret preparation owner before inference, inside the probe's exclusive offline state ownership. Gateway RPC probes continue using their existing runtime snapshots. The production change adds five lines; the regression adds 137 lines to exercise the real credential and HTTP paths.

## Evidence

**Shipped CLI proof (requested in review):** [successful run](https://github.com/Maximora-byte/openclaw/actions/runs/39983882929/job/120517911766) builds exact PR head `9dfef9601418cf0d93d4eab28d4ffd2db0a2f830` with `pnpm build:runtime` on Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0, then launches the shipped `node openclaw.mjs models status --probe` entry point in four isolated temporary state roots.

The [fixture](https://github.com/Maximora-byte/openclaw/blob/95627366be0fc7801dda8e94c1d4ef0b47fdaef5/.proof/offline-probe-cli.py) seeds synthetic profiles through the built public SDK and writes the protected-store value through `openclaw secrets store set` on stdin. It counts real HTTP requests and verifies their authorization at an isolated local endpoint. After each subprocess exits, it reads the canonical shared SQLite profile store read-only to compare the saved credentials before and after probing. Environment/store/missing cases retain their exact `keyRef` with no persisted `key`; inline is the control case. The [proof workflow](https://github.com/Maximora-byte/openclaw/blob/95627366be0fc7801dda8e94c1d4ef0b47fdaef5/.github/workflows/offline-probe-proof.yml) pins a separate candidate checkout; only the workflow and fixture exist on the fork's proof branch.

Sanitized terminal output from that run (no endpoint addresses or credential values are printed):

```text
CLI: openclaw models status --agent main --probe --probe-provider cli-proof-fixture --probe-profile cli-proof-fixture:default --probe-max-tokens 8 --probe-timeout 15000 --json
{"case": "inline", "cliExit": 0, "status": "ok", "reasonCode": null, "httpRequests": 1, "authorizedRequests": 1, "savedProfileUnchanged": true, "referenceRetained": true}
{"case": "env", "cliExit": 0, "status": "ok", "reasonCode": null, "httpRequests": 1, "authorizedRequests": 1, "savedProfileUnchanged": true, "referenceRetained": true}
{"case": "store", "cliExit": 0, "status": "ok", "reasonCode": null, "httpRequests": 1, "authorizedRequests": 1, "savedProfileUnchanged": true, "referenceRetained": true}
{"case": "missing", "cliExit": 0, "status": "unknown", "reasonCode": "unresolved_ref", "httpRequests": 0, "authorizedRequests": 0, "savedProfileUnchanged": true, "referenceRetained": true}
PASS: shipped CLI, four isolated credential cases, three authorized requests, references preserved
```

[Linux regression proof run](https://github.com/Maximora-byte/openclaw/actions/runs/39974645415) validates candidate `9dfef960` on Node 24.22.1 with the frozen workspace install:

- **Red on base:** the same regression fails against unchanged production source `4a0ce4e8`: inline credentials report `ok`, while environment and protected-store refs report `unknown`.
- **Green with fix:** the regression passes through real auth resolution and loopback HTTP: three authorized completion requests, an unresolved-ref result without an extra request, and unchanged persisted profiles.
- **Related tests:** all 80 tests across probe targets, resources, cleanup, status, local account-secret preparation, and Gateway model probing pass.
- Changed-file oxlint/oxfmt, the commands test typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent P0–P2 review of the changed code and regression found no actionable findings.
- New regression: **3.844 s test time**, **61.61 s command wall time** including cold runtime compilation/loading.

[Upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39975690502) has now completed successfully for head `9dfef960`, including the broader tests, production/test types, lint, boundaries, ratchets, and UI regression lanes.

prs.title: perf(agents): share remote catalog revisions across worker contexts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The model-catalog worker retains a separate structured clone of the same remote catalog for every prepared workspace. Multi-workspace catalogs therefore keep model rows and strings repeatedly even when all workspaces use the same publisher revision.

## User Impact

Reduces retained catalog-worker memory without changing catalog rows, source selection, credentials, or workspace plugin registrations. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before establishing a request's remote-catalog scope, reuse the same `(sourceUrl, revision)` already owned by the worker's startup snapshot or an existing workspace generation. The publisher hashes the catalog content into the revision, and this is already the prepared-context fingerprint's remote identity. Distinct sources and revisions remain distinct. Existing context replacement releases superseded ownership; there is no new cache or eviction policy.

Workspace registrations must remain separate: evicting them can recapture native ESM graphs that Node cannot unload. The production change adds 23 lines to share the immutable data while preserving that lifecycle contract. The script and test are separate proof scaffolding. Simplification pass: no additional cache, state owner, compatibility branch, or public export.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before baseline: local macOS, Node 26.12.1, real worker pool, 20 synthetic workspace contexts, 5,000 remote model rows, two successive revisions, 40 successful catalog requests per run; five alternating fresh-worker baseline/candidate runs with forced worker GC. Accept a consistent retained-heap reduction of at least approximately 5% with correctness preserved.

| Post-GC worker heap | Baseline mean (MiB) | Candidate mean (MiB) | Paired mean delta | Samples per side |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| One workspace | 130.140 | 130.147 | +0.007 MiB (+0.01%) | 5 |
| 20 workspaces, first revision | 163.254 | 133.763 | -29.491 MiB (-18.06%) | 5 |
| 20 workspaces, replacement revision | 165.039 | 135.081 | -29.958 MiB (-18.15%) | 5 |

All 200 catalog requests per side succeeded. Final baseline range: 164.884–165.090 MiB; candidate range: 135.078–135.089 MiB. External memory stayed at 6,249,553 bytes on both sides; ArrayBuffers differed by at most 16 bytes in the final samples.

Measurements used base `803ad1fdc36e3473b4a9c538fd3dfb4a15f4431a`; the candidate worker bytes are unchanged after rebasing onto current main for this PR.

Separate synthetic snapshot attribution: the largest catalog-context Map falls from 32,060,088 to 1,648,704 modeled retained bytes. Estimated excess duplicate-string bytes fall from 11,082,200 to 1,198,040. The baseline contains 4,591 unique script identities and no duplicate scripts; code-associated retained subtrees account for 56,946,456 bytes (overlapping categories, not additive). These source-runtime snapshots include tooling and do not predict an absolute production worker heap.

Reproduction (use fresh output paths; both owner directories mirror the same relative worker file):

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/catalog-worker-retention-measure.ts \
  --output /path/to/new-fixture --owner-dir /path/to/baseline-or-candidate
```

The regression fails on the original worker with two retained remote generations instead of one and passes on the candidate. It also exercises catalog output, source/revision separation, replacement, and null restoration. Snapshot proof covers actual collected heap beyond the diagnostic root counts.

Focused checks passed (32 tests across five files):

- `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.heap.integration.test.ts` (7 tests; approximately 29.1 seconds test time).
- `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.workspace-heap.integration.test.ts` (1 test).
- `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-retained-data.test.ts` (2 tests).
- `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts` (22 tests).
- Export-name collision guard, changed-file type-aware lint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`.

The focused invocation used the repository's pinned test runtime. Retention measurements used Node 26.12.1. Test worker preparation took 58.1 seconds; grouped test wall times were 14.29 / 82.98 / 67.07 seconds. An initial focused attempt was invalidated by formatting during artifact compilation and was rerun with fixed source; it is excluded from product results.

PR CI on `cf359de2a8b5282b37a415f152f2255a712589be` completed with three red checks (one substantive test shard and two aggregate gates); all other required checks passed or were skipped. The sole substantive failure is inherited: `models-dispatch.catalog.integration.test.ts` → “dispatches a discovered model outside the agent workspace and preserves it after withdrawal” → `Unknown model: opencode/live-only-model`, with the same `requireImageCapableModel` / `resolveImageRuntime` stack in both [this PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133639969/job/120990769479) and the [newest scheduled main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40130094950/job/120979998439), main SHA `a67706486489054461cf4ee9f8cca32cd5587517`. No CI reruns were requested. The aggregate CI gate reports the failed selected Node test shard; Security Review itself completed successfully. GitHub's Codex review also completed without findings.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The helper refused the requested route because it did not match the operator configuration; configuration was not changed. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated; broad validation belongs to PR CI.

Limits: synthetic owner-level retention, not full-Gateway throughput, allocation, promotion, GC-pause, or latency evidence. The fixture disables plugin execution/network discovery; the integration tests cover normal catalog and workspace lifetime behavior. The inherited startup snapshot still follows the existing worker lifetime; this change removes per-workspace copies, not that startup root. Production benefit depends on catalog size and the number of workspaces sharing a revision. After deployment, look for a lower catalog-worker heap plateau as workspaces warm, while catalog contents and refresh behavior remain unchanged. Leave this PR open for lead verification and merge.

prs.title: fix(googlechat): deliver remote attachments as links
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Google Chat rejects or silently drops remote media when an agent sends an attachment through a monitor reply, a direct message action, or outbound delivery.

## User Impact

Remote HTTP(S) media sent to Google Chat now shows up as a visible link alongside any caption, instead of being rejected or reduced to the caption alone.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Chat advertised media support, but each of its three media entry points handled attachments on its own and none turned them into visible content, while native upload needs user authentication the plugin's app credentials cannot provide. The channel now has one validator and formatter for remote HTTP(S) media, shared by monitor replies, direct actions, and outbound normalization, which reuses the SDK attachment-link formatter, preserves authored Markdown indentation, and rejects local files, non-web URLs, and URLs with control characters. The old attachment-presence detector and the unsupported-media warning and drop paths are removed, while typing-placeholder recovery, thread placement, and delivery receipts keep their current owners. This continues closed PR #119718.

Production LOC +71/-34 (net +37); tests +133/-7; docs +1/-1. No API, schema, config, auth scope, dependency, or upload capability is added.

## Evidence

- Red on main: media-only and caption-plus-remote-URL direct actions in `extensions/googlechat/src/actions.test.ts` failed with the old user-OAuth rejection.
- Green: 91 cases across seven Google Chat suites (actions, channel, format, monitor, typing cleanup, reply delivery, and delivery failure) passed; the reply-delivery suite reached 14 of 14 after one new fixture's expected blank line after a code fence was corrected to match the existing renderer. The HTTP fixtures cover partial sends, typing updates, missing-placeholder recovery, and no duplicate resend after a status-report failure.
- Targeted typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed; the one lint finding was the intentional control-character regex, now carrying an explained suppression. `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen` left all six fixtures unchanged (snapshot token delta 0).
- Independent review: clean, no actionable findings.
- Gap: no authenticated send to a live Google Chat space was run, so local evidence stops at the monitor harness and HTTP fixtures. Native uploads of local files remain unsupported because Google's media upload API requires user authentication.

Fixes #89430

## What Problem This Solves

prs.title: fix: allow fetched plugins and Code Mode in AOT builds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

AOT standalone hosts reject fetched plugins, Node Code Mode, and QA expressions even though these features can run in the interpreter.

## User Impact

Fetched CJS and TypeScript plugins can load through the existing loader and share the compiled host SDK. Code Mode cells, retained continuations, and QA expressions/lambdas execute normally. Each interpreted feature emits one performance notice per process, with the same execution facts visible in Doctor diagnostics.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous runtime profile conflated AOT compilation with a ban on runtime code. This removes its rejection branches and keeps the profile as the owner of execution diagnostics. Plugin trust, source capture, cache generations, and tool authority stay with their existing owners.

Actual failures retain actionable guidance: missing runtime modules identify the disk-loader/rebuild options, while a code-generation restriction names the disabling flag. No strict flag, new configuration, or automatic executor switch is introduced.

## Evidence

The execution regressions fail on the original profile guards and pass after the cutover. All 107 focused assertions pass with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| Test file | Passed | Wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/infra/runtime-profile.test.ts` | 8 | 10.52s |
| `src/infra/runtime-capabilities.test.ts` | 3 | 17.61s |
| `src/plugins/plugin-module-loader-cache.runtime-profile.test.ts` | 2 | 3.82s |
| `src/agents/code-mode-executor.runtime-profile.test.ts` | 3 | 200.08s |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-flow-runner.runtime-profile.test.ts` | 5 | 15.83s |
| `src/plugins/plugin-module-loader-cache.test.ts` | 12 | 231.77s |
| `src/agents/code-mode-executor.test.ts` | 4 | 6.75s |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-flow-runner.test.ts` | 19 | 310.79s |
| `test/scripts/bun-standalone-metadata.test.ts` | 51 | 27.96s |

The longer runs include cold compiled-worker preparation; the new Code Mode test body takes 2.06s. Its collection preload keeps that fixture work outside the unchanged cell execution budget. Targeted core/QA lint, source/test types, formatting, and documentation link/glossary checks pass.

Small probes use the experimental Bun AOT toolchain (`5d8fe974f`); no whole-application AOT build was run. The final six-module probe uses the production loader's bounded static closure and the standalone native/import/require adapters in the real two-stage order. With **no supplied factory**, fetched CJS and TypeScript/Jiti each return 42 and preserve compiled SDK object/class identity while the SDK source, staged Jiti CJS sources, and entire emitted module directory are hidden. Compilation took 4.592s. A separate repeated-load probe returns 42 then 44 from the same SDK object and emits one notice. Earlier raw-source fixture attempts lacked the builder's transformation order and CJS classification; those failures are not claimed as product defects.

The actual profile-owner probe returns 42 from VM and Function code, preserves actionable missing-import guidance, and emits exactly one notice per feature across the parent and a compiled worker. Its nine-module compile took 2.510s. Strict VM/Function/Jiti controls fail with code-generation guidance. The interpreter tripwire was not used as proof. These are execution/SDK boundary probes, not qualification of arbitrary native ESM, workers, child programs, or plugin dependencies.

CI initially found that the warning identifier used the environment-variable namespace. The diagnostic is now `AOT_INTERPRETED`; the unchanged environment-variable budget passes at 457/457. The eight runtime-profile tests, focused lint, and formatting pass after this correction. The initial CI run also hit a Telegram polling timing failure in unchanged code; the exact case passes locally without a source or timeout change (175.65s including cold worker preparation). The identical assertion reproduces on current main `e1e498602cec224ef4adb16f13512ca6aea26d98` with the same missing `status`/`stop` events (118.55s Vitest duration including cold worker preparation). The polling test and implementation are unchanged by this PR. These observations establish an inherited timing failure; the passing PR replay is not claimed as a fix.

The final independent Codex review through P2 is scoped-clean, including source-integrity verification. The owner retains diagnostics and removes the obsolete admission policy; no second SDK, loader, or authority owner is introduced.

Follow-up to #182346. Full artifact qualification remains with the standalone build lane.

Current-head [CI run 40126830978](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40126830978) completed all 86 jobs. The only failed test job is the identical Telegram polling assertion reproduced on main; its aggregate CI gate is red. The ratchet, security check, and all other jobs passed or were skipped. This PR uses the native pre-existing-failure landing route and does not claim green CI.

prs.title: feat(perf): attribute retained compiled code to scripts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Heap retention summaries cannot attribute compiled-code footprint to scripts or distinguish repeated Script objects from one large loaded codebase.

## User Impact

Operators can use `--code-by-script` to rank script-associated code bytes and list every repeated complete script identity, while keeping snapshot contents on the analysis host. There is no Gateway or plugin-loader behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new aggregate-only mode reuses the streaming parser and dominators. It identifies V8 Script/SharedFunctionInfo links, closure code/feedback links, and strong internal/hidden code edges. Shared associations and runtime builtins stay in a separate bucket. A separate reviewed build-file allowlist permits only exact script names after query/hash removal; other names are redacted and compared by SHA-256 identity. Anonymous/truncated identities remain separate.

Instance count means distinct compiled Script objects, not repeated module evaluation or reclaimable waste. Shallow code bytes partition nodes once. Retained bytes union same-group dominated subtrees, including non-code data; retained totals across groups can overlap. The runbook documents these limits and the deployed-file allowlist workflow.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/heap-snapshot-diff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **8 passed**, 271 ms test time / 1.73 s wrapper time. Covers existing modes plus exact-name redaction, query/hash duplicates, shared code, weak-edge exclusion, retained unions, anonymous names and truncated identities.
- Changed-file oxfmt, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json scripts/heap-snapshot-diff.mjs test/scripts/heap-snapshot-diff.test.ts`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Real synthetic Node **26.12.1** ESM snapshots, one fresh process per case, 10,000 warm calls per function and explicit GC before capture. Only the fixture filename was allowlisted. The analyzer correctly detected the added query-busted import:

| Fixture measurement | One import (n=1 snapshot) | Two query-busted imports (n=1 snapshot) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Script instances | 1 | 2 |
| Attributed code objects | 34 | 68 |
| Shallow code bytes | 2,296 | 4,592 |
| Retained bytes | 2,528 | 5,056 |
| Duplicate identities | 0 | 1 |

These are correctness controls, not a performance benchmark or evidence of production savings. Production attribution is pending coordinated profiling-window availability; no production snapshot has been analyzed by this lane yet. No Testbox/Crabbox allocation or broad local suite/build was run; broad proof belongs to PR CI.

Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**, fresh diff/context review through P2, no actionable findings. The autoreview helper refused the requested provider route because it did not match operator configuration; configuration was not changed.

Simplification pass: reuse the existing parser and retained-size owner; no second snapshot parser, runtime cache, compatibility path, or loader change. Runtime production LOC delta: **0**. Executable analyzer tooling: **+254 net lines**; tests: **+212**; runbook: **+42**. The requested new attribution/privacy contract requires that tooling growth; this is not a speculative runtime optimization. Exact-head [CI run 40124447127](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40124447127) passed, including changed tests, type/lint lanes, docs, guards and `openclaw/ci-gate`; the GitHub Codex review also completed with no findings. This PR is for lead review and must remain unmerged by this lane.

prs.title: perf(pairing): avoid re-inspecting decoded node snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing the device-pairing node publication re-inspects every property of records that its database worker already owns and decodes as plain data. This repeats the rejected experiment in #181723 with current source, identical-source controls, untraced timing, and the updated absolute-delta acceptance rules.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The shared node snapshot remains deeply frozen; public get/list callers retain independent mutable records. Revision reuse, mutation admission, revocation, database replacement, and close invalidation are unchanged. No configuration, schema, permission, or API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `freezeTrustedJsonSnapshot` at the publication owner. Its sole production caller supplies worker records constructed from scalar database columns and JSON-decoded fields, transferred through structured clone. The worker cache is filled by that same decoder. Removing generic property-descriptor/prototype inspection therefore preserves the existing ownership contract.

Runtime production LOC delta: **0 net** (two substitutions). No new cache or parallel path. The checked freezer remains for other callers whose contracts admit opaque values. The added benchmark exercises the real reader/SQLite worker/publication with exact contents, nested freezing, and shared-snapshot assertions.

## Evidence

**Decision: accept.** The two paired comparisons reduce sampled allocation **48.96%**, main-thread CPU **5.64%**, total GC/work **8.95%**, and promotion **2.36%**. Loop p99 rises **0.7465 ms** (+17.99%): this is context under the specified sub-1-ms rule because allocation improves more than 10%. Both maximum pauses remain below 13 ms, well below `max(50 ms, 2 × baseline max)`. Minor collections fall 45.5% and total GC falls, so longer individual scavenges do not reject the change.

### Protocol and limits

The workload and thresholds were recorded before paired results: 64 synthetic nodes, 4,000 forced publication misses per process, 100 warmup operations, concurrent sides, synchronized warmup/measurement barriers, and counterbalanced launch order. Four identical-source A/A pairs ran in **each** of timing, allocation, and promotion modes before two A/B pairs per mode. Timing is untraced; collected-object sampling and traced promotion use separate processes. No pauses or maintenance intervals were trimmed. The predeclared 20,000-operation fallback was not needed because no applicable calibrated rejection gate tripped.

Shared benchmark-host slots remained occupied, so the measurements used the authorized local-testing fallback: Apple M3 Ultra, 32 cores, Node 26.12.1. **macOS CPU affinity was unavailable; these are not Linux interleaved-core/quiet-slot results.** Simultaneous A/A controls quantify the shared-host variation. The queued remote campaign produced no paired results. This benchmark measures publication misses, not whole-Gateway latency or an observed production publication rate.

Local sources: base `83c4da899710`, candidate `42b1da31c94c`. Owner SHA-256 baseline `6fdeba25f4b1653b759f71f7cce5d4f097ffddbe1af1c042c2d4df22fc342d95`; candidate `9d9df95fb0a162de59329610866482f28c4a7cdb41b15f31632e0ecf8b452e2f`. Both sides share the same source/dependencies except the selected publication owner. Fixture SHA-256 `96927cb665b7f37036e696094cb03392e2d2a3a1bdb5231ce2a396ffc632ba48` matches every side.

### Candidate results

KB uses decimal bytes. Every row reports baseline → candidate and the mean of the paired differences.

| Metric | Pair 1 | Pair 2 | Mean absolute delta | Mean paired relative delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Allocation KB/publication | 971.4013 → 489.5212 | 964.4617 → 498.5405 | -473.9006 | -48.96% |
| Inspection KB/publication | 517.6432 → 0.0000 | 512.1489 → 0.0000 | -514.8961 | -100.00% |
| Main CPU ms/publication | 1.8593 → 1.7414 | 2.1421 → 2.0364 | -0.1118 | -5.64% |
| Process CPU ms/publication | 2.6893 → 2.5437 | 3.0366 → 2.9295 | -0.1263 | -4.47% |
| Total GC ms/publication | 0.1104 → 0.1002 | 0.1206 → 0.1102 | -0.0103 | -8.95% |
| Promotion KB/publication | 132.7193 → 131.2583 | 139.8401 → 134.7686 | -3.2663 | -2.36% |
| Publication latency p95 ms (n=4,000/side) | 3.4085 → 3.1547 | 4.8806 → 4.8870 | -0.1237 | -3.66% |
| Publication latency p99 ms (n=4,000/side) | 6.3311 → 6.2820 | 9.0976 → 8.8010 | -0.1728 | -2.02% |
| Loop p95 ms | 2.4760 → 2.3368 | 3.0454 → 2.9020 | -0.1413 | -5.17% |
| Loop p99 ms | 3.8236 → 4.7063 | 4.7309 → 5.3412 | +0.7465 | +17.99% |
| All-GC maximum ms | 9.3153 → 8.5667 | 10.0710 → 12.9150 | +1.0477 | +10.10% |

Loop samples: pair 1 **11,286 → 11,234**; pair 2 **11,796 → 11,828**. All latency/loop p95 and p99 sample thresholds are met. The sub-millisecond loop delta is disclosed, not reclassified as an improvement.

<details>
<summary>Per-kind GC and pause context</summary>

|---|---:|---:|

Minor counts are below 200 per side and major counts below 50; pause percentiles are context. Minor counts also fall by over 20% while total GC/work falls, satisfying the fewer/full-scavenge rule. No maximum exceeds its safeguard.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Four A/A controls per instrumentation mode</summary>

| Pair | CPU ms/op | GC ms/op | Loop p99 ms (samples) | All-GC max ms | Allocation KB/op | Promotion KB/op |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.5494 → 1.5365 | 0.1072 → 0.1061 | 5.0340 (n=10477) → 4.8333 (n=10531) | 10.4409 → 9.0706 | 974.7674 → 965.2942 | 137.3486 → 139.6251 |
| 2 | 1.4430 → 1.4611 | 0.0963 → 0.1016 | 4.9889 (n=10041) → 4.7882 (n=10132) | 11.1292 → 26.9225 | 983.5570 → 971.4596 | 134.5281 → 137.7684 |
| 3 | 1.8626 → 1.8712 | 0.0958 → 0.0986 | 3.8482 (n=11520) → 3.8646 (n=11486) | 4.9138 → 9.6561 | 983.7261 → 969.9124 | 137.8846 → 147.7355 |
| 4 | 1.9840 → 1.9874 | 0.1047 → 0.1024 | 6.9673 (n=11498) → 7.0902 (n=11541) | 16.3160 → 8.9542 | 966.2593 → 976.3588 | 141.0591 → 135.4160 |

Mean A/A main CPU delta: **+0.0043 ms/op (+0.27%)**; GC **+0.0012 ms/op (+1.31%)**; loop p99 **−0.0655 ms (−1.46%)**; promotion **+2.4312 KB/op (+1.80%)**. A/A maximum-pause percentages vary strongly on small baselines, but all maxima stay below 27 ms and none crosses the safeguard. Outside load was recorded per pair; it was not used to exclude windows.

</details>

### Built-Gateway proof and validation

Both isolated built-dist Gateway captures completed 128 committed `node.rename` → `node.list` revisions and eight mock-provider turns, with all 64 node contents checked. Synthetic state contained 10,000 sessions, 6,000 terminal runs, 2,000 archived sessions including 200 dashboards, and 40 fixture plugins plus two required plugins. In each 120-second collected-object profile, the inspection stack beneath `prepareNodes` fell from **66.733 MB to 0 sampled bytes**; all `prepareNodes` stacks fell **69.529 MB → 6.144 MB**. These sequential profiled captures prove reachability, correctness, and stack removal, not paired timing/GC acceptance. Owned Gateways/ports were cleaned up.

Local proof passed: publication integration **25 tests** (17.64 s file wall), immutable-data contracts **9 tests** (3.29 s), targeted lint/format, export-name guard, and both import-closure files **22 tests** (144.62 s). No new test-only seam or implementation-spy assertion. Existing behavior contracts stay green on both implementations; allocation attribution is the performance regression proof.

Full baseline build and candidate runtime build passed. Baseline CSS-size output was advisory. An initial proof driver connected during startup sidecars and received a retryable response; waiting for Gateway-ready fixed the setup before any mutation.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): **clean through P2**, including the later CI repair. The helper refused before reviewer launch because the selected provider did not match operator configuration; configuration was unchanged, and each fallback reviewer received only the diff and relevant source/docs/briefs.

The initial CI run `40134770120` caught a missing required `"both"` target in benchmark fixture seeding. It was repaired without changing runtime fixture behavior; targeted `pnpm tsgo:scripts` and lint/format passed. **Current-head CI run [40136081384](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136081384) passed**, including `check-test-types` and `openclaw/ci-gate`, on `42b1da31c94c2879fb21b990366da09910ef6484`. No CI rerun was used to chase green. The current-head GitHub Codex review also completed with no findings; ClawSweeper found no code findings on the earlier head and its then-missing performance evidence is now recorded above. No manual Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated.

Reproduce with `scripts/perf/device-pairing-publication-measure.ts` as documented in `scripts/perf/README.md`; use separate state, ready/start files, and process per instrumentation mode.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve discovered models for isolated completions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Image utilities reject an already-discovered provider model with `Unknown model: opencode/live-only-model`, even though chat can use it. This also breaks the catalog-dispatch integration test on main CI.

## User Impact

Restores plugin-discovered models for isolated image/completion runtimes while preserving separate plugin execution generations. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Commit 9b2de5727ed470a4d2074ad90fee36ef804e8957 (#171822) correctly introduced the `isolated-completion` execution purpose to avoid plugin reload freezes. The catalog-owner comparison also included that purpose, however, so image preparation lost the configured agent's published discovery results and saw only its static inventory.

Ignore execution purpose only when comparing the catalog source, alongside the already-excluded plugin loading and selection fields. Keep purpose in execution owner identity and keep isolated plugin loading intact. The configured agent remains the catalog owner; no discovery, cache, or fallback is added.

Simplification: +3 production lines (two identity-field exclusions and one ownership comment), no new machinery. The existing integration test already protects the regression, so its assertions remain unchanged instead of adding duplicate coverage. This restores the documented shared-catalog contract; no public contract changes.

## Evidence

- [Scheduled main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40130094950/job/120979998439), head a67706486489054461cf4ee9f8cca32cd5587517: `requireImageCapableModel` / `resolveImageRuntime` reports the unknown discovered model. The offending commit is an ancestor of this evidence head.
- Local unchanged-main reproduction: the exact integration test fails with the same error (90.56 seconds test time; 334.36 seconds wrapper wall time, including cold worker preparation).
- With the fix, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/models-dispatch.catalog.integration.test.ts src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.owner-selection.test.ts src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.catalog-owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes all 57 tests. The Gateway regression takes 20.38 seconds; the complete focused command takes 95.61 seconds including worker preparation. This proves chat and image dispatch, profile/transport selection, in-flight completion after withdrawal, later rejection, and separate execution generations.
- Changed-file oxfmt, repository lint, and `git diff --check` pass. No Testbox/Crabbox lease was allocated; broad validation belongs to PR CI. Timing differences are test-run context, not a performance claim.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. The helper refused the configured provider route; operator configuration was not changed. Review confirmed that execution generations stay separate and agent/auth/environment/workspace identity checks remain intact.

PR CI passed on exact head `19b719491f9d524eb2ae8854c62954c0cb86ef4a`: all 62 non-skipped checks green, including the required gate; no reruns. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40136465322).

prs.title: fix(matrix): stop treating unnamed two-member rooms as DMs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Before the Matrix `m.direct` cache has loaded, an unnamed room with exactly two members is classified as a direct message. Ingress no longer does that. A room is still a direct message when `is_direct` or `m.direct` says so, when a recent invite is promoted, or when per-room recovery is opted in. A remote invite is not closed by this change.

## Evidence

The production room-message handler, using the production direct-room tracker, with pairing policy and an empty group allowlist. Cache refresh fails. Two joined members.

```console
$ node --version
v26.12.1

unnamed_two_member pairing_writes=0 dispatch=0 log=drop room message
stored_m_direct pairing_writes=1 dispatch=0
is_direct_true pairing_writes=1
```

The unnamed room is dropped before any pairing write or agent dispatch. A room already stored in `m.direct` still creates a pairing request. A room whose member event has `is_direct: true` does too. No account-data shape changed.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Matrix ingress no longer treats a two-member room as a DM only because the direct-room cache has not seeded.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Node v26.12.1, worktree `/tmp/oc-f063` at `afa854dbf5fc`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Drive the production room-message handler with the production direct-room tracker. Send one text message in an unnamed two-member room, one in a room already listed in `m.direct`, and one whose member event has `is_direct: true`. Cache refresh fails. DM policy is pairing. Group policy is allowlist with no rooms configured.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```console
unnamed_two_member pairing_writes=0 dispatch=0 log=drop room message
stored_m_direct pairing_writes=1 dispatch=0
is_direct_true pairing_writes=1
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The unnamed room is dropped before pairing and before agent dispatch. Stored `m.direct` and `is_direct: true` still create one pairing request each and do not dispatch an agent turn. Existing `m.direct` records keep the same shape.
- **What was not tested:** A live federated homeserver. Recent-invite promotion and opted-in per-room recovery are unchanged and can still classify a room as direct.

## Summary

Remove the pre-seed two-member fallback in `createDirectRoomTracker`. Recent-invite promotion, opted-in per-room recovery, and an explicit `is_direct` or `m.direct` signal are unchanged.

Crabline smoke rooms are ad-hoc. They only received replies because two members counted as a direct message. The harness names the bot in the text and does not send a Matrix mention pill, so the Crabline wildcard group no longer requires one. Product group rooms are unchanged.

prs.title: perf(status): avoid resummarizing unchanged session stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated status requests reselected, sorted, and grouped unchanged session rows, allocating about 5 MB per read on a 10,000-session Gateway.

## User Impact

Status reads reuse unchanged session summaries. Counts, recent-session ordering, deletion/admission filtering, heartbeat settings, and displayed ages retain their existing behavior. No configuration or storage migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Status prepared a summary once per physical store on every RPC. Health already cached its prepared result; its scheduled refresh runs once per minute while clients are connected, with additional explicit/stale probes. The sampled allocation stack cannot establish the production call rate.

Keep raw summaries in the shared session-store owner, keyed by projection identity, its current selection revision, physical store, and requested window. Status and health consume that recorded result; the health-only prepared-result cache is deleted. Request-specific admission, store discovery, roster selection, and publication remain fresh. Failed reads are not retained, and a selection that changes its own revision is not cached.

The first read following a row revision still rebuilds the summary; this is reuse between writes, not incremental maintenance of every row. Only the latest revision is retained. Runtime code shrinks by **14 lines** (33 added, 47 deleted). The requested non-test diff is **+6 lines**: the existing measurement driver gains 18 net lines and its README gains two lines, making the real status/health workload rerunnable. All growth is proof tooling/documentation; there is no second runtime path. No projection-owner files change.

## Evidence

Acceptance was recorded before the baseline run: unchanged reads must stop repeating selection/sort work; writes and request-specific filtering must remain correct; measure warm status CPU/allocation and the health sibling. Baseline is `803ad1fdc36e3473b4a9c538fd3dfb4a15f4431a`; candidate measurements use that source plus this patch. Before publication, the branch was rebased onto `e111107c214e6588c10d12cb34a5dffc29474f6b`; runtime sources remain byte-for-byte identical to the measured/reviewed candidate. The benchmark-only conflict preserved the incoming `chat.startup` scenario alongside status/health and received a clean independent review.

An isolated built Gateway, loopback transport, synthetic 10,000 sessions (2,000 archived), 6,000 settled runs, 40 synthetic plugins, and a local mock provider were used. Five allocation rounds of 100 RPCs and a separate **untraced** five rounds of 200 RPCs followed 20 warmups, on Node 26.12.1.

| Warm status metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Allocated bytes/read (500 per side) | 4,977,057 | 954,581 | −80.8% |
| Main-thread CPU/read, untraced | 15.804 ms | 2.864 ms | −81.9% |
| Process CPU/read, untraced | 19.964 ms | 5.471 ms | −72.6% |
| RPC median (1,000 samples/side) | 19.224 ms | 4.604 ms | −76.1% |
| RPC p95 (1,000 samples/side) | 55.028 ms | 11.294 ms | −79.5% |
| RPC p99 (1,000 samples/side) | 127.703 ms | 19.851 ms | −84.5% |
| Total GC/read, untraced | 0.330 ms | 0.050 ms | −84.9% |
| GC collections, untraced | 177 | 35 | −80.2% |

Allocation-stack attribution confirms the targeted work disappeared: `summarizeProjectionRows` and descendants fell from about **4.01 MB/read to below 0.1 KB/read** across the five sampled rounds.

These are sequential local measurements on a busy shared Mac, **not controlled paired production-host results**. Early baseline timing rounds overlapped focused test execution. Both remote quiet slots were occupied and dirty pages exceeded the shared guard; no remote workload was started. Allocation/work and eliminated work are the strongest evidence. Timing differences are directional, and no production-wide savings are inferred from the original sampled stack. Traced allocation-run latency worsened under varying host load; it is not substituted for untraced timing. Promotion was not independently measured.

<details>
<summary>Untraced GC and event-loop observations, all rounds retained</summary>

Round order 1–5. GC total milliseconds: baseline `[129.794,98.772,44.274,27.623,29.336]`; candidate `[11.302,9.485,11.251,7.041,10.632]`. Maximum single pause: baseline `[64.616,40.980,11.312,1.765,1.599]` ms; candidate `[2.732,2.853,4.941,1.371,4.880]` ms. Baseline minor GC: 175 collections, 263.835 ms; incremental: one, 1.348 ms; major: one, 64.616 ms. Candidate: 35 minor collections, 49.710 ms, no major or incremental collections. GC pause percentiles have insufficient samples for gates; major GC is context only.

Event-loop p99: baseline `[107.807,161.350,110.494,48.857,42.729]` ms with counts `[213,241,207,132,132]`; candidate `[22.987,22.905,23.396,49.316,23.020]` ms with counts `[61,51,51,56,46]`. These are under-sampled context, not p99 gates. Maximum loop delay: baseline `[225.444,245.236,155.976,95.945,47.317]` ms; candidate `[26.001,29.409,26.690,55.771,23.020]` ms. No observations were trimmed.

</details>

Reproduce with the existing `scripts/perf/team-shape-fixture.ts` fixture generator and `scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts`:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts \
  --state-dir "$STATE" --entry dist/entry.js --scenario status \

```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the SQLite read-only copy regression fixture stops before exercising inactive-WAL activation when the asynchronous private-copy path does not call the process-global `fsyncSync` spy.

The two affected cases consequently observe the original version-7 database instead of reaching the existing retry and cleanup-aggregation behavior they are meant to protect.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible or production behavior change. This restores deterministic CI coverage for the existing SQLite snapshot retry and cleanup contracts while leaving copy semantics, database bytes, schemas, durability, assertions, timeouts, configuration, and dependencies unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture already creates a closed, inactive WAL database: direct observations on the failing base confirmed that neither `-wal` nor `-shm` exists before preparation. The missing transition came from its injection mechanism. The asynchronous fs-safe copy path does not cross the synchronous fsync spy, so the synthetic active WAL family was never installed.

The fixture now wraps the existing `sqliteCopy.copySqliteFile` test seam. After the first source-main copy completes—when the private destination exists but before the production generator rechecks source sidecars—it installs the same version-8 main/WAL/SHM family. This binds the race to the copied-destination boundary without changing production code or the tests' expected outcomes.

## Evidence

On the base, the two exact cases both failed: schema inspection returned version 7, and the raw-copy cleanup case returned version 7 instead of an `AggregateError`. The same focused selection passed after the fixture correction, demonstrating that both cases reach their original production assertions.

The final candidate also passed:

- changed-file formatting and lint, with zero warnings or errors;
- the affected core test type graph; and
- the complete `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.copy.test.ts` owner file, 24/24 tests.

Exact-head CI is green, including the selected changed-node, type, lint, boundary, guard, security, CodeQL, and final gate jobs. Independent calibrated review and canonical AutoReview are clean. Fixes: `plugins.reloadAndResume` can hand off a Gateway-owned conversation, then reject its authorized reload with `MISSING_SCOPE operator.admin` after the turn has already yielded.

prs.title: fix: keep local worker overload out of provider fallback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: local worker-capacity refusals are mistaken for model-provider overload, triggering unrelated model fallback and misleading provider-error advice.

## User Impact

OpenClaw stops provider fallback for a typed local worker-capacity refusal and explains that its local workers are at capacity. Genuine provider failures retain configured fallback. The guidance asks users to check for completed work before trying again; it does not claim that no work happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing typed local-worker deadline classifier already preserves original HTTP facts through nested errors. Extend that owner to capacity refusals and use the existing failure-reply path for curated local guidance, including provider-looking wrappers. No capacity, scheduling, retry, configuration or dependency changes.

Related: #162624 handles SQLite-worker capacity errors; #156650 handles generic-worker deadlines. Neither covers a generic `WorkerTaskError` with `code="overloaded"`. #180042 covers transcript admission and MCP cleanup faults, not this producer.

## Evidence

**Inspectable execution captures:** [before/after Gateway events, real HTTP503 controls, verification predicates, and captured curated auto-reply payload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182867#issuecomment-6390018083). The Gateway traces are retained exact-candidate captures; the additional auto-reply capture uses temporary logging-only instrumentation in the real-pool test, restored byte-for-byte afterward. It is a production-caller test capture, not live Discord delivery.

- Base: `c6facd08e4b5aa14c4424a716f097388537f52ae`.
- Real `WorkerTaskPool`, one held input, pending-task limit of one: an extra input emits the production admission error. On base, the configured next model runs; candidate preserves the original local error and does not advance fallback.
- Candidate: `6e19fbaecf01a68db6eedf27768f4410ff74df30`. Exact-commit focused run: **117/117 tests across five files**, covering classifier, real worker deadline/overload boundary, normal failure-reply and downstream provider/terminal execution consumers. HTTP 408/503 controls still advance fallback; typed worker timeout remains local. Three registered shards completed in 77.11s wall; hosted CI timings unavailable.
- Curated copy tested through the normal known-failure caller, including provider-looking wrappers and group context with verbose diagnostics off.
- Built isolated Gateway, same fixture before/after: a synthetic registered harness calls the real public `WorkerTaskPool`; byte admission rejects the input. Baseline attempts primary and fallback and persists “The AI service is temporarily overloaded.” Candidate attempts primary only, emits no fallback steps, and exposes “worker task capacity reached” in the actual terminal WebSocket event and persisted failure summary. This is shipped Gateway/protocol proof, not Discord transport or an external-model run.
- The Gateway route displays the raw truthful local diagnostic; the curated retry/check-completed-work guidance is proved through the normal auto-reply failure caller in tests. Do not conflate those outputs.
- Genuine provider control uses actual loopback HTTP 503 responses with `Retry-After: 120`, exceeding the existing 90-second transient-retry budget without production changes. Both revisions make exactly two requests (primary then fallback), with identical fallback events and provider-facing persisted copy. All nine before/after evidence assertions pass.
- Format, targeted lint, production core types and targeted test types passed. Full base build passed (4m19s); exact-commit candidate build passed (3m6s), including 157 public SDK subpaths. Independent canonical autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings. A subsequent braces-only test formatting fix was non-semantic.
- Hosted CI: exact-head `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses are successful (verified 2026-10-24).

Limits: this corrects attribution and fallback, not saturation. The original incident does not identify the rejecting pool. Persisted assistant output is not proof of channel delivery. No live Gateway was modified or restarted.

Simplification: reused the existing typed worker classifier and migrated its callers; no parallel name matcher. Production delta +26/-21 (net+5); tests +104/-19. New test cases extend existing registered suites.

prs.title: perf(process): scope Linux PTY cleanup scans to their session
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closing Linux PTY terminals synchronously transfers and parses the entire host process table twice, even though cleanup owns one session.

## User Impact

Less main-thread work during terminal cleanup on busy Linux hosts. Job-control groups and the second scan for newly created groups remain covered. The exec memory watchdog, including its five-second quiet-tree sampling interval, is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the PTY's session in Linux `ps` before transferring rows. Keep SID filtering and existing signal ordering. Darwin still selects by controlling tty; other Unix systems retain their existing query. This replaces the Linux whole-host query without a cache, timer, or new state. Runtime production LOC: +4, solely for selecting the Linux command while preserving other platforms' contracts. Measurement tooling adds 166 lines, measurement instructions add 19, and tests add 13 net lines.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before comparison: prepared synthetic live/exited sessions; 100 cleanup operations per side; concurrent, synchronized pairs on interleaved CPU sets, swapped in pair two. Accept materially less table-transfer/parse work with unchanged descendant cleanup and no material CPU/latency regression. Apply absolute-delta/sample-count rules to GC and tails; adverse GC signals require matched A/A controls.

Linux owner measurements completed with procps-ng 4.0.4 under the shared quiet-B lock and production guard: two concurrent pairs per workload, synchronized after warmup, 100 operations per side, CPUs 64,66,…,94 versus 65,67,…,95, swapped in pair two. No guard interruptions. Both sources used the same committed driver, and source/driver hashes were verified after transfer. No forced GC or GC tracing. Command: `node scripts/perf/pty-session-scan-measure.mjs <owner.ts> live|exited 100 <shared-start-epoch-ms>`.

| Workload | Main-thread CPU ms/op (base → head) | Absolute delta | Mean paired change | Median latency ms (base → head) | GC ms/op (base → head) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Live session | 3.0278 → 2.0410 | −0.9868 | −32.6% | 56.494 → 55.675 (−1.45%) | 0.15439 → 0.00574 (−96.3%) |
| Already exited | 2.9872 → 0.8164 | −2.1708 | −72.7% | 55.190 → 25.861 (−53.2%) | 0.15157 → 0 (−100%) |

Live-session output fell from about 10.16 MB to 9.6 KB per 100 cleanups; the two required session scans remain. Already-exited sessions return no rows and need one `ps` call instead of two. All sides completed the real descendant teardown check. These repeatable CPU/work reductions justify the four-line runtime increase needed to preserve platform contracts.

<details>
<summary>Per-pair work, GC, and tail evidence</summary>

All arrows are base → candidate. Latency p95 has 100 samples per side; event-loop p95/p99 have 99 per side. These tails are context, below the declared sample thresholds. Live event-loop p99 has mixed signs (−0.524 ms, +3.277 ms; absolute mean +1.376 ms), so it does not establish a tail regression. No matched A/A rejection protocol was invoked because no qualifying adverse GC gate occurred. Per-core outside-load sampling was not captured; the shared guard ran throughout.

- Regression is red on the current-main query (`-axo` instead of session selection), green with the change. The existing rescan regression now covers Linux and Darwin.
- Focused process tests: 51 passed, 5 Windows-only skips (5.60 seconds wall time). Includes real macOS PTY job-control teardown and the unchanged five-second memory watchdog tests.
- Focused type-aware lint and oxfmt checks passed on the changed files. Initial CI caught an unbound `process.kill` reference in the measurement driver; it is now bound to `process`, with focused lint and independent review passing. The runtime change is unchanged.
- Linux candidate functional probe passed with a real synthetic session and separate job-control group: two operations, four session scans, 192 returned bytes, expected signal targets, and successful real teardown. This smoke run is not a paired timing claim.

- Built baseline Gateway proof passed on macOS: 10,000 synthetic sessions (2,000 archived), 6,000 settled runs, 40 fixture plugins, ten terminal open/input/close cycles with ten exit events, and a successful loopback mock-provider turn. Gateway shut down cleanly. `pnpm build` passed; it emitted an unrelated CSS-size advisory (296.4 KiB versus 296.3 KiB). This is macOS flow proof; Linux behavior is exercised by the owner probe.

The owner probe checks every target while suppressing signals during repeated scans, then restores real signals and verifies teardown of its synthetic session and separate job-control group. Main-thread CPU excludes the `ps` subprocess; these are owner-boundary numbers, not whole-Gateway throughput or allocation-rate claims. README formatting and diff checks passed.
