prs.title: fix(cron): record designed heartbeat skips as successful no-ops
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent whose heartbeat file is intentionally empty (or comments-only) skips every interval by design, but each skip was recorded as a `skipped` cron run, which `resolveCronCompletionStatus` maps to `failed`. `openclaw tasks list --status failed` accrued one row per interval (~48/day) for the heartbeat cron and failure alerts fired, even though `consecutiveErrors` stayed 0 (#144959).

Designed no-op skips now settle as `ok` runs whose summary carries the skip reason (`heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file`), matching the busy-deferral handoff path that already returned `ok`. The heartbeat runner's own state (`system heartbeat last`, `consecutiveSkipped`) keeps reporting the precise skipped status, so no signal is lost.

## Evidence

- **Real-behavior proof (updated in f8c3fa97 and 6fb6ec66 per review):** `src/cron/service.heartbeat-real-preflight.test.ts` wires the **real heartbeat runner** (real preflight, no injected heartbeat results), a **real comments-only scratch row** in the sqlite state store (stock "keep this file empty" content), and the **real cron service**. The two review findings are addressed:
  - **Same-partition fixture:** the sandbox is now selected as the cron partition the preflight actually reads — `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` points the default partition (`<state>/cron/jobs.json`) at the seeded `cronStorePath`, so `resolveHeartbeatPreflight` genuinely consumes the seeded comments-only scratch instead of a different store.
  - **Required dependency supplied:** the `CronServiceDeps.requestHeartbeat` member is provided (non-waiting) alongside `requestHeartbeatAndWait`, matching the production contract.
  - **Safeguard restoration:** commit ffb0026a accidentally dropped the fixture safeguards; 6fb6ec66 restores them (partition stub, `requestHeartbeat` dependency, skip-summary + spy assertions), so the test again cannot pass through ordinary heartbeat execution.
  - **Skip assertions, not just success:** the finished event must carry `summary: "heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file"`, and the reply/telegram spies must stay unused — so an ordinary successful agent turn can no longer satisfy the test. Paused-reminder recovery stays covered: the operator `disabled` skip keeps its `skipped`/`failed` outcome in the unit matrix.

Runtime output (local vitest run at 6fb6ec66, cron config, redacted):

```
✓ src/cron/service.heartbeat-real-preflight.test.ts > real heartbeat preflight task accounting > settles a real empty-scratch preflight as a successful no-op task 1155ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Full local cron-suite run at 6fb6ec66 (`service.heartbeat-payload.test.ts` + `service.heartbeat-real-preflight.test.ts` + `service.test.ts`):

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

- The test also asserts the ledger that feeds `tasks list --status failed` contains zero failed cron rows after the designed skip.
- Unit-level matrix in `service.heartbeat-payload.test.ts` (10/10): designed skips settle `ok`/`succeeded` with `consecutiveErrors: 0`; the operator `disabled` skip keeps its `skipped` outcome for visibility.
- Matches the existing intentional-silence precedent in `resolveCronCompletionStatus`, and the busy-deferral handoff path in `timer-execution.ts` that already returned `ok`. The runner's own state (`system heartbeat last`, `consecutiveSkipped`) continues to report the precise skipped status.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep unfinished progress visible after delegation
prs.body:
Closes #137188.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unfinished progress steps receiving a completion check when the parent turn ends, even while delegated work is still running or has failed.

## User Impact

Control UI progress cards keep the saved checklist accurate and show current work separately: running, queued, waiting, failed or stopped. A disconnected or unavailable status read is visible instead of leaving an apparently live card. This applies to web chat, desktop/mobile Details, hovercards, dashboard widgets and session summaries. Telegram conversations viewed in the Control UI use these surfaces; messages inside Telegram are outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier fixes #137323 and #137255 cover stale later-run activity and dashboard target ownership. This deliberately changes the remaining terminal presentation discussed in #137188: completing a conversation turn does not complete an authored plan step. Saved counts, icons and accessibility labels now agree. Current matching failures remain visible without rewriting the plan or attributing an unrelated later run's outcome to it.

Area-owner approval of this change to terminal presentation remains outstanding.

A shared renderer derives activity from existing session facts and the already-loaded child roster. The dashboard observes its exact target instead of relying on membership in a bounded session list; a failed read offers Retry. Retired session observations rebind to their successor, and child failures/stops reuse the existing outcome classifier. No new model calls, polling, persisted state or Gateway protocol changes.

The author simplification pass removed the obsolete bounded-list helper and kept one runtime renderer/projection. Necessary growth is shared status rendering and wiring existing UI consumers: production +499/-122 lines, tests +593/-71, docs/config +2/-1 against the base. Obsolete composer styles already overridden by the current layout were removed to keep the CSS budget from growing.

## Evidence

Tested against main base `42f68fade98da4f30f56a182a3392700f62ef2d5`:

- The mounted card and dashboard regressions fail on the base for false completion and missing delegated activity; both pass with the fix. The full Control UI browser scenario also reproduces the false check on that exact base. With the fix it shows 2 running / 3 queued, updates to 1 running / 3 queued / 1 failed on a child event, retains the saved plan through reload, and displays the result in mobile Details. It asserts that no message or status-refresh model request was sent.
- 189 focused consumer tests passed for the original change. After review, 94 affected lifecycle/widget tests pass. The two new regressions both fail on the previously published production source and pass after repair: same-key session replacement continues receiving native events without leaking subscriptions, and an interrupted child counts as stopped only for the matching saved progress snapshot.
- UI and browser-fixture typechecks, targeted lint, CSS lint, controller guards, test-registration guard, i18n baseline, formatting and diff checks passed. Existing composer geometry/scroll proof also passed. The UI-only performance comparison against CI base `34e79bcbe9a07e3e0d0f7664f5121d2954facc8f` passed with CSS down 920 bytes raw / 132 bytes gzip; no limits or baselines changed. The latest lifecycle repair changes no CSS.
- [CI run 40128136541](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40128136541) passed fully on `1cfa8b9fce2877536ac54d8de509afa9338c439b`; the latest review repairs have the focused proof above and will receive new PR CI.
- Fresh Auto Review found no accepted findings at its default P0 threshold for the original change and the latest lifecycle repair. This does not claim a broader-priority review. The two concrete ClawSweeper findings are addressed; area-owner approval of the presentation direction remains outstanding.

The browser proof uses the actual Control UI with a synthetic Gateway boundary and installed Chromium 1243 through the supported executable override; pinned 1248 was unavailable. No live provider run, core build, full local suite or bundled-main dashboard browser run was performed. The main UI-only build was exercised by the performance comparison. The approved synthetic screenshots remain applicable: the review repair changes lifecycle ownership and stopped-outcome classification, with no layout changes.

The attached captures show the exact-base unfinished step incorrectly checked, then the corrected delegated-work and child-failure states. All content is synthetic.

## What Problem This Solves

Native macOS and iOS/iPadOS clients do not provide a direct navigation path to the Dashboard Systems page, making machine and worker status harder to reach from those apps.

## User Impact

Mac users can open Systems from **Navigate → Systems**, and iPhone/iPad users receive a pinned **Systems** sidebar destination that opens the same Gateway-backed machine inventory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native clients now reuse the shared `/systems` Dashboard route instead of implementing another machine inventory. The macOS menu and iOS/iPadOS sidebar both navigate to that route. A small closure rewrite also avoids a Swift 6.3.3 actor-thunk compiler crash encountered while building the verified macOS app.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix: stabilize cold session mutation reconciliation test
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The session mutation selection fixture could advance its only reconciliation window before the first rename or delete request crossed an intentionally lazy-loaded dispatch boundary. Under a cold module cache, those two cases then observed the original managed-list snapshot (`ts: 1`) even though production reconciliation was still correctly scheduled after dispatch.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible or production behavior change. The existing test now deterministically proves that rename and delete reconcile the authoritative managed list while preserving a newer foreground selection, without depending on module-loader speed or cache warmth.

All existing cases, assertions, operation order, the 5,000 ms fake-clock window, and the `ts: 2` managed-list oracle remain unchanged. Production lazy-loading and session mutation lifecycle code are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture now records when its existing patch/delete RPC handler is actually invoked and waits for that dispatch receipt before publishing the simulated committed state, resolving the deferred RPC response, and advancing fake time. This is the owner boundary that separates cold module loading from the paced reconciliation timer.

The change stays within the existing table instead of adding retries, wall-clock delay, polling, new helpers, or production instrumentation. It adds no second behavior contract: the same owner-level integration test continues to cover all mutation and foreground-selection variants.

## Evidence

The retained scheduled-main [UI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40098379185/job/120885426754) reports exactly the two cold first-use failures at the unchanged oracle. On current base `ff2c84117f607770fdc5671b37e899e824647333`, a remote run restricted to those same two cases reproduced both exactly:

- `rename preserves loaded selection and reconciles managed lists`: failed with actual `ts: 1`, expected `2`.
- `delete preserves loaded selection and reconciles managed lists`: failed with actual `ts: 1`, expected `2`.

On candidate tree `c4115e5b1eb1c8866ca33ff4c793d530caf430ef`, the same two-row selection passed. The complete owner file then passed all 20 cases. The personal OpenClaw remote recipe also passed changed-file formatting, oxlint, Control UI i18n verification, and the selected `core-test-ui-other` type graph on retained Testbox [run 40132923715](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40132923715).

Exact-head [CI run 40133667978](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133667978) passed every selected row, including all three UI shards, lint, test types, changed-node, boundaries, guards, security-fast, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. Fresh calibrated engineering review and canonical P0-P2 autoreview both concluded clean with no findings.

prs.title: fix: duplicate replies after agent runs that send files via the message tool
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI shows an agent's reply (and its attached file) twice when a Gateway agent run, such as a subagent-completion wake, ends with the agent sending its answer through the `message` tool with an attachment.

## User Impact

User impact: those replies now appear once, with one file card and one stored artifact. Turns started from the chat composer were already correct and are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the `message` tool replies to the active WebChat source, it commits its own transcript row and marks the reply payload as transcript-owned. The `chat.send` finalizer already skips payloads whose owned row is committed on the active branch. The agent-run finalizer (`finalizeAgentRunMedia`) did not. It prepared the same media a second time, minting a second managed artifact, and wrote the text and attachment into the run's otherwise empty final assistant message, so the reply rendered twice.

The committed-owner lookup now lives in one place (`chat-transcript-source-reply-owner.ts`) and both finalizers use it. The agent-run finalizer drops committed entries before preparing media and returns early when nothing uncommitted carries media. A payload flagged as owned whose row is missing or off-branch is still enriched, matching `chat.send`.

## Evidence

- Root cause came from stored transcript rows of an affected production session: a `delivery-mirror` row owned the reply, followed by the empty final answer carrying the same text plus a second managed attachment.
- New regression test in `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-media.test.ts` drives real dispatch, transcript, and managed-media stores, with the payload built by the real `buildSourceReplyPayloadState` producer.
  - Committed owner row: no display content on the final message and no managed media record. This case fails on `main` (`expected [text, image] to be undefined`).
  - Owner flag without a committed row: enrichment is unchanged.
- Focused tests: `pnpm test src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-media.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat.directive-tags.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-transcript-persistence.mirrors.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The `chat.send` source-media suite passes unchanged.
- `tsgo:core`, oxlint, and format checks on the touched files pass. Autoreview is clean.
- Gap: no live model-driven subagent wake was replayed end to end. The test covers the production dispatch path below the model. No UI code changed, so there are no before/after screenshots.

Release note context: fixes duplicated assistant replies and file cards in WebChat/Control UI after subagent-completion turns that answer through the message tool with an attachment.

prs.title: perf(gateway): avoid duplicate publication environment snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

GitHub publication commands repeatedly snapshot the entire process environment before the command runner performs its own canonical environment merge, adding avoidable Gateway main-thread work to every Git spawn.

## User Impact

Publication uses less CPU and allocates less memory per command. In the focused synthetic workload, main-thread CPU fell 7.1% and sampled allocation fell 22.8%. Inheritance, explicit overrides/deletions, admission, retries, deadlines, cleanup, and output memory bounds are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport now supplies only its overrides when no explicit environment was provided. The existing command runner remains the owner of live environment inheritance. Read-only Git flags and hook suppression still apply. Production LOC delta is zero: two defaults change, with no cache, new worker protocol, or new production machinery.

A separate 4,000-operation baseline CPU profile attributes approximately 0.34 ms/op to `gitReadOnlyEnvironment`, 0.20 ms/op to `mergeProcessEnv`, and 0.073 ms/op inclusive to execa option normalization. Spawn diagnostics' own sampled work is about 0.005 ms/op: its large inclusive frame contains the spawn itself. These are profile-attributed spans, not untraced CPU measurements. Diagnostics and stdout/stderr handling remain intact.

## Evidence

Node 26.12.1 on Linux; 209 synthetic environment keys; four verified local Git read commands; fresh fixtures; 100 warmup operations; 4,000 measured operations per side. Two concurrent pairs use synchronized starts and interleaved CPU placements, swapped for pair two. Both sides use the same sibling-module substitution hook. No forced GC or pause trimming. The shared host guard paused between passes for dirty-page pressure; no measured pair was interrupted.

The measured owner was main `721cdadccb93`; it is unchanged through the rebase to `1394145a435a`. This measures the native publication transport path, not whole-Gateway throughput or the brokered path.

| Untraced metric | Pair 1 base → candidate | Pair 2 base → candidate | Mean paired delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Main-thread CPU (ms/op) | 2.3648 → 2.1752 | 2.8883 → 2.7098 | -0.1840 (-7.10%) |
| Process CPU (ms/op) | 2.5579 → 2.3363 | 3.0993 → 2.9288 | -0.1961 (-7.08%) |
| Operation mean (ms) | 4.0939 → 3.9664 | 4.9702 → 4.8301 | -0.1338 (-2.97%) |
| Operation p95 (ms; n=4,000/side) | 5.0542 → 4.9242 | 7.0592 → 6.7899 | -0.1996 (-3.19%) |
| Operation p99 (ms; n=4,000/side) | 5.6669 → 5.4933 | 8.2741 → 8.1969 | -0.1254 (-2.00%) |
| Total GC (ms/op) | 0.0332 → 0.0296 | 0.0387 → 0.0358 | -0.0033 (-9.17%) |
| Loop p95 (ms) | 4.6080 → 4.4892 | 6.3406 → 6.2218 | -0.1188 (-2.23%) |
| Loop p99 (ms) | 5.0749 → 5.0217 | 7.3974 → 7.0984 | -0.1761 (-2.55%) |
| Native synchronous spawn span (ms/op) | 2.5954 → 2.7630 | 3.2459 → 3.4057 | +0.1637 (+5.69%) |

The native spawn sub-span increased about 0.164 ms/op (+5.69%) while total CPU and end-to-end latency improved in both pairs. Loop sample counts are 5,652/5,808 and 6,005/5,888 (base/candidate); loop maxima are 6.009/6.975 ms and 26.722/24.084 ms.

Separate allocation sampling (32 KiB interval, including collected objects) measured 552,108 → 426,520 bytes/op and 552,343 → 425,748 bytes/op: mean −126,091 bytes/op (−22.83%). Separate GC-traced runs measured promotion at 50,519.5 → 49,644.6 bytes/op and 51,222.8 → 49,741.1 bytes/op: mean −1,178.3 bytes/op (−2.31%). Traced timing is not used as a gate.

<details>
<summary>Untraced GC counts, per-kind cost, and pause tails</summary>

Each cell is `count / total ms / p95 ms / p99 ms / maximum ms`. Per-collection percentiles are context only: every kind has fewer than 200 samples, and major collections are below 50. Total GC/op carries the comparison. Both pairs improve total GC; no maximum approaches the 50 ms safeguard.

| Pair / side | Minor | Major | Incremental |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 / base | 89 / 119.989 / 1.695 / 2.069 / 2.069 | 3 / 11.048 / 3.974 / 3.974 / 3.974 | 3 / 1.896 / 0.762 / 0.762 / 0.762 |
| 1 / candidate | 77 / 110.408 / 1.834 / 2.629 / 2.629 | 2 / 6.966 / 4.253 / 4.253 / 4.253 | 2 / 1.208 / 0.617 / 0.617 / 0.617 |
| 2 / base | 88 / 141.197 / 2.146 / 7.766 / 7.766 | 3 / 11.576 / 4.840 / 4.840 / 4.840 | 3 / 1.947 / 0.852 / 0.852 / 0.852 |
| 2 / candidate | 77 / 126.809 / 2.291 / 2.731 / 2.731 | 4 / 13.987 / 4.941 / 4.941 / 4.941 | 4 / 2.264 / 0.731 / 0.731 / 0.731 |

</details>

Correctness proof passed on baseline and candidate through built, isolated Gateways: a 10,000-session mixed mock-model/dashboard flow with 41 loaded plugins completed four turns, and a separate 5,000-session, 44-plugin publication recovery fixture reached the actual Git transport and shut down cleanly. Recovery exercised local workspace inspection and stopped before credentialed publication; no live GitHub push was attempted. Local Gateway timings are not comparative performance claims. One candidate setup attempt encountered another lane's occupied port and was replaced on free ports.

Focused validation: 34 tests across `github-publication-git-index.test.ts`, `git-network-retry.test.ts`, and `exec-buffer-output.test.ts`; 22 import/wrapper closure tests; export-name collision guard; changed-file formatting and lint. Full baseline build and candidate `sourcePerformance` build passed. The new real-child test protects admission-time inheritance, explicit overrides, undefined deletion, and command markers. This behavior-preserving optimization uses the paired harness for performance proof rather than a timing assertion in a unit test.

Review: independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), clean P0–P2 verdict. No Testbox lease was allocated. The [first exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40134629234) passed on `90b58fb163cf`, and GitHub Codex review found no issues. Main then introduced a README append conflict; the rebase preserved both sections and moved this section beside existing Git command documentation. Production, test, and harness contents are byte-identical. The [rebased exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40135835761) also passed: 37 successful jobs, no failures. All required CI, dependency, and security gates were successful at merge.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Consolidates repeated test construction across CLI/commands, TUI, transport and Control UI fixtures. Matching builders reuse one existing or narrow sibling support owner; independent scenarios and expected values stay in their current tests.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. This is test/test-support-only cleanup: **68 paths, 409 additions, 596 deletions, 187 net lines removed; production LOC 0**. It is a residue batch under the approved **100+ net-line floor waiver**, not a LARGE-PR claim. No assertion, test case, registration, timeout, retry or skip is removed or relaxed.

The branch starts from fresh main `4d49d348a5c21381bdca622d053faa3b4f98e3b4`. Preceding PR #182766 is merged as `0b71e1b2eb07c3342ff522630603a554e1c8da14`, with ancestry verified in that base. Current main already contains 56 net placement lines from #182803; those are **not counted** here. There is **no hook-relocation exception**: raw hook and registration sites are preserved directly.

There are **18 cuts** below. The modal migration depends on the new frame-clock owner and is included with it as one 31-net clock family. Other cuts have no cross-cut behavior dependency; disjoint additions sharing an existing support file do not call one another.

Per-cut counts below are source syntax sites before→after, not expanded runtime cases. Registrations mean test+suite+hook+module-mock+onTestFinished sites; table factories and custom register-prefixed call sites are reported separately.

## Withdrawn Overlaps and Complete Family Cutover

The playback 36-net slice is excluded whole because active test-LOC PR #182852 owns it. A later exact-head collision with active test-LOC PR #182872 at `10c56d844896297de0e964d3a52386b7c55118c8` also required restoring `image-generate-tool.test.ts` and `dispatch-from-config.abort-and-dedupe.test-utils.ts` whole to this branch's base. No collision waiver is assumed.

Removing only the dedupe copy would leave an unnecessary singleton extraction: one remaining constructor moved into a 22-line export for 5 lines of growth. The **entire 12-net ACP-entry family** was therefore withdrawn, including the ACP-abort caller and shared entry-constructor export, along with the **3-net image deferred cut**. All four files now equal the exact base bytes, with no surviving new ACP entry export/import. A fifth whole-file withdrawal restores `get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`: narrow typecheck exposed TS2322 because the generic deferred resolver does not satisfy the backend cancellation callback's reason parameter. The complete 2-net extraction is removed; no callback adapter, cast or widened type is added. The same formerly failing messaging graph passes after restoring the original constructor. This was an attributable candidate defect, not an inherited failure. The final 68 retained changed files remain byte-identical to the reviewed candidate.

The retained arrival descriptor cleanup overlaps PR #182849 only at `05880451b14ebd2f57b11be02094108d8503e6ff`. Its current body records whole UI withdrawal/restoration after its CI failure, not active fixture consolidation on that path. The existing #167027 classification remains tied to `6bec1a32d7c1cddb2f008d82822a0fc15b05a9e7` and the same arrival path. These classifications are bound to these exact heads; changed heads require fresh classification.

## 1. Captured config-reader mocks — 18 net removed

Fifteen forwarding families use `createTestConfigReadMocks` in the existing commands runtime-config support owner. Synchronous aliases stay pinned to the captured function; each fresh async reader looks up the current owner member, retaining receiver, arguments, identities, throws and promise adoption. Dynamic imports remain inside Vitest mock factories; partial/closed exports remain local.

Source preservation: **assertions 794→794; registrations 394→394** (tests231, suites17, hooks23, mocks120, cleanup3, each unchanged). Tables80→80; custom registration sites11→11.

Provenance: Async-owner migration #169714 (`7e48efba1047`); existing support owner maintained in #182679 (`6b6b307ffe97`).

**Best-effort tradeoffs accepted:** none; no production config reader or authority check changes.

## 2. Backup captured config readers — 2 net removed

Git and SQLite backup fixtures reuse only the captured-reader member. Their synchronous aliases, real-module spreads, snapshot wrapper and export order remain explicit rather than being overwritten by a broad fixture spread.

Source preservation: **assertions 50→50; registrations 27→27** (tests16, suites2, hooks4, mocks5, cleanup0, each unchanged). Tables8→8; custom registration sites0→0.

Provenance: The backup form of #169714, using the same existing commands runtime-config owner.

**Best-effort tradeoffs accepted:** none; the distinct backup snapshot contract is retained.

## 3. macOS install-owner marker strings — 17 net removed

Five serialized marker literals become one immutable string constant in the existing commands support owner. Original temporary roots, write helpers, encodings and lifetimes remain; all127 serialized bytes are preserved. The fixture is independent expected input, not production-generated expected output.

Source preservation: **assertions 58→58; registrations 51→51** (tests21, suites3, hooks7, mocks20, cleanup0, each unchanged). Tables13→13; custom registration sites0→0.

Provenance: #161583 (`d7f8b2c3fddd`) introduced these install-owner marker literals.

**Best-effort tradeoffs accepted:** none; primitive-string sharing introduces no mutable state, marker/schema or permission change.

## 4. Response-hook collectors and held promise — 13 net removed

Replace three stream-drain IIFEs with the existing event collector and one held-promise constructor with the existing deferred owner. Consumption starts at the same points, appends to the same arrays and retains waits, settlement, hook/cancellation assertions and per-call promise freshness.

prs.title: refactor(channels): normalize bundled channel inputs once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu, Slack, and Nextcloud Talk repeat string normalization and empty-value checks after an existing owner has already established the same result. This removes 20 redundant sites: normalize once with the existing SDK helper, carry trimmed values through private helpers, and let the final parser or renderer decide whether a value is empty.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. External payload validation, malformed-input rejection, missing-cursor handling, and all credential/authorization checks remain. Blank lookup inputs still stay unresolved, blank rich text still has no preview, and receipts retain the same optional fields. No schema, SQL, database identity, transaction, worker-routing, or public SDK contract changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing string helpers and final parsers already own these decisions. Removing repeated normalization keeps one owner without a new cache or compatibility path.

## Acceptance rule — recorded before measurement, amendments recorded in comments

- Flow/workload: frozen synthetic Gateway workload v3.1.4, one count-only run per arm, ten warm execution windows each. The original zero-idle proposal was amended before the candidate run to match the reusable baseline's 5-second settle and 300-second connected idle. After the reused baseline was rejected for a Node/SQLite mismatch, only the baseline was rerun with the retained candidate's runtime. Cold/restart/background counts stay separate.
- Metrics: native SQL statements, worker requests, and MAIN statements per warm execution window; median/p95/min/max and per-operation totals. Win: remove 20 repeated validation/normalization sites with net-negative production LOC. Regression: any increase attributable to these channel owners or any warm MAIN increase. No wall-clock, CPU, causal-attribution or latency claim.
- Behavior: focused owner tests preserve target/lookup parsing, rich-text rendering, receipt construction, and webhook/media validation. Blank/mixed-whitespace cases extend existing Slack tests.
- Limitation recorded before the candidate: the frozen observer's causal hook uses retired diagnostic storage and misses all ten warm causal phases. Native execution-window counts remain available. The generic workload does not invoke these changed channel handlers; focused tests and CI provide their behavior proof.

## Evidence

Changed-file formatting, basic lint, and native precommit pass. The 18 selected owner test files have 382 passing cases; the rich-text expectation was corrected to match the existing event sanitizer and rerun alone. Both independent Codex review rounds are scoped-clean (P0–P3); the final test-only expectation correction was checked against the sanitizer owner. The repository type-aware lint wrapper cannot prepare declaration inputs from the campaign-required external virtual store; required CI will supply the type/static gates.

Exact-head CI run [40132673792](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40132673792) passed all 26 active jobs, including production/test types, all lint stripes, source/extension boundaries, architecture, ratchets, and changed-scope tests. The security review also passed for this head. The matching count-only baseline/candidate pair completed; detailed results and limitations are below. This cleanup makes no SQL or latency saving claim. The refreshed census covers 2,673 open PRs targeting main. All four overlapping heads (#104322, #142776, #144720, #156344) add zero conflict paths or hunks in base-only versus base-plus-candidate merge-tree comparisons. The three spool edits were dropped to avoid the original conflict with #178077.

Production delta: 27 lines removed net. No compatibility path or cache added.

Three additional Nextcloud Talk webhook-spool candidates were left unchanged because they would add a merge conflict with open PR #178077.

## Open-PR conflict check

Compared the original main base and the final candidate against each overlapping open main-targeted PR. All add zero conflict paths or hunks.

| PR | Pinned head | New conflict paths / hunks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #104322 | `70b58575edd3edc60dde7ff25141f36be29bb77f` | 0 / 0 |

## Measurement outcome


One completed frozen v3.1.4 run per arm; ten warmed execution windows each. Baseline was run from the exact base SHA with the same installed runtime as the retained candidate. Identical harness hashes, Node/SQLite versions, and workload options. No latency or causal claim.

| Warm metric | Base median / p95 [min–max] | Candidate median / p95 [min–max] |

| sql | 51 / 71 [50–71] | 50.5 / 54 [50–54] |
| requests | 12.5 / 22 [12–22] | 12 / 14 [12–14] |
| main | 0 / 0 [0–0] | 0 / 0 [0–0] |

p95 is the nearest-rank statistic from ten samples. The frozen causal hook is incompatible with the current AsyncContext owner; all ten causal phases are unavailable. Native SQL, request and MAIN counts remain valid. The generic fixture does not invoke the changed channel handlers; focused owner tests and exact-head CI cover them.

## Per-operation warm deltas

Totals across ten windows; unchanged operations are omitted.

| Operation | SQL base → candidate | Requests base → candidate | MAIN base → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NO_REQUEST / AsyncWorkScope.enter | 3 → 4 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| UNKNOWN | 19 → 0 | 9 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

## Separate raw phase totals

Fixture account setup is unmeasured. Cold/restart and background phases are separate from warmed windows.

Both full workloads and child cleanup passed. No statement/request saving is attributed to this channel normalization cleanup.

## Interpreting phase changes

Several individual phase cells moved by more than 20%; they were investigated and are not accepted as evidence of a speedup or a causal regression. The observer cannot separate turn-caused work from background work on this source version.

Startup through the ten warm windows totals 1,334 → 1,337 SQL, 339 → 341 requests, and 48 → 48 MAIN. Compaction plus settling totals exactly 248 → 248 SQL, with 40 → 43 requests. Restart boot/connect/first-turn totals 505 → 497 SQL and 182 → 180 requests. Whole workloads total 2,987 → 2,985 SQL, 799 → 800 requests, and 95 → 94 MAIN. The extra baseline MAIN statement is `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 4999` during restart admission; the busy-timeout, state-open and device-pairing migration owners are byte-identical between arms.

The ten warm-window totals are 545 → 511 SQL, 137 → 125 requests, and 0 → 0 MAIN. Warm operation deltas include plugin metadata refresh/admission, auth-profile reads, plugin-state entries and otherwise unclassified background work. These owners are outside this patch. The generic fixture does not run the changed channel handlers. The count pair is recorded transparently; it does not establish a handler performance improvement or a broad performance non-regression result. The demonstrated result is the 20-site/-27-production-LOC simplification with preserved owner behavior.

prs.title: fix: restore package update sync failure coverage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the package-update Linux test fixture that stopped injecting its staged-file sync failure after the native copy path moved to callback-based `fs.fsync`. The ordinary-copy regression case consequently resolved successfully instead of exercising its intended pre-publication `EIO` rejection.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. Package update production code, the fs-safe dependency, publication and journal behavior, assertions, and timeouts remain unchanged. CI once again exercises the existing guarantee that an ordinary staged-file sync failure rejects before replacing the live launcher, while retaining the separate journal-owned publication and recovery coverage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared fixture already identifies staged files by device and inode and intercepts both `FileHandle.sync` and synchronous `fsyncSync`. fs-safe 0.26.13's native async copy path instead calls callback-based `fs.fsync`, so neither existing spy observed the operation.

This change extends that same fixture owner to intercept `fs.fsync`, delivers the synthetic error through its callback on a microtask, and restores the new spy through the existing lifecycle. Both consumer test files remain unchanged.

## Evidence

On exact base `aaecd52e6bffc4cadb8e7525ffa2fdea3977ef69`, the maintained remote selector ran `src/infra/package-update-filesystem.test.ts`: 27 tests passed, 6 were platform-skipped, and the ordinary staged-file sync case was the sole failure because its promise resolved instead of rejecting.

On exact candidate tree `20b6d88b5805f39314c297ba29374eb15769877e`, the OpenClaw remote recipe passed:

- changed-file formatting and source lint with zero warnings or errors;
- the selected `core-test-services` and `core` type graphs; and
- both literal consumers, `package-update-filesystem.test.ts` and `package-update-publication-durability.test.ts`: 46 passed, 6 platform skips, 0 failures.

Hosted CI is terminal green on the exact published head, including both aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` contexts and every selected Node, lint, type, boundary, security, CodeQL, and workflow-sanity row. Independent calibrated review concluded clean with no findings, and the separate canonical automated review returned `scoped-clean` with no P0-P3 findings.

The exact ordinary-copy consumer was also rerun on fetched target `a31e54a90d6a57fc05f347aba72abf8919c3d504`; it still produced the same sole failure, proving current `main` does not already contain the fixture repair.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway collection projections allocate temporary arrays only to map their elements into another array. Transcript title reads also copy a newly constructed result object.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Session selection/search, mentions, worker tools, workspace manifests, and Control UI asset rewriting produce the same outputs with fewer temporary allocations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace 18 spread-then-map operations with `Array.from(iterable, mapper)` and return fresh title fields directly. Each mapper reads a private or stable collection synchronously; the output arrays remain newly allocated. The title cache retains scalar fields rather than the result object.

Keep sorting, deep clones, bounded slices, snapshots around mutable callbacks, cross-owner/public API copies, and all authorization and cancellation checks. No SQL, schema, database identity, SDK signature, lifecycle, or configuration changes. Production delta: 16 files, +24/-27 lines (net -3), 19 temporary allocation sites removed. No new caches or helper abstractions.

## Evidence

- Source ownership audit: all 19 removed intermediate copies have a retained output or a fresh result; no mutable collection escapes to a mapper.
- Basic oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Independent Codex review (P0–P2): scoped-clean, no actionable findings; final source integrity verification passed. One conflicting hunk was subsequently restored to the base; no new implementation was added.
- Exact-head CI [40132876443](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40132876443): 68 passed, 27 skipped, including selected owner tests, prefix stability, types, lint, source contracts, architecture/Madge and database ratchets. Standalone production/full-tree/scripts Knip export scans: 1,230 identical base/head findings, zero new or removed signatures, no resolution errors/timeouts, and no findings in touched files.
- Open-main PR conflict census: 2,686 other open main PRs, with 42 latest new/moved heads checked through complete file lists and eight overlaps (#182836, #182783, #177257, #160237, #160220, #155419, #153907, #153885). Dropped one session-search mapping that added a conflict with #182836; final base/candidate merge-tree comparison adds zero conflict files or hunks for all eight heads.

### Pre-registered acceptance rule

Before the first run: use the frozen v3.1.4 synthetic real-Gateway workload, including ten warmed turns, session/control RPCs, tool/spawn work, and restart. Run one baseline/candidate pair on the exact base and candidate commits, with one fresh fixture per head, `--repetitions 1 --settle-seconds 0 --idle-seconds 0`. Separate cold phases from warmed phases. Count SQL statements, worker requests, and MAIN statements; report the warmed phase-window median, p95, and range, plus available operation differences. Frozen v3.1.4 causal turn attribution is unavailable on current main after the diagnostic-scope move; phase-file counts remain valid, and will not be described as causal counts. This is a count comparison; it makes no wall-clock, CPU-time, or latency claim.

Acceptance: 19 source-proven temporary allocations removed per execution of the selected sites; identical public behavior; no added SQL, requests, or MAIN work attributable to the changed operations. Any measured user-facing regression requires investigation, and a 20% move in a reported count cell is a stop. Keep and report boundaries the standard workload does not exercise; no claim that all 19 sites execute in this workload.

### Measured result

Frozen v3.1.4, exact base `11c9161b4a1` and candidate `2491ac85dbc`, one independent synthetic real-Gateway run per head; ten warm execution windows each. All 36 frozen hashes match. Both workloads passed, including restart and shutdown.

| Warm metric | Baseline median / p95 [min–max] | Candidate median / p95 [min–max] |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SQL statements | 50 / 56 [50–56] | 50.5 / 56 [50–56] |
| Worker requests | 12 / 15 [12–15] | 12 / 15 [12–15] |
| MAIN statements | 0 / 0 [0–0] | 0 / 0 [0–0] |

Warm totals are identical: **512 statements / 125 requests / 0 MAIN**, with every per-operation count identical. The small median shift comes from distribution across phase windows, not extra warm work. This PR claims allocation removal, not SQL savings or latency/CPU improvement. The standard workload does not establish execution of all 19 selected sites; existing owner tests and the ownership audit cover the broader paths.

Whole workload: **2,895 / 758 / 95 → 2,888 / 760 / 94** statements / requests / MAIN. Investigated the >20% cold/background phase shifts: compaction +31 schema-admission and +6 WAL-maintenance statements moved from shutdown, with whole-run totals unchanged for both operations. The net +2 whole-run requests comes from extra memory-source/subagent/catalog reads and fewer device-pairing/catalog reads. All 54 code-only origin-stack source files for differing whole-run request operations are byte-identical between base and head. No warm MAIN increase. These phase-window differences are disclosed; frozen causal attribution is unavailable.

prs.title: fix: messages sent to another chat are missing from that chat's model history
prs.body:
Closes #168683
Closes #168684

Rebuild of #169438 by @obviyus on current main. It keeps his design and his conversation transcript ownership ADR, and it credits him as co-author.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: some messages a chat shows are missing from that chat's model history. Messages sent to another chat through the `message` tool were stored as transcript-only mirrors. Cron failure alerts were not recorded anywhere. Each outbound path also had its own transcript writer.

## User Impact

User impact: messages sent to another chat now enter that chat's model history once. This covers cross-chat message-tool sends, cron results and failure alerts, routed replies, subagent completions, Workshop notices and Gateway-executed plugin sends. A follow-up such as "what did you just send here?" can now see the message. Normal replies and same-chat sends do not gain a second row. There is no configuration, schema or stored-queue change.

The Plugin SDK `mirror` input is still accepted until the next SDK major. Using it logs one deprecation warning, and it no longer selects where history is written. `session.key` now names the conversation whose turn produced the send. A sender with no producing turn should pass the destination as `policyKey`; the migration guide documents this.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is step 2 of `docs/refactor/conversation-transcript-ownership.md`. The outbound send owner records each confirmed payload through `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts`. That module resolves the destination from the carried route, then the producer's delivery context, then an exact current local binding, and finally the channel resolver. It skips the producing conversation, cross-agent destinations, ambiguous destinations and native-only payloads, recording a diagnostic where useful. It writes through the existing background-result commit, which uses main's newer `allow-live` policy (#181506), so recording never waits for the destination's active turn. If recording fails after a send, it logs a warning and never resends.

Differences from #169438:
- Heartbeat changes are dropped because main has retired heartbeat.
- #175590's Gateway-action destination mirror now goes through the shared owner instead of the old mirror writer.
- `commitBackgroundResultToSession` keeps main's text API. Payload and media preparation moved to `src/sessions/background-result-payloads.ts`.
- Cron completion rows written through outbound still carry `openclawAutomation` cron provenance.
- Subagent completion rows are marked `subagent-completion`. The existing out-of-turn and prior-delivery checks recognize them.
- The Google Chat space-type cache is not included and will be a separate PR.
- When a caller pins the receiving chat (subagent completions, cron results), that chat is used even if several chats share the delivery address. Otherwise the send would be skipped as ambiguous. Isolated Gateway proof found this case.
- For a message action the Gateway executes for a remote client, the Gateway leaves destination history to that client, as main does today. This stops two writers from recording one send under different identities.
- A persistent-session cron job whose notification goes to its own conversation still gets one visible settled-result row there, as #182262 introduced. Outbound skips the run's own conversation, so the run writes that row itself, pinned to its generation.
- Workshop notices stay a marked row in their own session, because the Control UI needs that marker to render the Learned row. The notice belongs to that session, so outbound delivery does not record it a second time.

## Evidence

- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass on this head. `oxlint` reports no errors in the changed files.
- About 387 affected test files passed before the latest rebase. The owner, route-reply, Workshop, cron destination and subagent tests were rerun on the current head across outbound, cron, cron/isolated-agent, subagent announce and registry, route-reply, gateway send and cron completion, sessions and Workshop.
- New owner tests cover:
  - destination creation and replay deduplication for text, location and document sends
  - producer skips by session key and by delivery context, including different topics of one chat
  - native-only and cross-agent skips
  - a legacy SDK `mirror` that cannot redirect history
  - recovery recording
  - a subagent completion recorded during an active requester turn, without consuming that turn's wake input
- Isolated real-Gateway proof: QA Lab runs a real Gateway with the QA channel and a mock model. A new scenario, `cross-conversation-send-history`, has a message-tool send from one room into another. The receiving room gets exactly one history row and the sending room gets none. The receiving room's next model request replays that row once as assistant history. The same scenario fails on main, where no row is recorded. The proof comment has the Crabbox run details.
- Not done: a live third-party channel round on this head. #169438's live Telegram and Discord proofs ran against its own head.
- Autoreview: Codex was unavailable because the local Codex API key failed authentication, so the review ran on Claude. It reported one P1: SDK callers whose `session.key` names the destination would silently lose rows. I addressed it with migration-guide and type documentation.

prs.title: feat: let Android admins manage automations from chat
prs.body:
Related: #182831

Draft for the explicit Android permission-policy decision and the unresolved local test failure documented below.

## What Problem This Solves

Lets an authenticated Android administrator inspect and manage existing Gateway automations from a fresh chat turn, instead of receiving only the caller-scoped inventory.

## User Impact

Administrators can manage automations from the Android conversation under the same configured automation policy as the Control UI. This is an intentional extension of conversational administrator permissions and requires maintainer acceptance. It does not grant permissions to non-admin devices or change pairing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record a server-held Android admin fact after authentication and effective-scope resolution, then admit it through the existing direct-turn automation authority owner. Reuse run-bound grants, currentness checks, and revocation. Android does not acquire local-operator or Control UI identity; ordinary creation remains caller-scoped.

Replayed/recovered, incognito, synthetic, delegated, and system-generated turns keep their exclusions. Gateway policy `automations.scope: caller` still suppresses management grants. No restart-recovery snapshot extension, new persistent state, or protocol field is introduced. Tool guidance and documentation describe the added path.

## Evidence

- The original 2026.10.7 implementation passed 173 tests. Four gateway files passed in 275.96 seconds; the final authority-context run passed in 22.47 seconds. Its runtime build and isolated startup smoke passed.
- A real authenticated WebSocket probe using the Android client protocol ran the `automations` tool and returned `scope=gateway` and all 11 jobs already present before that probe. This was protocol-level evidence, not an instrumented physical Android device test.
- On upstream baseline `e1e498602cec224ef4adb16f13512ca6aea26d98`, the four focused gateway files completed with 169 passing tests and one failure in 555.30 seconds. The failure was the existing `attests agent runtime identity for a remote token` case: its close callback was not observed before the polling assertion expired. This is not a clean full-suite result; an isolated rerun reproduced the same failure (75.89 seconds, one failed and 54 skipped). The rejection branch precedes the added Android-admission block, but no current-main baseline run was performed, so this is not claimed to be a proven pre-existing failure. The port preserves newer automation policy and requester/recovery behavior.
- Tests cover resolved admin versus narrowed scopes, claimed client-name rejection, direct versus recovered/synthetic turns, actual grants, and revocation during mutation. No automatic recovery authority is added.
- `pnpm test src/agents/cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 21 tests in 95.22 seconds.
- Formatting, focused syntax lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent autoreview of the upstream candidate reported no actionable P0-P2 findings. The review did not execute tests.
- Simplification pass: one post-auth fact and one entitlement variant, consumed by the existing admission/grant owners. No new manager or lifecycle. Existing test tables and fixtures are reused. The review follow-up retains original device revocation through the existing requester-continuation owner rather than adding a parallel permission manager.

The live probe and runtime build evidence apply to the installed baseline, not a deployment of current main. Type-aware lint was stopped because its local graph was too costly alongside a serving Gateway; no successful type-aware result is claimed. Broad build/typecheck/test coverage and CI duration remain for PR CI.


## Review follow-up

- Added current-candidate protocol coverage using a real isolated Gateway, paired remote-attributed Android WebSocket clients, chat admission, model tool dispatch, and Cron persistence. Inference alone is synthetic. It exercises foreign-session get/update, narrowed write-only denial, and device revocation while a turn is running. This is protocol proof, not a physical-phone test.
- Added requester-continuation regressions. The pre-repair candidate `57244b9d44c0c8641c715379ee28415863212c3d` allowed the persisted update after Android device revocation; the same revocation assertion passes with repair `78383f282c9485747d679fcae3a52fce5af17db2`. The repair retains and rechecks the original device owner through continuation, including release and repeat-yield propagation. The normal administrator update and write-only denial cases also pass.
- Those first runs were not clean suites: two read tests used the wrong parameterized-test context API, and the protocol fixture used a noncanonical identity path. The fixtures are corrected in `b7e2173a3e4298d665d9163d0cb8be62341cbbe1`; direct-tool discovery is explicit and the revocation wait is cancellable. The next isolated VPS run passed 29 tests and exposed a mismatched read-denial assertion plus the fixture requirement for TLS when using proxy headers. The read assertion now matches the existing authority-currentness rejection; the remote Android fixture uses the canonical pinned test certificate and wss, without disabling verification. These fixes are in `15969e2f3a947d9eb0def28c4bcfc4483df4959a` and `57f2afdfa4a67e18ba66dee1cb7505f103074748`. Formatting passes on the latter head. Its runtime proof was killed at the isolated job's 4 GiB limit during compilation, before the continuation suite or protocol scenario completed. The next executor budget is 6 GiB with a 2 GiB host reserve; sufficient VPS capacity is still required. No green current-head runtime result is claimed.
- Independent review of the retention repair and fixture corrections found no actionable P0-P2 issue. These reviews were static. No clean full-suite or physical-device result is claimed until the runtime checks complete.

The fork now uses the `openclaw/vps-authority-proof` commit status for these focused checks. The upstream project's own CI remains independent. Maintainer/security-owner acceptance of the Android permission extension and the previously documented remote-token test failure remain outstanding. This PR stays draft.

prs.title: fix(exec): restore Windows S4U commands with Store PowerShell installed
prs.body:
Closes #182652

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent exec failing with `spawn EPERM` under a Windows S4U Scheduled Task when shell discovery selects an inaccessible Microsoft Store PowerShell app-execution alias.

## User Impact

Local commands work in the unattended Gateway session even while Store PowerShell is running in the desktop session. Native PowerShell 7 remains preferred; if only an inaccessible Store alias is available, exec uses Windows PowerShell 5.1. Users needing PowerShell 7 syntax such as `&&` should install its MSI or ZIP distribution.

No task logon policy, credentials, approval checks, or Job containment changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell resolver accepted candidates using only `access(X_OK)`. On Windows, the Store alias passes that check while `stat` fails with `EACCES`; activating it from another logon session can then fail with `EPERM`.

Reuse the existing executable-file checker so discovery continues to a native executable or the existing Windows PowerShell fallback. No subprocess probes, retries, caches, or path-name blacklist are added.

## Evidence

- **Parallels Windows 11 ARM64, Node 26.12.1 x64, signed Microsoft PowerShell 7.6.8 MSIX:** held Store PowerShell open in desktop session 1, then exercised the production shell resolver → process supervisor → native Windows Job launcher under otherwise matching S4U and Interactive tasks.

  | Task / session | Original resolver | Fixed resolver |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | S4U / 0 | `node --version`: `spawn EPERM` | `v26.12.1`, exit 0 |
  | Interactive / 1 | `v26.12.1`, exit 0 | `v26.12.1`, exit 0 |

  Both fixed tasks reported their expected session ID. Cancelling a long-running Node descendant confirmed Job extinction in both sessions. Ordinary Node and Windows PowerShell spawns were also verified before the repair. Test-only tasks and package installation were removed afterward; existing Gateway state was not changed.
- Two new resolver cases fail against the original production code and pass with the fix: continue to a later native PowerShell 7 executable, or fall back to PowerShell 5.1.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/shell-utils.test.ts src/agents/shell-snapshot.test.ts src/agents/github-exec-launch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **68 passed, 1 platform skip**, 38.41 seconds wall time. CI timing pending.
- Targeted typecheck using the repository test-shard configuration and ambient declarations: passed. Targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Simplification: existing executable-file owner reused; production delta +4/-5 lines, tests +30/-3, docs +6. Independent AutoReview: no actionable findings.

Proof scope: real Windows shell/process boundary, not a complete model-driven Gateway turn. The guest is ARM64 running the reporter's x64 Node version, not the reporter's exact x64 Windows build. The reporter's PowerShell installation was not supplied; the reproduced alias failure matches the reported S4U/Interactive symptom.

prs.title: perf(ui): share visible presentation clocks
prs.body:
Supersedes #182809. GitHub kept that PR at mergeability UNKNOWN through repeated native recovery attempts, a main refresh, and a close/reopen. This PR uses the identical reviewed commit and eight-file change. Full CI passed on that exact head; the reopened run also passed after one documented timing-flake rerun. A fresh PR record allows normal native admission to recompute.

## What Problem This Solves

Hundreds of running-session labels each allocate their own timer and visibility listener, even when they share the same refresh cadence.

## User Impact

Elapsed, relative-time, and working-phrase labels keep their existing appearance and formatting. Hidden tabs stop ticking and catch up when visible. Labels now share a cadence, so the first tick after mounting can arrive sooner than a full interval. Request polling and approval countdowns retain their existing owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two lazy presentation-clock projections replace per-instance signal/polling setup in three renderers. The existing `projectSource` owns subscription lifetime: ended, missing, disabled, and disposed readers keep no interval. No domain state, requests, or mutation authority moves into Solid.

This is the second proof from the UI architecture census. Production renderer/primitive LOC is 186 → 224 (+38); the extra shared primitive removes scheduling work proportional to mounted rows. The new regression test is 135 lines. The benchmark adds a real 200-running-child-session scenario to the existing harness, with unchanged default fixtures. No new dependencies, CSS, host tags, or eager page imports.

Refactor checklist: per-renderer signals 3 → 0, per-renderer visible-poll calls 3 → 0; direct listeners, DOM queries, render effects, cleanup hooks, untrack, flush and owner capture remain zero in the touched renderers/primitive.

## Evidence

Same-machine production builds on the integrated main base `4d49d348a5c2` and the clock candidate:

| Surface | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip | 281,184 B | 281,299 B | +115 B |
| Startup requests | 7 JS + 1 CSS | 7 JS + 1 CSS | unchanged |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,274,797 B | 1,274,584 B | −213 B |
| New Session boot JS gzip | 770,888 B | 771,021 B | +133 B |
| Mixed 300-reader active timers | 300 | 2 | −99.3% |
| Hidden / disabled / disposed timers | 0 | 0 | preserved |

`pnpm tsgo:ui` passes. The new lifecycle suite plus existing elapsed-time and working-phrase suites pass (15 tests across three files). The new timer-bound test fails against the original renderers (300 rather than 2). It also covers fresh mounts between ticks, surviving siblings, hidden initial mounts, visibility catch-up, and final-reader cleanup.

Targeted lint passes with one unchanged elapsed-time style warning. Independent Codex autoreview has no actionable P0–P2 findings. The production build passes. The strict performance check reports the same existing total CSS overage as the base: 303,527 B gzip / 1,595,522 B raw, with no CSS delta. Production Knip reports the same three unused non-UI files: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/protocol-validator-schemas.ts`, `src/gateway/mcp-app-standalone-host.ts`, and `src/gateway/worker-environments/repository-node-requirement.ts`.

The real production sidebar workload retains all 200 clocks, advances labels over five seconds, creates no replacement clock rows, and issues no RPCs. A ten-pair A/A control measured script medians 18.280/17.694 ms and p95 19.138/19.933 ms under shared-host load. The final 20-pair comparison per viewport passed all 80 samples, retaining 200/200 clocks with zero replacement rows and no RPCs. Wall time is intentionally dominated by the five-second observation window and is not a latency claim.

Inspected synthetic production screenshots at 1440 px and 390 px are attached. Sidebar desktop crops and full mobile captures are pixel-identical before/after. The full desktop differs only in unrelated animated composer placeholder text. Capture uses the native Vitest/Playwright helper with fixed fixture time; Node is used only for this Playwright harness. Full UI CI is selected with `ci:full`.

![Before: synthetic running sessions, desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1981bd91-19bc-4085-aa3e-93c54aafb23a)

![After: synthetic running sessions, desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3305538c-5dbd-41e1-81dd-4785b5bef3fe)

![Before: synthetic running sessions, mobile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2c9ef83-754c-4e05-9bf5-5416964aaf97)

![After: synthetic running sessions, mobile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d11d036-29cd-42ba-9483-00f5fe47bcf7)

### Final CPU comparison

Five real seconds per sample; 20 interleaved base/head pairs per viewport, thread CPU time enabled.

| Viewport | Script CPU median, base → head | Change | Script CPU p95, base → head |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Desktop | 17.493 → 15.821 ms | −9.6% | 20.552 → 18.608 ms |
| Mobile | 16.046 → 13.984 ms | −12.9% | 19.536 → 17.496 ms |

Host load ranged roughly 18–32. Desktop task CPU median was 158.081 → 154.427 ms; mobile 120.242 → 113.436 ms. Desktop task p95 moved 183.344 → 191.486 ms (+4.4%); script CPU, the directly affected work, improved at both median and p95. Wall medians stayed approximately 5.04 seconds, the intentional observation window. No latency claim is based on wall/frame timing. The committed scenario is `sidebar-clock-idle`; retained local evidence is `.artifacts/clock-pairs/warm-jiVwOU`.


Initial CI found a benchmark-only unused callback parameter and formatting issue. The repair changes only that callback spelling/formatting; the exact script typecheck, targeted lint, formatting check, and fresh repair review pass. Production code and measured bundles/CPU/screenshots are unchanged. The initial auto request was retired before the repair push; the replacement head will use native recovery.


GitHub left the green replacement head at mergeability UNKNOWN through two native recovery attempts. A conflict-free merge of current main forces a fresh calculation; the seven-file clock patch has identical stable patch ID `766d592c3160a1b55a0370887ff2cb98590fe700`. UI and script typechecks pass after integration. The CPU/visual proof above was captured against the original `820c30a3a010` base; the production clock patch is unchanged. Fresh base/head builds supply the current byte table above.

The current byte delta is an accepted CPU tradeoff under this performance lane: +115 B startup and +133 B New Session, below 0.5 KB per surface, with −213 B chat and unchanged request counts. Startup raw bytes are identical; shared compression changes with chunk layout. The official performance checker updates the startup baseline from 281,671 B to the measured 281,299 B and records the 20-pair CPU evidence. The unchanged total CSS overage is not waived or increased.


Reopening the stuck GitHub PR triggered another run on the same head. Run 40131307252 failed only `chat-motion.e2e.test.ts > animates new prompts without hiding streamed replies on mobile`: the sampled bubble y-position was not monotonic, while scrolling remained smooth, made no instant jump, and finished at zero distance. The same case passes on the unchanged merge base, and this exact PR head previously passed the full run 40129618170. The decorative phrase cannot appear before 30 seconds; the failing case finishes before that, and the patch does not change scrolling. One diagnosed animation-timing flake rerun is limited to job 120983789889. This records the intermittent assertion; it does not claim a product fix.

prs.title: fix: staged exclusive-create test misses pathname substitution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the staged exclusive-create substitution test when Linux reuses the unlinked source inode for the fixture's replacement, allowing a deliberate pathname swap to look unchanged.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible or production behavior change. The existing safety regression test now deterministically exercises the native helper's pathname-substitution rejection while preserving its assertions, dependency version, timeouts, configuration, and workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture previously unlinked the staged file only after the native helper had closed its payload descriptor. It then allocated a replacement with no remaining reference to the original inode, so the filesystem could reuse that inode and defeat the fixture's intended identity change.

The fixture now opens the original staged file first and keeps that descriptor live through unlink and replacement allocation. It closes the descriptor immediately afterward, leaving the production helper and its publication checks untouched. A simplification pass confirmed that this is the smallest correction in the existing fixture owner.

## Evidence

On current `origin/main`, the full owner file reproduced the failure remotely: 27 of 28 tests passed, while `fails when the staged exclusive-create pathname is substituted` returned status 0 at its unchanged assertion.

On the corrected tree, remote changed-file formatting/lint and the affected core test type graph passed. The same complete owner file then passed all 28 tests, including the unchanged substitution status, stderr, replacement-content, and directory assertions.

Hosted CI is terminal green on the exact head, including the selected Node, type, lint, guard, security, CodeQL, and OpenGrep rows. Calibrated independent review and canonical autoreview found no issues. ClawSweeper likewise reported no findings and rated patch quality Platinum; its overall/proof rating is Gold because the change and its evidence are test-only.

prs.title: fix(talk): GPT-Live relay closes when output arrives before mic input
prs.body:
Closes #134798 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a gateway-relay Talk session closes with "Realtime provider output has no live response owner." when GPT-Live sends audio, a transcript, or a tool call before the client's first microphone frame. ## User Impact GPT-Live Talk through the gateway relay stays open when the provider speaks first or the microphone opens late (for example on Bluetooth hands-free links), instead of failing right after `talk.session.create` succeeds. ## Why This Change Was Made `TalkRealtimeRelayOutputOwnership.resolve(true)` only claims output for an active turn. Continuous transports (`outputAudioMode: "continuous"`, the GPT-Live bridge) never send `response.created`, so output that arrives before client input has no owner and fails the session. The owner now starts the turn on the first unowned continuous output, the same way `responseCreated()` already does for an ID-less response. Response-mode providers are unchanged.
Root cause - `src/gateway/talk/relay/state.ts` `resolve()`: in phase `unowned` with no active turn, a claiming call goes straight to `fail()`. - Provider audio (`audioSink.sendAudio`), assistant transcripts, and tool calls all call `resolve(true)` in `session-create.ts`. - The guard comes from #127186 (cancellation ownership). That path is unaffected: explicit cancellation on a continuous transport closes the relay (`operations.ts`), barge-in is provider-owned, and the new branch only runs when there is no owner and no turn. - Overlap: #163880 drops all-zero idle PCM on the same path and keeps nonzero pre-input continuous audio as a failure. This change admits that audio as a turn, which covers the greeting and late-microphone traces in this issue. If both land, the zero-PCM filter still applies first.
## Evidence Isolated Gateway (Node 24.22.1, temp state/config/HOME, loopback port) loading a local realtime provider plugin with `outputAudioMode: "continuous"` that sends nonzero PCM 300 ms after connect and never sends `response.created`. A WebSocket client calls `talk.session.create` (realtime, gateway-relay, agent-consult) and sends no audio. - Main: `session.ready` → `session.error "Realtime provider output has no live response owner."` → `session.closed reason=error`; `talk.session.close` → `Unknown Talk session`. - Fix: `session.ready` → `output.audio.delta turnId=turn-1` ×2, no error; `talk.session.close` → `{"ok":true}`, `session.closed reason=completed`. - Control on the fix with `outputAudioMode: "response"`: same error and close as main. Main: Fix: Control (response mode, unchanged):
Client output **Main** (`relayDiff=` empty: relay files identical to upstream/main 325c87d4688) ```text gateway ready on loopback port (label=red mode=continuous head=325c87d4688 relayDiff=) + 3070ms talk.event type=ready talkEvent=session.ready turnId=- seq=1 + 3070ms talk.session.create ok transport=gateway-relay provider=proofvoice sessionId= + 3379ms talk.event type=error talkEvent=session.error turnId=- seq=2 message="Realtime provider output has no live response owner." + 3379ms talk.event type=close talkEvent=session.closed turnId=- seq=3 reason=error summary audioEvents=0 error=true closed=true talk.session.close failed: Error: Unknown Talk session client exit=0 ``` **Fix** ```text gateway ready on loopback port (label=green mode=continuous head=325c87d4688 relayDiff= 2 files changed, 9 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)) + 1417ms talk.event type=ready talkEvent=session.ready turnId=- seq=1 + 1417ms talk.session.create ok transport=gateway-relay provider=proofvoice sessionId= + 1718ms talk.event type=audio talkEvent=output.audio.delta turnId=turn-1 seq=3 + 1718ms talk.event type=audio talkEvent=output.audio.delta turnId=turn-1 seq=4 summary audioEvents=2 error=false closed=false + 3425ms talk.event type=close talkEvent=session.closed turnId=- seq=5 reason=completed talk.session.close ok {"ok":true} client exit=0 ``` **Control: fix with a response-mode provider (unchanged from main)** ```text gateway ready on loopback port (label=control-response mode=response head=325c87d4688 relayDiff= 2 files changed, 9 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)) + 604ms talk.event type=ready talkEvent=session.ready turnId=- seq=1 + 605ms talk.session.create ok transport=gateway-relay provider=proofvoice sessionId= + 909ms talk.event type=error talkEvent=session.error turnId=- seq=2 message="Realtime provider output has no live response owner." + 910ms talk.event type=close talkEvent=session.closed turnId=- seq=3 reason=error summary audioEvents=0 error=true closed=true talk.session.close failed: Error: Unknown Talk session client exit=0 ```
New regression `claims a Talk turn for continuous provider audio|transcript before browser audio` fails on main with the error above and passes with the fix. `pnpm test src/gateway/talk/relay/`: 182 passed. Consumer tests (`server-close.voice-session`, `relay-audio-base64`, OpenAI realtime bridge and quicksilver gateway bridge): 34 passed. oxlint and oxfmt clean on touched files; `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `git diff --check` clean. Not run: a live GPT-Live session (needs a GPT-Live account). Production delta +9/-1; test delta +24/-0. Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the prior behavior with no state or config migration. Blast radius is output on continuous realtime transports that arrives with no active Talk turn.

prs.title: fix: restore acknowledgements for bound ACP reset commands
prs.body:
Closes #164004.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing acknowledgements when `/new` or `/reset` runs inside a bound ACP conversation and cleanup aborts the command's own reply.

## User Impact

Users receive the reset acknowledgement instead of a silent command and a self-dependent cleanup wait. Competing work and external resets remain cancellable. No configuration, schema, model policy, or deadline changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime cleanup honors the exact live initiating reply covered by the lifecycle admission exemption. It does not exempt every reply for a session: replacement operations and embedded owners retain their cancellation and drain behavior. Deferred MCP retirement continues to observe the actual owner until it settles.

Helper responsibilities move to sibling modules to meet growth guards. No new command features are included. Related preservation work exists in #95700; this implementation does not reuse that PR's code. Binding retention is a separate inherited defect, tracked in #165746, and is not fixed by this PR.

## Evidence and revision boundaries

Current PR head: `d17ba1494da`, rebased onto `main` `10334ec913d` on October 6 to clear an import-only conflict in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts`. The PR's moved wait helper now sits beside main's new error-coercion and session-index imports. After the rebase, the agent-runner, reset-initiator, ACP-timeout and cleanup files pass (5 files, 54 tests), and the full changed-file gate passes. Its latest test-only commit removes the synthetic next-turn claim from the initiator fixture: manually supplying an ACP key is not proof of subsequent conversation routing. The fixture still tests reset acknowledgement and lifecycle ownership. Do not interpret historical test counts as a fresh full-suite run on this head.

- Initial baseline reproduction at base `e2b5de4ea14d223ff1443cbfe569c897784cd8af`: both `/new` and `/reset` acknowledgement regressions fail with byte-identical baseline production and pass with original repair `2d65061d41ed4746faab0150e0d736810241bc12`. Real dispatch/reset/cleanup/registry composition, competing admission, external reset, fail-closed timeout, replacement reply, and embedded owner controls cover distinct ownership contracts.
- The original repair and later revisions received scoped independent reviews. Historical build/type/lint/ratchet receipts are revision-qualified; they are not a claim of hosted CI or live Test Server proof for the latest head.
- Real **production-network Telegram**, manually driven through an isolated Gateway at `50d2ed7a1b9aff9d166b8ecb901abb1b23f8197d`, visibly delivered both bound reset acknowledgements. Follow-up prompts then routed to ordinary main because the unchanged reset service unbound the topic. Full step-by-step report: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164005#issuecomment-6001355455.
- A subsequent production-network Telegram run of stacked candidate `db0aaa0676b48c5faa42645ebaa6de98ec498745` combines this acknowledgement repair with the separate #165746 continuity fix. Codex handled the pre-reset, post-`/new`, and post-`/reset` turns on the same logical bound target; underlying runtime IDs changed. Report: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165746#issuecomment-6002574434. **That candidate is not this PR's head and is not proof of continuity on this PR alone.**

- **Baseline live control without this PR (October 6).** An isolated Gateway on Telegram's production network, built from standalone #165839 head `0ebf0add51f` on current `main`, which does not include this PR, with a real Codex ACP binding. Three typed commands in the bound topic (`/new`, `/new`, `/reset`) each produced no acknowledgement. The Gateway logged `acp reset failed … Session … is still active; try again in a moment` after the 15-second wait every time, and no reset was committed: the acpx runtime ID stayed the same, and `/acp status` showed the pre-reset runtime. So on `main`, a typed reset in a bound ACP conversation is not just silent; it does not happen. With this PR applied (runs at `50d2ed7a1b9` and stacked `db0aaa0676b`), both commands acknowledged and committed.

## Remaining proof / CI gates

- These manual runs used Telegram's production network, **not** the repository-required Telegram Test Server userbot skill. The official Test Server evidence remains outstanding. We do not claim its proof label is satisfied.
- The official QA doctor has no authenticated credential-broker route on our host. A broker lease and an explicitly scoped ACP authentication path, or a credentialed maintainer-assisted run, are needed; existing hosted recipes do not automatically configure this ACP case.
- Latest CI includes cancellations before runner execution. A sampled `resolve` job (`111953493991`) has `conclusion=cancelled` and an empty steps list after 15 minutes. That is not a test pass or proof all unexecuted jobs would pass. Maintainer rerun is still needed.
- Full repository suite, real lifecycle retirement races, and strict UI-performance approval are not claimed. Historical canonical builds exited 0 with report-only UI budget warnings; no budgets were relaxed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the acknowledgement regression</summary>

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-initiator.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The fixture uses real registry abort/wait behavior; it does not prove a subsequent real transport/backend turn. The actual bound-conversation continuation contract is owned by the separate #165746 persisted-binding regression and qualified live report.

</details>
