prs.title: test(perf): reproduce Reef audit boot retention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adds a reproducible real-Gateway boot workload for Reef audit retention, which dominates the remaining startup plugin-state traffic.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The workload uses only synthetic state and a loopback relay; it does not read operator state or call external model services.

## Why This Change Was Made

The normalized traffic attribution identifies 173 audit appends, each with three upserts, two keyed reads, two namespace quota/expiry aggregates, and one retention delete: 1,384 statements excluding transaction envelopes. Those writes maintain the audit chain and are already grouped into one transaction per append. This workload distinguishes that owner from generic plugin rehydration.

## Evidence

### Acceptance rule registered before measurement

Flow: isolated current-head Gateway, bundled Reef channel, real HTTP/WebSocket transport, frozen SQL observer, synthetic keys and a full 30,000-entry audit chain seeded offline. Deliver 173 signed receipts lacking an outbound binding, producing 346 appends (read plus quarantine for each receipt). Wait for the relay to observe the completed cursor, then record 60 seconds of warm polling separately from boot and shutdown. Verify the retained audit chain, capacity and all quarantined receipts offline after shutdown.

Metrics: successful SQL statements and worker requests per completed append and per warm minute, plus main-thread SQL; attribute all worker and main work. Counts and CPU profiles precede any candidate. Any candidate must reduce target work without increasing warm statements, requests or main-thread SQL, and preserve TTL cleanup, capacity and cross-writer visibility. A timed comparison requires five alternating samples per arm, separate cold/warm median, p95 and range, the campaign timing lock and host load below 24. Every user-facing metric must hold or improve; a 20% adverse cell stops the candidate. No timing claim from unqualified runs.

Controls: fresh audit without prefill and empty inbox. If the live shape does not reproduce, stop that item and report the measured gap. No schema or SDK signature change is intended.

Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/plugin-state-polling.mts --observer <frozen-observer> --output <isolated-output> --messages 0 --receipts 173 --audit-prefill --seconds 60 --profile`.

### Measured result

Production source is unchanged from `3f7b7765585ddcd72822d8b4e43ef928d23eecf7`; workload head is `c1b1d2750b37b44a12b7313e96b668821de2544d`. This is a reproducible baseline, not a performance improvement.

The full-window run completed through the real Gateway and relay. It verified sequence 30,346, exactly 30,000 retained audit entries, and all 173 quarantined receipts. Frozen observer hashes matched 36/36 files. Each of the 346 audit appends used one worker request containing ten SQL statements: three upserts, two keyed reads, two namespace quota/expiry aggregates, one retention delete, BEGIN and COMMIT. That is 2,768 data statements and 3,460 including transaction envelopes, reproducing the normalized live shape exactly at eight data statements per append.

| Full-window phase | SQL statements | Worker requests | Main-thread SQL |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Boot | 5,491 | 860 | 48 |
| Warm polling (60.0017 seconds) | 33 | 13 | 0 |
| Shutdown | 22 | 6 | 5 |
| Total | 5,546 | 879 | 53 |

The warm phase completed two relay polls, no acknowledgments, and no unexpected HTTP requests. The run captured 23 per-thread CPU profiles. Counts use recorded execution phases; the frozen observer's causal-turn hook does not support the current AsyncContext carrier, so no causal-turn or latency claim is made. Nineteen statements/thirteen requests outside the audit target remain unattributed; every audit request is accounted for.

### Control results

All three runs completed on the same unchanged production source. These are one observation per fixture, not A/B performance samples.

| Synthetic fixture | Boot SQL / requests / MAIN | Warm SQL / requests / MAIN | Audit data SQL | Audit requests |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full 30,000-entry window, 173 receipts | 5,491 / 860 / 48 | 33 / 13 / 0 | 2,768 | 346 |
| Fresh chain, 173 receipts | 5,144 / 860 / 48 | 33 / 13 / 0 | 2,421 | 346 |
| Empty inbox | 648 / 168 / 48 | 33 / 13 / 0 | 0 | 0 |

Each warm observation was 60 seconds. All had zero unexpected HTTP requests. Fresh-chain verification retained all 346 generated audit entries and 173 quarantines. The fresh chain used one eight-statement request and 345 nine-statement requests; the full chain used 346 ten-statement requests. The exact full-versus-fresh difference is 346 necessary retention deletions and the initial previous-entry update. Non-audit totals are identical between the two receipt fixtures. Shutdown was 22 SQL / 6 requests / 5 MAIN for all three.

### Optimization disposition

The dominant writes are changed values: the previous entry gains a successor link, the new entry is inserted, and the head advances. The deletion keeps the retained window at 30,000. These are retained. The keyed reads preserve persisted/legacy writer and chain-integrity contracts. Dropping count/expiry aggregates would also drop documented bounded TTL cleanup during mutations (`docs/plugins/sdk-runtime/state-and-system.md`). There is no safe local deletion demonstrated here.

Cross-namespace or multi-write batching needs an owner change preserving synchronous read-own-write, per-namespace quota/error behavior, TTL cleanup, and real-writer visibility. That is an owner-design follow-up, not an optimization in this PR. No checks, transactions, production lines, schemas, or public SDK signatures are removed. Net delta is +179 workload/documentation lines (+200/-21), with zero production delta.

### Validation and integration

Two independent Codex autoreview rounds completed with no accepted P0–P2 findings. Basic oxlint, oxfmt and diff checks pass. The first CI run identified two lint errors in the workload; a focused repair replaced the callback-updated loop condition and mutating sort. Exact repaired-head CI [40133114127](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133114127) passed, including the required CI gate, types, lint, source contracts, architecture and baseline ratchets. Standalone Knip export scans report identical baseline/head path-and-symbol findings: 67 production, 77 full-tree, and 1,136 script findings, with zero additions or removals. These existing findings remain red; this PR adds none. The baseline comparison used the same dependency graph and restored the two reviewed files byte-for-byte. No local check bypass was used.

The open-main census covered 2,681 other PRs (2,682 including this PR), refreshing 41 new/moved heads. Neither changed file overlaps another open PR; no new merge conflicts. No PostgreSQL-reachable SQL or identity changes, SDK surface change, or runtime lifecycle change; PostgreSQL review and the published-driver update cell do not apply.

prs.title: perf(ui): defer optional chat code until it is needed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cold chat load downloads publication controls, cron parsing, and voice continuation code before those features are needed.

## User Impact

Chat loads less JavaScript while preserving the same first screen and existing publication, schedule, and voice behavior. No config or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

V8 coverage on the populated synthetic chat fixture identified optional feature code that was downloaded but unused. Publication controls now load under the existing work/publication surface, cron grammar loads only for a displayed cron schedule, and voice continuation/camera code loads after synchronous gesture-bound audio preparation. The plain voice owner still admits starts, stops, disconnects, route changes, and retry consent.

The boot manifest generator also excludes the existing idle shell runtime so favicon decoration and navigation prefetch are not accidentally promoted into route preloads. Publication CSS keeps its original parent import position.

This is a measured first step toward the chat boot size goal, not a claim of a 30% reduction. The remaining cost is distributed across first-screen owners and Markdown processing; further restructuring is being investigated.

## Evidence

Final comparison: base `ff2c84117f607770fdc5671b37e899e824647333`, head `e2a8b8b2112a4701aa782ae6480163cac0e86418`. Same Mac and Node 26.12.1, production Gateway HTTP assets with synthetic RPC, 240-message chat, cold HTTP cache. Twenty interleaved base/control/head observations per profile; the control uses the identical base bundle. V8 coverage is collected separately from timings.

| Check | Base | Head | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Startup JS gzip / raw | 281,296 / 870,214 B | 281,281 / 870,239 B | −15 gzip / +25 raw B |
| Chat preload JS gzip / raw | 1,275,035 / 4,104,421 B | 1,271,042 / 4,092,452 B | −3,993 gzip / −11,969 raw B |
| New Session preload JS gzip / raw | 771,394 / 2,503,632 B | 767,071 / 2,492,248 B | −4,323 gzip / −11,384 raw B |
| Observed cold-chat JS gzip / raw | 1,384,571 / 4,364,979 B | 1,372,922 / 4,321,095 B | −11,649 gzip / −43,884 raw B |
| V8 executed / unused raw | 1,931,234 / 2,433,745 B | 1,921,500 / 2,399,595 B | 53 scripts on both sides |
| Startup / Chat / New requests | 7 / 19 / 16 JS; 1 / 3 / 3 CSS | Unchanged | No added critical-path requests |
| Local composer median / p95 | 224.8 / 458.8 ms | 224.8 / 308.6 ms | Passed |
| Local transcript median / p95 | 501.7 / 641.7 ms | 497.4 / 579.7 ms | Passed |
| Local script / task CPU median | 550.9 / 1,075.1 ms | 562.0 / 1,087.8 ms | +2.00% / +1.19%, within 5% band |
| 100 ms RTT composer median / p95 | 1,467.8 / 1,491.0 ms | 1,458.9 / 1,472.4 ms | Passed |
| 100 ms RTT transcript median / p95 | 1,651.8 / 1,713.9 ms | 1,638.3 / 1,690.6 ms | Passed |
| 100 ms RTT script / task CPU median | 607.7 / 1,248.1 ms | 621.0 / 1,268.7 ms | +2.20% / +1.65%, within 5% band |
| Strict performance comparison | — | Passed | CSS identical: 1,595,021 raw / 303,551 gzip B; existing gzip cap excess retained |
| Integrated composition tests | — | 36 passed | Mobile Details and automation result/schedule rendering |
| Earlier focused behavior proof | — | 87 original tests; 54 unit + 10 browser repair tests; 2 publication E2E cases passed | Reused where source inputs remain unchanged |
| Schema and cloud-reload CI repair | — | Both exact cases passed | Schema 10.5 s; cloud recovery 4.1 s; pre-fix cloud case reproduced the timeout |
| UI types / targeted lint / formatting | — | Passed | No new controller or lifecycle guard debt |
| Production Knip | Unchanged non-UI findings | No UI findings | 4 files, 31 export entries, 11 type entries outside UI |
| Independent review | — | Scoped-clean P0–P2 | Complete own diff reviewed after integration |

Host load medians were approximately 32–33 during both profiles. The A/A control showed lower wall-clock tails on the busy host; candidate readiness medians and p95s do not regress, and renderer CPU stays within the acceptance band. Instrumented coverage timings are not latency evidence.

Touched production UI: 2,824 → 2,952 lines (+128); tests/helpers: 4,616 → 4,693 (+77); tooling/docs/generated: 5,882 → 5,940 (+58); directly coupled core schema: 74 → 74. Growth supplies explicit lazy boundaries and coverage diagnostics. There is no duplicate renderer or new state owner. Solid census: controllers, effects, render effects, untrack, listeners, DOM queries, flush, owner APIs, and cleanup remain 0 → 0 in the touched production files.

The first CI failures came from synchronous fixture readers after lazy controls were introduced; those readers now await real controls or cron descriptions. A later run exposed two setup defects: a schema import compiled the worker graph for 87.5 seconds, and an automatic cloud retry could acknowledge and clear recovery before reload. The schema now imports the same pure roster owner directly, and the test holds retry acknowledgments. Existing assertions remain intact.

prs.title: fix(runtime): Windows respawn reports wrong exit code for Ctrl-Break, sometimes wrong code for Ctrl-C/terminate too
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a respawned Gateway process on Windows is stopped via Ctrl-Break (SIGBREAK), the parent CLI reports a generic exit code of 1 instead of the conventional signal-based code, making it indistinguishable from an ordinary failure. Separately, the exit handler for this same code path has a latent double-exit bug that made it effectively untestable.

## User Impact

User impact: on Windows, scripts or tooling that inspect the OpenClaw CLI's exit code after a respawned Gateway is stopped via Ctrl-Break now see the conventional 149 (128+21) instead of a generic 1, matching how Ctrl-C (130) and terminate (143) already behave. No other user-visible change; this is diagnostic/scripting-surface behavior, not a functional regression fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runRespawnedChild`'s win32 exit handler in `node-runtime-recovery.mjs` mapped SIGINT->130 and SIGTERM->143 but left SIGBREAK (present in `respawnSignals` for win32) unmapped, falling through to a generic `process.exit(1)`. Added a SIGBREAK->149 branch to the same ternary.

While verifying this, found the win32 branch called `process.exit(forwardedSignalExitCode ?? 1)` without a `return`, so execution fell through to a second `process.exit(code ?? 1)` call further down the same handler. Harmless in real Node (process.exit halts synchronously) but made the exit-code-mapping logic impossible to unit test with a spy-style mock, which is why it shipped with zero coverage. Added the missing `return` and test coverage in a separate commit.

A subsequent review found the new test itself had a platform-portability bug: `respawnSignals` is a module-level constant computed from `process.platform` at import time, but the test imported the module statically before mocking the platform — so on a non-win32 CI host, the module would never register a SIGBREAK listener, failing the test and leaking listeners. Fixed by using `vi.resetModules()` + a dynamic import after mocking `process.platform`, so the module is always re-evaluated against the mocked win32 value regardless of the real host OS, with `afterEach` cleanup for any registered listeners.

## Evidence

- Added `src/infra/node-runtime-recovery.exit-code.test.ts`: mocks `process.exit` and `process.platform` (host-independently, via `vi.resetModules()` + dynamic import), fires SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGBREAK through the real exit handler, asserts it's called exactly once with 130/143/149 respectively.
- Confirmed red before the `return` fix (process.exit called twice, second call overriding with 1), green after:
```
✓ maps a forwarded win32 SIGINT to exit code 130 exactly once
✓ maps a forwarded win32 SIGTERM to exit code 143 exactly once
✓ maps a forwarded win32 SIGBREAK to exit code 149 exactly once
```
- Ran full `node-runtime-recovery.*.test.ts` suite: `shutdown.test.ts` (5/5) and the new `exit-code.test.ts` (3/3) fully pass; `node-runtime-recovery.test.ts` has 23 pre-existing unrelated failures from a broken `path.win32.relative` mock (confirmed identical failure count on the unmodified parent commit, not introduced by this change).
- Verified 128+21=149 against Node's actual `os.constants.signals.SIGBREAK` value (21) on a real Windows host.

**Real Windows proof (Ctrl-Break injected via `GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_BREAK_EVENT)` against the real `runRespawnedChild`, Windows 11, Node child with no signal handlers):**

Before this revision (SIGBREAK mapping keyed on `signal === firstForwardedSignal`):
```
+4005ms parent received SIGBREAK
+4020ms child.kill(SIGBREAK) -> true
+4026ms child exit code=null signal=SIGKILL
+4027ms process.exit(1)        # shell exit code 1
```
Windows reports a child terminated by a forwarded SIGBREAK as `SIGKILL`, not `SIGBREAK`, so the earlier mapping (and its unit test, which synthesized `exit(null, "SIGBREAK")`) never matched on a real host.

After (compare against the reported signal; SIGBREAK -> SIGKILL):
```
+4077ms child.kill(SIGBREAK) -> true
+4085ms child exit code=null signal=SIGKILL
+4085ms process.exit(149)      # shell exit code 149
```

The same mapping exists in `src/process/respawn-child-runner.ts`; it gets the identical change and a SIGBREAK case in its existing table test. The exit-code test now emits the signal Windows actually reports and removes every listener the supervisor registered, even when an assertion fails early.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): skip heartbeat turns for legacy docs-link boilerplate scratch
prs.body:
## What was wrong

Agents carrying the legacy monitor scratch template were running a heartbeat model turn on every interval, while sibling agents with comment-only scratch correctly skipped with `empty-heartbeat-file`.

The legacy template ends with a "Related" section whose only non-header line is a bare documentation link:

```markdown
## Related

- [Heartbeat config](/gateway/config-agents)
```

`isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty` already strips headers, HTML comments, fence markers and empty list stubs, but a list item holding just a doc link fell through every branch and counted as real content. So the shipped boilerplate alone was enough to trigger heartbeat turns and token spend, exactly the thing the template tells users it prevents.

## The fix

One narrow addition to the emptiness check in `src/auto-reply/heartbeat.ts`: list items whose entire content is a single bare documentation link (a relative docs path or an anchor target, like the legacy Related link) are now treated as boilerplate.

Deliberately conservative:
- Links with surrounding prose, multiple links, or external URL targets still count as content.
- Fenced content with a real task still counts as content.
- Missing scratch still returns false so the monitor can run.

## Proof

- Reproduced on current main first: the exact scaffold from the issue returned `false` (not empty) before the fix.
- `src/auto-reply/heartbeat.test.ts`: 39/39 pass, including 3 new regression cases (legacy scaffold, bare docs-link items, links that must still count as content). The related prompt tests were also exercised; an infra-level runner test errors on an unrelated missing `@openclaw/fs-safe/path` module in this environment, identically with and without the change.

Fixes #152916

prs.title: perf(agents): reuse stable tool factory schemas
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Unchanged agent runs rebuild and retain tool-schema publications because four factories return fresh parameter objects on every construction. Real asynchronous coding-tool assembly with 50 tools identifies repeat misses in `exec`, `view_image`, `video_generate`, and `intent`; the other 46 tools already reuse their descriptors, and output schemas do not churn in this fixture.

## User Impact

Reduces repeated tool preparation and descriptor retention without changing tool definitions, arguments, or execution authority. No configuration changes or migration. On the measured assembly, allocation falls **17.7%**, sampled surviving allocation falls **87.5%**, and warm publication/prewarm calls fall from **4 each per run to zero**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exec rebuilt its host-constrained schema and completion projection; image rebuilt its vision variant; video copied/deleted properties before rebuilding; intent created a fresh fixed object. The factories now reuse schemas for the inputs that determine their shape. Exec variants remain keyed by resolved host and sandbox availability, with separate continuation/completion shapes. Image keeps two vision variants, video keeps two reference-audio variants, and intent uses one constant. Execution closures remain per invocation. Finalization, publication, cache bounds, and authority checks are unchanged; no hashing or new finalizer cache.

Runtime production delta: **+30 lines across five files**. The growth preserves the existing typed exec schema API and distinct host/continuation contracts while moving completion projection to the same schema owner. Media/intent construction moves out of the repeated path. Optional factories outside this measured fixture are not changed here.

## Evidence

### Measurement

Five alternating baseline/candidate samples on Linux, **Node v26.12.1**, **63 new sessions per sample: 315 runs per side per measurement mode**. The fixture uses real asynchronous coding-tool assembly with bundled Memory/Qwen plugins, synthetic configuration/state, and no provider execution. Attribution also repeats each session once: **630 runs per side**. Allocation sampling includes collected objects; survivor sampling, exact coverage counts, and untraced CPU are separate passes. Acceptance was declared before measurement: identical tool/provider bytes and capability differences, zero warm publication for affected tools, and five samples.

The owner-only runs were serialized under the exclusive slot-B lock, alternated AB/BA order, and swapped interleaved CPU sets between pairs. Shared production guard remained enabled, without interruption. After the slot helper made no progress behind queued waiters, the runner used the same exclusive lock directly; no unlocked measurements. This is owner evidence, not a concurrent whole-Gateway comparison.

Baseline source: `ae180dc0ad665bf5e537c3ccb2918fe2416d93d3`. Only the five factory-owner files were alternately overlaid with baseline/candidate versions in the same source/dependency environment. Those baseline owner files are unchanged on the final rebased PR base; candidate production files are unchanged from the measured overlay.

| Metric per assembly run | Baseline mean [min, max] | Candidate mean [min, max] | Absolute mean delta | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Allocated KiB | 8,845.849 [8,828.831, 8,891.638] | 7,276.592 [7,266.092, 7,281.461] | −1,569.257 | −17.7% |
| Publication allocation, KiB | 172.515 [167.153, 186.475] | 0 | −172.515 | −100% |
| Prewarm allocation, KiB | 882.380 [870.898, 915.510] | 0 | −882.380 | −100% |
| Sampled surviving allocation, KiB | 51.855 [50.139, 53.278] | 6.482 [5.897, 7.132] | −45.373 | −87.5% |
| Publication survivors, KiB | 11.720 [11.590, 11.999] | 0 | −11.720 | −100% |
| Prewarm survivors, KiB | 22.808 [21.556, 23.789] | 0 | −22.808 | −100% |
| CPU, ms (untraced, context) | 14.669 [12.464, 16.774] | 10.836 [10.498, 11.480] | −3.833 | −26.1% |
| Wall time, ms (context) | 10.149 [8.372, 11.973] | 7.577 [7.277, 8.135] | −2.572 | −25.3% |

Signed net post-GC heap drift was +43.045 → −5.151 KiB/run. This noisy delta is context, not a claim of negative retained memory. Survivor rows above describe sampled allocations surviving forced GC. Natural GC cost, pauses, promotion, event-loop tails, and whole-Gateway throughput were **not measured**; no claims about those metrics.

| Exact owner work | Baseline | Candidate | Sample count |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Warm publication calls | 1,260 (4/run) | 0 | 5 × 63 new sessions |
| Warm schema prewarm calls | 1,260 (4/run) | 0 | 5 × 63 new sessions |
| Each affected tool: first-run publication misses | 315 | 0 | 5 × 63 new sessions/tool |
| Each affected tool: same-session repeat misses | 315 | 0 | 5 × 63 repeats/tool |
| Cold publication/prewarm calls | 71 / 50 | 71 / 50 | Identical in all 5 samples/side |

Allocation-profile sampled-object counts, baseline/candidate by pair: 501648/409869, 505600/410262, 502434/409963, 502067/409723, 502121/409133. Survivor-profile counts: 2523/156, 2504/139, 2405/128, 2374/116, 2451/126. Every pair improved allocation and survivors.

All five pairs had byte-identical tool definitions and serialized provider payloads. Responses with requested loose/strict options: 111,856 bytes; Anthropic: 112,028 bytes. This catalog's existing strict-compatibility policy resolves the requested-strict payload to `strict:false`, so those goldens do not claim all-strict catalog coverage. Variant tests separately preserve host, continuation, vision, and reference-audio schema differences.

Reproduction:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/finalized-tool-schemas-measure.ts \
  --factory assembly --sessions 63 --samples 1 \
  --output /path/to/report.json --golden-output /path/to/provider-json.json
```

### Proof and Review

Focused local proof: **167 tests across eight source test files**, plus **22 source-closure tests**, passed. Files: `bash-tools.exec-host-contract`, `bash-tools.descriptions`, `agent-tools.finalize`, `agent-tools.prefix-stability`, `image-tool`, `image-tool.custom-provider-auth.regression`, `video-generate-tool`, and `extensions/memory-core/index`; closure files: `eager-import-closure` and `pr-wrapper-source-closure`. New exec/media/intent regressions were red on baseline and green with the fix. Exec distinct schemas across three sessions × four variants: 12 → 4; media publication on repeated/new sessions: 6 → 0 per variant.

Export-name collision guard, changed-file formatting/lint, `git diff --check`, and targeted agents-tools test typecheck passed. No Testbox lease; broad validation is PR CI. Initial CI caught a test-only `TSchema.properties` type error, fixed using property matchers without casts. No CI reruns to chase green. A subsequent review correctly identified media-runtime imports in the generic finalizer suite; the finalizer file is restored to baseline and factory integration tests now live in existing media suites with explicit metadata fixtures. Relocated tests passed.

Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**, clean after the test fixes and relocation. Autoreview preflight refused the configured provider mismatch; operator configuration was not changed. Source review covered the full diff, finalizer, factory contracts, and measurement harness.

Final head: `6479f2c2b657286b2c9938db4f708c8a3fd0517d`. Exact-head CI: **passed**, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40133198867. The latest automated Codex review also completed with no findings on this exact head; ClawSweeper re-review was requested after the fixes and completed evidence were posted.

## Deployment Signal and Limits

In the next production survivor profile, repeated `retireToolGeneration → publishParameters/prewarmOpenAISchema` allocations should disappear for these four unchanged tool shapes. Cold starts and genuine shape changes must still publish. This fixture does not cover every optional plugin/tool mode, and owner savings are not an estimate of whole-turn or Gateway savings.

**Ready for lead review; leave open. The lead owns merge.**

prs.title: fix: validate dynamic schemas without code generation in AOT builds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes dynamic MCP schema validation depending on runtime JavaScript generation in AOT standalone hosts, and avoids generating unused checker source for plugin configuration and tool arguments in those hosts.

## User Impact

Node, Bun and JIT standalone hosts keep their compiled validators. AOT hosts select a code-generation-free checker at each existing validation owner. MCP schemas retain draft-07/draft-2020-12 behavior, known-format policy, registered resources, relative references, encoded pointers and per-provider isolation. References identify schema resources and never trigger network requests.

AOT MCP validation requires actual input properties for `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype`; inherited JavaScript prototype members do not satisfy those requirements. This accounts for five documented legacy corpus differences. No new setting or dependency is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

AOT is a runtime profile, not a reason to slow down ordinary Node/Bun validation. The existing owners select their engine once when preparing a validator and retain their caches, defaults, coercion and diagnostics. A small shared walker owns fresh per-value evaluation state; MCP resource preparation owns reference registration and dialect normalization.

The runtime-profile fact moves to a bootstrap-only module, reexported by the diagnostic owner. Reading the executing image's compiler-installed fact avoids pulling CLI filesystem discovery into validation. Build/sidecar diagnostics retain their existing owner. This preserves the AOT plugin, Code Mode and QA execution enabled by #182818, including its once-per-feature notices and actual-error guidance. The standalone builder already sets Zod jitless before schema creation; that ordering is preserved. The proposed bundled-plugin static registry was dropped because it failed the startup budget.

## Evidence

- Initial CI caught two metadata omissions: the new root module was missing from the duplicate-scan inventory, and the shortened helper retained a stale max-lines exception. The two-line repair adds scan coverage and removes the exception; both original failing guard entrypoints now pass. No runtime behavior or test threshold changes.
- After integration with the runtime-profile owner, 112 selected owner/caller tests passed in 93.39s, including real Node Code Mode, fetched CJS/TypeScript plugins and QA expressions. The AOT probe closure has 777 unchanged executable inputs (one removed lint comment); the compiled proof below remains applicable.
- 145 owning/sibling tests passed in 17.73s with `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`; 29 MCP caller tests passed in 66.08s. After extracting unchanged keyword helpers, 77 affected tests passed in 8.71s. Both profiles cover code-generation denial, references, formats/defaults, coercion and independent cached checks.
- Actual MCP-owner corpus: 1,696 matching draft-07 outcomes plus the five prototype-policy differences above, and 1,246 matching draft-2020-12 outcomes. No additional candidate setup failures. Unsupported/unregistered external-resource groups remain outside the synchronous provider contract.
- Final-source small AOT probes (under 0.9 MB emitted JS): candidate passes all 11 fixture groups with zero Function-constructor calls both normally and with string code generation denied. Baseline passes 9/11 normally (18 Function calls) and 4/11 when hardened (7 calls). Includes legacy anchors, ambiguous IDs, resource replacement, encoded references, plugin defaults and tool coercion. No full-application AOT build or interpreter-tripwire claim.
- Targeted core/script/test/QA types, type-aware source/test lint and format pass after profile integration. Earlier unchanged-input wrapper-import closure and assertion/file-size ratchets passed; fresh Codex review covers the final implementation. prs.title: fix(doctor): explain database port credential mismatch
prs.body:
Closes #182773

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw database port --dry-run` reports an opaque `validation or I/O failure` when the local client credential receipt is bound to a different shared database file, and then suggests `--resume/--rollback` even when no recovery manifest exists.

## User Impact

Operators now see the failed fact (a credential receipt bound to another shared database file), the supported repair (`openclaw backup restore`), and only advice that applies to the current run. A preflight dry run no longer tells an offline operator to stop a Gateway or use a recovery manifest it did not create.

## Why This Change Was Made

The credential mismatch is now a typed error consumed by the database-port refusal owner instead of falling through to the catch-all as an unknown I/O failure. Refusal guidance now depends on whether a Gateway was observed and whether a recovery manifest actually exists. Unexpected failures still use the existing redacted-code path.

## Evidence

New regression in `src/infra/database-engine/port-command.credentials-local.test.ts` enters through `doctorDatabasePort({ family: "state", dryRun: true })`, corrupts only the local receipt's shared-file identity, and asserts the actionable message without changing either database.

Base-red on unmodified sources:

```text
Received: "... observed validation or I/O failure; required successful verified phase; preserve the recovery directory. Stop the Gateway first; correct this fact and retry, or use --resume/--rollback with .../manifest.json."
Expected: /local credential receipt bound to a different shared database file.*openclaw backup restore/u
Tests  1 failed | 3 passed (4)
```

With the fix:

```text
✓ database port local credential ownership (4 tests)
✓ database-port admission and existing doctor database-port tests (17 tests)
Test Files  3 passed (3)
```

### Shipped CLI proof

The current branch was run through `src/entry.ts` by invoking the real command below against an isolated state directory:

```text
openclaw database port --family state --to sqlite --dry-run
```

The local credential receipt was changed only in its recorded shared-file identity. Both database files remained byte-identical, and no recovery manifest existed:

```json
{
  "entrypoint": "openclaw database port --family state --to sqlite --dry-run",
  "exitCode": 1,
  "message": "Database port preflight: .../matrix/accounts/active/matrix.example__user/0123456789abcdef/client/credentials.sqlite; observed local credential receipt bound to a different shared database file; required a receipt matching this shared database; restore the archive with openclaw backup restore. Correct this fact and retry.",
  "filesByteIdentical": true,
  "recoveryManifestCreated": false,
  "misleadingFatalIoCopied": false,
  "misleadingRecoveryAdviceCopied": false,
  "misleadingGatewayAdviceCopied": false
}
```

After creating the actual recovery manifest, the same shipped command retained manifest-dependent recovery guidance:

```json
{
  "manifestGuidance": {
    "exitCode": 1,
    "resumeOrRollbackAdvicePresent": true,
    "output": "Database port preflight: .../openclaw.json; observed OWNER_UNAVAILABLE; required successful verified phase; preserve the recovery directory. Correct this fact and retry, or use --resume/--rollback with .../recovery/database-port/manifest.json."
  }
}
```

The full captured output is in `cli-mismatch.log`. The branch was also updated from base `4f66fa40729e` (merge commit `947e23e8b`). After the merge, the focused regression suite passed 14 tests across 3 files (`port-command.credentials-local.test.ts`, `doctor-database-port.test.ts`, and `doctor-database-port-memory.test.ts`).

Formatting, targeted `oxlint`, `git diff --check`, and all `check:changed` gates that can run in this host passed. `check:changed` cannot run `tsgo` on this host because its bundled binary requires glibc >= 2.29 while the host provides 2.28; the dead-export lane also reports the repository-wide existing baseline. The PostgreSQL-gated credential integration test was updated but not executed because no PostgreSQL DSN is available in this environment.

issues.title: Add OS-level sandboxing for tool execution via sandlock
issues.body:
## Problem

Nanobot gives the LLM full shell execution and filesystem access via `ExecTool`. The current security model relies on regex-based command blocking (9 deny patterns) and string-level path checks (`restrict_to_workspace`). These are bypassable — encoding tricks, aliases, scripting languages, or indirect execution can evade pattern matching. There is no kernel-level enforcement.

This matters because:
- LLM-driven execution is inherently unpredictable — the model decides what commands to run
- External web content fetched as context creates prompt injection risk
- Subagents and MCP server tools expand the attack surface
- A single bypass means full access as the nanobot user

## Proposal

Integrate [sandlock](https://github.com/multikernel/sandlock) — a lightweight Linux process sandbox that uses Landlock, seccomp-bpf, and user namespaces to confine processes without root or containers.

Sandlock would add kernel-enforced boundaries to each tool execution:

| Current defense | Sandlock addition |
|---|---|
| Regex command deny-list | seccomp-bpf syscall filtering at kernel level |
| String path checks | Landlock filesystem whitelisting (read-only / read-write paths) |
| No network restrictions | TCP port + domain allowlisting |
| No resource limits | Memory, process count, CPU, open file caps |
| No privilege escalation defense | User namespace confinement |

### Integration points

1. **`ExecTool` (`agent/tools/shell.py`)** — wrap `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell()` in a sandlock sandbox with per-execution filesystem + network + syscall policy
2. **Subagent spawning** — each subagent inherits sandbox constraints via sandlock's per-PID policy propagation
3. **MCP tool execution** — sandbox MCP server processes independently
4. **Cron tasks** — scheduled tasks run confined by default

### Characteristics that make this a good fit

- **No root required** : runs as the nanobot user
- **~20ms startup overhead** : negligible vs LLM inference latency
- **Python API** : `pip install sandlock`, simple decorator or context manager
- **Per-process granularity** :  each tool call gets its own sandbox
- **Linux-only** :  matches nanobot's primary platform; Docker users on macOS/Windows get it for free inside the container

### Example usage

```python
from sandlock import Sandbox

sandbox = Sandbox(
    fs_read=["/workspace", "/usr/lib", "/usr/bin"],
    fs_write=["/workspace/output"],
    net_allow=["api.example.com:443"],
    max_memory_mb=512,
    max_procs=10,
)

result = sandbox.run(["bash", "-c", user_command])
```

## Alternatives considered

- **Docker per-execution** — too slow (~200ms+ startup per tool call) and heavy
- **firejail** — requires root or setuid binary
- **bubblewrap (bwrap)** — viable but lower-level; no Python API, no resource limits without cgroups
- **Regex hardening** — fundamentally flawed as a security boundary (deny-list vs allow-list)

## References

- [sandlock GitHub](https://github.com/multikernel/sandlock)
- [Landlock LSM](https://landlock.io/)
- [seccomp-bpf](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/userspace-api/seccomp_filter.html)

issues.title: web_search (ddgs): ambiguous failures look like empty results

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

With the default search provider (DuckDuckGo, no API key), consecutive web_search calls in the same turn fail with an error that reads like an empty result set:
  Error: DuckDuckGo search failed (No results found.)

The original report observed that spacing the same distinct queries correlated with recovery. Follow-up diagnostics on the original host observed an explicit Mojeek HTTP 403 refusal, then intentionally stopped the remaining requests. These observations do not establish that every `No results found` exception is rate limiting, or that retry/backoff is the root-cause fix. ddgs can hide upstream refusal, empty parsing and aggregation failures behind that generic exception. The agreed nanobot-side resolution is to report search unavailability and uncertainty honestly, rather than interpret the exception as a completed search with zero matches.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Keep the default provider (tools.web.search.provider = "duckduckgo", empty api_key), no proxy.
2. In one turn, issue several distinct web_search calls with no pause between them (a normal multi-query research turn does this).
3. Observe that a subset of the calls fail with the "No results found" error; repeating the same queries with a pause succeeds.

Isolated library repro (no nanobot involved), same host:
  from ddgs import DDGS
  qs = ["capa galaxy a12 preco", "fone bluetooth barato", "notebook i5 usado", "cadeira gamer preco",
        "tenis corrida promocao", "panela eletrica preco", "mochila escolar", "lampada led preco"]
  d = DDGS(timeout=15)
  # no pause -> 0/8 results, all DDGSException: No results found
  # 3 s pause between queries -> 8/8 results

### Agreed acceptance criteria

- Return ambiguous ddgs failures as tool errors that explicitly say no usable search result was obtained and the cause is unknown. Do not present them as confirmed zero matches or infer rate limiting from `No results found`.
- Distinguish the tool's waiting deadline from a timeout reported by ddgs.
- Preserve successful result formatting, the configured network route, cancellation and existing diagnostic privacy behavior.
- Verify through a normal public entrypoint with a real model: live search succeeds and uses returned sources; controlled refusal and timeout cases report the failed lookup without claiming that matching pages do not exist or inventing sources.

### Outside this issue

- Removing upstream rate limits, IP restrictions or anti-automation blocks.
- Adding automatic retry, backoff or pacing configuration. These are not required for this issue's resolution.
- Recovering HTTP refusal/rate-limit facts already discarded by ddgs. Upstream error preservation and any later nanobot integration are separate follow-up work. Related upstream report: https://github.com/deedy5/ddgs/issues/478.

### Resolution

PR #6409 resolves the agreed nanobot-side scope when merged. This scope supersedes the original retry-based proposal; the original reproduction steps, measurements and environment are retained in this issue as reported evidence, not proof that every failure has the same cause.

### Relevant Logs

```shell
Two calls issued in the same second, then the failure (Telegram turn, 17/10/2026):
2026-10-17 21:32:33 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"query": "REDACTED_QUERY", "count": 8})
2026-10-17 21:32:33 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"query": "REDACTED_QUERY", "count": 8})
2026-10-17 21:32:44 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"count": 6, "query": "REDACTED_QUERY"})
2026-10-17 21:32:50 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.
2026-10-17 21:32:54 | INFO  | - | Tool call: web_search({"count": 6, "query": "REDACTED_QUERY"})
2026-10-17 21:33:40 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.
2026-10-17 21:33:51 | WARNING | - | DuckDuckGo search failed: No results found.

Additional measurements
- 8 distinct queries with no pause: 0/8 returned results (all DDGSException: No results found).
- The same 8 queries with a 3 s pause: 8/8 succeeded.
- The host recovers after idling, and a second host on a different IP served results while the first was failing — transient and rate/IP dependent, not a permanent block.
- exclusive=True only keeps DuckDuckGo out of the parallel batch; it does not pace calls, so consecutive searches still go out immediately.
- The per-turn guard in utils/runtime.py (_MAX_REPEAT_EXTERNAL_LOOKUPS = 2) only blocks repeating the same query or URL, so it does not help with distinct queries.
- ddgs 9.16.0 itself has no retry/backoff (checked its sources).
- Checked todays `main`: _search_duckduckgo is unchanged there.
```

### nanobot Version

0.3.5

### Python Version

3.14.4

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, aarch64 (Oracle Cloud VM, kernel 7.0.0-1013-oracle)

### Channel / Platform

Telegram (headless, systemd service)

opencode

deepseek-v4.1-flash

### Browser

N/A — headless VPS, no browser involved

### Connection

Direct outbound HTTPS from the host, no proxy (tools.web.proxy unset), datacenter IP

### Configuration (Optional)

```yaml

```

issues.title: feat(privacy): reversible PII de-identification at the provider boundary (distinct from secret redaction)
issues.body:
## Problem statement

Two different problems are currently conflated under "redaction":

1. **Secret redaction (lossy, one-way).** Drop or mask API keys/tokens before they reach the model or the logs. This is what the open PRs #1249, #1305, #1513, #1812 all implement. All four are still open and have had no maintainer engagement since 2026-08-16.
2. **PII de-identification (reversible).** For a *personal assistant*, the sensitive payload is mostly not credentials — it is third-party personal data: contact names, phone numbers, street addresses, order/contract numbers, and other participants in group chats. This data must stay **usable by the model** while never leaving the host in plaintext. One-way masking destroys the value (the agent can no longer reason about "the person" or produce a usable draft reply), and deleting it after the fact does not help, because the value already left the machine.

nanobot's memory model makes case (2) sharper than in a chatbot:

- conversation summaries are appended to `memory/history.jsonl`;
- Dream consolidates them into `SOUL.md` / `USER.md` / `memory/MEMORY.md`;
- those durable files are fed back into the system context **every turn**.

So a single leaked identifier does not stay in one turn — it gets consolidated, versioned in GitStore, and re-sent to the provider indefinitely.

## Proposed design

A config-driven, **reversible** de-identification filter at the provider boundary:

1. **Policy** — entity classes (person name, phone, email, postal address, national ID, plus user-supplied regex), and scope flags so each surface can be filtered independently: `llm_egress`, `persistence` (session store / history.jsonl / durable memory files), `tool_output`, `logs`.
2. **Deterministic reversible map** — `Alice <phone> → PERSON_7f3a1c / PHONE_7f3a1c`, stable within a scope so the model can still track that two mentions refer to the same entity. The map store lives **outside the agent-readable workspace** (same placement principle already used for `sessions/<workspace-id>/sessions.sqlite3`) with `0600` permissions, and is never sent anywhere.
3. **Restore on the return path** — model output and any persisted artifact are mapped back, so the user always sees real values. Only the placeholder form crosses the network.
4. **Fail-closed option** — if the map store is unavailable, block egress rather than silently sending plaintext.
5. **Zero-loss constraint** — masking must never drop or re-serialize content. Existing explicit truncation markers (read/grep/exec) must survive untouched; the filter is a pure token-for-token text substitution with no compression.
6. **Auditability** — per-turn counter of substituted/restored spans, so a user can verify the filter actually ran instead of trusting a "I understood your preference"-style claim.

## Where it needs to hook (the real blocker)

We run a private in-tree patch for this today, and the reason it has to be a patch is that there is currently no supported extension point for it:

- an **outbound** text transform over request messages (including tool results before they are persisted), and
- an **inbound** inverse transform over assistant text before it is persisted or delivered to a channel.

`nanobot/agent/plugins.py` covers skills/MCP packaging. `agent/hook.py` already offers useful seams — `finalize_content(context, content) -> str | None` for assistant output and `after_execute_tool(...)` for tool results — which covers roughly half of what is needed. What is missing is the symmetric pair:

- no hook sees the **outbound request messages** (prior turns + tool results) before they are handed to the provider, which is exactly where de-identification has to happen;
- no hook sits on the **persistence boundary** (session store, `memory/history.jsonl`, durable memory files), so filtered text and stored text cannot be kept consistent.

Hooks are also in-process code rather than something an installed Agent Plugin package can register today.

**Question for maintainers:** would you rather see this as core config (a `privacy` section next to `tools`/`gateway`), or as an Agent Plugin with two new hook points added? We are happy to build either.

## Suggested consolidation

The four open PRs would land more cleanly if unified under one **egress filter contract** with two filter kinds sharing the same plumbing:

| kind | direction | use |
|------|-----------|-----|
| `redact` | one-way, lossy | credentials, tokens (PRs #1249 / #1305 / #1513 / #1812) |
| `deidentify` | two-way, reversible | third-party PII in personal-assistant workloads (this request) |

## Willingness to contribute

We operate this in production as a private patch and would like to upstream it — as core config or as an agent plugin, whichever the maintainers prefer. Happy to open the PR if the shape above is acceptable.

issues.title: API session lock registry grows without bound for completed sessions
issues.body:
## Bug
The OpenAI-compatible API stores one `asyncio.Lock` per user supplied `session_id` in a regular dictionary. Completed sessions are never removed, so sending requests with many distinct session IDs grows the API process memory indefinitely.

## Reproduction
1. Start the API server.
2. Send one successful request to `/v1/chat/completions` for each of many unique `session_id` values.
3. Inspect the app's session lock registry: it retains one lock for every completed session.

## Expected behavior
Locks should remain available while requests for a session are active or waiting, then become reclaimable after the session's requests finish.

## Proposed fix
Store the locks in a weak-value registry, matching the existing AgentLoop session-lock lifecycle. Add a regression test that completes a request and verifies its lock is not retained.

prs.title: fix(tools): edit text files marked with a byte-order mark
prs.body:
## Summary
`edit_file` and `apply_patch` decoded every existing file as UTF-8. A UTF-16 or UTF-32 file that `read_file` opens failed before the replacement, with a decode error or `file is not UTF-8 text`.

Decode a leading byte-order mark and write the edited text back with the codec that preserves that mark. Files without a mark stay UTF-8, and a file that is not valid text still fails with the same error.

## Test
On base `3bd6725`:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_filesystem_tools.py::TestEditFileTool::test_bom_marked_unicode_text_keeps_its_encoding tests/tools/test_apply_patch_tool.py::test_apply_patch_updates_bom_marked_unicode_text -q --tb=line
```

Before: 4 failed. UTF-16 and UTF-32 were rejected by both tools. `edit_file` returned `'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte`. `apply_patch` returned `file is not UTF-8 text`.

After `9481f2a39a915f4fa5ac98a0f882ba4b061249de`: 4 passed. The saved bytes still start with the original mark and decode to the edited text. `tests/tools/test_filesystem_tools.py`, `tests/tools/test_apply_patch_tool.py`, `tests/tools/test_edit_advanced.py`, and `tests/tools/test_read_enhancements.py`: 174 passed.

prs.title: fix(grep): search text declared by a byte-order mark
prs.body:
## Summary
Grep treated UTF-16 and UTF-32 text as binary because those encodings contain NUL bytes, and it left a UTF-8 byte-order mark on the first line. `read_file` already decodes all three, so an anchored search such as `^Hello` found nothing in a file the user could read.

Decode a leading byte-order mark before the binary check. Invalid marked bytes are still skipped. Plain UTF-8 and real binary files are unchanged.

## Test
On base `3bd6725`:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_search_tools.py::test_grep_searches_bom_marked_unicode_text -q --tb=line
```

Before: 3 failed (`utf-8-sig`, `utf-16`, `utf-32`). Each reported no matches for `^Hello`; UTF-16 and UTF-32 also reported a skipped binary file.

After `7341ccc7a067f01330274796973f3fe91c8c5db0`: 3 passed. `tests/tools/test_search_tools.py`: 87 passed.

prs.title: feat(webui): add session-scoped reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Why

Tracking: [NAN-355](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-355).

Choose reasoning effort for the next message in one conversation without opening settings, modifying a shared preset, or changing a task that is already running. A click should not create a conversation or synchronize a separate server-side setting.

## What changed

- Reuse the preset editor's existing model catalog and recommendation helper. Chat offers click-only choices; there is no second capability policy or free-text field.
- Update the browser preference immediately and coalesce browser-storage writes for 250 ms. Sending takes the latest value synchronously, without a reasoning save request, acknowledgement, or first-message save barrier.
- Carry the optional effort in the ordinary message. The existing trusted WebUI admission transaction remembers the last-used value in session metadata; execution derives an independent generation snapshot. Preset changes clear the override. Shell/restart/other non-generating control commands retain their existing behavior.
- Remove the dedicated reasoning service, HTTP read/mutation, WebSocket settings action, scope/config signature, and prototype session-header API. Drop the shared segmented control's now-unused pending-save extension.
- Preserve the accepted compact menu, neutral provider icons, selected-row shading/shadow, aligned control edges, inset corners, and narrow-screen touch targets.

## Scope

A selected-but-unsent preference belongs to this browser. The last-used value is saved only with ordinary message admission, and is restored through the existing session list/attach projection after a Gateway restart. No config/preset write, new lock or settings synchronization subsystem is added. The optional `webui.reasoning-effort.v1` flag advertises message support to the UI; temporary chats do not expose this shortcut.

Omitted message effort preserves the saved session/preset value; explicit null follows the preset; native `none` remains a string. The gateway validates trusted generating input, rather than treating the recommendation list as a new authorization or provider-compatibility policy. Existing authentication and temporary-chat ownership checks remain in place.

## Tradeoffs

Recommendations intentionally match the preset editor, including its fallback recommendations. They are not real-generation capability probes or a guarantee that every upstream API accepts each value or gives it a distinct meaning. Existing provider serialization and request-body precedence are unchanged. Unreleased prototype hash-dict session metadata is not migrated.

## Blast Radius

The existing WebUI message admission and per-execution generation snapshot; existing session metadata/list/attach projection; model-menu local preference, first-message transfer, and send options. Regression checks cover token renewal, session/host isolation, preserving a newer target choice, preset switching, and ordinary shell/restart controls. No execution lifecycle, queue architecture, provider protocol, TUI, or deployment redesign is included.

## Verification

- Backend: 223 targeted mock/temporary-data tests passed; touched Ruff and import boundaries passed. The tested backend patch hash was checked against the final candidate.
- Frontend: final hook/menu/segmented-control/thread-shell set passed (135 tests), plus targeted transport, attachment, composer/model-menu tests and the preset-picker recommendation case. Overlapping test runs are not summed. TypeScript, touched ESLint, independent production build, and diff check passed.
- Isolated real Gateway + Chromium + loopback fake provider: clicking on a blank topic did not mutate session/config or send a settings action; latest effort reached the first model request; assistant responses and explicit turn-end events were persisted; another topic remained unchanged; in-flight effort stayed fixed; queued editing/resending and cancellation used the expected values; actual Gateway process restarts preserved both browser-local unsent choice and session last-used choice in a fresh browser. Desktop/320px, light/dark geometry checks confirmed aligned edges and 44px narrow-screen targets.
- Build assets and HOME/config/workspace/sessions were independent. Config bytes stayed unchanged; no real model, credential, daily instance, or handed-off preview was used or operated.
- Follow-up HEAD: `2fa444817f8232fec1b8bd706aeb5eb90f508b35` (normal commit/push). GitHub currently reports this Draft PR as `CONFLICTING` / `DIRTY`; the new head has no check rollup or workflow run. Exact-head remote CI is therefore not verified. No rebase, force-push, or base-merge was performed without authorization.

## Verification limits

Real providers, Safari, physical devices, and a full local suite were not tested. Very early Escape during menu opening was timing-sensitive in initial browser attempts; its cause is not established. Loaded-menu checks wait for the ordinary lazy catalog response and pass; no speculative Escape fallback was added. This remains a Draft PR, not an approval, Ready transition, merge, or deployment.

prs.title: fix(webui): show channel pairing prompts without polling delay
prs.body:
Related: [NAN-339](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-339)

## Why

A channel pairing request created just after an empty WebUI read could wait almost the entire 15-second polling interval before its prompt appeared. This PR fixes that existing pairing delay; it is not a new pairing feature or a general WebUI state-refresh/performance refactor.

## Changes

- Notify only authenticated WebUI connections when pending pairing requests change. The payload-free `pairing_changed` event contains no codes, sender identities or secrets; the existing HTTP snapshot and approval/denial checks remain authoritative.
- Replace only the pairing poll with initial and change-triggered reads. Keep serialized/coalesced reads, bounded retries, cancellation/deadlines through response-body consumption, foreground/reconnect recovery, approval, dismissal, snooze and expiry countdowns. Reconcile after pairing actions so a late mutation reply cannot leave a newer request hidden.
- Limit the gateway source to one non-recursive pairing-parent watch and pending expiration deadlines, including first creation, atomic replacement and another process's writes, watch recovery and joined shutdown.

## Documentation

Pairing already has usage instructions. Remove the new standalone implementation page and its WebUI README link, and remove the user-guide introduction promoting refresh behavior. The user guide and WebUI README now match the rebased main exactly. Retain only the event payload, authenticated audience, authoritative HTTP snapshot, initial/reconnect recovery and one real filesystem prerequisite in the existing [WebSocket protocol reference](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/9b68d7b7efd66d689428e4489a0a262071092df4/docs/websocket.md#wire-protocol).

## Scope and limits

Automations, Channels/feature summaries, Overview usage and remote-directory refresh retain the rebased main behavior. No generic resource-refresh framework, remote-health sampler or usage observer remains in this PR. The response-body lifetime helper is used only by pairing; other API reads retain their existing lifetime and share only the unchanged JSON parser. Agent execution, channel delivery, authentication and pairing authorization/persistence are unchanged.

WebUI and its Gateway are used as a paired release. The WebUI listener requires filesystem change-notification support in the instance data directory. This is a pairing responsiveness fix, not a claim about overall CPU, memory, energy or model latency.

## Verification

Candidate: `9b68d7b7efd66d689428e4489a0a262071092df4`, rebased onto main `3bd67254ba87555edbee4b1f3a47589fb75daf0b`. Git completed the rebase without textual conflicts; the twelve existing commits remained patch-equivalent in range-diff. A follow-up documentation-only commit removes the unnecessary material. The final PR diff has 21 paths. Publication used an explicit lease on the previous remote head.

- **Fresh production acceptance after rebase:** real isolated CLI Gateway and production WebUI, authenticated loopback, fresh HOME/config/workspace, fake local channel identities and a separate-process writer. After the initial empty read, write a request about one second later: writer commit to component-visible was **105 ms at 1440px** and **94 ms at 390px**. These are local samples, not percentiles or cross-platform guarantees; they do not include completion of the existing 200ms fade. The earlier original-base reproduction measured 13,848 ms; that historical baseline was not rerun for this rebase.
- The same fresh candidate passed real eight-second expiry, code entry through authenticated approval with persisted sender approval, actual WebSocket disconnect/reconnect recovering a missed request while retaining the draft, and another process denying a visible request. Frames contain only the event name. Bootstrap became ready while unrelated sibling writes continued every 50ms. All 1,093 captured Python/runtime-asset hashes matched the candidate content; independent checks confirmed cleanup of owned PIDs and ports.
- **Python:** 338 pairing/store/lifecycle/integration and original WebSocket channel checks passed. Scoped Ruff, BasedPyright and import-boundary checks passed.
- **Frontend:** full coverage suite **3,365 tests in 190 files passed**; statements/lines 94.20%, branches 88.93%, functions 91.76%. TypeScript, full ESLint, client import boundaries and production build passed. The build retains the existing large-chunk warning.
- **Complete local browser:** **304 passed, 1 failed**. The 360px `mobile-chat-layout.spec.ts:31` Context sheet remained open after a single Escape. Its log, screenshot and context are retained and inspected; the cause remains unconfirmed. The corresponding test, fixture and component paths are unchanged from the fetched main. prs.title: feat(webui): keep delegated work within reach
prs.body:
## Summary

Long replies push running delegated work out of reach, but keeping every finished task permanently above the composer would create another growing backlog. This iteration gives live work and saved results different homes.

- Keep a fixed **Subtasks** entry above the composer for queued, running, and stopping tasks. Desktop opens an upward, height-bounded popover; narrow screens use a bottom sheet. Each list scrolls independently of the conversation.
- Remove the old inline live-task panel. Terminal outcomes become compact, default-collapsed result records at their originating request and naturally scroll away with the conversation. Unmatched history remains available under **Other tasks**.
- When the live list is closed, partially completed tasks leave it; once all observed work ends, a truthful completion/failure receipt retires after four seconds. Focus, hover, open-list reading, and details pause retirement. Cold reload does not resurrect old completion receipts.
- Keep rows stable while the list is open, including outcomes arriving during reading and newly recovered active work. Closing prunes finished rows; if no work remains, focus returns to the composer. Real new input clears old closed receipts without hiding tasks still running across turns.
- Preserve full task conversation/details, per-task cancellation, saved history, revision ordering, reconnect, and pane/session boundaries. Parent response completion does not hide active child work.
- Reuse the shared loading ring and restrained reduced-motion-aware transitions. Separate archive/list focus registrations; preserve detail handoff across breakpoint changes and source relocation. Bounded plain-text excerpts stay non-interactive; full Markdown remains in details.

## Scope

Frontend presentation only: no gateway execution, authentication, task persistence, wire protocol, or cancellation contract changes. The PR stays Draft for UX feedback; it is not a new global task-monitoring page.

## Verification

- Focused Vitest: **333 passed** across task lifecycle, result archives, ThreadShell, ThreadViewport, ThreadMessages, thread motion, and PaneWorkbench.
- Playwright: **33 passed** across the task Dock and existing history-boundary flows. Coverage includes desktop/mobile reachability, list-scroll isolation, completion retirement, cold reload, cross-turn active work, reading-position stability, detail/focus handoff, outside-click editing, portal/session visibility, reduced motion, breakpoint changes, and a shortened visual viewport.
- Application/browser TypeScript checks, ESLint, client import-boundary checks, production build, and `git diff --check` passed. Import checker tests: **41 passed, 1 Windows-only case skipped on Linux**. The production build retains its large-chunk advisory.
- Built WebUI checked through an already-running isolated authenticated Gateway using a local fake model and real task executions: cancel one task without stopping the other two; preserve a completed list/detail while reading; close back to the composer; verify terminal records and refresh without a resurrected Dock. No browser page errors. Gateway-served entry assets match the local build; no Gateway/mock restart or daily-instance operation.

These are scoped local checks, not a claim of a complete local suite, real-device/Safari/native keyboard acceptance, or remote CI success. Remote checks are evaluated against the latest pushed commit. The isolated preview uses fictional sessions and local fake credentials, not real user history or paid model calls.

## Why

Chinese labels without spaces should wrap instead of stretching Mermaid diagrams, and generic text such as `List<T>` must remain intact. Upgrade both clients from Pele 1.6.0 to 1.9.0 to pick up these fixes and upstream layout improvements; a version-only bump would reject the new subscript, superscript and underline styles and fall back to source.

## What changed

- Pin Pele 1.9.0 in both clients, with matching Bun/npm locks, notices and relinking reference. No unrelated dependency changes.
- Measure the new native styles consistently. WebUI accepts only Pele's measured script-span attributes; TUI converts smaller/shifted glyphs and underlines into bounded vector geometry before rasterization.
- Cover real-engine mixed text, Chinese wrapping, generic text, browser image decoding and isolated-font raster parity.

## Scope

Tracks [NAN-354](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-354). No math resolver, inline SVG mounting, model calls, protocol changes, or runtime/service rollout. Worker/subprocess isolation, resource limits, external-resource rejection and missing-glyph behavior remain in place.

## Blast Radius

Both clients' Mermaid rendering and TUI standalone assets. Text metrics and vector conversion are the main regression risks; the tests exercise script sizing/baselines, underline pixels, existing font styles and forbidden author typography/resources.

## Verification

With Bun **1.3.13** and both resolved Pele packages **1.9.0**:

- WebUI focused units: **58 passed**; diagram browser suite: **8 passed**, including desktop/narrow and light/dark mixed-style/CJK rendering.
- WebUI typecheck, browser TypeScript, lint, import boundaries/checker tests and production build passed.
- Built WebUI through an isolated real gateway: mixed styles, source/viewer, reload plus canonical history replay, narrow layout and no page errors passed.
- Full TUI suite: **292 passed, 13 skipped, 0 failed**; typecheck, import boundaries/checker tests and POSIX PTY smoke passed. The skips include existing platform-specific cases.
- Linux x64 standalone and release notices built: **128,846,144 bytes**, within the unchanged **135 MiB** executable budget. Pele 1.9.0 is present in generated notices.
- Real WezTerm: reproduced the version-only failure, then verified source and standalone image rendering, Ctrl+G viewer, zoom/fit, back navigation and editable input. Independent Microsoft YaHei CJK flowchart/sequence/state raster probes passed; native-text versus outline probes matched with DejaVu and YaHei.
- All fixtures and services were isolated; owned test processes and ports were cleaned up. Native Windows/macOS execution and remote CI are not claimed by these local checks. Existing non-Pele npm audit findings are outside this dependency-only upgrade.

### Visual evidence

Built-WebUI and real-WezTerm standalone screenshots, using fictitious data, are attached to [NAN-354](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-354). They require workspace access; private Linear image URLs are intentionally not embedded here.

prs.title: refactor(webui): unify code and diff highlighting
prs.body:
## Why

Replace the WebUI's separate Prism code/preview/diff paths with shared highlighting while preserving the existing reading and file-change workflows. This also restores the earlier single-conversation preview layout: messages and Composer stay together in the left column, with the file preview filling the right column.

## What changed

- Replace `react-syntax-highlighter`/Prism with shared Highlights tokens and CSS-variable colors. Load Shiki only for grammars absent from Highlights; render source through React text/spans and preserve complete preview text, native find/selection, copy, ANSI, streaming settlement, wrapping, line numbers, themes and reading sizes.
- Render each complete read-only file diff through one Pierre instance, with bounded metadata/AST caches and a render window read from the existing chat scroller. Preserve file summaries, line limits, expansion/collapse, hunk gaps, truncation notices and local previews.
- Keep the single-conversation Composer inside its conversation column. Actual multi-pane tabs retain the shared footer, including compact rendering. Update both lockfiles, lazy-chunk guards, dependency notices and behavioral tests.

## Scope

WebUI only. No backend, TUI, provider, protocol or persistence-format changes; no patch editing/applying, new scroller ownership or bottom-mask removal. Uses pinned `@pierre/diffs` 1.6.1, `@pierre/highlights` 0.2.0 and Shiki 4.5.0.

## Tracking

Related: [NAN-343 — 统一 WebUI 代码与只读 diff 高亮，保留源码操作及侧栏布局](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-343).

## Tradeoffs

**Draft: large-diff scrolling and first-use transfer tradeoffs have not been remeasured after the fixes below.** This is not presented as a blanket performance improvement.

Five interleaved original-Prism/new-renderer trials on equivalent synthetic production fixtures, taken **before the final preview-layout follow-up**, found:

| Workload | Prism → replacement |
| --- | --- |
| 600-line code block, warm topic return | 316.6 → 190.0 ms |
| 600-row diff, warm expanded viewport | 189.5 → 30.7 ms |
| Code-block browser Private Working Set increment | 203.6 → 120.0 MiB |
| Diff browser Private Working Set increment | 217.8 → 171.6 MiB |
| Large-diff scroll p99, normal / Chromium 4× CPU throttle | 16.8 → 33.4 ms / 33.4 → 183.4 ms |
| Whole JS/CSS/WASM first-use transfer, code / diff | 708.8 → 797.1 KiB / 706.9 → 887.8 KiB |

Memory subtracts each independent browser's blank-host baseline; private commit was measured separately. Transfer is actual negotiated response-body bytes, not decoded size. Diff viewport readiness is separate from a complete source-coordinate traversal. The 600-row diff is a stress fixture above the ordinary default 500-row native output cap; 4× throttling is not a real low-end device. These figures are retained evidence for that earlier snapshot, **not a performance claim for this repaired head**.

## Blast Radius

Shared Markdown/code rendering, source-file previews, read-only file activity and single/multiple-pane Composer placement. Main review risks are grammar-loading failures and resource ownership, source/line-ending integrity, virtual-diff geometry and scrolling tails, and draft/attachment retention when changing pane ownership.

## Verification

The repaired source/build passed locally: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports`, `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2` (**3297 tests**), `bun run test:browser` (**246 cases**), `bun run build --outDir <isolated-output>` and `git diff --check`. The source inventory, normalized staged blobs/Git tree and frozen production assets were checked against the repair commit; no source change intervened after those checks.

A new isolated production gateway passed **32 normal black-box cases** on desktop/light and narrow/dark: code blocks including INI, PowerShell, C#, Docker and literal unknown-language HTML; exact clipboard content; themes; full previews/native find and selection; long-line plain-text budgets; six kinds of diff including the INI Worker path; complete retained coordinates, line limits, expansion, truncation and close/reopen. No browser or HTTP errors occurred in these normal cases. Preview open/close retained the same Composer DOM instance and its draft.

The targeted production regression checks also passed: a real failed INI grammar request in the direct source-file preview retained complete plain source, the same Composer and draft, working theme/close controls, and local diagnostics. The normal → blocked → normal controls each used a fresh browser context in the same Service-Worker-blocked interception mode; this is not a claim of automatic same-page module retry. Ordinary black-box cases used the normal Service Worker path. A real mouse drag plus native wheel across the original virtual-window boundary retained the exact selection; further scrolling kept both the selected rows and current viewport, native Copy matched the selection, and clearing it released the pinned rows without changing total scroll height.

The full browser suite additionally covers forward/backward selection and multi-hunk missing-context coordinates, native clipboard content and 26px localized gaps. Earlier built-gateway single → multiple → single pane checks with text and browser-File drafts remain recorded against the initial review commit; pane/Composer ownership source was unchanged by this repair, and the full current unit/browser checks were rerun.

## Review results

The initial review of `48e7177e9669f86f2f50ae462871ad296a19abd1` independently confirmed two P2 defects in the production UI. Both are repaired in [`d4469e316`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/commit/d4469e316ce26a9169d911d7ebd33ff765d51049):

1. **Contain grammar/highlighter failure in CodeBlock.** Optional syntax enhancement can fail without clearing the source-file preview or the app. Keep the full plain source and Copy control outside the failed child; discard failed cached resources after the fallback commits, while retaining diagnostics.
2. **Preserve native diff selection during window movement.** Replace the function-valued hunk separator that disabled Pierre 1.6.1 partial rendering with built-in separators and local shadow-root label updates. Convert composed/shadow selection coordinates to rendered rows, retain only the active selection's minimal continuous envelope with the current viewport, and return to the normal bounded window when selection clears. Chromium's retargeted document `Selection.isCollapsed` is not used to reject a real shadow selection.

A focused independent read-only review of the repair implementation and installed library APIs found no new confirmed actionable finding. The exact parent failure triggers now pass through the new production build, as detailed above. This was not a formal GitHub approval.

Keep Draft pending performance reassessment: earlier scrolling/transfer measurements remain tied to the older pre-layout snapshot, not this incremental-render repair. Non-Chromium native shadow-selection fallbacks are statically checked but not browser-accepted. CI for the pushed head is reported separately from local tests and these synthetic-fixture UI checks.

prs.title: fix(channels): notify chat channels when a fallback model serves a turn
prs.body:
Closes #6031

## Problem

Model failover already works (including across providers), but when it fires, users on chat channels (QQ, Telegram, Discord, Slack, …) get no signal at all. The only observer hooked into `FallbackProvider` publishes `TurnModelUpdatedEvent` for websocket turns only:

- `nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py` builds one observer for the whole gateway and attaches it to every `FallbackProvider`.
- `build_webui_fallback_model_observer` (`nanobot/session/webui_turns.py`) threw non-WebUI turns away:

  ```python
  context = current_request_context()
  if context is None or context.channel != "websocket":
      return
  ```

- The event had exactly one consumer: the WebUI projection (`nanobot/webui/outbound_projection.py`).

Reproduced before this patch: binding a `telegram`/`qq` request context (as the agent loop does for channel turns) and firing a fallback selection publishes nothing. The existing test `test_fallback_model_ignores_non_websocket_requests` codified exactly this behavior.

## Fix

`TurnModelUpdatedEvent` is now published for whichever channel the turn belongs to. The observer is renamed to `build_fallback_model_observer` (it is no longer WebUI-only):

- **WebUI unchanged** — websocket turns keep the per-selection event with the same wire format (empty text content; still projected by the WebUI outbound projection).
- **Chat channels** — the notice carries human-readable text (`Primary model unavailable; using fallback model <model>.`) and is **edge-triggered, not per-turn**: one notice when a fallback first serves a chat, then silence until a turn for that chat completes without a fallback. The latch is tracked per chat and re-armed via the `TurnCompleted` runtime event.
- **Opt-in delivery** — the outbound dispatcher only delivers fallback notices to a chat channel that opts in via `channels.notifyModelFallback` (default **off**), resolving like the other `channels.*` booleans (`sendProgress`, `showCompactionNotices`, …) with per-channel override:

  ```yaml
  channels:
    notifyModelFallback: true      # gateway-wide default
    telegram:
      notifyModelFallback: false   # per-channel override (snake_case also accepted)
  ```

## Tests

- `tests/utils/test_webui_turn_helpers.py`: the old `test_fallback_model_ignores_non_websocket_requests` (which asserted the bug) is replaced by an edge-trigger state-machine test — first notice → silent while the fallback keeps serving the chat (across its turn completions) → re-armed once a fallback-free turn completes; chats are notified independently; websocket content stays empty.
- `tests/channels/test_channel_manager_fallback_notices.py` (new): dispatcher gate (dropped by default, delivered on opt-in, websocket exempt from the flag, non-fallback model events unaffected) plus flag inheritance / camelCase override / config round-trip.

`ruff check` and strict `basedpyright` pass on the touched files. Full suite: 6967 passed; the 9 failures seen on this Windows machine (symlink permissions, process-tree termination, cwd/env handling) reproduce identically on `main` without this patch.
