prs.title: fix: recover oversized pending file reads after compaction
prs.body:
Fixes #5879.

Several new `read_file` results can exceed the request budget after a successful history summary. Those results have not reached the model, so they cannot be included in that summary. The current runner then raises `ContextWindowExceededError` and stops the turn.

After history compaction, this change replaces only the necessary unread text results with an explicit budget error. It checks the complete request after each replacement. The model can then request one file or a smaller range. User input, accepted results, multimodal results, and tool call IDs remain unchanged. Requests that still do not fit continue to fail the budget check.

The session saves the same text that the model receives. This prevents a later turn or restart from restoring an oversized result that the model never received. Source files remain unchanged. The normal `read_file` offload exemption remains in place, so recovery does not create another file to read. An omitted result does not satisfy the visible-content receipt check; a repeated read returns the requested content.

Validation:

- Reproduced the failure on the base runner with real file reads: 241825/190784 and 241825/90784 with conservative byte estimates, and 60586/30784 with the normal tokenizer.
- Added same-round and cross-round coverage with normal and fallback token counting. Tests cover one or two omitted results, successful rereads, unchanged source files, and provider-state reset.
- Added SQLite save/reopen and next-turn replay coverage. The tool results and schemas remain unchanged during replay, and no extra summary is needed. Both runner input forms are covered.
- 273 focused tests passed across context governance, file reads, file receipts, persistence, compaction, recovery, provider state, and prompt-cache behavior. Ruff, scoped BasedPyright, import-boundary checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

No storage migration, configuration change, or tool-schema change is required. Existing sessions remain readable. This is deterministic offline integration coverage, not a live-model behavior or cache-hit-rate measurement.

prs.title: perf(webui): defer non-chat startup interfaces
prs.body:
## Why

Mobile cold chat startup downloads management and connection UI that the user has not opened. Keep that code off the chat path without delaying the composer, host state, or history.

Tracks [NAN-352](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-352).

## What changed

- Share one lazy remote-management page across its route and both management entrypoints; keep host connections, selection, and iframe ownership eager.
- Load the QR encoder only when a QR URL must actually be displayed, retaining cancellation and stale-result isolation.
- Load session automation dialogs on first inspection, then retain their roots for close transitions and focus handoffs. Give pending views a close/back action and contain failed imports locally rather than dropping the chat shell.

## Scope

Frontend dependency boundaries and their regression coverage only. No gateway, protocol, permission, persistence, dependency-version, or animation changes. Settings payloads, history sequencing, Markdown layout, locale partitioning, and Motion remain follow-ups in NAN-352.

## Tradeoffs

First opening management or an automation dialog, and first displaying a QR code, now includes a chunk request. Existing loading UI remains available; management and dialogs can be closed while waiting. A failed management import offers Back and a localized reload hint, without automatically refreshing away drafts.

## Blast Radius

Remote management navigation and restored host frames, channel QR flows, and session automation detail/edit/delete dialogs. Tests cover cold imports, cancellation, late results, retained drafts/frames, and local import failure recovery. Live SSH pairing and real channel authorization were not exercised.

## Verification

- Typecheck, ESLint, client import boundaries, production build, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Vitest coverage run: 188 files / 3312 tests passed; statements/lines 94.15%, branches 88.83%, functions 91.71%. Focused final regression rerun: 33 tests passed.
- Existing Playwright suite: 276 passed.
- Production assets served by an isolated Gateway: desktop/390px, light/dark, first-open automation/edit/cancel/delete-cancel, management/pairing/SSH controls, actual 184px QR PNG generation, and a deliberately failed management chunk passed. Automation/channel/pair responses were synthetic; no real account or server was contacted.
- Five alternating cold-load pairs per viewport, same production fixture: mobile LCP median **3,988 → 3,796 ms (−4.8%)**, ranges 3,972–4,016 / 3,784–3,820 ms. Observed JS compressed response bodies: **688,887 → 650,619 B (−37.4 KiB / −5.6%)**. Desktop LCP median remains 224 ms; no desktop speedup or CPU/CLS improvement is claimed.
- Static chat JS closure separately: 444,446 → 406,029 response-body bytes (−8.6%); do not add this saving to the observed-request saving above. CDP applies 150 ms latency, ~1.6 Mibit/s download and 4× CPU slowdown directly; this is **not a new Lighthouse score** or a physical-phone measurement. Each sample has the same expected cancelled prompts refresh, with zero page/HTTP errors and equal rendered content.
- Exact-head [Test Suite, attempt 2](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40094279752/attempts/2): all selected checks and `CI required` passed. The first attempt failed an unchanged history-anchor assertion after clock resume; a scoped 10-case local repeat passed, then the single bounded same-head CI rerun passed. The initial cause remains unconfirmed; no history code or assertions were changed.
- [Full measurement table, conditions, verification scope, and limitations](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nan-352首屏优化前后测量与验证392d33c-8718841bd0cc) (Linear workspace access required). The original user report and real chat data were not uploaded.

prs.title: fix(agent): don't resume abandoned work after max_iterations
prs.body:
## Why

After a terminal tool-iteration limit, a later user request can still contain unfinished work in its replayed history. The model needs the stop outcome as context, without deleting that history or blocking an explicit retry.

Related: #5924. This addresses next-turn guidance only. It does not fix sudo authentication or detect repeated calls within a turn. Tests establish the request contract, not guaranteed behavior from every model.

## Changes

- Record terminal iteration stops through the existing session continuation policy. Do not mark a queued Goal handoff as abandoned.
- Resolve a registered runtime-context provider for the next ordinary input. Keep ephemeral calls and internal continuations unchanged.
- Append the note after the current input. Preserve it in model history for stable replay, and hide it from display history through the existing context projection. Keep structured tool calls and results intact.
- Drop the pending note on new or forked histories.

There is no system-prompt, tool-schema, storage-format, identity or dependency change. Old sessions without the optional metadata keep their behavior. No migration is required.

## Verification

- 278 focused tests passed locally, including recovery, Goal lifecycle, compaction, ordinary context providers and request-prefix checks.
- Three regressions fail on the original candidate and pass after repair: a new input before a queued Goal continuation, `/new`, and a fork before the stopped request.
- Real agent/runtime/storage tests with an offline provider cover restart, separate sessions, explicit retry, temporary calls and display-history filtering. No production model or sudo credentials are used.
- Serialized ordinary and post-stop prefixes remain stable across replay; ordered tool schemas are unchanged. No live-provider cache-hit claim is made.
- Changed-file Ruff, scoped BasedPyright, import boundaries and whitespace checks passed.

Remote CI must pass on the updated head before merge.

prs.title: fix(agent): recheck idle expiry after acquiring session lock
prs.body:
Fixes #6410.

An idle archive can be selected during a long direct turn, wait for the session lock, then summarize immediately after that turn saves its reply. Recheck the session's latest committed activity after acquiring the existing lock. A fresh completion defers idle compaction; a later scan still compacts a session that has remained idle for the full interval.

This is the remaining eligibility issue, not the transcript overwrite race fixed by #6221. It complements #6215's scan-time exclusion and also covers an archive queued before the direct turn begins. Explicit SDK/manual and context-pressure compaction remain unchanged. No extra activity registry, timestamp protocol, persisted field, or public interface is added.

The built-in retained path is a long gateway heartbeat. Custom integrations that combine direct calls with the idle scanner can also reach it. This does not establish ordinary-chat message loss or cross-process coordination.

Validation on the rebased code:

- 416 focused tests passed for idle compaction, session serialization/persistence, manual compaction, turn saving, and prompt-cache behavior.
- Removing only the four production lines makes the two controlled ordering tests and the scheduled SDK test fail at their freshness assertions. Restoring the fix makes them pass.
- Tests cover independent session progress, a later genuine-idle summary, and saved reply/summary data after restart. Provider responses and the clock are controlled; session storage and execution ownership are real.
- Scoped Ruff and BasedPyright, import-boundary checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

No migration or prompt/tool-schema change is required. No live-provider test, production cache-rate measurement, or full repository suite was run locally.

Validation: the acceptance regression failed before the fix; all 69 launcher, wheel, TUI packaging and release-candidate tests pass with it. The updated verifier also accepts the same real Windows archive that failed on main. Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.

The first Windows Python job hit a five-second wait in the existing archive-resume test, outside this change. The same three modes passed three times on both main and this revision locally; rerunning the unchanged Windows job passed 81 isolated update tests, 10,617 main tests and 244 serial CLI tests (5/135/9 skips). The [first attempt](https://github.com/Aschenbath/nanobot/actions/runs/40082151459/attempts/1) retains that timeout; no test or timeout was relaxed.

prs.title: perf(tui): shrink standalone builds and target native bindings
prs.body:
## Why

Reduce what users download and install instead of raising the executable-size limit. The current standalone build embeds minified JS plus an optional bytecode cache, and Ubuntu → Windows builds also capture installed Linux resvg bindings. This is the size-reduction approach tracked by [NAN-350](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-350), distinct from #6428's proposed increase to 160 MiB.

## What changed

- Disable the extra bytecode cache while keeping the standalone Bun runtime, minified JS, Mermaid worker, and all existing render features. Add a 135 MiB build budget for Windows/Linux x64, leaving at least 15 MiB below the unchanged 150 MiB archive limit; retain the existing ceiling for unmeasured targets.
- Share native target definitions across preparation, compilation, and notices. Redirect only the pinned resvg wrapper's internal loader to target bindings, retaining public options serialization, both Linux libc variants, OpenTUI loading, and baseline x64 CPU support. Dependency source/version changes require adapter review.
- Ship both new helpers in corresponding source, test their archived bytes and the cross-target binding boundary, and retain compiled-size/hash reports in CI. Preserve the existing archive, source, license, manifest, checksum, and wheel verification paths.

## Scope

Build/package changes only; no Python gateway or TUI interaction/worker-lifetime changes, dependency upgrades, feature removals, runtime downloads, new user switches, or relaxed archive limits. This is a **Draft**, not release-ready or a request to merge.

## Tradeoffs

Bytecode precomputes parsing/compilation work, so removing it saves space at a startup cost. On the local Linux paired worker experiment, fresh-process first-PNG p95 increased from **76.73 ms to 132.16 ms** (+55.44 ms); hot-render p95 was **11.28 → 9.01 ms**, and hot-raster **1.54 → 1.56 ms**. This is a simple diagram with fixed DejaVu fonts, 30 interleaved AB/BA pairs, valid identical PNGs, warm/uncontrolled OS file caches, and no system Bun/Node in the worker PATH—not a cold-cache or complete interactive-UI benchmark. Fresh-worker cost is inside the proposed +100 ms gate, but that does not establish the missing UI/restart gates.

Keeping bytecode and rewriting inflated font/dictionary dependencies remains an alternative if startup acceptance fails; nonfunctional dependency-removal ablations are not shipped or counted as savings.

## Blast Radius

All five standalone build targets consume the shared target map and bytecode policy. Native execution has only been checked locally on Linux x64/glibc; Linux musl payloads are retained, not claimed runtime-validated. Windows results below are Ubuntu cross-builds, not Windows-native performance evidence. macOS and arm64 execution, signing, and tighter per-target budgets remain unverified. The resvg adapter is deliberately pinned to 2.6.2 and its public-entry/internal-loader SHA-256 identities.

## Verification

Baseline source: `8af2d396ab7907fd93dd22c947a6cf038cb7e695`; candidate: `7d6a28822103a9292483138974432b43b919955c`; Bun **1.3.13**, revision `bf2e2cecf27e800962b1e7f03d66278f9d5d2e79`. Same source/runtime dependency versions and build host for each comparison.

| Artifact | Before (bytes) | After (bytes) | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Linux x64 executable | 152,586,560 | 128,821,568 | 15.57% |
| Linux x64 complete release ZIP | 53,040,486 | 47,829,237 | 9.82% |
| Windows x64 executable, Ubuntu cross-build | 166,895,616 | 134,377,984 | 19.48% |

The candidate Windows cross-build ZIP is 46,914,179 bytes. No baseline Windows ZIP/wheel acceptance is claimed: its original executable exceeds the existing verifier limit. The cross-build improvement must not be presented as the native Windows reduction.

- `bun run check`, `bun run check:imports`, and the client-import checker tests pass. Full TUI tests at the committed candidate: **286 passed, 13 platform/font-dependent skips**, no failures; skipped native/font coverage is not counted as execution evidence.
- Native Linux and Ubuntu → Windows production builds and complete ZIP packaging pass. Existing release-bundle verification accepts the candidate ZIPs, their architecture, manifests, licensed material, and exact corresponding source; it also accepts the baseline Linux ZIP. The original 150 MiB verifier is unchanged.
- A bounded Bun 1.3.13 module-graph audit matches embedded native-resource hashes against the installed target packages: Windows contains one Windows resvg binding and OpenTUI DLL, with no Linux payload; Linux retains both GNU/musl pairs. Candidate graphs contain no extra bytecode bytes.
- The compiled Linux executable passes the existing PTY smoke adapted externally to launch the binary with isolated HOME/workspace and no Bun/Node in PATH: Unicode editing, resize, local exit, terminal restoration, and session-resume output. The fixture deliberately uses an unavailable loopback gateway; this is not connected-UI acceptance or a first-interactive-frame timing.
- Thirty paired compiled-worker blocks produce **180 valid PNG replies**, with identical hashes across A/B for render/raster; raw timings, binary/font identities, native-resource audit, and archive checks are retained under the local evidence directory `/home/cyr/.nanobot/workspace/.nanobot-workflows/runs/nan350-pr-20261024/` (not uploaded as public attachments).
- `pytest -q tests/cli/test_tui_release_packaging.py tests/cli/test_tui_wheels.py tests/cli/test_tui_launcher.py`: **62 passed** against the committed source. Ruff on touched Python files and `git diff --check` pass. Wheel regression fixtures use synthetic native binaries; they are not installed-wheel runtime acceptance.

Still required before Ready: exact-head CI (including Windows native acceptance), real connected TUI first-frame timing, cancellation/restart timing, broader diagram/font/zoom behavior, native Windows measurements, macOS/arm64 coverage, and actual final-wheel byte comparisons plus clean installed-wheel execution. Executable/ZIP savings are not presented as measured final-wheel savings.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.title: fix(api): route each session_id to its own chat
prs.body:
## Why

API requests with an explicit `session_id` select their own history, but still pass `chat_id="default"` to the agent. Tools that inspect the current request therefore see a route that does not match the session.

Related: #5798. The reported ordinary-reply crossover was not reproduced. This change fixes the confirmed request-route mismatch; it does not claim to resolve every possible cause of that report.

## What changed

- Derive `chat_id` from the existing session key for both JSON responses and SSE.
- Preserve existing session IDs and histories. JSON IDs keep their spaces and existing value conversion. Multipart IDs keep their existing trimming. Missing or empty IDs still share `api:default`.

prs.title: perf(sdk): reuse consecutive effective model overrides
prs.body:
## Why

Repeated SDK calls with the same per-run `model=` override construct a new provider each time and retain it until SDK shutdown. Reuse the most recent complete effective configuration before constructing another client, while leaving the selected default unchanged.

## What changed

- Keep one private recent-override lookup in the existing ModelRuntimeResolver; derive typed, detached identity from the factory's full primary/fallback signature, not the model string alone.
- Include request-declaration presence in cache identity and preserve local primary route validation. Equivalent merged wire settings can hide an unsupported preset-level override, including a lazy fallback; fallback validation still runs only at its original failover boundary.
- On misses only, capture configuration/preset and the effective shared proxy so old lazy fallback clients do not read later credential/body/environment edits.
- Return detached signature metadata to each borrower. Clear lookup on invalidation/refresh/adoption/shutdown without closing active borrowers; the existing resolver remains the sole provider shutdown owner.
- Extend real resolver/SDK tests and MockTransport connection-isolation requests, including 1,000 repeated resolutions, nested typed changes, delayed fallback, active streaming across replacement/invalidation, unsupported identity and validation-equivalent invalid input.

## Scope

Only Config-backed raw `model=` overrides. No new public SDK options, cross-instance/global pool, dependency changes, default/preset-selection redesign, lease/draining system or early resource retirement. Unsupported identity values retain the existing uncached builder path.

## Tradeoffs

The lookup has **one slot**. Consecutive equivalent configurations reuse a provider; A/B/A, genuinely different configurations and explicit invalidations can still admit providers retained until shutdown. This PR does **not** bound all provider memory or prove the absence of leaks. Stateful client/circuit behavior is shared as it already is for default/preset providers. Hidden ambient authentication remains governed by the existing provider refresh/invalidation behavior.

## Blast Radius

Public SDK `run` and `run_streamed` per-run model overrides. Existing connection-isolation, primary setup validation, frozen generation, late fallback construction and shutdown ordering are preserved. Streams and background users are never retired merely because the lookup changes.

## Verification

- Focused Python suite: **320 passed** across resolver, SDK facade, session/runtime refresh and identity, fallback, model API and default headers. Python import-boundary checks also passed (13 rules / 217 files).
- Ruff on all changed Python files passed; BasedPyright 1.39.0 on both changed product modules: 0 errors/warnings; `git diff --check` passed.
- Reuse regression tests fail against the exact base. Two additional candidate regressions reproduced primary validation bypass and stale lazy-fallback validation before their corrections; the latter checks actual failover results without eagerly validating fallback setup.
- Equal-work public SDK measurement on exact base `8af2d396ab7907fd93dd22c947a6cf038cb7e695` and head `95c539bee08bf89406e4b9dfd1179082fdcc6d25`: **five interleaved pairs**, fresh process/HOME/config/workspace each time; 201 validated requests per run, every request with two messages (one warmup, 100 fixed-default, 100 same-config overrides).
- After 25/50/75/100 overrides, retained top-level providers changed from **26/51/76/101 → 2/2/2/2** in every pair. Override-stage CPU median **2.36 → 1.23 s** (ranges 2.33–2.38 / 1.23–1.24); wall median **2.400 → 1.272 s** (2.366–2.431 / 1.268–1.281). After the same 2-second idle, RSS median **220.69 → 143.70 MiB** (220.16–222.98 / 143.54–145.87); PSS **200.42 → 123.27 MiB**. The fixed-default control CPU medians were 1.17 / 1.17 s.
- These Linux/WSL local-fake-endpoint measurements include lookup/validation/copy costs, not cloud latency or a universal RSS/leak claim. Raw measurements and matching source hashes are retained locally outside tracked source; earlier candidate runs were superseded after the primary/fallback validation corrections. All child processes and the owned local model server were closed.
- Only synthetic credentials/state and loopback endpoints were used; no daily instance or real user history was accessed. CI supplies broader/platform checks.

prs.title: perf(webui): avoid redundant math layout setup
prs.body:
## Why

Streaming mathematical replies repeatedly reinstall resize observation and write the same tag spacing before measuring layout. Keep observation for the component lifetime and avoid unchanged spacing writes without delaying formula fitting.

## What changed

- Use a stable geometry callback and one ResizeObserver/font-ready subscription per DisplayMath instance.
- Refit synchronously when children change and retain width/font/resize handling; only write `--math-tag-width` when its value changes.
- Add streaming tagged-math coverage for desktop/mobile, viewport/font changes, completion and reduced motion; explicitly flush font readiness in the unit tests.

## Scope

Only DisplayMath layout work and its fixtures/tests. No Markdown parser, whole-tree cache, global throttling, transcript projection, scroll or loading-ring changes. No styling/appearance redesign.

## Tradeoffs

The tag write still precedes the final padded-width measurement when spacing changes, as required by the existing CSS. This eliminates redundant setup/writes, not all geometry reads or all browser CPU regression. No CPU-percentage improvement is claimed from the mechanism experiment.

## Blast Radius

Display formulas, especially tagged equations updated while streaming. Initial fitting and changed tags remain synchronous; existing centering, constrained-width scale and occupied-height behavior are preserved.

## Verification

- Focused unit suite: **3 files / 33 tests passed**. Typecheck, lint, production build and `git diff --check` passed. Four real Chromium fixture cases passed at 1280/390 px with normal/reduced motion.
- Real KaTeX mechanism experiment, exact base `8af2d396ab7907fd93dd22c947a6cf038cb7e695` versus this implementation: across **200 equal content updates**, additional observer creations **200 → 0** and unchanged tag-spacing writes **202 → 0**. Final TeX, scale and height matched; a subsequent changed tag caused one necessary candidate write. Observers disconnected on unmount. This counts work, not timing/total CPU.
- Production-built isolated Gateway acceptance: three real completed WebSocket turns, 25 streamed deltas, tagged formulas fitted on desktop/mobile/reduced motion and after reload; earlier history visibly retained and read back through authenticated HTTP. No page exceptions, external browser requests or unexpected HTTP failures. The initial draft 404 and one cancelled history read were recorded rather than hidden.
- Exact-head CI [40093154111](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40093154111) passed, including `CI required`, on the rerun. The first browser attempt timed out in the unchanged `prompt-rail.spec.ts:3` case at line 61 (290 other browser cases passed, including the new math cases). The successful rerun does not establish the timeout's cause.
- All state/provider data was synthetic and loopback-only. Owned Gateway/browser/listener processes were cleaned up; no daily instance was operated. Raw logs, comparison source hashes and screenshots are retained locally outside tracked source. CI supplies broader/platform checks.

## Why

Completing a WebUI turn only needs the persisted Goal metadata, but currently reloads the conversation and creates a full detached history draft. Use the existing header-only read so long conversations do not incur that work at every turn end.

## What changed

- Read the session header in `WebuiTurnCoordinator.handle_turn_end`; preserve create-if-missing and metadata ordering semantics.
- Exercise completed and failed turns against real cold SQLite state with history-table reads denied, checking Goal, usage, routing, outcome and preserved history.

## Scope

Only the turn-end metadata read. No storage schema, cache policy, history isolation, write transaction, fsync, client protocol or title-generation changes.

## Tradeoffs

The optimization is deliberately limited to a metadata-only caller; it does not replace detached history drafts for callers that edit or inspect messages.

## Blast Radius

WebSocket turn-end events. The existing session-state owner still serializes the read and provides detached metadata; readers that need conversation history are unchanged.

- Focused Python suite: **87 passed**, including turn helpers, incremental/async session state, progress, direct WebSocket status and recovery.

Base range 300.9–321.1 ms; head 2.77–4.94 ms. This measures the turn-end helper, **not end-to-end chat latency**; it does not claim recovery of the earlier overall RSS difference.
- Isolated real Gateway: three WebSocket turns completed, all `turn_end` events received, and all three assistant replies read back through HTTP persisted history. Owned processes and ports released afterward.

prs.title: fix(agent): preserve goal continuation lifecycle
prs.body:
## Why

Long `/goal` runs could be reported as finished at an internal iteration-budget boundary even though work continued. This reset the WebUI transcript sequence for the same public turn and could make loading earlier history fail with `Could not place earlier history` despite successful HTTP responses.

`/goal` replaces the inbound message and copies its metadata. The continuation helper wrote its pending flag onto that replacement, while dispatch checked the original message. Keep this execution state on the shared delivery instead of using message metadata as a side channel.

Related: [NAN-348](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-348).

## What changed

- Record the successful continuation handoff on the per-slice `TurnDelivery`; completion, failure and idle all consult that same result.
- Clear the handoff when the session worker is cancelled, so Stop still ends the visible run if a continuation was queued just before persistence was interrupted.
- Exercise the real `/goal` rewrite in the existing continuation lifecycle regression, and add the reachable Stop-after-enqueue regression for both ordinary goal messages and `/goal`.

## Scope

This is the causal prevention fix for newly executed goal continuations. It does not change the wire protocol, frontend reconciliation, database format, dependencies or user data. It does not disable live-history protection or add automatic refresh as a workaround.

**Existing history that already contains duplicate public turn/sequence identities is not repaired by this PR.** Physical records are not keyed by those logical identities, so they were not overwritten, but older/latest reconciliation can still collide. Non-destructive legacy read-side compatibility remains open under NAN-348. This prevention fix is ready for review independently of that remaining work; NAN-348 is not being marked Done. No production database has been rewritten.

## Tradeoffs

A delivery-owned result survives command replacement and remains available to exception/finally handling if persistence fails after enqueue. Expanding only `_process_message`'s return value would not cover that failure path; copying the flag back into another metadata dictionary would retain two state owners.

## Blast Radius

The common continuation completion path affects WebUI and other goal-capable channels. The new cancellation regression protects the narrow handoff/persistence window. Python recovery, inbox, delivery and channel regressions were included in the complete local suite; live browser acceptance used an isolated Gateway and synthetic sessions. These checks do not establish exhaustive platform compatibility, production deployment, or repair of pre-existing collisions.

## Verification

All results below apply to head `32c19d3c911c2d4ce3e1ca45fb10bc96c4f2f4b4`.

- Red/green: the `/goal` case produced an extra intermediate `idle` before the lifecycle fix; the Stop-after-enqueue cases produced only `running` before the cancellation correction. Both ordinary and `/goal` cases pass with this change.
- Local Python: **11,151 passed, 97 skipped** across the full parallel suite and the four separate serial CLI files; combined coverage **85.93%**, above the 75% gate. Dependencies and channel manifests were installed in a private verification environment; shared runtime dependencies were not changed.
- `ruff check` for the five changed files, scoped BasedPyright for the three changed Python runtime files, `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local WebUI: **3,292 tests / 185 files passed**, with coverage thresholds satisfied (94.14% statements/lines, 88.77% branches, 91.69% functions). `bun run build` passed. Existing React act/KaTeX test warnings and Vite chunk-size warnings remain.
- Isolated real Gateway + Chromium: `/goal` executed four distinct stream slices at an iteration budget of one. While held at the fourth slice, desktop (1400×1000) and narrow (390×844) clients accepted earlier history, retained the live tail, and reloaded while still active. Completion produced one `turn_end` and one idle; persisted projection sequences increased across slices without collisions (19 retained identities, spanning 1–28). Completed-history reload also passed.
- The narrow client disconnected and reconnected its own WebSocket during continuation: the active turn was preserved, without intermediate completion; final content rendered with one final `turn_end` and idle.
- Additional real-browser scenarios passed: Stop during `/goal` continuation, Stop during ordinary-input continuation of an already active goal, ordinary-input completion, and a deliberate provider failure followed by a new input. Stop retired the owner without reviving or replaying the cancelled turn; completion/failure emitted one final `turn_end` and idle. All four scenarios retained unique, increasing sequence identities, retired the backend owner, and had no page errors. The active ordinary-input goal was established through `/goal` and Stop, not by bypassing opt-in or writing session metadata.
- Remote Test Suite [40006206033](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40006206033) completed successfully on this exact head: Linux Python 3.11/3.14 with coverage, Windows Python/process checks, both TUI platforms, Docker, WebUI checks/build/browser and `CI required` passed. Native-package and Windows-installer checks were skipped by the workflow's scope selection.

Owned verification Gateway/provider/browser resources were cleaned up; the isolated Gateway ports were released. No daily or third-party instance was restarted. No formal GitHub review, merge or deployment is included.

prs.title: feat(mcp): add opt-in self-contained Apps hosting in WebUI
prs.body:
Nanobot currently reduces MCP results to model-facing text/image artifacts and exposes app-only tools to the model. This adds an opt-in MCP Apps host: structured results stay outside model context, while self-contained HTML Apps can render in the WebUI and call approved tools on their originating MCP connection.

Refs #5251. The earlier #5386 was withdrawn; this is an independent implementation. Enable with `channels.websocket.mcpAppsEnabled: true` and restart the gateway. It defaults to false, preserves WebUI protocol 1, and advertises the optional `webui.mcp-apps.v1` capability only when enabled.

The implementation spans the complete path:

- Preserve bounded, detached MCP rich results in `ToolResult.data`, including source identity, metadata, schemas and result fields. Error guidance retains this data; model observation normalization strips it before messages/checkpoints are built.
- Honor model/App visibility independently of `enabledTools`. Bind each App to its original connection and declared `ui://` resource, with URI/MIME/UTF-8 validation and connection-close revocation.
- Negotiate `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` for enabled gateway MCP connections. Carry only ephemeral App handles in ordinary progress attachments; rich UI data is fetched through authenticated WebUI mutations.
- Use the official AppBridge in an opaque-origin iframe with restrictive CSP. Every tool call requires host-owned approval outside the iframe, then consumes a single-use receipt bound to the exact recorded arguments and chat. Requests cannot reach another server or bypass its allowlist. Cancellation before approval removes the prompt and prevents dispatch.
- Load AppBridge on demand, reject stale loads after host/session switches, retain text fallbacks, localize controls in all ten locales, and document configuration, architecture and limits.

The current revision merges main through `3c022ada`. It preserves shared proxy configuration in MCP connection/reload/reconnect, all current update capabilities and translations, and the current ThreadShell structure. The real MCPProvider regression covers initial negotiation and reload with Apps both enabled and disabled; old App objects lose access after reload or shutdown. The channel-schema inventory now includes the internal WebSocket `mcpAppsEnabled` option.

This initial host supports **self-contained Apps**. It blocks external assets/fetches and does not grant requested browser/device permissions. Temporary-chat rendering, durable App recovery, external-domain policy and host-side App installation are outside this change. HTML is capped at 1 MiB; rich messages at 64 KiB/depth 16/4096 values; at most 32 handles are retained for 15 minutes. The bridge does not retry possibly committed tool actions or claim exactly-once execution. CSP is not a general network firewall against iframe navigation.

Current revision: `f7aa239acc12dce4feaf3d9340d5b84b6865e26f`. It adds the missing npm lockfile entries required by the Docker build and npm consistency check. Application source and the Bun lock are identical to functional merge `96b7382f`; the checks below retain their original identity where carried forward.

Validation:

- Windows Python 3.11 regression selection: 4,909 passed, 84 platform skips and one missing channel-schema inventory entry. After correcting that expectation, all 58 affected channel-contract/MCP Apps/client-contract tests passed. The broader selection covered tools, WebUI, channels, agent, gateway, config, security and architecture; its totals are not added to the follow-up.
- Complete WebUI: **3,298 passed across 186 files** with Bun 1.3.13 and two workers. The initial default-concurrency run timed out in four files; all 146 tests in those files and then the full suite passed at reduced concurrency without changing timeouts or assertions.
- All channel dependencies and package consistency, full CI Ruff selection, strict BasedPyright for the complete production tree, Python/client import boundaries, 42 import-checker tests, application/browser TypeScript, ESLint and production build passed. All ten merged locale files were compared against the fixed upstream and feature commits.
- Real in-memory MCP sessions exercise provider negotiation/reload, source/visibility/allowlist restrictions and revocation. The wider Python selection includes live authenticated WebSocket approval dispatch and identical-request replay without a second tool execution.
- Chrome 155 checks on the actual AppBridge/card fixture passed initialization, structured weather data, blocked parent access/fetches, rejection with zero executions, one approved call/result, forged message-source rejection, cancellation before approval, and a 390px viewport. The fixture is `/browser/mcp-apps.html`; it uses synthetic host transport rather than a model or external provider.
- On `f7aa239a`, `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run` and the actual Dockerfile's `webui-builder` stage passed clean npm installation and production build.

[The upstream workflow](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40080996868) awaits maintainer approval. [The fork Test Suite](https://github.com/Aschenbath/nanobot/actions/runs/40080993400) completed on the exact current head. Docker, WebUI checks/build/browser, both TUI jobs, all Python jobs and Linux native acceptance passed. Linux Python 3.11/3.14 each passed 10,956 main tests (79 skipped) and 252 serial tests (one skipped). Windows Python passed 81 isolated update tests (five skipped), 10,658 main tests (135 skipped) and 244 serial tests (nine skipped); the previous supervisor timeout did not recur. Windows installer compatibility passed 80 tests with one skip.

The sole failing test job is native Windows acceptance, so aggregate CI remains failed. A clean, unchanged `3c022ada` build reproduces its executable-size error: 157,286,912 bytes, 512 bytes over the 150 MiB ceiling. The builder, TUI sources and verifier are unchanged by this feature. Independent #6428 addresses this upstream size limit and passes both native acceptance jobs on its own head; this PR does not include that change or count the failed native acceptance as a pass.

Implemented and tested with AI assistance. No live model credentials or external MCP deployments were used.

prs.title: fix(webui): support well-known skills.sh sources
prs.body:
## What changed

skills.sh returns both GitHub repository sources such as `owner/repo` and
well-known discovery hosts such as `uizze.com`. Nanobot accepted only the
repository form, so well-known skills were omitted from search and trending
results. Their trend references were dropped, and direct installation rejected
them.

This change accepts either a repository source or a bounded DNS hostname.
Hostnames are converted to `https://<hostname>` when passed to the official
skills CLI. Schemes, paths, ports, IP addresses, localhost, and single-label
names are still rejected.

The official CLI remains responsible for fetching and validating the
well-known index. Related to #2571.

## Verification

- old behavior: the `uizze.com` search, trend, and CLI install cases produced
  `3 failed, 1 passed`
- `tests/webui/test_skills_marketplace.py`: 23 passed, 1 skipped
- `tests/webui`: 194 passed, 2 skipped
- restoring the repository-only checks makes the 3 regression tests fail again
- `npx --yes skills@latest add https://uizze.com --list` found 4 skills,
  including `anti-ui-slop`
- Ruff, BasedPyright, and `git diff --check` passed

prs.title: fix(tools): keep the stdin-closed ack across exec_session wait iterations
prs.body:
## What Problem Does This Solve?

`ExecSessionTool._wait` sends `input`/`close_stdin` on the **first** poll iteration only, and `manager.write` derives `stdin_closed` from that call's `close_stdin` argument — so the flag lives on the *first* poll object. When the wait loop iterates again (`wait_for` matched later, or the deadline expired), the tool formats the **last** poll and the `"Stdin closed."` confirmation is silently dropped — even though stdin really was closed (a process relying on the EOF still exits 0). The model cannot tell whether `close_stdin` took effect: the typical fallout is re-invoking `exec_session` just to close stdin again, or misjudging the state of an interactive process.

## Evidence

On clean `main` (POSIX shell): start a session whose script reads one stdin line, sleeps ~1.2 s, then prints the wait target and exits on the EOF from `close_stdin`. The wait necessarily spans ≥2 poll iterations (`step` is 500 ms), the target is observed, `Exit code: 0` proves stdin closed — yet the result contains no `"Stdin closed."`:

```
FAILED ... assert 'Stdin closed.' in 'start\ndone-marker\n\nExit code: 0\nElapsed: 1.2s'
```

Repro is the new `tests/tools/test_exec_session_stdin_ack.py` (fails on `main`, passes with this patch).

## What Changed

`_wait` now ORs each poll's `stdin_closed` into the final poll before formatting — mirroring how aggregate output and truncation counts are already accumulated across iterations (3 lines).

## Test Plan

- [x] New `tests/tools/test_exec_session_stdin_ack.py`: red on `main`, green with the patch (skipped on Windows).
- [x] Regression: `tests/tools/test_exec_session_tools.py` + `test_exec_session_timeout.py` + `test_shell_output.py` — 57 passed.
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

prs.title: fix(tools): drop xcrun cache-denial noise from sandboxed stderr
prs.body:
## What Problem Does This Solve?

On stock macOS (Command Line Tools toolchain), `/usr/bin/git` is an xcrun shim that must open/replace its shared `xcrun_db` cache under the host DARWIN_USER temp dir — which the seatbelt profile intentionally keeps private (host scratch directories are not shared, per `test_host_scratch_directories_are_not_shared`). The denial does not affect the command's outcome, but every invocation injects two lines into stderr:

```
git: error: couldn't create cache file '/var/folders/.../T/xcrun_db-...' (errno=Operation not permitted)
git: error: couldn't open cache file '/var/folders/.../T/xcrun_db-...' (errno=Operation not permitted)
```

`ExecSession.poll` surfaces stderr as a `STDERR:` section in the agent-visible tool output, so **every `git` call inside the sandbox looks like a failure while exiting 0** — misleading for the model (and for users reading transcripts).

## Evidence

Repro on clean `main` (macOS, `sandbox="seatbelt"`):

```python
tool = ExecTool(working_dir=ws, sandbox="seatbelt")
result = await tool.execute(command="git --version", timeout=10)
# result contains "git version 2.x" AND "Exit code: 0" AND a STDERR section
# with the two xcrun cache-denial lines above.
```

With this patch the same call returns clean output with no STDERR section (verified locally; the darwin integration test in this PR reproduces both directions). The sandbox profile itself is unchanged — strictness and the host-scratch contract stay as they are.

## What Changed

- `nanobot/agent/tools/shell_output.py`: new `filter_stderr_noise()` drops stderr lines matching the exact xcrun cache-denial shape (`<tool>: error: couldn't (create|open|replace) cache file '<path containing xcrun_db>' (errno=Operation not permitted)`). Any other stderr content — different file, different errno, any real error — is preserved.
- `nanobot/agent/tools/exec_session.py`: `poll()` applies the filter when draining stderr, so the whole STDERR section disappears when only noise was drained.

## Test Plan

- [x] `tests/tools/test_stderr_noise_filter.py`: cross-platform unit tests — noise dropped (create/open/replace, multiple tool names), real errors preserved, similar-but-different errors kept (other file / other errno), untouched passthrough; plus a darwin-only integration test (`git --version` under seatbelt stays free of noise) that fails on clean `main` and passes with the patch.
- [x] Regression: `tests/tools/test_shell_output.py`, `tests/tools/test_sandbox.py`, `tests/tools/test_exec_env.py` — 67 passed.

issues.title: Desktop Bot Mode: Create group chat blocked by 'Group driver unavailable' although groups.capabilities reports driver: true

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: comp/desktop
labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

issues.body:
## Environment

- Hermes `0.22.5` (stable channel, commit `bf0203a794a0`), source/git install on Windows 11 (x64)
- Hermes Desktop, packaged build (`apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked`), Bot Mode enabled
- Host gateway in **multiplex** mode (`gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`), one process serving 7 local profiles: `default, axcel, bastian, jekson, kodi, lerry, reyhan`
- Managed Python 3.14.9 (PM generation `e04b632f…`), model `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` via Nous provider
- Telegram is the only messaging platform; Desktop talks to the local gateway over its host-scoped socket

## Summary

**Create group chat is permanently unavailable in the Desktop even though the gateway reports `driver: true`.**

The "Create" button in *Bots → Create group chat* is disabled. Typing a group name and pressing Enter shows:

> Group driver unavailable. Update or reconnect the owning gateway.

The same happens after a clean gateway restart. An external client using the gateway's own RPC (host-scope ticket, i.e. the same socket shape the Desktop uses) gets a fully valid capability — `driver: true`, `persistent_process: true`, `protocol_version: 2`, all 7 profiles in `seatable_profiles` — and can create a room successfully. So the hosted-room driver is healthy; the Desktop create gate never accepts its answer.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a host gateway that multiplexes several local profiles (7 here) and open Hermes Desktop against it.
2. Go to **Bots → Create group chat**.
3. Observe: the **Create** button is disabled even after selecting 2–6 bots and typing a name.
4. Press **Enter** in the name field → toast/error `Group driver unavailable. Update or reconnect the owning gateway.`
5. Cross-check the gateway from a shell (see *Error Output*): `groups.capabilities` returns `driver: true`, `groups.create` then succeeds — so the backend is not the blocker.

## Expected behavior

With `groups.capabilities.driver === true`, `groupExecutionMode()` yields `canonical`, the dialog enables **Create**, and the room is created through `groups.create`.

## Actual behavior

- `mode` in the dialog appears to stay `checking`/`unavailable`, so `canCreate` (`create-dialog.tsx`) is false → **Create** disabled.
- `create()` throws the locale string `canonical.driverUnavailable` because `capability` is null/stale when `revalidateGroupCreationMode()` runs.
- Left panel's *Refresh gateway rooms* also appears inert (no rooms rendered; there were none before the test, so this may be the empty list, not a disabled control).
- A room created out-of-band (see evidence) is **not** listed either, which points at the capability/settle path rather than at room listing.

## Error output

Gateway answer to a host-scoped client (same scope the Desktop socket uses):

```json
{"protocol_version": 2, "driver": true, "persistent_process": true,
 "authority_gateway_id": "install:75d0506f…",
 "room_link": {"enabled": false, "reason": "canonical_driver_required"},
 "features": ["room_identity", "monotonic_log", "replayable_disband"],
 "methods": ["groups.capabilities", "groups.list", "groups.create", "groups.state", "groups.log",
             "groups.send", "groups.rename", "groups.disband", "groups.stop", "groups.retry",
             "groups.discard", "groups.approve", "groups.attachment.upload", "groups.attachment.download"],
 "max_log_limit": 500,
 "seatable_profiles": ["axcel", "bastian", "default", "jekson", "kodi", "lerry", "reyhan"]}
```

`groups.create` over that client then succeeded:

```json
{"room": {"room_id": "uji-8943fff491", "name": "Ruang Uji",
          "members": [{"member_id": "m-axcel", "profile": "axcel", "handle": "axcel"},
                      {"member_id": "m-jekson", "profile": "jekson", "handle": "jekson"}],
          "authority_gateway_id": "install:75d0506f…", "authority_epoch": 1, "revision": 1}}
```

and `groups.state` shows the driver alive for it:

```json
"driver_status": {"running": true, "working": false, "blocked": false, "counts": {}, "pending_actions": []}
```

The owner row `state_meta['gateway.hosted.owner.v1:uji-8943fff491']` was written with the Desktop's own subject (`sid:S-1-5-21-…-1001`), so visibility was not the issue.

The Desktop *did* call the method — 17 `groups.capabilities` calls in one session, each answered with a running hosted service (verified with a temporary diagnostic log line in `gateway/session_group_controls.py::_group().capabilities()`, since reverted). Response validation is clean: `GroupsCapabilitiesResult.model_validate(...)` passes and no `violates its wire contract` line exists for `groups.capabilities` in `gateway.log`, `errors.log` or `agent.log`.

Gateway boot context (same session): hosted-room services for all 7 authorities are created and started ~25 s after start (`ensure_hosted_service` → `start_ready_hosted_services`) and stay `running: true`.

## Hypothesis

The live capability is correct but the Desktop never publishes it:

- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-group-capabilities.ts` — `useGroupCapability()` only calls `settle()` when `groupCreationSource(...)()` is true at response time, i.e. `gatewayActivationEpoch()` unchanged **and** `host.state.connectionId/profile` still equal **and** `host.state.gateway === 'open'`. Any epoch bump or route re-activation while the dialog is open silently drops the answer, leaving `capability === null` → `mode: 'checking'` forever.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/create-dialog.tsx` — `create()` treats a null/stale capability as `canonical.driverUnavailable`, which is exactly the message users see even though `driver` is `true`.
- The dialog's effect re-fires repeatedly (capability calls observed every ~1–3 s in bursts, e.g. three calls inside one second), which is consistent with the source key churning rather than settling once.

So the gate's failure mode conflates three different states — *no driver*, *stale/failed read*, and *still checking* — into one message that says the driver is unavailable. Even if the settle predicate is correct, a transient read failure should not be reported as "driver unavailable, reconnect your gateway", and a null capability should not block creation when a follow-up read would return `canonical`.

## Frequency

- Reproducible on every attempt in this install (4 clean gateway restarts, 2 Desktop launches), 0 successful Desktop-side creations ever.
- `hosted_rooms` had 0 rows before the out-of-band test; 1 row after; `hosted_room_events` 0.
- 17 `groups.capabilities` calls in ~7 minutes from the Desktop, all answered with a running service.

## Affected component

`comp/desktop` — Bot Mode group-create gate (`canonical-group-capabilities.ts`, `create-dialog.tsx`). The gateway side (`gateway/session_group_controls.py`, `gateway/session_hosted_service.py`) behaves correctly in this install.

## Related

- #143391 (create gated on the driver capability; there it was `driver: false`)
- #141178, #142248 (cross-connection rooms disabled after #106742)
- #143256 (one supervisor thread per multiplexed profile — visible here too: the hosted service supervisor wakes every 1 s per profile)

## Attachments

Evidence file with the probe script, raw responses, the boot sequence and the call log: `evidence.txt` (pasted below in a comment if the issue form does not accept attachments).

issues.title: Feature request: profile-attributed active-work metadata and bounded activity intervals

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: area/profiles
labels.description: Multi-profile isolation, HERMES_HOME scoping

issues.body:
## Problem
A multi-profile Hermes deployment needs to distinguish work attributable to each served profile. A best-effort global active-work list without profile attribution cannot answer that question. Two empty snapshots also cannot establish that a profile remained inactive between samples.

## Requested capability
1. Attach a canonical profile identifier to each active-work entry, with documented handling for unknown or ambiguous attribution.
2. Expose a documented, read-only per-profile activity summary with an observation timestamp and an epoch or sequence fence, so consumers can detect restarts or gaps rather than silently join incompatible samples.
3. If activity intervals are exposed, document exactly which execution surfaces and transitions are covered. For example, a Bot Chat turn, a one-shot CLI execution and mailbox or receipt obligations may have different lifecycles; excluded domains should remain explicitly unknown.
4. Keep the payload metadata-only: no prompts, message bodies, tool arguments, credentials or transcript summaries. Reuse the existing authenticated local control boundary rather than introducing a public listener.

## Desired semantics
- A missing or unavailable source is not the same as a zero count.
- `idle_since` should only be supplied when its continuity and coverage are known; otherwise return an explicit unknown or partial result.
- A process restart or sequence gap should invalidate unsupported continuity claims.
- A consumer should be able to tell a best-effort present-time snapshot from a supported interval assertion.
- Runtime activity and application-level task readiness are separate concepts. This request does not ask Hermes to infer that a user's task list is complete.

## Acceptance examples
- Concurrent activity in two profiles is attributed to the correct profiles.
- A one-shot command cannot disappear from a claimed fully covered interval merely because no Bot Chat turn is active.
- Restart, missing retention or unavailable state produces a partial/unknown result, not a claim of continuous inactivity.
- Returned metadata contains no conversation or secret content.

## Scope and alternatives
This is a capability request, not a proposed implementation or delivery commitment. A minimal first step could be profile attribution on the existing active-work verb with its best-effort limits documented. A separate interval interface could follow only if its coverage is supportable.

No local reproduction data is required for this generic request.

Related: #67798, #125929, #143427 (adjacent, not duplicates).

issues.title: Feature request: supported producer delivery receipts with idempotent handoff and pre-send validity checks

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: comp/cron
labels.description: Cron scheduler and job management

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
# Feature request: supported producer delivery receipts with idempotent handoff and pre-send validity checks

## Summary

Is there a supported interface for a stateful local alert producer to hand a batch to Hermes cron delivery, correlate it with a durable receipt, and revalidate pause/expiry before sending or retrying?

We could not identify a complete contract in the interfaces examined. This is an integration/API request, not a claim that Hermes violates its documented cron guarantees. The immediate defect is in our custom producer: it commits its deduplication state after printing alerts, before downstream delivery is confirmed.

## Environment examined

- macOS, local execution.
- Installed CLI: Hermes Agent v0.22.3+275.gbf0203a, commit bf0203a794a0.
- Cron agent-backed pipeline; Telegram destination.
- Installed source was inspected read-only. The version loaded by the running gateway was not independently established.

No real message loss was established. A local test with the real producer and synthetic inputs demonstrated the loss window; no network or messaging calls were made.

## Current pipeline and failure window

1. Producer reads current data and its deduplication state.
2. Producer emits alerts and persists the new seen fingerprints/reminder counters.
3. Agent performs further work and returns its final response.
4. Scheduler hands the response to delivery and transport sends it.

An interruption between steps 2 and 4 can leave the alert suppressed on the next collection without a delivery receipt. Moving persistence later without a durable claim/receipt creates a duplicate-send window instead.

### Minimal standalone model

This intentionally models the producer boundary only. It does **not** run Hermes, simulate Telegram, or test the scheduler implementation. It uses no credentials, disk state or network.

```python
import json


def collect(seen):
    alert_id = "synthetic-alert-v1"
    return ([] if alert_id in seen else [alert_id]), seen | {alert_id}


state = set()
first, proposed = collect(state)
assert first == ["synthetic-alert-v1"]

# Model producer persistence, followed by interruption before downstream send.
persisted = set(json.loads(json.dumps(sorted(proposed))))
confirmed_receipts = set()
next_alerts, _ = collect(persisted)
assert not next_alerts and not confirmed_receipts
print("loss window: next collection suppresses an unconfirmed alert")

# Merely withholding persistence permits re-emission if a prior send happened
# but its acknowledgement was lost.
retry_alerts, _ = collect(state)
assert retry_alerts == first
print("duplicate window: uncommitted state allows the same alert again")
```

## Interfaces examined

- Public cron management/history and documented admission recovery: execution identity and durable delivery handoff exist, but we did not find a public producer-batch receipt and pre-send validity contract.
- Plugin/observer lifecycle hooks: completion of agent work is not confirmation of downstream Telegram delivery. Observer callbacks are not a fail-closed transport gate.
- `hermes send --json`: supported standalone transport and message ID on success, but the examined CLI does not expose a durable idempotency key/receipt lookup or a producer validity gate on retries. Exit 0 alone is not sufficient: skipped sends can also be successful command results. A custom journal may preserve uncertainty, but that alone does not solve validity checks during internal retry waits.
- Internal `cron/delivery_queue.py` has execution-scoped enqueue/claim/unknown handling. We did not import it or read/write its database, and do not want to depend on an internal schema or add a competing delivery queue.

Relevant source locations at the examined commit:

- `cron/delivery_queue.py`: enqueue, get_status, claim_next, recover_abandoned.
- `hermes_cli/send_cmd.py`: _emit_result.
- `tools/send_message_tool.py`: duplicate-send suppression and chunk sending.
- `tools/send_message_senders.py`: Telegram retry and multi-part send paths.

## Requested supported contract

An existing supported interface or a small extension could satisfy this; a particular implementation is not prescribed.

1. Stable producer batch/item identity, correlated with execution and destination, with idempotent durable handoff. Reusing an identity with different content must be rejected.
2. Durable, queryable outcomes distinguishing confirmed delivery, proven non-send, uncertain/partial delivery, and suppression/expiry. Missing history must not imply permission to resend.
3. A fail-closed gate before initial send, recovery and each retry that can enforce producer pause, time window, expiry and current semantic validity. Check/gate failures must not allow stale sends. Please specify the atomicity boundary and behavior once a request is already in flight.
4. Per-part evidence or an explicitly conservative partial outcome for split messages. Do not replay a partially delivered batch automatically.
5. A documented way for the producer to commit confirmed deduplication state only against the matching receipt, while retaining unresolved attempts visibly without replay.
6. Legacy producer state must remain unproven; it must not be promoted to delivered or reset to force replay.

Universal exactly-once delivery is **not** requested. In particular, Telegram may accept a request whose response is lost. Preserving visible uncertainty without automatic replay is the expected behavior in that case. Confirmed delivery means transport acknowledgement, not human reading.

## Acceptance scenarios

- Interrupt before handoff: no silent disappearance; safe retry only when non-send is established and the item remains valid.
- Interrupt after durable handoff but before claim: recover the same identity without a second sender.
- Interrupt after claim or lose the response: retain uncertain state and block automatic replay.
- Confirmed send followed by interruption before producer commit: reconcile from durable evidence without sending again, or remain explicitly uncertain if that evidence was not committed.
- Partial multi-part delivery: retain evidence/uncertainty and do not replay the whole batch.
- Concurrent duplicate submissions: one ownership path; conflicting payload rejected.
- Pause/expiry during collection, queueing, retry backoff and recovery: no new send after the gate denies it; define the in-flight limitation.
- Source event cancelled, started or answered before a retry: revalidate and suppress obsolete alerts.
- Missing/expired history: no inference of delivery or permission to replay.

## Operational containment

Affected incremental cycles are paused. Independent summaries are not treated as proof that incremental delivery is safe. No core patch, parallel queue, update or gateway restart was used to work around the missing contract.

## Documentation consulted

- https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron
- https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/hooks
- https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/observer-hooks
- https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/pipe-script-output

Please point us to an existing supported contract if we missed one; otherwise, would this be an appropriate extension to cron delivery?

issues.title: Linux desktop launches with 6% window opacity — translucency default applied via setOpacity, and Settings hides the control

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: comp/desktop
labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

labels.name: desktop/settings
labels.description: Settings, configuration and first-run pages inside the desktop app: model and provider settings, API

labels.name: desktop/shell
labels.description: The desktop app's window and OS integration: window chrome, title bar, tray, dock, menus, keyboard s

issues.body:
**Environment**

- Hermes `v0.22.5+9-g67491b50` (install stamp `fab9b01c915a`), packaged desktop build
  (`apps/desktop/release/linux-unpacked/Hermes`)
- Ubuntu 26.04, GNOME 50 on Wayland; the app runs under XWayland (`--ozone-platform=x11`)
- Electron reports `linux`, no `HERMES_DESKTOP_TRANSPARENT` set

**What happens**

On every launch the main window is ~94% opaque, so the desktop shows through it.
Measured on the live X11 window:

```
$ xprop -id 0x800004 _NET_WM_WINDOW_OPACITY
_NET_WM_WINDOW_OPACITY = 4025479151        # 4025479151 / 4294967295 = 0.9372
```

`~/.config/Hermes/translucency.json` matches exactly:

```json
{ "intensity": 29, "fade": 0, "mode": "clear", "material": "titlebar", "scope": "sidebar" }
```

and `opacityRamp(29) = 1 − 0.75·(29/100)² = 0.9372`, i.e. the value is the Clear-mode
intensity, not something a user set.

**Expected**

Fully opaque. Translucency is documented as macOS + Windows only, and
Settings → Appearance → Window layout correctly hides the row on Linux
(`appearance-settings.tsx:795`, `TRANSLUCENCY_SUPPORTED && …`). A platform that
does not support the feature should not get it on by default — and here it also
cannot be turned off, because the only control is the hidden row.

**Root cause (three separate holes)**

1. `apps/shared/src/translucency.ts:133` — `DEFAULT_VALUES` has only `mac` and
   `windows` tables, and both use `intensity: 29`. `defaultTranslucencyValues()`
   (`:148`) selects `isWindows ? 'windows' : 'mac'`, so **any non-Windows platform,
   including Linux, resolves to 29**.

2. `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1537` — `applyWindowOpacity()` calls
   `win.setOpacity(windowOpacityFor(state))` with no platform guard. The comment
   above the translucency block says "`setOpacity` is a no-op on Linux", but on X11
   Electron does implement it via `_NET_WM_WINDOW_OPACITY` — that is exactly the
   property measured above. So the guard that exists for the *UI*
   (`translucencySupportedOn`, `:202`) is missing on the *apply* path.

3. Because the value is not user-set, it cannot be cleared from the app: editing
   `translucency.json` to `intensity: 0` and restarting does not stick — the
   renderer store (`src/store/translucency.ts`, key
   `hermes.desktop.translucency.v2`) has no persisted book on Linux, so it re-seeds
   from `defaultTranslucencyValues()` on boot, pushes the resolved state to main,
   and main writes `29` back to the file. Reproduced: after a restart the file was
   `29` again and `_NET_WM_WINDOW_OPACITY` was `4025479151` again.

**Suggested fix**

Any one of these closes it; the first two are one-liners:

```ts
// electron/main.ts — don't touch native opacity where the feature is unsupported
function applyWindowOpacity(win) {
  if (!TRANSLUCENCY_SUPPORTED) return
  …
}
```

```ts
// shared/src/translucency.ts — a platform that can't do it defaults to off
export function defaultTranslucencyValues(appearance, isWindows) {
  return DEFAULT_VALUES[isWindows ? 'windows' : 'mac'][appearance]  // ← 29
}
// e.g. add an explicit `supported` argument and return intensity 0 when false
```

and, for good measure, have `windowOpacityFor()` return `1` when the platform has
no translucency, so a value persisted on another machine (profile import) cannot
fade a Linux window either.

**Related**

- #138887 adds an *opt-in* Linux transparent window (`HERMES_DESKTOP_TRANSPARENT=1`)
  and explicitly notes "Window `opacity` is never used, so text and images stay
  solid". That PR does not fix this: today's Linux default still goes through
  `setOpacity`, before any opt-in.

**Workaround for other Linux users hitting this**

A user-level watchdog that resets the property works, but it should not be needed:

```bash
xprop -id <win> -f _NET_WM_WINDOW_OPACITY 32c -set _NET_WM_WINDOW_OPACITY 4294967295
```

Tracks the provider/request-layer work: provider-specific behaviour moves out of core name checks and into `ProviderProfile` hooks and typed data, the auxiliary client stops sharing process-global runtime state, and request quirks become declarative. Every PR here stands alone and is reviewed alone. The refactors are proven behaviour-identical through the provider wire snapshot (`tests/agent/transports/test_provider_wire_snapshot.py`), and the fixes are proven with a test that fails on `main`.

Related plan item: [plan v0.12 C1.1](https://teknium.io/hermes-plans/#C1) (Code Health PRV-09).

## Merged

- [x] #134320: LM Studio and Tencent TokenHub get provider profiles; agents configured by base URL only get snapshot cells
- [x] #134356: closes the review gaps on the merged relay, classifier and prompt-cache tests
- [x] #134385: provider-catalog E2E green again (LM Studio and TokenHub profiles name their API-key env vars)
- [x] #134409: a profile missing its API-key env var now fails the default test lane, not only the skippable e2e lane
- [x] #134692: `/model` keeps TokenHub's curated model list when its normal endpoint is saved as `model.base_url`

## Open

| PR | What | State |
|---|---|---|
| #134578 | Gemini's native client comes from its provider profile, not core name checks (provider hooks, slice 1) | auto-merge armed, needs approving review |
| #134793 | Key-dependent base URLs (Z.AI endpoint probe, Kimi `sk-kimi-` keys, …) come from `ProviderProfile.resolve_base_url`, not core tables (slice 2) | review findings addressed |
| #142930 | The auxiliary client keeps the main runtime only per context: nine process-global mirrors and helpers removed, fixing a cross-session race (PRV-09 / C1.1, closes #105888) | review findings addressed; needs lane A/B/C approvals per the plan |
| #143094 | A known vendor is matched by hostname, not substring (`api.moonshot.ai.evil.example` no longer resolves to Kimi) | ready for review |
| #143095 | Copilot: only a plain `https` API base from the token exchange is trusted (no userinfo, no non-443 port; tampered persisted base forces a fresh exchange) | ready for review |

## Built, not yet opened

- [ ] **Z.AI endpoint probe single-flight.** Concurrent resolutions of one key probe once. Stacked on #134793, so it opens after that merges.
- [ ] **Rejection verdicts stay with their route.** Learned "this route rejected X" flags (reasoning effort, reasoning disable, reasoning floor, `stream_options`) no longer carry over to the next route after `/model`, fallback, or credential rotation to another base URL. The primary gets its own verdicts back on restore. Also fixes a voice turn dropping the main model's encrypted-reasoning replay verdict.
- [ ] **Typed request quirks, PR 1.** Widens the wire snapshot (per-model variants, explicit max-tokens, streaming kwargs, auxiliary request kwargs) and deletes 8 never-read legacy kwargs.

## Planned: typed request-compatibility train

Each step must leave the wire snapshot unchanged unless a deliberate change is stated.

- [ ] PR 2: `RequestCompat` dataclass and resolver: max-tokens field, system/developer role, prompt-cache key, stream usage, declared unsupported params. Per-model overrides come through the existing `model_capabilities` / `model_overrides`.
- [ ] PR 3: declarative reasoning for the profiles that only set a top-level effort, replacing their hand-written hooks.
- [ ] PR 4: the LM Studio and TokenHub special cases move behind their profiles.
- [ ] PR 5: retire the legacy `is_kimi` / `is_github_models` request path. This is a deliberate change: Kimi by base URL stops sending thinking and effort together, and Copilot's reasoning-off is aligned. The snapshot diff will be reviewed in the PR.
- [ ] Later: a single per-route rejection set keyed by (provider, host, model), replacing the scattered learned-rejection flags.

## Not yet started

- [ ] Provider hooks slice 3: Anthropic-wire credential selection via the profile
- [ ] Declared unsupported params per provider/model

issues.body:
## Summary

Opening a conversation that belongs to a messaging platform (Telegram DM/group, WeChat, Feishu, …) in Hermes Desktop leaves the composer's reasoning-effort pill in its loading state indefinitely. It never paints the chat's actual level. Picking any model or effort once clears it — that is the #141152 fix — but a cold resume (desktop restart) spins again.

Desktop-created (local) sessions are unaffected: their pill paints on open.

## Reproduced on

- Hermes v0.22.2+2953.g0b8dee0 (git main, commit 0b8dee00faf, 2026-10-20), Linux (Fedora 44), WeChat platform session, single-profile gateway serving weixin.
- Steps:
  1. Have a messaging chat with history so it appears in the Desktop session list.
  2. Open that conversation in Hermes Desktop.
  3. The composer's model pill paints (from the composer's own sticky state), the effort pill shows the pending spinner and never resolves.
  4. Pick any effort level once — the pill paints and the pick persists per chat across gateway restarts.
  5. Restart the desktop and reopen the chat — the pill spins again.
- Verified against the live state DB: the messaging session row has no `gateway.local_policy.v1.<session_id>` receipt.

## Why this happens (code reading at 0b8dee00)

1. Desktop marks a resumed slice's effort pending by design (`markReasoningEffortPending`, `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-runtime.ts`): the resume reply carries no `reasoning_effort` (since #79807), and the clearing value arrives as a later `session.info` event.
2. `session.resume` fills the reply's `info` only for `Platform.LOCAL` (`gateway/session_controls.py`); a messaging session gets `{'desktop_protocol': …}` and nothing else.
3. For local sessions the clearing event is published by the policy refresh on attach (`_publish` in `gateway/session_policy_refresh.py`, reached from `refresh_resumed_policy` → `commit_refresh` → `_prepare`). `_prepare` needs the session's local-policy receipt: `local_receipt` raises `storage_unavailable` when the row is missing — which is every messaging session — and even with a receipt it returns `None` when the policy's source is not a resumable CLI surface (`SURFACES` = cli/tui/gui/acp/tool/oneshot). Either way the refresh is skipped and nothing publishes.
4. The only `session.info` publisher left that carries `reasoning_effort` for a messaging session is the pick path (`gateway/session_messaging_picks.py`, the #141152 fix). The turn-end publishers (`run_turn_progress.py` title repaint, `session_local_inventory.publish_settled_info`) run for local-viewer turns only, and `_publish_pending` (`gateway/session_authority.py`) publishes `session.info` without the effort fields.
5. There is no fallback source for a cold resume: the `sessions` table stores `model` but no effort column, and the desktop tile path reads `info.reasoning_effort` from the resume reply, which is absent.

## Why this matters

- Every messaging chat opened from the desktop shows a control that never resolves. The pill is the only place the level is visible, so the user cannot tell what effort the next turn will use without opening the selector — and the selector paints from the same missing event.
- The per-chat `/model` and `/reasoning` overrides that #141152 made writable are invisible until a pick is made. A user who set the level from the chat itself (`/reasoning high`) gets no confirmation anywhere in the desktop.
- It reads as a hang. A spinner that never stops is indistinguishable from a broken surface, and it sits on the most-used screen.

## Suggested fix

The pieces already exist; only the publisher is missing.

- `messaging_route_info()` (`gateway/session_messaging_picks.py`) computes exactly the fields a messaging chat's next turn resolves — `model`, `reasoning_effort`, `reasoning_effort_wire`, `service_tier`, `fast` — without building an agent, and `local_session_info` already routes unbuilt messaging chats to it.
- Publish that `session.info` when a messaging session is attached or resumed — for example in `session.resume` after `attach` for non-LOCAL sources, mirroring what `_publish` does for local sessions — or include `messaging_route_info`'s output in the resume reply's `info` for messaging sources.
- Either way the pill then paints the chat's next-turn effort on open, and #141152's per-chat overrides become visible.

## Related

- #141152 (closed): the pick half — mutation refusal plus `session.info` content for an unbuilt messaging chat. This report is the delivery-on-open half that issue also mentioned ("The effort pill … stays in a loading state … Not confirmed").
- #79807 (closed): the local-session analogue that introduced the pending-until-`session.info` design.
- #47524 (open): pill stuck in loading after rapid profile switching — different trigger, same visual.
