prs.title: provider: llamacpp finds a self-run llama-server on its new default port 9931 (port oh-my-pi#16675)
prs.body:
`provider: llamacpp` now finds a llama-server you started yourself on llama.cpp's new default port 9931, not only on the old 8080.

Port of [can1357/oh-my-pi#16675](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16675) ("discover llama.cpp servers on the new default port 9931").

## Why

llama.cpp changed `llama-server`'s default port from 8080 to 9931 ([ggml-org/llama.cpp#30159](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30159), commit `b42b7e6`; the server README now says `port to listen (default: 9931)`). Hermes' detection of a user-run llama-server (`hermes_cli/local_runtime/detect.py::DEFAULT_PROBE_PORTS`) probed only 8080, so on a current build a plain `llama-server -m model.gguf` was invisible unless the user knew to add `local_runtime.detect_ports: [9931]`.

## What changes (real `hermes chat -q hello`, `model.provider: llamacpp`, no base_url, a llama-server-shaped stub answering `/props` + `/v1/chat/completions` on 127.0.0.1:9931)

| | `origin/main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Output | `The local model server is turned off. Turn it back on in Settings → Providers → Local models, or switch to another model.` | `☤ Hermes` / `STUB-9931-REPLY` |
| Requests reaching the server | 0 | `POST /v1/chat/completions` |

## Changes

- `DEFAULT_PROBE_PORTS = (8080, 9931)`: 8080 first so older builds and anything already working keep resolving exactly as before; 9931 second.
- Comment in `config_defaults.py` and the two docs pages that name llama-server's default port (`user-guide/local-models.md`, `integrations/providers.md`).

## Ours vs theirs

Same idea as oh-my-pi (legacy port first, then 9931). Theirs adds a `fallbackBaseUrls` list to their discovery provider config; ours is the existing probe-port tuple, so the change is one constant.

## Tests

No new test: the change is a constant, and a test asserting the tuple's contents would be a change detector. `tests/hermes_cli/test_local_runtime.py`: 50 passed. Docs link check clean.

**Live repro:** the table above, real `hermes chat` process against the stub, fresh HOME/HERMES_HOME per leg.

Not covered: a real llama.cpp binary (the stub answers the same `/props` `build_info` fingerprint detection keys on).

prs.title: feat(kanban): model-callable kanban_archive tool over the CLI archive path
prs.body:
feat(kanban): model-callable kanban_archive tool over the CLI archive path

## Why

Archiving a kanban card is CLI-only. `hermes kanban archive` routes through a proven single code path (`kanban_db.archive_task()`, including the #76196 worker-termination handling), but there is no model-callable equivalent: a profile restricted to the `kanban` toolset can create, comment, block, and complete cards from inside a session, yet cannot archive a finished card without a terminal. For deployments that deliberately run such profiles without terminal access, in-session board cleanup is impossible and completed cards pile up in the active list. This PR adds `kanban_archive(task_id, board?)` as a thin wrapper over the exact `archive_task()` the CLI uses — zero new DB logic, zero behavior divergence. The access model follows the open question in #143206: a lifecycle gate — visible to any profile holding the kanban toolset and to dispatcher workers, using the same registration pattern as `kanban_block`/`kanban_complete`; `kanban_list`/`kanban_unblock` stay orchestrator-only.

Linked issue: #143206, the anchor for the access-model decision. Intentionally not `Closes` — settling the access model is the maintainers' call, and this PR is one concrete answer on the table.

## What changes

Minimum footprint: 4 files, +319/−1, of which 277 lines are new tests. The implementation surface is 43 lines across three existing files, and the only touch to an existing line is the toolset registration in `toolsets.py`.

```
tests/tools/test_kanban_archive_tool.py | 277 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 tools/kanban_tools.py                   |  24 ++
 tools/kanban_tools_schemas.py           |  17 ++
 toolsets.py                             |   2 +-
 4 files changed, 319 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

## No behavior change to existing paths

- No new DB write logic — the tool delegates to the same `archive_task()` the CLI calls, including worker termination on archiving a running task and child-promote/workspace-reap side effects.
- `_ORCHESTRATOR_TOOLS`, board resolution, and the CLI archive path are untouched. Board pinning reuses the shared `_board()` helper; unknown and already-archived ids report the sibling not-found/CAS error shape.
- The tool is deliberately not stricter than the CLI on running+claimed cards; CLI archive regression receipts are byte-identical main vs branch across 9 scenarios, including `--rm` purge and the both-args / no-args error paths.
- Profiles without the kanban toolset see zero `kanban_*` tools — config-gated, flip-verified before and after the change.

## Test plan and results

- New unit tests `tests/tools/test_kanban_archive_tool.py`: 15/15 pass on the rebased branch.
- Real behavior through the tool registry on throwaway scratch boards (no shared state): create→archive, re-archive CAS error, unknown-id error byte-identical to sibling tools, archiving blocked/todo/running+claimed cards, parent-archive freeing a child, unknown arguments refused before any write — 20/20.
- Guardrail parity: scoped worker refused on a running+claimed sibling; delegate child refused outright; authorized caller archives running+claimed exactly as the CLI does — 7/7.
- `scripts/check`: 12 checks ok; code health vs the merge base: 0 blocking, 0 advisory.
- Full suite vs a main baseline on the same host: the set of failing files is identical to the baseline; the single branch-only failing file was proven flaky — 756/756 green in an isolated re-run on both bases.

prs.title: feat(plugins): replies stay hidden until a hold_stream transform rewrites them, on every surface (salvage #102481)
prs.body:
A plugin that rewrites replies (redaction, policy filters) can now register `transform_llm_output` with `hold_stream=True`, and its profile's sessions stop streaming: the user sees the typing or thinking indicator, then only the rewritten reply, on every surface.

```python
def register(ctx):
    ctx.register_hook("transform_llm_output", redact, hold_stream=True)
```

Without it, a streaming reply reaches the user raw and is then replaced. On messaging, split replies leave raw earlier chunks behind, and native-stream chats keep the raw stream. #144219 fixed the TUI/Desktop end state but not what streams first. Plugins that don't declare the flag keep normal streaming.

## What the user sees

Real `GatewayRunner._run_agent` with a real `AIAgent`, a slow loopback model (streams `…api key is SECRET-123 … SECRET-456…` in 4-char chunks) and recording chat transports. The redactor rewrites `SECRET-\d+` → `[REDACTED]`. Columns are main + plain redactor (the most main can do: a `hold_stream=True` plugin fails to load there) vs head + `hold_stream=True`:

| Chat shape | main: raw ever visible | main: ops | head (hold): raw ever visible | head (hold): what was sent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Telegram-style edits | **yes** | 24 sends/edits | no | 1 send: the rewrite, at 4.4 s |
| No edit support | no | 1 | no | 1 send: the rewrite |
| Split reply (60-char limit) | **yes**: raw `(1/3)` chunk stays | 20 | no | 3 sends: the rewrite `(1/3)…(3/3)` |
| Native stream (WeCom-style frames) | **yes** | 26 frames | no | 1 send: the rewrite |
| Slack over Relay (`chat.*Stream`) | **yes** | 24 | no | 1 send: the rewrite |

The typing indicator ran throughout every held turn (2–6 ticks per run). head + plain redactor matched main row for row, so streaming is unchanged for plugins that don't declare the flag.

**TUI (live `hermes --tui` in tmux, isolated home, same loopback model and plugin, captured every 0.25 s):**

| Arm | Frames showing `SECRET-` | During the turn | Final |
|---|---|---|---|
| head, plain redactor | 6 of 80 (`┊  Here is the config. Your api key is SECRET-123 and t…`) | the raw stream | `…[REDACTED]…[REDACTED]…` |
| head, `hold_stream=True` | **0 of 80** | `(¬‿¬) cogitating… · 2s` / `ruminating…` status, no reply text, for the ~3.2 s stream | `┊  Here is the config. Your api key is [REDACTED] and the backup key is [REDACTED]. Keep them safe.` |

## Per surface

| Surface | Held turn | Not held (plugin without the flag) |
|---|---|---|
| Messaging, edit-capable | typing → one send of the rewrite | stream drafts/edits as before |
| Messaging, no edits / split replies | typing → rewrite sent once (split like any long reply) | unchanged |
| Native stream adapters (WeCom) and Relay stream-is-the-message (Slack) | no stream message opened; one plain send of the sealed final | unchanged |
| TUI, Desktop, classic CLI (local viewers of the canonical gateway) | busy indicator; no `message.delta`; `message.complete` carries the rewrite | unchanged |
| ACP (gateway path) | no `agent_message_chunk` until the end; the final remainder is the whole rewrite | unchanged |
| API server `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses` (stream) | the SSE stream stays open (role chunk / `response.created`) with no text, then the rewrite is the only text | raw deltas, then the rewrite appended (existing behaviour) |
| Commentary between tool calls | **dropped** (the hook never sees it) | unchanged |
| Tool progress, reasoning | unchanged: not the reply, governed by `display.tool_progress` / `display.show_reasoning` (docs say to turn them off if needed) | unchanged |

## How

- `register_hook(..., hold_stream=True)`: recorded on the registration handle, so the flag lives exactly as long as the registration and belongs to the profile's plugin manager. `stream_held()` answers for the active profile. It applies only to `transform_llm_output` (any other hook warns and ignores it). The memory-provider hook proxy and the `plugins validate` stub forward the keyword.
- Agent (`agent/stream_delivery.py`, `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`, resolved per turn in `agent/conversation_loop.py`): no text delta, text that arrives after a tool call, or interim commentary leaves the agent's display/TTS callbacks during a held turn. Every surface reaches the reply through those callbacks, so each one falls through to its existing "nothing streamed" path and delivers the final once.
- Gateway (`gateway/run_turn_runner.py`): a held turn builds no stream consumer and no commentary relay, so nothing opens a draft, edit or native stream message. The final goes out as an ordinary send while `_keep_typing` runs. This keeps the gateway/AGENTS.md streaming contract: the consumer was never started, so the sealed final is the only message.

## Review fixes and a pre-existing bug fixed along the way

- **Codex app-server never ran `transform_llm_output` (pre-existing, fixed here)** — 47ea8becd6. That runtime returns before `finalize_turn`, so a rewriting plugin's change never reached the user or the stored assistant row on `codex_app_server` turns; with `hold_stream` the user would have waited, then received the raw reply. The transform now runs before the projected rows are persisted, and the result carries `response_transformed` / `pre_transform_response` like the generic loop. Test: `tests/agent/test_codex_app_server_transform.py`.
- **Guardrail halt reply streamed ahead of the hold** — 4bac9ce631. The tool-loop guardrail halt pushed its explanation straight to `stream_delta_callback`; a held turn now delivers it only as the final, after the transform. Test: `test_a_held_guardrail_halt_reply_is_not_streamed_ahead_of_the_rewrite`.
- **A turn starting mid-`reload-plugins` could miss the hold** — f01d6b7bc6. `holds_stream()` now reads the ledger under the discovery lock, so a turn waits for the reload's re-registration instead of reading the emptied ledger. Test: `test_a_turn_starting_during_a_plugin_reload_sees_the_settled_hold`.

Each new test is red with its fix reverted and green with it.

## Tests (loopback model + fake transports, no paid calls)

Each held case is red on main (all source files swapped to `origin/main`: 11 failed, 5 controls passed). Mutation-checked: removing the agent delta gate turns the agent, local-viewer and API tests red. Removing the commentary gate or the post-tool-call text gate turns the agent test red. Removing the TurnRunner hold turns the native-stream case red.

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_hold_stream.py`: the hold lasts exactly as long as the declaring registration, only the declaring profile holds, and the flag on other hooks holds nothing.
- `tests/agent/test_hold_stream_agent.py`: real `AIAgent`. A held turn emits nothing to the display callbacks, for both commentary-then-tool and text-after-tool-call stream shapes. The plain transform streams raw (control).
- `tests/gateway/test_hold_stream_delivery.py`: real `_run_agent` → edit-capable, non-edit, split and native-stream chats, plus Slack over Relay (stub connector). Covers the typing indicator and one send of the rewrite, and the control streams raw.
- `tests/gateway/test_hold_stream_local_viewer.py`: `LocalSessionAdapter` wire events (TUI/Desktop/CLI/ACP). No `message.delta`; `message.complete` carries the rewrite.
- `tests/gateway/test_hold_stream_api_server.py`: streaming `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` carry only the rewrite.

`scripts/run_tests.sh` on the touched areas (plugins, agent streaming, turn phases, tool guardrails, codex runtime, transform hooks, stream consumer, local viewer, relay, API server, run_progress): 271 files, 2734 passed, 0 failed. `python scripts/check`: ok.

Docs: `hooks.md` (new "Holding the reply until it is rewritten" section with the per-surface table) and the plugin guide.

## Credit

The shape comes from @Halldrix's #102481 (`mutates=` on `register_hook`, forwarding through the memory proxy and validate stub). That PR gated the flag in the classic CLI agent setup, which no longer runs turns (the CLI goes through the gateway), so this PR is a fresh implementation with a `Co-authored-by` trailer on the declaration commit. #102481 will be closed with thanks once this lands.

## Infographic

![hold-stream](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafbedc/X9jS_K2OYNrl8-Ujifp9r_Sm1lrK01.png)

prs.title: fix(telegram): label clarify buttons with compact choice text
prs.body:
## Summary

- Replace bare numeric Telegram `clarify` button captions with compact, human-readable choice text.
- Collapse whitespace, remove the presentation-only `(Recommended)` suffix, and shorten long captions to 48 characters at a word boundary.
- Keep the complete numbered choices in the message body.
- Keep callback data index-based (`cl:<clarify_id>:<idx>`), so dispatch and authorization behavior are unchanged.

## Why

Numeric buttons force mobile users to cross-reference each tap target against the numbered list above it. Descriptive captions make the action clear without sacrificing the full-text body or changing callback semantics.

A choice such as:

```text
Merge automatically when CI and independent review pass (Recommended)
```

becomes a concise button caption such as:

```text
Merge automatically when CI and independent…
```

The original choice remains intact in the message body.

## Verification

The patch was developed test-first against the stable v0.22.4 source, whose affected `send_clarify` and test baseline is unchanged on current `main`:

```text
Focused clarify coverage: 6 passed
Telegram regression set: 110 passed
git diff --check: clean
```

The exact verified patch was then transplanted onto current `main`; its stable patch ID remains `6c4d6b40957479152ba6aaf54542bb342cc4c620`.

## Related work

This overlaps #30892, #31640, and #110144. The distinguishing behavior here is normalization of whitespace, removal of the button-only recommendation suffix, and word-boundary truncation while preserving the complete body and existing callback contract. Happy to consolidate around the maintainers' preferred implementation.

prs.title: Connection failures name their cause (refused / TLS / no route) and TLS cert failures fail fast (port oh-my-pi#16036)
prs.body:
When a model endpoint refuses the connection, presents an untrusted TLS certificate, or has no route, Hermes now says which of those happened and where, and a certificate failure fails fast with its fix-it guidance instead of being retried for minutes.

Port of [can1357/oh-my-pi#16036](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16036) ("name offline/DNS failures instead of a generic Connection error"), adapted to Hermes' existing error summary and classifier.

## What changes (real `hermes chat -q hello`, custom provider, `api_max_retries: 1`)

| Endpoint | `origin/main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `http://127.0.0.1:18999/v1`, nothing listening (`auto_recovery_cycles: 0`) | `❌ API failed after 1 retries — Connection error.` / `Provider said: Connection error.` | `❌ API failed after 1 retries — Couldn't connect to 127.0.0.1:18999 (connection refused). Check that the model server is running and listening there.` |
| `https://127.0.0.1:18443/v1`, self-signed cert, **default config** | `⏳ Provider temporarily unavailable — retrying automatically in 17s (cycle 1/5)` → 35s → 65s … (a certificate failure is retried as an outage) | One attempt, then `❌ The provider's security certificate could not be verified: TLS certificate verification failed for 127.0.0.1:18443 (self-signed certificate)` plus the existing TLS guidance block (trust store / `ssl_ca_cert` / use `http://` for localhost). 12 s end to end. |
| same, `auto_recovery_cycles: 0` | `Provider said: Connection error.` with "didn't respond in time … temporarily unavailable" copy | as above |
| DNS failure | "Hermes can't reach the model provider. You may be offline…" | unchanged |

`no route to host` gets `Couldn't reach <host:port> (no route to host). Check the URL, your network, or proxy.`

## Changes

- `agent/api_error_summary.py`: the DNS chain walk becomes `_connect_failure_summary`, which also names refused / TLS-verify / no-route causes found on `__cause__`/`__context__`, with the endpoint `host:port` read from the SDK error's `request.url`. Each sentence keeps its marker phrase (`connection refused`, `no route to host`), so the gateway's existing `gateway.errors.unreachable` reply now matches it instead of falling to "no further detail from the SDK".
- `agent/error_classifier.py`: the TLS fail-fast from #57992 only matched a bare `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError`. Real requests go through the openai/anthropic SDK, which raises `APIConnectionError("Connection error.")` with the cert error as its cause, so the verdict never fired. `_by_transport` now also reads the cause chain for the existing cert patterns.

Root cause in one line: both functions read only the outer exception's text, and the SDKs put every connect failure's reason one level down.

## Ours vs theirs

| | oh-my-pi #16036 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Where | new `network-cause.ts` (cause/`errors` graph walk) + rethrow at the fetch call site | the existing `_summarize_api_error` chain walk, extended in place |
| Kinds | offline / unreachable / refused / tls | DNS (existing copy kept) / tls / refused / no-route |
| Retry semantics | unchanged (all stay retryable) | TLS cert failure is now non-retryable on the wrapped shape too, matching the classifier's existing intent |

## Tests

2 invariant tests in `tests/agent/test_summarize_api_error.py`, both red on `origin/main` (summary parametrized ×3: 3 failed; classifier: 1 failed), green here. Union run of every test file referencing `_summarize_api_error`, `ssl_cert_verification`, `APIConnectionError` or the offline/refused wording: 59 files, 1554 passed. `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking.

**Live repro:** before/after table above, real `hermes chat` process against a loopback self-signed HTTPS stub and a closed port, fresh HOME/HERMES_HOME per leg, idle-exit gateway killed between legs.

Not covered: Anthropic-SDK wire (same `APIConnectionError(...) from err` shape, but no Anthropic leg was run), Windows `WinError 10061` wording (matched by marker, not run).

## Infographic

![connect-failures-named](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafbf2b/r9yM9Y42_mZ2SxwJj3EGg_W0mHWL1e.png)

- **Maintainer:** thileman (the author of the pinned repo)
- **Surface:** Desktop only — `desktop/plugin.js`, inside the plugin SDK surface. No agent tools, hooks, middleware or env vars.

This is the second re-pin requested in review: the plugin has been rebuilt against the merged SDK seams, so the DOM reach-ins the previous entry disclosed are gone.

## What changed since the last review

The review of the previous pin left six items. All six are addressed:

| # | Requested | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Drop the context-menu injection (Radix query, inserted rows, keydown capture, `data-highlighted` writes, synthetic `pointerdown`) | **Done.** The plugin contributes rows through `COMPOSER_AREAS.contextMenu` ([#143678](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/143678), merged 2026-10-23). The app renders, orders and caps them; the plugin never draws, queries or mutates a menu of its own. |
| 2 | Drop the private bridge + focus juggling + startup replay; keep words in `ctx.storage` until a dictionary verb exists; make removal symmetric | **Done.** `host.spellcheck.addWord` / `removeWord` (from #143678). Removal is now symmetric — it previously only removed from the plugin's own list, so the app's dictionary kept accepting the word. |
| 3 | Replace the `el.spellcheck` / `el.lang` flips with `host.composer.setSpellcheck`; drop `QUICK_ENTRY_SELECTOR` | **Done**, feature-detected. `setSpellcheck` is [#143057](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/143057) (open). When it is absent the plugin leaves Chromium's spell check off rather than falling back to a DOM write. `QUICK_ENTRY_SELECTOR` is gone. |
| 4 | Apply corrections via `host.composer` (read/set draft), not `execCommand` / `insertNode` | **Done.** `document.execCommand('insertText')` and `range.insertNode()` are gone. The plugin reads the draft with `host.composer.getDraft` and writes it back with `host.composer.setDraft`, and prefers the app's own `action.replaceWord` when the contribution path provides it. |
| 5 | Remove `maskCodeSpans` | **Done.** Removed in full at the maintainer's request — `maskCodeSpans`, `caretInMaskedCode`, `MASKED_CODE_SELECTOR`, the `excludeCodeSpans` preference, the `data-sp-mask` writes, the input/focusout listeners that re-applied the mask, and the **Ignore code spans** settings row. The plugin now writes **nothing** into the composer's DOM: no attributes, no wrappers, no nodes, no caret moves, and no `querySelector` call anywhere in the file. A new suite asserts the machinery is **absent**, so re-adding it fails the tests. Tracker for re-adding it: `composer.nonProse` (#144007). |
| 6 | Pin `DICT_BASE` to a commit SHA, and fix the README's claim about when `auto` fetches | **Done.** The dictionary source is pinned to `8cfea406b505e4d7df52d5a19bce525df98c54ab` of `wooorm/dictionaries`. The README's fetch disclosure now says the locale follows the **app or OS** locale, and the plugin's own `plugin.yaml` floor was corrected (see below). |

## What it does

- **A right-click suggestion menu** ranked with Damerau-Levenshtein over the standard SCOWL/Hunspell English dictionary — the corpus Firefox and LibreOffice ship — contributed as rows in the app's own composer context menu.
- **The dictionary's capitalisation is preserved.** `Hermes` is a word and `hermes` is not, exactly as Chromium has it. Right-clicking a lowercase proper noun such as `english` offers the capitalised `English` — the spelling Chromium accepts, so the squiggle clears when you take it.
- **Custom words**, added from the right-click menu or from a **Custom Words** page in Settings. Each word is added to the app's own spell-check dictionary through the SDK, so the app remembers it.
- **Squiggles** in the composer and the message-edit composer, once #143057 lands (see the version note below).


## Version note

`requires_hermes` is **`>=0.22.5`**, the current release.

- The context-menu seam (#143678) is merged but **in no release yet**, so the right-click rows need a Hermes newer than 0.22.5. On 0.22.5 the plugin still loads, its dictionary and Custom Words page work, and it says once that the right-click suggestions are unavailable — it is not refused.
- The squiggles need `host.composer.setSpellcheck` (#143057), which is open and in no release. The plugin feature-detects it; until it lands the plugin's own suggestions work while Chromium's underline stays off. There is deliberately no DOM-attribute fallback.

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- **Writes nothing into the composer's DOM.** No attributes, no wrappers, no nodes, no caret moves, and no DOM query of any kind: the plugin contributes menu rows, reads and writes the draft through `host.composer`, and asks the app to flip spell check on.
- **Fetches a non-English dictionary on demand.** For a non-English locale the plugin fetches that locale's `.dic`/`.aff` word list from `raw.githubusercontent.com` (the `wooorm/dictionaries` corpus, the same source the embedded English dictionary came from), pinned to a commit SHA. The English dictionary is embedded, so an English user is fully offline. The fetched files are **data** — a word list; no code is fetched and nothing is executed.

**No telemetry, no usage reporting, no background processes, no shell commands, no credentials, no reads outside the app's own data directory.**

## Verification

Run against a clean clone at the pinned commit:

```
$ hermes plugins validate .
✓ manifest — plugin.yaml parses
✓ requires_hermes — spec '>=0.22.5' parses
✓ loadable — entry: desktop/plugin.js
✓ no core override — no runtime rebinds of Hermes core
✓ desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface
⚠ security scan caution: sudo_usage (plugin.js:51537)
◆ Isolation — portable plugin (no Python): runs anywhere

Validation passed.
```

The `sudo_usage` caution is a false positive: the flagged line is the word `sudo` inside the embedded English frequency list used to rank suggestions. The plugin never runs a command.

The entry file itself passes the catalog validator:

```
$ python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/hermes-composer-spellcheck-plugin.yaml
OK: 1 file(s) valid
```

The plugin's own suite is 13 suites, all passing (`node scripts/run-tests.cjs`), and its CI is green on this commit (Tests / Plugin Validate / SDK Surface).

## Screenshots

All images are pinned to the same commit as the code, so they change only when a re-pin lands.

**The banner** — the suggestion menu over the composer, with the flagged word visible:

![Banner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thileman/hermes-composer-spellcheck-plugin/29e1845af2f8b9ada589c43d73bc41a8cfbfd6c3/docs/images/banner.png)

![Suggestion menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thileman/hermes-composer-spellcheck-plugin/29e1845af2f8b9ada589c43d73bc41a8cfbfd6c3/docs/images/context-menu.png)

![Suggestion rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thileman/hermes-composer-spellcheck-plugin/29e1845af2f8b9ada589c43d73bc41a8cfbfd6c3/docs/images/suggestion-rows.png)

**Settings** — the plugin's settings page:

![Settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thileman/hermes-composer-spellcheck-plugin/29e1845af2f8b9ada589c43d73bc41a8cfbfd6c3/docs/images/settings.png)

**Custom Words** — the searchable list of words the spell checker always accepts:

![Custom words](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thileman/hermes-composer-spellcheck-plugin/29e1845af2f8b9ada589c43d73bc41a8cfbfd6c3/docs/images/custom-words.png)

> The banner and the suggestion-menu shot are recaptured from the current build. The
> previous ones were taken on 2026-10-22, before the SDK rewrite, and showed a
> menu state the current build cannot produce: SEVEN suggestion rows when the app
> caps a plugin's section at SIX, and a RED SQUIGGLE under the word, which needs
> `host.composer.setSpellcheck` — upstream PR #143057, in no release. The new shots
> show five ranked suggestions, **Add to dictionary** last, and no squiggle.

prs.title: refactor(process): one owner-death supervisor for every long-lived Hermes child, plus a ratchet against new detached spawns
prs.body:
## Why
Many issues share one shape: Hermes is killed (SIGKILL, OOM, a crash, a systemd stop) and a child it started keeps running. Examples: Chromium under agent-browser, Browser Use harness daemons, a llama-server router and its models, a language server's helpers, a slash command's shell, a code cell's subprocess, a background `npm run dev`, a WhatsApp bridge holding its port. Each family grew its own fix: an orphan sweep on the next start, a per-owner poller, a parent-pid watchdog, a death pipe, or an atexit hook. None of them acts at the moment the owner dies, and each copies the liveness logic. Open per-family attempts include #62615, #120739, #129655 and #126657.

`main` already has the central pieces: the spawn ledger in `hermes_cli/process_identity.py` and the pipe-EOF death supervisor that only stdio MCP servers used (`tools/mcp_death_supervisor.py`). This PR makes that supervisor the one owner-death path for every long-lived child, moves every family onto it, deletes the per-family mechanisms it replaces, and adds a CI ratchet so a new detached spawn can't bypass it.

## What changes
**One supervisor per Hermes process (`process_identity`, layer 4).**
- `hermes_cli/process_supervisor.sh` (POSIX sh, about 0.5 MB USS idle; the Python supervisor was 8.1 MB) holds the read end of a pipe whose only write end Hermes holds. Callers send `register` / `unregister <pgid>`.
- EOF means the owner died, whatever the cause. The supervisor sends TERM to each registered group, waits up to 3 s, then sends KILL. It refuses unsafe targets: its own group, Hermes's group, pgid ≤ 1.
- It starts lazily on the first registration and exits once nothing is registered. A release does not wait for it to exit (a daemon thread reaps it), so a foreground command that registers and releases its group each run pays about 0.05 ms, not the ~27 ms a blocking wait cost on macOS.
- The API:
  - `spawn_owned(argv, purpose=, **popen)`: the one way to start a long-lived child. It leads its own group, that group goes to the supervisor, and the child is recorded in the spawn ledger.
  - `own_process_groups` / `release_process_groups`: for groups something else spawned (the MCP SDK, a daemon's Chromium) and for stopping a child yourself.
  - `release_process_group_once_empty`: hands a group back only once no member is left. A survivor stays covered. The family stop paths release through it, except three that release right after their own group kill: terminal foreground commands and background jobs (a deliberately backgrounded `server &` that left the group is not kept covered), and MCP's orphan sweep after its SIGKILL pass.
  - `stop_owned_group_survivors`: after a leader crashed, stops what is left of a group this process still owns, then releases it (llama-server `stop()` during the restart backoff).
  - `spawned_by_this_process`: a shared daemon (one pid file or session every Hermes of the user can reach) is owned only when its inherited spawn tag names this process. A pid file proves what a process is, not who started it.
- Windows is unchanged: `spawn_owned` is a plain `Popen` there, and the layer-3 job object covers ownership.

**Families moved onto it.** Before/after = processes still alive after the owner is SIGKILLed. Each family has a real kill -9 test with a live control owner whose tree must survive. Each test goes red when its registration is removed.

| family | before (main) | after | replaced / deleted |
|---|---|---|---|
| stdio MCP servers | covered by the MCP-only supervisor | covered by the shared one | `tools/mcp_death_supervisor.py` (−216) and its client in `mcp_tool.py` |
| llama-server router + models | 2 | **0** | — |
| Browser Use harness daemons | 2 (and 4 left after a clean exit) | **0** (0) | — |
| agent-browser daemon + Chromium | 28 (342 MB) | **0** | — |
| LSP servers (descendants that ignore stdin EOF) | 1 | **0** | — |
| code-execution kernel cell subprocesses | 3/3 | **0/3** | the kernel-only POSIX death pipe |
| slash worker (quick command running) | 1 | **0** | the worker's parent-pid watchdog + `HERMES_SLASH_WATCHDOG_*` knobs (a narrow form stays for workers a pre-update gateway launches with `--parent-pid`) |
| terminal foreground command | 2 | **0** | — |
| terminal background jobs (pipe + PTY) | 3 | **0** | — (`persist_on_release`, gateway and managed-worker jobs still outlive it, below) |
| WhatsApp bridge / Raft bridge | 1 / 1 | **0 / 0** | — |
| verify app server / command TTS-STT | 3 / 3 | **0 / 0** | — |
| lightpanda serve | 1 | **0** | `reap_orphaned_lightpanda` next-start sweep (kept only for record files a pre-update Hermes left) |
| real-profile Chrome + attach daemon | 8 | **0** | — |
| embedded cua-driver (Linux) | 1 | **0** | — |
| dashboard WhatsApp pairing bridge | 1 | **0** | — |

The live-owner sweeps stay (LSP idle reaper, kernel idle reaper and atexit, whatsapp pidfile/port reaping for bridges from older versions). They do a different job, keeping things tidy while the owner lives.

**Ratchet.** `scripts/check_detached_spawns.py` (AST) runs in `scripts/check` and as a blocking `lint.yml` step. It fails on any `start_new_session` or `process_group` (as a keyword, a dict key or a `kwargs["…"] = …` item) / `os.setsid|setpgid|setpgrp` / `windows_detach_popen_kwargs` in the production trees unless the line or the line above says `detached-spawn: ok — <why>`. The baseline is empty: every remaining site is on `spawn_owned` or carries its reason. Teeth: an unmarked `start_new_session` Popen appended to a production file turns `scripts/check --only detached-spawns` red.

## Census (every detached / long-lived spawn site on main)
- **Migrated (16 families):** the table above.
- **Already covered, proved by a kill -9 probe:**
  - die on stdin EOF: copilot ACP, codex app-server, plugin host, photon sidecar, the cua-driver MCP proxy;
  - the compute host has its own parent guard (it flushes sessions on orphaning; a supervisor KILL could cut that flush short).
- **Deliberately not owned (marked with the reason):**
  - restart watchers and the `/update` / updater hand-offs: they must outlive the process they restart;
  - `hermes gateway` / dashboard / desktop / launchd service launches: services that outlive the CLI;
  - cron and kanban workers: restart-safe, they survive the gateway / dispatcher (#101940);
  - `persist_on_release` background jobs (#41225), every job of a gateway that re-adopts jobs from its checkpoint after a crash, and every job of a managed worker (the next turn's worker adopts it with its output log);
  - the gateway's managed session workers (covered: each kills its own group when its owner dies), exec quick commands (awaited; the timeout/cancel path kills the group) and the runtime gateway start (a daemon launch). These three arrived on main during review and carry markers.
  - the iron-proxy egress daemon (`hermes egress start/stop`);
  - the Google Meet bot (driven through files across turns);
  - the Bot Desktop screen (per profile, shared across turns);
  - `/browser connect` Chrome (the user's browser);
  - the update-custody watchdog (it must outlive the owner to kill the fetch).
- **Awaited with a group-killing timeout (N/A):** cron scripts, rg search, the Browser Use CLI, update completion, the secret-source command helper, ddgs, the Bot Desktop installer.

## Deliberately not owned: the three judgement calls
Each of these outlives its owner on purpose. Each is marked in code and kept as it is in this PR.

| Case | Why it outlives its owner | What cleans it up today | Residual risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Background jobs of a supervised or checkpoint-recovered gateway** (`tools/process_registry_ownership.py`, `_owns_job`) | systemd/launchd restart the gateway, which re-adopts the still-running jobs from its checkpoint, so the agent keeps their output and can stop them. CLI, TUI and foreground-gateway jobs ARE owned. | The restarted gateway re-adopts and manages them. | A supervised gateway that is killed and never restarted leaves those jobs running until noticed. |
| **Bot Desktop screen** (`tools/bot_desktop/runtime.py`) | One virtual screen per bot profile, shared across turns and open to human takeover. A restarted gateway re-attaches to it, with identity checked, so windows, browser state and a human session survive. | The gateway's idle stop (`bot_desktop.idle_stop_minutes`, default 30) and its orphan sweep at the next start. | Both run inside the gateway, so a gateway that never comes back leaves the screen up until reboot. **Follow-up: idle self-exit for an abandoned screen, in a separate PR for discussion: #141018.** |
| **Dashboard compute host** (`tui_gateway/host_supervisor.py`) | Its own parent guard notices orphaning within 1 s and shuts down cleanly. It stops running commands, flushes session state to `state.db`, then exits (kill -9 probe: gone by +2 s, 0 survivors at +30 s). The supervisor's TERM followed by KILL 3 s later could cut that flush short. Its own children are covered, because the host is a Hermes process with its own supervisor. | Its parent guard. | A host that hangs inside the flush (e.g. a wedged DB) has no hard deadline. A shutdown deadline is a possible later follow-up. |

## Size
| | insertions | deletions | net |
|---|---|---|---|
| production | 1062 | 721 | +341 for 16 families + the shared API (MCP included) + the review folds |
| tests | 2521 | 495 | +2026 |
| ratchet (script + CI) | 206 | 0 | +206 |

## Tests
_Head `7b8d309ce1`, rebased onto `origin/main` `85d57d9564` on 2026-10-22 (the branch was 1414 commits behind; three files conflicted, see "Rebase and review round" below)._

- **`scripts/check`:** 13 checks ok, including the `detached-spawns` guard. Code health: 0 blocking, 0 advisory across 105 files.
- **Live E2E, base vs head** (macOS; real `terminal_tool` background job and foreground command in an owner process, owner SIGKILLed, checked at +6 s, plus a live control owner):
  | | background job | foreground command | control owner's two |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `main` `85d57d9564` | survives | survives | alive |
  | this branch | gone | gone | alive |
- **Full suite on Linux (`scripts/run_tests.sh -j 6`, every test file, rebased head):** 65,889 passed, 58 failed, 1,009 skipped. Each failing file was rerun on head and on `main` `85d57d9564` on the same host: every failure but one fails the same way on `main` (host CA bundle, NixOS `/bin/bash`, DST-dependent stamps, installer and desktop-update fixtures). The one head-only failure was a test main gained while this was open (#142439) whose bridge double had no `pid`; `d1d8bc2e19` gives it one (red before, green after).
- **Owned-child test map (macOS, 190 files that name a touched symbol):** 3,709 passed, 16 failed; all 16 fail identically on `main` (update-routing and readiness fixtures, one whisper compute-type test).
- **Per family:** a real kill -9 test (owner SIGKILLed so no Python cleanup runs, plus a live control owner whose tree must survive), and a release test. Each was checked to go red when its registration, release or identity check is removed.
- **Greptile's 9 threads:** each fix is on this head (rebased SHAs in the thread replies' follow-up comment), each with a test that fails with the fix removed.
- **Frozen Track E workloads** (Linux, n=3, before the rebase): orphans 30 s after the owner's kill -9: llama-server 0 (steady tree +1 MB / +1 sh per owner), Browser Use 0 (and 0 after a clean exit), agent-browser + Chromium 0 with the control Chromium kept.

## Rebase and review round (2026-10-22)
Rebased over 1414 main commits. `tools/browser_use_cli.py` conflicted with main's per-profile harness daemons (`browser_harness_dirs`, `_driven_daemons` keyed by daemon identity, `stop_harness_daemons(home_key)`): the owned-daemon map is now keyed by the same daemon identity, so two served profiles' `default` daemons never share an entry. A fresh review pass on the rebased head (correctness, design, reuse, quality, efficiency, a second-model reviewer) led to these commits, each with a test that fails without it:
- The exit handler stopped every harness daemon this process had driven, including a shared one another live Hermes started; it now stops only daemons this process owns (Windows, which records no ownership, still stops every driven one). `cleanup_all_browsers` keeps main's stop-every-driven-daemon behaviour, because `/browser connect|disconnect` rely on it to move the next call to the new endpoint.
- Hot path: an already-owned agent-browser or harness daemon now costs one pid-file read per command (plus the children rescan that catches a relaunched Chromium) instead of the full identity and spawn-tag chain; an exited agent-browser session's entry is dropped; a replaced harness daemon releases the old group. The harness pid-file path has one resolver (`browser_harness_dirs.harness_pid_file`).
- Releasing the last owned group no longer `wait()`s on the exiting supervisor (about 27 ms per foreground command on macOS); a daemon thread runs the untimed `wait()` instead, so the exited supervisor is never left a zombie child (CI caught a psutil walker of the gateway's children tripping on one while it was reaped lazily).
- The ratchet also catches `process_group=` and `kwargs["start_new_session"] = …`; six existing sites now carry their reason.
- A llama-server crash restart stops the crashed router's surviving model children and releases its group, as `stop()` already did.
- A long first browser command (browser_exec or local agent-browser) owns its daemon (and Chromium) while it still runs: the existing ownership check re-runs every 0.5 s on the shared `agent.periodic_scheduler` until the command returns, so an owner killed mid-navigation takes them along.
- The exit handler reloads an owned harness daemon only while its name still publishes our pid, so a replacement another live Hermes started under the same name after ours exited is left alone.
- Smaller: the supervisor refuses a malformed parent pgid; dead imports from the deleted MCP supervisor are gone; two comments and the ddgs marker now match the code.

Considered and left as they are: releasing MCP groups only once empty after the SIGKILL pass (existing tests pin release-after-kill and the group is dead apart from unreaped zombies); one shared `stop_owned(proc)` helper for the eight terminate-wait-kill-release sites (each kill step reuses a family helper that predates this PR); caching the spawn tag (measured 36 µs per build).

## Known limits
- A descendant that leaves its group after the last registration (a Chromium relaunch between commands, a `setsid` inside a job) is covered from the next registration on, or not at all. The live-owner sweeps stay as the backstop.
- A shared agent-browser / harness daemon another live Hermes started stays that Hermes's: it is not covered by this one, and dies with its starter.
- Sandbox clients (`docker exec`, `ssh`): killing the host-side client does not stop the in-container process. Container lifetime belongs to the sandbox family, not to host process groups.
- The Bot Desktop screens a gateway started still outlive a SIGKILLed gateway, by design (see "Deliberately not owned"; follow-up #141018).
- Windows owner-death coverage comes only from the layer-3 job object, as before.
- A Hermes process that `exec`s itself in place (relaunch) closes the control pipe (Python opens it close-on-exec), so its owned children die with the old image, as on any other owner exit.
- `cleanup_all_browsers` (gateway shutdown, CLI exit with sessions open, `/browser connect|disconnect`) still reloads every harness daemon this process drove, including a shared one another Hermes started, as on `main`. Only the exit path this PR added is owner-only.

## Credit
This builds on Teknium's `process_identity` spawn ledger and the MCP death supervisor on `main`. The per-family investigations shaped what this had to cover:
- @o-aloqaily (#62615): exact-profile Chromium matching;
- @trevornk (#120739): owner claims for harness daemons;
- @mheals and @Diaspar4u (#129655, #99527): per-owner state;
- @liuhao1024 (#126657): reaping llama-server on owner death.

Refs #60152, #125949, #134348, #62615, #120739, #129655, #126657, #41225, #101940.

prs.title: An update that turns a plugin off keeps your memory provider and turns the plugin back on once it fits (#131216, #129198, #125919)
prs.body:
When `hermes update` has to turn a plugin off, the memory provider is no longer erased, the plugin comes back by itself on a later update once it fits, and every surface says it is off instead of reporting "All checks passed".

Fixes #131216, fixes #129198, fixes #125919. Salvages #131220 (@charan-rathore) and #125960 (@YS-OH-CORE) with their commits kept as authored; co-authored with #49302 (@AIalliAI) and #43313 (@bionicbutterfly13). Supersedes #137490, #129201 and #140944.

## What changes

| Situation | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Update disables plugin X | X sits in **both** `plugins.enabled` and `plugins.disabled` | X moves from `enabled` to `disabled`, and the change is recorded under `plugins.disabled_by_update` |
| X was the memory provider | `memory.provider` set to `''`, so the choice is lost for good | `memory.provider` kept; the dependency union and the loader both skip a provider `plugins.disabled` parks |
| X fits again (plugin fixed, network back, resolver bug fixed) | stays off until you find out and run two commands | a later update retries it and undoes exactly the edit: re-added to `enabled` if it was there, provider live again. A download failure is retried by the next update; a resolver/build verdict is retried once X or core's dependency inputs change (fingerprint in the record), so an unchanged misfit costs no build |
| X is retried while it still conflicts with enabled plugin Y | n/a | X is tried only on top of the enabled plugins that build; an update that has to disable an enabled plugin re-enables nothing, so a retry can never take Y's place |
| You run `hermes plugins disable X` after the update turned it off | "already disabled" (no-op) | writes the decision; later updates stop retrying X |
| Agent startup with X parked | silent built-in memory | one notice per home: why it is off (with the update's reason) and `hermes plugins enable X`. CLI prints it; Desktop and messaging get the sticky warning |
| `hermes memory status` | `Provider: (none — built-in only)` | `Plugin: turned off ✗` plus the same notice |
| `hermes doctor` | `✓ Built-in memory active … this is fine` | `⚠ X is turned off` and a "Plugins Turned Off by an Update" section, both counted as issues |
| Installed provider fails to import | logged only, user unaware | the user is told external memory is off for the session |
| Agent config cannot load (#125919) | swallowed silently, memory provider quietly built-in | WARNING naming the exception class (never its message) at each fallback site |

## How

- `pm/plugin_eviction.py`: `_EvictingUpdate` builds the enabled plugins exactly as before, then tries due recorded plugins one at a time on top. `PluginEviction` now disables (drops every spelling from `enabled`, records `{enabled, reason}`) and re-enables (`_rejoin`) in one journaled config edit. `sync_evicting` retries `recorded_evictions()` after the enabled plugins; static misfits stay out without a resolve. Spellings come from the plugin's own manifest instead of a plugin scan of the PM process's home, so a profile's plugins match in that profile.
- `pm/plugins_state.py`: `_provider_from_config` skips a provider `plugins.disabled` parks, using the spellings `plugins.memory._explicitly_disabled` already honours. This is what made clearing `memory.provider` necessary before.
- `pm/publication.py` + `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py` / `plugins_admission.py`: a user selection forgets the record of the plugin it settles (`settled`), so an update never undoes a user's choice.
- `agent/agent_init_memory_provider.py` (new sibling, offsets `agent_init.py` growth): resolves the configured provider; a parked provider is reported and never re-installed.
- `plugins/memory`: `parked_provider_notice()` shared by the loader, agent init, `memory status`, doctor and the dashboard status.
- Docs: `getting-started/updating.md` dependency step.

Changed existing test assertion (Teknium's ruling that the update must not quietly clear `memory.provider`): `test_update_sync_disables_plugin_excluded_by_requires_python` now asserts the provider survives, and extends into the rejoin invariant. #131220's 13-test file is replaced by that test plus `test_plugin_the_user_disables_after_an_update_stays_disabled`; agent side adds `test_parked_provider_is_reported_and_never_reinstalled`. All three new invariants fail on `origin/main`.

## Live A/B (real `hermes update` dependency step: `pm.sync_venv(explicit=True, evict_incompatible_plugins=True)`, uv 0.13.5, CPython 3.14.9)

Scratch home on each tree, the real catalog `mnemosyne` plugin enabled and set as memory provider. Its `requires-python` was set to `<3.14` (the shape hindsight hit in #140944) and later put back:

| Step | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| update while it doesn't fit | `enabled: [mnemosyne]`, `disabled: [mnemosyne]`, `provider: ''` | `enabled: []`, `disabled: [mnemosyne]`, record with reason, `provider: mnemosyne` |
| `hermes memory status` | `Provider: (none — built-in only)` | `Plugin: turned off ✗` + notice naming the update's reason |
| agent init (`AIAgent(...)`) | silent, no providers | one `⚠ Memory provider 'mnemosyne' is turned off … hermes plugins enable mnemosyne` |
| `hermes doctor` | `✓ Built-in memory active … this is fine` | `⚠ mnemosyne is turned off` + `Plugins Turned Off by an Update` |
| next update after it fits | unchanged: still both lists, provider `''` | `⚠ Turned plugin 'mnemosyne' … back on`; `enabled: [mnemosyne]`, provider live, `memory status`: installed ✓ available ✓ |
| evicted again → `hermes plugins disable mnemosyne` → fits → update | n/a | stays in `disabled`, record gone, not turned back on |

Not covered live: Desktop UI rendering of the sticky startup notice (same `AgentNotice` path existing provider warnings use), Windows/macOS hosts.

Not in this PR: configs already left in both lists by older updates are not migrated (no record exists to say an update did it). `hermes plugins enable <name>` repairs them.

## Infographic

prs.title: plugin-catalog: add sgme (self-hosted long-term memory engine)
prs.body:
Adds a catalog entry for **SGME (拾光记忆)** — a self-hosted long-term memory engine — as a memory provider plugin living in a monorepo subdir (`adapters/hermes` of `freehul/sgme`), same layout as the listed `hindsight` entry.

**Submission eligibility**: I am `freehul`, owner of the plugin repository ([freehul/sgme](https://github.com/freehul/sgme), MIT, public).

**Validation at the pinned commit** (`6ef74f8f6089c765670abc13e639eefad3f6123b`, tag `v1.10.5`): `hermes plugins validate adapters/hermes --install-deps` → **Validation passed** (security scan: safe, zero caution findings). One `⚠ private core imports` warning is expected and documented: `config_schema.py` imports only `plugins/memory/config_schema.py` — the pure-data module the framework's own docstring designates for provider config panels ("Schema files … may import only this pure-data module"). The listed `hindsight` entry ships the same import; the wire protocol serializes the schema as plain data, so no behavior depends on the private classes. Happy to move to a public seam if you'd rather add one.

**Disclosure lines (rule 13)**:
- **Network**: the plugin talks only to the user's own SGME server (default `http://127.0.0.1:9910`, configurable via `SGME_BASE_URL` to any host the user owns, e.g. a LAN box). No third-party services, no telemetry.
- **Credentials**: read exclusively through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret()` (rule 11) using the env names `SGME_AGENT_KEY` / `SGME_ADMIN_KEY`; never reads `.env` files, `auth.json`, or any other credential store; secrets are never written to disk (config-panel secret fields go through Hermes's env store).
- **Background work**: per-turn session capture is appended on a background thread inside the provider (non-blocking); refinement/distillation runs on the user's own SGME server, not from the plugin. No shells spawned, no subprocesses.
- **Reads outside its own data**: none beyond the session content Hermes passes to the memory-provider API and the plugin's own config file (`$HERMES_HOME/sgme/config.json`).
- **Approvals**: the provider never routes around Hermes's approval system; its tools surface through the standard memory-provider tool interface and follow normal tool approval. Under unattended runs (cron / gateway), SGME unreachability degrades silently to empty recall instead of hanging the agent.

**Compatibility (rule 14)**: `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.0"` declared in both this entry and `plugin.yaml` (0.22 introduced the plugin host and the config-panel wire format; on older versions the loader skips the plugin via the manifest floor). `version: 1.10.5` matches the pinned tag.

**Capabilities (rule 6)**: `provides_tools: []` — the 44 `sgme_*` tools are exposed through the memory-provider tool interface, not plugin tool registration (same convention as the other memory entries). `requires_env` lists the `SGME_*` env names the provider reads through the secret scope.

Images/screenshots are pinned to the same commit (`raw.githubusercontent.com`).

prs.title: feat(webapp): serve the Desktop workspace from the gateway
prs.body:
## What this does

The gateway serves the browser-hosted Desktop workspace (the Webapp) from its own listener. With
`webapp.enabled: true` in the config, `hermes webapp` opens it. Chats run on the profile's gateway, the
process that already serves the CLI, the native Desktop and messaging, so every surface sees one
conversation with one queue.

This follows teknium's direction on #93508
(https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/93508#issuecomment-6259130824): the gateway hosts the
Webapp, with no separate Webapp server and no relay. It carries @BearHuddleston's work from #93508 under
his authorship: the browser renderer and bridge, the browser terminal, staged uploads, file tickets,
the Webapp routes and the bundle build, plus two fixes from #93508's review rounds. The relay and the
profile-incarnation fence stay out; carried code follows main's named-profile rule and refuses a
missing or deleted profile home. #93508 stays open.

@IAvecilla's #142220 adds Settings → Web Access to native Desktop: one place to serve the Webapp on the
network or at your own URL, behind Nous sign-in.

## How it works

- **Config.** `webapp: {enabled, host, port, public_url}`, off by default, `127.0.0.1:9120` when on.
  A wildcard host (`0.0.0.0` / `::`) or a `webapp.public_url` engages the dashboard sign-in gate; any
  other non-loopback host keeps the Webapp off and `hermes webapp` says why. `dashboard.public_url`
  describes `hermes dashboard` and never applies to the Webapp's listener.
- **Listener.** With the Webapp on, the gateway binds its API listener to the Webapp's address and
  serves the bundle there; native clients keep dialing loopback. With it off, the listener is main's.
  When the Webapp's listener cannot start (port taken, the sign-in gate refusing with no provider),
  the gateway keeps main's private loopback listener for native clients, replaces the browser
  credential (someone else may hold the port), and `hermes webapp` says why. A Webapp with no built
  bundle, or one `hermes update` could not rebuild, reports as unavailable and says to run
  `hermes webapp`. On Windows the gateway holds the fixed port exclusively.
- **Sign-in on this machine.** The gateway keeps the browser credential in a user-only file in its
  home, so open tabs stay signed in across a gateway restart. `hermes webapp` asks the gateway for a
  one-use link (60 s) over its private control socket, which answers same-user peers only. On Linux
  and Windows the server checks who redeems the link and the command opens it. Elsewhere (macOS, the
  BSDs, illumos) the command prints the one-use link and never opens it. The secret redactor masks the
  credential and launch tickets in Webapp links that reach a transcript. Each browser socket,
  including each voice stream, opens with a one-use ticket named for that socket, so no socket URL
  carries the credential.
- **Sign-in from other machines.** Behind the sign-in gate, `hermes webapp` opens the Webapp's
  address (`webapp.public_url` when set; on the LAN, the address Web Access registered Nous sign-in
  for) and the user signs in there with a password or Nous account. Each login is bound to the browser
  credential by an HttpOnly cookie named for the gateway, so two gateways on one hostname keep their
  sign-ins apart. A write that carries the sign-in cookie has to come from the Webapp's own origin
  (Sec-Fetch-Site, else Origin). On the Webapp's listener a provider token works on its own (as a
  bearer token or on the native refresh route) only if a native app's sign-in received it there; a
  browser login's tokens work only inside its cookies.
- **Sign-out.** `hermes webapp --sign-out` replaces the credential. Every tab and every login behind
  the gate is signed out, and the account tokens those logins held stop working on the Webapp; the
  sockets, host terminals, screen viewers and media links they opened close or stop working, and the
  command reports how many connections closed. Native apps that signed in with their own sign-in stay
  signed in. With no gateway running it replaces the stored credential and says so.
- **Web Access (native Desktop).** Settings → Web Access serves the Webapp on the network or at your
  own URL, behind Nous sign-in (sign in to Nous under Providers first). Start builds the bundle, writes
  the `webapp:` block of the config, registers the Nous Portal callback when it changed (saving the
  client id as `HERMES_DASHBOARD_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` in `.env`), and restarts the gateway. A running chat
  refuses the restart: the settings are saved, the pane shows Restart needed, and they apply at the
  next restart. Only the native app or the loopback credential can call these routes. `hermes update`
  rebuilds the bundle for any home that serves the Webapp.
- **Profiles.** `hermes -p work webapp` opens the default gateway's Webapp on `work`. A standalone
  profile's own gateway serves its own Webapp when its config turns it on. Profile export and
  `--clone-all` leave the browser credential out.
- **Files.** One shared parser reads `file:` URLs (drive letter, UNC, POSIX) on every surface, decodes
  them once, and refuses one that encodes a separator or a dot-segment. Dropping files onto a terminal
  types their paths as a paste, and a path with a control character is skipped with a warning.
  Sessions and the terminal start in the profile's home unless its `terminal.cwd` names another
  folder. On a profile whose workspace is an SSH machine, images picked in the browser are read from
  the gateway's staged uploads.

## Commits

1. `feat(webapp)`, `feat(desktop)`: carried server pieces and browser host renderer (BearHuddleston)
2. `feat(gateway)`: serve the Webapp from the gateway's own listener
3. `feat(cli)`: `hermes webapp`
4. `feat(desktop)`: sign-in view for a signed-out tab
5. `test(webapp)`, `docs(webapp)`: e2e spec, smoke script, configuration, CLI reference, Desktop guide
6. Ported from #93508's review rounds (BearHuddleston): refuse cookie-authenticated writes from another
   origin; read `file:` URLs with one shared parser. Each has a gateway-side test.
7. Fixes from the review of #93508 and live runs on this branch, one per commit.
8. Web Access API, pane and docs (IAvecilla, #142220).
9. Fixes from this PR's reviews (teknium, unsupportedpastels, Greptile, yoniebans), one per commit,
   each with a test that fails without it.
10. `fix(desktop)`: the bots avatar escapes a bot's name in its face markup (from @bakon11's audit
    checks; main's code, reachable from the Webapp's origin).
11. `fix(desktop)` (yoniebans' review): carried renderer changes that only the browser needs are gated
    to the browser, so native Desktop keeps main's behaviour for each, with a native test.

### Native-only commits

These change native Desktop, TUI or CLI behaviour. Each is its own commit with a test.

- `6c9a8a8711d` `hermes sessions adopt` (new here) prints one line on an old or locked state.db
  instead of a traceback. The Webapp doesn't need it.
- `b3ba8906605` Native Desktop on a remote SSH-backend profile reads cached images while the SSH
  host is down. The Webapp's paste read-back uses the same rule.
- `6ec3b1f8372` + `5caf2b647df` + `534454e726e` Reattach replay on slow links for the dashboard `/chat`
  tab and the Webapp host terminal; a replay that timed out keeps the smaller size for the rest of
  the session. Native Desktop's terminal is node-pty and is unaffected.
- `23747ee47bd` + `b97f6169ea7` Native Desktop's remote default folder and the Webapp's start folder:
  the profile's `terminal.cwd`, else its home.
- `1440790ca57`, `ccd1da7adce` Put Electron's clipboard writes and native ticket fallback back to
  main's behaviour after the carried renderer changed them. Keep them, or Electron regresses.
- `82974d567d0` + `a11d787b1f8` Electron's media protocol and previews read `file:` URLs with the
  shared parser; a bare `%` in a file name is escaped first, so that media plays.
- `56c04c4d770` Terminal file drop: the control-character and paste handling applies to Electron too.
- `b265e3837f8` Native file attach: host files of any size are copied in chunks; inline data URLs
  stay at Electron's 256 MiB reader cap.
- `14cd7f862ce` Bot avatars escape the bot's name in their markup, in native Desktop as well.

### Changes to main's behaviour

Native Desktop:

- A pane on a collapsed layout side reads as hidden: the statusbar terminal button and terminal
  keybinds treat it as closed, and its toggle shows it on the first press (`e1e70f6beb0`, test
  `d61ec54f55b`).
- "Open image" on a remote gateway's generated image saves through the save dialog instead of handing
  the system browser a URL that carries the connection token (`e1e70f6beb0`, test `8791b570b8a`).
- `file:` URLs with a drive letter or UNC host open the Windows path in previews, media links and
  Electron's media protocol; a URL that encodes a path separator is refused. Remote audio and video
  send their file URIs to the gateway unconverted (`82974d567d0`).
- When the clipboard IPC write throws, copy buttons fall back to the renderer's clipboard API instead
  of reporting a failure (`1440790ca57`).
- "Open HTML artifact in browser" percent-encodes its `file:` URL, so a path containing `#`, `%` or
  `?` opens (`e1e70f6beb0`).
- Restored terminal scrollback finishes writing before the new shell starts, and terminal query
  replies inside the replay are no longer sent to the shell (`e1e70f6beb0`).
- Queued composer focus retries no longer take focus back from audio or video controls the user just
  focused, which completes main's #135228 (`e1e70f6beb0`, test `floating-target-media.test.ts`).
- Terminal file drop skips paths with control characters (`56c04c4d770`).

Once, after upgrading: browsers behind sign-in sign in again (the sign-in cookie now carries the
gateway's name), and native apps that signed in on a gated Webapp before this change sign in again.

## Testing

- Every fix from this PR's reviews has a test that fails without it. For each module they changed,
  the fixes ran its test files; every failure left also fails on main (`db1fa153fe2`) on this Windows
  machine (POSIX-only fixtures, symlinks, the space in the home path).
- `scripts/check` passes all 12 checks, code health included.
- Renderer: typecheck, lint (no errors), the i18n key check and the touched vitest files pass. A full
  Python and vitest comparison against main at the new base is running; the numbers follow in a
  comment.
- Live, Windows, headless Edge, isolated homes (earlier rounds): cold launch, single-use link, chat, CLI
  and browser on one session, host terminal and its tickets, reload, gateway restart keeps the tab
  signed in, sign-out closing open sockets and showing the sign-in view within about 2 s, Webapp off,
  named profile, terminal file drop, the default folder, Windows file URLs, the gated fallback with
  and without a password provider, sign-out behind the password gate (real gateway), and raw
  WebSocket upgrades with a foreign `Host` (all refused). A live gateway confirmed the stale-bundle
  report after a failed update.
- E2E: CI runs the desktop and Python e2e suites only on release or manual runs. Manual run at this
  head: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/40003439648

Not yet verified: a real Mac (the macOS launch path runs simulated on every host), a real Nous OAuth
sign-in, and the in-app gateway restart from Web Access.

## Known gaps

- Portal: whether any Nous account can authorize a self-hosted client, and whether registering a new
  callback replaces or adds a redirect URI on the shared dashboard client. If it replaces, Web Access
  and `hermes dashboard` cannot both use Nous sign-in on one client.
- Native apps signed in on the Webapp's listener stay signed in at sign-out. The bundled password
  provider cannot revoke their tokens; they end when the user signs out in that app or changes the
  provider's credentials.
- Where the printed link has no peer check (macOS, the BSDs, illumos), a local user who reads it first
  can redeem it within its 60 s; the owner then sees that it was already used.
- A reattach replay that timed out stays at the smaller size for that session, so a fast viewer after
  a slow one gets the shorter replay with the "output was trimmed" notice.
- A second profile that turns on Web Access without its own `webapp.port` finds 9120 taken and shows
  that reason; there is no automatic port choice.
- On macOS, `SO_REUSEADDR` stays on so a restart can rebind during TIME_WAIT.
- As on main, `dashboard.public_url` with no sign-in provider stops the gateway: hosted sign-in
  relies on that setting gating the gateway's own listener. Web Access never writes it.
- The other SSH file routes (`/api/fs/list`, `read-text`, `git-root`, `default-cwd`) still answer 500
  when the host is down; only the image route checks the cache first.
- On an SSH workspace, browser audio and video stream from the gateway host, as remote native
  Desktop's do; downloads come from the SSH machine.
- The browser attaches images up to 16 MiB; native Desktop takes 25 MiB.
- The Webapp page sends no Content-Security-Policy yet; the sign-in handoff pages do.
- Host shells survive sign-out for their 15-minute retention; their sockets close at sign-out.
- Unchanged from main: reloading mid-reply drops the text streamed so far, and the hermes-bots plugin
  keeps polling `/api/profiles` from a signed-out tab.

The read action was removed in 56ee8a5cc6 (2026-02-19, 2 files, 3 insertions, 14 deletions). The compensation since: 106 commits and 6,275 lines of churn on the memory path, 10 open tickets, 53 comments. The 5,000+ lines did not fix the issue; 14 changes might be what it takes.

The gap was verified live: memory(action='read') returned 'Unknown action read' in 0.00s, the log recorded the rejection, and the session's context ran at 321K tokens with the anchor over its char limit and no read path to manage it. An unprimed agent, shown only the three snapshots, named the same root cause and recommended the same fix.

This is a two-way door: simple to take back if it is not right, not worth the ledger if it is.

prs.title: fix(gateway): log every missed liveness probe and dump the loop's task state
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds the diagnostics #137838 asks for to the loop-liveness watchdog, leaving the restart contract untouched.

Today only the terminal strike is logged: the log says "missed 3 consecutive liveness probes" and nothing about how long the loop was starved or which task was holding it. The faulthandler dumps collected in that issue cannot name the culprit either, because thread stacks cannot see coroutine state.

- Each miss below the terminal strike now logs its strike count and the **measured** probe wait, so a recurrence is measurable from the log alone.
- The terminal dump carries a bounded, best-effort snapshot of the wedged loop's tasks: ready-queue depth, task names, cancellation counts (`Task.cancelling()`) and `file:line:function` frame locations. No locals and no coroutine arguments.
- The snapshot reads a loop owned by another thread, so it is non-atomic and bounded (40 tasks / 6 frames). Every read is individually suppressed, and a failure inside the snapshot can never prevent the restart exit.
- Stop/disarm rechecks, the exit-code-75 handshake, the lifecycle stamp and the dump path are unchanged.

This is instrumentation, not a root-cause fix: it makes the next occurrence name the task that refuses to acknowledge cancellation (`anyio._deliver_cancellation` spin, or something else), which the existing dumps could not.

## Related Issue

Fixes #137838

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/shutdown_watchdog.py`: `_task_frame_locations` / `_describe_task` / `_describe_loop_tasks` helpers (bounded, per-read suppressed); per-miss `logger.warning` with strike count and measured wait; `loop_tasks` and `missed_probe_wait_s` added to the terminal dump snapshot.

prs.title: OpenAI provider E2E suite green again: fake Responses server sends the cache_write_tokens openai 2.54 requires
prs.body:
## What

The 9 red tests in `Python tests / e2e` (`tests/e2e/core/providers/test_openai_responses.py`, `test_openai_codex_pool.py`) are green again. They were red on main's dispatch run [40056774214](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/40056774214) (job 120761409254, `5894e750c3`) and on #141864's run 40154952141.

## Root cause

The openai 2.54.0 SDK made `InputTokensDetails.cache_write_tokens` required, and the fake Responses server builds its `response.completed` usage from those pydantic types. Every completion raised `ValidationError` inside the server thread and the socket closed mid-stream.

Seen from Hermes, that was an `APIConnectionError` on every Responses call:
- the oneshots retried until the 150 s subprocess timeout
- the rejected-replay cases fell through to the fallback (`FROM-FALLBACK` instead of `FIRST`)
- the TUI gateway turn never sent its event

It was harness drift. Product code doesn't build these types (`git grep InputTokensDetails` only matches the fake).

**Culprit:** 128b101efd7 `chore(deps): bump openai to 2.54.0`. It landed between the last green e2e dispatch (39885728572, merge-base `73efa6753de`) and the red one. The local base run shows the exact traceback (`tests/fakes/providers/openai_responses.py:263 … ValidationError: InputTokensDetails cache_write_tokens Field required`).

## Fix

`Turn` gains `cache_write_tokens: int = 0` and the fake sends it, matching the current Responses wire shape. No test is skipped or loosened.

## Proof (local, `scripts/run_tests.sh`, fake HOME, locked test env with openai 2.54.0)

| base `4ea8d23cc9f` | `test_openai_responses.py::test_rejected_encrypted_replay_is_stripped_and_primary_retried` | 2 failed (`ValidationError … cache_write_tokens`) |
| base `4ea8d23cc9f` | both e2e provider files | both files hang until the runner's 300 s per-file timeout, 0 tests completed (CI: 2 + 7 failed) |
| head | both e2e provider files + `tests/agent/transports/test_codex_transport.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_api_mode_aliases.py` (other users of the fake) | **176 passed, 0 failed** in 80 s |

prs.title: fix(process_identity): use the kernel monotonic start on Linux too
prs.body:
## What this fixes

On Linux, `process_birth()` returns psutil's `create_time()`, which is `boot_time() + starttime/HZ`. **`boot_time()` re-reads `/proc/stat btime` on every call**, so when `btime` steps — NTP, sleep/wake, WSL2 clock resync — two readings of the *same live process* differ.

`gateway/session_worker.py::_claim()` compares with exact float equality:

```python
birth_now = process_birth(process)
if birth_now != birth or not running or status == psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE or not same_user:
    raise RuntimeStoreError('permission_denied')
```

A healthy worker is therefore refused as a stranger. Instrumenting that check produced:

```
worker_auth_refused: reason=process_identity op=compression.context pid=748940
  birth_matches=False running=True status=sleeping user_matches=True
```

`birth_matches=False` on a process that is running, sleeping and same-user is the impossible combination that indicts the comparison.

## Why it looked like a timeout

15 of 15 real kanban cards died at **56–58 s**; cards finishing under ~16 s passed. Duration is a red herring: a longer run makes more persist calls, so it gets more chances to cross a step. There is no timeout at that value (`dispatch_stale_timeout_seconds` 4 h, heartbeat staleness 1 h, ticket TTL 30 s, `HELLO_SECONDS`/`STOP_ACK_SECONDS` 60/30 s, all checked).

Also model-, provider- and version-independent — reproduced on v0.22.5 and v0.22.4, with Opus/Anthropic and DeepSeek/OpenRouter, which fits a bug nowhere near the model path.

## Evidence that `btime` is unstable

Three samples of `/proc/stat` on an **idle** host, 6 s apart:

```
sample 1: btime=1792770115 uptime=107313 sum=1792877428 wall=1792877428 skew=0s
sample 2: btime=1792770115 uptime=107319 sum=1792877434 wall=1792877435 skew=-1s
sample 3: btime=1792770112 uptime=107325 sum=1792877437 wall=1792877438 skew=-1s
                                    ^^^^^^^^^^ moved 3 s BACKWARDS
```

psutil 7.2.2, `psutil/_pslinux.py`:

```python
def create_time(self, monotonic=False):
    ...
    if monotonic:
        return self._ctime                       # <-- caller-independent
    # Add the boot time, returning time expressed in seconds since the
    # epoch. This is subject to system clock updates.
    return self._ctime + boot_time()             # <-- what the current code returns
```

Note `process_birth()`'s current docstring says *"Other platforms keep `create_time()`: Linux and Windows apply no per-process reference."* That premise is wrong for Linux: the boot-time term **is** the per-caller reference.

## The fix

Linux's platform implementation already accepts `create_time(monotonic=True)`, returning jiffies-since-boot with no boot-time term — so owner and worker read one identical value. Dropping the macOS-only gate is the whole fix; the existing `TypeError` fallback still covers Windows, whose implementation has no such keyword.

`monotonic=True` on the wrapper (`psutil.Process`) does **not** accept the keyword on Linux — the `_proc` route is required, which is exactly what the macOS branch already does.

## Affected call sites (same exact-equality pattern)

Fixing `process_birth()` covers all of these; they are worth auditing for the same assumption:

- `gateway/session_worker.py` — `_claim()` (the path in this report)
- `gateway/session_worker_delegation.py:73`
- `gateway/session_managed_worker.py:297`
- `gateway/session_worker_reservation.py:42`
- `hermes_cli/kanban_owner_recovery.py:29,85`
- `hermes_cli/process_identity.py:222` — exact; `:210` already tolerates the drift (`abs(...) < 2.0`), which suggests this instability was met before and papered over locally

## Verification

- `process_birth()` on a live pid returns **129067.26** = `starttime_ticks / CLOCK_TICKS`, with no boot-time term
- `create_time()` on the same pid returns **1792897272.26** — a different source, as intended
- **Two separate OS processes return the identical value** — the property `create_time()` failed
- A dead pid still raises `psutil.NoSuchProcess`, preserving the `worker_not_live` contract
- **A card that had failed 4× at ~56 s completed in 4 minutes** (10 timestamped steps over 1 m 45 s of continuous worker life), with zero refusals logged

## Compatibility note

The value's meaning changes from an epoch to seconds-since-boot, so any `birth` persisted before the fix (pending worker journals, identity-registry entries, owner bindings) mismatches once and must be regenerated. In practice: stale journals, at most one spurious owner-recovery attempt.

Environment: Hermes v0.22.5 and v0.22.4, Python 3.14.9, psutil 7.2.2, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, kernel `6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`.
