prs.title: fix(tools): bound a check_fn probe so a wedged availability check cannot hang the turn
prs.body:
## The problem

A `check_fn` probes external state (a Docker daemon, an MCP server, a browser control endpoint). The probe ran inline on the caller's thread, so a probe that never returned held its caller forever.

Two call sites, both on a turn's critical path:

- the boot warm-up — `gateway/run.py::_warm_turn_machinery_sync` → `model_tools.get_tool_definitions()` → `registry.get_definitions()` → the probe sweep
- the first inbound turn — `agent/agent_init.py::_load_tools` → the same build

#131145 reports the result: a boot whose warm-up never finished (`Turn-machinery warm-up still running after 20s; opening inbound gate anyway`) left the **first** inbound turn wedged forever. The agent was constructed, the tool `check_fn`s ran, and then the turn stopped dead **before issuing any provider request**:

```
tools.registry: check_fn _browser_cdp_check returned False; dependent tools will be unavailable this turn
tools.registry: check_fn _browser_dialog_check returned False; dependent tools will be unavailable this turn
tools.registry: check_fn is_browser_use_cli_mode returned False; dependent tools will be unavailable this turn
<no further lines, ever>
```

Nothing was logged, nothing was surfaced, `active_agents` stayed at `1`, and the messaging platform kept showing "typing" until a gateway restart. The probe that never answered was the one after those three verdicts.

The probe was unbounded, so nothing downstream could recover: the warm-up only logs `WARNING` and continues in the background, and the turn's inactivity watchdog waits `agent.gateway_timeout` (1800 s by default).

## The fix

The probe now runs on a worker thread with a **10 s budget** (the environment probe's budget — `tools/env_probe.py::_PROBE_WAIT_TIMEOUT`, healthy runtime ~0.5 s). A probe that cannot answer within it counts as "not available" instead of hanging the turn, and says so:

```
WARNING tools.registry: check_fn check_x_requirements did not answer within 10.0s;
        dependent tools will be unavailable this turn
```

Properties that had to survive the change:

- **The profile scope still resolves inside the probe.** The worker runs under the caller's contextvars (`spawn_context_thread`), so the profile secret scope and the Hermes-home override still resolve in the probe. Without this, every scoped probe would fail closed and strip its toolset (#110635).
- **The probe's own contextvar writes still reach the caller.** The memory tool publishes its availability snapshot from the `check_fn` for the `dynamic_schema_overrides` call that follows it ("one definition pass must use ONE config decision"). The probe's context is published back to the caller, so the snapshot still lands.
- **The tool surface is unchanged.** One wedged probe costs its own budget and nothing else: every other tool is still offered. The full `get_tool_definitions()` set is byte-identical to `main`'s.
- **A wedged probe parks one thread, not one per TTL window.** The parked probe is shared by every waiter, so the next sweep answers immediately instead of starting another thread and waiting again.
- **A build whose probes keep going silent stops probing.** Past three unanswered probes the build gives up rather than waiting once per probe.

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_check_fn_probe_timeout.py` (new). The wedged-probe cases fail on `main` with the hang itself (`a wedged check_fn must not hang its caller`), and the file also guards the two properties above plus the "a raised probe is still reported as raised" path.

```
tests/tools/test_check_fn_probe_timeout.py    9 passed
tests/tools/test_registry.py                   52 passed
tests/agent/test_builtin_memory_disabled_surface.py   13 passed
tests/hermes_cli/test_tool_availability_notices.py     4 passed
tests/agent/test_iteration_budget_warning.py           2 passed
```

`ruff` and the code-health ratchet are clean.

Fixes #131145

prs.title: Make profile-scope re-registration of a launch-owned dashboard-auth provider a quiet no-op
prs.body:
## Problem

On a multiplexed gateway, each served profile gets its own plugin manager, and every profile-scoped manager rediscovers the bundled dashboard-auth backend and calls `register_dashboard_auth_provider` with the same launch-owned provider name every boot. The profile-scope branch correctly refuses the registration, but it logs a `WARNING` every time:

```
Plugin 'basic' tried to register dashboard-auth provider 'basic' from profile scope ...; ignoring it because dashboard auth is owned by launch scope ...
```

On an 11-profile multiplexer this fires ~11x per boot, drowning genuine scope-isolation violations in noise. (We patched this in a production install and it keeps getting reverted by upstream updates, so it needs to live in the repo.)

## Fix

Before the warning, check `get_provider(provider.name)` against the process-global registry. When the launch scope already owns the name, the registry merge (`_merged()`) exposes the global slot to every profile scope anyway, so the refused re-registration is a provable no-op: demote it to `logger.debug` and return.

The `WARNING` is **retained** for genuinely first-time foreign-scope registrations — including the case where the launch plugin later releases the global slot (e.g. it is disabled) and a profile then tries to register.

## Tests

Three tests added to `tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_auth_plugin_hook.py`:

- `test_profile_re_registering_launch_provider_is_quiet_no_op` — launch-scope register succeeds; same-name profile-scope re-registration returns `None`, logs debug (not warning), and does not change ownership or profile-scope resolution of the launch provider.
- `test_first_foreign_scope_registration_still_warns` — first-ever registration from a foreign scope still warns and is refused.
- `test_foreign_registration_warns_after_launch_provider_released` — after a targeted unload releases the global slot, a later profile registration is first-time again and still warns.

Full file via the CI-parity runner (`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_auth_plugin_hook.py`): **15/15 passed** (12 pre-existing + 3 new).

prs.title: fix(discord): stop slash commands dying on a stale `discord = None`
prs.body:
## Problem

Every Discord slash command fails silently on a gateway that went through the plugin dependency probe at startup. The client shows *"The application did not respond"* / *"应用程序未响应"* and nothing is logged to the user — only to `agent.log`:

```
ERROR discord.app_commands.tree: Ignoring exception in command 'sethome'
  File ".../plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py", line 4511, in _run_simple_slash
    if not await self._check_slash_authorization(interaction, command_text):
  File ".../plugins/platforms/discord/adapter_slash_auth.py", line 31, in _evaluate_slash_authorization
    in_dm = isinstance(chan_obj, discord.DMChannel) if chan_obj is not None else False
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'DMChannel'
```

`/sethome`, `/new`, `/reset` — anything routed through `_check_slash_authorization` — is dead for the life of the process. Plain mentions still work, which is what makes it confusing.

## Root cause

On a cold start the gateway imports platform plugins once during its dependency probe, before the runtime venv is on `sys.path`:

```
INFO gateway.platform_registry: Platform 'Discord' dependencies missing — attempting install...
```

`adapter_slash_auth.py` imports discord at module level with `except ImportError: discord = None`. That probe import fails (discord.py is not importable *yet*), the `None` is cached in the module namespace, and the module object is then reused for the rest of the process — long after discord.py is available. Nothing re-resolves it, so every later `discord.DMChannel` / `discord.Thread` dereference in that module raises.

`adapter_thread_titles.py` has the same shape (`isinstance(channel, discord.Thread)` in `_guild_channel_labels`), so thread-title formatting carries the same latent crash.

## Fix

Resolve the module at call time instead of trusting the import-time fallback:

```python
def _dc():
    global discord
    if discord is None:
        import discord as _discord_mod
        discord = _discord_mod
    return discord
```

`_evaluate_slash_authorization` and `_guild_channel_labels` use `_dc()`; the stale `None` self-heals on first call. If discord.py really is unavailable, the deferred import raises at the call site — which is where the adapter already fails loudly — instead of turning into an `AttributeError` on a `None` that gets swallowed by the app-command tree.

## Tests

New regression test `test_gate_survives_stale_none_discord_module` in `tests/gateway/test_discord_slash_auth.py` pins `adapter_slash_auth.discord = None` and asserts the gate still returns its verdict and repairs the module.

- RED on `origin/main`: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'DMChannel'` (same traceback as the report)
- GREEN with this patch: `tests/gateway/test_discord_slash_auth.py` 20 passed

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add hermes-windows-process (what is running, who started it, what outlived its parent)
prs.body:
## What

One new catalog entry, `hermes-windows-process`, from
[`Yicheng-Mark/hermes-windows-plugins`](https://github.com/Yicheng-Mark/hermes-windows-plugins)
at `11b45e71`, subdirectory `windows-process`. It adds a third Windows diagnostic next to
`hermes-windows-eventlog` (why a process died) and `hermes-windows-ports` (who holds a port):

`win_process_table` answers **what is still running and who started it** — and, the part no
shell command gives you, **which of those processes outlived the parent that spawned them**.

## Why the parent column needs more than a PID

Windows records a parent PID, not a handle. Once the parent exits its PID is free for reuse,
so a surviving child goes on pointing at a PID that is either unused or now belongs to
something unrelated and newer. Listing the table and joining on PPID therefore reports a
plausible parent that never spawned anything.

The tool reads each process's creation time as well, which settles it: a parent that started
*after* its child cannot have spawned it. Each row carries `parent_state`:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `alive` | The parent PID is held by a process that started earlier — the real parent |
| `gone` | Nothing holds that PID any more |
| `reused` | The PID is in use, but by a newer process, so the real parent exited |
| `unknown` | The parent row exists but a start time could not be read |
| `root` | Parent PID 0 |

`orphans_only` returns the `gone` and `reused` rows, oldest first — the leftover
gateway/backend/server children after a quit, rather than the thing you just started.
`with_ancestry` walks a PID up to the top of the table.

## Read-only, and deliberately narrow

`PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION` only, for `QueryFullProcessImageName` and
`GetProcessTimes`. No `ReadProcessMemory`, so **command lines are out of scope on purpose**:
reading them on Windows means reading another process's PEB, and this plugin does not read
process memory. No handle duplication, no writes, no child processes, no network, no file
writes, no self-update. Stdlib only (`ctypes` against kernel32).

Processes the account cannot open (System, Idle, session managers, other accounts) come back
with no path and no start time instead of failing the call; the summary counts them.

## Validation

`validate_plugin_dir` from `main` today, run **on the tree at the pinned commit** (not a
working copy): **15/15 checks pass, security scan safe, zero warnings**. The same run on the
working copy agrees.

`scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` on this entry: `OK`.

Live evidence on the machine it was written on (Windows 11, Python 3.13), against the real
process table rather than fixtures:

- Building the table for ~305 processes takes **11 ms** (one `OpenProcess` +
  `QueryFullProcessImageName` + `GetProcessTimes` per row), so there is no cache and no wait.
- `orphans_only` with `include_system: false` returned four real leftovers: `cua-driver.exe`
  (35 h old, launcher long gone), `wps.exe`, `cc-switch.exe`, and a `tail.exe` whose shell
  had exited seconds earlier.
- The ancestry walk on the python process running the check returned
  `python.exe <- bash.exe <- bash.exe <- bash.exe <- claude.exe <- Code.exe <- Code.exe <- explorer.exe`,
  with `explorer.exe` reading `gone` (its own parent exits at logon) — the shape the tool
  exists to show.

Session and bootstrap processes (`csrss`, `wininit`, `winlogon`, `services`, `explorer`) are
started by a parent that exits by design, so they always read `gone` without being a leak.
They are flagged `system: true`, the notes say how many of the flagged rows are theirs, and
`include_system: false` drops them.

Tests: 18 (14 unit over the classification, filters, ordering and caps, plus 4 live against
the real table, skipping off Windows). They pass on the pinned tree.

prs.title: fix(weixin): preserve fresh context and partial text delivery receipts
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes Weixin context recovery generation-aware and preserves receipts when a split text send fails after earlier chunks were accepted.

On `main` at `b02fa681328bae7071412677d76448ff46582f68`:

- Stale text/media responses unconditionally remove the peer's shared cached context, including a context refreshed while the request was in flight. The removal is not persisted.
- Text sends capture context before waiting for the outbound gate and reuse it across chunks/retries.
- Content-fingerprint dedup returns before an otherwise intake-admitted new message can refresh context.
- A later text-chunk failure discards acknowledged IDs and does not mark partial delivery, allowing the base plain-text fallback to replay the visible head.

The fix snapshots `(token, generation)` within a single `ContextTokenStore` instance; it does not synchronize independent stores or processes. A stale response invalidates only the snapshot it used; a newer inbound generation in that instance survives even when its opaque token is identical. Persistence remains serialized and off the event loop. Text attempts read current context after acquiring the send gate and before every retry. Media item sends use the same snapshot protection. Recovery remains bounded to one extra attempt with the same `client_id`.

Inbound message-ID dedup and existing intake policies are preserved. Explicit non-user updates are ignored. Intake-admitted new IDs refresh context before content dedup, without dispatching duplicate business events. Referenced-media wrappers remain supported; no content-shape whitelist is added.

Partial text failures remain failures, but now include acknowledged IDs/counts and the existing `partial_overflow` marker. For successful and partial text sends, `message_id` is the last acknowledged ID, and `continuation_message_ids` contains every earlier acknowledged ID in send order, excluding the primary ID. The real stream consumer therefore tracks the complete acknowledged set without including an unconfirmed tail. The real base retry and delivery router recognize the visible head. **No safe tail-resume capability is claimed:** the failed request may already have reached iLink.

## Related Issue / Prior Work

Related to #135503 and #126399, not a claim to resolve every failure described there.

Overlap checked against open and closed PRs, including:

- #135511: protects shared context by never evicting it. This proposal instead durably invalidates only the rejected generation and preserves newer generations; these are alternative policies requiring maintainer coordination.
- #124295 and #129679: broader cross-adapter split-send/resume work. This proposal only marks Weixin text partials and intentionally does not implement resume.
- #136061: pairing-aware content dedup. This proposal does not solve its downstream pairing-approval issue; it changes context-refresh ordering while preserving existing intake policy.
- Closed, unmerged #74572 and #80426: earlier stale-context recovery work; token comparison alone does not protect same-token inbound generations.

These overlap notes should be reconciled before merging; this is not presented as unrelated work or as a platform security vulnerability.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/weixin/adapter.py`: context generations, conditional persisted invalidation, inbound ordering, current-context attempts, bounded media recovery, partial text receipts.
- `tests/gateway/test_weixin_context_recovery.py`: 29 parameterized regression cases using real adapter/store/base/router/stream-consumer paths and synthetic transports. Stream-consumer receipt coverage includes all chunks accepted, the first chunk failing, only the first accepted, and multiple accepted before a failure.
- `tests/gateway/test_weixin_plugin.py`: seed the real context store instead of stubbing `get()` to a constant that cannot reflect invalidation.

## How to Test

Use a fresh PM-built development/test environment as documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, then:

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/gateway/test_weixin_context_recovery.py \
  tests/gateway/test_weixin_plugin.py \
  tests/gateway/test_weixin_secret_scope.py \
  tests/gateway/test_weixin_typing.py \
  tests/gateway/test_weixin_voice_warning_policy.py \
  tests/gateway/test_delivery.py \
  tests/gateway/test_send_retry.py \
  tests/gateway/test_access_policy_mixin.py -q
python scripts/check --base b02fa681328bae7071412677d76448ff46582f68
git diff --check
```

Verified on native Windows 10, Python 3.14.9, through Git Bash and the canonical hermetic per-file runner:

- Exact upstream adapter with the original 25-case regression file: **22 failed, 3 passed**. Four failures reflect the missing snapshot API; the others expose incorrect behavior. This earlier baseline run predates the four stream-consumer cases.
- Receipt-contract regression against the pre-review candidate: **6 failed, 2 passed**; the real stream consumer omitted the first acknowledged ID on all-success and multi-chunk partial sends. After the two return-slice corrections: **8 passed**.
- Final patched adapter: regression file **29 passed**; all eight selected files **120 passed, 0 failed**.
- Repository checker: **12 checks passed**, code health **0 blocking, 0 advisory**; whitespace check passed.

No live Weixin calls were made for this preparation. The full repository suite and other operating systems were not tested. Tokenless recovery remains best-effort and cannot override server-side permission/session restrictions. Media partial-delivery transactions, upload-grant changes, durable tail redelivery, and cross-process token-store synchronization are outside this change.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the Contributing Guide and applicable repository instructions.
- [x] Searched existing PRs; overlapping work is disclosed above.
- [x] Focused code changes and regression coverage.
- [x] Tests run on native Windows using the canonical runner.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes.
- [ ] Full repository test suite passes (not run).
- [x] No configuration keys, dependency changes, or new tool schemas.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered; no OS-specific behavior added.
- [x] Changed method docstrings describe the bounded recovery contract.

prs.title: fix(opencode): a relay 403 stamped code=server_error retries instead of benching the key [risk 0.80]
prs.body:
## What

OpenCode's Go/Zen relay answers its own upstream failure (it couldn't parse the upstream's response) with:

```
HTTP 403 {"error": {"type": "server_error", "code": "server_error",
  "message": "Upstream request failed: [server_error] Upstream response was not valid JSON"}}
```

On main, the built-in 403 default reads that as `auth`. The turn aborts on attempt 1, the sole healthy key gets marked exhausted (`failure_reason=auth`, a one-hour bench), the session drops to fallback models, and Desktop tells the user to replace a key that works. Three independent field reports on hermes-agent 117869 show it, plus a `GET /models` → 200 with the same key.

## How

The OpenCode profiles (`opencode-go`, `opencode-zen`) now classify that envelope as `overloaded` through the existing `ProviderProfile.classify_api_error` seam (`plugins/model-providers/opencode-zen/__init__.py`). It gets the normal retry budget and the credential pool is never touched. Core `agent/error_classifier.py` is unchanged.

The hook fires only when all of these hold:
- the status is 403;
- `error.code` is explicitly `server_error`. The code `error.type` falls back to doesn't count, because a bare `type=server_error` isn't proof;
- the message carries the relay's `Upstream request failed` wrapper.

Every other 403 on these routes, and the same body from any other provider, keeps its built-in verdict (`auth`, `billing`, `upstream_blocked`).

## Why this shape and not the PRs it replaces

- hermes-agent 117871 adds a provider-scoped table plus a registry-backed alias resolver inside core `_status_403`. That's core code carrying one vendor's vocabulary. The plugin seam (`bce20d0b1f0`) exists so a provider owns its own error quirks, and it already resolves aliases and scopes by provider.
- hermes-agent 117874 is envelope-scoped but global across providers, and it reads `c.body["error"]["code"]`. **It doesn't fix the real error:** the OpenAI SDK passes `body = error` object (the inner dict), so `body["error"]` is missing. A real `openai.PermissionDeniedError` built from the captured response still classifies `auth` on that branch. I checked this against the SDK's `_make_status_error_from_response`. The hook here handles both the inner-object and the raw-body shapes, and both tests build the error the way the SDK does.

Kept from the contributors:
- the relay envelope fixture, unchanged (both captures, with provenance);
- the classifier → `recover_with_credential_pool` → real `CredentialPool` invariant test (@oppih);
- the explicit-`error.code`-only rule and the wrapper requirement (@kokhlo);
- billing and WAF evidence still win (both).

## Tests

- `tests/plugins/model_providers/test_opencode_go_profile.py::test_relay_403_server_error_is_an_upstream_outage_on_opencode_routes`: one table, eight rows. Go, a declared Go alias and Zen go `overloaded`. Another provider, type-only, code-without-wrapper, billing and WAF keep their verdicts.
- `tests/agent/test_403_relay_credential_recovery.py`: both captured envelopes; the sole `opencode-go` entry is never written to and stays selectable.

```
# main + these tests:  2 files, 35 passed, 5 failed  (both pool cases; go / alias / zen rows: auth != overloaded)
# branch:              scripts/run_tests.sh <both> tests/agent/test_error_classifier.py tests/agent/test_provider_profile_recovery_seam.py
                       4 files, 236 tests passed, 0 failed
```

## Side effects

- No persisted identity, config key or wire contract changes. The classification stage order is unchanged.
- Only OpenCode routes change, and only for the envelope above. An existing assertion isn't inverted.
- Not covered here (Refs only): the `auth list` "re-auth may be required" rendering for 403s, which the issue thread also raises.

Fixes #117869

Supersedes #117871
Supersedes #117874

Credit: @oppih for the captured relay envelopes, the pool-level invariant test and the provider-scoping argument. @kokhlo for the explicit-`error.code` rule and the wrapper requirement.

prs.title: fix(gateway): preserve replies followed by silence markers
prs.body:
## Summary

A model can write its answer alongside a housekeeping tool, then finish with `NO_REPLY`. The local gateway treats that marker as a missing answer and posts a warning. With segmented streaming, it can also remove the answer already on screen.

This patch reuses the completed reply before output transforms and persistence, following the existing empty-follow-up recovery path. It also reconciles the final with the reply's streamed message, including transformed text and fresh-final replacement, without deleting earlier independent commentary.

## Changes

- Scope reply recovery to local turns where the existing `silence_allowed()` policy requires an answer.
- Preserve output hooks, stored history, completion receipts and crash recovery by selecting the reply inside the agent loop.
- Keep short recovered answers such as `3pm` out of the abnormal-exit explainer, and sanitize recovered text before persistence.
- Replace only the recovered reply's stream previews. Leave earlier commentary and native cumulative-stream behavior intact.

A marker with no completed reply still warns where a reply is expected. Permitted silence and narration beside substantive tools are unchanged. Direct agent/CLI callers retain their existing behavior. Gateway-hosted CLI, TUI and Desktop viewers use the local turn policy. Remote `_run_agent_via_proxy` execution is unchanged.

## Verification

- Local checks: 456 passed across 36 affected-area files, plus 73 passed across four upstream-integration files. `scripts/check` passed all 12 checks.
- Real agent loop through the turn runner, response shaping and stream consumer, with scripted provider and platform I/O.
- Regression coverage for transforms, persisted receipts, crash recovery, short replies, split segments and edit/draft/native transport behavior.
- Regression tests fail on the relevant pre-fix revisions. Removing the policy, selection or reconciliation logic also makes its tests fail.

prs.title: Memory entries stay removable after the char limit is lowered (salvage #133029)
prs.body:
Memory entries stay removable after `memory.memory_char_limit` / `memory.user_char_limit` is lowered below one of them; only writes that add text are still refused.

Fixes #133028. Salvages #133029 by @jonpol01 (commit kept with authorship), adapted to current main.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafbd43/0bDa2yftAtfIOqY2U2Fyp_snZGFp3v.png)

## Root cause

The drift guard treats any entry longer than the whole-file limit as free text an outside writer appended (no tool write can produce one). Lowering the limit breaks that premise: a clean entry written under the old limit made every replace and remove refuse (tool, approval replay, Journey delete), so pruning, the way back under the limit, was blocked until the file was hand-edited.

## Changes

- `tools/memory_tool_store.py`: an oversized entry now refuses only a write that adds or rewrites text. A write that only deletes entries goes through; when it drops the oversized entry, the `.bak` snapshot is taken first and returned as `drift_backup` (that entry may hold glued free text). (@jonpol01)
- Adapted to main: main already dropped the round-trip/layout signal (#107270); the salvage keeps main's single signal (one entry over the whole-file limit) instead of re-adding it.
- A write refused for being over budget next to an oversized entry reports the drift error with its snapshot again (that entry is the real obstacle), instead of "shorten the new content". Other refusals (no match, would empty the store) pass through unchanged.
- `agent/learning_mutations.py`: the Journey edit/delete closure reports its budget refusal through `_error(..., "over_budget")`.

## Behaviour (real `MemoryStore`, entry written at a 1375-char limit, limit then lowered to 200)

| Action | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| remove the oversized entry | refused | removed, `.bak` snapshot saved |
| remove a small entry beside it | refused | removed |
| remove via `operations[]` | refused | removed, `.bak` saved |
| remove every entry in one batch | refused (drift) | refused (empty-store guard, #103419) |
| replace a small entry (store still over) | refused (drift) | refused (drift, `.bak`) |
| replace the oversized entry with short text | refused (drift) | refused (drift, `.bak`) |

## Changed existing test

`tests/agent/test_learning_mutations.py::test_memory_drift_is_refused_with_backup_like_memory_tool` (43d3d4e8514) pinned "a Journey delete beside free text is refused". Per the maintainer ruling on #133028 (removes must work while the store is over its limit) it now pins: a Journey edit is still refused with the drift error and snapshot, and a delete that leaves the oversized entry in place goes through.

## Validation

- New: `test_entries_stay_removable_after_the_limit_is_lowered`, `test_removing_an_entry_with_glued_free_text_keeps_a_snapshot` (both red on main), plus the changed Journey test (red on main).
- 21 memory/journey test files: 746 passed, 0 failed.
- `scripts/check --only health` clean, attribution audit clean.

prs.title: fix(desktop): stop completed todo flash on thread open
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops Hermes Desktop from replaying a historical completed task list when an idle conversation is opened.

`session.resume` and `session.activate` carry the latest persisted todo snapshot. The Desktop used to feed completed snapshots into the same four-second linger used for a completion observed live, so opening a thread made old work appear above the composer and then disappear. Idle activation snapshots are now treated as historical presentation state and cleared. Snapshots still restore when the backend reports that the turn is running, and post-turn hydration still owns the live final-checkmark linger.

## Related Issue

Fixes #100652

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- Update `apps/desktop/src/store/todos.ts` so idle resume/activate snapshots advance the revision watermark and clear presentation state instead of restarting the completion linger.
- Preserve active snapshot restoration for genuinely running turns and the existing post-turn completion linger.
- Add a regression test that fails on the previous behavior and verifies completed idle snapshots remain hidden.
- Correct the todo-store ownership comments to distinguish live events, active resume snapshots, and post-turn hydration.

## How to Test

1. Complete a Desktop conversation that uses and finishes a task list.
2. Open another conversation, then return to the completed conversation.
3. Confirm the historical completed task list does not appear above the composer; reconnect to a running conversation and confirm its active task list still restores.

Automated regression proof:

- Before the production change, the new test failed because `$todosBySession.s1` contained the completed item.
- After the production change, the same test passes and the accepted revision remains recorded.

prs.title: feat(desktop): fold cron sidebar jobs into one folder per name prefix
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Desktop sidebar's **CRON JOBS** section renders one flat list capped at `INITIAL_VISIBLE_JOBS = 3` rows plus a `…` expander. Job names are the one place a user naturally encodes their own taxonomy (`【巡检】…`, `【备份】…`), and the section throws that structure away — three rows from an arbitrary interleaving, everything else behind the expander.

This PR folds the section into one collapsible folder per `【prefix】` found in the job name:

- one folder header per distinct prefix, showing the prefix and its job count
- every folder starts collapsed, so a long job list costs one short block in the sidebar
- jobs whose name carries no `【prefix】` collect in a trailing **Uncategorized** folder, so nothing disappears
- the section's row cap still bounds how many jobs render; folders group whatever survives it
- the old load-more expander is gone — folders replace it

Display-only and additive: job creation, scheduling, cron expressions, the peek/dismiss behaviour and the run history are all untouched. It composes with the paused/completed ordering (#140653) — each folder keeps that ordering inside itself.

## Related Issue

Fixes #144252

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.tsx` — add `groupJobsByPrefix()` and `CronJobGroupHeader`; render folders instead of the flat list + expander; `isSyntheticCronOutputRun` filtering is preserved so synthesised run rows never become jobs. Folders order by prefix, the prefix-less bucket last; `UNCATEGORIZED_GROUP_KEY` is a sentinel that cannot collide with a real `【…】` match.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.test.tsx` — four behaviour tests: folders per prefix, Uncategorized after the prefixed ones, every folder collapsed by default, opening one leaves the others collapsed.
- `apps/desktop/src/i18n/types.ts`, `en.ts`, `zh.ts` — new `cron.uncategorized` label.
- `locales/_keys.desktop.json` — regenerated with `npm run i18n:keys`.

## How to Test

1. Open the Desktop app (or `cd apps/desktop && npm run dev`).
2. Create four cron jobs: `【A】one`, `【A】two`, `【B】three`, and one named `plain`.
3. The **CRON JOBS** section shows three folder headers — `【A】 (2)`, `【B】 (1)`, `Uncategorized (1)` — and no job rows.
4. Click `【A】`: its two jobs appear; `【B】` and `Uncategorized` stay collapsed.
5. Run the tests and the two static checks:

   - `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → **0 errors**

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes — **not run locally** (needs the separate dev environment). The commit hook's `lint desktop app` step passed; CI will run the full ratchet.

prs.title: fix(computer_use): surface the cua-driver setup root cause, not the group repr
prs.body:
## Problem

When a `cua-driver` session fails during setup, the model and the user see only:

```
computer_use backend unavailable: cua-driver session setup failed: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
```

That string is the `str()` of an anyio `BaseExceptionGroup`, not the actual failure. On this machine the real cause was:

```
cua-driver-rs: invalid daemon response: incompatible daemon:
contract version 0.8.0 does not match SDK 0.7.0
mcp.shared.exceptions.MCPError: Connection closed
```

The driver had already said exactly what was wrong — a daemon/SDK contract skew — and Hermes hid it behind an opaque group repr, so the failure presents as an unexplained backend outage. There is nothing actionable in the message and nothing to search for.

## Root cause

`tools/computer_use/cua_backend_session.py:312`:

```python
if self._setup_error is not None:
    raise RuntimeError(f"cua-driver session setup failed: {self._setup_error}") from self._setup_error
```

`_setup_error` is captured from a bare `except BaseException as e` in `_lifecycle_coro` (line ~249). Because the MCP `ClientSession` is entered inside an anyio TaskGroup, `e` is usually a `BaseExceptionGroup`, and formatting it with an f-string only yields the group repr.

This is the same failure mode the MCP tool paths already handle: `tools/mcp_tool_errors.py` documents it ("the transport's TaskGroup wrapper `str()` is `unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)`, which tells the model nothing") and exposes `_unwrap_exception_group`, which `mcp_tool_server_run.py` uses to reach the root cause. The computer-use path just never adopted it.

## Fix

* Unwrap `_setup_error` with the existing `mcp_tool_errors._unwrap_exception_group`, so the leaf exception's type and message reach the caller.
* Include the stuck startup phase in the message (the timeout branch already does this — setup errors did not).
* When the leaf is a driver/SDK contract skew, append the action that fixes it (`cua-driver update`, then `hermes computer-use doctor`).

The helper deliberately does not wrap the unwrapper in `try/except`: `_unwrap_exception_group` re-raises a `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit` leaf rather than flattening it, and that contract should hold here too.

New output for the case above:

```
cua-driver session setup failed (phase: mcp-init): MCPError: Connection closed
```

and for the contract skew specifically, the `incompatible daemon: contract version 0.8.0 does not match SDK 0.7.0` text plus the `cua-driver update` guidance now survive to the caller.

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_computer_use_cua_setup_error.py` (new, 5 cases):

* contract-skew leaf surfaces its text **and** the remediation hint, with the opaque group repr asserted absent
* a plain exception reports as `RuntimeError: <msg>`
* nested groups unwrap to the leaf
* `CancelledError` sibling noise does not mask the real error
* a `KeyboardInterrupt` leaf still propagates instead of being stringified

```
5 passed
```

Existing computer-use suite, unchanged by this branch (`tests/tools/ -k "cua or computer_use"`): same 6 failures before and after — they are environmental on this host (no cua-driver daemon running), verified by running the identical selection against the unmodified install. Passing count went 243 → 249 with the new tests.

## Reproducing

```python
# start the cua-driver session and unwrap the setup error
from tools.mcp_tool_errors import _unwrap_exception_group
from tools.computer_use.cua_backend_session import _AsyncBridge, _CuaDriverSession

bridge = _AsyncBridge(); bridge.start()
sess = _CuaDriverSession(bridge)
try:
    sess.start()
except BaseException as exc:
    print(_unwrap_exception_group(exc.__cause__))   # the real fault
```

Trivial to hit whenever the installed `cua-driver` daemon and the Python SDK disagree on the MCP contract — which is exactly the state after a driver update lands without the daemon restarting, or when a stale daemon is still bound.

prs.title: Update burnclock to 0.2.1: read-only dashboard page
prs.body:
## What changed

Updates the `burnclock` catalog entry from `0.1.0` to `0.2.1` at commit
`471c149d1699d115b593751e5d8a503e3036a072`, the `v0.2.1` release (superseding
`bb498129` and the earlier `0.2.0` candidate — see *Delta* below).

The desktop plugin ships:

- the existing `statusBar.right` watch chip, still cache-only;
- a **Burnclock** left-nav workspace page with cached balance, runway, budget
  and estimated spend;
- the DeepSeek Flash off-peak clock, window end, next peak, 2x delta and
  minimum-window status;
- a command reference and a feature index;
- click-through from the chip to the page, plus a palette command.

The page is strictly read-only. It runs `burnclock offpeak --json` on mount and
every 60 seconds; that subcommand is pure clock math with no provider key, no
network call and no cache write. There is no refresh button and no refresh
command.

## Delta since bb498129 (review feedback from @teknium1)

Requested change: *Refresh must not hand Hermes's `.env` keys to the CLI.*

Done — the branch is gone rather than reworked:

- deleted the `burnclock-shim.sh` preference and the `${BURNCLOCK_SHIM:-…}`
  fallback from `desktop/plugin.js`; the file now mentions no shim and no
  `~/.hermes` path at all;
- deleted the Refresh button, its `shell.exec` call, its exit-code handling and
  the now-unused `refreshIssue()` helper;
- the page keeps the "run `burnclock badge --refresh` in a terminal" hint and
  states that it is read-only and re-reads the cache every 60 s;
- the README drops the shim paragraph and records the constraint instead.

burnclock's CLI takes provider keys from *its own* environment (env-var names
only — no keyring, no config-side secret storage), so a refresh issued inside a
sanitized `shell.exec` could only work by routing Hermes credentials around that
sanitization, which is exactly what the review disallows. Per the review, no new
route is being requested here; if Hermes later offers a sanctioned way to pass a
configured secret to an external CLI, that belongs in a separate issue rather
than in this entry.

## Surfaces used

- `statusBar.right` chip
- `routes` page at `/burnclock`
- `sidebar.nav` row
- `palette` command

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- **Files read:** `badge.txt` and `badge.json`, resolved the way the CLI
  resolves them (`$BURNCLOCK_BADGE_CACHE`, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/burnclock/badge.json`,
  then `~/.cache/burnclock/badge.json`). Nothing else — not `~/.hermes/.env`, not
  provider keys, not browser profiles.
- **Shell commands:** the chip reads the two cache files with one `cat` every 60
  seconds. The page runs `burnclock offpeak --json` every 60 seconds — pure clock
  math, no key, no network, no cache write. Both run in the active local
  session. No other command is executed anywhere in the plugin.
- **Credentials:** the plugin does not read, ask for, receive or render
  credentials. Provider access stays in the separately installed CLI, which the
  user runs themselves.
- **Network:** none. The plugin makes no network calls.
- **Background work:** React Query refetches only; no daemon, watcher or
  updater. No telemetry.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` at the pinned tree
(`471c149d1699d115b593751e5d8a503e3036a072`, release `v0.2.1`):

```
✓ manifest — plugin.yaml parses
✓ manifest fields — name, version, description present
✓ requires_hermes — spec '>=0.22.0' parses
✓ config schema — not declared
✓ requires_env — all entries UPPER_SNAKE
✓ oauth — not declared
✓ loadable — entry: desktop/plugin.js
✓ python dependencies — none declared
✓ built-in tool collisions — no tools to check
✓ security scan — safe
✓ no core override — no runtime rebinds of Hermes core
✓ desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface
⚠ no __init__.py — capability probe skipped (manifest-only plugin)
◆ Isolation — portable plugin (no Python): runs anywhere

Validation passed.
```

`node --check desktop/plugin.js` passes. The banner and chip screenshot URLs at
the pinned sha return 200.

Manifest, `desktop/plugin.js`, README, banner, chip screenshot and LICENSE sit at
the repository root (no `subdir`). Owner submission: `jersilb` owns both this
entry's repo and the burnclock project.

prs.title: feat(plugins): ctx.side_question asks the session's own agent after a turn
prs.body:
A plugin you allow can now ask the session's own agent one short text-only question after each turn (same model, same system prompt and memory, the whole conversation, warm prompt cache), e.g. to suggest the user's next prompt. Fixes #143788.

```python
def register(ctx):
    def on_post_llm_call(**kwargs):
        token = kwargs.get("side_question_token")
        if token:  # post_llm_call is time-bounded: do the call on your own thread
            threading.Thread(target=_suggest, args=(token,), daemon=True).start()

    def _suggest(token):
        answer = ctx.side_question(token, "Suggest the user's most likely next prompt in one short line.")
        if answer:
            ctx.state.set("next_prompt", answer)

    ctx.register_hook("post_llm_call", on_post_llm_call)
```

## What a plugin can and can't do

| Can | Can't |
|---|---|
| Ask **one** question per turn (≤ 4,096 chars), within 60 s of the turn and before the next turn starts, from a plugin of the same profile | Ask without declaring `llm.side_question` in `plugin.yaml` **and** the user granting it (consent screen: "Ask your agent a short question after each turn. It sees the whole session, including memory, and spends your main model's tokens.") |
| Get back the agent's text reply, or `None` | Run any tool: tool calls in the reply are dropped, never dispatched; provider-executed tools (`web_search` rewrites, OpenRouter `web` plugin, `web_search_options`) are refused before sending |
| Read the whole session the agent sees (system prompt, memory, transcript) | Write anything into the transcript, memory or session state; change the model, tools, system prompt or output length |
| Spend the user's main-model tokens (mostly cache reads; billed to the session that issued the token as `plugin_side_question:<plugin_id>`) | Get a token on a cron run or a delegated subagent turn (nobody is waiting on those); use the legacy-key path (`llm.side_question` has no `allow_*` key: declare + consent only); run on MoA or agent-as-provider runtimes (ACP, external-process, Codex app-server), or after the session's model changed since the turn: refused with `None` |

One token per turn is shared by every plugin; the first call spends it, success or not. A plugin without the grant, or from another profile, gets `None` and does not spend it. Timeout defaults to 15 s, capped at 60 s, and covers the fork build as well as the request.

## Relation to background review

It runs on the background review's mechanism, not beside it: `build_cache_parity_fork` (the fork `/btw` and the memory/skill review use: same runtime, byte-identical system prompt and `tools[]`, inherited cache scope, persistence detached) plus its usage-attribution chokepoint. What differs is the driver: the review fork runs a tool loop under a dispatch whitelist; a side question sends exactly one request through the turn loop's own request phases and never enters the tool loop, so it does not depend on the thread whitelist (#136623).

## Changes

- **@curiouscleo** (`feat(plugins): ctx.side_question …`): turn lease (`agent/side_question_lease.py`), the one-request fork driver (`agent/side_question_request.py`), the `llm.side_question` capability row, `ctx.side_question` / `has_capability` in a `PluginContext` mixin, `side_question_token` on `post_llm_call`, docs.
- **Fork teardown on the shared mechanism** (`fix(agent): side-question forks release clients only …`): `/btw` and `ctx.side_question` closed their fork with `close()`. The fork shares the live session's id, so `close()` → `cleanup_vm(session_id)` / `cleanup_browser(session_id)` tore down the parent session's sandbox. Background review already releases only clients for this reason; that teardown is now one helper, `background_review.release_cache_parity_fork()`, used by both one-shot fork callers. `/btw` usage is now recorded under its own task name (`side_question`) instead of `background_review`.
- **Side request reports like other side calls** (`fix(agent): ctx.side_question reports through pre/post_auxiliary_call`): it fired the turn-scoped `pre/post_api_request` after the turn had closed. `turn_api_request.build_request_payload()` is the hook-free payload build (the turn loop's `build_api_request` wraps it unchanged); `auxiliary_hooks.start/finish_aux_call_hooks()` expose the pre/post pair to callers that drive the provider call themselves.

- **Review findings** (`fix(agent): side-question review findings …`): refuse when the session's model/provider/reasoning changed since the turn (a voice-chat routed turn switches back right after `post_llm_call`); the server-side-tool check also reads `extra_body.tools` (where `request_overrides` land); one `pre/post_auxiliary_call` bracket around the whole attempt so a reply that fails after the provider returned still closes with its error; drop the 32-lease global eviction that revoked live tokens on a busy gateway.

- **Independent-review fixes** (`fix(agent): side-question review fixes …`):
  - no `side_question_token` for cron runs (`platform="cron"`) or delegated subagent turns (`_delegate_depth > 0`; the `is_subagent` attribute some call sites read is never assigned in this tree), alongside the existing `_persist_disabled` fork skip;
  - each lease records the profile home (`hermes_home_key()`) it was issued under; `ctx.side_question` passes its manager's `home_path`, and a mismatch returns `None` without spending the lease;
  - usage bills to `capture.session_id` (the session the token was issued for) instead of the parent's id at release time, which a `/compress` or session reset can rotate between issue and redeem;
  - plugin side questions fire `pre/post_auxiliary_call` with `aux_task="plugin_side_question"` and a new `plugin_id` payload field, and record usage as `plugin_side_question:<plugin_id>` (per-plugin spend in `session_model_usage`); `/btw` keeps `side_question`;
  - the new legacy key `llm.allow_side_question` is gone: `CapabilitySpec.legacy_path` may be empty, which never opens the gate and is never mirrored by `record_consent`;
  - the timeout timer starts before `_build_fork`, so runtime resolution counts against it; a build cannot be interrupted, so one that outlasts the budget is caught right after and sends nothing.

## Live A/B (real `hermes chat` in tmux, OpenRouter `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`, real plugin granted in a scratch home)

Turn 1 `touch /root/probe_marker` in the session's sandbox (`terminal.backend: docker`, `container_persistent: false`); the plugin's side question runs; turn 2 `ls /root/probe_marker; hostname`.

| | PR head before (`bd09f6b`) | this head |
|---|---|---|
| side answer | "Verify the marker file exists at /root/probe_marker." (4.7 s) | "Check if the probe marker file exists: `ls -l /root/probe_marker` …" (3.2 s) |
| turn 2 sandbox | `ls: cannot access '/root/probe_marker'`, new container `7da27a470016` | `/root/probe_marker`, same container |
| hooks for the side request | `pre_api_request` / `post_api_request` (turn id `…:side_question`) | `pre_auxiliary_call` / `post_auxiliary_call`, `aux_task=side_question`, parent turn id |
| `session_model_usage` `side_question` | 2 calls, in 20, cache read 29,053, write 272, out 522 | 2 calls, in 20, cache read 29,053, write 252, out 559 |
| `messages` rows after 2 turns | 8 (user/assistant/tool only) | 8 (user/assistant/tool only) |

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_side_question_request.py`, `tests/agent/test_side_question_lease.py` (contributor's, plus): a parent-session terminal env survives a side question (red before); the side request runs under the turn's profile home and secret scope when redeemed from a fresh thread; a real plugin observing all four events sees `pre/post_api_request` for the turn only and `pre/post_auxiliary_call` (with usage) for the side request (red before).
- Review-finding tests: a changed runtime is refused with no request sent; `extra_body.tools` server-side tool rows; a `choices=[]` side reply still closes the auxiliary pair with an error; 40 live sessions keep their tokens.
- `tests/agent/test_side_question.py`: a real `/btw` fork's teardown leaves the session's terminal env (red before). The old assertion that `/btw` calls `shutdown_memory_provider()` + `close()` pinned the bug and is removed.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on every test file referencing side questions, background review, `turn_api_request`, `auxiliary_hooks`, `post_llm_call`, `PluginContext`, capabilities or `turn_finalizer` (133 files): 2,629 passed, 0 failed. `python scripts/check`: 12 checks ok.

- Independent-review fix tests (each red on `ac8acc8`): `test_side_question_lease.py::test_no_token_for_a_cron_run`, `::test_no_token_for_a_subagent_turn`, `::test_another_profile_cannot_redeem_the_lease`, `::test_side_request_fires_auxiliary_hooks_not_turn_request_hooks` (now asserts `plugin_side_question` + `plugin_id`); `test_side_question_request.py::test_side_call_bills_the_session_the_token_was_issued_for`, `::test_timeout_counts_the_fork_build`, `::test_side_call_writes_only_one_usage_row` (task now `plugin_side_question:next-prompt`); `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_capabilities.py::TestLegacyGateCompat::test_consent_only_capability_ignores_allow_keys`. Changed assertion on main: `TestRegistry::test_every_capability_has_legacy_gate` now exempts `llm.side_question` only (the reviewed ruling: declare + consent is its only path). `test_side_call_runs_under_the_turns_profile_and_secret_scope` now redeems as a plugin of that profile (`home=profile_home`).
- After the review fixes: `scripts/run_tests.sh` on side question, background review, auxiliary hooks, plugin capability and every test file referencing `has_capability` / `plugin_capability_granted` / `post_llm_call` / `side_question` (26 files): 380 passed, 0 failed. `python scripts/check`: 12 checks ok.

The live A/B table above predates the review fixes: the side request's `aux_task` and usage task now read `plugin_side_question` / `plugin_side_question:<plugin_id>`.

## Known limits

- The capability check logs one `capability_check` INFO line per turn while a plugin declares it.
- The fork does not inherit what the parent learned from provider rejections (`_reasoning_effort_rejected`, …): existing `build_cache_parity_fork` behaviour shared with `/btw` and background review.
- Review NITs, left as documented:
  - On `codex_responses` the transport's own single transport-level retry still applies to the side request; "no retries" means no turn-loop retry or fallback model.
  - The lease deep-copies the turn's messages and `tools[]` at every finalization while a consented plugin is loaded (cost scales with transcript size).
  - The server-side-tool refusal is a denylist (non-`function`/`custom` tool types, `web_search_options`, non-routing OpenRouter plugins); a new provider-executed mechanism outside those shapes would not be caught until added.
  - In-process plugins are fully trusted Python: the capability is consent and audit, not isolation; a malicious plugin can bypass every gate here.

## Infographic

![side-question](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafbb91/7HebC6-hqyTQ8ZsRGpXZW_4r4JebTk.png)

prs.title: fix(desktop): render internal notifications as system rows
prs.body:
## Bug

Gateway-originated synthetic turns intentionally persist as `role=user` to preserve strict model-message alternation. Issue #82888 added the structural `display_kind=internal_notification` marker, but Desktop hydration does not recognize that marker. It therefore falls through to `UserMessage` and paints runtime completion blocks as if the user authored them.

## Root cause

Desktop currently derives display authorship from the persisted role unless a recognized display kind overrides it. `internal_notification` is absent from that system-role projection even though the gateway now emits it specifically to distinguish synthetic turns.

## Fix

- Project `display_kind=internal_notification` to Desktop's existing compact `SystemMessage` renderer.
- Preserve the persisted backend role and full notification content.
- Keep ordinary user rows unchanged.
- Document the marker in the Desktop display-kind type.

This is complementary to #90104: that PR types direct CLI/TUI delegation completions as `async_delegation_complete`; this PR handles the generic gateway `internal_notification` path visible in Desktop.

## Reproduction

1. Run a Desktop conversation that delegates work to background agents.
2. Let an async delegation batch complete.
3. Reopen or hydrate the persisted session.
4. Observe the `[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE ...]` row rendered with user authorship.

## Expected behavior

Runtime-generated internal notifications use the compact system/timeline presentation and cannot be mistaken for user-authored turns.

## Verification

Run on exact head `cb66c006bd674486ba119c82a4259530d3b9eb2d`:

- Regression observed RED before the implementation and GREEN afterward: 73/73 focused Desktop hydration tests passed.
- Full Desktop UI suite: 6,752 tests passed across 683 files.
- `npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `npm run lint -- --quiet`: passed.
- `npm run build`: passed.
- Isolated Electron E2E with a real temporary SessionDB row: exactly one matching system-message root and zero matching user-message roots.
- Independent review: no blocking issues.
- `git diff --check`: passed against current `main`.

## Platform

Reproduced and verified on macOS 15.4.1. The projection is platform-independent Desktop hydration logic.

## Scope and risk

The patch changes only Desktop presentation for rows carrying the explicit `internal_notification` marker. It does not classify by content, alter backend role semantics, or change model context.

Follow-up to #82888.

prs.title: Add loaded-skills-indicator to the plugin catalog
prs.body:
Adds `plugin-catalog/loaded-skills-indicator.yaml` for
**[yugasurfer/loaded-skills-indicator](https://github.com/yugasurfer/loaded-skills-indicator)**,
pinned at `1c501473b192a45cbb36d08d1bc8c51f940ea416` (tag `v1.0.0`).

## What it does

One question, three surfaces: **which skills are read into this conversation's context right now?**

- **Status-bar chip** — `Skills: 6 loaded` in the right cluster. Clicking it opens a popover listing the skills whose bodies are still in the transcript (bold, accent dot, `in context`), the ones context compression reduced to a `[SKILL_PRUNED: …]` marker (ghosted, tagged `pruned`), and nothing else. A skill never loaded in this conversation is never listed — the plugin does not pad the list with inventory.
- **Dockable pane** — `⌘K` → *Skills: open pane* docks it beside the conversation (closable, re-running re-fronts it). A `( loaded | available )` toggle switches views: `available` lists the whole skill library grouped by category with descriptions, marks what is already loaded, and **click-to-load** puts `/<skill>` into the composer of the focused chat — it never submits, so a click costs no turn (clipboard fallback if the composer surface is unavailable).
- **`/loaded-skills` page** — the same list with a filter, for long sessions.

## Hermes surfaces used

Status-bar item + popover (`STATUSBAR_AREAS.right`, `variant: 'menu'`), ⌘K palette (`PALETTE_AREA`), a plugin workspace pane (`host.openWorkspace`), a route page (`ROUTES_AREA`), the composer door (`host.composer.insertText` / `focus`), gateway RPC (`skills.manage`, `session.history`) and its own dashboard namespace (`GET /skills`, `/available`, `/health`). No tools, hooks, middleware, env vars, OAuth or Python dependencies.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

1. **Reads the local transcript.** The backend opens the profile's `state.db` read-only (`mode=ro`) and reads the ACTIVE message rows of one session, to tell a live `skill_view` body from a `[SKILL_PRUNED: …]` marker. No writes, no other tables.
2. **Reads skill files.** `GET /available` reads `SKILL.md` frontmatter (name, description, category) under the profile and bundled skills directories — nothing else on disk.
3. **Types into the composer.** Clicking an available skill calls `host.composer.insertText` with `/<skill> `; it never submits. If that surface is missing the command is copied to the clipboard.

No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials, no subprocesses, no self-updater. The backend runs in the plugin host (`plugins.isolation: host`) and the frontend degrades to the display transcript if it is unavailable.

## Validation

On a clean clone of the repo at the pinned SHA:

- `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` → **16/16 checks, no warnings** — including `security scan — safe`, `desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface`, `no core override`, and `declared tools/hooks/middleware — matches registrations` (all empty).
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` → **18 tests pass** (stdlib only).
- `hermes plugins install yugasurfer/loaded-skills-indicator` into a scratch `HERMES_HOME` → clones, installs **disabled** (correct posture), enables cleanly, and the installed copy validates.
- The entry file passes `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py`: `OK: 1 file(s) valid`.

The README's **Disclosure** section carries the same three points for users, and the desktop half of the unified package ships opt-in — after install it is switched on in **Settings → Plugins** (documented in the README).

## Screenshots

![Status-bar chip popover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yugasurfer/loaded-skills-indicator/1c501473b192a45cbb36d08d1bc8c51f940ea416/media/popover.png)

Panes — `loaded` and `available`:

![Docked pane, loaded view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yugasurfer/loaded-skills-indicator/1c501473b192a45cbb36d08d1bc8c51f940ea416/media/pane-loaded.png) ![Docked pane, available view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yugasurfer/loaded-skills-indicator/1c501473b192a45cbb36d08d1bc8c51f940ea416/media/pane-available.png)

Built and tested on Linux (GNOME/Wayland) with Hermes v0.22.5; macOS and Windows are untested by the author, which the README states.

prs.title: Long gateway replies keep Markdown links and tables intact when split (#125885, salvage #125906 #103997)
prs.body:
Long gateway replies that get split into several messages no longer break Markdown links or pipe tables: a link stays whole in one message, a table that fits moves intact into the next message, and a table bigger than one message repeats its header row in every part.

Fixes #125885

Ported from [QwenLM/qwen-code#14043](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14043) (keep links, table rows and fenced code whole when splitting DingTalk/WeCom messages; big tables split between rows and repeat their header). It hit the same gap in hermes' shared `BasePlatformAdapter.truncate_message`, which the Telegram, Discord, Mattermost, Feishu, Slack and other adapters (44 call sites) use. Built as a salvage of the open contributor PRs on that function:

- **@liuhao1024 #125906**: split retreats out of an open `[label](url)` link; inline-code and link guards settle to a fixed point (2 commits, cherry-picked with authorship).
- **@GravityMsc #103997**: a split landing mid-table moves the whole table to the next chunk (cherry-picked with authorship).
- **Ours (qwen #14043 port)**: a table larger than one chunk splits between rows and each continuation is prefixed with the original header + separator. Hardening of the rollback: scans only the contiguous table (the original could jump to an earlier table's separator, or miss a separator sitting exactly at the cut), moves a table only when it fits a fresh chunk (otherwise repeat the header rather than emit a short chunk), never ends a chunk on a header/separator with no rows, and leaves pipes inside code fences alone.
- Credit also to @KagurazakaNyaa (#45020, the earliest table-boundary PR, co-author on our commit) and @Arxsher (#125938, a parallel link fix for #125885).

## What changes

Real output of `scratch/probe_chunks.py` (real Telegram `format_message` + `truncate_message` with `utf16_len`, which is the pipeline `TelegramAdapter.send` runs; raw `truncate_message(…, 2000)` for Discord-sized chunks):

| Scenario | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| #125885 fixture: prose + `[Mission Control issue 7](https://…)` near the 4096 Telegram limit | chunk 1 ends `…This [Mission Control issue (1/2)`, so the link breaks in both messages | chunk 1 ends `…source\. This (1/2)`, the whole link opens chunk 2 |
| 22-line table straddling a 2000-char boundary | rows spread over 2 chunks, second half is raw pipes | table in 1 chunk |
| 120-row table (4 chunks) | header only in chunk 1 (1/4 chunks render as a table) | header + separator at the top of 4/4 chunks, every row exactly once, max chunk 1950 ≤ 2000 |
| 200 pipe lines inside a ```` ```text ```` fence | unchanged | unchanged (no header injected) |

Sweep (pad 0–400 × limits 300/500/900, header at every offset around the cut): 0 chunks end on a stranded header or separator, 0 over the limit, all rows present.

## Layout

The chunker body moves out of the `gateway/platforms/base.py` facade into the new sibling `gateway/platforms/base_chunking.py::chunk_markdown_message`; `truncate_message` stays the public staticmethod (adapters override it) and delegates. Table helpers sit next to `TABLE_SEPARATOR_RE` in `gateway/platforms/helpers.py`. `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking (base.py shrinks).

## Tests

- `tests/gateway/test_platform_base_chunk_tables.py` (new, 2 tests): oversized table repeats its header in every chunk and keeps each row once (+ a fenced-pipes control); no split ever strands a header without its rows.
- Contributor tests in `tests/gateway/test_platform_base.py` (link retreat, escaped brackets, table rollback ×2).
- Red on base: all 6 new behavioural tests fail with `origin/main`'s `base.py`/`helpers.py` swapped in; the escaped-bracket control passes on both.
- Every test file referencing `truncate_message` / `split_text_fence_aware`: 15 files, 429 passed, 0 failed. `tests/gateway/` local run reached 5,719 tests with 0 failures before the host's timeout; CI has the full verdict.

**Live repro:** before/after above, from the real Telegram formatter + chunker pipeline. Not covered: an actual send to a live Telegram/Discord chat (no bot credentials in this cron run).

## Infographic

![chunk-markdown-structure](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafbda7/Rslx91Jq80kd_7Sz_q_9d_hlVVBBWd.png)

prs.title: feat(gateway): busy_result_mode carries mid-turn subagent and background-process results into the running turn
prs.body:
Fixes #136703

## What and why

When a background `delegate_task` child finishes while the parent is mid-turn, the session holds the result until the turn ends and then spends a separate model turn on it. This change adds an opt-in setting so the result can reach the turn that is already running:

```yaml
delegation:
  busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

With `steer`, the gateway's completion-delivery seam (`_deliver_completion_notification`) offers a claimed async-delegation completion to the session's running agent instead of admitting it as a new turn. Classic CLI runs its turns on the gateway (one-gateway runtime), so this one seam covers CLI, TUI and messaging sessions. `agent/background_results.py` appends them to the **next tool result just before that result is persisted**. This is the same mutable tail slot the iteration-budget and run-budget notices use, so:

- past context is never rewritten, and the prompt cache holds;
- the transcript matches what the model saw;
- the text is marked as background tool-channel evidence. It is deliberately **not** the `/steer` user-authority marker, because a child's output must not be given user authority.

If no later tool batch carries an offered result (the turn ends without another tool call, or is stopped), it goes back to the completion queue and arrives as the ordinary next turn, exactly as `queue` mode delivers it. Durable claims are acknowledged when the result is accepted, the same way the idle drain acknowledges them on enqueue.

Events owned by other sessions are returned to the completion queue untouched.

## Background-process completions

The same opt-in covers `terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` completions, under their own key next to `display.background_process_notifications`:

```yaml
display:
  background_process_busy_result_mode: steer   # queue (default, unchanged) | steer
```

They go through the same seam and carrier, with a process-specific marker (`a background process you started finished…`). The settle contract differs because a process completion has no durable claim and belongs to its per-process watcher: requeuing it onto `completion_queue` would strand it. So the delivery call waits on the carry (`gateway/run_notifications_busy_result.py`). If a tool result carried it, the call returns True and no turn starts. If the turn ended without carrying it, the same call continues into the ordinary `_inject_watch_notification`, so watcher retries and fallback notices are unchanged. A cancelled delivery (shutdown) withdraws the offer, so the turn cannot carry what the watcher retries. A completion the agent already read with `process(wait/log)` (`is_completion_consumed`, checked for every process in a coalesced batch) is not shown again. Watch-pattern matches, heartbeats and API-server sessions keep queueing.

## Relation to #104434

#104434 (`result_delivery="inject"`) only injects into the **originating** parent turn and is chosen per call by the model. This PR covers the common case where the result arrives during a *later* turn, and is a user-level config default. The two are orthogonal.

## Scope

- Durable claims stay held while the result rides the turn: acknowledged once a tool result carried it (watcher tick), deferred and requeued at turn cleanup otherwise, so nothing is lost and no delivery attempt is spent. API-server sessions and per-task failure notices keep queueing. `gateway/run_busy.py` is untouched: other internal events still never steer.
- New config keys are in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, plus the dashboard selects, `cli-config.yaml.example` and the docs (delegation, tools, gateway internals). No env var. `config_defaults.py` is over its file cap, so both keys are offset by folding neighbouring comments.
- #140296 / #142319 change how the *queue* path coalesces completions; they are orthogonal (with `queue`, the default, nothing here runs).

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_background_results.py`: a real `run_conversation` loop. A result offered while the model is thinking appears on the tool result of the next request, never as a user row. It is red without the `tool_executor` hook.
- `tests/gateway/test_delegation_busy_result_steer.py`: a busy-session result rides the running turn's tool result and no new turn is admitted; an uncarried result is deferred and requeued as the next turn. Both red on `main`.
- `tests/gateway/test_process_busy_result_steer.py` (mode read from a real `config.yaml` through the gateway loader): a busy-session process completion rides the tool result and no turn is admitted; an uncarried one is admitted once as the next turn; one already read with `process(wait)` is not shown again. The carry test is red without the process commit: the completion is delivered at once as a new turn.

Run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`: the two new files plus `tests/gateway/test_completion_delivery.py`, `test_completion_owner_retry.py`, `test_async_delegation_session_binding.py` (all passed). Process part: 14 files incl. `test_background_process_notifications.py`, `test_gateway_shutdown.py`, `test_display_config.py`, `test_web_server.py` → 498 passed. `python scripts/check`: ok. Platform: Linux.

---

**Rebase note (2026-10-15):** rebased onto `main` @ `3dd9e4edfd` (2 commits, clean); `tests/agent/test_background_results.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_delegation_busy_result_mode.py` → 3 passed.






**Update (2026-10-17):** the first version hooked the classic CLI's turn monitor, which no longer runs since classic CLI turns moved onto the gateway; live probe confirmed results still queued. The steer path now lives at the gateway completion-delivery seam and the dead CLI hook is removed. Rebased onto `main` @ `e7e839a5f4`.
**Update (2026-10-24):** rebased onto `main` @ `dd5bc7ee13`; added the background-process completion path (last commit) and a `config_defaults.py` line offset.

prs.title: fix: transform_llm_output rewrites now replace the streamed reply in the TUI and desktop app
prs.body:
A plugin that rewrites replies with `transform_llm_output` now has its rewrite shown in the TUI and desktop app, instead of the raw streamed reply staying on screen.

- `gateway/session_settlement_recovery.py`: a streamed local-viewer turn counts as delivered by the event stream, so the turn handler returns `None` and `message.complete` went out with `text: null` beside `response_transformed: true`. The completion frame now carries the rewritten final when the stream could not.
- `ui-tui/src/app/turnController.ts`: Ink flushed the raw streamed tail as its own segment before appending the final, so even with the text present it showed both. A `response_transformed` completion now replaces the streamed tail (the check moved into a small helper to keep `recordMessageComplete` under its complexity cap).
- Desktop needed no change: its reducer already replaces the bubble when the frame carries text with `response_transformed`.
- Docs: `hooks.md` says which surfaces replace the streamed reply, and that the raw reply is visible while it streams.

Root cause: on the canonical gateway the local adapter's edit is a no-op, so the transformed-final edit "succeeds", the turn is marked delivered, and the only frame left for the rewrite had no text.

## What changes (live, loopback model + real redactor plugin)

Scratch plugin: `transform_llm_output` replaces `SECRET-\d+` with `[REDACTED]`. Model: loopback SSE stub streaming word by word. No paid calls.

| Surface | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Ink TUI (`hermes --tui`, tmux capture after the turn) | `Here is the config. Your api key is SECRET-123 and the backup key is SECRET-456. …` (raw stays; rewrite never shown) | `Here is the config. Your api key is [REDACTED] and the backup key is [REDACTED]. …` (raw while streaming, then replaced) |
| Desktop wire (`message.complete` over the real gateway WS, `source=gui`) | `{"text": null, "status": "complete", "response_transformed": true}` | `{"text": "Here is the config. Your api key is [REDACTED] …", "status": "complete", "response_transformed": true}` |
| Desktop renderer (real `useMessageStream` reducer fed that exact frame sequence) | one bubble, raw text | one bubble, rewritten text |
| Classic CLI | raw box + `[Response transformed after streaming]` + rewrite | unchanged |
| Stored row (`state.db`) | rewrite | rewrite |

Untransformed streamed turns still complete with `text: null` (the stream is the delivery), and messaging turns are untouched (both covered by tests).

## Tests

- `tests/gateway/test_local_viewer_transformed_final.py`: real `TurnRunner.run_sync` on a LOCAL source → `completion_payload` with the streamed handler reply (`None`); asserts the frame carries the rewrite and validates against the `message.complete` contract; controls for an untransformed local turn and a messaging turn. Red on main (`None == '…[REDACTED].'`), green here.
- `ui-tui/src/__tests__/transformedFinal.test.ts`: real `createGatewayEventHandler` + `turnController`; stream raw deltas, complete with a rewrite → transcript holds only the rewrite; control keeps a genuinely distinct streamed tail. Red on main (raw + rewrite), green here.
- Mutation-checked: removing either production change turns its test red.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on 11 touched-area files (79 passed), full `ui-tui` vitest (1884 passed), `python scripts/check` ok.

## Not in this PR

- Every streaming surface still shows the raw reply while it streams, then swaps (Telegram/Discord edit, Slack native stream via `chat.update`). The hook runs on the finished text, so only holding the stream back can prevent that; tracked separately (#102203 / #102481 propose a hook-declared hold for the CLI).
- Messaging replies long enough to be split across several messages keep the raw earlier chunks, and the gateway then sends the whole rewrite again. Needs the stream consumer to rewrite its sealed chunks; separate follow-up.

## Infographic
![transformed-final-local-viewers](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafbb7a/xDJjpCIpMA0oeZMPZV0Fb_ikcdyb7W.png)

prs.title: fix(feishu): bind the profile scope for document-comment events
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes an `@`-mention on a Feishu/Lark **document** silently producing no reply on a multiplexed gateway: the comment agent's provider-key read failed closed with `UnscopedSecretError`.

`plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py::_on_drive_comment_event` submitted the handler as a bare callable, so the hop inherited whatever profile scope the lark WS thread carried. Secondary profiles get away with that: their adapter is created *and connected* inside `_profile_runtime_scope`, so the WS thread carries the override and the hop back onto the adapter loop copies it (`run_coroutine_threadsafe` copies the caller's context). The **primary** profile's adapter is created and connected on a path with no scope (`gateway/run_startup.py::_start_prefilter_platforms` / `_start_connect_pending`), so the hop arrives with an **empty** context. With multiplexing on, `get_secret("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY")` inside `_run_comment_agent` then raises by design, and the handler logs `agent failed: ... UnscopedSecretError` → `Agent returned NO_REPLY` after adding and deleting its `OK` reaction.

A gateway restart cannot help — an empty context is the steady state, not a boot artifact.

The fix binds the *whole-handler* runtime scope at the dispatch site, the same scope a chat message gets from the runner, and resolves the home from the coroutine's own context (the routed profile when one was carried, the launch profile otherwise), so secondary behaviour is unchanged.

Second, related item in the same bug class: `feishu_comment._session_key()` keyed the per-document history cache as `comment-doc:{file_type}:{file_token}` with no profile dimension — one process serves every profile, so once the primary path works, two profiles commenting on the same document would share one transcript. It now includes `hermes_home_key()`.

## Related Issue

No issue filed — found while exercising document-comment mentions end to end on a 7-profile gateway (macOS, Feishu China tenant). Say the word and I'll file one.

Fixes #

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made
