prs.title: feat(channels): add configurable XMPP/Prosody channel with optional OMEMO
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- Add opt-in direct XMPP text conversations through the existing channel supervisor, shared agent dispatch, sessions, tools and reply path. The compatibility worker provides verified Direct TLS or mandatory STARTTLS and optional explicitly pinned legacy OMEMO.
- Configure connection and encryption through the schema-driven WebUI; edit authorization through alias-scoped canonical peer groups. No separate transport allowlist is introduced.
- Remove the API-writable executable path. Only the trusted daemon environment selects the compatibility interpreter; existing virtualenv deployments must migrate before upgrading. Patch Tokio to 1.53.3 and retain the ctutils security fix.
- **Scope boundary:** one-to-one text; no MUC, attachments, MAM backfill, carbons, OMEMO v2, server provisioning or deployment-specific identities.
- **Blast radius:** feature-gated channel registration, channel configuration/attribution and the XMPP authorization tab. The shared agent loop remains authoritative.
- **Linked issues:** Related #12015 for the shared crypto dependency alignment used by the planned native transport follow-up. This published head still uses the compatibility worker; native transport and OMEMO v2 completion are not claimed.

**Not merge-ready:** the formal review's native Rust channel requirement remains open. This head still uses the compatibility worker. The TLS-only Rust prototype has not replaced it: native OMEMO and state migration must be validated first. Removal of the writable executable field and evidence cleanup do not resolve that architecture requirement.

### What this does, simply

An authorized XMPP account can talk to a configured agent and receive its replies without a second agent loop or an HTTP-to-chat relay. Peer policy is checked before dispatch and again before outbound delivery. Empty policy denies access. Encrypted configurations reject plaintext and unpinned devices.

The compatibility worker is currently embedded Python/Slixmpp; optional slixmpp-omemo is an external AGPL-3.0-only backend. This is explicitly part of the outstanding architecture review, not an approved first-party Rust solution.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces exercised:** `surface=web` configuration and `channel=xmpp` listener/reply.
- **Setup / preconditions:** build with `channel-xmpp`, install the documented compatibility dependencies, use an isolated XMPP server with a trusted certificate, configure peer policy and bind the alias to an agent. Set `ZEROCLAW_XMPP_PYTHON` in the trusted service environment when using a virtualenv.
- **Steps to run:** follow `docs/book/src/channels/xmpp.md`; compare an allowed sender with an unlisted sender, send a reply, restart and reconnect. In Advanced, verify there is no executable-path field. The config setter must reject `channels.xmpp.<alias>.python_path`.
- **Expected on this branch:** allowed input enters shared dispatch; unauthorized input produces neither model work nor replies; transport settings persist independently; the executable cannot be selected through channel settings.
- **Prior behavior on master:** no first-party XMPP channel. In this PR before the hardening commit, channel configuration could select an executable; before the pipe fix, simultaneous large frames could stall the listener.

### How I tested

- **Current merged-head validation:** `a5cc35b1c` merges `master` at `4db7afdcf`; the only lockfile conflict retains `ctutils` 0.4.5 and Tokio 1.53.3. On exact tree `ae98530b52848c44d478e5a361f302e40190cc79`, `cargo test --locked -j4 -p zeroclaw-config --test xmpp` passed 3 tests and `cargo test --locked -j4 -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --features channel-xmpp --lib xmpp::tests` passed 3 tests. `git diff --cached --check` passed. Fresh required CI remains pending; native implementation work is not claimed as shipped by this merge.
- **Earlier hardening validation:** `508ffa78c`; the evidence-only follow-ups update Markdown and the Advanced screenshot.
- `cargo test --locked --release -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --features channel-xmpp --lib xmpp::tests -j4`: **3 passed, 0 failed**, including simultaneous full-pipe incoming/outgoing frames and authorization/encryption admission.
- `cargo test --locked --release -p zeroclaw-config --test xmpp -j4`: **3 passed, 0 failed**, including rejection of the executable property, ignored legacy values, encrypted-secret metadata and option roundtrip.
- Rustfmt and `git diff --check` passed for the changed Rust files.
- Actual local WebUI renderer in visible Chrome, synthetic API matching the new schema: executable control absent; transport/password/OMEMO/enablement/peer-policy persistence passed; no page errors or mobile overflow. [Evidence](.pr-evidence/xmpp-executable-setting.md) and [Advanced screenshot](.pr-evidence/xmpp-omemo-desktop.png), 1440 x 1000. This fixture is not production authentication or OMEMO interoperability evidence.
- The earlier assembled listener/agent/reply proof remains attributed to its recorded code revision `37275ff8c`: [listener evidence](.pr-evidence/xmpp-listener.md). It used verified TLS and counted authorized versus unauthorized model calls, with OMEMO disabled. It is not relabeled as a fresh current-head encrypted test.
- **CI relied on:** fresh required CI must validate this published head; historical green gates belong to their recorded revisions.
- **Known gap:** native OMEMO implementation/migration and architecture acceptance remain open. No current-head production encrypted conversation is claimed.
- **Visual evidence:** screenshot above, English locale, real renderer with synthetic data. Temporary scripts and raw JSON have been removed from the PR as requested.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: feature-gated transport process/network and service-user state directory; no privilege elevation. Interpreter selection belongs to the trusted daemon environment, not Web/API channel settings.
- New external network calls? Yes: operator-selected XMPP endpoint, TLS verified against the account JID domain. No plaintext or trust-all fallback.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes: normal encrypted config storage, private worker pipe and protected OMEMO state; passwords are not placed in argv, environment, screenshots or logs.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; public fixtures use synthetic identities.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes: authorized remote messages enter the existing shared runtime as untrusted user input; they do not grant tools or widen peer policy.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for the prototype interpreter setting: `python_path` is removed and legacy serialized values are ignored. Other connection, encryption, state and peer-policy settings remain supported.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: remove `channels.xmpp.<alias>.python_path`; add operator-controlled `ZEROCLAW_XMPP_PYTHON` (default `python3`).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Upgrade steps:** before replacing an existing virtualenv deployment, set `ZEROCLAW_XMPP_PYTHON` to that existing interpreter in the service environment and restart with the new build. Preserve the state directory and manually pinned OMEMO fingerprints. Do not replace an encrypted deployment with the TLS-only native prototype.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** restore the previous binary/configuration and consistent state backup, then restart. Retain the old interpreter setting until the upgrade has been verified; the compatibility worker's state format is unchanged by this hardening.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** omit `channel-xmpp` or disable the alias to stop it. Removing the trusted interpreter environment setting returns to `python3`; it does not enable a channel-config executable override.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** offline channel, TLS/authentication error, missing interpreter dependencies, write deadline or send failure. Do not log bodies, credentials or private identity/session material while diagnosing.

prs.title: refactor(crypto): unify ChaCha20Poly1305 consumers
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Config and TLS currently use ChaCha20Poly1305 0.10 while other consumers already resolve 0.11. Move the two application encryption consumers to one reusable workspace declaration for 0.11, explicitly enabling key zeroization.
  - Remove the unused runtime dependency and the providers dependency used only to reach `OsRng`. OAuth now uses the existing `rand` dependency's operating-system RNG, preserving its entropy source and failure behavior.
  - Preserve `enc2:` secrets and `ZCCAKE1` encrypted CA-key envelopes. Frozen synthetic fixtures generated with 0.10.1 verify old ciphertext decryption, byte-identical ciphertext generation for rollback, and tampering/truncation rejection.
- **Scope boundary:** No new cipher implementation, format migration, key rotation, dependency-policy exception, XMPP transport replacement, or external-library changes. Optional Nostr dependencies can still retain older packages in the lockfile.
- **Blast radius:** Secret encryption in config, encrypted CA private keys in TLS, OAuth PKCE randomness, and dependency resolution for runtime consumers.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11847. This PR is independent of that PR and can be consumed by its native transport work.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw has two real users of this encryption library and two crates that do not need to depend on it directly. This change gives the real users a shared version and security feature definition, and removes the unnecessary direct dependencies. Stored secrets and encrypted certificate-authority keys keep their existing formats and keys; no conversion is required.

In a separate graph-only composition with the native XMPP candidate, this reduces the duplicate-crate policy errors from ten to eight by eliminating the older active `aead` and `universal-hash` families. That composition still fails on eight other duplicates and is not presented as merge-ready XMPP or complete OMEMO v2 support. This standalone PR passes the existing dependency policy.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Automated tests exercise the persisted formats, authentication failures, PKCE generation, and real TLS handshakes; no manual UI behavior changes.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None before submission. Pending CI is not counted as passing evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local checks ran on Linux x86_64 with Rust 1.98.0. Windows/macOS execution and a full workspace build were not performed locally.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo test --locked -j4 -p zeroclaw-config --lib secrets::tests
test result: ok. 78 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
cargo test --locked -j4 -p zeroclaw-tls --lib
test result: ok. 43 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
cargo test --locked -j4 -p zeroclaw-providers --lib auth::oauth_common::tests
test result: ok. 14 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
cargo check --locked -j4 -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
Finished dev profile; exit 0
cargo check --locked -j4 -p zeroclaw-config --no-default-features --lib
Finished dev profile; exit 0
cargo clippy --locked -j4 -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tls -p zeroclaw-providers --lib --tests -- -D warnings
Finished dev profile; exit 0
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0
cargo deny check
advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok; exit 0
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Generated the frozen vectors using a separate 0.10.1 fixture executable, without adding the old library as a test dependency. Compared all laboratory source files with the committed tree. Verified the native-XMPP composition's dependency result separately; no production deployment or combined native-channel runtime test is claimed here.
- **Warnings investigated:** The untouched upstream dependency check has eight warnings about unused policy skips/wrappers. This branch additionally leaves the `chacha20 =0.9.1` skip unused in the selected default profile, because the internal encryption consumers moved forward. The skip remains necessary for optional Nostr support and is preserved; `deny.toml` is unchanged. Strict Clippy passes without warnings.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no rendered interface or supported CLI output was changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `b7688549974280a1c9e54d7f118c99fd65539f4a`; automated tests in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/secrets.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-tls/src/certgen.rs`, and the existing OAuth/TLS suites. The final amendment only clarifies the RNG documentation; functional test code and behavior are unchanged.

prs.title: feat(session): implement append-only session event history
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Make versioned, append-only session events the canonical conversation and execution history, so replay rebuilds state without repeating external effects.
  - Separate the kernel coordinator, storage implementations and host composition into explicit ownership boundaries. CLI, RPC, ACP, gateway and channel adapters use the same Session model and authorized history queries.
  - Capture provider attempts, reasoning and multimodal output, tool progress and outcomes, approvals, model/policy observations, context compression and linked child execution. Preserve provider item identities and supplemental fields without copying normalized bodies.
  - Provide SQLite and JSONL persistence, crash recovery, idempotent receipts, branches, search and auditable payload erasure. Interrupted external effects retain diagnostics and an unknown outcome when completion cannot be proved.
  - Upgrade legacy SQLite, JSONL and ACP history into the configured native format with resumable imports, writer fencing and renamed source backups. No per-session locator or independent ACP history database remains after upgrade.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not replace the file/blob, memory, cost, task or live-config authorities; their historical references remain session evidence. No additional at-rest encryption, dashboard redesign or complete runtime/plugin extraction.
- **Blast radius:** Session startup, persistence and recovery; provider and tool dispatch; approvals; child agents; CLI/RPC/ACP/channel/gateway history; session cleanup, alias lifecycle and existing storage configuration.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10526. Related #9600. Related #9487. Related #9488. These broader coordination issues are not automatically closed.

### What this does, simply

A saved transcript currently cannot fully explain how a session reached its final answer. This change saves the observed execution as ordered events: what the user supplied, which model ran, what the model returned, which tools and approvals were involved, and what happened when execution failed or stopped. Conversation views and retained context are rebuilt from those facts.

All entrances use the same session storage. Existing histories are imported automatically and the original files become backups. Historical permissions explain past execution; they never grant permission to a resumed session. Unknown completion remains unknown, and reading or replaying history never reruns a tool.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, using a disposable configuration/data directory on each branch.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`, plus the ACP protocol entrance and messaging-channel adapters covered by automated tests.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure an agent named `fixture` with a working provider and tool policy in a disposable copy of an existing installation. Stop other processes using that directory. Use separate copies for `master` and this branch. Select `channels.session_backend` as `sqlite` or `jsonl` and repeat for both.
- **Steps to run:** Run `zeroclaw agent -a fixture --session-state-file /var/tmp/session-events-review.json`, exchange a message, request a harmless permitted tool action, exit, then reopen with the same command. Inspect the installation's `sessions` directory and the imported source backups. Repeat with a copy containing legacy ACP history, then open/resume it through ACP.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** A native event history and installation manifest are created; user/provider/tool/approval observations and retained context survive reopening. Legacy sources are renamed after successful import. ACP uses the standard session store. An interrupted effect without a proven outcome is not silently rerun.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Mutable transcripts and separate persistence paths retain conversation messages but do not provide the common execution-event history or installation-wide migration described above.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None claimed before PR creation. Local checks below provide the current evidence; PR CI remains to run.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Full workspace/all-features, cross-platform/MSRV builds, million-event performance and VM power-loss scenarios were not rerun in the final validation round. Summary/catalog queries still scan event history; this is not a constant-time performance claim.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux, Rust 1.99.0, locked dependencies, `TMPDIR=/var/tmp`. Tested production source matches commit `61d3eb2d24`; the only subsequent test change replaced a prohibited error macro with an equivalent constructor and its regression was rerun.

```sh
cargo +1.99.0 test --locked   -p zeroclaw-kernel -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-session-host   --lib --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4
# kernel:       137 passed; 0 failed
# providers:   2017 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored
# session-host:  10 passed; 0 failed

cargo +1.99.0 test --locked   -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway   --lib --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4
# runtime:  5777 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored
# channels: 2025 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
# gateway:   674 passed; 0 failed

cargo +1.99.0 test --locked   -p zeroclaw-kernel -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-session-host   --lib provider_content_metadata_survives_complete_and_interrupted_capture   -- --test-threads=4
# providers: 1 passed; 0 failed (SQLite/JSONL, complete/interrupted)

cargo +1.99.0 clippy --locked   -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-kernel   -p zeroclaw-session-host -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-tools   -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway   -p zeroclaw --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 58s

cargo +1.99.0 fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0

git diff --cached --check
# exit 0

DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/architecture/session-events.md   bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
# Linting: 1 file(s); Summary: 0 error(s)

python3 scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py
# Checked authored Markdown links in 219 file(s); no broken local targets.
```

Earlier validation of the session-unification stage also passed API 346, infra 357 and tools 1,368 library tests, plus three standalone ACP CLI component tests. The infra round skipped the expensive commit-byte-boundary test after its separate passing run; these earlier checks are not represented as a final full-workspace rerun. The final all-targets Clippy compiles the updated test and entrance call sites.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed migration publication and source-backup ordering, canonical field ownership, live read/effect authorization, partial/error/unknown distinctions and payload-reference reuse. Automated boundary tests exercise both stores, reopening, concurrent metadata observations, queued input recovery, owner isolation, reasoning access, erasure and child policy. No live-provider or production-data manual smoke is claimed. The staged secret scan flagged two synthetic redaction fixtures, including one moved existing fixture; both were inspected and contain no real credentials.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes execution and storage behavior, not interface layout or styling.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `61d3eb2d24`; library/integration boundaries and ACP wire tests listed above. Public storage and recovery contract: `docs/book/src/architecture/session-events.md`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A for presentation; relevant automated output tails are included above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Complete and interrupted provider captures retain supplemental fields in both backends; queued inputs retain the admitted workspace; ACP wire resume uses the shared store; current authorization remains effective after reopening and policy changes.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The complete feature/platform/MSRV and VM power-loss matrices require separate environments and were not repeated in the final round. Focused checks and the ten-crate all-targets lint cover the implemented boundaries without claiming those matrices.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Introduces session command/query capabilities and native history files within the existing configured data directory. They default to current owner/policy checks; history and reasoning access are separately authorized, and stored policy evidence cannot mint live grants.
- New external network calls? **No.** Existing provider, tool and delivery transports remain the effect owners.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** New durable capture paths use existing credential classification and preserve only recognized opaque replay material under its existing access rules. No new encryption system is added; ordinary messages, reasoning and media remain plaintext, so historical content retention expands the data available to authorized local readers.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Fixtures use synthetic values; private audit documents and local reports are excluded.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Context is restored from event-backed projections. Provider metadata and unknown fields remain classified evidence, cannot confer authority, and are not blindly injected into model-visible text; replay does not execute external effects.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Authorization is resolved live for reads and effects, incoming metadata cannot alter storage-graph identity, and erasure follows referenced content leaves. Backups remain outside an erasure guarantee and must follow the operator's retention policy.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for persisted writers after cutover; existing histories are imported.** Supported old fields/records remain readable, missing historical facts remain absent, and unknown variants do not fabricate successful execution.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes, existing CLI persistence behavior changes.** Reuses `channels.session_backend` and existing CLI options; no new storage-selection key or environment variable is required. Recorded model-provider aliases cannot be renamed while native history depends on them.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** The declared Rust 1.96.0 floor is unchanged; local validation used 1.99.0.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: Stop all old writers; take a consistent backup of the complete configured data directory, including SQLite WAL state where applicable; keep the desired `sqlite` or `jsonl` backend selected; start the new binary. Installation import resumes after interruption and publishes ready only after successful import and source archival. Legacy files are renamed as backups, including `acp-sessions.db`. Do not reopen the migrated installation with an older writer.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Before migration, reverting this commit is sufficient. After migration, stop all processes, preserve the native directory separately, restore the complete pre-upgrade data/config backup and deploy the prior binary. Reverting code alone does not reverse the storage cutover; writes made after migration must be retained separately for recovery.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None to restore legacy writers. Existing `channels.session_backend` selects SQLite or JSONL and native switching preserves event identity; it is not a rollback to the old format.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Startup/history admission refuses an incomplete or conflicting import; capture errors stop execution; interrupted effects appear as unknown with diagnostics. Inspect session initialization/migration/capture errors and the installation manifest state. Never bypass the fence or clear the manifest to force an older writer.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This PR does not supersede another PR.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): support stored OAuth profiles
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. This branch integrates upstream revision `4db7afdcfa9a4b07d55dc6df4331d8076b64c2cb`; gateway OAuth test helpers and upstream HTTP/2 connection-drain test support are both retained.

**What changed and why:**

- Adds optional Anthropic `auth_mode = "oauth"` so an alias can use its same-named stored setup-token profile. Missing or unsupported profiles fail closed at request time; streaming preserves sanitized underlying store-read/parse causes.
- Preserves static `api_key` behavior when OAuth is not selected, including inline setup tokens, and preserves the selected alias through provider construction and gateway/CLI consumers. The master integration also preserves opt-in single-tool policy through Anthropic chat and streaming, including hidden-thinking fallback and accepted whitespace-padded official endpoints.
- Keeps Quickstart's existing synthetic API-key/setup-token selector and inline mapping. The schema-field filter preserves that single legacy selector; it does not onboard stored-profile OAuth aliases. Whether this filter requires a recorded runtime holding-crate exception is a Core Team decision; no exception is claimed.
- Runs gateway and foundation-only CLI provider construction off Tokio workers, including existing Qwen/MiniMax token refresh operations.
- Keeps a credential-refresh failure distinct from missing configuration, so a failed gateway seed does not block unrelated configured agents behind Quickstart.

**Scope boundary:** no profile migration, new active-profile selection behavior, browser OAuth, refresh lifecycle or retry-policy redesign, custom OAuth endpoint, provider protocol change, or general configuration/readiness refactor. The existing setup-token command still sets its active profile; runtime OAuth selection ignores that selector and uses the configured alias.

**Blast radius:** Anthropic configuration, credential lookup and request headers, typed provider factories and fallback admission, gateway bootstrap/WebSocket construction, foundation-only CLI, Quickstart field generation, the schema-driven Web config editor, and provider documentation. Alias-aware gateway bootstrap and the foundation-only `zeroclaw agent` CLI can invoke existing Qwen/MiniMax refresh calls; the CLI now honors the selected alias's endpoint and options instead of configless defaults.

**Linked issue(s):** Related #9464: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9464

### What this does, simply

An Anthropic alias can use a setup token already saved under the same profile name. Setting `auth_mode = "oauth"` enables that lookup; replacing the saved token affects the next request. Existing supported static aliases and Quickstart setup-token onboarding keep their previous behavior. A gateway seed's credential-refresh failure remains a real error for that provider, but no longer makes unrelated configured agents appear to need onboarding.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: synthetic profile and loopback HTTP fixtures exercise selection, rejection and refresh failures without an operator token or live vendor call.

### How I tested

Current integration: `a53232680f67deb4f944c2faadd20142ad1648e8`, tree `4fd7aebf04024a3090046750023eacaff9829e4e`, merging master `4db7afdcfa`. The only manual conflict resolution retains both independent gateway dev-dependencies (`zeroclaw-providers/test-helpers` and `h2`); no production logic required manual editing.

**Commands run and tail output:**

exit 0

exit 0

Comment hygiene gate passed.

Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 41s

The gateway tests cover configured aliases, synthetic credential refresh success/failure, unrelated-agent readiness, legacy Quickstart and upstream HTTP/2 shutdown/drain behavior. Provider/config tests cover exact same-profile selection, fail-closed ownership and metadata/endpoint admission, legacy static credentials, lazy streaming lookup and sanitized underlying profile errors. The foundation-only CLI tests explicitly cover the feature configuration not selected by default-feature workspace tests.

**CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate run 40101869581](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40101869581) passed on `a53232680f67deb4f944c2faadd20142ad1648e8`, including workspace lint/rustdoc/comment hygiene, tests, repeated Parallel Runtime Test, MSRV, Security, Web Permission Tests, Linux build, macOS/Windows checks and plugin integration coverage. At completion, the PR check rollup had 50 successes, eight expected event/path-selected skips, no failures/cancellations and no pending check. No earlier-head check is represented as current validation.

**Known CI coverage gap:** none identified for this mechanical integration after the selected exact-head CI and focused local checks. Local tests cover the foundation-only CLI execution gap separately. Expected CI skips are push-only debounce, PR-excluded benchmarks, unchanged-path Nix/relay/targeted Windows Clippy, package preflight without a version bump, and the separate advisory Windows workflow. No full local container `./dev/ci.sh all`, exhaustive all-features/platform sweep, live vendor call or deployment was performed; those are not claimed by the selected CI coverage.

**Local diagnostics and historical limitations:** stable Rust 1.99 test builds emit `Atomic::fetch_update` deprecation warnings at `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/upload.rs:90` and `rpc/dispatch.rs:42208`; both files are byte-identical to master. Darwin test linking also emits `ld: __eh_frame section too large`, a platform-toolchain warning. Warnings-denied Clippy passed for the four named crates with installed Rust 1.98.1, matching CI's 1.98 minor line (CI pins 1.98.0); root-package lint is covered by the successful exact-head CI lint job. No lint suppression or unrelated production repair was added. Earlier Darwin parallel-runtime/timing failures and old MSRV timeouts remain historical failures, not current results; current exact-head Parallel Runtime Test and MSRV checks passed.

**Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** No live vendor call, operator credential/configuration change or deployment. Synthetic loopback refresh and production gateway-handler tests cover HTTP 200/401/503, original typed failure propagation and unrelated-agent completion. Static integration inspection checks adjacent consumers and unchanged credential writer behavior.

**Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot, reused from the earlier feature revision. Adding the schema field exposes an optional Auth Mode selector in the Web config editor's Connection tab; this merge does not change its descriptor or Web rendering code. The actual-interface captures show unset, `api_key`, and `oauth` choices and the unsaved OAuth selection at 1280×720 in English.

**Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** captures on `448bf7bf5ea38de6e58695cbf1feb9b27a4a0aec`, with identical interface code in `f05baa7e1edb210ae059d152027007e71c16f155`, using the real local gateway and Web config editor with a disposable schema-version-3 fixture. These are retained interface evidence, not screenshots of the entire current tree or proof of credential persistence/vendor authentication.

**Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Auth Mode choices](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3415bac0-b74e-4a1f-9f3d-e054c017b18a) and [unsaved OAuth selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0b1c79b-059b-45d7-b1ea-fcf32d5d0299).

![Auth Mode choices in the synthetic Web config editor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3415bac0-b74e-4a1f-9f3d-e054c017b18a)

![Unsaved OAuth selection in the synthetic Web config editor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0b1c79b-059b-45d7-b1ea-fcf32d5d0299)

**Action or changed state and observed result:** opening the selector displayed all three choices; selecting `oauth` produced one unsaved change. The draft was discarded and a backend read confirmed `auth_mode` remained unset. The gateway regression separately observes HTTP 200, `fixture answer`, `event: done`, no `event: error`, exactly one refresh request per case and a typed error for the failed seed, without incorrectly requiring onboarding for unrelated agents.

**If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no duplicate full container/platform sweep beyond the selected exact-head CI and focused local coverage; no real credentials, vendor calls or deployment are needed for this mechanical integration. No new visual state was introduced by the merge, so the unchanged presentation evidence above is reused.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? Yes: alias-aware gateway bootstrap and the foundation-only `zeroclaw agent` CLI can invoke the existing Qwen/MiniMax refresh operation when their selected alias supplies a refresh token. No endpoint implementation or protocol is added; the CLI now honors the alias's endpoint and options instead of configless defaults. Both construction paths are isolated from async workers.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- Store lookup uses the existing ZeroClaw state-directory auth store, not a broader file-access scope. Its existing legacy-encryption migration can rewrite that store during a request-time load; no migration or refresh policy is added by this PR. The state directory follows the configured location, defaulting to `~/.zeroclaw` (or relative `.zeroclaw` if no home directory is available).
- Risk and mitigation: Anthropic OAuth uses only the exactly matching supported stored setup-token profile and official API root. Invalid ownership, aliases, inline keys, profile kinds and custom endpoints fail closed. Stored-profile OAuth tokens do not enter configuration or diagnostics; existing static inline credentials retain their prior behavior. Boot refresh warnings deliberately omit raw vendor bodies, while request consumers retain the original typed cause. Tests use synthetic tokens and loopback servers.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? No for the fail-closed ownership changes and exhaustive Rust config literals below. Existing supported static aliases retain authentication behavior.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: optional Anthropic `auth_mode = "oauth"`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: supported static aliases need no change. To opt in, store a same-named profile using `zeroclaw auth setup-token --model-provider anthropic --profile <alias>`, select OAuth mode, and leave `api_key` and `kind` unset. OAuth requires a 1–63-character ASCII alias using only lowercase letters, digits and single internal underscores, starting and ending with a letter or digit; for example, `team_sub` is valid and `team:sub` is not. This PR does not tighten ordinary validation for non-OAuth aliases. The broader legacy-alias transition described in #9464 is tracked separately for v0.9.0.
- Renaming an OAuth configuration alias does not move its stored profile. Prepare the profile under the new alias name before using it; otherwise the renamed alias fails its request instead of borrowing the old or active profile.
- Explicit cross-provider profile IDs now fail closed for every `AuthService::get_profile` caller. Select a profile belonging to the requested provider.
- A non-Anthropic slot with `kind = "anthropic"` no longer inherits OAuth mode or `server_fallback_models` from a same-named Anthropic slot. Configure its own static credentials. Anthropic `server_fallback_models` are honored only on native `anthropic` aliases; use one if you need server-side fallback. Generic client-side `fallback_models` remain available on the slot. Fallback readiness now canonicalizes supported `kind` synonyms consistently with dispatch, such as `grok` to `xai`.
- Gateway bootstrap no longer invents an `openrouter.default` seed when no model is configured. A configured seed is a bare alias provider without the resilience wrapper; production chat still constructs its selected agent's provider independently. Existing Qwen/MiniMax refresh calls can now delay gateway bootstrap and the foundation-only `zeroclaw agent` CLI within their existing timeouts, but do not block Tokio workers. The CLI now honors the selected alias's endpoint and options. A gateway refresh failure retains configured readiness, not provider-health success; the affected CLI/request still returns the original failure, and missing/invalid configuration still stays unconfigured.
- Rust exhaustive `AnthropicModelProviderConfig` literals need `auth_mode: None` or `..Default::default()`. The optional serialized field remains omitted unless selected. The additive `AnthropicAuthMode` type and `AnthropicBuilder::auth_profile` method expose the explicit mode; `AnthropicModelProviderConfig::has_official_oauth_endpoint` exposes exact public-root admission. The provider auth module exports cloneable `ProviderCredentialRefreshError` for construction-time refresh failures. Error-chain formatting remains transparent; streamed profile-load errors now retain sanitized nested causes.
- OAuth accepts only stored token profiles resolving to the Authorization setup-token kind. A stored token tagged `auth_kind = "api-key"` and generic OAuth token sets remain unsupported. Metadata-less `sk-ant-oat01-` tokens now infer Authorization in `detect_auth_kind`, including `auth paste-token` without `--auth-kind`; existing API-key metadata is not rewritten. Re-store a genuine setup token with `auth setup-token` before OAuth opt-in if old metadata prevents use.
- Missing-credential diagnostics now mention explicit stored-profile OAuth, including for legacy aliases. OAuth warmup resolves the profile and reports a non-fatal warning on failure. The debug `credential_len` log attribute is removed; diagnostic consumers must not depend on it.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** remove `auth_mode` from opted-in aliases and restore their prior static `api_key` configuration; reverting the feature commits restores the earlier implementation.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `auth_mode = "oauth"` is the opt-in; no feature flag.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** unsupported/missing same-named profile, invalid alias, inline-key or `kind` conflict, unsupported endpoint, or `seed_credential_refresh_failed` warnings. A warning preserves configured readiness but does not certify credential health; correct the affected provider's credentials.
- **Ownership/bootstrap recovery:** correct foreign profile selectors, configure cross-family static slots independently, and select a model when onboarding is required. Reverting the feature commits restores earlier lookup/seed behavior; disabling OAuth alone does not revert those changes.
- **API/profile recovery:** adapt exhaustive Rust literals as above. Re-store a genuine setup token when old API-key metadata prevents OAuth; retain static mode for intended API-key authentication. Reverting code does not rewrite stored profile metadata.

## Supersede Attribution

Not applicable — this PR does not supersede another PR.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Depends on #11411. Related #8289 and #11576. Current head: 4535e321f4d65cf092903522540a4df66754dea7.
- **What changed and why:** Upstream #11576 now provides the canonical `TuiRegistry::for_config` implementation, fresh-key provisioning and domain-separated signing. This PR preserves that production code and retains a supplemental 42-line regression in one file relative to #11411.
- **Scope boundary:** The test covers separate config/data directories, a conflicting valid data key, a colocated control, and a corrupt canonical key. It does not change key derivation, provisioning, configuration, or authentication policy.
- **Blast radius:** Supplemental test coverage only; the cumulative PR diff still includes the declared prerequisite stack and retained contributor history.

### What this does, simply

The test ensures a second key in the runtime-data directory cannot silently become the signing authority. Corrupt canonical key material must not fall back to that unrelated key. Normal fresh-key creation remains covered by the upstream tests.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: verify the supplemental diff against #11411 and run `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib config_signing_key_is_used_when_runtime_data_lives_elsewhere`.
- **Interface exercised:** Internal registry signing used by remote RPC TUI continuity, with synthetic temporary directories and real SecretStore keys.
- **Expected:** Signatures use the config-owned authority with separate or colocated directories; corruption refuses signing rather than using or replacing the unrelated data key. The current master implementation should also pass when this supplemental test is transplanted; this is additional coverage of the merged repair.

### How I tested

- **Current integration:** Head `4535e321f4d65cf092903522540a4df66754dea7` retains its previous published head `92bfff06da18590ccbca8167b1818c898e09b4a9`, pinned master `7b84f9c806ee78bc1825df007ca14c6e222fb293`, and refreshed adjacent prerequisite `fc96815d43abdf01f877be73f725b60a3d68f1ab` as ancestors. The six draft refreshes were pushed atomically by ordinary fast-forward; contributor histories are retained. The old-to-new changes are six upstream files, with only independent Fluent additions requiring resolution. The separate #11234 author-adoption candidate is not imported into these drafts.
- **Current focused validation:** The [combined-stack job](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010452447/job/114088977130) passed on exact source `7d5d8f566d14cf3b7e4dc90446711d7a6c6c7fb7`: formatting; `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests`; config 7, storage 209, RPC 878, authority 26, principal 92, and steering 15 tests, all with zero failures/ignored; and Clippy for runtime/infra/config with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`. Fourteen selected RPC regressions each have exactly one passing record. Filters overlap; these are per-command results, not a unique-test total or full-workspace run. The separate superseded canonical-admission job in that workflow failed compilation; its failure is not hidden by this successful combined-stack job.
- **Current upstream CI:** Fresh required checks run on the published head above. Their exact status and the landing decision are recorded in the [coordination handoff](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11408#issuecomment-6023921255). A passed fork job is not a substitute for those checks or independent Core review.
- **Adversarial review:** The independent refresh review verified all six old heads and canonical `d5df4214` ancestry, every refreshed stack link, byte identity with master for the five non-Fluent upstream files, and exactly one occurrence of each retained SOP/timeout Fluent key. No actionable finding remained in this bounded refresh review. The broader prior security review remains recorded on its earlier source, not represented as a new full sweep.
- **Historical sensitivity evidence:** [Earlier validation](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000499635) on `29b123f08874cdc28f74e2b2338a8e4bc4eb5231` passed enrollment 46/46 and demonstrated intended failures when append guarding or steering revocation was removed. These tests were not rerun as mutation tests in the current six-draft refresh; the relevant OIDC implementation is unchanged by this upstream-only refresh.
- **Limits:** Local Rust execution remains blocked by Windows Application Control (OS 4551), without a bypass. No production deployment, provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, or milestone closure occurred. The earlier Keycloak 20/20 and Authentik 10/18 result does not certify this integration. Required CI, Core review, and a safe prerequisite landing decision remain distinct gates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or filesystem scope? No supplemental production changes.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets/tokens/credentials handling changed? No supplemental production changes. Generated temporary test keys exercise the upstream behavior.
- PII or real identities in fixtures? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for the supplemental test-only delta. Runtime compatibility belongs to upstream #11576 and the declared prerequisites.
- Config/env/CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Inherited session compatibility:** The #11408 prerequisite requires the existing `Sessions:Update` grant in addition to Create/Execute for `session/run-once`, because it closes the transient session. A late close refusal is reported explicitly after the completed turn; retrying the whole operation can repeat the turn. Unsupported guarded backend operations fail explicitly.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback path:** Remove this supplemental regression if needed; it has no production rollback effect. Preserve upstream #11576 and prerequisite fixes. The cumulative stack's rollback requires separate review.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** None.
- **Observable symptoms:** The regression fails when signing consults a conflicting runtime-data key or silently recovers from corrupt canonical key material.

## Supersede Attribution

The earlier production repair overlaps the now-merged #11576. This refresh adopts that upstream implementation unchanged and retains only the additional test. All original contributor and prerequisite commits remain in the ancestry.

prs.title: fix(memory): require vector evidence before automatic supersession
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Automatic Core conflict handling consumed ordinary recall scores. BM25 batch normalization and the LIKE fallback can assign `1.0` to an unrelated row, causing consolidation to soft-hide it at the default `0.85` threshold. Conflict selection now uses a separate `Memory::recall_for_supersession` contract whose scores must be raw cosine similarities. Its default returns no candidates.
- SQLite reuses its existing hydration and visibility filters, but bypasses keyword ranking, hybrid fusion, recent-row listing and LIKE fallback for this query. Auditing and read-time scanning remain in the existing decorators; the retrieval cache is bypassed. Principal- and agent-scoped wrappers retain the closed default.
- Configuration and trait documentation now make the scoped-wrapper limitation, model-dependent threshold risk, disable control and text-only deduplication limit explicit. No default or implementation behavior changes in the follow-up.
- Regression coverage exercises production `consolidate_turn` with SQLite: keyword/stopword/substring matches, both Daily-history controls, primary and typed-fact writes, absent stored vectors, orthogonal vectors, explicit BM25 mode, hybrid rank versus raw cosine, positive supersession, disabled supersession, wrapper forwarding and read filtering.
- **Scope boundary:** Ordinary recall ranking, deduplication, category choice, config defaults, schema and existing supersession markers are unchanged. Cosine similarity remains the existing heuristic, not proof that two statements contradict. This does not automatically restore previously hidden rows.
- **Blast radius:** Memory conflict selection and the memory trait's optional evidence query; API implementations remain source-compatible through the default method. No runtime routing or OIDC policy changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11655. Related #11657; its category-selection proposal remains separate.

### What this does, simply

Finding a memory near the top of a search result does not mean it replaces an older fact. Without embedding evidence, automatic consolidation will keep both facts visible instead of hiding one because of a shared word. With vectors, the existing similarity threshold still applies, using the vector score itself.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: the optional A/B negative control below adds signal beyond the passing final-head regressions.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Production memory consolidation and persisted SQLite visibility, shared by runtime surfaces; no rendered-interface claim.
- **Setup / preconditions:** An allowed Rust build environment; no external provider, credentials or paid service. Fixtures use a scripted consolidation provider and deterministic embedding vectors.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-memory --lib consolidation::consolidate_turn_tests --no-default-features --locked`. For the A/B negative control, keep the tests and replace the conflict candidate query in `conflict.rs` with the old `memory.recall(content, 10, None, None, None)` call, then run `keyword_only_consolidation_keeps_unrelated_core_visible` and `supersession_uses_raw_cosine_not_hybrid_rank`; restore the candidate query afterward.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Unrelated Core rows remain listed and recallable with `superseded_by` unset; positive vector-backed replacements still soft-hide their predecessor after the replacement is stored.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The ordinary-recall negative control can hide a Core row based on a keyword/fallback score. The repaired regressions passed in hosted CI. The old-code negative controls were also reproduced locally in the October 24 follow-up below.

### How I tested

- **Tested revision:** 60eda90a28cc346123dfae213898ef6f752086eb, an eleven-line documentation follow-up to 5aee41d7003514039893175470c52bed692d5f09. Only Rustdoc/configuration descriptions change; defaults, executable code, test bodies and Cargo.lock are unchanged.
- **Local validation, 2026-10-24:** Ubuntu 24.04, Rust/Cargo 1.98.0, locked offline dependencies, package default features disabled, two test threads. The focused suite passed before and after the negative controls:

  ```text
  cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-memory --lib --no-default-features consolidation::consolidate_turn_tests -- --test-threads=2
  17 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 541 filtered out

  Old ordinary-recall query restored temporarily:
  keyword_only_consolidation_keeps_unrelated_core_visible: FAILED (expected)
  supersession_uses_raw_cosine_not_hybrid_rank: FAILED (expected)

  Reviewed query restored byte-for-byte; focused suite rerun:
  17 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 541 filtered out

  rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/zeroclaw-api/src/memory_traits.rs crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs
  No output; exit 0.
  git diff --check
  No output; exit 0.
  ```

- **Negative-control observations:** The keyword-only case hid the existing Pixel phone fact; the hybrid-score case set the existing row's supersession marker. Both failures were assertion failures after successful compilation. Restoring the candidate query removed both failures. These checks used this PR's deterministic fixtures, not a live embedding provider or the reported production corpus.
- **Historical hosted CI:** [Quality Gate 38123013930](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38123013930) passed on the preceding 5aee41d7003514039893175470c52bed692d5f09 head through merge snapshot d57d9b3d52e749603f0ef8f02b5f0d7964c2ea8d. It includes Format, Lint, workspace Test, PostgreSQL Memory and CI Required Gate. [Memory receipt](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38123013930/job/114421530551). These are historical results, not checks on the documentation follow-up. Current-head required checks and independent review remain separate landing requirements.
- **Known coverage limits:** No full workspace rerun, live embedding-provider acceptance, full channel-turn reproduction, or replay of the reported private corpus. Historical Parallel Runtime Test and advisory Windows nextest were skipped, not passed. Original native-Windows test/formatter attempts stopped with Application Control error 4551; this follow-up used the existing Linux environment.
- **Source review:** Two adversarial passes traced both consolidation writes, scope defaults, candidate/marker ownership, scan forwarding, cache invalidation and the difference between similarity and replacement evidence. The new documentation does not enable scoped writes or select a new global threshold. Final re-review confirmed no executable changes.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; configuration descriptions change semantically, with no layout or interaction change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No new endpoints or provider capabilities; the candidate query uses the existing embedder/cache path.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; fixture facts are synthetic. The read-scan fixture uses a literal placeholder token reference and `example.invalid`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new trust source or scan bypass. Existing scanner filtering remains on candidate reads.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for storage/API/config compatibility. Intentional behavior correction: keyword-only searches no longer authorize automatic supersession; both Core entries remain visible.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No; existing field documentation clarifies the evidence requirement and recovery limit.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A; no migration. Previously hidden rows require a separate, deliberate recovery decision.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commit. No schema migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[memory] conflict_supersede_enabled = false` prevents future supersession; it does not unhide earlier rows.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected disappearance from Core list/recall, incorrect `superseded_by` markers, or genuine vector-backed replacements ceasing to supersede. Retaining more keyword-only facts is expected.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A; no other implementation or PR is superseded.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(web): keep the chat header on screen in narrow layouts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The chat header row (agent name, Files link, conversation picker, model picker) was a single `flex` row that did not wrap, and none of its items could shrink. On a phone it ran off the right edge: the model picker was mostly or entirely off screen and its menu opened off screen, so using it meant scrolling the chat area sideways. In a narrow split view (for example a 1024px window), each pane clipped the model picker, and at 1024px the left pane's model menu spilled into the right pane.
  - The row now wraps (`flex-wrap`), and the agent name and both picker buttons shrink and truncate (`min-w-0`, `max-w-full`, `truncate`, `shrink-0` on the icons).
  - A container query on the header (`@container`, Tailwind's built-in `@xl` = 36rem), rather than a viewport breakpoint, decides the narrow layout, so a narrow split pane counts as well as a phone: below 36rem of header content width the two pickers take their own full-width line, conversation picker at the start and model picker at the end, and the conversation menu opens from its picker's start edge (`start-0 @xl:start-auto @xl:end-0`, `max-w-[100cqw]`) so it stays within the header's width. This is the first container query in the dashboard; Tailwind v4 supports them without a plugin, and the `browserslist` targets (Chrome/Edge 111, Firefox 113, Safari 16.2) all support them.
  - The menus are anchored with logical positions (`start-0`/`end-0`) instead of `left-0`/`right-0`, and the pickers' group uses `ms-auto`, so the pickers' placement and the menus' anchoring would mirror if the dashboard ever sets `dir="rtl"` (it does not today; the menu items' text alignment is unchanged).
- **Scope boundary:** At 36rem of header content width and above, when the header's items fit on one line, the layout and both menu positions are unchanged; when they do not (long names in a medium-width window), the pickers now wrap to a second line, aligned to the end, instead of overflowing. No change to what the pickers do, to the chat toolbar row below the header (open PR #11920 makes that row wrap), or to the model menu's width (a model ID with no break points can still make that menu wider than a narrow pane; that predates this PR).
- **Blast radius:** The chat page header (`AgentChat.tsx`), in every open chat tab and split-view pane, and `SessionPicker`, whose menu position now depends on the header being the `@container` (it is rendered only there; a comment on the menu notes the dependency). On a phone or a narrow split pane, and in a wider header whose items do not fit on one line, the header is one line (32px) taller.
- **Linked issue(s):** None; noticed on a phone while using a local build that includes #11920. Related #11920.

### What this does, simply

On a phone, the bar at the top of a chat (the agent's name, Files, and the conversation and model pickers) was wider than the screen, so part of it was cut off and the page could be dragged sideways. Now, on narrow screens and panes, the pickers move to their own line, labels that don't fit are shortened with "…" (on a phone the conversation picker's label is usually shortened, for an unnamed conversation often to just "Conversation …" or less), and the conversation list opens where it fits. Split-view panes get the same layout when they're narrow. On a normal desktop window nothing changes unless the names are too long to fit, in which case the pickers move to a second line instead of running off.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `web` (dashboard chat)
- **Setup / preconditions:** an agent whose model or provider name is fairly long, and a phone or a browser window about 375px wide.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Open the agent's chat and look at the header row.
  2. Open the conversation picker, then the model picker.
  3. Open a second chat, switch to split view, and repeat at a window width of about 1024px.
  4. Repeat steps 1 and 2 in a full-width desktop window.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** in steps 1 to 3 the pickers sit on their own line, nothing runs off the edge, and both menus open within the header's (or pane's) width. Labels that don't fit are shortened with "…"; on a phone the conversation picker's label is usually shortened, for an unnamed conversation often to just "Conversation …" or less. In step 4 the header looks exactly as on `master`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** in step 1 the model picker is mostly or entirely off screen, and in step 2 its menu opens off screen, so using it means dragging the chat area sideways; in step 3 each pane clips the model picker.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `Web Permission Tests` job in `CI Required Gate` (`npm ci`, `cargo web check`, `test:permissions`, `test:contexts`, `test:sops`, `test:sop-editor`): `cargo web check` typechecks both changed files, and `test:contexts` (through `pretest:contexts`) renders `AgentChatInner`, but no test checks layout (see the gap below).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No CI check covers layout; the behaviour is covered by the browser checks and screenshots below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** in a Node 24 container on this branch, after generating the same API client files `cargo web check` writes, using its hermetic path (`cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- spec-dump --out <dir>` in a Rust container, copying `api-descriptions.ts` and `api-enums.ts` into `web/src/lib/`, then `npx openapi-typescript <dir>/openapi.json -o src/lib/api-generated.ts`):
  Summary of the runs (exit codes and `fail` counts from each run's output):
  ```text
  $ npm run typecheck   (exit 0)
  $ npm run test:permissions   (exit 0; 8 runs, fail 0 in each)
  $ npm run test:contexts   (exit 0; 4 runs, fail 0 in each)
  $ npm run test:sops   (exit 0; fail 0)
  $ npm run test:sop-editor   (exit 0; fail 0)
  $ npm run test   (exit 0; 8 runs, fail 0 in each)
  $ npx vite build   (exit 0)
  ✓ built in 956ms
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Against a local daemon (a v0.8.6-based build, pairing off, one agent with a long provider alias), with the dashboard from this branch served by the Vite dev server and the unpatched dashboard bundled in the daemon for comparison (its header code is the same as `master`), driven by Playwright:
  - Screenshots before and after at 320, 375 and 1280px with the conversation menu open and with the model menu open, at 640, 700, 768 and 900px with the conversation menu open, and in split view at 1024 and 1280px with each pane's conversation menu and model menu open. At 640 to 900px and 1280px, the conversation menu's position is the same before and after, in pixels; in split view at 1024px, the left pane's model menu spilled past the pane before (x 391 to 617, pane edge at 540) and stays inside it after (x 297 to 523).
  - A layout probe in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox: left-to-right and with `dir="rtl"` forced on the page; with normal labels and with the header labels replaced by a long agent alias, conversation title and model ID; at 12 widths from 320 to 1280px, including 607, 608 and 609px around the 36rem threshold. In all 144 cases the header had no horizontal overflow, and both picker buttons and the open conversation menu stayed within the header's left and right edges.
  - Not verified: a real phone, the model menu with a long model ID that has no break points, and Safari itself (WebKit through Playwright stood in for it).
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the web dashboard chat at `efec167a7`, served by the Vite dev server against the local daemon above, with screenshots in headless Chromium (Playwright) at the stated viewport widths; the layout probe also ran in WebKit and Firefox.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** in the first comment below, before and after: (1) 375px, menus closed; (2) 375px, model menu open; (3) split view at 1024px, model menu open in the left pane; (4) 1280px, menus closed (unchanged).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** opened the conversation menu at every width listed above and the model menu at 320, 375 and 1280px and in split view; on this branch every menu opened within the header's or pane's width and the header did not overflow, while on `master` the header ran off the edge at 320 and 375px and the model picker was clipped in split view at 1024px.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo web check` was not run directly; its generation and `tsc -b` steps were reproduced as described under Commands run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None

prs.title: feat(web): add a toggle to keep the live Thinking box collapsed
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - While a thinking model streams, the web chat's live Thinking box has `open={!streamingContent}` (from #4603): it is open until the answer starts, then closes. It opens again on every reply, and it snaps shut on anyone reading it when the answer arrives (#11919).
  - A new toolbar button, "Keep thinking collapsed", next to Compact and the tool-activity toggle, stores a per-browser preference in `localStorage` (`zeroclaw_keep_thinking_collapsed`) the same way they do. When it is on, React stops setting the live box's `open` attribute (`open={undefined}`), so the box starts collapsed and, while the toggle stays on, React never opens or closes it; the user opens or closes it as they like while the reply streams. The finished message shows it collapsed, as today. Turning the toggle on mid-stream collapses an open box at once; turning it off sets the box to today's state at once (open while reasoning, closed once the answer has started).
  - The button has one fixed label and reports its state with `aria-pressed`; when on, it shows the accent border and tint. (The neighbouring tool-activity button flips its label with its state, so with `aria-pressed` it is announced as something like "Hide tool activity, pressed"; a fixed label avoids that.)
  - A fourth button made the toolbar too wide for a phone or a narrow split-view pane; because the row is right-aligned and did not wrap, it overflowed off its left edge and the leftmost buttons could not be reached. The row now wraps onto a second line (`flex-wrap`), as other right-aligned button rows in the dashboard already do.
- **Scope boundary:** No change with the toggle off: the box keeps `open={!streamingContent}`. No change to finished messages, to how thinking is received, or to model thinking itself. The chat header row above the toolbar can also overflow on a phone; that predates this PR and is not changed here. English strings only, like the neighbouring toolbar keys; other locales fall back to English.
- **Blast radius:** The web chat page (`AgentChat.tsx`), including every open chat tab: `ChatWorkspace` keeps them all mounted, including both split-view panes. As with the compact and tool-activity toggles, each reads the preference when it mounts, so toggling in one tab does not update the others already open until they remount or the page reloads.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11919. Related #4603, #6388, #8803.

### What this does, simply

When a model thinks before answering, the web chat shows its reasoning in a "Thinking..." box that opens on its own and then closes when the answer starts. This adds a button to the chat toolbar that keeps that box closed instead, so you can open it only when you want to read the reasoning. The setting is remembered in your browser and is off unless you turn it on.

### Possible follow-ups (not in this PR)

- This is the third copy of the inline `localStorage` toggle in `AgentChat.tsx`. A small shared hook could replace all three, and could also keep open chat tabs in sync when one of them is toggled.
- The pressed state is shown by colour only (the accent border and tint; the label and icon stay the same). In lighter themes with a low-contrast accent, such as Everforest Light, it is subtle; in High Contrast Dark the tint matches the hover background. Swapping the icon when the toggle is on, as Compact does, would add a cue that does not depend on colour.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `web` (dashboard chat)
- **Setup / preconditions:** an agent on a model that streams reasoning (for example Qwen3 through llama.cpp), and a chat with at least one message so the toolbar shows.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Send a message and watch the Thinking box while the reply streams.
  2. Click "Keep thinking collapsed" in the toolbar and send another message.
  3. While the reasoning streams, open the box, then let the answer start.
  4. Reload the page and send another message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** with the toggle off (step 1), unchanged. In step 2, the box appears collapsed and stays collapsed when the answer starts. In step 3, the box stays open until the reply finishes. In step 4, the toggle is still on.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** there is no toggle (steps 2 and 4 do not apply); the box opens on every reply, and if you are reading it (step 3) it closes as soon as the answer starts.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `Web Permission Tests` job in `CI Required Gate` (`npm ci`, `cargo web check`, `test:permissions`, `test:contexts`, `test:sops`, `test:sop-editor`): `cargo web check` typechecks the changed `AgentChat.tsx`, and `test:contexts` (through `pretest:contexts`) renders `AgentChatInner`, but no test exercises the toggle (see the gap below).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The web suites render `AgentChatInner` (`sessionLifecycle.test.ts`), but none exercises the toolbar toggles or the live Thinking box's `open` state; the behaviour is covered by the manual check and screenshots below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** in a Node 24 container on this branch, after generating the same API client files `cargo web check` writes, using its hermetic path (`cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- spec-dump --out <dir>` in a Rust container, copying `api-descriptions.ts` and `api-enums.ts` into `web/src/lib/`, then `npx openapi-typescript <dir>/openapi.json -o src/lib/api-generated.ts`):
  ```text
  $ npm run typecheck   (exit 0)
  $ npm run test:permissions   (exit 0)
  ℹ tests 12 ℹ pass 12 ℹ fail 0   (+ 7 more files: 2, 3, 2, 2, 2, 4, 5 tests, all pass)
  $ npm run test:contexts   (exit 0)
  ℹ tests 8 ℹ pass 8 ℹ fail 0
  ℹ tests 14 ℹ pass 14 ℹ fail 0
  ℹ tests 19 ℹ pass 19 ℹ fail 0
  ℹ tests 32 ℹ pass 32 ℹ fail 0
  $ npm run test:sops   (exit 0)
  ℹ tests 5 ℹ pass 5 ℹ fail 0
  $ npm run test:sop-editor   (exit 0)
  ℹ tests 10 ℹ pass 10 ℹ fail 0
  $ npm run test   (exit 0; 8 runs over 17 files, fail 0 in each)
  $ npx vite build   (exit 0)
  ✓ built in 746ms
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** On a live daemon with a Qwen3.8 model through llama.cpp: with the toggle off, the Thinking box opened while the reasoning streamed; with it on, the box stayed collapsed while the model reasoned and after the answer had finished, and the button showed its pressed style. Turning the toggle on while the model was reasoning collapsed the open box; turning it off while the model was reasoning opened it. Not verified live: opening or closing the box by hand mid-stream with the toggle on, the box staying collapsed at the moment the answer starts, the toggle-off case once the answer has started, the setting surviving a reload, a screen reader's announcement, themes other than the one shown, split view, multiple tabs, and the toolbar wrapping on a phone or in a narrow pane (only reasoned about and built).
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the web dashboard chat, served by a local v0.8.6-based build carrying this branch's diff unchanged (plus unrelated local patches, including a chat-input change in the same file), in a desktop browser at full width.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** in the first comment below: (1) toggle off, reasoning streaming in the open box; (2) toggle on, the box collapsed to "Thinking..." while the model reasons, with the button pressed.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** sent the same kind of prompt twice, the second time after turning the toggle on; the first reply opened the box, the second did not.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo web check` was not run directly; its generation and `tsc -b` steps were reproduced as described under Commands run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** the toolbar toggle itself; it is off by default.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** the live Thinking box opens while the toggle is on, or behaves differently from before while it is off.
